They shanayam (two) chalam (dream) a chalawam (dream), each ayash (husband/individual man) his chalawam (dream), in achad (one) layal (night), each ayash (husband/individual man) according to the patharawan (interpretation) of his chalawam (dream), the cupbearer and the baker of the malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), who were asar (bound) in the bayath (house).
Yawasap (Joseph) bawaa (come) in to them in the baqar (morning), and saw them, and saw that they were zaip (sad).
He shaal (asked) Paraih (Pharaoh's) sarayas (officers) who were with him in custody in his adawan (master / lord) bayath (house), amar (spoke), Why do you panayam (look) so rai (sad) today?

They amar (spoke) to him, "We have chalam (dream) a chalawam (dream), and there is no one who can pathar (interpret) it." Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke) to them, Don't patharawan (interpretations) belong to Alahayam? Please sapar (book) it to me.
The shar (prince / ruler) cupbearer sapar (book) his chalawam (dream) to Yawasap (Joseph), and amar (spoke) to him, In my chalawam (dream), behold, a gapan (vine) panayam (was) in front of me,
And in the gapan (vine) were shalawash (three) branches. It was as though it parach (budded), it natz (blossomed), and its ashakawal (clusters) produced ripe inab (grapes).

Paraih (Pharaoh's) kawas (cup) was in my yad (hand); and I laqach (take / seized) the inab (grapes), and shachat (pressed) them into Paraih (Pharaoh's) kawas (cup), and I nathan (give) the kawas (cup) into Paraih (Pharaoh's) kap (hand).
Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke) to him, This is its patharawan (interpretation): the shalawash (three) branches are shalawash (three) yawam (day).

Within shalawash (three) more yawam (day), Paraih (Pharaoh) will nashaa (lift) up your raash (head), and shawab (turn back / repent) you to your kan (for sure). You will nathan (give) Paraih (Pharaoh's) kawas (cup) into his yad (hand), the mashapat (way) you did when you were his cupbearer.

But zakar (remembrance/memory) me when it will be yatab (well) with you, and please show chasad (grace) to me, and zakar (remembrance/memory) mention of me to Paraih (Pharaoh), and yatzaa (go out / come out) me out of this bayath (house).

For ganab (indeed), I was stolen away out of the aratz (Earth/land) of the ibaray (hebrews), and here also ishah (make) I done maawamah (nothing) that they should shawam (place / establish / appoint) me into the bawar (dungeon).

When the shar (prince / ruler) baker raah (see) that the interpretation was tawab (pleasant/functional), he amar (spoke) to Yawasap (Joseph), I also was in my chalawam (dream), and behold, shalawash (three) sal (baskets) of charay (white) bread were on my raash (head).
In the ilayawan (uppermost) sal (basket) there was all kinds of baked food for Paraih (Pharaoh), and the iwap (flying) akal (eat) them out of the sal (basket) on my raash (head).
Yawasap (Joseph) inah (answer / respond), This is its patharawan (interpretation). The shalawash (three) sal (baskets) are shalawash (three) yawam (day).

Within shalawash (three) more yawam (day), Paraih (Pharaoh) will nashaa (lift) up your raash (head) from off you, and will thalah (hang) you on a itz (tree); and the iwap (flying) will akal (eat) your bashar (flesh) from off you.

It happened the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), which was Paraih (Pharaoh's) birthday, that he ishah (make) a mashathah (feast) for all his ibad (servant), and he nashaa (lift) up the raash (head) of the shar (prince / ruler) cupbearer and the head of the shar (prince / ruler) baker thawak (midst) his ibad (servant).
He shawab (turn back / repent) the shar (prince / ruler) cupbearer to his position again, and he nathan (give) the kawas (cup) into Paraih (Pharaoh's) kap (hand);
But he hanged the shar (prince / ruler) baker, as Yawasap (Joseph) had pathar (interpreted) to them.
Yet the shar (prince / ruler) cupbearer didn't zakar (remembrance/memory) Yawasap (Joseph), but shakach (forgot) him.
It happened at the end of yawam (day) full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and behold, he stood by the yaar (river).
Behold, there ilah (go up / offer) up out of the yaar (river) shabai (seven) cattle, sleek and barayaa (fat), and they raih (fed) in the marsh grass.

Behold, shabai (seven) other cattle ilah (go up / offer) up achar (other) them out of the yaar (river), ugly and daq (thin), and imad (stood) by the other cattle on the shapah (brink) of the yaar (river).
The ugly and daq (thin) cattle akal (eat) up the shabai (seven) sleek and barayaa (fat) cattle. So Paraih (Pharaoh) awoke.

He yashan (slept) and chalam (dream) a shanay (second) time: and behold, shabai (seven) shabal (heads) of grain ilah (go up / offer) up on achad (one) qanah (stalk), healthy and tawab (pleasant/functional).
Behold, shabai (seven) shabal (heads) of grain, daq (thin) and shadap (blasted) with the east qadayam (wind), tzamach (sprung) up achar (other) them.
The daq (thin) shabal (heads) of grain balai (swallowed) up the shabai (seven) healthy and malaa (full) shabal (ears). Paraih (Pharaoh) awoke, and behold, it was a chalawam (dream).

It happened in the baqar (morning) that his rawach (spirit / wind) was paim (troubled), and he shalach (send) and qaraa (called) for all of Matzarayam (Egypt's) charatam (magicians) and chakam (wise) men. Paraih (Pharaoh) sapar (book) them his chalawam (dreams), but there was no one who could pathar (interpret) them to Paraih (Pharaoh).
Then the shar (prince / ruler) cupbearer dabar (word / matter) to Paraih (Pharaoh), amar (spoke), I zakar (remembrance/memory) my chataa (faults) today.

Paraih (Pharaoh) was qatzap (angry) with his ibad (servant), and nathan (give) me in custody in the bayath (house) of the shar (prince / ruler) of the tabach (guard), me and the shar (prince / ruler) baker.

We chalam (dream) a chalawam (dream) in achad (one) layal (night), I and he. We chalam (dream) each ayash (husband/individual man) according to the patharawan (interpretation) of his chalawam (dream).

There was with us there a nair (young) man, a ibaray (hebrew), ibad (servant) to the shar (prince / ruler) of the tabach (guard), and we sapar (book) him, and he pathar (interpreted) to us our chalawam (dreams). To each ayash (husband/individual man) according to his chalawam (dream) he pathar (interpreted).
It happened, as he pathar (interpreted) to us, so it was: he shawab (turn back / repent) me to my kan (for sure), and he hanged him.

Then Paraih (Pharaoh) shalach (send) and qaraa (called) Yawasap (Joseph), and they rawatz (brought) him hastily out of the bawar (dungeon). He galach (shaved) himself, chalap (changed) his shamalah (clothing), and bawaa (come) in to Paraih (Pharaoh).

Paraih (Pharaoh) amar (spoke) to Yawasap (Joseph), I have chalam (dream) a chalawam (dream), and there is no one who can pathar (interpret) it. I have shamai (hearken / hear) it amar (spoke) of you, that when you shamai (hearken / hear) a chalawam (dream) you can pathar (interpret) it.

Yawasap (Joseph) inah (answer / respond) Paraih (Pharaoh), amar (spoke), It isn't in me. Alahayam will inah (answer / respond) Paraih (Pharaoh) an inah (answer / respond) of shalawam (peace / safety).
Paraih (Pharaoh) dabar (word / matter) to Yawasap (Joseph), In my chalawam (dream), behold, I imad (stood) on the shapah (brink) of the yaar (river):
And behold, there ilah (go up / offer) up out of the yaar (river) shabai (seven) cattle, barayaa (fat) and sleek. They raih (fed) in the marsh grass,

And behold, shabai (seven) other cattle ilah (go up / offer) up achar (other) them, dalah (poor) and very ugly and raq (thin), such as I laa (NOT) raah (see) in all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) for ugliness.
The raq (thin) and ugly cattle akal (eat) up the raashawan (first) shabai (seven) barayaa (fat) cattle,
And when they bawaa (come) eaten them up, it couldn't be yadai (known) that they bawaa (come) eaten them, but they were still ugly, as at the thachalah (beginning). So I awoke.
I raah (see) in my chalawam (dream), and behold, shabai (seven) shabal (heads) of grain ilah (go up / offer) up on achad (one) qanah (stalk), malaa (full) and tawab (pleasant/functional):
And behold, shabai (seven) shabal (heads) of grain, tzanam (withered), daq (thin), and shadap (blasted) with the east qadayam (wind), tzamach (sprung) up achar (other) them.

The daq (thin) shabal (heads) of grain balai (swallowed) up the shabai (seven) tawab (pleasant/functional) shabal (heads) of grain. I amar (spoke) it to the charatam (magicians), but there was no nagad (one) who could explain it to me.
Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke) to Paraih (Pharaoh), The chalawam (dream) of Paraih (Pharaoh) is achad (one). What Alahayam is ishah (make) to do he has nagad (declared) to Paraih (Pharaoh).

The shabai (seven) tawab (pleasant/functional) cattle are shabai (seven) shanah (years); and the shabai (seven) tawab (pleasant/functional) shabal (heads) of grain are shabai (seven) shanah (years). The chalawam (dream) is achad (one).

The shabai (seven) raq (thin) and ugly cattle that ilah (go up / offer) up achar (other) them are shabai (seven) shanah (years), and also the shabai (seven) rayaq (empty) shabal (heads) of grain shadap (blasted) with the east qadayam (wind); they will be shabai (seven) shanah (years) of raib (famine).
That is the thing which I dabar (word / matter) to Paraih (Pharaoh). What Alahayam is ishah (make) to do he raah (see) shown to Paraih (Pharaoh).
Behold, there bawaa (come) shabai (seven) shanah (years) of gadawal (very great/important/mighty) plenty throughout all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

There will qawam (rise up) achar (other) them shabai (seven) shanah (years) of raib (famine), and all the plenty will be shakach (forgotten) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt). The raib (famine) will kalah (complete / finish) the aratz (Earth/land),
And the plenty yadai (will) not be known in the aratz (Earth/land) by panayam (reason) of that raib (famine) which achar (other); for it will be very kabad (grievous).
The chalawam (dream) was shanah (doubled) to Paraih (Pharaoh), dabar (word / matter) the thing is kawan (established) by Alahayam, and Alahayam will mahar (shortly) ishah (make) it to pass.

Now therefore let Paraih (Pharaoh) raah (see) for a discreet and chakam (wise) ayash (husband/individual man), and shayath (put / appoint / make) him over the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

Let Paraih (Pharaoh) ishah (make) this, and let him paqad (visit) overseers over the aratz (Earth/land), and take up the chamash (fifth) part of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt's) produce in the shabai (seven) shabai (plenteous) shanah (years).

Let them qabatz (gather) all the akal (food) of these tawab (pleasant/functional) shanah (years) that bawaa (come), and tzabar (lay) up grain under the yad (hand) of Paraih (Pharaoh) for akal (food) in the iyar (cities), and let them shamar (keep/guard) it.

The akal (food) will be for a paqadawan (store) to the aratz (Earth/land) against the shabai (seven) shanah (years) of raib (famine), which will be in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt); that the aratz (Earth/land) not karath (cut) through the raib (famine).
The thing was yatab (good) in the iyan (eye) of Paraih (Pharaoh), and in the iyan (eye) of all his ibad (servant).
Paraih (Pharaoh) amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), Can we matzaa (find) such a one as zah (this/that/these), a ayash (husband/individual man) in whom is the rawach (spirit / wind) of Alahayam?
Paraih (Pharaoh) amar (spoke) to Yawasap (Joseph), Because Alahayam yadai (has) shown you all of this, there is none so discreet and chakam (wise) as you.
You shall be over my bayath (house), and according to your pah (word) will all my im (people / nation) be nashaq (ruled). Only in the kasaa (throne) I will be greater than you.
Paraih (Pharaoh) amar (spoke) to Yawasap (Joseph), raah (see), I nathan (give) set you over all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

Paraih (Pharaoh) sawar (took) off his signet tabaith (ring) from his yad (hand), and nathan (give) it on Yawasap (Joseph's) yad (hand), and arrayed him in bagad (robes) of shash (six) linen, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) a zahab (gold) rabayad (chain) about his tzawaar (neck),

And he rakab (made) him to ride in the mashanah (second) marakabah (chariot) which he had. They qaraa (called) panayam (before) him, "abarak (bow) the knee!" He set him over all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

Paraih (Pharaoh) amar (spoke) to Yawasap (Joseph), I am Paraih (Pharaoh), and balaiday (without) you shall no ayash (husband/individual man) rawam (will lift up) up his yad (hand) or his ragal (feet / foot) in all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

Paraih (Pharaoh) qaraa (called) Yawasap (Joseph's) sham (name) Tzapanathapainach (Zaphenath-Paneah); and he nathan (give) him Asanath (Asenath), the bath (daughter) Pawatayaparai (of) Potiphera kahan (priest) Awan (of) On as a ashah (wife/individual woman). Yawasap (Joseph) yatzaa (go out / come out) out over the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

Yawasap (Joseph) was shalawashayam (thirty) shanah (years) ban (son) when he imad (stood) panayam (before) Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt). Yawasap (Joseph) yatzaa (go out / come out) out from the panayam (presence) of Paraih (Pharaoh), and ibar (pass over/through) throughout all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
In the shabai (seven) shabai (plenteous) shanah (years) the aratz (Earth/land) produced abundantly.

He qabatz (gathered) up all the akal (food) of the shabai (seven) shanah (years) which were in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and nathan (give) up the akal (food) in the iyar (cities): the akal (food) of the shadah (field), which was around every iyar (city), he nathan (give) up in the same.
Yawasap (Joseph) tzabar (laid) up grain as the chawal (sand) of the yam (sea/waters), very much, until he stopped sapar (book), for it was ayan (without) masapar (number).

To Yawasap (Joseph) were yalad (birth / begot) shanayam (two) ban (son) before the shanah (year) of raib (famine) bawaa (come), whom Asanath (Asenath), the bath (daughter) Pawatayaparai (of) Potiphera kahan (priest) Awan (of) On, yalad (birth / begot) to him.

Yawasap (Joseph) qaraa (called) the sham (name) of the bakawar (firstborn) Manashah (Manasseh), "For," he said, Alahayam has made me nashah (forget) all my imal (toil), and all my ab (father) bayath (house).
The sham (name) of the shanay (second), he qaraa (called) Aparayam (Ephraim): For Alahayam has parah (made) me fruitful in the aratz (Earth/land) of my inay (affliction).
The shabai (seven) shanah (years) of plenty, that were in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), came to an kalah (complete / finish).

The shabai (seven) shanah (years) of raib (famine) chalal (began) to bawaa (come), just as Yawasap (Joseph) had amar (spoke). There was raib (famine) in all aratz (Earth/land), but in all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) there was lacham (bread).

When all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) was raib (famished), the im (people / nation) tzaiq (cried) to Paraih (Pharaoh) for lacham (bread), and Paraih (Pharaoh) amar (spoke) to all the Matzarayam (Egyptians), yalak (go) to Yawasap (Joseph). What he amar (spoke) to you, ishah (make).

The raib (famine) panayam (was) over all the surface of the aratz (Earth/land). Yawasap (Joseph) pathach (opened) all the store houses, and shabar (sold) to the Matzarayam (Egyptians). The raib (famine) was severe in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
All aratz (Earth/land) bawaa (come) into Matzarayam (Egypt), to Yawasap (Joseph), to shabar (buy) grain, because the raib (famine) was severe in all the aratz (Earth/land).
Now Yaiqab (Jacob) raah (see) that there yash (was) grain in Matzarayam (Egypt), and Yaiqab (Jacob) amar (spoke) to his ban (son), Why do you raah (see) at one another?

He amar (spoke), Behold, I have shamai (hearken / hear) that there is grain in Matzarayam (Egypt). Yarad (go) down there, and shabar (buy) for us from there, so that we may chayah (live), and not mawath (death).
Yawasap (Joseph's) ishar (ten) ach (brother/kinsman) yarad (went) down to shabar (buy) grain from Matzarayam (Egypt).

But Yaiqab (Jacob) didn't shalach (send) Banayamayan (Benjamin), Yawasap (Joseph's) ach (brother/kinsman), with his ach (brother/kinsman); for he amar (spoke), Lest perhaps harm qaraa (called) to him.
The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) bawaa (come) to shabar (buy) thawak (midst) those who bawaa (come), for the raib (famine) was in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan).

Yawasap (Joseph) was the shalayat (governor) over the aratz (Earth/land). It was he who shabar (sold) to all the im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land). Yawasap (Joseph's) ach (brother/kinsman) bawaa (come), and shachah (bowed) themselves down to him with their ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land)

Yawasap (Joseph) raah (see) his ach (brother/kinsman), and he recognized them, but acted like a stranger to them, and dabar (word / matter) qashah (rough / hard) with them. He amar (spoke) to them, "ayan (where) did you bawaa (come) from?" They amar (spoke), From the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan) to shabar (buy) akal (food).
Yawasap (Joseph) recognized his ach (brother/kinsman), but they didn't recognize him.

Yawasap (Joseph) zakar (remembrance/memory) the chalawam (dreams) which he chalam (dream) about them, and amar (spoke) to them, You are ragal (spies)! You bawaa (come) come to raah (see) the irawah (nakedness) of the aratz (Earth/land).
They amar (spoke) to him, No, my Adawan, but your ibad (servant) bawaa (come) come to shabar (buy) akal (food).
We are all achad (one) ayash (husband/individual man) ban (son); we are honest men. Your ibad (servant) are not ragal (spies).
He amar (spoke) to them, No, but you bawaa (come) come to raah (see) the irawah (nakedness) of the aratz (Earth/land)!

They amar (spoke), We, your ibad (servant), are shanayam (two) ach (brother/kinsman), the ban (son) of achad (one) ayash (husband/individual man) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan); and behold, the youngest is this yawam (day) with our ab (father), and achad (one) is no more.
Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke) to them, It is like I dabar (word / matter) you, amar (spoke), ‘You are ragal (spies)!’
By this you shall be tested. By the chay (life) of Paraih (Pharaoh), you shall not yatzaa (go out / come out) out from here, unless your youngest ach (brother/kinsman) bawaa (come) here.

Shalach (send) achad (one) of you, and let him laqach (take / seized) your ach (brother/kinsman), and you shall be asar (bound), that your dabar (word / matter) may be tested, whether there is amath (truth) in you, or laa (NOT) by the chay (life) of Paraih (Pharaoh) surely you are ragal (spies).
He asap (put) them all together into custody for shalawash (three) yawam (day).
Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke) to them the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), "ishah (make) this, and chayah (live), for I yaraa (fear / be afraid) Alahayam.

If you are honest achad (one), then let one of your ach (brother/kinsman) be asar (bound) in your mashamar (prison); but you yalak (go), bawaa (come) grain for the raibawan (famine) of your bayath (house).
Bawaa (come) your youngest ach (brother/kinsman) to me; so will your dabar (word / matter) be aman (believe / have faith), and you won't mawath (death)." They ishah (make) so.

They amar (spoke) ayash (husband/individual man) to ach (brother/kinsman), We are certainly asham (guilty) concerning our ach (brother/kinsman), in that we raah (see) the tzarah (distress) of his napash (living being/soul), when he begged us, and we wouldn't shamai (hearken / hear). Therefore this tzarah (distress) bawaa (come) come upon us.

Raawaban (Reuben) inah (answer / respond) them, amar (spoke), Didn't I amar (spoke) you, saying, ‘Don't chataa (sin) against the yalad (birth / begot),’ and you wouldn't shamai (hearken / hear)? Therefore also, behold, his dam (blood) is darash (required).
They didn't yadai (know) that Yawasap (Joseph) shamai (hearken / hear) them; for there was an lawatz (interpreter) between them.

He sabab (turned) himself away from them, and bakah (wept). Then he shawab (turn back / repent) to them, and dabar (word / matter) to them, and laqach (take / seized) Shamaiwan (Simeon) from among them, and asar (bound) him before their iyan (eye).

Then Yawasap (Joseph) gave a tzawah (command) to malaa (fill) their kalay (bags) with grain, and to shawab (turn back / repent) each ayash (husband/individual man) kasap (money) into his shaq (sack), and to nathan (give) them food for the darak (way). So it was ishah (make) to them.
They loaded their donkeys with their grain, and departed from there.

As achad (one) of them pathach (opened) his shaq (sack) to nathan (give) his donkey food in the malawan (lodging) place, he raah (see) his kasap (money). Behold, it was in the pah (mouth) of his amathachath (sack).

He amar (spoke) to his ach (brother/kinsman), "My kasap (money) is shawab (turn back / repent)! Hanah (Behold), it is in my amathachath (sack)!" Their lab (heart) yatzaa (go out / come out) them, and they turned charad (trembling) ayash (husband/individual man) to ach (brother/kinsman), amar (spoke), What is this that Alahayam ishah (make) done to us?
They bawaa (come) to Yaiqab (Jacob) their ab (father), to the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), and nagad (told) him all that had qarah (happened) to them, amar (spoke),
The ayash (husband/individual man), the Adawan of the aratz (Earth/land), dabar (word / matter) qashah (rough / hard) with us, and nathan (give) us for ragal (spies) of the aratz (Earth/land).
We amar (spoke) to him, ‘We are honest men. We are no ragal (spies).

We are ishar (-teen) ach (brother/kinsman), ban (son) of our ab (father); achad (one) is no more, and the youngest is this yawam (day) with our ab (father) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan).’

The ayash (husband/individual man), the Adawan of the aratz (Earth/land), amar (spoke) to us, ‘By this I yadai (will) know that you are honest men: yanach (leave) achad (one) of your ach (brother/kinsman) with me, and laqach (take / seized) grain for the raibawan (famine) of your bayath (house), and go your yalak (way).

Bawaa (come) your youngest ach (brother/kinsman) to me. Then I yadai (will) know that you are not ragal (spies), but that you are honest men. So I will nathan (give) your ach (brother/kinsman) to you, and you shall sachar (trade) in the aratz (Earth/land).’

It happened as they rawaq (emptied) their shaq (sacks), that behold, each ayash (husband/individual man) tzarawar (bundle) of kasap (money) was in his shaq (sack). When they and their ab (father) raah (see) their tzarawar (bundles) of kasap (money), they were yaraa (fear / be afraid).

Yaiqab (Jacob), their ab (father), amar (spoke) to them, You have shakal (bereaved) me of my sons Yawasap (Joseph) is no more, Shamaiwan (Simeon) is no more, and you want to laqach (take / seized) Banayamayan (Benjamin) away. All these things are against me.

Raawaban (Reuben) amar (spoke) to his ab (father), amar (spoke), mawath (death) my shanayam (two) ban (son), if I don't bawaa (come) him to you. Entrust him to my care, and I will shawab (turn back / repent) him to you again.

He amar (spoke), My ban (son) shall not yarad (go) down with you; for his ach (brother/kinsman) is mawath (death), and he only is shaar (left). If harm qaraa (called) to him along the darak (way) in which you yalak (go), then you will yarad (bring) down my shayabah (old age / white hair (due to age)) hairs with yagawan (sorrow) to shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife).
The famine was severe in the aratz (Earth/land).

It happened, when they kalah (complete / finish) eaten up the grain which they bawaa (come) brought out of Matzarayam (Egypt), their ab (father) amar (spoke) to them, shawab (turn back / repent) again, shabar (buy) us a mait (little) more akal (food).

Yahawadah (Judah) amar (spoke) to him, amar (spoke), The ayash (husband/individual man) iwad (admonish/bear witness against) warned us, amar (spoke), ‘You shall not raah (see) my panayam (face), unless your ach (brother/kinsman) is with you.’
If you'll shalach (send) our ach (brother/kinsman) with us, we'll yarad (go) down and shabar (buy) you akal (food),

But if you'll not shalach (send) him, we'll not yarad (go) down, for the ayash (husband/individual man) amar (spoke) to us, ‘You shall not raah (see) my panayam (face), unless your ach (brother/kinsman) is with you.’
Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke), Why raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) you treat me so badly, nagad (telling) the ayash (husband/individual man) that you had another ach (brother/kinsman)?

They amar (spoke), The ayash (husband/individual man) shaal (asked) directly concerning ourselves, and concerning our relatives, amar (spoke), ‘Is your ab (father) still chay (life)? Yash (have) you another ach (brother/kinsman)?’ We just answered his dabar (word / matter). Is there any way we yadai (could) yadai (know) that he would amar (spoke), ‘yarad (bring) your ach (brother/kinsman) down?’

Yahawadah (Judah) amar (spoke) to Yasharaal (Israel), his ab (father), shalach (send) the nair (boy) with me, and we'll qawam (rise up) up and yalak (go), so that we may chayah (live), and not mawath (death), both we, and you, and also our little tap (ones).

I'll be collateral for him. From my yad (hand) will you baqash (require) him. If I don't bawaa (come) him to you, and yatzag (set) him panayam (before) you, then let me chataa (bear) the blame forever,
For if we hadn't mahah (delayed), shawab (turn back / repent) we would have returned a paim (second) time by now.

Their ab (father), Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke) to them, If it must be so, then ishah (make) this. Laqach (take / seized) from the choice zamarah (fruits) of the aratz (Earth/land) in your kalay (bags), and yarad (carry) down a manachah (present) for the ayash (husband/individual man), a mait (little) tzaray (balm), a mait (little) dabash (honey), nakaath (spices) and lat (myrrh), batan (nuts), and shaqad (almonds);

And laqach (take / seized) mashanah (double) kasap (money) in your yad (hand), and shawab (turn back / repent) back the kasap (money) that was shawab (turn back / repent) in the pah (mouth) of your amathachath (sacks). Perhaps it was an mashagah (oversight).
Laqach (take / seized) your ach (brother/kinsman) also, qawam (rise up) up, and shawab (turn back / repent) to the ayash (husband/individual man).

May Al Shaday nathan (give) you racham (mercy) panayam (before) the ayash (husband/individual man), that he may release to you your other ach (brother/kinsman) and Banayamayan (Benjamin). If I am shakal (bereaved) of my shakal (children), I am bereaved.

The ayash (husband/individual man) laqach (take / seized) that manachah (present), and they laqach (take / seized) mashanah (double) kasap (money) in their yad (hand), and Banayamayan (Benjamin); and qawam (rise up) up, yarad (went) down to Matzarayam (Egypt), and imad (stood) panayam (before) Yawasap (Joseph).

When Yawasap (Joseph) raah (see) Banayamayan (Benjamin) with them, he amar (spoke) to the steward of his bayath (house), bawaa (come) the ayash (husband/individual man) into the bayath (house), and butcher an animal, and kawan (prepare); for the ayash (husband/individual man) will akal (eat) with me at tzahar (noon).
The ayash (husband/individual man) ishah (make) as Yawasap (Joseph) commanded, and the ayash (husband/individual man) bawaa (come) the ishah (make) to Yawasap (Joseph's) bayath (house).

The ayash (husband/individual man) were yaraa (fear / be afraid), because they were bawaa (come) to Yawasap (Joseph's) bayath (house); and they amar (spoke), dabar (word / matter) of the kasap (money) that was shawab (turn back / repent) in our amathachath (sacks) at the thachalah (first) time, we're bawaa (come) in; that he may galal (seek) occasion against us, attack us, and laqach (take / seized) us as ibad (servant), along with our donkeys.
They nagash (came) near to the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yawasap (Joseph's) bayath (house), and they dabar (word / matter) to him at the pathach (door) of the bayath (house),
And amar (spoke), Oh, my Adawan, we yarad (indeed) yarad (came) down the thachalah (first) time to shabar (buy) akal (food).

When we bawaa (come) to the malawan (lodging) place, we pathach (opened) our amathachath (sacks), and behold, each ayash (husband/individual man) kasap (money) was in the pah (mouth) of his amathachath (sack), our kasap (money) in full mashaqal (weight). We have shawab (turn back / repent) it back in our yad (hand).

We have yarad (brought) down other kasap (money) in our yad (hand) to shabar (buy) akal (food). We don't yadai (know) who shawam (place / establish / appoint) our kasap (money) in our amathachath (sacks).

He amar (spoke), "shalawam (peace / safety) be to you. Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). Your Alahayam, and the Alahayam of your ab (father), nathan (give) given you matamawan (treasure) in your amathachath (sacks). I received your kasap (money)." He yatzaa (go out / come out) Shamaiwan (Simeon) out to them.

The ayash (husband/individual man) bawaa (come) the ayash (husband/individual man) into Yawasap (Joseph's) bayath (house), and nathan (give) them mayam (Waters), and they rachatz (washed) their ragal (feet / foot). He nathan (give) their donkeys fodder.
They kawan (prepared) the manachah (present) for Yawasap (Joseph's) bawaa (come) at tzahar (noon), for they shamai (hearken / hear) that they should akal (eat) lacham (bread) there.

When Yawasap (Joseph) bawaa (come) bayath (house), they bawaa (come) him the manachah (present) which was in their yad (hand) into the bayath (house), and shachah (bowed) themselves down to him to the aratz (Earth/land).
He shaal (asked) them of their shalawam (peace / safety), and amar (spoke), Is your ab (father) shalawam (peace / safety), the old zaqan (man) of whom you amar (spoke)? Is he yet chay (life)?
They amar (spoke), "Your ibad (servant), our ab (father), is shalawam (peace / safety). He is still chay (life)." They qadad (bowed) down shachah (humbly).

He nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye), and raah (see) Banayamayan (Benjamin), his ach (brother/kinsman), his am (mother) ban (son), and amar (spoke), "Is this your youngest ach (brother/kinsman), of whom you amar (spoke) to me?" He amar (spoke), Alahayam be gracious to you, my ban (son).
Yawasap (Joseph) hurried, for his racham (heart) kamar (yearned) over his ach (brother/kinsman); and he baqash (sought) a place to bakah (weep). He bawaa (come) into his room, and bakah (wept) there.
He rachatz (washed) his panayam (face), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out. He controlled himself, and amar (spoke), shawam (place / establish / appoint) the meal.

They served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Matzaray (Egyptians), that akal (eat) with him, by themselves, because the Matzaray (Egyptians) don't akal (eat) lacham (bread) with the ibaray (hebrews), for that is an thawaibah (abomination) to the Matzaray (Egyptians).

They yashab (inhabit/dwell) panayam (before) him, the bakawar (firstborn) according to his bakawarah (birthright), and the youngest according to his tzaiyarah (youth), and the ayash (husband/individual man) thamah (marveled) ayash (husband/individual man) with rai (neigbor/another person).

He sent portions to them from panayam (before) him, but Banayamayan (Benjamin's) portion was chamash (five) yad (hand) as much as any of theirs. They shathah (drinks), and were shakar (merry) with him.

He tzawah (commanded) the steward of his bayath (house), amar (spoke), "malaa (fill) the ayash (husband/individual man) amathachath (sacks) with akal (food), as much as they yakal (can) nashaa (lift), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) each ayash (husband/individual man) kasap (money) in his amathachath (sack's) pah (mouth).

Shawam (place / establish / appoint) my gabayai (cup), the kasap (silver) gabayai (cup), in the amathachath (sack's) pah (mouth) of the youngest, with his grain kasap (money)." He ishah (make) according to the dabar (word / matter) that Yawasap (Joseph) had dabar (word / matter).
As soon as the baqar (morning) was awar (light), the ayash (husband/individual man) were shalach (send) away, they and their donkeys.

When they yatzaa (go out / come out) gone out of the iyar (city), and were not yet rachaq (far) off, Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke) to his bayath (house), Up, radap (follow) achar (other) the ayash (husband/individual man). When you nashag (overtake) them, ask them, ‘Why have you shalam (rewarded) rai (evil) for tawab (pleasant/functional)?
Isn't this that from which my Adawan shathah (drinks), and by which he nachash (indeed) nachash (divines)? You have done raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) in so ishah (make).’
He overtook them, and he dabar (word / matter) these dabar (word / matter) to them.
They amar (spoke) to him, Why does my Adawan dabar (word / matter) such dabar (word / matter) as these? Chalayalah (far) be it from your ibad (servant) that they should ishah (make) such a thing!

Behold, the kasap (money), which we matzaa (found) in our amathachath (sacks)' pah (mouths), we shawab (turn back / repent) again to you out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan). How then should we ganab (steal) kasap (silver) or zahab (gold) out of your adawan (master / lord) bayath (house)?
With whomever of your ibad (servant) it is matzaa (found), let him mawath (death), and we also will be my adawan (master / lord) ibad (servant).
He amar (spoke), Now also let it be according to your kan (for sure): he with whom it is matzaa (found) will be my ibad (servant); and you will be naqay (blameless).
Then they hurried, and each ayash (husband/individual man) took his amathachath (sack) down to the aratz (Earth/land), and each ayash (husband/individual man) pathach (opened) his amathachath (sack).

He chapash (searched), beginning with the gadawal (very great/important/mighty), and kalah (complete / finish) at the youngest. The gabayai (cup) was matzaa (found) in Banayamayan (Benjamin's) amathachath (sack).
Then they qarai (tore) their clothes, and each ayash (husband/individual man) imas (loaded) his donkey, and shawab (turn back / repent) to the iyar (city).

Yahawadah (Judah) and his ach (brother/kinsman) bawaa (come) to Yawasap (Joseph's) bayath (house), and he was still there. They napal (fall / be cast down) on the aratz (Earth/land) panayam (before) him.
Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke) to them, What maishah (deed) is this that you ishah (make) done? Don't you know that such a ayash (husband/individual man) as I can nachash (indeed) divine?

Yahawadah (Judah) amar (spoke), What will we tell my Adawan? What will we dabar (word / matter)? Or how will we tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) ourselves? Alahayam matzaa (has) found out the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of your ibad (servant). Behold, we are my adawan (master / lord) ibad (servant), gam (indeed / moreover) we, and he also in whose hand the gabayai (cup) is matzaa (found).

He amar (spoke), chalayalah (far) be it from me that I should ishah (make) so. The ayash (husband/individual man) in whose yad (hand) the gabayai (cup) is matzaa (found), he will be my ibad (servant); but as for you, ilah (go up / offer) up in shalawam (peace / safety) to your ab (father).

Then Yahawadah (Judah) nagash (came) near to him, and amar (spoke), Oh, my Adawan, please let your ibad (servant) dabar (word / matter) a dabar (word / matter) in my adawan (master / lord) azan (ears), and don't let your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) charah (hot with anger) against your ibad (servant); for you are even as Paraih (Pharaoh).
My Adawan shaal (asked) his ibad (servant), amar (spoke), ‘yash (have) you a ab (father), or a ach (brother/kinsman)?’

We amar (spoke) to my Adawan, ‘We yash (have) a ab (father), an old zaqan (man), and a yalad (birth / begot) of his zaqan (old) age, a qatan (small/young/least) one; and his ach (brother/kinsman) is mawath (death), and he alone is yathar (left) of his am (mother); and his ab (father) ahab (love) him.’
You amar (spoke) to your ibad (servant), ‘yarad (bring) him down to me, that I may shawam (place / establish / appoint) my iyan (eye) on him.’
We amar (spoke) to my Adawan, ‘The boy can't izab (leave) his ab (father): for if he should izab (leave) his ab (father), his ab (father) would mawath (death).’
You amar (spoke) to your ibad (servant), ‘Unless your youngest ach (brother/kinsman) yarad (comes) down with you, you will see my panayam (face) no more.’
It happened when we ilah (go up / offer) up to your ibad (servant) my ab (father), we nagad (told) him the dabar (word / matter) of my Adawan.
Our ab (father) amar (spoke), ‘shawab (turn back / repent) again, shabar (buy) us a mait (little) akal (food).’

We amar (spoke), ‘We can't yarad (go) down. If our youngest ach (brother/kinsman) is with us, then we will yarad (go) down: for we may not raah (see) the ayash (husband/individual man) panayam (face), unless our youngest ach (brother/kinsman) is with us.’
Your ibad (servant), my ab (father), amar (spoke) to us, ‘You yadai (know) that my ashah (wife/individual woman) yalad (birth / begot) me shanayam (two) sons:
And the achad (one) yatzaa (go out / come out) out from me, and I amar (spoke), "tarap (surely) he is tarap (torn) in pieces;" and I haven't raah (see) him hanah (here).

If you laqach (take / seized) this im (one) also from me, and harm qarah (happens) to him, you will yarad (bring) down my shayabah (old age / white hair (due to age)) hairs with rai (sorrow) to shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife).’

Now therefore when I bawaa (come) to your ibad (servant) my ab (father), and the nair (boy) is not with us; since his napash (living being/soul) is qashar (bound) up in the boy's napash (living being/soul);

It will happen, when he raah (see) that the nair (boy) is no more, that he will mawath (death). Your ibad (servant) will yarad (bring) down the shayabah (old age / white hair (due to age)) hairs of your ibad (servant), our ab (father), with yagawan (sorrow) to shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife).
For your ibad (servant) became collateral for the nair (boy) to my ab (father), amar (spoke), ‘If I don't bawaa (come) him to you, then I will chataa (bear) the blame to my ab (father) yawam (day).’
Now therefore, please let your ibad (servant) stay instead of the nair (boy), a ibad (servant) to my Adawan; and let the nair (boy) ilah (go up / offer) up with his ach (brother/kinsman).
For ayak (how) will I ilah (go up / offer) up to my ab (father), if the nair (boy) isn't with me?—lest I raah (see) the rai (evil) that will matzaa (come) on my ab (father).

Then Yawasap (Joseph) couldn't control himself before all those who natzab (stood) before him, and he qaraa (called), "yatzaa (go out / come out) everyone to yatzaa (go out / come out) out from me!" No ayash (husband/individual man) else imad (stood) with him, while Yawasap (Joseph) yadai (made) himself known to his ach (brother/kinsman).
He wept aloud. The Matzaray (Egyptians) heard, and the bayath (house) of Paraih (Pharaoh) shamai (hearken / hear).

Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke) to his ach (brother/kinsman), "I am Yawasap (Joseph)! Does my ab (father) still chay (life)?" His ach (brother/kinsman) couldn't inah (answer / respond) him; for they were terrified at his panayam (presence).

Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke) to his ach (brother/kinsman), "nagash (come) near to me, please." They nagash (came) near. He amar (spoke), I am Yawasap (Joseph), your ach (brother/kinsman), whom you makar (sold) into Matzarayam (Egypt).
Now don't be itzab (grieved), nor charah (hot with anger) with iyan (eye), that you makar (sold) me here, for Alahayam shalach (send) me panayam (before) you to preserve machayah (life).

For these two shanah (years) the raib (famine) has been in the aratz (Earth/land), and there are yet chamash (five) shanah (years), in which there will be ayan (neither) plowing nor qatzayar (harvest).

Alahayam shalach (send) me panayam (before) you to shawam (place / establish / appoint) for you a remnant in the aratz (Earth/land), and to chayah (save) you alive by a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) palayatah (deliverance).

So now it wasn't you who shalach (send) me here, but Alahayam, and he has shawam (place / establish / appoint) me a ab (father) to Paraih (Pharaoh), Adawan of all his bayath (house), and mashal (rule/have dominion) over all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

Hurry, and ilah (go up / offer) up to my ab (father), and amar (spoke) him, ‘This is what your ban (son) Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke), "Alahayam has shawam (place / establish / appoint) me Adawan of all Matzarayam (Egypt). Yarad (come) down to me. Don't wait.

You shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Gashan (Goshen), and you will be qarawab (near) to me, you, your ban (son), your ban (son) ban (son), your tzaan (flocks), your baqar (morning), and all that you have.
There I will kawal (all/every/entire) you; for there are yet chamash (five) shanah (years) of raib (famine); lest you yarash (come) to poverty, you, and your bayath (house), and all that you have."’
Behold, your iyan (eye) raah (see), and the iyan (eye) of my ach (brother/kinsman) Banayamayan (Benjamin), that it is my pah (mouth) that dabar (word / matter) to you.
You shall nagad (tell) my ab (father) of all my kabawad (glory) in Matzarayam (Egypt), and of all that you raah (see) seen. You shall hurry and bring my ab (father) down here.
He napal (fall / be cast down) on his ach (brother/kinsman) Banayamayan (Benjamin's) tzawaar (neck), and bakah (wept), and Banayamayan (Benjamin) bakah (wept) on his tzawaar (neck).
He nashaq (kissed) all his ach (brother/kinsman), and bakah (wept) on them. Achar (other) that his ach (brother/kinsman) dabar (word / matter) with him.

The report of it was shamai (hearken / hear) in Paraih (Pharaoh's) bayath (house), amar (spoke), "Yawasap (Joseph's) ach (brother/kinsman) bawaa (come) come." It iyan (eye) Paraih (Pharaoh) yatab (well), and his ibad (servant).
Paraih (Pharaoh) amar (spoke) to Yawasap (Joseph), amar (spoke) your ach (brother/kinsman), ‘ishah (make) this. Load your animals, and yalak (go), travel to the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan).

Laqach (take / seized) your ab (father) and your bayath (house), and bawaa (come) to me, and I will nathan (give) you the tawab (pleasant/functional) of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and you will akal (eat) the chalab (fat) of the aratz (Earth/land).’

Now you are tzawah (commanded): ishah (make) this. Laqach (take / seized) igalah (wagons) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) for your little tap (ones), and for your wives, and nashaa (lift) your ab (father), and bawaa (come).
Also, don't concern yourselves about your belongings, for the tawab (pleasant/functional) of all of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) is yours.

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) ishah (make) so. Yawasap (Joseph) nathan (give) them igalah (wagons), pah (according) to the commandment of Paraih (Pharaoh), and nathan (give) them tzayadah (provision) for the darak (way).

He nathan (give) ayash (husband/individual man) one of them chalayapah (changes) of shamalah (clothing), but to Banayamayan (Benjamin) he nathan (give) shalawash (three) maah (hundred) pieces of kasap (silver) and chamash (five) chalayapah (changes) of shamalah (clothing).

He shalach (send) the following to his ab (father): ishar (ten) donkeys loaded with the tawab (pleasant/functional) things of Matzarayam (Egypt), and ishar (ten) female donkeys loaded with grain and lacham (bread) and provision for his ab (father) by the darak (way).
So he shalach (send) his ach (brother/kinsman) shalach (send), and they departed. He amar (spoke) to them, See that you don't quarrel on the darak (way).
They ilah (go up / offer) up out of Matzarayam (Egypt), and bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), to Yaiqab (Jacob) their ab (father).

They nagad (told) him, amar (spoke), "Yawasap (Joseph) is still chay (life), and he is mashal (rule/have dominion) over all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt)." His lab (heart) pawag (fainted), for he didn't aman (believe / have faith) them.

They dabar (word / matter) him all the dabar (word / matter) of Yawasap (Joseph), which he had dabar (word / matter) to them. When he raah (see) the igalah (wagons) which Yawasap (Joseph) had shalach (send) to nashaa (lift) him, the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yaiqab (Jacob), their ab (father), chayah (revived).
Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke), It is rab (enough). Yawasap (Joseph) my ban (son) is still chay (life). I will yalak (go) and raah (see) him before I mawath (death).
Yasharaal (Israel) traveled with all that he bawaa (come), and came Baarashabai (to) Beersheba, and zabach (offered) zabach (sacrifices) to the Alahayam of his ab (father), Yatzachaq (Isaac).
Alahayam amar (spoke) to Yasharaal (Israel) in the maraah (visions) of the layal (night), and amar (spoke), "Yaiqab (Jacob), Yaiqab (Jacob)!" He amar (spoke), Here I am.

He amar (spoke), I am Al, the Alahayam of your ab (father). Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) to yarad (go) down into Matzarayam (Egypt), for there I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) of you a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) gaway (nation / people).
I will yarad (go) down with you into Matzarayam (Egypt). I will also surely ilah (go up / offer) you up again. Yawasap (Joseph) will close your iyan (eye).

Yaiqab (Jacob) qawam (rise up) up Baarashabai (from) Beersheba, and the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) nashaa (lift) Yaiqab (Jacob), their ab (father), their little tap (ones), and their wives, in the igalah (wagons) which Paraih (Pharaoh) had shalach (send) to nashaa (lift) him.

They laqach (take / seized) their livestock, and their rakawash (wealth / property / goods / possessions), which they had rakash (gotten) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), and bawaa (come) into Matzarayam (Egypt)— Yaiqab (Jacob), and all his zarai (seed) with him,
His ban (son), and his ban (son)' ban (son) with him, his bath (daughter), and his ban (son)' bath (daughter), and he brought all his zarai (seed) with him into Matzarayam (Egypt).
These are the sham (name) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), who bawaa (come) into Matzarayam (Egypt), Yaiqab (Jacob) and his ban (son): Raawaban (Reuben), Yaiqab (Jacob's) bakawar (firstborn).
The ban (son) of Raawaban (Reuben): Chanawak (Hanoch), Palawaa (Pallu), Chatzarawan (Hezron), and Karamay (Carmi).
The ban (son) of Shamaiwan (Simeon): Yamawaal (Jemuel), Yamayan (Jamin), Ahad (Ohad), Yakayan (Jachin), Tzachar (Zohar), and Shaawal (Shaul) the ban (son) of a Kanainay (Canaanite) woman.
The ban (son) of Laway (Levi): Garashawan (Gershon), Qahath (Kohath), and Mararay (Merari).

The ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah): Ir (Er), Awanan (Onan), Shalah (Shelah), Paratz (Perez), and Zarach (Zerah); but Ir (Er) and Awanan (Onan) mawath (death) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan). The ban (son) of Paratz (Perez) were Chatzarawan (Hezron) and Chamawal (Hamul).
The ban (son) of Yashashakar (Issachar): Thawalai (Tola), Pawaah (Puvah), Yawab (Iob), and Shamarawan (Shimron).
The ban (son) of Zabawalawan (Zebulun): Sarad (Sered), Ayalawan (Elon), and Yachalaal (Jahleel).

These are the ban (son) of Laah (Leah), whom she yalad (birth / begot) to Yaiqab (Jacob) in Paddan Padan (Aram), with his bath (daughter) Dayanah (Dinah). All the napash (living being/soul) of his ban (son) and his bath (daughter) were shalawashayam (thirty) - shalawash (three).
The ban (son) of Gad (Gad): Tzapayawan (Ziphion), Chagay (Haggi), Shawanay (Shuni), Atzabawan (Ezbon), Iray (Eri), arawaday (arodi), and Araalay (Areli).

The ban (son) of Ashar (Asher): Yamanah (Imnah), Yashawah (Ishvah), Yashaway (Ishvi), Barayaih (Beriah), and Sharach (Serah) their achawath (sister). The ban (son) of Barayaih (Beriah): Chabar (Heber) and Malakayaal (Malchiel).

These are the ban (son) of Zalapah (Zilpah), whom Laban (Laban) nathan (give) to Laah (Leah), his bath (daughter), and these she yalad (birth / begot) to Yaiqab (Jacob), even sixteen napash (living being/soul).
The ban (son) of Rachal (Rachel), Yaiqab (Jacob's) ashah (wife/individual woman): Yawasap (Joseph) and Banayamayan (Benjamin).

To Yawasap (Joseph) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) were yalad (birth / begot) Manashah (Manasseh) and Aparayam (Ephraim), whom Asanath (Asenath), the bath (daughter) Pawatayaparai (of) Potiphera, kahan (priest) Awan (of) On, yalad (birth / begot) to him.
The ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin): Balai (Bela), Bakar (Becher), Ashabal (Ashbel), Garaa (Gera), Naiman (Naaman), Achay (Ehi), Raash (Rosh), Mapayam (Muppim), Chapayam (Huppim), and Arad (Ard).
These are the ban (son) of Rachal (Rachel), who were yalad (birth / begot) to Yaiqab (Jacob): all the napash (living being/soul) were fourteen.
The ban (son) Dan (of) Dan: Chawashayam (Hushim).
The ban (son) of Napathalay (Naphtali): Yachatzaal (Jahzeel), Gawanay (Guni), Yatzar (Jezer), and Shalam (Shillem).

These are the ban (son) of Balahah (Bilhah), whom Laban (Laban) nathan (give) to Rachal (Rachel), his bath (daughter), and these she yalad (birth / begot) to Yaiqab (Jacob): all the napash (living being/soul) were shabai (seven).

All the napash (living being/soul) who bawaa (come) with Yaiqab (Jacob) into Matzarayam (Egypt), who were his direct descendants, besides Yaiqab (Jacob's) ban (son)' wives, all the napash (living being/soul) were shashayam (sixty) - shash (six).

The ban (son) of Yawasap (Joseph), who were yalad (birth / begot) to him in Matzarayam (Egypt), were shanayam (two) napash (living being/soul). All the napash (living being/soul) of the bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob), who bawaa (come) into Matzarayam (Egypt), were shabaiyam (seventy).

He shalach (send) Yahawadah (Judah) panayam (before) him to Yawasap (Joseph), to show the panayam (way) before him to Gashan (Goshen), and they bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land) of Gashan (Goshen).

Yawasap (Joseph) asar (prepared) his marakabah (chariot), and ilah (go up / offer) up to qaraah (meet) Yasharaal (Israel), his ab (father), in Gashan (Goshen). He raah (see) himself to him, and napal (fall / be cast down) on his tzawaar (neck), and bakah (wept) on his tzawaar (neck) a iwad (more/again) while.
Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke) to Yawasap (Joseph), paim (now) let me mawath (death), achar (other) I raah (see) seen your panayam (face), that you are still chay (life).

Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke) to his ach (brother/kinsman), and to his ab (father) bayath (house), I will ilah (go up / offer) up, and amar (spoke) with Paraih (Pharaoh), and will amar (spoke) him, ‘My ach (brother/kinsman), and my ab (father) bayath (house), who were in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), bawaa (come) come to me.

These ayash (husband/individual man) are raih (shepherds), for they have been keepers of livestock, and they bawaa (come) brought their tzaan (flocks), and their baqar (morning), and all that they have.’
It will happen, when Paraih (Pharaoh) summons you, and will amar (spoke), ‘What is your maishah (occupation)?’

That you shall amar (spoke), ‘Your ibad (servant) have been keepers of livestock from our naiwar (youth) even until now, both we, and our ab (father):’ that you may yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Gashan (Goshen); for every raih (shepherd) is an thawaibah (abomination) to the Matzaray (Egyptians).

Then Yawasap (Joseph) bawaa (come) in and nagad (told) Paraih (Pharaoh), and amar (spoke), My ab (father) and my ach (brother/kinsman), with their tzaan (flocks), their baqar (morning), and all that they own, bawaa (come) come out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan); and behold, they are in the aratz (Earth/land) of Gashan (Goshen).
From among his ach (brother/kinsman) he laqach (take / seized) chamash (five) ayash (husband/individual man), and yatzag (presented) them to Paraih (Pharaoh).

Paraih (Pharaoh) amar (spoke) to his ach (brother/kinsman), "What is your maishah (occupation)?" They amar (spoke) to Paraih (Pharaoh), Your ibad (servant) are raih (shepherds), both we, and our ab (father).

They amar (spoke) to Paraih (Pharaoh), We bawaa (come) come to live as foreigners in the aratz (Earth/land), for there is no maraih (pasture) for your ibad (servant)' tzaan (flocks). For the raib (famine) is severe in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan). Now therefore, please let your ibad (servant) yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Gashan (Goshen).
Paraih (Pharaoh) amar (spoke) to Yawasap (Joseph), amar (spoke), Your ab (father) and your ach (brother/kinsman) bawaa (come) come to you.

The aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) is panayam (before) you. Yashab (inhabit/dwell) your ab (father) and your ach (brother/kinsman) yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the best of the aratz (Earth/land). Let them yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Gashan (Goshen). If you yadai (know) any able yadai (men) among them, then shawam (place / establish / appoint) them in charge of my livestock.
Yawasap (Joseph) bawaa (come) in Yaiqab (Jacob), his ab (father), and imad (set) him panayam (before) Paraih (Pharaoh), and Yaiqab (Jacob) barak (blessed) Paraih (Pharaoh).
Paraih (Pharaoh) amar (spoke) to Yaiqab (Jacob), mah (how) many are the yawam (day) of the years of your life?

Yaiqab (Jacob) amar (spoke) to Paraih (Pharaoh), The yawam (day) of the shanah (years) of my magawar (pilgrimage) are one maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) shanah (years). Mait (few) and rai (evil) have been the yawam (day) of the shanah (years) of my chay (life), and they have not nashag (attained) to the yawam (day) of the shanah (years) of the chay (life) of my ab (father) in the yawam (day) of their magawar (pilgrimage).
Yaiqab (Jacob) barak (blessed) Paraih (Pharaoh), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out from the panayam (presence) of Paraih (Pharaoh).

Yawasap (Joseph) yashab (inhabit/dwell) his ab (father) and his ach (brother/kinsman), and nathan (give) them a achazah (possession) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), in the mayatab (best) of the aratz (Earth/land), in the aratz (Earth/land) of Raimasas (Rameses), as Paraih (Pharaoh) had tzawah (commanded).
Yawasap (Joseph) kawal (all/every/entire) his ab (father), his ach (brother/kinsman), and all of his ab (father) bayath (house), with lacham (bread), pah (according) to their tap (families).

There was no lacham (bread) in all the aratz (Earth/land); for the raib (famine) was very severe, so that the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) and the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan) lahah (fainted) by panayam (reason) of the raib (famine).

Yawasap (Joseph) laqat (gathered) up all the kasap (money) that was matzaa (found) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), for the grain which they bought: and Yawasap (Joseph) bawaa (come) the kasap (money) into Paraih (Pharaoh's) bayath (house).

When the kasap (money) was thamam (all) spent in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), all the Matzarayam (Egyptians) bawaa (come) to Yawasap (Joseph), and amar (spoke), yahab (give) us lacham (bread), for why should we mawath (death) in your presence? For our kasap (money) apas (fails).
Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke), yahab (give) me your livestock; and I will nathan (give) you food for your livestock, if your kasap (money) is apas (gone).

They bawaa (come) their livestock to Yawasap (Joseph), and Yawasap (Joseph) nathan (give) them lacham (bread) in exchange for the sawas (horses), and for the tzaan (flocks), and for the baqar (morning), and for the donkeys: and he nahal (fed) them with lacham (bread) in exchange for all their livestock for that shanah (year).

When that shanah (year) was thamam (ended), they bawaa (come) to him the shanay (second) shanah (year), and amar (spoke) to him, We will not kachad (hide) from my Adawan how our kasap (money) is thamam (all) spent, and the maqanah (herds) of livestock are my adawan (master / lord). There is nothing shaar (left) in the panayam (sight) of my Adawan, but our gawayah (corpse), and our adamah (lands).

Why should we mawath (death) before your iyan (eye), both we and our adamah (land)? Qanah (buy) us and our adamah (land) for lacham (bread), and we and our adamah (land) will be ibad (servant) to Paraih (Pharaoh). Nathan (give) us zarai (seed), that we may chayah (live), and not mawath (death), and that the adamah (land) won't be yasham (desolate).

So Yawasap (Joseph) bought all the adamah (land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) for Paraih (Pharaoh), for every ayash (husband/individual man) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians) makar (sold) his shadah (field), because the raib (famine) was severe on them, and the aratz (Earth/land) became Paraih (Pharaoh's).

As for the im (people / nation), he moved them to the iyar (cities) from one qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the gabawal (border/boundary) of Matzarayam (Egypt) even to the other qatzah (end / extremity / border) of it.

Only he didn't buy the adamah (land) of the kahan (priest), for the kahan (priest) had a chaq (statute) from Paraih (Pharaoh), and akal (eat) their chaq (statute) which Paraih (Pharaoh) nathan (give) them. That is why they didn't makar (sell) their adamah (land).

Then Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke) to the im (people / nation), Behold, I have bought you and your adamah (land) today for Paraih (Pharaoh). Haa (behold), here is zarai (seed) for you, and you shall zarai (sow) the adamah (land).

It will happen at the harvests, that you shall nathan (give) a chamayashay (fifth) to Paraih (Pharaoh), and arabai (four) yad (hand) will be your own, for zarai (seed) of the shadah (field), for your akal (food), for them of your bayath (house), and for akal (eat) for your little tap (ones).
They amar (spoke), You have chayah (saved) our lives! Let us matzaa (find) favor in the iyan (eye) of my Adawan, and we will be Paraih (Pharaoh's) ibad (servant).

Yawasap (Joseph) shawam (place / establish / appoint) it a chaq (statute) concerning the adamah (land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) to this yawam (day), that Paraih (Pharaoh) should have the chamash (fifth). Only the adamah (land) of the kahan (priest) raq (alone) didn't become Paraih (Pharaoh's).

Yasharaal (Israel) lived in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), in the aratz (Earth/land) of Gashan (Goshen); and they got themselves achaz (possessions) therein, and were parah (fruitful), and rabah (multiplied) maad (exceedingly).

Yaiqab (Jacob) chayah (lived) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) seventeen shanah (years). So the days of Yaiqab (Jacob), the years of his life, were one maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - shabai (seven) shanah (years).

The yawam (day) qarab (come close) near that Yasharaal (Israel) must mawath (death), and he qaraa (called) his ban (son) Yawasap (Joseph), and amar (spoke) to him, "If now I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye), please shawam (place / establish / appoint) your yad (hand) under my yarak (thigh), and ishah (make) chasad (grace) and truly with me. Please don't qabar (bury) me in Matzarayam (Egypt),

But when I sleep with my ab (father), you shall nashaa (lift) me out of Matzarayam (Egypt), and qabar (bury) me in their qabawarah (burying) place." He amar (spoke), I will ishah (make) as you have dabar (word / matter).
He amar (spoke), "shabai (swear / take oath) to me," and he shabai (swear / take oath) to him. Yasharaal (Israel) shachah (bowed) himself on the matah (bed's) raash (head).

It happened achar (other) these things, that someone amar (spoke) to Yawasap (Joseph), "Behold, your ab (father) is chalah (afflict)." He laqach (take / seized) with him his shanayam (two) ban (son), Manashah (Manasseh) and Aparayam (Ephraim).

Someone nagad (told) Yaiqab (Jacob), and amar (spoke), "Behold, your ban (son) Yawasap (Joseph) bawaa (come) to you," and Yasharaal (Israel) chazaq (strengthened) himself, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the matah (bed).
Yaiqab (Jacob) amar (spoke) to Yawasap (Joseph), Al Shaday raah (see) to me at Lawaz (Luz) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), and barak (blessed) me,

And amar (spoke) to me, ‘Behold, I will parah (make) you fruitful, and rabah (multiply) you, and I will nathan (give) of you a qahal (company) of im (people / nation), and will nathan (give) this aratz (Earth/land) to your zarai (seed) achar (other) you for an iwalam (forever) achazah (possession).’

Now your shanayam (two) ban (son), who were yalad (birth / begot) to you in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) id (before) I bawaa (come) to you into Matzarayam (Egypt), are mine; Aparayam (Ephraim) and Manashah (Manasseh), even as Raawaban (Reuben) and Shamaiwan (Simeon), will be mine.

Your mawaladath (kindred / native land), whom you become the yalad (birth / begot) of achar (other) them, will be yours. They will be qaraa (called) il (over) the sham (name) of their ach (brother/kinsman) in their nachalah (inheritance).

As for me, when I bawaa (come) Padan (from) Paddan, Rachal (Rachel) mawath (death) by me in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan) in the darak (way), when there was still some distance to bawaa (come) to aparath (ephrath), and I qabar (bury) her there in the darak (way) to aparath (ephrath) (the same is Bayathalacham (Bethlehem)).
Yasharaal (Israel) raah (see) Yawasap (Joseph's) ban (son), and amar (spoke), Who are these?

Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke) to his ab (father), "They are my ban (son), whom Alahayam nathan (give) given me here." He amar (spoke), Please laqach (take / seized) them to me, and I will barak (bless) them.

Now the iyan (eye) of Yasharaal (Israel) were kabad (dim) for zaqan (age), so that he couldn't raah (see). He nagash (brought) them near to him; and he nashaq (kissed) them, and chabaq (embraced) them.
Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke) to Yawasap (Joseph), I didn't think I would raah (see) your panayam (face), and raah (see), Alahayam has let me see your zarai (seed) also.
Yawasap (Joseph) yatzaa (go out / come out) them out from im (between) his barak (knees), and he shachah (bowed) himself with his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land).

Yawasap (Joseph) laqach (take / seized) them shanayam (two), Aparayam (Ephraim) in his right yamayan (right hand) toward Yasharaal (Israel's) left shamaawal (left hand), and Manashah (Manasseh) in his left shamaawal (left hand) toward Yasharaal (Israel's) right yamayan (right hand), and nagash (brought) them near to him.

Yasharaal (Israel) shalach (send) out his right yamayan (right hand), and shayath (put / appoint / make) it on Aparayam (Ephraim's) raash (head), who was the younger, and his left shamaawal (left hand) on Manashah (Manasseh's) raash (head), shakal (guiding) his yad (hand) knowingly, for Manashah (Manasseh) was the bakawar (firstborn).

He barak (blessed) Yawasap (Joseph), and amar (spoke), The Alahayam panayam (before) whom my ab (father) Abaraham (Abraham) and Yatzachaq (Isaac) halak (move), the Alahayam who has raih (fed) me all my iwad (more/again) long to this yawam (day),

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) who has gaal (redeemed) me from all rai (evil), barak (bless) the nair (lads), and let my sham (name) be qaraa (called) on them, and the sham (name) of my ab (father) Abaraham (Abraham) and Yatzachaq (Isaac). Let them dagah (grow) into a rab (multitude) in the qarab (among / near) of the aratz (Earth/land).

When Yawasap (Joseph) raah (see) that his ab (father) shayath (put / appoint / make) his yamayan (right hand) yad (hand) on the raash (head) of Aparayam (Ephraim), it displeased him. He thamak (held) up his ab (father) yad (hand), to sawar (remove) it from Aparayam (Ephraim's) raash (head) to Manashah (Manasseh's) raash (head).

Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke) to his ab (father), Not so, my ab (father); for this is the bakawar (firstborn); shawam (place / establish / appoint) your right yamayan (right hand) on his raash (head).

His ab (father) maan (refused), and amar (spoke), I yadai (know), my ban (son), I yadai (know). He also will become a im (people / nation), and he also will be gadal (great). However, his younger ach (brother/kinsman) will be greater than he, and his zarai (seed) will become a malaa (multitude) of gaway (nation / people).

He barak (blessed) them that yawam (day), amar (spoke), "In you will Yasharaal (Israel) barak (bless), amar (spoke), ‘Alahayam shawam (place / establish / appoint) you as Aparayam (Ephraim) and as Manashah (Manasseh)’" He shawam (place / establish / appoint) Aparayam (Ephraim) panayam (before) Manashah (Manasseh).
Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke) to Yawasap (Joseph), Behold, I am dying, but Alahayam will be with you, and shawab (turn back / repent) you again to the aratz (Earth/land) of your ab (father).

Moreover I nathan (give) given to you achad (one) shakam (portion) above your ach (brother/kinsman), which I laqach (take / seized) out of the yad (hand) of the Amaray (Amorite) with my charab (sword) and with my qashath (bow).
Yaiqab (Jacob) qaraa (called) to his ban (son), and amar (spoke): asap (gather) yourselves together, that I may nagad (tell) you that which will qaraa (called) to you in the yawam (day) to come.
Qabatz (assemble) yourselves, and shamai (hearken / hear), you ban (son) of Yaiqab (Jacob). Shamai (hearken / hear) to Yasharaal (Israel), your ab (father).

Raawaban (Reuben), you are my bakawar (firstborn), my kach (strength / mighty / power), and the raashayath (beginning) of my awan (strength); excelling in shaath (dignity), and excelling in iz (power).

Boiling over as mayam (Waters), you shall not yathar (excel); because you ilah (go up / offer) up to your ab (father) mashakab (bed), then defiled it. He ilah (go up / offer) up to my yatzawai (couch).
Shamaiwan (Simeon) and Laway (Levi) are ach (brother/kinsman). Their makarah (swords) are kalay (weapons) of chamas (violence).

My napash (living being/soul), don't bawaa (come) into their council. My kabawad (glory), don't be yachad (united) to their qahal (assembly); for in their ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) they harag (killed) ayash (husband/individual man). In their self-will they hamstrung cattle.

Arar (cursed) be their ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), for it was iz (fierce); and their ibarah (wrath), for it was qashah (rough / hard). I will chalaq (divide) them in Yaiqab (Jacob), and pawatz (scatter) them in Yasharaal (Israel).
Yahawadah (Judah), your ach (brother/kinsman) will yadah (praise) you. Your yad (hand) will be on the irap (neck) of your ayab (enemy). Your ab (father) ban (son) will shachah (bow) down before you.

Yahawadah (Judah) is a aray (lion's) cub. From the tarap (prey), my ban (son), you have ilah (go up / offer) up. He stooped down, he rabatz (crouched) as a labayaa (lion), as a labayaa (lioness). Who will qawam (rise up) him up?

The scepter will not sawar (depart) from Yahawadah (Judah), nor the chaqaq (ruler's) staff from between his ragal (feet / foot), kay (surely) he bawaa (come) to whom it belongs. To him will the obedience of the im (people / nation) be.

Asar (binding) his iyar (foal) to the gapan (vine), his donkey's ban (son) to the sharaq (choice) vine; he has kabas (washed) his labawash (garments) in yayan (wine), his robes in the dam (blood) of inab (grapes).
His iyan (eye) will be chakalayal (red) with yayan (wine), his shan (teeth) laban (white) with chalab (milk).
Zabawalawan (Zebulun) will shakan (dwell) at the chawap (haven) of the yam (sea/waters). He will be for a chawap (haven) of anayah (ships). His yarakah (border) will be on Tzayadawan (Sidon).
Yashashakar (Issachar) is a garam (strong) donkey, lying down between the saddlebags.

He raah (see) a manawachah (resting) place, that it was tawab (pleasant/functional), the aratz (Earth/land), that it was naim (pleasant). He natah (bows) his shakam (shoulder) to the sabal (burden), and becomes a ibad (servant) doing forced mas (labor).
Dan (Dan) will dayan (judge) his im (people / nation), as achad (one) of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Dan (Dan) will be a nachash (serpent) in the darak (way), an shapayapan (adder) in the arach (path), That nashak (bites) the sawas (horse's) iqab (heels), so that his rider napal (fall / be cast down) backward.
I have qawah (gather/wait) for your yashawaih (salvation), Yahawah.
A gadawad (troop) will press on Gad (Gad), but he will press on their iqab (heel).
Ashar (Asher's) lacham (food) will be rich. He will nathan (give) malak (king) maidan (dainties).
Napathalay (Naphtali) is a doe shalach (send) free, who bears beautiful fawns.
Yawasap (Joseph) is a parah (fruitful) vine, a parah (fruitful) vine by a spring. His branches tzaid (run) over the shawar (wall).
The bail (archers) marar (have) severely grieved him, rabab (shot) at him, and persecute him:

But his qashath (bow) yashab (inhabit/dwell) ayathan (strong). The zarawai (arms) of his yad (hand) were pazaz (made) strong, by the yad (hand) of the abayar (mighty) One of Yaiqab (Jacob), (from there is the raih (shepherd), the aban (stone) of Yasharaal (Israel)),

Even by the Al of your ab (father), who will izar (help) you; by the Shaday, who will barak (bless) you, with barakah (blessings) of shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) il (over), barakah (blessings) of the thahawam (depths) that rabatz (lies) below, barakah (blessings) of the shad (breasts), and of the racham (womb).

The barakah (blessings) of your ab (father) have gabar (prevailed) above the barakah (blessings) of your ancestors, above the boundaries of the iwalam (forever) gabaih (hills). They will be on the qadaqad (head) of Yawasap (Joseph), on the qadaqad (crown) of the head of him who is nazayar (Nazayar/(Nazarite)) from his ach (brother/kinsman).
Banayamayan (Benjamin) is a ravenous zaab (wolf). In the baqar (morning) he will akal (eat) the id (prey). At irab (evening) he will chalaq (divide) the shalal (spoil).

All these are the ishar (-teen) shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), and this is what their ab (father) dabar (word / matter) to them and barak (blessed) them. He barak (blessed) everyone according to his barakah (blessing).

He instructed them, and amar (spoke) to them, I am to be asap (gathered) to my im (people / nation). Qabar (bury) me with my ab (father) in the mairah (cave) that is in the shadah (field) of Iparawan (Ephron) the Chathay (Hittite),

In the mairah (cave) that is in the shadah (field) of Makapalah (Machpelah), which is panayam (before) Mamaraa (Mamre), in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), which Abaraham (Abraham) bought with the shadah (field) from Iparawan (Ephron) the Chathay (Hittite) as a burial qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher).

There they qabar (bury) Abaraham (Abraham) and Sharah (Sarah), his ashah (wife/individual woman). There they qabar (bury) Yatzachaq (Isaac) and Rabaqah (Rebekah), his ashah (wife/individual woman), and there I qabar (bury) Laah (Leah):
The shadah (field) and the mairah (cave) that is therein, which was maqanah (purchased) from the ban (son) of Chath (Heth).

When Yaiqab (Jacob) kalah (complete / finish) an end of tzawah (charging) his ban (son), he asap (gathered) up his ragal (feet / foot) into the matah (bed), and yielded up the gawai (spirit), and was asap (gathered) to his im (people / nation).
Yawasap (Joseph) napal (fall / be cast down) on his ab (father) panayam (face), bakah (wept) on him, and nashaq (kissed) him.
Yawasap (Joseph) tzawah (commanded) his ibad (servant), the rapaa (physicians), to chanat (embalm) his ab (father); and the rapaa (physicians) chanat (embalmed) Yasharaal (Israel).

Arabaiyam (forty) yawam (day) were malaa (fulfilled) for him, for that is how many the yawam (day) it takes to chanat (embalm). The Matzaray (Egyptians) wept for him for shabaiyam (seventy) yawam (day).

When the yawam (day) of weeping for him were past, Yawasap (Joseph) dabar (word / matter) to the bayath (house) of Paraih (Pharaoh), amar (spoke), If now I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye), please dabar (word / matter) in the azan (ears) of Paraih (Pharaoh), amar (spoke),

‘My ab (father) made me shabai (swear / take oath), amar (spoke), "hanah (Behold), I am dying. Bury me in my qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) which I have karah (dug) for myself in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan)." Now therefore, please let me ilah (go up / offer) up and qabar (bury) my ab (father), and I will shawab (turn back / repent) again.’
Paraih (Pharaoh) amar (spoke), ilah (go up / offer) up, and qabar (bury) your ab (father), just like he made you shabai (swear / take oath).

Yawasap (Joseph) ilah (go up / offer) up to qabar (bury) his ab (father); and with him ilah (go up / offer) up all the ibad (servant) of Paraih (Pharaoh), the zaqan (elders) of his bayath (house), all the zaqan (elders) of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt),

All the bayath (house) of Yawasap (Joseph), his ach (brother/kinsman), and his ab (father) bayath (house). Only their little tap (ones), their tzaan (flocks), and their baqar (morning), they izab (left) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Gashan (Goshen).
There ilah (go up / offer) up with him both rakab (chariots) and horsemen. It was a very kabad (great) machanah (company).

They bawaa (come) to the garan (threshing) garan (floor) of atad (atad), which is ibar (beyond) the Yaradan (Jordan), and there they sapad (lamented) with a very gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and severe masapad (lamentation). He mourned for his ab (father) shabai (seven) yawam (day).

When the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the aratz (Earth/land), the Kanainay (Canaanites), raah (see) the abal (mourning) in the garan (floor) of atad (atad), they amar (spoke), "This is a kabad (grievous) abal (mourning) by the Matzaray (Egyptians)." Therefore, its qaraa (called) was called Abalamatzarayam (Abel) Mizraim, which is ibar (beyond) the Yaradan (Jordan).
His ban (son) ishah (make) to him just as he tzawah (commanded) them,

For his ban (son) nashaa (lift) him into the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), and qabar (bury) him in the mairah (cave) of the shadah (field) of Makapalah (Machpelah), which Abaraham (Abraham) bought with the shadah (field), for a achazah (possession) of a burial site, from Iparawan (Ephron) the Chathay (Hittite), panayam (before) Mamaraa (Mamre).

Yawasap (Joseph) shawab (turn back / repent) into Matzarayam (Egypt)— he, and his ach (brother/kinsman), and all that ilah (go up / offer) up with him to qabar (bury) his ab (father), achar (other) he had qabar (bury) his ab (father).

When Yawasap (Joseph's) ach (brother/kinsman) raah (see) that their ab (father) was mawath (death), they amar (spoke), It may be that Yawasap (Joseph) will shatam (hate) us, and will fully shawab (turn back / repent) us back for all of the rai (evil) which we gamal (did) to him.
They tzawah (sent) a message to Yawasap (Joseph), amar (spoke), "Your ab (father) tzawah (commanded) panayam (before) he mawath (death), amar (spoke),

‘You shall amar (spoke) Yawasap (Joseph), "Now please nashaa (lift) the disobedience of your ach (brother/kinsman), and their pashai (sin), because they gamal (did) rai (evil) to you."’ Now, please nashaa (lift) the disobedience of the ibad (servant) of the Alahayam of your ab (father)." Yawasap (Joseph) bakah (wept) when they dabar (word / matter) to him.
His ach (brother/kinsman) also yalak (went) and napal (fall / be cast down) down before his panayam (face); and they amar (spoke), Behold, we are your ibad (servant).
Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke) to them, "Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), for am I in the place of Alahayam?

As for you, you chashab (meant) rai (evil) against me, but Alahayam chashab (meant) it for tawab (pleasant/functional), to ishah (make) to pass, as it is this yawam (day), to chayah (save) many im (people / nation) chayah (alive).
Now therefore don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). I will kawal (all/every/entire) you and your little tap (ones)." He nacham (turn away / repent) them, and dabar (word / matter) lab (heart) to them.
Yawasap (Joseph) lived in Matzarayam (Egypt), he, and his ab (father) bayath (house). Yawasap (Joseph) chayah (lived) one maah (hundred) ishar (ten) shanah (years).

Yawasap (Joseph) raah (see) Aparayam (Ephraim's) ban (son) to the shalash (three) generation. The ban (son) also of Makayar (Machir), the ban (son) of Manashah (Manasseh), were yalad (birth / begot) on Yawasap (Joseph's) barak (knees).

Yawasap (Joseph) amar (spoke) to his ach (brother/kinsman), I am dying, but Alahayam will paqad (visit) paqad (visit) you, and ilah (go up / offer) you up out of this aratz (Earth/land) to the aratz (Earth/land) which he shabai (swear / take oath) to Abaraham (Abraham), to Yatzachaq (Isaac), and to Yaiqab (Jacob).

Yawasap (Joseph) took an shabai (swear / take oath) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), Alahayam will paqad (visit) paqad (visit) you, and you shall ilah (go up / offer) up my itzam (bones) from here.
So Yawasap (Joseph) mawath (death), being one maah (hundred) ishar (ten) shanah (years) ban (son), and they chanat (embalmed) him, and he was yasham (put) in a arawan (coffin) in Matzarayam (Egypt).
Now these are the sham (name) of the Yaiqab (sons) of Israel, who came into Egypt (Matzarayam (every) man and his bayath (house) bawaa (come) with Yaiqab (Jacob)):
Raawaban (Reuben), Shamaiwan (Simeon), Laway (Levi), and Yahawadah (Judah),
Yashashakar (Issachar), Zabawalawan (Zebulun), and Banayamayan (Benjamin),
Dan (Dan) and Napathalay (Naphtali), Gad (Gad) and Ashar (Asher).

All the napash (living being/soul) who yatzaa (go out / come out) out of Yaiqab (Jacob's) yarak (body) were shabaiyam (seventy) napash (living being/soul), and Yawasap (Joseph) was in Matzarayam (Egypt) already.
Yawasap (Joseph) mawath (death), as did all his ach (brother/kinsman), and all that dawar (generation / age / period).

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) were parah (fruitful), and sharatz (swarm as many) abundantly, and rabah (multiplied), and grew maad (exceedingly) itzam (mighty); and the aratz (Earth/land) was malaa (filled) with them.
Now there qawam (rise up) a chadash (new) malak (king) over Matzarayam (Egypt), who didn't yadai (know) Yawasap (Joseph).
He amar (spoke) to his im (people / nation), Behold, the im (people / nation) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) are more and mightier than we.

Yahab (come), let us chakam (deal) wisely with them, lest they rabah (multiply), and it happen that when any malachamah (war) breaks out, they also yasap (join) themselves to our shanaa (hate), and lacham (fight) against us, and escape out of the aratz (Earth/land).

Therefore they shawam (place / establish / appoint) mas (taskmasters) over them to inah (oppress / afflict) them with their sabalah (burdens). They banah (built) storage iyar (cities) for Paraih (Pharaoh): Patham (Pithom) and Raimasas (Raamses).
But the more they inah (oppress / afflict) them, the more they rabah (multiplied) and the more they spread out. They were qawatz (grieved) panayam (because) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel).
The Matzaray (Egyptians) ruthlessly ibad (servant) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) ibad (servant),
