And a bud under shanayam (two) branches of kapathar (one) piece with it, and a bud under shanayam (two) branches of kapathar (one) piece with it, and a bud under shanayam (two) branches of one piece with it, for the shash (six) branches yatzaa (go out / come out) out of it.
Their buds and their branches were of one piece with it. The whole thing was one beaten maqashah (work) of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold).
He ishah (make) its shabai (seven) nayar (lamps), and its malaqach (snuffers), and its snuff dishes, of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold).
He ishah (make) it of a kakar (talent) of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold), with all its kalay (vessels).

He ishah (make) the mazabach (altar) of qatarath (incense) of acacia itz (wood). It was rabai (fourth): its arak (length) was a amah (cubit), and its rachab (breadth) a amah (cubit). Its qawamah (height) was two amah (cubits). Its qaran (horn) were of one piece with it.
He overlaid it with tahawar (pure) zahab (gold), its gag (top), its qayar (sides) around it, and its qaran (horn). He ishah (make) a zahab (gold) molding around it.

He ishah (make) shanayam (two) zahab (gold) tabaith (rings) for it under its molding zar (crown), on its shanayam (two) tzalai (ribs), on its shanayam (two) tzad (sides), for bayath (house) for poles with which to nashaa (lift) it.
He ishah (make) the poles of acacia itz (wood), and overlaid them with zahab (gold).
He ishah (make) the qadash (set apart/make holy) mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil) and the tahawar (pure) qatarath (incense) of sam (sweet) spices, after the maishah (art) of the perfumer.

He ishah (make) the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering) of acacia itz (wood). It was rabai (fourth). Its arak (length) was chamash (five) amah (cubits), its rachab (breadth) was chamash (five) amah (cubits), and its qawamah (height) was shalawash (three) amah (cubits).
He ishah (make) its qaran (horn) on its arabai (four) panah (corners). Its qaran (horn) were of tzapah (one) piece with it, and he overlaid it with nachashath (brass).

He ishah (make) all the kalay (vessels) of the mazabach (altar), the sayar (pots), the yai (shovels), the basins, the forks, and the machathah (fire) pans. He ishah (make) all its kalay (vessels) of nachashath (brass).
He ishah (make) for the mazabach (altar) a makabar (grating) of a rashath (network) of nachashath (brass), under the ledge around it matah (beneath), reaching halfway up.
He yatzaq (cast) arabai (four) tabaith (rings) for the arabai (four) qatzath (ends) of nachashath (brass) makabar (grating), to be bayath (house) for the poles.
He ishah (make) the poles of acacia itz (wood), and overlaid them with nachashath (brass).
He bawaa (come) the poles into the tabaith (rings) on the tzalai (sides) of the mazabach (altar), with which to nashaa (lift) it. He ishah (make) it nabab (hollow) with planks.

He ishah (make) the basin of nachashath (brass), and its kan (for sure) of nachashath (brass), out of the mirrors of the ministering women who ministered at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

He ishah (make) the chatzar (court): for the nagab (south) paah (side) southward the qalai (hangings) of the chatzar (court) were of fine shazar (twined) shash (six), one maah (hundred) amah (cubits);

Their imawad (pillar) were isharayam (twenty), and their adan (sockets) isharayam (twenty), of nachashath (brass); the waw (hooks) of the imawad (pillar) and their chashaq (fillets) were of kasap (silver).

For the tzapawan (north) paah (side) one maah (hundred) amah (cubits), their imawad (pillar) isharayam (twenty), and their adan (sockets) isharayam (twenty), of nachashath (brass); the waw (hooks) of the imawad (pillar), and their chashaq (fillets), of kasap (silver).

For the yam (sea/waters) paah (side) were qalai (hangings) of chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits), their imawad (pillar) ishar (ten), and their adan (sockets) ishar (ten); the waw (hooks) of the imawad (pillar), and their chashaq (fillets), of kasap (silver).
For the qadam (east) paah (side) eastward chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits).
The qalai (hangings) for the one kathap (side) were chamash (fifteen) amah (cubits); their imawad (pillar) shalawash (three), and their adan (sockets) shalawash (three);

And so for the other kathap (side): on this hand and that hand by the shair (gate) of the chatzar (court) were qalai (hangings) of chamash (fifteen) amah (cubits); their imawad (pillar) shalawash (three), and their adan (sockets) shalawash (three).
All the qalai (hangings) around the chatzar (court) were of fine shazar (twined) shash (six).

The adan (sockets) for the imawad (pillar) were of nachashath (brass). The waw (hooks) of the imawad (pillar) and their chashaq (fillets) were of kasap (silver); and the tzapaway (overlaying) of their capitals, of kasap (silver); and all the imawad (pillar) of the chatzar (court) were chashaq (filleted) with kasap (silver).

The screen for the shair (gate) of the chatzar (court) was the raqam (work) of the embroiderer, of thakalath (blue), aragaman (purple), shanay (second), and fine shazar (twined) shash (six). Isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) was the arak (length), and the qawamah (height) in the rachab (breadth) was chamash (five) amah (cubits), like to the qalai (hangings) of the chatzar (court).

Their imawad (pillar) were arabai (four), and their adan (sockets) arabai (four), of nachashath (brass); their waw (hooks) of kasap (silver), and the tzapaway (overlaying) of their capitals, and their chashaq (fillets), of kasap (silver).
All the yathad (pins) of the mashakan (tabernacle), and around the chatzar (court), were of nachashath (brass).

Alah (these) is the amount of material used for the mashakan (tabernacle), even the mashakan (tabernacle) of the idawath (testimony), as they were paqad (visit), pah (according) to the commandment of Mashah (Moses), for the ibadah (service) of the Lawayay (Levites), by the yad (hand) of Ayathamar (Ithamar), the ban (son) of Aharawan (Aaron) the kahan (priest).

Batzalaal (Bezalel) the ban (son) of Awaray (Uri), the ban (son) of Chawar (Hur), of the matah (staff / rod / tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah), ishah (make) all that Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).

Ahalayaab (With) him was Oholiab, the ban (son) of Achayasamak (Ahisamach), of the matah (staff / rod / tribe) Dan (of) Dan, an charash (engraver), and a skillful chashab (workman), and an raqam (embroiderer) in thakalath (blue), in aragaman (purple), in shanay (second), and in shash (six) linen.

All the zahab (gold) that was used for the malaakah (work) in all the malaakah (work) of the qadash (set apart/make holy), even the zahab (gold) of the thanawapah (offering), was isharayam (twenty) thashai (nine) kakar (talents), and shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) shaqal (shekels), after the shaqal (shekel) of the qadash (set apart/make holy).

The kasap (silver) of those who were paqad (visit) of the idah (congregation) was one maah (hundred) kakar (talents), and one alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) five shaqal (shekels), after the shaqal (shekel) of the qadash (set apart/make holy):

A beka a galagalath (head), that is, machatzayath (half) a shaqal (shekel), after the shaqal (shekel) of the qadash (set apart/make holy), for everyone who ibar (pass over/through) over to those who were paqad (visit), from isharayam (twenty) shanah (years) ban (son) and upward, for shash (six) maah (hundred) shalawash (three) alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) men.

The one maah (hundred) kakar (talents) of kasap (silver) were for yatzaq (casting) the adan (sockets) of the qadash (set apart/make holy), and the adan (sockets) of the parakath (veil); one maah (hundred) adan (sockets) for the one maah (hundred) kakar (talents), a kakar (talent) for a adan (socket).

Of the one alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) chamash (five) shekels he ishah (make) waw (hooks) for the imawad (pillar), overlaid their capitals, and made chashaq (fillets) for them.
The nachashath (brass) of the thanawapah (offering) was shabaiyam (seventy) kakar (talents), and two alap (thousand) arabai (four) maah (hundred) shaqal (shekels).

With this he ishah (make) the adan (sockets) to the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, the bronze mazabach (altar), the bronze makabar (grating) for it, all the kalay (vessels) of the mazabach (altar),

The adan (sockets) around the chatzar (court), the adan (sockets) of the shair (gate) of the chatzar (court), all the yathad (pins) of the mashakan (tabernacle), and all the yathad (pins) around the chatzar (court).

Of the thakalath (blue), aragaman (purple), and shanay (second), they ishah (make) finely worked bagad (garments), for sharath (ministering) in the qadash (set apart/make holy) place, and ishah (make) the qadash (set apart/make holy) bagad (garments) for Aharawan (Aaron); as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).
He ishah (make) the apawad (ephod) of zahab (gold), thakalath (blue), aragaman (purple), thawalai (scarlet), and fine shazar (twined) shash (six).

They raqai (beat) the zahab (gold) into thin pach (plates), and qatzatz (cut) it into pathayal (wires), to ishah (make) it in the thakalath (blue), in the aragaman (purple), in the shanay (second), and in the shash (six) linen, the maishah (work) of the skillful chashab (workman).
They ishah (make) kathap (shoulder) straps for it, chabar (joined) together. At the shanayam (two) ends it was chabar (joined) together.

The skillfully woven band that was on it, with which to fasten it on, was of the same piece, like its maishah (work); of zahab (gold), of thakalath (blue), aragaman (purple), shanay (second), and fine shazar (twined) shash (six); as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).

They ishah (make) the shaham (Onyx) aban (stone), enclosed in settings of zahab (gold), pathach (engraved) with the pathach (engravings) of a chawatham (signet), according to the sham (name) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel).

He shawam (place / establish / appoint) them on the kathap (shoulder) straps of the apawad (ephod), to be aban (stone) of zakarawan (memorial) for the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).

He ishah (make) the chashan (breastplate), the maishah (work) of a skillful workman, like the maishah (work) of the apawad (ephod); of zahab (gold), of thakalath (blue), aragaman (purple), shanay (second), and fine shazar (twined) shash (six).
It was rabai (fourth). They ishah (make) the chashan (breastplate) kapal (double). Its arak (length) was a zarath (span), and its rachab (breadth) a zarath (span), being kapal (double).
They malaa (set) in it arabai (four) tawar (rows) of aban (stone). A tawar (row) of ruby, patadah (topaz), and beryl was the achad (one) tawar (row);
And the shanay (second) tawar (row), a turquoise, a sapayar (sapphire), and an napak (emerald);
And the shalayashay (third) tawar (row), a jacinth, an shabaw (agate), and an achalamah (amethyst);
And the rabayaiy (fourth) tawar (row), a chrysolite, an shaham (Onyx), and a yashapah (jasper). They were enclosed in zahab (gold) settings.

The aban (stone) were according to the sham (name) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), shanayam (two), according to their sham (name); like the engravings of a chawatham (signet), everyone according to his sham (name), for the shanayam (two) shabat (tribes).
They ishah (make) on the chashan (breastplate) sharasharah (chains) like cords, of braided maishah (work) of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold).

They ishah (make) shanayam (two) settings of zahab (gold), and shanayam (two) zahab (gold) tabaith (rings), and nathan (give) the shanayam (two) tabaith (rings) on the shanayam (two) ends of the chashan (breastplate).
They nathan (give) the shanayam (two) braided chains of zahab (gold) in the shanayam (two) tabaith (rings) at the ends of the chashan (breastplate).

The other shanayam (two) ends of the shanayam (two) braided chains they nathan (give) on the shanayam (two) settings, and nathan (give) them on the kathap (shoulder) straps of the apawad (ephod), in its panayam (front).

They ishah (make) shanayam (two) tabaith (rings) of zahab (gold), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them on the shanayam (two) ends of the chashan (breastplate), on its shapah (edge), which was toward the ibar (side) of the apawad (ephod) inward.

They ishah (make) shanayam (two) tabaith (rings) of zahab (gold), and nathan (give) them on the shanayam (two) kathap (shoulder) straps of the apawad (ephod) matah (underneath), in its panayam (front), close by its machabarath (coupling), mail (top/above) the skillfully woven band of the apawad (ephod).

They rakas (bound) the chashan (breastplate) by its tabaith (rings) to the tabaith (rings) of the apawad (ephod) with a pathayal (lace) of thakalath (blue), that it chashab (might) be on the skillfully woven band of the apawad (ephod), and that the chashan (breastplate) might not come zachach (loose) from the apawad (ephod), as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).
He ishah (make) the maiyal (robe) of the apawad (ephod) of woven maishah (work), kalayal (all) of thakalath (blue).
The opening of the maiyal (robe) in its thawak (midst) was like the opening of a coat of mail, with a shapah (binding) around its opening, that it should not be qarai (torn).
They ishah (make) on the shawal (skirts) of the maiyal (robe) ramawan (pomegranates) of thakalath (blue), aragaman (purple), shanay (second), and shazar (twined) linen.

They ishah (make) paiman (bells) of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold), and nathan (give) the paiman (bells) thawak (midst) the ramawan (pomegranates) around the shawal (skirts) of the maiyal (robe), thawak (midst) the ramawan (pomegranates);

A paiman (bell) and a ramawan (pomegranate), a paiman (bell) and a ramawan (pomegranate), around the shawal (skirts) of the maiyal (robe), to sharath (minister) in, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).
They ishah (make) the kathanath (coats) of shash (six) linen of woven maishah (work) for Aharawan (Aaron), and for his ban (son),
And the turban of shash (six) linen, and the shash (six) headbands of shash (six) linen, and the shash (six) breeches of fine shazar (twined) shash (six),
And the sash of fine shazar (twined) shash (six), and thakalath (blue), and aragaman (purple), and shanay (second), the raqam (work) of the embroiderer, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).

They ishah (make) the tzayatz (plate) of the qadash (set apart/make holy) nazar (crown / consecrate) of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold), and kathab (wrote) on it a makathab (writing), like the engravings of a chawatham (signet): qadash (set apart/make holy) TO Yahawah.
They tied to it a pathayal (lace) of thakalath (blue), to nathan (give) it on the turban mail (top/above), as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).

Thus all the ibadah (work) of the mashakan (tabernacle) of the mashakan (tent) of Meeting was kalah (complete / finish). The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) ishah (make) according to all that Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses); so they ishah (make).

They bawaa (come) the mashakan (tabernacle) to Mashah (Moses), the mashakan (tent), with all its kalay (furniture), its clasps, its qarash (boards), its barayach (bars), its imawad (pillar), its adan (sockets),
The makasah (covering) of ayal (rams)' iwar (skins) adam (dyed) red, the makasah (covering) of thachash (sea) cow iwar (hides), the parakath (veil) of the screen,
The arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony) with its poles, the kaparath (mercy) seat,
The shalachan (table), all its kalay (vessels), the show panayam (bread),
The tahawar (pure) lampstand, its nayar (lamps), even the nayar (lamps) to be mairakah (set) in order, all its kalay (vessels), the shaman (oil) for the maawar (Maawar/(Luminary)),
The zahab (gold) mazabach (altar), the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), the sam (sweet) qatarath (incense), the screen for the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent),
The bronze mazabach (altar), its makabar (grating) of nachashath (brass), its poles, all of its kalay (vessels), the basin and its kan (for sure),

The qalai (hangings) of the chatzar (court), its imawad (pillar), its adan (sockets), the screen for the shair (gate) of the chatzar (court), its mayathar (cords), its yathad (pins), all the kalay (instruments) of the ibadah (service) of the mashakan (tabernacle), for the mashakan (tent) of Meeting,

The finely worked bagad (garments) for sharath (ministering) in the qadash (set apart/make holy) place, the qadash (set apart/make holy) bagad (garments) for Aharawan (Aaron) the kahan (priest), and the bagad (garments) of his ban (son), to kahan (priest) in the priest's office.
According to all that Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses), so the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) ishah (make) all the ibadah (work).
Mashah (Moses) raah (see) all the malaakah (work), and behold, they ishah (make) done it as Yahawah had tzawah (commanded), even so ishah (make) they done it: and Mashah (Moses) barak (blessed) them.
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),
On the raashawan (first) yawam (day) of the achad (one) chadash (month) you shall qawam (rise up) up the mashakan (tabernacle) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
You shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony) in it, and you shall screen the arawan (ark) with the parakath (veil).
You shall bawaa (come) in the shalachan (table), and irak (set) in order the things that are on it. You shall bawaa (come) in the lampstand, and ilah (go up / offer) its nayar (lamps).

You shall nathan (give) the zahab (gold) mazabach (altar) for qatarath (incense) panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the screen of the pathach (door) to the mashakan (tabernacle).
You shall nathan (give) the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering) panayam (before) the pathach (door) of the mashakan (tabernacle) of the mashakan (tent) of Meeting.
You shall nathan (give) the basin between the ahal (tent) of Meeting and the mazabach (altar), and shall nathan (give) mayam (Waters) therein.
You shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) up the chatzar (court) around it, and hang up the screen of the shair (gate) of the chatzar (court).

You shall laqach (take / seized) the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), and mashach (anoint) the mashakan (tabernacle), and all that is in it, and shall make it qadash (set apart/make holy), and all its kalay (furniture): and it will be qadash (set apart/make holy).

You shall mashach (anoint) the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering), with all its kalay (vessels), and qadash (set apart/make holy) the mazabach (altar): and the mazabach (altar) will be most qadash (set apart/make holy).
You shall mashach (anoint) the basin and its kan (for sure), and qadash (set apart/make holy) it.
You shall qarab (come close) Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son) to the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and shall rachatz (wash) them with mayam (Waters).

You shall labash (put) on Aharawan (Aaron) the qadash (set apart/make holy) bagad (garments); and you shall mashach (anoint) him, and qadash (set apart/make holy) him, that he may kahan (priest) to me in the priest's office.
You shall qarab (come close) his ban (son), and labash (put) kathanath (coats) on them.

You shall mashach (anoint) them, as you mashach (anointed) their ab (father), that they may kahan (priest) to me in the priest's office. Their mashachah (anointing) shall be to them for an iwalam (forever) kahanah (priesthood) throughout their dawar (generation / age / period).
Mashah (Moses) ishah (make) so. According to all that Yahawah tzawah (commanded) him, so he ishah (make).
It happened in the raashawan (first) chadash (month) in the shanay (second) shanah (year), on the raashawan (first) day of the chadash (month), that the mashakan (tabernacle) was qawam (rise up) up.

Mashah (Moses) qawam (rise up) up the mashakan (tabernacle), and nathan (give) its adan (sockets), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) up its qarash (boards), and nathan (give) in its barayach (bars), and qawam (rise up) up its imawad (pillar).

He spread the ahal (covering) over the ahal (tent), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the roof of the mashakan (tabernacle) mail (top/above) on it, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).

He laqach (take / seized) and nathan (give) the idawath (testimony) into the arawan (ark), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the poles on the arawan (ark), and nathan (give) the kaparath (mercy) seat mail (top/above) on the arawan (ark).

He bawaa (come) the arawan (ark) into the mashakan (tabernacle), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) up the parakath (veil) of the screen, and screened the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony), as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).
He nathan (give) the shalachan (table) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting, on the yarak (side) of the mashakan (tabernacle) northward, outside of the parakath (veil).
He irak (set) the lacham (bread) in irak (order) on it panayam (before) Yahawah, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).
He shawam (place / establish / appoint) the lampstand in the ahal (tent) of Meeting, opposite the shalachan (table), on the yarak (side) of the mashakan (tabernacle) southward.
He ilah (go up / offer) the nayar (lamps) panayam (before) Yahawah, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).
He shawam (place / establish / appoint) the zahab (gold) mazabach (altar) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting panayam (before) the parakath (veil);
And he burnt qatarath (incense) of sam (sweet) spices on it, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).
He shawam (place / establish / appoint) up the screen of the pathach (door) to the mashakan (tabernacle).

He shawam (place / establish / appoint) the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering) at the pathach (door) of the mashakan (tabernacle) of the mashakan (tent) of Meeting, and ilah (go up / offer) on it the burnt ilah (offering) and the meal manachah (offering), as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).
He shawam (place / establish / appoint) the basin between the ahal (tent) of Meeting and the mazabach (altar), and nathan (give) mayam (Waters) therein, with which to rachatz (wash).
Mashah (Moses), Aharawan (Aaron), and his ban (son) rachatz (washed) their yad (hand) and their ragal (feet / foot) there.
When they bawaa (come) into the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and when they qarab (come close) near to the mazabach (altar), they rachatz (washed), as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).

He qawam (rise up) up the chatzar (court) around the mashakan (tabernacle) and the mazabach (altar), and nathan (give) up the screen of the shair (gate) of the chatzar (court). So Mashah (Moses) kalah (complete / finish) the malaakah (work).
Then the inan (cloud) kasah (covered) the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah malaa (filled) the mashakan (tabernacle).

Mashah (Moses) wasn't yakal (able) to bawaa (come) into the ahal (tent) of Meeting, because the inan (cloud) stayed on it, and yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) kabawad (glory) malaa (filled) the mashakan (tabernacle).
When the inan (cloud) was ilah (go up / offer) up from over the mashakan (tabernacle), the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) nasai (went) onward, throughout all their masai (journeys);
But if the inan (cloud) wasn't ilah (go up / offer) up, then they didn't travel until the yawam (day) that it was ilah (go up / offer) up.

For the inan (cloud) of Yahawah was on the mashakan (tabernacle) by yawamam (by day), and there was ash (fire) in the cloud by layal (night), in the iyan (eye) of all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), throughout all their masai (journeys).
Yahawah qaraa (called) to Mashah (Moses), and dabar (word / matter) to him out of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, amar (spoke),

Dabar (word / matter) to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (spoke) them, ‘When anyone of you qarab (come close) an qaraban (offering) to Yahawah, you shall qarab (come close) your qaraban (offering) of the livestock, from the baqar (morning) and from the tzaan (flock).

‘If his qaraban (offering) is a burnt ilah (offering) from the baqar (morning), he shall qarab (come close) a zakar (remembrance/memory) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish. He shall qarab (come close) it at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, that he may be panayam (accepted) before Yahawah.
He shall samak (lay) his yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the burnt ilah (offering), and it shall be ratzah (accepted) for him to make kapar (atonement) for him.

He shall shachat (kill) the bull panayam (before) Yahawah. Aharawan (Aaron's) ban (son), the kahan (priest), shall qarab (come close) the dam (blood) and zaraq (sprinkle) the dam (blood) around on the mazabach (altar) that is at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
He shall pashat (flay) the burnt ilah (offering), and nathach (cut) it into nathach (pieces).
The ban (son) of Aharawan (Aaron) the kahan (priest) shall nathan (give) ash (fire) on the mazabach (altar), and lay itz (wood) in irak (order) on the ash (fire);

And Aharawan (Aaron's) ban (son), the kahan (priest), shall irak (lay) the pieces, the raash (head), and the padar (fat) in irak (order) on the itz (wood) that is on the ash (fire) which is on the mazabach (altar);

But its innards and its karai (legs) he shall rachatz (wash) with mayam (Waters). The kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) the whole on the mazabach (altar), for a burnt ilah (offering), an ashah (wife/individual woman) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.

‘If his qaraban (offering) is from the tzaan (flock), from the sheep, or from the iz (goats), for a burnt ilah (offering), he shall qarab (come close) a zakar (remembrance/memory) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish.

He shall shachat (kill) it on the tzapawan (north) yarak (side) of the mazabach (altar) panayam (before) Yahawah. Aharawan (Aaron's) ban (son), the kahan (priest), shall zaraq (sprinkle) its dam (blood) around on the mazabach (altar).

He shall nathach (cut) it into its nathach (pieces), with its raash (head) and its padar (fat). The kahan (priest) shall irak (lay) them in order on the itz (wood) that is on the ash (fire) which is on the mazabach (altar),

But the innards and the karai (legs) he shall rachatz (wash) with mayam (Waters). The kahan (priest) shall qarab (come close) the whole, and qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar). It is a burnt ilah (offering), an ashah (wife/individual woman) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.
‘If his ilah (offering) to Yahawah is a burnt ilah (offering) of iwap (flying), then he shall qarab (come close) his qaraban (offering) of turtledoves, or of ban (son) yawanah (pigeons).

The kahan (priest) shall qarab (come close) it to the mazabach (altar), and malaq (wring) off its raash (head), and qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar); and its dam (blood) shall be drained out on the qayar (side) of the mazabach (altar);
And he shall sawar (take) away its maraah (crop) with its filth, and shalak (cast) it beside the mazabach (altar) on the qadam (east) part, in the maqawam (place) of the ashes.

He shall tear it by its kanap (wings), but shall not badal (separated) it apart. The kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar), on the itz (wood) that is on the ash (fire). It is a burnt ilah (offering), an ashah (wife/individual woman) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.

‘When anyone qarab (come close) an qaraban (offering) of a meal offering to Yahawah, his qaraban (offering) shall be of fine salath (flour); and he shall yatzaq (pour) shaman (oil) on it, and nathan (give) labawanah (frankincense) on it.

He shall bawaa (come) it to Aharawan (Aaron's) ban (son), the kahan (priest); and he shall qamatz (take) his qamatz (handful) of its fine salath (flour), and of its shaman (oil), with all its labawanah (frankincense); and the kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) its azakarah (memorial) on the mazabach (altar), an ashah (wife/individual woman) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.

That which is yathar (left) of the meal manachah (offering) shall be Aharawan (Aaron's) and his ban (son)’. It is a most qadash (set apart/make holy) thing of the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Yahawah made by ashah (wife/individual woman).

‘When you qarab (come close) an manachah (offering) of a meal manachah (offering) baked in the thanawar (oven), it shall be unleavened chalah (cakes) of fine salath (flour) balal (mixed) with shaman (oil), or unleavened raqayaq (wafers) mashach (anointed) with shaman (oil).
If your manachah (offering) is a meal manachah (offering) of the griddle, it shall be of unleavened fine salath (flour), balal (mixed) with shaman (oil).
You shall cut it in path (pieces), and yatzaq (pour) shaman (oil) on it. It is a meal manachah (offering).
If your manachah (offering) is a meal manachah (offering) of the pan, it shall be ishah (make) of fine salath (flour) with shaman (oil).

You shall bawaa (come) the meal manachah (offering) that is ishah (make) of these things to Yahawah: and it shall be qarab (come close) to the kahan (priest), and he shall nagash (bring) it to the mazabach (altar).

The kahan (priest) shall rawam (will lift up) from the meal manachah (offering) its azakarah (memorial), and shall qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar), an ashah (wife/individual woman) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.

That which is yathar (left) of the meal manachah (offering) shall be Aharawan (Aaron's) and his ban (son)’. It is a thing most qadash (set apart/make holy) of the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Yahawah made by ashah (wife/individual woman).

‘No meal manachah (offering), which you shall qarab (come close) to Yahawah, shall be ishah (make) with yeast; for you shall qatar (burn) no yeast, nor any dabash (honey), as an ashah (wife/individual woman) made by ashah (wife/individual woman) to Yahawah.
As an qaraban (offering) of firstfruits you shall qarab (come close) them to Yahawah: but they shall not ilah (go up / offer) for a pleasant aroma on the mazabach (altar).

Every qaraban (offering) of your meal qaraban (offering) you shall malach (season) with malach (salt); neither shall you allow the malach (salt) of the barayath (covenant) of your Alahayam to be shabath (shabath/rest) from your meal manachah (offering). With all your manachah (offerings) you shall qarab (come close) malach (salt).

‘If you qarab (come close) a meal manachah (offering) of bakawar (first) fruits to Yahawah, you shall qarab (come close) for the meal manachah (offering) of your bakawar (first) fruits grain in the abayab (ear) qalah (parched) with ash (fire), bruised grain of the fresh karamal (ear).
You shall nathan (give) shaman (oil) on it, and nathan (give) labawanah (frankincense) on it: it is a meal manachah (offering).

The kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) as its azakarah (memorial), part of its bruised grain, and part of its shaman (oil), along with all its labawanah (frankincense): it is an ashah (wife/individual woman) made by fire to Yahawah.

‘If his qaraban (offering) is a zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings; if he qarab (come close) it from the baqar (morning), whether zakar (remembrance/memory) or naqabah (female), he shall qarab (come close) it thamayam (complete / whole) blemish panayam (before) Yahawah.

He shall samak (lay) his yad (hand) on the raash (head) of his qaraban (offering), and shachat (kill) it at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting: and Aharawan (Aaron's) ban (son), the kahan (priest) shall zaraq (sprinkle) the dam (blood) around on the mazabach (altar).

He shall qarab (come close) of the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings an ashah (wife/individual woman) made by fire to Yahawah; the chalab (fat) that kasah (covers) the innards, and all the chalab (fat) that is on the innards,

And the shanayam (two) kalayah (kidneys), and the chalab (fat) that is on them, which is by the kasal (loins), and the cover on the kabad (liver), with the kalayah (kidneys), he shall sawar (take) away.

Aharawan (Aaron's) ban (son) shall qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar) on the burnt offering, which is on the itz (wood) that is on the ash (fire): it is an offering made by ash (fire), of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.

‘If his qaraban (offering) for a zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings to Yahawah is from the tzaan (flock); zakar (remembrance/memory) or naqabah (female), he shall qarab (come close) it thamayam (complete / whole) blemish.
If he qarab (come close) a kashab (lamb) for his qaraban (offering), then he shall qarab (come close) it panayam (before) Yahawah;

And he shall samak (lay) his yad (hand) on the raash (head) of his qaraban (offering), and shachat (kill) it panayam (before) the ahal (tent) of Meeting: and Aharawan (Aaron's) ban (son) shall zaraq (sprinkle) its dam (blood) around on the mazabach (altar).

He shall qarab (come close) from the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings an ashah (wife/individual woman) made by fire to Yahawah; its chalab (fat), the entire tail fat, he shall sawar (take) away close to the itzah (backbone); and the chalab (fat) that kasah (covers) the qarab (among / near), and all the chalab (fat) that is on the qarab (among / near),

And the shanayam (two) kalayah (kidneys), and the chalab (fat) that is on them, which is by the kasal (loins), and the cover on the kabad (liver), with the kalayah (kidneys), he shall sawar (take) away.
The kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar): it is the lacham (food) of the ashah (wife/individual woman) made by fire to Yahawah.
‘If his qaraban (offering) is a iz (goat), then he shall qarab (come close) it panayam (before) Yahawah:

And he shall samak (lay) his yad (hand) on its raash (head), and shachat (kill) it panayam (before) the ahal (tent) of Meeting; and the ban (son) of Aharawan (Aaron) shall zaraq (sprinkle) its dam (blood) around on the mazabach (altar).

He shall qarab (come close) from it as his qaraban (offering), an ashah (wife/individual woman) made by fire to Yahawah; the chalab (fat) that kasah (covers) the innards, and all the chalab (fat) that is on the innards,

And the shanayam (two) kalayah (kidneys), and the chalab (fat) that is on them, which is by the kasal (loins), and the cover on the kabad (liver), with the kalayah (kidneys), he shall sawar (take) away.

The kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) them on the mazabach (altar): it is the lacham (food) of the ashah (wife/individual woman) made by fire, for a pleasant aroma; all the chalab (fat) is yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)).
‘It shall be a iwalam (forever) chaqah (statute) throughout your dawar (generation / age / period) in all your mawashab (dwellings), that you shall akal (eat) neither chalab (fat) nor dam (blood).’
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

Dabar (word / matter) to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), ‘If anyone chataa (sins) unintentionally, in any of the things which Yahawah has commanded not to be ishah (make), and ishah (make) any hanah (Behold) of them:

If the mashayach (anointed one) kahan (priest) chataa (sins) so as to bring ashamah (guilt) on the im (people / nation), then let him qarab (come close) for his chataah (sin), which he has chataa (sinned), a young par (bull) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish to Yahawah for a chataah (sin) offering.

He shall bawaa (come) the par (bull) to the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting panayam (before) Yahawah; and he shall samak (lay) his yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the par (bull), and shachat (kill) the par (bull) panayam (before) Yahawah.
The mashayach (anointed one) kahan (priest) shall laqach (take / seized) some of the dam (blood) of the par (bull), and bawaa (come) it to the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

The kahan (priest) shall tabal (dip) his atzabai (finger) in the dam (blood), and nazah (sprinkle) some of the dam (blood) shabai (seven) paim (times) panayam (before) Yahawah, panayam (before) the parakath (veil) of the qadash (set apart/make holy).

The kahan (priest) shall nathan (give) some of the dam (blood) on the qaran (horn) of the mazabach (altar) of sam (sweet) qatarath (incense) panayam (before) Yahawah, which is in the ahal (tent) of Meeting; and he shall shapak (pour) out all of rest of the dam (blood) of the par (bull) at the base of the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering), which is at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
He shall take all the chalab (fat) of the par (bull) of the chataah (sin) offering off of it; the chalab (fat) that kasah (covers) the innards, and all the chalab (fat) that is on the innards,

And the shanayam (two) kalayah (kidneys), and the chalab (fat) that is on them, which is by the kasal (loins), and the cover on the kabad (liver), with the kalayah (kidneys), he shall sawar (take) away,

As it is rawam (will lift up) off of the shawar (bull) of the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings. The kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) them on the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering).
The par (bull's) iwar (skin), all its bashar (flesh), with its raash (head), and with its karai (legs), its innards, and its parash (dung),

Even the whole par (bull) shall he yatzaa (go out / come out) forth outside the machanah (camp) to a tahawar (clean) maqawam (place), where the ashes are shapak (poured) out, and sharap (burn) it on itz (wood) with ash (fire). Where the ashes are shapak (poured) out it shall be sharap (burned).

‘If the whole idah (congregation) of Yasharaal (Israel) shagah (sins), and the thing is ilam (hidden) from the iyan (eye) of the qahal (assembly), and they ishah (make) done any of the things which Yahawah has commanded not to be ishah (make), and are asham (guilty);

When the chataah (sin) in which they have chataa (sinned) is yadai (known), then the qahal (assembly) shall qarab (come close) a young par (bull) for a chataah (sin) offering, and bawaa (come) it panayam (before) the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

The zaqan (elders) of the idah (congregation) shall samak (lay) their yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the par (bull) panayam (before) Yahawah; and the par (bull) shall be shachat (killed) panayam (before) Yahawah.
The mashayach (anointed one) kahan (priest) shall bawaa (come) of the dam (blood) of the par (bull) to the ahal (tent) of Meeting:
And the kahan (priest) shall tabal (dip) his atzabai (finger) in the dam (blood), and nazah (sprinkle) it shabai (seven) paim (times) panayam (before) Yahawah, panayam (before) the parakath (veil).

He shall nathan (give) some of the dam (blood) on the qaran (horn) of the mazabach (altar) which is panayam (before) Yahawah, that is in the ahal (tent) of Meeting; and the rest of the dam (blood) he shall shapak (pour) out at the base of the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering), which is at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
All its chalab (fat) he shall rawam (will lift up) from it, and qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar).

Thus shall he ishah (make) with the par (bull); as he ishah (make) with the par (bull) of the chataah (sin) offering, so shall he ishah (make) with this; and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for them, and they shall be salach (forgive/pardon/make clean).

He shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth the par (bull) outside the machanah (camp), and sharap (burn) it as he sharap (burned) the raashawan (first) par (bull). It is the chataah (sin) offering for the qahal (assembly).
‘When a nashayaa (ruler) chataa (sins), and shagagah (unwittingly) ishah (make) any one of all the things which Yahawah his Alahayam has commanded not to be ishah (make), and is asham (guilty);

If his chataah (sin), in which he has chataa (sinned), is yadai (made) known to him, he shall bawaa (come) as his qaraban (offering) a shaiyar (goat), a zakar (remembrance/memory) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish.

He shall samak (lay) his yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the shaiyar (goat), and shachat (kill) it in the maqawam (place) where they shachat (kill) the burnt ilah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah. It is a sin ilah (offering).

The kahan (priest) shall laqach (take / seized) some of the dam (blood) of the chataah (sin) offering with his atzabai (finger), and nathan (give) it on the qaran (horn) of the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering). He shall shapak (pour) out the rest of its dam (blood) at the base of the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering).

All its chalab (fat) he shall qatar (burn) on the mazabach (altar), like the chalab (fat) of the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings; and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him concerning his chataah (sin), and he will be salach (forgive/pardon/make clean).

‘If anyone of the aratz (Earth/land) im (people / nation) chataa (sins) shagagah (unwittingly), in ishah (make) any of the things which Yahawah has commanded not to be ishah (make), and is asham (guilty);

If his chataah (sin), which he has chataa (sinned), is yadai (made) known to him, then he shall bawaa (come) for his qaraban (offering) a goat, a naqabah (female) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish, for his chataah (sin) which he has chataa (sinned).
He shall samak (lay) his yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the chataah (sin) offering, and shachat (kill) the chataah (sin) offering in the maqawam (place) of burnt chataah (sin).

The kahan (priest) shall laqach (take / seized) some of its dam (blood) with his atzabai (finger), and nathan (give) it on the qaran (horn) of the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering); and the rest of its dam (blood) he shall shapak (pour) out at the base of the mazabach (altar).

All its chalab (fat) he shall sawar (take) away, like the chalab (fat) is sawar (taken) away from off of the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings; and the kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar) for a pleasant aroma to Yahawah; and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him, and he will be salach (forgive/pardon/make clean).
‘If he bawaa (come) a kabash (lamb) as his chataah (sin) for a sin qaraban (offering), he shall bawaa (come) a naqabah (female) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish.

He shall samak (lay) his yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the chataah (sin) offering, and shachat (kill) it for a chataah (sin) offering in the maqawam (place) where they shachat (kill) the burnt ilah (offering).

The kahan (priest) shall laqach (take / seized) some of the dam (blood) of the chataah (sin) offering with his atzabai (finger), and nathan (give) it on the qaran (horn) of the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering); and all the rest of its dam (blood) he shall shapak (pour) out at the base of the mazabach (altar).

All its chalab (fat) he shall sawar (take) away, like the chalab (fat) of the kashab (lamb) is sawar (taken) away from the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings; and the kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) them on the mazabach (altar), on the offerings of Yahawah made by ashah (wife/individual woman); and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him concerning his chataah (sin) that he has chataa (sinned), and he will be salach (forgive/pardon/make clean).

‘If anyone chataa (sins), in that he shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of adjuration, he being a id (witness), aw (or) he raah (see) seen or yadai (known), if he doesn't nagad (report) it, then he shall nashaa (lift) his iwan (guilt/iniquity).

‘Or if anyone touches any tamaa (unclean) thing, whether it is the carcass of an tamaa (unclean) animal, or the carcass of tamaa (unclean) livestock, or the carcass of tamaa (unclean) sharatz (creeping) things, and it is ilam (hidden) from him, and he is tamaa (unclean), then he shall be asham (guilty).

‘Or if he touches the tamaah (uncleanness) of adam (man), whatever his tamaah (uncleanness) is with which he is tamaa (unclean), and it is ilam (hidden) from him; when he yadai (knows) of it, then he shall be asham (guilty).

‘Or if anyone shabai (swear / take oath) rashly with his shapah (lips) to do raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil), or to do yatab (good), whatever it is that a adam (man) might utter rashly with an shabawaih (oath), and it is ilam (hidden) from him; when he yadai (knows) of it, then he shall be asham (guilty) of achad (one) of these.
It shall be, when he is asham (guilty) of achad (one) of these, he shall yadah (confess) that in which he has chataa (sinned):

And he shall bawaa (come) his asham (trespass) offering to Yahawah for his chataah (sin) which he has chataa (sinned), a naqabah (female) from the tzaan (flock), a kashabah (lamb) or a goat, for a chataah (sin) offering; and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him concerning his chataah (sin).

‘If he can't afford a shah (lamb), then he shall nagai (bring) his asham (trespass) chataa (offering) for that in which he has sinned, shanayam (two) turtledoves, or shanayam (two) ban (son) yawanah (pigeons), to Yahawah; achad (one) for a chataah (sin) offering, and the other for a burnt chataah (sin).

He shall bawaa (come) them to the kahan (priest), who shall first qarab (come close) the one which is for the chataah (sin) offering, and malaq (wring) off its raash (head) from its irap (neck), but shall not badal (separated) it completely.

He shall nazah (sprinkle) some of the dam (blood) of the chataah (sin) offering on the qayar (side) of the mazabach (altar); and the shaar (rest) of the dam (blood) shall be drained out at the base of the mazabach (altar). It is a chataah (sin) offering.

He shall ishah (make) the shanay (second) for a burnt ilah (offering), according to the mashapat (ordinance); and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him concerning his chataah (sin) which he has chataa (sinned), and he shall be salach (forgive/pardon/make clean).

‘But if he can't afford shanayam (two) turtledoves, or shanayam (two) ban (son) yawanah (pigeons), then he shall bawaa (come) his qaraban (offering) for that in which he has chataa (sinned), the ishayaray (tenth) part of an ayapah (ephah) of fine salath (flour) for a chataah (sin) offering. He shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) no shaman (oil) on it, neither shall he nathan (give) any labawanah (frankincense) on it, for it is a chataah (sin) offering.

He shall bawaa (come) it to the kahan (priest), and the kahan (priest) shall qamatz (take) his handful of it as the azakarah (memorial) portion, and qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar), on the offerings of Yahawah made by ashah (wife/individual woman). It is a chataah (sin) offering.

The kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him concerning his chataah (sin) that he has chataa (sinned) in any of these things, and he will be salach (forgive/pardon/make clean); and the rest shall be the kahan (priest), as the meal manachah (offering).’
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

If anyone mail (top/above) a mail (top/above), and mail (top/above) shagagah (unwittingly), in the qadash (set apart/make holy) things of Yahawah; then he shall bawaa (come) his asham (trespass) offering to Yahawah, a ayal (ram) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish from the tzaan (flock), according to your irak (estimation) in kasap (silver) by shaqal (shekels), after the shaqal (shekel) of the qadash (set apart/make holy), for a asham (trespass) offering.

He shall shalam (make) restitution for that which he has chataa (done) wrong in the qadash (set apart/make holy) thing, and shall yasap (add) a chamayashay (fifth) part to it, and nathan (give) it to the kahan (priest); and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him with the ayal (ram) of the asham (trespass) offering, and he will be salach (forgive/pardon/make clean).

If anyone chataa (sins), and ishah (make) any of the things which Yahawah has commanded not to be ishah (make); though he didn't yadai (know) it, yet he is asham (guilty), and shall nashaa (lift) his iwan (guilt/iniquity).

He shall bawaa (come) a ayal (ram) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish from of the tzaan (flock), according to your irak (estimation), for a asham (trespass) offering, to the kahan (priest); and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him concerning the thing in which he shagag (sinned) and didn't yadai (know) it, and he will be salach (forgive/pardon/make clean).
It is a asham (trespass) offering. He is asham (certainly) asham (guilty) before Yahawah.
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),
If anyone sins, and commits a trespass against Yahawah, and deals falsely with his neighbor in a matter of deposit, or of bargain, or of robbery, or has oppressed his neighbor,
Or il (over) found that which was lost, and dealt falsely therein, and swearing to a lie; in any of all these things that a man shawam (place / establish / appoint), sinning therein;

Then it shall be, if he has sinned, and is guilty, he shall restore that which he yatzaa (go out / come out) by robbery, or the thing which he has yatzaa (go out / come out) by oppression, or the deposit which was committed to him, or the lost thing which he found,

Or any thing about which he has sworn falsely; he shall restore it even in full, and shall add a fifth part more to it. To him to whom it belongs he shall give it, in the baqar (morning) of his being found guilty.
He shall bring his trespass offering to Yahawah, a ram laa (NOT) blemish from the flock, according to your estimation, for a trespass offering, to the priest.
The priest shall make atonement for him panayam (before) Yahawah, and he will be forgiven concerning whatever he does to become guilty.
Yahawah spoke to Moses, saying,

Command Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son), saying, ‘This is the law of the burnt offering: the burnt offering shall be on the hearth on the altar all night until the morning; and the fire of the altar shall be kept akal (eat) on it.

The priest shall nathan (give) on his linen garment, and he shall nathan (give) on his linen breeches upon his body; and he shall remove the ashes from where the ashah (wife/individual woman) has consumed the burnt nathan (give) on the altar, and he shall nathan (give) them beside the altar.
He shall take off his garments, and put on other garments, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean kal (every).

The fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it, it shall not go out; and the priest shall burn wood on it every morning: and he shall lay the burnt offering in order upon it, and shall burn on it the fat of the peace offerings.
Fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it shall not qarab (come close) out.
‘This is the law of the meal manachah (offering): the sons of Aaron shall qarab (come close) it before Yahawah, before the altar.

He shall ishah (make) from there his handful of the fine flour of the meal ishah (make), and of its oil, and all the frankincense which is on the meal ishah (make), and shall qatar (burn) it on the altar for a pleasant aroma, as its memorial, to Yahawah.
That which is left of it Aaron and his sons shall akal (eat). It shall be akal (eat) laa (NOT) yeast in a holy kal (every). They shall akal (eat) it in the court of the Tent of Meeting.
It shall not be baked with yeast. I have given it as their portion of my offerings made by fire. It is most holy, as the sin offering, and as the trespass offering.

Every male among the ban (son) of Aharawan (Aaron) shall eat of it, as their qadash (set apart/make holy) forever throughout your generations, from the chataah (sin) of Yahawah made by fire. Whoever touches them shall be qadash (set apart/make holy).’
Yahawah spoke to Moses, saying,

This is the bagad (offering) of Aaron and of his sons, which they shall offer to Yahawah in the day when he is qadash (set apart/make holy): the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a meal bagad (offering) perpetually, half of it in the morning, and half of it in the evening.
It shall be kalay (made) with oil in a griddle. When it is soaked, you shall bashal (bring) it in. You shall offer the meal offering in bashal (baked) shabar (pieces) for a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.
The anointed kahan (priest) that will be in his place from among his sons shall offer it. By a statute forever, it shall be wholly burnt to Yahawah.
Every meal chataah (sin) of a priest shall be wholly burned. It shall not be akal (eat).
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

Dabar (word / matter) to Aharawan (Aaron) and to his ban (son), amar (spoke), ‘This is the thawarah (instruction) of the chataah (sin) offering: in the maqawam (place) where the burnt ilah (offering) is shachat (killed), the chataah (sin) offering shall be shachat (killed) panayam (before) Yahawah. It is most qadash (set apart/make holy).
The kahan (priest) who offers it for chataa (sin) shall akal (eat) it. It shall be akal (eat) in a qadawash (holy) maqawam (place), in the chatzar (court) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

Whatever shall nagai (touch) its bashar (flesh) shall be qadash (set apart/make holy). When there is any of its dam (blood) nazah (sprinkled) on a bagad (garment), you shall kabas (wash) that on which it was nazah (sprinkled) in a qadawash (holy) maqawam (place).

But the charash (earthen) kalay (vessel) in which it is bashal (boiled) shall be shabar (broken); and if it is bashal (boiled) in a bronze kalay (vessel), it shall be maraq (scoured), and shatap (rinsed) in mayam (Waters).
Every zakar (remembrance/memory) among the kahan (priest) shall akal (eat) of it: it is most qadash (set apart/make holy).

No chataah (sin) offering, of which any of the dam (blood) is bawaa (come) into the ahal (tent) of Meeting to make kapar (atonement) in the qadash (set apart/make holy) Place, shall be akal (eat): it shall be sharap (burned) with ash (fire).
‘This is the thawarah (instruction) of the asham (trespass) offering. It is most qadash (set apart/make holy).

In the maqawam (place) where they shachat (kill) the burnt ilah (offering), he shall shachat (kill) the asham (trespass) offering; and its dam (blood) he shall zaraq (sprinkle) around on the mazabach (altar).
He shall qarab (come close) all of its chalab (fat): the fat tail, and the chalab (fat) that kasah (covers) the innards,

And the shanayam (two) kalayah (kidneys), and the chalab (fat) that is on them, which is by the kasal (loins), and the cover on the kabad (liver), with the kalayah (kidneys), shall he sawar (take) away;
And the kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) them on the mazabach (altar) for an ashah (wife/individual woman) made by fire to Yahawah: it is a asham (trespass) offering.
Every zakar (remembrance/memory) among the kahan (priest) may akal (eat) of it. It shall be akal (eat) in a qadawash (holy) maqawam (place). It is most qadawash (holy).
‘As is the chataah (sin) offering, so is the asham (trespass) offering; there is achad (one) thawarah (instruction) for them. The kahan (priest) who makes kapar (atonement) with them shall have it.

The kahan (priest) who qarab (come close) any ayash (husband/individual man) burnt ilah (offering), even the kahan (priest) shall have for himself the iwar (skin) of the burnt ilah (offering) which he has qarab (come close).

Every meal manachah (offering) that is apah (baked) in the thanawar (oven), and all that is ishah (make) in the machabath (pan), and on the griddle, shall be the kahan (priest) who qarab (come close) it.
Every meal manachah (offering), balal (mixed) with shaman (oil) or charab (dry), belongs to all the ban (son) of Aharawan (Aaron), ayash (husband/individual man) as well as ach (brother/kinsman).
‘This is the thawarah (instruction) of the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings, which one shall qarab (come close) to Yahawah.

If he qarab (come close) it for a thanksgiving, then he shall qarab (come close) with the zabach (sacrifice) of thanksgiving unleavened chalah (cakes) balal (mixed) with shaman (oil), and unleavened raqayaq (wafers) mashach (anointed) with shaman (oil), and chalah (cakes) balal (mixed) with shaman (oil).
With chalah (cakes) of chamatz (leavened) lacham (bread) he shall qarab (come close) his qaraban (offering) with the zabach (sacrifice) of his shalam (peace) offerings for thanksgiving.

Of it he shall qarab (come close) achad (one) out of achad (one) qaraban (offering) for a heave qaraban (offering) to Yahawah. It shall be the kahan (priest) who sprinkles the dam (blood) of the shalam (peace) offerings.

The bashar (flesh) of the zabach (sacrifice) of his shalam (peace) offerings for thanksgiving shall be akal (eat) on the yawam (day) of his qaraban (offering). He shall not yanach (leave) any of it until the baqar (morning).

‘But if the zabach (sacrifice) of his qaraban (offering) is a nadar (vow), or a freewill nadabah (voluntary / freewill offering), it shall be akal (eat) on the yawam (day) that he qarab (come close) his zabach (sacrifice); and on the next macharath (day) what yathar (remains) of it shall be akal (eat):
But what yathar (remains) of the bashar (flesh) of the zabach (sacrifice) on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day) shall be sharap (burned) with ash (fire).

If any of the bashar (flesh) of the zabach (sacrifice) of his shalam (peace) offerings is akal (eat) on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), it will not be ratzah (accepted), neither shall it be chashab (imputed) to him who qarab (come close) it. It will be an pagawal (abomination), and the napash (living being/soul) who akal (eat) any of it will nashaa (lift) his iwan (guilt/iniquity).

‘The bashar (flesh) that touches any tamaa (unclean) thing shall not be akal (eat). It shall be sharap (burned) with ash (fire). As for the bashar (flesh), everyone who is tahawar (clean) may akal (eat) it;

But the napash (living being/soul) who akal (eat) of the bashar (flesh) of the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings, that belongs to Yahawah, having his tamaah (uncleanness) on him, that napash (living being/soul) shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people / nation).

When anyone touches any tamaah (unclean) thing, the tamaah (uncleanness) of adam (man), or an tamaah (unclean) animal, or any tamaa (unclean) shaqatz (abomination), and akal (eat) some of the bashar (flesh) of the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings, which belong to Yahawah, that napash (living being/soul) shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people / nation).’
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),
Dabar (word / matter) to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), ‘You shall akal (eat) no chalab (fat), of shawar (bull), or sheep, or iz (goat).

The chalab (fat) of that which dies of nabalah (itself), and the chalab (fat) of that which is tarapah (torn) of animals, may be used for any other service, but you shall in no akal (eat) akal (eat) of it.

For whoever akal (eat) the chalab (fat) of the animal, of which men qarab (come close) an ashah (wife/individual woman) made by fire to Yahawah, even the napash (living being/soul) who akal (eat) it shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people / nation).
You shall not akal (eat) any dam (blood), whether it is of iwap (flying) or of animal, in any of your mawashab (dwellings).
Whoever it is who akal (eat) any dam (blood), that napash (living being/soul) shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people / nation).’
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

Dabar (word / matter) to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), ‘He who qarab (come close) the zabach (sacrifice) of his shalam (peace) offerings to Yahawah shall bawaa (come) his qaraban (offering) to Yahawah out of the zabach (sacrifice) of his shalam (peace) offerings.

With his own yad (hand) he shall bawaa (come) the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Yahawah made by ashah (wife/individual woman). He shall bawaa (come) the chalab (fat) with the chazah (breast), that the chazah (breast) may be nawap (waved) for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah.
The kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) the chalab (fat) on the mazabach (altar), but the chazah (breast) shall be Aharawan (Aaron's) and his ban (son)’.
The yamayan (right hand) shawaq (thigh) you shall nathan (give) to the kahan (priest) for a heave tharawamah (offering) out of the zabach (sacrifices) of your shalam (peace) offerings.

He among the ban (son) of Aharawan (Aaron) who qarab (come close) the dam (blood) of the shalam (peace) offerings, and the chalab (fat), shall have the yamayan (right hand) shawaq (thigh) for a manah (portion).

For the thanawapah (waved) chazah (breast) and the tharawamah (heaved) shawaq (thigh) I have laqach (take / seized) from the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) out of the zabach (sacrifices) of their shalam (peace) offerings, and nathan (give) given them to Aharawan (Aaron) the kahan (priest) and to his ban (son) as their chaq (statute) iwalam (forever) from the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel).'

This is the mashachah (anointing) portion of Aharawan (Aaron), and the mashachah (anointing) portion of his ban (son), out of the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Yahawah made by ashah (wife/individual woman), in the yawam (day) when he qarab (come close) them to minister to Yahawah in the kahan (priest) office;

Which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) to be nathan (give) them of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), in the yawam (day) that he mashach (anointed) them. It is their portion iwalam (forever) throughout their dawar (generation / age / period).

This is the thawarah (instruction) of the burnt ilah (offering), of the meal manachah (offering), and of the chataah (sin) offering, and of the asham (trespass) offering, and of the malaa (consecration), and of the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings;

Which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses) in har (mountain) Sayanay (Sinai), in the yawam (day) that he tzawah (commanded) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) to qarab (come close) their qaraban (offerings) to Yahawah, in the madabar (wilderness) of Sayanay (Sinai).
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

Laqach (take / seized) Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son) with him, and the bagad (garments), and the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), and the par (bull) of the chataah (sin) offering, and the shanayam (two) ayal (rams), and the sal (basket) of unleavened matzah (bread);
And qahal (assemble) all the idah (congregation) at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
Mashah (Moses) ishah (make) as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) him; and the idah (congregation) was qahal (assembled) at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to the idah (congregation), This is the thing which Yahawah has tzawah (commanded) to be ishah (make).
Mashah (Moses) qarab (come close) Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son), and rachatz (washed) them with mayam (Waters).

He nathan (give) the kathanath (coat) on him, tied the sash on him, labash (clothed) him with the maiyal (robe), nathan (give) the apawad (ephod) on him, and he tied the skillfully woven band of the apawad (ephod) on him, and fastened it to him with it.
He shawam (place / establish / appoint) the chashan (breastplate) on him; and in the chashan (breastplate) he nathan (give) the awarayam (urim) and the thamayam (complete / whole).

He shawam (place / establish / appoint) the turban on his raash (head); and on the turban, in panayam (front), he shawam (place / establish / appoint) the zahab (gold) tzayatz (plate), the qadash (set apart/make holy) nazar (crown / consecrate); as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).
Mashah (Moses) laqach (take / seized) the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), and mashach (anointed) the mashakan (tabernacle) and all that was in it, and qadash (set apart/make holy) them.

He nazah (sprinkled) it on the mazabach (altar) shabai (seven) paim (times), and mashach (anointed) the mazabach (altar) and all its kalay (vessels), and the basin and its kan (for sure), to qadash (set apart/make holy) them.
He yatzaq (poured) some of the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil) on Aharawan (Aaron's) raash (head), and mashach (anointed) him, to qadash (set apart/make holy) him.

Mashah (Moses) qarab (come close) Aharawan (Aaron's) ban (son), and labash (clothed) them with kathanath (coats), and tied sashes on them, and chabash (put) headbands on them; as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).

He nagash (brought) the par (bull) of the chataah (sin) offering, and Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son) samak (laid) their yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the par (bull) of the chataah (sin) offering.

He shachat (killed) it; and Mashah (Moses) laqach (take / seized) the dam (blood), and nathan (give) it around on the qaran (horn) of the mazabach (altar) with his atzabai (finger), and chataa (purified) the mazabach (altar), and yatzaq (poured) out the dam (blood) at the base of the mazabach (altar), and qadash (set apart/make holy) it, to make kapar (atonement) for it.

He laqach (take / seized) all the chalab (fat) that was on the innards, and the cover of the kabad (liver), and the shanayam (two) kalayah (kidneys), and their chalab (fat); and Mashah (Moses) qatar (burned) it on the mazabach (altar).
But the par (bull), and its iwar (skin), and its bashar (flesh), and its parash (dung), he sharap (burned) with ash (fire) outside the machanah (camp); as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).
He qarab (come close) the ayal (ram) of the burnt ilah (offering): and Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son) samak (laid) their yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the ayal (ram).
He shachat (killed) it; and Mashah (Moses) zaraq (sprinkled) the dam (blood) around on the mazabach (altar).
He nathach (cut) the ayal (ram) into its nathach (pieces); and Mashah (Moses) qatar (burned) the raash (head), and the nathach (pieces), and the padar (fat).

He rachatz (washed) the innards and the karai (legs) with mayam (Waters); and Mashah (Moses) qatar (burned) the whole ayal (ram) on the mazabach (altar). It was a burnt ilah (offering) for a pleasant aroma. It was an ashah (wife/individual woman) made by fire to Yahawah; as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).
He qarab (come close) the other ayal (ram), the ayal (ram) of malaa (consecration): and Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son) samak (laid) their yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the ayal (ram).

He shachat (killed) it; and Mashah (Moses) laqach (take / seized) some of its dam (blood), and nathan (give) it on the thanawak (tip) of Aharawan (Aaron's) yamanay (right) azan (ear), and on the bahan (thumb) of his yamanay (right) yad (hand), and on the bahan (great) toe of his yamanay (right) ragal (feet / foot).

He qarab (come close) Aharawan (Aaron's) ban (son); and Mashah (Moses) nathan (give) some of the dam (blood) on the thanawak (tip) of their yamanay (right) azan (ear), and on the bahan (thumb) of their yamanay (right) yad (hand), and on the bahan (great) toe of their yamanay (right) ragal (feet / foot); and Mashah (Moses) zaraq (sprinkled) the dam (blood) around on the mazabach (altar).

He laqach (take / seized) the chalab (fat), and the fat tail, and all the chalab (fat) that was on the innards, and the cover of the kabad (liver), and the shanayam (two) kalayah (kidneys), and their chalab (fat), and the yamayan (right hand) shawaq (thigh);

And out of the sal (basket) of unleavened lacham (bread), that panayam (was) before Yahawah, he laqach (take / seized) achad (one) unleavened chalah (cake), and one chalah (cake) of shaman (oiled) bread, and one raqayaq (wafer), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them on the chalab (fat), and on the yamayan (right hand) shawaq (thigh).
He nathan (give) all these in Aharawan (Aaron's) kap (hands) and in his ban (son)' kap (hands), and nawap (waved) them for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah.

Mashah (Moses) laqach (take / seized) them from their kap (hands), and qatar (burned) them on the mazabach (altar) on the burnt ilah (offering). They were a malaa (consecration) for a pleasant aroma. It was an ashah (wife/individual woman) made by fire to Yahawah.

Mashah (Moses) laqach (take / seized) the chazah (breast), and nawap (waved) it for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah. It was Mashah (Moses)' manah (portion) of the ayal (ram) of malaa (consecration), as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).

Mashah (Moses) laqach (take / seized) some of the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), and some of the dam (blood) which was on the mazabach (altar), and nazah (sprinkled) it on Aharawan (Aaron), on his bagad (garments), and on his ban (son), and on his ban (son)' bagad (garments) with him, and qadash (set apart/make holy) Aharawan (Aaron), his bagad (garments), and his ban (son), and his ban (son)' bagad (garments) with him.

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to Aharawan (Aaron) and to his ban (son), bashal (boil) the bashar (flesh) at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and there akal (eat) it and the lacham (bread) that is in the sal (basket) of malaa (consecration), as I tzawah (commanded), amar (spoke), ‘Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son) shall akal (eat) it.’
What yathar (remains) of the bashar (flesh) and of the lacham (bread) you shall sharap (burn) with ash (fire).

You shall not yatzaa (go out / come out) out from the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting shabai (seven) yawam (day), until the yawam (day) of your malaa (consecration) are malaa (fulfilled): for he shall malaa (consecrate) you shabai (seven) yawam (day).
What ishah (make) been done this yawam (day), so Yahawah has tzawah (commanded) to ishah (make), to make kapar (atonement) for you.

You shall stay at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting yawamam (by day) and layal (night) shabai (seven) yawamam (by day), and shamar (keep/guard) yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) command, that you don't mawath (death): for so I am tzawah (commanded).
Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son) ishah (make) all the things which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) by Mashah (Moses).
It happened on the shamayanay (eighth) yawam (day), that Mashah (Moses) qaraa (called) Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son), and the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel);

And he amar (spoke) to Aharawan (Aaron), laqach (take / seized) a igal (calf) from the herd for a chataah (sin) offering, and a ayal (ram) for a burnt ilah (offering), thamayam (complete / whole) blemish, and qarab (come close) them panayam (before) Yahawah.

You shall dabar (word / matter) to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), ‘laqach (take / seized) a male iz (goat) for a chataah (sin) offering; and a igal (calf) and a kabash (lamb), both a shanah (year) old, thamayam (complete / whole) blemish, for a burnt ilah (offering);

And a shawar (bull) and a ayal (ram) for shalam (peace) offerings, to zabach (sacrifice) panayam (before) Yahawah; and a meal manachah (offering) balal (mixed) with shaman (oil): for today Yahawah raah (see) to you.’

They laqach (take / seized) what Mashah (Moses) tzawah (commanded) panayam (before) the ahal (tent) of Meeting: and all the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) qarab (come close) near and imad (stood) panayam (before) Yahawah.
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke), This is the thing which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) that you should ishah (make): and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah shall raah (see) to you.

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to Aharawan (Aaron), qarab (come close) near to the mazabach (altar), and ishah (make) your chataah (sin) offering, and your burnt ilah (offering), and make kapar (atonement) for yourself, and for the im (people / nation); and ishah (make) the qaraban (offering) of the im (people / nation), and make kapar (atonement) for them; as Yahawah tzawah (commanded).
So Aharawan (Aaron) drew near to the mazabach (altar), and shachat (killed) the igal (calf) of the chataah (sin) offering, which was for himself.

The ban (son) of Aharawan (Aaron) qarab (come close) the dam (blood) to him; and he tabal (dipped) his atzabai (finger) in the dam (blood), and nathan (give) it on the qaran (horn) of the mazabach (altar), and yatzaq (poured) out the dam (blood) at the base of the mazabach (altar):

But the chalab (fat), and the kalayah (kidneys), and the cover from the kabad (liver) of the chataah (sin) offering, he qatar (burned) upon the mazabach (altar); as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).
The bashar (flesh) and the iwar (skin) he sharap (burned) with ash (fire) outside the machanah (camp).
He shachat (killed) the burnt ilah (offering); and Aharawan (Aaron's) ban (son) matzaa (delivered) the dam (blood) to him, and he zaraq (sprinkled) it around on the mazabach (altar).
They matzaa (delivered) the burnt ilah (offering) to him, nathach (piece) by piece, and the raash (head): and he qatar (burned) them upon the mazabach (altar).
He rachatz (washed) the innards and the karai (legs), and qatar (burned) them on the burnt ilah (offering) on the mazabach (altar).

He qarab (come close) the im (people / nation) qaraban (offering), and laqach (take / seized) the shaiyar (goat) of the chataah (sin) offering which was for the im (people / nation), and shachat (killed) it, and offered it for chataa (sin), like the raashawan (first).
He qarab (come close) the burnt ilah (offering), and ishah (make) it according to the mashapat (ordinance).

He qarab (come close) the meal manachah (offering), and malaa (filled) his kap (hand) from there, and qatar (burned) it upon the mazabach (altar), bad (besides) the burnt ilah (offering) of the baqar (morning).

He also shachat (killed) the shawar (bull) and the ayal (ram), the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings, which was for the im (people / nation): and Aharawan (Aaron's) ban (son) matzaa (delivered) to him the dam (blood), which he zaraq (sprinkled) around on the mazabach (altar),
And the chalab (fat) of the shawar (bull) and of the ayal (ram), the fat tail, and that which makasah (covers) the innards, and the kalayah (kidneys), and the cover of the kabad (liver):
And they shawam (place / establish / appoint) the chalab (fat) upon the chazah (breasts), and he qatar (burned) the chalab (fat) on the mazabach (altar):
And the chazah (breasts) and the yamayan (right hand) shawaq (thigh) Aharawan (Aaron) nawap (waved) for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah, as Mashah (Moses) tzawah (commanded).

Aharawan (Aaron) nashaa (lift) up his yad (hand) toward the im (people / nation), and barak (blessed) them; and he yarad (came) down from ishah (make) the chataah (sin) offering, and the burnt chataah (sin), and the shalam (peace) offerings.

Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) bawaa (come) into the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and barak (blessed) the im (people / nation): and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah raah (see) to all the im (people / nation).

There yatzaa (go out / come out) forth ash (fire) from panayam (before) Yahawah, and akal (eat) the burnt ilah (offering) and the chalab (fat) upon the mazabach (altar): and when all the im (people / nation) raah (see) it, they ranan (shouted), and napal (fall / be cast down) on their panayam (faces).

Nadab (Nadab) and Abayahawaa (Abihu), the ban (son) of Aharawan (Aaron), ayash (husband/individual man) laqach (take / seized) his machathah (censer), and nathan (give) ash (fire) in it, and nathan (give) qatarath (incense) on it, and qarab (come close) zawar (strange) ash (fire) panayam (before) Yahawah, which he had not tzawah (commanded) them.
And ash (fire) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from before Yahawah, and akal (eat) them, and they mawath (death) panayam (before) Yahawah.

Then Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to Aharawan (Aaron), "This is what Yahawah dabar (word / matter) of, amar (spoke), ‘I will show myself qadash (set apart/make holy) to those who come qarawab (near) me, and panayam (before) all the im (people / nation) I will be kabad (glorified).’" Aharawan (Aaron) held his damam (peace).

Mashah (Moses) qaraa (called) Mayashaal (Mishael) and Alayatzapan (Elzaphan), the ban (son) of Izayaal (Uzziel) the dawad (uncle) of Aharawan (Aaron), and amar (spoke) to them, qarab (come close) near, nashaa (lift) your ach (brother/kinsman) from panayam (before) the qadash (set apart/make holy) out of the machanah (camp).
So they qarab (come close) near, and nashaa (lift) them in their kathanath (coats) out of the machanah (camp), as Mashah (Moses) had dabar (word / matter).

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to Aharawan (Aaron), and to Alaizar (Eleazar) and to Ayathamar (Ithamar), his ban (son), "Don't let the hair of your raash (head) parai (go) loose, neither tear your clothes; that you don't mawath (death), and that he not be qatzap (angry) with all the idah (congregation): but let your ach (brother/kinsman), the whole bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), bakah (bewail) the sharapah (burning) which Yahawah has sharap (kindled).

You shall not yatzaa (go out / come out) out from the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, lest you mawath (death); for the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil) of Yahawah is on you." They ishah (make) according to the dabar (word / matter) of Mashah (Moses).
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Aharawan (Aaron), amar (spoke),

Shathah (drinks) no yayan (wine) nor strong shathah (drinks), you, nor your ban (son) with you, when you bawaa (come) into the ahal (tent) of Meeting, that you don't mawath (death): it shall be a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) throughout your dawar (generation / age / period):
And that you are to badal (separated) a distinction between the qadash (set apart/make holy) and the chal (common), and between the tamaa (unclean) and the tahawar (clean);
And that you are to yarah (teach) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) all the chaq (statute) which Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) to them by Mashah (Moses).

Mashah (Moses) dabar (word / matter) to Aharawan (Aaron), and to Alaizar (Eleazar) and to Ayathamar (Ithamar), his ban (son) who were yathar (left), laqach (take / seized) the meal manachah (offering) that yathar (remains) of the manachah (offerings) of Yahawah made by ashah (wife/individual woman), and akal (eat) it matzah (without) yeast beside the mazabach (altar); for it is most qadash (set apart/make holy);

And you shall akal (eat) it in a qadawash (holy) maqawam (place), because it is your chaq (statute), and your ban (son)' chaq (statute), of the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Yahawah made by ashah (wife/individual woman): for so I am tzawah (commanded).

The thanawapah (waved) chazah (breast) and the tharawamah (heaved) shawaq (thigh) you shall akal (eat) in a tahawar (clean) maqawam (place), you, and your ban (son), and your bath (daughter) with you: for they are given as your chaq (statute), and your ban (son)' chaq (statute), out of the zabach (sacrifices) of the shalam (peace) offerings of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel).

The tharawamah (heaved) shawaq (thigh) and the thanawapah (waved) chazah (breast) they shall bawaa (come) with the ashah (wife/individual woman) made by fire of the chalab (fat), to nawap (wave) it for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah: and it shall be yours, and your ban (son)' with you, as a chaq (statute) iwalam (forever); as Yahawah has tzawah (commanded).
