Mashah (Moses) darash (diligently) darash (inquired) about the shaiyar (goat) of the chataah (sin) offering, and, behold, it was sharap (burned): and he was qatzap (angry) with Alaizar (Eleazar) and with Ayathamar (Ithamar), the ban (son) of Aharawan (Aaron) who were yathar (left), amar (spoke),

Why haven't you akal (eat) the chataah (sin) offering in the maqawam (place) of the qadash (set apart/make holy), since it is most qadash (set apart/make holy), and he nathan (give) given it you to nashaa (lift) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the idah (congregation), to make kapar (atonement) for them panayam (before) Yahawah?

Han (behold), its dam (blood) was not bawaa (come) into the inner part of the qadash (set apart/make holy): you certainly should have akal (eat) it in the qadash (set apart/make holy), as I tzawah (commanded).

Aharawan (Aaron) dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), Behold, this yawam (day) they have qarab (come close) their chataah (sin) offering and their burnt chataah (sin) panayam (before) Yahawah; and such things as these have qaraa (called) to me: and if I had akal (eat) the chataah (sin) offering today, would it yatab (have) been pleasing in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah?
When Mashah (Moses) shamai (hearken / hear) that, it was yatab (pleasing) in his sight.
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses) and to Aharawan (Aaron), amar (spoke) to them,
Dabar (word / matter) to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), ‘These are the chay (life) things which you may akal (eat) among all the animals that are on the aratz (Earth/land).
Whatever paras (parts) the parasah (hoof), and is cloven-footed, and chews the garah (cud) among the animals, that you may akal (eat).

‘ak (nevertheless) these you shall not akal (eat) of those that chew the garah (cud), or of those who paras (part) the parasah (hoof): the gamal (camel), because he chews the garah (cud) but doesn't paras (have) a parted parasah (hoof), he is tamaa (unclean) to you.
The Shapan (coney), because he chews the garah (cud) but doesn't paras (have) a parted parasah (hoof), he is tamaa (unclean) to you.
The aranabath (hare), because she chews the garah (cud) but doesn't paras (part) the parasah (hoof), she is tamaa (unclean) to you.
The pig, because he paras (has) a split parasah (hoof), and is cloven-footed, but doesn't garar (chew) the garah (cud), he is tamaa (unclean) to you.
Of their bashar (flesh) you shall not akal (eat), and their carcasses you shall not nagai (touch); they are tamaa (unclean) to you.

‘These you may akal (eat) of all that are in the mayam (Waters): whatever has sanapayar (fins) and qashaqashath (scales) in the mayam (Waters), in the yam (sea/waters), and in the nachal (stream / river), that you may akal (eat).

All that don't have sanapayar (fins) and qashaqashath (scales) in the yam (sea/waters), and in the nachal (stream / river), of all that sharatz (move) in the mayam (Waters), and of all the chay (life) napash (living being/soul) that are in the mayam (Waters), they are an shaqatz (abomination) to you,
And you detest them. You shall not akal (eat) of their bashar (flesh), and you shall detest their carcasses.
Whatever has no sanapayar (fins) nor qashaqashath (scales) in the mayam (Waters), that is an shaqatz (abomination) to you.
‘These you shall shaqatz (detest) man (from) the iwap (flying); they shall not be akal (eat), they are an shaqatz (abomination): the nashar (eagle), and the vulture, and the black vulture,
And the red ayah (kite), any mayan (species) of black ayah (kite),
Any mayan (species) of irab (evening),
The horned bath (daughter), the screech owl, and the gull, any mayan (species) of natz (hawk),
The little kawas (owl), the shalak (cormorant), the great kawas (owl),
The white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
The chasayadah (stork), any mayan (species) of anapah (heron), the hoopoe, and the italap (bat).
‘All iwap (flying) insects that walk on all arabai (four) are an shaqatz (abomination) to you.

Yet you may akal (eat) these: of all winged sharatz (creeping) things that halak (move) on all arabai (four), which have karai (legs) mail (top/above) their ragal (feet / foot), with which to hop on the aratz (Earth/land).
Even of these you may akal (eat): any mayan (species) of arabah (locust), any mayan (species) of katydid, any mayan (species) of cricket, and any mayan (species) of grasshopper.
But all winged sharatz (creeping) things which have arabai (four) ragal (feet / foot), are an shaqatz (abomination) to you.
‘By these you will become tamaa (unclean): whoever touches their carcass shall be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).
Whoever nashaa (lift) any part of their carcass shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).
‘Every animal which paras (parts) the parasah (hoof), and is not shasai (cloven-footed), nor chews the garah (cud), is tamaa (unclean) to you. Everyone who touches them shall be tamaa (unclean).

Whatever halak (move) on its kap (paws), among all animals that halak (move) on all arabai (four), they are tamaa (unclean) to you. Whoever touches their carcass shall be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).
He who nashaa (lift) their carcass shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening). They are tamaa (unclean) to you.

‘These are they which are tamaa (unclean) to you among the sharatz (creeping) things that sharatz (swarm as many) on the aratz (Earth/land): the chalad (weasel), the rat, any mayan (species) of great lizard,
The gecko, and the monitor lizard, the wall lataah (lizard), the skink, and the chameleon.
These are they which are tamaa (unclean) to you among all that sharatz (creep). Whoever touches them when they are mawath (death), shall be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).

On whatever any of them napal (fall / be cast down) when they are mawath (death), it shall be tamaa (unclean); whether it is any kalay (vessel) of itz (wood), or bagad (clothing), or iwar (skin), or shaq (sack), whatever kalay (vessel) it is, with which any malaakah (work) is ishah (make), it must be bawaa (come) into mayam (Waters), and it shall be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening); then it will be clean.
Every charash (earthen) kalay (vessel), into which any of them napal (fall / be cast down), all that is in it shall be tamaa (unclean), and you shall shabar (break) it.

All akal (food) which may be akal (eat), that on which mayam (Waters) bawaa (come), shall be tamaa (unclean); and all mashaqah (drink) that may be shathah (drinks) in every such kalay (vessel) shall be tamaa (unclean).

Everything whereupon part of their carcass napal (fall / be cast down) shall be tamaa (unclean); whether thanawar (oven), or range for pots, it shall be broken in pieces: they are tamaa (unclean), and shall be tamaa (unclean) to you.
Nevertheless a spring or a cistern in which mayam (Waters) is a gathered shall be tahawar (clean): but that which touches their carcass shall be tamaa (unclean).
If part of their carcass napal (fall / be cast down) on any zarawai (sowing) zarai (seed) which is to be zarai (sown), it is tahawar (clean).
But if mayam (Waters) is nathan (give) on the zarai (seed), and part of their carcass napal (fall / be cast down) on it, it is tamaa (unclean) to you.
‘If any animal, of which you may akalah (eat), mawath (death); he who touches its carcass shall be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).

He who akal (eat) of its carcass shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening). He also who nashaa (lift) its carcass shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).
‘Every sharatz (creeping) thing that sharatz (swarm as many) on the aratz (Earth/land) is an shaqatz (abomination). It shall not be akal (eat).

Whatever halak (move) on its gachawan (belly), and whatever halak (move) on all arabai (four), or whatever has many ragal (feet / foot), even all sharatz (creeping) things that sharatz (swarm as many) on the aratz (Earth/land), them you shall not akal (eat); for they are an shaqatz (abomination).

You shall not shaqatz (make) yourselves shaqatz (abominable) with any sharatz (creeping) thing that sharatz (swarm as many), neither shall you make yourselves tamaa (unclean) with them, that you should be tamaa (defiled) thereby.

For I am Yahawah your Alahayam. Qadash (set apart/make holy) yourselves therefore, and be qadawash (holy); for I am qadawash (holy): neither shall you tamaa (defile) yourselves with any kind of sharatz (creeping) thing that moves on the aratz (Earth/land).
For I am Yahawah who ilah (go up / offer) you up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), to be your Alahayam. You shall therefore be qadawash (holy), for I am qadawash (holy).

‘This is the thawarah (instruction) of the animal, and of the iwap (flying), and of every chay (life) napash (living being/soul) that ramash (moves) in the mayam (Waters), and of every napash (living being/soul) that sharatz (swarm as many) on the aratz (Earth/land),
To badal (separated) a distinction between the tamaa (unclean) and the tahawar (clean), and between the chay (life) thing that may be akal (eat) and the chay (life) thing that may not be akal (eat).’
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

Dabar (word / matter) to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), ‘If a ashah (wife/individual woman) zarai (conceives), and yalad (birth / begot) a zakar (remembrance/memory) child, then she shall be tamaa (unclean) shabai (seven) yawam (day); as in the yawam (day) of her monthly period she shall be tamaa (unclean).
In the shamayanay (eighth) yawam (day) the bashar (flesh) of his iralah (foreskin) shall be mawal (circumcised).

She shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the dam (blood) of taharah (purification) shalawashayam (thirty)- shalawash (three) yawam (day). She shall not nagai (touch) any qadash (set apart/make holy) thing, nor bawaa (come) into the maqadash (sanctuary), until the yawam (day) of her purifying are completed.

But if she yalad (birth / begot) a naqabah (female) child, then she shall be tamaa (unclean) two shabawai (weeks), as in her period; and she shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the dam (blood) of taharah (purification) shashayam (sixty) - shash (six) yawam (day).

‘When the yawam (day) of her purification are completed, for a ban (son), or for a bath (daughter), she shall bawaa (come) to the kahan (priest) at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, a shanah (year) old kabash (lamb) for a burnt ilah (offering), and a ban (son) yawanah (pigeon), or a turtledove, for a chataah (sin) offering:

And he shall qarab (come close) it panayam (before) Yahawah, and make kapar (atonement) for her; and she shall be tahar (cleansed) from the maqawar (fountain) of her dam (blood). ‘This is the thawarah (instruction) for her who yalad (birth / begot), whether a zakar (remembrance/memory) or a naqabah (female).

If she cannot afford a shah (lamb), then she shall take shanayam (two) turtledoves, or shanayam (two) ban (son) yawanah (pigeons); the achad (one) for a burnt ilah (offering), and the other for a sin ilah (offering): and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for her, and she shall be tahar (clean).’
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses) and to Aharawan (Aaron), amar (spoke),

When a adam (man) shall have a shaath (rising) in his bashar (flesh) iwar (skin), or a sapachath (scab), or a baharath (bright) spot, and it becomes in the iwar (skin) of his bashar (flesh) the nagai (plague) of tzaraith (leprosy), then he shall be bawaa (come) to Aharawan (Aaron) the kahan (priest), or to achad (one) of his ban (son), the kahan (priest):

And the kahan (priest) shall examine the nagai (plague) in the iwar (skin) of the bashar (flesh): and if the shair (hair) in the nagai (plague) has hapak (turned) laban (white), and the maraah (appearance) of the nagai (plague) is deeper than the bashar (flesh) iwar (skin), it is the nagai (plague) of tzaraith (leprosy); and the kahan (priest) shall examine him, and pronounce him tamaa (unclean).

If the baharath (bright) spot is laban (white) in the iwar (skin) of his bashar (flesh), and its maraah (appearance) isn't deeper than the iwar (skin), and its shair (hair) hasn't hapak (turned) laban (white), then the kahan (priest) shall isolate the infected person for shabai (seven) yawam (day).

The kahan (priest) shall examine him on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), and, behold, if in his iyan (eye) the nagai (plague) is arrested, and the nagai (plague) hasn't pashah (spread) in the iwar (skin), then the kahan (priest) shall isolate him for shabai (seven) more yawam (day).

The kahan (priest) shall examine him again on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day); and behold, if the nagai (plague) has faded, and the nagai (plague) hasn't pashah (spread) in the iwar (skin), then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tahar (clean). It is a masapachath (scab). He shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and be tahar (clean).

But if the masapachath (scab) pashah (spreads) on the iwar (skin), achar (other) he raah (see) shown himself to the kahan (priest) for his taharah (cleansing), he shall show himself to the kahan (priest) again.
The kahan (priest) shall examine him; and raah (see), if the masapachath (scab) has spread on the iwar (skin), then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tamaa (unclean). It is tzaraith (leprosy).
When the nagai (plague) of tzaraith (leprosy) is in a adam (man), then he shall be bawaa (come) to the kahan (priest);

And the kahan (priest) shall examine him. Behold, if there is a laban (white) shaath (rising) in the iwar (skin), and it has hapak (turned) the shair (hair) laban (white), and there is chay (life) bashar (flesh) in the shaath (rising),
It is a chronic tzaraith (leprosy) in the iwar (skin) of his bashar (flesh), and the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tamaa (unclean). He shall not isolate him, for he is tamaa (unclean).

If the tzaraith (leprosy) parach (breaks) out all over the iwar (skin), and the tzaraith (leprosy) kasah (covers) all the iwar (skin) of the infected person from his raash (head) even to his ragal (feet / foot), as far as it appears to the kahan (priest);

Then the kahan (priest) shall examine him; and, behold, if the tzaraith (leprosy) has kasah (covered) all his bashar (flesh), he shall pronounce him tahar (clean) of the nagai (plague). It has all hapak (turned) laban (white): he is tahawar (clean).
But whenever chay (life) bashar (flesh) raah (see) in him, he shall be tamaa (unclean).
The kahan (priest) shall examine the chay (life) bashar (flesh), and pronounce him tamaa (unclean): the chay (life) bashar (flesh) is tamaa (unclean). It is tzaraith (leprosy).
Or if the chay (life) bashar (flesh) shawab (turn back / repent) again, and is hapak (changed) to laban (white), then he shall bawaa (come) to the kahan (priest);

And the kahan (priest) shall examine him; and, behold, if the nagai (plague) has hapak (turned) laban (white), then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tahar (clean) of the nagai (plague). He is tahar (clean).
When the bashar (flesh) has a shachayan (boil) on its iwar (skin), and it has rapaa (healed),

And in the maqawam (place) of the shachayan (boil) there is a laban (white) shaath (rising), or a baharath (bright) spot, adamadam (reddish) - laban (white), then it shall be shown to the kahan (priest);

And the kahan (priest) shall examine it; and behold, if its maraah (appearance) is lower than the iwar (skin), and its shair (hair) has hapak (turned) laban (white), then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tamaa (unclean). It is the nagai (plague) of tzaraith (leprosy). It has parach (broken) out in the shachayan (boil).

But if the kahan (priest) examines it, and behold, there are no laban (white) shair (hair) in it, and it isn't deeper than the iwar (skin), but is kahah (dim), then the kahan (priest) shall isolate him shabai (seven) yawam (day).
If it pashah (spreads) in the iwar (skin), then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tamaa (unclean). It is a nagai (plague).
But if the baharath (bright) spot imad (stays) in its place, and hasn't pashah (spread), it is the scar from the shachayan (boil); and the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tahar (clean).
Or when the bashar (flesh) has a makawah (burn) from ash (fire) on its iwar (skin), and the raw flesh of the makawah (burn) becomes a bright baharath (spot), reddish-white, or laban (white),

Then the kahan (priest) shall examine it; and behold, if the shair (hair) in the baharath (bright) spot has hapak (turned) laban (white), and its maraah (appearance) is deeper than the iwar (skin); it is tzaraith (leprosy). It has parach (broken) out in the makawah (burning), and the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tamaa (unclean). It is the nagai (plague) of tzaraith (leprosy).

But if the kahan (priest) examines it, and behold, there is no laban (white) shair (hair) in the baharath (bright) spot, and it isn't lower than the iwar (skin), but is faded; then the kahan (priest) shall isolate him shabai (seven) yawam (day).

The kahan (priest) shall examine him on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day). If it has pashah (spread) in the iwar (skin), then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tamaa (unclean). It is the nagai (plague) of tzaraith (leprosy).

If the baharath (bright) baharath (spot) imad (stays) in its place, and hasn't pashah (spread) in the iwar (skin), but is faded, it is the swelling from the makawah (burn), and the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tahar (clean); for it is the scar from the makawah (burn).
When a ayash (husband/individual man) or ashah (wife/individual woman) has a nagai (plague) on the raash (head) or on the zaqan (beard),

Then the kahan (priest) shall examine the nagai (plague); and raah (see), if its maraah (appearance) is deeper than the iwar (skin), and the shair (hair) in it is tzahab (yellow) and daq (thin), then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tamaa (unclean): it is an itch, it is tzaraith (leprosy) of the raash (head) or of the zaqan (beard).

If the kahan (priest) examines the nagai (plague) of itching, and behold, its maraah (appearance) isn't deeper than the iwar (skin), and there is no shachar (black) shair (hair) in it, then the kahan (priest) shall isolate him the person infected with itching shabai (seven) yawam (day).

On the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) the kahan (priest) shall examine the nagai (plague); and behold, if the itch hasn't pashah (spread), and there is no tzahab (yellow) shair (hair) in it, and the maraah (appearance) of the itch isn't deeper than the iwar (skin),
Then he shall be galach (shaved), but he shall not galach (shave) the itch; and the kahan (priest) shall sagar (shut) him up who has the itch shabai (seven) more yawam (day).

On the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), the kahan (priest) shall examine the itch; and behold, if the itch hasn't pashah (spread) in the iwar (skin), and its maraah (appearance) isn't deeper than the iwar (skin), then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tahar (clean). He shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and be tahar (clean).
But if the itch pashah (spreads) in the iwar (skin) achar (other) his taharah (cleansing),

Then the kahan (priest) shall examine him; and behold, if the itch has pashah (spread) in the iwar (skin), the kahan (priest) shall not look for the tzahab (yellow) shair (hair); he is tamaa (unclean).

But if in his iyan (eye) the itch is arrested, and shachar (black) shair (hair) has tzamach (grown) in it; the itch is rapaa (healed), he is tahawar (clean). The kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tahawar (clean).
When a ayash (husband/individual man) or a ashah (wife/individual woman) has baharath (bright) spots in the iwar (skin) of the bashar (flesh), even laban (white) baharath (bright) spots;

Then the kahan (priest) shall examine them; and behold, if the baharath (bright) spots on the iwar (skin) of their bashar (flesh) are a dull laban (white), it is a harmless rash, it has parach (broken) out in the iwar (skin); he is tahawar (clean).
If a ayash (husband/individual man) marat (hair) has fallen from his raash (head), he is qarach (bald). He is tahawar (clean).
If his marat (hair) has fallen off from the front part of his raash (head), he is gabach (forehead) bald. He is tahawar (clean).

But if there is in the bald qarachath (head), or the gabachath (bald) forehead, a adamadam (reddish) - laban (white) nagai (plague); it is tzaraith (leprosy) parach (breaking) out in his bald qarachath (head), or his gabachath (bald) forehead.

Then the kahan (priest) shall examine him; and, behold, if the shaath (rising) of the nagai (plague) is adamadam (reddish) - laban (white) in his bald qarachath (head), or in his gabachath (bald) forehead, like the maraah (appearance) of tzaraith (leprosy) in the iwar (skin) of the bashar (flesh),
He is a tzarai (leprous) ayash (husband/individual man). He is tamaa (unclean). The kahan (priest) shall surely tamaa (pronounce) him tamaa (unclean). His nagai (plague) is on his raash (head).

The tzarai (leper) in whom the nagai (plague) is shall wear torn clothes, and the hair of his raash (head) shall hang loose. He shall itah (cover) his upper shapam (lip), and shall qaraa (called), ‘tamaa (unclean)! Tamaa (unclean)!’

All the yawam (day) in which the nagai (plague) is in him he shall be tamaa (unclean). He is tamaa (unclean). He shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) badad (alone). Outside of the machanah (camp) shall be his mawashab (dwelling).
The bagad (garment) also that the nagai (plague) of tzaraith (leprosy) is in, whether it is a tzamar (wool) bagad (garment), or a pashathah (linen) bagad (garment);
Whether it is in shathay (warp), or irab (evening); of pashathah (linen), or of tzamar (wool); whether in a iwar (skin), or in anything made of iwar (skin);

If the nagai (plague) is yaraqaraq (greenish) or adamadam (reddish) in the bagad (garment), or in the iwar (skin), or in the shathay (warp), or in the irab (evening), or in anything made of iwar (skin); it is the nagai (plague) of tzaraith (leprosy), and shall be shown to the kahan (priest).
The kahan (priest) shall examine the nagai (plague), and isolate the nagai (plague) shabai (seven) yawam (day).

He shall examine the nagai (plague) on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day). If the nagai (plague) has pashah (spread) in the bagad (garment), either in the shathay (warp), or in the irab (evening), or in the iwar (skin), whatever use the iwar (skin) is used for, the nagai (plague) is a destructive mildew. It is tamaa (unclean).

He shall sharap (burn) the bagad (garment), whether the shathay (warp) or the irab (evening), in tzamar (wool) or in pashathah (linen), or anything of iwar (skin), in which the nagai (plague) is: for it is a destructive mildew. It shall be sharap (burned) in the ash (fire).

If the kahan (priest) examines it, and behold, the nagai (plague) hasn't pashah (spread) in the bagad (garment), aw (or) in the shathay (warp), or in the irab (evening), or in anything of iwar (skin);
Then the kahan (priest) shall tzawah (command) that they kabas (wash) the thing in which the nagai (plague) is, and he shall isolate it shabai (seven) more yawam (day).

Then the kahan (priest) shall examine it, achar (other) the nagai (plague) is kabas (washed); and behold, if the nagai (plague) hasn't hapak (changed) its color, and the nagai (plague) hasn't pashah (spread), it is tamaa (unclean); you shall sharap (burn) it in the ash (fire). It is a mildewed spot, whether the bareness is inside or outside.

If the kahan (priest) raah (see), and behold, the nagai (plague) has faded achar (other) it is kabas (washed), then he shall qarai (tear) it out of the bagad (garment), or out of the iwar (skin), or out of the shathay (warp), or out of the irab (evening):

And if it raah (see) again in the bagad (garment), either in the shathay (warp), or in the irab (evening), or in anything of iwar (skin), it is parach (spreading). You shall sharap (burn) with ash (fire) that in which the nagai (plague) is.

The bagad (garment), either the shathay (warp), or the irab (evening), or whatever thing of iwar (skin) it is, which you shall kabas (wash), if the nagai (plague) has sawar (departed) from them, then it shall be kabas (washed) the shanay (second) time, and it will be tahar (clean).

This is the thawarah (instruction) of the nagai (plague) of mildew in a bagad (garment) of tzamar (wool) or pashathah (linen), either in the shathay (warp), or the irab (evening), or in anything of iwar (skin), to pronounce it tahar (clean), or to pronounce it tamaa (unclean).
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),
This shall be the thawarah (instruction) of the tzarai (leper) in the yawam (day) of his taharah (cleansing). He shall be bawaa (come) to the kahan (priest),

And the kahan (priest) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the machanah (camp). The kahan (priest) shall examine him, and behold, if the nagai (plague) of tzaraith (leprosy) is rapaa (healed) in the tzarai (leper),

Then the kahan (priest) shall tzawah (command) them to laqach (take / seized) for him who is to be tahar (cleansed) shanayam (two) chay (life) tahawar (clean) tzapawar (birds), and araz (cedar) itz (wood), and shanay (second), and azawab (hyssop).
The kahan (priest) shall tzawah (command) them to shachat (kill) achad (one) of the tzapawar (birds) in an charash (earthen) kalay (vessel) over chay (life) mayam (Waters).

As for the chay (life) tzapawar (bird), he shall laqach (take / seized) it, and the araz (cedar) itz (wood), and the shanay (second), and the azawab (hyssop), and shall tabal (dip) them and the chay (life) tzapawar (bird) in the dam (blood) of the tzapawar (bird) that was shachat (killed) over the chay (life) mayam (Waters).

He shall nazah (sprinkle) on him who is to be tahar (cleansed) from the tzaraith (leprosy) shabai (seven) paim (times), and shall pronounce him tahar (clean), and shall let the chay (life) tzapawar (bird) shalach (send) into the panayam (open) shadah (field).

He who is to be tahar (cleansed) shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and galach (shave) off all his shair (hair), and rachatz (bathe) himself in mayam (Waters); and he shall be tahar (clean). Achar (other) that he shall bawaa (come) into the machanah (camp), but shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) outside his ahal (tent) shabai (seven) yawam (day).

It shall be on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), that he shall galach (shave) all his shair (hair) off his raash (head) and his zaqan (beard) and his eyebrows, even all his shair (hair) he shall galach (shave) off. He shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and he shall bathe his bashar (flesh) in mayam (Waters), then he shall be tahar (clean).

On the shamayanay (eighth) yawam (day) he shall laqach (take / seized) shanayam (two) male kabash (lambs) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish, and achad (one) ewe kabashah (lamb) a shanah (year) old thamayam (complete / whole) blemish, and shalawash (three) isharawan (tenths) of an ephah of fine salath (flour) for a meal manachah (offering), balal (mingled) with shaman (oil), and achad (one) lag (log) of shaman (oil).

The kahan (priest) who tahar (cleanses) him shall imad (set) the ayash (husband/individual man) who is to be tahar (cleansed), and those things, panayam (before) Yahawah, at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

The kahan (priest) shall laqach (take / seized) achad (one) of the male kabash (lambs), and qarab (come close) him for a asham (trespass) offering, with the lag (log) of shaman (oil), and nawap (wave) them for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah.

He shall shachat (kill) the male kabash (lamb) in the maqawam (place) where they shachat (kill) the chataah (sin) offering and the burnt ilah (offering), in the maqawam (place) of the qadash (set apart/make holy); for as the chataah (sin) offering is the kahan (priest), so is the asham (trespass) offering. It is most qadash (set apart/make holy).

The kahan (priest) shall laqach (take / seized) some of the dam (blood) of the asham (trespass) offering, and the kahan (priest) shall nathan (give) it on the thanawak (tip) of the yamanay (right) azan (ear) of him who is to be tahar (cleansed), and on the bahan (thumb) of his yamanay (right) yad (hand), and on the big bahan (toe) of his yamanay (right) ragal (feet / foot).
The kahan (priest) shall laqach (take / seized) some of the lag (log) of shaman (oil), and yatzaq (pour) it into the kap (palm) of his kahan (priest) shamaalay (left) hand.

The kahan (priest) shall tabal (dip) his yamanay (right) atzabai (finger) in the shaman (oil) that is in his shamaalay (left) kap (hand), and shall nazah (sprinkle) some of the shaman (oil) with his atzabai (finger) shabai (seven) paim (times) panayam (before) Yahawah.

The kahan (priest) shall nathan (give) some of the yathar (rest) of the shaman (oil) that is in his kap (hand) on the thanawak (tip) of the yamanay (right) azan (ear) of him who is to be tahar (cleansed), and on the bahan (thumb) of his yamanay (right) yad (hand), and on the big bahan (toe) of his yamanay (right) ragal (feet / foot), upon the dam (blood) of the asham (trespass) offering.

The yathar (rest) of the shaman (oil) that is in the kahan (priest) kap (hand) he shall nathan (give) on the raash (head) of him who is to be tahar (cleansed), and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him panayam (before) Yahawah.

The kahan (priest) shall ishah (make) the chataah (sin) offering, and make kapar (atonement) for him who is to be tahar (cleansed) because of his tamaah (uncleanness): and afterward he shall shachat (kill) the burnt ilah (offering);

And the kahan (priest) shall ilah (go up / offer) the burnt ilah (offering) and the meal manachah (offering) on the mazabach (altar). The kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him, and he shall be tahar (clean).

If he is dal (poor), and can't afford so much, then he shall laqach (take / seized) achad (one) male kabash (lamb) for a asham (trespass) offering to be thanawapah (waved), to make kapar (atonement) for him, and achad (one) isharawan (tenth) of an ephah of fine salath (flour) balal (mingled) with shaman (oil) for a meal manachah (offering), and a lag (log) of shaman (oil);

And shanayam (two) turtledoves, or shanayam (two) ban (son) yawanah (pigeons), such as he is yad (hand) to afford; and the achad (one) shall be a chataah (sin) offering, and the other a burnt ilah (offering).
On the shamayanay (eighth) yawam (day) he shall bawaa (come) them for his taharah (cleansing) to the kahan (priest), to the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, panayam (before) Yahawah.

The kahan (priest) shall laqach (take / seized) the kabash (lamb) of the asham (trespass) offering, and the lag (log) of shaman (oil), and the kahan (priest) shall nawap (wave) them for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah.

He shall shachat (kill) the kabash (lamb) of the asham (trespass) offering. The kahan (priest) shall laqach (take / seized) some of the dam (blood) of the asham (trespass) offering and nathan (give) it on the thanawak (tip) of the yamanay (right) azan (ear) of him who is to be tahar (cleansed), and on the bahan (thumb) of his yamanay (right) yad (hand), and on the big bahan (toe) of his yamanay (right) ragal (feet / foot).
The kahan (priest) shall yatzaq (pour) some of the shaman (oil) into the kap (palm) of his kahan (priest) shamaalay (left) hand;

And the kahan (priest) shall nazah (sprinkle) with his yamanay (right) atzabai (finger) some of the shaman (oil) that is in his shamaalay (left) kap (hand) shabai (seven) paim (times) panayam (before) Yahawah.

Then the kahan (priest) shall nathan (give) some of the shaman (oil) that is in his kap (hand) on the thanawak (tip) of the yamanay (right) azan (ear) of him who is to be tahar (cleansed), and on the bahan (thumb) of his yamanay (right) yad (hand), and on the big bahan (toe) of his yamanay (right) ragal (feet / foot), on the maqawam (place) of the dam (blood) of the asham (trespass) offering.

The yathar (rest) of the shaman (oil) that is in the kahan (priest) kap (hand) he shall nathan (give) on the raash (head) of him who is to be tahar (cleansed), to make kapar (atonement) for him panayam (before) Yahawah.
He shall ishah (make) achad (one) of the turtledoves, or of the ban (son) yawanah (pigeons), such as he is yad (hand) to afford,

Even such as he is nashag (able) to afford, the achad (one) for a chataah (sin) offering, and the other for a burnt ilah (offering), with the meal manachah (offering). The kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him who is to be tahar (cleansed) panayam (before) Yahawah.
This is the thawarah (instruction) for him in whom is the nagai (plague) of tzaraith (leprosy), who is not nashag (able) to afford the sacrifice for his taharah (cleansing).
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses) and to Aharawan (Aaron), amar (spoke),

When you bawaa (come) come into the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), which I nathan (give) to you for a achazah (possession), and I nathan (give) a spreading mildew in a bayath (house) in the aratz (Earth/land) of your achazah (possession),
Then he who owns the bayath (house) shall bawaa (come) and nagad (tell) the kahan (priest), amar (spoke), ‘There seems to me to be some sort of nagai (plague) in the bayath (house).’

The kahan (priest) shall tzawah (command) that they panah (empty) the bayath (house), before the kahan (priest) bawaa (come) in to examine the nagai (plague), that all that is in the bayath (house) not be made tamaa (unclean): and afterward the kahan (priest) shall bawaa (come) in to inspect the bayath (house).

He shall examine the nagai (plague); and behold, if the nagai (plague) is in the qayar (walls) of the bayath (house) with shaqairawarah (hollow) streaks, yaraqaraq (greenish) or adamadam (reddish), and it appears to be deeper than the qayar (wall);
Then the kahan (priest) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the bayath (house) to the pathach (door) of the bayath (house), and sagar (shut) up the bayath (house) shabai (seven) yawam (day).

The kahan (priest) shall shawab (turn back / repent) again on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), and raah (see). If the nagai (plague) has pashah (spread) in the qayar (walls) of the bayath (house),

Then the kahan (priest) shall tzawah (command) that they chalatz (take) out the aban (stone) in which is the nagai (plague), and shalak (cast) them into an tamaa (unclean) maqawam (place) outside of the iyar (city):

And he shall cause the bayath (house) of the bayath (house) to be qatzai (scraped) all over, and they shall shapak (pour) out the mortar, that they qatzah (end / extremity / border) off, outside of the iyar (city) into an tamaa (unclean) maqawam (place).

They shall laqach (take / seized) other aban (stone), and bawaa (come) them in the thachath (under) of those aban (stone); and he shall laqach (take / seized) other mortar, and shall plaster the bayath (house).

If the nagai (plague) shawab (turn back / repent) again, and parach (breaks) out in the bayath (house), achar (other) he has chalatz (taken) out the aban (stone), and achar (other) he has qatzah (end / extremity / border) the bayath (house), and achar (other) it was plastered;

Then the kahan (priest) shall bawaa (come) in and raah (see); and behold, if the nagai (plague) has pashah (spread) in the bayath (house), it is a destructive mildew in the bayath (house). It is tamaa (unclean).

He shall nathatz (break) down the bayath (house), its aban (stone), and its itz (timber), and all the bayath (house) mortar. He shall carry them out of the iyar (city) into an tamaa (unclean) maqawam (place).
Moreover he who bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) yawam (day) it is sagar (shut) up shall be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).
He who shakab (lies) down in the bayath (house) shall kabas (wash) his clothes; and he who akal (eat) in the bayath (house) shall kabas (wash) his clothes.

If the kahan (priest) shall bawaa (come) in, and examine it, and behold, the nagai (plague) hasn't pashah (spread) in the bayath (house), achar (other) the bayath (house) was plastered, then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce the bayath (house) tahar (clean), because the nagai (plague) is rapaa (healed).
To chataa (cleanse) the bayath (house) he shall laqach (take / seized) shanayam (two) tzapawar (birds), and araz (cedar) itz (wood), and shanay (second), and azawab (hyssop).
He shall shachat (kill) achad (one) of the tzapawar (birds) in an charash (earthen) kalay (vessel) over chay (life) mayam (Waters).

He shall laqach (take / seized) the araz (cedar) itz (wood), and the azawab (hyssop), and the shanay (second), and the chay (life) tzapawar (bird), and tabal (dip) them in the dam (blood) of the shachat (slain) tzapawar (bird), and in the chay (life) mayam (Waters), and nazah (sprinkle) the bayath (house) shabai (seven) paim (times).

He shall chataa (cleanse) the bayath (house) with the dam (blood) of the tzapawar (bird), and with the chay (life) mayam (Waters), with the chay (life) tzapawar (bird), with the araz (cedar) itz (wood), with the azawab (hyssop), and with the shanay (second);

But he shall let the chay (life) tzapawar (bird) shalach (send) out of the iyar (city) into the panayam (open) shadah (field). So shall he make kapar (atonement) for the bayath (house); and it shall be tahar (clean).
This is the thawarah (instruction) for any nagai (plague) of tzaraith (leprosy), and for an itch,
And for the destructive mildew of a bagad (garment), and for a bayath (house),
And for a shaath (rising), and for a sapachath (scab), and for a baharath (bright) spot;
To yarah (teach) when it is tamaa (unclean), and when it is tahawar (clean). This is the thawarah (instruction) of tzaraith (leprosy).
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses) and to Aharawan (Aaron), amar (spoke),

Dabar (word / matter) to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (spoke) them, ‘When any ayash (husband/individual man) zawab (flow) a discharge from his bashar (flesh), because of his discharge he is tamaa (unclean).

This shall be his tamaah (uncleanness) in his discharge: whether his bashar (flesh) rawar (runs) with his discharge, or his bashar (flesh) has chatham (stopped) from his discharge, it is his tamaah (uncleanness).
‘Every mashakab (bed) whereon he who zawab (flow) the discharge shakab (lies) shall be tamaa (unclean); and everything he yashab (inhabit/dwell) on shall be tamaa (unclean).
Ayash (husband/individual man) touches his mashakab (bed) shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (Waters), and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).

He who yashab (inhabit/dwell) on anything whereon the man who zawab (flow) the discharge yashab (inhabit/dwell) shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (Waters), and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).
‘He who touches the bashar (flesh) of him who zawab (flow) the discharge shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (Waters), and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).

‘If he who zawab (flow) the discharge raqaq (spits) on him who is tahawar (clean), then he shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (Waters), and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).
‘Whatever marakab (saddle) he who zawab (flow) the discharge rakab (rides) on shall be tamaa (unclean).

Whoever touches anything that was under him shall be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening). He who nashaa (lift) those things shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (Waters), and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).

‘Whoever he who zawab (flow) the discharge touches, without having shatap (rinsed) his yad (hand) in mayam (Waters), he shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (Waters), and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).
‘The earthen kalay (vessel), which he who zawab (flow) the discharge touches, shall be shabar (broken); and every kalay (vessel) of itz (wood) shall be shatap (rinsed) in mayam (Waters).

‘When he who zawab (flow) a discharge is tahar (cleansed) of his discharge, then he shall sapar (book) to himself shabai (seven) yawam (day) for his taharah (cleansing), and kabas (wash) his clothes; and he shall bathe his bashar (flesh) in chay (life) mayam (Waters), and shall be tahar (clean).

‘On the shamayanay (eighth) yawam (day) he shall laqach (take / seized) shanayam (two) turtledoves, or shanayam (two) ban (son) yawanah (pigeons), and bawaa (come) panayam (before) Yahawah to the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and nathan (give) them to the kahan (priest):

And the kahan (priest) shall ishah (make) them, the achad (one) for a chataah (sin) offering, and the other for a burnt ilah (offering). The kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him panayam (before) Yahawah for his discharge.

‘If any ayash (husband/individual man) yatzaa (go out / come out) an emission of semen, then he shall rachatz (bathe) all his bashar (flesh) in mayam (Waters), and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).
Every bagad (garment), and every iwar (skin), whereon the semen is, shall be kabas (washed) with mayam (Waters), and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).

If a ayash (husband/individual man) shakab (lies) with a ashah (wife/individual woman) and there is an emission of semen, they shall both rachatz (bathe) themselves in mayam (Waters), and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).

‘If a ashah (wife/individual woman) zawab (flow) a discharge, and her discharge in her bashar (flesh) is dam (blood), she shall be in her impurity shabai (seven) yawam (day): and whoever touches her shall be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).
‘Everything that she shakab (lies) on in her impurity shall be tamaa (unclean). Everything also that she yashab (inhabit/dwell) on shall be tamaa (unclean).
Whoever touches her mashakab (bed) shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (Waters), and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).
Whoever touches anything that she yashab (inhabit/dwell) on shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (Waters), and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).
If it is on the mashakab (bed), or on anything whereon she yashab (inhabit/dwell), when he touches it, he shall be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).

‘If any ayash (husband/individual man) shakab (lies) with her, and her monthly flow is on him, he shall be tamaa (unclean) shabai (seven) yawam (day); and every mashakab (bed) whereon he shakab (lies) shall be tamaa (unclean).

‘If a ashah (wife/individual woman) zawab (flow) a discharge of her dam (blood) many yawam (day) not in the ith (time) of her period, or if she zawab (flow) a discharge il (over) the time of her period; all the yawam (day) of the discharge of her tamaah (uncleanness) shall be as in the yawam (day) of her period: she is tamaa (unclean).

Every mashakab (bed) whereon she shakab (lies) all the yawam (day) of her discharge shall be to her as the mashakab (bed) of her period: and everything whereon she yashab (inhabit/dwell) shall be tamaa (unclean), as the tamaah (uncleanness) of her period.
Whoever touches these things shall be tamaa (unclean), and shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (Waters), and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).
‘But if she is tahar (cleansed) of her discharge, then she shall sapar (book) to herself shabai (seven) yawam (day), and achar (other) that she shall be tahar (clean).

On the shamayanay (eighth) yawam (day) she shall laqach (take / seized) shanayam (two) turtledoves, or shanayam (two) ban (son) yawanah (pigeons), and bawaa (come) them to the kahan (priest), to the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

The kahan (priest) shall ishah (make) the achad (one) for a chataah (sin) offering, and the other for a burnt chataah (sin); and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for her panayam (before) Yahawah for the tamaah (uncleanness) of her discharge.

‘Thus you shall nazar (crown / consecrate) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) from their tamaah (uncleanness), so they will not mawath (death) in their tamaah (uncleanness), when they tamaa (defile) my mashakan (tabernacle) that is in their thawak (midst).’
This is the thawarah (instruction) of him who zawab (flow) a discharge, and of him who yatzaa (go out / come out) an emission of semen, so that he is tamaa (unclean) thereby;
And of her who has her period, and of a zakar (remembrance/memory) or naqabah (woman) who zawab (flow) a discharge, and of him who shakab (lies) with her who is tamaa (unclean).

Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), achar (other) the mawath (death) of the shanayam (two) ban (son) of Aharawan (Aaron), when they qarab (come close) near panayam (before) Yahawah, and mawath (death);

And Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), dabar (word / matter) Aharawan (Aaron) your ach (brother/kinsman), not to bawaa (come) at all ith (times) into the Most qadash (set apart/make holy) bayath (house) within the parakath (veil), panayam (before) the kaparath (mercy) seat which is on the arawan (ark); lest he mawath (death): for I will raah (see) in the inan (cloud) on the kaparath (mercy) seat.
Herewith shall Aharawan (Aaron) bawaa (come) into the qadash (set apart/make holy): with a ban (son) par (bull) for a chataah (sin) offering, and a ayal (ram) for a burnt chataah (sin).

He shall labash (put) on the qadash (set apart/make holy) bad (linen) kathanath (coat), and he shall have the bad (linen) breeches on his bashar (flesh), and shall chagar (put) on the bad (linen) sash, and he shall be clothed with the bad (linen) turban. They are the qadash (set apart/make holy) bagad (garments). He shall rachatz (bathe) his bashar (flesh) in mayam (Waters), and labash (put) them on.

He shall laqach (take / seized) from the idah (congregation) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) shanayam (two) male iz (goats) for a chataah (sin) offering, and achad (one) ayal (ram) for a burnt chataah (sin).
Aharawan (Aaron) shall qarab (come close) the par (bull) of the chataah (sin) offering, which is for himself, and make kapar (atonement) for himself and for his bayath (house).
He shall laqach (take / seized) the shanayam (two) shaiyar (goats), and imad (set) them panayam (before) Yahawah at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
Aharawan (Aaron) shall nathan (give) gawaral (lots) for the shanayam (two) shaiyar (goats); achad (one) gawaral (lot) for Yahawah, and the other gawaral (lot) for the Izaazal (scapegoat).
Aharawan (Aaron) shall qarab (come close) the shaiyar (goat) on which the gawaral (lot) ilah (go up / offer) for Yahawah, and ishah (make) him for a chataah (sin) offering.

But the shaiyar (goat), on which the gawaral (lot) ilah (go up / offer) for the Izaazal (scapegoat), shall be imad (presented) chay (life) panayam (before) Yahawah, to make kapar (atonement) for him, to shalach (send) him away for the Izaazal (scapegoat) into the madabar (wilderness).

Aharawan (Aaron) shall qarab (come close) the par (bull) of the chataah (sin) offering, which is for himself, and shall make kapar (atonement) for himself and for his bayath (house), and shall shachat (kill) the par (bull) of the chataah (sin) offering which is for himself.

He shall laqach (take / seized) a machathah (censer) malaa (full) of gachal (coals) of ash (fire) from off the mazabach (altar) panayam (before) Yahawah, and chapan (two) handfuls of sam (sweet) qatarath (incense) beaten daq (small), and bawaa (come) it bayath (house) the parakath (veil):

And he shall nathan (give) the qatarath (incense) on the ash (fire) panayam (before) Yahawah, that the inan (cloud) of the qatarath (incense) may kasah (cover) the kaparath (mercy) seat that is on the idawath (testimony), so that he will not mawath (death).

He shall laqach (take / seized) some of the dam (blood) of the par (bull), and nazah (sprinkle) it with his atzabai (finger) on the kaparath (mercy) seat on the qadam (east); and panayam (before) the kaparath (mercy) seat he shall nazah (sprinkle) some of the dam (blood) with his atzabai (finger) shabai (seven) paim (times).

Then he shall shachat (kill) the shaiyar (goat) of the chataah (sin) offering, that is for the im (people / nation), and bawaa (come) his dam (blood) bayath (house) the parakath (veil), and ishah (make) with his dam (blood) as he ishah (make) with the dam (blood) of the par (bull), and nazah (sprinkle) it on the kaparath (mercy) seat, and panayam (before) the kaparath (mercy) seat:

And he shall make kapar (atonement) for the qadash (set apart/make holy) Place, because of the tamaah (uncleanness) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), and because of their pashai (transgressions), even all their chataah (sin); and so he shall ishah (make) for the ahal (tent) of Meeting, that shakan (dwells) with them in the thawak (midst) of their tamaah (uncleanness).

No adam (one) shall be in the ahal (tent) of Meeting when he bawaa (come) to make kapar (atonement) in the qadash (set apart/make holy) Place, until he yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and has made kapar (atonement) for himself and for his bayath (house), and for all the qahal (assembly) of Yasharaal (Israel).

He shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out to the mazabach (altar) that is panayam (before) Yahawah and make kapar (atonement) for it, and shall laqach (take / seized) some of the par (bull's) dam (blood), and some of the shaiyar (goat's) dam (blood), and nathan (give) it around on the qaran (horn) of the mazabach (altar).

He shall nazah (sprinkle) some of the dam (blood) on it with his atzabai (finger) shabai (seven) paim (times), and tahar (cleanse) it, and make it qadash (set apart/make holy) from the tamaah (uncleanness) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel).

When he kalah (complete / finish) made an end of atoning for the qadash (set apart/make holy) Place, the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and the mazabach (altar), he shall qarab (come close) the chay (life) shaiyar (goat).

Aharawan (Aaron) shall samak (lay) shanayam (two) his yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the chay (life) shaiyar (goat), and yadah (confess) over him all the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), and all their pashai (transgressions), even all their chataah (sin); and he shall nathan (give) them on the raash (head) of the shaiyar (goat), and shall shalach (send) him away into the madabar (wilderness) by the yad (hand) of a ayash (husband/individual man) who is in readiness.
The shaiyar (goat) shall nashaa (lift) all their iwan (guilt/iniquity) on himself to a solitary aratz (Earth/land), and he shall let the shaiyar (goat) shalach (send) in the madabar (wilderness).

Aharawan (Aaron) shall bawaa (come) into the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and shall take off the bad (linen) bagad (garments), which he labash (put) on when he bawaa (come) into the qadash (set apart/make holy) yanach (place), and shall leave them there.

Then he shall rachatz (bathe) himself in mayam (Waters) in a qadawash (holy) maqawam (place), and labash (put) on his bagad (garments), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out and ishah (make) his burnt ilah (offering) and the burnt ilah (offering) of the im (people / nation), and make kapar (atonement) for himself and for the im (people / nation).
The chalab (fat) of the chataah (sin) offering he shall qatar (burn) on the mazabach (altar).

He who lets the shaiyar (goat) shalach (send) for the Izaazal (scapegoat) shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and bathe his bashar (flesh) in mayam (Waters), and afterward he shall bawaa (come) into the machanah (camp).

The par (bull) for the chataah (sin) offering, and the shaiyar (goat) for the chataah (sin) offering, whose dam (blood) was bawaa (come) in to make kapar (atonement) in the qadash (set apart/make holy) Place, shall be yatzaa (go out / come out) forth outside the machanah (camp); and they shall sharap (burn) their iwar (skins), their bashar (flesh), and their parash (dung) with ash (fire).
He who sharap (burns) them shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and bathe his bashar (flesh) in mayam (Waters), and afterward he shall bawaa (come) into the machanah (camp).

It shall be a chaqah (statute) to you iwalam (forever): in the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month), on the ishawar (tenth) day of the chadash (month), you shall inah (oppress / afflict) your napash (living being/soul), and shall ishah (make) no kind of malaakah (work), the native-born, or the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who lives as a foreigner thawak (midst) you:
For on this yawam (day) shall kapar (atonement) be tahar (made) for you, to cleanse you; from all your chataah (sin) you shall be tahar (clean) panayam (before) Yahawah.
It is a shabath (shabath/rest) of solemn shabathawan (rest) to you, and you shall inah (oppress / afflict) your napash (living being/soul); it is a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever).

The kahan (priest), who is mashach (anointed) and who is malaa (consecrated) to be kahan (priest) in his ab (father) place, shall make the kapar (atonement), and shall labash (put) on the bad (linen) bagad (garments), even the qadash (set apart/make holy) bagad (garments).

Then he shall make kapar (atonement) for the qadash (set apart/make holy) maqadash (sanctuary); and he shall make kapar (atonement) for the ahal (tent) of Meeting and for the mazabach (altar); and he shall make kapar (atonement) for the kahan (priest) and for all the im (people / nation) of the qahal (assembly).

"This shall be an iwalam (forever) chaqah (statute) for you, to make kapar (atonement) for the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) achad (one) in the shanah (year) because of all their chataah (sin)." It was ishah (make) as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),
Dabar (word / matter) to Aharawan (Aaron), and to his ban (son), and to all the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (spoke) to them: ‘This is the thing which Yahawah has tzawah (commanded),

Whatever ayash (husband/individual man) there is of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), who shachat (kills) a shawar (bull), or kashab (lamb), or iz (goat), in the machanah (camp), or who shachat (kills) it outside the machanah (camp),

And hasn't bawaa (come) it to the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, to qarab (come close) it as an qaraban (offering) to Yahawah panayam (before) the mashakan (tabernacle) of Yahawah: dam (blood) shall be chashab (imputed) to that ayash (husband/individual man). He has shapak (shed) dam (blood); and that ayash (husband/individual man) shall be karath (cut) off from qarab (among / near) his im (people / nation).

This is to the end that the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) may bawaa (come) their zabach (sacrifices), which they zabach (sacrifice) in the panayam (open) shadah (field), that they may bawaa (come) them to Yahawah, to the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, to the kahan (priest), and zabach (sacrifice) them for sacrifices of shalam (peace) zabach (offerings) to Yahawah.

The kahan (priest) shall zaraq (sprinkle) the dam (blood) on the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and qatar (burn) the chalab (fat) for a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.

They shall no more zabach (sacrifice) their zabach (sacrifices) to the shaiyar (goat) idols, achar (other) which they zanah (play) the prostitute. This shall be a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) to them throughout their dawar (generation / age / period).’

You shall amar (spoke) to them, ‘Any ayash (husband/individual man) there is of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), or of the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who live as foreigners thawak (midst) them, who ilah (go up / offer) a burnt ilah (offering) or zabach (sacrifice),

And doesn't bawaa (come) it to the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, to ishah (make) it to Yahawah; that ayash (husband/individual man) shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people / nation).

‘Any ayash (husband/individual man) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), or of the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who live as foreigners thawak (midst) them, who akal (eat) any kind of dam (blood), I will nathan (give) my panayam (face) against that napash (living being/soul) who akal (eat) dam (blood), and will karath (cut) him off from qarab (among / near) his im (people / nation).

For the napash (living being/soul) of the bashar (flesh) is in the dam (blood); and I nathan (give) given it to you on the mazabach (altar) to make kapar (atonement) for your napash (living being/soul): for it is the dam (blood) that makes kapar (atonement) by reason of the napash (living being/soul).

Therefore I have amar (spoke) to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), No napash (living being/soul) among you shall akal (eat) dam (blood), neither shall any gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who lives as a foreigner thawak (midst) you akal (eat) dam (blood).

‘Whatever ayash (husband/individual man) there is of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), or of the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who live as foreigners thawak (midst) them, who takes in tzawad (hunting) any animal or iwap (flying) that may be akal (eat); he shall shapak (pour) out its dam (blood), and kasah (cover) it with ipar (dust).

For as to the napash (living being/soul) of all bashar (flesh), its dam (blood) is with its napash (living being/soul): therefore I amar (spoke) to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), You shall not akal (eat) the dam (blood) of any bashar (flesh) of flesh; for the napash (living being/soul) of all bashar (flesh) is its dam (blood). Whoever akal (eat) it shall be karath (cut) off.

‘Every napash (living being/soul) that akal (eat) what dies of itself, or that which is tarapah (torn) by animals, whether he is native-born or a foreigner, he shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (Waters), and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening): then he shall be tahar (clean).
But if he doesn't kabas (wash) them, or rachatz (bathe) his bashar (flesh), then he shall nashaa (lift) his iwan (guilt/iniquity).’
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses),
Dabar (word / matter) to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (spoke) to them, ‘I am Yahawah your Alahayam.

You shall not ishah (make) as they maishah (do) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), where you lived: and you shall not ishah (make) as they ishah (make) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), where I am bawaa (come) you; neither shall you yalak (walk) in their chaqah (statutes).
You shall ishah (make) my mashapat (ordinances), and you shall shamar (keep/guard) my chaqah (statutes), and yalak (walk) in them: I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
You shall therefore shamar (keep/guard) my chaqah (statutes) and my mashapat (ordinances); which if a adam (man) ishah (make), he shall chayay (life) in them: I am Yahawah.
‘None of you shall qarab (come close) anyone who are his close relatives, to galah (uncover) their irawah (nakedness): I am Yahawah.

‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your ab (father), nor the irawah (nakedness) of your am (mother): she is your am (mother). You shall not galah (uncover) her irawah (nakedness).
‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your ab (father) ashah (wife/individual woman): it is your ab (father) irawah (nakedness).

‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your achawath (sister), the bath (daughter) of your ab (father), or the bath (daughter) of your am (mother), whether mawaladath (kindred / native land) at bayath (house), or mawaladath (kindred / native land) chawatz (abroad).

‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your ban (son) bath (daughter), or of your bath (daughter) bath (daughter), even their irawah (nakedness): for theirs is your own irawah (nakedness).
‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your ab (father) ashah (wife/individual woman) bath (daughter), conceived by your ab (father), since she is your achawath (sister).
‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your ab (father) achawath (sister): she is your ab (father) shaar (near) kinswoman.
‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your am (mother) achawath (sister): for she is your am (mother) shaar (near) kinswoman.
‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your ab (father) ach (brother/kinsman), you shall not qarab (come close) his ashah (wife/individual woman): she is your dawadah (aunt).
‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your daughter-in-law: she is your ban (son) ashah (wife/individual woman). You shall not galah (uncover) her irawah (nakedness).
‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your ach (brother/kinsman) ashah (wife/individual woman): it is your ach (brother/kinsman) irawah (nakedness).

‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of a ashah (wife/individual woman) and her bath (daughter). You shall not laqach (take / seized) her ban (son) bath (daughter), or her bath (daughter) bath (daughter), to galah (uncover) her irawah (nakedness); they are shaarah (near) kinswomen: it is zamah (wickedness).
‘You shall not laqach (take / seized) a ashah (wife/individual woman) to her achawath (sister), to be a rival, to galah (uncover) her irawah (nakedness), while her sister is yet chay (life).
‘You shall not qarab (come close) a ashah (wife/individual woman) to galah (uncover) her irawah (nakedness), as long as she is impure by her tamaah (uncleanness).
‘You shall not shakabath (lie) zarai (carnally) with your neighbor's ashah (wife/individual woman), and tamaa (defile) yourself with her.
‘You shall not give any of your zarai (children) to ibar (pass over/through) to Malak (Molech); neither shall you chalal (profane) the sham (name) of your Alahayam: I am Yahawah.
‘You shall not shakab (lie) with a zakar (remembrance/memory), as with a ashah (wife/individual woman). That is detestable.

‘You shall not shakabath (lie) with any animal to tamaa (defile) yourself with it; neither shall any ashah (wife/individual woman) give herself to an animal, to rabai (fourth) down with it: it is a perversion.
‘Don't tamaa (defile) yourselves in any of these things: for in all these the gaway (nation / people) which I am shalach (send) out panayam (before) you were tamaa (defiled).
The aratz (Earth/land) was tamaa (defiled): therefore I paqad (visit) its iwan (guilt/iniquity), and the aratz (Earth/land) qawaa (vomited) out her yashab (inhabit/dwell).

You therefore shall shamar (keep/guard) my chaqah (statutes) and my mashapat (ordinances), and shall not ishah (make) any of these thawaibah (abominations); neither the native-born, nor the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who lives as a foreigner thawak (midst) you;
(For all these thawaibah (abominations) have the ishah (make) of the aratz (Earth/land) ishah (make), that were panayam (before) you, and the aratz (Earth/land) became tamaa (defiled));
That the aratz (Earth/land) not qawaa (vomit) you out also, when you tamaa (defile) it, as it qawaa (vomited) out the gaway (nation / people) that panayam (was) before you.

‘For whoever shall ishah (make) any of these thawaibah (abominations), even the napash (living being/soul) that ishah (make) them shall be karath (cut) off from qarab (among / near) their im (people / nation).

Therefore you shall shamar (keep/guard) my requirements, that you ishah (make) not practice any of these thawaibah (abominable) chaqah (customs), which were practiced panayam (before) you, and that you do not tamaa (defile) yourselves with them: I am Yahawah your Alahayam.’
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),
Dabar (word / matter) to all the idah (congregation) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (spoke) them, ‘You shall be qadawash (holy); for I Yahawah your Alahayam am qadawash (holy).
‘ayash (husband/individual man) one of you shall respect his am (mother) and his ab (father). You shall shamar (keep/guard) my shabath (shabath/rest). I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
‘Don't panah (turn) to alayal (idols), nor ishah (make) masakah (molten) Alahayam for yourselves. I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
‘When you zabach (offer) a zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings to Yahawah, you shall zabach (offer) it so that you may be accepted.

It shall be akal (eat) the same yawam (day) you zabach (offer) it, and on the next macharath (day): and if anything yathar (remains) until the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), it shall be sharap (burned) with ash (fire).
If it is akal (eat) at akal (eat) on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), it is an pagawal (abomination). It will not be ratzah (accepted);

But everyone who akal (eat) it shall nashaa (lift) his iwan (guilt/iniquity), because he has chalal (profaned) the qadash (set apart/make holy) thing of Yahawah, and that napash (living being/soul) shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people / nation).

‘When you qatzar (reap) the qatzayar (harvest) of your aratz (Earth/land), you shall not kalah (complete / finish) reap the paah (corners) of your shadah (field), neither shall you laqat (gather) the laqat (gleanings) of your qatzayar (harvest).

You shall not ilal (glean) your karam (vineyard), neither shall you laqat (gather) the fallen parat (grapes) of your karam (vineyard); you shall izab (leave) them for the inay (poor) and for the foreigner. I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
‘You shall not ganab (steal). ‘You shall not shaqar (lie). ‘You shall not deceive ayash (husband/individual man) imayath (another).
‘You shall not shabai (swear / take oath) by my sham (name) falsely, and chalal (profane) the sham (name) of your Alahayam. I am Yahawah.
‘You shall not ishaq (oppress) your neighbor, nor gazal (rob) him. ‘The pailah (wages) of a shakayar (hired) servant shall not lawan (remain) with you all night until the baqar (morning).

‘You shall not qalal (curse) the charash (deaf), nor nathan (give) a makashawal (stumbling) block panayam (before) the iwar (blind); but you shall yaraa (fear / be afraid) your Alahayam. I am Yahawah.

‘You shall ishah (make) no injustice in mashapat (judgment): you shall not be partial to the dal (poor), nor show favoritism to the gadawal (very great/important/mighty); but you shall shapat (judge) your neighbor in tzadaq (righteous / just / fair).
‘You shall not yalak (go) up and down as a slanderer among your im (people / nation). ‘You shall not endanger the dam (life) of your neighbor. I am Yahawah.
‘You shall not shanaa (hate) your ach (brother/kinsman) in your labab (heart). You shall yakach (surely) yakach (rebuke) your neighbor, and not nashaa (lift) chataa (sin) because of him.
‘You shall not naqam (take) vengeance, nor natar (bear) any grudge against the ban (son) of your im (people / nation); but you shall ahab (love) your neighbor as yourself. I am Yahawah.

‘You shall shamar (keep/guard) my chaqah (statutes). ‘You shall not crossbreed different kinds of animals. ‘you shall not zarai (sow) your shadah (field) with two kinds of kalaayam (seed); ‘neither shall there ilah (go up / offer) upon on you a bagad (garment) made of kalaayam (two) kinds of material.

‘If a ayash (husband/individual man) shakab (lies) zarai (carnally) with a ashah (wife/individual woman) who is a shapachah (slave) girl, pledged to be married to another ayash (husband/individual man), and not padah (ransomed), or nathan (give) her chapashah (freedom); they shall be punished. They shall not be put to mawath (death), because she was not chapash (free).
He shall bawaa (come) his asham (trespass) offering to Yahawah, to the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, even a ayal (ram) for a asham (trespass) offering.

The kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him with the ayal (ram) of the asham (trespass) offering panayam (before) Yahawah for his chataah (sin) which he has chataa (committed): and the chataah (sin) which he has chataa (committed) shall be salach (forgive/pardon/make clean) him.

‘When you bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land), and have natai (planted) all kinds of itz (trees) for maakal (food), then you shall iral (count) their paray (fruit) as forbidden. Shalawash (three) shanah (years) shall they be forbidden to you. It shall not be akal (eat).
But in the rabayaiy (fourth) shanah (year) all its paray (fruit) shall be qadash (set apart/make holy), for giving halawal (praise) to Yahawah.
In the chamayashay (fifth) shanah (year) you shall akal (eat) its paray (fruit), that it may yasap (yield) its thabawaah (increase) to you. I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
‘You shall not akal (eat) any meat with the dam (blood) still in it; neither shall you use nachash (enchantments), nor practice sorcery.
‘You shall not naqap (cut) the hair on the paah (sides) of your raash (head), neither shall you clip off the edge of your zaqan (beard).
‘You shall not nathan (give) any sharat (cuttings) in your bashar (flesh) for the napash (living being/soul), nor tattoo any qaiqai (marks) on you. I am Yahawah.

‘Don't chalal (profane) your bath (daughter), to make her a chalal (prostitute); lest the aratz (Earth/land) zanah (fall) to prostitution, and the aratz (Earth/land) malaa (become) full of zamah (wickedness).
‘You shall shamar (keep/guard) my shabath (shabath/rest), and yaraa (fear / be afraid) my maqadash (sanctuary); I am Yahawah.
‘Don't panah (turn) to those who are mediums, nor to the yadainay (wizards). Don't baqash (seek) them out, to be tamaa (defiled) by them. I am Yahawah your Alahayam.

‘You shall qawam (rise up) up panayam (before) the gray shayabah (old age / white hair (due to age)), and honor the panayam (face) of an old zaqan (man), and you shall yaraa (fear / be afraid) your Alahayam. I am Yahawah.
‘If a gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) lives as a foreigner with you in your aratz (Earth/land), you shall not yanah (do) him wrong.

The gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who lives as a foreigner with you shall be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall ahab (love) him as yourself; for you lived as foreigners in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt). I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
‘You shall ishah (make) no iwal (unrighteousness) in mashapat (judgment), in mashawarah (measures) of length, of mashaqal (weight), or of quantity.

You shall have tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) maazan (balances), tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) aban (stone), a tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) ayapah (ephah), and a tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) hayan (hin). I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who yatzaa (go out / come out) you out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
‘You shall shamar (keep/guard) all my chaqah (statutes), and all my mashapat (ordinances), and ishah (make) them. I am Yahawah.’
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

Moreover, you shall amar (spoke) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘Anyone of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), or of the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who live as foreigners in Yasharaal (Israel), who nathan (give) any of his zarai (seed) to Malak (Molech); he shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death). The im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land) shall ragam (stone) him with ragam (stones).

I also will nathan (give) my panayam (face) against that ayash (husband/individual man), and will karath (cut) him off from qarab (among / near) his im (people / nation) because he nathan (give) given of his zarai (seed) to Malak (Molech), to tamaa (defile) my maqadash (sanctuary), and to chalal (profane) my qadash (set apart/make holy) sham (name).

If the im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land) all ilam (hide) their iyan (eye) from that ayash (husband/individual man), when he nathan (give) of his zarai (seed) to Malak (Molech), and don't put him to mawath (death);

Then I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) my panayam (face) against that ayash (husband/individual man), and against his mashapachah (tribe/clan/family), and will karath (cut) him off, and all who zanah (play) the prostitute achar (other) him, to zanah (play) the prostitute with Malak (Molech), from qarab (among / near) their im (people / nation).

‘The napash (living being/soul) that panah (turns) to those who are mediums, and to the yadainay (wizards), to zanah (play) the prostitute achar (other) them, I will even nathan (give) my panayam (face) against that napash (living being/soul), and will karath (cut) him off from qarab (among / near) his im (people / nation).
‘qadash (set apart/make holy) yourselves therefore, and be qadawash (holy); for I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
You shall shamar (keep/guard) my chaqah (statutes), and ishah (make) them. I am Yahawah who qadash (set apart/make holy) you.

‘For everyone who qalal (curses) his ab (father) or his am (mother) shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death): he has qalal (cursed) his ab (father) or his am (mother); his dam (blood) shall be upon him.

‘The ayash (husband/individual man) who naap (commits) adultery with another ayash (husband/individual man) ashah (wife/individual woman), even he who naap (commits) adultery with his neighbor's ashah (wife/individual woman), the naap (adulterer) and the naap (adulteress) shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death).

‘The ayash (husband/individual man) who shakab (lies) with his ab (father) ashah (wife/individual woman) has galah (uncovered) his ab (father) irawah (nakedness): shanayam (two) of them shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death); their dam (blood) shall be upon them.

‘If a ayash (husband/individual man) shakab (lies) with his kalah (complete / finish), shanayam (two) of them shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death): they ishah (make) committed a perversion; their dam (blood) shall be upon them.

‘If a ayash (husband/individual man) shakab (lies) with a zakar (remembrance/memory), as with a ashah (wife/individual woman), shanayam (two) of them ishah (make) committed an thawaibah (abomination): they shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death); their dam (blood) shall be upon them.

‘If a ayash (husband/individual man) laqach (take / seized) a ashah (wife/individual woman) and her am (mother), it is zamah (wickedness): they shall be sharap (burned) with ash (fire), both he and they; that there may be no zamah (wickedness) thawak (midst) you.
‘If a ayash (husband/individual man) nathan (give) with an animal, he shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death); and you shall harag (kill) the animal.

‘If a ashah (wife/individual woman) approaches any animal, and rabai (fourth) down with it, you shall harag (kill) the ashah (wife/individual woman), and the animal: they shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death); their dam (blood) shall be upon them.

‘If a ayash (husband/individual man) laqach (take / seized) his achawath (sister), his ab (father) bath (daughter), or his am (mother) bath (daughter), and raah (see) her irawah (nakedness), and she raah (see) his irawah (nakedness); it is a shameful thing; and they shall be karath (cut) off in the iyan (eye) of the children of their im (people / nation): he has galah (uncovered) his achawath (sister's) irawah (nakedness); he shall nashaa (lift) his iwan (guilt/iniquity).

‘If a ayash (husband/individual man) shakab (lies) with a ashah (wife/individual woman) dawah (having) her monthly period, and galah (uncovers) her irawah (nakedness); he has irah (made) naked her maqawar (fountain), and she has irah (uncovered) the maqawar (fountain) of her dam (blood): and shanayam (two) of them shall be karath (cut) off from qarab (among / near) their im (people / nation).

‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your am (mother) achawath (sister), nor of your ab (father) achawath (sister); for he has irah (made) naked his close relative: they shall nashaa (lift) their iwan (guilt/iniquity).

If a ayash (husband/individual man) shakab (lies) with his dawadah (uncle's) wife, he has galah (uncovered) his dawad (uncle's) irawah (nakedness): they shall nashaa (lift) their chataa (sin); they shall mawath (death) irayaray (childless).

‘If a ayash (husband/individual man) laqach (take / seized) his ach (brother/kinsman) ashah (wife/individual woman), it is an impurity: he has galah (uncovered) his ach (brother/kinsman) irawah (nakedness); they shall be irayaray (childless).

‘You shall therefore shamar (keep/guard) all my chaqah (statutes), and all my mashapat (ordinances), and ishah (make) them; that the aratz (Earth/land), where I am bawaa (come) you to yashab (inhabit/dwell), may not qawaa (vomit) you out.

You shall not yalak (walk) in the chaqah (customs) of the gaway (nation / people), which I am shalach (send) out panayam (before) you: for they ishah (make) all these things, and therefore I qawatz (abhorred) them.

But I have amar (spoke) to you, "You shall yarash (inherit) their adamah (land), and I will nathan (give) it to you to yarash (possess) it, a aratz (Earth/land) zawab (flow) with chalab (milk) and dabash (honey)." I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who has badal (separated) you from the im (people / nation).

‘You shall therefore badal (separated) a distinction between the tahawar (clean) animal and the tamaa (unclean), and between the tamaa (unclean) iwap (flying) and the tahawar (clean): and you shall not make yourselves shaqatz (abominable) by animal, or by iwap (flying), or by anything with which the adamah (ground) teems, which I have badal (separated) from you as tamaa (unclean) for you.
You shall be qadawash (holy) to me: for I, Yahawah, am qadawash (holy), and have set you apart from the im (people / nation), that you should be mine.

‘A ayash (husband/individual man) or a ashah (wife/individual woman) that is a medium, or is a yadainay (wizard), shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death): they shall ragam (stone) them with ragam (stones); their dam (blood) shall be upon them.’

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke) to the kahan (priest), the ban (son) of Aharawan (Aaron), and amar (spoke) to them, ‘A priest shall not tamaa (defile) himself for the napash (living being/soul) among his im (people / nation);
Except for his relatives that are qarawab (near) to him: for his am (mother), for his ab (father), for his ban (son), for his bath (daughter), for his ach (brother/kinsman),
And for his bathawalah (virgin) achawath (sister) who is qarawab (near) to him, who has had no ayash (husband/individual man); for her he may tamaa (defile) himself.
He shall not tamaa (defile) himself, being a chief bail (man) among his im (people / nation), to chalal (profane) himself.
‘They shall not shave their raash (head), neither shall they galach (shave) off the paah (corners) of their zaqan (beards), nor sharat (make) any sharat (cuttings) in their bashar (flesh).

They shall be qadash (set apart/make holy) to their Alahayam, and not chalal (profane) the sham (name) of their Alahayam; for they qarab (come close) the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Yahawah made by ashah (wife/individual woman), the lacham (bread) of their Alahayam; therefore they shall be qadawash (holy).

‘They shall not marry a ashah (wife/individual woman) who is a prostitute, or chalal (profane); neither shall they marry a ashah (wife/individual woman) garash (divorced) from her ayash (husband/individual man): for he is qadawash (holy) to his Alahayam.
