Shamai (hearken / hear), Yasharaal (Israel): you are to ibar (pass over/through) over the Yaradan (Jordan) this yawam (day), to bawaa (come) in to yarash (dispossess) gaway (nation / people) greater and mightier than yourself, iyar (cities) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and batzar (fortified) up to the sky,

A im (people / nation) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and rawam (will lift up), the ban (son) of the inaqay (anakim), whom you yadai (know), and of whom you have shamai (hearken / hear) say, Who yatzab (can) stand panayam (before) the ban (son) of Inaq (Anak)?

Yadai (know) therefore this yawam (day), that Yahawah your Alahayam is he who ibar (pass over/through) over panayam (before) you as a akal (eat) ash (fire); he will shamad (destroy) them, and he will kanai (bring) them down panayam (before) you: so you shall yarash (drive) them out, and make them to abad (destroy/perish) mahar (quickly), as Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) to you.

Don't amar (spoke) in your labab (heart), after Yahawah your Alahayam has hadap (thrust) them out from panayam (before) you, amar (spoke), "For my tzadaqah (righteousness) Yahawah bawaa (come) brought me in to yarash (possess) this aratz (Earth/land);" because Yahawah yarash (drives) them out panayam (before) you because of the rashaih (wickedness) of these gaway (nation / people).

Not for your tzadaqah (righteousness), or for the yashar (uprightness) of your labab (heart), do you bawaa (come) in to yarash (possess) their aratz (Earth/land); but for the rashaih (wickedness) of these gaway (nation / people) Yahawah your Alahayam does yarash (drive) them out from panayam (before) you, and that he may qawam (rise up) the dabar (word / matter) which Yahawah shabai (swear / take oath) to your ab (father), to Abaraham (Abraham), to Yatzachaq (Isaac), and to Yaiqab (Jacob).

Yadai (know) therefore, that Yahawah your Alahayam doesn't nathan (give) you this tawab (pleasant/functional) aratz (Earth/land) to yarash (possess) it for your tzadaqah (righteousness); for you are a irap (neck) im (people / nation).

Zakar (remembrance/memory), don't shakach (forget), how you provoked Yahawah your Alahayam to qatzap (wrath) in the madabar (wilderness): from the yawam (day) that you yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), until you bawaa (come) to this maqawam (place), you have been rebellious im (against) Yahawah.
Also in Charab (Horeb) you provoked Yahawah to qatzap (wrath), and Yahawah was anap (angry) with you to shamad (destroy) you.

When I was ilah (go up / offer) up onto the har (mountain) to laqach (take / seized) the lawach (tables) of aban (stone), even the lawach (tables) of the barayath (covenant) which Yahawah karath (cut) with you, then I stayed on the har (mountain) arabaiyam (forty) yawam (day) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights); I neither akal (eat) lacham (bread) nor shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters).

Yahawah nathan (give) to me the shanayam (two) lawach (tables) of aban (stone) kathab (written) with the atzabai (finger) of Alahayam; and on them were all the dabar (word / matter) which Yahawah dabar (word / matter) with you on the har (mountain) out of the thawak (midst) of the ash (fire) in the yawam (day) of the qahal (assembly).

It came to pass at the qatz (end) of arabaiyam (forty) yawam (day) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights), that Yahawah nathan (give) me the shanayam (two) lawach (tables) of aban (stone), even the lawach (tables) of the barayath (covenant).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, qawam (rise up), yarad (get) down mahar (quickly) from here; for your im (people / nation) whom you yatzaa (go out / come out) brought out of Matzarayam (Egypt) have shachath (corrupted) themselves; they have mahar (quickly) sawar (turned) aside out of the darak (way) which I tzawah (commanded) them; they ishah (make) made them a masakah (molten) image.
Furthermore Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, amar (spoke), I raah (see) seen this im (people / nation), and behold, it is a irap (neck) im (people / nation):

Let me rapah (alone), that I may shamad (destroy) them, and machah (blot) out their sham (name) from under the sky; and I will ishah (make) of you a gaway (nation / people) mightier and greater than they.

So I panah (turned) and yarad (came) down from the har (mountain), and the har (mountain) was bair (burning) with ash (fire): and the shanayam (two) lawach (tables) of the barayath (covenant) were in my shanayam (two) yad (hand).

I raah (see), and behold, you had chataa (sinned) against Yahawah your Alahayam; you ishah (make) made yourselves a masakah (molten) igal (calf): you had sawar (turned) aside mahar (quickly) out of the darak (way) which Yahawah had tzawah (commanded) you.
I thapash (took) hold of the shanayam (two) lawach (tables), and shalak (cast) them out of my shanayam (two) yad (hand), and shabar (broke) them before your iyan (eye).

I napal (fall / be cast down) down panayam (before) Yahawah, as at the raashawan (first), arabaiyam (forty) yawam (day) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights); I neither akal (eat) lacham (bread) nor shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters); because of all your chataah (sin) which you chataa (sinned), in ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, to provoke him to kais (anger).

For I was yagar (afraid) of the ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) and chamah (hot) displeasure, with which Yahawah was qatzap (angry) against you to shamad (destroy) you. But Yahawah shamai (hearken / hear) to me that paim (time) also.
Yahawah was very anap (angry) with Aharawan (Aaron) to shamad (destroy) him: and I palal (prayed) for Aharawan (Aaron) also at the same ith (time).

I laqach (take / seized) your chataah (sin), the igal (calf) which you ishah (make) made, and burnt it with ash (fire), and kathath (stamped) it, tachan (grinding) it very yatab (small), until it was as fine as ipar (dust): and I shalak (cast) its ipar (dust) into the nachal (stream / river) that descended out of the har (mountain).
At Thabairah (Taberah), and at Masah (Massah), and at Qabarawathahathaawah (Kibroth) Hattaavah, you provoked Yahawah to qatzap (wrath).

When Yahawah shalach (send) you Qadashabaranai (from) Kadesh Barnea, amar (spoke), "ilah (go up / offer) up and yarash (possess) the aratz (Earth/land) which I nathan (give) given you;" then you marah (rebelled) against the commandment of Yahawah your Alahayam, and you didn't aman (believe / have faith) him, nor shamai (hearken / hear) to his qawal (sound / voice).
You have been rebellious against Yahawah from the yawam (day) that I yadai (knew) you.

So I napal (fall / be cast down) down panayam (before) Yahawah the arabaiyam (forty) yawam (day) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights) that I napal (fall / be cast down) down, because Yahawah had amar (spoke) he would shamad (destroy) you.

I palal (prayed) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), Adawan Yahawah, don't shachath (destroy) your im (people / nation) and your nachalah (inheritance), that you have padah (redeemed) through your gadal (greatness), that you yatzaa (go out / come out) brought out of Matzarayam (Egypt) with a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand).

Zakar (remembrance/memory) your ibad (servant), Abaraham (Abraham), Yatzachaq (Isaac), and Yaiqab (Jacob); don't panah (look) to the qashay (stubbornness) of this im (people / nation), nor to their rashai (wickedness), nor to their chataah (sin),

Lest the aratz (Earth/land) you yatzaa (go out / come out) us out from amar (spoke), ‘Because Yahawah was not yakal (able) to bawaa (come) them into the aratz (Earth/land) which he dabar (word / matter) to them, and because he shanaah (hated) them, he yatzaa (go out / come out) brought them out to mawath (death) them in the madabar (wilderness).’

Yet they are your im (people / nation) and your nachalah (inheritance), which you yatzaa (go out / come out) out by your gadawal (very great/important/mighty) kach (strength / mighty / power) and by your natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm).

At that ith (time) Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, Cut shanayam (two) lawach (tables) of aban (stone) like the raashawan (first), and ilah (go up / offer) up to me onto the har (mountain), and ishah (make) an arawan (ark) of itz (wood).

I will kathab (write) on the lawach (tables) the dabar (word / matter) that were on the raashawan (first) lawach (tables) which you shabar (broke), and you shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) them in the arawan (ark).

So I ishah (make) an arawan (ark) of acacia itz (wood), and cut shanayam (two) lawach (tables) of aban (stone) like the raashawan (first), and ilah (go up / offer) up onto the har (mountain), having the shanayam (two) lawach (tables) in my yad (hand).

He kathab (wrote) on the lawach (tables), according to the raashawan (first) makathab (writing), the ishar (ten) commandments, which Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to you on the har (mountain) out of the thawak (midst) of the ash (fire) in the yawam (day) of the qahal (assembly): and Yahawah nathan (give) them to me.

I panah (turned) and yarad (came) down from the har (mountain), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the lawach (tables) in the arawan (ark) which I ishah (make) made; and there they are as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) me.

(The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) traveled from Baarathabanayayaiqan (Beeroth) Bene Jaakan Mawasarah (to) Moserah. There Aharawan (Aaron) mawath (death), and there he was qabar (bury); and Alaizar (Eleazar) his ban (son) ministered in the kahan (priest) office in his place.
From there they traveled to Gadagadah (Gudgodah); and from Gadagadah (Gudgodah) to Yatabathah (Jotbathah), a aratz (Earth/land) of nachal (stream / river) of mayam (Waters).

At that ith (time) Yahawah set apart the shabat (tribe) of Laway (Levi), to nashaa (lift) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, to imad (stand) panayam (before) Yahawah to sharath (minister) to him, and to barak (bless) in his sham (name), to this yawam (day).

Therefore Laway (Levi) has no chalaq (portion) nor nachalah (inheritance) with his ach (brother/kinsman); Yahawah is his nachalah (inheritance), according as Yahawah your Alahayam dabar (word / matter) to him.)

I imad (stayed) on the har (mountain), as at the raashawan (first) yawam (day), arabaiyam (forty) yawam (day) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights): and Yahawah shamai (hearken / hear) to me that paim (time) also; Yahawah would not shachath (destroy) you.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, qawam (rise up), yalak (take) your masai (journey) panayam (before) the im (people / nation); and they shall bawaa (come) in and yarash (possess) the aratz (Earth/land), which I shabai (swear / take oath) to their ab (father) to nathan (give) to them.

Now, Yasharaal (Israel), what does Yahawah your Alahayam shaal (require) of you, but to yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah your Alahayam, to yalak (walk) in all his darak (ways), and to ahab (love) him, and to ibad (servant) Yahawah your Alahayam with all your labab (heart) and with all your napash (living being/soul),
To shamar (keep/guard) the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah, and his chaqah (statutes), which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day) for your tawab (pleasant/functional)?
Behold, to Yahawah your Alahayam belongs shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) and the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) of shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), the aratz (Earth/land), with all that is therein.

Only Yahawah chashaq (had) a delight in your ab (father) to ahab (love) them, and he bachar (chose) their zarai (seed) achar (other) them, even you above all im (people / nation), as at this yawam (day).
Mawal (circumcise) therefore the iralah (foreskin) of your labab (heart), and be no more irap (neck).

For Yahawah your Alahayam, he is Alahayam of Alahayam, and Adawan of adawan (master / lord), the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) Al, the gabawar (mighty), and the awesome, who doesn't nashaa (lift) panayam (persons), nor laqach (take / seized) shachad (reward).
He ishah (make) execute mashapat (justice) for the yathawam (fatherless) and alamanah (widow), and ahab (love) the foreigner, in nathan (give) him lacham (food) and shamalah (clothing).
Therefore ahab (love) the foreigner; for you were foreigners in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
You shall yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah your Alahayam; you shall ibad (servant) him; and you shall cling to him, and you shall shabai (swear / take oath) by his sham (name).
He is your thahalah (praise), and he is your Alahayam, who ishah (make) done for you these gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and awesome things, which your iyan (eye) raah (see) seen.

Your ab (father) yarad (went) down into Matzarayam (Egypt) with shabaiyam (seventy) napash (living being/soul); and now Yahawah your Alahayam has shawam (place / establish / appoint) you as the kawakab (star) of the sky for rab (multitude).

Therefore you shall ahab (love) Yahawah your Alahayam, and shamar (keep/guard) his instructions, and his chaqah (statutes), and his mashapat (ordinances), and his matzawah (commandments), yawam (day).

Yadai (know) this yawam (day): for I don't speak with your ban (son) who yadai (have) not known, and who raah (see) not seen the mawasar (chastisement) of Yahawah your Alahayam, his gadal (greatness), his chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and his natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm),

And his awath (sign / mark / miracle), and his maishah (works), which he ishah (make) in the thawak (midst) of Matzarayam (Egypt) to Paraih (Pharaoh) the malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and to all his aratz (Earth/land);

And what he ishah (make) to the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) of Matzarayam (Egypt), to their sawas (horses), and to their rakab (chariots); how he made the mayam (Waters) of the sawap (red) yam (sea/waters) to overflow them as they radap (pursued) achar (other) you, and how Yahawah abad (destroy/perish) destroyed them to this yawam (day);
And what he ishah (make) to you in the madabar (wilderness), until you bawaa (come) to this maqawam (place);

And what he ishah (make) to Dathan (Dathan) and Abayaram (Abiram), the ban (son) of Alayaab (Eliab), the ban (son) of Raawaban (Reuben); how the aratz (Earth/land) patzah (opened) its pah (mouth), and balai (swallowed) them up, and their bayath (house), and their ahal (tents), and every living thing that ragal (feet / foot) them, in the qarab (among / near) of all Yasharaal (Israel):
But your iyan (eye) raah (see) seen all the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) maishah (work) of Yahawah which he ishah (make).

Therefore you shall shamar (keep/guard) all the matzawah (commandment) which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), that you may be chazaq (strong), and bawaa (come) in and yarash (possess) the aratz (Earth/land), where you ibar (pass over/through) over to yarash (possess) it;

And that you may prolong your yawam (day) in the adamah (land), which Yahawah shabai (swear / take oath) to your ab (father) to nathan (give) to them and to their zarai (seed), a aratz (Earth/land) zawab (flow) with chalab (milk) and dabash (honey).

For the aratz (Earth/land), where you bawaa (come) in to yarash (possess) it, isn't as the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), that you yatzaa (go out / come out) out from, where you zarai (sowed) your zarai (seed), and shaqah (watered) it with your ragal (feet / foot), as a gan (garden) of yaraq (herbs);

But the aratz (Earth/land), where you ibar (pass over/through) over to yarash (possess) it, is a aratz (Earth/land) of har (mountain) and baqaih (valleys) which shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters) of the matar (rain) of the sky,

A aratz (Earth/land) which Yahawah your Alahayam darash (cares) for: the iyan (eye) of Yahawah your Alahayam are thamayad (always) on it, from the raashayath (beginning) of the shanah (year) even to the acharayath (end) of the shanah (year).

It shall happen, if you shall shamai (hearken / hear) shamai (hearken / hear) to my matzawah (commandments) which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), to ahab (love) Yahawah your Alahayam, and to ibad (servant) him with all your labab (heart) and with all your napash (living being/soul),

That I will nathan (give) the matar (rain) of your aratz (Earth/land) in its ith (season), the yawarah (former) rain and the latter yawarah (rain), that you may asap (gather) in your grain, and your new thayarawash (wine), and your yatzahar (fresh oil).
I will nathan (give) ishab (grass) in your shadah (fields) for your livestock, and you shall akal (eat) and be shabai (full).
Shamar (keep/guard) heed to yourselves, lest your labab (heart) be pathah (deceived), and you sawar (turn) aside, and ibad (servant) other Alahayam, and shachah (worship) them;

And the ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah be charah (hot with anger) against you, and he itzar (shut) up the sky, so that there shall be no matar (rain), and the adamah (land) shall not nathan (give) its yabawal (fruit); and you abad (destroy/perish) maharah (quickly) from off the tawab (pleasant/functional) aratz (Earth/land) which Yahawah nathan (give) you.

Therefore you shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) up these my dabar (word / matter) in your labab (heart) and in your napash (living being/soul); and you shall qashar (bind) them for a awath (sign / mark / miracle) on your yad (hand), and they shall be for symbols between your iyan (eye).

You shall lamad (teach/instruct) them your ban (son), dabar (word / matter) of them, when you yashab (inhabit/dwell) in your bayath (house), and when you yalak (walk) by the darak (way), and when you shakab (lie) down, and when you qawam (rise up) up.
You shall kathab (write) them on the mazawazah (door) posts of your bayath (house), and on your shair (gates);

That your yawam (day) may be rabah (multiplied), and the yawam (day) of your ban (son), in the adamah (land) which Yahawah shabai (swear / take oath) to your ab (father) to nathan (give) them, as the yawam (day) of the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) above the aratz (Earth/land).

For if you shall diligently shamar (keep/guard) all this matzawah (commandment) which I tzawah (command) you, to ishah (make) it, to ahab (love) Yahawah your Alahayam, to yalak (walk) in all his darak (ways), and to cling to him;
Then will Yahawah yarash (drive) out all these gaway (nation / people) from panayam (before) you, and you shall yarash (dispossess) gaway (nation / people) greater and mightier than yourselves.

Every maqawam (place) whereon the kap (sole) of your ragal (feet / foot) shall darak (tread) shall be yours: from the madabar (wilderness), and Labanawan (Lebanon), from the nahar (river), the nahar (river) Parath (Euphrates), even to the hinder yam (sea/waters) shall be your gabawal (border/boundary).

No ayash (husband/individual man) shall be yatzab (able) to stand panayam (before) you: Yahawah your Alahayam shall nathan (give) the pachad (fear / dread) of you and the mawaraa (dread) of you on all the aratz (Earth/land) that you shall darak (tread) on, as he has dabar (word / matter) to you.
Raah (see), I nathan (give) panayam (before) you this yawam (day) a barakah (blessing) and a qalalah (curse):
The barakah (blessing), if you shall shamai (hearken / hear) to the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah your Alahayam, which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day);

And the qalalah (curse), if you shall not shamai (hearken / hear) to the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah your Alahayam, but sawar (turn) aside out of the darak (way) which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), to yalak (go) achar (other) other Alahayam, which you yadai (have) not known.

It shall happen, when Yahawah your Alahayam shall bawaa (come) you into the aratz (Earth/land) where you bawaa (come) to yarash (possess) it, that you shall nathan (give) the barakah (blessing) on har (mountain) Garazayam (Gerizim), and the qalalah (curse) on har (mountain) Iyabal (Ebal).

Aren't they ibar (beyond) the Yaradan (Jordan), achar (other) the darak (way) of the mabawaa (going) down of the shamash (sun), in the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kanainay (Canaanites) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the irabah (arabah), over mawal (against) Galagal (Gilgal), beside the oaks of Mawarah (Moreh)?

For you are to ibar (pass over/through) over the Yaradan (Jordan) to bawaa (come) in to yarash (possess) the aratz (Earth/land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you, and you shall yarash (possess) it, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein.
You shall shamar (keep/guard) to ishah (make) all the chaq (statute) and the mashapat (ordinances) which I nathan (give) panayam (before) you this yawam (day).

These are the chaq (statute) and the mashapat (ordinances) which you shall shamar (keep/guard) to ishah (make) in the aratz (Earth/land) which Yahawah, the Alahayam of your ab (father), nathan (give) given you to yarash (possess) it, all the yawam (day) that you chay (life) on the adamah (earth).

You shall abad (destroy/perish) abad (destroy/perish) all the maqawam (place) in which the gaway (nation / people) that you shall yarash (dispossess) ibad (servant) their Alahayam, on the rawam (will lift up) har (mountain), and on the gabaih (hills), and under every rainan (green) itz (tree):

And you shall shabar (break) down their mazabach (altars), and dash in pieces their matzabah (pillars), and sharap (burn) their Asharah (Asherim) with ash (fire); and you shall gadai (cut) down the engraved pasayal (images) of their Alahayam; and you shall abad (destroy/perish) their sham (name) out of that maqawam (place).
You shall not ishah (make) so to Yahawah your Alahayam.

But to the maqawam (place) which Yahawah your Alahayam shall bachar (choose) out of all your shabat (tribes), to shawam (place / establish / appoint) his sham (name) there, even to his shakan (habitation) you shall darash (seek), and there you shall bawaa (come);

And there you shall bawaa (come) your burnt ilah (offerings), and your zabach (sacrifices), and your maishar (tithes), and the wave tharawamah (offering) of your yad (hand), and your nadar (vow), and your freewill nadabah (voluntary / freewill offering), and the bakawarah (firstborn) of your baqar (morning) and of your tzaan (flock):

And there you shall akal (eat) panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam, and you shall shamach (rejoice) in all that you mashalawach (put) your yad (hand) to, you and your bayath (house), in which Yahawah your Alahayam has barak (blessed) you.
You shall not ishah (make) after all the things that we ishah (make) here this yawam (day), every ayash (husband/individual man) whatever is yashar (right) in his own iyan (eye);
For you haven't yet bawaa (come) to the manawachah (rest) and to the nachalah (inheritance), which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you.

But when you ibar (pass over/through) over the Yaradan (Jordan), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the aratz (Earth/land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nachal (causes) you to inherit, and he gives you nawach (rest) from all your ayab (enemy) around you, so that you yashab (inhabit/dwell) in safety;

Then it shall happen that to the maqawam (place) which Yahawah your Alahayam shall bachar (choose), to cause his sham (name) to shakan (dwell) there, there you shall bawaa (come) all that I tzawah (command) you: your burnt ilah (offerings), and your zabach (sacrifices), your maishar (tithes), and the wave tharawamah (offering) of your yad (hand), and all your mabachar (choice) nadar (vow) which you nadar (make vow) to Yahawah.

You shall shamach (rejoice) panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam, you, and your ban (son), and your bath (daughter), and your male ibad (servant), and your female amah (servants), and the Lawayay (Levite) who is within your shair (gates), kay (surely) he has no chalaq (portion) nor nachalah (inheritance) with you.
Shamar (keep/guard) heed to yourself that you don't ilah (go up / offer) your burnt ilah (offerings) in every maqawam (place) that you raah (see);

But in the maqawam (place) which Yahawah shall bachar (choose) in achad (one) of your shabat (tribes), there you shall ilah (go up / offer) your burnt ilah (offerings), and there you shall ishah (make) all that I tzawah (command) you.

Notwithstanding, you may zabach (kill) and akal (eat) bashar (flesh) within all your shair (gates), awah (after) all the awah (desire) of your napash (living being/soul), according to the barakah (blessing) of Yahawah your Alahayam which he nathan (give) given you: the tamaa (unclean) and the tahawar (clean) may akal (eat) of it, as of the gazelle, and as of the ayal (hart).
Only you shall not akal (eat) the dam (blood); you shall shapak (pour) it out on the aratz (Earth/land) as mayam (Waters).

You may not akal (eat) within your shair (gates) the maishar (tithe) of your grain, or of your new thayarawash (wine), or of your yatzahar (fresh oil), or the bakawarah (firstborn) of your baqar (morning) or of your tzaan (flock), nor any of your nadar (vow) which you nadar (make vow), nor your freewill nadabah (voluntary / freewill offering), nor the wave tharawamah (offering) of your yad (hand);

But you shall akal (eat) them panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam in the maqawam (place) which Yahawah your Alahayam shall bachar (choose), you, and your ban (son), and your bath (daughter), and your male ibad (servant), and your female amah (servant), and the Lawayay (Levite) who is within your shair (gates): and you shall shamach (rejoice) panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam in all that you mashalawach (put) your yad (hand) to.
Shamar (keep/guard) heed to yourself that you don't izab (forsake) the Lawayay (Levite) as yawam (day) as you live in your adamah (land).

When Yahawah your Alahayam shall enlarge your gabawal (border/boundary), as he has dabar (word / matter) you, and you shall amar (spoke), "I want to akal (eat) meat," because your napash (living being/soul) desires to akal (eat) meat; you may akal (eat) meat, awah (after) all the awah (desire) of your napash (living being/soul).

If the maqawam (place) which Yahawah your Alahayam shall bachar (choose), to shawam (place / establish / appoint) his sham (name) there, is rachaq (too) far from you, then you shall zabach (kill) of your baqar (morning) and of your tzaan (flock), which Yahawah nathan (give) given you, as I have tzawah (commanded) you; and you may akal (eat) within your shair (gates), awah (after) all the desire of your napash (living being/soul).
Even as the gazelle and as the ayal (hart) is akal (eat), so you shall akal (eat) of it: the tamaa (unclean) and the tahawar (clean) may akal (eat) of it yachad (alike).

Only be chazaq (sure) that you don't akal (eat) the dam (blood): for the dam (blood) is the napash (living being/soul); and you shall not akal (eat) the napash (living being/soul) with the bashar (flesh).
You shall not akal (eat) it; you shall shapak (pour) it out on the aratz (Earth/land) as mayam (Waters).
You shall not akal (eat) it; that it may yatab (go) well with you, and with your ban (son) achar (other) you, when you shall ishah (make) that which is yashar (right) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah.
Only your qadash (set apart/make holy) things which you have, and your nadar (vow), you shall nashaa (lift), and bawaa (come) to the maqawam (place) which Yahawah shall bachar (choose):

And you shall ishah (make) your burnt ilah (offerings), the bashar (flesh) and the dam (blood), on the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah your Alahayam; and the dam (blood) of your zabach (sacrifices) shall be shapak (poured) out on the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah your Alahayam; and you shall akal (eat) the bashar (flesh).

Shamar (keep/guard) and shamai (hearken / hear) all these dabar (word / matter) which I tzawah (command) you, that it may yatab (go) well with you, and with your ban (son) achar (other) you iwalam (forever), when you ishah (make) that which is tawab (pleasant/functional) and yashar (right) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah your Alahayam.

When Yahawah your Alahayam shall karath (cut) off the gaway (nation / people) from panayam (before) you, where you bawaa (come) in to yarash (dispossess) them, and you yarash (dispossess) them, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) in their aratz (Earth/land);

Shamar (keep/guard) heed to yourself that you not be ensnared to achar (other) them, achar (other) that they are destroyed from panayam (before) you; and that you not darash (inquire) after their Alahayam, amar (spoke), How do these gaway (nation / people) ibad (servant) their Alahayam? I will ishah (make) gam (indeed / moreover).

You shall not ishah (make) so to Yahawah your Alahayam: for every thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, which he shanaa (hate), ishah (make) they done to their Alahayam; for even their ban (son) and their bath (daughter) do they sharap (burn) in the ash (fire) to their Alahayam.
Whatever thing I tzawah (command) you, that you shall shamar (keep/guard) to ishah (make): you shall not yasap (add) thereto, nor garai (diminish) from it.
If there arise in the midst of you a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and he tzawah (give) you a dabar (word / matter) or a wonder,

And the awath (sign / mark / miracle) or the mawapath (wonder) nathan (give) to pass, of which he spoke to you, saying, "nathan (give) us go al (after) other Alahayam" (which you nathan (give) not known) and let us serve them;

You shall not listen to the words of that prophet, or to that dreamer of dreams: for Yahawah your Alahayam proves you, to yadai (know) whether you love Yahawah your Alahayam with all your heart and with all your soul.
You shall walk al (after) Yahawah your Alahayam, and fear him, and keep his dabar (word / matter), and shamai (hearken / hear) his voice, and you shall serve him, and cling to him.

That prophet, or that dreamer of dreams, shall be put to death, because he has spoken rebellion against Yahawah your Alahayam, who yalak (brought) you out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you out of the house of ibad (servant), to draw you aside out of the yalak (way) which Yahawah your Alahayam matzawah (commanded) you to yalak (walk) in. So you shall put achar (other) the evil from the midst of you.

If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son, or your bayath (house), or the wife of your bosom, or your friend, who is as your own soul, entice you secretly, dabar (word / matter), "yalak (let) us go and serve other Alahayam," which you il (over) not known, you, nor your fathers;
Of the Alahayam of the ban (son) who are around you, near to you, or far off from you, from the one end of the am (mother) even to the other end of the am (mother);
You shall not consent to him, nor listen to him; neither shall your eye pity him, neither shall you spare, neither shall you conceal him:
But you shall laa (NOT) kill him; your hand shall be first on him to put him to death, and afterwards the hand of all the people.
You shall stone him to death with stones, because he has sought to yad (hand) you away from Yahawah your Alahayam, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
All Israel shall hear, and fear, and shall not do any more such wickedness as this is in the midst of you.
If you shall shamai (hearken / hear) tell concerning one of your cities, which Yahawah your Alahayam shamai (hearken / hear) you to dwell there, dabar (word / matter),

Certain base fellows are gone out from the midst of you, and have drawn away the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of their iyar (city), amar (spoke), "shamai (hearken / hear) us go and serve other Alahayam," which you nathan (give) not known;

Then you shall inquire, and make search, and ask diligently; and, behold, if it be laa (NOT), and the thing ayash (husband/individual man), that such abomination is ibad (servant) in the qarab (among / near) of you,
You shall darash (surely) strike the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, destroying it utterly, and all that is therein and its livestock, with the edge of the sword.

You shall gather all its spoil into the midst of its street, and shall burn with fire the iyar (city), and all its spoil kal (every) whit, to Yahawah your Alahayam: and it shall be a heap forever; it shall not be built again.

Kal (every) of the devoted thing shall cling to your hand; that Yahawah may turn from the fierceness of his anger, and show you mercy, and hayah (came to pass) compassion on you, and multiply you, as he has sworn to your fathers;

When you shall listen to the voice of Yahawah your Alahayam, to dabaq (keep) all his commandments which I command you this day, to shawab (turn back / repent) that which is right in the eyes of Yahawah your Alahayam.
You are the ban (son) of Yahawah your Alahayam: you shall not gadad (cut) yourselves, nor shawam (place / establish / appoint) any qarachah (baldness) between your iyan (eye) for the mawath (death).

For you are a qadawash (holy) im (people / nation) to Yahawah your Alahayam, and Yahawah has bachar (chosen) you to be a im (people / nation) for his own sagalah (possession), above all im (people / nation) who are on the face of the adamah (earth).
You shall not akal (eat) any thawaibah (abominable) thing.
These are the animals which you may akal (eat): the shawar (ox), the shah (sheep), and the iz (goat),
The ayal (hart), and the gazelle, and the tzabay (roebuck), and the aqaw (wild) goat, and the ibex, and the antelope, and the zamar (chamois).
Every animal that paras (parts) the parasah (hoof), and has the parasah (hoof) cloven in shanayam (two) and chews the garah (cud), among the animals, that may you akal (eat).

Nevertheless these you shall not akal (eat) of them that chew the garah (cud), or of those who paras (have) the parasah (hoof) shasai (cloven): the gamal (camel), and the aranabath (hare), and the Shapan (rabbit); because they chew the garah (cud) but don't paras (part) the parasah (hoof), they are tamaa (unclean) to you.

The pig, because it paras (has) a split parasah (hoof) but doesn't chew the garah (cud), is tamaa (unclean) to you: of their bashar (flesh) you shall not akal (eat), and their carcasses you shall not nagai (touch).
These you may akal (eat) of all that are in the mayam (Waters): whatever has sanapayar (fins) and qashaqashath (scales) may you akal (eat);
And whatever doesn't have sanapayar (fins) and qashaqashath (scales) you shall not akal (eat); it is tamaa (unclean) to you.
Of all tahawar (clean) tzapawar (birds) you may akal (eat).
But these are they of which you shall not akal (eat): the nashar (eagle), and the vulture, and the osprey,
And the red ayah (kite), and the falcon, and the ayah (kite) after its mayan (species),
And every irab (evening) after its mayan (species),
And the ostrich, and the bath (daughter), and the seagull, and the thachamas (hawk) after its mayan (species),
The little kawas (owl), and the great yanashawap (owl), and the horned owl,
And the pelican, and the vulture, and the shalak (cormorant),
And the chasayadah (stork), and the anapah (heron) after its mayan (species), and the hoopoe, and the italap (bat).
All winged sharatz (creeping) things are tamaa (unclean) to you: they shall not be akal (eat).
Of all tahawar (clean) iwap (flying) you may akal (eat).

You shall not akal (eat) of anything that dies of nabalah (itself): you may nathan (give) it to the foreigner living among you who is within your shair (gates), that he may akal (eat) it; or you may makar (sell) it to a nakaray (foreigner): for you are a qadawash (holy) im (people / nation) to Yahawah your Alahayam. You shall not bashal (boil) a young goat in its am (mother) chalab (milk).
You shall ishar (surely) ishar (tithe) all the thabawaah (increase) of your zarai (seed), that which yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from the shadah (field) shanah (year) by shanah (year).

You shall akal (eat) panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam, in the maqawam (place) which he shall bachar (choose), to cause his sham (name) to shakan (dwell) there, the maishar (tithe) of your grain, of your new thayarawash (wine), and of your yatzahar (fresh oil), and the bakawarah (firstborn) of your baqar (morning) and of your tzaan (flock); that you may lamad (teach/instruct) to yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah your Alahayam yawam (day).

If the darak (way) is too rabah (long) for you, so that you are not yakal (able) to nashaa (lift) it, because the maqawam (place) is rachaq (too) far from you, which Yahawah your Alahayam shall bachar (choose), to shawam (place / establish / appoint) his sham (name) there, when Yahawah your Alahayam shall barak (bless) you;

Then you shall nathan (give) it into kasap (money), and tzarar (bind) up the kasap (money) in your yad (hand), and shall halak (move) to the maqawam (place) which Yahawah your Alahayam shall bachar (choose):

And you shall nathan (give) the kasap (money) for whatever your napash (living being/soul) awah (desires), for cattle, or for tzaan (sheep), or for yayan (wine), or for shakar (strong) drink, or for whatever your napash (living being/soul) shaal (asks) of you; and you shall akal (eat) there panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam, and you shall shamach (rejoice), you and your bayath (house).
The Lawayay (Levite) who is within your shair (gates), you shall not izab (forsake) him; for he has no chalaq (portion) nor nachalah (inheritance) with you.

At the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of every shalawash (three) shanah (years) you shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth all the maishar (tithe) of your thabawaah (increase) in the same shanah (year), and shall yanach (lay) it up within your shair (gates):

And the Lawayay (Levite), because he has no chalaq (portion) nor nachalah (inheritance) with you, and the foreigner living among you, and the yathawam (fatherless), and the alamanah (widow), who are within your shair (gates), shall bawaa (come), and shall akal (eat) and be shabai (satisfied); that Yahawah your Alahayam may barak (bless) you in all the maishah (work) of your yad (hand) which you ishah (make).
At the qatz (end) of every shabai (seven) shanah (years) you shall ishah (make) a shamatah (release).

This is the dabar (word / matter) of the shamatah (release): every mashah (Mashah/(Moses)) shall shamatah (release) that which he has nashah (lent) to his neighbor; he shall not nagash (exact) it of his neighbor and his ach (brother/kinsman); because yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) shamatah (release) has been qaraa (called).
Of a nakaray (foreigner) you may nagash (exact) it: but whatever of your is with your ach (brother/kinsman) your yad (hand) shall shamat (release).

However there shall be no abayawan (poor) with you; (for Yahawah will surely barak (bless) you in the aratz (Earth/land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you for an nachalah (inheritance) to yarash (possess) it;)

If only you shamai (hearken / hear) shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam, to shamar (keep/guard) to ishah (make) all this matzawah (commandment) which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day).

For Yahawah your Alahayam will barak (bless) you, as he dabar (word / matter) you: and you shall ibat (lend) to many gaway (nation / people), but you shall not ibat (borrow); and you shall mashal (rule/have dominion) over many gaway (nation / people), but they shall not mashal (rule/have dominion) over you.

If a abayawan (poor) man, abayawan (one) of your ach (brother/kinsman), is with you within any of your shair (gates) in your aratz (Earth/land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you, you shall not amatz (harden) your labab (heart), nor qapatz (shut) your yad (hand) from your abayawan (poor) ach (brother/kinsman);
But you shall surely pathach (open) your yad (hand) to him, and shall ibat (surely) ibat (lend) him day (sufficient) for his machasawar (need), which he chasar (lacks).

Beware that there not be a base dabar (word / matter) in your labab (heart), amar (spoke), "The shabai (seven) shanah (year), the shanah (year) of shamatah (release), is at qarab (come close);" and your iyan (eye) be raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) against your abayawan (poor) ach (brother/kinsman), and you nathan (give) him nothing; and he qaraa (called) to Yahawah against you, and it be chataa (sin) to you.

You shall nathan (give) nathan (give) him, and your labab (heart) shall not be grieved when you nathan (give) to him; galal (because) that for this thing Yahawah your Alahayam will barak (bless) you in all your maishah (work), and in all that you mashalawach (put) your yad (hand) to.

For the abayawan (poor) will never chadal (cease) out of the aratz (Earth/land): therefore I tzawah (command) you, amar (spoke), You shall surely pathach (open) your yad (hand) to your ach (brother/kinsman), to your abayawan (needy), and to your inay (poor), in your aratz (Earth/land).

If your ach (brother/kinsman), a ibaray (hebrew) man, or a Hebrew ibaray (woman), is makar (sold) to you, and ibad (servant) you shash (six) shanah (years); then in the shabayaiy (seventh) shanah (year) you shall shalach (send) him go chapashay (free) from you.
When you shalach (send) him go chapashay (free) from you, you shall not shalach (send) him go rayaqam (empty):

You shall inaq (furnish) him inaq (liberally) out of your tzaan (flock), and out of your garan (threshing) floor, and out of your yaqab (winepress); as Yahawah your Alahayam has barak (blessed) you, you shall nathan (give) to him.

You shall zakar (remembrance/memory) that you were a ibad (servant) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and Yahawah your Alahayam padah (redeemed) you: therefore I tzawah (command) you this thing today.
It shall be, if he amar (spoke) you, "I will not yatzaa (go out / come out) out from you;" because he ahab (love) you and your bayath (house), because he is tawab (pleasant/functional) with you;

Then you shall laqach (take / seized) an awl, and nathan (give) it through his azan (ear) to the dalath (door), and he shall be your ibad (servant) iwalam (forever). Also to your female amah (servant) you shall ishah (make) likewise.

It shall not qashah (rough / hard) hard to you, when you shalach (send) him go chapashay (free) from you; for to the mashanah (double) of the shakar (hire) of a shakayar (hireling) has he ibad (servant) you shash (six) shanah (years): and Yahawah your Alahayam will barak (bless) you in all that you ishah (make).

All the bakawar (firstborn) zakar (remembrance/memory) that are yalad (birth / begot) of your baqar (morning) and of your tzaan (flock) you shall qadash (set apart/make holy) to Yahawah your Alahayam: you shall do no ibad (servant) with the bakawar (firstborn) of your herd, nor gazaz (shear) the bakawar (firstborn) of your tzaan (flock).
You shall akal (eat) it panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam shanah (year) by shanah (year) in the maqawam (place) which Yahawah shall bachar (choose), you and your bayath (house).
If it has any maawam (blemish), is pasach (lame) or iwar (blind), or has any defect whatever, you shall not zabach (sacrifice) it to Yahawah your Alahayam.
You shall akal (eat) it within your shair (gates): the tamaa (unclean) and the tahawar (clean) shall eat it yachad (alike), as the gazelle, and as the ayal (hart).
Only you shall not akal (eat) its dam (blood); you shall shapak (pour) it out on the aratz (Earth/land) as mayam (Waters).

Shamar (keep/guard) the chadash (month) of abayab (abib), and ishah (make) the pasach (passover) to Yahawah your Alahayam; for in the chadash (month) of abayab (abib) Yahawah your Alahayam yatzaa (go out / come out) you forth out of Matzarayam (Egypt) by layal (night).

You shall zabach (sacrifice) the pasach (passover) to Yahawah your Alahayam, of the tzaan (flock) and the baqar (morning), in the maqawam (place) which Yahawah shall bachar (choose), to cause his sham (name) to shakan (dwell) there.

You shall akal (eat) no chamatz (leavened) bread with it. You shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread) with it seven days, even the matzah (bread) of inay (affliction); for you yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) in chapazawan (haste): that you may zakar (remembrance/memory) the yawam (day) when you yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) all the yawam (day) of your chay (life).

No yeast shall be raah (see) with you in all your gabawal (border/boundary) shabai (seven) yawam (day); neither shall any of the bashar (flesh), which you zabach (sacrifice) the raashawan (first) yawam (day) at irab (evening), lawan (remain) all night until the baqar (morning).
You may not zabach (sacrifice) the pasach (passover) within any of your shair (gates), which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you;

But at the maqawam (place) which Yahawah your Alahayam shall bachar (choose), to cause his sham (name) to dwell in, there you shall zabach (sacrifice) the pasach (passover) at irab (evening), at the bawaa (come) down of the shamash (sun), at the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) that you yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of Matzarayam (Egypt).

You shall bashal (roast) and akal (eat) it in the maqawam (place) which Yahawah your Alahayam shall bachar (choose): and you shall panah (turn) in the baqar (morning), and halak (move) to your ahal (tents).

Shash (six) yawam (day) you shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread). On the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) shall be a solemn itzarah (assembly) to Yahawah your Alahayam; you shall ishah (make) no malaakah (work).

You shall sapar (book) for yourselves shabai (seven) shabawai (weeks): from the time you chalal (begin) to put the charamash (sickle) to the standing grain you shall chalal (begin) to sapar (book) shabai (seven) shabawai (weeks).

You shall ishah (make) the chag (feast/festival) of shabawai (weeks) to Yahawah your Alahayam with a masah (tribute) of a freewill nadabah (voluntary / freewill offering) of your yad (hand), which you shall nathan (give), according as Yahawah your Alahayam blesses you:

And you shall shamach (rejoice) panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam, you, and your ban (son), and your bath (daughter), and your male ibad (servant), and your female amah (servant), and the Lawayay (Levite) who is within your shair (gates), and the foreigner, and the yathawam (fatherless), and the alamanah (widow), who are in the qarab (among / near) of you, in the maqawam (place) which Yahawah your Alahayam shall bachar (choose), to cause his sham (name) to shakan (dwell) there.
You shall zakar (remembrance/memory) that you were a ibad (servant) in Matzarayam (Egypt): and you shall shamar (keep/guard) and ishah (make) these chaq (statute).
You shall ishah (make) the chag (feast/festival) of sakah (tents) shabai (seven) yawam (day), after that you have asap (gathered) in from your garan (threshing) floor and from your yaqab (winepress):

And you shall shamach (rejoice) in your chag (feast/festival), you, and your ban (son), and your bath (daughter), and your male ibad (servant), and your female amah (servant), and the Lawayay (Levite), and the foreigner, and the yathawam (fatherless), and the alamanah (widow), who are within your shair (gates).

You shall chagag (keep) a feast to Yahawah your Alahayam shabai (seven) yawam (day) in the maqawam (place) which Yahawah shall bachar (choose); because Yahawah your Alahayam will barak (bless) you in all your thabawaah (increase), and in all the maishah (work) of your yad (hand), and you shall be altogether shamach (joyful).

Shalawash (three) paim (times) in a shanah (year) shall all your zakawar (remember/recall) raah (see) panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam in the maqawam (place) which he shall bachar (choose): in the chag (feast/festival) of unleavened matzah (bread), and in the chag (feast/festival) of shabawai (weeks), and in the chag (feast/festival) of sakah (tents); and they shall not raah (see) panayam (before) Yahawah rayaqam (empty):
Every ayash (husband/individual man) shall give as he is able, according to the barakah (blessing) of Yahawah your Alahayam which he nathan (give) given you.

You shall nathan (give) shapat (judges) and shatar (officers) in all your shair (gates), which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you, according to your shabat (tribes); and they shall shapat (judge) the im (people / nation) with tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) mashapat (judgment).

You shall not natah (wrest) mashapat (justice): you shall not nakar (respect) panayam (persons); neither shall you laqach (take / seized) a shachad (bribe); for a shachad (bribe) does iwar (blind) the iyan (eye) of the chakam (wise), and salap (pervert) the dabar (word / matter) of the tzadayaq (righteous).

You shall radap (follow) that which is altogether tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), that you may chayah (live), and yarash (inherit) the aratz (Earth/land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you.
You shall not natai (plant) Asharah (for) yourselves an Asherah of any kind of itz (tree) beside the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah your Alahayam, which you shall ishah (make) for yourselves.
Neither shall you qawam (rise up) yourself up a matzabah (pillar); which Yahawah your Alahayam shanaa (hate).

You shall not zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah your Alahayam an shawar (ox), or a shah (sheep), in which is a maawam (blemish), or anything rai (evil); for that is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah your Alahayam.

If there is matzaa (found) in the qarab (among / near) of you, within any of your shair (gates) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you, ayash (husband/individual man) or ashah (wife/individual woman), who ishah (make) that which is rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah your Alahayam, in ibar (pass over/through) his barayath (covenant),

And has yalak (gone) and ibad (servant) other Alahayam, and shachah (worshiped) them, or the shamash (sun), or the yarach (moon), or any of the tzabaa (troop) of the sky, which I have not tzawah (commanded);

And it be nagad (told) you, and you have shamai (hearken / hear) of it, then you shall darash (inquire) yatab (diligently); and behold, if it be amath (truth), and the thing kawan (certain), that such thawaibah (abomination) is ishah (make) in Yasharaal (Israel),

Then you shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth that ayash (husband/individual man) or that ashah (wife/individual woman), who ishah (make) done this rai (evil) thing, to your shair (gates), even the ayash (husband/individual man) or the ashah (wife/individual woman); and you shall saqal (stone) them to mawath (death) with saqal (stones).

At the pah (mouth) of shanayam (two) witnesses, or shalawash (three) witnesses, shall he who is to mawath (death) be put to mawath (death); at the pah (mouth) of achad (one) id (witness) he shall not be put to mawath (death).

The yad (hand) of the witnesses shall be raashawan (first) on him to put him to mawath (death), and acharawan (afterward) the yad (hand) of all the im (people / nation). So you shall bair (put) bair (away) the rai (evil) from the qarab (among / near) of you.

If there arises a dabar (word / matter) palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) hard for you in mashapat (judgment), between dam (blood) and dam (blood), between dayan (judge) and dayan (judge), and between nagai (stroke) and nagai (stroke), being dabar (word / matter) of rayab (controversy) within your shair (gates); then you shall qawam (rise up), and ilah (go up / offer) up to the maqawam (place) which Yahawah your Alahayam shall bachar (choose);

And you shall bawaa (come) to the kahan (priest) the Lawayay (Levites), and to the shapat (judge) who shall be in those yawam (day): and you shall darash (inquire); and they shall show you the dabar (word / matter) of mashapat (judgment).

You shall ishah (make) pah (according) to the tenor of the sentence which they shall show you from that maqawam (place) which Yahawah shall bachar (choose); and you shall shamar (keep/guard) to ishah (make) according to all that they shall yarah (teach) you:

Pah (according) to the tenor of the thawarah (instruction) which they shall yarah (teach) you, and according to the mashapat (judgment) which they shall amar (spoke) you, you shall ishah (make); you shall not sawar (turn) aside from the dabar (word / matter) which they shall show you, to the right yamayan (right hand), nor to the shamaawal (left hand).

The ayash (husband/individual man) who ishah (make) zadawan (presumptuously), in not shamai (hearken / hear) to the kahan (priest) who imad (stands) to sharath (minister) there before Yahawah your Alahayam, or to the shapat (judge), even that ayash (husband/individual man) shall mawath (death): and you shall bair (put) away the rai (evil) from Yasharaal (Israel).
All the im (people / nation) shall shamai (hearken / hear), and yaraa (fear / be afraid), and do no more zawad (presumptuously).

When you bawaa (come) come to the aratz (Earth/land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you, and shall yarash (possess) it, and shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein, and shall amar (spoke), I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) a malak (king) over me, like all the gaway (nation / people) that are around me;

You shall surely shawam (place / establish / appoint) him malak (king) over yourselves, whom Yahawah your Alahayam shall bachar (choose): one from qarab (among / near) your ach (brother/kinsman) you shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) malak (king) over you; you may not nathan (give) a nakaray (foreigner) over you, who is not your ach (brother/kinsman).

Only he shall not rabah (multiply) sawas (horses) to himself, nor cause the im (people / nation) to shawab (turn back / repent) to Matzarayam (Egypt), to the end that he may rabah (multiply) sawas (horses); because Yahawah has amar (spoke) to you, You shall not shawab (turn back / repent) back that darak (way) again.
Neither shall he rabah (multiply) wives to himself, that his labab (heart) not sawar (turn) away: neither shall he maad (greatly) rabah (multiply) to himself kasap (silver) and zahab (gold).

It shall be, when he yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the kasaa (throne) of his mamalakah (kingdom), that he shall kathab (write) him a mashanah (copy) of this thawarah (instruction) in a sapar (book / scribed document), out of that which is panayam (before) the kahan (priest) the Lawayay (Levites):

And it shall be with him, and he shall qaraa (called) therein all the yawam (day) of his chay (life); that he may lamad (teach/instruct) to yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah his Alahayam, to shamar (keep/guard) all the dabar (word / matter) of this thawarah (instruction) and these chaq (statute), to ishah (make) them;

That his labab (heart) not be rawam (will lift up) up above his ach (brother/kinsman), and that he not sawar (turn) aside from the matzawah (commandment), to the right yamayan (right hand), or to the shamaawal (left hand): to the end that he may prolong his yawam (day) in his mamalakah (kingdom), he and his ban (son), in the qarab (among / near) of Yasharaal (Israel).

The kahan (priest) the Lawayay (Levites), all the shabat (tribe) of Laway (Levi), shall have no chalaq (portion) nor nachalah (inheritance) with Yasharaal (Israel): they shall akal (eat) the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Yahawah made by ashah (wife/individual woman), and his nachalah (inheritance).
They shall have no nachalah (inheritance) qarab (among / near) their ach (brother/kinsman): Yahawah is their nachalah (inheritance), as he has dabar (word / matter) to them.

This shall be the kahan (priest)' mashapat (due) from the im (people / nation), from those who zabach (offer) a zabach (sacrifice), whether it be shawar (ox) or shah (sheep), that they shall nathan (give) to the kahan (priest) the zarawai (shoulder), and the two lachay (cheeks), and the qabah (maw).

The raashayath (beginning) fruits of your grain, of your new thayarawash (wine), and of your yatzahar (fresh oil), and the raashayath (beginning) of the gaz (fleece) of your tzaan (sheep), you shall nathan (give) him.
For Yahawah your Alahayam has bachar (chosen) him out of all your shabat (tribes), to imad (stand) to sharath (minister) in the sham (name) of Yahawah, him and his ban (son) for yawam (day).

If a Lawayay (Levite) bawaa (come) from any of your shair (gates) out of all Yasharaal (Israel), where he lives as a foreigner, and bawaa (come) with all the awah (desire) of his napash (living being/soul) to the maqawam (place) which Yahawah shall bachar (choose);
Then he shall sharath (minister) in the sham (name) of Yahawah his Alahayam, as all his ach (brother/kinsman) the Lawayay (Levites) do, who imad (stand) there panayam (before) Yahawah.
They shall have like chalaq (portions) to akal (eat), besides that which comes of the mamakar (sale) of his ab (father).

When you bawaa (come) come into the aratz (Earth/land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you, you shall not lamad (teach/instruct) to ishah (make) after the thawaibah (abominations) of those gaway (nation / people).

There shall not be matzaa (found) with you anyone who makes his ban (son) or his bath (daughter) to ibar (pass over/through) through the ash (fire), qasam (one) who uses qasam (divination), inan (cloud intepreting / soothsaying / astrology) who practices sorcery, or an nachash (enchanter), or a kashap (sorcerer),
Or a chabar (charmer), or a consulter with a familiar awab (spirit), or a yadainay (wizard), or a darash (necromancer).

For whoever ishah (make) these things is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah: and galal (because) of these thawaibah (abominations) Yahawah your Alahayam does yarash (drive) them out from panayam (before) you.
You shall be thamayam (complete / whole) with Yahawah your Alahayam.

For these gaway (nation / people), that you shall yarash (dispossess), shamai (hearken / hear) to those who practice sorcery, and to diviners; but as for you, Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) not allowed you so to do.

Yahawah your Alahayam will qawam (rise up) up to you a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) from the qarab (among / near) of you, of your ach (brother/kinsman), like me. You shall shamai (hearken / hear) to him.

This is according to all that you shaal (desired) of Yahawah your Alahayam in Charab (Horeb) in the yawam (day) of the qahal (assembly), amar (spoke), shamai (hearken / hear) me not hear again the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah my Alahayam, neither raah (see) me see this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) ash (fire) any more, that I not mawath (death).
Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, They yatab (have) well dabar (word / matter) that which they have spoken.

I will qawam (rise up) them up a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) from qarab (among / near) their ach (brother/kinsman), like you; and I will nathan (give) my dabar (word / matter) in his pah (mouth), and he shall dabar (word / matter) to them all that I shall tzawah (command) him.

It shall happen, that ayash (husband/individual man) will not shamai (hearken / hear) to my dabar (word / matter) which he shall dabar (word / matter) in my sham (name), I will darash (require) it of him.

But the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), who shall dabar (word / matter) a dabar (word / matter) zawad (presumptuously) in my sham (name), which I have not tzawah (commanded) him to dabar (word / matter), or who shall dabar (word / matter) in the sham (name) of other Alahayam, that same nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) shall mawath (death).
If you amar (spoke) in your labab (heart), How shall we yadai (know) the dabar (word / matter) which Yahawah has not dabar (word / matter)?

When a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) dabar (word / matter) in the sham (name) of Yahawah, if the thing doesn't bawaa (come), nor happen, that is the thing which Yahawah has not dabar (word / matter): the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) has dabar (word / matter) it zadawan (presumptuously), you shall not be gawar (afraid) of him.

When Yahawah your Alahayam shall karath (cut) off the gaway (nation / people), whose aratz (Earth/land) Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you, and you yarash (succeed) them, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) in their iyar (cities), and in their bayath (house);
You shall set apart shalawash (three) iyar (cities) for you in the thawak (midst) of your aratz (Earth/land), which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you to yarash (possess) it.

You shall kawan (prepare) you the darak (way), and divide the gabawal (border/boundary) of your aratz (Earth/land), which Yahawah your Alahayam nachal (causes) you to inherit, into shalash (three) parts, that every manslayer may nawas (flee) there.

This is the dabar (word / matter) of the manslayer, that shall nawas (flee) there and chayay (life): whoever nakah (kills) his neighbor unawares, and didn't shanaa (hate) him in thamawal (time) shalashawam (past);

As when a man bawaa (come) into the yair (forest) with his neighbor to chop itz (wood), and his yad (hand) fetches a nadach (stroke) with the axe to karath (cut) down the itz (tree), and the barazal (head) nashal (slips) from the handle, and matzaa (lights) on his neighbor, so that he mawath (death); he shall nawas (flee) to achad (one) of these iyar (cities) and chayay (life):

Lest the gaal (avenger) of dam (blood) radap (pursue) the manslayer, kay (surely) his labab (heart) is yacham (hot), and nashag (overtake) him, because the darak (way) is rabah (long), and strike him mortally; whereas he was not mashapat (worthy) of mawath (death), kay (surely) as he didn't shanaa (hate) him in thamawal (time) shalashawam (past).
Therefore I tzawah (command) you, amar (spoke), You shall set apart shalawash (three) iyar (cities) for yourselves.

If Yahawah your Alahayam enlarges your gabawal (border/boundary), as he has shabai (swear / take oath) to your ab (father), and nathan (give) you all the aratz (Earth/land) which he dabar (word / matter) to nathan (give) to your ab (father);

If you shamar (keep/guard) all this matzawah (commandment) to ishah (make) it, which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), to ahab (love) Yahawah your Alahayam, and to yalak (walk) yawam (day) in his darak (ways); then you shall yasap (add) shalawash (three) iyar (cities) more for yourselves, besides these shalawash (three):

That naqay (innocent) dam (blood) not be shapak (shed) in the midst of your aratz (Earth/land), which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you for an nachalah (inheritance), and so dam (blood) be on you.

But if any ayash (husband/individual man) shanaa (hate) his neighbor, and lies in arab (wait) for him, and qawam (rise up) up against him, and nakah (strikes) him napash (living being/soul) so that he mawath (death), and he nawas (flees) into achad (one) of these iyar (cities);

Then the zaqan (elders) of his iyar (city) shall shalach (send) and laqach (take / seized) him there, and nathan (give) him into the yad (hand) of the gaal (avenger) of dam (blood), that he may mawath (death).
Your iyan (eye) shall not chawas (pity) him, but you shall bair (put) away the naqay (innocent) dam (blood) from Yasharaal (Israel), that it may go well with you.

You shall not nasag (remove) your neighbor's gabawal (border/boundary), which they of raashawan (old) time have gabal (set), in your nachalah (inheritance) which you shall nachal (inherit), in the aratz (Earth/land) that Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you to yarash (possess) it.

Achad (one) id (witness) shall not qawam (rise up) up against a ayash (husband/individual man) for any iwan (guilt/iniquity), or for any chataah (sin), in any chataa (sin) that he chataa (sins): at the pah (mouth) of shanayam (two) witnesses, or at the pah (mouth) of shalawash (three) witnesses, shall a dabar (word / matter) be qawam (rise up).
If an chamas (unrighteous) id (witness) qawam (rise up) up against any ayash (husband/individual man) to inah (answer / respond) against him of wrongdoing,

Then shanayam (two) the ayash (husband/individual man), between whom the rayab (controversy) is, shall imad (stand) panayam (before) Yahawah, panayam (before) the kahan (priest) and the shapat (judges) who shall be in those yawam (day);

And the shapat (judges) shall yatab (make) diligent darash (inquisition): and, behold, if the id (witness) is a shaqar (false) id (witness), and has inah (answer / respond) falsely against his ach (brother/kinsman);
Then you shall ishah (make) to him as he had zamam (thought) to ishah (make) to his ach (brother/kinsman): so you shall bair (put) bair (away) the rai (evil) from the qarab (among / near) of you.
Those who shaar (remain) shall shamai (hearken / hear), and yaraa (fear / be afraid), and shall yasap (henceforth) ishah (make) no more any such rai (evil) in the qarab (among / near) of you.

Your iyan (eye) shall not chawas (pity): napash (living being/soul) for napash (living being/soul), iyan (eye) for iyan (eye), shan (tooth) for shan (tooth), yad (hand) for yad (hand), ragal (feet / foot) for ragal (feet / foot).

When you yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to malachamah (battle) against your ayab (enemy), and raah (see) sawas (horses), rakab (chariots), and a im (people / nation) more than you, you shall not be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of them; for Yahawah your Alahayam is with you, who ilah (go up / offer) you up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
It shall be, when you qarab (come close) near to the malachamah (battle), that the kahan (priest) shall nagash (approach) and dabar (word / matter) to the im (people / nation),

And shall amar (spoke) them, shamai (hearken / hear), Yasharaal (Israel), you qarab (draw) near this yawam (day) to malachamah (battle) against your ayab (enemy): don't let your labab (heart) rakak (faint); don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), nor chapaz (tremble), neither be scared of them;
For Yahawah your Alahayam is he who halak (move) with you, to lacham (fight) for you against your ayab (enemy), to yashai (salvation) you.

The shatar (officers) shall dabar (word / matter) to the im (people / nation), amar (spoke), What ayash (husband/individual man) is there who has banah (built) a chadash (new) bayath (house), and has not chanak (dedicated) it? Yalak (let) him go and shawab (turn back / repent) to his bayath (house), lest he mawath (death) in the malachamah (battle), and achar (other) ayash (husband/individual man) chanak (dedicate) it.

What ayash (husband/individual man) is there who has natai (planted) a karam (vineyard), and has not used its fruit? Yalak (let) him go and shawab (turn back / repent) to his bayath (house), lest he mawath (death) in the malachamah (battle), and achar (other) ayash (husband/individual man) use its fruit.

What ayash (husband/individual man) is there who has pledged to be married a ashah (wife/individual woman), and has not laqach (take / seized) her? Yalak (let) him go and shawab (turn back / repent) to his bayath (house), lest he mawath (death) in the malachamah (battle), and achar (other) ayash (husband/individual man) laqach (take / seized) her.

The shatar (officers) shall dabar (word / matter) yasap (further) to the im (people / nation), and they shall amar (spoke), What ayash (husband/individual man) is there who is yaraa (fearful) and rak (fainthearted)? Yalak (let) him go and shawab (turn back / repent) to his bayath (house), lest his ach (brother/kinsman) labab (heart) masas (melt) as his labab (heart).

It shall be, when the shatar (officers) kalah (complete / finish) made an end of dabar (word / matter) to the im (people / nation), that they shall paqad (visit) shar (prince / ruler) of tzabaa (troop) at the raash (head) of the im (people / nation).
When you qarab (come close) near to a iyar (city) to lacham (fight) against it, then qaraa (called) shalawam (peace / safety) to it.

It shall be, if it makes you inah (answer / respond) of shalawam (peace / safety), and pathach (opens) to you, then it shall be, that all the im (people / nation) who are matzaa (found) therein shall become mas (tributary) to you, and shall ibad (servant) you.
If it will make no shalam (peace) with you, but will ishah (make) malachamah (war) against you, then you shall tzawar (besiege) it:
And when Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) it into your yad (hand), you shall nakah (strike) every zakawar (remember/recall) of it with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword):

But the ashah (wife/individual woman), and the little tap (ones), and the livestock, and all that is in the iyar (city), even all its shalal (spoil), you shall bazaz (take) for a prey to yourself; and you shall akal (eat) the shalal (spoil) of your ayab (enemy), which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) given you.
Thus you shall ishah (make) to all the iyar (cities) which are very rachawaq (far) off from you, which are not of the iyar (cities) of these gaway (nation / people).
But of the iyar (cities) of these im (people / nation), that Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you for an nachalah (inheritance), you shall chayah (save) alive nothing that breathes;

But you shall charam (utterly) charam (destroy) them: the Chathay (Hittite), and the Amaray (Amorite), the Kanainay (Canaanite), and the Parazay (Perizzite), the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite); as Yahawah your Alahayam has tzawah (commanded) you;

That they not lamad (teach/instruct) you to ishah (make) after all their thawaibah (abominations), which they ishah (make) done to their Alahayam; so would you chataa (sin) against Yahawah your Alahayam.

When you shall tzawar (besiege) a iyar (city) a rab (long) yawam (day), in making lacham (war) against it to thapash (take) it, you shall not shachath (destroy) its itz (trees) by wielding an axe against them; for you may akal (eat) of them, and you shall not karath (cut) them down; for is the itz (tree) of the shadah (field) adam (man), that it should be besieged of you?

Only the itz (trees) of which you yadai (know) that they are not itz (trees) for maakal (food), you shall shachath (destroy) and karath (cut) them down; and you shall banah (build) matzawar (bulwarks) against the iyar (city) that ishah (make) malachamah (war) with you, until it yarad (fall).

If one be matzaa (found) chalal (slain) in the adamah (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you to yarash (possess) it, napal (fall / be cast down) in the shadah (field), and it isn't yadai (known) who has nakah (struck) him;
Then your zaqan (elders) and your shapat (judges) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and they shall madad (measure) to the iyar (cities) which are around him who is chalal (slain):

And it shall be, that the iyar (city) which is nearest to the chalal (slain) man, even the zaqan (elders) of that iyar (city) shall laqach (take / seized) a baqar (morning) of the herd, which hasn't been ibad (servant) with, and which has not mashak (drawn) in the il (over);

And the zaqan (elders) of that iyar (city) shall yarad (bring) down the igalah (heifer) to a nachal (stream / river) with running ibad (servant), which is neither plowed nor zarai (sown), and shall irap (break) the igalah (heifer's) irap (neck) there in the nachal (stream / river).

The kahan (priest) the ban (son) of Laway (Levi) shall nagash (come) near; for them Yahawah your Alahayam has bachar (chosen) to sharath (minister) to him, and to barak (bless) in the sham (name) of Yahawah; and according to their pah (word) shall every rayab (controversy) and every nagai (stroke) be.

All the zaqan (elders) of that iyar (city), who are nearest to the chalal (slain) man, shall rachatz (wash) their yad (hand) over the igalah (heifer) whose irap (neck) was broken in the nachal (stream / river);
And they shall inah (answer / respond) and amar (spoke), "Our yad (hand) have not shapak (shed) this dam (blood), neither have our iyan (eye) raah (see) it.

Kapar (forgive), Yahawah, your im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel), whom you have padah (redeemed), and don't allow naqay (innocent) dam (blood) in the qarab (among / near) of your im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel)." The dam (blood) shall be kapar (forgiven) them.
So you shall bair (put) away the naqay (innocent) dam (blood) from the qarab (among / near) of you, when you shall ishah (make) that which is yashar (right) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah.

When you yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to malachamah (battle) against your ayab (enemy), and Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) them into your yad (hand), and you shabah (carry) them shabay (away) captive,

And raah (see) among the shabayah (captives) a thaar (beautiful) ashah (wife/individual woman), and you chashaq (have) a desire to her, and would laqach (take / seized) her to you as ashah (wife/individual woman);
Then you shall bawaa (come) her home to your bayath (house); and she shall galach (shave) her raash (head), and ishah (make) her tzaparan (nails);

And she shall sawar (put) the shamalah (clothing) of her shabayah (captivity) from off her, and shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) in your bayath (house), and bakah (bewail) her ab (father) and her am (mother) a yawam (day) yarach (month): and achar (other) that you shall bawaa (come) in to her, and be her bail (husband), and she shall be your ashah (wife/individual woman).

It shall be, if you chapatz (have) no delight in her, then you shall shalach (send) her go where she napash (living being/soul); but you shall not makar (sell) her at makar (all) for kasap (money), you shall not deal with her as a slave, ashar (who/that) you have inah (oppress / afflict) her.

If a ayash (husband/individual man) have shanayam (two) wives, the achad (one) ahab (love), and the other shanaa (hate), and they have yalad (birth / begot) him ban (son), both the ahab (love) and the shanaa (hate); and if the bakawar (firstborn) ban (son) be hers who was shanayaa (hated);

Then it shall be, in the yawam (day) that he causes his ban (son) to nachal (inherit) that which he yakal (has), that he may not make the ban (son) of the ahab (love) the bakar (firstborn) panayam (before) the ban (son) of the shanaa (hate), who is the bakawar (firstborn):

But he shall nakar (acknowledge) the bakawar (firstborn), the ban (son) of the shanaa (hate), by nathan (give) him a shanayam (two) pah (portion) of all that he matzaa (has); for he is the raashayath (beginning) of his awan (strength); the mashapat (right) of the bakawarah (firstborn) is his.

If a ayash (husband/individual man) have a sarar (stubborn) and rebellious ban (son), who will not shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of his ab (father), or the qawal (sound / voice) of his am (mother), and, though they yasar (chasten) him, will not shamai (hearken / hear) to them;

Then shall his ab (father) and his am (mother) thapash (lay) hold on him, and yatzaa (go out / come out) him out to the zaqan (elders) of his iyar (city), and to the shair (gate) of his maqawam (place);

And they shall amar (spoke) the zaqan (elders) of his iyar (city), This our ban (son) is sarar (stubborn) and rebellious, he will not shamai (hearken / hear) our qawal (sound / voice); he is a zalal (glutton), and a drunkard.

All the ayash (husband/individual man) of his iyar (city) shall ragam (stone) him to mawath (death) with ragam (stones): so you shall bair (put) bair (away) the rai (evil) from the qarab (among / near) of you; and all Yasharaal (Israel) shall shamai (hearken / hear), and yaraa (fear / be afraid).
If a ayash (husband/individual man) have committed a chataa (sin) mashapat (worthy) of mawath (death), and he be put to mawath (death), and you thalah (hang) him on a itz (tree);

His nabalah (body) shall not remain all lawan (night) on the itz (tree), but you shall surely qabar (bury) him the same yawam (day); for he who is hanged is qalalah (accursed) of Alahayam; that you don't tamaa (defile) your adamah (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you for an nachalah (inheritance).

You shall not raah (see) your ach (brother/kinsman) shawar (ox) or his shah (sheep) nadach (go) astray, and ilam (hide) yourself from them: you shall shawab (turn back / repent) shawab (turn back / repent) them again to your ach (brother/kinsman).

If your ach (brother/kinsman) isn't qarawab (near) to you, or if you don't yadai (know) him, then you shall asap (bring) it home to your bayath (house), and it shall be with you until your ach (brother/kinsman) darash (seek) after it, and you shall shawab (turn back / repent) it to him.

So you shall ishah (make) with his donkey; and so you shall ishah (make) with his shamalah (garment); and so you shall ishah (make) with every abadah (lost) thing of your ach (brother/kinsman), which he abad (destroy/perish) lost, and you matzaa (have) found: you may not ilam (hide) yourself.

You shall not raah (see) your ach (brother/kinsman) donkey or his shawar (ox) napal (fall / be cast down) down by the darak (way), and ilam (hide) yourself from them: you shall qawam (rise up) qawam (rise up) him to lift them up again.

A ashah (wife/individual woman) shall not wear gabar (men's) clothing, neither shall a gabar (man) labash (put) on ashah (wife/individual woman) shamalah (clothing); for whoever ishah (make) these things is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah your Alahayam.

If a tzapawar (bird's) qan (nest) qaraa (called) to be panayam (before) you in the darak (way), in any itz (tree) or on the aratz (Earth/land), with aparach (young) ones or bayatzah (eggs), and the hen sitting on the aparach (young), or on the bayatzah (eggs), you shall not laqach (take / seized) the hen with the ban (son):
You shall surely let the hen shalach (send), but the ban (son) you may laqach (take / seized) to yourself; that it may be yatab (well) with you, and that you may prolong your yawam (day).

When you banah (build) a chadash (new) bayath (house), then you shall ishah (make) a maiqah (battlement) for your gag (roof), that you don't shawam (place / establish / appoint) dam (blood) on your bayath (house), if any napal (fall / be cast down) napal (fall / be cast down) from there.

You shall not zarai (sow) your karam (vineyard) with two kinds of zarai (seed), lest the whole malaah (fruit) be forfeited, the zarai (seed) which you have zarai (sown), and the thabawaah (increase) of the karam (vineyard).
You shall not charash (plow) with an shawar (ox) and a donkey yachad (together).
You shall not labash (wear) a mixed stuff, tzamar (wool) and pashathah (linen) yachad (together).
You shall ishah (make) yourselves gadal (fringes) on the arabai (four) kanap (borders) of your cloak, with which you kasah (cover) yourself.
If any ayash (husband/individual man) laqach (take / seized) a ashah (wife/individual woman), and bawaa (come) in to her, and shanaa (hate) her,

And accuses her of shameful things, and yatzaa (go out / come out) up an rai (evil) sham (name) on her, and amar (spoke), I laqach (take / seized) this ashah (wife/individual woman), and when I qarab (come close) near to her, I didn't matzaa (find) in her the tokens of bathawalayam (virginity);

Then shall the ab (father) of the nairah (young) lady, and her am (mother), laqach (take / seized) and yatzaa (go out / come out) forth the tokens of the nairah (young) lady's bathawalayam (virginity) to the zaqan (elders) of the iyar (city) in the shair (gate);

And the nairah (young) lady's ab (father) shall amar (spoke) the zaqan (elders), "I nathan (give) my bath (daughter) to this ayash (husband/individual man) to ashah (wife/individual woman), and he shanaa (hate) her;

And behold, he has accused her of shameful things, amar (spoke), ‘I didn't matzaa (find) in your bath (daughter) the tokens of bathawalayam (virginity);’ and yet these are the tokens of my bath (daughter) bathawalayam (virginity)." They shall parash (spread) the shamalah (cloth) panayam (before) the zaqan (elders) of the iyar (city).
