Yadai (know) for a certainty that Yahawah your Alahayam will no yasap (longer) drive these gaway (nation / people) from out of your panayam (sight); but they shall be a pach (snare) and a mawaqash (trap) to you, a shatat (scourge) in your tzad (sides), and tzanayan (thorns) in your iyan (eye), until you abad (destroy/perish) from off this tawab (pleasant/functional) adamah (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) given you.

Behold, today I am halak (move) the darak (way) of all the aratz (Earth/land). You yadai (know) in all your labab (hearts) and in all your napash (living being/soul) that not achad (one) thing napal (fall / be cast down) failed of all the tawab (pleasant/functional) things which Yahawah your Alahayam dabar (word / matter) concerning you. All bawaa (come) happened to you. Not achad (one) thing napal (fall / be cast down) failed of it.

It shall happen that as all the tawab (pleasant/functional) things bawaa (come) come on you of which Yahawah your Alahayam dabar (word / matter) to you, so Yahawah will bawaa (come) on you all the rai (evil) things, until he has destroyed you from off this tawab (pleasant/functional) adamah (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) given you,

When you disobey the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah your Alahayam, which he tzawah (commanded) you, and halak (move) and ibad (servant) other Alahayam, and shachah (bow) down yourselves to them. Then the ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah will be charah (hot with anger) against you, and you will abad (destroy/perish) maharah (quickly) from off the tawab (pleasant/functional) aratz (Earth/land) which he nathan (give) given to you.

Yahawashawai (Joshua) asap (gathered) all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) to Shakam (Shechem), and qaraa (called) for the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel), for their raash (head), for their shapat (judges), and for their shatar (officers); and they yatzab (presented) panayam (themselves) before Alahayam.

Yahawashawai (Joshua) amar (spoke) to all the im (people / nation), Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘Your ab (father) lived of iwalam (forever) time ibar (beyond) the nahar (river), even Tharach (Terah), the ab (father) of Abaraham (Abraham), and the ab (father) of Nachawar (Nahor): and they ibad (servant) other Alahayam.

I laqach (take / seized) your ab (father) Abaraham (Abraham) from ibar (beyond) the nahar (river), and yalak (led) him throughout all the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), and rabah (multiplied) his zarai (seed), and nathan (give) him Yatzachaq (Isaac).

I nathan (give) to Yatzachaq (Isaac) Yaiqab (Jacob) and Ishaw (Esau): and I nathan (give) to Ishaw (Esau) har (mountain) Shaiyar (Seir), to yarash (possess) it. Yaiqab (Jacob) and his ban (son) yarad (went) down into Matzarayam (Egypt).

‘I shalach (send) Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron), and I nagap (plagued) Matzarayam (Egypt), according to that which I ishah (make) in its qarab (among / near): and afterward I yatzaa (go out / come out) you out.

I yatzaa (go out / come out) your ab (father) out of Matzarayam (Egypt): and you bawaa (come) to the yam (sea/waters). The Matzarayam (Egyptians) radap (pursued) achar (other) your ab (father) with rakab (chariots) and with horsemen to the sawap (red) yam (sea/waters).

When they tzaiq (cried) out to Yahawah, he shawam (place / establish / appoint) maapal (darkness) between you and the Matzaray (Egyptians), and bawaa (come) the yam (sea/waters) on them, and kasah (covered) them; and your iyan (eye) raah (see) what I ishah (make) in Matzarayam (Egypt): and you lived in the madabar (wilderness) many yawam (day).

‘I bawaa (come) you into the aratz (Earth/land) of the Amaray (Amorites), that lived ibar (beyond) the Yaradan (Jordan): and they lacham (fought) with you; and I nathan (give) them into your yad (hand). You yarash (possessed) their aratz (Earth/land); and I destroyed them from panayam (before) you.

Then Balaq (Balak) the ban (son) of Tzapawar (Zippor), malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab), qawam (rise up) and lacham (fought) against Yasharaal (Israel). He shalach (send) and qaraa (called) Balaim (Balaam) the ban (son) of Baiwar (Beor) to qalal (curse) you;
But I would not shamai (hearken / hear) to Balaim (Balaam); therefore he barak (blessed) you still. So I natzal (delivered) you out of his yad (hand).

‘You ibar (pass over/through) over the Yaradan (Jordan), and bawaa (come) to Yarayachaw (Jericho). The bail (men) of Yarayachaw (Jericho) lacham (fought) against you, the Amaray (Amorite), the Parazay (Perizzite), the Kanainay (Canaanite), the Chathay (Hittite), the Garagashay (Girgashite), the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite); and I nathan (give) them into your yad (hand).

I shalach (send) the tzaraih (hornet) panayam (before) you, which garash (drove) them out from panayam (before) you, even the shanayam (two) malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites); not with your charab (sword), nor with your qashath (bow).

I nathan (give) you a aratz (Earth/land) whereon you had not labored, and iyar (cities) which you didn't banah (build), and you live in them. You akal (eat) of karam (vineyards) and zayath (olive) groves which you didn't natai (plant).’

Now therefore yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah, and ibad (servant) him in thamayam (complete / whole) and in amath (truth). Sawar (put) away the Alahayam which your ab (father) ibad (servant) ibar (beyond) the nahar (river), in Matzarayam (Egypt); and ibad (servant) Yahawah.

If it seems rai (evil) to you to ibad (servant) Yahawah, bachar (choose) this yawam (day) whom you will ibad (servant); whether the Alahayam which your ab (father) ibad (servant) that were ibar (beyond) the nahar (river), or the Alahayam of the Amaray (Amorites), in whose aratz (Earth/land) you yashab (inhabit/dwell): but as for me and my bayath (house), we will ibad (servant) Yahawah.
The im (people / nation) inah (answer / respond), chalayalah (far) be it from us that we should izab (forsake) Yahawah, to ibad (servant) other Alahayam;

For it is Yahawah our Alahayam who brought us and our ab (father) up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), from the bayath (house) of ibad (servant), and who ishah (make) those gadawal (very great/important/mighty) awath (sign / mark / miracle) in our iyan (eye), and shamar (keep/guard) us in all the darak (way) in which we halak (move), and among all the im (people / nation) qarab (among / near) the midst of whom we ibar (pass over/through).

Yahawah garash (drove) out from panayam (before) us all the im (people / nation), even the Amaray (Amorites) who lived in the aratz (Earth/land). Therefore we also will ibad (servant) Yahawah; for he is our Alahayam.

Yahawashawai (Joshua) amar (spoke) to the im (people / nation), You can't ibad (servant) Yahawah; for he is a qadawash (holy) Alahayam. He is a qanawaa (jealous) Alahayam. He will not nashaa (lift) your disobedience nor your chataah (sin).

If you izab (forsake) Yahawah, and ibad (servant) foreign Alahayam, then he will shawab (turn back / repent) and do you raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil), and kalah (complete / finish) you, achar (other) he has done you yatab (good).
The im (people / nation) amar (spoke) to Yahawashawai (Joshua), No; but we will ibad (servant) Yahawah.

Yahawashawai (Joshua) amar (spoke) to the im (people / nation), "You are witnesses against yourselves that you have bachar (chosen) Yahawah yourselves, to ibad (servant) him." They amar (spoke), We are witnesses.
Now therefore sawar (put) away the foreign Alahayam which are qarab (among / near) you, and natah (incline) your labab (heart) to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
The im (people / nation) amar (spoke) to Yahawashawai (Joshua), We will ibad (servant) Yahawah our Alahayam, and we will shamai (hearken / hear) to his qawal (sound / voice).

So Yahawashawai (Joshua) karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with the im (people / nation) that yawam (day), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) for them a chaq (statute) and an mashapat (ordinance) in Shakam (Shechem).

Yahawashawai (Joshua) kathab (wrote) these dabar (word / matter) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the thawarah (instruction) of Alahayam; and he laqach (take / seized) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) aban (stone), and qawam (rise up) it up there under the alah (these) that was by the maqadash (sanctuary) of Yahawah.

Yahawashawai (Joshua) amar (spoke) to all the im (people / nation), Behold, this aban (stone) shall be a idah (witness) against us; for it has shamai (hearken / hear) all the amar (spoke) of Yahawah which he dabar (word / matter) to us. It shall be therefore a idah (witness) against you, lest you kachash (deny) your Alahayam.
So Yahawashawai (Joshua) sent the im (people / nation) shalach (send), every ayash (husband/individual man) to his nachalah (inheritance).

It happened achar (other) these things, that Yahawashawai (Joshua) the ban (son) of Nawan (Nun), the ibad (servant) of Yahawah, mawath (death), being one maah (hundred) and ishar (ten) shanah (years) ban (son).

They qabar (bury) him in the gabawal (border/boundary) of his nachalah (inheritance) in Thamanathacharas (Timnathserah), which is in the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), on the tzapawan (north) of the har (mountain) of Gaish (Gaash).

Yasharaal (Israel) ibad (servant) Yahawah all the yawam (day) of Yahawashawai (Joshua), and all the yawam (day) of the zaqan (elders) who yawam (day) Yahawashawai (Joshua), and yadai (had) known all the maishah (work) of Yahawah, that he ishah (make) worked for Yasharaal (Israel).

They qabar (bury) the itzam (bones) of Yawasap (Joseph), which the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up out of Matzarayam (Egypt), in Shakam (Shechem), in the chalaqah (parcel) of shadah (ground) which Yaiqab (Jacob) bought of the ban (son) of Chamawar (Hamor) the ab (father) of Shakam (Shechem) for a maah (hundred) qashayatah (pieces) of money. They became the nachalah (inheritance) of the ban (son) of Yawasap (Joseph).

Alaizar (Eleazar) the ban (son) of Aharawan (Aaron) mawath (death). They qabar (bury) him in the gabaih (hill) of Payanachas (Phinehas) his ban (son), which was nathan (give) him in the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim).

It happened achar (other) the mawath (death) of Yahawashawai (Joshua), the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) shaal (asked) of Yahawah, amar (spoke), Who should ilah (go up / offer) up for us thachalah (first) against the Kanainay (Canaanites), to lacham (fight) against them?
Yahawah amar (spoke), Yahawadah (Judah) shall ilah (go up / offer) up. Behold, I nathan (give) delivered the aratz (Earth/land) into his yad (hand).

Yahawadah (Judah) amar (spoke) to Shamaiwan (Simeon) his ach (brother/kinsman), "ilah (go up / offer) up with me into my gawaral (lot), that we may lacham (fight) against the Kanainay (Canaanites); and I likewise will halak (move) with you into your gawaral (lot)." So Shamaiwan (Simeon) yalak (went) with him.

Yahawadah (Judah) ilah (go up / offer) up; and Yahawah nathan (give) the Kanainay (Canaanites) and the Parazay (Perizzites) into their yad (hand): and they nakah (struck) of them in Bazaq (Bezek) ishar (ten) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man).
They matzaa (found) Adanayabazaq (Adoni-Bezek) in Bazaq (Bezek); and they lacham (fought) against him, and they nakah (struck) the Kanainay (Canaanites) and the Parazay (Perizzites).
But Adanayabazaq (Adoni-Bezek) nawas (fled); and they radap (pursued) achar (other) him, and achaz (caught) him, and qatzatz (cut) off his bahan (thumbs) and his ragal (feet / foot) toes.

Adanayabazaq (Adoni-Bezek) amar (spoke), "shabaiyam (seventy) malak (king), having their bahan (thumbs) and their ragal (feet / foot) toes qatzatz (cut) off, scavenged under my shalachan (table): as I ishah (make) done, so Alahayam has shalam (requited) me." They bawaa (come) him to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and he mawath (death) there.

The ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah) lacham (fought) against Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and lakad (took) it, and nakah (struck) it with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), and shalach (send) the iyar (city) on ash (fire).

Afterward the ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah) yarad (went) down to lacham (fight) against the Kanainay (Canaanites) who lived in the har (mountain) nagab (country), and in the South, and in the lowland.

Yahawadah (Judah) yalak (went) against the Kanainay (Canaanites) who lived in Chabarawan (Hebron) (now the sham (name) of Chabarawan (Hebron) panayam (before) was Kiriath Qarayathaarabai (Arba)); and they nakah (struck) Shashay (Sheshai), and Achayaman (Ahiman), and Thalamay (Talmai).
From there he yalak (went) against the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Dabayar (Debir). (Now the sham (name) of Dabayar (Debir) panayam (before) was Kiriath Qarayathasanah (Sepher).)

Kalab (Caleb) amar (spoke), He who nakah (strikes) Kiriath Qarayathasanah (Sepher), and lakad (takes) it, to him will I nathan (give) Ikasah (Achsah) my bath (daughter) as ashah (wife/individual woman).

Ithanayaal (Othniel) the ban (son) of Qanaz (Kenaz), Kalab (Caleb's) younger ach (brother/kinsman), lakad (took) it: and he nathan (give) him Ikasah (Achsah) his bath (daughter) as ashah (wife/individual woman).

It happened, when she bawaa (come), that she got him to shaal (ask) her ab (father) for a shadah (field): and she alighted from off her donkey; and Kalab (Caleb) amar (spoke) to her, What would you like?

She amar (spoke) to him, "yahab (give) me a barakah (blessing); for that you nathan (give) set me in the aratz (Earth/land) of the nagab (south), nathan (give) me also galah (spring / basin / bowl) of mayam (Waters)." Then Kalab (Caleb) nathan (give) her the ilay (went up) galah (spring / basin / bowl) and the lower galah (spring / basin / bowl).

The ban (son) of the Qayanay (Kenite), Mashah (Moses)' brother-in-law, ilah (go up / offer) up out of the iyar (city) of thamar (palm) trees with the ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah) into the madabar (wilderness) of Yahawadah (Judah), which is in the nagab (south) of Irad (Arad); and they yalak (went) and lived with the im (people / nation).

Yahawadah (Judah) yalak (went) with Shamaiwan (Simeon) his ach (brother/kinsman), and they nakah (struck) the Kanainay (Canaanites) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) Tzapath (Zephath), and charam (utterly) destroyed it. The sham (name) of the iyar (city) was qaraa (called) Charamah (Hormah).

Also Yahawadah (Judah) lakad (took) Izah (Gaza) with its gabawal (border/boundary), and Ashaqalawan (Ashkelon) with its gabawal (border/boundary), and Iqarawan (Ekron) with its gabawal (border/boundary).

Yahawah was with Yahawadah (Judah); and yarash (drove) out the inhabitants of the har (mountain) country; for he could not yarash (drive) out the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the imaq (valley), because they had rakab (chariots) of barazal (iron).
They nathan (give) Chabarawan (Hebron) to Kalab (Caleb), as Mashah (Moses) had dabar (word / matter): and he yarash (drove) out there the shalawash (three) ban (son) of Inaq (Anak).

The ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) did not yarash (drive) out the Yabawasay (Jebusites) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); but the Yabawasay (Jebusites) yashab (inhabit/dwell) with the ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) to this yawam (day).
The bayath (house) of Yawasap (Joseph), they also ilah (go up / offer) up against Bayathaal (Bethel); and Yahawah was with them.
The bayath (house) of Yawasap (Joseph) thawar (sent) to spy out Bayathaal (Bethel). (Now the sham (name) of the iyar (city) panayam (before) was Lawaz (Luz).)

The watchers raah (see) a ayash (husband/individual man) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the iyar (city), and they amar (spoke) to him, Please show us the mabawaa (entrance) into the iyar (city), and we will ishah (make) chasad (grace) with you.

He showed them the mabawaa (entrance) into the iyar (city); and they nakah (struck) the iyar (city) with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword); but they let the ayash (husband/individual man) shalach (send) and all his mashapachah (tribe/clan/family).

The ayash (husband/individual man) yalak (went) into the aratz (Earth/land) of the Chathay (Hittites), and banah (built) a iyar (city), and qaraa (called) its sham (name) Lawaz (Luz), which is its sham (name) to this yawam (day).

Manashah (Manasseh) did not yarash (drive) out the inhabitants of Bayathashaan (Beth) Shean and its bath (daughter), nor Thainak (Taanach) and its bath (daughter), nor the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Dawar (Dor) and its bath (daughter), nor the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Yabalaim (Ibleam) and its bath (daughter), nor the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Magadawan (Megiddo) and its bath (daughter); but the Kanainay (Canaanites) yaal (would) yashab (inhabit/dwell) in that aratz (Earth/land).

It happened, when Yasharaal (Israel) had grown chazaq (strong), that they shawam (place / establish / appoint) the Kanainay (Canaanites) to forced mas (labor), and did not yarash (utterly) yarash (drive) them out.
Aparayam (Ephraim) didn't yarash (drive) out the Kanainay (Canaanites) who lived in Gazar (Gezer); but the Kanainay (Canaanites) lived in Gazar (Gezer) qarab (among / near) them.

Zabawalawan (Zebulun) didn't yarash (drive) out the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Qatarawan (Kitron), nor the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Nahalal (Nahalol); but the Kanainay (Canaanites) lived qarab (among / near) them, and became subject to forced mas (labor).

Ashar (Asher) didn't yarash (drive) out the yashab (inhabit/dwell) Ikaw (of) Acco, nor the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Tzayadawan (Sidon), nor of Achalab (Ahlab), nor of Akazayab (Achzib), nor of Chalabah (Helbah), nor of Apaq (Aphik), nor of Rachab (Rehob);
But the Asharay (Asherites) lived qarab (among / near) the Kanainay (Canaanites), the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the aratz (Earth/land); for they did not yarash (drive) them out.

Napathalay (Naphtali) didn't yarash (drive) out the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Bayathashamash (Beth) Shemesh, nor the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Bayathainath (Beth) Anath; but he lived qarab (among / near) the Kanainay (Canaanites), the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the aratz (Earth/land): nevertheless the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Bayathashamash (Beth) Shemesh and of Bayathainath (Beth) Anath became subject to forced mas (labor).
The Amaray (Amorites) lachatz (forced) the ban (son) Dan (of) Dan into the har (mountain) country; for they nathan (give) not allow them to yarad (come) down to the imaq (valley);

But the Amaray (Amorites) yaal (would) yashab (inhabit/dwell) in har (mountain) Charas (Heres), in Ayalawan (Aijalon), and in Shailabayam (Shaalbim): yet the yad (hand) of the bayath (house) of Yawasap (Joseph) kabad (prevailed), so that they became subject to forced mas (labor).
The gabawal (border/boundary) of the Amaray (Amorites) was from the mailahaiqarabayam (ascent) of mailahaiqarabayam (akrabbim), from the salai (rock), and upward.

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah ilah (go up / offer) up from Galagal (Gilgal) to Bakayam (Bochim). He amar (spoke), I ilah (go up / offer) you to go up out of Matzarayam (Egypt), and bawaa (come) brought you to the aratz (Earth/land) which I shabai (swear / take oath) to your ab (father); and I amar (spoke), ‘I will iwalam (forever) parar (break) my barayath (covenant) with you:

And you shall karath (cut) no barayath (covenant) with the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of this aratz (Earth/land); you shall nathatz (break) down their mazabach (altars).’ But you have not shamai (hearken / hear) to my qawal (sound / voice): why ishah (make) you done this?
Therefore I also amar (spoke), I will not garash (drive) them out from panayam (before) you; but they shall be in your tzad (sides), and their Alahayam shall be a mawaqash (snare) to you.

It happened, when the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah dabar (word / matter) these dabar (word / matter) to all the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), that the im (people / nation) nashaa (lift) up their qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept).
They qaraa (called) the sham (name) of that maqawam (place) Bakayam (Bochim): and they zabach (sacrificed) there to Yahawah.

Now when Yahawashawai (Joshua) had sent the im (people / nation) shalach (send), the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) yalak (went) every ayash (husband/individual man) to his nachalah (inheritance) to yarash (possess) the aratz (Earth/land).

The im (people / nation) ibad (servant) Yahawah all the yawam (day) of Yahawashawai (Joshua), and all the yawam (day) of the zaqan (elders) who yawam (day) Yahawashawai (Joshua), who raah (see) seen all the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) maishah (work) of Yahawah that he ishah (make) worked for Yasharaal (Israel).
Yahawashawai (Joshua) the ban (son) of Nawan (Nun), the ibad (servant) of Yahawah, mawath (death), being one maah (hundred) ishar (ten) shanah (years) ban (son).
They qabar (bury) him in the gabawal (border/boundary) of his nachalah (inheritance) in Timnath Heres, in the hill country of Aparayam (Ephraim), on the north of the har (mountain) of Gaish (Gaash).

Also all that dawar (generation / age / period) were asap (gathered) to their ab (father): and there qawam (rise up) achar (other) dawar (generation / age / period) achar (other) them, who didn't yadai (know) Yahawah, nor yet the maishah (work) which he ishah (make) worked for Yasharaal (Israel).
The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, and ibad (servant) the Bail (Baals);

And they forsook Yahawah, the Alahayam of their ab (father), who yatzaa (go out / come out) them out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and yalak (followed) other Alahayam, of the Alahayam of the im (people / nation) who were around them, and shachah (bowed) themselves down to them: and they provoked Yahawah to kais (anger).
They forsook Yahawah, and ibad (servant) Bail (Baal) and the Ishatharawath (Ashtaroth).

The ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah was charah (hot with anger) against Yasharaal (Israel), and he nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of shasah (spoilers) who despoiled them; and he makar (sold) them into the yad (hand) of their ayab (enemy) all around, so that they yakal (could) not any iwad (more/again) imad (stand) panayam (before) their ayab (enemy).

Wherever they yatzaa (go out / come out) out, the yad (hand) of Yahawah was against them for rai (evil), as Yahawah had dabar (word / matter), and as Yahawah had shabai (swear / take oath) to them: and they were very yatzar (distressed).
Yahawah qawam (rise up) up shapat (judges), who yashai (salvation) them out of the yad (hand) of those who despoiled them.

Yet they didn't shamai (hearken / hear) to their shapat (judges); for they zanah (played) the prostitute achar (other) other Alahayam, and shachah (bowed) themselves down to them: they sawar (turned) aside mahar (quickly) out of the darak (way) in which their ab (father) halak (move), shamai (hearken / hear) the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah. They didn't ishah (make) so.

When Yahawah qawam (rise up) them up shapat (judges), then Yahawah was with the shapat (judge), and yashai (salvation) them out of the yad (hand) of their ayab (enemy) all the yawam (day) of the shapat (judge): for it grieved Yahawah panayam (because) of their naaqah (groaning) by reason of those who lachatz (oppressed) them and troubled them.

But it happened, when the shapat (judge) was mawath (death), that they shawab (turn back / repent) back, and dealt more corruptly than their ab (father), in yalak (following) other Alahayam to ibad (servant) them, and to shachah (bow) down to them; they didn't napal (fall / be cast down) from their mailal (doings), nor from their qashah (rough / hard) darak (way).

The ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah was charah (hot with anger) against Yasharaal (Israel); and he amar (spoke), Because this gaway (nation / people) ibar (pass over/through) transgressed my barayath (covenant) which I tzawah (commanded) their ab (father), and have not shamai (hearken / hear) to my qawal (sound / voice);
I also will not yasap (henceforth) yarash (drive) out any from panayam (before) them of the gaway (nation / people) that Yahawashawai (Joshua) izab (left) when he mawath (death);
That by them I may nasah (prove) Yasharaal (Israel), whether they will shamar (keep/guard) the darak (way) of Yahawah to yalak (walk) therein, as their ab (father) shamar (keep/guard) it, or not.
So Yahawah yanach (left) those gaway (nation / people), balathay (without) yarash (driving) them out mahar (hastily); neither nathan (give) he them into the yad (hand) of Yahawashawai (Joshua).
Now these are the gaway (nation / people) which Yahawah yanach (left), to nasah (prove) Yasharaal (Israel) by them, even as many as yadai (had) not known all the malachamah (wars) of Kanain (Canaan);

Only that the dawar (generation / age / period) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) might yadai (know), to lamad (teach/instruct) them malachamah (war), at the least such as panayam (before) yadai (knew) nothing of it:

The chamash (five) saran (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and all the Kanainay (Canaanites), and the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), and the Chaway (Hivites) who lived on har (mountain) Labanawan (Lebanon), from har (mountain) Bailacharamawan (Baal) Hermon to the entrance of Chamath (Hamath).

They were left to test Yasharaal (Israel) by them, to yadai (know) whether they would shamai (hearken / hear) to the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah, which he tzawah (commanded) their ab (father) by Mashah (Moses).

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) lived qarab (among / near) the Kanainay (Canaanites), the Chathay (Hittites), and the Amaray (Amorites), and the Parazay (Perizzites), and the Chaway (Hivites), and the Yabawasay (Jebusites):
And they laqach (take / seized) their bath (daughter) to be their wives, and nathan (give) their own bath (daughter) to their ban (son) and ibad (servant) their Alahayam.

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, and shakach (forgot) Yahawah their Alahayam, and ibad (servant) the Bail (Baals) and the Asharah (Asheroth).

Therefore the ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah was charah (hot with anger) against Yasharaal (Israel), and he makar (sold) them into the yad (hand) Kawashanarashaithayam (of) Cushan Rishathaim malak (king) of Aramanaharayam (Mesopotamia): and the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) ibad (servant) Kawashanarashaithayam (Cushan) Rishathaim shamanah (eight) shanah (years).

When the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) zaiq (cried) to Yahawah, Yahawah qawam (rise up) up a savior to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), who yashai (salvation) them, even Ithanayaal (Othniel) the ban (son) of Qanaz (Kenaz), Kalab (Caleb's) younger ach (brother/kinsman).

The rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah came on him, and he shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel); and he yatzaa (go out / come out) out to malachamah (war), and Yahawah nathan (give) Kawashanarashaithayam (Cushan) Rishathaim malak (king) of Aram (Mesopotamia) into his yad (hand): and his yad (hand) izaz (prevailed) Kawashanarashaithayam (against) Cushan Rishathaim.
The aratz (Earth/land) had shaqat (rest) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years). Ithanayaal (Othniel) the ban (son) of Qanaz (Kenaz) mawath (death).

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) again ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah: and Yahawah chazaq (strengthened) Igalawan (Eglon) the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab) against Yasharaal (Israel), because they ishah (make) done that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah.

He asap (gathered) to him the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) and Imalaq (Amalek); and he yalak (went) and nakah (struck) Yasharaal (Israel), and they yarash (possessed) the iyar (city) of thamar (palm) trees.
The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) ibad (servant) Igalawan (Eglon) the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab) eighteen shanah (years).

But when the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) zaiq (cried) to Yahawah, Yahawah qawam (rise up) them up a savior, Ahawad (Ehud) the ban (son) of Garaa (Gera), the Banayamayanay (Benjamite), a ayash (husband/individual man) atar (left-handed). The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) shalach (send) tribute by him to Igalawan (Eglon) the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab).
Ahawad (Ehud) ishah (make) him a charab (sword) which had shanayam (two) payah (edges), a gamad (cubit) in arak (length); and he wore it under his clothing on his yamayan (right hand) yarak (thigh).
He qarab (come close) the tribute to Igalawan (Eglon) malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab): now Igalawan (Eglon) was a very barayaa (fat) ayash (husband/individual man).
When he kalah (complete / finish) made an end of qarab (come close) the tribute, he shalach (send) away the im (people / nation) who nashaa (lift) the tribute.

But he himself shawab (turn back / repent) back from the pasayal (quarries) that were by Galagal (Gilgal), and amar (spoke), "I have a sathar (secret / hidden) dabar (word / matter) to you, malak (king)." The king amar (spoke), "Keep hasah (silence)!" All who imad (stood) by him yatzaa (go out / come out) out from him.

Ahawad (Ehud) bawaa (come) to him; and he was sitting by himself maqarah (alone) in the cool upper room. Ahawad (Ehud) amar (spoke), "I have a dabar (word / matter) from Alahayam to you." He qawam (rise up) out of his kasaa (seat).

Ahawad (Ehud) shalach (send) forth his shamaawal (left hand) yad (hand), and laqach (take / seized) the charab (sword) from his yamayan (right hand) yarak (thigh), and thaqai (blow / sound alarm) it into his batan (body):

And the handle also bawaa (come) in achar (other) the lahab (blade); and the chalab (fat) sagar (closed) on the lahab (blade), for he didn't shalap (draw) the charab (sword) out of his batan (body); and it yatzaa (go out / come out) out behind.
Then Ahawad (Ehud) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth into the masadarawan (porch), and sagar (shut) the dalath (doors) of the upper room on him, and nail (locked) them.

Now when he was yatzaa (go out / come out) out, his ibad (servant) bawaa (come); and they raah (see), and behold, the dalath (doors) of the upper room were nail (locked); and they amar (spoke), Surely he is sakak (covering) his ragal (feet / foot) in the upper room.

They chawal (waited) until they were bawash (ashamed); and behold, he didn't pathach (open) the dalath (doors) of the upper room: therefore they laqach (take / seized) the mapathach (key), and pathach (opened) them, and behold, their Adawan was napal (fall / be cast down) down mawath (death) on the aratz (Earth/land).
Ahawad (Ehud) malat (escaped) while they waited, and ibar (pass over/through) beyond the pasayal (quarries), and malat (escaped) Shaiyarah (to) Seirah.

It happened, when he bawaa (come) come, that he thaqai (blow / sound alarm) a shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)) in the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim); and the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) yarad (went) down with him from the har (mountain) country, and he panayam (before) them.

He amar (spoke) to them, "radap (follow) me; for Yahawah nathan (give) delivered your ayab (enemy) the Mawaab (Moabites) into your yad (hand)." They followed him, and lakad (took) the maibar (fords) of the Yaradan (Jordan) Mawaab (against) the Moabites, and didn't allow any ayash (husband/individual man) to ibar (pass over/through) over.

They nakah (struck) of Mawaab (Moab) at that ith (time) about ishar (ten) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man), every shaman (lusty) ayash (husband/individual man), and every man of valor; and there malat (escaped) not a ayash (husband/individual man).
So Mawaab (Moab) was kanai (subdued) that yawam (day) under the yad (hand) of Yasharaal (Israel). The aratz (Earth/land) had shaqat (rest) shamanayam (eighty) shanah (years).

Achar (other) him was Shamagar (Shamgar) the ban (son) of Inath (Anath), who nakah (struck) of the Palashathay (Philistines) shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man) with an baqar (morning) - malamad (goad): and he also yashai (salvation) Yasharaal (Israel).
The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) again ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, when Ahawad (Ehud) was mawath (death).

Yahawah makar (sold) them into the yad (hand) of Yabayan (Jabin) malak (king) of Kanain (Canaan), who malak (king) in Chatzawar (Hazor); the shar (prince / ruler) of whose tzabaa (troop) was Sayasaraa (Sisera), who lived in Charashath (Harosheth) of the gaway (nation / people).

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) tzaiq (cried) to Yahawah: for he had thashai (nine) maah (hundred) rakab (chariots) of barazal (iron); and isharayam (twenty) shanah (years) he chazaqah (mightily) lachatz (oppressed) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel).
Now Dabawarah (Deborah), a nabayaah (prophetess), the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Lapayadawath (Lappidoth), she shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel) at that ith (time).

She lived under the thamar (palm) tree of Dabawarah (Deborah) between Ramah (Ramah) and Bayathaal (Bethel) in the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim): and the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up to her for mashapat (judgment).

She shalach (send) and qaraa (called) Baraq (Barak) the ban (son) of Abayanaim (Abinoam) out of Qadash (Kedesh) Naphtali, and amar (spoke) to him, Hasn't Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), tzawah (commanded), ‘yalak (go) and mashak (draw) to har (mountain) Thabawar (Tabor), and laqach (take / seized) with you ishar (ten) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man) of the ban (son) of Napathalay (Naphtali) and of the ban (son) of Zabawalawan (Zebulun)?

I will mashak (draw) to you, to the nachal (stream / river) Qayashawan (Kishon), Sayasaraa (Sisera), the shar (prince / ruler) of Yabayan (Jabin's) tzabaa (troop), with his rakab (chariots) and his hamawan (multitude); and I will nathan (give) him into your yad (hand).’
Baraq (Barak) amar (spoke) to her, If you will yalak (go) with me, then I will yalak (go); but if you will not halak (move) with me, I will not yalak (go).

She amar (spoke), "I will halak (move) yalak (go) with you: apas (nevertheless), the darak (journey) that you take shall not be for your honor; for Yahawah will makar (sell) Sayasaraa (Sisera) into the yad (hand) of a ashah (wife/individual woman)." Dabawarah (Deborah) qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) with Baraq (Barak) to Qadash (Kedesh).

Baraq (Barak) zaiq (called) Zabawalawan (Zebulun) and Napathalay (Naphtali) together to Qadash (Kedesh); and there ilah (go up / offer) up ishar (ten) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man) at his ragal (feet / foot): and Dabawarah (Deborah) ilah (go up / offer) up with him.

Now Chabar (Heber) the Qayanay (Kenite) had parad (separated) himself from the Qayanay (Kenites), even from the ban (son) of Chabab (Hobab) the brother-in-law of Mashah (Moses), and had natah (pitched) his ahal (tent) as far as the oak Tzainanayam (in) Zaanannim, which is by Qadash (Kedesh).
They nagad (told) Sayasaraa (Sisera) that Baraq (Barak) the ban (son) of Abayanaim (Abinoam) was ilah (go up / offer) up to har (mountain) Thabawar (Tabor).

Sayasaraa (Sisera) zaiq (gathered) together all his rakab (chariots), even thashai (nine) maah (hundred) rakab (chariots) of barazal (iron), and all the im (people / nation) who were with him, from Charashath (Harosheth) of the gaway (nation / people), to the nachal (stream / river) Qayashawan (Kishon).

Dabawarah (Deborah) amar (spoke) to Baraq (Barak), "Go; for this is the yawam (day) in which Yahawah nathan (give) delivered Sayasaraa (Sisera) into your yad (hand). Hasn't Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) out panayam (before) you?" So Baraq (Barak) yarad (went) down from har (mountain) Thabawar (Tabor), and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man) achar (other) him.

Yahawah confused Sayasaraa (Sisera), and all his rakab (chariots), and all his machanah (army), with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword) panayam (before) Baraq (Barak); and Sayasaraa (Sisera) alighted from his marakabah (chariot), and nawas (fled) away on his ragal (feet / foot).

But Baraq (Barak) radap (pursued) achar (other) the rakab (chariots), and after the machanah (army), to Charashath (Harosheth) of the gaway (nation / people): and all the machanah (army) of Sayasaraa (Sisera) napal (fall / be cast down) by the pah (edge) of the charab (sword); there was not a achad (one) shaar (left).

However Sayasaraa (Sisera) nawas (fled) away on his ragal (feet / foot) to the ahal (tent) of Yail (Jael) the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Chabar (Heber) the Qayanay (Kenite); for there was shalawam (peace / safety) between Yabayan (Jabin) the malak (king) of Chatzawar (Hazor) and the bayath (house) of Chabar (Heber) the Qayanay (Kenite).

Yail (Jael) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) Sayasaraa (Sisera), and amar (spoke) to him, "sawar (turn) in, my Adawan, sawar (turn) in to me; don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid)." He came in to her into the ahal (tent), and she kasah (covered) him with a rug.

He amar (spoke) to her, "Please give me a mait (little) mayam (Waters) to shaqah (drink); for I am tzamaa (thirsty)." She pathach (opened) a naad (bottle) of chalab (milk), and shaqah (gave) him drink, and kasah (covered) him.

He amar (spoke) to her, imad (stand) in the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent), and it shall be, when any ayash (husband/individual man) bawaa (come) and inquires of you, and amar (spoke), ‘Is there any ayash (husband/individual man) here?’ That you shall amar (spoke), ‘No.’

Then Yail (Jael) Chabar (Heber's) ashah (wife/individual woman) laqach (take / seized) a ahal (tent) peg, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) a maqabath (hammer) in her yad (hand), and bawaa (come) laat (softly) to him, and thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the peg into his raqah (temples), and it pierced through into the aratz (Earth/land); for he was in a radam (deep) sleep; so he swooned and mawath (death).

Behold, as Baraq (Barak) radap (pursued) Sayasaraa (Sisera), Yail (Jael) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) him, and amar (spoke) to him, "yalak (come), and I will show you the ayash (husband/individual man) whom you baqash (seek)." He bawaa (come) to her; and behold, Sayasaraa (Sisera) napal (fall / be cast down) mawath (death), and the yathad (tent) peg was in his raqah (temples).
So Alahayam kanai (subdued) on that yawam (day) Yabayan (Jabin) the malak (king) of Kanain (Canaan) panayam (before) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel).

The yad (hand) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) qashah (rough / hard) more and more against Yabayan (Jabin) the malak (king) of Kanain (Canaan), until they had karath (cut) Yabayan (Jabin) malak (king) of Kanain (Canaan).
Then Dabawarah (Deborah) and Baraq (Barak) the ban (son) of Abayanaim (Abinoam) shayar (sang) on that yawam (day), amar (spoke),
Because the leaders took the lead in Yasharaal (Israel), because the im (people / nation) nadab (offered) themselves willingly, be barak (blessed), Yahawah!
Shamai (hearken / hear), you malak (king)! Azan (give) ear, you razan (princes)! I, even I, will shayar (sing) to Yahawah. I will zamar (sing) praise to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).

Yahawah, when you yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of Shaiyar (Seir), when you tzaid (marched) out of the shadah (field) of Adam (Edom), the aratz (Earth/land) raish (trembled), the sky also natap (dropped). Yes, the ib (clouds) natap (dropped) mayam (Waters).
The har (mountain) quaked at the panayam (presence) of Yahawah, even Sayanay (Sinai), at the panayam (presence) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).

In the yawam (day) of Shamagar (Shamgar) the ban (son) of Inath (Anath), in the yawam (day) of Yail (Jael), the highways were chadal (unoccupied). The halak (move) yalak (walked) through iqalaqal (byways).
The parazawan (rulers) chadal (ceased) in Yasharaal (Israel). They chadal (ceased) until I, Dabawarah (Deborah), qawam (rise up); Until I qawam (rise up) a am (mother) in Yasharaal (Israel).

They bachar (chose) chadash (new) Alahayam. Then lacham (war) was in the shair (gates). Was there a magan (shield) or ramach (spear) raah (see) among arabaiyam (forty) alap (thousand) in Yasharaal (Israel)?
My lab (heart) is toward the chaqaq (governors) of Yasharaal (Israel), who nadab (offered) themselves willingly among the im (people / nation). Barak (bless) Yahawah!
Shayach (meditate), you who rakab (ride) on tzachar (bright / glisten) donkeys, you who yashab (inhabit/dwell) on rich carpets, and you who halak (move) by the darak (way).

Far from the qawal (sound / voice) of chatzatz (archers), in the places of drawing mashaab (water), there they will thanah (rehearse) the tzadaqah (righteousness) acts of Yahawah, the tzadaqah (righteousness) acts of his rule in Yasharaal (Israel). Then the im (people / nation) of Yahawah yarad (went) down to the shair (gates).

‘Iwar (rouse / awaken), iwar (rouse / awaken), Dabawarah (Deborah)! Iwar (rouse / awaken), iwar (rouse / awaken), dabar (word / matter) a shayar (song)! Qawam (rise up), Baraq (Barak), and lead shabay (away) your shabah (captives), you ban (son) of Abayanaim (Abinoam).’
Then a sharayad (remnant) of the adayar (nobles) and the im (people / nation) came down. Yahawah radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) down for me against the gabawar (mighty).

Those whose sharash (root) is in Imalaq (Amalek) came out of Aparayam (Ephraim), achar (other) you, Banayamayan (Benjamin), among your im (people / nation). Chaqaq (governors) yarad (come) down out of Makayar (Machir). Those who mashak (handle) the marshal's shabat (staff) came out of Zabawalawan (Zebulun).

The shar (prince / ruler) of Yashashakar (Issachar) were with Dabawarah (Deborah). As was Yashashakar (Issachar), so was Baraq (Barak). They rushed into the imaq (valley) at his ragal (feet / foot). By the watercourses of Raawaban (Reuben), there were gadawal (very great/important/mighty) resolves of lab (heart).

Why did you yashab (inhabit/dwell) bayan (between) the mashapath (sheepfolds), To shamai (hearken / hear) the whistling for the idar (flocks)? At the watercourses of Raawaban (Reuben) There were gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chaqar (searchings) of lab (heart).

Galaid (Gilead) lived ibar (beyond) the Yaradan (Jordan). Dan (Why) did Dan gawar (remain) in anayah (ships)? Ashar (Asher) yashab (inhabit/dwell) still at the chawap (haven) of the yam (sea/waters), and lived by his creeks.
Zabawalawan (Zebulun) was a im (people / nation) that jeopardized their lives to the mawath (death); Napathalay (Naphtali) also, on the marawam (high) places of the shadah (field).

The malak (king) bawaa (come) and lacham (fought), then the malak (king) of Kanain (Canaan) lacham (fought) at Thainak (Taanach) by the mayam (Waters) of Magadawan (Megiddo). They laqach (take / seized) no plunder of kasap (silver).
From the sky the kawakab (star) lacham (fought). From their masalah (courses), they lacham (fought) against Sayasaraa (Sisera).

The nachal (stream / river) Qayashawan (Kishon) garap (swept) them away, that qadawam (ancient) nachal (stream / river), the nachal (stream / river) Qayashawan (Kishon). My napash (living being/soul), march on with iz (strength / might / refuge).
Then the horse iqab (hoofs) stamped because of the prancings, the prancings of their abayar (strong) ones.

‘Arar (curse) Marawaz (Meroz),’ amar (spoke) the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah. ‘Arar (curse) arar (bitterly) its yashab (inhabit/dwell), because they didn't bawaa (come) to izarah (help) Yahawah, to izarah (help) Yahawah against the gabawar (mighty).’

Yail (Jael) shall be barak (blessed) above ashah (wife/individual woman), the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Chabar (Heber) the Qayanay (Kenite); barak (blessed) shall she be above ashah (wife/individual woman) in the ahal (tent).
He shaal (asked) for mayam (Waters). She nathan (give) him chalab (milk). She qarab (come close) him chamaah (butter) in a adayar (lordly) sapal (dish).

She shalach (send) her yad (hand) to the yathad (tent) peg, and her right yamayan (right hand) to the workmen's halamawath (hammer). With the hammer she struck Sayasaraa (Sisera). She struck through his raash (head). Yes, she machatz (crush / shatter) and chalap (struck) through his raqah (temples).

At her ragal (feet / foot) he karai (bowed), he napal (fall / be cast down), he shakab (lay). At her ragal (feet / foot) he karai (bowed), he napal (fall / be cast down). Ashar (who/that) he karai (bowed), there he napal (fall / be cast down) down shadad (dead).

Through the chalawan (window) she shaqap (looked) out, and yabab (cried): Sayasaraa (Sisera's) am (mother) looked through the ashanab (lattice). ‘Why is his rakab (chariot) so bawash (long) in bawaa (come)? Why do the paim (wheels) of his marakabah (chariots) wait?’
Her chakam (wise) sharah (ladies) inah (answer / respond) her, Yes, she shawab (turn back / repent) amar (spoke) to herself,

‘Matzaa (have) they not found, chalaq (have) they not divided the shalal (spoil)? A lady, rachamah (two) ladies to raash (head) gabar (man); to Sayasaraa (Sisera) a shalal (spoil) of dyed garments, a shalal (spoil) of dyed garments embroidered, of dyed garments embroidered on both sides, on the tzawaar (necks) of the shalal (spoil)?’

"So let all your ayab (enemy) abad (destroy/perish), Yahawah, but let those who ahab (love) him be as the shamash (sun) when it yatzaa (go out / come out) forth in its gabawarah (strength)." Then the aratz (Earth/land) had shaqat (rest) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years).

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah: and Yahawah nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of Madayan (Midian) shabai (seven) shanah (years).

The yad (hand) of Madayan (Midian) izaz (prevailed) against Yasharaal (Israel); and panayam (because) of Madayan (Midian) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) ishah (make) them the manaharah (dens) which are in the har (mountain), and the mairah (caves), and the strongholds.

So it was, when Yasharaal (Israel) had zarai (sown), that the Madayan (Midianites) ilah (go up / offer) up, and the Imalaq (Amalekites), and the ban (son) of the qadam (east); they ilah (go up / offer) up against them;

And they chanah (encamped) against them, and shachath (destroyed) the yabawal (increase) of the aratz (Earth/land), until you bawaa (come) to Izah (Gaza), and shaar (left) no machayah (sustenance) in Yasharaal (Israel), neither shah (sheep), nor shawar (ox), nor donkey.

For they ilah (go up / offer) up with their livestock and their ahal (tents); they bawaa (come) in as arabah (locusts) for rab (multitude); both they and their gamal (camels) were without masapar (number): and they bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land) to shachath (destroy) it.
Yasharaal (Israel) was brought very dalal (low) panayam (because) of Madayan (Midian); and the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) zaiq (cried) to Yahawah.
It happened, when the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) zaiq (cried) to Yahawah awadawath (because) of Madayan (Midian),

That Yahawah shalach (send) a ayash (husband/individual man) to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel): and he amar (spoke) to them, Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘I ilah (go up / offer) you up from Matzarayam (Egypt), and yatzaa (go out / come out) you forth out of the bayath (house) of ibad (servant);

And I natzal (delivered) you out of the yad (hand) of the Matzaray (Egyptians), and out of the yad (hand) of all who lachatz (oppressed) you, and garash (drove) them out from panayam (before) you, and nathan (give) you their aratz (Earth/land);

And I amar (spoke) to you, "I am Yahawah your Alahayam; you shall not yaraa (fear / be afraid) the Alahayam of the Amaray (Amorites), in whose aratz (Earth/land) you yashab (inhabit/dwell)." But you have not shamai (hearken / hear) to my qawal (sound / voice).’

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah bawaa (come), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) under the alah (these) which was in Iparah (Ophrah), that pertained to Yawaash (Joash) the abayahaizaray (abiezrite): and his ban (son) Gadaiwan (Gideon) was chabat (beating) out chatah (wheat) in the gath (winepress), to nawas (hide) it from the Madayan (Midianites).
The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah raah (see) to him, and amar (spoke) to him, Yahawah is with you, you gabawar (mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) of valor!

Gadaiwan (Gideon) amar (spoke) to him, Oh, my Adawan, if Yahawah is with us, why then matzaa (has) all this happened to us? Where are all his wondrous palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) which our ab (father) sapar (book) us of, amar (spoke), ‘Didn't Yahawah ilah (go up / offer) us up from Matzarayam (Egypt)?’ But now Yahawah has natash (cast) us off, and nathan (give) us into the kap (hand) of Madayan (Midian).

Yahawah panah (looked) at him, and amar (spoke), yalak (go) in this your kach (strength / mighty / power), and yashai (salvation) Yasharaal (Israel) from the kap (hand) of Madayan (Midian). Haven't I shalach (send) you?

He amar (spoke) to him, O Adanay, mah (how) shall I yashai (salvation) Yasharaal (Israel)? Behold, my alap (family) is the poorest in Manashah (Manasseh), and I am the tzaiyar (least) in my ab (father) bayath (house).
Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, nakah (surely) I will be with you, and you shall strike the Madayan (Midianites) as achad (one) ayash (husband/individual man).
He amar (spoke) to him, "If now I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye), then show me a awath (sign / mark / miracle) that it is you who dabar (word / matter) with me.

Please don't mawash (go) away, until I bawaa (come) to you, and yatzaa (go out / come out) out my manachah (present), and yanach (lay) it panayam (before) you." He amar (spoke), I will wait until you shawab (turn back / repent) back.

Gadaiwan (Gideon) bawaa (come) in, and ishah (make) a young iz (goat), and unleavened matzah (cakes) of an ayapah (ephah) of qamach (meal). He shawam (place / establish / appoint) the meat in a sal (basket) and he shawam (place / establish / appoint) the maraq (broth) in a parawar (pot), and yatzaa (go out / come out) it out to him under the alah (these), and nagash (presented) it.

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Alahayam amar (spoke) to him, "laqach (take / seized) the meat and the unleavened matzah (cakes), and yanach (lay) them on halaz (this) salai (rock), and shapak (pour) out the maraq (broth)." He ishah (make) so.

Then the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah shalach (send) out the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the mashainah (staff) that was in his yad (hand), and nagai (touched) the meat and the unleavened matzah (cakes); and ash (fire) ilah (go up / offer) up out of the tzawar (rock), and akal (eat) the meat and the unleavened matzah (cakes); and the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah departed out of his iyan (eye).

Gadaiwan (Gideon) raah (see) that he was the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah; and Gadaiwan (Gideon) amar (spoke), ahah (alas), Adawan Yahawah! Because I raah (see) seen the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah panayam (face) to panayam (face)!
Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, shalawam (peace / safety) be to you! Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). You shall not mawath (death).

Then Gadaiwan (Gideon) banah (built) an mazabach (altar) there to Yahawah, and qaraa (called) it "Yahawah is Peace." To this yawam (day) it is still in Iparah (Ophrah) of the abayahaizaray (abiezrites).

It happened the same layal (night), that Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, laqach (take / seized) your ab (father) shawar (bull), even the shanay (second) shawar (bull) shabai (seven) shanah (years) old, and haras (throw) down the mazabach (altar) of Bail (Baal) that your ab (father) has, and cut down the Asharah (Asherah) that is by it;

And banah (build) an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah your Alahayam on the raash (head) of this stronghold, in an orderly mairakah (way), and laqach (take / seized) the shanay (second) par (bull), and ilah (go up / offer) a burnt ilah (go up / offer) with the itz (wood) Asharah (of) the Asherah which you shall karath (cut) down.

Then Gadaiwan (Gideon) laqach (take / seized) ishar (ten) ayash (husband/individual man) of his ibad (servant), and ishah (make) as Yahawah had dabar (word / matter) to him: and it happened, because he yaraa (fear / be afraid) his ab (father) bayath (house) and the ayash (husband/individual man) of the iyar (city), so that he could not ishah (make) it by yawamam (by day), that he ishah (make) it by layal (night).

When the ayash (husband/individual man) of the iyar (city) arose shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), behold, the mazabach (altar) of Bail (Baal) was nathatz (broken) down, and the Asharah (Asherah) was cut down that was by it, and the shanay (second) par (bull) was ilah (go up / offer) on the mazabach (altar) that was banah (built).

They amar (spoke) ayash (husband/individual man) to rai (neigbor/another person), "Who ishah (make) done this thing?" When they darash (inquired) and baqash (asked), they amar (spoke), Gadaiwan (Gideon) the ban (son) of Yawaash (Joash) ishah (make) done this thing.

Then the ayash (husband/individual man) of the iyar (city) amar (spoke) to Yawaash (Joash), yatzaa (go out / come out) out your ban (son), that he may mawath (death), because he has nathatz (broken) down the mazabach (altar) of Bail (Baal), and because he has karath (cut) down the Asharah (Asherah) that was by it.

Yawaash (Joash) amar (spoke) to all who imad (stood) against him, Will you rayab (contend) for Bail (Baal)? Or will you yashai (salvation) him? He who will rayab (contend) for him, let him be put to mawath (death) by baqar (morning). If he is a Alahayam, let him rayab (contend) for himself, because someone has nathatz (broken) down his mazabach (altar).
Therefore on that yawam (day) he qaraa (called) him Yarabail (Jerub-Baal), amar (spoke), Let Bail (Baal) rayab (contend) against him, because he has nathatz (broken) down his mazabach (altar).

Then all the Madayan (Midianites) and the Imalaq (Amalekites) and the ban (son) of the qadam (east) asap (assembled) themselves yachad (together); and they ibar (pass over/through) over, and chanah (encamped) in the imaq (valley) of Yazaraial (Jezreel).

But the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah labash (came) on Gadaiwan (Gideon); and he thaqai (blow / sound alarm) a shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)); and Abayaizar (Abiezer) was zaiq (gathered) together achar (other) him.

He shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) throughout all Manashah (Manasseh); and they also were zaiq (gathered) together achar (other) him: and he shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to Ashar (Asher), and to Zabawalawan (Zebulun), and to Napathalay (Naphtali); and they ilah (go up / offer) up to qaraah (meet) them.
Gadaiwan (Gideon) amar (spoke) to Alahayam, If you yash (will) yashai (salvation) Yasharaal (Israel) by my yad (hand), as you have dabar (word / matter),

Behold, I will yatzag (put) a gazah (fleece) of tzamar (wool) on the garan (threshing) floor; if there is tal (dew) on the gazah (fleece) only, and it is charab (dry) on all the aratz (Earth/land), then shall I yadai (know) that you will yashai (salvation) Yasharaal (Israel) by my yad (hand), as you have dabar (word / matter).

It was so; for he shakam (rose) up early on the next macharath (day), and pressed the gazah (fleece) zawar (together), and wrung the tal (dew) out of the gazah (fleece), a sapal (bowl) malaa (full) of mayam (Waters).

Gadaiwan (Gideon) amar (spoke) to Alahayam, Don't let your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) be charah (hot with anger) against me, and I will dabar (word / matter) but paim (this) once. Please let me make a trial just paim (this) once with the gazah (fleece). Let it now be charab (dry) only on the gazah (fleece), and on all the aratz (Earth/land) let there be tal (dew).
Alahayam ishah (make) so that layal (night): for it was charab (dry) on the gazah (fleece) only, and there was tal (dew) on all the aratz (Earth/land).

Then Yarabail (Jerubbaal), who is Gadaiwan (Gideon), and all the im (people / nation) who were with him, shakam (rose) up early, and chanah (encamped) beside the spring of Iyanacharad (Harod): and the machanah (camp) of Madayan (Midian) was on the tzapawan (north) side of them, by the gabaih (hill) of Mawarah (Moreh), in the imaq (valley).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Gadaiwan (Gideon), "The im (people / nation) who are with you are rab (too) many for me to nathan (give) the Madayan (Midianites) into their yad (hand), lest Yasharaal (Israel) paar (vaunt) themselves amar (spoke) me, saying, ‘My own yad (hand) has yashai (salvation) me.’

Naa (now) therefore qaraa (called) in the azan (ears) of the im (people / nation), amar (spoke), 'Whoever is yaraa (fearful) and charad (trembling), let him shawab (turn back / repent) and depart from har (mountain) Galaid (Gilead).'" Isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) of the im (people / nation) shawab (turn back / repent), and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) shaar (remained).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Gadaiwan (Gideon), The im (people / nation) are still rab (too) many. Yarad (bring) them down to the mayam (Waters), and I will test them for you there. It shall be, that of whom I amar (spoke) you, ‘This shall yalak (go) with you,’ the same shall yalak (go) with you; and of whoever I amar (spoke) you, ‘This shall not yalak (go) with you,’ the same shall not yalak (go).

So he yarad (brought) down the im (people / nation) to the mayam (Waters); and Yahawah amar (spoke) to Gadaiwan (Gideon), Everyone who laqaq (laps) of the mayam (Waters) with his lashawan (tongue/language), like a kalab (dog) laqaq (laps), you shall yatzag (set) him by himself; likewise everyone who karai (bows) down on his barak (knees) to shathah (drinks).

The masapar (number) of those who laqaq (lapped), putting their yad (hand) to their pah (mouth), was shalawash (three) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man); but all the yathar (rest) of the im (people / nation) karai (bowed) down on their barak (knees) to shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Gadaiwan (Gideon), By the shalawash (three) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man) who laqaq (lapped) will I yashai (salvation) you, and nathan (give) the Madayan (Midianites) into your yad (hand). Let all the other im (people / nation) yalak (go), ayash (husband/individual man) to his own maqawam (place).

So the im (people / nation) laqach (take / seized) food in their yad (hand), and their shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)); and he shalach (send) all the men of Yasharaal (Israel) every ayash (husband/individual man) to his ahal (tent), but chazaq (retained) the shalawash (three) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man): and the machanah (camp) of Madayan (Midian) was beneath him in the imaq (valley).
It happened the same layal (night), that Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, "qawam (rise up), yarad (go) down into the machanah (camp); for I nathan (give) delivered it into your yad (hand).
But if you are yaraa (afraid) to yarad (go) down, yarad (go) Parah (with) Purah your nair (servant) down to the machanah (camp):

And you shall shamai (hearken / hear) what they dabar (word / matter); and afterward your yad (hand) will be chazaq (strengthened) to yarad (go) down into the machanah (camp)." Then yarad (went) he down Parah (with) Purah his nair (servant) to the outermost part of the chamash (armed) men who were in the machanah (camp).

The Madayan (Midianites) and the Imalaq (Amalekites) and all the ban (son) of the qadam (east) napal (fall / be cast down) along in the imaq (valley) like arabah (locusts) for rab (multitude); and their gamal (camels) were without masapar (number), as the chawal (sand) which is on the shapah (seashore) for rab (multitude).

When Gadaiwan (Gideon) bawaa (come) come, behold, there was a ayash (husband/individual man) sapar (book) a chalawam (dream) to his rai (neigbor/another person); and he said, Behold, I chalam (dream) a chalawam (dream); and behold, a tzalawal (cake) of shairah (barley) lacham (bread) hapak (tumbled) into the machanah (camp) of Madayan (Midian), and bawaa (come) to the ahal (tent), and nakah (struck) it so that it napal (fall / be cast down), and hapak (turned) it upside down, so that the ahal (tent) napal (fall / be cast down) flat.

His rai (neigbor/another person) inah (answer / respond), This is nothing other than the charab (sword) of Gadaiwan (Gideon) the ban (son) of Yawaash (Joash), a ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel). Alahayam nathan (give) delivered Madayan (Midian) into his yad (hand), with all the machanah (army).

It was so, when Gadaiwan (Gideon) shamai (hearken / hear) the masapar (telling) of the chalawam (dream), and its shabar (interpretation), that he shachah (worshiped); and he shawab (turn back / repent) into the machanah (camp) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (spoke), qawam (rise up); for Yahawah nathan (give) delivered the machanah (army) of Madayan (Midian) into your yad (hand)!

He chatzah (divided) the shalawash (three) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man) into shalawash (three) raash (head), and he nathan (give) into the yad (hand) of all of them shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), and rayaq (empty) kad (pitchers), with torches thawak (midst) the kad (pitchers).
He amar (spoke) to them, Watch me, and ishah (make) likewise. Behold, when I bawaa (come) to the outermost part of the machanah (camp), it shall be that, as I ishah (make), so you shall ishah (make).

When I thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), I and all who are with me, then thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)) also on sabayab (surrounding) side of all the machanah (camp), and shout, ‘For Yahawah and for Gadaiwan (Gideon)!’

So Gadaiwan (Gideon), and the maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man) who were with him, bawaa (come) to the outermost part of the machanah (camp) in the raash (head) of the thayakawan (middle) ashamarah (watch), when they had but qawam (rise up) qawam (rise up) the shamar (keep/guard): and they thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), and napatz (broke) in pieces the kad (pitchers) that were in their yad (hand).

The shalawash (three) raash (head) thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), and shabar (broke) the kad (pitchers), and chazaq (held) the torches in their shamaawal (left hand) yad (hand), and the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)) in their yamayan (right hand) yad (hand) with which to thaqai (blow / sound alarm); and they shouted, The charab (sword) of Yahawah and of Gadaiwan (Gideon)!

They ayash (husband/individual man) imad (stood) in his sabayab (surrounding) around the machanah (camp); and all the machanah (army) rawatz (ran); and they rawai (shouted), and nawas (put) them to flight.

They thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), and Yahawah shawam (place / establish / appoint) every ayash (husband/individual man) charab (sword) against his rai (neigbor/another person), and against all the machanah (army); and the machanah (army) nawas (fled) as far as Bayathahashatah (Beth) Shittah Tzararah (toward) Zererah, as far as the shapah (border) of Abalamachawalah (Abel) Meholah, by Tabath (Tabbath).

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) were tzaiq (gathered) together out of Napathalay (Naphtali), and out of Ashar (Asher), and out of all Manashah (Manasseh), and radap (pursued) achar (other) Madayan (Midian).

Gadaiwan (Gideon) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) throughout all the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), amar (spoke), "yarad (come) down qaraah (against) Madayan (Midian), and lakad (take) before them the mayam (Waters), as far as Bayathabarah (Beth) Barah, even the Yaradan (Jordan)!" So all the ayash (husband/individual man) of Aparayam (Ephraim) were tzaiq (gathered) together, and lakad (took) the mayam (Waters) as far as Bayathabarah (Beth) Barah, even the Yaradan (Jordan).

They lakad (took) the shanayam (two) shar (prince / ruler) of Madayan (Midian), Irab (Oreb) and Zaab (Zeeb); and they harag (killed) Irab (Oreb) at the tzawar (rock) of Irab (Oreb), and Zaab (Zeeb) they harag (killed) at the yaqab (winepress) of Zaab (Zeeb), and radap (pursued) Madayan (Midian): and they bawaa (come) the raash (head) of Irab (Oreb) and Zaab (Zeeb) to Gadaiwan (Gideon) ibar (beyond) the Yaradan (Jordan).

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Aparayam (Ephraim) amar (spoke) to him, "mah (why) have you treated us this mah (way), that you didn't qaraa (called) us, when you halak (move) to lacham (fight) with Madayan (Midian)?" They rebuked him chazaqah (sharply).

He amar (spoke) to them, "What ishah (make) I now done in comparison with you? Isn't the gleaning of the grapes of Aparayam (Ephraim) tawab (pleasant/functional) than the batzayar (vintage) of Abayaizar (Abiezer)?

Alahayam nathan (give) delivered into your yad (hand) the shar (prince / ruler) of Madayan (Midian), Irab (Oreb) and Zaab (Zeeb)! What was I yakal (able) to ishah (make) in comparison with you?" Then their rawach (spirit / wind) was rapah (abated) toward him, when he had dabar (word / matter) that.

Gadaiwan (Gideon) bawaa (come) to the Yaradan (Jordan), and ibar (pass over/through) over, he, and the shalawash (three) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man) who were with him, iyap (faint), yet radap (pursuing).

He amar (spoke) to the ayash (husband/individual man) of Sakawath (Succoth), Please nathan (give) loaves of lacham (bread) to the im (people / nation) who ragal (feet / foot) me; for they are iyap (faint), and I am radap (pursuing) achar (other) Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna), the malak (king) of Madayan (Midian).

The shar (prince / ruler) of Sakawath (Succoth) amar (spoke), Are the kap (hands) of Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna) now in your yad (hand), that we should nathan (give) lacham (bread) to your tzabaa (troop)?

Gadaiwan (Gideon) amar (spoke), Therefore when Yahawah nathan (give) delivered Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna) into my yad (hand), then I will dawash (tear) your bashar (flesh) with the qawatz (thorns) of the madabar (wilderness) and with baraqan (briers).

He ilah (go up / offer) up there to Panawaal (Penuel), and dabar (word / matter) to them in the same way; and the ayash (husband/individual man) of Panawaal (Penuel) inah (answer / respond) him as the ayash (husband/individual man) of Sakawath (Succoth) had inah (answer / respond).

He amar (spoke) also to the ayash (husband/individual man) of Panawaal (Penuel), amar (spoke), When I shawab (turn back / repent) again in shalawam (peace / safety), I will nathatz (break) down this magadal (tower).

Now Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna) were in Qaraqar (Karkor), and their machanah (armies) with them, about chamash (fifteen) alap (thousand) men, all who were yathar (left) of all the machanah (army) of the ban (son) of the qadam (east); for there napal (fall / be cast down) one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man) who shalap (drew) charab (sword).

Gadaiwan (Gideon) ilah (go up / offer) up by the darak (way) of those who lived in ahal (tents) on the qadam (east) of Nabach (Nobah) and Yagabahah (Jogbehah), and nakah (struck) the machanah (army); for the machanah (army) was batach (secure).

Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna) nawas (fled); and he radap (pursued) achar (other) them; and he lakad (took) the shanayam (two) malak (king) of Madayan (Midian), Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna), and confused all the machanah (army).
Gadaiwan (Gideon) the ban (son) of Yawaash (Joash) shawab (turn back / repent) from the malachamah (battle) from the ascent of Heres.

He lakad (caught) a nair (young) man of the ayash (husband/individual man) of Sakawath (Succoth), and inquired of him: and he kathab (described) for him the shar (prince / ruler) of Sakawath (Succoth), and its zaqan (elders), seventy-seven ayash (husband/individual man).

He bawaa (come) to the ayash (husband/individual man) of Sakawath (Succoth), and amar (spoke), See Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna), concerning whom you taunted me, amar (spoke), ‘Are the kap (hands) of Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna) now in your kap (hand), that we should nathan (give) lacham (bread) to your ayash (husband/individual man) who are yaip (weary)?’

He laqach (take / seized) the zaqan (elders) of the iyar (city), and qawatz (thorns) of the madabar (wilderness) and baraqan (briers), and with them he yadai (taught) the zaqan (men) of Sakawath (Succoth).
He nathatz (broke) down the magadal (tower) of Panawaal (Penuel), and harag (killed) the ayash (husband/individual man) of the iyar (city).

Then he amar (spoke) to Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna), "ayapah (what) kind of ayash (husband/individual man) were they whom you harag (killed) at Thabawar (Tabor)?" They amar (spoke), They were kamaw (like) you. Achad (one) one thaar (resembled) the ban (son) of a malak (king).
He amar (spoke), They were my ach (brother/kinsman), the ban (son) of my am (mother). As Yahawah chay (life), if you had chayah (saved) them alive, I would not harag (kill) you.

He amar (spoke) to Yathar (Jether) his bakawar (firstborn), "qawam (rise up) up, and harag (kill) them!" But the youth didn't shalap (draw) his charab (sword); for he was yaraa (fear / be afraid), because he was yet a youth.

Then Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna) amar (spoke), "qawam (rise up) and pagai (fall) on us; for as the ayash (husband/individual man) is, so is his gabawarah (strength)." Gadaiwan (Gideon) qawam (rise up), and harag (killed) Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna), and laqach (take / seized) the crescents that were on their gamal (camels)' tzawaar (necks).

Then the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke) to Gadaiwan (Gideon), mashal (rule/have dominion) over us, both you, and your ban (son), and your ban (son) ban (son) also; for you have yashai (salvation) us out of the yad (hand) of Madayan (Midian).

Gadaiwan (Gideon) amar (spoke) to them, I will not mashal (rule/have dominion) over you, neither shall my ban (son) mashal (rule/have dominion) over you. Yahawah shall mashal (rule/have dominion) over you.

Gadaiwan (Gideon) amar (spoke) to them, "I would make a shaalah (request) of you, that you nathan (give) give me every ayash (husband/individual man) the nazam (earrings) of his shalal (spoil)." (For they had zahab (gold) nazam (earrings), because they were Yashamaialay (Ishmaelites).)

They amar (spoke), "We will nathan (give) nathan (give) them." They parash (spread) a shamalah (garment), and every ayash (husband/individual man) shalak (threw) the nazam (earrings) of his shalal (spoil) into it.

The mashaqal (weight) of the zahab (gold) nazam (earrings) that he shaal (requested) was one alap (thousand) and shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shekels of zahab (gold), besides the crescents, and the pendants, and the aragaman (purple) bagad (clothing) that was on the malak (king) of Madayan (Midian), and besides the inaq (chains) that were about their gamal (camels)' tzawaar (necks).

Gadaiwan (Gideon) ishah (make) an apawad (ephod) of it, and yatzag (put) it in his iyar (city), even in Iparah (Ophrah): and all Yasharaal (Israel) zanah (played) the prostitute achar (other) it there; and it became a mawaqash (snare) to Gadaiwan (Gideon), and to his bayath (house).

So Madayan (Midian) was kanai (subdued) panayam (before) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), and they nashaa (lift) up their raash (head) no more. The aratz (Earth/land) had shaqat (rest) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years) in the yawam (day) of Gadaiwan (Gideon).
Yarabail (Jerubbaal) the ban (son) of Yawaash (Joash) yalak (went) and lived in his own bayath (house).
Gadaiwan (Gideon) had shabaiyam (seventy) ban (son) conceived from his yarak (body); for he rab (had) many wives.
His payalagash (concubine) who was in Shakam (Shechem), she also yalad (birth / begot) him a ban (son), and he shawam (place / establish / appoint) him Abayamalak (Abimelech).

Gadaiwan (Gideon) the ban (son) of Yawaash (Joash) mawath (death) in a tawab (pleasant/functional) shayabah (old age / white hair (due to age)) age, and was qabar (bury) in the tomb of Yawaash (Joash) his ab (father), in Iparah (Ophrah) of the abayahaizaray (abiezrites).

It happened, as soon as Gadaiwan (Gideon) was mawath (death), that the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) shawab (turn back / repent) again, and zanah (played) the prostitute achar (other) the Bail (Baals), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) Bailabarayath (Baal) Berith their Alahayam.

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) didn't zakar (remembrance/memory) Yahawah their Alahayam, who had natzal (delivered) them out of the yad (hand) of all their ayab (enemy) on sabayab (surrounding) side;
Neither ishah (make) they show chasad (grace) to the bayath (house) of Yarabail (Jerubbaal), Gadaiwan (Gideon), according to all the goodness which he ishah (make) shown to Yasharaal (Israel).

Abayamalak (Abimelech) the ban (son) of Yarabail (Jerubbaal) yalak (went) to Shakam (Shechem) to his am (mother) ach (brother/kinsman), and dabar (word / matter) with them, and with all the mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) of the bayath (house) of his am (mother) ab (father), amar (spoke),

Please dabar (word / matter) in the azan (ears) of all the bail (men) of Shakam (Shechem), ‘Is it tawab (pleasant/functional) for you that all the ban (son) of Yarabail (Jerubbaal), who are shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (husband/individual man), mashal (rule/have dominion) over you, or that achad (one) mashal (rule/have dominion) over you?’ Zakar (remembrance/memory) also that I am your itzam (bone) and your bashar (flesh).

His am (mother) ach (brother/kinsman) dabar (word / matter) of him in the azan (ears) of all the bail (men) of Shakam (Shechem) all these dabar (word / matter): and their lab (heart) natah (inclined) to achar (other) Abayamalak (Abimelech); for they amar (spoke), He is our ach (brother/kinsman).

They nathan (give) him shabaiyam (seventy) pieces of kasap (silver) out of the bayath (house) of Bailabarayath (Baal) Berith, with which Abayamalak (Abimelech) shakar (hired) rayaq (vain) and pachaz (light) ayash (husband/individual man), who yalak (followed) him.

He bawaa (come) to his ab (father) bayath (house) at Iparah (Ophrah), and harag (killed) his ach (brother/kinsman) the ban (son) of Yarabail (Jerubbaal), being shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (husband/individual man), on achad (one) aban (stone): but Yawatham (Jotham) the youngest ban (son) of Yarabail (Jerubbaal) was yathar (left); for he chabaa (hid) himself.

All the bail (men) of Shakam (Shechem) asap (assembled) themselves together, and all the bayath (house) of Malawaa (Millo), and yalak (went) and malak (king) Abayamalak (Abimelech) malak (king), by the oak of the natzab (pillar) that was in Shakam (Shechem).

When they nagad (told) it to Yawatham (Jotham), he yalak (went) and imad (stood) on the raash (head) of har (mountain) Garazayam (Gerizim), and nashaa (lift) up his qawal (sound / voice), and qaraa (called), and amar (spoke) to them, shamai (hearken / hear) to me, you bail (men) of Shakam (Shechem), that Alahayam may shamai (hearken / hear) to you.
The itz (trees) halak (move) forth on a time to mashach (anoint) a malak (king) over them; and they amar (spoke) to the zayath (olive) tree, ‘malak (king) over us.’

But the zayath (olive) tree amar (spoke) to them, ‘Should I chadal (leave) my dashan (fatness), with which by me they honor Alahayam and ayash (husband/individual man), and halak (move) to wave back and forth over the itz (trees)?’
The itz (trees) amar (spoke) to the thaan (fig) tree, ‘yalak (come) and malak (king) over us.’

But the thaan (fig) tree amar (spoke) to them, ‘Should I chadal (leave) my mathaq (sweetness), and my tawab (pleasant/functional) thanawabah (fruit), and halak (move) to wave back and forth over the itz (trees)?’
The itz (trees) amar (spoke) to the gapan (vine), ‘yalak (come) and malak (king) over us.’

The gapan (vine) amar (spoke) to them, ‘Should I chadal (leave) my new thayarawash (wine), which shamach (cheers) Alahayam and ayash (husband/individual man), and halak (move) to wave back and forth over the itz (trees)?’
Then all the itz (trees) amar (spoke) to the atad (bramble), ‘yalak (come) and malak (king) over us.’

The atad (bramble) amar (spoke) to the itz (trees), ‘If in amath (truth) you mashach (anoint) me malak (king) over you, then bawaa (come) and take chasah (refuge) in my tzal (shade); and if not, let ash (fire) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the atad (bramble), and akal (eat) the araz (cedars) of Labanawan (Lebanon).’

Now therefore, if you ishah (make) dealt truly and righteously, in that you have made Abayamalak (Abimelech) malak (king), and if you ishah (make) dealt tawab (pleasant/functional) with Yarabail (Jerubbaal) and his bayath (house), and ishah (make) done to him according to the gamawal (deserving) of his yad (hand)
(For my ab (father) lacham (fought) for you, and risked his napash (living being/soul), and natzal (delivered) you out of the yad (hand) of Madayan (Midian):

And you have qawam (rise up) up against my ab (father) bayath (house) this yawam (day), and have harag (slain) his ban (son), shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (husband/individual man), on achad (one) aban (stone), and have made Abayamalak (Abimelech), the ban (son) of his female amah (servant), malak (king) over the bail (men) of Shakam (Shechem), because he is your ach (brother/kinsman));

If you then ishah (make) dealt truly and righteously with Yarabail (Jerubbaal) and with his bayath (house) this yawam (day), then shamach (rejoice) in Abayamalak (Abimelech), and let him also shamach (rejoice) in you:

But if not, let ash (fire) yatzaa (go out / come out) out from Abayamalak (Abimelech), and akal (eat) the bail (men) of Shakam (Shechem), and the bayath (house) of Malawaa (Millo); and let ash (fire) yatzaa (go out / come out) out from the bail (men) of Shakam (Shechem), and from the bayath (house) of Malawaa (Millo), and akal (eat) Abayamalak (Abimelech).
Yawatham (Jotham) barach (ran) away, and nawas (fled), and yalak (went) to Baar (Beer), and lived there, for panayam (fear) of Abayamalak (Abimelech) his ach (brother/kinsman).
Abayamalak (Abimelech) was shawar (prince) over Yasharaal (Israel) shalawash (three) shanah (years).

Alahayam shalach (send) an rai (evil) rawach (spirit / wind) between Abayamalak (Abimelech) and the bail (men) of Shakam (Shechem); and the bail (men) of Shakam (Shechem) dealt bagad (treacherously) with Abayamalak (Abimelech):
