That the chamas (violence) done to the shabaiyam (seventy) ban (son) of Yarabail (Jerubbaal) might bawaa (come), and that their dam (blood) might be shawam (place / establish / appoint) on Abayamalak (Abimelech) their ach (brother/kinsman), who harag (killed) them, and on the bail (men) of Shakam (Shechem), who chazaq (strengthened) his harag (hands) to kill his ach (brother/kinsman).

The bail (men) of Shakam (Shechem) shawam (place / establish / appoint) an arab (ambush) for him on the raash (head) of the har (mountain), and they gazal (robbed) ibar (pass over/through) who came along that darak (way) by them: and it was nagad (told) Abayamalak (Abimelech).

Gail (Gaal) the ban (son) of Ibad (Ebed) bawaa (come) with his ach (brother/kinsman), and ibar (pass over/through) over to Shakam (Shechem); and the bail (men) of Shakam (Shechem) batach (put) their trust in him.

They yatzaa (go out / come out) out into the shadah (field), and harvested their karam (vineyards), and darak (trod) the grapes, and ishah (make) festival, and bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of their Alahayam, and akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and qalal (cursed) Abayamalak (Abimelech).

Gail (Gaal) the ban (son) of Ibad (Ebed) amar (spoke), "Who is Abayamalak (Abimelech), and who is Shakam (Shechem), that we should ibad (servant) him? Isn't he the ban (son) of Yarabail (Jerubbaal)? And Zabal (Zebul) his officer? Ibad (servant) the ban (son) of Chamawar (Hamor) the ab (father) of Shakam (Shechem): but why should we ibad (servant) him?

Would that this im (people / nation) were under my yad (hand)! Then I would sawar (remove) Abayamalak (Abimelech)." He amar (spoke) to Abayamalak (Abimelech), rabah (increase) your tzabaa (troop), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out!

When Zabal (Zebul) the shar (prince / ruler) of the iyar (city) shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Gail (Gaal) the ban (son) of Ibad (Ebed), his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger).

He shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to Abayamalak (Abimelech) craftily, amar (spoke), Behold, Gail (Gaal) the ban (son) of Ibad (Ebed) and his ach (brother/kinsman) bawaa (come) come to Shakam (Shechem); and behold, they incite the iyar (city) against you.
Now therefore, go up by layal (night), you and the im (people / nation) who are with you, and lie in arab (wait) in the shadah (field):

And it shall be, that in the baqar (morning), as soon as the shamash (sun) is up, you shall shakam (rise) early, and rush on the iyar (city); and behold, when he and the im (people / nation) who are with him yatzaa (go out / come out) out against you, then may you ishah (make) to them as you shall matzaa (find) occasion.
Abayamalak (Abimelech) qawam (rise up) up, and all the im (people / nation) who were with him, by layal (night), and they arab (laid) wait against Shakam (Shechem) in arabai (four) raash (head).

Gail (Gaal) the ban (son) of Ibad (Ebed) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and imad (stood) in the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate) of the iyar (city): and Abayamalak (Abimelech) qawam (rise up) up, and the im (people / nation) who were with him, from the maarab (ambush).

When Gail (Gaal) raah (see) the im (people / nation), he amar (spoke) to Zabal (Zebul), "Behold, im (people / nation) are yarad (coming) down from the raash (head) of the har (mountain)." Zabal (Zebul) amar (spoke) to him, You raah (see) the tzal (shadow) of the har (mountain) as if they were im (people / nation).

Gail (Gaal) dabar (word / matter) again and dabar (word / matter), Behold, im (people / nation) are yarad (coming) down by the tabawar (middle) of the aratz (Earth/land), and one raash (head) bawaa (come) by the darak (way) of the oak of Meonenim.

Then Zabal (Zebul) amar (spoke) to him, apaw (now) where is your pah (mouth), that you amar (spoke), ‘Who is Abayamalak (Abimelech), that we should ibad (servant) him?’ Isn't this the im (people / nation) that you have maas (despised)? Please yatzaa (go out / come out) out naa (now) and lacham (fight) with them.
Gail (Gaal) yatzaa (go out / come out) out panayam (before) the bail (men) of Shakam (Shechem), and lacham (fought) with Abayamalak (Abimelech).
Abayamalak (Abimelech) radap (chased) him, and he nawas (fled) panayam (before) him, and many napal (fall / be cast down) chalal (wounded), even to the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate).
Abayamalak (Abimelech) lived at Arawamah (Arumah): and Zabal (Zebul) garash (drove) out Gail (Gaal) and his ach (brother/kinsman), that they should not yashab (inhabit/dwell) in Shakam (Shechem).
It happened on the next macharath (day), that the im (people / nation) yatzaa (go out / come out) out into the shadah (field); and they nagad (told) Abayamalak (Abimelech).

He laqach (take / seized) the im (people / nation), and chatzah (divided) them into shalawash (three) raash (head), and arab (laid) wait in the shadah (field); and he raah (see), and behold, the im (people / nation) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the iyar (city); He qawam (rise up) up against them, and nakah (struck) them.

Abayamalak (Abimelech), and the raash (head) that were with him, pashat (rushed) forward, and imad (stood) in the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate) of the iyar (city): and the shanayam (two) raash (head) pashat (rushed) on all who were in the shadah (field), and nakah (struck) them.

Abayamalak (Abimelech) lacham (fought) against the iyar (city) all that yawam (day); and he lakad (took) the iyar (city), and harag (killed) the im (people / nation) who were therein: and he nathatz (beat) down the iyar (city), and zarai (sowed) it with malach (salt).
When all the bail (men) of the magadal (tower) of Shakam (Shechem) shamai (hearken / hear) of it, they bawaa (come) into the stronghold of the bayath (house) of Barayath (Elberith).
It was nagad (told) Abayamalak (Abimelech) that all the bail (men) of the magadal (tower) of Shakam (Shechem) were qabatz (gathered) together.

Abayamalak (Abimelech) ilah (go up / offer) up to har (mountain) Tzalamawan (Zalmon), he and all the im (people / nation) who were with him; and Abayamalak (Abimelech) laqach (take / seized) an axe in his yad (hand), and karath (cut) down a shawak (bough) from the itz (trees), and nashaa (lift) it up, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it on his shakam (shoulder): and he amar (spoke) to the im (people / nation) who were with him, What you raah (see) seen me ishah (make), mahar (make) haste, and ishah (make) as I have done!

All the im (people / nation) likewise ayash (husband/individual man) karath (cut) down his shawak (bough), and yalak (followed) Abayamalak (Abimelech), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them at the base of the stronghold, and yatzath (set) the stronghold on ash (fire) on them; so that all the im (people / nation) of the magadal (tower) of Shakam (Shechem) mawath (death) also, about a alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man) and ashah (wife/individual woman).
Then yalak (went) Abayamalak (Abimelech) to Thabatz (Thebez), and chanah (encamped) against Thabatz (Thebez), and lakad (took) it.

But there was a iz (strength / might / refuge) magadal (tower) thawak (midst) the iyar (city), and there nawas (fled) all the ayash (husband/individual man) and ashah (wife/individual woman), and all they of the iyar (city), and sagar (shut) themselves in, and ilah (go up / offer) up to the gag (roof) of the magadal (tower).
Abayamalak (Abimelech) bawaa (come) to the magadal (tower), and lacham (fought) against it, and nagash (drew) near to the pathach (door) of the magadal (tower) to sharap (burn) it with ash (fire).
A achad (one) ashah (wife/individual woman) shalak (cast) an upper rakab (millstone) on Abayamalak (Abimelech's) raash (head), and ratzatz (broke) his galagalath (skull).

Then he qaraa (called) maharah (hastily) to the nair (young) man his armor bearer, and amar (spoke) to him, shalap (draw) your charab (sword), and mawath (death) me, that men not amar (spoke) of me, ‘A ashah (wife/individual woman) harag (killed) him.’ His nair (young) man thrust him daqar (through), and he mawath (death).
When the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) raah (see) that Abayamalak (Abimelech) was mawath (death), they departed every ayash (husband/individual man) to his maqawam (place).
Thus Alahayam shawab (turn back / repent) the rai (wickedness) of Abayamalak (Abimelech), which he ishah (make) to his ab (father), in harag (killing) his shabaiyam (seventy) ach (brother/kinsman);

And all the rai (wickedness) of the rai (men) of Shakam (Shechem) did Alahayam shawab (turn back / repent) on their raash (head): and on them bawaa (come) the qalalah (curse) of Yawatham (Jotham) the ban (son) of Yarabail (Jerubbaal).

Achar (other) Abayamalak (Abimelech) there qawam (rise up) to yashai (salvation) Yasharaal (Israel) Thawalai (Tola) the ban (son) of Pawaah (Puah), the ban (son) of Dawadaw (Dodo), a ayash (husband/individual man) of Yashashakar (Issachar); and he lived in Shamayar (Shamir) in the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim).
He shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel) isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three) shanah (years), and mawath (death), and was qabar (bury) in Shamayar (Shamir).
Achar (other) him qawam (rise up) Yaayar (Jair), the Galaiday (Gileadite); and he shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel) isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) shanah (years).

He had shalawashayam (thirty) ban (son) who rakab (rode) on shalawashayam (thirty) donkey iyar (colts), and they had shalawashayam (thirty) cities, which are qaraa (called) Havvoth chawawathayaiyar (jair) to this yawam (day), which are in the aratz (Earth/land) of Galaid (Gilead).
Yaayar (Jair) mawath (death), and was qabar (bury) Qamawan (in) Kamon.

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) again ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, and ibad (servant) the Bail (Baals), and the Ishatharawath (Ashtaroth), and the Alahayam of Aram (Syria), and the Alahayam of Tzayadawan (Sidon), and the Alahayam of Mawaab (Moab), and the Alahayam of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon), and the Alahayam of the Palashathay (Philistines); and they forsook Yahawah, and didn't ibad (servant) him.

The ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah was charah (hot with anger) against Yasharaal (Israel), and he makar (sold) them into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and into the yad (hand) of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon).

They troubled and ratzatz (oppressed) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) that year. For eighteen shanah (years), they ratzatz (oppressed) all the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) that were ibar (beyond) the Yaradan (Jordan) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the Amaray (Amorites), which is in Galaid (Gilead).

The ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) ibar (pass over/through) over the Yaradan (Jordan) to lacham (fight) also against Yahawadah (Judah), and against Banayamayan (Benjamin), and against the bayath (house) of Aparayam (Ephraim); so that Yasharaal (Israel) was very yatzar (distressed).
The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) zaiq (cried) to Yahawah, amar (spoke), We have chataa (sinned) against you, even because we have forsaken our Alahayam, and have ibad (servant) the Bail (Baals).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), Didn't I save you from the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and from the Amaray (Amorites), from the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon), and from the Palashathay (Philistines)?
The Tzayadanay (Sidonians) Imalaq (also), and the Amalekites, and the maiwan (maonites), lachatz (oppressed) you; and you tzaiq (cried) to me, and I yashai (salvation) you out of their yad (hand).
Yet you have forsaken me, and ibad (servant) other Alahayam: therefore I will yashai (salvation) you no more.
Yalak (go) and zaiq (cry) to the Alahayam which you have bachar (chosen). Let them yashai (salvation) you in the ith (time) of your tzarah (distress)!

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke) to Yahawah, We have chataa (sinned): ishah (make) you to us whatever seems tawab (pleasant/functional) to you; only natzal (deliver) us, please, this yawam (day).
They sawar (put) away the foreign Alahayam from qarab (among / near) them, and ibad (servant) Yahawah; and his napash (living being/soul) was qatzar (grieved) for the misery of Yasharaal (Israel).

Then the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) were tzaiq (gathered) together, and chanah (encamped) in Galaid (Gilead). The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) asap (assembled) themselves together, and chanah (encamped) Matzapah (in) Mizpah.

The im (people / nation), the shar (prince / ruler) of Galaid (Gilead), amar (spoke) ayash (husband/individual man) to rai (neigbor/another person), What ayash (husband/individual man) is he who will chalal (begin) to lacham (fight) against the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon)? He shall be raash (head) over all the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Galaid (Gilead).

Now Yapathach (Jephthah) the Galaiday (Gileadite) was a gabawar (mighty) man of valor, and he was the ban (son) of a prostitute: and Galaid (Gilead) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Yapathach (Jephthah).

Galaid (Gilead's) ashah (wife/individual woman) yalad (birth / begot) him ban (son); and when his ashah (wife/individual woman) ban (son) gadal (grew) up, they garash (drove) out Yapathach (Jephthah), and amar (spoke) to him, You shall not nachal (inherit) in our ab (father) bayath (house); for you are the ban (son) of achar (other) ashah (wife/individual woman).

Then Yapathach (Jephthah) barach (fled) from his ach (brother/kinsman), and lived in the aratz (Earth/land) of Tawab (Tob): and there were laqat (gathered) rayaq (vain) ayash (husband/individual man) to Yapathach (Jephthah), and they yatzaa (go out / come out) out with him.
It happened after a yawam (day), that the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) made lacham (war) against Yasharaal (Israel).

It was so, that when the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) made lacham (war) against Yasharaal (Israel), the zaqan (elders) of Galaid (Gilead) yalak (went) to laqach (take / seized) Yapathach (Jephthah) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Tawab (Tob);
And they amar (spoke) to Yapathach (Jephthah), yalak (come) and be our chief, that we may lacham (fight) with the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon).

Yapathach (Jephthah) amar (spoke) to the zaqan (elders) of Galaid (Gilead), Didn't you shanaa (hate) me, and garash (drive) me out of my ab (father) bayath (house)? Why bawaa (come) you come to me now when you are in tzar (oppressor / distressor)?

The zaqan (elders) of Galaid (Gilead) amar (spoke) to Yapathach (Jephthah), Therefore we have shawab (turn back / repent) again to you now, that you may halak (move) with us, and lacham (fight) with the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon); and you shall be our raash (head) over all the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Galaid (Gilead).

Yapathach (Jephthah) amar (spoke) to the zaqan (elders) of Galaid (Gilead), If you shawab (turn back / repent) me home again to lacham (fight) with the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon), and Yahawah nathan (give) them panayam (before) me, shall I be your raash (head)?

The zaqan (elders) of Galaid (Gilead) amar (spoke) to Yapathach (Jephthah), Yahawah shall be shamai (hearken / hear) between us; surely according to your dabar (word / matter) so will we ishah (make).

Then Yapathach (Jephthah) yalak (went) with the zaqan (elders) of Galaid (Gilead), and the im (people / nation) shawam (place / establish / appoint) him raash (head) and chief over them: and Yapathach (Jephthah) dabar (word / matter) all his dabar (word / matter) panayam (before) Yahawah Matzapah (in) Mizpah.

Yapathach (Jephthah) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to the malak (king) of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon), amar (spoke), What bawaa (come) you to do with me, that you have come to me to lacham (fight) against my aratz (Earth/land)?

The malak (king) of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) amar (spoke) to the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yapathach (Jephthah), Because Yasharaal (Israel) laqach (take / seized) away my aratz (Earth/land), when he ilah (go up / offer) up out of Matzarayam (Egypt), from the Aranawan (Arnon) even to the Yabaq (Jabbok), and to the Yaradan (Jordan): now therefore shawab (turn back / repent) that territory again peaceably.
Yapathach (Jephthah) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) again to the malak (king) of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon);

And he amar (spoke) to him, Thus amar (spoke) Yapathach (Jephthah): Yasharaal (Israel) didn't laqach (take / seized) away the aratz (Earth/land) of Mawaab (Moab), nor the aratz (Earth/land) of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon),

But when they ilah (go up / offer) up from Matzarayam (Egypt), and Yasharaal (Israel) yalak (went) through the madabar (wilderness) to the sawap (red) yam (sea/waters), and bawaa (come) to Qadash (Kadesh);

Then Yasharaal (Israel) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to the malak (king) of Adam (Edom), amar (spoke), ‘Please let me ibar (pass over/through) through your aratz (Earth/land);’ but the malak (king) of Adam (Edom) didn't shamai (hearken / hear). In the same way, he shalach (send) to the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab); but he would not: and Yasharaal (Israel) stayed in Qadash (Kadesh).

Then they yalak (went) through the madabar (wilderness), and sabab (went) around the aratz (Earth/land) of Adam (Edom), and the aratz (Earth/land) of Mawaab (Moab), and bawaa (come) by the mazarach (east) side of the aratz (Earth/land) of Mawaab (Moab), and they chanah (encamped) on the other ibar (side) of the Aranawan (Arnon); but they didn't bawaa (come) within the gabawal (border/boundary) of Mawaab (Moab), for the Aranawan (Arnon) was the gabawal (border/boundary) of Mawaab (Moab).

Yasharaal (Israel) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to Sayachawan (Sihon) malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), the malak (king) of Chashabawan (Heshbon); and Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke) to him, ‘Please let us ibar (pass over/through) through your aratz (Earth/land) to my maqawam (place).’

But Sayachawan (Sihon) didn't aman (believe / have faith) Yasharaal (Israel) to ibar (pass over/through) through his gabawal (border/boundary); but Sayachawan (Sihon) asap (gathered) all his im (people / nation) asap (together), and chanah (encamped) in Yahatz (Jahaz), and lacham (fought) against Yasharaal (Israel).

Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), nathan (give) Sayachawan (Sihon) and all his im (people / nation) into the yad (hand) of Yasharaal (Israel), and they nakah (struck) them: so Yasharaal (Israel) yarash (possessed) all the aratz (Earth/land) of the Amaray (Amorites), the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of that aratz (Earth/land).

They yarash (possessed) all the gabawal (border/boundary) of the Amaray (Amorites), from the Aranawan (Arnon) even to the Yabaq (Jabbok), and from the madabar (wilderness) even to the Yaradan (Jordan).

So now Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), has yarash (dispossessed) the Amaray (Amorites) from panayam (before) his im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel), and should you yarash (possess) them?

Won't you yarash (possess) that which Kamawash (Chemosh) your Alahayam yarash (gives) you to possess? So whoever Yahawah our Alahayam has yarash (dispossessed) from panayam (before) us, them will we yarash (possess).

Now are you anything tawab (pleasant/functional) than Balaq (Balak) the ban (son) of Tzapawar (Zippor), malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab)? Did he rayab (ever) rayab (strive) against Yasharaal (Israel), or did he rayab (ever) lacham (fight) against them?

While Yasharaal (Israel) lived in Chashabawan (Heshbon) and its bath (daughter), and in Irawair (Aroer) and its bath (daughter), and in all the iyar (cities) that are along by the yad (hand) of the Aranawan (Arnon), shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shanah (years); why didn't you natzal (recover) them within that ith (time)?

I therefore have not chataa (sinned) against you, but you ishah (make) me rai (wrong) to lacham (war) against me. Yahawah, the shapat (judge), be shapat (judge) this yawam (day) between the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) and the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon).
However the malak (king) of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) didn't shamai (hearken / hear) to the dabar (word / matter) of Yapathach (Jephthah) which he shalach (send) him.

Then the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah came on Yapathach (Jephthah), and he ibar (pass over/through) over Galaid (Gilead) and Manashah (Manasseh), and ibar (pass over/through) over Matzapah (Mizpeh) of Galaid (Gilead), and from Matzapah (Mizpeh) of Galaid (Gilead) he ibar (pass over/through) over to the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon).
Yapathach (Jephthah) nadar (make vow) a nadar (vow) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), If you will nathan (give) nathan (give) the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) into my yad (hand),

Then it shall be, that whatever yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from the dalath (doors) of my bayath (house) to qaraah (meet) me, when I shawab (turn back / repent) in shalawam (peace / safety) from the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon), it shall be yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)), and I will ilah (go up / offer) it up for a burnt ilah (offering).
So Yapathach (Jephthah) ibar (pass over/through) over to the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) to lacham (fight) against them; and Yahawah nathan (give) them into his yad (hand).

He nakah (struck) them from Irawair (Aroer) until you bawaa (come) to Manayath (Minnith), even isharayam (twenty) iyar (cities), and to Abelcheramim, with a very gadawal (very great/important/mighty) makah (slaughter). So the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) were kanai (subdued) panayam (before) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Yapathach (Jephthah) bawaa (come) Matzapah (to) Mizpah to his bayath (house); and behold, his bath (daughter) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) him with tambourines and with machalah (dances): and she was his only yachayad (child); besides her he had neither ban (son) aw (or) bath (daughter).

It happened, when he raah (see) her, that he qarai (tore) his clothes, and amar (spoke), ahah (alas), my bath (daughter)! You have karai (brought) me very low, and you are one of those who ikar (trouble) me; for I have patzah (opened) my pah (mouth) to Yahawah, and I can't shawab (turn back / repent) back.

She amar (spoke) to him, My ab (father), you have patzah (opened) your pah (mouth) to Yahawah; ishah (make) to me according to that which yatzaa (go out / come out) proceeded out of your pah (mouth), because Yahawah ishah (make) taken naqamah (vengeance) for you on your ayab (enemy), even on the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon).

She amar (spoke) to her ab (father), Let this thing be ishah (make) for me: let me rapah (alone) shanayam (two) chadash (month), that I may depart and yarad (go) down on the har (mountain), and bakah (bewail) my bathawalayam (virginity), I and my companions.

He amar (spoke), "yalak (go)." He shalach (send) her away for shanayam (two) chadash (month): and she departed, she and her raih (companions), and bakah (mourned) her bathawalayam (virginity) on the har (mountain).

It happened at the qatz (end) of shanayam (two) chadash (month), that she shawab (turn back / repent) to her ab (father), who ishah (make) with her according to his nadar (vow) which he had nadar (make vow): and she was a virgin. It was a chaq (statute) in Yasharaal (Israel),
That the bath (daughter) of Yasharaal (Israel) yalak (went) yawam (day) to celebrate the bath (daughter) of Yapathach (Jephthah) the Galaiday (Gileadite) arabai (four) yawam (day) in a shanah (year).

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Aparayam (Ephraim) were tzaiq (gathered) together, and ibar (pass over/through) northward; and they amar (spoke) to Yapathach (Jephthah), Why ibar (pass over/through) you pass over to lacham (fight) against the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon), and didn't qaraa (called) us to yalak (go) with you? We will sharap (burn) your bayath (house) around you with ash (fire)!

Yapathach (Jephthah) amar (spoke) to them, I and my im (people / nation) were at maad (great) strife with the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon); and when I zaiq (called) you, you didn't yashai (salvation) me out of their yad (hand).

When I raah (see) that you didn't yashai (salvation) me, I shawam (place / establish / appoint) my napash (living being/soul) in my kap (hand), and ibar (pass over/through) over against the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon), and Yahawah nathan (give) them into my yad (hand). Why then have you ilah (go up / offer) up to me this yawam (day), to lacham (fight) against me?

Then Yapathach (Jephthah) qabatz (gathered) together all the ayash (husband/individual man) of Galaid (Gilead), and lacham (fought) with Aparayam (Ephraim); and the ayash (husband/individual man) of Galaid (Gilead) nakah (struck) Aparayam (Ephraim), because they amar (spoke), You are palayat (fugitives) of Aparayam (Ephraim), you Galaid (Gileadites), in the thawak (midst) of Aparayam (Ephraim), and in the thawak (midst) of Manashah (Manasseh).

The Galaid (Gileadites) lakad (took) the maibar (fords) of the Yaradan (Jordan) against the Aparayam (Ephraimites). It was so, that when the palayat (fugitives) of Aparayam (Ephraim) amar (spoke), "Let me ibar (pass over/through) over," the ibar (pass over/through) of Galaid (Gilead) amar (spoke) to him, "Are you an Aparathay (Ephraimite)?" If he amar (spoke), No;

Then they amar (spoke) to him, "Now amar (spoke) ‘shabal (shibboleth);’" and he amar (spoke) "sabalath (sibboleth);" for he couldn't manage to dabar (word / matter) it kawan (right): then they siezed him, and shachat (killed) him at the maibar (fords) of the Yaradan (Jordan). At that ith (time), arabaiyam (forty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) of Aparayam (Ephraim) napal (fall / be cast down).

Yapathach (Jephthah) shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel) shash (six) shanah (years). Then Yapathach (Jephthah) the Galaiday (Gileadite) mawath (death), and was qabar (bury) in the iyar (cities) of Galaid (Gilead).
Achar (other) him Abatzan (Ibzan) of Bayathalacham (Bethlehem) shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel).

He had shalawashayam (thirty) ban (son); and shalawashayam (thirty) bath (daughter) he shalach (send) chawatz (abroad), and shalawashayam (thirty) bath (daughter) he bawaa (come) in from chawatz (abroad) for his ban (son). He shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel) shabai (seven) shanah (years).
Abatzan (Ibzan) mawath (death), and was qabar (bury) at Bayathalacham (Bethlehem).
Achar (other) him Ayalawan (Elon) the Zabawalanay (Zebulunite) shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel); and he shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel) ishar (ten) shanah (years).
Ayalawan (Elon) the Zabawalanay (Zebulunite) mawath (death), and was qabar (bury) in Ayalawan (Aijalon) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Zabawalawan (Zebulun).
Achar (other) him Ibadawan (Abdon) the ban (son) of Halal (Hillel) the paraithawanay (pirathonite) shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel).

He had arabaiyam (forty) ban (son) and shalawashayam (thirty) ban (son)' sons, who rakab (rode) on shabaiyam (seventy) donkey iyar (colts): and he shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel) shamanah (eight) shanah (years).

Ibadawan (Abdon) the ban (son) of Halal (Hillel) the paraithawanay (pirathonite) mawath (death), and was qabar (bury) in Paraithawan (Pirathon) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Aparayam (Ephraim), in the har (mountain) country of the Imalaqay (Amalekites).

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) again ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah; and Yahawah nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years).

There was a achad (one) ayash (husband/individual man) of Tzaraih (Zorah), of the mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) of the Danay (Danites), whose sham (name) was Manawach (Manoah); and his ashah (wife/individual woman) was iqar (barren), and didn't yalad (birth / begot).

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah raah (see) to the ashah (wife/individual woman), and amar (spoke) to her, See now, you are iqar (barren), and don't yalad (birth / begot); but you shall harah (conceive), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son).
Now therefore please beware and shathah (drinks) no yayan (wine) nor strong shathah (drinks), and don't akal (eat) any tamaa (unclean) thing:

For, behold, you shall harah (conceive), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son); and no mawarah (razor) shall ilah (go up / offer) on his raash (head); for the nair (child) shall be a Nazirite to Alahayam from the batan (womb): and he shall chalal (begin) to yashai (salvation) Yasharaal (Israel) out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines).

Then the ashah (wife/individual woman) bawaa (come) and amar (spoke) her ayash (husband/individual man), amar (spoke), A ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam bawaa (come) to me, and his maraah (face) was like the maraah (face) of the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Alahayam, very awesome; and I didn't shaal (ask) him where he was from, neither did he nagad (tell) me his sham (name):

But he amar (spoke) to me, ‘Behold, you shall harah (conceive), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son); and now shakar (drink) no yayan (wine) nor strong shathah (drinks), and akal (eat) not any tamaah (unclean) thing; for the nair (child) shall be a Nazirite to Alahayam from the batan (womb) to the yawam (day) of his mawath (death).’

Then Manawach (Manoah) entreated Yahawah, and amar (spoke), Oh, Adawan, please let the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam whom you did shalach (send) bawaa (come) again to us, and yarah (teach) us what we shall ishah (make) to the nair (child) who shall be yalad (birth / begot).

Alahayam shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of Manawach (Manoah); and the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Alahayam bawaa (come) again to the ashah (wife/individual woman) as she yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the shadah (field): but Manawach (Manoah), her ayash (husband/individual man), wasn't with her.

The ashah (wife/individual woman) mahar (made) haste, and rawatz (ran), and amar (spoke) her ayash (husband/individual man), and amar (spoke) to him, Behold, the ayash (husband/individual man) has raah (see) to me, who bawaa (come) to me that yawam (day).

Manawach (Manoah) qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) achar (other) his ashah (wife/individual woman), and bawaa (come) to the ayash (husband/individual man), and amar (spoke) to him, "Are you the ayash (husband/individual man) who dabar (word / matter) to the ashah (wife/individual woman)?" He amar (spoke), I am.
Manawach (Manoah) amar (spoke), Now let your dabar (word / matter) happen. What shall the nair (child's) mashapat (way) of maishah (life) and mission be?
The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah amar (spoke) to Manawach (Manoah), Of all that I amar (spoke) to the ashah (wife/individual woman) let her beware.

She may not akal (eat) of anything that yatzaa (go out / come out) of the gapan (vine), neither let her shathah (drinks) yayan (wine) or strong shathah (drinks), nor akal (eat) any tamaah (unclean) thing; all that I tzawah (commanded) her let her shamar (keep/guard).
Manawach (Manoah) amar (spoke) to the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah, Please, let us itzar (detain) you, that we may make a young goat ready for you.

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah amar (spoke) to Manawach (Manoah), "Though you itzar (detain) me, I won't akal (eat) of your lacham (bread); and if you will ishah (make) a burnt ishah (make), you must ishah (make) it to Yahawah." For Manawach (Manoah) didn't yadai (know) that he was the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah.
Manawach (Manoah) amar (spoke) to the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah, What is your sham (name), that when your dabar (word / matter) happen, we may honor you?
The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, Why do you shaal (ask) about my sham (name), since it is palaay (wonderful)?

So Manawach (Manoah) laqach (take / seized) the young goat with the meal manachah (offering), and ilah (go up / offer) it on the tzawar (rock) to Yahawah. Then the angel ishah (make) a palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) thing as Manawach (Manoah) and his ashah (wife/individual woman) raah (see) on.

For it happened, when the lahab (flame) ilah (go up / offer) up toward the sky from off the mazabach (altar), that the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah ilah (go up / offer) in the lahab (flame) of the mazabach (altar): and Manawach (Manoah) and his ashah (wife/individual woman) raah (see) on; and they fell on their panayam (faces) to the aratz (Earth/land).

But the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah didn't raah (see) to Manawach (Manoah) or to his ashah (wife/individual woman) any more. Then Manawach (Manoah) yadai (knew) that he was the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah.
Manawach (Manoah) amar (spoke) to his ashah (wife/individual woman), We shall mawath (death) mawath (death), because we raah (see) seen Alahayam.

But his ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke) to him, If Yahawah were chapatz (pleased) to mawath (death) us, he wouldn't have laqach (take / seized) a burnt ilah (offering) and a meal ilah (offering) at our yad (hand), neither would he raah (see) shown us all these things, nor would at this ith (time) have shamai (hearken / hear) such things as these.
The ashah (wife/individual woman) yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son), and qaraa (called) him Shamashawan (Samson): and the nair (child) gadal (grew), and Yahawah barak (blessed) him.
The rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah chalal (began) to paim (move) him in Mahaneh Dan (Dan), between Tzaraih (Zorah) and Ashathaal (Eshtaol).
Shamashawan (Samson) yarad (went) down to Thamanah (Timnah), and raah (see) a ashah (wife/individual woman) in Thamanah (Timnah) of the bath (daughter) of the Palashathay (Philistines).

He ilah (go up / offer) up, and nagad (told) his ab (father) and his am (mother), and said, I raah (see) seen a ashah (wife/individual woman) in Thamanah (Timnah) of the bath (daughter) of the Palashathay (Philistines): now therefore laqach (take / seized) her for me as ashah (wife/individual woman).

Then his ab (father) and his am (mother) amar (spoke) to him, "Is there ayan (never) a ashah (wife/individual woman) among the bath (daughter) of your ach (brother/kinsman), or among all my im (people / nation), that you halak (move) to laqach (take / seized) a ashah (wife/individual woman) of the iral (uncircumcised) Palashathay (Philistines)?" Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke) to his ab (father), laqach (take / seized) her for me; for she yashar (pleases) me well.

But his ab (father) and his am (mother) didn't yadai (know) that it was of Yahawah; for he baqash (sought) an thaanah (occasion) against the Palashathay (Philistines). Now at that ith (time) the Palashathay (Philistines) mashal (rule/have dominion) rule over Yasharaal (Israel).

Then yarad (went) Shamashawan (Samson) down, and his ab (father) and his am (mother), to Thamanah (Timnah), and bawaa (come) to the karam (vineyards) of Thamanah (Timnah): and behold, a young aray (lion) shaag (roared) qaraah (against) him.

The rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah tzalach (came) mightily on him, and he tore him as he would have torn a young goat; and he had maawamah (nothing) in his yad (hand): but he didn't nagad (tell) his ab (father) or his am (mother) what he ishah (make) done.
He yarad (went) down, and dabar (word / matter) with the ashah (wife/individual woman), and she yashar (pleased) Shamashawan (Samson) well.

After a yawam (day) he shawab (turn back / repent) to laqach (take / seized) her; and he shawab (turn back / repent) sawar (aside) to raah (see) the carcass of the aray (lion): and raah (see), there was a idah (swarm) of dabawarah (bees) in the gawayah (corpse) of the aray (lion), and dabash (honey).

He radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) it into his kap (hands), and yalak (went) on, akal (eat) as he halak (move); and he came to his ab (father) and am (mother), and nathan (give) to them, and they akal (eat): but he didn't nagad (tell) them that he radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) taken the dabash (honey) out of the gawayah (corpse) of the aray (lion).
His ab (father) yarad (went) down to the ashah (wife/individual woman): and Shamashawan (Samson) ishah (make) there a mashathah (feast); for so used the bachawar (young) men to ishah (make).
It happened, when they raah (see) him, that they laqach (take / seized) shalawashayam (thirty) marai (companions) to be with him.

Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke) to them, "Let me tell you a chayadah (riddle) now. If you can nagad (declare) it to me within the shabai (seven) yawam (day) of the mashathah (feast), and matzaa (find) it out, then I will nathan (give) you shalawashayam (thirty) sadayan (linen) garments and shalawashayam (thirty) chalayapah (changes) of bagad (clothing);

But if you can't nagad (declare) it to me, then you shall nathan (give) me shalawashayam (thirty) sadayan (linen) garments and shalawashayam (thirty) chalayapah (changes) of bagad (clothing)." They amar (spoke) to him, chawad (put) forth your chayadah (riddle), that we may shamai (hearken / hear) it.

He amar (spoke) to them, "Out of the eater yatzaa (go out / come out) forth maakal (food). Out of the iz (strong) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth sweetness." They couldn't in shalawash (three) yawam (day) nagad (declare) the chayadah (riddle).

It happened on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), that they amar (spoke) to Shamashawan (Samson's) ashah (wife/individual woman), pathah (entice) your ayash (husband/individual man), that he may nagad (declare) to us the chayadah (riddle), lest we sharap (burn) you and your ab (father) bayath (house) with ash (fire). Have you qaraa (called) us to impoverish us? Is it not so?

Shamashawan (Samson's) ashah (wife/individual woman) bakah (wept) before him, and amar (spoke), "You just shanaa (hate) me, and don't ahab (love) me. You have chawad (put) forth a chayadah (riddle) to the ban (son) of my im (people / nation), and haven't nagad (told) it me." He said to her, Behold, I haven't amar (spoke) it my ab (father) nor my am (mother), and shall I nagad (tell) you?

She bakah (wept) before him the shabai (seven) yawam (day), while their mashathah (feast) hayah (came to pass): and it happened on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), that he nagad (told) her, because she tzawaq (pressed) him severely; and she nagad (told) the chayadah (riddle) to the ban (son) of her im (people / nation).

The ayash (husband/individual man) of the iyar (city) amar (spoke) to him on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) before the charas (sun) bawaa (come) down, "What is sweeter than dabash (honey)? What is stronger than a aray (lion)?" He amar (spoke) to them, If you hadn't charash (plowed) with my igalah (heifer), you wouldn't matzaa (have) found out my chayadah (riddle).

The rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah tzalach (came) mightily on him, and he yarad (went) down to Ashaqalawan (Ashkelon), and nakah (struck) shalawashayam (thirty) ayash (husband/individual man) of them, and took their spoil, and nathan (give) the chalayapah (changes) of clothing to those who nagad (declared) the chayadah (riddle). His ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger), and he ilah (go up / offer) up to his ab (father) bayath (house).
But Shamashawan (Samson's) ashah (wife/individual woman) was given to his marai (companion), whom he had used as his raih (friend).

But it happened after a yawam (day), in the time of chatah (wheat) qatzayar (harvest), that Shamashawan (Samson) paqad (visit) his ashah (wife/individual woman) with a young goat; and he amar (spoke), "I will bawaa (come) in to my ashah (wife/individual woman) into the room." But her ab (father) wouldn't allow him to bawaa (come) in.

Her ab (father) amar (spoke), I most certainly amar (spoke) that you had shanaa (hate) shanaa (hate) her; therefore I nathan (give) her to your marai (companion). Isn't her younger achawath (sister) more tawab (pleasant/functional) than she? Please take her, instead.
Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke) to them, paim (this) time I will be naqah (clean/innocent) in regard of the Palashathay (Philistines), when I rai (harm) them.

Shamashawan (Samson) yalak (went) and lakad (caught) shalawash (three) maah (hundred) foxes, and laqach (take / seized) torches, and panah (turned) zanab (tail) to zanab (tail), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) a lapayad (torch) in the thawak (midst) between every shanayam (two) zanab (tails).

When he had bair (set) the lapayad (brands) on ash (fire), he shalach (send) them go into the standing grain of the Palashathay (Philistines), and burnt up both the gadayash (shocks) and the standing grain, and also the zayath (olive) groves.

Then the Palashathay (Philistines) amar (spoke), "Who ishah (make) done this?" They amar (spoke), "Shamashawan (Samson), the son-in-law of the Thamanay (Timnite), because he has laqach (take / seized) his ashah (wife/individual woman), and nathan (give) her to his marai (companion)." The Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up, and burnt her and her ab (father) with ash (fire).
Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke) to them, If you behave like zaath (this), naqam (surely) I will be avenged of you, and achar (other) that I will chadal (cease).

He nakah (struck) them shawaq (hip) and yarak (thigh) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) makah (slaughter): and he yarad (went) down and lived in the cleft of the salai (rock) of Iyatam (Etam).
Then the Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up, and chanah (encamped) in Yahawadah (Judah), and natash (spread) themselves in Lachay (Lehi).

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Yahawadah (Judah) amar (spoke), "Why have you ilah (go up / offer) up amar (spoke) us?" They said, We have ilah (go up / offer) up to asar (bind) Shamashawan (Samson), to ishah (make) to him as he ishah (make) done to us.

Then shalawash (three) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man) of Yahawadah (Judah) yarad (went) down to the cleft of the salai (rock) of Iyatam (Etam), and amar (spoke) to Shamashawan (Samson), "Don't you yadai (know) that the Palashathay (Philistines) are mashal (rule/have dominion) over us? What then is this that you ishah (make) done to us?" He amar (spoke) to them, As they ishah (make) to me, so ishah (make) I done to them.

They amar (spoke) to him, "We have yarad (come) down to asar (bind) you, that we may nathan (give) you into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines)." Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke) to them, shabai (swear / take oath) to me that you will not pagai (fall) on me yourselves.

They amar (spoke) to him, amar (spoke), "No; but we will asar (bind) you asar (fast), and nathan (give) you into their yad (hand); but mawath (death) we will not mawath (death) you." They asar (bound) him with shanayam (two) chadash (new) ibath (ropes), and ilah (go up / offer) him up from the salai (rock).

When he bawaa (come) to Lachay (Lehi), the Palashathay (Philistines) rawai (shouted) as they met him: and the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah tzalach (came) mightily on him, and the ibath (ropes) that were on his zarawai (arms) became as pashathah (flax) that was burnt with ash (fire), and his asawar (bands) dropped from off his yad (hand).
He matzaa (found) a fresh jawbone of a donkey, and shalach (send) forth his yad (hand), and laqach (take / seized) it, and nakah (struck) a alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man) therewith.

Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke), With the jawbone of a donkey, chamarah (heaps) on chamarah (heaps); with the jawbone of a donkey I have nakah (struck) a alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man).

It happened, when he kalah (complete / finish) made an end of dabar (word / matter), that he shalak (cast) away the jawbone out of his yad (hand); and that maqawam (place) was qaraa (called) Ramathalachay (Ramath) Lehi.

He was very tzamaa (thirsty), and qaraa (called) on Yahawah, and amar (spoke), You nathan (give) given this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thashawaih (deliverance) by the yad (hand) of your ibad (servant); and now shall I mawath (death) for tzamaa (thirst), and napal (fall / be cast down) into the yad (hand) of the iral (uncircumcised)?

But Alahayam split the makathash (hollow) place that is in Lehi, and mayam (Waters) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of it. When he had shathah (drinks), his rawach (spirit / wind) shawab (turn back / repent) again, and he chayah (revived): therefore its sham (name) was qaraa (called) Iyanahaqawaraa (En) Hakkore, which is in Lachay (Lehi), to this yawam (day).
He shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel) in the yawam (day) of the Palashathay (Philistines) isharayam (twenty) shanah (years).
Shamashawan (Samson) yalak (went) to Izah (Gaza), and raah (see) there a prostitute, and bawaa (come) in to her.

The izathay (gazites) were amar (spoke), "Shamashawan (Samson) is here!" They surrounded him, and arab (laid) wait for him all layal (night) in the shair (gate) of the iyar (city), and were charash (quiet) all the layal (night), amar (spoke), Wait until baqar (morning) awar (light), then we will harag (kill) him.

Shamashawan (Samson) shakab (lay) until chatzay (midnight), and qawam (rise up) at chatzay (midnight), and achaz (laid) hold of the dalath (doors) of the shair (gate) of the iyar (city), and the shanayam (two) mazawazah (posts), and plucked them up, barayach (bar) and all, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them on his kathap (shoulders), and carried them up to the raash (head) of the har (mountain) that is panayam (before) Chabarawan (Hebron).
It came to pass afterward, that he ahab (love) a ashah (wife/individual woman) in the nachal (stream / river) of Shawaraq (Sorek), whose sham (name) was Dalayalah (Delilah).

The saran (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up to her, and amar (spoke) to her, pathah (entice) him, and raah (see) in which his gadawal (very great/important/mighty) kach (strength / mighty / power) lies, and by what means we may yakal (prevail) against him, that we may asar (bind) him to inah (oppress / afflict) him; and we will ayash (husband/individual man) nathan (give) you eleven hundred pieces of kasap (silver).

Dalayalah (Delilah) amar (spoke) to Shamashawan (Samson), Please nagad (tell) me where your gadawal (very great/important/mighty) kach (strength / mighty / power) lies, and what you might be asar (bound) to inah (oppress / afflict) you.

Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke) to her, If they asar (bind) me with shabai (seven) lach (green) yathar (cords) that were never charab (dried), then shall I become chalah (afflict), and be as another adam (man).

Then the saran (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up to her shabai (seven) lach (green) yathar (cords) which had not been charab (dried), and she asar (bound) him with them.

Now she had an arab (ambush) waiting in the chadar (inner) room. She amar (spoke) to him, "The Palashathay (Philistines) are on you, Shamashawan (Samson)!" He nathaq (broke) the yathar (cords), as a string of nairath (tow) is nathaq (broken) when it touches the ash (fire). So his kach (strength / mighty / power) was not yadai (known).

Dalayalah (Delilah) amar (spoke) to Shamashawan (Samson), Behold, you have hathal (mocked) me, and dabar (word / matter) me kazab (lies): now please nagad (tell) me with which you might be asar (bound).
He amar (spoke) to her, If they only asar (bind) me with chadash (new) ibath (ropes) with which no malaakah (work) has been done, then shall I become chalah (afflict), and be as another adam (man).

So Dalayalah (Delilah) laqach (take / seized) chadash (new) ibath (ropes), and asar (bound) him therewith, and amar (spoke) to him, "The Palashathay (Philistines) are on you, Shamashawan (Samson)!" The arab (ambush) was waiting in the chadar (inner) room. He nathaq (broke) them off his zarawai (arms) like a chawat (thread).

Dalayalah (Delilah) amar (spoke) to Shamashawan (Samson), "Until hanah (here), you have hathal (mocked) me and dabar (word / matter) me kazab (lies). Nagad (tell) me with what you might be asar (bound)." He amar (spoke) to her, If you weave the shabai (seven) machalapah (locks) of my raash (head) with the masakath (web).

She thaqai (blow / sound alarm) it with the yathad (pin), and amar (spoke) to him, "The Palashathay (Philistines) are on you, Shamashawan (Samson)!" He awakened out of his shanah (sleep), and plucked nasai (away) the yathad (pin) of the arag (beam), and the masakath (web).

She amar (spoke) to him, ayak (how) can you amar (spoke), ‘I ahab (love) you,’ when your lab (heart) is not with me? You have hathal (mocked) me these shalawash (three) paim (times), and have not nagad (told) me where your gadawal (very great/important/mighty) kach (strength / mighty / power) lies.
It happened, when she tzawaq (pressed) him yawam (day) with her dabar (word / matter), and alatz (urged) him, that his napash (living being/soul) was qatzar (troubled) to mawath (death).

He nagad (told) her all his lab (heart), and said to her, No mawarah (razor) has ever ilah (go up / offer) on my raash (head); for I have been a Nazirite to Alahayam from my am (mother) batan (womb). If I am galach (shaved), then my kach (strength / mighty / power) will sawar (go) from me, and I will become chalah (afflict), and be like any other adam (man).

When Dalayalah (Delilah) raah (see) that he had nagad (told) her all his lab (heart), she shalach (send) and qaraa (called) for the saran (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines), amar (spoke), "ilah (go up / offer) up paim (this) once, for he has nagad (told) me all his lab (heart)." Then the saran (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up to her, and ilah (go up / offer) the kasap (money) in their yad (hand).

She made him sleep on her barak (knees); and she qaraa (called) for a ayash (husband/individual man), and galach (shaved) off the shabai (seven) machalapah (locks) of his raash (head); and she chalal (began) to inah (oppress / afflict) him, and his kach (strength / mighty / power) sawar (went) from him.

She amar (spoke), "The Palashathay (Philistines) are upon you, Shamashawan (Samson)!" He awoke out of his shanah (sleep), and amar (spoke), "I will yatzaa (go out / come out) out as at other paim (times), and nair (shake) myself free." But he didn't yadai (know) that Yahawah had sawar (departed) from him.

The Palashathay (Philistines) achaz (laid) hold on him, and naqar (put) out his iyan (eye); and they yarad (brought) him down to Izah (Gaza), and asar (bound) him with nachashath (fetters) of brass; and he tachan (ground) at the mill in the asar (prison).
However the shair (hair) of his raash (head) chalal (began) to tzamach (grow) again ashar (who/that) he was galach (shaved).

The saran (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) asap (gathered) them together to zabach (offer) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) zabach (sacrifice) to Dagawan (Dagon) their Alahayam, and to shamachah (rejoice); for they amar (spoke), Our Alahayam nathan (give) delivered Shamashawan (Samson) our ayab (enemy) into our yad (hand).

When the im (people / nation) raah (see) him, they halal (praise) their Alahayam; for they amar (spoke), Our Alahayam nathan (give) delivered our ayab (enemy) and the charab (destroyer) of our aratz (Earth/land), who has chalal (slain) many of us, into our yad (hand).

It happened, when their lab (heart) were tawab (pleasant/functional), that they amar (spoke), "qaraa (called) for Shamashawan (Samson), that he may entertain us." They qaraa (called) for Shamashawan (Samson) out of the bayath (house); and he performed panayam (before) them. They imad (set) him between the imawad (pillar);

And Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke) to the nair (boy) who chazaq (held) him by the yad (hand), Allow me to yamash (feel) the imawad (pillar) whereupon the bayath (house) kawan (rests), that I may shain (lean) on them.

Now the bayath (house) was malaa (full) of ayash (husband/individual man) and ashah (wife/individual woman); and all the saran (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) were there; and there were on the gag (roof) about shalawash (three) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man) and ashah (wife/individual woman), who raah (see) while Shamashawan (Samson) performed.

Shamashawan (Samson) qaraa (called) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), Adawan Yahawah, zakar (remembrance/memory) me, please, and chazaq (strengthen) me, please, only paim (this) once, Alahayam, that I may be at paim (once) naqam (avenged) of the Palashathay (Philistines) for my shanayam (two) iyan (eye).

Shamashawan (Samson) lapath (took) hold of the shanayam (two) thawak (midst) imawad (pillar) on which the bayath (house) rested, and leaned on them, the achad (one) with his right yamayan (right hand), and the other with his shamaawal (left hand).

Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke), "Let me mawath (death) with the Palashathay (Philistines)!" He natah (bowed) himself with all his kach (strength / mighty / power); and the bayath (house) napal (fall / be cast down) on the saran (lords), and on all the im (people / nation) who were therein. So the mawath (death) that he mawath (death) at his mawath (death) were more than those who he mawath (death) in his chay (life).

Then his ach (brother/kinsman) and all the bayath (house) of his ab (father) yarad (came) down, and nashaa (lift) him, and ilah (go up / offer) him up, and qabar (bury) him between Tzaraih (Zorah) and Ashathaal (Eshtaol) in the burial site of Manawach (Manoah) his ab (father). He shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel) isharayam (twenty) shanah (years).
There was a ayash (husband/individual man) of the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), whose sham (name) was Mayakahaw (Micah).

He amar (spoke) to his am (mother), "The eleven hundred pieces of kasap (silver) that were laqach (take / seized) from you, about which you uttered a alah (these), and also amar (spoke) it in my azan (ears), behold, the kasap (silver) is with me; I laqach (take / seized) it." His am (mother) amar (spoke), barak (blessed) be my ban (son) of Yahawah.

He shawab (turn back / repent) the eleven hundred pieces of kasap (silver) to his am (mother); and his am (mother) amar (spoke), I most certainly qadash (set apart/make holy) the kasap (silver) to Yahawah from my yad (hand) for my ban (son), to ishah (make) an engraved pasal (idol/graven image) and a molten pasal (idol/graven image). Now therefore I will shawab (turn back / repent) it to you.

When he shawab (turn back / repent) the kasap (money) to his am (mother), his am (mother) laqach (take / seized) two maah (hundred) pieces of kasap (silver), and nathan (give) them to the tzarap (founder), who ishah (make) of it an engraved pasal (idol/graven image) and a masakah (molten) image: and it was in the bayath (house) of Mayakahaw (Micah).

The ayash (husband/individual man) Mayakah (Micah) had a bayath (house) of Alahayam, and he ishah (make) an apawad (ephod), and tharapayam (teraphim), and malaa (consecrated) achad (one) of his ban (son), who became his kahan (priest).
In those yawam (day) there was no malak (king) in Yasharaal (Israel): every ayash (husband/individual man) ishah (make) that which was yashar (right) in his own iyan (eye).
There was a nair (young) man out of Bayathalacham (Bethlehem) Judah, of the mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) of Yahawadah (Judah), who was a Lawayay (Levite); and he lived there.

The ayash (husband/individual man) departed out of the iyar (city), out of Bayathalacham (Bethlehem) Judah, to live where he could matzaa (find) a place, and he bawaa (come) to the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim) to the bayath (house) of Mayakah (Micah), as he traveled.

Mayakah (Micah) amar (spoke) to him, "ayan (where) did you bawaa (come) from?" He amar (spoke) to him, I am a Lawayay (Levite) of Bayathalacham (Bethlehem) Judah, and I am looking for a halak (move) to live.

Mayakah (Micah) amar (spoke) to him, "yashab (inhabit/dwell) with me, and be to me a ab (father) and a kahan (priest), and I will nathan (give) you ishar (ten) pieces of kasap (silver) per yawam (day), a irak (suit) of bagad (clothing), and your food." So the Lawayay (Levite) yalak (went) in.
The Lawayay (Levite) was yaal (content) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) with the ayash (husband/individual man); and the young ayash (husband/individual man) was to him as nair (one) of his ban (son).
Mayakah (Micah) malaa (consecrated) the Lawayay (Levite), and the nair (young) man became his kahan (priest), and was in the bayath (house) of Mayakah (Micah).
Then Mayakah (Micah) amar (spoke), Now yadai (know) I that Yahawah will do yatab (good) to me, since I have a Lawayay (Levite) to my kahan (priest).

In those yawam (day) there was no malak (king) in Yasharaal (Israel): and in those yawam (day) the shabat (tribe) of the Danay (Danites) baqash (sought) an nachalah (inheritance) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) in; for to that yawam (day), their nachalah (inheritance) napal (fall / be cast down) not fallen to them thawak (midst) the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel).

The ban (son) Dan (of) Dan shalach (send) of their mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) chamash (five) ban (son) from their whole number, ban (son) of valor, from Tzaraih (Zorah), and from Ashathaal (Eshtaol), to ragal (spy) out the aratz (Earth/land), and to chaqar (search) it; and they amar (spoke) to them, "yalak (go), explore the aratz (Earth/land)!" They bawaa (come) to the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), to the bayath (house) of Mayakah (Micah), and lawan (lodged) there.

When they were by the bayath (house) of Mayakah (Micah), they nakar (knew) the qawal (sound / voice) of the nair (young) man the Lawayay (Levite); and they sawar (turned) aside there, and amar (spoke) to him, Who bawaa (come) you here? What ishah (make) you do in this place? What do you have here?
He amar (spoke) to them, zah (this/that/these) and zah (this/that/these) has Mayakah (Micah) dealt with me, and he has shakar (hired) me, and I am become his kahan (priest).
They amar (spoke) to him, Please ask shaal (counsel) of Alahayam, that we may yadai (know) whether our darak (way) which we halak (move) shall be prosperous.
The kahan (priest) amar (spoke) to them, yalak (go) in shalawam (peace / safety). Your darak (way) in which you yalak (go) is nakach (before) Yahawah.

Then the chamash (five) ayash (husband/individual man) departed, and bawaa (come) to Layash (Laish), and raah (see) the im (people / nation) who were qarab (among / near), how they lived in security, in the mashapat (way) of the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), shaqat (quiet) and batach (secure); for there was none in the aratz (Earth/land), yarash (possessing) authority, that might kalam (put) them to shame in anything, and they were rachawaq (far) from the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), and had no dealings with any adam (man).
They bawaa (come) to their ach (brother/kinsman) to Tzaraih (Zorah) and Ashathaal (Eshtaol): and their ach (brother/kinsman) amar (spoke) to them, What do you say?

They amar (spoke), qawam (rise up), and let us ilah (go up / offer) up against them; for we raah (see) seen the aratz (Earth/land), and behold, it is very tawab (pleasant/functional). Do you stand still? Don't be itzal (slothful) to yalak (go) and to bawaa (come) in to yarash (possess) the aratz (Earth/land).

When you bawaa (come), you shall bawaa (come) to a batach (secure) im (people / nation), and the aratz (Earth/land) is rachab (large); for Alahayam nathan (give) given it into your yad (hand), a maqawam (place) where there is no machasawar (want) of anything that is in the aratz (Earth/land).

There nasai (set) forth from there of the mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) of the Danay (Danites), out of Tzaraih (Zorah) and out of Ashathaal (Eshtaol), shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man) girt with kalay (weapons) of malachamah (war).

They ilah (go up / offer) up, and chanah (encamped) in Kiriath Qarayathayairayam (Jearim), in Yahawadah (Judah): therefore they qaraa (called) that maqawam (place) Machanahadan (Mahaneh) Dan, to this yawam (day); behold, it is achar (other) Kiriath Qarayathayairayam (Jearim).
They ibar (pass over/through) there to the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), and bawaa (come) to the bayath (house) of Mayakah (Micah).

Then the chamash (five) ayash (husband/individual man) who halak (move) to ragal (spy) out the aratz (Earth/land) of Layash (Laish) inah (answer / respond), and amar (spoke) to their ach (brother/kinsman), Do you yadai (know) that there is in these bayath (house) an apawad (ephod), and tharapayam (teraphim), and an engraved pasal (idol/graven image), and a masakah (molten) image? Now therefore yadai (consider) what you ishah (make) to do.

They sawar (turned) aside there, and bawaa (come) to the bayath (house) of the nair (young) man the Lawayay (Levite), even to the bayath (house) of Mayakah (Micah), and shaal (asked) him of his welfare.

The shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man) girt with their kalay (weapons) of malachamah (war), who were of the ban (son) Dan (of) Dan, natzab (stood) by the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate).

The chamash (five) ayash (husband/individual man) who halak (move) to ragal (spy) out the aratz (Earth/land) ilah (go up / offer) up, and bawaa (come) in there, and laqach (take / seized) the engraved pasayal (image), and the apawad (ephod), and the tharapayam (teraphim), and the masakah (molten) image: and the kahan (priest) natzab (stood) by the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate) with the shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man) girt with kalay (weapons) of malachamah (war).

When these bawaa (come) into Mayakah (Micah's) bayath (house), and laqach (take / seized) the engraved pasal (idol/graven image), the apawad (ephod), and the tharapayam (teraphim), and the masakah (molten) image, the kahan (priest) amar (spoke) to them, What are you ishah (make)?

They amar (spoke) to him, Hold your charash (peace), put your yad (hand) on your pah (mouth), and yalak (go) with us, and be to us a ab (father) and a kahan (priest). Is it tawab (pleasant/functional) for you to be kahan (priest) to the bayath (house) of achad (one) ayash (husband/individual man), or to be kahan (priest) to a shabat (tribe) and a mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) in Yasharaal (Israel)?

The kahan (priest) lab (heart) was yatab (glad), and he laqach (take / seized) the apawad (ephod), and the tharapayam (teraphim), and the engraved pasal (idol/graven image), and bawaa (come) in the qarab (among / near) of the im (people / nation).
So they panah (turned) and departed, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the little tap (ones) and the livestock and the kabawadah (goods) panayam (before) them.

When they were a rachaq (good) way from the bayath (house) of Mayakah (Micah), the ayash (husband/individual man) who were in the bayath (house) near to Mayakah (Micah's) bayath (house) were zaiq (gathered) together, and overtook the ban (son) Dan (of) Dan.
They qaraa (called) to the ban (son) Dan (of) Dan. They sabab (turned) their panayam (faces), and amar (spoke) to Mayakah (Micah), What ails you, that you zaiq (come) with such a company?

He amar (spoke), You have laqach (take / seized) away my Alahayam which I ishah (make), and the kahan (priest), and have yalak (gone) away, and what more do I have? How then do you amar (spoke) to me, ‘What ails you?’

The ban (son) Dan (of) Dan amar (spoke) to him, Don't let your qawal (sound / voice) be shamai (hearken / hear) among us, lest mar (angry) ayash (husband/individual man) pagai (fall) on you, and you asap (lose) your napash (living being/soul), with the lives of your bayath (house).

The ban (son) Dan (of) Dan yalak (went) their darak (way): and when Mayakah (Micah) raah (see) that they were too chazaq (strong) for him, he panah (turned) and shawab (turn back / repent) back to his bayath (house).

They laqach (take / seized) that which Mayakah (Micah) ishah (make) made, and the kahan (priest) whom he bawaa (come), and came to Layash (Laish), to a im (people / nation) shaqat (quiet) and batach (secure), and nakah (struck) them with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword); and they burnt the iyar (city) with ash (fire).

There was no deliverer, because it was rachawaq (far) from Tzayadawan (Sidon), and they had no dealings with any adam (man); and it was in the imaq (valley) that lies by Bayatharachawab (Beth) Rehob. They banah (built) the iyar (city), and lived therein.

They qaraa (called) the sham (name) of the iyar (city) Dan (Dan), after the sham (name) Dan (of) Dan their ab (father), who was yalad (birth / begot) to Yasharaal (Israel): however the sham (name) of the iyar (city) was Layash (Laish) at the raashawan (first).

The ban (son) Dan (of) Dan qawam (rise up) up for themselves the engraved pasal (idol/graven image): and Yawanathan (Jonathan), the ban (son) of Garasham (Gershom), the ban (son) Manashah (of) Moses, he and his ban (son) were kahan (priest) to the shabat (tribe) of the Danay (Danites) until the yawam (day) of the captivity of the aratz (Earth/land).

So they shawam (place / establish / appoint) them up Mayakah (Micah's) engraved pasal (idol/graven image) which he ishah (make), all the yawam (day) that the bayath (house) of Alahayam was in Shayalah (Shiloh).

It happened in those yawam (day), when there was no malak (king) in Yasharaal (Israel), that there was a ayash (husband/individual man) Lawayay (Levite) living on the farther yarakah (side) of the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), who laqach (take / seized) to him a concubine out of Bayathalacham (Bethlehem) Judah.

His payalagash (concubine) zanah (played) the prostitute against him, and yalak (went) away from him to her ab (father) bayath (house) to Bayathalacham (Bethlehem) Judah, and was there the space of arabai (four) chadash (month).

Her ayash (husband/individual man) qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) achar (other) her, to dabar (word / matter) lab (heart) to her, to shawab (turn back / repent) her again, having his nair (servant) with him, and a tzamad (couple) of donkeys: and she bawaa (come) him into her ab (father) bayath (house); and when the ab (father) of the nairah (young) lady raah (see) him, he shamach (rejoiced) to qaraah (meet) him.

His father-in-law, the nairah (young) lady's ab (father), chazaq (retained) him; and he stayed with him shalawash (three) yawam (day): so they akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and lawan (lodged) there.

It happened on the rabayaiy (fourth) yawam (day), that they arose shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and he qawam (rise up) up to depart: and the nairah (young) lady's ab (father) amar (spoke) to his son-in-law, said (strengthen) your lab (heart) with a path (morsel) of lacham (bread), and afterward you shall go your yalak (way).

So they yashab (inhabit/dwell) down, akal (eat), and shathah (drinks), shanayam (two) of them yachad (together): and the nairah (young) lady's ab (father) amar (spoke) to the ayash (husband/individual man), yaal (please) be pleased to stay all lawan (night), and let your lab (heart) be yatab (merry).
The ayash (husband/individual man) qawam (rise up) up to depart; but his father-in-law patzar (urged) him, and he lawan (lodged) there again.

He arose shakam (early) in the baqar (morning) on the chamayashay (fifth) yawam (day) to depart; and the nairah (young) lady's ab (father) amar (spoke), "Please said (strengthen) your labab (heart) and mahah (stay) until the yawam (day) declines;" and they shanayam (two) akal (eat).

When the ayash (husband/individual man) qawam (rise up) up to depart, he, and his payalagash (concubine), and his nair (servant), his father-in-law, the nairah (young) lady's ab (father), amar (spoke) to him, Behold, now the yawam (day) rapah (draws) toward irab (evening), please stay all lawan (night): behold, the yawam (day) chanah (grows) to an end, lawan (lodge) here, that your labab (heart) may be yatab (merry); and machar (tomorrow) go on your darak (way) shakam (early), that you may halak (move) ahal (home).

But the ayash (husband/individual man) wouldn't stay that lawan (night), but he qawam (rise up) up and departed, and bawaa (come) over nakach (against) Yabawas (Jebus) (the same is Yarawashalam (Jerusalem)): and there were with him a tzamad (couple) of donkeys chabash (saddled); his payalagash (concubine) also was with him.

When they were by Yabawas (Jebus), the yawam (day) was maad (far) radad (spent); and the nair (servant) amar (spoke) to his adawan (master / lord), Please yalak (come) and let us sawar (turn) aside into this iyar (city) of the Yabawasay (Jebusites), and lawan (lodge) in it.

His adawan (master / lord) amar (spoke) to him, We won't sawar (turn) aside into the iyar (city) of a nakaray (foreigner), that is not of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel); but we will ibar (pass over/through) over to Gabaih (Gibeah).
He amar (spoke) to his nair (servant), yalak (come) and let us qarab (come close) near to achad (one) of these maqawam (place); and we will lawan (lodge) in Gabaih (Gibeah), or in Ramah (Ramah).
So they ibar (pass over/through) on and went their yalak (way); and the shamash (sun) bawaa (come) down on them atzal (near) to Gabaih (Gibeah), which belongs to Banayamayan (Benjamin).

They sawar (turned) aside there, to bawaa (come) in to lawan (lodge) in Gabaih (Gibeah): and he bawaa (come) in, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) him down in the rachab (street) of the iyar (city); for there was no ayash (husband/individual man) who asap (took) them into his bayath (house) to lawan (lodge).

Behold, there bawaa (come) an zaqan (old) ayash (husband/individual man) from his maishah (work) out of the shadah (field) at irab (evening): now the ayash (husband/individual man) was of the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), and he lived in Gabaih (Gibeah); but the ayash (husband/individual man) of the maqawam (place) were Banayamayanay (Benjamites).

He nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye), and raah (see) the arach (wayfaring) ayash (husband/individual man) in the rachab (street) of the iyar (city); and the zaqan (old) ayash (husband/individual man) amar (spoke), Where are you yalak (going)? Ayan (where) did you bawaa (come) from?

He amar (spoke) to him, We are ibar (pass over/through) from Bayathalacham (Bethlehem) Judah to the farther yarakah (side) of the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim). I am from there, and I yalak (went) to Bayathalacham (Bethlehem) Judah. I am halak (move) to the bayath (house) of Yahawah; and there is no ayash (husband/individual man) who asap (takes) me into his bayath (house).

Yet there is both thaban (straw) and masapawaa (provender) for our donkeys; and there is lacham (bread) and yayan (wine) also for me, and for your handmaid, and for the nair (young) man who is with your ibad (servant): there is no machasawar (want) of anything.

The zaqan (old) ayash (husband/individual man) amar (spoke), shalawam (peace / safety) be to you; raq (howsoever) let all your machasawar (wants) lawan (lie) on me; only don't lodge in the rachab (street).
So he bawaa (come) him into his bayath (house), and gave the donkeys fodder; and they rachatz (washed) their ragal (feet / foot), and akal (eat) and shathah (drinks).

As they were making their lab (heart) yatab (merry), behold, the ayash (husband/individual man) of the iyar (city), ayash (husband/individual man) base ayash (husband/individual man), surrounded the bayath (house), dapaq (beating) at the dalath (door); and they amar (spoke) to the bail (master) of the bayath (house), the zaqan (old) ayash (husband/individual man), amar (spoke), yatzaa (go out / come out) out the ayash (husband/individual man) who bawaa (come) into your bayath (house), that we may yadai (have) sex with him!

The ayash (husband/individual man), the bail (master) of the bayath (house), yatzaa (go out / come out) out to them, and amar (spoke) to them, No, my ach (brother/kinsman), please don't act so wickedly; achar (other) this ayash (husband/individual man) bawaa (come) come into my bayath (house), don't ishah (make) this nabalah (folly).

Behold, here is my bathawalah (virgin) bath (daughter) and his payalagash (concubine). I will yatzaa (go out / come out) them out now. Inah (oppress / afflict) them, and ishah (make) with them what seems tawab (pleasant/functional) to you; but to this ayash (husband/individual man) don't ishah (make) any such nabalah (folly).

But the ayash (husband/individual man) wouldn't shamai (hearken / hear) to him: so the ayash (husband/individual man) laid hold of his payalagash (concubine), and yatzaa (go out / come out) her out to them; and they yadai (had) sex with her, and ilal (abused) her all layal (night) until the baqar (morning): and when the shachar (day) began to ilah (go up / offer), they shalach (send) her go.

Then bawaa (come) the ashah (wife/individual woman) in the panah (dawning) of the baqar (morning), and napal (fall / be cast down) down at the pathach (door) of the ayash (husband/individual man) bayath (house) where her Adawan was, until it was awar (light).

Her Adawan qawam (rise up) up in the baqar (morning), and pathach (opened) the dalath (doors) of the bayath (house), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out to yalak (go) his darak (way); and behold, the ashah (wife/individual woman) his payalagash (concubine) was napal (fall / be cast down) down at the pathach (door) of the bayath (house), with her yad (hand) on the sap (threshold).

He amar (spoke) to her, "qawam (rise up) up, and yalak (let) us be going!" But no ayash (husband/individual man) inah (answer / respond). Then he laqach (take / seized) her up on the donkey; and the ayash (husband/individual man) qawam (rise up) up, and went to his maqawam (place).

When he bawaa (come) come into his bayath (house), he laqach (take / seized) a maakalath (knife), and laid chazaq (hold) on his payalagash (concubine), and nathach (divided) her, limb by limb, into shanayam (two) nathach (pieces), and shalach (send) her throughout all the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yasharaal (Israel).

It was so, that all who raah (see) it amar (spoke), There was no such deed done nor raah (see) from the yawam (day) that the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) to this yawam (day)! Shawam (place / establish / appoint) it, iwatz (take) counsel, and dabar (word / matter).

Then all the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and the idah (congregation) was qahal (assembled) as achad (one) ayash (husband/individual man), Dan (from) Dan Baarashabai (even) to Beersheba, with the aratz (Earth/land) of Galaid (Gilead), to Yahawah Matzapah (at) Mizpah.

The panah (chiefs) of all the im (people / nation), even of all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), yatzab (presented) themselves in the qahal (assembly) of the im (people / nation) of Alahayam, arabai (four) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) footmen who shalap (drew) charab (sword).

(Now the ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) shamai (hearken / hear) that the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) had ilah (go up / offer) up Matzapah (to) Mizpah.) The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke), dabar (word / matter) us, how hayah (came to pass) this rai (wickedness) happen?

The Lawayay (Levite), the ayash (husband/individual man) of the ashah (wife/individual woman) who was ratzach (murdered), inah (answer / respond), I bawaa (come) into Gabaih (Gibeah) that belongs to Banayamayan (Benjamin), I and my payalagash (concubine), to lawan (lodge).

The bail (men) of Gabaih (Gibeah) qawam (rise up) against me, and surrounded the bayath (house) by layal (night). They damah (thought) to have harag (slain) me, and they inah (oppress / afflict) my payalagash (concubine), and she is mawath (death).

I achaz (took) my payalagash (concubine), and nathach (cut) her in pieces, and shalach (send) her throughout all the shadah (country) of the nachalah (inheritance) of Yasharaal (Israel); for they ishah (make) committed lewdness and nabalah (folly) in Yasharaal (Israel).
Behold, you ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), all of you, yahab (give) here your dabar (word / matter) and itzah (counsel).

All the im (people / nation) qawam (rise up) as achad (one) ayash (husband/individual man), amar (spoke), ayash (husband/individual man) of us will yalak (go) to his ahal (tent), neither will any of us sawar (turn) to his bayath (house).
But now this is the thing which we will ishah (make) to Gabaih (Gibeah): we will go up against it by gawaral (lot);

And we will laqach (take / seized) ishar (ten) ayash (husband/individual man) of one maah (hundred) throughout all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), and one maah (hundred) of one alap (thousand), and a alap (thousand) out of rababah (ten) thousand, to laqach (take / seized) food for the im (people / nation), that they may ishah (make), when they bawaa (come) to Gabai (Gibeah) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), according to all the nabalah (folly) that they ishah (make) worked in Yasharaal (Israel).
So all the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) were asap (gathered) against the iyar (city), chabar (knit) together as achad (one) ayash (husband/individual man).

The shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) shalach (send) ayash (husband/individual man) through all the shabat (tribe) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), amar (spoke), "What rai (wickedness) is this that is hayah (came to pass) among you?

Now therefore nathan (give) up the ayash (husband/individual man), the base fellows, who are in Gabaih (Gibeah), that we may put them to mawath (death), and bair (put) away rai (evil) from Yasharaal (Israel)." But Banayamayan (Benjamin) would not shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of their ach (brother/kinsman) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel).

The ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) asap (gathered) themselves together out of the iyar (cities) to Gabaih (Gibeah), to yatzaa (go out / come out) out to malachamah (battle) against the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel).

The ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) were paqad (visit) on that yawam (day) out of the iyar (cities) isharayam (twenty) - shash (six) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man) who shalap (drew) the charab (sword), besides the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Gabaih (Gibeah), who were paqad (visit) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) bachar (chosen) ayash (husband/individual man).

Among all this im (people / nation) there were shabai (seven) maah (hundred) bachar (chosen) ayash (husband/individual man) yad (hand); everyone could qalai (sling) aban (stone) at a hair-breadth, and not chataa (miss).

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel), besides Banayamayan (Benjamin), were paqad (visit) arabai (four) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man) who shalap (drew) charab (sword): all these were ayash (husband/individual man) of malachamah (war).

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) qawam (rise up), and went up to Bethel, and shaal (asked) counsel of Alahayam; and they amar (spoke), "Who shall ilah (go up / offer) up for us thachalah (first) to malachamah (battle) against the ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin)?" Yahawah amar (spoke), Yahawadah (Judah) thachalah (first).
