The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) qawam (rise up) up in the baqar (morning), and chanah (encamped) against Gabaih (Gibeah).

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to malachamah (battle) against Banayamayan (Benjamin); and the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) set the malachamah (battle) in irak (array) against them at Gabaih (Gibeah).

The ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of Gabaih (Gibeah), and shachath (destroyed) down to the aratz (Earth/land) Yasharaal (of) the Israelites on that yawam (day) isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man).

The im (people / nation), the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel), chazaq (encouraged) themselves, and set the malachamah (battle) again in irak (array) in the maqawam (place) where they irak (set) themselves in array the raashawan (first) yawam (day).

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up and bakah (wept) panayam (before) Yahawah until irab (evening); and they shaal (asked) of Yahawah, amar (spoke), "Shall I again nagash (draw) near to malachamah (battle) against the ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) my ach (brother/kinsman)?" Yahawah amar (spoke), ilah (go up / offer) up against him.
The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) qarab (come close) near against the ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) the shanay (second) yawam (day).

Banayamayan (Benjamin) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth qaraah (against) them out of Gabaih (Gibeah) the shanay (second) yawam (day), and shachath (destroyed) down to the aratz (Earth/land) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) again eighteen alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man); all these shalap (drew) the charab (sword).

Then all the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), and all the im (people / nation), ilah (go up / offer) up, and bawaa (come) to Bethel, and bakah (wept), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) there panayam (before) Yahawah, and tzawam (fasted) that yawam (day) until irab (evening); and they ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilah (offerings) and peace ilah (offerings) panayam (before) Yahawah.
The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) shaal (asked) of Yahawah (for the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Alahayam was there in those yawam (day),

And Payanachas (Phinehas), the ban (son) of Alaizar (Eleazar), the ban (son) of Aharawan (Aaron), imad (stood) panayam (before) it in those yawam (day)), amar (spoke), "Shall I yet again yatzaa (go out / come out) out to malachamah (battle) against the ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) my ach (brother/kinsman), or shall I chadal (cease)?" Yahawah amar (spoke), ilah (go up / offer) up; for machar (tomorrow) I will nathan (give) him into your yad (hand).
Yasharaal (Israel) shawam (place / establish / appoint) ambushes all around Gabaih (Gibeah).

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up against the ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), and irak (set) themselves in array against Gabaih (Gibeah), as at other paim (times).

The ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) yatzaa (go out / come out) out qaraah (against) the im (people / nation), and were nathaq (drawn) away from the iyar (city); and they chalal (began) to nakah (strike) and chalal (kill) of the im (people / nation), as at other paim (times), in the masalah (highways), of which achad (one) ilah (go up / offer) up to Bethel, and the other to Gabaih (Gibeah), in the shadah (field), about shalawashayam (thirty) ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel).

The ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) amar (spoke), "They are nagap (struck) down panayam (before) us, as at the raashawan (first)." But the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke), Let us nawas (flee), and nathaq (draw) them away from the iyar (city) to the masalah (highways).

All the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) qawam (rise up) up out of their maqawam (place), and irak (set) themselves in array at Bailathamar (Baal) Tamar: and the ambushers of Yasharaal (Israel) gayach (broke) forth out of their maqawam (place), even out of Maareh Geba.

There bawaa (come) over nagad (against) Gabaih (Gibeah) ishar (ten) alap (thousand) bachar (chosen) ayash (husband/individual man) out of all Yasharaal (Israel), and the malachamah (battle) was severe; but they didn't yadai (know) that rai (evil) was close on them.

Yahawah nagap (struck) Banayamayan (Benjamin) panayam (before) Yasharaal (Israel); and the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) shachath (destroyed) of banayamayan (benjamin) that yawam (day) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) one maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man): all these shalap (drew) the charab (sword).

So the ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) raah (see) that they were nagap (struck); for the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) nathan (give) maqawam (place) to banayamayan (benjamin), because they batach (trusted) the ambushers whom they had shawam (place / establish / appoint) against Gabaih (Gibeah).
The ambushers hurried, and pashat (rushed) on Gabaih (Gibeah); and the ambushers mashak (drew) themselves along, and nakah (struck) all the iyar (city) with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword).

Now the appointed mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) between the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) and the ambushers was that they should rabah (make) a great cloud of ishan (smoke) ilah (go up / offer) up out of the iyar (city).

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) hapak (turned) in the malachamah (battle), and Banayamayan (Benjamin) chalal (began) to nakah (strike) and chalal (kill) of the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) about shalawashayam (thirty) ayash (husband/individual man); for they amar (spoke), nagap (surely) they are nagap (struck) down panayam (before) us, as in the raashawan (first) malachamah (battle).

But when the cloud chalal (began) to arise up out of the iyar (city) in a imawad (pillar) of ishan (smoke), the Benjamites panah (looked) achar (other) them; and behold, the whole of the iyar (city) ilah (go up / offer) up in kalayal (smoke) to the sky.

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) hapak (turned), and the ayash (husband/individual man) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) were bahal (dismayed); for they raah (see) that rai (evil) had nagai (come) on them.

Therefore they panah (turned) their backs panayam (before) the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) to the darak (way) of the madabar (wilderness); but the malachamah (battle) dabaq (followed) hard after them; and those who came out of the iyar (cities) shachath (destroyed) them in its thawak (midst).
They surrounded the Benjamites, radap (chased) them, and darak (trod) them down at their manawachah (resting) place, as far as over nakach (against) Gabaih (Gibeah) toward the sunrise.
There napal (fall / be cast down) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) eighteen alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man); all these were ayash (husband/individual man) of valor.

They panah (turned) and nawas (fled) toward the madabar (wilderness) to the salai (rock) of Ramawan (Rimmon): and they ilal (gleaned) of them in the masalah (highways) chamash (five) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man), and dabaq (followed) hard achar (other) them to Gadaim (Gidom), and nakah (struck) of them two alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man).

So that all who napal (fall / be cast down) that yawam (day) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) were isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man) who shalap (drew) the charab (sword); all these were ayash (husband/individual man) of valor.

But shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man) panah (turned) and nawas (fled) toward the madabar (wilderness) to the salai (rock) of Ramawan (Rimmon), and stayed in the salai (rock) of Ramawan (Rimmon) arabai (four) chadash (month).

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) shawab (turn back / repent) again on the ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), and nakah (struck) them with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), both the entire iyar (city), and the livestock, and all that they matzaa (found): moreover all the iyar (cities) which they matzaa (found) they shalach (send) on ash (fire).

Now the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) had shabai (swear / take oath) Matzapah (in) Mizpah, amar (spoke), There shall not any of us nathan (give) his bath (daughter) to Banayamayan (Benjamin) as ashah (wife/individual woman).

The im (people / nation) bawaa (come) to Bethel, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) there until irab (evening) panayam (before) Alahayam, and nashaa (lift) up their qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept) severely.
They amar (spoke), Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), why has this happened in Yasharaal (Israel), that there should be today achad (one) shabat (tribe) paqad (visit) in Yasharaal (Israel)?

It happened on the next macharath (day) that the im (people / nation) shakam (rose) early, and banah (built) there an mazabach (altar), and ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilah (offerings) and peace ilah (offerings).

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke), "Who is there among all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) who didn't ilah (go up / offer) up in the qahal (assembly) to Yahawah?" For they had made a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shabawaih (oath) concerning him who didn't ilah (go up / offer) up to Yahawah Matzapah (to) Mizpah, amar (spoke), He shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death).

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) grieved for Banayamayan (Benjamin) their ach (brother/kinsman), and amar (spoke), There is achad (one) shabat (tribe) gadai (cut) off from Yasharaal (Israel) this yawam (day).
How shall we provide wives for those who yathar (remain), since we have shabai (swear / take oath) by Yahawah that we will not nathan (give) them of our bath (daughter) to wives?

They amar (spoke), "What achad (one) is there of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) who didn't ilah (go up / offer) up to Yahawah Matzapah (to) Mizpah?" Behold, there bawaa (come) ayash (husband/individual man) to the machanah (camp) Yabash (from) Jabesh Gilead to the qahal (assembly).
For when the im (people / nation) were paqad (visit), behold, there were ayash (husband/individual man) of the yashab (inhabit/dwell) Yabash (of) Jabesh Gilead there.

The idah (congregation) shalach (send) there shanayam (two) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man) of the most ban (son), and tzawah (commanded) them, amar (spoke), yalak (go) and nakah (strike) the yashab (inhabit/dwell) Yabash (of) Jabesh Gilead with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), with the ashah (wife/individual woman) and the little tap (ones).
This is the thing that you shall ishah (make): you shall utterly charam (destroy) every zakar (remembrance/memory), and every ashah (wife/individual woman) who has lain with a yadai (man).

They matzaa (found) among the yashab (inhabit/dwell) Yabash (of) Jabesh Gilead arabai (four) maah (hundred) nairah (young) bathawalah (virgins), who yadai (had) not known ayash (husband/individual man) by lying with him; and they bawaa (come) them to the machanah (camp) to Shayalah (Shiloh), which is in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan).

The whole idah (congregation) shalach (send) and dabar (word / matter) to the ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) who were in the salai (rock) of Ramawan (Rimmon), and qaraa (called) shalawam (peace / safety) to them.

Banayamayan (Benjamin) shawab (turn back / repent) at that ith (time); and they nathan (give) them the ashah (wife/individual woman) whom they had chayah (saved) alive of the ashah (wife/individual woman) Yabash (of) Jabesh Gilead: and yet so they weren't matzaa (enough) for them.
The im (people / nation) grieved for Banayamayan (Benjamin), because that Yahawah ishah (make) made a paratz (breach) in the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Then the zaqan (elders) of the idah (congregation) amar (spoke), How shall we ishah (make) wives for those who yathar (remain), since the ashah (wife/individual woman) are destroyed out of Banayamayan (Benjamin)?
They amar (spoke), There must be an yarashah (inheritance) for those who are palayatah (escaped) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), that a shabat (tribe) not be machah (blotted) out from Yasharaal (Israel).

However we may not nathan (give) them wives of our bath (daughter), for the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) had shabai (swear / take oath), amar (spoke), ‘arar (cursed) is he who nathan (give) a ashah (wife/individual woman) to Banayamayan (Benjamin).’

They amar (spoke), Behold, there is a chag (feast/festival) of Yahawah from yawam (day) to year in Shayalah (Shiloh), which is on the tzapawan (north) of Bayathaal (Bethel), on the east tzapawan (side) of the masalah (highway) that ilah (go up / offer) up from Bayathaal (Bethel) to Shakam (Shechem), and on the nagab (south) of Labawanah (Lebonah).
They tzawah (commanded) the ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), amar (spoke), yalak (go) and lie in arab (wait) in the karam (vineyards),

And raah (see), and behold, if the bath (daughter) of Shayalah (Shiloh) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to chawal (dance) in the machalah (dances), then yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the karam (vineyards), and each ayash (husband/individual man) chatap (catch) his ashah (wife/individual woman) of the bath (daughter) of Shayalah (Shiloh), and halak (move) to the aratz (Earth/land) of Banayamayan (Benjamin).

It shall be, when their ab (father) or their ach (brother/kinsman) bawaa (come) to rayab (complain) to us, that we will amar (spoke) to them, ‘chanan (grant) them graciously to us, because we didn't laqach (take / seized) for each ayash (husband/individual man) his ashah (wife/individual woman) in malachamah (battle), neither nathan (give) you give them to them, otherwise you would now be asham (guilty).’

The ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) ishah (make) so, and nashaa (lift) them wives, according to their masapar (number), of those who chawal (danced), whom they carried off. They yalak (went) and shawab (turn back / repent) to their nachalah (inheritance), banah (built) the iyar (cities), and lived in them.

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) departed there at that ith (time), every ayash (husband/individual man) to his shabat (tribe) and to his mashapachah (tribe/clan/family), and they yatzaa (go out / come out) out from there every ayash (husband/individual man) to his nachalah (inheritance).
In those yawam (day) there was no malak (king) in Yasharaal (Israel): every ayash (husband/individual man) ishah (make) that which was yashar (right) in his own iyan (eye).

It happened in the yawam (day) when the shapat (judges) shapat (judged), that there was a raib (famine) in the aratz (Earth/land). A certain ayash (husband/individual man) of Bayathalacham (Bethlehem) Judah yalak (went) to live in the shadah (country) of Mawaab (Moab), he, and his ashah (wife/individual woman), and his shanayam (two) ban (son).

The sham (name) of the ayash (husband/individual man) was Alayamalak (Elimelech), and the sham (name) of his ashah (wife/individual woman) Naimay (Naomi), and the sham (name) of his shanayam (two) ban (son) Machalawan (Mahlon) and Kalayawan (Chilion), aparathay (ephrathites) of Bayathalacham (Bethlehem) Judah. They bawaa (come) into the shadah (country) of Mawaab (Moab), and continued there.
Alayamalak (Elimelech), Naimay (Naomi's) ayash (husband/individual man), mawath (death); and she was shaar (left), and her shanayam (two) ban (son).

They nashaa (lift) them wives of the ashah (wife/individual woman) of mawaabay (moab); the sham (name) of the achad (one) was Irapah (Orpah), and the sham (name) of the other Rawath (Ruth): and they lived there about ishar (ten) shanah (years).

Machalawan (Mahlon) and Kalayawan (Chilion) shanayam (two) mawath (death), and the ashah (wife/individual woman) was bereaved of her shanayam (two) yalad (birth / begot) and of her ayash (husband/individual man).

Then she qawam (rise up) with her daughters-in-law, that she might shawab (turn back / repent) from the shadah (country) of Mawaab (Moab): for she had shamai (hearken / hear) in the shadah (country) of Mawaab (Moab) how that Yahawah paqad (visit) visited his im (people / nation) in nathan (give) them lacham (bread).

She yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the maqawam (place) where she was, and her shanayam (two) daughters-in-law with her; and they yalak (went) on the darak (way) to shawab (turn back / repent) to the aratz (Earth/land) of Yahawadah (Judah).

Naimay (Naomi) amar (spoke) to her shanayam (two) daughters-in-law, "yalak (go), shawab (turn back / repent) ashah (wife/individual woman) of you to her am (mother) bayath (house): Yahawah ishah (make) chasad (grace) with you, as you ishah (make) dealt with the mawath (death), and with me.

Yahawah nathan (give) you that you may matzaa (find) manawachah (rest), ashah (wife/individual woman) of you in the bayath (house) of her ayash (husband/individual man)." Then she nashaq (kissed) them, and they nashaa (lift) up their qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept).
They amar (spoke) to her, No, but we will shawab (turn back / repent) with you to your im (people / nation).

Naimay (Naomi) amar (spoke), shawab (turn back / repent) back, my bath (daughter). Why do you want to yalak (go) with me? Do I still have ban (son) in my maih (womb), that they may be your ayash (husband/individual man)?

Shawab (turn back / repent) back, my bath (daughter), yalak (go) your way; for I am too zaqan (old) to have a ayash (husband/individual man). If I should amar (spoke), ‘I yash (have) thaqawah (hope),’ if I should even have a ayash (husband/individual man) tonight, and should also yalad (birth / begot) ban (son);

Would you then shabar (wait) until they were gadal (grown)? Would you then refrain from having ayash (husband/individual man)? No, my bath (daughter), for it grieves me much for your sakes, for the yad (hand) of Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) gone out against me.
They nashaa (lift) up their qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept) again: and Irapah (Orpah) nashaq (kissed) her mother-in-law, but Ruth dabaq (joined) with her.
She amar (spoke), Behold, your sister-in-law has shawab (turn back / repent) back to her im (people / nation), and to her Alahayam. Follow your sister-in-law.

Ruth amar (spoke), Don't pagai (entreat) me to izab (leave) you, and to shawab (turn back / repent) from achar (other) after you, for where you yalak (go), I will yalak (go); and where you lawan (lodge), I will lawan (lodge); your im (people / nation) shall be my im (people / nation), and your Alahayam my Alahayam;
Where you mawath (death), will I mawath (death), and there will I be qabar (bury). Yahawah ishah (make) so to me, and more also, if anything but mawath (death) parad (part) you and me.
When she raah (see) that she was steadfastly amatz (minded) to yalak (go) with her, she chadal (left) off dabar (word / matter) to her.

So they shanayam (two) yalak (went) until they bawaa (come) to Bayathalacham (Bethlehem). It happened, when they bawaa (come) come to Bayathalacham (Bethlehem), that all the iyar (city) was hawam (moved) about them, and they asked, Is this Naimay (Naomi)?
She amar (spoke) to them, Don't qaraa (called) me Naimay (Naomi). Qaraa (called) me Maraa (Mara); for the Shaday has dealt very bitterly with me.

I halak (move) out malaa (full), and Yahawah has shawab (turn back / repent) me home again rayaqam (empty); why do you qaraa (called) me Naimay (Naomi), since Yahawah has inah (answer / respond) against me, and the Shaday has raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) me?

So Naimay (Naomi) shawab (turn back / repent), and Ruth the Moabitess, her kalah (complete / finish), with her, who shawab (turn back / repent) out of the shadah (country) of Mawaab (Moab): and they bawaa (come) to Bayathalacham (Bethlehem) in the thachalah (beginning) of shairah (barley) qatzayar (harvest).

Naimay (Naomi) had a kinsman of her ayash (husband/individual man), a gabawar (mighty) ayash (husband/individual man) of wealth, of the mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) of Alayamalak (Elimelech), and his sham (name) was Baiz (Boaz).

The Moabitess amar (spoke) to Naimay (Naomi), "yalak (let) me now go to the shadah (field), and laqat (glean) among the shabal (ears) of grain achar (other) him in whose iyan (eye) I shall matzaa (find) favor." She amar (spoke) to her, yalak (go), my bath (daughter).

She yalak (went), and bawaa (come) and laqat (gleaned) in the shadah (field) achar (other) the qatzar (reapers): and she happened to qarah (come) to the chalaqah (portion) of the shadah (field) belonging to Baiz (Boaz), who was of the mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) of Alayamalak (Elimelech).
Behold, Baiz (Boaz) bawaa (come) from Bayathalacham (Bethlehem), and amar (spoke) to the qatzar (reapers), "Yahawah be with you." They amar (spoke) him, Yahawah barak (bless) you.
Then Baiz (Boaz) amar (spoke) to his nair (servant) who was natzab (set) over the qatzar (reapers), Whose nairah (young) lady is this?

The nair (servant) who was natzab (set) over the qatzar (reapers) inah (answer / respond), It is the Mawaabay (Moabite) lady who shawab (turn back / repent) back with Naimay (Naomi) out of the shadah (country) of Mawaab (Moab).

She amar (spoke), ‘Please let me laqat (glean) and asap (gather) achar (other) the qatzar (reapers) among the sheaves.’ So she bawaa (come), and has imad (continued) even from the baqar (morning) until now, except that she stayed a mait (little) in the bayath (house).

Then Baiz (Boaz) amar (spoke) to Rawath (Ruth), shamai (hearken / hear), my bath (daughter). Don't yalak (go) to laqat (glean) in achar (other) shadah (field), and don't ibar (pass over/through) from here, but stay here close to my nairah (maidens).

Let your iyan (eye) be on the shadah (field) that they qatzar (reap), and halak (move) achar (other) them. Haven't I tzawah (commanded) the nair (young) men not to nagai (touch) you? When you are tzamaa (thirsty), halak (move) to the kalay (vessels), and shathah (drinks) from that which the nair (young) men have shaab (drawn).

Then she napal (fall / be cast down) on her panayam (face), and shachah (bowed) herself to the aratz (Earth/land), and amar (spoke) to him, Why matzaa (have) I found favor in your iyan (eye), that you should take nakar (knowledge) of me, since I am a nakaray (foreigner)?

Baiz (Boaz) inah (answer / respond) her, It has nagad (fully) been shown me, all that you ishah (make) done to your mother-in-law achar (other) the mawath (death) of your ayash (husband/individual man); and how you have izab (left) your ab (father) and your am (mother), and the aratz (Earth/land) of your birth, and have yalak (come) to a im (people / nation) that you didn't yadai (know) thamawal (before).

May Yahawah shalam (repay) your pail (work), and a shalam (full / whole / complete) mashakarath (reward) be given you from Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), under whose kanap (wings) you bawaa (come) come to take chasah (refuge).

Then she amar (spoke), Let me matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (eye), my Adawan, because you have nacham (turn away / repent) me, and because you have dabar (word / matter) lab (heart) to your handmaid, though I am not as achad (one) of your handmaidens.

At meal ith (time) Baiz (Boaz) amar (spoke) to her, "nagash (come) here, and akal (eat) of the lacham (bread), and tabal (dip) your path (morsel) in the chamatz (vinegar)." She yashab (inhabit/dwell) tzad (beside) the qatzar (reapers), and they tzabat (reached) her qalay (parched) grain, and she akal (eat), and was shabai (satisfied), and yathar (left) some of it.
When she had qawam (rise up) up to laqat (glean), Baiz (Boaz) tzawah (commanded) his nair (young) men, amar (spoke), Let her laqat (glean) even among the sheaves, and don't kalam (reproach) her.
Also pull out some for her from the bundles, and izab (leave) it, and let her laqat (glean), and don't gair (rebuke) her.
So she laqat (gleaned) in the shadah (field) until irab (evening); and she chabat (beat) out that which she had laqat (gleaned), and it was about an ayapah (ephah) of shairah (barley).

She nashaa (lift) it up, and bawaa (come) into the iyar (city); and her mother-in-law raah (see) what she had laqat (gleaned): and she yatzaa (go out / come out) out and nathan (give) to her that which she had yathar (left) after she was sufficed.

Her mother-in-law amar (spoke) to her, "Where have you laqat (gleaned) today? Ayapah (where) ishah (make) you worked? Barak (blessed) be he who noticed you." She showed her mother-in-law with whom she ishah (make) worked, and amar (spoke), The ayash (husband/individual man) sham (name) with whom I ishah (make) today is Baiz (Boaz).

Naimay (Naomi) amar (spoke) to her daughter-in-law, "barak (blessed) be he of Yahawah, who has not izab (left) off his chasad (grace) to the chay (life) and to the mawath (death)." Naimay (Naomi) amar (spoke) to her, The ayash (husband/individual man) is a close relative to us, ayash (husband/individual man) of our gaal (near) kinsmen.
The Moabitess amar (spoke), Yes, he amar (spoke) to me, ‘You shall stay dabaq (close) to my nair (young) men, until they kalah (complete / finish) ended all my qatzayar (harvest).’

Naimay (Naomi) amar (spoke) Rawath (to) her kalah (complete / finish), It is tawab (pleasant/functional), my bath (daughter), that you yatzaa (go out / come out) out with his nairah (maidens), and that they not pagai (meet) you in any other shadah (field).

So she stayed dabaq (close) to the nairah (maidens) of Baiz (Boaz), to laqat (glean) to the kalah (complete / finish) of shairah (barley) qatzayar (harvest) and of chatah (wheat) qatzayar (harvest); and she lived with her mother-in-law.
Naimay (Naomi) her mother-in-law amar (spoke) to her, My bath (daughter), shall I not baqash (seek) manawach (rest) for you, that it may be yatab (well) with you?
Now isn't Baiz (Boaz) our kinsman, with whose nairah (maidens) you were? Behold, he zarah (winnows) shairah (barley) tonight in the garan (threshing) floor.

Therefore rachatz (wash) yourself, sawak (anoint) yourself, shawam (place / establish / appoint) dressed, and yarad (go) down to the garan (threshing) floor, but don't yadai (make) yourself known to the ayash (husband/individual man) until he kalah (complete / finish) finished akal (eat) and shathah (drinks).

It shall be, when he shakab (lies) down, that you shall yadai (mark) the maqawam (place) where he shall shakab (lie), and you shall bawaa (come) in, and galah (uncover) his maragalah (feet), and shakab (lay) down; then he will nagad (tell) you what you shall ishah (make).
She amar (spoke) to her, All that you amar (spoke) I will ishah (make).
She yarad (went) down to the garan (threshing) floor, and ishah (make) according to all that her mother-in-law told her.

When Baiz (Boaz) had akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and his lab (heart) was yatab (merry), he bawaa (come) to shakab (lie) down at the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the iram (heap) of grain. She bawaa (come) lat (softly), galah (uncovered) his maragalah (feet), and shakab (laid) her down.
It happened at chatzay (midnight), that the ayash (husband/individual man) was startled and lapath (turned) himself; and behold, a ashah (wife/individual woman) shakab (lay) at his maragalah (feet).
He amar (spoke), "Who are you?" She amar (spoke), I am your handmaid. Therefore parash (spread) your kanap (skirt) over your handmaid; for you are a gaal (near) kinsman.

He amar (spoke), barak (blessed) are you by Yahawah, my bath (daughter). You yatab (have) shown more chasad (grace) in the acharawan (latter) end than at the raashawan (beginning), inasmuch as you didn't yalak (follow) bachawar (young) men, whether dal (poor) or ishayar (rich).

Now, my bath (daughter), don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid); I will ishah (make) to you all that you amar (spoke); for all the shair (city) of my im (people / nation) does yadai (know) that you are a chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ashah (wife/individual woman).
Now it is amanam (true) that I am a gaal (near) kinsman; however there is a gaal (kinsman) nearer than I.

Stay this layal (night), and it shall be in the baqar (morning), that if he will gaal (perform) for you the part of a kinsman, tawab (pleasant/functional); let him gaal (do) the kinsman's part. But if he chapatz (will) not gaal (do) the part of a kinsman for you, then will I gaal (do) the part of a kinsman for you, as Yahawah chay (life). Shakab (lie) down until the baqar (morning).

She shakab (lay) at his maragalah (feet) until the baqar (morning). She qawam (rise up) up tarawam (before) ayash (husband/individual man) nakar (could) discern rai (neigbor/another person). For he amar (spoke), yadai (let) it not be known that the ashah (wife/individual woman) bawaa (come) to the garan (threshing) floor.

He amar (spoke), "yahab (bring) the mantle that is on you, and achaz (hold) it." She achaz (held) it; and he madad (measured) shash (six) measures of shairah (barley), and shayath (put / appoint / make) it on her; and he bawaa (come) into the iyar (city).
When she bawaa (come) to her mother-in-law, she amar (spoke), "How did it go, my bath (daughter)?" She amar (spoke) her all that the ayash (husband/individual man) ishah (make) done to her.
She amar (spoke), He nathan (give) me these shash (six) measures of shairah (barley); for he amar (spoke), ‘Don't bawaa (come) rayaqam (empty) to your mother-in-law.’

Then she amar (spoke), yashab (inhabit/dwell) still, my bath (daughter), until you yadai (know) how the dabar (word / matter) will napal (fall / be cast down); for the ayash (husband/individual man) will not shaqat (rest), until he kalah (complete / finish) finished the thing this yawam (day).

Now Baiz (Boaz) ilah (go up / offer) up to the shair (gate), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) down there. Behold, the gaal (near) kinsman of whom Baiz (Boaz) dabar (word / matter) ibar (pass over/through) by; to whom he dabar (word / matter), "ibar (pass over/through) over here, friend, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) down!" He sawar (turned) aside, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) down.
He laqach (take / seized) ishar (ten) ayash (husband/individual man) of the zaqan (elders) of the iyar (city), and amar (spoke), "yashab (inhabit/dwell) down here." They yashab (inhabit/dwell) down.

He amar (spoke) to the gaal (near) kinsman, “Naimay (Naomi), who has shawab (turn back / repent) back out of the shadah (country) of Mawaab (Moab), is makar (selling) the chalaqah (parcel) of shadah (land), which was our ach (brother/kinsman) Alayamalak (Elimelech's).

I amar (spoke) to galah (disclose) it to you, amar (spoke), ‘qanah (buy) it before those who sit here, and before the zaqan (elders) of my im (people / nation).’ If you will gaal (redeem) it, gaal (redeem) it; but if you will not gaal (redeem) it, then nagad (tell) me, that I may yadai (know). For there is no one to gaal (redeem) it zawalah (besides) you; and I am achar (other) you.” He amar (spoke), I will gaal (redeem) it.

Then Baiz (Boaz) amar (spoke), On the yawam (day) you qanah (buy) the shadah (field) from the yad (hand) of Naimay (Naomi), you must qanah (buy) it Rawath (also) from the Moabitess, the ashah (wife/individual woman) of the mawath (death), to qawam (rise up) up the sham (name) of the mawath (death) on his nachalah (inheritance).

The gaal (near) kinsman amar (spoke), I can't gaal (redeem) it for myself, lest I shachath (mar) my own nachalah (inheritance). Take my gaalah (right) of yakal (redemption) for yourself; for I can't gaal (redeem) it.

Now this panayam (was) the custom in former time in Yasharaal (Israel) concerning gaalah (redeeming) and concerning thamawarah (exchanging), to qawam (rise up) all things: a ayash (husband/individual man) took off his nail (shoe), and nathan (give) it to his neighbor; and this was the thaiwadah (way) of attestation in Yasharaal (Israel).
So the gaal (near) kinsman amar (spoke) to Baiz (Boaz), "qanah (buy) it for yourself." He took off his nail (shoe).

Baiz (Boaz) amar (spoke) to the zaqan (elders), and to all the im (people / nation), You are witnesses this yawam (day), that I have bought all that was Alayamalak (Elimelech's), and all that was Kalayawan (Chilion's) and Machalawan (Mahlon's), from the yad (hand) of Naimay (Naomi).

Rawath (Moreover) the Moabitess, the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Machalawan (Mahlon), I have qanah (purchased) to be my ashah (wife/individual woman), to qawam (rise up) up the sham (name) of the mawath (death) on his nachalah (inheritance), that the sham (name) of the mawath (death) not be karath (cut) off from im (among) his ach (brother/kinsman), and from the shair (gate) of his maqawam (place). You are witnesses this yawam (day).

All the im (people / nation) who were in the shair (gate), and the zaqan (elders), amar (spoke), We are witnesses. May Yahawah nathan (give) the ashah (wife/individual woman) who bawaa (come) come into your bayath (house) like Rachal (Rachel) and like Laah (Leah), which shanayam (two) banah (built) the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel); and treat you chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) in Ephrathah, and be qaraa (called) in Bayathalacham (Bethlehem).

Let your bayath (house) be like the bayath (house) of Paratz (Perez), whom Thamar (Tamar) yalad (birth / begot) to Yahawadah (Judah), of the zarai (seed) which Yahawah shall nathan (give) you of this nairah (young) woman.

So Baiz (Boaz) laqach (take / seized) Rawath (Ruth), and she became his ashah (wife/individual woman); and he bawaa (come) in to her, and Yahawah nathan (give) her harawan (conception), and she yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son).

The ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke) to Naimay (Naomi), barak (blessed) be Yahawah, who has not shabath (shabath/rest) you this yawam (day) without a gaal (near) kinsman; and let his sham (name) be qaraa (called) in Yasharaal (Israel).

He shall be to you a restorer of napash (living being/soul), and kawal (all/every/entire) you in your shayabah (old age / white hair (due to age)) age, for your kalah (complete / finish), who ahab (love) you, who is tawab (pleasant/functional) to you than shabai (seven) ban (son), has yalad (birth / begot) him.
Naimay (Naomi) laqach (take / seized) the yalad (birth / begot), and shayath (put / appoint / make) it in her chayaq (bosom), and became aman (believe / have faith) to it.

The women, her neighbors, gave him a sham (name), amar (spoke), "There is a ban (son) yalad (birth / begot) to Naimay (Naomi);" and they sham (name) him Iwabad (Obed). He is the ab (father) of Yashay (Jesse), the ab (father) of Dawad (David).
Now this is the history of the thawaladah (generation) of Paratz (Perez): Paratz (Perez) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Chatzarawan (Hezron),
And Chatzarawan (Hezron) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Ram (Ram), and Ram (Ram) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Imayanadab (Amminadab),
And Imayanadab (Amminadab) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Nachashawan (Nahshon), and Nachashawan (Nahshon) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Shalamah (Salmon),
And Shalamawan (Salmon) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Baiz (Boaz), and Baiz (Boaz) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Iwabad (Obed),
And Iwabad (Obed) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Yashay (Jesse), and Yashay (Jesse) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Dawad (David).

Now there was a achad (one) ayash (husband/individual man) Ramathayamatzawapayam (of) Ramathaim Zophim, of the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), and his sham (name) was Alaqanah (Elkanah), the ban (son) of Yaracham (Jeroham), the ban (son) of Alayahaw (Elihu), the ban (son) of Thachaw (Tohu), the ban (son) of Tzawap (Zuph), an Aparathay (Ephraimite):

And he had shanayam (two) wives; the sham (name) of the achad (one) was Chanah (Hannah), and the sham (name) of other Pananah (Peninnah): and Pananah (Peninnah) had yalad (birth / begot), but Chanah (Hannah) had no yalad (birth / begot).

Hawaa (which/who/that is) ayash (husband/individual man) ilah (go up / offer) up out of his iyar (city) from yawam (day) to year to shachah (worship) and to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) in Shayalah (Shiloh). The shanayam (two) ban (son) of Ilay (Eli), Chapanay (Hophni) and Payanachas (Phinehas), kahan (priest) to Yahawah, were there.

When the yawam (day) came that Alaqanah (Elkanah) zabach (sacrificed), he nathan (give) to Pananah (Peninnah) his ashah (wife/individual woman), and to all her ban (son) and her bath (daughter), manah (portions):
But to Chanah (Hannah) he nathan (give) a double manah (portion); for he ahab (love) Chanah (Hannah), but Yahawah had sagar (shut) up her racham (womb).
Her rival kais (provoked) her severely, to raim (make) her fret, because Yahawah had sagar (shut) up her racham (womb).
As he ishah (make) so shanah (year) by shanah (year), when she ilah (go up / offer) up to the bayath (house) of Yahawah, so she kais (provoked) her; therefore she bakah (wept), and didn't akal (eat).

Alaqanah (Elkanah) her ayash (husband/individual man) amar (spoke) to her, Chanah (Hannah), why do you bakah (weep)? Why don't you akal (eat)? Why is your labab (heart) grieved? Am I not tawab (pleasant/functional) to you than ishar (ten) ban (son)?

So Chanah (Hannah) qawam (rise up) up achar (other) they had akal (eat) in Shayalah (Shiloh), and achar (other) they had shathah (drinks). Now Ilay (Eli) the kahan (priest) was sitting on his kasaa (seat) by the doorpost of the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah.
She was in bitterness of napash (living being/soul), and palal (prayed) to Yahawah, and bakah (wept) bitterly.

She nadar (make vow) a nadar (vow), and amar (spoke), Yahawah of tzabaa (troop), if you will raah (see) raah (see) on the inay (affliction) of your handmaid, and zakar (remembrance/memory) me, and not shakach (forget) your handmaid, but will nathan (give) to your handmaid a boy, then I will nathan (give) him to Yahawah all the yawam (day) of his chay (life), and no mawarah (razor) shall ilah (go up / offer) on his raash (head).
It happened, as she rabah (continued) palal (praying) panayam (before) Yahawah, that Ilay (Eli) Ilay (saw) her pah (mouth).

Now Chanah (Hannah) dabar (word / matter) in her lab (heart). Only her shapah (lips) nawai (moved), but her qawal (sound / voice) was not shamai (hearken / hear). Therefore Ilay (Eli) chashab (thought) she had been shakawar (drunken).
Ilay (Eli) amar (spoke) to her, How long will you be shakar (drunken)? Sawar (put) away your yayan (wine) from you.

Chanah (Hannah) inah (answer / respond), No, my Adawan, I am a ashah (wife/individual woman) of a qashah (rough / hard) rawach (spirit / wind). I have shathah (drinks) neither yayan (wine) nor shakar (strong) drink, but I shapak (poured) out my napash (living being/soul) panayam (before) Yahawah.
Don't nathan (give) your handmaid for a balayail (wicked) bath (daughter); for I have been dabar (word / matter) out of the rab (abundance) of my shayach (complaint) and my kais (provocation).
Then Ilay (Eli) inah (answer / respond), yalak (go) in shalawam (peace / safety); and may the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) nathan (give) your shaalah (petition) that you have shaal (asked) of him.

She amar (spoke), "Let your handmaid matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (eye)." So the ashah (wife/individual woman) yalak (went) her darak (way), and akal (eat); and her facial expression wasn't sad any more.

They shakam (rose) up in the baqar (morning) shakam (early), and shachah (worshiped) panayam (before) Yahawah, and shawab (turn back / repent), and bawaa (come) to their bayath (house) to Ramah (Ramah): and Alaqanah (Elkanah) yadai (knew) Chanah (Hannah) his ashah (wife/individual woman); and Yahawah zakar (remembrance/memory) her.

It happened, when the yawam (day) had thaqawapah (come), that Chanah (Hannah) harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son); and she qaraa (called) him Shamawaal (Samuel), saying, Because I have shaal (asked) him of Yahawah.
The ayash (husband/individual man) Alaqanah (Elkanah), and all his bayath (house), ilah (go up / offer) up to zabach (offer) to Yahawah the yawam (day) zabach (sacrifice), and his nadar (vow).

But Chanah (Hannah) didn't ilah (go up / offer) up; for she amar (spoke) to her ayash (husband/individual man), Not until the nair (child) is weaned; then I will bawaa (come) him, that he may raah (see) panayam (before) Yahawah, and stay there iwalam (forever).

Alaqanah (Elkanah) her ayash (husband/individual man) amar (spoke) to her, "ishah (make) what seems tawab (pleasant/functional) to you. Wait until you have weaned him; only may Yahawah qawam (rise up) his dabar (word / matter)." So the ashah (wife/individual woman) waited and yanaq (nursed) her ban (son), until she weaned him.

When she had weaned him, she ilah (go up / offer) him up with her, with shalawash (three) par (bulls), and achad (one) ayapah (ephah) of qamach (meal), and a nabal (bottle) of yayan (wine), and bawaa (come) him to yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) bayath (house) in Shayalah (Shiloh). The nair (child) was nair (young).
They shachat (killed) the par (bull), and bawaa (come) the nair (child) to Ilay (Eli).
She amar (spoke), "Oh, my Adawan, as your napash (living being/soul) chay (life), my Adawan, I am the ashah (wife/individual woman) who natzab (stood) by you here, palal (praying) to Yahawah.
For this nair (child) I palal (prayed); and Yahawah nathan (give) given me my shaalah (petition) which I shaal (asked) of him.
Therefore also I have granted him to Yahawah. As yawam (day) as he lives he is granted to Yahawah." He shachah (worshiped) Yahawah there.

Chanah (Hannah) palal (prayed), and amar (spoke): My lab (heart) exults in Yahawah! My qaran (horn) is rawam (will lift up) in Yahawah. My pah (mouth) is enlarged over my ayab (enemy), because I shamach (rejoice) in your yashawaih (salvation).
There is no one as qadawash (holy) as Yahawah, For there is no one balathay (besides) you, nor is there any tzawar (rock) like our Alahayam.

Dabar (word / matter) no more so gabah (exceeding) gabah (proudly). Don't let arrogance yatzaa (go out / come out) out of your pah (mouth), For Yahawah is a Al of daih (knowledge). By him ilayalah (actions) are thakan (weighed).
The qashath (bows) of the gabawar (mighty) men are chath (broken). Those who kashal (stumble / stagger) are armed with chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor).

Those who were shabai (full) have shakar (hired) themselves out for lacham (bread). Those who were raib (hungry) are satisfied. Yes, the iqar (barren) has yalad (birth / begot) shabai (seven). She who rab (has) many ban (son) languishes.
Yahawah mawath (death), and chayah (makes) alive. He yarad (brings) down to shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife), and ilah (go up / offer) up.
Yahawah yarash (makes) poor, and ishar (makes) rich. He shapal (brings) low, he also rawam (will lift up) up.

He qawam (rise up) up the dal (poor) out of the ipar (dust). He rawam (will lift up) up the abayawan (needy) from the dunghill, To yashab (inhabit/dwell) them sit with nadayab (princes), and nachal (inherit) the kasaa (throne) of kabawad (glory). For the matzawaq (pillars) of the aratz (Earth/land) are yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)). He has shayath (put / appoint / make) the thabal (world) on them.

He will shamar (keep/guard) the ragal (feet / foot) of his chasayad (holy) ones, but the rashai (wicked) shall be put to damam (silence) in chashak (darkness); for no ayash (husband/individual man) shall gabar (prevail) by kach (strength / mighty / power).

Those who rayab (strive) with Yahawah shall be broken to pieces. He will raim (thunder) against them in the sky. Yahawah will dayan (judge) the apas (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land). He will nathan (give) iz (strength / might / refuge) to his malak (king), and rawam (will lift up) the qaran (horn) of his mashayach (anointed one).
Alaqanah (Elkanah) yalak (went) to Ramah (Ramah) to his bayath (house). The nair (child) sharath (served) Yahawah panayam (before) Ilay (Eli) the kahan (priest).
Now the ban (son) of Ilay (Eli) were base ban (son); they didn't yadai (know) Yahawah.

The mashapat (custom) of the kahan (priest) with the im (people / nation) was that when any ayash (husband/individual man) zabach (offered) zabach (sacrifice), the kahan (priest) nair (servant) bawaa (come), while the bashar (flesh) was bashal (boiling), with a fork of shalawash (three) shan (teeth) in his yad (hand);

And he nakah (struck) it into the kayawar (pan), or dawad (kettle), or qalachath (caldron), or parawar (pot); all that the fork ilah (go up / offer) up the kahan (priest) laqach (take / seized) therewith. So they ishah (make) in Shayalah (Shiloh) Yasharaal (to) all the Israelites who bawaa (come) there.

Yes, before they burnt the chalab (fat), the kahan (priest) nair (servant) bawaa (come), and amar (spoke) to the ayash (husband/individual man) who zabach (sacrificed), nathan (give) meat to tzalah (roast) for the kahan (priest); for he will not laqach (take / seized) bashal (boiled) meat from you, but chay (life).

If the ayash (husband/individual man) amar (spoke) to him, "Let the chalab (fat) be qatar (burned) yawam (day), and then laqach (take / seized) as much as your napash (living being/soul) amar (spoke);" then he would amar (spoke), No, but you shall nathan (give) it to me now; and if not, I will laqach (take / seized) it by chazaqah (force).

The chataah (sin) of the nair (young) men was very gadawal (very great/important/mighty) panayam (before) Yahawah; for the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) naatz (despised) the manachah (offering) of Yahawah.
But Shamawaal (Samuel) sharath (ministered) panayam (before) Yahawah, being a nair (child), clothed with a bad (linen) apawad (ephod).

Moreover his am (mother) ishah (make) him a qatan (small/young/least) maiyal (robe), and ilah (go up / offer) it to him from yawam (day) to yawam (day), when she ilah (go up / offer) up with her ayash (husband/individual man) to zabach (offer) the yawam (day) zabach (sacrifice).

Ilay (Eli) barak (blessed) Alaqanah (Elkanah) and his ashah (wife/individual woman), and amar (spoke), "Yahawah shawam (place / establish / appoint) you zarai (seed) of this ashah (wife/individual woman) for the shaalah (petition) which was shaal (asked) of Yahawah." They halak (move) to their own maqawam (place).

Yahawah paqad (visit) Chanah (Hannah), and she harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) shalawash (three) ban (son) and shanayam (two) bath (daughter). The nair (child) Shamawaal (Samuel) gadal (grew) im (before) Yahawah.

Now Ilay (Eli) was very zaqan (old); and he shamai (hearken / hear) all that his ban (son) ishah (make) to all Yasharaal (Israel), and how that they shakab (lay) with the ashah (wife/individual woman) who served at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
He amar (spoke) to them, "Why ishah (make) you do such things? For I shamai (hearken / hear) of your rai (evil) dealings from all this im (people / nation).
No, my ban (son); for it is no tawab (pleasant/functional) shamawaih (report) that I shamai (hearken / hear): you make yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) im (people / nation) disobey.

If one ayash (husband/individual man) chataa (sin) against ayash (husband/individual man), Alahayam shall palal (judge) him; but if a ayash (husband/individual man) chataa (sin) against Yahawah, who shall entreat for him?" Notwithstanding, they didn't shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of their ab (father), because Yahawah intended to mawath (death) them.
The nair (child) Shamawaal (Samuel) gadal (grew) on, and increased in favor both with Yahawah, and also with halak (move).

A ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam bawaa (come) to Ilay (Eli), and amar (spoke) to him, Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘Did I galah (reveal) myself to the bayath (house) of your ab (father), when they were in Matzarayam (Egypt) in bondage to Paraih (Pharaoh's) bayath (house)?

Did I bachar (choose) him out of all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) to be my kahan (priest), to ilah (go up / offer) up to my mazabach (altar), to qatar (burn) qatarath (incense), to nashaa (lift) an apawad (ephod) panayam (before) me? Nathan (give) I give to the bayath (house) of your ab (father) all the offerings of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) made by ashah (wife/individual woman)?

Why do you bait (kick) at my zabach (sacrifice) and at my zabach (offering), which I have tzawah (commanded) in my maiwan (habitation), and honor your ban (son) above me, to baraa (created) yourselves fat with the best of all the manachah (offerings) of Yasharaal (Israel) my im (people / nation)?’

Therefore Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), naam (declares (prophetically)), ‘I naam (declares (prophetically)) amar (spoke) that your bayath (house), and the bayath (house) of your ab (father), should halak (move) panayam (before) me iwalam (forever).’ But now Yahawah naam (declares (prophetically)), ‘Be it chalayalah (far) from me; for those who honor me I will honor, and those who bazah (despise) me shall be lightly qalal (esteemed).

Behold, the yawam (day) bawaa (come), that I will gadai (cut) off your zarawai (arm), and the zarawai (arm) of your ab (father) bayath (house), that there shall not be an old zaqan (man) in your bayath (house).

You shall nabat (see) the tzar (oppressor / distressor) of my maiwan (habitation), in all the wealth which I shall yatab (give) Yasharaal (Israel); and there shall not be an old zaqan (man) in your bayath (house) yawam (day).

The ayash (husband/individual man) of yours, whom I shall not karath (cut) off from my mazabach (altar), shall kalah (complete / finish) your iyan (eye), and adab (grieve) your napash (living being/soul); and all the marabayath (increase) of your bayath (house) shall mawath (death) in the flower of their age.

‘This shall be the awath (sign / mark / miracle) to you, that shall bawaa (come) on your shanayam (two) ban (son), on Chapanay (Hophni) and Payanachas (Phinehas): in achad (one) yawam (day) they shall shanayam (two) mawath (death).

I will qawam (rise up) me up a aman (believe / have faith) kahan (priest), that shall ishah (make) according to that which is in my labab (heart) and in my napash (living being/soul). I will banah (build) him a aman (believe / have faith) bayath (house); and he shall halak (move) panayam (before) my mashayach (anointed one) yawam (day).

It shall happen, that everyone who is yathar (left) in your bayath (house) shall bawaa (come) and shachah (bow) down to him for a agawarah (piece) of kasap (silver) and a kakar (loaf) of lacham (bread), and shall amar (spoke), "Please put me into achad (one) of the kahanah (priests)' offices, that I may akal (eat) a path (morsel) of lacham (bread)."’

The nair (child) Shamawaal (Samuel) sharath (ministered) to Yahawah panayam (before) Ilay (Eli). The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah was yaqar (precious) in those yawam (day); there was no frequent chazawan (vision).
It happened at that yawam (day), when Ilay (Eli) was shakab (laid) down in his maqawam (place) (now his iyan (eye) had chalal (begun) to grow kahah (dim), so that he yakal (could) not raah (see)),
And the nayar (lamp) of Alahayam hadn't yet kabah (gone) out, and Shamawaal (Samuel) had shakab (laid) down in the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, where the arawan (ark) of Alahayam was;
That Yahawah qaraa (called) Shamawaal (Samuel); and he amar (spoke), Here I am.
He rawatz (ran) to Ilay (Eli), and amar (spoke), "Here I am; for you amar (spoke) me." He said, "I didn't qaraa (called); shakab (lie) down again." He yalak (went) and shakab (lay) down.

Yahawah qaraa (called) yet again, "Shamawaal (Samuel)!" Shamawaal (Samuel) qawam (rise up) and yalak (went) to Ilay (Eli), and amar (spoke), "Here I am; for you qaraa (called) me." He amar (spoke), I didn't qaraa (called), my ban (son); shakab (lie) down again.
Now Shamawaal (Samuel) didn't yet yadai (know) Yahawah, neither was the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah yet galah (revealed) to him.

Yahawah qaraa (called) Shamawaal (Samuel) again the shalayashay (third) time. He qawam (rise up) and yalak (went) to Ilay (Eli), and amar (spoke), "Here I am; for you qaraa (called) me." Ilay (Eli) bayan (between) that Yahawah had qaraa (called) the nair (child).

Therefore Ilay (Eli) amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), "yalak (go), shakab (lie) down: and it shall be, if he qaraa (called) you, that you shall amar (spoke), ‘dabar (word / matter), Yahawah; for your ibad (servant) shamai (hearken / hear).’" So Shamawaal (Samuel) yalak (went) and shakab (lay) down in his maqawam (place).

Yahawah bawaa (come), and yatzab (stood), and qaraa (called) as at other paim (times), "Shamawaal (Samuel)! Shamawaal (Samuel)!" Then Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), dabar (word / matter); for your ibad (servant) shamai (hearken / hear).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), Behold, I will ishah (make) a thing in Yasharaal (Israel), at which shanayam (two) the azan (ears) of everyone who shamai (hearken / hear) it shall tzalal (tingle).
In that yawam (day) I will qawam (rise up) against Ilay (Eli) all that I have dabar (word / matter) al (concerning) his bayath (house), from the beginning even to the kalah (complete / finish).

For I have nagad (told) him that I will shapat (judge) his bayath (house) iwalam (forever), for the iwan (guilt/iniquity) which he yadai (knew), because his ban (son) brought a qalal (curse) on themselves, and he didn't kahah (restrain) them.

Therefore I have shabai (swear / take oath) to the bayath (house) of Ilay (Eli), that the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of Ilay (Eli's) bayath (house) shall not be removed with zabach (sacrifice) nor zabach (offering) iwalam (forever).

Shamawaal (Samuel) shakab (lay) until the baqar (morning), and pathach (opened) the dalath (doors) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah. Shamawaal (Samuel) yaraa (fear / be afraid) to show Ilay (Eli) the maraah (vision).
Then Ilay (Eli) qaraa (called) Shamawaal (Samuel), and amar (spoke), "Shamawaal (Samuel), my ban (son)!" He amar (spoke), Here I am.

He amar (spoke), dabar (word / matter) is the thing that he has dabar (word / matter) to you? Please don't kachad (hide) it from me. Alahayam ishah (make) so to you, and more also, if you kachad (hide) anything from me of all the things that he dabar (word / matter) to you.
Shamawaal (Samuel) nagad (told) him every bit, and kachad (hid) nothing from him. He amar (spoke), It is Yahawah. Let him ishah (make) what seems tawab (pleasant/functional) to him.
Shamawaal (Samuel) gadal (grew), and Yahawah was with him, and let none of his dabar (word / matter) napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land).
All Yasharaal (Israel) Dan (from) Dan Baarashabai (even) to Beersheba yadai (knew) that Shamawaal (Samuel) was aman (believe / have faith) to be a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Yahawah.
Yahawah raah (see) again in Shayalah (Shiloh); for Yahawah galah (revealed) himself to Shamawaal (Samuel) in Shayalah (Shiloh) by the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah.

The dabar (word / matter) of Shamawaal (Samuel) came to all Yasharaal (Israel). Now Yasharaal (Israel) yatzaa (go out / come out) out il (over) the Palashathay (Philistines) to malachamah (battle), and chanah (encamped) beside Abanahaizar (Ebenezer): and the Palashathay (Philistines) chanah (encamped) in Apaq (Aphek).

The Palashathay (Philistines) irak (put) themselves in array panayam (against) Yasharaal (Israel): and when they natash (joined) malachamah (battle), Yasharaal (Israel) was nagap (struck) panayam (before) the Palashathay (Philistines); and they nakah (killed) of the mairakah (army) in the shadah (field) about arabai (four) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man).

When the im (people / nation) bawaa (come) come into the machanah (camp), the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke), Why has Yahawah nagap (struck) us today panayam (before) the Palashathay (Philistines)? Let us laqach (take / seized) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah out of Shayalah (Shiloh) to us, that it may bawaa (come) qarab (among / near) us, and yashai (salvation) us out of the kap (hand) of our ayab (enemy).

So the im (people / nation) shalach (send) to Shayalah (Shiloh); and they nashaa (lift) from there the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah of tzabaa (troop), who yashab (inhabit/dwell) above the karawab (cherubim): and the shanayam (two) ban (son) of Ilay (Eli), Chapanay (Hophni) and Payanachas (Phinehas), were there with the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Alahayam.

When the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah bawaa (come) into the machanah (camp), all Yasharaal (Israel) rawai (shouted) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) tharawaih (shout), so that the aratz (Earth/land) hawam (rang) again.

When the Palashathay (Philistines) shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the tharawaih (shout), they amar (spoke), "What does the qawal (sound / voice) of this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) tharawaih (shout) in the machanah (camp) of the ibaray (hebrews) mean?" They yadai (understood) that the arawan (ark) of Yahawah bawaa (come) come into the machanah (camp).

The Palashathay (Philistines) were yaraa (fear / be afraid), for they amar (spoke), "Alahayam bawaa (come) come into the machanah (camp)." They amar (spoke), away (woe) to us! For there has not been such a thing athamawal (before).

Away (woe) to us! Who shall natzal (deliver) us out of the yad (hand) of these adayar (mighty) Alahayam? These are the Alahayam that nakah (struck) the Matzarayam (Egyptians) with all kinds of makah (plagues) in the madabar (wilderness).

Be chazaq (strong), and behave like chazaq (men), O you Palashathay (Philistines), that you not be ibad (servant) to the ibaray (hebrews), as they have been to you. Strengthen yourselves like chazaq (men), and lacham (fight)!

The Palashathay (Philistines) lacham (fought), and Yasharaal (Israel) was nagap (struck), and they nawas (fled) every ayash (husband/individual man) to his ahal (tent): and there was a very gadawal (very great/important/mighty) makah (slaughter); for there napal (fall / be cast down) of Yasharaal (Israel) shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand) footmen.
The arawan (ark) of Alahayam was laqach (take / seized); and the shanayam (two) ban (son) of Ilay (Eli), Chapanay (Hophni) and Payanachas (Phinehas), were mawath (death).

There rawatz (ran) a ayash (husband/individual man) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) out of the mairakah (army), and bawaa (come) to Shayalah (Shiloh) the same yawam (day), with his mad (clothes) qarai (torn), and with adamah (earth) on his raash (head).

When he bawaa (come), behold, Ilay (Eli) was sitting on his kasaa (seat) by the road tzapah (watchman / keep watch); for his lab (heart) trembled for the arawan (ark) of Alahayam. When the ayash (husband/individual man) bawaa (come) into the iyar (city), and nagad (told) it, all the iyar (city) zaiq (cried) out.

When Ilay (Eli) shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the tzaiqah (crying), he amar (spoke), "What does the qawal (sound / voice) of this tumult mean?" The ayash (husband/individual man) hurried, and bawaa (come) and nagad (told) Ilay (Eli).
Now Ilay (Eli) was thashaiyam (ninety) - shamanah (eight) shanah (years) ban (son); and his iyan (eye) were qawam (rise up), so that he yakal (could) not raah (see).

The ayash (husband/individual man) amar (spoke) to Ilay (Eli), "I am he who bawaa (come) out of the mairakah (army), and I nawas (fled) today out of the mairakah (army)." He amar (spoke), How dabar (word / matter) the matter go, my ban (son)?

He who inah (answer / respond) the news answered, Yasharaal (Israel) has nawas (fled) panayam (before) the Palashathay (Philistines), and there has been also a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) magapah (slaughter) among the im (people / nation). Your shanayam (two) ban (son) also, Chapanay (Hophni) and Payanachas (Phinehas), are mawath (death), and the arawan (ark) of Alahayam has been captured.

It happened, when he zakar (remembrance/memory) mention of the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, that Eli napal (fall / be cast down) from off his kasaa (seat) backward by the yad (hand) of the shair (gate); and his maparaqath (neck) shabar (broke), and he mawath (death); for he was an zaqan (old) ayash (husband/individual man), and kabad (heavy). He had shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years).

His kalah (complete / finish), Payanachas (Phinehas)' ashah (wife/individual woman), was with harah (child), near to be yalad (birth / begot). When she shamai (hearken / hear) the shamawaih (news) that the arawan (ark) of Alahayam was laqach (take / seized), and that her father-in-law and her ayash (husband/individual man) were mawath (death), she karai (bowed) herself and gave yalad (birth / begot); for her tzayar (pains) hapak (came) on her.

About the ith (time) of her mawath (death) the women who natzab (stood) by her dabar (word / matter) to her, "Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid); for you have given yalad (birth / begot) to a ban (son)." But she didn't inah (answer / respond), neither did she shayath (put / appoint / make) it.

She qaraa (called) the nair (child) Ayakabawad (Ichabod), amar (spoke), "The kabawad (glory) has departed from Yasharaal (Israel);" al (because) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam was laqach (take / seized), and because of her father-in-law and her ayash (husband/individual man).
She amar (spoke), The kabawad (glory) has departed from Yasharaal (Israel); for the arawan (ark) of Alahayam is laqach (take / seized).
Now the Palashathay (Philistines) had laqach (take / seized) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, and they bawaa (come) it from Abanahaizar (Ebenezer) Ashadawad (to) Ashdod.
The Palashathay (Philistines) laqach (take / seized) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, and bawaa (come) it into the bayath (house) of Dagawan (Dagon), and yatzag (set) it by Dagawan (Dagon).

When they of ashadawaday (ashdod) arose shakam (early) on the next macharath (day), behold, Dagawan (Dagon) was napal (fall / be cast down) on his panayam (face) to the aratz (Earth/land) panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah. They laqach (take / seized) Dagawan (Dagon), and shawab (turn back / repent) him in his maqawam (place) again.

When they arose shakam (early) on the next macharath (day) baqar (morning), behold, Dagawan (Dagon) was napal (fall / be cast down) on his panayam (face) to the aratz (Earth/land) panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah; and the raash (head) of Dagawan (Dagon) and shanayam (two) the kap (palms) of his yad (hand) were karath (cut) off on the mapathan (threshold). Only Dagawan (Dagon's) torso was intact.

Therefore neither the kahan (priest) of Dagawan (Dagon), nor any who bawaa (come) into Dagawan (Dagon's) bayath (house), darak (tread) on the mapathan (threshold) of Dagawan (Dagon) Ashadawad (in) Ashdod, to this yawam (day).

But the yad (hand) of Yahawah was kabad (heavy) on them of ashadawaday (ashdod), and he shamam (destroyed) them, and nakah (struck) them with tumors, Ashadawad (even) Ashdod and its gabawal (border/boundary).

When the ayash (husband/individual man) Ashadawad (of) Ashdod raah (see) that it was so, they amar (spoke), The arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) shall not stay with us; for his yad (hand) is severe on us, and on Dagawan (Dagon) our Alahayam.

They shalach (send) therefore and asap (gathered) all the saran (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) to them, and amar (spoke), "What shall we ishah (make) with the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel)?" They amar (spoke), "Let the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) be sabab (carried) over to gath (gath)." They sabab (carried) the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) there.

It was so, that achar (other) they had sabab (carried) it about, the yad (hand) of Yahawah was against the iyar (city) with a very gadawal (very great/important/mighty) mahawamah (confusion): and he nakah (struck) the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) of the iyar (city), both qatan (small/young/least) and gadawal (very great/important/mighty); and tumors broke out on them.

So they shalach (send) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam to Iqarawan (Ekron). It happened, as the arawan (ark) of Alahayam bawaa (come) to Iqarawan (Ekron), that the iqarawanay (ekronites) zaiq (cried) out, amar (spoke), They have sabab (brought) about the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) to us, to mawath (death) us and our im (people / nation).

They shalach (send) therefore and asap (gathered) together all the saran (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and they amar (spoke), "shalach (send) away the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), and shawab (turn back / repent) it go again to its own maqawam (place), that it not mawath (death) us and our im (people / nation)." For there was a mawath (death) mahawamah (confusion) throughout all the iyar (city); the yad (hand) of Alahayam was very kabad (heavy) there.
The ayash (husband/individual man) who didn't mawath (death) were nakah (struck) with the tumors; and the cry of the iyar (city) ilah (go up / offer) up to shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)).
The arawan (ark) of Yahawah was in the shadah (country) of the Palashathay (Philistines) shabai (seven) chadash (month).

The Palashathay (Philistines) qaraa (called) for the kahan (priest) and the diviners, amar (spoke), What shall we ishah (make) with the arawan (ark) of Yahawah? Show us with which we shall shalach (send) it to its maqawam (place).

They amar (spoke), If you shalach (send) away the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), don't shalach (send) it rayaqam (empty); but by shawab (turn back / repent) means shawab (turn back / repent) him a asham (trespass) offering: then you shall be rapaa (healed), and it shall be yadai (known) to you why his yad (hand) is not sawar (removed) from you.

Then they amar (spoke), "What shall be the asham (trespass) offering which we shall shawab (turn back / repent) to him?" They amar (spoke), chamash (five) zahab (gold) tumors, and chamash (five) zahab (gold) ikabar (mice), for the masapar (number) of the saran (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines); for achad (one) magapah (plague) was on you all, and on your saran (lords).

Therefore you shall ishah (make) tzalam (likeness) of your tumors, and tzalam (likeness) of your ikabar (mice) that shachath (mar) the aratz (Earth/land); and you shall nathan (give) kabawad (glory) to the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): perhaps he will lighten his yad (hand) from off you, and from off your Alahayam, and from off your aratz (Earth/land).

Why then kabad (do) you harden your labab (hearts), as the Matzaray (Egyptians) and Paraih (Pharaoh) kabad (hardened) their lab (heart)? When he had ilal (worked) wonderfully among them, didn't they shalach (send) the people go, and they departed?

Now therefore laqach (take / seized) and ishah (make) yourselves a chadash (new) igalah (cart), and shanayam (two) milk parah (cows), on which there has ilah (go up / offer) no il (over); and asar (tie) the parah (cows) to the igalah (cart), and shawab (turn back / repent) their calves bayath (house) from them;

And laqach (take / seized) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, and nathan (give) it on the igalah (cart); and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the kalay (jewels) of zahab (gold), which you shawab (turn back / repent) him for a asham (trespass) offering, in a aragaz (coffer) by its tzad (side); and shalach (send) it away, that it may halak (move).

Raah (see); if it ilah (go up / offer) up by the darak (way) of its own gabawal (border/boundary) to Bayathashamash (Beth) Shemesh, then he ishah (make) done us this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) rai (evil): but if not, then we shall yadai (know) that it is not his yad (hand) that nagai (struck) us; it was a maqarah (chance) that hayah (came to pass) to us.
The ishah (make) ishah (make) so, and laqach (take / seized) shanayam (two) milk parah (cows), and asar (tied) them to the igalah (cart), and kalaa (shut) up their calves at bayath (house);

And they shawam (place / establish / appoint) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah on the igalah (cart), and the aragaz (coffer) with the ikabar (mice) of zahab (gold) and the tzalam (likeness) of their tumors.

The parah (cows) took the yashar (straight) darak (way) by the darak (way) to Bayathashamash (Beth) Shemesh; they halak (move) along the masalah (highway), gaih (lowing) as they halak (move), and didn't sawar (turn) aside to the right yamayan (right hand) or to the shamaawal (left hand); and the saran (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) halak (move) achar (other) them to the gabawal (border/boundary) of Bayathashamash (Beth) Shemesh.

They of Bayathashamash (Beth) Shemesh were qatzar (reaping) their chatah (wheat) qatzayar (harvest) in the imaq (valley); and they nashaa (lift) up their iyan (eye), and raah (see) the arawan (ark), and shamach (rejoiced) to raah (see) it.

The igalah (cart) bawaa (come) into the shadah (field) of Yahawashawai (Joshua) of Beth Shemesh, and imad (stood) there, where there was a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) aban (stone): and they split the itz (wood) of the igalah (cart), and ilah (go up / offer) up the parah (cows) for a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah.

The Lawayay (Levites) yarad (took) down the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, and the aragaz (coffer) that was with it, in which the kalay (jewels) of zahab (gold) were, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them on the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) aban (stone): and the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) of Bayathashamash (Beth) Shemesh ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilah (offerings) and zabach (sacrificed) zabach (sacrifices) the same yawam (day) to Yahawah.
When the chamash (five) saran (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) raah (see) seen it, they shawab (turn back / repent) to Iqarawan (Ekron) the same yawam (day).

These are the zahab (gold) tumors which the Palashathay (Philistines) shawab (turn back / repent) for a asham (trespass) offering to Yahawah: Ashadawad (for) Ashdod achad (one), for Izah (Gaza) achad (one), for Ashaqalawan (Ashkelon) achad (one), for gath (gath) achad (one), for Iqarawan (Ekron) achad (one);

And the zahab (gold) ikabar (mice), according to the masapar (number) of all the iyar (cities) of the Palashathay (Philistines) belonging to the chamash (five) saran (lords), both of fortified iyar (cities) and of country kapar (villages), even to the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) Abal (stone), whereon they yanach (set) down the arawan (ark) of Yahawah. That stone remains to this yawam (day) in the shadah (field) of Yahawashawai (Joshua) of Beth Shemesh.

He nakah (struck) of the ayash (husband/individual man) of Bayathashamash (Beth) Shemesh, because they raah (see) looked into the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, he nakah (struck) of the im (people / nation) chamashayam (fifty) alap (thousand) shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (husband/individual man); and the im (people / nation) abal (mourned), because Yahawah had nakah (struck) the ayash (husband/individual man) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) makah (slaughter).

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Bayathashamash (Beth) Shemesh amar (spoke), Who is yakal (able) to imad (stand) panayam (before) Yahawah, this qadawash (holy) Alahayam? To whom shall he ilah (go up / offer) up from us?

They shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Kiriath Qarayathayairayam (Jearim), amar (spoke), The Palashathay (Philistines) have shawab (turn back / repent) back the arawan (ark) of Yahawah; yarad (come) down, and ilah (go up / offer) it up to yourselves.

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Kiriath Qarayathayairayam (Jearim) bawaa (come), and ilah (go up / offer) up the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, and bawaa (come) it into the bayath (house) of Abayanadab (Abinadab) in the gabaih (hill), and qadash (set apart/make holy) Alaizar (Eleazar) his ban (son) to shamar (keep/guard) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah.

It happened, from the yawam (day) that the arawan (ark) stayed in Kiriath Qarayathayairayam (Jearim), that the yawam (day) was rabah (long); for it was isharayam (twenty) shanah (years): and all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) nahah (lamented) achar (other) Yahawah.

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), If you do shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah with all your labab (heart), then sawar (put) away the foreign Alahayam and the Ishatharawath (Ashtaroth) from thawak (midst) you, and kawan (direct) your labab (hearts) to Yahawah, and ibad (servant) him only; and he will natzal (deliver) you out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines).
Then the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) sawar (removed) the Bail (Baals) and the Ishatharawath (Ashtaroth), and ibad (servant) Yahawah only.
Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), qabatz (gather) all Yasharaal (Israel) to Mizpah, and I will palal (pray) for you to Yahawah.

They qabatz (gathered) together Matzapah (to) Mizpah, and shaab (drew) mayam (Waters), and shapak (poured) it out panayam (before) Yahawah, and tzawam (fasted) on that yawam (day), and amar (spoke) there, "We have chataa (sinned) against Yahawah." Shamawaal (Samuel) shapat (judged) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) in Mizpah.

When the Palashathay (Philistines) shamai (hearken / hear) that the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) were qabatz (gathered) together at Mizpah, the saran (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up against Yasharaal (Israel). When the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) shamai (hearken / hear) it, they were yaraa (fear / be afraid) of the Palashathay (Philistines).

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), Don't charash (cease) to zaiq (cry) to Yahawah our Alahayam for us, that he will yashai (salvation) us out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines).

Shamawaal (Samuel) laqach (take / seized) a suckling talah (lamb), and ilah (go up / offer) it for a kalayal (whole) burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah: and Shamawaal (Samuel) zaiq (cried) to Yahawah for Yasharaal (Israel); and Yahawah inah (answer / respond) him.

As Shamawaal (Samuel) was ilah (go up / offer) up the burnt ilah (offering), the Palashathay (Philistines) nagash (drew) near to malachamah (battle) against Yasharaal (Israel); but Yahawah raim (thundered) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice) on that yawam (day) on the Palashathay (Philistines), and confused them; and they were nagap (struck) down panayam (before) Yasharaal (Israel).

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) yatzaa (go out / come out) out Matzapah (of) Mizpah, and radap (pursued) the Palashathay (Philistines), and nakah (struck) them, until they came under Bayathakar (Beth) Kar.

Then Shamawaal (Samuel) laqach (take / seized) a aban (stone), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it Matzapah (between) Mizpah and Shan (Shen), and qaraa (called) its sham (name) Abanahaizar (Ebenezer), amar (spoke), Yahawah izar (helped) us until now.

So the Palashathay (Philistines) were kanai (subdued), and they bawaa (come) no more within the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yasharaal (Israel). The yad (hand) of Yahawah was against the Palashathay (Philistines) all the yawam (day) of Shamawaal (Samuel).

The iyar (cities) which the Palashathay (Philistines) had laqach (take / seized) from Yasharaal (Israel) were shawab (turn back / repent) to Yasharaal (Israel), from Iqarawan (Ekron) even to gath (gath); and Yasharaal (Israel) natzal (recovered) its gabawal (border/boundary) out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines). There was shalawam (peace / safety) between Yasharaal (Israel) and the Amaray (Amorites).
Shamawaal (Samuel) shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel) all the yawam (day) of his chay (life).

He halak (move) from shanah (year) to shanah (year) in sabab (circuit) to Bayathaal (Bethel) and Galagal (Gilgal), and Matzapah (Mizpah); and he shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel) in all those maqawam (place).
His thashawabah (return) was to Ramah (Ramah), for there was his bayath (house); and there he shapat (judged) Yasharaal (Israel): and he banah (built) there an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah.
It happened, when Shamawaal (Samuel) was zaqan (old), that he shawam (place / establish / appoint) his ban (son) shapat (judges) over Yasharaal (Israel).
Now the sham (name) of his ban (son) was Yawaal (Joel); and the sham (name) of his mashanah (second), Abayah (Abijah): they were shapat (judges) Baarashabai (in) Beersheba.
His ban (son) didn't halak (move) in his darak (ways), but natah (turned) aside achar (other) batzai (lucre), and laqach (take / seized) shachad (bribes), and natah (perverted) mashapat (justice).
Then all the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) qabatz (gathered) themselves together, and bawaa (come) to Shamawaal (Samuel) to Ramah (Ramah);

And they amar (spoke) to him, Behold, you are zaqan (old), and your ban (son) don't halak (move) in your darak (ways): now shawam (place / establish / appoint) us a malak (king) to shapat (judge) us like all the gaway (nation / people).
But the thing displeased Shamawaal (Samuel), when they amar (spoke), "nathan (give) us a malak (king) to shapat (judge) us." Shamawaal (Samuel) palal (prayed) to Yahawah.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of the im (people / nation) in all that they amar (spoke) you; for they have not maas (rejected) you, but they have maas (rejected) me, that I should not be malak (king) over them.

According to all the maishah (works) which they ishah (make) done since the yawam (day) that I ilah (go up / offer) them up out of Matzarayam (Egypt) even to this yawam (day), in that they have forsaken me, and ibad (servant) other Alahayam, so ishah (make) they also to you.

Now therefore shamai (hearken / hear) to their qawal (sound / voice): however you shall iwad (admonish/bear witness against) iwad (admonish/bear witness against) to them, and shall show them the mashapat (way) of the malak (king) who shall malak (king) over them.
Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) all the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah to the im (people / nation) who shaal (asked) of him a malak (king).

He amar (spoke), This will be the mashapat (way) of the malak (king) who shall malak (king) over you: he will laqach (take / seized) your ban (son), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them to him, for his marakabah (chariots), and to be his horsemen; and they shall rawatz (run) panayam (before) his marakabah (chariots);

And he will shawam (place / establish / appoint) them to him for shar (prince / ruler) of alap (thousands), and shar (prince / ruler) of chamashayam (fifties); and he will assign some to charash (plow) his charayash (ground), and to qatzar (reap) his qatzayar (harvest), and to ishah (make) his kalay (instruments) of malachamah (war), and the kalay (instruments) of his rakab (chariots).
He will laqach (take / seized) your bath (daughter) to be perfumers, and to be tabachah (cooks), and to be bakers.
