He will laqach (take / seized) your shadah (fields), and your karam (vineyards), and your zayath (olive) groves, even their tawab (pleasant/functional), and nathan (give) them to his ibad (servant).
He will take the ishar (tenth) of your zarai (seed), and of your karam (vineyards), and nathan (give) to his sarayas (officers), and to his ibad (servant).

He will laqach (take / seized) your male ibad (servant), and your female ibad (servant), and your tawab (pleasant/functional) bachawar (young) men, and your donkeys, and ishah (make) them to his malaakah (work).
He will take the ishar (tenth) of your tzaan (flocks): and you shall be his ibad (servant).
You shall zaiq (cry) out in that yawam (day) panayam (because) of your malak (king) whom you shall have bachar (chosen) you; and Yahawah will not inah (answer / respond) you in that yawam (day).
But the im (people / nation) maan (refused) to shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of Shamawaal (Samuel); and they amar (spoke), No; but we will have a malak (king) over us,

That we also may be like all the gaway (nation / people), and that our malak (king) may shapat (judge) us, and yatzaa (go out / come out) out panayam (before) us, and lacham (fight) our malachamah (battles).
Shamawaal (Samuel) shamai (hearken / hear) all the dabar (word / matter) of the im (people / nation), and he dabar (word / matter) them in the azan (ears) of Yahawah.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), "shamai (hearken / hear) to their qawal (sound / voice), and malak (king) them a malak (king)." Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel), Every ayash (husband/individual man) yalak (go) to his iyar (city).

Now there was a ayash (husband/individual man) of Benjamin, whose sham (name) was Qayash (Kish), the ban (son) of Abayaal (Abiel), the ban (son) of Zeror, the ban (son) Bakawarath (of) Becorath, the ban (son) of Apayach (Aphiah), the son of a Benjamite, a gabawar (mighty) ayash (husband/individual man) of valor.

He had a ban (son), whose sham (name) was Shaawal (Saul), an impressive bachawar (young) man; and there was not among the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) a tawab (pleasant/functional) ayash (husband/individual man) than he. From his shakam (shoulders) and upward he was gabah (higher) than any of the im (people / nation).

The donkeys of Qayash (Kish), Shaawal (Saul's) ab (father), were abad (destroy/perish). Qayash (Kish) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul) his ban (son), laqach (take / seized) now achad (one) of the nair (servants) with you, and qawam (rise up), yalak (go) baqash (seek) the donkeys.

He ibar (pass over/through) through the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), and ibar (pass over/through) through the aratz (Earth/land) Shalashah (of) Shalishah, but they didn't matzaa (find) them: then they ibar (pass over/through) through the aratz (Earth/land) Shailayam (of) Shaalim, and there they weren't there: and he ibar (pass over/through) through the aratz (Earth/land) of the Benjamites, but they didn't matzaa (find) them.

When they bawaa (come) come to the aratz (Earth/land) of Tzawap (Zuph), Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to his nair (servant) who was with him, yalak (come), and let us shawab (turn back / repent), lest my ab (father) stop caring about the donkeys, and be anxious for us.

He amar (spoke) to him, See now, there is in this iyar (city) a ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, and he is a ayash (husband/individual man) who is held in honor. All that he dabar (word / matter) bawaa (come) bawaa (come) to pass. Now yalak (let) us go there. Perhaps he can nagad (tell) us concerning our darak (journey) whereon we halak (move).

Then Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to his nair (servant), But, behold, if we yalak (go), what shall we bawaa (come) the ayash (husband/individual man)? For the lacham (bread) is spent in our kalay (vessels), and there is not a thashawarah (present) to bawaa (come) to the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam. What do we have?

The nair (servant) inah (answer / respond) Shaawal (Saul) again, and inah (answer / respond), Behold, I matzaa (have) in my yad (hand) the rabai (fourth) part of a shaqal (shekel) of kasap (silver). I will nathan (give) that to the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, to nagad (tell) us our darak (way).

(In earlier times in Yasharaal (Israel), when a ayash (husband/individual man) yalak (went) to darash (inquire) of Alahayam, thus he amar (spoke), "yalak (come), and yalak (let) us go to the seer;" for he who is yawam (day) qaraa (called) a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) panayam (was) before qaraa (called) a Seer.)

Then Shaawal (Saul) dabar (word / matter) to his nair (servant), "tawab (pleasant/functional) amar (spoke). Yalak (come), yalak (let) us go." So they yalak (went) to the iyar (city) where the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam was.

As they ilah (go up / offer) up the ascent to the iyar (city), they matzaa (found) nairah (young) maidens yatzaa (go out / come out) out to shaab (draw) mayam (Waters), and amar (spoke) to them, Is the seer here?

They inah (answer / respond) them, and inah (answer / respond), He is. Behold, he is panayam (before) you. Hurry now, for he bawaa (come) come today into the iyar (city); for the people have a zabach (sacrifice) today in the bamah (high) place.

As soon as you bawaa (come) come into the iyar (city), you shall immediately matzaa (find) him, before he ilah (go up / offer) up to the bamah (high) place to akal (eat); for the im (people / nation) will not akal (eat) until he bawaa (come), because he blesses the zabach (sacrifice). Afterwards those who are qaraa (called) akal (eat). Now therefore ilah (go up / offer) up; for at this yawam (day) you shall matzaa (find) him.

They ilah (go up / offer) up to the iyar (city). As they bawaa (come) within the iyar (city), behold, Shamawaal (Samuel) yatzaa (go out / come out) out toward them, to ilah (go up / offer) up to the bamah (high) place.
Now Yahawah had galah (revealed) to Shamawaal (Samuel) a yawam (day) panayam (before) Shaawal (Saul) bawaa (come), amar (spoke),

Machar (tomorrow) about this ith (time) I will shalach (send) you a ayash (husband/individual man) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), and you shall mashach (anoint) him to be nagayad (prince) over my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel); and he shall yashai (salvation) my im (people / nation) out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines): for I raah (see) looked on my im (people / nation), because their tzaiqah (cry) bawaa (come) come to me.

When Shamawaal (Samuel) raah (see) Shaawal (Saul), Yahawah inah (answer / respond) to him, Behold, the ayash (husband/individual man) of whom I amar (spoke) to you! This same shall have authority over my im (people / nation).
Then Shaawal (Saul) nagash (drew) near to Shamawaal (Samuel) in the shair (gate), and amar (spoke), Please nagad (tell) me ay (where) the seer's bayath (house) is.

Shamawaal (Samuel) inah (answer / respond) Shaawal (Saul), and inah (answer / respond), I am the seer. Ilah (go up / offer) up panayam (before) me to the bamah (high) place, for you shall akal (eat) with me today. In the baqar (morning) I will shalach (send) you go, and will nagad (tell) you all that is in your labab (heart).

As for your donkeys who were abad (destroy/perish) shalawash (three) yawam (day) ago, don't shawam (place / establish / appoint) your lab (heart) on them; for they are matzaa (found). For whom is all that is desirable in Yasharaal (Israel)? Is it not for you, and for all your ab (father) bayath (house)?

Shaawal (Saul) inah (answer / respond), Am I not a Banayamayanay (Benjamite), of the smallest of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel)? And my mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) the tzaiyar (least) of all the mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) of the shabat (tribe) of Banayamayan (Benjamin)? Why then do you dabar (word / matter) to me like this?

Shamawaal (Samuel) laqach (take / seized) Shaawal (Saul) and his nair (servant), and bawaa (come) them into the guest room, and nathan (give) them sit in the best maqawam (place) among those who were qaraa (called), who were about shalawashayam (thirty) ayash (husband/individual man).
Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to the tabach (cook), nathan (give) the manah (portion) which I nathan (give) you, of which I amar (spoke) to you, ‘shawam (place / establish / appoint) it aside.’

The tabach (cook) rawam (will lift up) up the shawaq (thigh), and that which was on it, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it panayam (before) Shaawal (Saul). Samuel amar (spoke), "Behold, that which has been shaar (reserved)! Shawam (place / establish / appoint) it panayam (before) yourself and akal (eat); because for the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) time has it been shamar (keep/guard) for you, for I amar (spoke), ‘I have qaraa (called) the im (people / nation).’" So Shaawal (Saul) akal (eat) with Shamawaal (Samuel) that yawam (day).
When they had yarad (come) down from the bamah (high) place into the iyar (city), he dabar (word / matter) with Shaawal (Saul) on the housetop.

They arose shakam (early): and it happened about the ilah (go up / offer) of the shachar (day), that Shamawaal (Samuel) qaraa (called) to Shaawal (Saul) on the housetop, amar (spoke), "qawam (rise up) up, that I may shalach (send) you away." Shaawal (Saul) qawam (rise up), and they yatzaa (go out / come out) out shanayam (two) of them, he and Shamawaal (Samuel), chawatz (abroad).

As they were yarad (going) down at the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the iyar (city), Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "amar (spoke) the nair (servant) ibar (pass over/through) on panayam (before) us" (and he ibar (pass over/through) on), but imad (stand) still yawam (day), that I may shamai (hearken / hear) you to hear the dabar (word / matter) of Alahayam.

Then Shamawaal (Samuel) laqach (take / seized) the pak (vial) of shaman (oil), and yatzaq (poured) it on his raash (head), and nashaq (kissed) him, and amar (spoke), Isn't it that Yahawah has mashach (anointed) you to be nagayad (prince) over his nachalah (inheritance)?

When you have departed from me today, then you shall matzaa (find) shanayam (two) ayash (husband/individual man) by Rachal (Rachel's) tomb, in the gabawal (border/boundary) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) at Tzalatzach (Zelzah); and they will amar (spoke) you, ‘The donkeys which you halak (move) to baqash (seek) matzaa (have) been found; and behold, your ab (father) has stopped dabar (word / matter) about the donkeys, and is anxious for you, amar (spoke), "What shall I ishah (make) for my ban (son)?"’

Then you shall chalap (go) on halaah (forward) from there, and you shall bawaa (come) to the oak of Thabawar (Tabor); and shalawash (three) ayash (husband/individual man) shall matzaa (meet) you there ilah (go up / offer) up to Alahayam to Bayathaal (Bethel), achad (one) nashaa (lift) shalawash (three) young goats, and another nashaa (lift) shalawash (three) loaves of lacham (bread), and another nashaa (lift) a nabal (bottle) of yayan (wine):
And they will greet you, and nathan (give) you shanayam (two) loaves of lacham (bread), which you shall laqach (take / seized) of their yad (hand).

Achar (other) that you shall bawaa (come) to the gabaih (hill) of Alahayam, where is the natzayab (garrison) of the Palashathay (Philistines): and it shall happen, when you bawaa (come) come there to the iyar (city), that you shall pagai (meet) a chabal (band) of nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) yarad (coming) down from the bamah (high) place with a nabal (psaltery), and a tambourine, and a chalayal (pipe), and a kanawar (harp), panayam (before) them; and they will be nabaa (prophesying):
And the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah will tzalach (come) mightily on you, and you shall nabaa (prophesy) with them, and shall be hapak (turned) into achar (other) ayash (husband/individual man).
Let it be, when these awath (sign / mark / miracle) bawaa (come) come to you, that you ishah (make) as matzaa (occasion) shall yad (hand) you; for Alahayam is with you.

You shall yarad (go) down panayam (before) me to Galagal (Gilgal); and behold, I will yarad (come) down to you, to ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilah (offerings), and to ilah (go up / offer) zabach (sacrifices) of peace ilah (offerings): you shall yachal (wait) shabai (seven) yawam (day), until I bawaa (come) to you, and show you what you shall ishah (make).

It was so, that when he had panah (turned) his shakam (back) to yalak (go) from Shamawaal (Samuel), Alahayam hapak (gave) him achar (other) lab (heart): and all those awath (sign / mark / miracle) happened that yawam (day).

When they bawaa (come) there to the gabaih (hill), behold, a chabal (band) of nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) qaraa (called) him; and the rawach (spirit / wind) of Alahayam tzalach (came) mightily on him, and he nabaa (prophesied) thawak (midst) them.

It happened, when all who yadai (knew) him athamawal (before) raah (see) that, behold, he nabaa (prophesied) with the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), then the im (people / nation) amar (spoke) ayash (husband/individual man) to rai (neigbor/another person), What is this that has come to the ban (son) of Qayash (Kish)? Is Shaawal (Saul) also among the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy)?

Ayash (husband/individual man) of the same place inah (answer / respond), "Who is their ab (father)?" Therefore it became a mashal (proverb), Is Shaawal (Saul) also among the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy)?
When he kalah (complete / finish) made an end of nabaa (prophesying), he bawaa (come) to the bamah (high) place.

Shaawal (Saul's) dawad (uncle) amar (spoke) to him and to his nair (servant), "an (where) did you halak (move)?" He amar (spoke), To baqash (seek) the donkeys. When we raah (see) that they were not found, we bawaa (come) to Shamawaal (Samuel).
Shaawal (Saul's) dawad (uncle) amar (spoke), Please nagad (tell) me what Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to you.

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to his dawad (uncle), "He amar (spoke) us nagad (plainly) that the donkeys were matzaa (found)." But dabar (word / matter) the matter of the malawakah (kingdom), of which Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), he didn't nagad (tell) him.
Shamawaal (Samuel) tzaiq (called) the im (people / nation) together to Yahawah Matzapah (to) Mizpah;

And he amar (spoke) to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘I ilah (go up / offer) up Yasharaal (Israel) out of Matzarayam (Egypt), and I natzal (delivered) you out of the yad (hand) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and out of the yad (hand) of all the mamalakah (kingdoms) that lachatz (oppressed) you:’

But you have this yawam (day) maas (rejected) your Alahayam, who himself yashai (salvation) you out of all your rai (calamities) and your distresses; and you have amar (spoke) to him, ‘No! Shawam (place / establish / appoint) a malak (king) over us.’ Now therefore yatzab (present) yourselves panayam (before) Yahawah by your shabat (tribes), and by your alap (thousands).
So Shamawaal (Samuel) brought all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) qarab (come close), and the shabat (tribe) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) was lakad (taken).

He brought the shabat (tribe) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) qarab (come close) by their mashapachah (tribe/clan/family); and the mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) of the Matrites was lakad (taken); and Shaawal (Saul) the ban (son) of Qayash (Kish) was lakad (taken): but when they baqash (sought) him, he could not be matzaa (found).
Therefore they shaal (asked) of Yahawah further, "Is there yet a ayash (husband/individual man) to bawaa (come) here?" Yahawah amar (spoke), Behold, he has chabaa (hidden) himself among the baggage.

They rawatz (ran) and laqach (take / seized) him there; and when he yatzab (stood) thawak (midst) the im (people / nation), he was gabah (higher) than any of the im (people / nation) from his shakam (shoulders) and upward.

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to all the im (people / nation), "You raah (see) him whom Yahawah has bachar (chosen), that there is none like him among all the im (people / nation)?" All the im (people / nation) rawai (shouted), and amar (spoke), Let the malak (king) chayah (live)!

Then Shamawaal (Samuel) dabar (word / matter) the im (people / nation) the regulations of the malawakah (kingdom), and kathab (wrote) it in a sapar (book / scribed document), and yanach (laid) it up panayam (before) Yahawah. Shamawaal (Samuel) shalach (send) all the im (people / nation) shalach (send), every ayash (husband/individual man) to his bayath (house).

Shaawal (Saul) also halak (move) to his bayath (house) to Gabaih (Gibeah); and there yalak (went) with him the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), whose lab (heart) Alahayam had nagai (touched).
But certain worthless fellows amar (spoke), "How shall this man yashai (salvation) us?" They bazah (despised) him, and bawaa (come) him no manachah (present). But he held his charash (peace).

Then Nachash (Nahash) the Imawanay (Ammonite) ilah (go up / offer) up, and chanah (encamped) Yabash (against) Jabesh Gilead: and all the ayash (husband/individual man) Yabash (of) Jabesh amar (spoke) to Nachash (Nahash), karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with us, and we will ibad (servant) you.

Nachash (Nahash) the Imawanay (Ammonite) amar (spoke) to them, On zaath (this) condition I will karath (cut) it with you, that all your yamayan (right hand) iyan (eye) be naqar (put) out; and I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) it for a charapah (reproach) on all Yasharaal (Israel).

The zaqan (elders) Yabash (of) Jabesh amar (spoke) to him, Give us shabai (seven) yawam (day), that we may shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to all the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yasharaal (Israel); and then, if there is no one to yashai (salvation) us, we will yatzaa (go out / come out) out to you.

Then the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) bawaa (come) to Gabaih (Gibeah) of Shaawal (Saul), and dabar (word / matter) these dabar (word / matter) in the azan (ears) of the im (people / nation): and all the im (people / nation) nashaa (lift) up their qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept).

Behold, Shaawal (Saul) bawaa (come) achar (other) the oxen out of the shadah (field); and Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "What ails the im (people / nation) that they bakah (weep)?" They sapar (book) him the dabar (word / matter) of the im (people / nation) Yabash (of) Jabesh.

The rawach (spirit / wind) of Alahayam tzalach (came) mightily on Shaawal (Saul) when he shamai (hearken / hear) those dabar (word / matter), and his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger) maad (greatly).

He laqach (take / seized) a tzamad (yoke) of oxen, and nathach (cut) them in pieces, and shalach (send) them throughout all the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yasharaal (Israel) by the yad (hand) of malaak (angel / messenger of Yah), amar (spoke), "Whoever doesn't yatzaa (go out / come out) forth achar (other) Shaawal (Saul) and achar (other) Shamawaal (Samuel), so shall it be ishah (make) to his oxen." The pachad (fear / dread) of Yahawah napal (fall / be cast down) on the im (people / nation), and they yatzaa (go out / come out) out as achad (one) ayash (husband/individual man).

He paqad (visit) them in Bazaq (Bezek); and the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) were shalawash (three) maah (hundred) alap (thousand), and the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yahawadah (Judah) shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand).

They amar (spoke) to the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) who bawaa (come), "Thus you shall amar (spoke) the ayash (husband/individual man) Yabash (of) Jabesh Gilead, ‘machar (tomorrow), by the time the shamash (sun) is cham (hot), you shall have thashawaih (deliverance).’" The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) bawaa (come) and nagad (told) the ayash (husband/individual man) Yabash (of) Jabesh; and they were shamach (glad).

Therefore the ayash (husband/individual man) Yabash (of) Jabesh amar (spoke), machar (tomorrow) we will yatzaa (go out / come out) out to you, and you shall ishah (make) with us all that seems tawab (pleasant/functional) to you.

It was so on the next macharath (day), that Shaawal (Saul) shawam (place / establish / appoint) the im (people / nation) in shalawash (three) raash (head); and they bawaa (come) into the thawak (midst) of the machanah (camp) in the baqar (morning) ashamarah (watch), and nakah (struck) the Imawan (Ammonites) until the cham (heat) of the yawam (day): and it happened, that those who shaar (remained) were pawatz (scattered), so that no shanayam (two) of them were shaar (left) yachad (together).
The im (people / nation) amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), Who is he who amar (spoke), ‘Shall Shaawal (Saul) malak (king) over us?’ Nathan (give) those men, that we may put them to mawath (death)!

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), There shall not a ayash (husband/individual man) be put to mawath (death) this yawam (day); for today Yahawah ishah (make) worked thashawaih (deliverance) in Yasharaal (Israel).
Then Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to the im (people / nation), yalak (come), and yalak (let) us go to Galagal (Gilgal), and chadash (renew) the malawakah (kingdom) there.

All the im (people / nation) yalak (went) to Galagal (Gilgal); and there they made Shaawal (Saul) malak (king) panayam (before) Yahawah in Galagal (Gilgal); and there they zabach (offered) zabach (sacrifices) of shalam (peace) offerings panayam (before) Yahawah; and there Shaawal (Saul) and all the im (people / nation) of Yasharaal (Israel) shamach (rejoiced) maad (greatly).

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to all Yasharaal (Israel), Behold, I have shamai (hearken / hear) to your qawal (sound / voice) in all that you amar (spoke) to me, and have malak (king) a malak (king) over you.

Now, behold, the malak (king) halak (move) panayam (before) you; and I am zaqan (old) and shayab (gray-headed); and behold, my ban (son) are with you: and I have halak (move) panayam (before) you from my naiwar (youth) to this yawam (day).

Here I am. Inah (answer / respond) against me before Yahawah, and before his mashayach (anointed one). Whose shawar (ox) have I laqach (take / seized)? Whose donkey have I laqach (take / seized)? Whom have I ishaq (defrauded)? Whom have I ratzatz (oppressed)? Of whose yad (hand) have I taken a kapar (ransom) to ilam (blind) my iyan (eye) therewith? I will shawab (turn back / repent) it to you.
They amar (spoke), You have not ishaq (defrauded) us, nor ratzatz (oppressed) us, neither have you laqach (take / seized) anything of any ayash (husband/individual man) yad (hand).

He amar (spoke) to them, "Yahawah is id (witness) against you, and his mashayach (anointed one) is id (witness) this yawam (day), that you matzaa (have) not found anything in my yad (hand)." They amar (spoke), He is id (witness).

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to the im (people / nation), It is Yahawah who ishah (make) Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron), and that ilah (go up / offer) your ab (father) up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

Now therefore yatzab (stand) still, that I may shapat (plead) with you panayam (before) Yahawah concerning all the tzadaqah (righteousness) acts of Yahawah, which he ishah (make) to you and to your ab (father).

When Yaiqab (Jacob) bawaa (come) come into Matzarayam (Egypt), and your ab (father) zaiq (cried) to Yahawah, then Yahawah shalach (send) Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron), who brought your ab (father) out of Matzarayam (Egypt), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) them to dwell in this maqawam (place).

But they shakach (forgot) Yahawah their Alahayam; and he makar (sold) them into the yad (hand) of Sayasaraa (Sisera), shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop) of Chatzawar (Hazor), and into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab); and they lacham (fought) against them.

They zaiq (cried) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), ‘We have chataa (sinned), because we have forsaken Yahawah, and have ibad (servant) the Bail (Baals) and the Ishatharawath (Ashtaroth): but now natzal (deliver) us out of the yad (hand) of our ayab (enemy), and we will ibad (servant) you.’

Yahawah shalach (send) Yarabail (Jerubbaal), and Badan (Bedan), and Yapathach (Jephthah), and Shamawaal (Samuel), and natzal (delivered) you out of the yad (hand) of your ayab (enemy) on sabayab (surrounding) side; and you lived in safety.

When you raah (see) that Nachash (Nahash) the malak (king) of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) bawaa (come) amar (spoke) you, you said to me, ‘No, but a malak (king) shall malak (king) over us;’ when Yahawah your Alahayam was your malak (king).
Now therefore see the malak (king) whom you have bachar (chosen), and whom you have shaal (asked) for: and behold, Yahawah nathan (give) set a malak (king) over you.

If you will yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah, and ibad (servant) him, and shamai (hearken / hear) to his qawal (sound / voice), and not marah (rebel) against the commandment of Yahawah, then both you and also the malak (king) who malak (king) over you are followers of Yahawah your Alahayam.

But if you will not shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah, but marah (rebel) against the commandment of Yahawah, then will the yad (hand) of Yahawah be against you, as it was against your ab (father).
Now gam (indeed / moreover) yatzab (stand) still and raah (see) this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thing, which Yahawah will ishah (make) before your iyan (eye).

Isn't it chatah (wheat) qatzayar (harvest) today? I will qaraa (called) to Yahawah, that he may nathan (give) qawal (sound / voice) and matar (rain); and you shall yadai (know) and raah (see) that your rai (wickedness) is rab (great), which you ishah (make) done in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, in shaal (asking) for a malak (king).

So Shamawaal (Samuel) qaraa (called) to Yahawah; and Yahawah nathan (give) qawal (sound / voice) and matar (rain) that yawam (day): and all the im (people / nation) maad (greatly) yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah and Shamawaal (Samuel).

All the im (people / nation) amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), palal (pray) for your ibad (servant) to Yahawah your Alahayam, that we not mawath (death); for we have yasap (added) to all our chataah (sin) this rai (evil), to shaal (ask) us a malak (king).

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to the im (people / nation), Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). You ishah (make) indeed done all this rai (evil); yet don't sawar (turn) aside from achar (other) Yahawah, but ibad (servant) Yahawah with all your labab (heart).
Don't sawar (turn) aside to go achar (other) thahaw (formless) things which can't yail (profit) nor natzal (deliver), for they are thahaw (formless).

For Yahawah will not natash (forsake) his im (people / nation) for his gadawal (very great/important/mighty) sham (name) sake, because it has yaal (pleased) Yahawah to ishah (make) you a im (people / nation) to himself.

Moreover as for me, chalayalah (far) be it from me that I should chataa (sin) against Yahawah in chadal (ceasing) to palal (pray) for you: but I will yarah (instruct) you in the tawab (pleasant/functional) and the yashar (right) darak (way).
Only yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah, and ibad (servant) him in amath (truth) with all your labab (heart); for raah (see) how gadal (great) things he has done for you.
But if you shall still raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) wickedly, you shall be sapah (consumed), both you and your malak (king).
Shaawal (Saul) malak (king) a year; and when he had malak (king) shanayam (two) shanah (years) over Yasharaal (Israel),

Shaawal (Saul) bachar (chose) for himself shalawash (three) alap (thousand) men of Yasharaal (Israel), of which two alap (thousand) were with Shaawal (Saul) in Makamas (Michmash) and in the har (mountain) of Bayathaal (Bethel), and one alap (thousand) were with Yawanathan (Jonathan) in Gabaih (Gibeah) of Banayamayan (Benjamin): and the yathar (rest) of the im (people / nation) he shalach (send) every ayash (husband/individual man) to his ahal (tent).

Yawanathan (Jonathan) nakah (struck) the natzayab (garrison) of the Palashathay (Philistines) that was in Gabai (Geba): and the Palashathay (Philistines) shamai (hearken / hear) of it. Shaawal (Saul) thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)) throughout all the aratz (Earth/land), amar (spoke), Let the ibaray (hebrews) shamai (hearken / hear)!

All Yasharaal (Israel) shamai (hearken / hear) that Shaawal (Saul) had nakah (struck) the natzayab (garrison) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and also that Yasharaal (Israel) was had in baash (abomination) with the Palashathay (Philistines). The im (people / nation) were tzaiq (gathered) together achar (other) Shaawal (Saul) to Galagal (Gilgal).

The Palashathay (Philistines) asap (assembled) themselves together to lacham (fight) with Yasharaal (Israel), shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand) rakab (chariots), and shash (six) alap (thousand) horsemen, and im (people / nation) as the chawal (sand) which is on the seashore in rab (multitude): and they ilah (go up / offer) up, and chanah (encamped) in Makamas (Michmash), qadamah (eastward) of Bayathaawan (Beth) Aven.

When the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) raah (see) that they were in a tzar (oppressor / distressor) (for the im (people / nation) were nagash (distressed)), then the im (people / nation) chabaa (hid) themselves in mairah (caves), and in chawach (thickets), and in salai (rocks), and in coverts, and in bawar (pits).

Now some of the ibaray (hebrews) ibar (pass over/through) gone over the Yaradan (Jordan) to the aratz (Earth/land) of Gad (Gad) and Galaid (Gilead); but as for Shaawal (Saul), he was yet in Galagal (Gilgal), and all the im (people / nation) achar (other) him charad (trembling).

He yachal (stayed) shabai (seven) yawam (day), according to the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) set by Shamawaal (Samuel): but Shamawaal (Samuel) didn't bawaa (come) to Galagal (Gilgal); and the im (people / nation) were pawatz (scattered) from him.
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "nagash (bring) here the burnt ilah (offering) to me, and the shalam (peace) offerings." He ilah (go up / offer) the burnt ilah (offering).

It came to kalah (complete / finish) that as soon as he had made an end of ilah (go up / offer) the burnt ilah (go up / offer), behold, Shamawaal (Samuel) bawaa (come); and Shaawal (Saul) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraa (called) him, that he might greet him.

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), "What ishah (make) you done?" Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), Because I raah (see) that the im (people / nation) were napatz (scattered) from me, and that you didn't bawaa (come) within the yawam (day) mawaid (Feast/Holy Day), and that the Palashathay (Philistines) asap (assembled) themselves together at Makamas (Michmash);

Therefore I amar (spoke), ‘Now the Palashathay (Philistines) will yarad (come) down on me to Galagal (Gilgal), and I haven't entreated the favor of Yahawah.’ I apaq (forced) myself therefore, and ilah (go up / offer) the burnt ilah (offering).

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), You have sakal (done) foolishly. You have not shamar (keep/guard) the matzawah (commandment) of Yahawah your Alahayam, which he tzawah (commanded) you; for now Yahawah would have kawan (established) your mamalakah (kingdom) on Yasharaal (Israel) iwalam (forever).

But now your mamalakah (kingdom) shall not qawam (rise up). Yahawah has baqash (sought) for himself a ayash (husband/individual man) after his own labab (heart), and Yahawah has tzawah (appointed) him to be nagayad (prince) over his im (people / nation), because you have not shamar (keep/guard) that which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) you.

Shamawaal (Samuel) qawam (rise up), and ilah (go up / offer) from Galagal (Gilgal) to Gabaih (Gibeah) of Banayamayan (Benjamin). Shaawal (Saul) paqad (visit) the im (people / nation) who were matzaa (present) with him, about shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man).

Shaawal (Saul), and Yawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son), and the im (people / nation) who were matzaa (present) with them, stayed in Gabai (Geba) of Banayamayan (Benjamin): but the Palashathay (Philistines) chanah (encamped) in Makamas (Michmash).

The shachath (spoilers) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the machanah (camp) of the Palashathay (Philistines) in shalawash (three) raash (head): achad (one) raash (head) panah (turned) to the darak (way) that leads to Iparah (Ophrah), to the aratz (Earth/land) of Shawail (Shual);

And another raash (head) panah (turned) the darak (way) to Bayathachawarawan (Beth) Horon; and another raash (head) panah (turned) the darak (way) of the gabawal (border/boundary) that shaqap (looks) down on the gayaa (valley) of Tzabaiyam (Zeboim) toward the madabar (wilderness).

Now there was no charash (smith) matzaa (found) throughout all the aratz (Earth/land) of Yasharaal (Israel); for the Palashathay (Philistines) amar (spoke), Lest the ibaray (hebrews) ishah (make) them charab (sword) or chanayath (spears);
Yasharaal (but) all the Israelites yarad (went) down to the Palashathay (Philistines), to latash (sharpen) every ayash (husband/individual man) his plowshare, macharashah (mattock), axe, and sickle;
Yet they had a patzayarah (file) for the macharashah (mattocks), and for the ath (entirety), and for the shalawash (three), and for the axes, and to natzab (set) the darabawan (goads).

So it came to pass in the yawam (day) of malachamah (battle), that there was neither charab (sword) nor chanayath (spear) matzaa (found) in the yad (hand) of any of the im (people / nation) who were with Shaawal (Saul) and Yawanathan (Jonathan): but with Shaawal (Saul) and with Yawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son) was there matzaa (found).
The matzab (garrison) of the Palashathay (Philistines) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to the maibar (pass) of Makamas (Michmash).

Now it fell on a yawam (day), that Yawanathan (Jonathan) the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to the nair (young) man who nashaa (lift) his armor, "yalak (come), and let us ibar (pass over/through) over to the Palashathay (Philistines)' matzab (garrison), that is on the other ibar (side)." But he didn't nagad (tell) his ab (father).

Shaawal (Saul) stayed in the uttermost part of Gabaih (Gibeah) under the ramawan (pomegranate) tree which is in Magarawan (Migron): and the im (people / nation) who were with him were about shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man);

And Achayah (Ahijah), the ban (son) of Achayatawab (Ahitub), Ayakabawad (Ichabod's) ach (brother/kinsman), the ban (son) of Payanachas (Phinehas), the ban (son) of Ilay (Eli), the kahan (priest) of Yahawah in Shayalah (Shiloh), nashaa (lift) an apawad (ephod). The im (people / nation) didn't yadai (know) that Yawanathan (Jonathan) was halak (move).

Between the passes, by which Yawanathan (Jonathan) baqash (sought) to ibar (pass over/through) over to the Palashathay (Philistines)' matzab (garrison), there was a rocky shan (crag) on the one ibar (side), and a rocky shan (crag) on the other ibar (side): and the sham (name) of the achad (one) was Bawatzatz (Bozez), and the sham (name) of the other Sanah (Seneh).
The achad (one) shan (crag) rose up on the tzapawan (north) in front of Makamas (Michmash), and the other on the nagab (south) in mawal (front) of Gabai (Geba).

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke) to the nair (young) man who nashaa (lift) his armor, yalak (come), and let us ibar (pass over/through) over to the matzab (garrison) of these iral (uncircumcised). It may be that Yahawah will ishah (make) for us; for there is no maitzawar (restraint) on Yahawah to yashai (salvation) by many or by mait (few).
His armor bearer amar (spoke) to him, ishah (make) all that is in your labab (heart). Natah (turn) and, behold, I am with you according to your labab (heart).
Then Yahawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke), Behold, we will ibar (pass over/through) over to the ibar (pass over/through), and we will galah (reveal) ourselves to them.
If they amar (spoke) thus to us, ‘damam (wait) until we nagai (come) to you!’ Then we will imad (stand) still in our place, and will not ilah (go up / offer) up to them.

But if they amar (spoke) this, ‘ilah (go up / offer) up to us!’ Then we will ilah (go up / offer) up; for Yahawah nathan (give) delivered them into our yad (hand). This shall be the awath (sign / mark / miracle) to us.

Shanayam (two) of them galah (revealed) themselves to the matzab (garrison) of the Palashathay (Philistines): and the Palashathay (Philistines) amar (spoke), Behold, the ibaray (hebrews) are yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the chawar (holes) where they had chabaa (hidden) themselves!

The ayash (husband/individual man) of the matzabah (garrison) inah (answer / respond) Yawanathan (Jonathan) and his armor bearer, and amar (spoke), "ilah (go up / offer) up to us, and we yadai (will) show you something!" Yawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke) to his armor bearer, ilah (go up / offer) up achar (other) me; for Yahawah nathan (give) delivered them into the yad (hand) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Yawanathan (Jonathan) ilah (go up / offer) up on his yad (hand) and on his ragal (feet / foot), and his armor bearer achar (other) him: and they napal (fall / be cast down) panayam (before) Yawanathan (Jonathan); and his armor bearer mawath (death) them achar (other) him.

That raashawan (first) makah (slaughter), which Yawanathan (Jonathan) and his armor bearer nakah (made), was about isharayam (twenty) ayash (husband/individual man), within as it were chatzay (half) a furrow's length in an mainah (acre) of shadah (land).

There was a charadah (trembling) in the machanah (camp), in the shadah (field), and among all the im (people / nation); the matzab (garrison), and the shachath (spoilers), they also charad (trembled); and the aratz (Earth/land) ragaz (quaked): so there was an alahayam (Alahayam) great charadah (trembling).
The watchmen of Shaawal (Saul) in Gabaih (Gibeah) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) raah (see); and behold, the hamawan (multitude) mawag (melted) away, and scattered.

Then Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to the im (people / nation) who were with him, "paqad (visit) now, and raah (see) who is missing from us." When they paqad (visit) counted, behold, Yawanathan (Jonathan) and his armor bearer were not there.
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Achayah (Ahijah), "Bring the arawan (ark) of Alahayam here." For the arawan (ark) of Alahayam was with the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) at that yawam (day).

It happened, while Shaawal (Saul) dabar (word / matter) to the kahan (priest), that the hamawan (tumult) that was in the machanah (camp) of the Palashathay (Philistines) yalak (went) on and rab (increased): and Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to the kahan (priest), asap (withdraw) your yad (hand)!

Shaawal (Saul) and all the im (people / nation) who were with him were zaiq (gathered) together, and bawaa (come) to the malachamah (battle): and behold, every ayash (husband/individual man) charab (sword) was against his rai (neigbor/another person): a very gadawal (very great/important/mighty) mahawamah (confusion).

Now the ibaray (hebrews) who were with the Palashathay (Philistines) as athamawal (before), and who ilah (go up / offer) up with them into the machanah (camp), from all around, Yasharaal (even) they also turned to be with the Israelites who were with Shaawal (Saul) and Yawanathan (Jonathan).

Likewise all the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) who had chabaa (hidden) themselves in the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), when they shamai (hearken / hear) that the Palashathay (Philistines) nawas (fled), even they also dabaq (followed) hard achar (other) them in the malachamah (battle).
So Yahawah yashai (salvation) Yasharaal (Israel) that yawam (day): and the malachamah (battle) ibar (pass over/through) over by Bayathaawan (Beth) Aven.

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) were nagash (distressed) that yawam (day); for Shaawal (Saul) had alah (these) the im (people / nation), amar (spoke), "arar (cursed) is the ayash (husband/individual man) who akal (eat) any lacham (food) until it is irab (evening), and I am naqam (avenged) of my ayab (enemy)." So none of the im (people / nation) taim (tasted) lacham (food).
All the aratz (Earth/land) bawaa (come) into the yair (forest); and there was dabash (honey) on the shadah (ground).

When the im (people / nation) bawaa (come) come to the yair (forest), behold, the dabash (honey) halak (move): but no man nashag (put) his yad (hand) to his pah (mouth); for the im (people / nation) yaraa (fear / be afraid) the shabawaih (oath).

But Yawanathan (Jonathan) didn't shamai (hearken / hear) when his ab (father) commanded the im (people / nation) with the shabai (swear / take oath): therefore he shalach (send) forth the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the matah (staff / rod / tribe) who was in his yad (hand), and tabal (dipped) it in the yairah (honeycomb), and shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand) to his pah (mouth); and his iyan (eye) were enlightened.

Then ayash (husband/individual man) of the im (people / nation) inah (answer / respond), and amar (spoke), "Your ab (father) directly commanded the im (people / nation) with an shabai (swear / take oath), amar (spoke), ‘arar (cursed) is the ayash (husband/individual man) who akal (eat) lacham (food) this yawam (day).’" The im (people / nation) were iwap (flying).

Then Yawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke), My ab (father) has ikar (troubled) the aratz (Earth/land). Please raah (see) how my iyan (eye) have been enlightened, because I taim (tasted) a mait (little) of this dabash (honey).

Ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) much more, if perhaps the im (people / nation) had akal (eat) akal (eat) today of the shalal (spoil) of their ayab (enemy) which they matzaa (found)? For now rabah (has) there been no great makah (slaughter) among the Palashathay (Philistines).
They nakah (struck) of the Palashathay (Philistines) that yawam (day) from Makamas (Michmash) to Ayalawan (Aijalon). The im (people / nation) were very iwap (flying);

And the im (people / nation) ishah (make) on the shalal (spoil), and laqach (take / seized) tzaan (sheep), and cattle, and calves, and shachat (killed) them on the aratz (Earth/land); and the im (people / nation) akal (eat) them with the dam (blood).

Then they nagad (told) Shaawal (Saul), amar (spoke), "Behold, the im (people / nation) are chataa (sinning) against Yahawah, in that they akal (eat) meat with the dam (blood)." He amar (spoke), You have dealt bagad (treacherously). Galal (roll) a large aban (stone) to me this yawam (day)!

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "pawatz (disperse) yourselves among the im (people / nation), and amar (spoke) them, ‘nagash (bring) me here every ayash (husband/individual man) his shawar (ox), and every ayash (husband/individual man) his shah (sheep), and shachat (kill) them here, and akal (eat); and don't chataa (sin) against Yahawah in akal (eat) meat with the dam (blood).’" All the im (people / nation) nagash (brought) every ayash (husband/individual man) his shawar (ox) with him that layal (night), and shachat (killed) them there.
Shaawal (Saul) banah (built) an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah. This was the chalal (first) mazabach (altar) that he banah (built) to Yahawah.

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "yarad (let) us go down achar (other) the Palashathay (Philistines) by layal (night), and bazaz (take) spoil among them until the baqar (morning) awar (light), and shaar (let) us not leave a ayash (husband/individual man) of them." They amar (spoke), "ishah (make) whatever seems tawab (pleasant/functional) to you." Then the kahan (priest) amar (spoke), Let us qarab (come close) near here to Alahayam.

Shaawal (Saul) shaal (asked) counsel of Alahayam, "Shall I yarad (go) down achar (other) the Palashathay (Philistines)? Will you nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of Yasharaal (Israel)?" But he didn't inah (answer / respond) him that yawam (day).
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "nagash (draw) near here, all you panah (chiefs) of the im (people / nation); and yadai (know) and raah (see) in which this chataah (sin) has been this yawam (day).

For, as Yahawah chay (life), who yashai (salvation) Yasharaal (Israel), though it is in Yawanathan (Jonathan) my ban (son), he shall mawath (death) mawath (death)." But there was not a man among all the im (people / nation) who inah (answer / respond) him.

Then he amar (spoke) to all Yasharaal (Israel), "You be on achad (one) ibar (side), and I and Yawanathan (Jonathan) my ban (son) will be on the other ibar (side)." The im (people / nation) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), ishah (make) what seems tawab (pleasant/functional) to you.

Therefore Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), "Show the right." Yawanathan (Jonathan) and Shaawal (Saul) were chosen; but the im (people / nation) yatzaa (go out / come out).
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "napal (fall / be cast down) lots between me and Yawanathan (Jonathan) my ban (son)." Yawanathan (Jonathan) was selected.

Then Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Yawanathan (Jonathan), "nagad (tell) me what you ishah (make) done!" Yawanathan (Jonathan) nagad (told) him, and said, I certainly did taim (taste) a mait (little) dabash (honey) with the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the matah (staff / rod / tribe) that was in my yad (hand); and han (behold), I must mawath (death).
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), Alahayam ishah (make) so and more also; for you shall mawath (death) mawath (death), Yawanathan (Jonathan).

The im (people / nation) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "Shall Yawanathan (Jonathan) mawath (death), who ishah (make) worked this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) yashawaih (salvation) in Yasharaal (Israel)? Chalayalah (far) from it! As Yahawah chay (life), there shall not one shairah (hair) of his raash (head) napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land); for he ishah (make) worked with Alahayam this yawam (day)!" So the im (people / nation) padah (rescued) Yawanathan (Jonathan), that he didn't mawath (death).
Then Shaawal (Saul) ilah (go up / offer) up from achar (other) the Palashathay (Philistines); and the Palashathay (Philistines) halak (move) to their own maqawam (place).

Now when Shaawal (Saul) had lakad (taken) the malawakah (kingdom) over Yasharaal (Israel), he lacham (fought) against all his ayab (enemy) on sabayab (surrounding) side, against Mawaab (Moab), and against the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon), and against Adam (Edom), and against the malak (king) of Tzawabaa (Zobah), and against the Palashathay (Philistines): and wherever he panah (turned) himself, he defeated them.

He ishah (make) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), and nakah (struck) the Imalaq (Amalekites), and natzal (delivered) Yasharaal (Israel) out of the yad (hand) of those who despoiled them.

Now the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul) were Yawanathan (Jonathan), and Yashaway (Ishvi), and Malakayashawai (Malchishua); and the sham (name) of his shanayam (two) bath (daughter) were these: the sham (name) of the bakayarah (firstborn) Marab (Merab), and the sham (name) of the younger Mayakal (Michal):

And the sham (name) of Shaawal (Saul's) ashah (wife/individual woman) was Achayanaim (Ahinoam) the bath (daughter) of Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz). The sham (name) of the shar (prince / ruler) of his tzabaa (troop) was Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner), Shaawal (Saul's) dawad (uncle).
Qayash (Kish) was the ab (father) of Shaawal (Saul); and Nar (Ner) the ab (father) of Abanar (Abner) was the ban (son) of Abayaal (Abiel).

There was severe malachamah (war) against the Palashathay (Philistines) all the yawam (day) of Shaawal (Saul): and when Shaawal (Saul) raah (see) any gabawar (mighty) ayash (husband/individual man), or any chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ayash (husband/individual man), he asap (took) him to him.

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), Yahawah shalach (send) me to mashach (anoint) you to be malak (king) over his im (people / nation), over Yasharaal (Israel). Now therefore shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaa (troop), ‘I paqad (visit) marked that which Imalaq (Amalek) ishah (make) to Yasharaal (Israel), how he shawam (place / establish / appoint) himself against him in the darak (way), when he ilah (go up / offer) up out of Matzarayam (Egypt).

Now yalak (go) and nakah (strike) Imalaq (Amalek), and utterly charam (destroy) all that they chamal (have), and don't spare them; but mawath (death) both ayash (husband/individual man) and ashah (wife/individual woman), iwalal (infant) and yanaq (nursing) baby, shawar (ox) and shah (sheep), gamal (camel) and donkey.’
Shaawal (Saul) summoned the im (people / nation), and paqad (visit) them in Talaayam (Telaim), two maah (hundred) alap (thousand) footmen, and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) men of Yahawadah (Judah).
Shaawal (Saul) bawaa (come) to the iyar (city) of Imalaq (Amalek), and rayab (laid) wait in the nachal (stream / river).

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to the Qayanay (Kenites), "yalak (go), sawar (depart), yarad (go) down from thawak (midst) the Imalaq (Amalekites), lest I asap (destroy) you with them; for you showed chasad (grace) to all the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), when they ilah (go up / offer) up out of Matzarayam (Egypt)." So the Qayanay (Kenites) sawar (departed) from thawak (midst) the Imalaqay (Amalekites).
Shaawal (Saul) nakah (struck) the Imalaq (Amalekites), from Chawayalah (Havilah) as you bawaa (come) to Shawar (Shur), that is panayam (before) Matzarayam (Egypt).
He thapash (took) Agag (Agag) the malak (king) Imalaq (of) the Amalekites chay (life), and charam (utterly) destroyed all the im (people / nation) with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword).

But Shaawal (Saul) and the im (people / nation) chamal (spared) Agag (Agag), and the mayatab (best) of the tzaan (sheep), and of the cattle, and of the mashanah (fatlings), and the kar (lambs), and all that was tawab (pleasant/functional), and wouldn't utterly charam (destroy) them: but everything that was namabazah (vile) and masas (refuse), that they charam (destroyed) utterly.
Then the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Shamawaal (Samuel), amar (spoke),

"It grieves me that I have malak (king) up Shaawal (Saul) to be malak (king); for he is shawab (turn back / repent) back from achar (other) me, and has not qawam (rise up) my commandments." Shamawaal (Samuel) was charah (hot with anger); and he zaiq (cried) to Yahawah all layal (night).

Shamawaal (Samuel) shakam (rose) early to qaraa (called) Shaawal (Saul) in the baqar (morning); and it was nagad (told) Shamawaal (Samuel), amar (spoke), Shaawal (Saul) bawaa (come) to Karamal (Carmel), and behold, he natzab (set) up a monument for himself, and sabab (turned), and ibar (pass over/through) on, and yarad (went) down to Galagal (Gilgal).
Shamawaal (Samuel) bawaa (come) to Shaawal (Saul); and Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to him, You are barak (blessed) by Yahawah! I have qawam (rise up) the commandment of Yahawah.
Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), Then what does this qawal (sound / voice) of the tzaan (sheep) in my azan (ears), and the qawal (sound / voice) of the cattle which I shamai (hearken / hear) mean?

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), They bawaa (come) brought them from the Imalaqay (Amalekites); for the im (people / nation) chamal (spared) the mayatab (best) of the tzaan (sheep) and of the cattle, to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah your Alahayam. We charam (have) utterly destroyed the yathar (rest).

Then Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "rapah (stay), and I will nagad (tell) you what Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) to me last layal (night)." He dabar (word / matter) to him, dabar (word / matter) on.

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), Though you were qatan (small/young/least) in your own iyan (eye), weren't you made the raash (head) of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel)? Yahawah mashach (anointed) you malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel);

And Yahawah shalach (send) you on a darak (journey), and amar (spoke), ‘yalak (go), and utterly charam (destroy) the chataa (sinners) the Imalaq (Amalekites), and lacham (fight) against them until they are kalah (complete / finish).’
Why then didn't you shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah, but took the shalal (spoils), and ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah?

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), But I have shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah, and have yalak (gone) the darak (way) which Yahawah shalach (send) me, and bawaa (come) brought Agag (Agag) the malak (king) of Imalaq (Amalek), and charam (have) utterly destroyed the Imalaq (Amalekites).

But the im (people / nation) laqach (take / seized) of the shalal (spoil), tzaan (sheep) and cattle, the raashayath (beginning) of the charam (devoted) things, to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah your Alahayam in Galagal (Gilgal).

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), Has Yahawah as great chapatz (delight) in burnt ilah (offerings) and zabach (sacrifices), as in shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah? Behold, to shamai (hearken / hear) is tawab (pleasant/functional) than zabach (sacrifice), and to shamai (hearken / hear) than the chalab (fat) of ayal (rams).

For rebellion is as the chataah (sin) of qasam (witchcraft), and patzar (stubbornness) is as tharapayam (idolatry) and teraphim. Because you have maas (rejected) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, he has also maas (rejected) you from being malak (king).

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), I have chataa (sinned); for I ibar (pass over/through) transgressed the commandment of Yahawah, and your dabar (word / matter), because I yaraa (fear / be afraid) the im (people / nation), and shamai (hearken / hear) their qawal (sound / voice).
Now therefore, please nashaa (lift) my chataah (sin), and shawab (turn back / repent) again with me, that I may shachah (worship) Yahawah.

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) with you; for you have maas (rejected) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, and Yahawah has maas (rejected) you from being malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel).
As Shamawaal (Samuel) sabab (turned) about to yalak (go) away, Saul grabbed the kanap (skirt) of his maiyal (robe), and it qarai (tore).

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to him, Yahawah has qarai (torn) the mamalakawath (kingdom) of Yasharaal (Israel) from you this yawam (day), and nathan (give) given it to a neighbor of yours who is tawab (pleasant/functional) than you.
Also the natzach (strength) of Yasharaal (Israel) will not shaqar (lie) nor nacham (turn away / repent); for he is not a adam (man), that he should nacham (turn away / repent).

Then he amar (spoke), I have chataa (sinned): yet please honor me now before the zaqan (elders) of my im (people / nation), and before Yasharaal (Israel), and shawab (turn back / repent) back with me, that I may shachah (worship) Yahawah your Alahayam.
So Shamawaal (Samuel) shawab (turn back / repent) back with Shaawal (Saul); and Shaawal (Saul) shachah (worshiped) Yahawah.

Then Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), "nagash (bring) here to me Agag (Agag) the malak (king) Imalaq (of) the Amalekites!" Agag (Agag) yalak (came) to him cheerfully. Agag (Agag) amar (spoke), akan (surely) the bitterness of mawath (death) is sawar (past).

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), "As your charab (sword) has made ashah (wife/individual woman) shakal (childless), so your am (mother) will be shakal (childless) among ashah (wife/individual woman)!" Shamawaal (Samuel) cut Agag (Agag) in shasap (pieces) panayam (before) Yahawah in Galagal (Gilgal).
Then Shamawaal (Samuel) yalak (went) to Ramah (Ramah); and Shaawal (Saul) ilah (go up / offer) up to his bayath (house) to Gabaih (Gibeah) of Shaawal (Saul).

Shamawaal (Samuel) yasap (came) no more to raah (see) Shaawal (Saul) until the yawam (day) of his mawath (death); for Shamawaal (Samuel) abal (mourned) for Shaawal (Saul): and Yahawah grieved that he had made Shaawal (Saul) malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), How long will you abal (mourn) for Shaawal (Saul), since I have maas (rejected) him from being malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel)? Malaa (fill) your qaran (horn) with shaman (oil), and yalak (go). I will shalach (send) you to Yashay (Jesse) the bayathahalachamay (bethlehemite); for I raah (see) provided a malak (king) for myself among his ban (son).

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), "How can I yalak (go)? If Shaawal (Saul) shamai (hearken / hear) it, he will harag (kill) me." Yahawah amar (spoke), laqach (take / seized) a baqar (morning) with you, and amar (spoke), I bawaa (come) come to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah.
Qaraa (called) Yashay (Jesse) to the zabach (sacrifice), and I yadai (will) show you what you shall ishah (make). You shall mashach (anoint) to me him whom I amar (spoke) to you.

Shamawaal (Samuel) ishah (make) that which Yahawah dabar (word / matter), and bawaa (come) to Bayathalacham (Bethlehem). The zaqan (elders) of the iyar (city) came to meet him charad (trembling), and amar (spoke), Do you bawaa (come) peaceably?

He amar (spoke), "Peaceably; I bawaa (come) come to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah. Qadash (set apart/make holy) yourselves, and bawaa (come) with me to the zabach (sacrifice)." He qadash (set apart/make holy) Yashay (Jesse) and his ban (son), and qaraa (called) them to the zabach (sacrifice).
It happened, when they bawaa (come) come, that he raah (see) at Alayaab (Eliab), and amar (spoke), Surely yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) mashayach (anointed one) is before him.

But Yahawah amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), Don't nabat (look) on his maraah (face), or on the gabah (height) of his qawamah (stature); because I have maas (rejected) him: for I see not as adam (man) raah (see); for adam (man) raah (see) at the iyan (eye) appearance, but Yahawah raah (see) at the labab (heart).
Then Yashay (Jesse) qaraa (called) Abayanadab (Abinadab), and ibar (pass over/through) him pass panayam (before) Shamawaal (Samuel). He amar (spoke), Neither has Yahawah bachar (chosen) this one.
Then Yashay (Jesse) made Shamah (Shammah) to ibar (pass over/through) by. He amar (spoke), Neither has Yahawah bachar (chosen) this one.

Yashay (Jesse) made shabai (seven) of his ban (son) to ibar (pass over/through) panayam (before) Shamawaal (Samuel). Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Yashay (Jesse), Yahawah has not bachar (chosen) these.

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Yashay (Jesse), "Are thamam (all) your nair (children) here?" He amar (spoke), "There shaar (remains) yet the youngest, and behold, he is raih (keeping) the tzaan (sheep)." Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Yashay (Jesse), shalach (send) and laqach (take / seized) him; for we will not sabab (sit) down until he bawaa (come) here.

He shalach (send), and bawaa (come) him in. Now he was adamanay (ruddy), and im (withal) of a yapah (beautiful) iyan (eye), and goodly to look on. Yahawah amar (spoke), qawam (rise up), mashach (anoint) him; for this is he.

Then Shamawaal (Samuel) laqach (take / seized) the qaran (horn) of shaman (oil), and mashach (anointed) him in the qarab (among / near) of his ach (brother/kinsman): and the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah tzalach (came) mightily on Dawad (David) from that yawam (day) mail (top/above). So Shamawaal (Samuel) qawam (rise up) up, and yalak (went) to Ramah (Ramah).
Now the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah sawar (departed) from Shaawal (Saul), and an rai (evil) rawach (spirit / wind) from Yahawah baith (troubled) him.
Shaawal (Saul's) ibad (servant) amar (spoke) to him, See now, an rai (evil) rawach (spirit / wind) from Alahayam baith (troubles) you.

Let our Adawan now command your ibad (servant) who are panayam (before) you, to baqash (seek) out a ayash (husband/individual man) who is a skillful nagan (player) on the kanawar (harp). It shall happen, when the rai (evil) rawach (spirit / wind) from Alahayam is on you, that he shall nagan (play) with his yad (hand), and you shall be tawab (pleasant/functional).
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), raah (see) me now a ayash (husband/individual man) who can nagan (play) yatab (well), and bawaa (come) him to me.

Then achad (one) of the young men inah (answer / respond), and amar (spoke), raah (see), I have seen a ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse) the bayathahalachamay (bethlehemite), who is skillful in nagan (playing), a gabawar (mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) of valor, a ayash (husband/individual man) of malachamah (war), bayan (between) in dabar (word / matter), and a thaar (comely) ayash (husband/individual man); and Yahawah is with him.
Therefore Shaawal (Saul) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to Yashay (Jesse), and amar (spoke), shalach (send) me Dawad (David) your ban (son), who is with the tzaan (sheep).

Yashay (Jesse) laqach (take / seized) a donkey loaded with lacham (bread), and a naad (bottle) of yayan (wine), and a young goat, and shalach (send) them by Dawad (David) his ban (son) to Shaawal (Saul).
Dawad (David) bawaa (come) to Shaawal (Saul), and imad (stood) panayam (before) him. He ahab (love) him maad (greatly); and he became his armor bearer.
Shaawal (Saul) shalach (send) to Yashay (Jesse), amar (spoke), Please let Dawad (David) imad (stand) panayam (before) me; for he matzaa (has) found favor in my iyan (eye).

It happened, when the rawach (spirit / wind) from Alahayam was on Shaawal (Saul), that Dawad (David) laqach (take / seized) the kanawar (harp), and nagan (played) with his yad (hand): so Shaawal (Saul) was rawach (spirit / wind), and was tawab (pleasant/functional), and the rai (evil) rawach (spirit / wind) sawar (departed) from him.

Now the Palashathay (Philistines) asap (gathered) together their machanah (armies) to malachamah (battle); and they were asap (gathered) together at Shawakah (Socoh), which belongs to Yahawadah (Judah), and chanah (encamped) between Shawakah (Socoh) and Izaqah (Azekah), in Apasadamayam (Ephesdammim).

Shaawal (Saul) and the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) were asap (gathered) together, and chanah (encamped) in the imaq (valley) of Alah (Elah), and set the malachamah (battle) in irak (array) against the Palashathay (Philistines).

The Palashathay (Philistines) imad (stood) on the har (mountain) on the one side, and Yasharaal (Israel) imad (stood) on the har (mountain) on the other side: and there was a gayaa (valley) between them.

There yatzaa (go out / come out) out a ayash (husband/individual man) out of the machanah (camp) of the Palashathay (Philistines), sham (name) Galayath (Goliath), of gath (gath), whose gabah (height) was shash (six) amah (cubits) and a zarath (span).

He had a kawabai (helmet) of nachashath (brass) on his raash (head), and he was clad with a sharayawan (coat) of qashaqashath (mail); and the mashaqal (weight) of the sharayawan (coat) was chamash (five) alap (thousand) shaqal (shekels) of nachashath (brass).
He had nachashath (brass) shin armor on his ragal (feet / foot), and a javelin of nachashath (brass) between his kathap (shoulders).

The chatz (staff) of his chanayath (spear) was like a arag (weaver's) manawar (beam); and his chanayath (spear's) lahabah (head) weighed shash (six) maah (hundred) shaqal (shekels) of barazal (iron): and his tzanah (shield) bearer halak (move) panayam (before) him.

He imad (stood) and qaraa (called) to the mairakah (armies) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (spoke) to them, Why yatzaa (go out / come out) you come out to set your malachamah (battle) in irak (array)? Am I not a Palashathay (Philistine), and you ibad (servant) to Shaawal (Saul)? Barah (choose) a ayash (husband/individual man) for yourselves, and yarad (let) him come down to me.

If he be yakal (able) to lacham (fight) with me, and nakah (kill) me, then will we be your ibad (servant); but if I yakal (prevail) against him, and nakah (kill) him, then you will be our ibad (servant), and ibad (servant) us.

The Palashathay (Philistine) amar (spoke), I charap (defy) the mairakah (armies) of Yasharaal (Israel) this yawam (day)! Nathan (give) me a ayash (husband/individual man), that we may lacham (fight) yachad (together)!

When Shaawal (Saul) and all Yasharaal (Israel) shamai (hearken / hear) those dabar (word / matter) of the Palashathay (Philistine), they were chathath (dismayed), and maad (greatly) yaraa (fear / be afraid).

Now Dawad (David) was the ban (son) of that Ephrathite of Bayathalacham (Bethlehem) Judah, whose sham (name) was Yashay (Jesse); and he had shamanah (eight) ban (son): and the ayash (husband/individual man) was an old zaqan (man) in the yawam (day) of Shaawal (Saul), stricken among ban (son).

The shalawash (three) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse) had yalak (gone) achar (other) Shaawal (Saul) to the malachamah (battle): and the sham (name) of his shalawash (three) ban (son) who halak (move) to the malachamah (battle) were Alayaab (Eliab) the bakawar (firstborn), and mashanah (next) to him Abayanadab (Abinadab), and the shalayashay (third) Shamah (Shammah).
Dawad (David) was the youngest; and the shalawash (three) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) halak (move) Shaawal (Saul).
Now Dawad (David) halak (move) shawab (turn back / repent) and forth from Shaawal (Saul) to raih (feed) his ab (father) tzaan (sheep) at Bayathalacham (Bethlehem).
The Palashathay (Philistine) nagash (drew) near shakam (morning) and irab (evening), and yatzab (presented) himself arabaiyam (forty) yawam (day).

Yashay (Jesse) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David) his ban (son), Now laqach (take / seized) for your ach (brother/kinsman) an ayapah (ephah) of zah (this/that/these) qalay (parched) grain, and these ishar (ten) loaves, and carry them quickly to the machanah (camp) to your ach (brother/kinsman);

And bawaa (come) these ishar (ten) chalab (milk) to the shar (prince / ruler) of their alap (thousand), and paqad (visit) how your ach (brother/kinsman) are shalawam (peace / safety), and laqach (take / seized) back news.
Now Shaawal (Saul), and they, and all the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel), were in the imaq (valley) of Alah (Elah), lacham (fighting) with the Palashathay (Philistines).

Dawad (David) shakam (rose) up early in the baqar (morning), and natash (left) the tzaan (sheep) with a keeper, and nashaa (lift), and yalak (went), as Yashay (Jesse) had tzawah (commanded) him; and he bawaa (come) to the place of the wagons, as the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) which was yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to the mairakah (fight) rawai (shouted) for the malachamah (battle).
Yasharaal (Israel) and the Palashathay (Philistines) irak (put) the battle in array, mairakah (army) against mairakah (army).
Dawad (David) natash (left) his baggage in the yad (hand) of the keeper of the baggage, and rawatz (ran) to the mairakah (army), and bawaa (come) and shaal (greeted) his ach (brother/kinsman).

As he dabar (word / matter) with them, behold, there ilah (go up / offer) up the ayash (husband/individual man), the Palashathay (Philistine) of gath (gath), Galayath (Goliath) by sham (name), out of the ranks of the Palashathay (Philistines), and dabar (word / matter) according to the same dabar (word / matter): and Dawad (David) shamai (hearken / hear) them.
All the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel), when they raah (see) the ayash (husband/individual man), nawas (fled) from him, and were terrified.

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke), raah (see) you seen this ayash (husband/individual man) who has ilah (go up / offer) up? He has surely ilah (go up / offer) up to charap (defy) Yasharaal (Israel). It shall be, that the ayash (husband/individual man) who nakah (kills) him, the malak (king) will enrich him with gadawal (very great/important/mighty) riches, and will nathan (give) him his bath (daughter), and ishah (make) his ab (father) bayath (house) chapashay (free) in Yasharaal (Israel).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to the ayash (husband/individual man) who imad (stood) by him, amar (spoke), What shall be ishah (make) to the ayash (husband/individual man) who nakah (kills) halaz (this) Palashathay (Philistine), and sawar (takes) away the charapah (reproach) from Yasharaal (Israel)? For who is this iral (uncircumcised) Palashathay (Philistine), that he should charap (defy) the mairakah (armies) of the chay (life) Alahayam?
The im (people / nation) amar (spoke) him in this dabar (word / matter), amar (spoke), So shall it be ishah (make) to the ayash (husband/individual man) who nakah (kills) him.

Alayaab (Eliab) his gadawal (very great/important/mighty) ach (brother/kinsman) shamai (hearken / hear) when he dabar (word / matter) to the gadawal (very great/important/mighty); and Alayaab (Eliab's) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger) against Dawad (David), and he amar (spoke), Why have you yarad (come) down? With whom have you natash (left) those mait (few) tzaan (sheep) in the madabar (wilderness)? I yadai (know) your zadawan (pride), and the rai (naughtiness) of your labab (heart); for you have yarad (come) down that you might raah (see) the malachamah (battle).
Dawad (David) amar (spoke), What ishah (make) I now done? Is there not a dabar (word / matter)?
He sabab (turned) away from him mawal (toward) achar (other), and amar (spoke) like that again; and the im (people / nation) dabar (word / matter) him again the same dabar (word / matter).

When the dabar (word / matter) were shamai (hearken / hear) which Dawad (David) dabar (word / matter), they nagad (rehearsed) them panayam (before) Shaawal (Saul); and he laqach (take / seized) for him.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), Let no adam (man's) lab (heart) napal (fall / be cast down) because of him. Your ibad (servant) will yalak (go) and lacham (fight) with this Palashathay (Philistine).

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), You are not yakal (able) to yalak (go) against this Palashathay (Philistine) to lacham (fight) with him; for you are but a youth, and he a ayash (husband/individual man) of malachamah (war) from his naiwar (youth).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), Your ibad (servant) was raih (keeping) his ab (father) tzaan (sheep); and when a aray (lion) or a dab (bear) bawaa (come), and nashaa (lift) a shah (lamb) out of the idar (flock),

I yatzaa (go out / come out) out achar (other) him, and nakah (struck) him, and natzal (rescued) it out of his pah (mouth). When he qawam (rise up) against me, I chazaq (caught) him by his zaqan (beard), and nakah (struck) him, and mawath (death) him.

Your ibad (servant) nakah (struck) both the aray (lion) and the dab (bear). This iral (uncircumcised) Palashathay (Philistine) shall be as achad (one) of them, since he has charap (defied) the mairakah (armies) of the chay (life) Alahayam.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "Yahawah who natzal (delivered) me out of the paw of the aray (lion), and out of the paw of the dab (bear), he will natzal (deliver) me out of the yad (hand) of this Palashathay (Philistine)." Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), yalak (go); and Yahawah shall be with you.
Shaawal (Saul) dressed Dawad (David) with his clothing. He nathan (give) a qawabai (helmet) of nachashath (brass) on his raash (head), and he clad him with a sharayawan (coat) of mail.

Dawad (David) strapped his charab (sword) on his clothing, and he tried to move; for he had not tested it. Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "I can't yalak (go) with these; for I yakal (have) not tested them." Dawad (David) took them off.

He laqach (take / seized) his maqal (staff) in his yad (hand), and bachar (chose) for himself chamash (five) chalaq (smooth) aban (stone) out of the nachal (stream / river), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them in the raih (shepherd's) kalay (bag) which he had, even in his wallet. His qalai (sling) was in his yad (hand); and he nagash (drew) near to the Palashathay (Philistine).
The Palashathay (Philistine) yalak (came) on and qarab (drew) near to Dawad (David); and the ayash (husband/individual man) who nashaa (lift) the tzanah (shield) went panayam (before) him.

When the Palashathay (Philistine) nabat (looked) about, and raah (see) Dawad (David), he bazah (disdained) him; for he was but a youth, and adamanay (ruddy), and withal of a yapah (fair) maraah (face).
The Palashathay (Philistine) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "Am I a kalab (dog), that you bawaa (come) to me with sticks?" The Palashathay (Philistine) qalal (cursed) Dawad (David) by his Alahayam.
The Palashathay (Philistine) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), yalak (come) to me, and I will nathan (give) your bashar (flesh) to the iwap (flying) of the sky, and to the animals of the shadah (field).

Then Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to the Palashathay (Philistine), You bawaa (come) to me with a charab (sword), and with a chanayath (spear), and with a javelin: but I bawaa (come) to you in the sham (name) of Yahawah of tzabaa (troop), the Alahayam of the tzabaa (troop) of Yasharaal (Israel), whom you have charap (defied).

Today, Yahawah will sagar (deliver) you into my yad (hand). I will nakah (strike) you, and sawar (take) your raash (head) from off you. I will nathan (give) the pagar (dead) bodies of the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines) this yawam (day) to the iwap (flying) of the sky, and to the wild animals of the aratz (Earth/land); that all the aratz (Earth/land) may yadai (know) that there is a Alahayam in Yasharaal (Israel),

And that all this qahal (assembly) may yadai (know) that Yahawah doesn't yashai (salvation) with charab (sword) and chanayath (spear): for the malachamah (battle) is yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)), and he will nathan (give) you into our yad (hand).

It happened, when the Palashathay (Philistine) qawam (rise up), and yalak (came) and qarab (come close) near to qaraa (called) Dawad (David), that Dawad (David) hurried, and rawatz (ran) toward the mairakah (army) to qaraa (called) the Palashathay (Philistine).

Dawad (David) shalach (send) his yad (hand) in his kalay (bag), laqach (take / seized) a aban (stone), and slung it, and nakah (struck) the Palashathay (Philistine) in his matzach (forehead); and the aban (stone) tabai (sank) into his matzach (forehead), and he napal (fall / be cast down) on his panayam (face) to the aratz (Earth/land).

So Dawad (David) chazaq (prevailed) over the Palashathay (Philistine) with a qalai (sling) and with a aban (stone), and nakah (struck) the Palashathay (Philistine), and mawath (death) him; but there was no charab (sword) in the yad (hand) of Dawad (David).

Then Dawad (David) rawatz (ran), and imad (stood) over the Palashathay (Philistine), and laqach (take / seized) his charab (sword), and shalap (drew) it out of its thair (razor), and mawath (death) him, and karath (cut) off his raash (head) therewith. When the Palashathay (Philistines) raah (see) that their gabawar (champion) was mawath (death), they nawas (fled).

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) and of Yahawadah (Judah) qawam (rise up), and rawai (shouted), and radap (pursued) the Palashathay (Philistines), until you bawaa (come) to Gai, and to the shair (gates) of Iqarawan (Ekron). The chalal (wounded) of the Palashathay (Philistines) napal (fall / be cast down) down by the darak (way) to Shairayam (Shaaraim), even to gath (gath), and to Iqarawan (Ekron).
The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) shawab (turn back / repent) from dalaq (chasing) achar (other) the Palashathay (Philistines), and they plundered their machanah (camp).

Dawad (David) laqach (take / seized) the raash (head) of the Palashathay (Philistine), and bawaa (come) it to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); but he shawam (place / establish / appoint) his armor in his ahal (tent).

When Shaawal (Saul) raah (see) Dawad (David) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth amar (spoke) the Palashathay (Philistine), he amar (spoke) to Abanar (Abner), the shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop), "Abanar (Abner), whose ban (son) is this youth?" Abanar (Abner) amar (spoke), As your napash (living being/soul) chay (life), O malak (king), I can't yadai (tell).
The malak (king) amar (spoke), Inquire whose ban (son) the young ilam (man) is!

As Dawad (David) shawab (turn back / repent) from the nakah (slaughter) of the Palashathay (Philistine), Abanar (Abner) laqach (take / seized) him, and bawaa (come) him panayam (before) Shaawal (Saul) with the raash (head) of the Palashathay (Philistine) in his yad (hand).

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to him, "Whose ban (son) are you, you nair (young) man?" Dawad (David) amar (spoke), I am the ban (son) of your ibad (servant) Yashay (Jesse) the bayathahalachamay (bethlehemite).

It happened, when he kalah (complete / finish) made an end of dabar (word / matter) to Shaawal (Saul), that the napash (living being/soul) of Yahawanathan (Jonathan) was qashar (knit) with the napash (living being/soul) of Dawad (David), and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) ahab (love) him as his own napash (living being/soul).
Shaawal (Saul) laqach (take / seized) him that yawam (day), and nathan (give) let him shawab (turn back / repent) no more home to his ab (father) shawab (turn back / repent).
Then Yahawanathan (Jonathan) and Dawad (David) karath (cut) a barayath (covenant), because he ahabah (loved) him as his own napash (living being/soul).

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) pashat (stripped) himself of the maiyal (robe) that was on him, and nathan (give) it to Dawad (David), and his clothing, even to his charab (sword), and to his qashath (bow), and to his sash.

Dawad (David) yatzaa (go out / come out) out wherever Shaawal (Saul) shalach (send) him, and shakal (behaved) himself wisely: and Shaawal (Saul) shawam (place / establish / appoint) him over the ayash (husband/individual man) of malachamah (war), and it was yatab (good) in the iyan (eye) of all the im (people / nation), and also in the iyan (eye) of Shaawal (Saul's) ibad (servant).

It happened as they bawaa (come), when Dawad (David) shawab (turn back / repent) from the nakah (slaughter) of the Palashathay (Philistine), that the ashah (wife/individual woman) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of all the iyar (cities) of Yasharaal (Israel), shayar (singing) and machalah (dancing), to qaraa (called) malak (king) Shaawal (Saul), with tambourines, with shamachah (joy), and with shalayash (instruments) of music.

The ashah (wife/individual woman) inah (answer / respond) one to another as they shachaq (played), and amar (spoke), Shaawal (Saul) has nakah (slain) his alap (thousands), Dawad (David) his ten alap (thousands).

Shaawal (Saul) was very charah (hot with anger), and this dabar (word / matter) displeased him; and he amar (spoke), They nathan (give) ascribed to Dawad (David) rababah (ten) thousands, and to me they nathan (give) ascribed but alap (thousands). What can he have more but the malawakah (kingdom)?
