Shaawal (Saul) eyed Dawad (David) from that yawam (day) and halaah (forward).

It happened on the next macharath (day), that an rai (evil) rawach (spirit / wind) from Alahayam tzalach (came) mightily on Shaawal (Saul), and he nabaa (prophesied) in the thawak (midst) of the bayath (house). Dawad (David) nagan (played) with his yad (hand), as he did yawam (day) by day. Shaawal (Saul) had his chanayath (spear) in his yad (hand);
And Shaawal (Saul) threw the chanayath (spear); for he amar (spoke), "I will pin Dawad (David) even to the qayar (wall)!" Dawad (David) escaped from his panayam (presence) paim (twice).
Shaawal (Saul) was yaraa (fear / be afraid) of Dawad (David), because Yahawah was with him, and was sawar (departed) from Shaawal (Saul).

Therefore Shaawal (Saul) sawar (removed) him from him, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) him his shar (prince / ruler) over a alap (thousand); and he yatzaa (go out / come out) out and bawaa (come) in panayam (before) the im (people / nation).
Dawad (David) shakal (behaved) himself wisely in all his darak (ways); and Yahawah was with him.
When Shaawal (Saul) raah (see) that he shakal (behaved) himself very shakal (wisely), he gawar (stood) in awe of him.
But all Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah) ahab (love) Dawad (David); for he yatzaa (go out / come out) out and bawaa (come) in panayam (before) them.

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "Behold, my gadawal (very great/important/mighty) bath (daughter) Marab (Merab), I will nathan (give) her to you as ashah (wife/individual woman). Only be ban (son) for me, and lacham (fight) yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) malachamah (battles)." For Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), Don't let my yad (hand) be on him, but let the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines) be on him.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), Who am I, and what is my chay (life), or my ab (father) mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) in Yasharaal (Israel), that I should be son-in-law to the malak (king)?

But it happened at the ith (time) when Marab (Merab), Shaawal (Saul's) bath (daughter), should nathan (give) been given to Dawad (David), that she was nathan (give) to Idarayaal (Adriel) the Meholathite as ashah (wife/individual woman).
Mayakal (Michal), Shaawal (Saul's) bath (daughter), ahab (love) Dawad (David); and they nagad (told) Shaawal (Saul), and the thing yashar (pleased) him.

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), I will nathan (give) her to him, that she may be a mawaqash (snare) to him, and that the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines) may be against him. Therefore Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), You shall this yawam (day) be my son-in-law a shanayam (two) time.

Shaawal (Saul) tzawah (commanded) his ibad (servant), dabar (word / matter) with Dawad (David) lat (secretly), and amar (spoke), ‘Behold, the malak (king) chapatz (has) delight in you, and all his ibad (servant) ahab (love) you: now therefore be the malak (king) son-in-law.’

Shaawal (Saul's) ibad (servant) dabar (word / matter) those dabar (word / matter) in the azan (ears) of Dawad (David). Dawad (David) amar (spoke), Does it seems to you a qalal (light) thing to be the malak (king) son-in-law, since I am a rawash (poor) ayash (husband/individual man), and qalah (lightly) esteemed?
The ibad (servant) of Shaawal (Saul) nagad (told) him, amar (spoke), Dawad (David) nagad (spoke) like this.

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "You shall amar (spoke) Dawad (David), ‘The malak (king) chapatz (desires) no mahar (dowry) except one maah (hundred) iralah (foreskins) of the Palashathay (Philistines), to be naqam (avenged) of the malak (king) ayab (enemy).’" Now Shaawal (Saul) chashab (thought) to make Dawad (David) napal (fall / be cast down) by the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines).

When his ibad (servant) nagad (told) Dawad (David) these dabar (word / matter), it dabar (word / matter) Dawad (David) well to be the malak (king) son-in-law. The yawam (day) were not malaa (expired);

And Dawad (David) qawam (rise up) and yalak (went), he and his ayash (husband/individual man), and nakah (killed) of the Palashathay (Philistines) two maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man); and Dawad (David) bawaa (come) their iralah (foreskins), and they malaa (gave) them in full number to the malak (king), that he might be the malak (king) son-in-law. Shaawal (Saul) nathan (give) him Mayakal (Michal) his bath (daughter) as ashah (wife/individual woman).
Shaawal (Saul) raah (see) and yadai (knew) that Yahawah was with Dawad (David); and Mayakal (Michal), Shaawal (Saul's) bath (daughter), ahab (love) him.
Shaawal (Saul) was yet the more yaraa (fear / be afraid) of Dawad (David); and Shaawal (Saul) was Dawad (David's) ayab (enemy) yawam (day).

Then the shar (prince / ruler) of the Palashathay (Philistines) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth: and it happened, as often as they yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, that Dawad (David) shakal (behaved) himself more wisely than all the ibad (servant) of Shaawal (Saul); so that his sham (name) was highly esteemed.

Shaawal (Saul) dabar (word / matter) to Yawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son), and to all his ibad (servant), that they should mawath (death) Dawad (David). But Jonathan, Saul's son, delighted much in David.

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) nagad (told) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), Shaawal (Saul) my ab (father) baqash (seeks) to mawath (death) you. Now therefore, please shamar (keep/guard) care of yourself in the baqar (morning), and live in a sathar (secret / hidden) place, and chabaa (hide) yourself.

I will yatzaa (go out / come out) out and imad (stand) yad (hand) my ab (father) in the shadah (field) where you are, and I will dabar (word / matter) with my ab (father) about you; and if I raah (see) anything, I will nagad (tell) you.

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) dabar (word / matter) tawab (pleasant/functional) of Dawad (David) to Shaawal (Saul) his ab (father), and amar (spoke) to him, Don't let the malak (king) chataa (sin) against his ibad (servant), against Dawad (David); because he has not chataa (sinned) against you, and because his maishah (works) have been very tawab (pleasant/functional) toward you;

For he shawam (place / establish / appoint) his napash (living being/soul) in his kap (hand), and nakah (struck) the Palashathay (Philistine), and Yahawah ishah (make) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thashawaih (deliverance) for all Yasharaal (Israel). You raah (see) it, and shamach (rejoiced). Why then will you chataa (sin) against naqay (innocent) dam (blood), to mawath (death) Dawad (David) chanam (without) a cause?

Shaawal (Saul) shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawanathan (Jonathan): and Shaawal (Saul) shabai (swear / take oath), As Yahawah chay (life), he shall not be put to mawath (death).

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) qaraa (called) Dawad (David), and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) showed him all those things. Yahawanathan (Jonathan) bawaa (come) Dawad (David) to Shaawal (Saul), and he panayam (was) in his presence, as athamawal (before).

There was malachamah (war) again. Dawad (David) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and lacham (fought) with the Palashathay (Philistines), and nakah (killed) them with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) makah (slaughter); and they nawas (fled) panayam (before) him.

An rai (evil) rawach (spirit / wind) from Yahawah was on Shaawal (Saul), as he yashab (inhabit/dwell) in his bayath (house) with his chanayath (spear) in his yad (hand); and Dawad (David) was nagan (playing) with his yad (hand).

Shaawal (Saul) baqash (sought) to pin Dawad (David) even to the qayar (wall) with the chanayath (spear); but he patar (slipped) away out of Shaawal (Saul's) panayam (presence), and he stuck the chanayath (spear) into the qayar (wall). Dawad (David) nawas (fled), and malat (escaped) that layal (night).

Shaawal (Saul) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to Dawad (David's) bayath (house), to shamar (keep/guard) him, and to mawath (death) him in the baqar (morning). Mayakal (Michal), Dawad (David's) ashah (wife/individual woman), nagad (told) him, amar (spoke), If you don't malat (save) your napash (living being/soul) tonight, machar (tomorrow) you will be mawath (death).
So Mayakal (Michal) yarad (let) Dawad (David) down through the chalawan (window). He yalak (went), barach (fled), and malat (escaped).

Mayakal (Michal) laqach (take / seized) the tharapayam (teraphim), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it in the matah (bed), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) a kabayar (pillow) of iz (goats)' hair at its maraashah (head), and kasah (covered) it with the clothes.
When Shaawal (Saul) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to laqach (take / seized) Dawad (David), she amar (spoke), He is chalah (afflict).
Shaawal (Saul) shalach (send) the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to raah (see) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), ilah (go up / offer) him up to me in the matah (bed), that I may mawath (death) him.
When the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) bawaa (come) in, behold, the tharapayam (teraphim) was in the matah (bed), with the kabayar (pillow) of iz (goats)' hair at its head.

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Mayakal (Michal), "Why have you ramah (deceived) me thus, and let my ayab (enemy) go, so that he is malat (escaped)?" Mayakal (Michal) amar (spoke) Shaawal (Saul), He amar (spoke) to me, ‘shalach (send) me go! Why should I mawath (death) you?’

Now Dawad (David) barach (fled), and malat (escaped), and bawaa (come) to Shamawaal (Samuel) to Ramah (Ramah), and nagad (told) him all that Shaawal (Saul) ishah (make) done to him. He and Shamawaal (Samuel) yalak (went) and lived in Nawayath (Naioth).
It was nagad (told) Shaawal (Saul), amar (spoke), Behold, Dawad (David) is at Nawayath (Naioth) in Ramah (Ramah).

Shaawal (Saul) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to laqach (take / seized) Dawad (David): and when they raah (see) the lahaqah (company) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) nabaa (prophesying), and Shamawaal (Samuel) imad (standing) as natzab (head) over them, the rawach (spirit / wind) of Alahayam came on the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Shaawal (Saul), and they also nabaa (prophesied).

When it was nagad (told) Shaawal (Saul), he shalach (send) other malaak (angel / messenger of Yah), and they also nabaa (prophesied). Shaawal (Saul) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) again the shalayashay (third) time, and they also nabaa (prophesied).

Then yalak (went) he also to Ramah (Ramah), and bawaa (come) to the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) bawar (well) that is Shakaw (in) Secu: and he shaal (asked), "ayapah (where) are Shamawaal (Samuel) and Dawad (David)?" One amar (spoke), Behold, they are at Nawayath (Naioth) in Ramah (Ramah).

He yalak (went) there to Nawayath (Naioth) in Ramah (Ramah). Then the rawach (spirit / wind) of Alahayam yalak (came) on him also, and he went on, and nabaa (prophesied), until he bawaa (come) to Nawayath (Naioth) in Ramah (Ramah).

He also pashat (stripped) off his clothes, and he also nabaa (prophesied) panayam (before) Shamawaal (Samuel), and napal (fall / be cast down) down irawam (naked) all that yawam (day) and all that layal (night). Therefore they amar (spoke), Is Shaawal (Saul) also among the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy)?

Dawad (David) barach (fled) from Nawayath (Naioth) in Ramah (Ramah), and bawaa (come) and amar (spoke) panayam (before) Yahawanathan (Jonathan), What ishah (make) I done? What is my iwan (guilt/iniquity)? What is my chataah (sin) panayam (before) your ab (father), that he baqash (seeks) my napash (living being/soul)?

He amar (spoke) to him, chalayalah (far) from it; you shall not mawath (death). Behold, my ab (father) ishah (make) nothing either gadawal (very great/important/mighty) or qatan (small/young/least), but that he galah (discloses) it to me; and why should my ab (father) sathar (hide) this thing from me? It is not so.

Dawad (David) shabai (swear / take oath) moreover, and amar (spoke), Your ab (father) yadai (knows) well that I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye); and he amar (spoke), ‘Don't let Yahawanathan (Jonathan) yadai (know) this, lest he be itzab (grieved):’ but awalam (truly) as Yahawah chay (life), and as your napash (living being/soul) chay (life), there is but a pashai (step) between me and mawath (death).
Then Yahawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), Whatever your napash (living being/soul) amar (spoke), I will even ishah (make) it for you.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Yahawanathan (Jonathan), Behold, machar (tomorrow) is the new chadash (month), and I should not yashab (inhabit/dwell) to akal (eat) with the malak (king); but shalach (send) me go, that I may sathar (hide) myself in the shadah (field) to the shalayashay (third) irab (evening) at evening.

If your ab (father) paqad (visit) me at paqad (visit), then amar (spoke), ‘Dawad (David) shaal (earnestly) shaal (asked) leave of me that he might rawatz (run) to Bayathalacham (Bethlehem) his iyar (city); for it is the yawam (day) zabach (sacrifice) there for all the mashapachah (tribe/clan/family).’

If he amar (spoke), ‘It is tawab (pleasant/functional);’ your ibad (servant) shall have shalawam (peace / safety): but if he be charah (hot with anger), then yadai (know) that rai (evil) is kalah (complete / finish) by him.

Therefore ishah (make) chasad (grace) with your ibad (servant); for you bawaa (come) brought your ibad (servant) into a barayath (covenant) of Yahawah with you: but if there is iwan (guilt/iniquity) in me, mawath (death) me yourself; for why should you bawaa (come) me to your ab (father)?

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke), chalayalah (far) be it from you; for if I should at all yadai (know) that rai (evil) were kalah (complete / finish) by my ab (father) to bawaa (come) on you, then wouldn't I nagad (tell) you that?
Then Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Yahawanathan (Jonathan), Who shall nagad (tell) me if perchance your ab (father) inah (answer / respond) you qashah (rough / hard)?

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "yalak (come), and yatzaa (go out / come out) us go out into the shadah (field)." They shanayam (two) yatzaa (go out / come out) out into the shadah (field).

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), By Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), when I have chaqar (sounded) my ab (father) about this ith (time) machar (tomorrow), or the shalayashay (third) machar (day), behold, if there is tawab (pleasant/functional) toward Dawad (David), shall I not then shalach (send) to you, and disclose it to you?

Yahawah ishah (make) so to Yahawanathan (Jonathan), and more also, should it yatab (please) my ab (father) to do you rai (evil), if I don't galah (disclose) it to you, and shalach (send) you away, that you may halak (move) in shalawam (peace / safety): and Yahawah be with you, as he has been with my ab (father).
You shall not only am (mother) yet I chay (life) show me the loving chasad (grace) of Yahawah, that I not mawath (death);

But also you shall not karath (cut) off your chasad (grace) from my bayath (house) iwalam (forever); no, not when Yahawah has karath (cut) off the ayab (enemy) of Dawad (David) everyone from the surface of the adamah (earth).
So Yahawanathan (Jonathan) karath (cut) a covenant with the bayath (house) of Dawad (David), saying, Yahawah will baqash (require) it at the yad (hand) of Dawad (David's) ayab (enemy).

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) caused Dawad (David) to shabai (swear / take oath) again, for the ahabah (love) that he had to him; for he ahab (love) him as he ahabah (loved) his own napash (living being/soul).
Then Yahawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke) to him, machar (tomorrow) is the new chadash (month): and you will be paqad (visit), because your mawashab (seat) will be paqad (visit).

When you have stayed shalash (three) days, you shall bawaa (come) down maad (quickly), and bawaa (come) to the maqawam (place) where you sathar (hid) yourself when this started, and shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) by the aban (stone) Azal (Ezel).
I will yarah (shoot) shalawash (three) chatzay (arrows) on its tzad (side), as though I shalach (send) at a mataraa (mark).

Behold, I will shalach (send) the nair (boy), amar (spoke), ‘yalak (go), matzaa (find) the chatzay (arrows)!’ If I amar (spoke) the nair (boy), ‘Behold, the chatzay (arrows) are on this side of you. Laqach (take / seized) them;’ then bawaa (come); for there is shalawam (peace / safety) to you and no dabar (word / matter), as Yahawah chay (life).
But if I amar (spoke) this to the boy, ‘Behold, the chatzay (arrows) are halaah (beyond) you;’ then go your yalak (way); for Yahawah has shalach (send) you away.
Dabar (word / matter) the matter which you and I have dabar (word / matter) of, behold, Yahawah is between you and me iwalam (forever).
So Dawad (David) sathar (hid) himself in the shadah (field): and when the new chadash (month) had come, the malak (king) yashab (inhabit/dwell) him down to akal (eat) lacham (food).

The malak (king) yashab (inhabit/dwell) on his mawashab (seat), as at other paim (times), even on the mawashab (seat) by the qayar (wall); and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) qawam (rise up) up, and Abanar (Abner) yashab (inhabit/dwell) by Shaawal (Saul's) tzad (side): but Dawad (David's) maqawam (place) was paqad (visit).

Nevertheless Shaawal (Saul) didn't dabar (word / matter) anything that yawam (day): for he amar (spoke), maqarah (something) has happened to him. He is not tahawar (clean). Surely he is not tahawar (clean).

It happened on the next macharath (day) after the new chadash (month), the shanay (second) day, that Dawad (David's) maqawam (place) was paqad (visit). Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Yahawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son), Why doesn't the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse) bawaa (come) to lacham (eat), neither thamawal (yesterday), nor today?
Yahawanathan (Jonathan) inah (answer / respond) Shaawal (Saul), Dawad (David) shaal (earnestly) shaal (asked) leave of me to go to Bayathalacham (Bethlehem).

He amar (spoke), ‘Please shalach (send) me go, for our mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) has a zabach (sacrifice) in the iyar (city). My ach (brother/kinsman) has tzawah (commanded) me to be there. Now, if I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye), please malat (let) me go away and raah (see) my ach (brother/kinsman).’ Therefore he bawaa (come) not come to the malak (king) shalachan (table).

Then Shaawal (Saul's) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger) against Yahawanathan (Jonathan), and he amar (spoke) to him, You ban (son) of a iwah (perverse) maradawath (rebellious) woman, don't I yadai (know) that you have bachar (chosen) the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse) to your own bashath (shame), and to the bashath (shame) of your am (mother) irawah (nakedness)?

For as yawam (day) as the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse) chayay (life) on the adamah (earth), you shall not be kawan (established), nor your malakawath (kingdom). Therefore now shalach (send) and laqach (take / seized) him to me, for he shall ban (son) die!
Yahawanathan (Jonathan) inah (answer / respond) Shaawal (Saul) his ab (father), and amar (spoke) to him, Why should he be put to mawath (death)? What ishah (make) he done?

Shaawal (Saul) tawal (cast) his chanayath (spear) at him to nakah (strike) him. By this Yahawanathan (Jonathan) yadai (knew) that his ab (father) kalah (complete / finish) determined to put Dawad (David) to mawath (death).

So Yahawanathan (Jonathan) qawam (rise up) from the shalachan (table) in charay (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and akal (eat) no lacham (food) the shanay (second) yawam (day) of the chadash (month); for he was itzab (grieved) for Dawad (David), because his ab (father) had kalam (done) him shame.

It happened in the baqar (morning), that Yahawanathan (Jonathan) yatzaa (go out / come out) out into the shadah (field) at the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) appointed with Dawad (David), and a qatan (small/young/least) nair (boy) with him.

He amar (spoke) to his nair (boy), "rawatz (run), matzaa (find) now the chatzay (arrows) which I yarah (shoot)." As the nair (boy) rawatz (ran), he yarah (shot) an chatzay (arrow) ibar (pass over/through) him.

When the nair (boy) bawaa (come) come to the maqawam (place) of the chatzay (arrow) which Yahawanathan (Jonathan) had yarah (shot), Yahawanathan (Jonathan) qaraa (called) achar (other) the nair (boy), and amar (spoke), Isn't the chatzay (arrow) halaah (beyond) you?

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) qaraa (called) achar (other) the nair (boy), "Go fast! Hurry! Don't delay!" Yahawanathan (Jonathan's) nair (boy) laqat (gathered) up the chatzay (arrows), and bawaa (come) to his adawan (master / lord).
But the nair (boy) didn't yadai (know) anything. Only Yahawanathan (Jonathan) and Dawad (David) yadai (knew) the dabar (word / matter).
Yahawanathan (Jonathan) nathan (give) his kalay (weapons) to his nair (boy), and amar (spoke) to him, yalak (go), bawaa (come) them to the iyar (city).

As soon as the nair (boy) was bawaa (come), Dawad (David) qawam (rise up) out of the nagab (south), and napal (fall / be cast down) on his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land), and shachah (bowed) himself shalawash (three) paim (times). They nashaq (kissed) ayash (husband/individual man) rai (neigbor/another person), and bakah (wept) ayash (husband/individual man) with rai (neigbor/another person), and Dawad (David) bakah (wept) the most.

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "halak (move) in shalawam (peace / safety), because we have shanayam (two) shabai (swear / take oath) in the sham (name) of Yahawah, amar (spoke), ‘Yahawah shall be between me and you, and between my zarai (seed) and your zarai (seed), iwalam (forever).’" He arose and departed; and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) halak (move) into the city.
Then bawaa (come) David to Nob to Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech came to meet David trembling, and said to him, Why are you alone, and no man with you?

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Achayamalak (Ahimelech) the kahan (priest), The king has amar (spoke) me a business, and has amar (spoke) to me, ‘Let no ayash (husband/individual man) know anything of the business about which I bawaa (come) you, and what I have amar (spoke) you; and I have amar (spoke) the young men to such and such a place.’
Now therefore what is under your hand? Amar (spoke) me five loaves of bread in my hand, or whatever there is present.
The priest answered David, and said, There is no common lacham (bread) under my yad (hand), but there is holy lacham (bread); if only the young men have kept themselves from women.

Dawad (David) inah (answer / respond) the kahan (priest), and inah (answer / respond) to him, Truly, ashah (wife/individual woman) have been shamar (keep/guard) from us about these three qadash (set apart/make holy). When I came out, the vessels of the nair (young) men were qadash (set apart/make holy), though it was but a chal (common) journey. How much more then today shall their vessels be qadash (set apart/make holy)?

So the kahan (priest) inah (answer / respond) him qadash (set apart/make holy) chal (bread); for there was no bread there but the show chal (bread), that was yatzaa (go out / come out) from thamawal (before) Yahawah, to yatzaa (go out / come out) hot chal (bread) in the yawam (day) when it was yatzaa (go out / come out) away.

Now a certain man of the servants of Yahawah (Saul) was there that yawam (day), detained panayam (before) Yahawah; and his shawam (place / establish / appoint) was Doeg the Edomite, the best of the herdsmen who belonged to Yahawah (Saul).
Yahawah (David) said to Ahimelech, Isn't there here under your hand spear or sword? For I have neither brought my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king's business yawam (day) haste.

The priest amar (spoke), "The charab (sword) of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the valley of Elah, behold, it is here wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you will laqach (take / seized) that, laqach (take / seized) it; for there is no other except that here." Dawad (David) amar (spoke), There is none like that. Amar (spoke) it to me.
Dawad (David) arose, and fled that day for fear of Saul, and nakah (went) to Achish the king of Gath.

The servants of Akayash (Achish) said to him, Isn't this Dawad (David) the malak (king) of the land? Didn't they sing one to another about him in dances, saying, ‘Shaawal (Saul) has slain his thousands, Dawad (David) his ten thousands?’
Dawad (David) laid up these words in his heart, and was very afraid of Akayash (Achish) the malak (king) of Gath.
He shawam (place / establish / appoint) his behavior panayam (before) them, and pretended to be mad in their hands, and scrabbled on the doors of the gate, and let his spittle fall down on his beard.
Then Achish said to his servants, iyan (eye), you see the man is halal (praise). Why then il (over) you brought him to me?
Do I lack madmen, that you bawaa (come) brought this fellow to shagai (play) the madman in my presence? Shall this fellow bawaa (come) into my house?

Dawad (David) therefore departed there, and malat (escaped) to the mairah (cave) of Idalam (Adullam). When his ach (brother/kinsman) and all his ab (father) bayath (house) shamai (hearken / hear) it, they yarad (went) down there to him.

Everyone who was in matzawaq (distress), and everyone who was in nashaa (lift), and everyone who was mar (discontented), qabatz (gathered) themselves to him; and he became shar (prince / ruler) over them: and there were with him about arabai (four) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man).

Dawad (David) yalak (went) there to Matzapah (Mizpeh) of Mawaab (Moab), and he amar (spoke) to the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab), Please let my ab (father) and my am (mother) yatzaa (go out / come out) out with you, until I yadai (know) what Alahayam will ishah (make) for me.
He nachah (brought) them panayam (before) the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab); and they lived with him all the yawam (day) that Dawad (David) was in the stronghold.

The nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) Gad (Gad) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "Don't stay in the stronghold. Depart, and bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land) of Yahawadah (Judah)." Then Dawad (David) departed, and bawaa (come) into the yair (forest) of Charath (Hereth).

Shaawal (Saul) shamai (hearken / hear) that Dawad (David) was yadai (discovered), and the yadai (men) who were with him. Now Shaawal (Saul) was sitting in Gabaih (Gibeah), under the tamarisk ashal (tree) in Ramah, with his chanayath (spear) in his yad (hand), and all his ibad (servant) were natzab (standing) about him.

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant) who natzab (stood) about him, shamai (hearken / hear) now, you Benjamites! Will the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse) nathan (give) everyone of you shadah (fields) and karam (vineyards), will he shawam (place / establish / appoint) you all shar (prince / ruler) of alap (thousands) and shar (prince / ruler) of maah (hundred),

That all of you have qashar (conspired) against me, and there is none who galah (discloses) to me when my ban (son) karath (cut) a treaty with the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse), and there is none of you who is chalah (afflict) for me, or galah (discloses) to me that my ban (son) has qawam (rise up) up my ibad (servant) against me, to lie in arab (wait), as at this yawam (day)?

Then Daag (Doeg) the Adamay (Edomite), who natzab (stood) by the ibad (servant) of Shaawal (Saul), amar (spoke) and amar (spoke), I raah (see) the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse) bawaa (come) to Nab (Nob), to Achayamalak (Ahimelech) the ban (son) of Achayatawab (Ahitub).
He inquired of Yahawah for him, nathan (give) him food, and nathan (give) him the charab (sword) of Galayath (Goliath) the Palashathay (Philistine).

Then the malak (king) shalach (send) to qaraa (called) Achayamalak (Ahimelech) the kahan (priest), the ban (son) of Achayatawab (Ahitub), and all his ab (father) bayath (house), the kahan (priest) who were in Nab (Nob): and they bawaa (come) all of them to the malak (king).
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "shamai (hearken / hear) now, you ban (son) of Achayatawab (Ahitub)." He amar (spoke), Here I am, my Adawan.

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to him, Why have you qashar (conspired) against me, you and the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse), in that you nathan (give) given him lacham (bread), and a charab (sword), and have inquired of Alahayam for him, that he should qawam (rise up) against me, to lie in arab (wait), as at this yawam (day)?

Then Achayamalak (Ahimelech) inah (answer / respond) the malak (king), and amar (spoke), Who among all your ibad (servant) is so aman (believe / have faith) as Dawad (David), who is the malak (king) son-in-law, and is sawar (taken) into your council, and is honorable in your bayath (house)?

Have I today chalal (begun) to inquire of Alahayam for him? Be it chalayalah (far) from me! Don't let the malak (king) shawam (place / establish / appoint) anything to his ibad (servant), nor to all the bayath (house) of my ab (father); for your ibad (servant) yadai (knows) nothing of all this, qatan (small/young/least) or more.
The malak (king) amar (spoke), You shall mawath (death) mawath (death), Achayamalak (Ahimelech), you, and all your ab (father) bayath (house).

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to the rawatz (guard) who natzab (stood) about him, "sabab (turn), and mawath (death) the kahan (priest) of Yahawah; because their yad (hand) also is with Dawad (David), and because they yadai (knew) that he barach (fled), and didn't galah (disclose) it to me." But the ibad (servant) of the malak (king) wouldn't shalach (send) forth their yad (hand) to pagai (fall) on the kahan (priest) of Yahawah.

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Daag (Doeg), "sabab (turn) and attack the kahan (priest)!" Daag (Doeg) the Adamay (Edomite) sabab (turned), and he attacked the kahan (priest), and he mawath (death) on that yawam (day) shamanayam (eighty) - chamash (five) ayash (husband/individual man) who nashaa (lift) a bad (linen) apawad (ephod).

He nakah (struck) Nab (Nob), the iyar (city) of the kahan (priest), with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), both ayash (husband/individual man) and ashah (wife/individual woman), iwalal (children) and yanaq (nursing) babies, and cattle and donkeys and shah (sheep), with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword).
Achad (one) of the ban (son) of Achayamalak (Ahimelech), the ban (son) of Achayatawab (Ahitub), sham (name) Abayathar (Abiathar), malat (escaped), and barach (fled) achar (other) Dawad (David).
Abayathar (Abiathar) nagad (told) Dawad (David) that Shaawal (Saul) had harag (slain) yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) kahan (priest).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Abayathar (Abiathar), I yadai (knew) on that yawam (day), when Daag (Doeg) the Adamay (Edomite) was there, that he would nagad (surely) nagad (tell) Shaawal (Saul). I am responsible for the death of all the napash (living being/soul) of your ab (father) bayath (house).

Stay with me, don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid); for he who baqash (seeks) my napash (living being/soul) baqash (seeks) your napash (living being/soul). For with me you shall be in mashamarath (duty / watch).
Dawad (David) was nagad (told), Behold, the Palashathay (Philistines) are lacham (fighting) against Qaiyalah (Keilah), and are shasah (robbing) the garan (threshing) floors.

Therefore Dawad (David) inquired of Yahawah, amar (spoke), "Shall I yalak (go) and nakah (strike) these Palashathay (Philistines)?" Yahawah amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), yalak (go) nakah (strike) the Palashathay (Philistines), and yashai (salvation) Qaiyalah (Keilah).

Dawad (David's) ayash (husband/individual man) amar (spoke) to him, Behold, we are yaraa (fear / be afraid) here in Yahawadah (Judah): how much more then if we yalak (go) to Qaiyalah (Keilah) against the mairakah (armies) of the Palashathay (Philistines)?

Then Dawad (David) inquired of Yahawah yet again. Yahawah inah (answer / respond) him, and inah (answer / respond), qawam (rise up), yarad (go) down to Qaiyalah (Keilah); for I will nathan (give) the Palashathay (Philistines) into your yad (hand).

Dawad (David) and his ayash (husband/individual man) yalak (went) to Qaiyalah (Keilah), and lacham (fought) with the Palashathay (Philistines), and nahag (brought) away their livestock, and nakah (killed) them with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) makah (slaughter). So Dawad (David) yashai (salvation) the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Qaiyalah (Keilah).

It happened, when Abayathar (Abiathar) the ban (son) of Achayamalak (Ahimelech) barach (fled) to Dawad (David) to Qaiyalah (Keilah), that he yarad (came) down with an apawad (ephod) in his yad (hand).

It was nagad (told) Shaawal (Saul) that Dawad (David) bawaa (come) come to Qaiyalah (Keilah). Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), Alahayam has nakar (delivered) him into my yad (hand); for he is sagar (shut) in, by bawaa (come) into a iyar (town) that has dalath (gates) and barayach (bars).
Shaawal (Saul) summoned all the im (people / nation) to malachamah (war), to yarad (go) down to Qaiyalah (Keilah), to tzawar (besiege) Dawad (David) and his im (people / nation).
Dawad (David) yadai (knew) that Shaawal (Saul) was charash (devising) rai (mischief) amar (spoke) him; and he said to Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahan (priest), Bring the apawad (ephod) here.

Then Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "O Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), your ibad (servant) has shamai (hearken / hear) shamai (hearken / hear) that Shaawal (Saul) baqash (seeks) to bawaa (come) to Qaiyalah (Keilah), to shachath (destroy) the iyar (city) for my sake.

Will the bail (men) of Qaiyalah (Keilah) sagar (deliver) me up into his yad (hand)? Will Shaawal (Saul) yarad (come) down, as your ibad (servant) has shamai (hearken / hear)? Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), I beg you, nagad (tell) your ibad (servant)." Yahawah amar (spoke), He will yarad (come) down.

Then Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "Will the bail (men) of Qaiyalah (Keilah) sagar (deliver) me and my bail (men) into the yad (hand) of Shaawal (Saul)?" Yahawah amar (spoke), They will sagar (deliver) you up.

Then Dawad (David) and his ayash (husband/individual man), who were about shash (six) maah (hundred), qawam (rise up) and departed out of Qaiyalah (Keilah), and halak (move) wherever they could halak (move). It was nagad (told) Shaawal (Saul) that Dawad (David) was malat (escaped) from Qaiyalah (Keilah); and he gave up yatzaa (go out / come out) there.

Dawad (David) stayed in the madabar (wilderness) in the strongholds, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the har (mountain) country in the madabar (wilderness) of Zayap (Ziph). Shaawal (Saul) baqash (sought) him every yawam (day), but Alahayam didn't nathan (give) him into his yad (hand).

Dawad (David) raah (see) that Shaawal (Saul) yatzaa (go out / come out) come out to baqash (seek) his napash (living being/soul). Dawad (David) was in the madabar (wilderness) of Zayap (Ziph) in the Charash (wood).
Yahawanathan (Jonathan), Shaawal (Saul's) ban (son), qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) to Dawad (David) into the Charash (woods), and chazaq (strengthened) his yad (hand) in Alahayam.

He amar (spoke) to him, Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid); for the yad (hand) of Shaawal (Saul) my ab (father) shall not matzaa (find) you; and you shall be malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel), and I shall be mashanah (next) to you; and that also Shaawal (Saul) my ab (father) yadai (knows).
They shanayam (two) karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) panayam (before) Yahawah: and Dawad (David) stayed in the Charash (woods), and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) halak (move) to his bayath (house).

Then the zayapay (ziphites) ilah (go up / offer) up to Shaawal (Saul) to Gabaih (Gibeah), amar (spoke), Doesn't Dawad (David) sathar (hide) himself with us in the strongholds in the Charash (wood), in the gabaih (hill) of Chakayalah (Hachilah), which is on the yamayan (right hand) of the yashayamawan (desert)?

Now therefore, O malak (king), yarad (come) down, according to all the awah (desire) of your napash (living being/soul) to yarad (come) down; and our part shall be to sagar (deliver) him up into the malak (king) yad (hand).
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), You are barak (blessed) by Yahawah; for you chamal (have) had compassion on me.

Please yalak (go) kawan (make) yet more yadai (sure), and know and raah (see) his maqawam (place) where his ragal (feet / foot) is, and who raah (see) seen him there; for it is amar (spoke) me that he iram (deals) very subtly.

Raah (see) therefore, and take yadai (knowledge) of all the lurking machabaa (places) where he chabaa (hides) himself, and shawab (turn back / repent) again to me with kawan (certainty), and I will halak (move) with you: and it yash (shall) happen, if he is in the aratz (Earth/land), that I will chapash (search) him out among all the alap (thousands) of Yahawadah (Judah).

They qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) to Zayap (Ziph) panayam (before) Shaawal (Saul): but Dawad (David) and his ayash (husband/individual man) were in the madabar (wilderness) of maiwan (maon), in the irabah (arabah) on the yamayan (right hand) of the yashayamawan (desert).

Shaawal (Saul) and his ayash (husband/individual man) yalak (went) to baqash (seek) him. When Dawad (David) was nagad (told), he yarad (went) down to the salai (rock), and stayed in the madabar (wilderness) of maiwan (maon). When Shaawal (Saul) shamai (hearken / hear) that, he radap (pursued) Dawad (David) in the madabar (wilderness) of maiwan (maon).

Shaawal (Saul) yalak (went) on this tzad (side) of the har (mountain), and Dawad (David) and his zah (this/that/these) on that tzad (side) of the har (mountain): and Dawad (David) made chapaz (haste) to yalak (get) away for panayam (fear) of Shaawal (Saul); for Shaawal (Saul) and his zah (this/that/these) surrounded Dawad (David) and his zah (this/that/these) to thapash (take) them.
But a malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) bawaa (come) to Shaawal (Saul), amar (spoke), Hurry and yalak (come); for the Palashathay (Philistines) have pashat (made) a raid on the aratz (Earth/land)!

So Shaawal (Saul) shawab (turn back / repent) from radap (pursuing) achar (other) Dawad (David), and yalak (went) il (over) the Palashathay (Philistines): therefore they qaraa (called) that maqawam (place) Salaihamachalaqawath (Sela) Hammahlekoth.
Dawad (David) ilah (go up / offer) up from there, and lived in the strongholds of Iyanagaday (En) Gedi.
It happened, when Saul was yashab (inhabit/dwell) from following the Philistines, that it was told him, saying, Behold, Dawad (David) is in the wilderness of Iyanagaday (En) Gedi.
Then Shaawal (Saul) shawab (turn back / repent) three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and shawab (turn back / repent) to seek Dawad (David) and his men on the rocks of the wild goats.

He yalak (came) to the sheep pens by the yalak (way), where there was a cave; and Shaawal (Saul) yalak (went) in to relieve himself. Now Dawad (David) and his ayash (husband/individual man) were abiding in the innermost parts of the cave.

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Dawad (David) said to him, "Behold, the day of which Yahawah said to you, ‘Behold, I will deliver your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as it shall seem ayash (husband/individual man) to you.’" Then Dawad (David) arose, and cut off the skirt of Shaawal (Saul's) robe secretly.
It happened afterward, that Dawad (David's) heart nathan (give) him, because he had karath (cut) off Shaawal (Saul's) kanap (skirt).

He said to his men, Yahawah forbid that I should hayah (came to pass) this thing to my Adawan, dawad (Dawad/(David) - Patriarch) anointed, to put forth my hand against him, since he is dawad (Dawad/(David) - Patriarch) anointed.

So Yahawah (David) checked his ayash (husband/individual man) with these dabar (word / matter), and didn't allow them to rise against Yahawah (Saul). Yahawah (Saul) rose up out of the cave, and ishah (make) on his way.

Dawad (David) also qawam (rise up) afterward, and yalak (went) out of the mairah (cave), and nathan (give) al (after) Shaawal (Saul), dabar (word / matter), "My Adawan the king!" When Shaawal (Saul) looked behind him, Dawad (David) bowed with his face to the earth, and showed respect.
Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), Why do you listen to men's words, amar (spoke), ‘Behold, Dawad (David) seeks your hurt?’

Behold, this day your eyes have seen how that Yahawah had delivered you today into my hand in the cave. Some urged me to kill you; but I spared you; and I amar (spoke), I will not put forth my hand against my Adawan; for he is Yahweh's anointed.

Moreover, my father, raah (see), yes, raah (see) the skirt of your robe in my yad (hand); for in that I cut off the skirt of your robe, and didn't harag (kill) you, know and raah (see) that there is neither evil nor disobedience in my yad (hand), and I have not sinned against you, though you hunt for my yawam (day) to raah (see) it.
May Yahawah judge between me and you, and may Yahawah avenge me of you; but my yad (hand) shall not be on you.
As the proverb of the ancients says, ‘Out of the wicked hayah (came to pass) forth wickedness;’ but my yad (hand) shall not be on you.
Against whom has the king of Israel yatzaa (go out / come out) out? Whom do you pursue? A dead dog? A flea?
May Yahawah therefore be judge, and give sentence between me and you, and see, and plead my yatzaa (go out / come out), and deliver me out of your hand.

It came to pass, when Yahawah (David) hayah (came to pass) made an end of speaking these words to Yahawah (Saul), that Yahawah (Saul) said, "Is this your voice, my son Yahawah (David)?" Yahawah (Saul) lifted up his voice, and wept.
He amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), You are more righteous than I; for you have hayah (came to pass) good to me, whereas I have hayah (came to pass) evil to you.
You have amar (spoke) this day how you have dealt tawab (pleasant/functional) with me, because when Yahawah had delivered me up into your hand, you didn't kill me.
For if a ishah (make) finds his enemy, will he let him go away unharmed? Therefore may Yahawah reward you tawab (pleasant/functional) for that which you ishah (make) done to me this yawam (day).
Now, behold, I know that you shall kay (surely) be king, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be established in your matzaa (hand).
Yad (hand) now therefore to me by Yahawah, that you will not cut off my seed after me, and that you will not destroy my name out of my father's house.
Yahawah (David) shabai (swear / take oath) to Yahawah (Saul). Yahawah (Saul) went bayath (house); but Yahawah (David) and his men went up to the stronghold.

Shamawaal (Samuel) mawath (death); and all Yasharaal (Israel) qabatz (gathered) themselves together, and sapad (lamented) him, and qabar (bury) him in his bayath (house) at Ramah (Ramah). Dawad (David) qawam (rise up), and yarad (went) down to the madabar (wilderness) of Paaran (Paran).

There was a ayash (husband/individual man) in maiwan (maon), whose maishah (possessions) were in Karamal (Carmel); and the ayash (husband/individual man) was very gadawal (very great/important/mighty), and he had shalawash (three) alap (thousand) tzaan (sheep), and a alap (thousand) iz (goats): and he was gazaz (shearing) his tzaan (sheep) in Karamal (Carmel).

Now the sham (name) of the ayash (husband/individual man) was Nabal (Nabal); and the sham (name) of his ashah (wife/individual woman) Abayagayal (Abigail); and the ashah (wife/individual woman) was of tawab (pleasant/functional) shakal (understanding), and of a yapah (beautiful) thaar (face): but the ayash (husband/individual man) was qashah (rough / hard) and rai (evil) in his mailal (doings); and he was of the house of Caleb.
Dawad (David) shamai (hearken / hear) in the madabar (wilderness) that Nabal (Nabal) was gazaz (shearing) his tzaan (sheep).

Dawad (David) shalach (send) ishar (ten) nair (young) men, and Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to the nair (young) men, ilah (go up / offer) up to Karamal (Carmel), and bawaa (come) to Nabal (Nabal), and shaal (greet) him in my sham (name).
You shall amar (spoke) him, ‘Long life to you! Shalawam (peace / safety) be to you, and shalawam (peace / safety) be to your bayath (house), and shalawam (peace / safety) be to all that you have.

Now I have shamai (hearken / hear) that you have gazaz (shearers). Your raih (shepherds) have now been with us, and we didn't kalam (hurt) them, neither was there anything paqad (visit) from them, all the yawam (day) they were in Karamal (Carmel).

Shaal (ask) your nair (young) men, and they will nagad (tell) you. Therefore, let the nair (young) men matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (eye); for we bawaa (come) in a tawab (pleasant/functional) yawam (day). Please nathan (give) whatever matzaa (comes) to your yad (hand), to your ibad (servant), and to your ban (son) Dawad (David).’
When Dawad (David's) nair (young) men bawaa (come), they dabar (word / matter) to Nabal (Nabal) according to all those dabar (word / matter) in the sham (name) of Dawad (David), and nawach (ceased).

Nabal (Nabal) inah (answer / respond) Dawad (David's) ibad (servant), and inah (answer / respond), Who is Dawad (David)? Who is the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse)? There are many ibad (servant) who paratz (break) away from their adawan (master / lord) these yawam (day).

Shall I then laqach (take / seized) my lacham (bread), and my mayam (Waters), and my meat that I have tabach (killed) for my gazaz (shearers), and nathan (give) it to ayash (husband/individual man) who I don't yadai (know) where they come from?
So Dawad (David's) nair (young) men hapak (turned) on their darak (way), and shawab (turn back / repent) back, and bawaa (come) and nagad (told) him according to all these dabar (word / matter).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to his ayash (husband/individual man), "Every ayash (husband/individual man) chagar (put) on his charab (sword)!" Every ayash (husband/individual man) chagar (put) on his charab (sword). Dawad (David) also chagar (put) on his charab (sword). About arabai (four) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man) achar (other) Dawad (David); and two maah (hundred) stayed by the baggage.

But achad (one) of the nair (young) men nagad (told) Abayagayal (Abigail), Nabal (Nabal's) ashah (wife/individual woman), amar (spoke), Behold, Dawad (David) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) out of the madabar (wilderness) to Greet our adawan (master / lord); and he iyat (railed) at them.

But the ayash (husband/individual man) were very tawab (pleasant/functional) to us, and we were not kalam (hurt), neither paqad (visit) we anything, as yawam (day) as we halak (move) with them, when we were in the shadah (fields).
They were a chawamah (wall) to us both by layal (night) and by yawamam (by day), all the yawam (day) we were with them raih (keeping) the tzaan (sheep).

Now therefore yadai (know) and raah (see) what you will ishah (make); for rai (evil) is kalah (complete / finish) against our adawan (master / lord), and against all his bayath (house); for he is such a worthless fellow that one can't dabar (word / matter) to him.

Then Abayagayal (Abigail) hurried and laqach (take / seized) two maah (hundred) loaves of bread, shanayam (two) nabal (bottles) of yayan (wine), chamash (five) tzaan (sheep) ready ishah (make), chamash (five) saah (measures) of qalay (parched) grain, one maah (hundred) clusters of tzamawaq (raisins), and two maah (hundred) dabalah (fig cake) of figs, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them on donkeys.

She amar (spoke) to her nair (young) men, "ibar (pass over/through) on panayam (before) me. Behold, I bawaa (come) achar (other) you." But she didn't nagad (tell) her ayash (husband/individual man), Nabal (Nabal).

It was so, as she rakab (rode) on her donkey, and yarad (came) down by the sathar (secret / hidden) of the har (mountain), that behold, Dawad (David) and his ayash (husband/individual man) yarad (came) down toward her; and she pagash (met) them.

Now Dawad (David) had amar (spoke), Surely in shaqar (vain) have I shamar (keep/guard) all that zah (this/that/these) fellow has in the madabar (wilderness), so that maawamah (nothing) was paqad (visit) of shawab (turn back / repent) that pertained to him. He has returned me rai (evil) for tawab (pleasant/functional).

Alahayam ishah (make) so to the ayab (enemy) of Dawad (David), and more also, if I shaar (leave) of all that belongs to him by the baqar (morning) light so much as shathan (one) who urinates on a qayar (wall).

When Abayagayal (Abigail) raah (see) Dawad (David), she hurried, and alighted from her donkey, and napal (fall / be cast down) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) Dawad (David) on her panayam (face), and shachah (bowed) herself to the aratz (Earth/land).

She napal (fall / be cast down) at his ragal (feet / foot), and amar (spoke), On me, my Adawan, on me be the iwan (guilt/iniquity); and please let your handmaid dabar (word / matter) in your azan (ears). Shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of your handmaid.

Please don't let my Adawan lab (heart) this worthless ayash (husband/individual man), even Nabal (Nabal); for as his sham (name) is, so is he. Nabal (Nabal) is his sham (name), and nabalah (folly) is with him; but I, your handmaid, didn't raah (see) the nair (young) men of my Adawan, whom you shalach (send).

Now therefore, my Adawan, as Yahawah chay (life), and as your napash (living being/soul) chay (life), since Yahawah has withheld you from dam (blood) guiltiness, and from yashai (salvation) yourself with your own yad (hand), now therefore let your ayab (enemy), and those who baqash (seek) rai (evil) to my Adawan, be as Nabal (Nabal).
Now this barakah (present) which your shapachah (servant) bawaa (come) brought to my Adawan, nathan (give) it be given to the nair (young) men who halak (move) my Adawan.

Please nashaa (lift) the pashai (trespass) of your handmaid. For Yahawah will ishah (make) ishah (make) my Adawan a aman (believe / have faith) bayath (house), because my Adawan lacham (fights) the malachamah (battles) of Yahawah; and rai (evil) shall not be matzaa (found) in you all your yawam (day).

Though adam (men) may qawam (rise up) up to radap (pursue) you, and to baqash (seek) your napash (living being/soul), yet the napash (living being/soul) of my Adawan shall be tzarar (bound) in the tzarawar (bundle) of chay (life) with Yahawah your Alahayam. He will qalai (sling) out the napash (living being/soul) of your ayab (enemy), as from the hollow of a qalai (sling).

It shall come to pass, when Yahawah ishah (make) done to my Adawan according to all the tawab (pleasant/functional) that he has dabar (word / matter) concerning you, and shall have tzawah (appointed) you nagayad (prince) over Yasharaal (Israel),

That this shall be no pawaqah (grief) to you, nor offense of lab (heart) to my Adawan, either that you have shapak (shed) dam (blood) chanam (without) cause, or that my Adawan has avenged himself. When Yahawah yatab (has) dealt well with my Adawan, then zakar (remembrance/memory) your handmaid.
Dawad (David) amar (spoke) Abayagayal (to) Abigail, barak (blessed) is Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), who shalach (send) you this yawam (day) to qaraa (called) me!

Barak (blessed) is your taim (discretion), and barak (blessed) are you, that have kalaa (kept) me this yawam (day) from dam (blood) guiltiness, and from yashai (salvation) myself with my own yad (hand).

For indeed, as Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), chay (life), who has withheld me from raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) you, lawalaa (unless) you had hurried and bawaa (come) to qaraa (called) me, surely there wouldn't have been yathar (left) to Nabal (Nabal) by the baqar (morning) awar (light) so much as shathan (one) who urinates on a qayar (wall).

So Dawad (David) laqach (take / seized) of her yad (hand) that which she bawaa (come) brought him: and he amar (spoke) to her, ilah (go up / offer) up in shalawam (peace / safety) to your bayath (house). Raah (see), I have shamai (hearken / hear) to your qawal (sound / voice), and have granted your request.

Abayagayal (Abigail) bawaa (come) to Nabal (Nabal); and behold, he held a mashathah (feast) in his bayath (house), like the mashathah (feast) of a malak (king). Nabal (Nabal's) lab (heart) was tawab (pleasant/functional) within him, for he was very shakawar (drunken). Therefore she nagad (told) him nothing, qatan (small/young/least) or more, until the baqar (morning) awar (light).

It happened in the baqar (morning), when the yayan (wine) was yatzaa (go out / come out) out of Nabal (Nabal), that his ashah (wife/individual woman) nagad (told) him these things, and his lab (heart) mawath (death) qarab (among / near) him, and he became as a aban (stone).
It happened about ishar (ten) yawam (day) after, that Yahawah nagap (struck) Nabal (Nabal), so that he mawath (death).

When Dawad (David) shamai (hearken / hear) that Nabal (Nabal) was mawath (death), he amar (spoke), "barak (blessed) is Yahawah, who has rayab (pleaded) the rayab (cause) of my charapah (reproach) from the yad (hand) of Nabal (Nabal), and has chashak (darkness) back his ibad (servant) from rai (evil). Yahawah has shawab (turn back / repent) the evildoing of Nabal (Nabal) on his own raash (head)." Dawad (David) shalach (send) and dabar (word / matter) Abayagayal (concerning) Abigail, to laqach (take / seized) her to him as ashah (wife/individual woman).

When the ibad (servant) of Dawad (David) bawaa (come) come Abayagayal (to) Abigail to Karamal (Carmel), they dabar (word / matter) to her, amar (spoke), Dawad (David) has shalach (send) us to you, to laqach (take / seized) you to him as ashah (wife/individual woman).

She qawam (rise up), and shachah (bowed) herself with her ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land), and amar (spoke), Behold, your handmaid is a shapachah (servant) to rachatz (wash) the ragal (feet / foot) of the shapachah (servants) of my Adawan.

Abayagayal (Abigail) hurried, and qawam (rise up), and rakab (rode) on a donkey, with chamash (five) ladies of hers who ragal (feet / foot) her; and she halak (move) ragal (feet / foot) the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Dawad (David), and became his ashah (wife/individual woman).
Dawad (David) also laqach (take / seized) Achayanaim (Ahinoam) of Yazaraial (Jezreel); and they shanayam (two) became his wives.

Now Shaawal (Saul) nathan (give) given Mayakal (Michal) his bath (daughter), Dawad (David's) ashah (wife/individual woman), to Palatay (Palti) the ban (son) of Layash (Laish), who was of Galayam (Gallim).

The zayapay (ziphites) bawaa (come) to Shaawal (Saul) to Gabaih (Gibeah), amar (spoke), Doesn't Dawad (David) sathar (hide) himself in the gabaih (hill) of Chakayalah (Hachilah), which is panayam (before) the yashayamawan (desert)?

Then Shaawal (Saul) qawam (rise up), and yarad (went) down to the madabar (wilderness) of Zayap (Ziph), having shalawash (three) alap (thousand) bachar (chosen) ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) with him, to baqash (seek) Dawad (David) in the madabar (wilderness) of Zayap (Ziph).

Shaawal (Saul) chanah (encamped) in the gabaih (hill) of Chakayalah (Hachilah), which is panayam (before) the yashayamawan (desert), by the darak (way). But Dawad (David) stayed in the madabar (wilderness), and he raah (see) that Shaawal (Saul) bawaa (come) achar (other) him into the madabar (wilderness).
Dawad (David) therefore shalach (send) out ragal (spies), and yadai (understood) that Shaawal (Saul) had certainly bawaa (come).

Dawad (David) qawam (rise up), and bawaa (come) to the maqawam (place) where Shaawal (Saul) had chanah (encamped); and Dawad (David) raah (see) the maqawam (place) where Shaawal (Saul) shakab (lay), and Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner), the shar (prince / ruler) of his tzabaa (troop): and Shaawal (Saul) shakab (lay) within the place of the wagons, and the im (people / nation) were chanah (encamped) around him.

Then inah (answer / respond) Dawad (David) and amar (spoke) to Achayamalak (Ahimelech) the Chathay (Hittite), and to Abayashay (Abishai) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah), ach (brother/kinsman) to Yawaab (Joab), amar (spoke), "Who will yarad (go) down with me to Shaawal (Saul) to the machanah (camp)?" Abayashay (Abishai) amar (spoke), I will yarad (go) down with you.

So Dawad (David) and Abayashay (Abishai) bawaa (come) to the im (people / nation) by layal (night): and, behold, Shaawal (Saul) shakab (lay) yashan (sleeping) within the place of the wagons, with his chanayath (spear) maik (stuck) in the aratz (Earth/land) at his maraashah (head); and Abanar (Abner) and the im (people / nation) shakab (lay) around him.

Then Abayashay (Abishai) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), Alahayam has sagar (delivered) up your ayab (enemy) into your yad (hand) this yawam (day). Now therefore please let me nakah (strike) him with the chanayath (spear) to the aratz (Earth/land) at paim (one) stroke, and I will not strike him the shanah (second) time.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Abayashay (Abishai), Don't shachath (destroy) him; for who can shalach (send) forth his yad (hand) against yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) mashayach (anointed one), and be naqah (clean/innocent)?

Dawad (David) amar (spoke), As Yahawah chay (life), Yahawah will nagap (strike) him; or his yawam (day) shall bawaa (come) to mawath (death); or he shall bawaa (come) down into malachamah (battle) and sapah (perish).

Yahawah chalayalah (forbid) that I should shalach (send) forth my yad (hand) against yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) mashayach (anointed one); but now please laqach (take / seized) the chanayath (spear) that is at his maraashah (head), and the jar of mayam (Waters), and yalak (let) us go.

So Dawad (David) laqach (take / seized) the chanayath (spear) and the jar of mayam (Waters) from Shaawal (Saul's) raashath (head); and they yalak (went) away: and no man raah (see) it, nor yadai (knew) it, neither did any qawatz (awake); for they were all asleep, because a tharadamah (deep) sleep from Yahawah was napal (fall / be cast down) on them.

Then Dawad (David) ibar (pass over/through) over to the other ibar (side), and imad (stood) on the raash (head) of the har (mountain) rachawaq (afar) off; a rab (great) maqawam (place) being between them;

And Dawad (David) qaraa (called) to the im (people / nation), and to Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner), amar (spoke), "Don't you inah (answer / respond), Abanar (Abner)?" Then Abanar (Abner) inah (answer / respond), Who are you who qaraa (called) to the malak (king)?

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Abanar (Abner), Aren't you a ayash (husband/individual man)? Who is like you in Yasharaal (Israel)? Why then have you not shamar (keep/guard) watch over your Adawan, the malak (king)? For achad (one) of the im (people / nation) bawaa (come) in to shachath (destroy) the malak (king) your Adawan.

This thing isn't tawab (pleasant/functional) that you ishah (make) done. As Yahawah chay (life), you are ban (son) to mawath (death), because you have not shamar (keep/guard) watch over your Adawan, yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) mashayach (anointed one). Now raah (see) where the malak (king) chanayath (spear) is, and the jar of mayam (Waters) that was at his maraashah (head).

Shaawal (Saul) nakar (knew) Dawad (David's) qawal (sound / voice), and amar (spoke), "Is this your qawal (sound / voice), my ban (son) Dawad (David)?" Dawad (David) amar (spoke), It is my qawal (sound / voice), my Adawan, O malak (king).
He amar (spoke), Why does my Adawan radap (pursue) achar (other) his ibad (servant)? For what ishah (make) I done? Or what rai (evil) is in my yad (hand)?

Now therefore, please let my Adawan the malak (king) shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of his ibad (servant). If it is so that Yahawah has sawath (stirred) you up against me, let him rawach (spirit / wind) an manachah (offering). But if it is the ban (son) of adam (men), they are arar (cursed) panayam (before) Yahawah; for they have garash (driven) me out this yawam (day) that I shouldn't cling to yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) nachalah (inheritance), amar (spoke), ‘yalak (go), ibad (servant) other Alahayam!’

Now therefore, don't let my dam (blood) napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land) away from the panayam (presence) of Yahawah; for the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) yatzaa (go out / come out) come out to baqash (seek) a paraish (flea), as when one radap (hunts) a qaraa (called) in the har (mountain).

Then Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), I have chataa (sinned). Shawab (turn back / repent), my ban (son) Dawad (David); for I will no more raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) you harm, because my napash (living being/soul) was yaqar (precious) in your iyan (eye) this yawam (day). Behold, I have sakal (played) the fool, and have shagah (erred) rabah (exceedingly).
Dawad (David) inah (answer / respond), Behold the chanayath (spear), O malak (king)! Then let achad (one) of the nair (young) men ibar (pass over/through) over and laqach (take / seized) it.

Yahawah will shawab (turn back / repent) to every ayash (husband/individual man) his tzadaqah (righteousness) and his amawanah (faithfulness); because Yahawah nathan (give) you into my yad (hand) today, and I wouldn't shalach (send) forth my yad (hand) against yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) mashayach (anointed one).

Behold, as your napash (living being/soul) was respected this yawam (day) in my iyan (eye), so let my napash (living being/soul) be respected in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, and let him natzal (deliver) me out of all oppression.

Then Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "You are barak (blessed), my ban (son) Dawad (David). You shall both ishah (make) mightily, and shall surely yakal (prevail)." So Dawad (David) yalak (went) his darak (way), and Shaawal (Saul) shawab (turn back / repent) to his maqawam (place).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) in his lab (heart), I shall now sapah (perish) achad (one) yawam (day) by the yad (hand) of Shaawal (Saul). There is nothing tawab (pleasant/functional) for me kay (surely) that I should malat (escape) into the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines); and Shaawal (Saul) will yaash (despair) of me, to baqash (seek) me any more in all the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yasharaal (Israel). So shall I malat (escape) out of his yad (hand).

Dawad (David) qawam (rise up), and ibar (pass over/through) over, he and the shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man) who were with him, to Akayash (Achish) the ban (son) of Maiwak (Maoch), malak (king) of gath (gath).

Dawad (David) lived with Akayash (Achish) at gath (gath), he and his ayash (husband/individual man), every ayash (husband/individual man) with his bayath (house), even Dawad (David) with his shanayam (two) wives, Achayanaim (Ahinoam) the yazaraialayath (jezreelitess), and Abayagayal (Abigail) the karamalayath (carmelitess), Nabal (Nabal's) ashah (wife/individual woman).
It was nagad (told) Shaawal (Saul) that Dawad (David) was barach (fled) to gath (gath): and he baqash (sought) no more again for him.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Akayash (Achish), If now I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye), nathan (give) them give me a maqawam (place) in achad (one) of the iyar (cities) in the shadah (country), that I may yashab (inhabit/dwell) there. For why should your ibad (servant) yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the mamalakah (royal) iyar (city) with you?
Then Akayash (Achish) nathan (give) him Tzaqalag (Ziklag) that yawam (day): why Tzaqalag (Ziklag) pertains to the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) to this yawam (day).
The masapar (number) of the days that Dawad (David) lived in the shadah (country) of the Palashathay (Philistines) was a yawam (day) year and arabai (four) chadash (month).

Dawad (David) and his ayash (husband/individual man) ilah (go up / offer) up, and pashat (made) a raid on the Gashawaray (Geshurites), and the Girzites, and the Imalaqay (Amalekites); for those were the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the aratz (Earth/land), who were of iwalam (forever), as you bawaa (come) to Shawar (Shur), even to the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

Dawad (David) nakah (struck) the aratz (Earth/land), and saved neither ayash (husband/individual man) nor ashah (wife/individual woman) chayah (alive), and laqach (take / seized) away the tzaan (sheep), and the cattle, and the donkeys, and the gamal (camels), and the bagad (clothing); and he shawab (turn back / repent), and bawaa (come) to Akayash (Achish).

Akayash (Achish) amar (spoke), "Against whom have you pashat (made) a raid today?" Dawad (David) amar (spoke), Against the nagab (south) of Yahawadah (Judah), against the nagab (south) of the Yarachamaalay (Jerahmeelites), and against the nagab (south) of the Qayanay (Kenites).

Dawad (David) chayah (saved) neither ayash (husband/individual man) nor ashah (wife/individual woman) chayah (alive), to bawaa (come) them to gath (gath), amar (spoke), Lest they should nagad (tell) of us, amar (spoke), ‘Dawad (David) this, and this has been his mashapat (way) all the yawam (day) he has lived in the shadah (country) of the Palashathay (Philistines).’

Akayash (Achish) aman (believe / have faith) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), He has made his im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel) baash (utterly) to abhor him. Therefore he shall be my ibad (servant) iwalam (forever).

It happened in those yawam (day), that the Palashathay (Philistines) qabatz (gathered) their machanah (armies) qabatz (together) for tzabaa (troop), to lacham (fight) with Yasharaal (Israel). Akayash (Achish) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), yadai (know) yadai (assuredly) that you shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out with me in the machanah (army), you and your yadai (men).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Akayash (Achish), "Therefore you shall yadai (know) what your ibad (servant) will ishah (make)." Akayash (Achish) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), Therefore will I shawam (place / establish / appoint) you my bodyguard for yawam (day).

Now Shamawaal (Samuel) was mawath (death), and all Yasharaal (Israel) had sapad (lamented) him, and qabar (bury) him in Ramah (Ramah), even in his own iyar (city). Shaawal (Saul) had sawar (put) away those who had familiar awab (spirits), and the yadainay (wizards), out of the aratz (Earth/land).

The Palashathay (Philistines) qabatz (gathered) themselves together, and bawaa (come) and chanah (encamped) in Shawanam (Shunem): and Shaawal (Saul) qabatz (gathered) all Yasharaal (Israel) qabatz (together), and they chanah (encamped) in Galabai (Gilboa).
When Shaawal (Saul) raah (see) the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines), he was yaraa (fear / be afraid), and his lab (heart) charad (trembled) maad (greatly).
When Shaawal (Saul) inquired of Yahawah, Yahawah didn't inah (answer / respond) him, neither by chalawam (dreams), nor by awarayam (urim), nor by nabayaa (prophet/prophecy).

Then Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), "baqash (seek) me a ashah (wife/individual woman) who has a familiar awab (spirit), that I may yalak (go) to her, and darash (inquire) of her." His ibad (servant) amar (spoke) to him, Behold, there is a ashah (wife/individual woman) who has a familiar awab (spirit) at Iyanadaar (Endor).

Shaawal (Saul) disguised himself, and labash (put) on other bagad (clothing), and yalak (went), he and shanayam (two) achar (other) with him, and they bawaa (come) to the ashah (wife/individual woman) by layal (night): and he amar (spoke), Please qasam (divine) to me by the familiar awab (spirit), and ilah (go up / offer) me up whomever I shall amar (spoke) to you.

The ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke) to him, Behold, you yadai (know) what Shaawal (Saul) ishah (make) done, how he has karath (cut) off those who have familiar awab (spirits), and the yadainay (wizards), out of the aratz (Earth/land). Why then do you lay a naqash (snare) for my napash (living being/soul), to cause me to mawath (death)?
Shaawal (Saul) shabai (swear / take oath) to her by Yahawah, amar (spoke), As Yahawah chay (life), no iwan (guilt/iniquity) shall qarah (happen) to you for this thing.
Then the ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke), "Whom shall I ilah (go up / offer) up to you?" He amar (spoke), Bring Shamawaal (Samuel) up for me.

When the ashah (wife/individual woman) raah (see) Shamawaal (Samuel), she zaiq (cried) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice); and the ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), amar (spoke), Why have you ramah (deceived) me? For you are Shaawal (Saul)!

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to her, "Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). For what do you raah (see)?" The ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), I raah (see) a Alahayam coming up out of the aratz (Earth/land).

He amar (spoke) to her, "What does he look like?" She amar (spoke), "An zaqan (old) ayash (husband/individual man) ilah (go up / offer) up. He is itah (covered) with a maiyal (robe)." Shaawal (Saul) yadai (perceived) that it was Shamawaal (Samuel), and he qadad (bowed) with his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land), and showed respect.

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "Why have you disturbed me, to ilah (go up / offer) me up?" Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), I am very tzarar (distressed); for the Palashathay (Philistines) make lacham (war) against me, and Alahayam has sawar (departed) from me, and answers me no more, neither by nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), nor by chalawam (dreams). Therefore I have qaraa (called) you, that you may yadai (make) known to me what I shall ishah (make).
Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), Why then do you shaal (ask) of me, since Yahawah has sawar (departed) from you and has become your ir (adversary)?

Yahawah ishah (make) done to you as he dabar (word / matter) by me. Yahawah has qarai (torn) the mamalakah (kingdom) out of your yad (hand), and nathan (give) it to your neighbor, even to Dawad (David).

Ashar (who/that) you didn't obey the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah, and didn't ishah (make) his charawan (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) on Imalaq (Amalek), therefore Yahawah ishah (make) done this thing to you this yawam (day).

Moreover Yahawah will nathan (give) Yasharaal (Israel) also with you into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines); and machar (tomorrow) you and your ban (son) will be with me. Yahawah will nathan (give) the machanah (army) of Yasharaal (Israel) also into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines).

Then Shaawal (Saul) napal (fall / be cast down) immediately his malaa (full) length on the aratz (Earth/land), and was terrified, because of the dabar (word / matter) of Shamawaal (Samuel). There was no kach (strength / mighty / power) in him; for he had akal (eat) no lacham (bread) all the yawam (day), nor all the layal (night).

The ashah (wife/individual woman) bawaa (come) to Shaawal (Saul), and raah (see) that he was very bahal (troubled), and amar (spoke) to him, Behold, your handmaid has shamai (hearken / hear) to your qawal (sound / voice), and I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) my napash (living being/soul) in my kap (hand), and have shamai (hearken / hear) to your dabar (word / matter) which you dabar (word / matter) to me.

Now therefore, please shamai (hearken / hear) also to the qawal (sound / voice) of your handmaid, and let me shawam (place / establish / appoint) a path (morsel) of lacham (bread) panayam (before) you; and akal (eat), that you may have kach (strength / mighty / power), when you yalak (go) on your darak (way).

But he maan (refused), and amar (spoke), I will not akal (eat). But his ibad (servant), together with the ashah (wife/individual woman), constrained him; and he shamai (hearken / hear) to their qawal (sound / voice). So he qawam (rise up) from the aratz (Earth/land), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the matah (bed).

The ashah (wife/individual woman) had a fattened igal (calf) in the bayath (house). She hurried and zabach (killed) it; and she laqach (take / seized) qamach (flour), and lawash (kneaded) it, and apah (baked) unleavened matzah (bread) of it.
She nagash (brought) it panayam (before) Shaawal (Saul), and panayam (before) his ibad (servant); and they akal (eat). Then they qawam (rise up) up, and yalak (went) away that layal (night).

Now the Palashathay (Philistines) qabatz (gathered) together all their machanah (armies) to Apaq (Aphek): and the Yasharaal (Israelites) chanah (encamped) by the spring which is in Yazaraial (Jezreel).

The saran (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) ibar (pass over/through) on by maah (hundred), and by alap (thousands); and Dawad (David) and his ibar (pass over/through) ibar (pass over/through) on in the rear with Akayash (Achish).

Then the shar (prince / ruler) of the Palashathay (Philistines) amar (spoke), "What about these ibaray (hebrews)?" Akayash (Achish) amar (spoke) to the shar (prince / ruler) of the Palashathay (Philistines), Isn't this Dawad (David), the ibad (servant) of Shaawal (Saul) the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), who has been with me these yawam (day), or rather these shanah (years), and I matzaa (have) found no maawamah (fault) in him yawam (day) he napal (fall / be cast down) away to this yawam (day)?

But the shar (prince / ruler) of the Palashathay (Philistines) were qatzap (angry) with him; and the shar (prince / ruler) of the Palashathay (Philistines) amar (spoke) to him, shawab (turn back / repent) the ayash (husband/individual man) shawab (turn back / repent), that he may shawab (turn back / repent) back to his maqawam (place) where you paqad (visit) appointed him, and yarad (let) him not go down with us to malachamah (battle), lest in the malachamah (battle) he become an shatan (adversary) to us. For with what should this fellow ratzah (reconcile) himself to his Adawan? Should it not be with the raash (head) of these ayash (husband/individual man)?

Is not this Dawad (David), of whom they inah (answer / respond) one to another in machalah (dances), amar (spoke), ‘Shaawal (Saul) has nakah (slain) his alap (thousands), Dawad (David) his rababah (ten) thousands?’

Then Akayash (Achish) qaraa (called) Dawad (David), and amar (spoke) to him, As Yahawah chay (life), you have been yashar (upright), and your yatzaa (go out / come out) out and your bawaa (come) in with me in the machanah (army) is tawab (pleasant/functional) in my iyan (eye); for I matzaa (have) not found rai (evil) in you since the yawam (day) of your bawaa (come) to me to this yawam (day). Nevertheless, the saran (lords) don't favor you.
Therefore now shawab (turn back / repent), and yalak (go) in shalawam (peace / safety), that you not rai (displease) the saran (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Akayash (Achish), But what ishah (make) I done? What matzaa (have) you found in your ibad (servant) so yawam (day) as I have been panayam (before) you to this yawam (day), that I may not bawaa (come) and lacham (fight) against the ayab (enemy) of my Adawan the malak (king)?

Akayash (Achish) inah (answer / respond) Dawad (David), I yadai (know) that you are tawab (pleasant/functional) in my iyan (eye), as an malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Alahayam. Notwithstanding the shar (prince / ruler) of the Palashathay (Philistines) have amar (spoke), ‘He shall not ilah (go up / offer) up with us to the malachamah (battle).’

Therefore now shakam (rise) up early in the baqar (morning) with the ibad (servant) of your Adawan who bawaa (come) come with you; and as soon as you are up shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and have awar (light), depart.

So Dawad (David) shakam (rose) up early, he and his ayash (husband/individual man), to depart in the baqar (morning), to shawab (turn back / repent) into the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines). The Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up to Yazaraial (Jezreel).

It happened, when Dawad (David) and his ayash (husband/individual man) bawaa (come) come to Tzaqalag (Ziklag) on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), that the Imalaqay (Amalekites) had pashat (made) a raid on the nagab (south), and on Tzaqalag (Ziklag), and had nakah (struck) Tzaqalag (Ziklag), and sharap (burned) it with ash (fire),

And had shabah (taken) captive the ashah (wife/individual woman) and all who were therein, both qatan (small/young/least) and gadawal (very great/important/mighty). They didn't mawath (death) any, but nahag (carried) them off, and yalak (went) their darak (way).

When Dawad (David) and his ayash (husband/individual man) bawaa (come) to the iyar (city), behold, it was sharap (burned) with ash (fire); and their wives, and their ban (son), and their bath (daughter), were shabah (taken) captive.

Then Dawad (David) and the im (people / nation) who were with him nashaa (lift) up their qawal (sound / voice) and bakah (wept), until they had no more kach (strength / mighty / power) to bakah (weep).

Dawad (David's) shanayam (two) wives were shabah (taken) captive, Achayanaim (Ahinoam) the yazaraialayath (jezreelitess), and Abayagayal (Abigail) the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Nabal (Nabal) the karamalay (carmelite).

Dawad (David) was maad (greatly) yatzar (distressed); for the im (people / nation) amar (spoke) of saqal (stoning) him, because the napash (living being/soul) of all the im (people / nation) was grieved, every ayash (husband/individual man) for his ban (son) and for his bath (daughter): but Dawad (David) chazaq (strengthened) himself in Yahawah his Alahayam.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahan (priest), the ban (son) of Achayamalak (Ahimelech), "Please nagash (bring) me here the apawad (ephod)." Abayathar (Abiathar) nagash (brought) the apawad (ephod) to Dawad (David).

Dawad (David) inquired of Yahawah, amar (spoke), "If I radap (pursue) achar (other) this gadawad (troop), shall I nashag (overtake) them?" He amar (spoke) him, radap (pursue); for you shall nashag (surely) nashag (overtake) them, and shall natzal (without) fail natzal (recover) all.

So Dawad (David) yalak (went), he and the shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man) who were with him, and bawaa (come) to the nachal (stream / river) Bashawar (Besor), where those who were yathar (left) behind imad (stayed).

But Dawad (David) radap (pursued), he and arabai (four) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man); for two maah (hundred) imad (stayed) behind, who were so pagar (faint) that they couldn't ibar (pass over/through) over the nachal (stream / river) Bashawar (Besor).

They matzaa (found) an Egyptian in the shadah (field), and laqach (take / seized) him to Dawad (David), and nathan (give) him lacham (bread), and he akal (eat); and they gave him mayam (Waters) to shaqah (drink).

They nathan (give) him a palach (piece) of a dabalah (fig cake) of figs, and shanayam (two) clusters of tzamawaq (raisins). When he had akal (eat), his rawach (spirit / wind) shawab (turn back / repent) again to him; for he had akal (eat) no lacham (bread), nor shathah (drinks) any mayam (Waters), shalawash (three) yawam (day) and shalawash (three) layal (nights).
