Dawad (David) asked him, "To whom do you belong? Where are you from?" He amar (spoke), I am a nair (young) man of Matzaray (Egypt), ibad (servant) to an Amalekite; and my adawan (master / lord) izab (left) me, because shalawash (three) yawam (day) ago I chalah (afflict) sick.

We pashat (made) a raid on the nagab (south) of the Karathay (Cherethites), and on that which belongs to Yahawadah (Judah), and on the nagab (south) of Kalab (Caleb); and we sharap (burned) Tzaqalag (Ziklag) with ash (fire).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to him, "Will you yarad (bring) me down to this gadawad (troop)?" He amar (spoke), shabai (swear / take oath) to me by Alahayam that you will neither mawath (death) me, am (mother) sagar (deliver) me up into the yad (hand) of my adawan (master / lord), and I will yarad (bring) you down to this gadawad (troop).

When he had yarad (brought) him down, behold, they were natash (spread) around over all the aratz (Earth/land), akal (eat), shathah (drinks), and chagag (dancing), because of all the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shalal (spoil) that they had laqach (take / seized) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Yahawadah (Judah).

Dawad (David) nakah (struck) them from the nashap (twilight) even to the irab (evening) of the next macharath (day). Not a ayash (husband/individual man) of them malat (escaped) from there, except arabai (four) maah (hundred) nair (young) ayash (husband/individual man), who rakab (rode) on gamal (camels) and nawas (fled).
Dawad (David) natzal (recovered) all that the Imalaq (Amalekites) had laqach (take / seized); and Dawad (David) natzal (rescued) his shanayam (two) wives.

There was nothing idar (lacking) to them, man (from) qatan (small/young/least) nor gadawal (very great/important/mighty), neither ban (son) nor bath (daughter), neither shalal (spoil), nor anything that they had laqach (take / seized) to them. Dawad (David) laqach (take / seized) back all.

Dawad (David) laqach (take / seized) all the tzaan (flocks) and the baqar (morning), which they nahag (drove) panayam (before) hawaa (which/who/that is) other livestock, and amar (spoke), This is Dawad (David's) shalal (spoil).

Dawad (David) bawaa (come) to the two maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man), who were so pagar (faint) that they could not yalak (follow) Dawad (David), whom also they had yashab (inhabit/dwell) to stay at the nachal (stream / river) Bashawar (Besor); and they yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to qaraa (called) Dawad (David), and to qaraa (called) the im (people / nation) who were with him. When Dawad (David) nagash (came) near to the im (people / nation), he shaal (greeted) them.

Then all the rai (wicked) ayash (husband/individual man) and base ayash (husband/individual man), of those who halak (move) with Dawad (David), amar (spoke) and amar (spoke), Because they didn't go with us, we will not nathan (give) them anything of the shalal (spoil) that we have natzal (recovered), except to every ayash (husband/individual man) his ashah (wife/individual woman) and his ban (son), that he may nahag (lead) them away, and depart.

Then Dawad (David) amar (spoke), You shall not ishah (make) so, my ach (brother/kinsman), with that which Yahawah nathan (give) given to us, who has shamar (keep/guard) us, and nathan (give) the gadawad (troop) that bawaa (come) against us into our yad (hand).

Who will shamai (hearken / hear) to you in this dabar (word / matter)? For as his share is who yarad (goes) down to the malachamah (battle), so shall his share be who yashab (inhabit/dwell) by the baggage: they shall share yachad (alike).
It was so from that yawam (day) mail (top/above), that he shawam (place / establish / appoint) it a chaq (statute) and an mashapat (ordinance) for Yasharaal (Israel) to this yawam (day).

When Dawad (David) bawaa (come) to Tzaqalag (Ziklag), he shalach (send) of the shalal (spoil) to the zaqan (elders) of Yahawadah (Judah), even to his rai (neigbor/another person), amar (spoke), Behold, a barakah (present) for you of the shalal (spoil) of the ayab (enemy) of Yahawah.
He sent it to those who were in Bayathaal (Bethel), and to those who were in Ramawath (Ramoth) of the ramawath (south), and to those who were in Yathayar (Jattir),
And to those who were in Irawair (Aroer), and to those who were in Shapamawath (Siphmoth), and to those who were in Ashathamai (Eshtemoa),
And Rakal (to) those who were in Racal, and to those who were in the iyar (cities) of the Yarachamaalay (Jerahmeelites), and to those who were in the iyar (cities) of the Qayanay (Kenites),
And to those who were in Charamah (Hormah), and Kawaraishan (to) those who were in Borashan, and to those who were in Ithak (Athach),
And to those who were in Chabarawan (Hebron), and to all the maqawam (place) where Dawad (David) himself and his halak (move) used to stay.

Now the Palashathay (Philistines) lacham (fought) against Yasharaal (Israel): and the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) nawas (fled) from panayam (before) the Palashathay (Philistines), and napal (fall / be cast down) down chalal (slain) on har (mountain) Galabai (Gilboa).

The Palashathay (Philistines) dabaq (followed) hard on Shaawal (Saul) and on his ban (son); and the Palashathay (Philistines) nakah (killed) Yahawanathan (Jonathan), and Abayanadab (Abinadab), and Malakayashawai (Malchishua), the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul).
The malachamah (battle) went hard against Shaawal (Saul), and the archers overtook him; and he was maad (greatly) distressed by reason of the archers.

Then Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to his armor bearer, "shalap (draw) your charab (sword), and thrust me daqar (through) with it, lest these iral (uncircumcised) bawaa (come) and thrust me daqar (through), and ilal (abuse) me!" But his armor bearer would not; for he was terrified. Therefore Shaawal (Saul) laqach (take / seized) his charab (sword), and napal (fall / be cast down) on it.
When his armor bearer raah (see) that Shaawal (Saul) was mawath (death), he likewise napal (fall / be cast down) on his charab (sword), and mawath (death) with him.
So Shaawal (Saul) mawath (death), and his shalawash (three) ban (son), and his armor bearer, and all his mawath (death), that same yawam (day) yachad (together).

When the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) who were on the other ibar (side) of the imaq (valley), and those who were ibar (beyond) the Yaradan (Jordan), raah (see) that the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) nawas (fled), and that Shaawal (Saul) and his ban (son) were mawath (death), they forsook the iyar (cities), and nawas (fled); and the Palashathay (Philistines) bawaa (come) and lived in them.

It happened on the next macharath (day), when the Palashathay (Philistines) bawaa (come) to pashat (strip) the chalal (slain), that they matzaa (found) Shaawal (Saul) and his shalawash (three) ban (son) napal (fall / be cast down) on har (mountain) Galabai (Gilboa).

They karath (cut) off his raash (head), and stripped off his armor, and shalach (send) into the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines) all around, to bashar (carry) the news to the bayath (house) of their itzab (idols), and to the im (people / nation).

They shawam (place / establish / appoint) his armor in the bayath (house) Ishatharawath (of) the Ashtaroth; and they thaqai (blow / sound alarm) his gawayah (corpse) to the chawamah (wall) of Bayathashaan (Beth) Shan.
When the yashab (inhabit/dwell) Yabash (of) Jabesh Gilead shamai (hearken / hear) concerning him that which the Palashathay (Philistines) ishah (make) done to Shaawal (Saul),

All the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ayash (husband/individual man) qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) all layal (night), and laqach (take / seized) the gawayah (corpse) of Shaawal (Saul) and the gawayah (corpse) of his ban (son) from the chawamah (wall) of Bayathashaan (Beth) Shan; and they bawaa (come) Yabash (to) Jabesh, and burnt them there.
They laqach (take / seized) their itzam (bones), and qabar (bury) them under the tamarisk ashal (tree) Yabash (in) Jabesh, and tzawam (fasted) shabai (seven) yawam (day).

It happened achar (other) the mawath (death) of Shaawal (Saul), when Dawad (David) was shawab (turn back / repent) from the nakah (slaughter) Imalaq (of) the Amalekites, and Dawad (David) had stayed shanayam (two) yawam (day) in Tzaqalag (Ziklag);

It happened on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), that behold, a ayash (husband/individual man) bawaa (come) out of the machanah (camp) from Shaawal (Saul), with his clothes qarai (torn), and adamah (earth) on his raash (head): and so it was, when he bawaa (come) to Dawad (David), that he napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land), and showed respect.
Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to him, "Where do you bawaa (come) from?" He amar (spoke) to him, I have malat (escaped) out of the machanah (camp) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to him, "mah (how) dabar (word / matter) it go? Please nagad (tell) me." He amar (spoke), The im (people / nation) have nawas (fled) from the malachamah (battle), and many of the im (people / nation) also napal (fall / be cast down) fallen and are mawath (death); and Shaawal (Saul) and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son) are mawath (death) also.
Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to the nair (young) man who amar (spoke) him, How do you yadai (know) that Shaawal (Saul) and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son) are mawath (death)?

The nair (young) man who nagad (told) him said, As I qarah (happened) by qaraa (called) on har (mountain) Galabai (Gilboa), behold, Shaawal (Saul) was shain (leaning) on his chanayath (spear); and behold, the rakab (chariots) and the horsemen dabaq (followed) hard after him.
When he panah (looked) achar (other) him, he saw me, and qaraa (called) to me. I amar (spoke), ‘Here I am.’
He amar (spoke) to me, ‘Who are you?’ I amar (spoke) him, ‘I am an Imalaqay (Amalekite).’
He amar (spoke) to me, ‘Please imad (stand) beside me, and mawath (death) me; for shabatz (anguish) achaz (has) taken hold of me, because my napash (living being/soul) is yet whole in me.’

So I imad (stood) beside him, and mawath (death) him, because I was yadai (sure) that he could not chayah (live) achar (other) that he napal (fall / be cast down) fallen. I laqach (take / seized) the nazar (crown / consecrate) that was on his raash (head), and the atzaidah (bracelet) that was on his zarawai (arm), and bawaa (come) brought them here to my Adawan.
Then Dawad (David) chazaq (took) hold on his clothes, and qarai (tore) them; and likewise all the chazaq (men) who were with him.

They sapad (mourned), and bakah (wept), and tzawam (fasted) until irab (evening), for Shaawal (Saul), and for Yahawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son), and for the im (people / nation) of Yahawah, and for the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel); because they were napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword).
Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to the nair (young) man who amar (spoke) him, "Where are you from?" He amar (spoke), I am the ban (son) of a foreigner, an Imalaqay (Amalekite).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to him, How were you not yaraa (fear / be afraid) to shalach (send) forth your yad (hand) to shachath (destroy) yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) mashayach (anointed one)?
Dawad (David) qaraa (called) achad (one) of the nair (young) men, and amar (spoke), "nagash (go) near, and pagai (fall) on him." He nakah (struck) him, so that he mawath (death).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to him, Your dam (blood) be on your raash (head); for your pah (mouth) has inah (answer / respond) amar (spoke) you, saying, ‘I have mawath (death) yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) mashayach (anointed one).’
Dawad (David) qawan (lamented) with this qayanah (lamentation) over Shaawal (Saul) and over Yahawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son)
(And he commanded them to lamad (teach/instruct) the ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah) the song of the qashath (bow): behold, it is kathab (written) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of Jashar):
Your glory, Yasharaal (Israel), is chalal (slain) on your bamah (high) places! How the gabawar (mighty) napal (fall / be cast down) fallen!

Don't nagad (tell) it in gath (gath). Don't bashar (publish) it in the chawatz (streets) of Ashaqalawan (Ashkelon), lest the bath (daughter) of the Palashathay (Philistines) shamach (rejoice), lest the bath (daughter) of the iral (uncircumcised) ilaz (triumph).

You har (mountain) of Galabai (Gilboa), let there be no tal (dew) nor matar (rain) on you, neither shadah (fields) of tharawamah (offerings); For there the magan (shield) of the gabawar (mighty) was gail (vilely) cast away, The magan (shield) of Shaawal (Saul) was not mashayach (anointed one) with shaman (oil).

From the dam (blood) of the chalal (slain), from the chalab (fat) of the gabawar (mighty), Yahawanathan (Jonathan's) qashath (bow) didn't shawag (turn) achawar (back). Shaawal (Saul's) charab (sword) didn't shawab (turn back / repent) rayaqam (empty).

Shaawal (Saul) and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) were lovely and naiyam (pleasant) in their chay (life). In their mawath (death), they were not parad (divided). They were qalal (swifter) than nashar (eagles). They were gabar (stronger) than aray (lions).

You bath (daughter) of Yasharaal (Israel), bakah (weep) over Shaawal (Saul), who labash (clothed) you in shanay (second) delicately, who ilah (go up / offer) iday (ornament / adornment) of zahab (gold) on your labawash (clothing).
How are the gabawar (mighty) napal (fall / be cast down) in the thawak (midst) of the malachamah (battle)! Yahawanathan (Jonathan) is chalal (slain) on your bamah (high) places.

I am tzarar (distressed) for you, my ach (brother/kinsman) Yahawanathan (Jonathan). You have been very naim (pleasant) to me. Your ahabah (love) to me was palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous), passing the ahabah (love) of ashah (wife/individual woman).
How are the gabawar (mighty) napal (fall / be cast down), and the kalay (weapons) of malachamah (war) abad (destroy/perish)!

It happened achar (other) this, that Dawad (David) inquired of Yahawah, amar (spoke), "Shall I ilah (go up / offer) up into any of the iyar (cities) of Yahawadah (Judah)?" Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, "ilah (go up / offer) up." Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "Where shall I ilah (go up / offer) up?" He amar (spoke), To Chabarawan (Hebron).

So Dawad (David) ilah (go up / offer) up there, and his shanayam (two) wives also, Achayanaim (Ahinoam) the yazaraialayath (jezreelitess), and Abayagayal (Abigail) the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Nabal (Nabal) the karamalay (carmelite).

Dawad (David) ilah (go up / offer) up his ayash (husband/individual man) who were with him, every ayash (husband/individual man) with his bayath (house). They lived in the iyar (cities) of Chabarawan (Hebron).

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Yahawadah (Judah) bawaa (come), and there they mashach (anointed) Dawad (David) malak (king) over the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah). They nagad (told) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), The ayash (husband/individual man) Yabash (of) Jabesh Gilead were those who qabar (bury) Shaawal (Saul).

Dawad (David) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to the ayash (husband/individual man) Yabash (of) Jabesh Gilead, and amar (spoke) to them, barak (blessed) are you by Yahawah, that you ishah (make) shown this chasad (grace) to your Adawan, even to Shaawal (Saul), and have qabar (bury) him.
Now may Yahawah show loving chasad (grace) and amath (truth) to you. I also will reward you for this tawab (pleasant/functional), because you ishah (make) done this thing.

Now therefore let your yad (hand) be chazaq (strong), and be ban (son); for Shaawal (Saul) your Adawan is mawath (death), and also the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) have mashach (anointed) me malak (king) over them.

Now Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner), shar (prince / ruler) of Shaawal (Saul's) tzabaa (troop), had laqach (take / seized) Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth) the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul), and ibar (pass over/through) him over to Machanayam (Mahanaim);

And he made him malak (king) over Galaid (Gilead), and over the ashawaray (ashurites), and over Yazaraial (Jezreel), and over Aparayam (Ephraim), and over Banayamayan (Benjamin), and over all Yasharaal (Israel).

Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth), Shaawal (Saul's) ban (son), was arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years) ban (son) when he began to malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel), and he malak (king) shanayam (two) shanah (years). But the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) achar (other) Dawad (David).
The masapar (time) that Dawad (David) was malak (king) in Chabarawan (Hebron) over the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) was shabai (seven) shanah (years) and shash (six) chadash (month).

Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner), and the ibad (servant) of Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth) the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul), yatzaa (go out / come out) out from Machanayam (Mahanaim) to Gabaiwan (Gibeon).

Yawaab (Joab) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah), and the ibad (servant) of Dawad (David), yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and pagash (met) them by the barakah (pool) of Gabaiwan (Gibeon); and they yashab (inhabit/dwell) down, the one on the one side of the barakah (pool), and the other on the other side of the barakah (pool).
Abanar (Abner) amar (spoke) to Yawaab (Joab), "Please let the nair (young) men qawam (rise up) and shachaq (play) panayam (before) us!" Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke), Let them qawam (rise up)!

Then they qawam (rise up) and ibar (pass over/through) over by masapar (number): shanayam (two) for Banayamayan (Benjamin), and for Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth) the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul), and shanayam (two) of the ibad (servant) of Dawad (David).

They ayash (husband/individual man) chazaq (caught) his opponent by the raash (head), and thrust his charab (sword) in his rai (neigbor/another person) tzad (side); so they napal (fall / be cast down) down yachad (together): therefore that maqawam (place) was qaraa (called) Chalaqathahatzarayam (Helkath) Hazzurim, which is in Gabaiwan (Gibeon).

The malachamah (battle) was very severe that yawam (day): and Abanar (Abner) was nagap (beaten), and the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel), panayam (before) the ibad (servant) of Dawad (David).

The shalawash (three) ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah) were there, Yawaab (Joab), and Abayashay (Abishai), and Ishahaal (Asahel): and Ishahaal (Asahel) was as qal (light) of ragal (feet / foot) as a shadah (wild) gazelle.

Ishahaal (Asahel) radap (pursued) achar (other) Abanar (Abner); and in yalak (going) he didn't natah (turn) to the right yamayan (right hand) nor to the shamaawal (left hand) from achar (other) Abanar (Abner).
Then Abanar (Abner) panah (looked) achar (other) him, and amar (spoke), "Is it you, Ishahaal (Asahel)?" He amar (spoke), It is I.

Abanar (Abner) amar (spoke) to him, "natah (turn) aside to your right yamayan (right hand) or to your shamaawal (left hand), and grab achad (one) of the nair (young) men, and laqach (take / seized) his armor." But Ishahaal (Asahel) would not sawar (turn) aside from achar (other) him.

Abanar (Abner) amar (spoke) again to Ishahaal (Asahel), sawar (turn) aside from achar (other) me. Why should I nakah (strike) you to the aratz (Earth/land)? How then should I nashaa (lift) up my panayam (face) to Yawaab (Joab) your ach (brother/kinsman)?

However he maan (refused) to sawar (turn) aside. Therefore Abanar (Abner) with the achar (other) end of the chanayath (spear) nakah (struck) him in the body, so that the chanayath (spear) yatzaa (go out / come out) out achar (other) him; and he napal (fall / be cast down) down there, and mawath (death) in the same thachath (under). It happened, that as many as bawaa (come) to the maqawam (place) where Ishahaal (Asahel) napal (fall / be cast down) down and mawath (death) imad (stood) still.

But Yawaab (Joab) and Abayashay (Abishai) radap (pursued) achar (other) Abanar (Abner): and the shamash (sun) bawaa (come) down when they bawaa (come) come to the gabaih (hill) of Amah (Ammah), that lies panayam (before) Gayach (Giah) by the darak (way) of the madabar (wilderness) of Gabaiwan (Gibeon).
The ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) qabatz (gathered) themselves together achar (other) Abanar (Abner), and became achad (one) band, and imad (stood) on the raash (head) of a gabaih (hill).

Then Abanar (Abner) qaraa (called) to Yawaab (Joab), and amar (spoke), Shall the charab (sword) akal (eat) natzach (forever)? Don't you yadai (know) that it will be bitterness in the acharawan (latter) end? How long shall it be then, before you ask the im (people / nation) to shawab (turn back / repent) from achar (other) their ach (brother/kinsman)?

Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke), As Alahayam chay (life), if you lawalaa (had) not dabar (word / matter), surely then in the baqar (morning) the im (people / nation) would have ilah (go up / offer) away, and not ayash (husband/individual man) achar (other) his ach (brother/kinsman).

So Yawaab (Joab) thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)); and all the im (people / nation) imad (stood) still, and radap (pursued) achar (other) Yasharaal (Israel) no more, neither lacham (fought) they any more.

Abanar (Abner) and his ayash (husband/individual man) halak (move) all that layal (night) through the irabah (arabah); and they ibar (pass over/through) over the Yaradan (Jordan), and yalak (went) through all Batharawan (Bithron), and bawaa (come) to Machanayam (Mahanaim).

Yawaab (Joab) shawab (turn back / repent) from achar (other) Abanar (Abner): and when he had qabatz (gathered) all the im (people / nation) qabatz (together), there paqad (visit) of Dawad (David's) ibad (servant) nineteen ayash (husband/individual man) and Ishahaal (Asahel).

But the ibad (servant) of Dawad (David) had nakah (struck) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), and of Abanar (Abner's) ayash (husband/individual man), so that shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty) ayash (husband/individual man) mawath (death).

They nashaa (lift) up Ishahaal (Asahel), and qabar (bury) him in the tomb of his ab (father), which was in Bayathalacham (Bethlehem). Yawaab (Joab) and his ayash (husband/individual man) yalak (went) all layal (night), and the awar (light) broke on them at Chabarawan (Hebron).

Now there was arak (long) malachamah (war) between the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul) and the bayath (house) of Dawad (David): and Dawad (David) halak (move) chazaq (stronger) and chazaq (stronger), but the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul) halak (move) dal (weaker) and dal (weaker).
To Dawad (David) were ban (son) yalad (birth / begot) in Chabarawan (Hebron): and his bakawar (firstborn) was Amanawan (Amnon), of Achayanaim (Ahinoam) the yazaraialayath (jezreelitess);

And his mashanah (second), Kalaab (Chileab), Abayagayal (of) Abigail the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Nabal (Nabal) the karamalay (carmelite); and the shalayashay (third), Abayashalawam (Absalom) the ban (son) Maikah (of) Maacah the bath (daughter) of Thalamay (Talmai) malak (king) of Gashawar (Geshur);
And the rabayaiy (fourth), Adanayah (Adonijah) the ban (son) of Chagayath (Haggith); and the chamayashay (fifth), Shapatayah (Shephatiah) the ban (son) of Abayatal (Abital);
And the shashay (sixth), Yatharaim (Ithream), of Igalah (Eglah), Dawad (David's) ashah (wife/individual woman). These were yalad (birth / begot) to Dawad (David) in Chabarawan (Hebron).

It happened, while there was malachamah (war) between the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul) and the bayath (house) of Dawad (David), that Abanar (Abner) chazaq (made) himself strong in the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul).

Now Shaawal (Saul) had a payalagash (concubine), whose sham (name) was Ratzapah (Rizpah), the bath (daughter) of Ayah (Aiah): and Ishbosheth amar (spoke) to Abanar (Abner), Why bawaa (come) you gone in to my ab (father) payalagash (concubine)?

Then was Abanar (Abner) very charah (hot with anger) for the dabar (word / matter) of Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth), and amar (spoke), Am I a kalab (dog's) raash (head) that belongs to Yahawadah (Judah)? Today I show chasad (grace) to the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul) your ab (father), to his ach (brother/kinsman), and to his marai (friends), and matzaa (have) not delivered you into the yad (hand) of Dawad (David); and yet you paqad (visit) me this yawam (day) with a iwan (guilt/iniquity) concerning this ashah (wife/individual woman)!
Alahayam ishah (make) so to Abanar (Abner), and more also, if, as Yahawah has shabai (swear / take oath) to Dawad (David), I don't ishah (make) even so to him;

To transfer the mamalakah (kingdom) from the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul), and to qawam (rise up) up the kasaa (throne) of Dawad (David) over Yasharaal (Israel) and over Yahawadah (Judah), Dan (from) Dan Baarashabai (even) to Beersheba.
He yakal (could) not shawab (turn back / repent) Abanar (Abner) another dabar (word / matter), because he yaraa (fear / be afraid) him.

Abanar (Abner) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to Dawad (David) on his behalf, amar (spoke), "Whose is the aratz (Earth/land)?" And amar (spoke), karath (cut) your alliance with me, and behold, my yad (hand) shall be with you, to bring all Yasharaal (Israel) around to you.

He amar (spoke), tawab (pleasant/functional); I will karath (cut) a treaty with you; but achad (one) thing I shaal (require) of you. That is, you shall not raah (see) my panayam (face), unless you panayam (first) bawaa (come) Mayakal (Michal), Shaawal (Saul's) bath (daughter), when you bawaa (come) to raah (see) my panayam (face).

Dawad (David) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth), Shaawal (Saul's) ban (son), amar (spoke), nathan (give) me my ashah (wife/individual woman) Mayakal (Michal), whom I pledged to be married to me for one maah (hundred) iralah (foreskins) of the Palashathay (Philistines).
Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth) shalach (send), and laqach (take / seized) her from her ayash (husband/individual man), even from Palatayaal (Paltiel) the ban (son) of Lawash (Laish).

Her ayash (husband/individual man) yalak (went) with her, weeping as he yalak (went), and achar (other) her to Bacharayam (Bahurim). Then Abanar (Abner) amar (spoke) to him, "yalak (go)! Shawab (turn back / repent)!" And he shawab (turn back / repent).

Abanar (Abner) hayah (came to pass) communication with the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), In thamawal (times) shalashawam (past), you baqash (sought) for Dawad (David) to be malak (king) over you.

Now then ishah (make) it; for Yahawah has amar (spoke) of Dawad (David), amar (spoke), ‘By the yad (hand) of my ibad (servant) Dawad (David), I will yashai (salvation) my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel) out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and out of the yad (hand) of all their ayab (enemy).’

Abanar (Abner) also dabar (word / matter) in the azan (ears) of Banayamayan (Benjamin): and Abanar (Abner) yalak (went) also to dabar (word / matter) in the azan (ears) of Dawad (David) in Chabarawan (Hebron) all that seemed tawab (pleasant/functional) to Yasharaal (Israel), and to the whole bayath (house) of Banayamayan (Benjamin).

So Abanar (Abner) bawaa (come) to Dawad (David) to Chabarawan (Hebron), and isharayam (twenty) ayash (husband/individual man) with him. Dawad (David) ishah (make) Abanar (Abner) and the ayash (husband/individual man) who were with him a mashathah (feast).

Abanar (Abner) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "I will qawam (rise up) and yalak (go), and will qabatz (gather) all Yasharaal (Israel) to my Adawan the malak (king), that they may karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with you, and that you may malak (king) over all that your napash (living being/soul) awah (desires)." Dawad (David) shalach (send) Abanar (Abner) shalach (send); and he yalak (went) in shalawam (peace / safety).

Behold, the ibad (servant) of Dawad (David) and Yawaab (Joab) bawaa (come) from a foray, and bawaa (come) in a rab (great) shalal (spoil) with them: but Abanar (Abner) was not with Dawad (David) in Chabarawan (Hebron); for he had shalach (send) him away, and he was yalak (gone) in shalawam (peace / safety).

When Yawaab (Joab) and all the tzabaa (troop) who was with him bawaa (come) come, they nagad (told) Yawaab (Joab), amar (spoke), Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner) bawaa (come) to the malak (king), and he has shalach (send) him away, and he is yalak (gone) in shalawam (peace / safety).

Then Yawaab (Joab) bawaa (come) to the malak (king), and amar (spoke), What ishah (make) you done? Behold, Abanar (Abner) bawaa (come) to you. Why is it that you have shalach (send) him away, and he is halak (move) yalak (gone)?

You yadai (know) Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner), that he bawaa (come) to pathah (deceive) you, and to yadai (know) your mawatzaa (going) out and your mawabaa (coming) in, and to yadai (know) all that you ishah (make).

When Yawaab (Joab) yatzaa (go out / come out) come out from Dawad (David), he shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) achar (other) Abanar (Abner), and they shawab (turn back / repent) him back from the bawar (well) of Sarah (Sirah); but Dawad (David) didn't yadai (know) it.

When Abanar (Abner) was shawab (turn back / repent) to Chabarawan (Hebron), Yawaab (Joab) natah (took) him aside into the midst of the shair (gate) to dabar (word / matter) with him shalay (quietly), and nakah (struck) him there in the body, so that he mawath (death), for the dam (blood) of Ishahaal (Asahel) his ach (brother/kinsman).

Afterward, when Dawad (David) shamai (hearken / hear) it, he amar (spoke), I and my mamalakah (kingdom) are naqay (guiltless) before Yahawah iwalam (forever) of the dam (blood) of Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner).

Let it chawal (fall) on the raash (head) of Yawaab (Joab), and on all his ab (father) bayath (house). Let there not karath (cut) from the bayath (house) of Yawaab (Joab) one who zawab (flow) an issue, or who is a tzarai (leper), or who chazaq (leans) on a palak (staff), or who napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword), or who chasar (lacks) lacham (bread).

So Yawaab (Joab) and Abayashay (Abishai) his ach (brother/kinsman) harag (killed) Abanar (Abner), because he had harag (killed) their ach (brother/kinsman) Ishahaal (Asahel) at Gabaiwan (Gibeon) in the malachamah (battle).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Yawaab (Joab), and to all the im (people / nation) who were with him, qarai (tear) your clothes, and clothe yourselves with sackcloth, and sapad (mourn) panayam (before) Abanar (Abner). Malak (king) Dawad (David) halak (move) the matah (bier).

They qabar (bury) Abanar (Abner) in Chabarawan (Hebron): and the malak (king) nashaa (lift) up his qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept) at the qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) of Abanar (Abner); and all the im (people / nation) bakah (wept).
The malak (king) qawan (lamented) for Abanar (Abner), and amar (spoke), "Should Abanar (Abner) mawath (death) as a nabal (fool) mawath (death)?

Your yad (hand) were not asar (bound), nor your ragal (feet / foot) nagash (put) into nachashath (fetters). As a man napal (fall / be cast down) panayam (before) the ban (son) of iwal (iniquity), so you napal (fall / be cast down)." All the im (people / nation) bakah (wept) again over him.

Kal (every) the im (people / nation) bawaa (come) to cause Dawad (David) to barah (eat) lacham (bread) while it was yet yawam (day); but Dawad (David) shabai (swear / take oath), amar (spoke), Alahayam ishah (make) so to me, and more also, if I taim (taste) lacham (bread), or anything else, until the shamash (sun) bawaa (come) down.
All the im (people / nation) nakar (took) notice of it, and it yatab (pleased) them; as whatever the malak (king) ishah (make) yatab (pleased) all the im (people / nation).
So all the im (people / nation) and all Yasharaal (Israel) yadai (understood) that yawam (day) that it was not of the malak (king) to mawath (death) Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner).

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), Don't you yadai (know) that there a shar (prince / ruler) and a great gadawal (very great/important/mighty) napal (fall / be cast down) fallen this yawam (day) in Yasharaal (Israel)?

I am this yawam (day) rak (weak), though mashach (anointed) malak (king); and these ayash (husband/individual man) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah) are too qashah (rough / hard) for me. May Yahawah shalam (reward) the evildoer according to his ishah (make).

When Shaawal (Saul's) ban (son) shamai (hearken / hear) that Abanar (Abner) was mawath (death) in Chabarawan (Hebron), his yad (hand) became rapah (feeble), and all the Yasharaal (Israelites) were bahal (troubled).

Shaawal (Saul's) ban (son) hayah (came to pass) shanayam (two) ayash (husband/individual man) who were shar (prince / ruler) of gadawad (bands): the sham (name) of the achad (one) was Bainah (Baanah), and the sham (name) of the other Rakab (Rechab), the ban (son) of Ramawan (Rimmon) the Baarathay (Beerothite), of the ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) (for Baarawath (Beeroth) also is chashab (reckoned) to Banayamayan (Benjamin):
And the Baarathay (Beerothites) barach (fled) to Gathayam (Gittaim), and have lived as foreigners there until this yawam (day)).

Now Yahawanathan (Jonathan), Shaawal (Saul's) ban (son), had a ban (son) who was nakah (lame) of his ragal (feet / foot). He was chamash (five) shanah (years) ban (son) when the shamawaih (news) bawaa (come) of Shaawal (Saul) and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) out of Yazaraial (Jezreel); and his aman (believe / have faith) nashaa (lift) him up, and nawas (fled): and it happened, as she made chapaz (haste) to nawas (flee), that he napal (fall / be cast down), and pasach (became) lame. His sham (name) was Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth).

The ban (son) of Ramawan (Rimmon) the Baarathay (Beerothite), Rakab (Rechab) and Bainah (Baanah), yalak (went), and bawaa (come) about the cham (heat) of the yawam (day) to the bayath (house) of Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth), as he shakab (took) his mashakab (rest) at tzahar (noon).

They bawaa (come) there into the thawak (midst) of the bayath (house), as though they would have laqach (take / seized) chatah (wheat); and they nakah (struck) him in the body: and Rakab (Rechab) and Bainah (Baanah) his ach (brother/kinsman) malat (escaped).

Now when they bawaa (come) into the bayath (house), as he shakab (lay) on his matah (bed) in his bedroom, they nakah (struck) him, and nakah (killed) him, and sawar (beheaded) him, and laqach (take / seized) his raash (head), and yalak (went) by the darak (way) of the irabah (arabah) all layal (night).

They bawaa (come) the raash (head) of Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth) to Dawad (David) to Chabarawan (Hebron), and amar (spoke) to the malak (king), Behold, the raash (head) of Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth), the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul), your ayab (enemy), who baqash (sought) your napash (living being/soul)! Yahawah nathan (give) naqamah (avenged) my Adawan the malak (king) this yawam (day) of Shaawal (Saul), and of his zarai (seed).

Dawad (David) inah (answer / respond) Rakab (Rechab) and Bainah (Baanah) his ach (brother/kinsman), the ban (son) of Ramawan (Rimmon) the Baarathay (Beerothite), and amar (spoke) to them, As Yahawah chay (life), who has padah (redeemed) my napash (living being/soul) out of all tzarah (adversity),

When someone nagad (told) me, ‘Behold, Shaawal (Saul) is mawath (death),’ iyan (eye) to have brought bashar (good) news, I took achaz (hold) of him, and harag (killed) him in Tzaqalag (Ziklag), which was the reward I nathan (give) him for his news.

How much more, when rashai (wicked) ayash (husband/individual man) have harag (slain) a tzadayaq (righteous) ayash (husband/individual man) in his own bayath (house) on his mashakab (bed), shall I not now baqash (require) his dam (blood) of your yad (hand), and bair (take) you away from the aratz (Earth/land)?

Dawad (David) tzawah (commanded) his nair (young) men, and they harag (killed) them, and qatzatz (cut) off their yad (hand) and their ragal (feet / foot), and hanged them up beside the barakah (pool) in Chabarawan (Hebron). But they laqach (take / seized) the raash (head) of Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth), and qabar (bury) it in the qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) of Abanar (Abner) in Chabarawan (Hebron).
Then bawaa (come) all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) to Dawad (David) to Chabarawan (Hebron), and amar (spoke), amar (spoke), Behold, we are your itzam (bone) and your bashar (flesh).

In athamawal (times) past, when Shaawal (Saul) was malak (king) over us, it was you who yatzaa (go out / come out) out and bawaa (come) in Yasharaal (Israel). Yahawah amar (spoke) to you, ‘You shall be raih (shepherd) of my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel), and you shall be nagayad (prince) over Yasharaal (Israel).’

So all the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) bawaa (come) to the malak (king) to Chabarawan (Hebron); and malak (king) Dawad (David) karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with them in Chabarawan (Hebron) panayam (before) Yahawah; and they mashach (anointed) Dawad (David) malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel).
Dawad (David) was shalawashayam (thirty) shanah (years) ban (son) when he began to malak (king), and he malak (king) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years).

In Chabarawan (Hebron) he malak (king) over Yahawadah (Judah) shabai (seven) shanah (years) and shash (six) chadash (month); and in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) he malak (king) thirty-three shanah (years) over all Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah).

The malak (king) and his ayash (husband/individual man) yalak (went) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) against the Yabawasay (Jebusites), the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the aratz (Earth/land), who amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), amar (spoke), "Unless you sawar (take) away the iwar (blind) and the pasach (lame), you shall not bawaa (come) in here;" amar (spoke), Dawad (David) can't bawaa (come) in here.
Nevertheless Dawad (David) lakad (took) the stronghold of Tzayawan (Zion); the same is the iyar (city) of Dawad (David).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) on that yawam (day), "Whoever nakah (strikes) the Yabawasay (Jebusites), let him nagai (get) up to the watercourse, and strike the pasach (lame) and the iwar (blind), who are shanaa (hate) by Dawad (David's) napash (living being/soul)." Therefore they amar (spoke), The iwar (blind) and the pasach (lame) can't bawaa (come) into the bayath (house).
Dawad (David) lived in the stronghold, and qaraa (called) it the iyar (city) of Dawad (David). Dawad (David) banah (built) around from Malawaa (Millo) and inward.
Dawad (David) yalak (grew) greater and halak (move); for Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (troop), was with him.

Chayaram (Hiram) malak (king) of Tzar (Tyre) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to Dawad (David), and araz (cedar) itz (trees), and charash (carpenters), and qayar (masons); and they banah (built) Dawad (David) a bayath (house).

Dawad (David) yadai (perceived) that Yahawah had kawan (established) him malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel), and that he had nashaa (lift) his mamalakah (kingdom) for his im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel's) sake.

Dawad (David) laqach (take / seized) him more payalagash (concubines) and wives out of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), achar (other) he bawaa (come) come from Chabarawan (Hebron); and there were yet ban (son) and bath (daughter) yalad (birth / begot) to Dawad (David).
These are the sham (name) of those who were yalawad (born) to him in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem): Shamawai (Shammua), and Shawabab (Shobab), and Nathan (Nathan), and Shalamah (Solomon),
And Yabachar (Ibhar), and Alayashawai (Elishua), and Napag (Nepheg), and Yapayai (Japhia),
And Alayashamai (Elishama), and Alayadai (Eliada), and Alayapalat (Eliphelet).

When the Palashathay (Philistines) shamai (hearken / hear) that they had mashach (anointed) Dawad (David) malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel), all the Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up to baqash (seek) Dawad (David); and Dawad (David) shamai (hearken / hear) of it, and yarad (went) down to the stronghold.
Now the Palashathay (Philistines) bawaa (come) come and natash (spread) themselves in the imaq (valley) of Rapaa (Rephaim).

Dawad (David) inquired of Yahawah, amar (spoke), "Shall I ilah (go up / offer) up against the Palashathay (Philistines)? Will you nathan (give) them into my yad (hand)?" Yahawah amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), ilah (go up / offer) up; for I will certainly nathan (give) the Palashathay (Philistines) into your yad (hand).

Dawad (David) bawaa (come) to Baal Perazim, and Dawad (David) nakah (struck) them there; and he amar (spoke), "Yahawah has paratz (broken) my ayab (enemy) panayam (before) me, like the paratz (breach) of mayam (Waters)." Therefore he qaraa (called) the sham (name) of that maqawam (place) Baal Perazim.
They izab (left) their itzab (images) there; and Dawad (David) and his ayash (husband/individual man) nashaa (lift) them away.
The Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up yet again, and natash (spread) themselves in the imaq (valley) of Rapaa (Rephaim).
When Dawad (David) inquired of Yahawah, he amar (spoke), You shall not ilah (go up / offer) up. Circle around achar (other) them, and attack them over mawal (against) the bakaa (mulberry) trees.

It shall be, when you shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of marching in the raash (head) of the bakaa (mulberry) trees, that then you shall stir yourself up; for then Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) gone out panayam (before) you to nakah (strike) the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines).
Dawad (David) ishah (make) so, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) him, and nakah (struck) the Palashathay (Philistines) from Gabai (Geba) until you bawaa (come) to Gazar (Gezer).
Dawad (David) again asap (gathered) together all the bachar (chosen) men of Yasharaal (Israel), shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand).

Dawad (David) qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) with all the im (people / nation) who were with him, from Bailayayahawadah (Baale) Judah, to ilah (go up / offer) up from there the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, which is qaraa (called) by the sham (name), even the sham (name) of Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) above the karawab (cherubim).

They rakab (set) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam on a chadash (new) igalah (cart), and nashaa (lift) it out of the bayath (house) of Abayanadab (Abinadab) that was in the Gabaih (hill): and Izaa (Uzzah) and Achayaw (Ahio), the ban (son) of Abayanadab (Abinadab), nahag (drove) the chadash (new) igalah (cart).

They nashaa (lift) it out of the bayath (house) of Abayanadab (Abinadab), which was in the Gabaih (hill), with the arawan (ark) of Alahayam: and Achayaw (Ahio) halak (move) panayam (before) the arawan (ark).

Dawad (David) and all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) shachaq (played) panayam (before) Yahawah with all kinds of instruments made of barawash (fir) itz (wood), and with kanawar (harps), and with stringed instruments, and with tambourines, and with castanets, and with tzalatzal (cymbals).
When they bawaa (come) to the garan (threshing) Nakawan (floor) of Nacon, Izaa (Uzzah) shalach (send) for the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, and achaz (took) hold of it; for the cattle shamat (stumbled).

The ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah was charah (hot with anger) against Izaa (Uzzah); and Alahayam nakah (struck) him there for his shal (error); and there he mawath (death) by the arawan (ark) of Alahayam.
Dawad (David) was charah (hot with anger), because Yahawah had broken paratz (forth) on Izaa (Uzzah); and he qaraa (called) that maqawam (place) Perez Izaa (Uzzah), to this yawam (day).
Dawad (David) was yaraa (fear / be afraid) of Yahawah that yawam (day); and he amar (spoke), How shall the arawan (ark) of Yahawah bawaa (come) to me?

So Dawad (David) would not move the arawan (ark) of Yahawah to be with him in the iyar (city) of Dawad (David); but Dawad (David) natah (carried) it aside into the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom) the Gathay (Gittite).

The arawan (ark) of Yahawah yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom) the Gathay (Gittite) shalawash (three) chadash (month): and Yahawah barak (blessed) Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom), and all his bayath (house).

It was nagad (told) malak (king) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), "Yahawah has barak (blessed) the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom), and all that pertains to him, because of the arawan (ark) of Alahayam." Dawad (David) yalak (went) and ilah (go up / offer) up the arawan (ark) of Alahayam from the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom) into the iyar (city) of Dawad (David) with shamachah (joy).
It was so, that, when those who nashaa (lift) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah had tzaid (gone) shash (six) tzaid (paces), he zabach (sacrificed) an shawar (ox) and a fattened calf.
Dawad (David) karar (danced) panayam (before) Yahawah with all his iz (strength / might / refuge); and Dawad (David) was clothed in a bad (linen) apawad (ephod).

So Dawad (David) and all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up the arawan (ark) of Yahawah with tharawaih (shouting), and with the qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)).

It was so, as the arawan (ark) of Yahawah bawaa (come) into the iyar (city) of Dawad (David), that Mayakal (Michal) the bath (daughter) of Shaawal (Saul) shaqap (looked) out at the chalawan (window), and raah (see) malak (king) Dawad (David) pazaz (leaping) and karar (dancing) panayam (before) Yahawah; and she bazah (despised) him in her lab (heart).

They bawaa (come) in the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, and yatzag (set) it in its maqawam (place), in the thawak (midst) of the ahal (tent) that Dawad (David) had natah (pitched) for it; and Dawad (David) ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilah (offerings) and peace ilah (offerings) panayam (before) Yahawah.

When Dawad (David) kalah (complete / finish) made an end of ilah (go up / offer) the burnt ilah (offering) and the shalam (peace) offerings, he barak (blessed) the im (people / nation) in the sham (name) of Yahawah of tzabaa (troop).

He chalaq (gave) to all the im (people / nation), even among the whole multitude of Yasharaal (Israel), both to ayash (husband/individual man) and ashah (wife/individual woman), to everyone a portion of lacham (bread), dates, and raisins. So all the im (people / nation) departed everyone to his bayath (house).

Then Dawad (David) shawab (turn back / repent) to barak (bless) his bayath (house). Mayakal (Michal) the bath (daughter) of Shaawal (Saul) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) Dawad (David), and amar (spoke), How kabad (glorious) the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) was today, who galah (uncovered) himself today in the iyan (eye) of the handmaids of his ibad (servant), as achad (one) of the rayaq (vain) fellows galah (shamelessly) galah (uncovers) himself!

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Mayakal (Michal), It panayam (was) before Yahawah, who bachar (chose) me above your ab (father), and above all his bayath (house), to tzawah (appoint) me nagayad (prince) over the im (people / nation) of Yahawah, over Yasharaal (Israel). Therefore will I celebrate panayam (before) Yahawah.
I will be yet more qalal (vile) than zaath (this), and will be shapal (base) in my own iyan (eye). But of the handmaids of whom you have amar (spoke), they shall honor me.
Mayakal (Michal) the bath (daughter) of Shaawal (Saul) had no yalad (birth / begot) to the yawam (day) of her mawath (death).
It happened, when the malak (king) lived in his bayath (house), and Yahawah had given him nawach (rest) from all his ayab (enemy) all around,

That the malak (king) amar (spoke) to Nathan (Nathan) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), raah (see) now, I yashab (inhabit/dwell) in a bayath (house) of araz (cedar), but the arawan (ark) of Alahayam yashab (inhabit/dwell) thawak (midst) yarayaih (curtains).
Nathan (Nathan) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), yalak (go), ishah (make) all that is in your labab (heart); for Yahawah is with you.
It happened the same layal (night), that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Nathan (Nathan), amar (spoke),
Yalak (go) and amar (spoke) my ibad (servant) Dawad (David), ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, “Shall you banah (build) me a bayath (house) for me to yashab (inhabit/dwell) in?

For I have not lived in a bayath (house) since the yawam (day) that I ilah (go up / offer) up the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) out of Matzarayam (Egypt), even to this yawam (day), but have halak (move) around in a ahal (tent) and in a mashakan (tabernacle).

In all halak (move) in which I have walked with all the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), did I dabar (word / matter) a dabar (word / matter) to any of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), whom I tzawah (commanded) to be raih (shepherd) of my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), ‘Why have you not banah (built) me a bayath (house) of araz (cedar)?’”’

Now therefore you shall amar (spoke) my ibad (servant) Dawad (David) this, ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaa (troop), “I laqach (take / seized) you from the tzaan (sheep) pen, from achar (other) the tzaan (sheep), that you should be nagayad (prince) over my im (people / nation), over Yasharaal (Israel).

I have been with you wherever you halak (move), and have karath (cut) off all your ayab (enemy) from panayam (before) you. I will ishah (make) you a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) sham (name), like the sham (name) of the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) ones who are in the aratz (Earth/land).

I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) a maqawam (place) for my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel), and will natai (plant) them, that they may shakan (dwell) in their own place, and be ragaz (moved) no more; neither shall the ban (son) of iwal (wickedness) inah (oppress / afflict) them any more, as at the raashawan (first),

And as from the yawam (day) that I tzawah (commanded) shapat (judges) to be over my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel). I will cause you to nawach (rest) from all your ayab (enemy). Moreover Yahawah nagad (tells) you that Yahawah will make you a bayath (house).

When your yawam (day) are malaa (fulfilled), and you shall sleep with your ab (father), I will qawam (rise up) up your zarai (seed) achar (other) you, who shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out of your maih (bowels), and I will kawan (establish) his mamalakah (kingdom).
He shall banah (build) a bayath (house) for my sham (name), and I will kawan (establish) the kasaa (throne) of his mamalakah (kingdom) iwalam (forever).

I will be his ab (father), and he shall be my ban (son). If he commits iwah (iniquity), I will yakach (chasten) him with the shabat (rod) of ban (son), and with the nagai (stripes) of the ban (son) of adam (men);
But my loving chasad (grace) shall not sawar (depart) from him, as I sawar (took) it from Shaawal (Saul), whom I sawar (put) away panayam (before) you.
Your bayath (house) and your mamalakah (kingdom) shall be made sure iwalam (forever) panayam (before) you. Your kasaa (throne) shall be kawan (established) iwalam (forever).”’
According to all these dabar (word / matter), and according to all this chazayawan (vision), so Nathan (Nathan) dabar (word / matter) to Dawad (David).

Then Dawad (David) the malak (king) bawaa (come) in, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) panayam (before) Yahawah; and he amar (spoke), Who am I, Adanay Yahawah, and what is my bayath (house), that you bawaa (come) brought me thus far?

This was yet a qatan (small/young/least) thing in your iyan (eye), Adanay Yahawah; but you have dabar (word / matter) also of your ibad (servant) bayath (house) for a rachawaq (great) while to come; and this after the thawarah (Thawarah/(Torah) - Instruction) of adam (men), Adanay Yahawah!
What more can Dawad (David) dabar (word / matter) to you? For you yadai (know) your ibad (servant), Adanay Yahawah.
For your dabar (word / matter) sake, and according to your own lab (heart), you ishah (make) worked all this gadawalah (greatness), to make your ibad (servant) yadai (know) it.

Therefore you are gadal (great), Yahawah Alahayam. For there is none like you, neither is there any Alahayam zawalah (besides) you, according to all that we have shamai (hearken / hear) with our azan (ears).

What achad (one) gaway (nation / people) in the aratz (Earth/land) is like your im (people / nation), even like Yasharaal (Israel), whom Alahayam halak (move) to padah (redeem) to himself for a im (people / nation), and to shawam (place / establish / appoint) himself a sham (name), and to ishah (make) gadawalah (great) things for you, and awesome things for your aratz (Earth/land), panayam (before) your im (people / nation), whom you padah (redeem) to yourself out of Matzarayam (Egypt), from the gaway (nation / people) and their Alahayam?
You kawan (established) for yourself your im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel) to be a im (people / nation) to you iwalam (forever); and you, Yahawah, hayah (came to pass) their Alahayam.

Now, Yahawah Alahayam, the dabar (word / matter) that you have dabar (word / matter) concerning your ibad (servant), and concerning his bayath (house), qawam (rise up) it iwalam (forever), and ishah (make) as you have dabar (word / matter).

Let your sham (name) be gadal (magnified) iwalam (forever), amar (spoke), ‘Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) is Alahayam over Yasharaal (Israel); and the bayath (house) of your ibad (servant) Dawad (David) shall be kawan (established) panayam (before) you.’

For you, Yahawah of tzabaa (troop), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), have galah (revealed) to your ibad (servant), amar (spoke), ‘I will banah (build) you a bayath (house).’ Therefore your ibad (servant) matzaa (has) found in his lab (heart) to palal (pray) this thapalah (prayer) to you.
Now, O Adanay Yahawah, you are Alahayam, and your dabar (word / matter) are amath (truth), and you have dabar (word / matter) this tawab (pleasant/functional) thing to your ibad (servant).

Now therefore let it yaal (please) you to barak (bless) the bayath (house) of your ibad (servant), that it may continue iwalam (forever) panayam (before) you; for you, Adanay Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it. Let the bayath (house) of your ibad (servant) be barak (blessed) iwalam (forever) with your barakah (blessing).

Achar (other) this it happened that Dawad (David) nakah (struck) the Palashathay (Philistines), and kanai (subdued) them: and Dawad (David) laqach (take / seized) the bridle of the mother city out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines).

He nakah (struck) Mawaab (Moab), and madad (measured) them with the chabal (line), making them to shakab (lie) down on the aratz (Earth/land); and he madad (measured) shanayam (two) chabal (lines) to put to mawath (death), and one malaa (full) chabal (line) to chayah (keep) alive. The Mawaab (Moabites) became ibad (servant) to Dawad (David), and nashaa (lift) tribute.

Dawad (David) nakah (struck) also Hadadaizar (Hadadezer) the ban (son) of Rachab (Rehob), malak (king) of Tzawabaa (Zobah), as he yalak (went) to shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand) at the nahar (river).

Dawad (David) lakad (took) from him one alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) horsemen, and isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) footmen: and Dawad (David) hamstrung all the rakab (chariot) horses, but yathar (reserved) of them for one maah (hundred) rakab (chariots).

When the Aram (Syrians) of Damashaq (Damascus) bawaa (come) to izar (help) Hadadaizar (Hadadezer) malak (king) of Tzawabaa (Zobah), Dawad (David) nakah (struck) of the Aram (Syrians) shanayam (two) and isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man).

Then Dawad (David) shawam (place / establish / appoint) natzayab (garrisons) in Aram (Syria) of Damashaq (Damascus); and the Aram (Syrians) became ibad (servant) to Dawad (David), and nashaa (lift) tribute. Yahawah gave yashai (salvation) to Dawad (David) wherever he halak (move).
Dawad (David) laqach (take / seized) the shalat (shields) of zahab (gold) that were on the ibad (servant) of Hadadaizar (Hadadezer), and bawaa (come) them to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).
From Batach (Betah) and from Barawathah (Berothai), iyar (cities) of Hadadaizar (Hadadezer), malak (king) Dawad (David) laqach (take / seized) maad (exceeding) much nachashath (brass).
When Thaiw (Toi) malak (king) of Chamath (Hamath) shamai (hearken / hear) that Dawad (David) had nakah (struck) all the chayal (army) of Hadadaizar (Hadadezer),

Then Thaiw (Toi) shalach (send) Yawaram (Joram) his ban (son) to malak (king) Dawad (David), to shaal (greet) him, and to barak (bless) him, because he had lacham (fought) against Hadadaizar (Hadadezer) and nakah (struck) him: for Hadadaizar (Hadadezer) had wars with Thaiw (Toi). Joram brought with him kalay (vessels) of kasap (silver), and kalay (vessels) of zahab (gold), and kalay (vessels) of nachashath (brass):

Malak (king) Dawad (David) also qadash (set apart/make holy) these to Yahawah, with the kasap (silver) and zahab (gold) that he qadash (set apart/make holy) of all the gaway (nation / people) which he kabash (subdued);

Of Aram (Syria), and of Mawaab (Moab), and of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon), and of the Palashathay (Philistines), and of Imalaq (Amalek), and of the shalal (spoil) of Hadadaizar (Hadadezer), ban (son) of Rachab (Rehob), malak (king) of Tzawabaa (Zobah).
Dawad (David) earned a reputation when he shawab (turn back / repent) from nakah (smiting) the Aram (Syrians) in the gayaa (valley) of malach (salt), even eighteen alap (thousand) men.

He shawam (place / establish / appoint) natzayab (garrisons) in Adam (Edom); throughout all Adam (Edom) shawam (place / establish / appoint) he natzayab (garrisons), and all the Adam (Edomites) became ibad (servant) to Dawad (David). Yahawah gave yashai (salvation) to Dawad (David) wherever he halak (move).
Dawad (David) malak (king) over all Yasharaal (Israel); and Dawad (David) ishah (make) tzadaqah (righteousness) and mashapat (righteousness) to all his im (people / nation).
Yawaab (Joab) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah) was over the tzabaa (troop); and Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the ban (son) of Achayalawad (Ahilud) was zakar (remembrance/memory);
And Tzadawaq (Zadok) the ban (son) of Achayatawab (Ahitub), and Achayamalak (Ahimelech) the ban (son) of Abayathar (Abiathar), were kahan (priest); and Sharayah (Seraiah) was sapar (book);
And Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) was over the Karathay (Cherethites) and the Palathay (Pelethites); and Dawad (David's) ban (son) were kahan (priest) ministers.
Dawad (David) amar (spoke), Is there yet any who is yathar (left) of the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul), that I may show him chasad (grace) for Yahawanathan (Jonathan's) sake?

There was of the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul) a ibad (servant) whose sham (name) was Tzayabaa (Ziba), and they qaraa (called) him to Dawad (David); and the malak (king) amar (spoke) to him, "Are you Tzayabaa (Ziba)?" He amar (spoke), Your ibad (servant) is he.

The malak (king) amar (spoke), "Is there not yet any of the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul), that I may show the chasad (grace) of Alahayam to him?" Tzayabaa (Ziba) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), Yahawanathan (Jonathan) has yet a ban (son), who is nakah (lame) of his ragal (feet / foot).

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to him, "ayapah (where) is he?" Tzayabaa (Ziba) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), Behold, he is in the bayath (house) of Makayar (Machir) the ban (son) of Imayaal (Ammiel), Laadabar (in) Lo Debar.
Then malak (king) Dawad (David) shalach (send), and laqach (take / seized) him out of the bayath (house) of Makayar (Machir) the ban (son) of Imayaal (Ammiel), Laadabar (from) Lo Debar.

Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth), the ban (son) of Yahawanathan (Jonathan), the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul), bawaa (come) to Dawad (David), and napal (fall / be cast down) on his panayam (face), and showed respect. Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth)." He amar (spoke), Behold, your ibad (servant)!

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to him, Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of him; for I will ishah (make) show you chasad (grace) for Yahawanathan (Jonathan) your ab (father) sake, and will shawab (turn back / repent) to you all the shadah (land) of Shaawal (Saul) your ab (father). You shall akal (eat) lacham (bread) at my shalachan (table) continually.
He shachah (bowed) down, and amar (spoke), What is your ibad (servant), that you should panah (look) on such a mawath (death) kalab (dog) as I am?

Then the malak (king) qaraa (called) to Tzayabaa (Ziba), Shaawal (Saul's) nair (servant), and amar (spoke) to him, "All that hayah (came to pass) to Shaawal (Saul) and to all his bayath (house) nathan (give) I given to your adawan (master / lord) ban (son).

You shall ibad (servant) the adamah (land) for him, you, and your ban (son), and your ibad (servant); and you shall bawaa (come) in the harvest, that your adawan (master / lord) ban (son) may have lacham (bread) to akal (eat): but Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth) your adawan (master / lord) ban (son) shall akal (eat) lacham (bread) thamayad (always) at my shalachan (table)." Now Tzayabaa (Ziba) had chamash (fifteen) ban (son) and isharayam (twenty) ibad (servant).

Then Tzayabaa (Ziba) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "According to all that my Adawan the malak (king) tzawah (commands) his ibad (servant), so your shall ibad (servant) ishah (make)." So Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth) akal (eat) at the king's shalachan (table), like achad (one) of the malak (king) ban (son).

Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth) had a qatan (small/young/least) ban (son), whose sham (name) was Mayakaa (Mica). All that lived in the bayath (house) of Tzayabaa (Ziba) were ibad (servant) to Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth).
So Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth) lived in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); for he akal (eat) continually at the malak (king) shalachan (table). He was pasach (lame) in shanayam (two) his ragal (feet / foot).
It happened achar (other) this, that the malak (king) of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) mawath (death), and Chanawan (Hanun) his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "I will show chasad (grace) to Chanawan (Hanun) the ban (son) of Nachash (Nahash), as his ab (father) showed chasad (grace) to me." So Dawad (David) shalach (send) by his ibad (servant) to nacham (turn away / repent) him concerning his ab (father). Dawad (David's) ibad (servant) bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land) of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon).

But the shar (prince / ruler) of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) amar (spoke) to Chanawan (Hanun) their Adawan, Do you iyan (eye) that Dawad (David) honors your ab (father), in that he has shalach (send) comforters to you? Hasn't Dawad (David) shalach (send) his ibad (servant) to you to chaqar (search) the iyar (city), and to ragal (spy) it out, and to hapak (overthrow) it?

So Chanawan (Hanun) laqach (take / seized) Dawad (David's) ibad (servant), and galach (shaved) off the one chatzay (half) of their zaqan (beards), and karath (cut) off their madaw (garments) in the chatzay (middle), even to their shathah (drinks), and shalach (send) them away.

When they nagad (told) it to Dawad (David), he shalach (send) to qaraah (meet) them; for the ayash (husband/individual man) were maad (greatly) kalam (ashamed). The malak (king) amar (spoke), Wait at Yarayachaw (Jericho) until your zaqan (beards) have tzamach (grown), and then shawab (turn back / repent).

When the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) raah (see) that they were become baash (odious) to Dawad (David), the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) shalach (send) and shakar (hired) the Aram (Syrians) of Bayatharachawab (Beth) Rehob, and the Aram (Syrians) of Tzawabaa (Zobah), isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) footmen, and the malak (king) Maikah (of) Maacah with one alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man), and the ayash (husband/individual man) of Tob ishar (-teen) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man).
When Dawad (David) shamai (hearken / hear) of it, he shalach (send) Yawaab (Joab), and all the tzabaa (troop) of the gabawar (mighty) men.

The ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and put the malachamah (battle) in irak (array) at the entrance of the shair (gate): and the Aram (Syrians) of Tzawabaa (Zobah) and of Rachab (Rehob), and the Maikah (men) of Tob and Maacah, were by themselves in the shadah (field).

Now when Yawaab (Joab) raah (see) that the malachamah (battle) panayam (was) set panayam (against) him before and achawar (behind), he bachar (chose) of all the choice men of Yasharaal (Israel), and irak (put) them in array qaraah (against) the Aram (Syrians):

The yathar (rest) of the im (people / nation) he nathan (give) into the yad (hand) of Abayashay (Abishai) his ach (brother/kinsman); and he irak (put) them in array qaraah (against) the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon).

He amar (spoke), If the Aram (Syrians) are too chazaq (strong) for me, then you shall chazaq (help) me; but if the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) are too chazaq (strong) for you, then I will halak (move) and yashai (salvation) you.
Be courageous, and let us be chazaq (strong) for our im (people / nation), and for the iyar (cities) of our Alahayam; and Yahawah ishah (make) that which seems tawab (pleasant/functional) to him.
So Yawaab (Joab) and the im (people / nation) who were with him nagash (drew) near to the malachamah (battle) against the Aram (Syrians): and they nawas (fled) panayam (before) him.

When the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) raah (see) that the Aram (Syrians) had nawas (fled), they likewise nawas (fled) panayam (before) Abayashay (Abishai), and bawaa (come) into the iyar (city). Then Yawaab (Joab) shawab (turn back / repent) from the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon), and bawaa (come) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).
When the Aram (Syrians) raah (see) that they were defeated by Yasharaal (Israel), they asap (gathered) themselves yachad (together).

Hadadezer shalach (send), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out the Aram (Syrians) who were ibar (beyond) the nahar (river): and they bawaa (come) to Chayalam (Helam), with Shawabak (Shobach) the shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop) of Hadadezer at their panayam (head).

It was nagad (told) Dawad (David); and he asap (gathered) all Yasharaal (Israel) asap (together), and ibar (pass over/through) over the Yaradan (Jordan), and bawaa (come) to Chayalam (Helam). The Aram (Syrians) irak (set) themselves in array qaraah (against) Dawad (David), and lacham (fought) with him.

The Aram (Syrians) nawas (fled) panayam (before) Yasharaal (Israel); and Dawad (David) harag (killed) of the Aram (Syrians) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) charioteers, and arabaiyam (forty) alap (thousand) horsemen, and nakah (struck) Shawabak (Shobach) the shar (prince / ruler) of their tzabaa (troop), so that he mawath (death) there.

When all the malak (king) who were ibad (servant) to Hadadezer raah (see) that they were defeated panayam (before) Yasharaal (Israel), they made shalam (peace) with Yasharaal (Israel), and ibad (servant) them. So the Aram (Syrians) yaraa (fear / be afraid) to yashai (salvation) the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon) any more.

It happened, at the thashawabah (return) of the shanah (year), at the ith (time) when malak (king) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, that Dawad (David) shalach (send) Yawaab (Joab), and his ibad (servant) with him, and all Yasharaal (Israel); and they shachath (destroyed) the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon), and tzawar (besieged) Rabah (Rabbah). But Dawad (David) stayed at Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

It happened at irab (evening), that Dawad (David) qawam (rise up) from off his mashakab (bed), and halak (move) on the gag (roof) of the malak (king) bayath (house): and from the gag (roof) he raah (see) a ashah (wife/individual woman) rachatz (bathing); and the ashah (wife/individual woman) was very tawab (pleasant/functional) to maraah (look) on.

Dawad (David) shalach (send) and darash (inquired) after the ashah (wife/individual woman). One amar (spoke), Isn't this Bathashabai (Bathsheba), the bath (daughter) of Alayaim (Eliam), the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite)?

Dawad (David) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah), and laqach (take / seized) her; and she bawaa (come) in to him, and he shakab (lay) with her (for she was qadash (set apart/make holy) from her tamaah (uncleanness)); and she shawab (turn back / repent) to her bayath (house).
The ashah (wife/individual woman) harah (conceived); and she shalach (send) and nagad (told) Dawad (David), and amar (spoke), I am with harah (child).
Dawad (David) shalach (send) to Yawaab (Joab), "shalach (send) me Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite)." Yawaab (Joab) shalach (send) Awarayah (Uriah) to Dawad (David).

When Awarayah (Uriah) bawaa (come) come to him, Dawad (David) shaal (asked) of him how Yawaab (Joab) shalawam (peace / safety), and how the im (people / nation) shalawam (peace / safety), and how the malachamah (war) shalawam (peace / safety).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Awarayah (Uriah), "yarad (go) down to your bayath (house), and rachatz (wash) your ragal (feet / foot)." Awarayah (Uriah) departed out of the malak (king) bayath (house), and a mashaath (gift) from the malak (king) was sent achar (other) him.
But Awarayah (Uriah) shakab (slept) at the pathach (door) of the malak (king) bayath (house) with all the ibad (servant) of his Adawan, and didn't yarad (go) down to his bayath (house).

When they had nagad (told) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), "Awarayah (Uriah) didn't yarad (go) down to his bayath (house)," Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Awarayah (Uriah), Haven't you bawaa (come) from a darak (journey)? Why didn't you yarad (go) down to your bayath (house)?

Awarayah (Uriah) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), The arawan (ark), Yasharaal (Israel), and Yahawadah (Judah), are staying in sakah (tents); and my Adawan Yawaab (Joab), and the ibad (servant) of my Adawan, are chanah (encamped) in the panayam (open) shadah (field). Shall I then bawaa (come) into my bayath (house) to akal (eat) and to shathah (drinks), and to shakab (lie) with my ashah (wife/individual woman)? As you chay (life), and as your napash (living being/soul) chay (life), I will not ishah (make) this thing!

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Awarayah (Uriah), "Stay here today also, and machar (tomorrow) I will shalach (send) you depart." So Awarayah (Uriah) stayed in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) that yawam (day), and the next yawam (day).

When Dawad (David) had qaraa (called) him, he akal (eat) and shathah (drinks) panayam (before) him; and he shakar (made) him drunk. At irab (evening), he yatzaa (go out / come out) out to shakab (lie) on his mashakab (bed) with the ibad (servant) of his Adawan, but didn't yarad (go) down to his bayath (house).
It happened in the baqar (morning), that Dawad (David) kathab (wrote) a sapar (book / scribed document) to Yawaab (Joab), and shalach (send) it by the yad (hand) of Awarayah (Uriah).

He kathab (wrote) in the sapar (book / scribed document), amar (spoke), Send Awarayah (Uriah) to the panayam (forefront) of the chazaq (hottest) malachamah (battle), and retreat from him, that he may be nakah (struck), and mawath (death).

It happened, when Yawaab (Joab) shamar (keep/guard) watch on the iyar (city), that he nathan (give) Awarayah (Uriah) to the maqawam (place) where he yadai (knew) that chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) yadai (men) were.

The ayash (husband/individual man) of the iyar (city) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and lacham (fought) with Yawaab (Joab). Some of the im (people / nation) napal (fall / be cast down), even of the ibad (servant) of Dawad (David); and Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite) mawath (death) also.
Then Yawaab (Joab) shalach (send) and nagad (told) Dawad (David) all the things concerning the malachamah (war);

And he tzawah (commanded) the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah), amar (spoke), When you kalah (complete / finish) finished dabar (word / matter) all the things concerning the malachamah (war) to the malak (king),

It shall be that, if the malak (king) chamah (wrath) arise, and he asks you, ‘Why did you nagash (go) so near to the iyar (city) to lacham (fight)? Didn't you yadai (know) that they would yarah (shoot) from the chawamah (wall)?

Who nakah (struck) Abayamalak (Abimelech) the ban (son) of Yarabashath (Jerubbesheth)? Didn't a ashah (wife/individual woman) shalak (cast) an upper rakab (millstone) on him from the chawamah (wall), so that he mawath (death) at Thabatz (Thebez)? Why did you nagash (go) so near the chawamah (wall)?’ Then you shall amar (spoke), ‘Your ibad (servant) Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite) is mawath (death) also.’
So the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) yalak (went), and bawaa (come) and showed Dawad (David) all that Yawaab (Joab) had shalach (send) him for.

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), The ayash (husband/individual man) gabar (prevailed) against us, and yatzaa (go out / come out) out to us into the shadah (field), and we were on them even to the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate).

The shooters yarah (shot) at your ibad (servant) from off the chawamah (wall); and some of the malak (king) ibad (servant) are mawath (death), and your ibad (servant) Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite) is mawath (death) also.

Then Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah), Thus you shall amar (spoke) Yawaab (Joab), ‘Don't let this thing displease you, for the charab (sword) akal (eat) one as zah (this/that/these) as another. Make your malachamah (battle) chazaq (stronger) against the iyar (city), and haras (overthrow) it.’ Chazaq (encourage) him.

When the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Awarayah (Uriah) shamai (hearken / hear) that Awarayah (Uriah) her ayash (husband/individual man) was mawath (death), she made lamentation for her bail (husband).

When the abal (mourning) was past, Dawad (David) shalach (send) and asap (took) her home to his bayath (house), and she became his ashah (wife/individual woman), and yalad (birth / begot) him a ban (son). But the thing that Dawad (David) ishah (make) done displeased Yahawah.

Yahawah shalach (send) Nathan (Nathan) to Dawad (David). He bawaa (come) to him, and amar (spoke) to him, There were shanayam (two) ayash (husband/individual man) in achad (one) iyar (city); the achad (one) ishayar (rich), and the other rawash (poor).
The ishayar (rich) maad (man) had very many tzaan (flocks) and baqar (morning),

But the rawash (poor) achad (one) had nothing, except one qatan (small/young/least) ewe kabashah (lamb), which he had bought and raised. It grew up yachad (together) with him, and with his ban (son). It akal (eat) of his own food, shathah (drinks) of his own kawas (cup), and shakab (lay) in his chayaq (bosom), and was to him like a bath (daughter).

A traveler bawaa (come) to the ishayar (rich) ayash (husband/individual man), and he chamal (spared) to laqach (take / seized) of his own tzaan (flock) and of his own baqar (morning), to ishah (make) for the arach (wayfaring) man who bawaa (come) come to him, but laqach (take / seized) the rawash (poor) ayash (husband/individual man) kabashah (lamb), and ishah (make) it for the ayash (husband/individual man) who bawaa (come) come to him.

Dawad (David's) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was maad (greatly) charah (hot with anger) against the ayash (husband/individual man), and he amar (spoke) to Nathan (Nathan), As Yahawah chay (life), the ayash (husband/individual man) who ishah (make) done this is ban (son) to mawath (death)!

He shall shalam (restore) the kabashah (lamb) arabaithayam (fourfold), iqab (award / effect after the cause) he ishah (make) this thing, and iqab (award / effect after the cause) he chamal (had) no pity!

Nathan (Nathan) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), You are the ayash (husband/individual man). This is what Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke): ‘I mashach (anointed) you malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel), and I natzal (delivered) you out of the yad (hand) of Shaawal (Saul).

I nathan (give) you your adawan (master / lord) bayath (house), and your adawan (master / lord) wives into your chayaq (bosom), and nathan (give) you the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) and of Yahawadah (Judah); and if that would have been too mait (little), I would have yasap (added) to you many more such things.

Why have you bazah (despised) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, to ishah (make) that which is rai (evil) in his iyan (eye)? You have nakah (struck) Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite) with the charab (sword), and have laqach (take / seized) his ashah (wife/individual woman) to be your ashah (wife/individual woman), and have harag (slain) him with the charab (sword) of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon).

Now therefore the charab (sword) will never sawar (depart) from your bayath (house), iqab (award / effect after the cause) you have bazah (despised) me, and have laqach (take / seized) the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite) to be your ashah (wife/individual woman).’

This is what Yahawah amar (spoke): ‘Behold, I will qawam (rise up) up rai (evil) against you out of your own bayath (house); and I will laqach (take / seized) your wives before your iyan (eye), and nathan (give) them to your neighbor, and he will shakab (lie) with your wives in the iyan (eye) of this shamash (sun).
For you ishah (make) it secretly, but I will ishah (make) this thing before all Yasharaal (Israel), and before the shamash (sun).’

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Nathan (Nathan), "I have chataa (sinned) against Yahawah." Nathan (Nathan) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), Yahawah also ibar (pass over/through) put away your chataah (sin). You will not mawath (death).

However, dabar (word / matter) by this deed you have given naatz (great) occasion to yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) ayab (enemy) to naatz (blaspheme), the ban (son) also who is yalawad (born) to you shall mawath (death) mawath (death).

Nathan (Nathan) departed to his bayath (house). Yahawah nagap (struck) the yalad (birth / begot) that Awarayah (Uriah's) ashah (wife/individual woman) yalad (birth / begot) to Dawad (David), and it was very anash (sick).
Dawad (David) therefore baqash (begged) Alahayam for the nair (child); and Dawad (David) tzawam (fasted), and bawaa (come) in, and shakab (lay) all lawan (night) on the aratz (Earth/land).
The zaqan (elders) of his bayath (house) qawam (rise up) beside him, to qawam (rise up) him up from the aratz (Earth/land): but he would not, neither did he barah (eat) lacham (bread) with them.

It happened on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), that the yalad (birth / begot) mawath (death). The ibad (servant) of Dawad (David) yaraa (fear / be afraid) to nagad (tell) him that the yalad (birth / begot) was mawath (death); for they amar (spoke), Behold, while the yalad (birth / begot) was yet chay (life), we amar (spoke) to him, and he didn't shamai (hearken / hear) to our qawal (sound / voice).
