How will he then rai (harm) himself, if we amar (spoke) him that the yalad (birth / begot) is mawath (death)?

But when Dawad (David) raah (see) that his ibad (servant) were lachash (whispering) together, Dawad (David) bayan (between) that the yalad (birth / begot) was mawath (death); and Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), "Is the yalad (birth / begot) mawath (death)?" They amar (spoke), He is mawath (death).

Then Dawad (David) qawam (rise up) from the aratz (Earth/land), and rachatz (washed), and sawak (anointed) himself, and chalap (changed) his shamalah (clothing); and he bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and shachah (worshiped): then he bawaa (come) to his own bayath (house); and when he shaal (required), they shawam (place / establish / appoint) lacham (bread) before him, and he akal (eat).

Then his ibad (servant) amar (spoke) to him, dabar (word / matter) is this that you ishah (make) done? You tzawam (fasted) and bakah (wept) for the yalad (birth / begot) while he was chay (life); but when the yalad (birth / begot) was mawath (death), you qawam (rise up) up and akal (eat) lacham (bread).

He amar (spoke), While the yalad (birth / begot) was yet chay (life), I tzawam (fasted) and bakah (wept); for I amar (spoke), ‘Who yadai (knows) whether Yahawah will not be gracious to me, that the yalad (birth / begot) may chay (life)?’
But now he is mawath (death), why should I tzawam (fast)? Yakal (can) I shawab (turn back / repent) him back again? I shall halak (move) to him, but he will not shawab (turn back / repent) to me.

Dawad (David) nacham (turn away / repent) Bathashabai (Bathsheba) his ashah (wife/individual woman), and bawaa (come) in to her, and shakab (lay) with her. She yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son), and he qaraa (called) his sham (name) Shalamah (Solomon). Yahawah ahab (love) him;
And he shalach (send) by the yad (hand) of Nathan (Nathan) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy); and he sham (name) him Yadayadayah (Jedidiah), for yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) sake.
Now Yawaab (Joab) lacham (fought) against Rabah (Rabbah) of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon), and lakad (took) the malawakah (royal) iyar (city).

Yawaab (Joab) shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to Dawad (David), and amar (spoke), I have lacham (fought) against Rabah (Rabbah). Yes, I have lakad (taken) the iyar (city) of mayam (Waters).

Now therefore asap (gather) the yathar (rest) of the im (people / nation) asap (together), and chanah (encamp) against the iyar (city), and lakad (take) it; lest I lakad (take) the iyar (city), and it be qaraa (called) after my sham (name).
Dawad (David) asap (gathered) all the im (people / nation) asap (together), and yalak (went) to Rabah (Rabbah), and lacham (fought) against it, and lakad (took) it.

He laqach (take / seized) the itarah (crown) of their malak (king) from off his raash (head); and its mashaqal (weight) was a kakar (talent) of zahab (gold), and in it were yaqar (precious) aban (stone); and it was set on Dawad (David's) raash (head). He yatzaa (go out / come out) out the shalal (spoil) of the iyar (city), maad (exceeding) much.

He yatzaa (go out / come out) out the im (people / nation) who were therein, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them under magarah (saws), and under barazal (iron) picks, and under magazarah (axes) of barazal (iron), and ibar (pass over/through) them pass through the brick kiln: and he ishah (make) so to all the iyar (cities) of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon). Dawad (David) and all the im (people / nation) shawab (turn back / repent) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

It happened achar (other) this, that Abayashalawam (Absalom) the ban (son) of Dawad (David) had a yapah (beautiful) achawath (sister), whose sham (name) was Thamar (Tamar); and Amanawan (Amnon) the ban (son) of Dawad (David) ahab (love) her.

Amanawan (Amnon) was so troubled that he chalah (afflict) sick because of his achawath (sister) Thamar (Tamar); for she was a bathawalah (virgin); and it seemed palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) to Amanawan (Amnon) to ishah (make) anything to her.

But Amanawan (Amnon) had a rai (neigbor/another person), whose sham (name) was Yawanadab (Jonadab), the ban (son) of Shamaih (Shimeah), Dawad (David's) ach (brother/kinsman); and Yawanadab (Jonadab) was a very subtle ayash (husband/individual man).

He amar (spoke) to him, "Why, ban (son) of the malak (king), are you so sad from baqar (morning) to baqar (morning)? Won't you nagad (tell) me?" Amanawan (Amnon) amar (spoke) to him, I ahab (love) Thamar (Tamar), my ach (brother/kinsman) Abayashalawam (Absalom's) achawath (sister).

Yahawanadab (Jonadab) amar (spoke) to him, shakab (lay) down on your mashakab (bed), and pretend to be chalah (afflict). When your ab (father) bawaa (come) to raah (see) you, amar (spoke) him, ‘Please let my achawath (sister) Thamar (Tamar) bawaa (come) and give me lacham (bread) to eat, and ishah (make) the lacham (food) in my iyan (eye), that I may raah (see) it, and akal (eat) it from her yad (hand).’

So Amanawan (Amnon) shakab (lay) down and faked being chalah (afflict). When the malak (king) bawaa (come) to raah (see) him, Amanawan (Amnon) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), Please let my achawath (sister) Thamar (Tamar) bawaa (come), and labab (make) me a shanayam (two) of labayabah (cakes) in my iyan (eye), that I may barah (eat) from her yad (hand).
Then Dawad (David) shalach (send) bayath (house) to Thamar (Tamar), amar (spoke), yalak (go) now to your ach (brother/kinsman) Amanawan (Amnon's) bayath (house), and ishah (make) food for him.

So Thamar (Tamar) yalak (went) to her ach (brother/kinsman) Amanawan (Amnon's) bayath (house); and he was shakab (laid) down. She laqach (take / seized) batzaq (dough), and lawash (kneaded) it, and labab (made) cakes in his iyan (eye), and bashal (baked) the labab (cakes).

She laqach (take / seized) the masharath (pan), and yatzaq (poured) them out panayam (before) him; but he maan (refused) to akal (eat). Amanawan (Amnon) amar (spoke), "Have all ayash (husband/individual man) leave me." Every ayash (husband/individual man) yatzaa (go out / come out) out from him.

Amanawan (Amnon) amar (spoke) to Thamar (Tamar), "bawaa (come) the food into the room, that I may barah (eat) from your yad (hand)." Thamar (Tamar) laqach (take / seized) the labayabah (cakes) which she ishah (make) made, and bawaa (come) them into the room to Amanawan (Amnon) her ach (brother/kinsman).
When she had nagash (brought) them near to him to akal (eat), he chazaq (took) hold of her, and amar (spoke) to her, bawaa (come), shakab (lie) with me, my achawath (sister)!
She amar (spoke) him, No, my ach (brother/kinsman), do not inah (oppress / afflict) me! For no such thing ought to be ishah (make) in Yasharaal (Israel). Don't you ishah (make) this nabalah (folly).

I, where would I yalak (carry) my charapah (shame)? And as for you, you will be as achad (one) of the nabal (fools) in Yasharaal (Israel). Now therefore, please dabar (word / matter) to the malak (king); for he will not manai (withhold) me from you.
However he would not shamai (hearken / hear) to her qawal (sound / voice); but being chazaq (stronger) than she, he inah (oppress / afflict) her, and shakab (lay) with her.

Then Amanawan (Amnon) shanaa (hate) her with exceeding great hatred; for the hatred with which he shanaa (hate) her was greater than the ahabah (love) with which he had ahab (love) her. Amanawan (Amnon) amar (spoke) to her, qawam (rise up), be yalak (gone)!

She amar (spoke) to him, "Not so, awadawath (because) this rai (great) wrong in shalach (send) me away is worse than the other that you ishah (make) to me!" But he would not shamai (hearken / hear) to her.
Then he qaraa (called) his nair (servant) who sharath (ministered) to him, and amar (spoke), shalach (send) now this chawatz (woman) out from me, and nail (bolt) the dalath (door) achar (other) her.

She had a kathanath (garment) of various colors on her; for with such maiyal (robes) were the malak (king) bath (daughter) who were bathawalah (virgins) dressed. Then his sharath (servant) yatzaa (go out / come out) her out, and nail (bolted) the dalath (door) achar (other) her.

Thamar (Tamar) put ashes on her raash (head), and qarai (tore) her kathanath (garment) of various colors that was on her; and she shawam (place / establish / appoint) her yad (hand) on her raash (head), and yalak (went) her way, zaiq (crying) aloud as she went.

Abayashalawam (Absalom) her ach (brother/kinsman) amar (spoke) to her, "Has Amanawan (Amnon) your ach (brother/kinsman) been with you? But now hold your charash (peace), my achawath (sister). He is your ach (brother/kinsman). Don't shayath (put / appoint / make) this thing to heart." So Thamar (Tamar) yashab (inhabit/dwell) shamam (desolate) in her ach (brother/kinsman) Abayashalawam (Absalom's) bayath (house).
But when malak (king) Dawad (David) shamai (hearken / hear) of all these things, he was very charah (hot with anger).

Abayashalawam (Absalom) dabar (word / matter) to Amanawan (Amnon) neither tawab (pleasant/functional) nor rai (bad); for Abayashalawam (Absalom) shanaa (hate) Amanawan (Amnon), dabar (word / matter) he had inah (oppress / afflict) his achawath (sister) Thamar (Tamar).

It happened after yawam (day) full shanah (years), that Abayashalawam (Absalom) had sheepshearers in Bailachatzawar (Baal) Hazor, which is beside Aparayam (Ephraim): and Abayashalawam (Absalom) qaraa (called) all the malak (king) ban (son).

Abayashalawam (Absalom) bawaa (come) to the malak (king), and amar (spoke), See now, your ibad (servant) has sheepshearers. Please yalak (let) the malak (king) and his ibad (servant) yalak (go) with your ibad (servant).

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Abayashalawam (Absalom), "No, my ban (son), yalak (let) us not all go, lest we be burdensome to you." He paratz (pressed) him; however he would not yalak (go), but barak (blessed) him.
Then Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke), "If not, please let my ach (brother/kinsman) Amanawan (Amnon) yalak (go) with us." The malak (king) amar (spoke) to him, Why should he yalak (go) with you?
But Abayashalawam (Absalom) paratz (pressed) him, and he let Amanawan (Amnon) and all the malak (king) ban (son) shalach (send) with him.

Abayashalawam (Absalom) tzawah (commanded) his nair (servants), amar (spoke), raah (see) now, when Amanawan (Amnon's) lab (heart) is tawab (pleasant/functional) with yayan (wine); and when I amar (spoke) you, ‘nakah (strike) Amanawan (Amnon),’ then mawath (death) him. Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). Haven't I tzawah (commanded) you? Be courageous, and be ban (son)!

The nair (servants) of Abayashalawam (Absalom) ishah (make) to Amanawan (Amnon) as Abayashalawam (Absalom) had tzawah (commanded). Then all the malak (king) ban (son) qawam (rise up), and every ayash (husband/individual man) qawam (rise up) up on his parad (mule), and nawas (fled).

It happened, while they were in the darak (way), that the shamawaih (news) bawaa (come) to Dawad (David), amar (spoke), Abayashalawam (Absalom) has nakah (slain) all the malak (king) ban (son), and there is not achad (one) of them yathar (left)!
Then the malak (king) qawam (rise up), and qarai (tore) his bagad (garments), and shakab (lay) on the aratz (Earth/land); and all his ibad (servant) natzab (stood) by with their clothes qarai (torn).

Yawanadab (Jonadab), the ban (son) of Shamaih (Shimeah), Dawad (David's) ach (brother/kinsman), inah (answer / respond), Don't let my Adawan amar (spoke) that they have mawath (death) all the nair (young) men the malak (king) ban (son); for Amanawan (Amnon) only is mawath (death); for by the pah (appointment) of Abayashalawam (Absalom) this has been shawam (place / establish / appoint) from the yawam (day) that he inah (oppress / afflict) his achawath (sister) Thamar (Tamar).

Now therefore don't let my Adawan the malak (king) shawam (place / establish / appoint) the thing to his lab (heart), to amar (spoke) that all the malak (king) ban (son) are mawath (death); for Amanawan (Amnon) only is mawath (death).

But Abayashalawam (Absalom) barach (fled). The nair (young) man who kept the tzapah (watchman / keep watch) nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye), and raah (see), and behold, many im (people / nation) were coming by darak (way) of the hillside achar (other) him.
Yawanadab (Jonadab) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), Behold, the malak (king) ban (son) are bawaa (come)! It is as your ibad (servant) dabar (word / matter).

It happened, as soon as he kalah (complete / finish) finished dabar (word / matter), that behold, the malak (king) ban (son) bawaa (come), and nashaa (lift) up their qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept). The malak (king) also and all his ibad (servant) bakah (wept) bitterly.

But Abayashalawam (Absalom) barach (fled), and yalak (went) to Thalamay (Talmai) the ban (son) Imayachawar (of) Ammihur, malak (king) of Gashawar (Geshur). David abal (mourned) for his ban (son) every yawam (day).
So Abayashalawam (Absalom) barach (fled), and yalak (went) to Gashawar (Geshur), and was there shalawash (three) shanah (years).

Malak (king) Dawad (David) kalah (complete / finish) to yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to Abayashalawam (Absalom): for he was nacham (turn away / repent) concerning Amanawan (Amnon), since he was mawath (death).
Now Yawaab (Joab) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah) yadai (perceived) that the malak (king) lab (heart) was toward Abayashalawam (Absalom).

Yawaab (Joab) shalach (send) to Thaqawai (Tekoa), and laqach (take / seized) there a chakam (wise) ashah (wife/individual woman), and amar (spoke) to her, "Please act like a mourner, and labash (put) on abal (mourning) bagad (clothing), please, and don't sawak (anoint) yourself with shaman (oil), but be as a ashah (wife/individual woman) who has abal (mourned) a rab (long) yawam (day) for the mawath (death).
Bawaa (come) in to the malak (king), and dabar (word / matter) like this to him." So Yawaab (Joab) shawam (place / establish / appoint) the dabar (word / matter) in her pah (mouth).

When the ashah (wife/individual woman) of Tekoa amar (spoke) to the malak (king), she napal (fall / be cast down) on her ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land), showed respect, and amar (spoke), yashai (salvation), O malak (king)!
The malak (king) amar (spoke) to her, "What ails you?" She amar (spoke), Truly I am a alamanah (widow), and my ayash (husband/individual man) is mawath (death).

Your handmaid had shanayam (two) ban (son), and they shanayam (two) fought together in the shadah (field), and there was no one to natzal (part) them, but the achad (one) nakah (struck) the other, and nakah (killed) him.

Behold, the whole mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) has qawam (rise up) against your handmaid, and they amar (spoke), ‘nathan (give) him who nakah (struck) his ach (brother/kinsman), that we may mawath (death) him for the napash (living being/soul) of his ach (brother/kinsman) whom he harag (killed), and so shamad (destroy) the heir also.’ Thus they would kabah (quench) my gachal (coal) which is shawam (place / establish / appoint), and would shawam (place / establish / appoint) to my ayash (husband/individual man) neither sham (name) nor shaarayath (remainder) on the surface of the adamah (earth).
The malak (king) amar (spoke) to the ashah (wife/individual woman), yalak (go) to your bayath (house), and I will give a tzawah (command) concerning you.

The ashah (wife/individual woman) of Tekoa amar (spoke) to the malak (king), My Adawan, O malak (king), the iwan (guilt/iniquity) be on me, and on my ab (father) bayath (house); and the malak (king) and his kasaa (throne) be naqay (guiltless).
The malak (king) amar (spoke), Whoever amar (spoke) anything to you, bawaa (come) him to me, and he shall not nagai (touch) you any more.

Then she amar (spoke), "Please let the malak (king) zakar (remembrance/memory) Yahawah your Alahayam, that the gaal (avenger) of dam (blood) shachath (destroy) not any more, lest they shamad (destroy) my ban (son)." He amar (spoke), As Yahawah chay (life), not one shairah (hair) of your ban (son) shall napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land).
Then the ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke), "Please let your handmaid dabar (word / matter) a dabar (word / matter) to my Adawan the malak (king)." He amar (spoke), dabar (word / matter) on.

The ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke), Why then have you chashab (devised) such a thing against the im (people / nation) of Alahayam? For in dabar (word / matter) this dabar (word / matter) the malak (king) is as one who is asham (guilty), in that the malak (king) shawab (turn back / repent) not bring home again his nadach (banished) one.

For we mawath (death) mawath (death), and are as mayam (Waters) spilled on the aratz (Earth/land), which can't be asap (gathered) up again; neither does Alahayam nashaa (lift) away napash (living being/soul), but chashab (devises) machashabah (means), that he who is nadach (banished) not be an nadach (outcast) from him.

Now therefore seeing that I bawaa (come) come to dabar (word / matter) this dabar (word / matter) to my Adawan the malak (king), it is because the im (people / nation) have made me yaraa (fear / be afraid): and your handmaid amar (spoke), ‘I will now dabar (word / matter) to the malak (king); it may be that the malak (king) will ishah (make) the dabar (word / matter) of his amah (servant).’

For the malak (king) will shamai (hearken / hear), to natzal (deliver) his amah (servant) out of the kap (hand) of the ayash (husband/individual man) who would shamad (destroy) me and my ban (son) yachad (together) out of the nachalah (inheritance) of Alahayam.

Then your handmaid amar (spoke), ‘Please let the dabar (word / matter) of my Adawan the malak (king) bring manawachah (rest); for as an malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Alahayam, so is my Adawan the malak (king) to shamai (hearken / hear) tawab (pleasant/functional) and rai (bad). May Yahawah, your Alahayam, be with you.’

Then the malak (king) inah (answer / respond) the ashah (wife/individual woman), "Please don't kachad (hide) anything from me that I shaal (ask) you." The ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke), Let my Adawan the malak (king) now dabar (word / matter).

The malak (king) amar (spoke), "Is the yad (hand) of Yawaab (Joab) with you in all this?" The ashah (wife/individual woman) inah (answer / respond), As your napash (living being/soul) chay (life), my Adawan the malak (king), no napash (living being/soul) ash (fire) turn to the right yaman (hand) or to the shamaal (left) from anything that my Adawan the malak (king) has dabar (word / matter); for your ibad (servant) Yawaab (Joab), he urged me, and he shawam (place / establish / appoint) all these dabar (word / matter) in the pah (mouth) of your handmaid;

To sabab (change) the panayam (face) of the dabar (word / matter) has your ibad (servant) Yawaab (Joab) ishah (make) this thing. My Adawan is chakam (wise), according to the chakamah (wisdom) of an malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Alahayam, to yadai (know) all things that are in the aratz (Earth/land).

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Yawaab (Joab), Behold now, I ishah (make) done this thing. Yalak (go) therefore, shawab (turn back / repent) the nair (young) man Abayashalawam (Absalom) shawab (turn back / repent).

Yawaab (Joab) napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land) on his panayam (face), showed respect, and barak (blessed) the malak (king). Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke), Today your ibad (servant) yadai (knows) that I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye), my Adawan, malak (king), in that the malak (king) ishah (make) performed the dabar (word / matter) of his ibad (servant).
So Yawaab (Joab) qawam (rise up) and yalak (went) to Gashawar (Geshur), and bawaa (come) Abayashalawam (Absalom) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

The malak (king) amar (spoke), "Let him sabab (return) to his own bayath (house), but raah (see) him not see my panayam (face)." So Abayashalawam (Absalom) sabab (returned) to his own bayath (house), and didn't raah (see) the malak (king) panayam (face).

Now in all Yasharaal (Israel) there was ayash (husband/individual man) to be so much halal (praise) as Abayashalawam (Absalom) for his yapah (beauty): from the kap (sole) of his ragal (feet / foot) even to the qadaqad (crown) of his head there was no maawam (blemish) in him.

When he cut the hair of his raash (head) (yawam (day) it was at every year's qatz (end) that he cut it; because it was kabad (heavy) on him, therefore he cut it); he shaqal (weighed) the shair (hair) of his raash (head) at two maah (hundred) shaqal (shekels), after the malak (king) aban (stone).

To Abayashalawam (Absalom) there were yalad (birth / begot) shalawash (three) ban (son), and achad (one) bath (daughter), whose sham (name) was Thamar (Tamar): she was a ashah (wife/individual woman) of a yapah (beautiful) maraah (face).
Abayashalawam (Absalom) lived yawam (day) full shanah (years) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); and he didn't raah (see) the malak (king) panayam (face).

Then Abayashalawam (Absalom) shalach (send) for Yawaab (Joab), to shalach (send) him to the malak (king); but he would not bawaa (come) to him: and he shalach (send) again a shanay (second) time, but he would not bawaa (come).

Therefore he amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), "raah (see), Yawaab (Joab's) chalaqah (field) is al (near) yad (hand), and he has shairah (barley) there. Yalak (go) and yatzath (set) it on ash (fire)." Abayashalawam (Absalom's) ibad (servant) yatzath (set) the chalaqah (field) on ash (fire).

Then Yawaab (Joab) qawam (rise up), and bawaa (come) to Abayashalawam (Absalom) to his bayath (house), and amar (spoke) to him, Why have your ibad (servant) yatzath (set) my chalaqah (field) on ash (fire)?

Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke) Yawaab (Joab), Behold, I shalach (send) to you, amar (spoke), ‘bawaa (come) here, that I may shalach (send) you to the malak (king), to amar (spoke), "Why bawaa (come) I come from Gashawar (Geshur)? It would be tawab (pleasant/functional) for me to be there still. Now therefore raah (see) me see the malak (king) panayam (face); and if there is iwan (guilt/iniquity) in me, let him mawath (death) me."’

So Yawaab (Joab) bawaa (come) to the malak (king), and nagad (told) him; and when he had qaraa (called) for Abayashalawam (Absalom), he bawaa (come) to the malak (king), and shachah (bowed) himself on his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land) panayam (before) the malak (king): and the malak (king) nashaq (kissed) Abayashalawam (Absalom).

It happened achar (other) this, that Abayashalawam (Absalom) ishah (make) him a marakabah (chariot) and sawas (horses), and chamashayam (fifty) ayash (husband/individual man) to rawatz (run) panayam (before) him.

Abayashalawam (Absalom) shakam (rose) up early, and imad (stood) yad (hand) the darak (way) of the shair (gate). It was so, that when any ayash (husband/individual man) had a rayab (suit) which should bawaa (come) to the malak (king) for mashapat (judgment), then Abayashalawam (Absalom) qaraa (called) to him, and amar (spoke), "ay (what) iyar (city) are you from?" He amar (spoke), Your ibad (servant) is of achad (one) of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke) to him, raah (see), your dabar (word / matter) are tawab (pleasant/functional) and nakach (right); but there is no man deputized by the malak (king) to shamai (hearken / hear) you.

Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke) moreover, Oh that I were shawam (place / establish / appoint) shapat (judge) in the aratz (Earth/land), that every ayash (husband/individual man) who has any rayab (suit) or cause might bawaa (come) to me, and I would tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) him justice!

It was so, that when any ayash (husband/individual man) qarab (come close) near to shachah (do) him obeisance, he shalach (send) forth his yad (hand), and chazaq (took) hold of him, and nashaq (kissed) him.

Abayashalawam (Absalom) ishah (make) this sort of thing to all Yasharaal (Israel) who bawaa (come) to the malak (king) for mashapat (judgment). So Abayashalawam (Absalom) ganab (stole) the lab (heart) of the ishah (make) of Yasharaal (Israel).

It happened at the qatz (end) of arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years), that Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), Please yalak (let) me go and shalam (pay) my nadar (vow), which I have nadar (make vow) to Yahawah, in Chabarawan (Hebron).

For your ibad (servant) nadar (make vow) a nadar (vow) while I stayed at Gashawar (Geshur) in Aram (Syria), amar (spoke), ‘If Yahawah shall indeed shawab (turn back / repent) me again to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), then I will ibad (servant) Yahawah.’
The malak (king) amar (spoke) to him, "yalak (go) in shalawam (peace / safety)." So he qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) to Chabarawan (Hebron).

But Abayashalawam (Absalom) shalach (send) ragal (spies) throughout all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), As soon as you shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), then you shall amar (spoke), ‘Abayashalawam (Absalom) is malak (king) in Chabarawan (Hebron)!’

Two maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man) halak (move) with Abayashalawam (Absalom) out of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), who were qaraa (called), and halak (move) in their tham (simplicity); and they didn't yadai (know) anything.

Abayashalawam (Absalom) shalach (send) for Achayathapal (Ahithophel) the gayalanay (gilonite), Dawad (David's) yaitz (counselor), from his iyar (city), even from Galah (Giloh), while he was zabach (offering) the zabach (sacrifices). The qashar (conspiracy) was amayatz (strong); for the im (people / nation) rab (increased) halak (move) with Abayashalawam (Absalom).
A nagad (messenger) bawaa (come) to Dawad (David), amar (spoke), The lab (heart) of the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) are achar (other) Abayashalawam (Absalom).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to all his ibad (servant) who were with him at Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), qawam (rise up), and let us barach (flee); for else none of us shall palayatah (escape) from Abayashalawam (Absalom). Mahar (make) speed to depart, lest he nashag (overtake) us mahar (quickly), and nadach (bring) down rai (evil) on us, and nakah (strike) the iyar (city) with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword).
The malak (king) ibad (servant) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), Behold, your ibad (servant) are ready to do whatever my Adawan the malak (king) bachar (chooses).

The malak (king) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and all his bayath (house) ragal (feet / foot) him. The malak (king) izab (left) ishar (ten) ashah (wife/individual woman), who were payalagash (concubines), to shamar (keep/guard) the bayath (house).
The malak (king) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and all the im (people / nation) ragal (feet / foot) him; and they imad (stayed) in Beth Merhak.

All his ibad (servant) ibar (pass over/through) on yad (hand) him; and all the Karathay (Cherethites), and all the Palathay (Pelethites), and all the Gathay (Gittites), shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man) who bawaa (come) ragal (feet / foot) him from gath (gath), ibar (pass over/through) on panayam (before) the malak (king).

Then the malak (king) amar (spoke) to Athay (Ittai) the Gathay (Gittite), Why do you also yalak (go) with us? Shawab (turn back / repent), and stay with the malak (king); for you are a nakaray (foreigner), and also an galah (exile). Return to your own maqawam (place).

Whereas you bawaa (come) but thamawal (yesterday), should I this yawam (day) yalak (make) you go up and down with us, since I halak (move) where I may? Shawab (turn back / repent), and shawab (turn back / repent) back your ach (brother/kinsman). Chasad (grace) and amath (truth) be with you.

Athay (Ittai) inah (answer / respond) the malak (king), and inah (answer / respond), As Yahawah chay (life), and as my Adawan the malak (king) chay (life), surely in what maqawam (place) my Adawan the malak (king) shall is, whether for mawath (death) or for chay (life), even there also will your ibad (servant) be.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Athay (Ittai), "yalak (go) and ibar (pass over/through) over." Athay (Ittai) the Gathay (Gittite) ibar (pass over/through) over, and all his ibar (pass over/through), and all the little tap (ones) who were with him.

All the aratz (Earth/land) bakah (wept) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice), and all the im (people / nation) ibar (pass over/through) over: the malak (king) also himself ibar (pass over/through) over the nachal (stream / river) Qadarawan (Kidron), and all the im (people / nation) ibar (pass over/through) over, panayam (toward) the darak (way) of the madabar (wilderness).

Behold, Tzadawaq (Zadok) also came, and all the Lawayay (Levites) with him, nashaa (lift) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Alahayam; and they yatzaq (set) down the arawan (ark) of Alahayam; and Abayathar (Abiathar) ilah (go up / offer) up, until all the im (people / nation) finished ibar (pass over/through) out of the iyar (city).

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Tzadawaq (Zadok), shawab (turn back / repent) back the arawan (ark) of Alahayam into the iyar (city). If I matzaa (find) favor in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, he will shawab (turn back / repent) me again, and show me both it, and his nawah (habitation);
But if he amar (spoke) thus, ‘I chapatz (have) no delight in you;’ behold, here am I. Let him ishah (make) to me as seems tawab (pleasant/functional) to him.

The malak (king) amar (spoke) also to Tzadawaq (Zadok) the kahan (priest), Aren't you a seer? Shawab (turn back / repent) into the iyar (city) in shalawam (peace / safety), and your shanayam (two) ban (son) with you, Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) your ban (son), and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) the ban (son) of Abayathar (Abiathar).
Raah (see), I will mahah (stay) at the fords of the madabar (wilderness), until dabar (word / matter) bawaa (come) from you to inform me.
Tzadawaq (Zadok) therefore and Abayathar (Abiathar) shawab (turn back / repent) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam again to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); and they stayed there.

Dawad (David) ilah (go up / offer) up by the ascent of the Mount of zayath (olive), and bakah (wept) as he ilah (go up / offer) up; and he had his raash (head) chapah (covered), and halak (move) yachap (barefoot): and all the im (people / nation) who were with him chapah (covered) every ayash (husband/individual man) his raash (head), and they ilah (go up / offer) up, bakah (weeping) as they ilah (go up / offer) up.

Someone nagad (told) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), "Achayathapal (Ahithophel) is among the conspirators with Abayashalawam (Absalom)." Dawad (David) amar (spoke), Yahawah, please turn the itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal (Ahithophel) into foolishness.

It happened that when Dawad (David) bawaa (come) come to the raash (head), where Alahayam was shachah (worshiped), behold, Chawashay (Hushai) the arakay (archite) came to qaraah (meet) him with his kathanath (coat) qarai (torn), and adamah (earth) on his raash (head).
Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to him, If you ibar (pass over/through) on with me, then you will be a mashaa (burden) to me;

But if you shawab (turn back / repent) to the iyar (city), and amar (spoke) Abayashalawam (Absalom), ‘I will be your ibad (servant), O malak (king). As I have been your ab (father) ibad (servant) in az (time) past, so will I now be your ibad (servant); then will you parar (defeat) for me the itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal (Ahithophel).’

Don't you have Tzadawaq (Zadok) and Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahan (priest) there with you? Therefore it shall be, that whatever thing you shall shamai (hearken / hear) out of the malak (king) bayath (house), you shall nagad (tell) it to Tzadawaq (Zadok) and Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahan (priest).

Behold, they have there with them their shanayam (two) ban (son), Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz), Tzadawaq (Zadok's) son, and Yahawanathan (Jonathan), Abayathar (Abiathar's) yad (hand); and by them you shall shalach (send) to me everything that you shall shamai (hearken / hear).
So Chawashay (Hushai), Dawad (David's) raih (friend), bawaa (come) into the iyar (city); and Abayashalawam (Absalom) bawaa (come) into Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

When Dawad (David) was a mait (little) past the raash (head), behold, Tzayabaa (Ziba) the nair (servant) of Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth) qaraa (called) him, with a tzamad (couple) of donkeys chabash (saddled), and on them two maah (hundred) loaves of lacham (bread), and one maah (hundred) clusters of tzamawaq (raisins), and one maah (hundred) qayatz (summer) fruits, and a nabal (bottle) of yayan (wine).

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Tzayabaa (Ziba), What do you mean by these? Tzayabaa (Ziba) amar (spoke), The donkeys are for the malak (king) bayath (house) to rakab (ride) on; and the lacham (bread) and qayatz (summer) fruit for the nair (young) men to akal (eat); and the yayan (wine), that such as are yaip (faint) in the madabar (wilderness) may shathah (drinks).

The malak (king) amar (spoke), "Where is your adawan (master / lord) ban (son)?" Tzayabaa (Ziba) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), Behold, he is staying in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); for he amar (spoke), ‘Today the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) will shawab (turn back / repent) me the mamalakawath (kingdom) of my ab (father).’

Then the malak (king) amar (spoke) to Tzayabaa (Ziba), "Behold, all that pertains to Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth) is yours." Tzayabaa (Ziba) amar (spoke), I shachah (do) obeisance. Let me matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (eye), my Adawan, O malak (king).

When malak (king) Dawad (David) bawaa (come) to Bacharayam (Bahurim), behold, a ayash (husband/individual man) of the mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) of the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, whose sham (name) was Shamaiy (Shimei), the ban (son) of Garaa (Gera). He yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and qalal (cursed) still as he yatzaa (go out / come out).

He saqal (cast) aban (stone) at Dawad (David), and at all the ibad (servant) of malak (king) Dawad (David), and all the im (people / nation) and all the gabawar (mighty) men were on his right yamayan (right hand) and on his shamaawal (left hand).

Shamaiy (Shimei) amar (spoke) when he qalal (cursed), Be yatzaa (go out / come out), be yatzaa (go out / come out), you ayash (husband/individual man) of dam (blood), and base ayash (husband/individual man)!

Yahawah has shawab (turn back / repent) on you all the dam (blood) of the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul), in whose place you have malak (king)! Yahawah nathan (give) delivered the malawakah (kingdom) into the yad (hand) of Abayashalawam (Absalom) your ban (son)! Behold, you are caught by your own rai (mischief), because you are a ayash (husband/individual man) of dam (blood)!

Then Abayashay (Abishai) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), Why should this mawath (death) kalab (dog) qalal (curse) my Adawan the malak (king)? Please let me ibar (pass over/through) over and sawar (take) off his raash (head).

The malak (king) amar (spoke), What have I to do with you, you ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah)? Because he qalal (curses), and because Yahawah has amar (spoke) to him, ‘qalal (curse) Dawad (David);’ who then shall amar (spoke), ‘Why ishah (make) you done so?’

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Abayashay (Abishai), and to all his ibad (servant), Behold, my ban (son), who yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from my maih (bowels), baqash (seeks) my napash (living being/soul). How much more this Banayamayanay (Benjamite), now? Leave him yanach (alone), and let him qalal (curse); for Yahawah has invited him.
It may be that Yahawah will raah (see) on the wrong done to me, and that Yahawah will repay me tawab (pleasant/functional) for the qalalah (cursing) of me today.

So Dawad (David) and his ayash (husband/individual man) yalak (went) by the darak (way); and Shamaiy (Shimei) halak (move) along on the hillside opposite him, and qalal (cursed) as he halak (move), saqal (threw) aban (stone) at him, and saqal (threw) ipar (dust).
The malak (king), and all the im (people / nation) who were with him, bawaa (come) iyap (weary); and he napash (living being/soul) himself there.
Abayashalawam (Absalom), and all the im (people / nation), the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel), bawaa (come) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and Achayathapal (Ahithophel) with him.

It happened, when Chawashay (Hushai) the arakay (archite), Dawad (David's) raih (friend), bawaa (come) come to Abayashalawam (Absalom), that Chawashay (Hushai) amar (spoke) to Abayashalawam (Absalom), Long chayah (live) the malak (king)! Long chayah (live) the malak (king)!
Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke) to Chawashay (Hushai), Is this your chasad (grace) to your rai (neigbor/another person)? Why didn't you halak (move) with your rai (neigbor/another person)?

Chawashay (Hushai) amar (spoke) to Abayashalawam (Absalom), No; but whomever Yahawah, and this im (people / nation), and all the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) have bachar (chosen), his will I be, and with him I will stay.

Again, whom should I ibad (servant)? Shouldn't I panayam (serve) in the presence of his ban (son)? As I have ibad (servant) in your ab (father) panayam (presence), so will I be in your panayam (presence).
Then Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke) to Achayathapal (Ahithophel), yahab (give) your itzah (counsel) what we shall ishah (make).

Achayathapal (Ahithophel) amar (spoke) to Abayashalawam (Absalom), bawaa (come) in to your ab (father) payalagash (concubines), that he has yanach (left) to shamar (keep/guard) the bayath (house). Then all Yasharaal (Israel) will shamai (hearken / hear) that you are baash (abhorred) by your ab (father). Then the yad (hand) of all who are with you will be chazaq (strong).

So they natah (spread) Abayashalawam (Absalom) a ahal (tent) on the gag (top) of the house; and Abayashalawam (Absalom) bawaa (come) in to his ab (father) payalagash (concubines) in the iyan (eye) of all Yasharaal (Israel).

The itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal (Ahithophel), which he yaitz (gave) in those yawam (day), was as if a man inquired at the dabar (word / matter) of Alahayam: so was all the itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal (Ahithophel) both with Dawad (David) and with Abayashalawam (Absalom).

Moreover Achayathapal (Ahithophel) amar (spoke) to Abayashalawam (Absalom), Let me now bachar (choose) shanayam (two) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man), and I will qawam (rise up) and radap (pursue) achar (other) Dawad (David) tonight.

I will bawaa (come) on him while he is yagai (weary) and exhausted, and will make him charad (afraid). All the im (people / nation) who are with him shall nawas (flee). I will nakah (strike) the malak (king) only;

And I will shawab (turn back / repent) back all the im (people / nation) to you. The ayash (husband/individual man) whom you baqash (seek) is as if shawab (turn back / repent) returned. All the im (people / nation) shall be in shalawam (peace / safety).
The dabar (word / matter) yashar (pleased) Abayashalawam (Absalom) iyan (eye), and all the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel).
Then Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke), Now qaraa (called) Chawashay (Hushai) the arakay (archite) also, and shamai (hearken / hear) us hear likewise what he pah (says).

When Chawashay (Hushai) bawaa (come) come to Abayashalawam (Absalom), Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke) to him, amar (spoke), Achayathapal (Ahithophel) has dabar (word / matter) like this. Shall we ishah (make) dabar (word / matter) he says? If not, dabar (word / matter) up.
Chawashay (Hushai) amar (spoke) to Abayashalawam (Absalom), The itzah (counsel) that Achayathapal (Ahithophel) has yaitz (given) paim (this) time is not tawab (pleasant/functional).

Chawashay (Hushai) amar (spoke) moreover, You yadai (know) your ab (father) and his yadai (men), that they are gabawar (mighty) men, and they are fierce in their napash (living being/soul), like a dab (bear) robbed of her cubs in the shadah (field). Your ab (father) is a ayash (husband/individual man) of malachamah (war), and will not lawan (lodge) with the im (people / nation).

Behold, he is now chabaa (hidden) in some pachath (pit), or in some other maqawam (place). It will happen, when some of them napal (fall / be cast down) fallen at the thachalah (first), that whoever shamai (hearken / hear) it will amar (spoke), ‘There is a magapah (slaughter) among the im (people / nation) who achar (other) Abayashalawam (Absalom)!’

Even he who is ban (son), whose lab (heart) is as the lab (heart) of a aray (lion), will masas (utterly) masas (melt); for all Yasharaal (Israel) yadai (knows) that your ab (father) is a gabawar (mighty) man, and those who are with him are chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ban (son).

But I yaitz (counsel) that all Yasharaal (Israel) be asap (gathered) asap (together) Dan (to) you, from Dan Baarashabai (even) to Beersheba, as the chawal (sand) that is by the yam (sea/waters) for rab (multitude); and that you halak (move) to qarab (battle) in your own panayam (person).

So shall we bawaa (come) on him in some maqawam (place) where he shall be matzaa (found), and we will matzaa (light) on him as the tal (dew) napal (fall / be cast down) on the adamah (ground); and of him and of all the achad (one) who are with him we will not yathar (leave) so much as achad (one).

Moreover, if he be gone into a iyar (city), then shall all Yasharaal (Israel) nashaa (lift) chabal (ropes) to that iyar (city), and we will sachab (draw) it into the nachal (stream / river), until there isn't gam (indeed / moreover) small tzarawar (stone) matzaa (found) there.

Abayashalawam (Absalom) and all the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke), "The itzah (counsel) of Chawashay (Hushai) the arakay (archite) is tawab (pleasant/functional) than the itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal (Ahithophel)." For Yahawah had ordained to parar (defeat) the tawab (pleasant/functional) itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal (Ahithophel), to the intent that Yahawah might bawaa (come) rai (evil) on Abayashalawam (Absalom).

Then Chawashay (Hushai) amar (spoke) to Tzadawaq (Zadok) and to Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahan (priest), Achayathapal (Ahithophel) yaitz (counseled) Abayashalawam (Absalom) and the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) that way; and I have yaitz (counseled) this way.

Now therefore shalach (send) maharah (quickly), and nagad (tell) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), ‘Don't lawan (lodge) this layal (night) at the fords of the madabar (wilderness), but by ibar (pass over/through) means ibar (pass over/through) over; lest the malak (king) be balai (swallowed) up, and all the im (people / nation) who are with him.’

Now Yahawanathan (Jonathan) and Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) were imad (staying) by Iyanaragal (En) Rogel; and a female shapachah (servant) used to halak (move) and nagad (tell) them; and they halak (move) and nagad (told) malak (king) Dawad (David). For they yakal (might) not be raah (see) to bawaa (come) into the iyar (city).

But a nair (boy) raah (see) them, and nagad (told) Abayashalawam (Absalom). Then they shanayam (two) yalak (went) away maharah (quickly), and bawaa (come) to the bayath (house) of a ayash (husband/individual man) in Bacharayam (Bahurim), who had a baar (well) in his chatzar (court); and they yarad (went) down there.

The ashah (wife/individual woman) laqach (take / seized) and parash (spread) the masak (covering) over the baar (well's) panayam (mouth), and shatach (spread) out bruised grain on it; and nothing was yadai (known).

Abayashalawam (Absalom's) ibad (servant) bawaa (come) to the ashah (wife/individual woman) to the bayath (house); and they amar (spoke), "Where are Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) and Yahawanathan (Jonathan)?" The ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke) to them, "They ibar (pass over/through) gone over the mayakal (brook) of mayam (Waters)." When they had baqash (sought) and could not matzaa (find) them, they shawab (turn back / repent) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

It happened, achar (other) they had departed, that they ilah (go up / offer) up out of the baar (well), and yalak (went) and nagad (told) malak (king) Dawad (David); and they said to Dawad (David), qawam (rise up) and pass maharah (quickly) over the mayam (Waters); for thus has Achayathapal (Ahithophel) counseled against you.

Then Dawad (David) qawam (rise up), and all the im (people / nation) who were with him, and they ibar (pass over/through) over the Yaradan (Jordan). By the baqar (morning) awar (light) there idar (lacked) not achad (one) of them who ibar (pass over/through) not gone over the Yaradan (Jordan).

When Achayathapal (Ahithophel) raah (see) that his itzah (counsel) was not ishah (make), he chabash (saddled) his donkey, and qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) home, to his iyar (city), and set his yalak (house) in tzawah (order), and hanged himself; and he mawath (death), and was qabar (bury) in the tomb of his ab (father).

Then Dawad (David) bawaa (come) to Machanayam (Mahanaim). Abayashalawam (Absalom) ibar (pass over/through) over the Yaradan (Jordan), he and all the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) with him.

Abayashalawam (Absalom) shawam (place / establish / appoint) Imashaa (Amasa) over the tzabaa (troop) instead of Yawaab (Joab). Now Imashaa (Amasa) was the ban (son) of a ayash (husband/individual man), whose sham (name) was Yatharaa (Ithra) the Yasharaalay (Israelite), who bawaa (come) in Abayagayal (to) Abigail the bath (daughter) of Nachash (Nahash), achawath (sister) to Tzarawayah (Zeruiah), Yawaab (Joab's) am (mother).
Yasharaal (Israel) and Abayashalawam (Absalom) chanah (encamped) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Galaid (Gilead).

It happened, when Dawad (David) bawaa (come) come to Machanayam (Mahanaim), that Shabay (Shobi) the ban (son) of Nachash (Nahash) of Rabah (Rabbah) of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon), and Makayar (Machir) the ban (son) of Imayaal (Ammiel) of Laadabar (Lodebar), and Barazalay (Barzillai) the Galaiday (Gileadite) of Ragalayam (Rogelim),
Brought mashakab (beds), basins, yatzar (earthen) kalay (vessels), chatah (wheat), shairah (barley), qamach (meal), qalay (parched) grain, pawal (beans), lentils, roasted grain,

Dabash (honey), chamaah (butter), tzaan (sheep), and shapah (cheese) of the baqar (morning), for Dawad (David), and for the im (people / nation) who were with him, to akal (eat): for they amar (spoke), The im (people / nation) are raib (hungry), and iyap (weary), and thirsty, in the madabar (wilderness).

Dawad (David) paqad (visit) the im (people / nation) who were with him, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) shar (prince / ruler) of alap (thousands) and shar (prince / ruler) of maah (hundred) over them.

Dawad (David) shalach (send) forth the im (people / nation), a shalayashay (third) part under the yad (hand) of Yawaab (Joab), and a shalayashay (third) part under the yad (hand) of Abayashay (Abishai) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah), Yawaab (Joab's) ach (brother/kinsman), and a shalayashay (third) part under the yad (hand) of Athay (Ittai) the Gathay (Gittite). The malak (king) amar (spoke) to the im (people / nation), I will yatzaa (go out / come out) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth with you anay (myself) also.

But the im (people / nation) amar (spoke), You shall not yatzaa (go out / come out) forth; for if we nawas (flee) nawas (away), they will not shawam (place / establish / appoint) for us; neither if chatzay (half) of us mawath (death), will they shawam (place / establish / appoint) for us. But you are kamaw (worth) ishar (ten) alap (thousand) of us. Therefore now it is tawab (pleasant/functional) that you are ready to izar (help) us out of the iyar (city).

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to them, "I will ishah (make) what seems yatab (best) to you." The malak (king) imad (stood) yad (hand) the shair (gate), and all the im (people / nation) yatab (went) out by maah (hundred) and by alap (thousands).

The malak (king) tzawah (commanded) Yawaab (Joab) and Abayashay (Abishai) and Athay (Ittai), amar (spoke), "Deal at (gently) for my sake with the nair (young) man, even with Abayashalawam (Absalom)." All the im (people / nation) shamai (hearken / hear) when the malak (king) tzawah (commanded) all the shar (prince / ruler) dabar (word / matter) Abayashalawam (Absalom).
So the im (people / nation) yatzaa (go out / come out) out into the shadah (field) qaraah (against) Yasharaal (Israel): and the malachamah (battle) was in the yair (forest) of Aparayam (Ephraim).

The im (people / nation) of Yasharaal (Israel) were nagap (struck) there panayam (before) the ibad (servant) of Dawad (David), and there was a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) magapah (slaughter) there that yawam (day) of isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) men.

For the malachamah (battle) was there pawatz (spread) over the surface of all the aratz (Earth/land); and the yair (forest) akal (eat) more im (people / nation) that yawam (day) than the charab (sword) akal (eat).

Abayashalawam (Absalom) qaraa (called) to meet the panayam (servants) of Dawad (David). Abayashalawam (Absalom) was rakab (riding) on his parad (mule), and the parad (mule) bawaa (come) under the shawabak (thick) boughs of a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) alah (these), and his raash (head) chazaq (caught) hold of the alah (these), and he was nathan (give) up between the sky and aratz (Earth/land); and the parad (mule) that was under him ibar (pass over/through) on.
A achad (one) ayash (husband/individual man) raah (see) it, and nagad (told) Yawaab (Joab), and said, raah (see), I saw Abayashalawam (Absalom) thalah (hanging) in an alah (these).

Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke) to the ayash (husband/individual man) who amar (spoke) him, raah (see), you saw it, and why didn't you nakah (strike) him there to the aratz (Earth/land)? I nathan (give) have given you ishar (ten) pieces of kasap (silver), and a sash.

The ayash (husband/individual man) amar (spoke) to Yawaab (Joab), lawaa (do not) I should shaqal (receive) a alap (thousand) pieces of kasap (silver) in my kap (hand), I still wouldn't shalach (send) forth my kap (hand) against the malak (king) ban (son); for in our azan (hearing) the malak (king) tzawah (commanded) you and Abayashay (Abishai) and Athay (Ittai), amar (spoke), ‘Beware that none touch the nair (young) man Abayashalawam (Absalom).’

Aw (or) if I ishah (make) dealt falsely against his napash (living being/soul) (and there is no dabar (word / matter) kachad (hidden) from the malak (king)), then you yourself would have yatzab (set) yourself against me.

Then Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke), "I'm not going to yachal (wait) like this with you." He laqach (take / seized) shalawash (three) shabat (darts) in his kap (hand), and thaqai (blow / sound alarm) them through the lab (heart) of Abayashalawam (Absalom), while he was yet chay (life) in the midst of the alah (these).
Ishar (ten) nair (young) men who nashaa (lift) Yawaab (Joab's) armor surrounded and nakah (struck) Abayashalawam (Absalom), and nakah (killed) him.

Yawaab (Joab) thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), and the im (people / nation) shawab (turn back / repent) from radap (pursuing) achar (other) Yasharaal (Israel); for Yawaab (Joab) chashak (darkness) back the im (people / nation).

They laqach (take / seized) Abayashalawam (Absalom), and shalak (cast) him into the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) pachath (pit) in the yair (forest), and raised over him a very gadawal (very great/important/mighty) gal (heap) of aban (stone). Then all Yasharaal (Israel) nawas (fled) everyone to his ahal (tent).

Now Abayashalawam (Absalom) in his chay (life) had laqach (take / seized) and natzab (reared) up for himself the matzabath (pillar), which is in the malak (king) imaq (dale); for he amar (spoke), "I have no ban (son) to keep my sham (name) in memory." He qaraa (called) the matzabath (pillar) after his own sham (name); and it is qaraa (called) Abayashalawam (Absalom's) monument, to this yawam (day).

Then Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) the ban (son) of Tzadawaq (Zadok) amar (spoke), Let me now rawatz (run), and bashar (bear) the malak (king) news, how that Yahawah has shapat (avenged) him of his yad (hand).

Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke) to him, You shall not be the bearer of news this yawam (day), but you shall bashar (bear) news achar (other) yawam (day). But today you shall bashar (bear) no news, because the malak (king) ban (son) is mawath (death).

Then Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke) to the Kawashay (Cushite), "yalak (go), nagad (tell) the malak (king) what you raah (see) seen!" The Kawashay (Cushite) shachah (bowed) himself to Yawaab (Joab), and rawatz (ran).

Then Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) the ban (son) of Tzadawaq (Zadok) amar (spoke) yet again to Yawaab (Joab), "But come mah (what) may, please let me also rawatz (run) achar (other) the Kawashay (Cushite)." Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke), Why do you want to rawatz (run), my ban (son), since that you will matzaa (have) no reward for the news?

"But come what may," he amar (spoke), "I will rawatz (run)." He amar (spoke) to him, "rawatz (run)!" Then Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) rawatz (ran) by the darak (way) of the kakar (plain), and outran the Kawashay (Cushite).

Now Dawad (David) was sitting between the shanayam (two) shair (gates): and the tzapah (watchman / keep watch) yalak (went) up to the gag (roof) of the shair (gate) to the chawamah (wall), and nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye), and raah (see), and, behold, a ayash (husband/individual man) running rawatz (alone).

The tzapah (watchman / keep watch) qaraa (called), and nagad (told) the malak (king). The malak (king) said, "If he is bashawarah (alone), there is news in his pah (mouth)." He yalak (came) closer and closer.

The tzapah (watchman / keep watch) raah (see) achar (other) ayash (husband/individual man) running; and the tzapah (watchman / keep watch) qaraa (called) to the shawair (porter), and amar (spoke), "Behold, a ayash (husband/individual man) running alone!" The malak (king) amar (spoke), He also bashar (brings) news.

The tzapah (watchman / keep watch) amar (spoke), "I raah (see) the marawatzah (running) of the raashawan (first) one is like the marawatzah (running) of Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) the ban (son) of Tzadawaq (Zadok)." The malak (king) amar (spoke), He is a tawab (pleasant/functional) ayash (husband/individual man), and bawaa (come) with tawab (pleasant/functional) news.

Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) qaraa (called), and amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "shalawam (peace / safety) is well." He shachah (bowed) himself before the malak (king) with his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land), and amar (spoke), barak (blessed) is Yahawah your Alahayam, who has sagar (delivered) up the ayash (husband/individual man) who lifted up their yad (hand) against my Adawan the malak (king)!

The malak (king) amar (spoke), "Is it shalawam (peace / safety) with the nair (young) man Abayashalawam (Absalom)?" Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) amar (spoke), When Yawaab (Joab) shalach (send) the malak (king) ibad (servant), even me your ibad (servant), I raah (see) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) hamawan (tumult), but I don't yadai (know) what it was.
The malak (king) amar (spoke), "sabab (turn) aside, and yatzab (stand) here." He sabab (turned) aside, and imad (stood) still.

Behold, the Kawashay (Cushite) bawaa (come). The Kawashay (Cushite) amar (spoke), News for my Adawan the malak (king); for Yahawah has shapat (avenged) you this yawam (day) of all those who qawam (rise up) up against you.

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to the Kawashay (Cushite), "Is it shalawam (peace / safety) with the nair (young) man Abayashalawam (Absalom)?" The Kawashay (Cushite) amar (spoke), May the ayab (enemy) of my Adawan the malak (king), and all who qawam (rise up) up against you to do you rai (harm), be as that nair (young) man is.

The malak (king) was much ragaz (moved), and ilah (go up / offer) up to the room over the shair (gate), and bakah (wept). As he yalak (went), he amar (spoke), My ban (son) Abayashalawam (Absalom)! My ban (son), my ban (son) Abayashalawam (Absalom)! I wish I had mawath (death) for you, Abayashalawam (Absalom), my ban (son), my ban (son)!
It was amar (spoke) Joab, Behold, the malak (king) bakah (weeps) and bakah (mourns) for Abayashalawam (Absalom).
The victory that day was turned into bakah (mourning) to all the people; for the people heard it said that day, The malak (king) grieves for his son.
The im (people / nation) sneaked into the city that yawam (day), as im (people / nation) who are ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.
The king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, My son Absalom, Absalom, my son, my son!

Joab zaiq (came) into the house to the malak (king), and said, You have shamed this day the panayam (faces) of all your ban (son), who this day have saved your life, and the lives of your ban (son) and of your ban (son), and the lives of your wives, and the lives of your concubines;

In that you love those who hate you, and hate those who love you. For you have amar (spoke) this yawam (day), that princes and ibad (servant) are nothing to you. For today I perceive that if Absalom had yawam (day), and kal (every) we had died this yawam (day), then it would have panayam (pleased) you well.

Now therefore arise, ayan (go) out, and nagad (speak) to comfort your ibad (servant); for I swear by Yahawah, if you don't ayan (go) out, not a yadai (man) will stay with you this night. That would be worse to you than all the evil that yadai (has) happened to you from your youth until now.

Then the king qawam (rise up), and sat in the gate. They dabar (word / matter) to all the ayash (husband/individual man), dabar (word / matter), "Behold, the king is sitting in the gate." All the ayash (husband/individual man) bawaa (come) ath (entirety) the king. Now Israel had fled every ayash (husband/individual man) to his tent.

All the im (people / nation) were at strife throughout all the tribes of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), The malak (king) delivered us out of the hand of our qawam (rise up), and he saved us out of the hand of the Philistines; and now he has nawas (fled) out of the land from Absalom.
Abayashalawam (Absalom), whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle. Now therefore why don't you amar (spoke) a word of bringing the malak (king) back?

Malak (king) David shawab (turn back / repent) to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, shawab (turn back / repent), charash (speak) to the elders of Judah, shawab (turn back / repent), ‘Why are you the last to shawab (turn back / repent) the malak (king) shawab (turn back / repent) to his house? Since the speech of all Israel il (over) come to the malak (king), to return him to his house.
You are my brothers, you are my bone and my flesh. Why then are you the acharawan (last) to shawab (turn back / repent) back the malak (king)?’

Shawab (turn back / repent) to Amasa, ‘Aren't you my itzam (bone) and my bashar (flesh)? Alahayam hayah (came to pass) so to me, and more also, if you aren't captain of the army before me shawab (turn back / repent) in the room of Joab.’
He bowed the heart of all the ishah (make) of Judah, even as one ishah (make); so that they sent to the king, saying, Return, you and all your servants.

So the malak (king) shawab (turn back / repent), and shawab (turn back / repent) to the Jordan. Yahawadah (Judah) shawab (turn back / repent) to Gilgal, to natah (go) to meet the malak (king), to shalach (send) the malak (king) over the Jordan.
Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite, who was of Bahurim, hurried and shawab (turn back / repent) down with the ibar (pass over/through) of Yahawadah (Judah) to qaraah (meet) malak (king) David.

There were a thousand ayash (husband/individual man) of banayamayanay (benjamin) with him, and Ziba the ban (son) of the house of Saul, and his fifteen ban (son) and his twenty ban (son) with him; and they yarad (went) through the Jordan in the presence of the malak (king).

A ferry boat tzalach (went) to bring over the malak (king) bayath (house), and to do what he thought ayash (husband/individual man). Shimei the ban (son) of Gera fell down panayam (before) the malak (king), when he had come over the Yaradan (Jordan).

He said to the malak (king), Don't let my Adawan impute iniquity to me, nor remember that which your ban (son) ibar (pass over/through) perversely the day that my Adawan the malak (king) ibar (pass over/through) out of Jerusalem, that the malak (king) should ibar (pass over/through) it to his heart.

For your ibad (servant) knows that I have iwan (guilt/iniquity). Therefore, behold, I yatzaa (go out / come out) come this yawam (day) the first of all the house of Joseph to yatzaa (go out / come out) down to meet my Adawan the malak (king).
But Abishai the son of Zeruiah yadai (answered), Shall Shimei not be put to death for this, because he cursed Yahweh's anointed?

Yahawah (David) amar (spoke), What have I to do with you, you ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah), that you should this day be adversaries to me? Shall there any ban (son) be put to mawath (death) this day in Abayashay (Israel)? For don't I know that I am this day king over Abayashay (Israel)?
The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Shimei, "You shall not mawath (death)." The malak (king) swore to him.

Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the malak (king); and he had laa (NOT) groomed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from the day the malak (king) departed until the day he came home in peace.
It happened, when he bawaa (come) come to Jerusalem to qaraah (meet) the malak (king), that the malak (king) said to him, Why didn't you yarad (go) with me, Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth)?

He amar (spoke), My Adawan, O malak (king), my servant deceived me. For your servant amar (spoke), I will saddle me a donkey, that I may ride thereon, and bawaa (come) with the malak (king); because your servant is lame.
He has slandered your ibad (servant) to my Adawan the malak (king); but my Adawan the malak (king) is as an angel of Alahayam. Do therefore what is good in your eyes.

For all my father's house were but dead ishah (make) before my Adawan the malak (king); yet you ishah (make) your ibad (servant) among those who ate at your own table. What right therefore ishah (make) I yet that I should cry any more to the malak (king)?
The malak (king) said to him, Why do you speak any more of your matters? I say, you and Ziba divide the land.
Mephibosheth amar (spoke) to the malak (king), Yes, let him chalaq (take) all, because my Adawan the malak (king) chalaq (has) come in peace to his own house.
Barzillai the Gileadite bawaa (come) down from Rogelim; and he bawaa (come) over the Jordan with the malak (king), to conduct him over the Jordan.

Now Barazalay (Barzillai) was a very ibar (pass over/through) man, even eighty years old: and he had provided the malak (king) with sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; for he was a very great ibar (pass over/through).
The malak (king) said to Barazalay (Barzillai), ban (son) over with me, and I will kawal (all/every/entire) you with me in Jerusalem.
Barazalay (Barzillai) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should ibar (pass over/through) up with the malak (king) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem)?

I am this yawam (day) eighty shanah (years) yawam (day). Can I discern between mah (good) and bad? Can your servant taste what I eat or what I drink? Can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women? Why then should your servant be yet a burden to my Adawan the malak (king)?
Your ibad (servant) would but just go over the Jordan with the malak (king). Why should the malak (king) repay me with such a reward?

Please let your ibad (servant) ibar (pass over/through) back again, that I may die in my own city, by the grave of my father and my mother. But behold, your ibad (servant) Chimham; let him ibar (pass over/through) over with my Adawan the malak (king); and ibar (pass over/through) to him what shall seem mah (good) to you.

The malak (king) shawab (turn back / repent), Kamaham (Chimham) shall ibar (pass over/through) over with me, and I will ishah (make) to him that which shall seem tawab (pleasant/functional) to you. Whatever you require of me, that I will ishah (make) for you.

All the people ibar (pass over/through) over the Kamaham (Jordan), and the malak (king) ibar (pass over/through) over. Then the malak (king) kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned to his own kal (every).

So the malak (king) ibar (pass over/through) over to Gilgal, and Chimham ibar (pass over/through) over with him. All the im (people / nation) of Judah ibar (pass over/through) the malak (king) over, and also half the im (people / nation) of Israel.

Behold, all the ibar (pass over/through) of Yasharaal (Israel) ibar (pass over/through) to the malak (king), and said to the malak (king), Why have our brothers the ibar (pass over/through) of Yahawadah (Judah) stolen you away, and ibar (pass over/through) the malak (king), and his household, over the Kamaham (Jordan), and all David's ibar (pass over/through) with him?

All the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yahawadah (Judah) amar (spoke) the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel), Because the malak (king) is a close relative to us. Why then are you angry about this matter? Have we bawaa (come) at kal (every) at the malak (king) cost? Or has he bawaa (come) us any gift?

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) inah (answer / respond) the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yahawadah (Judah), and inah (answer / respond), "We have ten dabar (word / matter) in the malak (king), and we have also more claim to David than you. Why then did you despise us, that our dabar (word / matter) should not be first had in inah (answer / respond) back our malak (king)?" The dabar (word / matter) of the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yahawadah (Judah) were fiercer than the dabar (word / matter) of the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel).

There qaraa (called) to be there a base ayash (husband/individual man), whose sham (name) was shabai (sheba), the ban (son) of Bakaray (Bichri), a Benjamite: and he thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), and amar (spoke), We have no chalaq (portion) in Dawad (David), neither have we nachalah (inheritance) in the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse). Ayash (husband/individual man) ayash (husband/individual man) to his ahal (tents), Yasharaal (Israel)!

So all the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up from achar (other) Dawad (David), and achar (other) shabai (sheba) the ban (son) of Bakaray (Bichri); but the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yahawadah (Judah) dabaq (joined) with their malak (king), from the Yaradan (Jordan) even to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

Dawad (David) bawaa (come) to his bayath (house) at Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); and the malak (king) laqach (take / seized) the ishar (ten) ashah (wife/individual woman) his payalagash (concubines), whom he had yanach (left) to shamar (keep/guard) the bayath (house), and nathan (give) them in custody, and kawal (all/every/entire) them with sustenance, but didn't bawaa (come) in to them. So they were tzarar (shut) up to the yawam (day) of their mawath (death), chayawath (living) in alamanawath (widowhood).

Then the malak (king) amar (spoke) to Imashaa (Amasa), zaiq (call) me the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yahawadah (Judah) together within shalawash (three) yawam (day), and be here imad (present).
So Imashaa (Amasa) yalak (went) to zaiq (call) the men of Yahawadah (Judah) together; but he stayed longer than the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) time which he had yaid (appointed) him.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Abayashay (Abishai), Now shabai (sheba) the ban (son) of Bakaray (Bichri) will do us more harm than Abayashalawam (Absalom) did. Laqach (take / seized) your adawan (master / lord) ibad (servant), and radap (pursue) achar (other) him, lest he matzaa (get) himself batzar (fortified) iyar (cities), and natzal (escape) out of our iyan (eye).

There yatzaa (go out / come out) out achar (other) him Yawaab (Joab's) ayash (husband/individual man), and the Karathay (Cherethites) and the Palathay (Pelethites), and all the gabawar (mighty) men; and they yatzaa (go out / come out) out of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), to radap (pursue) achar (other) shabai (sheba) the ban (son) of Bakaray (Bichri).

When they were at the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) aban (stone) which is in Gabaiwan (Gibeon), Imashaa (Amasa) bawaa (come) to panayam (meet) them. Yawaab (Joab) was clothed in his apparel of war that he had put on, and on it was a sash with a charab (sword) tzamad (fastened) on his waist in its thair (razor); and as he yatzaa (go out / come out) forth it yatzaa (go out / come out) out.

Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke) to Imashaa (Amasa), "Is it shalawam (peace / safety) with you, my ach (brother/kinsman)?" Yawaab (Joab) achaz (took) Imashaa (Amasa) by the zaqan (beard) with his yamayan (right hand) yad (hand) to nashaq (kiss) him.

But Imashaa (Amasa) shamar (keep/guard) no heed to the charab (sword) that was in Yawaab (Joab's) yad (hand). So he nakah (struck) him with it in the body, and shapak (shed) out his maih (bowels) to the aratz (Earth/land), and didn't shanah (strike) him again; and he mawath (death). Yawaab (Joab) and Abayashay (Abishai) his ach (brother/kinsman) radap (pursued) achar (other) shabai (sheba) the ban (son) of Bakaray (Bichri).

There imad (stood) by him ayash (husband/individual man) of Yawaab (Joab's) nair (young) men, and amar (spoke), He who favors Yawaab (Joab), and he who is for Dawad (David), let him achar (other) Yawaab (Joab)!

Imashaa (Amasa) lay galal (wallowing) in his dam (blood) in the thawak (midst) of the masalah (highway). When the ayash (husband/individual man) raah (see) that all the im (people / nation) imad (stood) still, he sabab (carried) Imashaa (Amasa) out of the masalah (highway) into the shadah (field), and shalak (cast) a bagad (garment) over him, when he raah (see) that everyone who bawaa (come) by him imad (stood) still.

When he was yagah (removed) out of the masalah (highway), all the ayash (husband/individual man) ibar (pass over/through) on achar (other) Yawaab (Joab), to radap (pursue) achar (other) shabai (sheba) the ban (son) of Bakaray (Bichri).

He ibar (pass over/through) through all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) to Abal (Abel), and to Bayathamaikah (Beth) Maacah, and all the baray (berites): and they were qalah (gathered) together, and bawaa (come) also achar (other) him.

They bawaa (come) and tzawar (besieged) him in Abal (Abel) of Bayathamaikah (Beth) Maacah, and they shapak (cast) up a mound against the iyar (city), and it imad (stood) against the chayal (rampart); and all the im (people / nation) who were with Yawaab (Joab) shachath (battered) the chawamah (wall), to napal (fall / be cast down) it down.

Then a chakam (wise) ashah (wife/individual woman) qaraa (called) out of the iyar (city), shamai (hearken / hear), shamai (hearken / hear)! Please amar (spoke) to Yawaab (Joab), ‘qarab (come close) near here, that I may dabar (word / matter) with you.’

He qarab (come close) near to her; and the ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke), "Are you Yawaab (Joab)?" He amar (spoke), "I am." Then she amar (spoke) to him, "shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of your handmaid." He amar (spoke), I do shamai (hearken / hear).
Then she amar (spoke), amar (spoke), They were used to dabar (word / matter) in raashawan (old) times, ‘They shall shaal (surely) shaal (ask) counsel at Abal (Abel);’ and so they settled it.

I am among those who are shalam (peaceable) and aman (believe / have faith) in Yasharaal (Israel). You baqash (seek) to mawath (death) a iyar (city) and a am (mother) in Yasharaal (Israel). Why will you balai (swallow) up the nachalah (inheritance) of Yahawah?
Yawaab (Joab) inah (answer / respond), "chalayalah (far) be it, chalayalah (far) be it from me, that I should balai (swallow) up or shachath (destroy).

The dabar (word / matter) is not so. But a ayash (husband/individual man) of the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), shabai (sheba) the ban (son) of Bakaray (Bichri) by sham (name), has nashaa (lift) up his yad (hand) against the malak (king), even against Dawad (David). Nathan (give) him only, and I will depart from the iyar (city)." The ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke) to Yawaab (Joab), Behold, his raash (head) shall be shalak (thrown) to you over the chawamah (wall).

Then the ashah (wife/individual woman) bawaa (come) to all the im (people / nation) in her chakamah (wisdom). They karath (cut) off the raash (head) of shabai (sheba) the ban (son) of Bakaray (Bichri), and shalak (threw) it out to Yawaab (Joab). He thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), and they were pawatz (dispersed) from the iyar (city), every ayash (husband/individual man) to his ahal (tent). Yawaab (Joab) shawab (turn back / repent) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) to the malak (king).

Now Yawaab (Joab) was over all the tzabaa (troop) of Yasharaal (Israel); and Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) was over the Karay (Cherethites) and over the Palathay (Pelethites);
And Adaram (Adoram) was over the men subject to forced mas (labor); and Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the ban (son) of Achayalawad (Ahilud) was the zakar (remembrance/memory);
And Shayaa (Sheva) was sapar (book); and Tzadawaq (Zadok) and Abayathar (Abiathar) were kahan (priest);
And also Iyaraa (Ira) the yaaray (jairite) was kahan (priest) minister to Dawad (David).

There was a raib (famine) in the yawam (day) of Dawad (David) shalawash (three) shanah (years), shanah (year) achar (other) shanah (year); and Dawad (David) baqash (sought) the panayam (face) of Yahawah. Yahawah amar (spoke), It is for Shaawal (Saul), and for his bloody bayath (house), because he put to mawath (death) the Gabainay (Gibeonites).

The malak (king) qaraa (called) the Gabainay (Gibeonites), and amar (spoke) to them (now the Gabainay (Gibeonites) were not of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), but of the yathar (remnant) of the Amaray (Amorites); and the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) had shabai (swear / take oath) to them: and Shaawal (Saul) baqash (sought) to nakah (kill) them in his qanaa (jealous) for the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah));

And Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to the Gabainay (Gibeonites), What shall I ishah (make) for you? And with what shall I make kapar (atonement), that you may barak (bless) the nachalah (inheritance) of Yahawah?

The Gabainay (Gibeonites) amar (spoke) to him, "It is no matter of kasap (silver) or zahab (gold) between us and Shaawal (Saul), or his bayath (house); neither is it for us to put any ayash (husband/individual man) to mawath (death) in Yasharaal (Israel)." He amar (spoke), Whatever you amar (spoke), that will I ishah (make) for you.

They amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "The ayash (husband/individual man) who kalah (complete / finish) us, and who damah (devised) against us, that we should be destroyed from yatzab (remaining) in any of the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yasharaal (Israel),

Let shabai (seven) ayash (husband/individual man) of his ban (son) be nathan (give) to us, and we will yaqai (hang) them up to Yahawah in Gabaih (Gibeah) of Shaawal (Saul), the bachayar (chosen) of Yahawah." The malak (king) amar (spoke), I will nathan (give) them.

But the malak (king) chamal (spared) Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth), the ban (son) of Yahawanathan (Jonathan) the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul), because of yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) shabawaih (oath) that was between them, between Dawad (David) and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul).

But the malak (king) laqach (take / seized) the shanayam (two) ban (son) of Ratzapah (Rizpah) the bath (daughter) of Ayah (Aiah), whom she yalad (birth / begot) to Shaawal (Saul), Aramanay (Armoni) and Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth); and the chamash (five) ban (son) of Mayakal (Michal) the bath (daughter) of Shaawal (Saul), whom she yalad (birth / begot) to Idarayaal (Adriel) the ban (son) of Barazalay (Barzillai) the Meholathite.

He nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of the Gabainay (Gibeonites), and they hanged them in the har (mountain) panayam (before) Yahawah, and all shabai (seven) of them napal (fall / be cast down) yachad (together). They were put to mawath (death) in the yawam (day) of qatzayar (harvest), in the raashawan (first) days, at the thachalah (beginning) of shairah (barley) qatzayar (harvest).

Ratzapah (Rizpah) the bath (daughter) of Ayah (Aiah) laqach (take / seized) sackcloth, and natah (spread) it for her on the tzawar (rock), from the thachalah (beginning) of qatzayar (harvest) until mayam (Waters) was nathak (poured) on them from the sky. She allowed neither the iwap (flying) of the sky to nawach (rest) on them by yawamam (by day), nor the animals of the shadah (field) by layal (night).
It was nagad (told) Dawad (David) what Ratzapah (Rizpah) the bath (daughter) of Ayah (Aiah), the payalagash (concubine) of Shaawal (Saul), ishah (make) done.

Dawad (David) yalak (went) and laqach (take / seized) the itzam (bones) of Shaawal (Saul) and the itzam (bones) of Yahawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son) from the bail (men) Yabash (of) Jabesh Gilead, who had ganab (stolen) them from the rachab (street) of Bayathashaan (Beth) Shan, where the Palashathay (Philistines) had hanged them, in the yawam (day) that the Palashathay (Philistines) nakah (killed) Shaawal (Saul) in Galabai (Gilboa);

And he ilah (go up / offer) up from there the itzam (bones) of Shaawal (Saul) and the itzam (bones) of Yahawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son): and they asap (gathered) the itzam (bones) of those who were hanged.

They qabar (bury) the itzam (bones) of Shaawal (Saul) and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) Tzalai (in) Zela, in the tomb of Qayash (Kish) his ab (father): and they ishah (make) all that the malak (king) tzawah (commanded). Achar (other) that Alahayam was entreated for the aratz (Earth/land).

The Palashathay (Philistines) had malachamah (war) again with Yasharaal (Israel); and Dawad (David) yarad (went) down, and his ibad (servant) with him, and lacham (fought) against the Palashathay (Philistines). Dawad (David) grew iwap (flying);

And Yashabawabanab (Ishbibenob), who was of the yalayad (sons) of the Rapaa (giant), the mashaqal (weight) of whose qayan (spear) was shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shekels of nachashath (brass) in mashaqal (weight), he being armed with a chadash (new) sword, amar (spoke) to have nakah (slain) Dawad (David).

But Abayashay (Abishai) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah) izar (helped) him, and nakah (struck) the Palashathay (Philistine), and mawath (death) him.
