Then the ban (son) of Dawad (David) shabai (swear / take oath) to him, amar (spoke), You shall yatzaa (go out / come out) no more out with us to malachamah (battle), that you don't kabah (quench) the nayar (lamp) of Yasharaal (Israel).

It came to pass achar (other) this, that there was again malachamah (war) with the Palashathay (Philistines) at Gab (Gob): then Sabakay (Sibbecai) the chashathay (hushathite) nakah (killed) Sap (Saph), who was of the yalayad (sons) of the Rapaa (giant).

There was again malachamah (war) with the Palashathay (Philistines) at Gab (Gob); and Alachanan (Elhanan) the ban (son) of Yairayaaragayam (Jaareoregim) the bayathahalachamay (bethlehemite) nakah (killed) Galayath (Goliath) the gathay (gittite's) brother, the itz (staff) of whose chanayath (spear) was like a arag (weaver's) manawar (beam).

There was again malachamah (war) at gath (gath), where there was a ayash (husband/individual man) of great madawan (stature), who had on every yad (hand) shash (six) atzabai (fingers), and on every ragal (feet / foot) shash (six) atzabai (toes), arabai (four) and isharayam (twenty) in masapar (number); and he also was yalad (birth / begot) to the Rapaa (giant).
When he charap (defied) Yasharaal (Israel), Yahawanathan (Jonathan) the ban (son) of Shamaiy (Shimei), Dawad (David's) ach (brother/kinsman), nakah (killed) him.

These arabai (four) were yalad (birth / begot) to the Rapaa (giant) in gath (gath); and they napal (fall / be cast down) by the yad (hand) of Dawad (David), and by the yad (hand) of his ibad (servant).

Dawad (David) dabar (word / matter) to Yahawah the dabar (word / matter) of this shayar (song) in the yawam (day) that Yahawah natzal (delivered) him out of the kap (hand) of all his ayab (enemy), and out of the kap (hand) of Shaawal (Saul):
And he amar (spoke), Yahawah is my salai (rock), my matzawad (fortress), and my deliverer, even mine;

Alahayam, my tzawar (rock), in him I will take chasah (refuge); my magan (shield), and the qaran (horn) of my yashai (salvation), my high tower, and my manawas (refuge). My savior, you yashai (salvation) me from chamas (violence).
I will qaraa (called) on Yahawah, who is halal (praise) to be praised: So shall I be yashai (salvation) from my ayab (enemy).
For the mashabar (waves) of mawath (death) surrounded me. The nachal (stream / river) of ungodliness made me baith (afraid).
The chabal (cords) of shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife) were around me. The mawaqash (snares) of mawath (death) caught me.

In my tzar (oppressor / distressor) I qaraa (called) on Yahawah. Yes, I qaraa (called) to my Alahayam. He shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice) out of his hayakal (temple). My cry came into his azan (ears).

Then the aratz (Earth/land) gaish (shook) and raish (trembled). The mawasadah (foundations) of shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) ragaz (quaked) and were gaish (shaken), because he was charah (hot with anger).
Ishan (smoke) ilah (go up / offer) up out of his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting). Ash (fire) out of his pah (mouth) akal (eat). Gachal (coals) were bair (kindled) by it.
He natah (bowed) the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) also, and yarad (came) down. Irapal (thick) darkness was under his ragal (feet / foot).
He rakab (rode) on a karawab (cherub), and iwap (flying). Yes, he was raah (see) on the kanap (wings) of the rawach (spirit / wind).
He shayath (put / appoint / make) chashak (darkness) sakah (pavilions) around himself: gathering of mayam (Waters), and ib (thick) clouds of the shachaq (skies).
At the nagah (brightness) before him, gachal (coals) of ash (fire) were bair (kindled).
Yahawah raim (thundered) from shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)). The Most ilayawan (high) nathan (give) his qawal (sound / voice).
He shalach (send) out chatz (arrows), and pawatz (scattered) them; baraq (lightning), and confused them.

Then the apayaq (channels) of the yam (sea/waters) raah (see). The mawasadah (foundations) of the thabal (world) were laid bare by the gairah (rebuke) of Yahawah, At the nashamah (breathing thing) of the rawach (spirit / wind) of his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).
He shalach (send) from on marawam (high) and he laqach (take / seized) me. He mashah (Mashah/(Moses)) me out of many mayam (Waters).
He natzal (delivered) me from my iz (strong) ayab (enemy), from those who shanaa (hate) me, for they were too amatz (mighty) for me.
They qadam (came) on me in the yawam (day) of my ayad (calamity), but Yahawah was my support.
He also yatzaa (go out / come out) me out into a marachab (large) place. He chalatz (delivered) me, because he chapatz (delighted) in me.
Yahawah gamal (rewarded) me according to my tzadaqah (righteousness). He shawab (turn back / repent) me according to the bar (cleanness) of my yad (hand).
For I have shamar (keep/guard) the darak (ways) of Yahawah, and have not wickedly departed from my Alahayam.
For all his mashapat (ordinances) were before me. As for his chaqah (statutes), I did not sawar (depart) from them.
I was also thamayam (complete / whole) toward him. I shamar (keep/guard) myself from my iwan (guilt/iniquity).
Therefore Yahawah has shawab (turn back / repent) me according to my tzadaqah (righteousness), According to my bar (cleanness) in his eyesight.
With the chasayad (merciful) you will show yourself chasad (grace). With the thamayam (complete / whole) gabawar (man) you will show yourself thamayam (complete / whole).
With the barar (pure) you will show yourself barar (pure). With the iqash (crooked) you will show yourself shrewd.
You will yashai (salvation) the inay (afflicted) im (people / nation), But your iyan (eye) are on the rawam (will lift up), that you may shapal (bring) them down.
For you are my nayar (lamp), Yahawah. Yahawah will nagah (light) up my chashak (darkness).
For by you, I rawatz (run) against a gadawad (troop). By my Alahayam, I dalag (leap) over a shawar (wall).
As for Al, his darak (way) is thamayam (complete / whole). The amarah (sayings) of Yahawah is tested. He is a magan (shield) to all those who take chasah (refuge) in him.
For who is Al, balaiday (besides) Yahawah? Who is a tzawar (rock), balaiday (besides) our Alahayam?
Al is my maiwaz (stronghold / fortress / protection) fortress. He nathar (makes) my darak (way) thamayam (complete / whole).
He shawah (makes) his ragal (feet / foot) shawah (like) ayalah (hinds)' feet, and imad (sets) me on my bamah (high) places.
He teaches my yad (hand) to malachamah (war), so that my zarawai (arms) bend a qashath (bow) of nachawashah (brass).
You nathan (give) also given me the magan (shield) of your yashai (salvation). Your inah (oppress / afflict) rabah (has) made me great.
You have enlarged my tzaid (steps) under me. My qarasal (feet) have not maid (slipped).
I have radap (pursued) my ayab (enemy) and destroyed them. I didn't shawab (turn back / repent) again until they were kalah (complete / finish).
I napal (fall / be cast down) consumed them, and machatz (crush / shatter) them through, so that they can't qawam (rise up). Yes, they napal (fall / be cast down) fallen under my ragal (feet / foot).
For you have armed me with chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) for the malachamah (battle). You have karai (subdued) under me those who qawam (rise up) up against me.
You nathan (give) also made my ayab (enemy) turn their irap (neck) to me, that I might tzamath (cut) off those who shanaa (hate) me.
They shaih (looked), but there was none to yashai (salvation); even to Yahawah, but he didn't inah (answer / respond) them.
Then I shachaq (beat) them as small as the ipar (dust) of the aratz (Earth/land). I crushed them as the tayat (mire) of the chawatz (streets), and raqai (spread) them abroad.

You also have palat (delivered) me from the rayab (strivings) of my im (people / nation). You have shamar (keep/guard) me to be the raash (head) of the gaway (nation / people). A im (people / nation) whom I yadai (have) not known will ibad (servant) me.
The foreigners will kachash (submit) themselves to me. As soon as they shamai (hearken / hear) of me, they will shamai (hearken / hear) me.
The foreigners will nabal (fade) away, and will come trembling out of their masagarath (close) places.
Yahawah chay (life)! Barak (blessed) be my tzawar (rock)! Rawam (will lift up) be Alahayam, the tzawar (rock) of my yashai (salvation),
Even the Al who executes vengeance for me, who yarad (brings) down im (people / nation) under me,

Who yatzaa (go out / come out) me away from my ayab (enemy). Yes, you rawam (will lift up) me up above those who qawam (rise up) up against me. You natzal (deliver) me from the chamas (violent) ayash (husband/individual man).
Therefore I will give yadah (thanks) to you, Yahawah, among the gaway (nation / people). Will sing zamar (praises) to your sham (name).
He gives great yashawaih (salvation) to his malak (king), and shows loving chasad (grace) to his mashayach (anointed one), to Dawad (David) and to his zarai (seed), forevermore.

Now these are the acharawan (last) dabar (word / matter) of Dawad (David). Dawad (David) the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse) naam (declares (prophetically)), the gabar (man) who was qawam (rise up) on il (over) naam (declares (prophetically)), the mashayach (anointed one) of the Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob), the naiyam (sweet) zamayar (psalmist) of Yasharaal (Israel):
The rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah dabar (word / matter) by me. His malah (word) was on my lashawan (tongue/language).

The Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke), the tzawar (rock) of Yasharaal (Israel) dabar (word / matter) to me, ‘One who mashal (rule/have dominion) over adam (men) righteously, who mashal (rule/have dominion) in the yaraah (fear) of Alahayam,

Shall be as the awar (light) of the baqar (morning), when the shamash (sun) zarach (rises), a baqar (morning) laa (NOT) ib (clouds), when the tender dashaa (grass) springs out of the aratz (Earth/land), through clear nagah (shining) after matar (rain).’

Most certainly my bayath (house) is not so with Al, yet he has shawam (place / establish / appoint) with me an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant), irak (ordered) in all things, and shamar (keep/guard), for it is all my yashai (salvation), and all my chapatz (desire), although he doesn't tzamach (make) it grow.
But all of the balayail (ungodly) shall be as qawatz (thorns) to be nadad (thrust) away, because they can't be laqach (take / seized) with the yad (hand),

But the ayash (husband/individual man) who touches them must be armed with barazal (iron) and the itz (staff) of a chanayath (spear). They shall be sharap (utterly) sharap (burned) with ash (fire) in their shabath (shabath/rest).

These are the sham (name) of the gabawar (mighty) men whom Dawad (David) had: Josheb Basshebeth a Tahchemonite, raash (head) of the shalayash (captains); the same was Idayanaw (Adino) the itzan (eznite), against shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) chalal (slain) at achad (one) paim (time).

Achar (other) him was Alaizar (Eleazar) the ban (son) Dawadaw (of) Dodai the son of an Achawachay (Ahohite), one of the shalawash (three) gabawar (mighty) men with Dawad (David), when they charap (defied) the Palashathay (Philistines) who were there asap (gathered) together to malachamah (battle), and the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yasharaal (Israel) were ilah (go up / offer) away.

He qawam (rise up), and nakah (struck) the Palashathay (Philistines) kay (surely) his yad (hand) was yagai (weary), and his yad (hand) froze to the charab (sword); and Yahawah ishah (make) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thashawaih (deliverance) that yawam (day); and the im (people / nation) shawab (turn back / repent) achar (other) him only to take pashat (spoil).

Achar (other) him was Shammah the ban (son) of Agaa (Agee) a hararay (hararite). The Palashathay (Philistines) were asap (gathered) together into a chay (life), where there was a plot of shadah (ground) full of lentils; and the im (people / nation) nawas (fled) from the Palashathay (Philistines).

But he yatzab (stood) in the thawak (midst) of the plot, and natzal (defended) it, and nakah (killed) the Palashathay (Philistines); and Yahawah ishah (make) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thashawaih (deliverance).

Three of the shalawashayam (thirty) raash (head) men yarad (went) down, and bawaa (come) to Dawad (David) in the qatzayar (harvest) time to the mairah (cave) of Idalam (Adullam); and the chay (life) of the Palashathay (Philistines) was chanah (encamped) in the imaq (valley) of Rapaa (Rephaim).
Dawad (David) was then in the stronghold; and the matzab (garrison) of the Palashathay (Philistines) was then in Bayathalacham (Bethlehem).
Dawad (David) awah (longed), and amar (spoke), Oh that one would give me mayam (Waters) to shaqah (drink) of the well of Bayathalacham (Bethlehem), which is by the shair (gate)!

The shalawash (three) gabawar (mighty) men baqai (broke) through the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and shaab (drew) mayam (Waters) out of the well of Bayathalacham (Bethlehem), that was by the shair (gate), and nashaa (lift) it, and bawaa (come) it to Dawad (David): but he would not shathah (drinks) of it, but nasak (poured) it out to Yahawah.

He amar (spoke), "Be it chalayalah (far) from me, Yahawah, that I should ishah (make) this! Isn't it the dam (blood) of the ishah (make) who halak (move) in napash (living being/soul) of their lives?" Therefore he would not shathah (drinks) it. The shalawash (three) gabawar (mighty) men ishah (make) these things.

Abayashay (Abishai), the ach (brother/kinsman) of Yawaab (Joab), the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah), was raash (head) of the shalayashay (third). He iwar (rouse / awaken) up his chanayath (spear) against shalawash (three) maah (hundred) and chalal (killed) them, and had a sham (name) among the shalawash (three).
Wasn't he most honorable of the shalawash (three)? Therefore he was made their shar (prince / ruler): however he didn't bawaa (come) to the shalawash (three).

Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada), the ban (son) of a ban (son) ayash (husband/individual man) of Qabatzaal (Kabzeel), who had done rab (mighty) pail (deeds), he nakah (killed) the shanayam (two) Arayaal (sons) of Ariel of Mawaab (Moab): he yarad (went) down also and nakah (killed) a aray (lion) in the thawak (midst) of a bawar (pit) in yawam (day) of shalag (snow).

He harag (killed) an Matzaray (Egyptian), a maraah (goodly) ayash (husband/individual man): and the Matzaray (Egyptian) had a chanayath (spear) in his yad (hand); but he yarad (went) down to him with a shabat (staff), and gazal (plucked) the chanayath (spear) out of the Matzaray (Egyptian's) yad (hand), and nakah (killed) him with his own chanayath (spear).
Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) ishah (make) these things, and had a sham (name) among the shalawash (three) gabawar (mighty) men.
He was more honorable than the shalawashayam (thirty), but he didn't bawaa (come) to the shalawash (three). Dawad (David) shawam (place / establish / appoint) him over his mashamaith (guard).
Ishahaal (Asahel) the ach (brother/kinsman) of Yawaab (Joab) was one of the shalawashayam (thirty); Alachanan (Elhanan) the ban (son) of Dawadaw (Dodo) of Bayathalacham (Bethlehem),
Shamah (Shammah) the Charaday (Harodite), Alayaqaa (Elika) the Charaday (Harodite),
Chalatz (Helez) the Palatay (Paltite), Iyaraa (Ira) the ban (son) of Iqash (Ikkesh) the Thaqawaiy (Tekoite),
Abayaizar (Abiezer) the Inathathay (Anathothite), Mabanay (Mebunnai) the chashathay (hushathite),
Tzalamawan (Zalmon) the Achawachay (Ahohite), Maharay (Maharai) the Natapathay (Netophathite),
Chalab (Heleb) the ban (son) of Bainah (Baanah) the Natapathay (Netophathite), Athay (Ittai) the ban (son) of Rayabay (Ribai) of Gabaih (Gibeah) of the ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin),
Banayah (Benaiah) a paraithawanay (pirathonite), Haday (Hiddai) of the nachal (stream / river) of Gaish (Gaash).
Abayailabawan (Abialbon) the Arbathite, Izamawath (Azmaveth) the barachamay (barhumite),
Alayachabaa (Eliahba) the shailabanay (shaalbonite), the ban (son) of Yashan (Jashen), Yahawanathan (Jonathan),
Shamah (Shammah) the hararay (hararite), Achayaam (Ahiam) the ban (son) of Sharar (Sharar) the Ararite,
Alayapalat (Eliphelet) the ban (son) of Achasabay (Ahasbai), the ban (son) of the Maikathay (Maacathite), Alayaim (Eliam) the ban (son) of Achayathapal (Ahithophel) the gayalanay (gilonite),
Chatzaraw (Hezro) the karamalay (carmelite), Pairay (Paarai) the arabay (arbite),
Yagaal (Igal) the ban (son) of Nathan (Nathan) of Tzawabaa (Zobah), Banay (Bani) the Gaday (Gadite),
Tzalaq (Zelek) the Imawanay (Ammonite), Nacharay (Naharai) the Baarathay (Beerothite), armor bearers to Yawaab (Joab) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah),
Iyaraa (Ira) the yatharay (ithrite), Garab (Gareb) the yatharay (ithrite),
Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite): shalawashayam (thirty) - shabai (seven) in all.

Again the ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah was charah (hot with anger) against Yasharaal (Israel), and he sawath (moved) Dawad (David) amar (spoke) them, saying, yalak (go), manah (number) Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah).

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Yawaab (Joab) the shar (prince / ruler) of the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), who was with him, Now shawat (go) back and forth through all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), Dan (from) Dan Baarashabai (even) to Beersheba, and paqad (visit) the im (people / nation), that I may yadai (know) the sum of the im (people / nation).

Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), Now may Yahawah your Alahayam yasap (add) to the im (people / nation), however many they may be, one maah (hundred) times; and may the iyan (eye) of my Adawan the malak (king) raah (see) it. But why does my Adawan the malak (king) chapatz (delight) in this thing?

Notwithstanding, the malak (king) dabar (word / matter) chazaq (prevailed) against Yawaab (Joab), and against the shar (prince / ruler) of the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor). Yawaab (Joab) and the shar (prince / ruler) of the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) yatzaa (go out / come out) out from the panayam (presence) of the malak (king), to paqad (visit) the im (people / nation) of Yasharaal (Israel).

They ibar (pass over/through) over the Yaradan (Jordan), and chanah (encamped) in Irawair (Aroer), on the yamayan (right hand) side of the iyar (city) that is in the thawak (midst) of the nachal (stream / river) of Gad (Gad), and to Yaizayar (Jazer):
Then they bawaa (come) to Galaid (Gilead), and to the aratz (Earth/land) of Thachathayamachadashay (Tahtim) Hodshi; and they bawaa (come) to Danayain (Dan) Jaan, and around to Tzayadawan (Sidon),

And bawaa (come) to the stronghold of Tzar (Tyre), and to all the iyar (cities) of the Chaway (Hivites), and of the Kanainay (Canaanites); and they yatzaa (go out / come out) out to the nagab (south) of Yahawadah (Judah), Baarashabai (at) Beersheba.

So when they had shawat (gone) back and forth through all the aratz (Earth/land), they bawaa (come) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) at the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of thashai (nine) chadash (month) and isharayam (twenty) yawam (day).

Yawaab (Joab) nathan (give) up the sum of the mapaqad (numbering) of the im (people / nation) to the malak (king): and there were in Yasharaal (Israel) shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ayash (husband/individual man) who shalap (drew) the charab (sword); and the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yahawadah (Judah) were chamash (five) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man).

Dawad (David's) lab (heart) nakah (struck) him achar (other) that he had sapar (book) the im (people / nation). Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Yahawah, I have chataa (sinned) maad (greatly) in that which I ishah (make) done. But now, Yahawah, ibar (pass over/through) away, I beg you, the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of your ibad (servant); for I have done very foolishly.
When Dawad (David) qawam (rise up) up in the baqar (morning), the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) Gad (Gad), Dawad (David's) chazah (seer), amar (spoke),
Halak (move) and amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "I natal (offer) you shalawash (three) things. Bachar (choose) achad (one) of them, that I may ishah (make) it to you."’

So Gad (Gad) bawaa (come) to Dawad (David), and nagad (told) him, and amar (spoke) to him, Shall shabai (seven) shanah (years) of raib (famine) bawaa (come) to you in your aratz (Earth/land)? Or will you nawas (flee) shalawash (three) chadash (month) panayam (before) your tzar (oppressor / distressor) while they radap (pursue) you? Or shall there be shalawash (three) yawam (day)' dabar (word / matter) in your aratz (Earth/land)? Now yadai (answer), and raah (see) dabar (word / matter) answer I shall shawab (turn back / repent) to him who shalach (send) me.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Gad (Gad), I am in tzar (oppressor / distressor). Napal (fall / be cast down) us fall now into the yad (hand) of Yahawah; for his racham (mercies) are rab (great). Napal (fall / be cast down) me not fall into the yad (hand) of adam (man).

So Yahawah nathan (give) a dabar (word / matter) on Yasharaal (Israel) from the baqar (morning) even to the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) ith (time); and there mawath (death) of the im (people / nation) Dan (from) Dan Baarashabai (even) to Beersheba shabaiyam (seventy) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man).

When the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) shalach (send) out his yad (hand) toward Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) to shachath (destroy) it, Yahawah relented of the disaster, and amar (spoke) to the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) who shachath (destroyed) the im (people / nation), "It is rab (enough). Now rapah (stay) your yad (hand)." The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah was by the garan (threshing) floor of Arawanah (Araunah) the Yabawasay (Jebusite).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Yahawah when he raah (see) the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) who nakah (struck) the im (people / nation), and amar (spoke), Behold, I have chataa (sinned), and I have iwah (done) perversely; but these tzaan (sheep), what ishah (make) they done? Please let your yad (hand) be against me, and against my ab (father) bayath (house).

Gad (Gad) bawaa (come) that yawam (day) to Dawad (David), and amar (spoke) to him, ilah (go up / offer) up, build an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah on the garan (threshing) floor of Arawanah (Araunah) the Yabawasay (Jebusite).
Dawad (David) ilah (go up / offer) up according to the dabar (word / matter) of Gad (Gad), as Yahawah tzawah (commanded).

Arawanah (Araunah) shaqap (looked) out, and raah (see) the malak (king) and his ibad (servant) ibar (pass over/through) on toward him. Then Arawanah (Araunah) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and shachah (bowed) himself before the malak (king) with his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land).

Arawanah (Araunah) amar (spoke), "Why has my Adawan the malak (king) bawaa (come) to his ibad (servant)?" Dawad (David) amar (spoke), To qanah (buy) your garan (threshing) floor, to banah (build) an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah, that the magapah (plague) may be itzar (stopped) from afflicting the im (people / nation).

Arawanah (Araunah) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "Let my Adawan the malak (king) laqach (take / seized) and ilah (go up / offer) up what seems tawab (pleasant/functional) to him. Raah (see), the cattle for the burnt ilah (offering), and the mawarag (threshing) instruments and the yokes of the oxen for the itz (wood):
All this, malak (king), does Arawanah (Araunah) nathan (give) to the malak (king)." Arawanah (Araunah) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), May Yahawah your Alahayam ratzah (accept) you.

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Arawanah (Araunah), "No; but I will most certainly qanah (buy) it from you for a machayar (price). I will not ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilah (offerings) to Yahawah my Alahayam which chanam (cost) me nothing." So Dawad (David) bought the garan (threshing) floor and the oxen for chamashayam (fifty) shaqal (shekels) of kasap (silver).

Dawad (David) banah (built) an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah there, and ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilah (offerings) and peace ilah (offerings). So Yahawah was entreated for the aratz (Earth/land), and the magapah (plague) was itzar (stayed) from Yasharaal (Israel).
Now malak (king) Dawad (David) was zaqan (old) and bawaa (come) in yawam (day); and they kasah (covered) him with clothes, but he couldn't keep yacham (warm).

Therefore his ibad (servant) amar (spoke) to him, Let there be baqash (sought) for my Adawan the malak (king) a nairah (young) bathawalah (virgin). Let her imad (stand) panayam (before) the malak (king), and cherish him; and let her shakab (lie) in your chayaq (bosom), that my Adawan the malak (king) may keep chamam (warm).

So they baqash (sought) for a yapah (beautiful) nairah (young) lady throughout all the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yasharaal (Israel), and matzaa (found) Abayashag (Abishag) the Shunammite, and bawaa (come) her to the malak (king).
The nairah (young) lady was very yapah (beautiful); and she cherished the malak (king), and sharath (ministered) to him; but the malak (king) didn't yadai (know) her intimately.

Then Adanayah (Adonijah) the ban (son) of Chagayath (Haggith) mathanashaa (exalted) himself, amar (spoke), "I will be malak (king)." Then he ishah (make) him rakab (chariots) and horsemen, and chamashayam (fifty) ayash (husband/individual man) to rawatz (run) panayam (before) him.

His ab (father) had not itzab (displeased) him at any yawam (day) in amar (spoke), "Why ishah (make) you done so?" And he was also a very handsome man; and he was yalad (birth / begot) achar (other) Abayashalawam (Absalom).
He dabar (word / matter) with Yawaab (Joab) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah), and with Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahan (priest): and they achar (other) Adanayah (Adonijah) izar (helped) him.

But Tzadawaq (Zadok) the kahan (priest), and Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada), and Nathan (Nathan) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and Shamaiy (Shimei), and Raiy (Rei), and the gabawar (mighty) men who belonged to Dawad (David), were not with Adanayah (Adonijah).

Adanayah (Adonijah) zabach (killed) tzaan (sheep) and cattle and fatlings by the aban (stone) of Zachalath (Zoheleth), which is beside Iyanaragal (En) Rogel; and he qaraa (called) all his ach (brother/kinsman), the malak (king) ban (son), and all the ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah), the malak (king) ibad (servant):
But Nathan (Nathan) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and Banayah (Benaiah), and the gabawar (mighty) men, and Shalamah (Solomon) his ach (brother/kinsman), he didn't qaraa (called).

Then Nathan (Nathan) amar (spoke) to Bathashabai (Bathsheba) the am (mother) of Shalamah (Solomon), amar (spoke), Haven't you shamai (hearken / hear) that Adanayah (Adonijah) the ban (son) of Chagayath (Haggith) malak (king), and Dawad (David) our Adawan doesn't yadai (know) it?

Now therefore yalak (come), please let me give you yaitz (counsel), that you may malat (save) your own napash (living being/soul), and the napash (living being/soul) of your ban (son) Shalamah (Solomon).

Yalak (go) in to malak (king) Dawad (David), and amar (spoke) him, ‘Didn't you, my Adawan, malak (king), shabai (swear / take oath) to your handmaid, amar (spoke), kay (surely) Shalamah (Solomon) your ban (son) shall malak (king) achar (other) me, and he shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) on my kasaa (throne)? Why then does Adanayah (Adonijah) malak (king)?’
Behold, while you yet dabar (word / matter) there with the malak (king), I also will bawaa (come) in achar (other) you, and malaa (confirm) your dabar (word / matter).
Bathashabai (Bathsheba) bawaa (come) in to the malak (king) into the room. The malak (king) was very zaqan (old); and Abayashag (Abishag) the Shunammite was sharath (ministering) to the malak (king).
Bathashabai (Bathsheba) qadad (bowed), and showed respect to the malak (king). The malak (king) amar (spoke), What would you like?

She amar (spoke) to him, My Adawan, you shabai (swear / take oath) by Yahawah your Alahayam to your handmaid, ‘Assuredly Shalamah (Solomon) your ban (son) shall malak (king) achar (other) me, and he shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) on my kasaa (throne).’
Now, behold, Adanayah (Adonijah) malak (king); and you, my Adawan the malak (king), don't yadai (know) it.

He has zabach (slain) cattle and fatlings and tzaan (sheep) in rab (abundance), and has qaraa (called) all the ban (son) of the malak (king), and Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahan (priest), and Yawaab (Joab) the shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop); but he hasn't qaraa (called) Shalamah (Solomon) your ibad (servant).

You, my Adawan the malak (king), the iyan (eye) of all Yasharaal (Israel) are on you, that you should nagad (tell) them who shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the kasaa (throne) of my Adawan the malak (king) achar (other) him.
Otherwise it will happen, when my Adawan the malak (king) shall sleep with his ab (father), that I and my ban (son) Shalamah (Solomon) shall be counted chataa (offenders).
Behold, while she yet dabar (word / matter) with the malak (king), Nathan (Nathan) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) bawaa (come) in.

They nagad (told) the malak (king), amar (spoke), "Behold, Nathan (Nathan) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy)!" When he bawaa (come) come in panayam (before) the malak (king), he shachah (bowed) himself before the malak (king) with his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land).
Nathan (Nathan) amar (spoke), My Adawan, malak (king), have you amar (spoke), ‘Adanayah (Adonijah) shall malak (king) achar (other) me, and he shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) on my kasaa (throne)?’

For he is yarad (gone) down this yawam (day), and has zabach (slain) cattle and fatlings and tzaan (sheep) in rab (abundance), and has qaraa (called) all the malak (king) ban (son), and the shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop), and Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahan (priest). Behold, they are akal (eat) and shathah (drinks) panayam (before) him, and amar (spoke), ‘Long chayah (live) malak (king) Adanayah (Adonijah)!’

But he hasn't qaraa (called) me, even me your ibad (servant), and Tzadawaq (Zadok) the kahan (priest), and Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada), and your ibad (servant) Shalamah (Solomon).

Is this thing hayah (came to pass) by my Adawan the malak (king), and you haven't shown to your ibad (servant) who should yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the kasaa (throne) of my Adawan the malak (king) achar (other) him?

Then malak (king) Dawad (David) inah (answer / respond), "qaraa (called) to me Bathashabai (Bathsheba)." She bawaa (come) into the malak (king) panayam (presence), and imad (stood) panayam (before) the malak (king).
The malak (king) shabai (swear / take oath), and amar (spoke), As Yahawah chay (life), who has padah (redeemed) my napash (living being/soul) out of all tzarah (adversity),

Most certainly as I shabai (swear / take oath) to you by Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), ‘Assuredly Shalamah (Solomon) your ban (son) shall malak (king) achar (other) me, and he shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) on my kasaa (throne) in my place;’ most ishah (make) so will I do this yawam (day).

Then Bathashabai (Bathsheba) qadad (bowed) with her ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land), and showed respect to the malak (king), and amar (spoke), Let my Adawan malak (king) Dawad (David) chayah (live) iwalam (forever)!

Malak (king) Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "qaraa (called) to me Tzadawaq (Zadok) the kahan (priest), Nathan (Nathan) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada)." They bawaa (come) panayam (before) the malak (king).

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to them, laqach (take / seized) with you the ibad (servant) of your Adawan, and cause Shalamah (Solomon) my ban (son) to rakab (ride) on my own paradah (mule), and yarad (bring) him down to Gayachawan (Gihon).

Let Tzadawaq (Zadok) the kahan (priest) and Nathan (Nathan) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) mashach (anoint) him there malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel). Thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), and amar (spoke), ‘Long chayah (live) malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon)!’

Then you shall ilah (go up / offer) up achar (other) him, and he shall bawaa (come) and yashab (inhabit/dwell) on my kasaa (throne); for he shall be malak (king) in my place. I have tzawah (appointed) him to be nagayad (prince) over Yasharaal (Israel) and over Yahawadah (Judah).

Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) inah (answer / respond) the malak (king), and inah (answer / respond), aman (believe / have faith). May Yahawah, the Alahayam of my Adawan the malak (king), amar (spoke) so.

As Yahawah has been with my Adawan the malak (king), even so may he be with Shalamah (Solomon), and gadal (make) his kasaa (throne) greater than the kasaa (throne) of my Adawan malak (king) Dawad (David).

So Tzadawaq (Zadok) the kahan (priest), and Nathan (Nathan) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada), and the Karathay (Cherethites) and the Palathay (Pelethites), yarad (went) down, and caused Shalamah (Solomon) to rakab (ride) on malak (king) Dawad (David's) paradah (mule), and yalak (brought) him to Gayachawan (Gihon).

Tzadawaq (Zadok) the kahan (priest) laqach (take / seized) the qaran (horn) of shaman (oil) out of the ahal (tent), and mashach (anointed) Shalamah (Solomon). They thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)); and all the im (people / nation) amar (spoke), Long chayah (live) malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon)!

All the im (people / nation) ilah (go up / offer) up achar (other) him, and the im (people / nation) chalal (piped) with chalayal (pipes), and shamach (rejoiced) with gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shamachah (joy), so that the aratz (Earth/land) shook with their qawal (sound / voice).

Adanayah (Adonijah) and all the qaraa (called) who were with him shamai (hearken / hear) it as they kalah (complete / finish) made an end of akal (eat). When Yawaab (Joab) shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), he amar (spoke), Why is this qawal (sound / voice) of the qarayah (city) being in an hamah (they)?

While he yet dabar (word / matter), behold, Yawanathan (Jonathan) the ban (son) of Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahan (priest) bawaa (come): and Adanayah (Adonijah) amar (spoke), bawaa (come) in; for you are a worthy ayash (husband/individual man), and bashar (bring) tawab (pleasant/functional) news.
Yawanathan (Jonathan) inah (answer / respond) Adanayah (Adonijah), Most certainly our Adawan malak (king) Dawad (David) has made Shalamah (Solomon) malak (king).

The malak (king) has shalach (send) with him Tzadawaq (Zadok) the kahan (priest), Nathan (Nathan) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada), and the Karathay (Cherethites) and the Palathay (Pelethites); and they have rakab (caused) him to ride on the malak (king) paradah (mule).

Tzadawaq (Zadok) the kahan (priest) and Nathan (Nathan) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) have mashach (anointed) him malak (king) in Gayachawan (Gihon). They have ilah (go up / offer) up from there shamach (rejoicing), so that the qarayah (city) hawam (rang) again. This is the qawal (sound / voice) that you have shamai (hearken / hear).
Also, Shalamah (Solomon) yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the kasaa (throne) of the malawakah (kingdom).

Moreover the malak (king) ibad (servant) bawaa (come) to barak (bless) our Adawan malak (king) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), ‘May your Alahayam make the sham (name) of Shalamah (Solomon) yatab (better) than your sham (name), and gadal (make) his kasaa (throne) greater than your kasaa (throne);’ and the malak (king) shachah (bowed) himself on the mashakab (bed).

Also thus amar (spoke) the malak (king), ‘barak (blessed) be Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), who nathan (give) given one to yashab (inhabit/dwell) on my kasaa (throne) this yawam (day), my iyan (eye) even seeing it.’
All the qaraa (called) of Adanayah (Adonijah) were charad (afraid), and qawam (rise up) up, and each ayash (husband/individual man) yalak (went) his darak (way).
Adanayah (Adonijah) yaraa (fear / be afraid) panayam (because) of Shalamah (Solomon); and he qawam (rise up), and yalak (went), and chazaq (caught) hold on the qaran (horn) of the mazabach (altar).

It was nagad (told) Shalamah (Solomon), amar (spoke), Behold, Adanayah (Adonijah) yaraa (fear / be afraid) malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon); for, behold, he achaz (has) laid hold on the qaran (horn) of the mazabach (altar), amar (spoke), ‘Let malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon) shabai (swear / take oath) to me yawam (day) that he will not mawath (death) his ibad (servant) with the charab (sword).’

Shalamah (Solomon) amar (spoke), If he shows himself a chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ban (son), not a shairah (hair) of him shall napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land); but if rai (wickedness) be matzaa (found) in him, he shall mawath (death).

So malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon) shalach (send), and they yarad (brought) him down from the mazabach (altar). He bawaa (come) and shachah (bowed) down to malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon); and Shalamah (Solomon) amar (spoke) to him, yalak (go) to your bayath (house).
Now the yawam (day) of Dawad (David) qarab (come close) near that he should mawath (death); and he tzawah (commanded) Shalamah (Solomon) his ban (son), amar (spoke),
I am halak (move) the darak (way) of all the aratz (Earth/land). You be chazaq (strong) therefore, and show yourself a ayash (husband/individual man);

And shamar (keep/guard) the instruction of Yahawah your Alahayam, to yalak (walk) in his darak (ways), to shamar (keep/guard) his chaqah (statutes), his matzawah (commandments), his mashapat (ordinances), and his idawath (testimonies), according to that which is kathab (written) in the thawarah (instruction) of Mashah (Moses), that you may shakal (prosper) in all that you ishah (make), and wherever you panah (turn) yourself.

That Yahawah may qawam (rise up) his dabar (word / matter) which he dabar (word / matter) concerning me, amar (spoke), ‘If your ban (son) shamar (keep/guard) heed to their darak (way), to yalak (walk) panayam (before) me in amath (truth) with all their labab (heart) and with all their napash (living being/soul), there shall not karath (cut) you,’ he amar (spoke), ‘a ayash (husband/individual man) on the kasaa (throne) of Yasharaal (Israel).’

Moreover you yadai (know) also what Yawaab (Joab) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah) ishah (make) to me, even what he ishah (make) to the shanayam (two) shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop) of Yasharaal (Israel), to Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner), and to Imashaa (Amasa) the ban (son) of Yathar (Jether), whom he harag (killed), and shed the dam (blood) of malachamah (war) in shalawam (peace / safety), and nathan (give) the dam (blood) of malachamah (war) on his sash that was about his waist, and in his nail (shoes) that were on his ragal (feet / foot).

Ishah (make) therefore according to your chakamah (wisdom), and don't let his gray shayabah (old age / white hair (due to age)) yarad (go) down to shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife) in shalawam (peace / safety).

But show chasad (grace) to the ban (son) of Barazalay (Barzillai) the Galaiday (Gileadite), and let them be of those who akal (eat) at your shalachan (table); for so they qarab (come close) to me when I barach (fled) from Abayashalawam (Absalom) your ach (brother/kinsman).

Behold, there is with you Shamaiy (Shimei) the ban (son) of Garaa (Gera), the Banayamayanay (Benjamite), of Bacharayam (Bahurim), who qalal (cursed) me with a maratz (grievous) qalalah (curse) in the yawam (day) when I yalak (went) to Machanayam (Mahanaim); but he yarad (came) down to qaraah (meet) me at the Yaradan (Jordan), and I shabai (swear / take oath) to him by Yahawah, amar (spoke), ‘I will not put you to mawath (death) with the charab (sword).’

Now therefore don't hold him naqah (clean/innocent), for you are a chakam (wise) ayash (husband/individual man); and you yadai (will) know what you ought to ishah (make) to him, and you shall bring his gray shayabah (old age / white hair (due to age)) down to shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife) with dam (blood).
Dawad (David) shakab (slept) with his ab (father), and was qabar (bury) in the iyar (city) of Dawad (David).

The yawam (day) that Dawad (David) malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel) were arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years); he malak (king) shabai (seven) shanah (years) in Chabarawan (Hebron), and he malak (king) shalawashayam (thirty) - shalawash (three) shanah (years) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).
Shalamah (Solomon) yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the kasaa (throne) of Dawad (David) his ab (father); and his malakawath (kingdom) was firmly kawan (established).

Then Adanayah (Adonijah) the ban (son) of Chagayath (Haggith) bawaa (come) to Bathashabai (Bathsheba) the am (mother) of Shalamah (Solomon). She amar (spoke), "Do you bawaa (come) peaceably?" He amar (spoke), "Peaceably.
He amar (spoke) moreover, I have something to tell you." She dabar (word / matter), dabar (word / matter) on.

He amar (spoke), "You yadai (know) that the malawakah (kingdom) was mine, and that all Yasharaal (Israel) shawam (place / establish / appoint) their panayam (faces) on me, that I should malak (king). However the malawakah (kingdom) is sabab (turned) around, and has become my ach (brother/kinsman); for it was his from Yahawah.
Now I shaal (ask) achad (one) shaalah (petition) of you. Don't shawab (turn back / repent) me." She amar (spoke) to him, dabar (word / matter) on.

He amar (spoke), Please amar (spoke) to Shalamah (Solomon) the malak (king) (for he will not tell you ‘no’), that he nathan (give) me Abayashag (Abishag) the Shunammite as ashah (wife/individual woman).
Bathashabai (Bathsheba) amar (spoke), Alright. I will dabar (word / matter) for you to the malak (king).

Bathashabai (Bathsheba) therefore bawaa (come) to malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon), to dabar (word / matter) to him for Adanayah (Adonijah). The malak (king) qawam (rise up) up to qaraah (meet) her, and shachah (bowed) himself to her, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) down on his kasaa (throne), and caused a kasaa (throne) to be shawam (place / establish / appoint) for the malak (king) am (mother); and she sat on his right yamayan (right hand).

Then she said, "I shaal (ask) achad (one) qatan (small/young/least) shaalah (petition) of you; don't shawab (turn back / repent) me." The malak (king) shawab (turn back / repent) to her, Ask on, my am (mother); for I will not shawab (turn back / repent) you.
She amar (spoke), Let Abayashag (Abishag) the Shunammite be nathan (give) to Adanayah (Adonijah) your ach (brother/kinsman) as ashah (wife/individual woman).

Malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon) inah (answer / respond) his am (mother), Why do you shaal (ask) Abayashag (Abishag) the Shunammite for Adanayah (Adonijah)? Shaal (ask) for him the malawakah (kingdom) also; for he is my gadawal (very great/important/mighty) ach (brother/kinsman); even for him, and for Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahan (priest), and for Yawaab (Joab) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah).

Then malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon) shabai (swear / take oath) by Yahawah, amar (spoke), Alahayam ishah (make) so to me, and more also, if Adanayah (Adonijah) has not dabar (word / matter) this dabar (word / matter) against his own napash (living being/soul).

Now therefore as Yahawah chay (life), who has kawan (established) me, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) me on the kasaa (throne) of Dawad (David) my ab (father), and who ishah (make) made me a bayath (house), as he dabar (word / matter), surely Adanayah (Adonijah) shall be put to mawath (death) this yawam (day).
Malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon) shalach (send) by Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada); and he pagai (fell) on him, so that he mawath (death).

To Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahan (priest) the malak (king) amar (spoke), yalak (go) to Inathawath (Anathoth), to your own shadah (fields); for you are ayash (husband/individual man) of mawath (death). But I will not at this yawam (day) put you to mawath (death), because you nashaa (lift) the arawan (ark) of the Adanay Yahawah panayam (before) Dawad (David) my ab (father), and because you were inah (oppress / afflict) in all in which my ab (father) was inah (oppress / afflict).

So Shalamah (Solomon) garash (thrust) out Abayathar (Abiathar) from being kahan (priest) to Yahawah, that he might fulfill the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, which he dabar (word / matter) concerning the bayath (house) of Ilay (Eli) in Shayalah (Shiloh).

The shamawaih (news) bawaa (come) to Yawaab (Joab); for Yawaab (Joab) had natah (turned) achar (other) Adanayah (Adonijah), though he didn't natah (turn) achar (other) Abayashalawam (Absalom). Yawaab (Joab) nawas (fled) to the ahal (tent) of Yahawah, and chazaq (caught) hold on the qaran (horn) of the mazabach (altar).

It was nagad (told) malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon), "Yawaab (Joab) has nawas (fled) to the ahal (tent) of Yahawah, and behold, he is by the mazabach (altar)." Then Shalamah (Solomon) shalach (send) Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada), amar (spoke), yalak (go), pagai (fall) on him.

Banayah (Benaiah) bawaa (come) to the ahal (tent) of Yahawah, and amar (spoke) to him, "Thus amar (spoke) the malak (king), ‘yatzaa (go out / come out) forth!’" He amar (spoke), "No; but I will mawath (death) here." Banayah (Benaiah) shawab (turn back / repent) the malak (king) dabar (word / matter) again, amar (spoke), Thus dabar (word / matter) Yawaab (Joab), and thus he dabar (word / matter) me.

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to him, ishah (make) as he has amar (spoke), and pagai (fall) on him, and qabar (bury) him; that you may sawar (take) away the dam (blood), which Yawaab (Joab) shapak (shed) chanam (without) cause, from me and from my ab (father) bayath (house).

Yahawah will shawab (turn back / repent) his dam (blood) on his own raash (head), because he pagai (fell) on shanayam (two) raash (head) more tzadayaq (righteous) and tawab (pleasant/functional) than he, and harag (killed) them with the charab (sword), and my ab (father) Dawad (David) didn't yadai (know) it: Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner), shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop) of Yasharaal (Israel), and Imashaa (Amasa) the ban (son) of Yathar (Jether), shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop) of Yahawadah (Judah).

So shall their dam (blood) shawab (turn back / repent) on the raash (head) of Yawaab (Joab), and on the raash (head) of his zarai (seed) iwalam (forever). But to Dawad (David), and to his zarai (seed), and to his bayath (house), and to his kasaa (throne), there shall be shalawam (peace / safety) iwalam (forever) from Yahawah.

Then Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) ilah (go up / offer) up, and pagai (fell) on him, and mawath (death) him; and he was qabar (bury) in his own bayath (house) in the madabar (wilderness).

The malak (king) nathan (give) Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) in his place over the tzabaa (troop); and the malak (king) nathan (give) Tzadawaq (Zadok) the kahan (priest) in the place of Abayathar (Abiathar).

The malak (king) shalach (send) and qaraa (called) for Shamaiy (Shimei), and amar (spoke) to him, banah (build) yourself a bayath (house) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) there, and don't yatzaa (go out / come out) out from there anywhere.

For on the yawam (day) you yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and ibar (pass over/through) over the nachal (stream / river) Qadarawan (Kidron), yadai (know) for certain that you shall mawath (death) mawath (death): your dam (blood) shall be on your own raash (head).

Shamaiy (Shimei) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "The amar (spoke) is tawab (pleasant/functional). As my Adawan the malak (king) has dabar (word / matter), so will your ibad (servant) ishah (make)." Shamaiy (Shimei) lived in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) many yawam (day).

It happened at the qatz (end) of shalawash (three) shanah (years), that shanayam (two) of the ibad (servant) of Shamaiy (Shimei) barach (ran) away to Akayash (Achish), ban (son) Maikah (of) Maacah, malak (king) of gath (gath). They nagad (told) Shamaiy (Shimei), amar (spoke), Behold, your ibad (servant) are in gath (gath).

Shamaiy (Shimei) qawam (rise up), and chabash (saddled) his donkey, and yalak (went) to gath (gath) to Akayash (Achish), to baqash (seek) his ibad (servant); and Shamaiy (Shimei) yalak (went), and bawaa (come) his ibad (servant) from gath (gath).
It was nagad (told) Shalamah (Solomon) that Shamaiy (Shimei) had halak (move) from Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) to gath (gath), and had shawab (turn back / repent) again.

The malak (king) shalach (send) and qaraa (called) for Shamaiy (Shimei), and amar (spoke) to him, Didn't I shabai (swear / take oath) you by Yahawah, and warn you, amar (spoke), ‘yadai (know) for certain, that on the yawam (day) you yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and halak (move) abroad any an (where), you shall mawath (death) mawath (death)?’ You amar (spoke) to me, ‘The dabar (word / matter) that I have shamai (hearken / hear) is tawab (pleasant/functional).’
Why then have you not shamar (keep/guard) the shabawaih (oath) of Yahawah, and the matzawah (commandment) that I have instructed you with?

The malak (king) amar (spoke) moreover to Shamaiy (Shimei), You yadai (know) all the rai (wickedness) which your labab (heart) is yadai (privy) to, that you ishah (make) to Dawad (David) my ab (father). Therefore Yahawah shall shawab (turn back / repent) your rai (wickedness) on your own raash (head).
But malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon) shall be barak (blessed), and the kasaa (throne) of Dawad (David) shall be kawan (established) panayam (before) Yahawah iwalam (forever).

So the malak (king) tzawah (commanded) Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada); and he yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and pagai (fell) on him, so that he mawath (death). The mamalakah (kingdom) was kawan (established) in the yad (hand) of Shalamah (Solomon).

Shalamah (Solomon) chathan (made) affinity with Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and laqach (take / seized) Paraih (Pharaoh's) bath (daughter), and bawaa (come) her into the iyar (city) of Dawad (David), until he kalah (complete / finish) made an end of banah (building) his own bayath (house), and the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the chawamah (wall) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) all around.
Only the im (people / nation) zabach (sacrificed) in the bamah (high) places, because there was no bayath (house) banah (built) for the sham (name) of Yahawah until those yawam (day).
Shalamah (Solomon) ahab (love) Yahawah, yalak (walking) in the chaqah (statutes) of Dawad (David) his ab (father): only he zabach (sacrificed) and burnt qatar (incense) in the bamah (high) places.

The malak (king) yalak (went) to Gabaiwan (Gibeon) to zabach (sacrifice) there; for that was the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) bamah (high) place. Shalamah (Solomon) ilah (go up / offer) a alap (thousand) burnt ilah (offerings) on that mazabach (altar).
In Gabaiwan (Gibeon) Yahawah raah (see) to Shalamah (Solomon) in a chalawam (dream) by layal (night); and Alahayam amar (spoke), shaal (ask) what I shall nathan (give) you.

Shalamah (Solomon) amar (spoke), You ishah (make) shown to your ibad (servant) Dawad (David) my ab (father) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) loving chasad (grace), according as he halak (move) panayam (before) you in amath (truth), and in tzadaqah (righteousness), and in yasharah (uprightness) of labab (heart) with you. You have shamar (keep/guard) for him this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) loving chasad (grace), that you nathan (give) given him a ban (son) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) on his kasaa (throne), as it is this yawam (day).

Now, Yahawah my Alahayam, you have made your ibad (servant) malak (king) instead of Dawad (David) my ab (father). I am but a qatan (small/young/least) nair (child). I don't yadai (know) how to yatzaa (go out / come out) out or bawaa (come) in.

Your ibad (servant) is in the thawak (midst) of your im (people / nation) which you have bachar (chosen), a rab (great) im (people / nation), that can't be manah (numbered) nor sapar (book) for rab (multitude).

Nathan (give) your ibad (servant) therefore an shamai (hearken / hear) lab (heart) to shapat (judge) your im (people / nation), that I may bayan (between) between tawab (pleasant/functional) and rai (evil); for who is yakal (able) to shapat (judge) this your kabad (great) im (people / nation)?
The dabar (word / matter) yatab (pleased) the Adanay, that Shalamah (Solomon) had shaal (asked) this thing.

Alahayam amar (spoke) to him, Because you have asked this thing, and have not shaal (asked) for yourself rab (long) yawam (day), neither have shaal (asked) riches for yourself, nor have shaal (asked) the napash (living being/soul) of your ayab (enemy), but have shaal (asked) for yourself bayan (between) to shamai (hearken / hear) mashapat (justice);

Behold, I ishah (make) done according to your dabar (word / matter). Behold, I nathan (give) given you a chakam (wise) and an bayan (between) lab (heart); so that there has been none like you panayam (before) you, neither achar (other) you shall any qawam (rise up) like you.
I nathan (give) also given you that which you have not shaal (asked), both riches and honor, so that there shall not be any among the malak (king) like you, all your yawam (day).

If you will yalak (walk) in my darak (ways), to shamar (keep/guard) my chaq (statute) and my matzawah (commandments), as your ab (father) Dawad (David) halak (move), then I will arak (lengthen) your yawam (day).

Shalamah (Solomon) awoke; and behold, it was a chalawam (dream). Then he bawaa (come) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and imad (stood) panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, and ilah (go up / offer) up burnt ilah (offerings), ishah (make) peace ilah (offerings), and ishah (make) a mashathah (feast) to all his ibad (servant).
Then shanayam (two) ashah (wife/individual woman) who were prostitutes bawaa (come) to the malak (king), and imad (stood) panayam (before) him.

The achad (one) ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke), Oh, my Adawan, I and this ashah (wife/individual woman) yashab (inhabit/dwell) in achad (one) bayath (house). I yalad (birth / begot) a child with her in the bayath (house).

It happened the shalayashay (third) yawam (day) after I yalad (birth / begot), that this ashah (wife/individual woman) yalad (birth / begot) also. We were yachad (together). There was no stranger with us in the bayath (house), just us shanayam (two) in the bayath (house).
This ashah (wife/individual woman) ban (son) mawath (death) in the layal (night), because she shakab (lay) on it.

She qawam (rise up) at thawak (midst), and laqach (take / seized) my ban (son) from beside me, while your handmaid yashan (slept), and shakab (laid) it in her chayaq (bosom), and shakab (laid) her mawath (death) ban (son) in my chayaq (bosom).

When I qawam (rise up) in the baqar (morning) to yanaq (nurse) my ban (son), behold, it was mawath (death); but when I bayan (between) looked at it in the baqar (morning), behold, it was not my ban (son), whom I yalad (birth / begot).

The other ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke), "No; but the chay (life) is my ban (son), and the mawath (death) is your ban (son)." This amar (spoke), "No; but the mawath (death) is your ban (son), and the chay (life) is my ban (son)." Thus they dabar (word / matter) panayam (before) the malak (king).

Then the malak (king) amar (spoke), The zaath (this) amar (spoke), ‘This is my ban (son) who chay (life), and your ban (son) is the mawath (death);’ and the other amar (spoke), ‘No; but your ban (son) is the mawath (death) one, and my ban (son) is the chay (life) one.’
The malak (king) amar (spoke), "laqach (take / seized) me a charab (sword)." They laqach (take / seized) a charab (sword) panayam (before) the malak (king).
The malak (king) amar (spoke), gazar (divide) the chay (life) yalad (birth / begot) in shanayam (two), and nathan (give) chatzay (half) to the achad (one), and chatzay (half) to the other.

Then the ashah (wife/individual woman) whose the chay (life) ban (son) was amar (spoke) to the malak (king), for her racham (heart) kamar (yearned) over her ban (son), and she amar (spoke), "Oh, my Adawan, nathan (give) her the chay (life) yalad (birth / begot), and in no mawath (death) mawath (death) it!" But the other amar (spoke), It shall be neither mine nor yours. Gazar (divide) it.
Then the malak (king) inah (answer / respond), nathan (give) her the chay (life) yalad (birth / begot), and in no mawath (death) mawath (death) it. She is its am (mother).

All Yasharaal (Israel) shamai (hearken / hear) of the mashapat (judgment) which the malak (king) had shapat (judged); and they yaraa (fear / be afraid) the malak (king): for they raah (see) that the chakamah (wisdom) of Alahayam was in him, to ishah (make) mashapat (justice).
Malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon) was malak (king) over all Yasharaal (Israel).
These were the shar (prince / ruler) whom he had: Izarayah (Azariah) the ban (son) of Tzadawaq (Zadok), the kahan (priest);
Alayacharap (Elihoreph) and Achayah (Ahijah), the ban (son) of Shayashaa (Shisha), sapar (book); Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the ban (son) of Achayalawad (Ahilud), the zakar (remembrance/memory);
And Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) was over the tzabaa (troop); and Tzadawaq (Zadok) and Abayathar (Abiathar) were kahan (priest);

And Izarayah (Azariah) the ban (son) of Nathan (Nathan) was over the natzab (officers); and Zabawad (Zabud) the ban (son) of Nathan (Nathan) was kahan (priest) minister, the malak (king) raih (friend);
And Achayashar (Ahishar) was over the bayath (house); and Adanayaram (Adoniram) the ban (son) of Ibadaa (Abda) was over the men subject to forced mas (labor).

Shalamah (Solomon) had shanayam (two) natzab (officers) over all Yasharaal (Israel), who kawal (all/every/entire) food for the malak (king) and his bayath (house): each achad (one) had to kawal (all/every/entire) provision for a chadash (month) in the shanah (year).
These are their sham (name): Ben banachawar (hur), in the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim);
Ben Deker, in Maqatz (Makaz), and in Shailabayam (Shaalbim), and Bayathashamash (Beth) Shemesh, and Ayalawanabayathachanan (Elon) Beth Hanan;
Ben banachasad (hesed), Arabawath (in) Arubboth (to him belonged Shawakah (Socoh), and all the aratz (Earth/land) of Chapar (Hepher));
Ben banaabayanadab (abinadab), in all the height of Dawar (Dor) (he had Tapath (Taphath) the bath (daughter) of Shalamah (Solomon) as ashah (wife/individual woman));

Bainaa (Baana) the ban (son) of Achayalawad (Ahilud), in Thainak (Taanach) and Magadawan (Megiddo), and all Bayathashaan (Beth) Shean which is beside Tzarathan (Zarethan), beneath Yazaraial (Jezreel), from Bayathashaan (Beth) Shean to Abalamachawalah (Abel) Meholah, as far as ibar (beyond) Yaqamaim (Jokmeam);

Ben banagabar (geber), in Ramoth Galaid (Gilead) (to him belonged the chawah (town/named location) of Yaayar (Jair) the ban (son) of Manashah (Manasseh), which are in Galaid (Gilead); to him belonged the chabal (region) of Aragab (Argob), which is in Bashan (Bashan), shashayam (sixty) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) iyar (cities) with chawamah (walls) and bronze barayach (bars));
Achayanadab (Ahinadab) the ban (son) of Idaw (Iddo), in Machanayam (Mahanaim);
Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz), in Napathalay (Naphtali) (he also laqach (take / seized) Bashamath (Basemath) the bath (daughter) of Shalamah (Solomon) as ashah (wife/individual woman));
Bainaa (Baana) the ban (son) of Chawashay (Hushai), in Ashar (Asher) and Bailawath (Bealoth);
Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the ban (son) of Parawach (Paruah), in Yashashakar (Issachar);
Shamaiy (Shimei) the ban (son) Alaa (of) Ela, in Banayamayan (Benjamin);

Gabar (Geber) the ban (son) of Awaray (Uri), in the aratz (Earth/land) of Galaid (Gilead), the aratz (Earth/land) of Sayachawan (Sihon) malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites) and of Iwag (Og) malak (king) of Bashan (Bashan); and he was the only natzayab (officer) who was in the aratz (Earth/land).
Yahawadah (Judah) and Yasharaal (Israel) were many as the chawal (sand) which is by the yam (sea/waters) in rab (multitude), akal (eat) and shathah (drinks) and making shamach (merry).

Shalamah (Solomon) mashal (rule/have dominion) over all the mamalakah (kingdoms) from the nahar (river) to the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and to the gabawal (border/boundary) of Matzarayam (Egypt): they nagash (brought) tribute, and ibad (servant) Shalamah (Solomon) all the yawam (day) of his chay (life).
Shalamah (Solomon's) provision for achad (one) yawam (day) was shalawashayam (thirty) kar (measures) of fine salath (flour), and shashayam (sixty) kar (measures) of qamach (meal),

Ishar (ten) head of barayaa (fat) cattle, and isharayam (twenty) baqar (morning) of cattle out of the raiy (pastures), and one maah (hundred) tzaan (sheep), besides ayal (harts), and gazelles, and tzabay (roebucks), and fattened barabar (fowl).

For he radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) dominion over all on ibar (this) side the nahar (river), Thapasach (from) Tiphsah even to Izah (Gaza), over all the malak (king) on ibar (this) side the nahar (river): and he had shalawam (peace / safety) on all sides around him.

Yahawadah (Judah) and Yasharaal (Israel) lived safely, every ayash (husband/individual man) under his gapan (vine) and under his thaan (fig) tree, Dan (from) Dan Baarashabai (even) to Beersheba, all the yawam (day) of Shalamah (Solomon).
Shalamah (Solomon) had arabaiyam (forty) alap (thousand) arawah (stalls) of sawas (horses) for his marakab (chariots), and shanayam (two) alap (thousand) horsemen.

Those natzab (officers) kawal (all/every/entire) food for malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon), and for all who qarab (came) to malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon's) shalachan (table), every ayash (husband/individual man) in his chadash (month); they let nothing be idar (lacking).

Shairah (barley) also and thaban (straw) for the sawas (horses) and rakash (swift) steeds bawaa (come) they to the maqawam (place) where the officers were, every ayash (husband/individual man) according to his duty.
Alahayam nathan (give) Shalamah (Solomon) chakamah (wisdom) and thabawan (understanding) maad (exceeding) much, and very great lab (heart), even as the chawal (sand) that is on the seashore.
Shalamah (Solomon's) chakamah (wisdom) rabah (excelled) the chakamah (wisdom) of all the ban (son) of the qadam (east), and all the chakamah (wisdom) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

For he was chakam (wiser) than all adam (men); than Ayathan (Ethan) the azarachay (ezrahite), and Hayaman (Heman), and Kalakal (Calcol), and Daradai (Darda), the ban (son) of Machawal (Mahol): and his sham (name) was in all the gaway (nation / people) all around.
He dabar (word / matter) shalawash (three) alap (thousand) mashal (proverbs); and his shayar (song) were one alap (thousand) chamash (five).

He dabar (word / matter) of itz (trees), from the araz (cedar) that is in Labanawan (Lebanon) even to the azawab (hyssop) that yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the qayar (wall); he dabar (word / matter) also of animals, and of iwap (flying), and of ramash (creeping) things, and of dag (fish).

There bawaa (come) of all im (people / nation) to shamai (hearken / hear) the chakamah (wisdom) of Shalamah (Solomon), from all malak (king) of the aratz (Earth/land), who had shamai (hearken / hear) of his chakamah (wisdom).

Hiram mamalakah (king) of Tyre sent his ibad (servant) to Shalamah (Solomon); for he had heard that they had anointed him mamalakah (king) in the place of his father: for Hiram was yawam (day) a lover of David.
Shalamah (Solomon) sent to Hiram, saying,
You know how that David my father could not build a house for the name of Yahawah his Alahayam for the wars which were about him on every side, until Yahawah put them under the soles of his feet.
But now Yahawah my Alahayam has given me shalawam (peace / safety) on sabayab (surrounding) side. There is neither adversary, nor evil occurrence.

Behold, I purpose to build a house for the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Yahawah my Alahayam, as Yahawah spoke to David my father, saying, ‘Your son, whom I will yashab (inhabit/dwell) on your throne in your place, he shall build the house for my yashab (inhabit/dwell).’

Now therefore command that they cut me cedar trees out of Shalamah (Lebanon). My servants shall be with your servants; and I will give you wages for your servants according to all that you shall say. For you know that there is not among us any who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians.

It happened, when Hiram heard the dabar (word / matter) of Shalamah (Solomon), that he rejoiced greatly, and dabar (word / matter), Blessed is Yahawah this day, who has given to David a wise son over this ayash (husband/individual man) ayash (husband/individual man).

Hiram bawaa (come) to Solomon, saying, I have heard the message which you have bawaa (come) to me. I will hayah (came to pass) all your desire concerning timber of cedar, and concerning timber of fir.

My servants shall nathan (give) them down from Shalamah (Lebanon) to the yam (sea/waters). I will nathan (give) them into rafts to go by yam (sea/waters) to the nathan (give) that you shall nathan (give) me, and will nathan (give) them to be broken up there, and you shall receive them. You shall accomplish my desire, in nathan (give) food for my household.
So Hiram rabah (gave) Shalamah (Solomon) timber of cedar and timber of fir according to all his desire.
Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand measures of wheat for food to his household, and twenty measures of pure oil. Solomon gave this to Hiram year by year.
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) Solomon wisdom, as he dabar (word / matter) him; and there was peace between Hiram and Solomon; and they two made a treaty together.
King Solomon raised a levy out of all Israel; and the levy was thirty thousand men.
He bawaa (come) them to Shalamah (Lebanon), ten thousand a month by courses; a month they were in Shalamah (Lebanon), and two months at home; and Adoniram was over the men subject to forced labor.
Shalamah (Solomon) had seventy thousand who bore burdens, and eighty thousand who were stone cutters in the mountains;
Besides Shalamah (Solomon's) chief officers who were over the work, three thousand and three hundred, who bore rule over the people who labored in the work.
The king commanded, and they cut out bayath (house) stones, costly stones, to yadai (lay) the foundation of the bayath (house) with worked stone.
Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders and the Gebalites cut them, and prepared the timber and the stones to build the house.

It happened in the arabai (four) maah (hundred) and shamanayam (eightieth) shanah (year) after the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) yatzaa (go out / come out) come out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), in the rabayaiy (fourth) shanah (year) of Shalamah (Solomon's) malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel), in the chadash (month) Zaw (Ziv), which is the shanay (second) chadash (month), that he began to banah (build) the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

The bayath (house) which malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon) banah (built) for Yahawah, its arak (length) was shashayam (sixty) amah (cubits), and its rachab (breadth) isharayam (twenty), and its qawamah (height) shalawashayam (thirty) amah (cubits).

The awalam (porch) panayam (before) the hayakal (temple) of the bayath (house), isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) was its arak (length), according to the rachab (breadth) of the bayath (house). Ishar (ten) amah (cubits) was its rachab (breadth) before the bayath (house).
For the bayath (house) he ishah (make) chalawan (windows) of fixed lattice shaqap (work).

Against the qayar (wall) of the bayath (house) he banah (built) stories all around, against the qayar (walls) of the bayath (house) all around, both of the hayakal (temple) and of the dabayar (oracle); and he ishah (make) tzalai (side) rooms all around.

The thachathawan (nethermost) story was chamash (five) amah (cubits) rachab (broad), and the thayakawan (middle) was shash (six) amah (cubits) rachab (broad), and the shalayashay (third) was shabai (seven) amah (cubits) rachab (broad); for on the outside he nathan (give) offsets in the wall of the bayath (house) all around, that the beams should not achaz (have) hold in the qayar (walls) of the bayath (house).

The bayath (house), when it was in banah (building), was banah (built) of aban (stone) prepared at the quarry; and there was neither maqabah (hammer) nor axe nor any kalay (tool) of barazal (iron) shamai (hearken / hear) in the bayath (house), while it was in banah (building).

The pathach (door) for the thayakawan (middle) tzalai (side) rooms was in the yamanay (right) kathap (side) of the bayath (house): and they ilah (go up / offer) up by lawal (winding) stairs into the thayakawan (middle) story, and out of the thayakawan (middle) into the shalayashay (third).
So he banah (built) the bayath (house), and kalah (complete / finish) it; and he sapan (covered) the bayath (house) with gab (beams) and planks of araz (cedar).
He banah (built) the stories against all the bayath (house), each chamash (five) amah (cubits) qawamah (high): and they rested on the bayath (house) with itz (timber) of araz (cedar).
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Shalamah (Solomon), amar (spoke),

Concerning this bayath (house) which you are banah (building), if you will yalak (walk) in my chaqah (statutes), and ishah (make) my mashapat (ordinances), and shamar (keep/guard) all my matzawah (commandments) to yalak (walk) in them; then will I qawam (rise up) my dabar (word / matter) with you, which I dabar (word / matter) to Dawad (David) your ab (father).
I will shakan (dwell) thawak (midst) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), and will not izab (forsake) my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel).
So Shalamah (Solomon) banah (built) the bayath (house), and kalah (complete / finish) it.

He banah (built) the qayar (walls) of the bayath (house) bayath (house) with tzalai (boards) of araz (cedar): from the qaraqai (floor) of the bayath (house) to the qayar (walls) of the ceiling, he tzapah (covered) them on the bayath (house) with itz (wood); and he tzapah (covered) the qaraqai (floor) of the bayath (house) with tzalai (boards) of barawash (fir).

He banah (built) isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) on the hinder part of the bayath (house) with tzalai (boards) of araz (cedar) from the qaraqai (floor) to the ceiling: he banah (built) them for it bayath (house), for an dabayar (oracle), even for the most qadash (set apart/make holy) place.
In front of the hayakal (temple) bayath (house) was arabaiyam (forty) amah (cubits).
There was araz (cedar) on the bayath (house) panayamah (within), maqalaith (carved) with buds and open tzayatz (flowers): all was araz (cedar); there was no aban (stone) raah (see).
He kawan (prepared) an dabayar (oracle) in the midst of the bayath (house) panayamah (within), to nathan (give) there the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah.

Within the dabayar (oracle) was isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) in arak (length), and isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) in rachab (breadth), and isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) in its qawamah (height); and he overlaid it with sagar (pure) zahab (gold): and he tzapah (covered) the mazabach (altar) with araz (cedar).

So Shalamah (Solomon) overlaid the bayath (house) panayamah (within) with sagar (pure) zahab (gold): and he drew rathayaqah (chains) of zahab (gold) across panayam (before) the dabayar (oracle); and he overlaid it with zahab (gold).
The whole bayath (house) he overlaid with zahab (gold), until all the bayath (house) was finished: also the whole mazabach (altar) that belonged to the dabayar (oracle) he overlaid with zahab (gold).
In the dabayar (oracle) he ishah (make) shanayam (two) karawab (cherubim) of shaman (olive) itz (wood), each ishar (ten) amah (cubits) qawamah (high).

Chamash (five) amah (cubits) was the achad (one) kanap (wing) of the karawab (cherub), and chamash (five) amah (cubits) the other kanap (wing) of the karawab (cherub): from the uttermost part of the one kanap (wing) to the uttermost part of the other were ishar (ten) amah (cubits).
The other karawab (cherub) was ishar (ten) amah (cubits): shanayam (two) the karawab (cherubim) were of achad (one) madah (measure) and achad (one) form.
The qawamah (height) of the achad (one) karawab (cherub) was ishar (ten) amah (cubits), and so was it of the other karawab (cherub).

He nathan (give) the karawab (cherubim) thawak (midst) the inner bayath (house); and the kanap (wings) of the karawab (cherubim) were parash (stretched) forth, so that the kanap (wing) of the achad (one) nagai (touched) the one qayar (wall), and the kanap (wing) of the other karawab (cherub) nagai (touched) the other qayar (wall); and their kanap (wings) nagai (touched) kanap (one) another in the thawak (midst) of the bayath (house).
He overlaid the karawab (cherubim) with zahab (gold).
He qalai (carved) all the qayar (walls) of the bayath (house) around with pathawach (carved) figures of karawab (cherubim) and thamar (palm) trees and open tzayatz (flowers), inside and outside.
The qaraqai (floor) of the bayath (house) he overlaid with zahab (gold), inside and outside.

For the pathach (entrance) of the dabayar (oracle) he ishah (make) dalath (doors) of shaman (olive) itz (wood): the ayal (lintel) and mazawazah (door) posts were a chamayashay (fifth) part of the wall.

So he made shanayam (two) dalath (doors) of shaman (olive) itz (wood); and he qalai (carved) on them maqalaith (carvings) of karawab (cherubim) and thamar (palm) trees and open tzayatz (flowers), and overlaid them with zahab (gold); and he radad (spread) the zahab (gold) on the karawab (cherubim), and on the thamar (palm) trees.
So also ishah (make) he for the pathach (entrance) of the hayakal (temple) mazawazah (door) posts of shaman (olive) itz (wood), out of a rabayaiy (fourth) part of the wall;

And shanayam (two) dalath (doors) of barawash (fir) itz (wood): the shanayam (two) leaves of the achad (one) dalath (door) were galayal (folding), and the shanayam (two) leaves of the other dalath (door) were galayal (folding).
He qalai (carved) karawab (cherubim) and thamar (palm) trees and open tzayatz (flowers); and he overlaid them with zahab (gold) yashar (fitted) on the engraved chaqah (work).
He banah (built) the inner chatzar (court) with shalawash (three) courses of cut gazayath (stone), and a course of araz (cedar) karathah (beams).
In the rabayaiy (fourth) shanah (year) was the yasad (foundation) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah yasad (laid), in the yarach (month) Zaw (Ziv).

In the eleventh shanah (year), in the yarach (month) Bawal (Bul), which is the shamayanay (eighth) yarach (month), was the bayath (house) kalah (complete / finish) throughout all its dabar (word / matter), and according to all its mashapat (fashion). So was he shabai (seven) shanah (years) in banah (building) it.
Shalamah (Solomon) was banah (building) his own bayath (house) thirteen shanah (years), and he kalah (complete / finish) all his bayath (house).

For he banah (built) the bayath (house) of the yair (forest) of Labanawan (Lebanon); its arak (length) was one maah (hundred) amah (cubits), and its rachab (breadth) chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits), and its qawamah (height) shalawashayam (thirty) amah (cubits), on arabai (four) tawar (rows) of araz (cedar) imawad (pillar), with araz (cedar) karathah (beams) on the imawad (pillar).
It was sapan (covered) with araz (cedar) mail (top/above) over the arabaiyam (forty) - chamash (five) tzalai (beams), that were on the imawad (pillar); fifteen in a tawar (row).
There were beams in shalawash (three) tawar (rows), and window was over against window in shalawash (three) paim (ranks).
All the pathach (doors) and mazawazah (posts) were made rabai (fourth) with beams: and window was over mawal (against) window in shalawash (three) paim (ranks).

He ishah (make) the awalam (porch) of imawad (pillar); its arak (length) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits), and its rachab (breadth) shalawashayam (thirty) amah (cubits); and a awalam (porch) panayam (before) them; and imawad (pillar) and a threshold panayam (before) them.

He ishah (make) the awalam (porch) of the kasaa (throne) where he was to shapat (judge), even the awalam (porch) of mashapat (judgment): and it was sapan (covered) with araz (cedar) from qaraqai (floor) to qaraqai (floor).

His bayath (house) where he was to yashab (inhabit/dwell), the other chatzar (court) bayath (house) the awalam (porch), was of the like maishah (work). He ishah (make) also a bayath (house) for Paraih (Pharaoh's) bath (daughter) (whom Solomon had laqach (take / seized) as wife), like this awalam (porch).

All these were of yaqar (costly) aban (stone), even of cut gazayath (stone), according to madah (measure), sawed with magarah (saws), bayath (house) and outside, even from the masad (foundation) to the tapach (coping), and so on the outside to the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chatzar (court).

The yasad (foundation) was of yaqar (costly) aban (stone), even gadawal (very great/important/mighty) aban (stone), aban (stone) of ishar (ten) amah (cubits), and aban (stone) of shamanah (eight) amah (cubits).
Mail (top/above) were yaqar (costly) aban (stone), even cut aban (stone), according to madah (measure), and araz (cedar) wood.

The gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chatzar (court) around had shalawash (three) courses of cut gazayath (stone), and a course of araz (cedar) karathah (beams); like as the inner chatzar (court) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the awalam (porch) of the bayath (house).
Malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon) shalach (send) and laqach (take / seized) Chayaram (Hiram) out of Tzar (Tyre).

He was the ban (son) of a widow of the matah (staff / rod / tribe) of Napathalay (Naphtali), and his ab (father) was a ayash (husband/individual man) of tzaray (tyre), a worker in nachashath (brass); and he was malaa (filled) with chakamah (wisdom) and thabawan (understanding) and skill, to ishah (make) all ishah (make) in nachashath (brass). He bawaa (come) to malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon), and ishah (make) all his malaakah (work).

For he tzawar (fashioned) the shanayam (two) imawad (pillar) of nachashath (brass), eighteen amah (cubits) qawamah (high) imawad (pillar): and a chawat (line) of shanayam (two) amah (cubits) encircled shanay (second) of them sabab (about).
