There was malachamah (war) between Rachabaim (Rehoboam) and Yarabaim (Jeroboam) yawam (day).

Rachabaim (Rehoboam) shakab (slept) with his ab (father), and was qabar (bury) with his ab (father) in the iyar (city) of Dawad (David): and his am (mother) sham (name) was Naimah (Naamah) the imawanayath (ammonitess). Abayam (Abijam) his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.
Now in the eighteenth shanah (year) of malak (king) Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Nabat (Nebat) began Abayam (Abijam) to malak (king) over Yahawadah (Judah).
He malak (king) shalawash (three) shanah (years) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem): and his am (mother) sham (name) was Maikah (Maacah) the bath (daughter) of Abayashalawam (Abishalom).

He yalak (walked) in all the chataah (sin) of his ab (father), which he ishah (make) done panayam (before) him; and his labab (heart) was not shalam (full / whole / complete) with Yahawah his Alahayam, as the labab (heart) of Dawad (David) his ab (father).

Nevertheless for Dawad (David's) sake, Yahawah his Alahayam nathan (give) him a nayar (lamp) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), to qawam (rise up) up his ban (son) achar (other) him, and to imad (establish) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem);

Because Dawad (David) ishah (make) that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, and didn't sawar (turn) aside from anything that he tzawah (commanded) him all the yawam (day) of his chay (life), except only in the dabar (word / matter) of Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite).
Now there was malachamah (war) between Rachabaim (Rehoboam) and Yarabaim (Jeroboam) all the yawam (day) of his chay (life).

The yathar (rest) of the dabar (word / matter) of Abayam (Abijam), and all that he ishah (make), aren't they kathab (written) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabar (word / matter) of the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah)? There was malachamah (war) between Abayam (Abijam) and Yarabaim (Jeroboam).
Abayam (Abijam) shakab (slept) with his ab (father); and they qabar (bury) him in the iyar (city) of Dawad (David): and Asaa (Asa) his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.
In the isharayam (twenty) shanah (year) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) began Asaa (Asa) to malak (king) over Yahawadah (Judah).
He malak (king) arabaiyam (forty) - achad (one) shanah (years) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem): and his am (mother) sham (name) was Maikah (Maacah) the bath (daughter) of Abayashalawam (Abishalom).
Asaa (Asa) ishah (make) that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, as did Dawad (David) his ab (father).
He ibar (pass over/through) away the qadash (set apart/make holy) out of the aratz (Earth/land), and sawar (removed) all the galawal (idols) that his ab (father) ishah (make) made.

Maikah (Also) Maacah his am (mother) he sawar (removed) from being gabayarah (queen), because she ishah (make) made an abominable mapalatzath (image) Asharah (for) an Asherah; and Asaa (Asa) karath (cut) down her mapalatzath (image), and burnt it at the nachal (stream / river) Qadarawan (Kidron).
But the bamah (high) places were not sawar (taken) away: nevertheless the labab (heart) of Asaa (Asa) was shalam (full / whole / complete) with Yahawah all his yawam (day).

He bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah the things that his ab (father) had qadash (set apart/make holy), and the things that himself had qadash (set apart/make holy), kasap (silver), and zahab (gold), and kalay (vessels).
There was malachamah (war) between Asaa (Asa) and Baishaa (Baasha) malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) all their yawam (day).

Baishaa (Baasha) malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up against Yahawadah (Judah), and banah (built) Ramah (Ramah), that he might not allow anyone to yatzaa (go out / come out) out or bawaa (come) in to Asaa (Asa) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah).

Then Asaa (Asa) laqach (take / seized) all the kasap (silver) and the zahab (gold) that were yathar (left) in the awatzar (treasures) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the awatzar (treasures) of the malak (king) bayath (house), and nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of his ibad (servant); and malak (king) Asaa (Asa) shalach (send) them Banahadad (to) Ben Hadad, the ban (son) of Tabaramawan (Tabrimmon), the ban (son) of Chazayawan (Hezion), malak (king) of Aram (Syria), who lived at Damashaq (Damascus), amar (spoke),

There is a treaty between me and you, between my ab (father) and your ab (father). Behold, I have shalach (send) to you a shachad (present) of kasap (silver) and zahab (gold). Yalak (go), parar (break) your treaty with Baishaa (Baasha) malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), that he may depart from me.

Banahadad (Ben) Hadad shamai (hearken / hear) to malak (king) Asaa (Asa), and shalach (send) the shar (prince / ruler) of his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) against the iyar (cities) of Yasharaal (Israel), and nakah (struck) Iyawan (Ijon), and Dan (Dan), and Abalabayathamaikah (Abel) Beth Maacah, and all Kanarawath (Chinneroth), with all the aratz (Earth/land) of Napathalay (Naphtali).
It happened, when Baishaa (Baasha) shamai (hearken / hear) of it, that he chadal (left) off banah (building) Ramah (Ramah), and lived in Tharatzah (Tirzah).

Then malak (king) Asaa (Asa) shamai (hearken / hear) a proclamation to all Yahawadah (Judah); none was naqay (exempted): and they nashaa (lift) away the aban (stone) of Ramah (Ramah), and its itz (timber), with which Baishaa (Baasha) had banah (built); and malak (king) Asaa (Asa) banah (built) therewith Gabai (Geba) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), and Matzapah (Mizpah).

Now the yathar (rest) of all the dabar (word / matter) of Asaa (Asa), and all his gabawarah (might), and all that he ishah (make), and the iyar (cities) which he banah (built), aren't they kathab (written) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabar (word / matter) of the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah)? But in the ith (time) of his zaqanah (old) age he was chalah (afflict) in his ragal (feet / foot).

Asaa (Asa) shakab (slept) with his ab (father), and was qabar (bury) with his ab (father) in the iyar (city) of Dawad (David) his ab (father); and Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.

Nadab (Nadab) the ban (son) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) began to malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel) in the shanayam (two) shanah (year) of Asaa (Asa) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah); and he malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel) shanayam (two) shanah (years).

He ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, and yalak (walked) in the darak (way) of his ab (father), and in his chataah (sin) with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).

Baishaa (Baasha) the ban (son) of Achayah (Ahijah), of the bayath (house) of Yashashakar (Issachar), qashar (conspired) against him; and Baishaa (Baasha) nakah (struck) him at Gabathawan (Gibbethon), which belonged to the Palashathay (Philistines); for Nadab (Nadab) and all Yasharaal (Israel) were tzawar (laying) siege to Gabathawan (Gibbethon).
Even in the shalawash (three) shanah (year) of Asaa (Asa) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Baishaa (Baasha) mawath (death) him, and malak (king) in his place.

It happened that, as soon as he was malak (king), he nakah (struck) all the bayath (house) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam): he didn't shaar (leave) to Yarabaim (Jeroboam) any who nashamah (breathing thing), until he had destroyed him; according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, which he dabar (word / matter) by his ibad (servant) Achayah (Ahijah) the Shayalawanay (Shilonite);

For the chataah (sin) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) which he chataa (sinned), and with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin), because of his kais (provocation) with which he provoked Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), to kais (anger).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (word / matter) of Nadab (Nadab), and all that he ishah (make), aren't they kathab (written) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabar (word / matter) of the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
There was malachamah (war) between Asaa (Asa) and Baishaa (Baasha) malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) all their yawam (day).

In the shalawash (three) shanah (year) of Asaa (Asa) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Baishaa (Baasha) the ban (son) of Achayah (Ahijah) began to malak (king) over all Yasharaal (Israel) in Tharatzah (Tirzah) for isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) shanah (years).

He ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, and yalak (walked) in the darak (way) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam), and in his chataah (sin) with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Yahawaa (Jehu) the ban (son) of Chananay (Hanani) against Baishaa (Baasha), amar (spoke),

Because I rawam (will lift up) you out of the ipar (dust), and nathan (give) you nagayad (prince) over my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel), and you have yalak (walked) in the darak (way) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam), and have made my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin), to provoke me to kais (anger) with their chataah (sin);

Behold, I will utterly sweep bair (away) Baishaa (Baasha) and his bayath (house); and I will nathan (give) your bayath (house) like the bayath (house) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Nabat (Nebat).

The kalab (dogs) will akal (eat) Baishaa (Baasha's) descendants who mawath (death) in the iyar (city); and he who mawath (death) of his in the shadah (field) the iwap (flying) of the sky will akal (eat).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (word / matter) of Baishaa (Baasha), and what he ishah (make), and his gabawarah (might), aren't they kathab (written) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabar (word / matter) of the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
Baishaa (Baasha) shakab (slept) with his ab (father), and was qabar (bury) in Tharatzah (Tirzah); and Alah (Elah) his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.

Moreover by the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) Yahawaa (Jehu) the ban (son) of Chananay (Hanani) came the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah against Baishaa (Baasha), and against his bayath (house), both because of all the rai (evil) that he ishah (make) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, to provoke him to kais (anger) with the maishah (work) of his yad (hand), in being like the bayath (house) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam), and because he nakah (struck) him.

In the isharayam (twenty) - shash (six) shanah (year) of Asaa (Asa) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Alah (Elah) the ban (son) of Baishaa (Baasha) began to malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel) in Tharatzah (Tirzah) for two shanah (years).

His ibad (servant) Zamaray (Zimri), shar (prince / ruler) of machatzayath (half) his rakab (chariots), qashar (conspired) against him. Now he was in Tharatzah (Tirzah), shathah (drinks) himself shakawar (drunk) in the bayath (house) of Aratzaa (Arza), who was over the bayath (house) in Tharatzah (Tirzah):

And Zamaray (Zimri) bawaa (come) in and nakah (struck) him, and mawath (death) him, in the isharayam (twenty) - shabai (seven) shanah (year) of Asaa (Asa) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and malak (king) in his place.

It happened, when he began to malak (king), as soon as he yashab (inhabit/dwell) on his kasaa (throne), that he nakah (struck) all the bayath (house) of Baishaa (Baasha): he didn't shaar (leave) him a single shathan (one) who urinates on a qayar (wall), neither of his relatives, nor of his rai (neigbor/another person).

Thus Zamaray (Zimri) destroyed all the bayath (house) of Baishaa (Baasha), according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, which he dabar (word / matter) against Baishaa (Baasha) by Yahawaa (Jehu) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy),

For all the chataah (sin) of Baishaa (Baasha), and the chataah (sin) of Alah (Elah) his ban (son), which they chataa (sinned), and with which they made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin), to provoke Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), to kais (anger) with their habal (vanities).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (word / matter) of Alah (Elah), and all that he ishah (make), aren't they kathab (written) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabar (word / matter) of the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel)?

In the isharayam (twenty) - shabai (seven) shanah (year) of Asaa (Asa) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Zamaray (Zimri) malak (king) shabai (seven) yawam (day) in Tharatzah (Tirzah). Now the im (people / nation) were chanah (encamped) against Gabathawan (Gibbethon), which belonged to the Palashathay (Philistines).

The im (people / nation) who were chanah (encamped) shamai (hearken / hear) amar (spoke), Zamaray (Zimri) has qashar (conspired), and has also nakah (struck) the malak (king): therefore all Yasharaal (Israel) made Imaray (Omri), the shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop), malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel) that yawam (day) in the machanah (camp).
Imaray (Omri) ilah (go up / offer) up from Gabathawan (Gibbethon), and all Yasharaal (Israel) with him, and they tzawar (besieged) Tharatzah (Tirzah).

It happened, when Zamaray (Zimri) raah (see) that the iyar (city) was lakad (taken), that he bawaa (come) into the aramawan (castle) of the malak (king) bayath (house), and burnt the malak (king) bayath (house) over him with ash (fire), and mawath (death),

For his chataah (sin) which he chataa (sinned) in ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, in yalak (walking) in the darak (way) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam), and in his chataah (sin) which he ishah (make), to make Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (word / matter) of Zamaray (Zimri), and his qashar (treason) that he committed, aren't they kathab (written) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabar (word / matter) of the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel)?

Then were the im (people / nation) of Yasharaal (Israel) chalaq (divided) into chatzay (two) parts: chatzay (half) of the im (people / nation) hayah (came to pass) Thabanay (Tibni) the ban (son) of Gayanath (Ginath), to make him malak (king); and chatzay (half) achar (other) Imaray (Omri).

But the im (people / nation) who achar (other) Imaray (Omri) chazaq (prevailed) ath (entirety) the im (people / nation) who achar (other) Thabanay (Tibni) the ban (son) of Gayanath (Ginath): so Thabanay (Tibni) mawath (death), and Imaray (Omri) malak (king).

In the shalawashayam (thirty) - achad (one) shanah (year) of Asaa (Asa) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Imaray (Omri) began to malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel) for shanayam (two) shanah (years). He malak (king) shash (six) shanah (years) in Tharatzah (Tirzah).

He bought the har (mountain) Shamarawan (Samaria) of Shamar (Shemer) for two kakar (talents) of kasap (silver); and he banah (built) on the har (mountain), and qaraa (called) the sham (name) of the iyar (city) which he banah (built), after the sham (name) of Shamar (Shemer), the adawan (master / lord) of the har (mountain), Shamarawan (Samaria).
Imaray (Omri) ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, and dealt wickedly above all who were panayam (before) him.

For he yalak (walked) in all the darak (way) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Nabat (Nebat), and in his chataah (sin) with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin), to provoke Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), to kais (anger) with their habal (vanities).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (word / matter) of Imaray (Omri) which he ishah (make), and his gabawarah (might) that he showed, aren't they kathab (written) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabar (word / matter) of the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
So Imaray (Omri) shakab (slept) with his ab (father), and was qabar (bury) in Shamarawan (Samaria); and Achaab (Ahab) his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.

In the shalawashayam (thirty) - shamanah (eighth) shanah (year) of Asaa (Asa) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) began Achaab (Ahab) the ban (son) of Imaray (Omri) to malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel): and Achaab (Ahab) the ban (son) of Imaray (Omri) malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel) in Shamarawan (Samaria) isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) shanah (years).
Achaab (Ahab) the ban (son) of Imaray (Omri) ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah above all that were panayam (before) him.

It happened, as if it had been a qalal (light) thing for him to yalak (walk) in the chataah (sin) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Nabat (Nebat), that he laqach (take / seized) as ashah (wife/individual woman) Ayazabal (Jezebel) the bath (daughter) of Athabail (Ethbaal) malak (king) of the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), and yalak (went) and ibad (servant) Bail (Baal), and shachah (worshiped) him.
He qawam (rise up) up an mazabach (altar) for Bail (Baal) in the bayath (house) of Bail (Baal), which he had banah (built) in Shamarawan (Samaria).

Achaab (Ahab) ishah (make) the Asharah (Asherah); and Achaab (Ahab) ishah (make) yet more to provoke Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), to kais (anger) than all the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) who were panayam (before) him.

In his yawam (day) Chayaal (Hiel) the bayathahaalay (bethelite) banah (built) Yarayachaw (Jericho): he yasad (laid) its foundation with the loss of Abayaram (Abiram) his bakawar (firstborn), and natzab (set) up its dalath (gates) with the loss of his youngest son Shagawab (Segub), according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, which he dabar (word / matter) by Yahawashawai (Joshua) the ban (son) of Nawan (Nun).

Alayah (Elijah) the thashabay (tishbite), who was of the thawashab (foreigners) of Galaid (Gilead), amar (spoke) to Achaab (Ahab), As Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), chay (life), panayam (before) whom I imad (stand), there shall not be tal (dew) nor matar (rain) these shanah (years), but pah (according) to my dabar (word / matter).
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to him, amar (spoke),
Yalak (go) away from here, panah (turn) eastward, and sathar (hide) yourself by the nachal (stream / river) Karayath (Cherith), that is panayam (before) the Yaradan (Jordan).
It shall be, that you shall shathah (drinks) of the nachal (stream / river). I have tzawah (commanded) the irab (evening) to kawal (all/every/entire) you there.

So he yalak (went) and ishah (make) according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah; for he yalak (went) and lived by the nachal (stream / river) Karayath (Cherith), that is panayam (before) the Yaradan (Jordan).

The irab (evening) bawaa (come) him lacham (bread) and bashar (flesh) in the baqar (morning), and lacham (bread) and bashar (flesh) in the irab (evening); and he shathah (drinks) of the nachal (stream / river).
It happened qatz (after) a yawam (day), that the nachal (stream / river) yabash (dry land) up, because there was no gasham (rain) in the aratz (Earth/land).
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to him, amar (spoke),
Qawam (rise up), yalak (go) to Tzarapath (Zarephath), which belongs to Tzayadawan (Sidon), and stay there. Behold, I have tzawah (commanded) a alamanah (widow) there to kawal (all/every/entire) you.

So he qawam (rise up) and yalak (went) to Tzarapath (Zarephath); and when he bawaa (come) to the pathach (gate) of the iyar (city), behold, a alamanah (widow) was there qashash (gathering) itz (sticks): and he qaraa (called) to her, and amar (spoke), Please laqach (take / seized) me a mait (little) mayam (Waters) in a kalay (vessel), that I may shathah (drinks).
As she was yalak (going) to laqach (take / seized) it, he qaraa (called) to her, and amar (spoke), Please laqach (take / seized) me a path (morsel) of lacham (bread) in your yad (hand).

She amar (spoke), As Yahawah your Alahayam chay (life), I don't yash (have) a maiwag (cake), but a handful of qamach (meal) in the jar, and a mait (little) shaman (oil) in the jar. Behold, I am qashash (gathering) shanayam (two) itz (sticks), that I may bawaa (come) in and bake it for me and my ban (son), that we may akal (eat) it, and mawath (death).

Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to her, Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). Bawaa (come) and ishah (make) as you have dabar (word / matter); but ishah (make) me of it a qatan (small/young/least) igah (cake) raashawan (first), and yatzaa (go out / come out) it out to me, and acharawan (afterward) ishah (make) some for you and for your ban (son).

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘The jar of qamach (meal) shall not empty, neither shall the jar of shaman (oil) chasar (fail), until the yawam (day) that Yahawah nathan (give) gasham (rain) on the adamah (earth).’
She yalak (went) and ishah (make) according to the dabar (word / matter) of Alayah (Elijah): and she, and he, and her bayath (house), akal (eat) many yawam (day).
The jar of qamach (meal) didn't empty, neither did the jar of shaman (oil) chasar (fail), according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, which he dabar (word / matter) by Alayah (Elijah).

It happened achar (other) these things, that the ban (son) of the ashah (wife/individual woman), the bailah (mistress) of the bayath (house), chalah (afflict) sick; and his chalay (sickness) was so severe, that there was no nashamah (breathing thing) yathar (left) in him.

She amar (spoke) to Alayah (Elijah), What have I to do with you, you ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam? You bawaa (come) come to me to zakar (remembrance/memory) my iwan (guilt/iniquity) to memory, and to mawath (death) my ban (son)!

He amar (spoke) to her, "nathan (give) me your ban (son)." He laqach (take / seized) him out of her chayaq (bosom), and ilah (go up / offer) him up into the room where he stayed, and shakab (laid) him on his own matah (bed).

He qaraa (called) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), Yahawah my Alahayam, have you also brought raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) on the alamanah (widow) with whom I stay, by mawath (death) her ban (son)?

He madad (stretched) himself on the yalad (birth / begot) shalawash (three) paim (times), and qaraa (called) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), Yahawah my Alahayam, please let this yalad (birth / begot) napash (living being/soul) shawab (turn back / repent) into him again.

Yahawah shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of Alayah (Elijah); and the napash (living being/soul) of the yalad (birth / begot) shawab (turn back / repent) into him again, and he chayah (revived).

Alayah (Elijah) laqach (take / seized) the yalad (birth / begot), and yarad (brought) him down out of the room into the bayath (house), and nathan (give) him to his am (mother); and Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke), raah (see), your ban (son) chay (life).

The ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke) to Alayah (Elijah), zah (this/that/these) I yadai (know) that you are a ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, and that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah in your pah (mouth) is amath (truth).

It happened after many yawam (day), that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Alayah (Elijah), in the shalayashay (third) shanah (year), amar (spoke), yalak (go), show yourself to Achaab (Ahab); and I will nathan (give) matar (rain) on the adamah (earth).
Alayah (Elijah) yalak (went) to show himself to Achaab (Ahab). The raib (famine) was severe in Shamarawan (Samaria).
Achaab (Ahab) qaraa (called) Ibadayah (Obadiah), who was over the bayath (house). (Now Ibadayah (Obadiah) yaraa (feared) Yahawah maad (greatly):

For it was so, when Ayazabal (Jezebel) karath (cut) off the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Yahawah, that Ibadayah (Obadiah) laqach (take / seized) one maah (hundred) nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and chabaa (hid) them by ayash (husband/individual man) in a mairah (cave), and kawal (all/every/entire) them with lacham (bread) and mayam (Waters).)

Achaab (Ahab) amar (spoke) to Ibadayah (Obadiah), yalak (go) through the aratz (Earth/land), to all the maiyan (springs) of mayam (Waters), and to all the nachal (stream / river). Perhaps we may matzaa (find) chatzayar (grass) and chayah (save) the sawas (horses) and parad (mules) chayah (alive), that we not karath (cut) all the animals.

So they chalaq (divided) the aratz (Earth/land) between them to ibar (pass over/through) throughout it: Achaab (Ahab) halak (move) achad (one) darak (way) by himself, and Ibadayah (Obadiah) halak (move) another darak (way) by himself.

As Ibadayah (Obadiah) was in the darak (way), behold, Alayah (Elijah) qaraah (met) him: and he recognized him, and napal (fall / be cast down) on his panayam (face), and amar (spoke), Is it you, my Adawan Alayah (Elijah)?
He amar (spoke) him, It is I. Yalak (go), amar (spoke) your Adawan, ‘Behold, Alayah (Elijah) is here!’
He amar (spoke), Wherein have I chataa (sinned), that you nathan (give) deliver your ibad (servant) into the yad (hand) of Achaab (Ahab), to mawath (death) me?

As Yahawah your Alahayam chay (life), there is no gaway (nation / people) or mamalakah (kingdom), ashar (who/that) my Adawan has not shalach (send) to baqash (seek) you. When they amar (spoke), ‘He is not here,’ he took an shabai (swear / take oath) of the mamalakah (kingdom) and gaway (nation / people), that they didn't matzaa (find) you.
Now you amar (spoke), ‘yalak (go), amar (spoke) your Adawan, "Behold, Alayah (Elijah) is here."’

It will happen, as soon as I am yalak (gone) from you, that the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah will nashaa (lift) you I don't yadai (know) where; and so when I bawaa (come) and nagad (tell) Achaab (Ahab), and he can't matzaa (find) you, he will harag (kill) me. But I, your ibad (servant), have yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah from my naiwar (youth).

Wasn't it nagad (told) my Adawan what I ishah (make) when Ayazabal (Jezebel) harag (killed) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Yahawah, how I chabaa (hid) one maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man) of yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) with chamashayam (fifty) to a mairah (cave), and kawal (all/every/entire) them with lacham (bread) and mayam (Waters)?
Now you amar (spoke), ‘yalak (go), amar (spoke) your Adawan, "Behold, Alayah (Elijah) is here;"’ and he will harag (kill) me.
Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke), As Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) chay (life), panayam (before) whom I imad (stand), I will raah (see) show myself to him today.
So Ibadayah (Obadiah) yalak (went) to qaraah (meet) Achaab (Ahab), and nagad (told) him; and Achaab (Ahab) yalak (went) to qaraah (meet) Alayah (Elijah).
It happened, when Achaab (Ahab) raah (see) Alayah (Elijah), that Achaab (Ahab) amar (spoke) to him, Is that you, you troubler of Yasharaal (Israel)?

He amar (spoke), I have not ikar (troubled) Yasharaal (Israel); but you, and your ab (father) bayath (house), in that you have forsaken the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah, and you have yalak (followed) the Bail (Baals).

Now therefore shalach (send), and qabatz (gather) to me all Yasharaal (Israel) to har (mountain) Karamal (Carmel), and arabai (four) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Bail (Baal), and arabai (four) maah (hundred) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) Asharah (of) the Asherah, who akal (eat) at Ayazabal (Jezebel's) shalachan (table).
So Achaab (Ahab) shalach (send) to all the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), and qabatz (gathered) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) qabatz (together) to har (mountain) Karamal (Carmel).

Alayah (Elijah) nagash (came) near to all the im (people / nation), and amar (spoke), "How long will you waver between the shanayam (two) sides? If Yahawah is Alahayam, yalak (follow) him; but if Bail (Baal), then yalak (follow) him." The im (people / nation) inah (answer / respond) him not a dabar (word / matter).

Then Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to the im (people / nation), “I, even I only, am yathar (left) a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Yahawah; but Bail (Baal's) nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) are arabai (four) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) ayash (husband/individual man).

Nathan (give) them therefore give us shanayam (two) par (bulls); and let them bachar (choose) achad (one) par (bull) for themselves, and nathach (cut) it in pieces, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it on the itz (wood), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) no ash (fire) under; and I will ishah (make) the other par (bull), and nathan (give) it on the itz (wood), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) no ash (fire) under it.

You qaraa (called) on the sham (name) of your Alahayam, and I will qaraa (called) on the sham (name) of Yahawah. The Alahayam who inah (answer / respond) by ash (fire), let him be Alahayam.” All the im (people / nation) inah (answer / respond), It is tawab (pleasant/functional) inah (answer / respond).

Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Bail (Baal), bachar (choose) achad (one) par (bull) for yourselves, and ishah (make) it raashawan (first); for you are many; and qaraa (called) on the sham (name) of your Alahayam, but shawam (place / establish / appoint) no ash (fire) under it.

They laqach (take / seized) the par (bull) which was nathan (give) them, and they ishah (make) it, and qaraa (called) on the sham (name) of Bail (Baal) from baqar (morning) even until tzahar (noon), amar (spoke), Bail (Baal), inah (answer / respond) us. But there was no qawal (sound / voice), nor any who inah (answer / respond). They pasach (leaped) about the mazabach (altar) which was ishah (make).

It happened at tzahar (noon), that Alayah (Elijah) hathal (mocked) them, and amar (spoke), qaraa (called) gadawal (very great/important/mighty); for he is a Alahayam. Either he is musing, or he has gone aside, or he is on a darak (journey), or perhaps he sleeps and must be awakened.
They qaraa (called) qawal (sound / voice), and gadad (cut) themselves in their mashapat (way) with knives and lances, until the dam (blood) shapak (gushed) out on them.

It was so, when tzahar (midday) was past, that they nabaa (prophesied) until the time of the ilah (go up / offer) of the ilah (go up / offer); but there was neither qawal (sound / voice), nor any to inah (answer / respond), nor any who qashab (regarded).

Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to all the im (people / nation), "nagash (come) near to me;" and all the im (people / nation) nagash (came) near to him. He rapaa (repaired) the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah that was haras (thrown) down.

Alayah (Elijah) laqach (take / seized) shanayam (two) aban (stone), according to the masapar (number) of the shabat (tribes) of the ban (son) of Yaiqab (Jacob), to whom the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came, amar (spoke), Yasharaal (Israel) shall be your sham (name).

With the aban (stone) he banah (built) an mazabach (altar) in the sham (name) of Yahawah. He ishah (make) a thailah (trench) around the mazabach (altar), large enough to bayath (house) two saah (measures) of zarai (seed).

He irak (put) the itz (wood) in irak (order), and nathach (cut) the par (bull) in pieces, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it on the itz (wood). He said, Fill four jars with water, and pour it on the burnt offering, and on the itz (wood).
He amar (spoke), "Do it a shanah (second) time;" and they did it the shanah (second) time. He amar (spoke), "shanah (do) it a third time;" and they did it the shalash (three) time.
The mayam (Waters) yalak (ran) around the mazabach (altar); and he also malaa (filled) the thailah (trench) with mayam (Waters).

It happened at the time of the ilah (go up / offer) of the manachah (offering), that Alayah (Elijah) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) nagash (came) near, and amar (spoke), Yahawah, the Alahayam of Abaraham (Abraham), of Yatzachaq (Isaac), and of Yasharaal (Israel), yadai (let) it be known this yawam (day) that you are Alahayam in Yasharaal (Israel), and that I am your ibad (servant), and that I ishah (make) done all these things at your dabar (word / matter).

Inah (answer / respond) me, Yahawah, inah (answer / respond) me, that this im (people / nation) may yadai (know) that you, Yahawah, are Alahayam, and that you have sabab (turned) their lab (heart) sabab (back) again.

Then the ash (fire) of Yahawah napal (fall / be cast down), and akal (eat) the burnt ilah (offering), and the itz (wood), and the aban (stone), and the ipar (dust), and lachak (licked) up the mayam (Waters) that was in the thailah (trench).
When all the im (people / nation) raah (see) it, they napal (fall / be cast down) on their panayam (faces). They amar (spoke), Yahawah, he is Alahayam! Yahawah, he is Alahayam!

Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to them, "Seize the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Bail (Baal)! Don't let ayash (husband/individual man) of them malat (escape)!" They seized them. Alayah (Elijah) yarad (brought) them down to the nachal (stream / river) Qayashawan (Kishon), and shachat (killed) them there.
Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to Achaab (Ahab), ilah (go up / offer) up, akal (eat) and shathah (drinks); for there is the qawal (sound / voice) of hamawan (abundance) of gasham (rain).

So Achaab (Ahab) ilah (go up / offer) up to akal (eat) and to shathah (drinks). Alayah (Elijah) ilah (go up / offer) up to the raash (head) of Karamal (Carmel); and he bowed himself down on the aratz (Earth/land), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) his panayam (face) between his barak (knees).

He amar (spoke) to his nair (servant), "ilah (go up / offer) up now, nabat (look) darak (toward) the yam (sea/waters)." He ilah (go up / offer) up, and nabat (looked), and amar (spoke), "There is maawamah (nothing)." He amar (spoke), "shawab (turn back / repent) again" shabai (seven) paim (times).

It happened at the shabayaiy (seventh) time, that he amar (spoke), "Behold, a qatan (small/young/least) ib (cloud), like a ayash (husband/individual man) kap (hand), is ilah (go up / offer) out of the yam (sea/waters)." He amar (spoke), ilah (go up / offer) up, amar (spoke) Achaab (Ahab), ‘Get asar (ready) and yarad (go) down, so that the gasham (rain) doesn't itzar (stop) you.’

It happened in a little kah (while), that the sky grew qadar (black) with ib (clouds) and rawach (spirit / wind), and there was a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) gasham (rain). Achaab (Ahab) rakab (rode), and yalak (went) to Yazaraial (Jezreel).
The yad (hand) of Yahawah was on Alayah (Elijah); and he tucked his cloak into his belt and rawatz (ran) panayam (before) Achaab (Ahab) to the entrance of Yazaraial (Jezreel).
Achaab (Ahab) nagad (told) Ayazabal (Jezebel) all that Alayah (Elijah) ishah (make) done, and how he had harag (killed) all the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) with the charab (sword).

Then Ayazabal (Jezebel) shalach (send) a malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to Alayah (Elijah), amar (spoke), So let the Alahayam ishah (make) to me, and more also, if I don't shawam (place / establish / appoint) your napash (living being/soul) as the napash (living being/soul) of achad (one) of them by machar (tomorrow) about this ith (time)!

When he raah (see) that, he qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) for his napash (living being/soul), and bawaa (come) Baarashabai (to) Beersheba, which belongs to Yahawadah (Judah), and yanach (left) his nair (servant) there.

But he himself halak (move) a yawam (day) darak (journey) into the madabar (wilderness), and bawaa (come) and yashab (inhabit/dwell) down under a ratham (juniper) tree: and he shaal (requested) for himself that he might mawath (death), and amar (spoke), It is rab (enough). Now, O Yahawah, laqach (take / seized) away my napash (living being/soul); for I am not tawab (pleasant/functional) than my ab (father).
He shakab (lay) down and yashan (slept) under a ratham (juniper) tree; and behold, an malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) nagai (touched) him, and amar (spoke) to him, qawam (rise up) and akal (eat)!

He nabat (looked), and behold, there was at his maraashah (head) a igah (cake) baked on the ratzap (coals), and a jar of mayam (Waters). He akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and shakab (lay) down again.

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah shawab (turn back / repent) again the shanay (second) time, and nagai (touched) him, and amar (spoke), qawam (rise up) and akal (eat), darak (because) the journey is rab (too) great for you.

He qawam (rise up), and akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and yalak (went) in the kach (strength / mighty / power) of that food arabaiyam (forty) yawam (day) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights) to Charab (Horeb) the har (mountain) of Alahayam.
He bawaa (come) there to a mairah (cave), and lawan (lodged) there; and behold, the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to him, and he amar (spoke) to him, What are you doing here, Alayah (Elijah)?

He amar (spoke), I have been very qanaa (jealous) for Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (troop); for the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) have forsaken your barayath (covenant), haras (thrown) down your mazabach (altars), and harag (slain) your nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) with the charab (sword). I, even I only, am yathar (left); and they baqash (seek) my napash (living being/soul), to laqach (take / seized) it away.

He amar (spoke), "yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and imad (stand) on the har (mountain) panayam (before) Yahawah." Behold, Yahawah ibar (pass over/through) by, and a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and chazaq (strong) rawach (spirit / wind) paraq (tore) the har (mountain), and shabar (broke) in pieces the salai (rocks) panayam (before) Yahawah; but Yahawah was not in the rawach (spirit / wind). Achar (other) the rawach (spirit / wind) an raish (earthquake); but Yahawah was not in the raish (earthquake).
Achar (other) the raish (earthquake) a ash (fire) passed; but Yahawah was not in the ash (fire): and achar (other) the ash (fire) a still daq (small) qawal (sound / voice).

It was so, when Alayah (Elijah) shamai (hearken / hear) it, that he lawat (wrapped) his panayam (face) in his adarath (mantle), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and imad (stood) in the entrance of the mairah (cave). Behold, a qawal (sound / voice) came to him, and amar (spoke), What are you doing here, Alayah (Elijah)?

He amar (spoke), I have been very qanaa (jealous) for Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (troop); for the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) have forsaken your barayath (covenant), haras (thrown) down your mazabach (altars), and harag (slain) your nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) with the charab (sword). I, even I only, am yathar (left); and they baqash (seek) my napash (living being/soul), to laqach (take / seized) it away.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, yalak (go), shawab (turn back / repent) on your darak (way) to the madabar (wilderness) of Damashaq (Damascus). When you arrive, you shall mashach (anoint) Chazaal (Hazael) to be malak (king) over Aram (Syria).

You shall mashach (anoint) Yahawaa (Jehu) the ban (son) of Namashay (Nimshi) to be malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel); and you shall mashach (anoint) Alayashai (Elisha) the ban (son) of Shapat (Shaphat) of Abalamachawalah (Abel) Meholah to be nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) in your place.

It shall happen, that he who malat (escapes) from the charab (sword) of Chazaal (Hazael), Yahawaa (Jehu) will mawath (death); and he who malat (escapes) from the charab (sword) of Yahawaa (Jehu), Alayashai (Elisha) will mawath (death).

Yet will I shaar (leave) shabai (seven) alap (thousand) in Yasharaal (Israel), all the barak (knees) which have not karai (bowed) to Bail (Baal), and every pah (mouth) which has not nashaq (kissed) him.

So he departed there, and matzaa (found) Alayashai (Elisha) the ban (son) of Shapat (Shaphat), who was charash (plowing), with shanayam (two) tzamad (yoke) of oxen panayam (before) him, and he with the shanayam (two): and Alayah (Elijah) ibar (pass over/through) over to him, and shalak (cast) his adarath (mantle) on him.

He izab (left) the oxen, and rawatz (ran) achar (other) Alayah (Elijah), and amar (spoke), "Let me please nashaq (kiss) my ab (father) and my am (mother), and then I will yalak (follow) you." He amar (spoke) to him, yalak (go) back again; for what ishah (make) I done to you?

He shawab (turn back / repent) from achar (other) him, and laqach (take / seized) the tzamad (yoke) of oxen, and zabach (killed) them, and bashal (boiled) their bashar (flesh) with the kalay (instruments) of the oxen, and nathan (give) to the im (people / nation), and they akal (eat). Then he qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) achar (other) Alayah (Elijah), and sharath (served) him.

Banahadad (Ben) Hadad the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) qabatz (gathered) all his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) qabatz (together); and there were shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) malak (king) with him, and sawas (horses) and rakab (chariots): and he ilah (go up / offer) up and tzawar (besieged) Shamarawan (Samaria), and lacham (fought) against it.
He shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to Achaab (Ahab) malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), into the iyar (city), and said to him, Thus says Ben Hadad,
‘Your kasap (silver) and your zahab (gold) is mine. Your wives also and your ban (son), even the tawab (pleasant/functional), are mine.’
The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) inah (answer / respond), It is according to your amar (spoke), my Adawan, O malak (king). I am yours, and all that I have.

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) shawab (turn back / repent) again, and amar (spoke), Banahadad (Ben) Hadad amar (spoke), ‘I shalach (send) amar (spoke) to you, saying, "You shall nathan (give) me your kasap (silver), and your zahab (gold), and your wives, and your ban (son);

But I will shalach (send) my ibad (servant) to you machar (tomorrow) about this ith (time), and they shall chapash (search) your bayath (house), and the bayath (house) of your ibad (servant); and it shall be, that whatever is machamad (pleasant) in your iyan (eye), they shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) it in their yad (hand), and laqach (take / seized) it away."’

Then the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) qaraa (called) all the zaqan (elders) of the aratz (Earth/land), and amar (spoke), Please notice how this man baqash (seeks) rai (mischief); for he shalach (send) to me for my wives, and for my ban (son), and for my kasap (silver), and for my zahab (gold); and I didn't manai (deny) him.
All the zaqan (elders) and all the im (people / nation) amar (spoke) to him, Don't shamai (hearken / hear), neither abah (be willing / desire).

Therefore he amar (spoke) to the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) Banahadad (of) Ben Hadad, "amar (spoke) my Adawan the malak (king), ‘All that you shalach (send) for to your ibad (servant) at the raashawan (first) I will ishah (make); but this thing I cannot ishah (make).’" The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) departed, and shawab (turn back / repent) him shawab (turn back / repent) the dabar (word / matter).

Banahadad (Ben) Hadad shalach (send) to him, and amar (spoke), The Alahayam ishah (make) so to me, and more also, if the ipar (dust) of Shamarawan (Samaria) shall sapaq (suffice) for shail (handfuls) for all the im (people / nation) who ragal (feet / foot) me.
The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) inah (answer / respond), dabar (word / matter) him, ‘Don't let him who chagar (puts) on his armor brag like he who takes it off.’

It happened, when Ben Hadad shamai (hearken / hear) this dabar (word / matter), as he was shathah (drinks), he and the malak (king), in the sakah (pavilions), that he amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), "Prepare to attack!" They prepared to attack the iyar (city).

Behold, a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) nagash (came) near to Achaab (Ahab) malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘raah (see) you seen all this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) hamawan (multitude)? Behold, I will nathan (give) it into your yad (hand) this yawam (day); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.’

Achaab (Ahab) amar (spoke), "By whom?" He amar (spoke), "Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘By the nair (young) men of the shar (prince / ruler) of the madayanah (provinces).’" Then he amar (spoke), "Who shall begin the malachamah (battle)?" He amar (spoke), You.

Then he mustered the nair (young) men of the shar (prince / ruler) of the madayanah (provinces), and they were shanayam (two) maah (hundred) and shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two). Achar (other) them, he mustered all the im (people / nation), even all the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), being shabai (seven) alap (thousand).

They yatzaa (go out / come out) out at tzahar (noon). Banahadad (But) Ben Hadad was shathah (drinks) himself shakawar (drunk) in the sakah (pavilions), he and the malak (king), the shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) malak (king) who izar (helped) him.

The nair (young) men of the shar (prince / ruler) of the madayanah (provinces) yatzaa (go out / come out) out raashawan (first); and Banahadad (Ben) Hadad shalach (send) out, and they nagad (told) him, amar (spoke), ayash (husband/individual man) are yatzaa (go out / come out) out from Shamarawan (Samaria).

He amar (spoke), If they yatzaa (go out / come out) come out for shalawam (peace / safety), thapash (take) them chay (life); or if they yatzaa (go out / come out) come out for malachamah (war), thapash (take) them chay (life).

So these yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the iyar (city), the nair (young) men of the shar (prince / ruler) of the madayanah (provinces), and the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) which achar (other) them.

They ayash (husband/individual man) nakah (killed) his ayash (husband/individual man). The Aram (Syrians) nawas (fled), and Yasharaal (Israel) radap (pursued) them. Banahadad (Ben) Hadad the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) malat (escaped) on a sawas (horse) with horsemen.

The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and nakah (struck) the sawas (horses) and rakab (chariots), and nakah (killed) the Aram (Syrians) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) makah (slaughter).

The nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) nagash (came) near to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (spoke) to him, yalak (go), chazaq (strengthen) yourself, and yadai (mark), and raah (see) what you ishah (make); for at the thashawabah (return) of the shanah (year) the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) will ilah (go up / offer) up against you.

The ibad (servant) of the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) amar (spoke) to him, “Their Alahayam is a Alahayam of the har (mountain); therefore they were chazaq (stronger) than we. But let us lacham (fight) against them in the mayashawar (plain), and laa (NOT) we shall be chazaq (stronger) than they.

Ishah (make) this thing: sawar (take) the malak (king) away, every ayash (husband/individual man) out of his maqawam (place), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) pachah (captains) in their place.

Muster an chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), like the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) that you napal (fall / be cast down) lost, sawas (horse) for sawas (horse), and rakab (chariot) for rakab (chariot). We will lacham (fight) against them in the mayashawar (plain), and surely we will be chazaq (stronger) than them.” He shamai (hearken / hear) to their qawal (sound / voice), and ishah (make) so.

It happened at the thashawabah (return) of the shanah (year), that Banahadad (Ben) Hadad mustered the Aram (Syrians), and ilah (go up / offer) up to Apaq (Aphek), to malachamah (fight) against Yasharaal (Israel).

The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) were mustered, and were kawal (all/every/entire), and yalak (went) qaraah (against) them. The ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) chanah (encamped) before them like shanayam (two) chashap (little) flocks of young iz (goats); but the Aram (Syrians) malaa (filled) the aratz (Earth/land).

A ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam nagash (came) near and amar (spoke) to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘Because the Aram (Syrians) have amar (spoke), "Yahawah is a Alahayam of the har (mountain), but he is not a Alahayam of the imaq (valleys);" therefore I will nathan (give) all this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) hamawan (multitude) into your yad (hand), and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.’

They chanah (encamped) alah (these) over nakach (against) the other shabai (seven) yawam (day). So it was, that in the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) the malachamah (battle) was qarab (come close); and the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) nakah (killed) one maah (hundred) alap (thousand) footmen of the Aram (Syrians) in achad (one) yawam (day).

But the yathar (rest) nawas (fled) to Apaq (Aphek), into the iyar (city); and the chawamah (wall) napal (fall / be cast down) on isharayam (twenty) - shabai (seven) alap (thousand) ayash (husband/individual man) who were yathar (left). Banahadad (Ben) Hadad nawas (fled), and bawaa (come) into the iyar (city), into an chadar (inner) room.

His ibad (servant) amar (spoke) to him, See now, we have shamai (hearken / hear) that the malak (king) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) are chasad (grace) malak (king). Please let us shawam (place / establish / appoint) sackcloth on our bodies, and chabal (ropes) on our raash (head), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel). Maybe he will chayah (save) your napash (living being/soul).

So they chagar (put) sackcloth on their bodies and chabal (ropes) on their raash (head), and bawaa (come) to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (spoke), "Your ibad (servant) Banahadad (Ben) Hadad amar (spoke), ‘Please chayah (let) me live.’" He amar (spoke), Is he still chay (life)? He is my ach (brother/kinsman).

Now the ayash (husband/individual man) nachash (observed) diligently, and hurried to take this phrase; and they amar (spoke), "Your ach (brother/kinsman) Banahadad (Ben) Hadad." Then he amar (spoke), "bawaa (come), laqach (take / seized) him." Then Banahadad (Ben) Hadad yatzaa (go out / come out) out to him; and he ilah (go up / offer) him to come up into the marakabah (chariot).

Ben Hadad amar (spoke) to him, "The iyar (cities) which my ab (father) laqach (take / seized) from your ab (father) I will shawab (turn back / repent). You shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) chawatz (streets) for yourself in Damashaq (Damascus), as my ab (father) shawam (place / establish / appoint) in Shamarawan (Samaria)." "I," said Ahab, "will shalach (send) you go with this barayath (covenant)." So he karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with him, and shalach (send) him go.

A achad (one) ayash (husband/individual man) of the ban (son) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) amar (spoke) to his rai (neigbor/another person) by the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, "Please nakah (strike) me!" The ayash (husband/individual man) maan (refused) to nakah (strike) him.

Then he amar (spoke) to him, "Because you have not shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah, behold, as soon as you are departed from me, a aray (lion) shall nakah (kill) you." As soon as he was departed from him, a aray (lion) matzaa (found) him, and nakah (killed) him.

Then he matzaa (found) achar (other) ayash (husband/individual man), and amar (spoke), "Please nakah (strike) me." The ayash (husband/individual man) nakah (struck) him, nakah (smiting) and patzai (wounding) him.
So the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) departed, and waited for the malak (king) by the darak (way), and disguised himself with his headband over his iyan (eye).

As the malak (king) ibar (pass over/through) by, he tzaiq (cried) to the malak (king); and he amar (spoke), "Your ibad (servant) yatzaa (go out / come out) out into the qarab (among / near) of the malachamah (battle); and behold, a ayash (husband/individual man) sawar (turned) aside, and bawaa (come) a ayash (husband/individual man) to me, and amar (spoke), ‘Guard this ayash (husband/individual man)! If by any paqad (visit) he be paqad (visit), then your napash (living being/soul) shall be for his napash (living being/soul), or else you shall shaqal (pay) a kakar (talent) of kasap (silver).’

As your ibad (servant) was ishah (make) here and there, he was ayan (gone)." The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke) to him, So your mashapat (judgment) shall be; you yourself have charatz (decided) it.
He hurried, and took the headband sawar (away) from his iyan (eye); and the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) recognized that he was of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy).

He amar (spoke) to him, Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘Because you have shalach (send) go out of your yad (hand) the ayash (husband/individual man) whom I charam (had) devoted to destruction, therefore your napash (living being/soul) shall go for his napash (living being/soul), and your im (people / nation) for his im (people / nation).’
The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) yalak (went) to his bayath (house) sullen and angry, and bawaa (come) to Shamarawan (Samaria).

It happened achar (other) these things, that Nabawath (Naboth) the yazaraialay (jezreelite) had a karam (vineyard), which was in Yazaraial (Jezreel), hard by the hayakal (palace) of Achaab (Ahab) malak (king) of Shamarawan (Samaria).

Achaab (Ahab) dabar (word / matter) to Nabawath (Naboth), amar (spoke), nathan (give) me your karam (vineyard), that I may have it for a gan (garden) of yaraq (herbs), because it is qarawab (near) to my bayath (house); and I will nathan (give) you for it a tawab (pleasant/functional) karam (vineyard) than it. Or, if it seems tawab (pleasant/functional) to you, I will nathan (give) you its machayar (worth) in kasap (money).
Nabawath (Naboth) amar (spoke) to Achaab (Ahab), May Yahawah chalayalah (forbid) me, that I should nathan (give) the nachalah (inheritance) of my ab (father) to you!

Achaab (Ahab) bawaa (come) into his bayath (house) sullen and angry because of the dabar (word / matter) which Nabawath (Naboth) the yazaraialay (jezreelite) had dabar (word / matter) to him; for he had amar (spoke), "I will not nathan (give) you the nachalah (inheritance) of my ab (father)." He shakab (laid) himself down on his matah (bed), and sabab (turned) away his panayam (face), and would akal (eat) no lacham (bread).
But Ayazabal (Jezebel) his ashah (wife/individual woman) bawaa (come) to him, and dabar (word / matter) to him, Why is your rawach (spirit / wind) so sar (sad), that you akal (eat) no lacham (bread)?

He dabar (word / matter) to her, Because I dabar (word / matter) to Nabawath (Naboth) the yazaraialay (jezreelite), and dabar (word / matter) to him, ‘nathan (give) me your karam (vineyard) for kasap (money); or else, if it chapatz (pleases) you, I will nathan (give) you another karam (vineyard) for it.’ He amar (spoke), ‘I will not nathan (give) you my karam (vineyard).’

Ayazabal (Jezebel) his ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke) to him, ishah (make) you now govern the malawakah (kingdom) of Yasharaal (Israel)? Qawam (rise up), and akal (eat) lacham (bread), and let your lab (heart) be yatab (merry). I will nathan (give) you the karam (vineyard) of Nabawath (Naboth) the yazaraialay (jezreelite).

So she kathab (wrote) sapar (book / scribed document) in Achaab (Ahab's) sham (name), and chatham (sealed) them with his chawatham (seal), and shalach (send) the sapar (book / scribed document) to the zaqan (elders) and to the char (nobles) who were in his iyar (city), who lived with Nabawath (Naboth).
She kathab (wrote) in the sapar (book / scribed document), amar (spoke), qaraa (called) a tzawam (fast), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) Nabawath (Naboth) on raash (head) among the im (people / nation).

Yashab (inhabit/dwell) shanayam (two) ayash (husband/individual man), base fellows, before him, and let them iwad (admonish/bear witness against) amar (spoke) him, saying, ‘You barak (cursed) Alahayam and the malak (king)!’ Then yatzaa (go out / come out) him out, and saqal (stone) him to mawath (death).

The ishah (make) of his iyar (city), even the zaqan (elders) and the char (nobles) who lived in his iyar (city), ishah (make) as Ayazabal (Jezebel) had shalach (send) to them, according as it was kathab (written) in the sapar (book / scribed document) which she had shalach (send) to them.
They qaraa (called) a tzawam (fast), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) Nabawath (Naboth) on raash (head) among the im (people / nation).

The shanayam (two) ayash (husband/individual man), the base fellows, bawaa (come) in and yashab (inhabit/dwell) before him. The base ayash (husband/individual man) iwad (admonish/bear witness against) against him, even against Nabawath (Naboth), in the presence of the im (people / nation), amar (spoke), "Nabawath (Naboth) barak (cursed) Alahayam and the malak (king)!" Then they yatzaa (go out / come out) him out of the iyar (city), and saqal (stoned) him to mawath (death) with aban (stone).
Then they shalach (send) to Ayazabal (Jezebel), amar (spoke), Nabawath (Naboth) has been saqal (stoned), and is mawath (death).

It happened, when Ayazabal (Jezebel) shamai (hearken / hear) that Nabawath (Naboth) was saqal (stoned), and was mawath (death), that Ayazabal (Jezebel) amar (spoke) to Achaab (Ahab), qawam (rise up), take yarash (possession) of the karam (vineyard) of Nabawath (Naboth) the yazaraialay (jezreelite), which he maan (refused) to nathan (give) you for kasap (money); for Nabawath (Naboth) is not chay (life), but mawath (death).

It happened, when Achaab (Ahab) shamai (hearken / hear) that Nabawath (Naboth) was mawath (death), that Achaab (Ahab) qawam (rise up) up to yarad (go) down to the karam (vineyard) of Nabawath (Naboth) the yazaraialay (jezreelite), to take yarash (possession) of it.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Alayah (Elijah) the thashabay (tishbite), amar (spoke),

Qawam (rise up), yarad (go) down to qaraah (meet) Achaab (Ahab) malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), who dwells in Shamarawan (Samaria). Behold, he is in the karam (vineyard) of Nabawath (Naboth), where he has yarad (gone) down to take yarash (possession) of it.

You shall dabar (word / matter) to him, amar (spoke), ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "Have you ratzach (killed) and also taken yarash (possession)?"’ You shall dabar (word / matter) to him, amar (spoke), ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "In the maqawam (place) where kalab (dogs) laqaq (licked) the dam (blood) of Nabawath (Naboth), kalab (dogs) will laqaq (lick) your dam (blood), even yours."’

Achaab (Ahab) amar (spoke) to Alayah (Elijah), "matzaa (have) you found me, my ayab (enemy)?" He amar (spoke), I matzaa (have) found you, because you have makar (sold) yourself to ishah (make) that which is rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah.

Behold, I will bawaa (come) rai (evil) on you, and will utterly sweep you bair (away) and will karath (cut) off from Achaab (Ahab) everyone who urinates against a qayar (wall), and him who is itzar (shut) up and him who is izab (left) at large in Yasharaal (Israel).

I will nathan (give) your bayath (house) like the bayath (house) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Nabat (Nebat), and like the bayath (house) of Baishaa (Baasha) the ban (son) of Achayah (Ahijah) for the kais (provocation) with which you have provoked me to kais (anger), and have made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).
Yahawah also dabar (word / matter) of Ayazabal (Jezebel), amar (spoke), The kalab (dogs) shall akal (eat) Ayazabal (Jezebel) by the chayal (rampart) of Yazaraial (Jezreel).
The kalab (dogs) will akal (eat) he who mawath (death) of Achaab (Ahab) in the iyar (city); and the iwap (flying) of the sky will akal (eat) he who mawath (death) in the shadah (field).

But there was none like Achaab (Ahab), who makar (sold) himself to ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, whom Ayazabal (Jezebel) his ashah (wife/individual woman) sawath (stirred) up.

He did very thaib (abominably) in yalak (following) galawal (idols), according to all that the Amaray (Amorites) ishah (make), whom Yahawah yarash (cast) out panayam (before) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel).

It happened, when Achaab (Ahab) shamai (hearken / hear) those dabar (word / matter), that he qarai (tore) his clothes, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) sackcloth on his bashar (flesh), and tzawam (fasted), and shakab (lay) in sackcloth, and halak (move) at (softly).
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Alayah (Elijah) the thashabay (tishbite), amar (spoke),

Raah (see) how Achaab (Ahab) kanai (humbles) panayam (himself) before me? Yain (because) he kanai (humbles) panayam (himself) before me, I will not bawaa (come) the rai (evil) in his yawam (day); but in his ban (son) yawam (day) will I bawaa (come) the rai (evil) on his bayath (house).
They yashab (inhabit/dwell) shalawash (three) shanah (years) without malachamah (war) between Aram (Syria) and Yasharaal (Israel).
It happened in the shalayashay (third) shanah (year), that Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) yarad (came) down to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).

The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), You yadai (know) that Ramathagalaid (Ramoth) Galaid (Gilead) is ours, and we are still, and don't laqach (take / seized) it out of the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Aram (Syria)?

He amar (spoke) to Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat), "Will you yalak (go) with me to malachamah (battle) to Ramathagalaid (Ramoth) Gilead?" Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) amar (spoke) to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), I am as you are, my im (people / nation) as your im (people / nation), my sawas (horses) as your sawas (horses).
Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) amar (spoke) to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), Please darash (inquire) yawam (day) for the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah.

Then the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) qabatz (gathered) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) qabatz (together), about arabai (four) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man), and amar (spoke) to them, "Shall I yalak (go) against Ramathagalaid (Ramoth) Gilead to malachamah (battle), or shall I chadal (forbear)?" They amar (spoke), ilah (go up / offer) up; for the Adanay will nathan (give) it into the yad (hand) of the malak (king).
But Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) amar (spoke), Isn't there here a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Yahawah, that we may darash (inquire) of him?

The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke) to Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat), "There is yet achad (one) ayash (husband/individual man) by whom we may darash (inquire) of Yahawah, Mayakayahaw (Micaiah) the ban (son) of Yamalaa (Imlah); but I shanaa (hate) him; for he does not nabaa (prophesy) tawab (pleasant/functional) concerning me, but rai (evil)." Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) amar (spoke), Don't let the malak (king) amar (spoke) so.
Then the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) qaraa (called) an sarayas (officer), and amar (spoke), mahar (quickly) get Mayakayahaw (Micaiah) the ban (son) of Yamalaa (Imlah).

Now the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) were sitting ayash (husband/individual man) on his kasaa (throne), labash (arrayed) in their bagad (robes), in an open garan (place) at the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate) of Shamarawan (Samaria); and all the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) were prophesying panayam (before) them.

Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah) the ban (son) of Kanainah (Chenaanah) ishah (make) him qaran (horn) of barazal (iron), and amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘With these you shall nagach (push) the Aram (Syrians), until they are kalah (complete / finish).’

All the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) nabaa (prophesied) so, amar (spoke), ilah (go up / offer) up to Ramathagalaid (Ramoth) Gilead, and tzalach (prosper); for Yahawah will nathan (give) it into the yad (hand) of the malak (king).

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) who halak (move) to qaraa (called) Mayakayahaw (Micaiah) dabar (word / matter) to him, amar (spoke), See now, the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) declare tawab (pleasant/functional) to the malak (king) with achad (one) pah (mouth). Please let your dabar (word / matter) be like the dabar (word / matter) of achad (one) of them, and dabar (word / matter) tawab (pleasant/functional).
Mayakayahaw (Micaiah) amar (spoke), As Yahawah chay (life), what Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, that I will dabar (word / matter).

When he bawaa (come) come to the malak (king), the malak (king) amar (spoke) to him, "Mayakayahaw (Micaiah), shall we yalak (go) to Ramathagalaid (Ramoth) Gilead to malachamah (battle), or shall we chadal (forbear)?" He amar (spoke) him, ilah (go up / offer) up and tzalach (prosper); and Yahawah will nathan (give) it into the yad (hand) of the malak (king).

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to him, How many paim (times) do I have to shabai (swear / take oath) you that you dabar (word / matter) to me nothing but the amath (truth) in the sham (name) of Yahawah?

He amar (spoke), I raah (see) all Yasharaal (Israel) pawatz (scattered) on the har (mountain), as tzaan (sheep) that have no raih (shepherd). Yahawah amar (spoke), ‘These have no adawan (master / lord). Let them ayash (husband/individual man) shawab (turn back / repent) to his bayath (house) in shalawam (peace / safety).’

The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke) to Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat), Didn't I amar (spoke) you that he would not nabaa (prophesy) tawab (pleasant/functional) concerning me, but rai (evil)?

Micaiah amar (spoke), Therefore shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah. I raah (see) Yahawah sitting on his kasaa (throne), and all the tzabaa (troop) of shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) imad (standing) by him on his right yamayan (right hand) and on his shamaawal (left hand).

Yahawah amar (spoke), ‘Who shall pathah (entice) Achaab (Ahab), that he may ilah (go up / offer) up and napal (fall / be cast down) at Ramathagalaid (Ramoth) Gilead?’ One amar (spoke) kah (one) thing; and another amar (spoke) another.
A rawach (spirit / wind) yatzaa (go out / come out) out and imad (stood) panayam (before) Yahawah, and amar (spoke), ‘I will pathah (entice) him.’

Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, ‘How?’ He amar (spoke), ‘I will yatzaa (go out / come out) out and will be a shaqar (lying) rawach (spirit / wind) in the pah (mouth) of all his nabayaa (prophet/prophecy).’ He amar (spoke), ‘You will pathah (entice) him, and will also yakal (prevail). Yatzaa (go out / come out) out and ishah (make) so.’

Now therefore, behold, Yahawah nathan (give) put a shaqar (lying) rawach (spirit / wind) in the pah (mouth) of all these your nabayaa (prophet/prophecy); and Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) rai (evil) concerning you.

Then Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah) the ban (son) of Kanainah (Chenaanah) nagash (came) near, and nakah (struck) Mayakayahaw (Micaiah) on the lachay (cheek), and amar (spoke), Which ay (way) did the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah ibar (pass over/through) from me to dabar (word / matter) to you?
Mayakayahaw (Micaiah) amar (spoke), raah (see), you will see on that yawam (day), when you bawaa (come) into an chadar (inner) room to chabah (hide) yourself.

The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke), laqach (take / seized) Mayakayahaw (Micaiah), and shawab (turn back / repent) him back to Amawan (Amon) the shar (prince / ruler) of the iyar (city), and to Yawaash (Joash) the malak (king) ban (son).

Amar (spoke), ‘Thus amar (spoke) the malak (king), "shawam (place / establish / appoint) this fellow in the bayath (house), and akal (eat) him with lacham (bread) of lachatz (affliction) and with mayam (Waters) of lachatz (affliction), until I bawaa (come) in shalawam (peace / safety)."’

Mayakayahaw (Micaiah) amar (spoke), "If you shawab (turn back / repent) at shawab (turn back / repent) in shalawam (peace / safety), Yahawah has not dabar (word / matter) by me." He amar (spoke), shamai (hearken / hear), all you im (people / nation)!
So the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) ilah (go up / offer) up to Ramathagalaid (Ramoth) Gilead.

The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke) to Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat), "I will disguise myself, and bawaa (come) into the malachamah (battle); but you labash (put) on your bagad (robes)." The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) disguised himself, and bawaa (come) into the malachamah (battle).

Now the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) had tzawah (commanded) the shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) shar (prince / ruler) of his rakab (chariots), amar (spoke), lacham (fight) neither with qatan (small/young/least) nor gadawal (very great/important/mighty), except only with the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).

It happened, when the shar (prince / ruler) of the rakab (chariots) raah (see) Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat), that they amar (spoke), "Surely that is the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel)!" And they sawar (turned) aside to lacham (fight) against him. Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) zaiq (cried) out.

It happened, when the shar (prince / ruler) of the rakab (chariots) raah (see) that it was not the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), that they shawab (turn back / repent) back from achar (other) him.

A certain ayash (husband/individual man) mashak (drew) his qashath (bow) at random, and nakah (struck) the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) between the dabaq (joints) of the armor. Therefore he amar (spoke) to the rakab (driver) of his chariot, hapak (turn) your yad (hand), and yatzaa (go out / come out) me out of the machanah (battle); for I am severely chalah (afflict).

The malachamah (battle) ilah (go up / offer) that yawam (day). The malak (king) was propped up in his marakabah (chariot) facing the Aram (Syrians), and mawath (death) at irab (evening). The dam (blood) yatzaq (ran) out of the makah (wound) into the chayaq (bottom) of the rakab (chariot).

A ranah (cry) ibar (pass over/through) throughout the machanah (army) about the bawaa (come) down of the shamash (sun), amar (spoke), Every ayash (husband/individual man) to his iyar (city), and every ayash (husband/individual man) to his aratz (Earth/land)!
So the malak (king) mawath (death), and was bawaa (come) to Shamarawan (Samaria); and they qabar (bury) the malak (king) in Shamarawan (Samaria).

They shatap (washed) the rakab (chariot) by the barakah (pool) of Shamarawan (Samaria); and the kalab (dogs) laqaq (licked) up his dam (blood) where the prostitutes rachatz (washed) themselves; according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah which he dabar (word / matter).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (word / matter) of Achaab (Ahab), and all that he ishah (make), and the shan (ivory) bayath (house) which he banah (built), and all the iyar (cities) that he banah (built), aren't they kathab (written) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabar (word / matter) of the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
So Achaab (Ahab) shakab (slept) with his ab (father); and Achazayah (Ahaziah) his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.
Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the ban (son) of Asaa (Asa) began to malak (king) over Yahawadah (Judah) in the arabai (four) shanah (year) of Achaab (Ahab) malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) was shalawashayam (thirty) - chamash (five) shanah (years) ban (son) when he began to malak (king); and he malak (king) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) shanah (years) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem). His am (mother) sham (name) was Izawabah (Azubah) the bath (daughter) of Shalachay (Shilhi).

He yalak (walked) in all the darak (way) of Asaa (Asa) his ab (father); He didn't sawar (turn) aside from it, ishah (make) that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah: however the high places were not sawar (taken) away; the people still ishah (make) and burnt incense in the high places.
Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
Now the rest of the acts of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat), and his might that he showed, and how he warred, aren't they written in the book of the chronicles of the malak (king) of Judah?
The yathar (remnant) of the sodomites, that remained in the yawam (day) of his father Asa, he ishah (make) away out of the land.
There was no king in Edom: a deputy was king.
Jehoshaphat made ships of Tarshish to ayan (go) to Ophir for gold: but they didn't ayan (go); for the ships were broken at Ezion Geber.
Then Ahaziah the son of Ahab said to Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat), "Let my servants yalak (go) with your servants in the anayah (ships)." But Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) would not.
Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father; Jehoram his ban (son) reigned in his place.
Ahaziah the ban (son) of Ahab began to malak (king) over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) malak (king) of Judah, and he malak (king) two years over Israel.

He did that which was evil in the sight of Yahawah, and walked in the way of his father, and in the way of his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam the ban (son) of Nebat, in which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to sin.
He ishah (make) Baal, and worshiped him, and provoked to anger Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), according to all that his ab (father) ishah (make) done.
Mawaab (Moab) pashai (rebelled) against Yasharaal (Israel) achar (other) the mawath (death) of Achaab (Ahab).

Achazayah (Ahaziah) napal (fall / be cast down) down through the shabakah (lattice) in his upper room that was in Shamarawan (Samaria), and was chalah (afflict). So he shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah), and amar (spoke) to them, yalak (go), darash (inquire) of Bailazabawab (Baal) Zebub, the Alahayam of Iqarawan (Ekron), whether I will chayah (recover) of this chalay (sickness).

But the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Alayah (Elijah) the thashabay (tishbite), "qawam (rise up), ilah (go up / offer) up to qaraah (meet) the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of the malak (king) of Shamarawan (Samaria), and dabar (word / matter) them, ‘Is it because there is no Alahayam in Yasharaal (Israel), that you halak (move) to darash (inquire) of Bailazabawab (Baal) Zebub, the Alahayam of Iqarawan (Ekron)?

Now therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "You shall not yarad (come) down from the matah (bed) where you have ilah (go up / offer) up, but shall mawath (death) mawath (death)."’" Alayah (Elijah) departed.
The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) shawab (turn back / repent) to him, and he amar (spoke) to them, Why is it that you have shawab (turn back / repent)?

They amar (spoke) to him, A ayash (husband/individual man) ilah (go up / offer) up to qaraah (meet) us, and amar (spoke) to us, ‘yalak (go), shawab (turn back / repent) to the malak (king) who shalach (send) you, and dabar (word / matter) him, "Thus dabar (word / matter) Yahawah, ‘Is it because there is no Alahayam in Yasharaal (Israel), that you shalach (send) to darash (inquire) of Bailazabawab (Baal) Zebub, the Alahayam of Iqarawan (Ekron)? Therefore you shall not yarad (come) down from the matah (bed) where you have ilah (go up / offer) up, but shall mawath (death) mawath (death).’"’
He dabar (word / matter) to them, What kind of ayash (husband/individual man) was he who ilah (go up / offer) up to qaraah (meet) you, and dabar (word / matter) you these dabar (word / matter)?
They amar (spoke) him, "He was a shair (hair) bail (man), and wearing a iwar (leather) belt around his waist." He amar (spoke), It is Alayah (Elijah) the thashabay (tishbite).

Then the malak (king) shalach (send) a shar (prince / ruler) of chamashayam (fifty) with his chamashayam (fifty) to him. He ilah (go up / offer) up to him; and behold, he was sitting on the raash (head) of the har (mountain). He dabar (word / matter) to him, ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, the malak (king) has dabar (word / matter), ‘yarad (come) down!’

Alayah (Elijah) inah (answer / respond) to the shar (prince / ruler) of chamashayam (fifty), "If I am a ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, let ash (fire) yarad (come) down from the sky, and akal (eat) you and your chamashayam (fifty)!" Ash (fire) yarad (came) down from the sky, and akal (eat) him and his chamashayam (fifty).

Again he shalach (send) to him achar (other) shar (prince / ruler) of chamashayam (fifty) and his chamashayam (fifty). He inah (answer / respond) him, ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, the malak (king) has inah (answer / respond), ‘yarad (come) down maharah (quickly)!’

Alayah (Elijah) inah (answer / respond) them, "If I am a ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, let ash (fire) yarad (come) down from the sky, and akal (eat) you and your chamashayam (fifty)!" The ash (fire) of Alahayam yarad (came) down from the sky, and akal (eat) him and his chamashayam (fifty).

Again he shalach (send) the shar (prince / ruler) of a shalayashay (third) chamashayam (fifty) with his chamashayam (fifty). The shalayashay (third) shar (prince / ruler) of chamashayam (fifty) ilah (go up / offer) up, and bawaa (come) and karai (fell) on his barak (knees) before Alayah (Elijah), and begged him, and dabar (word / matter) to him, ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, please let my napash (living being/soul), and the napash (living being/soul) of these chamashayam (fifty) your ibad (servant), be yaqar (precious) in your iyan (eye).

Behold, ash (fire) yarad (came) down from the sky, and akal (eat) the shanayam (two) raashawan (former) shar (prince / ruler) of chamashayam (fifty) with their chamashayam (fifties). But now let my napash (living being/soul) be yaqar (precious) in your iyan (eye).

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Alayah (Elijah), "yarad (go) down with him. Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of him." He qawam (rise up), and yarad (went) down with him to the malak (king).

He dabar (word / matter) to him, Thus dabar (word / matter) Yahawah, ‘Because you have shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to darash (inquire) of Bailazabawab (Baal) Zebub, the Alahayam of Iqarawan (Ekron), is it because there is no Alahayam in Yasharaal (Israel) to darash (inquire) of his dabar (word / matter)? Therefore you shall not yarad (come) down from the matah (bed) where you have ilah (go up / offer) up, but shall mawath (death) mawath (death).’

So he mawath (death) according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah which Alayah (Elijah) had dabar (word / matter). Yahawaram (Jehoram) began to malak (king) in his place in the shanayam (two) shanah (year) of Yahawaram (Jehoram) the ban (son) of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah); because he had no ban (son).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (word / matter) of Achazayah (Ahaziah) which he ishah (make), aren't they kathab (written) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabar (word / matter) of the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel)?

It happened, when Yahawah would ilah (go up / offer) up Alayah (Elijah) by a sair (whirlwind) into shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), that Alayah (Elijah) yalak (went) with Alayashai (Elisha) from Galagal (Gilgal).

Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to Alayashai (Elisha), "Please wait here, for Yahawah has shalach (send) me as far as Bayathaal (Bethel)." Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke), "As Yahawah chay (life), and as your napash (living being/soul) chay (life), I will not izab (leave) you." So they yarad (went) down to Bayathaal (Bethel).
