The ban (son) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) who were at Bayathaal (Bethel) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to Alayashai (Elisha), and amar (spoke) to him, "Do you yadai (know) that Yahawah will laqach (take / seized) away your adawan (master / lord) from your raash (head) today?" He amar (spoke), Yes, I yadai (know) it; hold your chashah (peace).

Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to him, "Alayashai (Elisha), please wait here, for Yahawah has shalach (send) me to Yarayachaw (Jericho)." He amar (spoke), "As Yahawah chay (life), and as your napash (living being/soul) chay (life), I will not izab (leave) you." So they bawaa (come) to Yarayachaw (Jericho).

The ban (son) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) who were at Yarayachaw (Jericho) nagash (came) near to Alayashai (Elisha), and amar (spoke) to him, "Do you yadai (know) that Yahawah will laqach (take / seized) away your adawan (master / lord) from your raash (head) today?" He amar (spoke), Yes, I yadai (know) it. Hold your chashah (peace).

Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to him, "Please wait here, for Yahawah has shalach (send) me to the Yaradan (Jordan)." He amar (spoke), "As Yahawah chay (life), and as your napash (living being/soul) chay (life), I will not izab (leave) you." They shanayam (two) yalak (went) on.

Chamashayam (fifty) ayash (husband/individual man) of the ban (son) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) halak (move), and imad (stood) opposite them at a distance; and they shanayam (two) imad (stood) by the Yaradan (Jordan).

Alayah (Elijah) laqach (take / seized) his adarath (mantle), and galam (wrapped) it together, and nakah (struck) the mayam (Waters), and they were chatzah (divided) here and there, so that they shanayam (two) ibar (pass over/through) over on dry charabah (ground).

It happened, when they ibar (pass over/through) gone over, that Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to Alayashai (Elisha), "shaal (ask) what I shall ishah (make) for you, before I am laqach (take / seized) from you." Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke), Please let a shanayam (two) pah (portion) of your rawach (spirit / wind) be on me.
He amar (spoke), You have shaal (asked) a qashah (rough / hard) thing. If you raah (see) me when I am laqach (take / seized) from you, it shall be so for you; but if not, it shall not be so.

It happened, as they still halak (move) on, and dabar (word / matter), that behold, a rakab (chariot) of ash (fire) and sawas (horses) of ash (fire) parad (separated) them; and Alayah (Elijah) ilah (go up / offer) up by a sair (whirlwind) into shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)).

Alayashai (Elisha) raah (see) it, and he tzaiq (cried), "My ab (father), my ab (father), the rakab (chariots) of Yasharaal (Israel) and its horsemen!" He raah (see) him no more: and he chazaq (took) hold of his own clothes, and qarai (tore) them in shanayam (two) qarai (pieces).

He rawam (will lift up) up also the adarath (mantle) of Alayah (Elijah) that napal (fall / be cast down) from him, and shawab (turn back / repent) back, and imad (stood) by the shapah (bank) of the Yaradan (Jordan).

He laqach (take / seized) the adarath (mantle) of Alayah (Elijah) that napal (fall / be cast down) from him, and nakah (struck) the mayam (Waters), and amar (spoke), "Where is Yahawah, the Alahayam of Alayah (Elijah)?" When he also had nakah (struck) the mayam (Waters), they were chatzah (divided) here and there; and Alayashai (Elisha) ibar (pass over/through) over.

When the ban (son) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) who were at Yarayachaw (Jericho) over against him raah (see) him, they amar (spoke), "The rawach (spirit / wind) of Alayah (Elijah) nawach (rests) on Alayashai (Elisha)." They bawaa (come) to qaraah (meet) him, and shachah (bowed) themselves to the aratz (Earth/land) before him.

They amar (spoke) to him, See now, there are with your ibad (servant) chamashayam (fifty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ban (son). Please yalak (let) them go and baqash (seek) your adawan (master / lord). Perhaps the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah has nashaa (lift) him up, and put him on some har (mountain), or into some gayaa (valley). He amar (spoke), You shall not shalach (send) them.

When they patzar (urged) him until he was bawash (ashamed), he amar (spoke), "shalach (send) them." They shalach (send) therefore chamashayam (fifty) ayash (husband/individual man); and they searched for shalawash (three) yawam (day), but didn't matzaa (find) him.
They shawab (turn back / repent) back to him, while he stayed at Yarayachaw (Jericho); and he amar (spoke) to them, Didn't I amar (spoke) you, ‘Don't yalak (go)?’

The ayash (husband/individual man) of the iyar (city) amar (spoke) to Alayashai (Elisha), Behold, please, the mawashab (situation) of this iyar (city) is tawab (pleasant/functional), as my Adawan raah (see); but the mayam (Waters) is rai (bad), and the aratz (Earth/land) shakal (miscarries).
He amar (spoke), "laqach (take / seized) me a chadash (new) jar, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) malach (salt) in it." They laqach (take / seized) it to him.

He yatzaa (go out / come out) out to the mawatzaa (spring) of the mayam (Waters), and shalak (threw) malach (salt) into it, and amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘I have rapaa (healed) these mayam (Waters). There shall not be from there any more mawath (death) or shakal (miscarrying).’
So the mayam (Waters) were rapaa (healed) to this yawam (day), according to the dabar (word / matter) of Alayashai (Elisha) which he dabar (word / matter).

He ilah (go up / offer) up from there to Bayathaal (Bethel). As he was ilah (go up / offer) up by the darak (way), some youths yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the iyar (city) and qalas (mocked) him, and amar (spoke) to him, ilah (go up / offer) up, you baldy! Ilah (go up / offer) up, you baldhead!

He raah (see) achar (other) him and raah (see) them, and qalal (cursed) them in the sham (name) of Yahawah. Shanayam (two) female dab (bears) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the yair (woods), and mauled arabaiyam (forty) - shanayam (two) of those youths.
He yalak (went) from there to har (mountain) Karamal (Carmel), and from there he shawab (turn back / repent) to Shamarawan (Samaria).

Now Yahawaram (Jehoram) the ban (son) of Achaab (Ahab) began to malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel) in Shamarawan (Samaria) in the eighteenth shanah (year) of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and malak (king) shanayam (two) shanah (years).

He ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, but not like his ab (father), and like his am (mother); for he sawar (put) away the matzabah (pillar) of Bail (Baal) that his ab (father) ishah (make) made.
Nevertheless he held to the chataah (sin) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Nabat (Nebat), with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin); he didn't sawar (depart) from it.

Now Mayashai (Mesha) malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab) was a sheep breeder; and he shawab (turn back / repent) to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) the tzamar (wool) of one maah (hundred) alap (thousand) kar (lambs), and of one maah (hundred) alap (thousand) ayal (rams).
But it happened, when Achaab (Ahab) was mawath (death), that the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab) pashai (rebelled) against the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).
Malak (king) Yahawaram (Jehoram) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of Shamarawan (Samaria) at that yawam (day), and mustered all Yasharaal (Israel).

He yalak (went) and shalach (send) to Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), amar (spoke), "The malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab) has pashai (rebelled) against me. Will you yalak (go) with me against Mawaab (Moab) to malachamah (battle)?" He amar (spoke), I will ilah (go up / offer) up. I am as you are, my im (people / nation) as your im (people / nation), my sawas (horses) as your sawas (horses).
He amar (spoke), "Which darak (way) shall we ilah (go up / offer) up?" He amar (spoke), The darak (way) of the madabar (wilderness) of Adam (Edom).

So the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) yalak (went), and the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and the malak (king) of Adam (Edom); and they sabab (made) a circuit of shabai (seven) yawam (day)' darak (journey). There was no mayam (Waters) for the machanah (army), nor for the animals that ragal (feet / foot) them.

The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke), ahah (alas)! For Yahawah has qaraa (called) these shalawash (three) malak (king) together to nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of Mawaab (Moab).

But Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) amar (spoke), "Isn't there here a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Yahawah, that we may darash (inquire) of Yahawah by him?" Achad (one) of the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel's) ibad (servant) inah (answer / respond), Alayashai (Elisha) the ban (son) of Shapat (Shaphat) is here, who yatzaq (poured) mayam (Waters) on the yad (hand) of Alayah (Elijah).

Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) amar (spoke), "The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah is with him." So the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) and the malak (king) of Adam (Edom) yarad (went) down to him.

Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke) to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), "What have I to do with you? Yalak (go) to the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of your ab (father), and to the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of your am (mother)." The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke) to him, No; for Yahawah has qaraa (called) these shalawash (three) malak (king) together to nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of Mawaab (Moab).

Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke), "As Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) chay (life), panayam (before) whom I imad (stand), surely, were it not that I nashaa (lift) the panayam (presence) of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), I would not nabat (look) toward you, nor raah (see) you.
But now laqach (take / seized) me a minstrel." It happened, when the minstrel nagan (played), that the yad (hand) of Yahawah came on him.
He amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘ishah (make) this nachal (stream / river) full of trenches.’

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘You will not raah (see) rawach (spirit / wind), neither will you raah (see) gasham (rain); yet that nachal (stream / river) shall be malaa (filled) with mayam (Waters), and you will shathah (drinks), both you and your livestock and your animals.
This is but a qalal (light) thing in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah. He will also nathan (give) the Mawaab (Moabites) into your yad (hand).

You shall nakah (strike) every fortified iyar (city), and every mabachawar (choice) iyar (city), and shall napal (fall / be cast down) every tawab (pleasant/functional) itz (tree), and satham (stop) all maiyan (springs) of mayam (Waters), and kaab (mar) every tawab (pleasant/functional) chalaqah (piece) of land with aban (stone).’

It happened in the baqar (morning), about the time of ilah (go up / offer) the ilah (go up / offer), that behold, mayam (Waters) bawaa (come) by the darak (way) of Adam (Edom), and the aratz (Earth/land) was malaa (filled) with mayam (Waters).

Mawaab (Now) when all the Moabites shamai (hearken / hear) that the malak (king) had ilah (go up / offer) up to lacham (fight) against them, they tzaiq (gathered) themselves together, all who were chagar (able) to put on armor, and upward, and imad (stood) on the gabawal (border/boundary).

They shakam (rose) up early in the baqar (morning), and the shamash (sun) shone on the mayam (Waters), and the Mawaab (Moabites) raah (see) the mayam (Waters) over nagad (against) them as adam (red) as dam (blood).

They amar (spoke), This is dam (blood). The malak (king) are charab (surely) charab (destroyed), and they have struck ayash (husband/individual man) other. Now therefore, Mawaab (Moab), to the shalal (spoil)!

When they bawaa (come) to the machanah (camp) of Yasharaal (Israel), the Yasharaal (Israelites) qawam (rise up) up and nakah (struck) the Mawaab (Moabites), so that they nawas (fled) panayam (before) them; and they nakah (went) forward into the land nakah (smiting) the Mawaab (Moabites).

They haras (beat) down the iyar (cities); and on every tawab (pleasant/functional) chalaqah (piece) of land they shalak (cast) every ayash (husband/individual man) his aban (stone), and malaa (filled) it; and they satham (stopped) all the maiyan (springs) of mayam (Waters), and felled all the tawab (pleasant/functional) itz (trees), until in Qayaracharash (Kir) Hareseth only they shaar (left) its aban (stone); however the men armed with slings sabab (went) about it, and nakah (struck) it.

When the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab) raah (see) that the malachamah (battle) was too severe for him, he laqach (take / seized) with him shabai (seven) maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man) who shalap (drew) charab (sword), to baqai (break) through to the malak (king) of Adam (Edom); but they yakal (could) not.

Then he laqach (take / seized) his bakawar (eldest) ban (son) who would have malak (king) in his place, and ilah (go up / offer) him for a burnt ilah (offering) on the chawamah (wall). There was gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qatzap (wrath) against Yasharaal (Israel): and they departed from him, and shawab (turn back / repent) to their own aratz (Earth/land).

Now there tzaiq (cried) a achad (one) ashah (wife/individual woman) of the wives of the ban (son) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) to Alayashai (Elisha), amar (spoke), Your ibad (servant) my ayash (husband/individual man) is mawath (death). You yadai (know) that your ibad (servant) yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah. Now the nashah (creditor) bawaa (come) come to laqach (take / seized) for himself my shanayam (two) yalad (birth / begot) to be ibad (servant).

Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke) to her, "What shall I ishah (make) for you? Nagad (tell) me: what yash (do) you have in the bayath (house)?" She amar (spoke), Your handmaid has nothing in the bayath (house), except a asawak (pot) of shaman (oil).
Then he amar (spoke), yalak (go), shaal (borrow) containers from of all your neighbors, even rayaq (empty) containers. Don't mait (borrow) just a few.

You shall bawaa (come) in, and sagar (shut) the dalath (door) on you and on your ban (son), and yatzaq (pour) out into all those containers; and you shall nasai (set) aside that which is malaa (full).
So she yalak (went) from him, and sagar (shut) the dalath (door) on her and on her ban (son); they nagash (brought) the containers to her, and she yatzaq (poured) out.

It happened, when the containers were malaa (full), that she amar (spoke) to her ban (son), "nagash (bring) me kalay (another) container." He amar (spoke) to her, "There isn't kalay (another) container." The shaman (oil) stopped flowing.

Then she bawaa (come) and nagad (told) the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam. He amar (spoke), yalak (go), makar (sell) the shaman (oil), and shalam (pay) your nashay (debt); and you and your ban (son) chayah (live) on the yathar (rest).

It fell on a yawam (day), that Alayashai (Elisha) ibar (pass over/through) to Shawanam (Shunem), where there was a prominent ashah (wife/individual woman); and she persuaded him to akal (eat) lacham (bread). So it was, that as often as he ibar (pass over/through) by, he sawar (turned) in there to akal (eat) lacham (bread).
She amar (spoke) to her ayash (husband/individual man), See now, I yadai (perceive) that this is a qadawash (holy) ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, that passes by us continually.

Please let us ishah (make) a qatan (small/young/least) room on the qayar (wall). Let us shawam (place / establish / appoint) for him there a matah (bed), a shalachan (table), a chair, and a manawarah (lamp) stand. It shall be, when he bawaa (come) to us, that he shall sawar (turn) in there.
One yawam (day) he bawaa (come) there, and he sawar (turned) into the room and shakab (lay) there.
He amar (spoke) to Gayachazay (Gehazi) his nair (servant), "qaraa (called) this Shunammite." When he had qaraa (called) her, she imad (stood) panayam (before) him.

He amar (spoke) to him, "amar (spoke) now to her, ‘Behold, you have cared for us with all this charadah (care). What is to be ishah (make) for you? Would you like to be dabar (word / matter) for to the malak (king), or to the shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop)?’" She amar (spoke), I yashab (inhabit/dwell) thawak (midst) my own im (people / nation).
He amar (spoke), "What then is to be ishah (make) for her?" Gayachazay (Gehazi) amar (spoke), Most certainly she has no ban (son), and her ayash (husband/individual man) is zaqan (old).
He amar (spoke), "qaraa (called) her." When he had qaraa (called) her, she imad (stood) in the pathach (door).

He amar (spoke), "At this mawaid (Feast/Holy Day), when the ith (time) comes around, you will chabaq (embrace) a ban (son)." She amar (spoke), No, my Adawan, you ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, do not kazab (lie) to your handmaid.

The ashah (wife/individual woman) harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son) at that mawaid (Feast/Holy Day), when the ith (time) came around, as Alayashai (Elisha) had dabar (word / matter) to her.
When the yalad (birth / begot) was gadal (grown), it happened one yawam (day) that he yatzaa (go out / come out) out to his ab (father) to the qatzar (reapers).
He amar (spoke) to his ab (father), "My raash (head)! My raash (head)!" He amar (spoke) to his nair (servant), nashaa (lift) him to his am (mother).
When he had nashaa (lift) him, and bawaa (come) him to his am (mother), he yashab (inhabit/dwell) on her barak (knees) until tzahar (noon), and then mawath (death).
She ilah (go up / offer) up and shakab (laid) him on the matah (bed) of the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, and sagar (shut) the door on him, and yatzaa (go out / come out) out.

She qaraa (called) to her ayash (husband/individual man), and amar (spoke), Please shalach (send) me achad (one) of the nair (servants), and achad (one) of the donkeys, that I may rawatz (run) to the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, and shawab (turn back / repent) again.
He amar (spoke), "Why would you want halak (move) to him today? It is neither new chadash (month) nor shabath (shabath/rest)." She amar (spoke), It's alright.
Then she chabash (saddled) a donkey, and amar (spoke) to her nair (servant), nahag (drive), and yalak (go) forward! Don't slow down for me, unless I ask you to.

So she yalak (went), and bawaa (come) to the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam to har (mountain) Karamal (Carmel). It happened, when the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam raah (see) her afar off, that he amar (spoke) to Gayachazay (Gehazi) his nair (servant), "Behold, there is the Shunammite.

Please rawatz (run) now to qaraah (meet) her, and ask her, ‘Is it shalawam (peace / safety) with you? Is it shalawam (peace / safety) with your ayash (husband/individual man)? Is it shalawam (peace / safety) with the yalad (birth / begot)?’" She amar (spoke), It is shalawam (peace / safety).

When she bawaa (come) to the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam to the har (mountain), she chazaq (caught) hold of his ragal (feet / foot). Gayachazay (Gehazi) nagash (came) near to hadap (thrust) her away; but the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam amar (spoke), Leave her rapah (alone); for her napash (living being/soul) is troubled within her; and Yahawah has ilam (hidden) it from me, and has not nagad (told) me.
Then she amar (spoke), Did I shaal (desire) a ban (son) of my Adawan? Didn't I amar (spoke), Do not shalah (deceive) me?

Then he amar (spoke) to Gayachazay (Gehazi), Tuck your cloak into your belt, laqach (take / seized) my mashainah (staff) in your yad (hand), and go your yalak (way). If you matzaa (meet) any ayash (husband/individual man), don't greet him; and if anyone greets you, don't inah (answer / respond) him again. Then shawam (place / establish / appoint) my mashainah (staff) on the panayam (face) of the nair (child).

The am (mother) of the nair (child) amar (spoke), "As Yahawah chay (life), and as your napash (living being/soul) chay (life), I will not izab (leave) you." He qawam (rise up), and yalak (followed) her.

Gayachazay (Gehazi) ibar (pass over/through) on panayam (before) them, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the mashainah (staff) on the panayam (face) of the nair (child); but there was neither qawal (sound / voice), nor qashab (hearing). Therefore he shawab (turn back / repent) to qaraah (meet) him, and nagad (told) him, amar (spoke), The nair (child) has not awakened.
When Alayashai (Elisha) bawaa (come) come into the bayath (house), behold, the nair (child) was mawath (death), and shakab (laid) on his matah (bed).
He bawaa (come) in therefore, and sagar (shut) the dalath (door) on them shanayam (two), and palal (prayed) to Yahawah.

He ilah (go up / offer) up, and shakab (lay) on the yalad (birth / begot), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) his pah (mouth) on his pah (mouth), and his iyan (eye) on his iyan (eye), and his kap (hands) on his kap (hands). He gahar (stretched) himself on him; and the bashar (flesh) of the yalad (birth / begot) grew chamam (warm).

Then he shawab (turn back / repent), and yalak (walked) in the bayath (house) achad (one) back and forth; and ilah (go up / offer) up, and gahar (stretched) himself on him. Then the nair (child) zarar (sneezed) shabai (seven) paim (times), and the nair (child) paqach (opened) his iyan (eye).

He qaraa (called) Gayachazay (Gehazi), and amar (spoke), "qaraa (called) this Shunammite!" So he qaraa (called) her. When she bawaa (come) come in to him, he amar (spoke), nashaa (lift) up your ban (son).

Then she bawaa (come) in, and napal (fall / be cast down) at his ragal (feet / foot), and shachah (bowed) herself to the aratz (Earth/land); and she nashaa (lift) up her ban (son), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out.

Alayashai (Elisha) shawab (turn back / repent) again to Galagal (Gilgal). There was a raib (famine) in the aratz (Earth/land); and the ban (son) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) were sitting panayam (before) him; and he amar (spoke) to his nair (servant), shapath (set) on the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) sayar (pot), and bashal (boil) stew for the ban (son) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy).

Achad (one) yatzaa (go out / come out) out into the shadah (field) to laqat (gather) awarah (herbs), and matzaa (found) a shadah (wild) gapan (vine), and laqat (gathered) of it shadah (wild) paqaih (gourds) his bagad (lap) malaa (full), and bawaa (come) and palach (shred) them into the sayar (pot) of stew; for they didn't recognize them.

So they yatzaq (poured) out for the ayash (husband/individual man) to akal (eat). It happened, as they were akal (eat) of the stew, that they tzaiq (cried) out, and amar (spoke), "ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, there is mawath (death) in the sayar (pot)!" They yakal (could) not akal (eat) of it.

But he amar (spoke), "Then laqach (take / seized) qamach (meal)." He shalak (cast) it into the sayar (pot); and he amar (spoke), "yatzaq (pour) out for the im (people / nation), that they may akal (eat)." There was no dabar (word / matter) in the sayar (pot).

A ayash (husband/individual man) from Baal Shalishah bawaa (come), and bawaa (come) the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam lacham (bread) of the bakawar (first) bakawar (fruits), isharayam (twenty) loaves of shairah (barley), and fresh karamal (ears) of grain in his sack. He amar (spoke), nathan (give) to the im (people / nation), that they may akal (eat).

His sharath (servant) amar (spoke), "What, should I nathan (give) this panayam (before) a maah (hundred) ayash (husband/individual man)?" But he amar (spoke), nathan (give) the im (people / nation), that they may akal (eat); for thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘They will akal (eat), and will have some yathar (left) over.’
So he nathan (give) it panayam (before) them, and they akal (eat), and yathar (left) some of it, according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah.

Now Naiman (Naaman), shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop) of the malak (king) of Aram (Syria), was a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) ayash (husband/individual man) with his adawan (master / lord), and nashaa (lift), because by him Yahawah nathan (give) given thashawaih (deliverance) to Aram (Syria): he was also a gabawar (mighty) ayash (husband/individual man) of valor, but he was a tzarai (leper).

The Aram (Syrians) yatzaa (go out / come out) gone out in gadawad (bands), and had shabah (brought) away captive out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Yasharaal (Israel) a qatan (small/young/least) nairah (maiden); and she waited on Naiman (Naaman's) ashah (wife/individual woman).
She amar (spoke) to her gabarath (mistress), I wish that my Adawan were with the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) who is in Shamarawan (Samaria)! Then he would heal him of his tzaraith (leprosy).
Someone bawaa (come) in, and nagad (told) his Adawan, amar (spoke), The nairah (maiden) who is from the aratz (Earth/land) of Yasharaal (Israel) dabar (word / matter) this.

The malak (king) of Aram (Syria) amar (spoke), "bawaa (come) now, and I will shalach (send) a sapar (book / scribed document) to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel)." He departed, and laqach (take / seized) with him ishar (ten) kakar (talents) of kasap (silver), and shash (six) alap (thousand) pieces of zahab (gold), and ishar (ten) chalayapah (changes) of bagad (clothing).

He bawaa (come) the sapar (book / scribed document) to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), Now when this sapar (book / scribed document) bawaa (come) come to you, behold, I have shalach (send) Naiman (Naaman) my ibad (servant) to you, that you may heal him of his tzaraith (leprosy).

It happened, when the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) had qaraa (called) the sapar (book / scribed document), that he qarai (tore) his clothes, and amar (spoke), Am I Alahayam, to mawath (death) and to chayah (make) alive, that this zah (this/that/these) shalach (send) to me to heal a ayash (husband/individual man) of his tzaraith (leprosy)? But please yadai (consider) and raah (see) how he anah (seeks) a quarrel against me.

It was so, when Alayashai (Elisha) the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam shamai (hearken / hear) that the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) had qarai (torn) his clothes, that he shalach (send) to the malak (king), amar (spoke), Why have you qarai (torn) your clothes? Bawaa (come) him come now to me, and he shall yadai (know) that there is a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) in Yasharaal (Israel).
So Naiman (Naaman) bawaa (come) with his sawas (horses) and with his rakab (chariots), and imad (stood) at the pathach (door) of the bayath (house) of Alayashai (Elisha).

Alayashai (Elisha) shalach (send) a malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to him, amar (spoke), halak (move) and rachatz (wash) in the Yaradan (Jordan) shabai (seven) paim (times), and your bashar (flesh) shall shawab (turn back / repent) again to you, and you shall be tahar (clean).

But Naiman (Naaman) was qatzap (angry), and yalak (went) away, and amar (spoke), "Behold, I amar (spoke), ‘He will yatzaa (go out / come out) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to me, and imad (stand), and qaraa (called) on the sham (name) of Yahawah his Alahayam, and nawap (wave) his yad (hand) over the maqawam (place), and heal the tzarai (leper).’

Abanah (Aren't) Abanah and Parapar (Pharpar), the nahar (rivers) of Damashaq (Damascus), tawab (pleasant/functional) than all the mayam (Waters) of Yasharaal (Israel)? Couldn't I rachatz (wash) in them, and be tahar (clean)?" So he panah (turned) and yalak (went) away in a chamah (rage).

His ibad (servant) nagash (came) near, and dabar (word / matter) to him, and amar (spoke), My ab (father), if the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) had asked you do some gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thing, wouldn't you ishah (make) done it? Ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) much rather then, when he amar (spoke) to you, ‘rachatz (wash), and be tahar (clean)?’

Then yarad (went) he down, and tabal (dipped) himself shabai (seven) paim (times) in the Yaradan (Jordan), according to the dabar (word / matter) of the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam; and his bashar (flesh) was shawab (turn back / repent) like the bashar (flesh) of a qatan (small/young/least) nair (child), and he was tahar (clean).

He shawab (turn back / repent) to the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, he and all his machanah (company), and bawaa (come), and imad (stood) panayam (before) him; and he amar (spoke), See now, I yadai (know) that there is no Alahayam in all the aratz (Earth/land), but in Yasharaal (Israel). Now therefore, please laqach (take / seized) a barakah (gift) from your ibad (servant).
But he amar (spoke), "As Yahawah chay (life), panayam (before) whom I imad (stand), I will laqach (take / seized) none." He patzar (urged) him to laqach (take / seized) it; but he maan (refused).

Naiman (Naaman) amar (spoke), If not, then, please let tzamad (two) parad (mules)' mashaa (burden) of adamah (earth) be nathan (give) to your ibad (servant); for your ibad (servant) will from now on ishah (make) neither burnt ilah (offering) nor zabach (sacrifice) to other Alahayam, but to Yahawah.

In this thing may Yahawah salach (forgive/pardon/make clean) your ibad (servant): when my adawan (master / lord) bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of Ramawan (Rimmon) to shachah (worship) there, and he shain (leans) on my yad (hand), and I shachah (bow) myself in the bayath (house) of Ramawan (Rimmon). When I shachah (bow) myself in the bayath (house) of Ramawan (Rimmon), may Yahawah salach (forgive/pardon/make clean) your ibad (servant) in this thing.
He amar (spoke) to him, "yalak (go) in shalawam (peace / safety)." So he departed from him a kabarah (little) aratz (Earth/land).

But Gayachazay (Gehazi) the nair (servant) of Alayashai (Elisha) the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, amar (spoke), Behold, my adawan (master / lord) has chashak (darkness) this Naiman (Naaman) the Aramay (Syrian), in not laqach (take / seized) at his yad (hand) that which he bawaa (come). As Yahawah chay (life), I will rawatz (run) achar (other) him, and laqach (take / seized) something from him.

So Gayachazay (Gehazi) radap (followed) achar (other) Naiman (Naaman). When Naiman (Naaman) raah (see) rawatz (one) running achar (other) him, he came down from the marakabah (chariot) to qaraah (meet) him, and amar (spoke), Is shalawam (peace / safety) well?

He amar (spoke), shalawam (peace / safety) is well. My adawan (master / lord) has shalach (send) me, amar (spoke), ‘Behold, even now shanayam (two) nair (young) men of the ban (son) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) bawaa (come) come to me from the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim). Please nathan (give) them a kakar (talent) of kasap (silver) and shanayam (two) chalayapah (changes) of bagad (clothing).’

Naiman (Naaman) amar (spoke), "Be yaal (pleased) to laqach (take / seized) two kakar (talents)." He paratz (urged) him, and tzarar (bound) shanayam (two) kakar (talents) of kasap (silver) in shanayam (two) charayat (bags), with shanayam (two) chalayapah (changes) of bagad (clothing), and nathan (give) them on shanayam (two) of his nair (servants); and they nashaa (lift) them panayam (before) him.

When he bawaa (come) to the hill, he laqach (take / seized) them from their yad (hand), and stored them in the bayath (house). Then he let the ayash (husband/individual man) shalach (send), and they departed.

But he bawaa (come) in, and imad (stood) before his adawan (master / lord). Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke) to him, "an (where) did you come from, Gayachazay (Gehazi)?" He amar (spoke), Your ibad (servant) halak (move) nowhere.

He amar (spoke) to him, "Didn't my lab (heart) halak (move) with you, when the ayash (husband/individual man) hapak (turned) from his marakabah (chariot) to qaraah (meet) you? Is it a ith (time) to laqach (take / seized) kasap (money), and to laqach (take / seized) bagad (garments), and zayath (olive) groves and karam (vineyards), and tzaan (sheep) and cattle, and male ibad (servant) and female shapachah (servants)?

Therefore the tzaraith (leprosy) of Naiman (Naaman) will cling to you and to your zarai (seed) iwalam (forever)." He yatzaa (go out / come out) out from his panayam (presence) a tzarai (leper), as white as shalag (snow).

The ban (son) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) amar (spoke) to Alayashai (Elisha), "See now, the maqawam (place) where we yashab (inhabit/dwell) before you is too tzar (oppressor / distressor) for us.

Please yalak (let) us go to the Yaradan (Jordan), and every ayash (husband/individual man) laqach (take / seized) a qawarah (beam) from there, and let us ishah (make) us a maqawam (place) there, where we may yashab (inhabit/dwell)." He amar (spoke), yalak (go)!
Achad (one) amar (spoke), "yaal (please) be pleased to yalak (go) with your ibad (servant)." He amar (spoke), I will yalak (go).
So he yalak (went) with them. When they bawaa (come) to the Yaradan (Jordan), they gazar (cut) down itz (wood).

But as achad (one) was napal (fall / be cast down) a qawarah (beam), the axe barazal (head) napal (fall / be cast down) into the mayam (Waters). Then he tzaiq (cried), and amar (spoke), ahah (alas), my adawan (master / lord)! For it was shaal (borrowed).

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam asked, "an (where) did it napal (fall / be cast down)?" He showed him the maqawam (place). He qatzab (cut) down a itz (stick), shalak (threw) it in there, and made the barazal (iron) float.
He amar (spoke), "rawam (will lift up) it." So he shalach (send) out his yad (hand) and laqach (take / seized) it.

Now the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) was lacham (warring) against Yasharaal (Israel); and he took yaitz (counsel) with his ibad (servant), amar (spoke), My thachanah (camp) will be in such and such a maqawam (place).

The ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam shalach (send) to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), Beware that you not ibar (pass over/through) such a maqawam (place); for the Aram (Syrians) are nachath (coming) down there.

The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) shalach (send) to the maqawam (place) which the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam amar (spoke) him and zahar (warn) him of; and he shamar (keep/guard) himself there, not achad (one) nor shanayam (two).

The lab (heart) of the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) was very sair (troubled) about this. He qaraa (called) his ibad (servant), and amar (spoke) to them, Won't you show me which of us is for the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel)?

Achad (one) of his ibad (servant) amar (spoke), No, my Adawan, O malak (king); but Alayashai (Elisha), the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) who is in Yasharaal (Israel), nagad (tells) the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) the dabar (word / matter) that you dabar (word / matter) in your bedroom.
He amar (spoke), "yalak (go) and raah (see) ayakah (where) he is, that I may shalach (send) and laqach (take / seized) him." It was nagad (told) him, amar (spoke), Behold, he is in Dathan (Dothan).

Therefore he shalach (send) sawas (horses), rakab (chariots), and a kabad (great) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) there. They bawaa (come) by layal (night), and surrounded the iyar (city).

When the sharath (servant) of the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam had qawam (rise up) shakam (early), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out, behold, an chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) with sawas (horses) and rakab (chariots) was around the iyar (city). His nair (servant) amar (spoke) to him, ahah (alas), my adawan (master / lord)! What shall we ishah (make)?
He amar (spoke), Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid); for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.

Alayashai (Elisha) palal (prayed), and amar (spoke), "Yahawah, please paqach (open) his iyan (eye), that he may raah (see)." Yahawah paqach (opened) the iyan (eye) of the nair (young) man; and he raah (see): and behold, the har (mountain) was malaa (full) of sawas (horses) and rakab (chariots) of ash (fire) around Alayashai (Elisha).

When they yarad (came) down to him, Alayashai (Elisha) palal (prayed) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "Please nakah (strike) this gaway (nation / people) with sanawar (blindness)." He nakah (struck) them with sanawar (blindness) according to the dabar (word / matter) of Alayashai (Elisha).

Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke) to them, "This is not the darak (way), neither is zah (this/that/these) the iyar (city). Yalak (follow) me, and I will yalak (bring) you to the ayash (husband/individual man) whom you baqash (seek)." He yalak (led) them to Shamarawan (Samaria).

It happened, when they bawaa (come) come into Shamarawan (Samaria), that Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke), "Yahawah, paqach (open) the iyan (eye) of these men, that they may raah (see)." Yahawah paqach (opened) their iyan (eye), and they raah (see); and behold, they were in the thawak (midst) of Shamarawan (Samaria).
The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke) to Alayashai (Elisha), when he raah (see) them, My ab (father), shall I nakah (strike) them? Shall I nakah (strike) them?

He amar (spoke), You shall not nakah (strike) them. Would you nakah (strike) those whom you have shabah (taken) captive with your charab (sword) and with your qashath (bow)? Shawam (place / establish / appoint) lacham (bread) and mayam (Waters) panayam (before) them, that they may akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and yalak (go) to their adawan (master / lord).

He karah (prepared) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) feast for them. When they had akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), he shalach (send) them away, and they yalak (went) to their adawan (master / lord). The gadawad (bands) of Aram (Syria) stopped raiding the aratz (Earth/land) of Yasharaal (Israel).

It happened achar (other) this, that Banahadad (Benhadad) malak (king) of Aram (Syria) qabatz (gathered) all his machanah (army), and ilah (go up / offer) up and tzawar (besieged) Shamarawan (Samaria).

There was a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) raib (famine) in Shamarawan (Samaria). Behold, they tzawar (besieged) it, until a donkey's raash (head) was sold for shamanayam (eighty) pieces of kasap (silver), and the rabai (fourth) part of a kab of yawanah (dove's) dung for chamash (five) pieces of kasap (silver).

As the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) was ibar (pass over/through) by on the chawamah (wall), a ashah (wife/individual woman) tzaiq (cried) to him, amar (spoke), yashai (salvation), my Adawan, O malak (king)!
He amar (spoke), If Yahawah doesn't yashai (salvation) you, from ayan (where) could I yashai (salvation) you? From of the garan (threshing) floor, or from the yaqab (winepress)?

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to her, "What ails you?" She amar (spoke), This ashah (wife/individual woman) amar (spoke) to me, ‘nathan (give) your ban (son), that we may akal (eat) him today, and we will akal (eat) my ban (son) machar (tomorrow).’

So we bashal (boiled) my ban (son), and akal (eat) him: and I amar (spoke) to her on the achar (other) yawam (day), ‘nathan (give) your ban (son), that we may akal (eat) him;’ and she has chabaa (hidden) her ban (son).

It happened, when the malak (king) shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of the ashah (wife/individual woman), that he qarai (tore) his clothes (now he was ibar (pass over/through) by on the chawamah (wall)); and the im (people / nation) raah (see), and behold, he had sackcloth underneath on his bashar (flesh).
Then he amar (spoke), Alahayam ishah (make) so to me, and more also, if the raash (head) of Alayashai (Elisha) the ban (son) of Shapat (Shaphat) shall imad (stay) on him this yawam (day).

But Alayashai (Elisha) was sitting in his bayath (house), and the zaqan (elders) were sitting with him. Then the king shalach (send) a ayash (husband/individual man) from panayam (before) him; but before the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) bawaa (come) to him, he amar (spoke) to the zaqan (elders), Do you raah (see) how this ban (son) of a ratzach (murderer) has shalach (send) to sawar (take) away my raash (head)? Raah (see), when the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) bawaa (come), sagar (shut) the dalath (door), and hold the dalath (door) shut against him. Isn't the qawal (sound / voice) of his adawan (master / lord) ragal (feet / foot) achar (other) him?

While he was still dabar (word / matter) with them, behold, the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) yarad (came) down to him. Then he amar (spoke), Behold, this rai (evil) is from Yahawah. Why should I yachal (wait) for Yahawah any longer?

Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah. Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘machar (tomorrow) about this ith (time) a saah (measure) of fine salath (flour) will be sold for a shaqal (shekel), and two saah (measures) of shairah (barley) for a shaqal (shekel), in the shair (gate) of Shamarawan (Samaria).’

Then the shalayash (captain) on whose yad (hand) the malak (king) shain (leaned) inah (answer / respond) the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, and amar (spoke), "Behold, if Yahawah ishah (make) arabah (windows) in shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), could this thing be?" He amar (spoke), raah (see), you shall see it with your iyan (eye), but shall not akal (eat) of it.

Now there were arabai (four) tzarai (leprous) ayash (husband/individual man) at the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate). They amar (spoke) ayash (husband/individual man) to rai (neigbor/another person), Why do we yashab (inhabit/dwell) here until we mawath (death)?

If we amar (spoke), ‘We will bawaa (come) into the iyar (city),’ then the raib (famine) is in the iyar (city), and we shall mawath (death) there. If we yashab (inhabit/dwell) still here, we also mawath (death). Now therefore yalak (come), and napal (fall / be cast down) us surrender to the machanah (army) of the Aram (Syrians). If they chayah (save) us alive, we will chayah (live); and if they mawath (death) us, we will only mawath (death).

They qawam (rise up) up in the nashap (twilight), to bawaa (come) to the machanah (camp) of the Aram (Syrians). When they bawaa (come) come to the outermost part of the machanah (camp) of the Aram (Syrians), behold, there was no ayash (husband/individual man) there.

For the Adanay had made the machanah (army) of the Aram (Syrians) to shamai (hearken / hear) a qawal (sound / voice) of rakab (chariots), and a qawal (sound / voice) of sawas (horses), even the qawal (sound / voice) of a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor): and they amar (spoke) ayash (husband/individual man) to ach (brother/kinsman), Behold, the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) has shakar (hired) against us the malak (king) of the Chathay (Hittites), and the malak (king) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians), to bawaa (come) on us.

Therefore they qawam (rise up) and nawas (fled) in the nashap (twilight), and izab (left) their ahal (tents), and their sawas (horses), and their donkeys, even the machanah (camp) as it was, and nawas (fled) for their napash (living being/soul).

When these tzarai (lepers) bawaa (come) to the outermost part of the machanah (camp), they bawaa (come) into achad (one) ahal (tent), and akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and nashaa (lift) there kasap (silver), and zahab (gold), and bagad (clothing), and yalak (went) and taman (hid) it. Then they shawab (turn back / repent) back, and bawaa (come) into achar (other) ahal (tent), and nashaa (lift) there also, and yalak (went) and taman (hid) it.

Then they amar (spoke) ayash (husband/individual man) to rai (neigbor/another person), We aren't ishah (make) right. This yawam (day) is a yawam (day) of bashawarah (good) news, and we chashah (keep) silent. If we chakah (wait) until the baqar (morning) awar (light), iwan (guilt/iniquity) will overtake us. Now therefore matzaa (come), yalak (let) us go and nagad (tell) the malak (king) bayath (house).

So they bawaa (come) and qaraa (called) to the shawair (porter) of the iyar (city); and they nagad (told) them, amar (spoke), We bawaa (come) to the machanah (camp) of the Aram (Syrians), and, behold, there was no ayash (husband/individual man) there, neither qawal (sound / voice) of adam (man), but the sawas (horses) asar (tied), and the donkeys asar (tied), and the ahal (tents) as they were.
He qaraa (called) the shawair (porters); and they nagad (told) it to the malak (king) bayath (house) panayamah (within).

The malak (king) qawam (rise up) in the layal (night), and amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), I will now show you what the Aram (Syrians) ishah (make) done to us. They yadai (know) that we are raib (hungry). Therefore are they yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the machanah (camp) to chabah (hide) themselves in the shadah (field), amar (spoke), ‘When they yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the iyar (city), we shall thapash (take) them chay (life), and bawaa (come) into the iyar (city).’

Achad (one) of his ibad (servant) inah (answer / respond), Please let some laqach (take / seized) chamash (five) of the sawas (horses) that shaar (remain), which are shaar (left) in the city. Behold, they are like all the hamawan (multitude) of Yasharaal (Israel) who are shaar (left) in it. Behold, they are like all the hamawan (multitude) of Yasharaal (Israel) who are thamam (consumed). Shalach (send) us send and raah (see).

They laqach (take / seized) therefore shanayam (two) rakab (chariots) with sawas (horses); and the malak (king) shalach (send) achar (other) the machanah (army) of the Aram (Syrians), amar (spoke), yalak (go) and raah (see).

They yalak (went) achar (other) them to the Yaradan (Jordan); and behold, all the darak (way) malaa (was) full of bagad (garments) and kalay (vessels), which the Aram (Syrians) had shalak (cast) away in their chapaz (haste). The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) shawab (turn back / repent), and nagad (told) the malak (king).

The im (people / nation) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and plundered the machanah (camp) of the Aram (Syrians). So a saah (measure) of fine salath (flour) was sold for a shaqal (shekel), and two saah (measures) of shairah (barley) for a shaqal (shekel), according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah.

The malak (king) paqad (visit) the shalayash (captain) on whose yad (hand) he shain (leaned) to be in charge of the shair (gate): and the im (people / nation) ramas (trod) on him in the shair (gate), and he mawath (death) as the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam had dabar (word / matter), who dabar (word / matter) when the malak (king) yarad (came) down to him.

It happened, as the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam had dabar (word / matter) to the malak (king), amar (spoke), Two saah (measures) of shairah (barley) for a shaqal (shekel), and a saah (measure) of fine salath (flour) for a shaqal (shekel), shall be machar (tomorrow) about this ith (time) in the shair (gate) of Shamarawan (Samaria);

And that shalayash (captain) inah (answer / respond) the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, and amar (spoke), "Now, behold, if Yahawah should ishah (make) arabah (windows) in shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), might such a thing be?" And he amar (spoke), raah (see), you shall see it with your iyan (eye), but shall not akal (eat) of it.
It happened like that to him; for the im (people / nation) ramas (trod) on him in the shair (gate), and he mawath (death).

Now Alayashai (Elisha) had dabar (word / matter) to the ashah (wife/individual woman), whose ban (son) he had restored to chayah (life), amar (spoke), qawam (rise up), and yalak (go), you and your bayath (house), and stay for a while wherever you can; for Yahawah has qaraa (called) for a raib (famine). It shall also bawaa (come) on the aratz (Earth/land) shabai (seven) shanah (years).

The ashah (wife/individual woman) qawam (rise up), and ishah (make) according to the dabar (word / matter) of the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam. She yalak (went) with her bayath (house), and lived in the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines) shabai (seven) shanah (years).

It happened at the shabai (seven) shanah (years)' qatzah (end / extremity / border), that the ashah (wife/individual woman) shawab (turn back / repent) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines). Then she yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to tzaiq (cry) to the malak (king) for her bayath (house) and for her shadah (land).

Now the malak (king) was dabar (word / matter) with Gayachazay (Gehazi) the nair (servant) of the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, amar (spoke), Please sapar (book) me all the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) things that Alayashai (Elisha) ishah (make) done.

It happened, as he was sapar (book) the malak (king) how he had chayah (restored) to chayah (life) him who was mawath (death), that behold, the ashah (wife/individual woman), whose ban (son) he had restored to chayah (life), tzaiq (cried) to the malak (king) for her bayath (house) and for her shadah (land). Gayachazay (Gehazi) amar (spoke), My Adawan, O malak (king), this is the ashah (wife/individual woman), and this is her ban (son), whom Alayashai (Elisha) restored to chayah (life).

When the malak (king) shaal (asked) the ashah (wife/individual woman), she sapar (book) him. So the malak (king) nathan (give) to her a achad (one) sarayas (officer), amar (spoke), shawab (turn back / repent) all that was hers, and all the thabawaah (fruits) of the shadah (field) since the yawam (day) that she izab (left) the aratz (Earth/land), even until now.

Alayashai (Elisha) bawaa (come) to Damashaq (Damascus); and Banahadad (Benhadad) the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) was chalah (afflict). It was nagad (told) him, amar (spoke), The ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam bawaa (come) come here.

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Chazaal (Hazael), laqach (take / seized) a manachah (present) in your yad (hand), and yalak (go), qaraah (meet) the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam, and darash (inquire) of Yahawah by him, amar (spoke), ‘Will I chayah (recover) from this chalay (sickness)?’

So Chazaal (Hazael) yalak (went) to qaraah (meet) him, and laqach (take / seized) a manachah (present) with him, even of every tawab (pleasant/functional) thing of Damashaq (Damascus), arabaiyam (forty) gamal (camels)' mashaa (burden), and bawaa (come) and imad (stood) panayam (before) him, and amar (spoke), Your ban (son) Banahadad (Benhadad) malak (king) of Aram (Syria) has shalach (send) me to you, amar (spoke), ‘Will I chayah (recover) from this chalay (sickness)?’
Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke) to him, yalak (go), amar (spoke) him, ‘You shall chayah (surely) chayah (recover);’ however Yahawah raah (see) shown me that he shall mawath (death) mawath (death).
He settled his gaze steadfastly on him, until he was bawash (ashamed). Then the ayash (husband/individual man) of Alahayam bakah (wept).

Chazaal (Hazael) amar (spoke), "Why do you bakah (weep), my Adawan?" He amar (spoke), Because I yadai (know) the rai (evil) that you will ishah (make) to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel). You will shalach (send) their strongholds on ash (fire), and you will harag (kill) their bachawar (young) men with the charab (sword), and will ratash (dash) in pieces their iwalal (little) ones, and baqai (rip) up their harah (women) with child.

Chazaal (Hazael) amar (spoke), "But what is your ibad (servant), who is but a kalab (dog), that he should ishah (make) this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thing?" Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke), Yahawah raah (see) shown me that you will be malak (king) over Aram (Syria).

Then he departed from Alayashai (Elisha), and bawaa (come) to his adawan (master / lord), who amar (spoke) to him, "What did Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke) to you?" He amar (spoke), He amar (spoke) me that you would chayah (surely) chayah (recover).

It happened on the next macharath (day), that he laqach (take / seized) a makabar (thick) cloth, tabal (dipped) it in mayam (Waters), and parash (spread) it on his panayam (face), so that he mawath (death). Then Chazaal (Hazael) malak (king) in his place.

In the chamash (fifth) shanah (year) of Yawaram (Joram) the ban (son) of Achaab (Ahab) malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) being malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) then, Yahawaram (Jehoram) the ban (son) of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) began to malak (king).
He was shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) shanah (years) ban (son) when he began to malak (king). He malak (king) shamanah (eight) shanah (years) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

He yalak (walked) in the darak (way) of the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), as ishah (make) the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab); for he had the bath (daughter) of Achaab (Ahab) as ashah (wife/individual woman). He ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah.
However Yahawah would not shachath (destroy) Yahawadah (Judah), for Dawad (David) his ibad (servant) sake, as he amar (spoke) him to nathan (give) to him a nayar (lamp) for his ban (son) yawam (day).
In his yawam (day) Adam (Edom) pashai (revolted) from under the yad (hand) of Yahawadah (Judah), and malak (king) a malak (king) over themselves.

Then Yawaram (Joram) ibar (pass over/through) over to Tzaiyar (Zair), and all his rakab (chariots) with him: and he qawam (rise up) up by layal (night), and nakah (struck) the Adam (Edomites) who surrounded him, and the shar (prince / ruler) of the rakab (chariots); and the im (people / nation) nawas (fled) to their ahal (tents).
So Adam (Edom) pashai (revolted) from under the yad (hand) of Yahawadah (Judah) to this yawam (day). Then Labanah (Libnah) pashai (revolted) at the same ith (time).

The yathar (rest) of the dabar (word / matter) of Yawaram (Joram), and all that he ishah (make), aren't they kathab (written) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabar (word / matter) of the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah)?
Yawaram (Joram) shakab (slept) with his ab (father), and was qabar (bury) with his ab (father) in the iyar (city) of Dawad (David); and Achazayah (Ahaziah) his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.

In the twelfth shanah (year) of Yawaram (Joram) the ban (son) of Achaab (Ahab) malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), Achazayah (Ahaziah) the ban (son) of Yahawaram (Jehoram) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) began to malak (king).

Isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) shanah (years) ban (son) was Achazayah (Ahaziah) when he began to malak (king); and he malak (king) achad (one) shanah (year) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem). His am (mother) sham (name) was Ithalayah (Athaliah) the bath (daughter) of Imaray (Omri) malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).

He yalak (walked) in the darak (way) of the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab), and ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, as did the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab); for he was the son-in-law of the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab).

He yalak (went) with Yawaram (Joram) the ban (son) of Achaab (Ahab) to malachamah (war) against Chazaal (Hazael) malak (king) of Aram (Syria) at Ramathagalaid (Ramoth) Gilead: and the Aramay (Syrians) wounded Yawaram (Joram).

Malak (king) Yawaram (Joram) shawab (turn back / repent) to be rapaa (healed) in Yazaraial (Jezreel) of the makah (wounds) which the Aramay (Syrians) had nakah (given) him at Ramah (Ramah), when he lacham (fought) against Chazaal (Hazael) malak (king) of Aram (Syria). Achazayah (Ahaziah) the ban (son) of Yahawaram (Jehoram) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) yarad (went) down to raah (see) Yawaram (Joram) the ban (son) of Achaab (Ahab) in Yazaraial (Jezreel), because he was chalah (afflict).

Alayashai (Elisha) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) qaraa (called) achad (one) of the ban (son) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and amar (spoke) to him, chagar (put) your belt on your waist, laqach (take / seized) this pak (vial) of shaman (oil) in your yad (hand), and yalak (go) to Ramathagalaid (Ramoth) Gilead.

When you bawaa (come) there, find Yahawaa (Jehu) the ban (son) of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the ban (son) of Namashay (Nimshi), and bawaa (come) in, and make him qawam (rise up) up from thawak (midst) his ach (brother/kinsman), and bawaa (come) him to an chadar (inner) room.

Then laqach (take / seized) the pak (vial) of shaman (oil), and yatzaq (pour) it on his raash (head), and amar (spoke), ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "I have mashach (anointed) you malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel)."’ Then pathach (open) the dalath (door), nawas (flee), and don't chakah (wait).
So the nair (young) man, even the nair (young) man the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), yalak (went) to Ramathagalaid (Ramoth) Gilead.

When he bawaa (come), behold, the shar (prince / ruler) of the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) were sitting. Then he amar (spoke), "I have a dabar (word / matter) for you, shar (prince / ruler)." Yahawaa (Jehu) amar (spoke), "To which of us all?" He amar (spoke), To you, O shar (prince / ruler).

He qawam (rise up), and bawaa (come) into the bayath (house). Then he yatzaq (poured) the shaman (oil) on his raash (head), and amar (spoke) to him, “Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘I have mashach (anointed) you malak (king) over the im (people / nation) of Yahawah, even over Yasharaal (Israel).

You shall nakah (strike) the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab) your adawan (master / lord), that I may naqam (avenge) the dam (blood) of my ibad (servant) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and the dam (blood) of all the ibad (servant) of Yahawah, at the yad (hand) of Ayazabal (Jezebel).

For the whole bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab) shall abad (destroy/perish). I will karath (cut) off from Achaab (Ahab) everyone who urinates against a qayar (wall), both him who is itzar (shut) up and him who is izab (left) at large in Yasharaal (Israel).

I will nathan (give) the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab) like the bayath (house) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Nabat (Nebat), and like the bayath (house) of Baishaa (Baasha) the ban (son) of Achayah (Ahijah).

The kalab (dogs) will akal (eat) Ayazabal (Jezebel) on the plot of ground of Yazaraial (Jezreel), and there shall be none to qabar (bury) her.’” He pathach (opened) the dalath (door), and nawas (fled).

Then Yahawaa (Jehu) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to the ibad (servant) of his Adawan: and one amar (spoke) to him, "Is shalawam (peace / safety) well? Why did this shagai (mad) fellow bawaa (come) to you?" He amar (spoke) to them, You yadai (know) the ayash (husband/individual man) and what his shayach (talk) was.

They amar (spoke), "That is a shaqar (lie). Nagad (tell) us now." He amar (spoke), He amar (spoke) to me, ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, I have mashach (anointed) you malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel).’

Then they hurried, and laqach (take / seized) every ayash (husband/individual man) his bagad (garment), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it under him on the garam (top) of the mailah (ascent/climbing up), and thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), amar (spoke), Yahawaa (Jehu) is malak (king).

So Yahawaa (Jehu) the ban (son) of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the ban (son) of Namashay (Nimshi) qashar (conspired) against Yawaram (Joram). (Now Yawaram (Joram) was shamar (keep/guard) Ramathagalaid (Ramoth) Gilead, he and all Yasharaal (Israel), panayam (because) of Chazaal (Hazael) malak (king) of Aram (Syria);

But malak (king) Yahawaram (Joram) was shawab (turn back / repent) to be rapaa (healed) in Yazaraial (Jezreel) of the makah (wounds) which the Aramay (Syrians) had nakah (given) him, when he lacham (fought) with Chazaal (Hazael) malak (king) of Aram (Syria).) Yahawaa (Jehu) amar (spoke), If this is your thinking, then let no al (one) palayat (escape) and yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the iyar (city), to yalak (go) to nagad (tell) it in Yazaraial (Jezreel).

So Yahawaa (Jehu) rakab (rode) in a chariot, and yalak (went) to Yazaraial (Jezreel); for Yawaram (Joram) shakab (lay) there. Achazayah (Ahaziah) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) had yarad (come) down to raah (see) Yawaram (Joram).

Now the tzapah (watchman / keep watch) was imad (standing) on the magadal (tower) in Yazaraial (Jezreel), and he raah (see) the shapaih (company) of Yahawaa (Jehu) as he bawaa (come), and amar (spoke), "I raah (see) a shapaih (company)." Yahawaram (Joram) amar (spoke), laqach (take / seized) a rakab (horseman), and shalach (send) to qaraah (meet) them, and let him amar (spoke), ‘Is it shalawam (peace / safety)?’

So there yalak (went) one on rakab (horseback) to qaraah (meet) him, and amar (spoke), "Thus amar (spoke) the malak (king), ‘Is it shalawam (peace / safety)?’" Yahawaa (Jehu) amar (spoke), "What do you have to do with shalawam (peace / safety)? Fall in achar (other) me!" The tzapah (watchman / keep watch) said, The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) bawaa (come) to them, but he isn't shawab (turn back / repent) back.

Then he shalach (send) out a shanay (second) on rakab (horseback), who bawaa (come) to them, and amar (spoke), "Thus amar (spoke) the malak (king), ‘Is it shalawam (peace / safety)?’" Yahawaa (Jehu) amar (spoke), What do you have to do with shalawam (peace / safety)? Fall in achar (other) me!

The tzapah (watchman / keep watch) said, He bawaa (come) to them, and isn't shawab (turn back / repent) back. The manahag (driving) is like the manahag (driving) of Yahawaa (Jehu) the ban (son) of Namashay (Nimshi); for he nahag (drives) shagaiwan (furiously).

Yahawaram (Joram) amar (spoke), "Get asar (ready)!" They got his rakab (chariot) asar (ready). Yahawaram (Joram) malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) and Achazayah (Ahaziah) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, ayash (husband/individual man) in his rakab (chariot), and they yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) Yahawaa (Jehu), and matzaa (found) him in the chalaqah (portion) of Nabawath (Naboth) the yazaraialay (jezreelite).

It happened, when Yahawaram (Joram) raah (see) Yahawaa (Jehu), that he amar (spoke), "Is it shalawam (peace / safety), Yahawaa (Jehu)?" He amar (spoke), What shalawam (peace / safety), so id (long) as the prostitution of your am (mother) Ayazabal (Jezebel) and her kashap (witchcraft) rab (abound)?
Yahawaram (Joram) hapak (turned) his yad (hand), and nawas (fled), and amar (spoke) to Achazayah (Ahaziah), There is treason, Achazayah (Ahaziah)!

Yahawaa (Jehu) drew his qashath (bow) with his malaa (full) yad (hand), and nakah (struck) Yahawaram (Joram) between his zarawai (arms); and the chatzay (arrow) yatzaa (go out / come out) out at his lab (heart), and he karai (sunk) down in his rakab (chariot).

Then Jehu amar (spoke) to Badaqar (Bidkar) his shalayash (captain), Pick him up, and shalak (throw) him in the plot of the shadah (field) of Nabawath (Naboth) the yazaraialay (jezreelite); for zakar (remembrance/memory) how, when you and I rakab (rode) tzamad (together) achar (other) Achaab (Ahab) his ab (father), Yahawah nashaa (lift) this mashaa (burden) on him:

‘Raah (see) I have seen amash (yesterday) the dam (blood) of Nabawath (Naboth), and the dam (blood) of his ban (son),’ naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah; ‘and I will shalam (repay) you in this plot of ground,’ naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah. Now therefore nashaa (lift) and shalak (cast) him onto the plot of ground, according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah.

But when Achazayah (Ahaziah) the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) raah (see) this, he nawas (fled) by the darak (way) of the gan (garden) bayath (house). Yahawaa (Jehu) radap (followed) achar (other) him, and amar (spoke), "nakah (strike) him also in the marakabah (chariot)!" They struck him at the mailah (ascent) of Gawar (Gur), which is by Yabalaim (Ibleam). He nawas (fled) to Magadawan (Megiddo), and mawath (death) there.
His ibad (servant) rakab (carried) him in a chariot to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and qabar (bury) him in his tomb with his ab (father) in the iyar (city) of Dawad (David).
In the ishar (-teen) shanah (year) of Yawaram (Joram) the ban (son) of Achaab (Ahab) began Achazayah (Ahaziah) to malak (king) over Yahawadah (Judah).

When Yahawaa (Jehu) bawaa (come) come to Yazaraial (Jezreel), Ayazabal (Jezebel) shamai (hearken / hear) of it; and she shawam (place / establish / appoint) her iyan (eye), and attired her raash (head), and shaqap (looked) out at the chalawan (window).
As Yahawaa (Jehu) bawaa (come) in at the shair (gate), she amar (spoke), Do you come in shalawam (peace / safety), Zamaray (Zimri), you harag (murderer) of your adawan (master / lord)?
He nashaa (lift) up his panayam (face) to the chalawan (window), and amar (spoke), "Who is on my side? Who?" Shanayam (two) or shalawash (three) sarayas (eunuchs) shaqap (looked) out at him.

He amar (spoke), "shamat (throw) her down!" So they shamat (threw) her down; and some of her dam (blood) was nazah (sprinkled) on the qayar (wall), and on the sawas (horses). Then he ramas (trampled) her under foot.
When he bawaa (come) come in, he akal (eat) and shathah (drinks); and he amar (spoke), paqad (visit) now to this arar (cursed) woman, and qabar (bury) her; for she is a malak (king) bath (daughter).
They yalak (went) to qabar (bury) her; but they matzaa (found) no more of her am (mother) the galagalath (skull), and the ragal (feet / foot), and the kap (palms) of her yad (hand).

Therefore they shawab (turn back / repent) back, and nagad (told) him. He amar (spoke), This is the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, which he dabar (word / matter) by his ibad (servant) Alayah (Elijah) the thashabay (tishbite), amar (spoke), ‘The kalab (dogs) will akal (eat) the bashar (flesh) of Ayazabal (Jezebel) on the plot of Yazaraial (Jezreel),

And the nabalah (body) of Ayazabal (Jezebel) shall be as daman (dung) on the panayam (face) of the shadah (field) in the chalaq (portion) of Yazaraial (Jezreel), so that they shall not amar (spoke), "This is Ayazabal (Jezebel)."’

Now Achaab (Ahab) had shabaiyam (seventy) ban (son) in Shamarawan (Samaria). Yahawaa (Jehu) kathab (wrote) sapar (book / scribed document), and shalach (send) to Shamarawan (Samaria), to the shar (prince / ruler) of Yazaraial (Jezreel), even the zaqan (elders), and to those who aman (believe / have faith) up the sons of Achaab (Ahab), amar (spoke),

Now as soon as this sapar (book / scribed document) bawaa (come) to you, since your adawan (master / lord) ban (son) are with you, and there are with you rakab (chariots) and sawas (horses), a fortified iyar (city) also, and armor.

Select the tawab (pleasant/functional) and fittest of your adawan (master / lord) ban (son), shawam (place / establish / appoint) him on his ab (father) kasaa (throne), and lacham (fight) for your adawan (master / lord) bayath (house).
But they were maad (exceedingly) yaraa (fear / be afraid), and amar (spoke), Behold, the shanayam (two) malak (king) didn't imad (stand) panayam (before) him! How then shall we imad (stand)?

He who was over the bayath (house), and he who was over the iyar (city), the zaqan (elders) also, and those who raised the children, shalach (send) to Yahawaa (Jehu), amar (spoke), We are your ibad (servant), and will ishah (make) all that you ask us. We will not make any man malak (king). You ishah (make) that which is tawab (pleasant/functional) in your iyan (eye).

Then he kathab (wrote) a sapar (book / scribed document) the shanay (second) time to them, amar (spoke), "If you are on my side, and if you will shamai (hearken / hear) to my qawal (sound / voice), laqach (take / seized) the raash (head) of the raash (head) your adawan (master / lord) ban (son), and bawaa (come) to me to Yazaraial (Jezreel) by machar (tomorrow) this ith (time)." Now the malak (king) ban (son), being shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (husband/individual man), were with the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) men of the iyar (city), who gadal (brought) them up.

It happened, when the sapar (book / scribed document) bawaa (come) to them, that they laqach (take / seized) the malak (king) ban (son), and shachat (killed) them, even shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (husband/individual man), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) their raash (head) in dawad (baskets), and shalach (send) them to him to Yazaraial (Jezreel).

A malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) bawaa (come), and nagad (told) him, "They bawaa (come) brought the raash (head) of the malak (king) ban (son)." He amar (spoke), shawam (place / establish / appoint) them in shanayam (two) tzabar (heaps) at the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate) until the baqar (morning).

It happened in the baqar (morning), that he yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and imad (stood), and amar (spoke) to all the im (people / nation), You are tzadayaq (righteous). Behold, I qashar (conspired) against my adawan (master / lord), and harag (killed) him; but who nakah (struck) all these?

Yadai (know) apaw (now) that nothing shall napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land) of the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, which Yahawah dabar (word / matter) concerning the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab). For Yahawah ishah (make) done that which he dabar (word / matter) by his ibad (servant) Alayah (Elijah).

So Yahawaa (Jehu) nakah (struck) all that shaar (remained) of the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab) in Yazaraial (Jezreel), with all his gadawal (very great/important/mighty) men, his yadai (familiar) friends, and his kahan (priest), until he shaar (left) him none sharayad (remaining).
He qawam (rise up) and departed, and yalak (went) to Shamarawan (Samaria). As he was at the raih (shearing) bayathaiqad (house) of the shepherds on the darak (way),

Yahawaa (Jehu) matzaa (met) with the ach (brother/kinsman) of Achazayah (Ahaziah) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and amar (spoke), "Who are you?" They amar (spoke), We are the ach (brother/kinsman) of Achazayah (Ahaziah). We are yarad (going) down to greet the ban (son) of the malak (king) and the ban (son) of the gabayarah (queen).

He amar (spoke), "thapash (take) them chay (life)!" They thapash (took) them chay (life), and shachat (killed) them at the bawar (pit) of the shearing bayathaiqad (house), even arabaiyam (forty) - shanayam (two) ayash (husband/individual man). He didn't shaar (leave) any of them.

When he had departed from there, he met Yahawanadab (Jehonadab) the ban (son) of Rakab (Rechab) coming to qaraah (meet) him. He greeted him, and amar (spoke) to him, "Is your labab (heart) yashar (right), as my labab (heart) is with your labab (heart)?" Yahawanadab (Jehonadab) amar (spoke), "It is." "If it is, nathan (give) me your yad (hand)." He nathan (give) him his yad (hand); and he ilah (go up / offer) him up to him into the marakabah (chariot).
He amar (spoke), "yalak (come) with me, and raah (see) my qanaah (zeal) for Yahawah." So they rakab (made) him ride in his rakab (chariot).

When he bawaa (come) to Shamarawan (Samaria), he nakah (struck) all who shaar (remained) to Achaab (Ahab) in Shamarawan (Samaria), until he had destroyed him, according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, which he dabar (word / matter) to Alayah (Elijah).

Yahawaa (Jehu) qabatz (gathered) all the im (people / nation) qabatz (together), and amar (spoke) to them, "Achaab (Ahab) ibad (servant) Bail (Baal) a mait (little); but Yahawaa (Jehu) will ibad (servant) him much.

Now therefore qaraa (called) to me all the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Bail (Baal), all of his ibad (servant), and all of his kahan (priest). Let ayash (husband/individual man) be absent; for I have a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) zabach (sacrifice) to Bail (Baal). Whoever is absent, he shall not chayah (live)." But Yahawaa (Jehu) ishah (make) it in subtlety, intending that he might abad (destroy/perish) the ibad (servant) of Bail (Baal).
Yahawaa (Jehu) amar (spoke), "qadash (set apart/make holy) a solemn itzarah (assembly) for Bail (Baal)!" They qaraa (called) it.

Yahawaa (Jehu) shalach (send) through all Yasharaal (Israel); and all the ibad (servant) of Bail (Baal) bawaa (come), so that there was not a ayash (husband/individual man) shaar (left) that didn't bawaa (come). They bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of Bail (Baal); and the bayath (house) of Bail (Baal) was malaa (filled) from one pah (end) to another.
He amar (spoke) to him who was over the malathachah (vestry), "yatzaa (go out / come out) out robes for all the ibad (servant) of Bail (Baal)!" He brought robes out to them.

Yahawaa (Jehu) bawaa (come) with Yahawanadab (Jehonadab) the ban (son) of Rakab (Rechab) into the bayath (house) of Bail (Baal). Then he amar (spoke) to the ibad (servant) of Bail (Baal), chapash (search), and raah (see) that there are here with you none of the ibad (servant) of Yahawah, but the ibad (servant) of Bail (Baal) only.

They bawaa (come) in to ishah (make) zabach (sacrifices) and burnt ilah (offerings). Now Yahawaa (Jehu) had shawam (place / establish / appoint) him shamanayam (eighty) ayash (husband/individual man) outside, and amar (spoke), If any of the ishah (make) whom I bawaa (come) into your yad (hand) malat (escape), he who lets him go, his napash (living being/soul) shall be for the napash (living being/soul) of him.

It happened, as soon as he kalah (complete / finish) made an end of ilah (offering) the burnt ishah (make), that Yahawaa (Jehu) amar (spoke) to the rawatz (guard) and to the shalayash (captains), "bawaa (come) in, and nakah (kill) them! Let ayash (husband/individual man) yatzaa (go out / come out)." They nakah (struck) them with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword); and the rawatz (guard) and the shalayash (captains) shalak (cast) them out, and yalak (went) to the iyar (city) of the bayath (house) of Bail (Baal).
They yatzaa (go out / come out) out the matzabah (pillars) that were in the bayath (house) of Bail (Baal), and sharap (burned) them.
They nathatz (broke) down the matzabah (pillar) of Bail (Baal), and nathatz (broke) down the bayath (house) of Bail (Baal), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it a latrine, to this yawam (day).
Thus Yahawaa (Jehu) destroyed Bail (Baal) out of Yasharaal (Israel).

However from the chataa (sins) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Nabat (Nebat), with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin), Yahawaa (Jehu) didn't sawar (depart) from achar (other) them, the zahab (gold) calves that were in Bayathaal (Bethel), and that were Dan (in) Dan.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Yahawaa (Jehu), Because you have tawab (pleasant/functional) well in ishah (make) that which is yashar (right) in my iyan (eye), and ishah (make) done to the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab) according to all that was in my labab (heart), your ban (son) of the rabayaiy (fourth) generation shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the kasaa (throne) of Yasharaal (Israel).

But Yahawaa (Jehu) shamar (keep/guard) no heed to yalak (walk) in the thawarah (instruction) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), with all his labab (heart). He didn't sawar (depart) from the chataah (sin) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam), with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).

In those yawam (day) Yahawah chalal (began) to qatzah (end / extremity / border) off from Yasharaal (Israel); and Chazaal (Hazael) nakah (struck) them in all the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yasharaal (Israel);

From the Yaradan (Jordan) eastward, all the aratz (Earth/land) of Galaid (Gilead), the Gaday (Gadites), and the Raawabanay (Reubenites), and the Manashay (Manassites), from Irawair (Aroer), which is by the nachal (stream / river) of the Aranawan (Arnon), even Galaid (Gilead) and Bashan (Bashan).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawaa (Jehu), and all that he ishah (make), and all his gabawarah (might), aren't they kathab (written) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabar (word / matter) of the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
Yahawaa (Jehu) shakab (slept) with his ab (father); and they qabar (bury) him in Shamarawan (Samaria). Yahawaachaz (Jehoahaz) his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.
The yawam (day) that Yahawaa (Jehu) malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel) in Shamarawan (Samaria) was isharayam (twenty) - shamanah (eight) shanah (years).

Now when Ithalayah (Athaliah) the am (mother) of Achazayah (Ahaziah) raah (see) that her ban (son) was mawath (death), she qawam (rise up) and abad (destroy/perish) all the zarai (seed) mamalakah (royal).

But Yahawashabai (Jehosheba), the bath (daughter) of malak (king) Yawaram (Joram), achawath (sister) of Achazayah (Ahaziah), laqach (take / seized) Yawaash (Joash) the ban (son) of Achazayah (Ahaziah), and ganab (stole) him away from thawak (midst) the malak (king) ban (son) who were mawath (death), even him and his yanaq (nurse), and put them in the bedroom; and they sathar (hid) him from Ithalayah (Athaliah), so that he was not mawath (death);
He was with her chabaa (hidden) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah shash (six) shanah (years). Ithalayah (Athaliah) malak (king) over the aratz (Earth/land).

In the shabayaiy (seventh) shanah (year) Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) shalach (send) and laqach (take / seized) the karay (captains) over maah (hundred) of the Carites and of the rawatz (guard), and bawaa (come) them to him into the bayath (house) of Yahawah; and he karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with them, and took an shabai (swear / take oath) of them in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and showed them the malak (king) ban (son).

He tzawah (commanded) them, amar (spoke), This is the thing that you shall ishah (make): a shalayashay (third) part of you, who bawaa (come) in on the shabath (shabath/rest), shall be keepers of the mashamarath (duty / watch) of the malak (king) bayath (house);

A shalayashay (third) part shall be at the shair (gate) Sawar (Sur); and a shalayashay (third) part at the shair (gate) achar (other) the rawatz (guard). So you shall shamar (keep/guard) the mashamarath (duty / watch) of the bayath (house), and be a barrier.

The shanayam (two) companies of you, even all who yatzaa (go out / come out) out on the shabath (shabath/rest), shall shamar (keep/guard) the mashamarath (duty / watch) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah around the malak (king).

You shall surround the malak (king), sabayab (surrounding) ayash (husband/individual man) with his kalay (weapons) in his yad (hand); and he who bawaa (come) within the ranks, let him be mawath (death). Be with the malak (king) when he yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and when he bawaa (come) in.

The shar (prince / ruler) over maah (hundred) ishah (make) according to all that Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) the kahan (priest) tzawah (commanded); and they laqach (take / seized) every ayash (husband/individual man) his ishah (make), those who were to bawaa (come) in on the shabath (shabath/rest), with those who were to yatzaa (go out / come out) out on the shabath (shabath/rest), and bawaa (come) to Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) the kahan (priest).

The kahan (priest) nathan (give) to the shar (prince / ruler) over maah (hundred) the chanayath (spears) and shalat (shields) that had been malak (king) Dawad (David's), which were in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
