For Yahawah ahab (love) mashapat (justice), and doesn't izab (forsake) his chasayad (saints). They are shamar (keep/guard) iwalam (forever), but the zarai (children) of the rashai (wicked) shall be karath (cut) off.
The tzadayaq (righteous) shall yarash (inherit) the aratz (Earth/land), and live in it id (forever).
The pah (mouth) of the tzadayaq (righteous) hagah (talks) of chakamah (wisdom). His lashawan (tongue/language) hagah (speaks) mashapat (justice).
The thawarah (instruction) of his Alahayam is in his lab (heart). None of his ashar (who/that) shall maid (slide).
The rashai (wicked) watches the tzadayaq (righteous), and baqash (seeks) to mawath (death) him.
Yahawah will not izab (leave) him in his yad (hand), nor rashai (condemn) him when he is shapat (judged).

Qawah (gather/wait) for Yahawah, and shamar (keep/guard) his darak (way), and he will rawam (will lift up) you to yarash (inherit) the aratz (Earth/land). When the rashai (wicked) are karath (cut) off, you shall raah (see) it.
I raah (see) seen the rashai (wicked) in great irayatz (power), irah (spreading) himself like a rainan (green) azarach (tree) in its native soil.
But he ibar (pass over/through) away, and behold, he was not. Yes, I baqash (sought) him, but he could not be matzaa (found).
Shamar (keep/guard) the tham (perfect) man, and raah (see) the yashar (upright), for there is a future for the ayash (husband/individual man) of shalawam (peace / safety).
As for transgressors, they shall be destroyed yachad (together). The future of the rashai (wicked) shall be karath (cut) off.
But the thashawaih (deliverance) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is from Yahawah. He is their stronghold in the ith (time) of tzarah (trouble).
Yahawah izar (helps) them, and rescues them. He rescues them from the rashai (wicked), and yashai (salvation) them, Because they chasah (have) taken refuge in him.
Yahawah, don't yakach (rebuke) me in your qatzap (wrath), neither yasar (chasten) me in your chamah (hot) displeasure.
For your chatz (arrows) have pierced me, your yad (hand) presses hard on me.

There is no matham (soundness) in my bashar (flesh) panayam (because) of your zaim (indignation), neither is there any shalawam (peace / safety) in my itzam (bones) panayam (because) of my chataah (sin).
For my iwan (guilt/iniquity) ibar (pass over/through) gone over my raash (head). As a kabad (heavy) mashaa (burden), they are too kabad (heavy) for me.
My chabawarah (wounds) are baash (loathsome) and maqaq (corrupt), panayam (because) of my awalath (foolishness).
I am pained and shachach (bowed) down maad (greatly). I halak (move) qadar (mourning) all yawam (day) long.
For my waist is malaa (filled) with burning. There is no matham (soundness) in my bashar (flesh).
I am pawag (faint) and severely bruised. I have groaned by reason of the anguish of my lab (heart).
Adanay, all my thaawah (desire) is before you. My anachah (groaning) is not sathar (hidden) from you.
My lab (heart) throbs. My kach (strength / mighty / power) izab (fails) me. As for the awar (light) of my iyan (eye), it has also left me.
My lovers and my rai (neigbor/another person) imad (stand) nagad (aloof) from my nagai (plague). My kinsmen imad (stand) rachawaq (far) away.

They also who baqash (seek) after my napash (living being/soul) lay naqash (snares). Those who darash (seek) my rai (hurt) dabar (word / matter) hawah (calamity/destruction) things, and hagah (meditate) maramah (deceits) all yawam (day) long.
But I, as a charash (deaf) man, don't shamai (hearken / hear). I am as a mute alam (man) who doesn't pathach (open) his pah (mouth).
Yes, I am as a ayash (husband/individual man) who doesn't shamai (hearken / hear), in whose pah (mouth) are no thawakachah (reproofs).
For in you, Yahawah, do I yachal (hope). You will inah (answer / respond), Adanay my Alahayam.
For I amar (spoke), Don't let them gloat over me, or exalt themselves over me when my ragal (feet / foot) mawat (slips).
For I am kawan (ready) to fall. My makaab (pain) is continually before me.
For I will nagad (declare) my iwan (guilt/iniquity). I will be daag (sorry) for my chataah (sin).
But my ayab (enemy) are vigorous and many. Those who shanaa (hate) me shaqar (without) reason are numerous.
They who also shalam (render) rai (evil) for tawab (pleasant/functional) are shatan (adversaries) to me, because I radap (follow) what is tawab (pleasant/functional).
Don't izab (forsake) me, Yahawah. My Alahayam, don't be rachaq (far) from me.
Hurry to izarah (help) me, Adanay, my thashawaih (deliverance).

I amar (spoke), I will shamar (keep/guard) my darak (ways), so that I don't chataa (sin) with my lashawan (tongue/language). I will shamar (keep/guard) my pah (mouth) with a machasawam (bridle) while the rashai (wicked) is before me.
I was mute with dawamayah (silence). I held my chashah (peace), even from tawab (pleasant/functional). My kaab (sorrow) was ikar (stirred).
My lab (heart) was chamam (hot) qarab (among / near) me. While I meditated, the ash (fire) bair (burned): I dabar (word / matter) with my lashawan (tongue/language):
"Yahawah, show me my qatz (end), what is the madah (measure) of my yawam (day). Yadai (let) me know how chadal (frail) I am.
Behold, you nathan (give) made my yawam (day) tapach (handbreadths). My lifetime is as kal (every) before you. Surely every adam (man) natzab (stands) as a habal (breath)." Salah (selah).
“Surely every ayash (husband/individual man) halak (move) like a shadow. Surely they busy themselves in habal (vain). He tzabar (heaps) up, and doesn't yadai (know) who shall asap (gather).
Now, Adanay, what do I qawah (gather/wait) for? My thawachalath (hope) is in you.
Natzal (deliver) me from all my pashai (transgressions). Don't shawam (place / establish / appoint) me the charapah (reproach) of the foolish.
I was mute. I didn't pathach (open) my pah (mouth), because you ishah (make) it.
Sawar (remove) your scourge sawar (away) from me. I am overcome by the thagarah (blow) of your yad (hand).

When you thawakachah (rebuke) and yasar (correct) ayash (husband/individual man) for iwan (guilt/iniquity), You masah (consume) his wealth like a ish (made). Surely every adam (man) is but a habal (breath).” Salah (selah).

Shamai (hearken / hear) my thapalah (prayer), Yahawah, and azan (give) ear to my cry. Don't be charash (silent) at my damaih (tears). For I am a gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) with you, a thawashab (foreigner), as all my ab (father) were.
Oh shaih (spare) me, that I may recover balag (strength), before I yalak (go) away, and exist no more.
I qawah (gather/wait) qawah (gather/wait) for Yahawah. He natah (turned) to me, and shamai (hearken / hear) my cry.

He ilah (go up / offer) me up also out of a shaawan (horrible) bawar (pit), out of the yawan (miry) tayat (clay). He qawam (rise up) my ragal (feet / foot) on a salai (rock), and gave me a kawan (firm) place to stand.

He nathan (give) put a chadash (new) shayar (song) in my pah (mouth), even thahalah (praise) to our Alahayam. Many shall raah (see) it, and yaraa (fear / be afraid), and shall batach (trust) in Yahawah.

Ashar (who/that) is the gabar (man) who shawam (place / establish / appoint) Yahawah his mabatach (trust), and doesn't panah (respect) the rahab (proud), nor such as shawat (turn) aside to kazab (lies).

Many, Yahawah, my Alahayam, are the palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) ishah (make) which you have done, and your machashabah (thoughts) which are toward us. They can't be nagad (declared) back to you. If I would nagad (declare) and dabar (word / matter) of them, they are more than can be sapar (book).
Zabach (sacrifice) and manachah (offering) you didn't chapatz (desire). You have karah (opened) my azan (ears). You have not shaal (required) burnt ilah (offering) and chataah (sin) offering.
Then I amar (spoke), Behold, I bawaa (come) come. It is kathab (written) about me in the sapar (book / scribed document) in the scroll.
I chapatz (delight) to ishah (make) your ratzawan (will), my Alahayam. Yes, your thawarah (instruction) is thawak (midst) my maih (heart).
I have proclaimed glad news of tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) in the rab (great) qahal (assembly). Behold, I will not seal my shapah (lips), Yahawah, you yadai (know).

I have not kasah (hidden) your tzadaqah (righteousness) thawak (midst) my lab (heart). I have amar (spoke) your amawanah (faithfulness) and your thashawaih (deliverance). I have not kachad (concealed) your loving chasad (grace) and your amath (truth) from the rab (great) qahal (assembly).
Don't kalaa (withhold) your tender racham (mercies) from me, Yahawah. Let your loving chasad (grace) and your amath (truth) continually natzar (preserve) me.

For innumerable rai (evils) have surrounded me. My iwan (guilt/iniquity) have overtaken me, so that I am not yakal (able) to raah (see) up. They are more than the shairah (hairs) of my raash (head). My lab (heart) has izab (failed) me.
Be ratzah (pleased), Yahawah, to natzal (deliver) me. Hurry to izarah (help) me, Yahawah.

Let them be disappointed and chapar (confounded) yachad (together) who baqash (seek) after my napash (living being/soul) to sapah (destroy) it. Let them be sawag (turned) backward and brought to dishonor who chapatz (delight) in my rai (hurt).
Let them be shamam (desolate) by reason of their bashath (shame) that amar (spoke) me, haach (aha)! Haach (aha)!
Let all those who baqash (seek) you shawash (rejoice) and be shamach (glad) in you. Let such as ahab (love) your thashawaih (deliverance) amar (spoke) continually, Let Yahawah be exalted!
But I am inay (poor) and abayawan (needy). May the Adanay chashab (think) about me. You are my izarah (help) and my deliverer. Don't achar (other), my Alahayam.
Ashar (who/that) is he who shakal (considers) the dal (poor). Yahawah will malat (deliver) him in the yawam (day) of rai (evil).

Yahawah will shamar (keep/guard) him, and chayah (keep) him alive. He shall be ashar (who/that) on the aratz (Earth/land), and he will not surrender him to the napash (living being/soul) of his ayab (enemy).
Yahawah will sustain him on his sickbed, and hapak (restore) him from his irash (bed) of illness.
I amar (spoke), Yahawah, have chanan (mercy) on me! Rapaa (heal) me, for I have chataa (sinned) against you.
My ayab (enemy) amar (spoke) rai (evil) against me: When will he mawath (death), and his sham (name) abad (destroy/perish)?

If he bawaa (come) to raah (see) me, he dabar (word / matter) falsehood. His lab (heart) qabatz (gathers) awan (iniquity) to itself. When he yatzaa (go out / come out) chawatz (abroad), he dabar (word / matter) it.
All who shanaa (hate) me lachash (whisper) yachad (together) against me. They chashab (imagine) the rai (worst) for me.
"An balayail (evil) dabar (word / matter)," they say, has afflicted him. Now that he shakab (lies) he shall qawam (rise up) up no more.
Yes, my own shalawam (peace / safety) friend, in whom I batach (trusted), who akal (eat) lacham (bread) with me, has gadal (lifted) up his iqab (heel) against me.
But you, Yahawah, have chanan (mercy) on me, and qawam (rise up) me up, that I may shalam (repay) them.
By this I yadai (know) that you chapatz (delight) in me, because my ayab (enemy) doesn't rawai (triumph) over me.
As for me, you uphold me in my tham (integrity), and natzab (set) me in your panayam (presence) iwalam (forever).
Barak (blessed) be Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), from iwalam (forever) and to iwalam (forever)! Aman (believe / have faith) and aman (believe / have faith).
As the deer irag (pants) for the mayam (Waters) apayaq (brooks), so my napash (living being/soul) irag (pants) after you, Alahayam.
My napash (living being/soul) tzamaa (thirsts) for Alahayam, for the chay (life) Al. When shall I bawaa (come) and raah (see) panayam (before) Alahayam?
My damaih (tears) have been my lacham (food) yawamam (by day) and layal (night), yawam (day) they continually ask me, Where is your Alahayam?

These things I zakar (remembrance/memory), and shapak (pour) out my napash (living being/soul) within me, how I used to ibar (pass over/through) with the crowd, and led them to the bayath (house) of Alahayam, with the qawal (sound / voice) of ranah (joy) and thawadah (praise), a hamawan (multitude) chagag (keeping) a holy day.

Why are you in despair, my napash (living being/soul)? Why are you disturbed within me? Yachal (hope) in Alahayam! For I shall still yadah (praise) him for the yashawaih (salvation) help of his panayam (presence).

My Alahayam, my napash (living being/soul) is in despair within me. Therefore I zakar (remembrance/memory) you from the aratz (Earth/land) of the Yaradan (Jordan), the Charamawanayam (heights) of Hermon, from the har (mountain) matzair (mizar).
Thahawam (depths) qaraa (called) to thahawam (depths) at the qawal (sound / voice) of your waterfalls. All your mashabar (waves) and your gal (billows) ibar (pass over/through) swept over me.
Yahawah will tzawah (command) his loving chasad (grace) in the yawamam (by day). In the layal (night) his shayar (song) shall be with me: a thapalah (prayer) to the Al of my chay (life).
I will ask Al, my salai (rock), Why have you shakach (forgotten) me? Why do I yalak (go) qadar (mourning) because of the lachatz (oppression) of the ayab (enemy)?
As with a ratzach (sword) in my itzam (bones), my tzarar (adversaries) charap (reproach) me, yawam (day) they continually ask me, Where is your Alahayam?

Why are you in despair, my napash (living being/soul)? Why are you disturbed within me? Yachal (hope) in Alahayam! For I shall still yadah (praise) him, the yashawaih (salvation) help of my panayam (countenance), and my Alahayam.
Vindicate me, Alahayam, and rayab (plead) my rayab (cause) against an ungodly gaway (nation / people). Oh, palat (deliver) me from deceitful and iwal (wicked) ayash (husband/individual man).
For you are the Alahayam of my maiwaz (stronghold / fortress / protection). Why have you rejected me? Why do I halak (move) qadar (mourning) because of the lachatz (oppression) of the ayab (enemy)?
Oh, shalach (send) out your awar (light) and your amath (truth). Let them nachah (lead) me. Bawaa (come) them bring me to your qadash (set apart/make holy) har (mountain), To your mashakan (tents).
Then I will bawaa (come) to the mazabach (altar) of Alahayam, to Al, my shamachah (exceeding) gayal (joy). I will yadah (praise) you on the kanawar (harp), Alahayam, my Alahayam.
Why are you in despair, my napash (living being/soul)? Why are you disturbed within me? Yachal (hope) in Alahayam! For I shall still yadah (praise) him: my Savior, my helper, and my Alahayam.
We have shamai (hearken / hear) with our azan (ears), Alahayam; our ab (father) have sapar (book) us, what pail (work) you pail (did) in their yawam (day), in the yawam (day) of qadam (old).
You yarash (drove) out the gaway (nation / people) with your yad (hand), but you natai (planted) them. You raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) the laam (peoples), but you shalach (send) them abroad.

For they didn't yarash (get) the aratz (Earth/land) in yarash (possession) by their own charab (sword), neither did their own zarawai (arm) yashai (salvation) them; but your right yamayan (right hand), and your zarawai (arm), and the awar (light) of your panayam (face), because you were favorable to them.
You are my malak (king), Alahayam. Tzawah (command) victories for Yaiqab (Jacob)!
Through you, will we nagach (push) down our tzar (oppressor / distressor). Through your sham (name), will we bawas (tread) them under who qawam (rise up) up against us.
For I will not batach (trust) in my qashath (bow), neither shall my charab (sword) yashai (salvation) me.
But you have yashai (salvation) us from our tzar (oppressor / distressor), and have bawash (shamed) those who shanaa (hate) us.
In Alahayam we have halal (praise) our boast all yawam (day) long, we will give yadah (thanks) to your sham (name) iwalam (forever). Salah (selah).
But now you rejected us, and brought us to dishonor, and don't yatzaa (go out / come out) out with our tzabaa (troop).
You make us shawab (turn back / repent) achawar (back) from the tzar (oppressor / distressor). Those who shanaa (hate) us take shasah (spoil) for themselves.
You nathan (give) made us like tzaan (sheep) for maakal (food), and have zarah (scattered) us among the gaway (nation / people).
You makar (sell) your im (people / nation) for nothing, and have gained nothing from their sale.
You shawam (place / establish / appoint) us a charapah (reproach) to our neighbors, a scoffing and a qalas (derision) to those who are around us.
You shawam (place / establish / appoint) us a mashal (byword) among the gaway (nation / people), a manawad (shaking) of the raash (head) among the laam (peoples).
All bashath (day) long my dishonor is before me, and bashath (shame) kasah (covers) my panayam (face),
At the taunt of charap (one) who reproaches and verbally abuses, panayam (because) of the ayab (enemy) and the avenger.
All this bawaa (come) come on us, yet have we not shakach (forgotten) you, Neither have we been false to your barayath (covenant).
Our lab (heart) has not sawag (turned) achawar (back), neither have our ashar (who/that) strayed from your arach (path),
Though you have crushed us in the haunt of jackals, and kasah (covered) us with the shadow of tzalamawath (death).
If we have shakach (forgotten) the sham (name) of our Alahayam, or parash (spread) forth our kap (hands) to a zawar (strange) Al;
Won't Alahayam chaqar (search) this out? For he yadai (knows) the thailamah (secrets) of the lab (heart).
Yes, for your sake we are harag (killed) all yawam (day) long. We are chashab (regarded) as tzaan (sheep) for the tabachah (slaughter).
Iwar (rouse / awaken) up! Why do you sleep, Adanay? Arise! Don't reject us natzach (forever).
Why do you sathar (hide) your panayam (face), and shakach (forget) our inay (affliction) and our lachatz (oppression)?
For our napash (living being/soul) is shawach (bowed) down to the ipar (dust). Our batan (body) clings to the aratz (Earth/land).
Qawam (rise up) up to izarah (help) us. Padah (redeem) us for your loving chasad (grace)' sake.
My lab (heart) overflows with a noble theme. I recite my verses for the malak (king). My lashawan (tongue/language) is like the it (pen) of a skillful sapar (book).
You are the most excellent of the ban (son) of adam (men). Chan (grace) has yatzaq (anointed) your shapah (lips), therefore Alahayam has barak (blessed) you iwalam (forever).
Strap your charab (sword) on your yarak (thigh), gabawar (mighty) hawad (one): your splendor and your hadar (glory / majesty / splendor).

In your hadar (glory / majesty / splendor) rakab (ride) on victoriously on behalf of amath (truth), humility, and tzadaq (righteous / just / fair). Let your right yamayan (right hand) display awesome deeds.
Your chatz (arrows) are shanan (sharp). The im (people / nation) napal (fall / be cast down) under you, with arrows in the lab (heart) of the malak (king) ayab (enemy).
Your kasaa (throne), Alahayam, is id (forever) and iwalam (forever). A scepter of mayashawar (equity) is the scepter of your malakawath (kingdom).

You have ahab (love) tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and shanaa (hate) rashai (wickedness). Therefore Alahayam, your Alahayam, has mashach (anointed) you with the shaman (oil) of shashawan (gladness) above your chabar (fellows).
All your bagad (garments) smell like mar (myrrh), ahalayam (aloes), and qatzayaih (cassia). Out of shan (ivory) hayakal (palaces) man (from) instruments shamach (have) made you glad.
Malak (king)' bath (daughter) are among your honorable yaqar (women). At your right yamayan (right hand) the shagal (queen) natzab (stands) in katham (gold) of Awapayar (Ophir).
Shamai (hearken / hear), bath (daughter), raah (see), and natah (turn) your azan (ear). Shakach (forget) your own im (people / nation), and also your ab (father) bayath (house).
So the malak (king) will awah (desire) your yapay (beauty), honor him, for he is your Adawan.
The bath (daughter) of Tzar (Tyre) comes with a manachah (gift). The ishayar (rich) among the im (people / nation) entreat your favor.
The bath (daughter) inside is kabawadah (all) glorious. Her labawash (clothing) is interwoven with zahab (gold).
She shall be yabal (led) to the malak (king) in embroidered raqamah (work). The bathawalah (virgins), her raih (companions) who achar (other) her, shall be bawaa (come) to you.
With shamachah (gladness) and gayal (rejoicing) they shall be yabal (led). They shall bawaa (come) into the malak (king) hayakal (palace).
Your ban (son) will take the place of your ab (father). You shall shayath (put / appoint / make) them shar (prince / ruler) in all the aratz (Earth/land).

I will make your sham (name) to be zakar (remembrance/memory) in all dawar (generation / age / period). Therefore the im (people / nation) shall give you yadah (thanks) iwalam (forever) and iwalam (forever).
Alahayam is our machasah (refuge) and iz (strength / might / refuge), a very matzaa (present) izarah (help) in tzarah (trouble).
Therefore we won't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), though the aratz (Earth/land) mawar (changes), though the har (mountain) are mawat (shaken) into the lab (heart) of the yam (sea/waters);
Though its mayam (Waters) hamah (they) and are chamar (troubled), though the har (mountain) raish (tremble) with their gaawah (swelling). Salah (selah).
There is a nahar (river), the palag (streams) of which make the iyar (city) of Alahayam shamach (glad), the qadawash (holy) place of the mashakan (tents) of the Most ilayawan (high).
Alahayam is in her qarab (among / near). She shall not be mawat (moved). Alahayam will izar (help) her at dawn.
The gaway (nation / people) hamah (they). The mamalakah (kingdoms) were mawat (moved). He nathan (give) his qawal (sound / voice), and the aratz (Earth/land) mawag (melted).
Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) is with us. The Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob) is our refuge. Salah (selah).
Yalak (come), chazah (see) yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) mapail (works), what shamah (desolations) he has shawam (place / establish / appoint) in the aratz (Earth/land).

He makes malachamah (wars) shabath (shabath/rest) to the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land). He shabar (breaks) the qashath (bow), and shatters the chanayath (spear). He sharap (burns) the igalah (chariots) in the ash (fire).
Be still, and yadai (know) that I am Alahayam. I will be rawam (will lift up) among the gaway (nation / people). I will be rawam (will lift up) in the aratz (Earth/land).
Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) is with us. The Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob) is our refuge. Mashagab (selah).
Oh thaqai (blow / sound alarm) your kap (hands), all you im (people / nation). Rawai (shout) to Alahayam with the qawal (sound / voice) of ranah (triumph)!
For Yahawah Most ilayawan (high) is awesome. He is a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) malak (king) over all the aratz (Earth/land).
He dabar (word / matter) im (people / nation) under us, and im (people / nation) under our ragal (feet / foot).
He bachar (chooses) our nachalah (inheritance) for us, the glory of Yaiqab (Jacob) whom he ahab (love). Salah (selah).
Alahayam has ilah (go up / offer) up with a tharawaih (shout), Yahawah with the qawal (sound / voice) of a shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)).
Sing zamar (praise) to Alahayam, sing zamar (praises). Sing zamar (praises) to our malak (king), sing zamar (praises).
For Alahayam is the malak (king) of all the aratz (Earth/land). Sing zamar (praises) with shakal (understanding).
Alahayam malak (king) over the gaway (nation / people). Alahayam yashab (inhabit/dwell) on his qadash (set apart/make holy) kasaa (throne).

The nadayab (princes) of the im (people / nation) are asap (gathered) together, the im (people / nation) of the Alahayam of Abaraham (Abraham). For the magan (shield) of the aratz (Earth/land) belong to Alahayam. He is maad (greatly) ilah (go up / offer)!
Gadawal (very great/important/mighty) is Yahawah, and maad (greatly) to be halal (praise), in the iyar (city) of our Alahayam, in his qadash (set apart/make holy) har (mountain).

Yapah (beautiful) in elevation, the mashawash (joy) of the whole aratz (Earth/land), is har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion), on the tzapawan (north) yarakah (sides), the qarayah (city) of the rab (great) malak (king).
Alahayam yadai (has) shown himself in her citadels as a refuge.
For, behold, the malak (king) yaid (assembled) themselves, they ibar (pass over/through) by yachad (together).
They raah (see) it, then they were thamah (amazed). They were bahal (dismayed). They hurried away.
Raid (trembling) achaz (took) hold of them there, chayal (pain), as of a yalad (birth / begot) in travail.
With the qadayam (east) rawach (spirit / wind), you shabar (break) the anayah (ships) of Tharashayash (Tarshish).

As we have shamai (hearken / hear), so we raah (see) seen, in the iyar (city) of Yahawah of tzabaa (troop), in the iyar (city) of our Alahayam. Alahayam will kawan (establish) it iwalam (forever). Salah (selah).
We have damah (thought) about your loving chasad (grace), Alahayam, in the qarab (among / near) of your hayakal (temple).
As is your sham (name), Alahayam, so is your thahalah (praise) to the qatzaw (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land). Your right yamayan (right hand) is malaa (full) of tzadaq (righteous / just / fair).
Let har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion) be gayal (glad)! Let the bath (daughter) of Yahawadah (Judah) gayal (rejoice), Because of your mashapat (judgments).
Sabab (walk) about Tzayawan (Zion), and naqap (go) around her. Sapar (book) its magadal (towers).
Shayath (put / appoint / make) lab (heart) her chayalah (bulwarks). Pasag (consider) her aramawan (palaces), that you may sapar (book) it to the next dawar (generation / age / period).
For this Alahayam is our Alahayam iwalam (forever) and iwalam (forever). He will be our nahag (guide) even to mawath (death).
Shamai (hearken / hear) this, all you im (people / nation). Shamai (hearken / hear), all you yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the chalad (world),
Both low and high, ishayar (rich) and abayawan (poor) yachad (together).
My pah (mouth) will dabar (word / matter) words of chakamawath (wisdom). My lab (heart) shall utter thabawan (understanding).
I will natah (incline) my azan (ear) to a mashal (proverb). I will pathach (open) my chayadah (riddle) on the kanawar (harp).
Why should I yaraa (fear / be afraid) in the yawam (day) of rai (evil), when iwan (guilt/iniquity) at my iqab (heels) surrounds me?
Those who batach (trust) in their wealth, and halal (praise) in the rab (multitude) of their riches—
Ayash (husband/individual man) of them can by any padah (means) padah (redeem) his ach (brother/kinsman), nor nathan (give) Alahayam a kapar (ransom) for him.
For the padayawam (redemption) of their napash (living being/soul) is costly, no payment is iwalam (forever) enough,
That he should chayah (live) on natzach (forever), that he should not raah (see) shachath (corruption).
For he raah (see) that chakam (wise) men mawath (death); yachad (likewise) the kasayal (fool) and the senseless abad (destroy/perish), and izab (leave) their wealth to others.

Their qarab (among / near) thought is that their bayath (house) will endure iwalam (forever), and their mashakan (dwelling) places to all dawar (generation / age / period). They qaraa (called) their adamah (lands) after themselves.
But adam (man), despite his riches, doesn't lawan (endure). He is mashal (speak in proverb/parable) the animals that damah (perish).
This is the destiny of those who are foolish, and of those who ratzah (approve) their pah (sayings). Salah (selah).

They are appointed as a tzaan (flock) for shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife). Mawath (death) shall be their raih (shepherd). The yashar (upright) shall radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) dominion over them in the baqar (morning). Their beauty shall decay in shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife), far from their mansion.
But Alahayam will padah (redeem) my napash (living being/soul) from the yad (hand) of shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife), for he will laqach (take / seized) me. Salah (selah).
Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) when a ayash (husband/individual man) is ishar (made) rich, when the kabawad (glory) of his bayath (house) is rabah (increased).
For when he mawath (death) he shall laqach (take / seized) nothing away. His kabawad (glory) shall not descend achar (other) him.
Though while he chay (life) he barak (blessed) his napash (living being/soul)— and men yadah (praise) you when you yatab (do) well for yourself—
He shall bawaa (come) to the dawar (generation / age / period) of his ab (father). They shall laa (NOT) raah (see) the awar (light).
A adam (man) who has riches without bayan (between), is mashal (speak in proverb/parable) the animals that damah (perish).
The al (mighty) One, Alahayam, Yahawah, dabar (word / matter), and qaraa (called) the aratz (Earth/land) from sunrise to sunset.
Out of Tzayawan (Zion), the makalal (perfection) of yapay (beauty), Alahayam yapai (shines) forth.
Our Alahayam bawaa (come), and does not charash (keep) silent. A ash (fire) akal (eat) panayam (before) him. It is very stormy around him.
He qaraa (called) to the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) il (over), to the aratz (Earth/land), that he may dayan (judge) his im (people / nation):
Asap (gather) my chasayad (saints) together to me, those who have karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with me by zabach (sacrifice).
The shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) shall nagad (declare) his tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), for Alahayam himself is shapat (judge). Salah (selah).
Shamai (hearken / hear), my im (people / nation), and I will dabar (word / matter); Yasharaal (Israel), and I will testify against you. I am Alahayam, your Alahayam.
I don't yakach (rebuke) you for your zabach (sacrifices). Your burnt ilah (offerings) are continually before me.
I have no need for a par (bull) from your stall, nor male ithawad (goats) from your pens.
For every animal of the yair (forest) is mine, and the livestock on a alap (thousand) harar (hills).
I yadai (know) all the iwap (flying) of the har (mountain). The zayaz (wild) animals of the shadah (field) are imad (mine).
If I were raib (hungry), I would not amar (spoke) you, for the thabal (world) is mine, and malaa (all) that is in it.
Will I akal (eat) the bashar (flesh) of abayar (bulls), or shathah (drinks) the dam (blood) of ithawad (goats)?
Zabach (offer) to Alahayam the thawadah (sacrifice) of thanksgiving. Shalam (pay) your nadar (vow) to the Most ilayawan (high).
Qaraa (called) on me in the yawam (day) of tzarah (trouble). I will chalatz (deliver) you, and you will honor me.
But to the rashai (wicked) Alahayam amar (spoke), What right do you have to sapar (book) my chaq (statute), that you have nashaa (lift) my barayath (covenant) on your lips,
Since you shanaa (hate) mawasar (instruction), and shalak (throw) my dabar (word / matter) achar (other) you?
When you raah (see) a ganab (thief), you ratzah (consented) with him, and have participated with naap (adulterers).
You shalach (send) your pah (mouth) to rai (evil). Your lashawan (tongue/language) tzamad (frames) maramah (deceit).
You yashab (inhabit/dwell) and dabar (word / matter) against your ach (brother/kinsman). You slander your own am (mother) ban (son).
You ishah (make) done these things, and I charash (kept) silent. You damah (thought) that I was just like you. I will yakach (rebuke) you, and accuse you in front of your iyan (eye).
Now bayan (between) this, you who shakach (forget) Alawah, lest I tarap (tear) you into pieces, and there be none to natzal (deliver).
Whoever zabach (offers) the thawadah (sacrifice) of thanksgiving kabad (glorifies) me, and prepares his darak (way) so that I will show alahayam (Alahayam) yashai (salvation) to him.
Have chanan (mercy) on me, Alahayam, according to your loving chasad (grace). According to the rab (multitude) of your tender racham (mercies), machah (blot) out my pashai (transgressions).
Kabas (wash) me rabah (thoroughly) from my iwan (guilt/iniquity). Tahar (cleanse) me from my chataah (sin).
For I yadai (know) my pashai (transgressions). My chataah (sin) is constantly before me.

Against you, and you only, have I chataa (sinned), and ishah (make) that which is rai (evil) in your iyan (eye); that you may be proved right when you dabar (word / matter), and justified when you shapat (judge).
Behold, I was chawal (brought) forth in iwan (guilt/iniquity). In chataa (sin) my am (mother) yacham (conceived) me.
Behold, you chapatz (desire) amath (truth) in the tachah (inward) parts. You yadai (teach) me chakamah (wisdom) in the inmost place.
Chataa (purify) me with azawab (hyssop), and I will be tahar (clean). Kabas (wash) me, and I will be laban (whiter) than shalag (snow).
Shamai (hearken / hear) me hear shashawan (joy) and shashawan (gladness), That the itzam (bones) which you have dakah (broken) may gayal (rejoice).
Sathar (hide) your panayam (face) from my chataa (sins), and machah (blot) out all of my iwan (guilt/iniquity).
Baraa (created) in me a tahawar (clean) lab (heart), O Alahayam. Chadash (renew) a kawan (right) rawach (spirit / wind) qarab (among / near) me.
Don't shalak (throw) me from your panayam (presence), and don't laqach (take / seized) your qadash (set apart/make holy) rawach (spirit / wind) from me.
Shawab (turn back / repent) to me the shashawan (joy) of your yashai (salvation). Samak (uphold) me with a nadayab (willing) rawach (spirit / wind).
Then I will lamad (teach/instruct) transgressors your darak (ways). Chataa (sinners) shall be shawab (turn back / repent) to you.
Natzal (deliver) me from bloodguiltiness, O Alahayam, the Alahayam of my thashawaih (deliverance). My lashawan (tongue/language) shall ranan (sing) aloud of your tzadaqah (righteousness).
Adanay, pathach (open) my shapah (lips). My pah (mouth) shall nagad (declare) your thahalah (praise).
For you don't chapatz (delight) in zabach (sacrifice), or else I nathan (give) give it. You ratzah (have) no pleasure in burnt ilah (offering).
The zabach (sacrifices) of Alahayam are a shabar (broken) rawach (spirit / wind). A shabar (broken) and dakah (contrite) lab (heart), O Alahayam, you will not bazah (despise).
Do well in your yatab (good) ratzawan (pleasure) to Tzayawan (Zion). Banah (build) the chawamah (walls) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

Then you chapatz (will) delight in the zabach (sacrifices) of tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), in burnt ilah (offerings) and in kalayal (whole) burnt ilah (offerings). Then they will ilah (go up / offer) par (bulls) on your mazabach (altar).
Why do you halal (praise) of rai (mischief), gabawar (mighty) man? Al (god's) loving chasad (grace) endures yawam (day).
Your lashawan (tongue/language) plots destruction, like a latash (sharp) thair (razor), ishah (make) deceitfully.
You ahab (love) rai (evil) more than tawab (pleasant/functional), shaqar (lying) rather than dabar (word / matter) the tzadaq (righteous / just / fair). Salah (selah).
You ahab (love) all balai (devouring) dabar (word / matter), you deceitful lashawan (tongue/language).

Al will likewise nathatz (destroy) you natzach (forever). He will chathah (take) you up, and nasach (pluck) you out of your ahal (tent), and sharash (root) you out of the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life). Salah (selah).
The tzadayaq (righteous) also will raah (see) it, and yaraa (fear / be afraid), and shachaq (laugh) at him, saying,

Behold, this is the gabar (man) who didn't shawam (place / establish / appoint) Alahayam his maiwaz (stronghold / fortress / protection), but batach (trusted) in the rab (abundance) of his riches, and izaz (strengthened) himself in his hawah (calamity/destruction).
But as for me, I am like a rainan (green) zayath (olive) tree in alahayam (Alahayam) bayath (house). I batach (trust) in alahayam (Alahayam) loving chasad (grace) iwalam (forever) and id (ever).
I will give you yadah (thanks) iwalam (forever), because you ishah (make) done it. I will hope in your sham (name), for it is tawab (pleasant/functional), in the presence of your chasayad (saints).

The nabal (fool) has amar (spoke) in his lab (heart), "There is no Alahayam." They are shachath (corrupt), and have thaib (done) abominable iwal (iniquity). There is no one who ishah (make) tawab (pleasant/functional).
Alahayam shaqap (looks) down from shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) on the ban (son) of adam (men), to raah (see) if there are any who shakal (understood), who darash (seek) after Alahayam.
Every one of them has sawag (gone) back. They have alach (become) filthy yachad (together). There is no one who ishah (make) tawab (pleasant/functional), no, not achad (one).
Have the pail (workers) of awan (iniquity) no yadai (knowledge), who akal (eat) up my im (people / nation) as they akal (eat) lacham (bread), and don't qaraa (called) on Alahayam?

There they were in pachad (fear / dread) pachad (fear / dread), where no pachad (fear / dread) was, for Alahayam has pazar (scattered) the itzam (bones) of him who chanah (encamps) against you. You have bawash (put) them to shame, because Alahayam has maas (rejected) them.

Oh that the yashawaih (salvation) of Yasharaal (Israel) would come out of Tzayawan (Zion)! When Alahayam shawab (turn back / repent) back his im (people / nation) from shabawath (captivity), then Yaiqab (Jacob) shall gayal (rejoice), and Yasharaal (Israel) shall be shamach (glad).
Yashai (salvation) me, Alahayam, by your sham (name). Vindicate me in your gabawarah (might).
Shamai (hearken / hear) my thapalah (prayer), Alahayam. Listen to the amar (spoke) of my pah (mouth).

For strangers have qawam (rise up) up against me. Irayatz (violent) men have baqash (sought) after my napash (living being/soul). They haven't shawam (place / establish / appoint) Alahayam before them. Salah (selah).
Behold, Alahayam is my helper. The Adanay is the napash (living being/soul) who sustains my napash (living being/soul).
He will repay the rai (evil) to my sharar (enemies). Tzamath (destroy) them in your amath (truth).
With a free will nadabah (voluntary / freewill offering), I will zabach (sacrifice) to you. I will give yadah (thanks) to your sham (name), Yahawah, for it is tawab (pleasant/functional).
For he has natzal (delivered) me out of all tzarah (trouble). My iyan (eye) raah (see) seen triumph over my ayab (enemy).
Listen to my thapalah (prayer), Alahayam. Don't ilam (hide) yourself from my thachanah (supplication).
Qashab (attend) to me, and inah (answer / respond) me. I am restless in my shayach (complaint), and moan,

Because of the qawal (sound / voice) of the ayab (enemy), panayam (because) of the iqah (oppression) of the rashai (wicked). For they bring suffering on me. In ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) they hold a grudge shatam (against) me.
My lab (heart) is severely chawal (pained) qarab (among / near) me. The ayamah (terrors) of mawath (death) napal (fall / be cast down) fallen on me.
Yaraah (fearfulness) and raid (trembling) bawaa (come) come on me. Palatzawath (horror) has kasah (overwhelmed) me.
I amar (spoke), "Oh that I had abar (wings) like a yawanah (dove)! Then I would iwap (flying) away, and be at shakan (rest).
Behold, then I would nadad (wander) rachaq (far) off. I would lawan (lodge) in the madabar (wilderness)." Salah (selah).
I would hurry to a shelter from the stormy rawach (spirit / wind) and saih (storm).
Confuse them, Adanay, and palag (confound) their lashawan (tongue/language), for I raah (see) seen chamas (violence) and rayab (strife) in the iyar (city).
Yawamam (by day) and layal (night) they prowl around on its chawamah (walls). Malice and abuse are also qarab (among / near) her.
Destructive forces are qarab (among / near) her. Threats and lies don't depart from her rachab (streets).

For it was not an ayab (enemy) who insulted me, then I could have endured it. Neither was it he who shanaa (hate) me who raised himself up against me, then I would have sathar (hidden) myself from him.
But it was you, a anawash (man) like me, my companion, and my yadai (familiar) friend.
We mathaq (took) sweet fellowship yachad (together). We halak (move) in alahayam (Alahayam) bayath (house) with ragash (company).

Let yashayamah (death) come suddenly on them. Yarad (let) them go down chay (life) into shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife). For rai (wickedness) is in their magawar (dwelling), in their qarab (among / near).
As for me, I will qaraa (called) on Alahayam. Yahawah will yashai (salvation) me.
Irab (evening), baqar (morning), and at tzahar (noon), I will cry out in distress. He will shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice).
He has padah (redeemed) my napash (living being/soul) in shalawam (peace / safety) from the qarab (battle) that was against me, although there are many who oppose me.
Al, who is enthroned qadam (forever), will shamai (hearken / hear), and inah (oppress / afflict) them. Salah (selah). They never chalayapah (change), who don't yaraa (fear / be afraid) Alahayam.
He raises his yad (hand) against his shalawam (peace / safety). He has violated his barayath (covenant).

His pah (mouth) was chalaq (smooth) as machamaah (butter), but his lab (heart) was qarab (war). His dabar (word / matter) were rakak (softer) than shaman (oil), yet they were drawn pathachah (swords).
Shalak (cast) your yahab (burden) on Yahawah, and he will kawal (all/every/entire) you. He will iwalam (forever) allow the tzadayaq (righteous) to be mawat (moved).

But you, Alahayam, will yarad (bring) them down into the baar (pit) of shachath (destruction). Bloodthirsty and deceitful ayash (husband/individual man) shall not chatzah (live) out half their yawam (day), but I will batach (trust) in you.
Be chanan (merciful) to me, Alahayam, for anawash (man) wants to shaap (swallow) me up. All yawam (day) long, he attacks and oppresses me.
My sharar (enemies) want to shaap (swallow) me up all yawam (day) long, for they are many who lacham (fight) proudly against me.
When I am yaraa (fear / be afraid), I will batach (put) my trust in you.
In Alahayam, I halal (praise) his dabar (word / matter). In Alahayam, I batach (put) my trust. I will not be yaraa (fear / be afraid). What can bashar (flesh) ishah (make) to me?
All yawam (day) long they twist my dabar (word / matter). All their machashabah (thoughts) are against me for rai (evil).
They conspire and tzapan (lurk), shamar (keep/guard) my iqab (steps), they are eager to take my napash (living being/soul).
Shall they palat (escape) by awan (iniquity)? In ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) yarad (cast) down the im (people / nation), Alahayam.
You sapar (book) my nawad (wanderings). You shawam (place / establish / appoint) my damaih (tears) into your naad (bottle). Aren't they in your sapar (book / scribed document)?
Then my ayab (enemy) shall shawab (turn back / repent) achawar (back) in the yawam (day) that I qaraa (called). I yadai (know) this, that Alahayam is for me.
In Alahayam, I will halal (praise) his dabar (word / matter). In Yahawah, I will halal (praise) his dabar (word / matter).
I have batach (put) my trust in Alahayam. I will not be yaraa (fear / be afraid). What can adam (man) ishah (make) to me?
Your nadar (vow) are on me, Alahayam. I will shalam (give) thank thawadah (offerings) to you.

For you have natzal (delivered) my napash (living being/soul) from mawath (death), and prevented my ragal (feet / foot) from dachay (falling), that I may halak (move) panayam (before) Alahayam in the awar (light) of the chay (life).

Be chanan (merciful) to me, Alahayam, be chanan (merciful) to me, for my napash (living being/soul) takes chasah (refuge) in you. Yes, in the tzal (shadow) of your kanap (wings), I will take chasah (refuge), until disaster ibar (pass over/through) passed.
I qaraa (called) out to Alahayam Most ilayawan (high), to Al who accomplishes my requests for me.

He will shalach (send) from shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), and yashai (salvation) me, he rebukes the shaap (one) who is pursuing me. Salah (selah). Alahayam will shalach (send) out his loving chasad (grace) and his amath (truth).

My napash (living being/soul) is thawak (midst) labayaa (lions). I shakab (lie) among those who are set on lahat (fire), even the ban (son) of adam (men), whose shan (teeth) are chanayath (spears) and chatz (arrows), and their lashawan (tongue/language) a chad (sharp) charab (sword).
Be rawam (will lift up), Alahayam, above the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens))! Let your kabawad (glory) be above all the aratz (Earth/land)!

They have kawan (prepared) a rashath (net) for my paim (steps). My napash (living being/soul) is kapap (bowed) down. They karah (dig) a shayachah (pit) panayam (before) me. They napal (fall / be cast down) into its thawak (midst) themselves. Salah (selah).
My lab (heart) is steadfast, Alahayam, my lab (heart) is steadfast. I will shayar (sing), yes, I will sing zamar (praises).
Iwar (rouse / awaken) up, my kabawad (glory)! Iwar (rouse / awaken) up, nabal (psaltery) and harp! I will iwar (rouse / awaken) up the dawn.
I will give yadah (thanks) to you, Adanay, among the im (people / nation). I will zamar (sing) praises to you among the laam (nations).
For your gadawal (very great/important/mighty) loving chasad (grace) reaches to the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), and your amath (truth) to the shachaq (skies).
Be rawam (will lift up), Alahayam, above the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)). Let your kabawad (glory) be over all the aratz (Earth/land).
Do you indeed dabar (word / matter) tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), silent alam (ones)? Do you shapat (judge) blamelessly, you ban (son) of adam (men)?
No, in your lab (heart) you plot injustice. You measure out the chamas (violence) of your yad (hand) in the aratz (Earth/land).
The rashai (wicked) zawar (go) astray from the racham (womb). They are wayward as soon as they are batan (born), dabar (word / matter) kazab (lies).
Their chamah (poison) is damawath (like) the chamah (poison) of a snake; like a charash (deaf) cobra that atam (stops) its azan (ear),
Which doesn't shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of lachash (charmers), no matter how skillful the chabar (charmer) may be.
Haras (break) their shan (teeth), Alahayam, in their pah (mouth). Nathatz (break) out the malathaih (great) teeth of the young kapayar (lions), Yahawah.
Let them vanish as mayam (Waters) that flows maas (away). When they darak (draw) the bow, let their chatz (arrows) be made blunt.
Let them be like a shabalawal (snail) which thamas (melts) and passes halak (move), like the stillborn child, who has not chazah (seen) the shamash (sun).
Before your sayar (pots) can bayan (between) the heat of the atad (thorns), he will sweep away the green and the burning alike.
The tzadayaq (righteous) shall shamach (rejoice) when he chazah (sees) the naqam (vengeance). He shall rachatz (wash) his paim (feet) in the dam (blood) of the rashai (wicked);
So that adam (men) shall amar (spoke), Most certainly there is a paray (reward) for the tzadayaq (righteous). Most certainly there is a Alahayam who shapat (judges) the aratz (Earth/land).
Natzal (deliver) me from my ayab (enemy), my Alahayam. Shagab (set) me on high from those who qawam (rise up) up against me.
Natzal (deliver) me from the pail (workers) of awan (iniquity). Yashai (salvation) me from the bloodthirsty ayash (husband/individual man).
For, behold, they lie in arab (wait) for my napash (living being/soul). The iz (mighty) gawar (gather) themselves together against me, not for my disobedience, nor for my chataah (sin), Yahawah.
I have done no wrong, yet they are kawan (ready) to attack me. Iwar (rouse / awaken) up, raah (see), and qaraah (help) me!

You, Yahawah Alahayam of tzabaa (troop), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), rouse yourself to paqad (visit) the gaway (nation / people). Show no chanan (mercy) to the awan (wicked) traitors. Salah (selah).
They shawab (turn back / repent) at irab (evening), howling like kalab (dogs), and prowl around the iyar (city).
Behold, they spew with their pah (mouth). Charab (sword) are in their shapah (lips), "For," they say, who shamai (hearken / hear) us?
But you, Yahawah, shachaq (laugh) at them. You scoff at all the gaway (nation / people).
Oh, my iz (strength / might / refuge), I shamar (keep/guard) for you, for Alahayam is my high tower.
My Alahayam will qadam (go) before me with his loving chasad (grace). Alahayam will raah (see) me look at my sharar (enemies) in triumph.

Don't harag (kill) them, or my im (people / nation) may shakach (forget). Nawai (scatter) them by your chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), and yarad (bring) them down, Adanay our magan (shield).

For the chataah (sin) of their pah (mouth), and the dabar (word / matter) of their shapah (lips), let them be lakad (caught) in their gaawan (pride), for the alah (these) and kachash (lies) which they utter.

Kalah (complete / finish) them in chamah (wrath). Kalah (complete / finish) them, and they yadai (will) be no more. Let them know that Alahayam mashal (rule/have dominion) in Yaiqab (Jacob), to the apas (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land). Salah (selah).
At irab (evening) let them shawab (turn back / repent). Let them howl like a kalab (dog), and sabab (go) around the iyar (city).
They shall nawai (wander) up and down for akal (eat), and wait all night if they aren't shabai (satisfied).

But I will shayar (sing) of your iz (strength / might / refuge). Yes, I will ranan (sing) aloud of your loving chasad (grace) in the baqar (morning). For you have been my high tower, a manawas (refuge) in the yawam (day) of my tzar (oppressor / distressor).
To you, my iz (strength / might / refuge), I will zamar (sing) praises. For Alahayam is my high tower, the Alahayam of my chasad (grace).
Alahayam, you have rejected us. You have paratz (broken) us down. You have been anap (angry). Shawab (turn back / repent) us, again.
You have made the aratz (Earth/land) raish (tremble). You have torn it. Mend its fractures, for it quakes.
You raah (see) shown your im (people / nation) qashah (rough / hard) things. You have shaqah (made) us drink the yayan (wine) that makes us stagger.
You nathan (give) given a nas (banner) to those who yaraa (fear) you, that it may be nawas (displayed) panayam (because) of the qashat (truth). Salah (selah).
So that your yadayad (beloved) may be chalatz (delivered), chalatz (save) with your right yamayan (right hand), and inah (oppress / afflict) us.

Alahayam has dabar (word / matter) from his qadash (set apart/make holy): I will ilaz (triumph). I will chalaq (divide) Shakam (Shechem), and madad (measure) out the imaq (valley) of Sakawath (Succoth).
Galaid (Gilead) is mine, and Manashah (Manasseh) is mine. Aparayam (Ephraim) also is the defense of my raash (head). Yahawadah (Judah) is my scepter.
Mawaab (Moab) is my wash basin. I will shalak (throw) my nail (shoe) on Adam (Edom). I rawai (shout) in triumph over Palashath (Philistia).
Who will yabal (bring) me into the matzawar (strong) iyar (city)? Who has nachah (led) me to Adam (Edom)?
Haven't you, Alahayam, rejected us? You don't go out with our armies, Alahayam.
Yahab (give) us izarah (help) against the tzar (oppressor / distressor), for the thashawaih (deliverance) of adam (man) is shawaa (vanity).
Through Alahayam we shall ishah (make) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), for it is he who will bawas (tread) down our tzar (oppressor / distressor).
Shamai (hearken / hear) my ranah (cry), Alahayam. Listen to my thapalah (prayer).

From the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land), I will qaraa (called) to you, when my lab (heart) is itap (overwhelmed). Nachah (lead) me to the tzawar (rock) that is higher than I.
For you have been a machasah (refuge) for me, a iz (strength / might / refuge) magadal (tower) from the ayab (enemy).
I will gawar (dwell) in your ahal (tent) iwalam (forever). I will take chasah (refuge) in the shelter of your kanap (wings). Salah (selah).
For you, Alahayam, have shamai (hearken / hear) my nadar (vow). You nathan (give) given me the yarashah (heritage) of those who yaraa (fear) your sham (name).
You will yasap (prolong) the malak (king) yawam (day); his shanah (years) shall be for dawar (generation / age / period).
He shall be enthroned in alahayam (Alahayam) panayam (presence) iwalam (forever). Appoint your loving chasad (grace) and amath (truth), that they may natzar (preserve) him.
So I will zamar (sing) praise to your sham (name) id (forever), that I may fulfill my nadar (vow) yawam (day).
My napash (living being/soul) dawamayah (rests) in Alahayam alone. My yashawaih (salvation) is from him.
He alone is my tzawar (rock) and my yashawaih (salvation), my fortress— I will never be greatly mawat (shaken).
How long will you assault a ayash (husband/individual man), would all of you throw him down, Like a leaning qayar (wall), like a dachah (tottering) gadar (fence)?
They fully intend to throw him down from his lofty place. They ratzah (delight) in kazab (lies). They barak (bless) with their pah (mouth), but they qalal (curse) inwardly. Salah (selah).
My napash (living being/soul), damam (wait) in silence for Alahayam alone, for my thaqawah (expectation) is from him.
He alone is my tzawar (rock) and my yashawaih (salvation), my fortress. I will not be mawat (shaken).
With Alahayam is my yashai (salvation) and my honor. The tzawar (rock) of my iz (strength / might / refuge), and my machasah (refuge), is in Alahayam.
Batach (trust) in him at all ith (times), you im (people / nation). Shapak (pour) out your labab (heart) panayam (before) him. Alahayam is a machasah (refuge) for us. Salah (selah).

Surely adam (men) of low degree are just a habal (breath), and ayash (husband/individual man) of high degree are a kazab (lie). In the maazan (balances) they will go up. They are yachad (together) lighter than a habal (breath).
Don't batach (trust) in ishaq (oppression). Don't habal (become) vain in gazal (robbery). If riches nawab (increase), don't shayath (put / appoint / make) your lab (heart) on them.
Alahayam has dabar (word / matter) achad (one); shanayam (two) I have shamai (hearken / hear) zaw (this), that iz (strength / might / refuge) belongs to Alahayam.
Also to you, Adanay, belongs loving chasad (grace), for you shalam (reward) every ayash (husband/individual man) according to his maishah (work).

Alahayam, you are my Alahayam. I will earnestly shachar (seek) you. My napash (living being/soul) tzamaa (thirsts) for you. My bashar (flesh) kamah (longs) for you, in a tzayah (dry) and iyap (weary) aratz (Earth/land), balay (where) there is no mayam (Waters).
So I have chazah (seen) you in the kabawad (sanctuary), watching your iz (strength / might / refuge) and your kabawad (glory).
Because your loving chasad (grace) is tawab (pleasant/functional) than chay (life), my shapah (lips) shall shabach (praise) you.
So I will barak (bless) you while I chay (life). I will nashaa (lift) up my kap (hands) in your sham (name).
My napash (living being/soul) shall be shabai (satisfied) as with the richest food. My pah (mouth) shall halal (praise) you with rananah (joyful) shapah (lips),
When I zakar (remembrance/memory) you on my yatzawai (bed), and think about you in the ashamarah (night) watches.
For you have been my izarah (help). I will ranan (rejoice) in the tzal (shadow) of your kanap (wings).
My napash (living being/soul) stays dabaq (close) to you. Your right yamayan (right hand) thamak (holds) me up.
But those who baqash (seek) my napash (living being/soul), to shawaa (vanity) it, shall bawaa (come) into the lower thachathay (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land).
They shall be given over to the yad (hand) of the sword. They shall be jackal food.

But the malak (king) shall shamach (rejoice) in Alahayam. Everyone who shabai (swear / take oath) by him will halal (praise) him, for the pah (mouth) of those who dabar (word / matter) shaqar (lies) shall be silenced.
Shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice), Alahayam, in my shayach (complaint). Natzar (preserve) my chay (life) from pachad (fear / dread) of the ayab (enemy).
Sathar (hide) me from the conspiracy of the raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil), from the noisy crowd of the ones pail (doing) awan (evil);
Who shanan (sharpen) their lashawan (tongue/language) like a charab (sword), and aim their chatz (arrows), deadly dabar (word / matter),
To yarah (shoot) innocent men from ambushes. They yarah (shoot) at him pathaawam (suddenly) and fearlessly.
They chazaq (encourage) themselves in rai (evil) plans. They sapar (book) about taman (laying) mawaqash (snares) secretly. They amar (spoke), Who will raah (see) them?
They plot injustice, saying, "We thamam (have) made a perfect plan!" Surely ayash (husband/individual man) qarab (among / near) and qarab (among / near) are cunning.
But Alahayam will yarah (shoot) at them. They will be pathaawam (suddenly) struck down with an chatz (arrow).
Their own lashawan (tongue/language) shall kashal (stumble / stagger) them. All who raah (see) them will shake their nadad (heads).
All mankind shall be yaraa (fear / be afraid). They shall nagad (declare) the pail (work) of Alahayam, and shall shakal (wisely) ponder what he has maishah (done).
The tzadayaq (righteous) shall be shamach (glad) in Yahawah, and shall take chasah (refuge) in him. All the yashar (upright) in lab (heart) shall halal (praise) him!
Thahalah (praise) waits for you, Alahayam, in Tzayawan (Zion). To you shall nadar (vow) be shalam (performed).
You who shamai (hearken / hear) thapalah (prayer), to you all men will bawaa (come).
Dabar (word / matter) overwhelmed me, but you atoned for our pashai (transgressions).

Ashar (who/that) is one whom you bachar (choose), and cause to qarab (come close) near, that he may live in your chatzar (courts). We will be shabai (filled) with the goodness of your bayath (house), your qadawash (holy) hayakal (temple).

By awesome deeds of tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), you inah (answer / respond) us, Alahayam of our yashai (salvation). You who are the mabatach (hope) of all the qatzaw (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land), of those who are rachawaq (far) away on the yam (sea/waters);
Who by his kach (strength / mighty / power) forms the har (mountain), having armed yourself with gabawarah (strength);
Who stills the roaring of the yam (sea/waters), the roaring of their gal (waves), and the turmoil of the laam (nations).

They also who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in faraway places are yaraa (fear / be afraid) at your awath (sign / mark / miracle). You call the baqar (morning) dawn and the irab (evening) with songs of ranan (joy).

You paqad (visit) the aratz (Earth/land), and shawaq (water) it. You greatly enrich it. The palag (river) of Alahayam is malaa (full) of mayam (Waters). You kawan (provide) them grain, for so you have kawan (ordained) it.
You drench its thalam (furrows). You nachath (level) its thalam (ridges). You soften it with rabayab (showers). You barak (bless) it with a crop.
You itar (crown) the shanah (year) with your bounty. Your carts overflow with abundance.
The madabar (wilderness) grasslands overflow. The gabaih (hills) are clothed with gayal (gladness).
The kar (pastures) are covered with tzaan (flocks). The imaq (valleys) also are clothed with grain. They rawai (shout) for joy! They also shayar (sing).
Rawai (make) a joyful shout to Alahayam, all the aratz (Earth/land)!
Zamar (sing) to the kabawad (glory) of his sham (name)! Offer kabawad (glory) and thahalah (praise)!
Amar (spoke) Alahayam, "How awesome are your maishah (deeds)! Through the greatness of your iz (strength / might / refuge), your ayab (enemy) kachash (submit) themselves to you.
All the aratz (Earth/land) will shachah (worship) you, and will zamar (sing) to you; they will zamar (sing) to your sham (name)." Salah (selah).
Yalak (come), and raah (see) alahayam (Alahayam) deeds— awesome mapail (work) on behalf of the ban (son) of adam (men).
He hapak (turned) the yam (sea/waters) into yabashah (dry land) land. They ibar (pass over/through) through the nahar (river) on ragal (feet / foot). There, we shamach (rejoiced) in him.

He mashal (rule/have dominion) by his gabawarah (might) iwalam (forever). His iyan (eye) tzapah (watchman / keep watch) the gaway (nation / people). Don't let the sarar (rebellious) rawam (will lift up) up against him. Salah (selah).
Barak (praise) our Alahayam, you im (people / nation)! Make the qawal (sound / voice) of his thahalah (praise) shamai (hearken / hear),
Who shawam (place / establish / appoint) our napash (living being/soul) among the chay (life), and doesn't allow our ragal (feet / foot) to be mawat (moved).
For you, Alahayam, have tested us. You have tzarap (refined) us, as kasap (silver) is tzarap (refined).
You bawaa (come) us into prison. You shawam (place / establish / appoint) a burden on our backs.
You allowed anawash (men) to rakab (ride) over our raash (head). We bawaa (come) through ash (fire) and through mayam (Waters), but you yatzaa (go out / come out) us to the place of abundance.
I will bawaa (come) into your bayath (house) with burnt ilah (offerings). I will shalam (pay) my nadar (vow) to you,
Which my shapah (lips) promised, and my pah (mouth) spoke, when I was in tzar (oppressor / distressor).
I will ilah (go up / offer) to you burnt ilah (offerings) of fat animals, with the qatarath (offering) of ayal (rams), I will ishah (make) baqar (morning) with ithawad (goats). Salah (selah).
Yalak (come), and shamai (hearken / hear), all you who yaraa (fear) Alahayam. I will sapar (book) what he ishah (make) done for my napash (living being/soul).
I qaraa (called) to him with my pah (mouth). He was rawamam (extolled) with my lashawan (tongue/language).
If I cherished sin in my lab (heart), the Adanay wouldn't have listened.
But most akan (certainly), Alahayam has shamai (hearken / hear). He has shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of my thapalah (prayer).
Barak (blessed) be Alahayam, who has not sawar (turned) away my thapalah (prayer), nor his loving chasad (grace) from me.
May Alahayam be chanan (merciful) to us, barak (bless) us, and cause his panayam (face) to awar (light) on us. Salah (selah).
That your darak (way) may be yadai (known) on aratz (Earth/land), and your yashawaih (salvation) among all gaway (nation / people),
Let the im (people / nation) yadah (praise) you, Alahayam. Let all the im (people / nation) yadah (praise) you.

Oh let the laam (nations) be shamach (glad) and ranan (sing) for joy, for you will shapat (judge) the im (people / nation) with mayashawar (equity), and nachah (govern) the laam (nations) on aratz (Earth/land). Salah (selah).
Let the im (people / nation) yadah (praise) you, Alahayam. Let all the im (people / nation) yadah (praise) you.
The aratz (Earth/land) nathan (give) yielded its yabawal (increase). Alahayam, even our own Alahayam, will barak (bless) us.
Alahayam will barak (bless) us. All the apas (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land) shall yaraa (fear / be afraid) him.
Let Alahayam qawam (rise up)! Let his ayab (enemy) be pawatz (scattered)! Let them who shanaa (hate) him also nawas (flee) panayam (before) him.

As ishan (smoke) is nadap (driven) away, so nadap (drive) them away. As dawanag (wax) masas (melts) panayam (before) the ash (fire), so let the rashai (wicked) abad (destroy/perish) at the panayam (presence) of Alahayam.
But let the tzadayaq (righteous) be shamach (glad). Let them ilatz (rejoice) panayam (before) Alahayam. Yes, let them shawash (rejoice) with shamachah (gladness).
Shayar (sing) to Alahayam! Sing zamar (praises) to his sham (name)! Salal (extol) him who rakab (rides) on the clouds: to Yah, his sham (name)! Ilaz (rejoice) panayam (before) him!
A ab (father) of the yathawam (fatherless), and a defender of the alamanah (widows), is Alahayam in his qadash (set apart/make holy) maiwan (habitation).

Alahayam yashab (inhabit/dwell) the lonely in bayath (house). He yatzaa (go out / come out) out the asayar (prisoners) with singing, but the sarar (rebellious) shakan (dwell) in a sun-scorched tzachayachah (land).
Alahayam, when you yatzaa (go out / come out) forth panayam (before) your im (people / nation), when you tzaid (marched) through the yashayamawan (wilderness)... Salah (selah).

The aratz (Earth/land) raish (trembled). The sky also poured down rain at the panayam (presence) of the Alahayam of Sayanay (Sinai)— at the panayam (presence) of Alahayam, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
You, Alahayam, nawap (sent) a nadabah (voluntary / freewill offering) gasham (rain). You kawan (confirmed) your nachalah (inheritance), when it was laah (weary).
Your chay (life) lived therein. You, Alahayam, kawan (prepared) your goodness for the inay (poor).
The Adanay announced the amar (spoke). The bashar (ones) who proclaim it are a rab (great) tzabaa (troop).
"Malak (king) of tzabaa (troop) nadad (flee)! They nadad (flee)!" She who waits at bayath (house) chalaq (divides) the shalal (spoil),
While you sleep among the campfires, the kanap (wings) of a yawanah (dove) sheathed with kasap (silver), her kanap (feathers) with shining charawatz (gold).
When the Shaday parash (scattered) malak (king) in her, it shalag (snow) on Tzalamawan (Zalmon).
The har (mountain) of Bashan are majestic har (mountain). The har (mountain) of Bashan (Bashan) are rugged.
Why do you look in envy, you rugged har (mountain), at the har (mountain) where Alahayam chooses to yashab (inhabit/dwell)? Yes, Yahawah will shakan (dwell) there natzach (forever).
The rakab (chariots) of Alahayam are rabaw (tens) of thousands and rabaw (thousands) of shanaan (thousands). The Adanay is among them, from Sayanay (Sinai), into the qadash (set apart/make holy).

You have ilah (go up / offer) on marawam (high). You have led shabay (away) shabay (captives). You have laqach (take / seized) mathanah (gifts) among adam (men), yes, among the sarar (rebellious) also, that Yah Alahayam might shakan (dwell) there.
Barak (blessed) be the Adanay, who yawam (day) imas (bears) our burdens, even the Al who is our yashawaih (salvation). Salah (selah).
Al is to us a Al of deliverance. To Yahawah, the Adanay, belongs escape from mawath (death).
But Alahayam will machatz (crush / shatter) through the raash (head) of his ayab (enemy), the shair (hair) qadaqad (scalp) of such a halak (move) as still continues in his asham (guiltiness).
The Adanay amar (spoke), I will shawab (turn back / repent) you again from Bashan (Bashan), I will shawab (turn back / repent) you again from the matzawalah (depths) of the yam (sea/waters);
That you may crush them, machatz (crush / shatter) your ragal (feet / foot) in dam (blood), that the lashawan (tongue/language) of your kalab (dogs) may have their portion from your ayab (enemy).
They raah (see) seen your processions, Alahayam, even the processions of my Al, my malak (king), into the qadash (set apart/make holy).
The singers qadam (went) before, the minstrels achar (other) after, in the thawak (midst) of the ladies thapap (playing) with tambourines,
Barak (bless) Alahayam in the maqahal (congregations), even the Adanay in the maqawar (assembly) of Yasharaal (Israel)!

There is tzaiyar (little) Banayamayan (Benjamin), their radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue), the shar (prince / ruler) of Yahawadah (Judah), their ragamah (council), the shar (prince / ruler) of Zabawalawan (Zebulun), and the shar (prince / ruler) of Napathalay (Naphtali).
Your Alahayam has tzawah (commanded) your iz (strength / might / refuge). Izaz (strengthen), Alahayam, that which you have pail (done) for us.
Because of your hayakal (temple) at Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), malak (king) shall yabal (bring) shay (presents) to you.

Gair (rebuke) the wild animal of the qanah (reeds), the idah (multitude) of the abayar (bulls), with the calves of the im (people / nation). Being rapas (humbled), may it bring bars of kasap (silver). Bazar (scatter) the im (people / nation) that chapatz (delight) in qarab (war).
Chashaman (princes) shall athah (come) out of Matzarayam (Egypt). Kawash (Ethiopia) shall hurry to stretch out her yad (hand) to Alahayam.
Shayar (sing) to Alahayam, you mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (Earth/land)! Sing zamar (praises) to the Adanay! Salah (selah).

To him who rakab (rides) on the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) of shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), which are of qadam (old); behold, he nathan (give) his qawal (sound / voice), a iz (strength / might / refuge) qawal (sound / voice).
Nathan (give) iz (strength / might / refuge) to Alahayam! His gaawah (excellency) is over Yasharaal (Israel), his iz (strength / might / refuge) is in the shachaq (skies).

You are awesome, Alahayam, in your maqadash (sanctuaries). The Al of Yasharaal (Israel) nathan (give) iz (strength / might / refuge) and iz (strength / might / refuge) to his im (people / nation). Barak (praise) be to Alahayam!
Yashai (salvation) me, Alahayam, for the mayam (Waters) bawaa (come) come up to my neck!
I tabai (sink) in matzawalah (deep) yawan (mire), where there is no foothold. I bawaa (come) come into maimaq (deep) mayam (Waters), where the shabal (floods) shatap (overflow) me.
I am yagai (weary) with my qaraa (called). My garawan (throat) is charar (dry). My iyan (eye) kalah (complete / finish), looking for my Alahayam.

Those who shanaa (hate) me chanam (without) a cause are more than the shairah (hairs) of my raash (head). Those who want to tzamath (cut) me off, being my ayab (enemy) shaqar (wrongfully), are itzam (mighty). I have to shawab (turn back / repent) what I didn't gazal (take) away.
Alahayam, you yadai (know) my awalath (foolishness). My ashamah (sins) aren't kachad (hidden) from you.

Don't let those who qawah (gather/wait) for you be bawash (shamed) through me, Adanay Yahawah of tzabaa (troop). Don't let those who baqash (seek) you be brought to dishonor through me, Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
Because for your sake, I have nashaa (lift) charapah (reproach). Kalamah (shame) has kasah (covered) my panayam (face).
I have become a stranger to my ach (brother/kinsman), an nakaray (alien) to my am (mother) ban (son).
For the qanaah (zeal) of your bayath (house) akal (eat) me. The reproaches of those who charap (reproach) you napal (fall / be cast down) fallen on me.
When I bakah (wept) and I tzawam (fasted), that was to my charapah (reproach).
When I nathan (give) sackcloth my labawash (clothing), I became a mashal (byword) to them.
Those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the shair (gate) shayach (meditate) about me. I am the nagayanah (song) of the drunkards.

But as for me, my thapalah (prayer) is to you, Yahawah, in an ratzawan (acceptable) ith (time). Alahayam, in the rab (abundance) of your loving chasad (grace), inah (answer / respond) me in the amath (truth) of your yashai (salvation).
Natzal (deliver) me out of the tayat (mire), and don't let me tabai (sink). Let me be natzal (delivered) from those who shanaa (hate) me, and out of the maimaq (deep) mayam (Waters).
Don't let the mayam (Waters) waters shatap (overwhelm) me, neither let the matzawalah (deep) balai (swallow) me up. Don't let the baar (pit) atar (shut) its pah (mouth) on me.
Inah (answer / respond) me, Yahawah, for your loving chasad (grace) is tawab (pleasant/functional). According to the rab (multitude) of your tender racham (mercies), panah (turn) to me.
Don't sathar (hide) your panayam (face) from your ibad (servant), for I am in tzarar (distress). Inah (answer / respond) me mahar (speedily)!
Qarab (come close) near to my napash (living being/soul), and gaal (redeem) it. Padah (ransom) me because of my ayab (enemy).
You yadai (know) my charapah (reproach), my charapah (shame), and my dishonor. My tzarar (adversaries) are all before you.

Charapah (reproach) has shabar (broken) my lab (heart), and I am nawash (full) of heaviness. I qawah (gather/wait) for some to nawad (take) pity, but there was none; for comforters, but I matzaa (found) none.
They also nathan (give) me raash (head) for my food. In my tzamaa (thirst), they gave me chamatz (vinegar) to shaqah (drink).
Let their shalachan (table) panayam (before) them become a pach (snare). May it become a retribution and a mawaqash (trap).
Let their iyan (eye) be chashak (darkness), so that they can't raah (see). Let their backs be continually bent.
Shapak (pour) out your zaim (indignation) on them. Let the charawan (fierceness) of your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) nashag (overtake) them.
Let their tayarah (habitation) be shamam (desolate). Let no one yashab (inhabit/dwell) in their ahal (tents).
For they radap (persecute) him whom you have wounded. They sapar (book) of the makaab (sorrow) of those whom you have hurt.
Nathan (give) them with crime upon crime. Don't bawaa (come) them come into your tzadaqah (righteousness).
Let them be machah (blotted) out of the sapar (book / scribed document) of chay (life), and not be kathab (written) with the tzadayaq (righteous).
But I am in pain and distress. Let your yashawaih (salvation), Alahayam, protect me.
I will halal (praise) the sham (name) of Alahayam with a shayar (song), and will gadal (magnify) him with thanksgiving.
It will yatab (please) Yahawah yatab (better) than an shawar (ox), or a shawar (bull) that has qaran (horns) and paras (hoofs).
The inaw (humble) raah (see) seen it, and are shamach (glad). You who darash (seek) after Alahayam, let your labab (heart) chayah (live).
For Yahawah shamai (hearken / hear) the abayawan (needy), and doesn't bazah (despise) his captive asayar (people).
Let shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) and aratz (Earth/land) halal (praise) him; the yam (sea/waters), and everything that ramash (moves) therein!
For Alahayam will yashai (salvation) Tzayawan (Zion), and banah (build) the iyar (cities) of Yahawadah (Judah). They shall settle there, and own it.
The zarai (children) also of his ibad (servant) shall nachal (inherit) it. Those who ahab (love) his sham (name) shall shakan (dwell) therein.
Hurry, Alahayam, to natzal (deliver) me. Come quickly to izarah (help) me, Yahawah.
Let them be disappointed and chapar (confounded) who baqash (seek) my napash (living being/soul). Let those who chapatz (desire) my ruin be sawag (turned) achawar (back) in disgrace.
Shawab (turn back / repent) them be turned iqab (award / effect after the cause) of their bashath (shame) Who amar (spoke), haach (aha)! Haach (aha)!
Let all those who baqash (seek) you shawash (rejoice) and be shamach (glad) in you. Let those who ahab (love) your yashawaih (salvation) continually amar (spoke), Let Alahayam be exalted!
But I am inay (poor) and abayawan (needy). Come to me quickly, Alahayam. You are my izar (help) and my deliverer. Yahawah, don't achar (other).
In you, Yahawah, I take chasah (refuge). Al (never) let me be disappointed.
Natzal (deliver) me in your tzadaqah (righteousness), and rescue me. Natah (turn) your azan (ear) to me, and yashai (salvation) me.
Be to me a tzawar (rock) of refuge to which I may thamayad (always) bawaa (come). Give the tzawah (command) to yashai (salvation) me, for you are my salai (rock) and my matzawad (fortress).
Rescue me, my Alahayam, from the yad (hand) of the rashai (wicked), from the yad (hand) of the unrighteous and chamatz (cruel) man.
For you are my thaqawah (hope), Adanay Yahawah; my mabatach (confidence) from my naiwar (youth).
I have relied on you from the batan (womb). You are he who gazah (took) me out of my am (mother) maih (womb). I will thamayad (always) thahalah (praise) you.
I am a marvel to many, but you are my iz (strength / might / refuge) machasah (refuge).
My pah (mouth) shall be malaa (filled) with your thahalah (praise), with your honor all the yawam (day).
Don't reject me in my zaqanah (old) age. Don't izab (forsake) me when my kach (strength / mighty / power) kalah (complete / finish).
For my ayab (enemy) amar (spoke) about me. Those who shamar (keep/guard) for my napash (living being/soul) conspire yachad (together),
Amar (spoke), Alahayam has forsaken him. Radap (pursue) and thapash (take) him, for no one will natzal (rescue) him.
Alahayam, don't be rachaq (far) from me. My Alahayam, hurry to izarah (help) me.
Let my accusers be disappointed and kalah (complete / finish). Let them be itah (covered) with disgrace and scorn who want to rai (harm) me.
But I will thamayad (always) yachal (hope), and will yasap (add) to all of your thahalah (praise).
My pah (mouth) will sapar (book) about your tzadaqah (righteousness), and of your thashawaih (deliverance) all yawam (day), though I don't yadai (know) its full measure.
I will bawaa (come) with the gabawarah (mighty) acts of the Adanay Yahawah. I will zakar (remembrance/memory) mention of your tzadaqah (righteousness), even of yours alone.
Alahayam, you have lamad (teach/instruct) me from my naiwar (youth). Until now, I have nagad (declared) your wondrous palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous).

Yes, even when I am zaqanah (old) and gray-haired, Alahayam, don't izab (forsake) me, until I have nagad (declared) your zarawai (strength) to the next dawar (generation / age / period), your gabawarah (might) to everyone who is to bawaa (come).
Your tzadaqah (righteousness) also, Alahayam, reaches to the marawam (heavens); you ishah (make) done gadawal (very great/important/mighty) things. Alahayam, who is like you?

You, who raah (see) shown us many and bitter tzarah (troubles), you will shawab (turn back / repent) me chayah (live). You will ilah (go up / offer) us up again from the thahawam (depths) of the aratz (Earth/land).
Rabah (increase) my honor, and nacham (turn away / repent) me again.
I will also yadah (praise) you with the harp for your amath (truth), my Alahayam. I zamar (sing) kanawar (praises) to you with the lyre, qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).
My shapah (lips) shall ranan (shout) for joy! My napash (living being/soul), which you have padah (redeemed), sings zamar (praises) to you!

My lashawan (tongue/language) will also hagah (talk) about your tzadaqah (righteousness) all yawam (day) bawash (long), for they are disappointed, and they are bawash (confounded), who want to rai (harm) me.
Alahayam, nathan (give) the malak (king) your mashapat (justice); your tzadaqah (righteousness) to the malak (king) ban (son).
He will dayan (judge) your im (people / nation) with tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and your inay (poor) with mashapat (justice).
The har (mountain) shall nashaa (lift) prosperity to the im (people / nation). The gabaih (hills) bring the fruit of tzadaqah (righteousness).
He will shapat (judge) the inay (poor) of the im (people / nation). He will yashai (salvation) the ban (son) of the abayawan (needy), and will break the oppressor in dakaa (pieces).
They shall yaraa (fear / be afraid) you while the shamash (sun) panayam (endures); and as long as the yarach (moon), throughout all dawar (generation / age / period).
He will yarad (come) down like matar (rain) on the gaz (mown) grass, as rabayab (showers) that zarazayap (water) the aratz (Earth/land).
In his yawam (day), the tzadayaq (righteous) shall parach (flourish), and rab (abundance) of shalawam (peace / safety), until the yarach (moon) is no more.
He shall radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) dominion also from yam (sea/waters) to yam (sea/waters), from the nahar (river) to the apas (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land).
Those who dwell in the tzayay (wilderness) shall karai (bow) panayam (before) him. His ayab (enemy) shall lachak (lick) the ipar (dust).
