Give yadah (thanks) to the Adawan of adawan (master / lord); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever):
To him who alone ishah (make) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever):
To him who by thabawan (understanding) ishah (make) the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever):
To him who raqai (spread) out the aratz (Earth/land) above the mayam (Waters); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever):
To him who ishah (make) the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) awar (light); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever):
The shamash (sun) to mamashalah (rule) by yawam (day); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever);
The yarach (moon) and kawakab (star) to mamashalah (rule) by layal (night); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever):
To him who nakah (struck) down the Matzarayam (Egyptian) bakawar (firstborn); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever);
And yatzaa (go out / come out) out Yasharaal (Israel) from thawak (midst) them; for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever);
With a chazaq (strong) yad (hand), and with an natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever):
To him who gazar (divided) the sawap (red) yam (sea/waters) apart; for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever);
And made Yasharaal (Israel) to ibar (pass over/through) through its thawak (midst); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever);
But overthrew Paraih (Pharaoh) and his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) in the sawap (red) yam (sea/waters); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever):
To him who yalak (led) his im (people / nation) through the madabar (wilderness); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever):
To him who nakah (struck) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) malak (king); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever);
And harag (killed) adayar (mighty) malak (king); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever):
Sayachawan (Sihon) malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever);
Iwag (Og) malak (king) of Bashan (Bashan); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever);
And nathan (give) their aratz (Earth/land) as an nachalah (inheritance); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever);
Even a nachalah (heritage) to Yasharaal (Israel) his ibad (servant); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever):
Who zakar (remembrance/memory) us in our shapal (low) estate; for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever);
And has paraq (delivered) us from our tzar (oppressor / distressor); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever):
Who nathan (give) lacham (food) to every creature; for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever).
Oh give yadah (thanks) to the Al of shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)); for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever).
By the nahar (rivers) of Babal (Babylon), there we yashab (inhabit/dwell) down. Yes, we bakah (wept), when we zakar (remembrance/memory) Tzayawan (Zion).
On the irab (evening) in its thawak (midst), we thalah (hung) up our kanawar (harps).

For there, those who shabah (led) us captive shaal (asked) us for dabar (word / matter). Those who tormented us demanded dabar (word / matter) of joy: shayar (sing) us one of the shayar (song) of Tzayawan (Zion)!
How can we shayar (sing) yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) shayar (song) in a foreign adamah (land)?
If I shakach (forget) you, Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), let my right yamayan (right hand) shakach (forget) its skill.

Let my lashawan (tongue/language) dabaq (stick) to the roof of my chak (mouth) if I don't zakar (remembrance/memory) you; if I don't ilah (go up / offer) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) above my raash (head) shamachah (joy).
Zakar (remembrance/memory), Yahawah, against the ban (son) of Adam (Edom), the yawam (day) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); who amar (spoke), Raze it! Raze it even to its yasawad (foundation)!
Bath (daughter) of Babal (Babylon), doomed to destruction, he will be ashar (who/that) who shalam (rewards) you, as you have gamal (served) us.
Ashar (who/that) shall he be, who achaz (takes) and dashes your iwalal (little) ones against the salai (rock).
I will give you yadah (thanks) with my whole lab (heart). Before the Alahayam, I will sing zamar (praises) to you.

I will shachah (bow) down toward your qadash (set apart/make holy) hayakal (temple), and give yadah (thanks) to your sham (name) for your loving chasad (grace) and for your amath (truth); for you have exalted your sham (name) and your amarah (sayings) above all.
In the yawam (day) that I qaraa (called), you inah (answer / respond) me. You encouraged me with iz (strength / might / refuge) in my napash (living being/soul).
All the malak (king) of the aratz (Earth/land) will give you yadah (thanks), Yahawah, for they have shamai (hearken / hear) the amar (spoke) of your pah (mouth).
Yes, they will shayar (sing) of the darak (ways) of Yahawah; for gadawal (very great/important/mighty) is yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) kabawad (glory).
For though Yahawah is rawam (will lift up), yet he raah (see) after the lowly; but the gabah (proud), he yadai (knows) from afar.

Though I yalak (walk) in the qarab (among / near) of tzarah (trouble), you will chayah (revive) me. You will shalach (send) forth your yad (hand) against the ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of my ayab (enemy). Your right yamayan (right hand) will yashai (salvation) me.
Yahawah will fulfill that which concerns me; your loving chasad (grace), Yahawah, endures iwalam (forever). Don't rapah (forsake) the maishah (works) of your own yad (hand).
Yahawah, you have chaqar (searched) me, and you yadai (know) me.
You yadai (know) my sitting down and my qawam (rise up) up. You bayan (between) my rai (thoughts) from rachawaq (afar).
You search out my arach (path) and my rabai (fourth) down, and are sakan (acquainted) with all my darak (ways).
For there is not a malah (word) on my lashawan (tongue/language), but, behold, Yahawah, you yadai (know) it altogether.
You hem me in achawar (behind) and qadam (before). You shayath (put / appoint / make) your kap (hand) on me.
This daith (knowledge) is beyond me. It's shagab (lofty). I can't yakal (attain) it.
Where could I yalak (go) from your rawach (spirit / wind)? Or where could I barach (flee) from your panayam (presence)?
If I nasaq (ascend) up into shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), you are there. If I yatzai (make) my bed in shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife), behold, you are there!
If I nashaa (lift) the kanap (wings) of the dawn, and settle in the uttermost parts of the yam (sea/waters);
Even there your yad (hand) will nachah (lead) me, and your right yamayan (right hand) will achaz (hold) me.
If I amar (spoke), Surely the chashak (darkness) will overwhelm me; the awar (light) around me will be layal (night);
Even the chashak (darkness) doesn't chashak (darkness) from you, but the layal (night) awar (light) as the yawam (day). The chashakah (darkness) is like awarah (light) to you.
For you formed my inmost being. You knit me together in my am (mother) batan (womb).

I will give yadah (thanks) to you, for I am fearfully and palah (wonderfully) made. Your maishah (works) are palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous). My napash (living being/soul) yadai (knows) that very maad (well).
My frame wasn't kachad (hidden) from you, when I was ishah (make) in sathar (secret / hidden), woven together in the depths of the aratz (Earth/land).
Your iyan (eye) raah (see) my body. In your sapar (book / scribed document) they were all kathab (written), the yawam (day) that were ordained for me, when as yet there were none of them.
How yaqar (precious) to me are your rai (thoughts), Al! How vast is their raash (head)!
If I would sapar (book) them, they are more in number than the chawal (sand). When I qawatz (wake) up, I am still with you.
If only you, Alawah, would qatal (kill) the rashai (wicked). Sawar (get) away from me, you bloodthirsty ayash (husband/individual man)!
For they amar (spoke) against you mazamah (wickedly). Your ir (enemies) nashaa (lift) your name in shawaa (vanity).
Yahawah, don't I shanaa (hate) those who shanaa (hate) you? Am I not grieved with those who thaqawamam (rise) up against you?
I shanaa (hate) them with thakalayath (perfect) hatred. They have become my ayab (enemy).
Chaqar (search) me, Al, and yadai (know) my labab (heart). Bachan (try) me, and yadai (know) my sharaip (thoughts).
Raah (see) if there is any itzab (wicked) darak (way) in me, and nachah (lead) me in the iwalam (forever) darak (way).
Chalatz (deliver) me, Yahawah, from the rai (evil) adam (man). Natzar (preserve) me from the chamas (violent) ayash (husband/individual man);
Those who chashab (devise) rai (mischief) in their lab (heart). They yawam (day) gawar (gather) themselves together for malachamah (war).
They have shanan (sharpened) their lashawan (tongue/language) like a nachash (serpent). Viper's chamah (poison) is under their shapah (lips). Salah (selah).
Yahawah, shamar (keep/guard) me from the yad (hand) of the rashai (wicked). Natzar (preserve) me from the chamas (violent) ayash (husband/individual man) who have determined to trip my paim (feet).

The gaah (proud) have taman (hidden) a pach (snare) for me, they have parash (spread) the chabal (cords) of a rashath (net) by the yad (hand). They have shayath (put / appoint / make) mawaqash (traps) for me. Salah (selah).
I amar (spoke) to Yahawah, "You are my Al." Listen to the qawal (sound / voice) of my petitions, Yahawah.
Yahawah, the Adanay, the iz (strength / might / refuge) of my yashawaih (salvation), you have sakak (covered) my raash (head) in the yawam (day) of nashaq (battle).
Yahawah, don't nathan (give) the maaway (desires) of the rashai (wicked). Don't let their rashai (evil) plans succeed, or they will become rawam (will lift up). Salah (selah).
As for the raash (head) of those who surround me, let the imal (mischief) of their own shapah (lips) kasah (cover) them.
Let burning gachal (coals) mawat (fall) on them. Napal (fall / be cast down) them be thrown into the ash (fire), into miry mahamarah (pits), from where they never qawam (rise up).

An ayash (husband/individual man) speaker won't be kawan (established) in the aratz (Earth/land). Rai (evil) will tzawad (hunt) the chamas (violent) ayash (husband/individual man) to madachapah (overthrow) him.
I yadai (know) that Yahawah will ishah (make) the dayan (judge) of the inay (afflicted), and mashapat (justice) for the abayawan (needy).
Surely the tzadayaq (righteous) will give yadah (thanks) to your sham (name). The yashar (upright) will yashab (inhabit/dwell) in your panayam (presence).
Yahawah, I have qaraa (called) on you. Come to me quickly! Listen to my qawal (sound / voice) when I qaraa (called) to you.
Let my thapalah (prayer) be kawan (set) panayam (before) you like qatarath (incense); the mashaath (lifting) up of my kap (hands) like the irab (evening) manachah (sacrifice).
Shayath (put / appoint / make) a shamarah (watch), Yahawah, before my pah (mouth). Natzar (keep) the dalath (door) of my shapah (lips).

Don't natah (incline) my lab (heart) to any rai (evil) thing, to practice ilayalah (deeds) of rashai (wickedness) with ayash (husband/individual man) who ilayalah (work) awan (iniquity). Don't let me lacham (eat) of their delicacies.

Let the tzadayaq (righteous) strike me, it is chasad (grace); let him yakach (reprove) me, it is like shaman (oil) on the raash (head); don't let my raash (head) refuse it; Yet my thapalah (prayer) is always against rai (evil) deeds.
Their shapat (judges) are shamat (thrown) down by the yad (hand) of the salai (rock). They will shamai (hearken / hear) my amar (spoke), for they are well spoken.
As when palach (one) plows and baqai (breaks) up the aratz (Earth/land), our itzam (bones) are pazar (scattered) at the pah (mouth) of shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife).
For my iyan (eye) are on you, Yahawah, the Adanay. In you, I take chasah (refuge). Don't irah (leave) my napash (living being/soul) irah (destitute).
Shamar (keep/guard) me from the snare which they have laid for me, from the mawaqash (traps) of the pail (workers) of awan (iniquity).
Let the rashai (wicked) napal (fall / be cast down) together into their own makamar (nets), while I ibar (pass over/through) by.
I zaiq (cry) with my qawal (sound / voice) to Yahawah. With my qawal (sound / voice), I ask Yahawah for chanan (mercy).
I shapak (pour) out my shayach (complaint) panayam (before) him. I nagad (tell) him my tzarah (troubles).
When my rawach (spirit / wind) was itap (overwhelmed) within me, you yadai (knew) my nathayab (path). In the arach (way) in which I halak (move), they have taman (hidden) a pach (snare) for me.

Nabat (look) on my yamayan (right hand), and raah (see); for there is no nakar (one) who is concerned for me. Manawas (refuge) abad (destroy/perish) fled from me. No one darash (cares) for my napash (living being/soul).
I zaiq (cried) to you, Yahawah. I amar (spoke), You are my machasah (refuge), my chalaq (portion) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life).
Listen to my ranah (cry), for I am in desperate need. Natzal (deliver) me from my persecutors, For they are amatz (stronger) than me.

Yatzaa (go out / come out) my napash (living being/soul) out of masagar (prison), that I may give yadah (thanks) to your sham (name). The tzadayaq (righteous) will surround me, for you will be gamal (good) to me.
Shamai (hearken / hear) my thapalah (prayer), Yahawah. Listen to my petitions. In your amawanah (faithfulness) and tzadaqah (righteousness), relieve me.
Don't bawaa (come) into mashapat (judgment) with your ibad (servant), for in your panayam (sight) no man chay (life) is tzadaq (righteous / just / fair).

For the ayab (enemy) radap (pursues) my napash (living being/soul). He has struck my chay (life) down to the aratz (Earth/land). He has yashab (inhabit/dwell) me live in machashak (dark) places, as those who have been iwalam (forever) mawath (death).
Therefore my rawach (spirit / wind) is itap (overwhelmed) within me. My lab (heart) thawak (midst) me is shamam (desolate).
I zakar (remembrance/memory) the yawam (day) of qadam (old). I hagah (meditate) on all your pail (doings). I contemplate the pail (work) of your yad (hand).
I parash (spread) forth my yad (hand) to you. My napash (living being/soul) thirsts for you, like a parched aratz (Earth/land). Salah (selah).

Hurry to inah (answer / respond) me, Yahawah. My rawach (spirit / wind) kalah (complete / finish). Don't sathar (hide) your panayam (face) from me, so that I don't mashal (speak in proverb/parable) like those who yarad (go) down into the bawar (pit).

Shamai (hearken / hear) me to hear your loving chasad (grace) in the baqar (morning), for I batach (trust) in you. Yadai (cause) me to know the darak (way) in which I should yalak (walk), for I nashaa (lift) up my napash (living being/soul) to you.
Natzal (deliver) me, Yahawah, from my ayab (enemy). I flee to you to kasah (hide) me.

Lamad (teach/instruct) me to ishah (make) your ratzawan (will), for you are my Alahayam. Your rawach (spirit / wind) is tawab (pleasant/functional). Nachah (lead) me in the aratz (Earth/land) of mayashawar (uprightness).
Chayah (revive) me, Yahawah, for your sham (name) sake. In your tzadaqah (righteousness), yatzaa (go out / come out) my napash (living being/soul) out of tzarah (trouble).
In your loving chasad (grace), tzamath (cut) off my ayab (enemy), and abad (destroy/perish) all those who tzarar (afflict) my napash (living being/soul), For I am your ibad (servant).
Barak (blessed) be Yahawah, my tzawar (rock), who teaches my yad (hand) to qarab (war), and my atzabai (fingers) to malachamah (battle):
My loving chasad (grace), my matzawad (fortress), my high tower, my deliverer, my magan (shield), and he in whom I take chasah (refuge); who radad (subdues) my im (people / nation) under me.
Yahawah, what is adam (man), that you care for him? Or the ban (son) of anawash (man), that you chashab (think) of him?
Adam (man) is damah (like) a habal (breath). His yawam (day) are like a tzal (shadow) that passes ibar (pass over/through).
Part your shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), Yahawah, and yarad (come) down. Nagai (touch) the har (mountain), and they will ishan (smoke).
Throw out baraq (lightning), and pawatz (scatter) them. Shalach (send) out your chatz (arrows), and rout them.
Shalach (send) out your yad (hand) from marawam (above), natzal (rescue) me, and natzal (deliver) me out of rab (great) mayam (Waters), out of the yad (hand) of foreigners;
Whose pah (mouths) dabar (word / matter) deceit, Whose right yamayan (right hand) is a right yamayan (right hand) of falsehood.
I will shayar (sing) a chadash (new) shayar (song) to you, Alahayam. On a ten-stringed lyre, I will sing zamar (praises) to you.
You are he who nathan (give) thashawaih (deliverance) to malak (king), who rescues Dawad (David), his ibad (servant), from the deadly charab (sword).
Rescue me, and natzal (deliver) me out of the yad (hand) of foreigners, whose pah (mouths) dabar (word / matter) deceit, whose right yamayan (right hand) is a right yamayan (right hand) of falsehood.
Then our ban (son) will be like well-nurtured natayai (plants), our bath (daughter) like pillars carved to adorn a hayakal (palace).
Our barns are malaa (full), filled with all kinds of provision. Our tzaan (sheep) bring forth alap (thousands) and ten alap (thousands) in our chawatz (fields).
Our oxen will pull heavy loads. There is no paratz (breaking) in, and no yatzaa (go out / come out) away, and no outcry in our rachab (streets).
Ashar (who/that) are the im (people / nation) who are in such a situation. Ashar (who/that) are the im (people / nation) whose Alahayam is Yahawah.
I will rawam (will lift up) you, my Alahayam, the malak (king). I will barak (praise) your sham (name) iwalam (forever) and iwalam (forever).
Every yawam (day) I will barak (praise) you. I will extol your sham (name) iwalam (forever) and iwalam (forever).
Gadawal (very great/important/mighty) is Yahawah, and maad (greatly) to be halal (praise)! His gadawalah (greatness) is unsearchable.
Dawar (generation / age / period) dawar (generation / age / period) will shabach (commend) your maishah (works) to another, and will nagad (declare) your gabawarah (mighty) acts.
Of the kabawad (glorious) majesty of your honor, of your palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) dabar (word / matter), I will shayach (meditate).
Men will amar (spoke) of the izawaz (might) of your awesome yaraa (fear / be afraid). I will sapar (book) your gadawalah (greatness).
They will nabai (utter) the zakar (remembrance/memory) of your rab (great) goodness, and will ranan (sing) of your tzadaqah (righteousness).
Yahawah is chanawan (gracious), rachawam (merciful), arak (slow) to ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and of gadawal (very great/important/mighty) loving chasad (grace).
Yahawah is tawab (pleasant/functional) to all. His tender racham (mercies) are over all his maishah (works).
All your maishah (works) will give yadah (thanks) to you, Yahawah. Your chasayad (saints) will extol you.
They will amar (spoke) of the kabawad (glory) of your malakawath (kingdom), and dabar (word / matter) about your gabawarah (power);
To yadai (make) known to the ban (son) of adam (men) his gabawarah (mighty) acts, the kabawad (glory) of the majesty of his malakawath (kingdom).

Your malakawath (kingdom) is an iwalam (forever) malakawath (kingdom). Your mamashalah (dominion) endures throughout all generations. Yahawah is faithful in all his words, and loving in all his deeds.
Yahawah samak (upholds) all who napal (fall / be cast down), and zaqap (raises) up all those who are kapap (bowed) down.
The iyan (eye) of all shabar (wait) for you. You nathan (give) them their akal (food) in due ith (season).
You pathach (open) your yad (hand), and shabai (satisfy) the ratzawan (desire) of every chay (life) thing.
Yahawah is tzadayaq (righteous) in all his darak (ways), and gracious in all his maishah (works).
Yahawah is qarawab (near) to all those who qaraa (called) on him, to all who qaraa (called) on him in amath (truth).
He will ishah (make) the ratzawan (desire) of those who yaraa (fear) him. He also will shamai (hearken / hear) their cry, and will yashai (salvation) them.
Yahawah shamar (keep/guard) all those who ahab (love) him, but all the rashai (wicked) he will shamad (destroy).
My pah (mouth) will dabar (word / matter) the thahalah (praise) of Yahawah. Let all bashar (flesh) barak (bless) his qadash (set apart/make holy) sham (name) id (forever) and iwalam (forever).
Halal (praise) Yah! Halal (praise) Yahawah, my napash (living being/soul).
While I chay (life), I will halal (praise) Yahawah. I will sing zamar (praises) to my Alahayam as long as I exist.
Don't batach (put) your trust in nadayab (princes), each a ban (son) of adam (man) in whom there is no thashawaih (deliverance).
His rawach (spirit / wind) departs, and he shawab (turn back / repent) to the adamah (earth). In that very yawam (day), his ishathanah (thoughts) abad (destroy/perish).
Ashar (who/that) is he who has the Al of Yaiqab (Jacob) for his izar (help), whose shabar (hope) is in Yahawah, his Alahayam:
Who ishah (make) shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) and aratz (Earth/land), the yam (sea/waters), and all that is in them; who shamar (keep/guard) amath (truth) iwalam (forever);
Who ishah (make) mashapat (justice) for the ishaq (oppressed); who nathan (give) lacham (food) to the raib (hungry). Yahawah frees the asar (prisoners).
Yahawah paqach (opens) the eyes of the iwar (blind). Yahawah zaqap (raises) up those who are kapap (bowed) down. Yahawah ahab (love) the tzadayaq (righteous).
Yahawah shamar (keep/guard) the foreigners. He upholds the yathawam (fatherless) and alamanah (widow), but the darak (way) of the rashai (wicked) he iwath (turns) upside down.
Yahawah will malak (king) iwalam (forever); your Alahayam, O Tzayawan (Zion), to all dawar (generation / age / period). Halal (praise) Yah!
Halal (praise) Yah, for it is tawab (pleasant/functional) to sing zamar (praises) to our Alahayam; for it is naiyam (pleasant) and fitting to thahalah (praise) him.
Yahawah banah (builds) up Yarawashalam (Jerusalem). He kanas (gathers) together the dachah (outcasts) of Yasharaal (Israel).
He rapaa (heals) the shabar (broken) in lab (heart), and chabash (binds) up their itzabath (wounds).
He manah (counts) the masapar (number) of the kawakab (star). He qaraa (called) them all by their sham (name).
Gadawal (very great/important/mighty) is our Adawan, and rab (mighty) in kach (strength / mighty / power). His thabawan (understanding) is masapar (infinite).
Yahawah upholds the inaw (humble). He shapal (brings) the rashai (wicked) down to the aratz (Earth/land).
Inah (answer / respond) to Yahawah with thanksgiving. Sing zamar (praises) on the kanawar (harp) to our Alahayam,
Who kasah (covers) the sky with ib (clouds), who kawan (prepares) matar (rain) for the aratz (Earth/land), who makes chatzayar (grass) tzamach (grow) on the har (mountain).
He provides lacham (food) for the livestock, and for the ban (son) irab (evening) when they qaraa (called).
He doesn't chapatz (delight) in the gabawarah (strength) of the sawas (horse). He ratzah (takes) no pleasure in the shawaq (legs) of a ayash (husband/individual man).
Yahawah ratzah (takes) pleasure in those who yaraa (fear) him, in those who yachal (hope) in his loving chasad (grace).
Shabach (praise) Yahawah, Yarawashalam (Jerusalem)! Halal (praise) your Alahayam, Tzayawan (Zion)!
For he has chazaq (strengthened) the barayach (bars) of your shair (gates). He has barak (blessed) your ban (son) inside you.
He shawam (place / establish / appoint) shalawam (peace / safety) in your gabawal (border/boundary). He shabai (fills) you with the chalab (finest) of the chatah (wheat).
He shalach (send) out his commandment to the aratz (Earth/land). His dabar (word / matter) rawatz (runs) very maharah (swiftly).
He nathan (give) shalag (snow) like tzamar (wool), and pazar (scatters) kapawar (frost) like ashes.
He shalak (hurls) down his hail like pebbles. Who can imad (stand) panayam (before) his qarah (cold)?
He shalach (send) out his dabar (word / matter), and masah (melts) them. He causes his rawach (spirit / wind) to nashab (blow), and the mayam (Waters) nazal (flow).
He shows his dabar (word / matter) to Yaiqab (Jacob); his chaq (statute) and his mashapat (ordinances) to Yasharaal (Israel).
He ishah (make) not done this for just any gaway (nation / people). They don't yadai (know) his mashapat (ordinances). Halal (praise) Yah!
Halal (praise) Yah! Halal (praise) Yahawah from the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens))! Halal (praise) him in the marawam (heights)!
Halal (praise) him, all his malaak (angel / messenger of Yah)! Halal (praise) him, all his tzabaa (troop)!
Halal (praise) him, shamash (sun) and yarach (moon)! Halal (praise) him, all you shining kawakab (star)!
Halal (praise) him, you shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) of shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), You mayam (Waters) that are above the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)).
Let them halal (praise) the sham (name) of Yahawah, For he tzawah (commanded), and they were baraa (created).
He has also imad (established) them id (forever) and id (ever). He nathan (give) made a chaq (statute) which will not ibar (pass over/through) away.
Halal (praise) Yahawah from the aratz (Earth/land), you great thanayan (sea) creatures, and all thahawam (depths)!
Lightning and barad (hail), shalag (snow) and clouds; sair (stormy) rawach (spirit / wind), ishah (make) his dabar (word / matter);
Har (mountain) and all gabaih (hills); paray (fruit) itz (trees) and all araz (cedars);
Wild animals and all livestock; small creatures and kanap (flying) tzapawar (birds);
Malak (king) of the aratz (Earth/land) and all laam (peoples); shar (prince / ruler) and all shapat (judges) of the aratz (Earth/land);
Both bachawar (young) men and maidens; zaqan (old) men and children:
Let them halal (praise) the sham (name) of Yahawah, for his sham (name) alone is shagab (exalted). His glory is above the aratz (Earth/land) and the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)).

He has rawam (will lift up) up the qaran (horn) of his im (people / nation), the thahalah (praise) of all his chasayad (saints); even of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), a im (people / nation) qarawab (near) to him. Halal (praise) Yah!
Halal (praise) Yahawah! Shayar (sing) to Yahawah a chadash (new) shayar (song), his thahalah (praise) in the qahal (assembly) of the chasayad (saints).
Let Yasharaal (Israel) shamach (rejoice) in him who ishah (make) them. Let the ban (son) of Tzayawan (Zion) be gayal (joyful) in their malak (king).
Let them halal (praise) his sham (name) in the machawal (dance)! Let them sing zamar (praises) to him with tambourine and kanawar (harp)!
For Yahawah ratzah (takes) pleasure in his im (people / nation). He paar (crowns) the inaw (humble) with yashawaih (salvation).
Let the chasayad (saints) rejoice in honor. Let them ranan (sing) for joy on their mashakab (beds).
May the rawamamah (high) praises of Al be in their garawan (mouths), and a payapayah (two-edged) charab (sword) in their yad (hand);
To ishah (make) naqamah (vengeance) on the gaway (nation / people), and punishments on the laam (peoples);
To asar (bind) their malak (king) with zayaqah (chains), and their kabad (nobles) with kabal (fetters) of barazal (iron);
To ishah (make) on them the kathab (written) mashapat (judgment). All his chasayad (saints) have this honor. Halal (praise) Yah!
Halal (praise) Yah! Halal (praise) Al in his qadash (set apart/make holy)! Halal (praise) him in his raqayai (Raqayai/(Firmament)) for his acts of iz (strength / might / refuge)!
Halal (praise) him for his gabawarah (mighty) acts! Halal (praise) him according to his rab (excellent) gadal (greatness)!
Halal (praise) him with the thaqai (blow / sound alarm) of the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument))! Halal (praise) him with harp and lyre!
Halal (praise) him with tambourine and machawal (dancing)! Halal (praise) him with man (from) instruments and flute!
Halal (praise) him with shamai (loud) tzalatzal (cymbals)! Halal (praise) him with resounding tzalatzal (cymbals)!
Let everything that has nashamah (breathing thing) halal (praise) Yah! Halal (praise) Yah!
The mashal (proverbs) of Shalamah (Solomon), the ban (son) of Dawad (David), malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel):
To yadai (know) chakamah (wisdom) and mawasar (instruction); to bayan (between) the amar (spoke) of bayanah (understanding);
To laqach (take / seized) mawasar (instruction) in shakal (wise) dealing, in tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and mayashar (equity);
To nathan (give) iramah (prudence) to the pathay (simple), daith (knowledge) and mazamah (discretion) to the nair (young) man:
That the chakam (wise) man may shamai (hearken / hear), and yasap (increase) in laqach (learning); that the bayan (between) of understanding may qanah (attain) to sound thachabalah (counsel):
To bayan (between) a mashal (proverb), and parables, the dabar (word / matter) and chayadah (riddles) of the chakam (wise).
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is the raashayath (beginning) of daith (knowledge); but the awayal (foolish) bawaz (despise) chakamah (wisdom) and mawasar (instruction).
My ban (son), shamai (hearken / hear) to your ab (father) mawasar (instruction), and don't natash (forsake) your am (mother) teaching:
For they will be a garland to chan (grace) your raash (head), and inaq (chains) around your garagarawath (neck).
My ban (son), if chataa (sinners) pathah (entice) you, don't abah (be willing / desire).
If they amar (spoke), yalak (come) with us, Let's arab (lay) in wait for dam (blood); let's tzapan (lurk) secretly for the naqay (innocent) chanam (without) cause;
Let's balai (swallow) them up chay (life) like shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife), and thamayam (complete / whole), like those who yarad (go) down into the bawar (pit).
We'll matzaa (find) all valuable hawan (wealth). We'll malaa (fill) our bayath (house) with shalal (spoil).
You shall napal (fall / be cast down) your gawaral (lot) thawak (midst) us. We'll all have achad (one) kayas (purse).
My ban (son), don't yalak (walk) in the darak (way) with them. Manai (keep) your ragal (feet / foot) from their nathayab (path),
For their ragal (feet / foot) rawatz (run) to rai (evil). They hurry to shapak (shed) dam (blood).
For in chanam (vain) is the rashath (net) zarah (spread) in the iyan (eye) of any bail (bird):
But these arab (lay) wait for their own dam (blood). They tzapan (lurk) secretly for their napash (living being/soul) lives.
So are the arach (ways) of everyone who is batzai (greedy) for batzai (gain). It laqach (take / seized) away the napash (living being/soul) of its owners.
Chakamawath (wisdom) calls aloud in the chawatz (street). She nathan (give) her qawal (sound / voice) in the public squares.
She qaraa (called) at the raash (head) of noisy raash (head). At the pathach (entrance) of the iyar (city) shair (gates), she amar (spoke) her amar (spoke):
How long, you pathay (simple) ones, will you ahab (love) simplicity? How long will lawatz (mockers) chamad (delight) themselves in mockery, and kasayal (fools) shanaa (hate) daith (knowledge)?
Shawab (turn back / repent) at my thawakachah (reproof). Behold, I will nabai (pour) out my rawach (spirit / wind) on you. I yadai (will) make known my dabar (word / matter) to you.
Because I have qaraa (called), and you have maan (refused); I have natah (stretched) out my yad (hand), and no qashab (one) has paid attention;
But you have ignored all my itzah (counsel), and wanted none of my thawakachah (reproof);
I also will shachaq (laugh) at your disaster. I will laig (mock) when calamity overtakes you;
When calamity overtakes you like a sawapah (storm), when your disaster athah (comes) on like a sawapah (whirlwind); when tzarah (distress) and tzawaq (anguish) bawaa (come) on you.
Then will they qaraa (called) on me, but I will not inah (answer / respond). They will shachar (seek) me diligently, but they will not matzaa (find) me;
Because they shanaa (hate) daith (knowledge), and didn't bachar (choose) the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah.
They wanted none of my itzah (counsel). They naatz (despised) all my thawakachah (reproof).
Therefore they will akal (eat) of the paray (fruit) of their own darak (way), and be shabai (filled) with their own schemes.
For the mashawabah (backsliding) of the pathay (simple) will harag (kill) them. The careless ease of kasayal (fools) will abad (destroy/perish) them.
But whoever shamai (hearken / hear) to me will shakan (dwell) securely, and will be at shaan (ease), without pachad (fear / dread) of rai (harm).
My ban (son), if you will laqach (take / seized) my amar (spoke), and store up my matzawah (commandments) within you;
So as to qashab (turn) your azan (ear) to chakamah (wisdom), and natah (apply) your lab (heart) to thabawan (understanding);
Yes, if you qaraa (called) out for discernment, and nathan (give) up your qawal (sound / voice) for thabawan (understanding);
If you baqash (seek) her as kasap (silver), and chapash (search) for her as for matamawan (hidden) treasures:
Then you will bayan (between) the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah, and matzaa (find) the daith (knowledge) of Alahayam.
For Yahawah nathan (give) chakamah (wisdom). Out of his pah (mouth) comes daith (knowledge) and thabawan (understanding).
He tzapan (lays) up sound thawashayah (wisdom) for the yashar (upright). He is a magan (shield) to those who halak (move) in tham (integrity);
That he may guard the arach (paths) of mashapat (justice), and shamar (keep/guard) the darak (way) of his chasayad (saints).
Then you will bayan (between) tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) and mashapat (justice), mayashar (equity) and every tawab (pleasant/functional) maigal (path).
For chakamah (wisdom) will bawaa (come) into your lab (heart). Daith (knowledge) will be naim (pleasant) to your napash (living being/soul).
Mazamah (discretion) will shamar (keep/guard) over you. Thabawan (understanding) will shamar (keep/guard) you,
To natzal (deliver) you from the darak (way) of rai (evil), from the ayash (husband/individual man) who dabar (word / matter) thahapakah (perverse) things;
Who izab (forsake) the arach (paths) of yashar (uprightness), to yalak (walk) in the darak (ways) of chashak (darkness);
Who shamach (rejoice) to ishah (make) rai (evil), and delight in the perverseness of rai (evil);
Who are iqash (crooked) in their arach (ways), and wayward in their maigal (paths):
To natzal (deliver) you from the zawar (strange) ashah (wife/individual woman), even from the nakaray (foreigner) who chalaq (flatters) with her amar (spoke);
Who izab (forsakes) the alawap (friend) of her naiwar (youth), and shakach (forgets) the barayath (covenant) of her Alahayam:
For her bayath (house) leads down to mawath (death), her maigal (paths) to the rapaa (dead).
None who bawaa (come) to her shawab (turn back / repent) again, neither do they nashag (attain) to the arach (paths) of chay (life):
That you may yalak (walk) in the darak (way) of tawab (pleasant/functional) men, and shamar (keep/guard) the arach (paths) of the tzadayaq (righteous).
For the yashar (upright) will shakan (dwell) in the aratz (Earth/land). The thamayam (complete / whole) will yathar (remain) in it.
But the rashai (wicked) will be karath (cut) off from the aratz (Earth/land). The bagad (treacherous) will be nasach (rooted) out of it.
My ban (son), don't shakach (forget) my teaching; but let your lab (heart) natzar (keep) my matzawah (commandments):
For arak (length) of yawam (day), and shanah (years) of chay (life), and shalawam (peace / safety), will they yasap (add) to you.
Don't let chasad (grace) and amath (truth) izab (forsake) you. Qashar (bind) them around your garagarawath (neck). Kathab (write) them on the tablet of your lab (heart).
So you will matzaa (find) favor, and tawab (pleasant/functional) shakal (understanding) in the iyan (eye) of Alahayam and adam (man).
Batach (trust) in Yahawah with all your lab (heart), and don't shain (lean) on your own bayanah (understanding).
In all your darak (ways) yadai (acknowledge) him, and he will make your arach (paths) yashar (straight).
Don't be chakam (wise) in your own iyan (eye). Yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah, and sawar (depart) from rai (evil).
It will be rapaawath (health) to your body, and nourishment to your itzam (bones).
Honor Yahawah with your hawan (substance), with the raashayath (beginning) fruits of all your thabawaah (increase):
So your asam (barns) will be malaa (filled) with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new thayarawash (wine).
My ban (son), don't maas (despise) yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) mawasar (discipline), neither be qawatz (weary) of his thawakachah (reproof):
For whom Yahawah ahab (love), he yakach (reproves); even as a ab (father) reproves the ban (son) in whom he ratzah (delights).
Ashar (who/that) is the adam (man) who matzaa (finds) chakamah (wisdom), the adam (man) who pawaq (gets) thabawan (understanding).
For her sachar (good) profit is tawab (pleasant/functional) than getting kasap (silver), and her thabawaah (return) is better than fine charawatz (gold).
She is more yaqar (precious) than panayan (rubies). None of the things you can chapatz (desire) are to be shawah (compared) to her.
Arak (length) of yawam (day) is in her right yamayan (right hand). In her left shamaawal (left hand) are riches and honor.
Her darak (ways) are darak (ways) of naim (pleasantness). All her nathayab (paths) are shalawam (peace / safety).
She is a itz (tree) of chay (life) to those who lay chazaq (hold) of her. Ashar (who/that) is everyone who thamak (retains) her.
By chakamah (wisdom) Yahawah founded the aratz (Earth/land). By chakamah (understanding), he kawan (established) the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)).
By his daith (knowledge), the thahawam (depths) were baqai (broken) up, and the shachaq (skies) raip (drop) down the tal (dew).
My ban (son), let them not depart from your iyan (eye). Natzar (keep) sound thawashayah (wisdom) and discretion:
So they will be chay (life) to your napash (living being/soul), and chan (grace) for your garagarawath (neck).
Then you shall yalak (walk) in your darak (way) securely. Your ragal (feet / foot) won't nagap (stumble).
When you shakab (lie) down, you will not be pachad (fear / dread). Yes, you will shakab (lie) down, and your shanah (sleep) will be irab (evening).
Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of pathaawam (sudden) pachad (fear / dread), neither of the shawaa (vanity) of the rashai (wicked), when it bawaa (come):
For Yahawah will be your kasal (confidence), and will shamar (keep/guard) your ragal (feet / foot) from lakad (being) taken.
Don't manai (withhold) tawab (pleasant/functional) from bail (those) to whom it is due, when it is in the al (power) of your yad (hand) to ishah (make) it.
Don't amar (spoke) to your neighbor, "yalak (go), and shawab (turn back / repent) again; machar (tomorrow) I will nathan (give) it to you," when you yash (have) it by you.
Don't charash (devise) rai (evil) against your neighbor, since he yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely by you.
Don't rayab (strive) with a adam (man) chanam (without) cause, if he has gamal (done) you no rai (harm).
Don't qanaa (jealous) the ayash (husband/individual man) of violence. Bachar (choose) none of his darak (ways).
For the lawaz (perverse) is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, but his friendship is with the yashar (upright).
Yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) maarah (curse) is in the bayath (house) of the rashai (wicked), but he blesses the nawah (habitation) of the tzadayaq (righteous).
Surely he lawatz (mocks) the lawatz (mockers), but he nathan (give) chan (grace) to the inay (humble).
The chakam (wise) will nachal (inherit) kabawad (glory), but qalawan (shame) will be the rawam (will lift up) of kasayal (fools).
Shamai (hearken / hear), ban (son), to a ab (father) mawasar (instruction). Pay attention and yadai (know) bayanah (understanding);
For I nathan (give) you sound laqach (learning). Don't izab (forsake) my thawarah (instruction).
For I was a ban (son) to my ab (father), rak (tender) and an only child in the panayam (sight) of my am (mother).
He yarah (taught) me, and amar (spoke) to me: Let your lab (heart) thamak (retain) my dabar (word / matter). Shamar (keep/guard) my matzawah (commandments), and chayah (live).
Qanah (get) chakamah (wisdom). Qanah (get) bayanah (understanding). Don't shakach (forget), neither swerve from the amar (spoke) of my pah (mouth).
Don't izab (forsake) her, and she will shamar (keep/guard) you. Ahab (love) her, and she will natzar (keep) you.
Chakamah (wisdom) is supreme. Qanah (get) chakamah (wisdom). Yes, though it costs all your qanayan (possessions), get bayanah (understanding).
Esteem her, and she will salal (exalt) you. She will kabad (bring) you to honor, when you chabaq (embrace) her.
She will nathan (give) to your raash (head) a garland of chan (grace). She will magan (deliver) a itarah (crown) of splendor to you.
Shamai (hearken / hear), my ban (son), and laqach (take / seized) my amar (spoke). The shanah (years) of your chay (life) will be many.
I have yarah (taught) you in the darak (way) of chakamah (wisdom). I have darak (led) you in yashar (straight) maigal (paths).
When you yalak (go), your tzaid (steps) will not be hampered. When you rawatz (run), you will not kashal (stumble / stagger).
Chazaq (take) firm hold of mawasar (instruction). Don't rapah (let) her go. Natzar (keep) her, for she is your chay (life).
Don't bawaa (come) into the arach (path) of the rashai (wicked). Don't walk in the darak (way) of rai (evil) men.
Parai (avoid) it, and don't ibar (pass over/through) by it. Shatah (turn) from it, and ibar (pass over/through) on.
For they don't sleep, unless they do raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil). Their shanah (sleep) is gazal (taken) away, unless they kashal (stumble / stagger) someone fall.
For they lacham (eat) the lacham (bread) of rashai (wickedness), and shathah (drinks) the yayan (wine) of chamas (violence).
But the arach (path) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is like the dawning awar (light), that awar (light) more and more until the kawan (perfect) yawam (day).
The darak (way) of the rashai (wicked) is like apalah (darkness). They don't yadai (know) what they kashal (stumble / stagger) over.
My ban (son), qashab (attend) to my dabar (word / matter). Natah (turn) your azan (ear) to my amar (spoke).
Let them not depart from your iyan (eye). Shamar (keep/guard) them in the thawak (midst) of your thawak (midst).
For they are chay (life) to those who matzaa (find) them, and marapaa (health) to their whole bashar (flesh).
Natzar (keep) your lab (heart) with all mashamar (diligence), for out of it is the wellspring of chay (life).
Sawar (put) away from yourself a perverse pah (mouth). Put corrupt shapah (lips) rachaq (far) from you.
Let your iyan (eye) nabat (look) nakach (straight) ahead. Fix your gaze directly before you.
Make the maigal (path) of your ragal (feet / foot) level. Let all of your darak (ways) be kawan (established).
Don't natah (turn) to the right yamayan (right hand) nor to the shamaawal (left hand). Sawar (remove) your ragal (feet / foot) from rai (evil).
My ban (son), pay attention to my chakamah (wisdom). Natah (turn) your azan (ear) to my thabawan (understanding):
That you may maintain mazamah (discretion), that your shapah (lips) may natzar (preserve) daith (knowledge).
For the shapah (lips) of an adulteress drip honey. Her chak (mouth) is smoother than shaman (oil),
But in the acharayath (end) she is as mar (bitter) as lainah (wormwood), and as chad (sharp) as a pah (two-edged) charab (sword).
Her ragal (feet / foot) yarad (go) down to mawath (death). Her tzaid (steps) lead thamak (straight) to shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife).
She gives no thought to the maigal (way) of chay (life). Her maigal (ways) are crooked, and she doesn't yadai (know) it.
Now therefore, my ban (son), shamai (hearken / hear) to me. Don't sawar (depart) from the amar (spoke) of my pah (mouth).
Rachaq (remove) your darak (way) rachaq (far) from her. Don't qarab (come close) near the pathach (door) of her bayath (house),
Lest you nathan (give) your honor to others, and your shanah (years) to the akazaray (cruel) one;
Lest strangers feast on your kach (strength / mighty / power), and your itzab (labors) enrich another nakaray (man's) bayath (house).
You will groan at your acharayath (latter) end, when your bashar (flesh) and your bashar (flesh) are kalah (complete / finish),
And amar (spoke), How I have shanaa (hate) mawasar (instruction), and my lab (heart) naatz (despised) thawakachah (reproof);
Neither have I shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of my teachers, nor natah (turned) my azan (ear) to those who lamad (teach/instruct) me!
I have come to the brink of utter ruin, in the thawak (midst) of the gathered qahal (assembly).
Shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters) out of your own bawar (cistern), running nazal (water) out of your own baar (well).
Should your maiyan (springs) overflow in the rachab (streets), palag (streams) of mayam (Waters) in the public squares?
Let them be for yourself zawar (alone), not for strangers with you.
Let your maqawar (spring) be barak (blessed). Shamach (rejoice) in the ashah (wife/individual woman) of your naiwar (youth).
A ahab (love) doe and a graceful deer— let her dad (breasts) rawah (satisfy) you at all ith (times). Be captivated thamayad (always) with her ahabah (love).
For why should you, my ban (son), be captivated with an adulteress? Why chabaq (embrace) the chayaq (bosom) of another?
For the darak (ways) of ayash (husband/individual man) are nakach (before) the iyan (eye) of Yahawah. He examines all his maigal (paths).
The iwan (guilt/iniquity) deeds of the rashai (wicked) ensnare him. The chabal (cords) of his chataah (sin) thamak (hold) him firmly.
He will mawath (death) for lack of mawasar (instruction). In the greatness of his awalath (folly), he will shagah (go) astray.
My ban (son), if you have become collateral for your neighbor, if you have thaqai (blow / sound alarm) your kap (hands) in pledge for a stranger;
You are trapped by the amar (spoke) of your pah (mouth). You are ensnared with the amar (spoke) of your pah (mouth).

Ishah (make) this apaw (now), my ban (son), and natzal (deliver) yourself, since you bawaa (come) come into the kap (hand) of your neighbor. Yalak (go), rapas (humble) yourself. Press your plea with your neighbor.
Nathan (give) no shanah (sleep) to your iyan (eye), nor thanawamah (slumber) to your ipaip (eyelids).
Free yourself, like a gazelle from the yad (hand) of the hunter, like a tzapawar (bird) from the snare of the yaqawash (fowler).
Yalak (go) to the namalah (ant), you itzal (sluggard). Raah (see) her darak (ways), and be chakam (wise);
Which having no chief, shatar (overseer), or mashal (rule/have dominion),
Kawan (provides) her lacham (bread) in the qayatz (summer), and agar (gathers) her maakal (food) in the qatzayar (harvest).
How long will you sleep, itzal (sluggard)? When will you qawam (rise up) out of your shanah (sleep)?
A mait (little) shanah (sleep), a mait (little) thanawamah (slumber), a mait (little) chabaq (folding) of the yad (hand) to sleep:
So your rayash (poverty) will bawaa (come) as a robber, and your scarcity as an magan (shield) ayash (husband/individual man).
A worthless adam (person), a ayash (husband/individual man) of awan (iniquity), is he who halak (move) with a perverse pah (mouth);
Who qaratz (winks) with his iyan (eye), who signals with his ragal (feet / foot), who motions with his atzabai (fingers);
In whose lab (heart) is perverseness, who devises rai (evil) ith (continually), who ith (always) shalach (send) madan (discord).
Therefore his ayad (calamity) will bawaa (come) pathaawam (suddenly). He will be shabar (broken) pathai (suddenly), and that without marapaa (remedy).
There are shash (six) things which Yahawah shanaa (hate); yes, shabai (seven) which are an thawaibah (abomination) to him:
Rawam (will lift up) iyan (eye), a shaqar (lying) lashawan (tongue/language), yad (hand) that shapak (shed) naqay (innocent) dam (blood);
A lab (heart) that charash (devises) awan (wicked) schemes, ragal (feet / foot) that are mahar (swift) in running to rai (mischief),
A shaqar (false) id (witness) who pawach (utters) kazab (lies), and he who shalach (send) madan (discord) among ach (brother/kinsman).
My ban (son), natzar (keep) your ab (father) matzawah (commandment), and don't natash (forsake) your am (mother) teaching.
Qashar (bind) them continually on your lab (heart). Inad (tie) them around your garagarawath (neck).
When you halak (move), it will nachah (lead) you. When you sleep, it will shamar (keep/guard) over you. When you qawatz (awake), it will shayach (meditate) with you.
For the matzawah (commandment) is a nayar (lamp), and the thawarah (instruction) is awar (light). Thawakachah (reproofs) of mawasar (instruction) are the darak (way) of darak (life),
To shamar (keep/guard) you from the immoral ashah (wife/individual woman), from the chalaqah (flattery) of the wayward wife's lashawan (tongue/language).
Don't chamad (lust) after her yapay (beauty) in your labab (heart), neither let her captivate you with her ipaip (eyelids).
For a prostitute reduces you to a kakar (piece) of lacham (bread). The adulteress tzawad (hunts) for your yaqar (precious) napash (living being/soul).
Can a ayash (husband/individual man) scoop ash (fire) into his chayaq (lap), and his clothes not be sharap (burned)?
Or can ayash (husband/individual man) halak (move) on hot gachal (coals), and his ragal (feet / foot) not be scorched?
So is he who bawaa (come) in to his neighbor's ashah (wife/individual woman). Whoever touches her will not be naqah (clean/innocent).
Men don't bawaz (despise) a ganab (thief), if he ganab (steals) to malaa (satisfy) himself when he is raib (hungry):
But if he is matzaa (found), he shall shalam (restore) shabaithayam (seven) times. He shall nathan (give) all the hawan (wealth) of his bayath (house).
He who naap (commits) adultery with a ashah (wife/individual woman) is chasar (void) of lab (heart). He who ishah (make) it shachath (destroys) his own napash (living being/soul).
He will matzaa (get) nagai (wounds) and dishonor. His charapah (reproach) will not be machah (wiped) away.
For qanaah (jealousy) arouses the fury of the gabar (husband). He won't chamal (spare) in the yawam (day) of naqam (vengeance).
He won't nashaa (lift) any kapar (ransom), neither will he abah (be willing / desire) content, though you rabah (give) many shachad (gifts).
My ban (son), shamar (keep/guard) my amar (spoke). Tzapan (lay) up my matzawah (commandments) within you.
Shamar (keep/guard) my matzawah (commandments) and chayah (live)! Guard my teaching as the ayashawan (apple) of your iyan (eye).
Qashar (bind) them on your atzabai (fingers). Kathab (write) them on the tablet of your lab (heart).
Amar (spoke) chakamah (wisdom), "You are my achawath (sister)." Qaraa (called) chakamah (understanding) your relative,
That they may shamar (keep/guard) you from the zawar (strange) ashah (wife/individual woman), from the nakaray (foreigner) who chalaq (flatters) with her amar (spoke).
For at the chalawan (window) of my bayath (house), I shaqap (looked) out through my ashanab (lattice).
I raah (see) among the pathay (simple) ones. I bayan (between) among the ban (son) a nair (young) man chasar (void) of lab (heart),
Ibar (pass over/through) through the shawaq (street) atzal (near) her panah (corner), he tzaid (went) the darak (way) to her bayath (house),
In the nashap (twilight), in the yawam (day) of the ayashawan (day), in the middle of the layal (night) and in the apalah (darkness).
Behold, there a ashah (wife/individual woman) qaraah (met) him with the shayath (attire) of a prostitute, and with crafty intent.
She is hamah (they) and defiant. Her ragal (feet / foot) don't stay in her bayath (house).
Paim (now) she is in the rachab (streets), paim (now) in the squares, and lurking at every panah (corner).
So she chazaq (caught) him, and nashaq (kissed) him. With an izaz (impudent) panayam (face) she amar (spoke) to him:
Sacrifices of shalam (peace) zabach (offerings) are with me. This yawam (day) I have shalam (paid) my nadar (vow).
Therefore I yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) you, to shachar (diligently) seek your panayam (face), and I matzaa (have) found you.
I have spread my irash (couch) with carpets of tapestry, with striped cloths of the yarn of Matzarayam (Egypt).
I have nawap (perfumed) my mashakab (bed) with mar (myrrh), ahalayam (aloes), and qanamawan (cinnamon).
Yalak (come), let's take our rawah (fill) of dawad (loving) until the baqar (morning). Let's ilas (solace) ourselves with ahab (love).
For my ayash (husband/individual man) isn't at bayath (house). He has halak (move) on a rachawaq (long) darak (journey).
He has laqach (take / seized) a tzarawar (bag) of kasap (money) with him. He will bawaa (come) bayath (house) at the yawam (day) kasaa (moon).
With persuasive laqach (words), she led him astray. With the flattering of her shapah (lips), she seduced him.
He halak (move) her immediately, as an shawar (ox) bawaa (come) to the tabach (slaughter), as a awayal (fool) stepping into a noose.
Until an chatz (arrow) palach (strikes) through his kabad (liver), as a tzapawar (bird) hurries to the pach (snare), and doesn't yadai (know) that it will cost his napash (living being/soul).
Now therefore, ban (son), shamai (hearken / hear) to me. Pay attention to the amar (spoke) of my pah (mouth).
Don't let your lab (heart) shatah (turn) to her darak (ways). Don't thaih (go) astray in her nathayab (paths),
For she napal (fall / be cast down) thrown down many chalal (wounded). Yes, all her harag (slain) are a itzawam (mighty) army.
Her bayath (house) is the darak (way) to shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife), yarad (going) down to the rooms of mawath (death).
Doesn't chakamah (wisdom) qaraa (called) out? Doesn't chakamah (understanding) raise her qawal (sound / voice)?
On the raash (head) of marawam (high) places by the darak (way), where the nathayab (paths) meet, she natzab (stands).
Beside the shair (gates), at the pah (entry) of the qarath (city), at the pah (entry) pathach (doors), she ranan (cries) aloud:
To you ayash (husband/individual man), I qaraa (called)! I send my qawal (sound / voice) to the ban (son) of mankind.
You pathay (simple), bayan (between) iramah (prudence). You kasayal (fools), be of an iramah (understanding) lab (heart).
Shamai (hearken / hear), for I will dabar (word / matter) nagayad (excellent) things. The mapathach (opening) of my shapah (lips) is for mayashar (right) things.
For my chak (mouth) hagah (speaks) amath (truth). Rashai (wickedness) is an thawaibah (abomination) to my shapah (lips).
All the amar (spoke) of my pah (mouth) are in tzadaq (righteous / just / fair). There is nothing crooked or perverse in them.
They are all nakach (plain) to him who bayan (between), yashar (right) to those who matzaa (find) daith (knowledge).
Laqach (take / seized) my mawasar (instruction) rather than kasap (silver); daith (knowledge) bachar (rather) than choice charawatz (gold).
For chakamah (wisdom) is tawab (pleasant/functional) than panayan (rubies). All the things that may be chapatz (desired) can't be shawah (compared) to it.
I, chakamah (wisdom), have made iramah (prudence) my shakan (dwelling). Matzaa (find) out daith (knowledge) and discretion.
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is to shanaa (hate) rai (evil). I shanaa (hate) gaah (pride), arrogance, the rai (evil) darak (way), and the thahapakah (perverse) pah (mouth).
Itzah (counsel) and sound thawashayah (knowledge) are mine. I have thawashayah (understanding) and gabawarah (power).
By me malak (king) malak (king), and razan (princes) chaqaq (decree) tzadaq (righteous / just / fair).
By me shar (prince / ruler) sharar (rule); nadayab (nobles), and all the righteous shapat (rulers) of the earth.
I ahab (love) those who ahab (love) me. Those who shachar (seek) me diligently will matzaa (find) me.
With me are riches, honor, enduring hawan (wealth), and prosperity.
My paray (fruit) is tawab (pleasant/functional) than charawatz (gold), yes, than paz (fine) gold; my yield than choice kasap (silver).
I halak (move) in the arach (way) of tzadaqah (righteousness), in the thawak (midst) of the nathayab (paths) of mashapat (justice);
That I may nachal (give) wealth to those who ahab (love) me. I malaa (fill) their awatzar (treasuries).
Yahawah qanah (possessed) me in the raashayath (beginning) of his mapail (work), qadam (before) his deeds of old.
I was nasak (set) up from iwalam (forever), from the raash (head), qadam (before) the aratz (Earth/land) existed.
When there were no thahawam (depths), I was chawal (brought) forth, when there were no maiyan (springs) kabad (abounding) with mayam (Waters).
Before the har (mountain) were tabai (settled) in place, panayam (before) the gabaih (hills), I was chawal (brought) forth;
While as yet he ishah (make) not made the aratz (Earth/land), nor the chawatz (fields), nor the raash (head) of the ipar (dust) of the thabal (world).
When he kawan (established) the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), I was there; when he chaqaq (set) a chawag (circle) on the surface of the thahawam (depths),
When he amatz (established) the shachaq (clouds) mail (top/above), when the springs of the thahawam (depths) became izaz (strong),

When he shawam (place / establish / appoint) to the yam (sea/waters) its boundary, that the mayam (Waters) should not violate his commandment, when he marked out the mawasad (foundations) of the aratz (Earth/land);
Then I was the craftsman by his side. I was a shaishai (delight) yawam (day) by day, ith (always) shachaq (rejoicing) panayam (before) him,
Shachaq (rejoicing) in his whole aratz (Earth/land). My shaishai (delight) was with the ban (son) of adam (men).
Now therefore, my ban (son), shamai (hearken / hear) to me, for ashar (who/that) are those who shamar (keep/guard) my darak (ways).
Shamai (hearken / hear) mawasar (instruction), and be chakam (wise). Don't parai (refuse) it.
Ashar (who/that) is the adam (man) who shamai (hearken / hear) me, shaqad (watching) yawam (day) at my dalath (gates), shamar (keep/guard) at my pathach (door) mazawazah (posts).
For whoever matzaa (finds) me, matzaa (finds) chay (life), and will pawaq (obtain) favor from Yahawah.
But he who chataa (sins) against me chamas (wrongs) his own napash (living being/soul). All those who shanaa (hate) me ahab (love) mawath (death).
Chakamawath (wisdom) has banah (built) her bayath (house). She has carved out her shabai (seven) imawad (pillar).
She has prepared her meat. She has mixed her yayan (wine). She has also irak (set) her shalachan (table).
She has shalach (send) out her nairah (maidens). She qaraa (called) from the highest marawam (places) of the qarath (city):
"Whoever is pathay (simple), let him sawar (turn) in here!" As for him who is chasar (void) of lab (heart), she amar (spoke) to him,
Yalak (come), lacham (eat) some of my lacham (bread), shathah (drinks) some of the yayan (wine) which I have mixed!
Izab (leave) your pathay (simple) ways, and chayah (live). Walk in the darak (way) of bayanah (understanding).
He who yasar (corrects) a lawatz (mocker) invites insult. He who yakach (reproves) a rashai (wicked) maawam (man) invites abuse.
Don't yakach (reprove) a lawatz (scoffer), lest he shanaa (hate) you. Yakach (reprove) a wise chakam (man), and he will ahab (love) you.
Instruct a chakam (wise) chakam (man), and he will be still wiser. Yadai (teach) a tzadayaq (righteous) man, and he will yasap (increase) in laqach (learning).
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is the thachalah (beginning) of chakamah (wisdom). The daith (knowledge) of the qadawash (holy) One is bayanah (understanding).
For by me your yawam (day) will be rabah (multiplied). The shanah (years) of your chay (life) will be yasap (increased).
If you are chakam (wise), you are chakam (wise) for yourself. If you lawatz (mock), you alone will nashaa (lift) it.
The kasayalawath (foolish) ashah (wife/individual woman) is hamah (they), Undisciplined, and yadai (knows) mah (nothing).
She yashab (inhabit/dwell) at the pathach (door) of her bayath (house), on a kasaa (seat) in the marawam (high) places of the qarath (city),
To qaraa (called) to those who ibar (pass over/through) by, who go yashar (straight) on their arach (ways),
"Whoever is pathay (simple), let him sawar (turn) in here." As for him who is chasar (void) of lab (heart), she amar (spoke) to him,
Ganab (stolen) mayam (Waters) is mathaq (sweet). Lacham (food) eaten in sathar (secret / hidden) is naim (pleasant).
But he doesn't yadai (know) that the rapaa (dead) are there, that her qaraa (called) are in the imaq (depths) of shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife).
The mashal (proverbs) of Shalamah (Solomon). A chakam (wise) ban (son) shamach (makes) a glad ab (father); but a kasayal (foolish) ban (son) brings grief to his am (mother).
Awatzar (treasures) of rashai (wickedness) yail (profit) nothing, but tzadaqah (righteousness) natzal (delivers) from mawath (death).
Yahawah will not allow the napash (living being/soul) of the tzadayaq (righteous) to go raib (hungry), but he hadap (thrusts) away the desire of the rashai (wicked).
He becomes rawash (poor) who ishah (make) with a lazy kap (hand), but the yad (hand) of the charawatz (diligent) brings wealth.
He who agar (gathers) in qayatz (summer) is a shakal (wise) ban (son), but he who sleeps during the qatzayar (harvest) is a ban (son) who bawash (causes) shame.
Barakah (blessings) are on the raash (head) of the tzadayaq (righteous), but chamas (violence) kasah (covers) the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked).
The zakar (remembrance/memory) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is blessed, but the sham (name) of the rashai (wicked) will raqab (rot).
The chakam (wise) in lab (heart) laqach (take / seized) matzawah (commandments), but a chattering awayal (fool) will labat (fall).
He who yalak (walks) blamelessly yalak (walks) batach (surely), but he who iqash (perverts) his darak (ways) yadai (will) be found out.
One qaratz (winking) with the iyan (eye) nathan (give) itzabath (sorrow), but a chattering awayal (fool) will labat (fall).
The pah (mouth) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is a maqawar (spring) of chay (life), but chamas (violence) kasah (covers) the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked).
Hatred iwar (rouse / awaken) up madan (strife), but ahabah (love) kasah (covers) all wrongs.
Chakamah (wisdom) is matzaa (found) on the shapah (lips) of him who bayan (between) discernment, but a shabat (rod) is for the gaw (back) of him who is chasar (void) of lab (heart).
Chakam (wise) men tzapan (lay) up daith (knowledge), but the pah (mouth) of the awayal (foolish) is qarawab (near) machathah (ruin).
The ishayar (rich) man's hawan (wealth) is his iz (strength / might / refuge) qarayah (city). The machathah (destruction) of the dal (poor) is their rayash (poverty).
The pailah (labor) of the tzadayaq (righteous) leads to chay (life). The thabawaah (increase) of the rashai (wicked) leads to chataah (sin).
He is in the arach (way) of chay (life) who shamar (keep/guard) mawasar (correction), but he who izab (forsakes) thawakachah (reproof) leads others thaih (astray).
He who kasah (hides) hatred has shaqar (lying) shapah (lips). He who yatzaa (go out / come out) a dabah (slander) is a kasayal (fool).
In the rab (multitude) of dabar (word / matter) there is no lack of disobedience, but he who restrains his shapah (lips) does shakal (wisely).
The lashawan (tongue/language) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is like choice kasap (silver). The lab (heart) of the rashai (wicked) is of mait (little) worth.
The shapah (lips) of the tzadayaq (righteous) raih (feed) many, but the awayal (foolish) mawath (death) for chasar (lack) of lab (heart).
Yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) barakah (blessing) brings wealth, and he yasap (adds) no trouble to it.
It is a kasayal (fool's) pleasure to ishah (make) zamah (wickedness), but chakamah (wisdom) is a ayash (husband/individual man) of thabawan (understanding's) pleasure.
What the rashai (wicked) magawarah (fear), will overtake them, but the thaawah (desire) of the tzadayaq (righteous) will be nathan (give).
When the sawapah (whirlwind) passes, the rashai (wicked) is no more; but the tzadayaq (righteous) stand firm iwalam (forever).
As chamatz (vinegar) to the shan (teeth), and as ishan (smoke) to the iyan (eye), so is the itzal (sluggard) to those who shalach (send) him.
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah yasap (prolongs) yawam (day), but the shanah (years) of the rashai (wicked) shall be shortened.
The prospect of the tzadayaq (righteous) is shamachah (joy), but the thaqawah (hope) of the rashai (wicked) will abad (destroy/perish).
The darak (way) of Yahawah is a stronghold to the tham (upright), but it is a machathah (destruction) to the pail (workers) of awan (iniquity).
The tzadayaq (righteous) will iwalam (forever) be mawat (removed), but the rashai (wicked) will not shakan (dwell) in the aratz (Earth/land).
The pah (mouth) of the tzadayaq (righteous) nawab (brings) forth chakamah (wisdom), but the thahapakah (perverse) lashawan (tongue/language) will be karath (cut) off.
The shapah (lips) of the tzadayaq (righteous) yadai (know) what is ratzawan (acceptable), but the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked) is thahapakah (perverse).
A maramah (false) maazan (balance) is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, but accurate aban (stone) are his ratzawan (delight).
When zadawan (pride) bawaa (come), then bawaa (come) qalawan (shame), but with humility bawaa (come) chakamah (wisdom).
The thamah (integrity) of the yashar (upright) shall nachah (guide) them, but the salap (perverseness) of the bagad (treacherous) shall shadad (destroy) them.
Riches don't yail (profit) in the yawam (day) of ibarah (wrath), but tzadaqah (righteousness) natzal (delivers) from mawath (death).
The tzadaqah (righteousness) of the blameless will yashar (direct) his darak (way), but the rashai (wicked) shall napal (fall / be cast down) by his own rashaih (wickedness).
The tzadaqah (righteousness) of the yashar (upright) shall natzal (deliver) them, but the bagad (unfaithful) will be trapped by hawah (calamity/destruction) desires.
When a rashai (wicked) adam (man) mawath (death), thaqawah (hope) perishes, and thaqawah (expectation) of awan (power) comes to nothing.
A tzadayaq (righteous) person is chalatz (delivered) out of tzarah (trouble), and the rashai (wicked) takes his place.
With his pah (mouth) the godless man shachath (destroys) his neighbor, but the tzadayaq (righteous) will be chalatz (delivered) through daith (knowledge).
When it tawab (pleasant/functional) well with the tzadayaq (righteous), the qarayah (city) ilatz (rejoices). When the rashai (wicked) abad (destroy/perish), there is ranah (shouting).
By the barakah (blessing) of the yashar (upright), the qarath (city) is rawam (will lift up), but it is overthrown by the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked).
One who bawaz (despises) his neighbor is chasar (void) of lab (heart), but a ayash (husband/individual man) of thabawan (understanding) holds his charash (peace).
Halak (move) who brings gossip betrays a confidence, but aman (believe / have faith) who is of a trustworthy rawach (spirit / wind) is kasah (one) who keeps a secret.
Where there is no wise guidance, the im (people / nation) napal (fall / be cast down), but in the rab (multitude) of yaitz (counselors) there is thashawaih (deliverance).
He who is collateral for a stranger will suffer for it, but he who refuses pledges of collateral is batach (secure).
A chan (gracious) ashah (wife/individual woman) obtains honor, but irayatz (violent) men obtain riches.
The chasad (grace) ayash (husband/individual man) gamal (does) good to his own napash (living being/soul), but he who is akazaray (cruel) ikar (troubles) his own shaar (flesh).
Rashai (wicked) ishah (make) earn shaqar (deceitful) pailah (wages), but one who zarai (sows) tzadaqah (righteousness) reaps a amath (truth) shakar (reward).
He who is truly tzadaqah (righteousness) gets chay (life). He who radap (pursues) rai (evil) gets mawath (death).
Those who are iqash (perverse) in lab (heart) are an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, but those whose darak (ways) are blameless are his ratzawan (delight).
Most certainly, the rai (evil) man will not be naqah (clean/innocent), but the zarai (seed) of the tzadayaq (righteous) will be malat (delivered).
Like a zahab (gold) ring in a pig's ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), is a yapah (beautiful) ashah (wife/individual woman) who lacks taim (discretion).
The thaawah (desire) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is only tawab (pleasant/functional). The thaqawah (expectation) of the rashai (wicked) is ibarah (wrath).
There is one who pazar (scatters), and yasap (increases) yet more. There is yashar (one) who withholds more than is appropriate, but gains machasawar (poverty).
The barakah (liberal) napash (living being/soul) shall be dashan (made) fat. He who rawah (waters) shall be watered also himself.
Laam (people) naqab (curse) someone who manai (withholds) grain, but barakah (blessing) will be on the raash (head) of him who shabar (sells) it.
He who shachar (diligently) seeks tawab (pleasant/functional) shachar (seeks) favor, but he who searches after rai (evil), it shall bawaa (come) to him.
He who batach (trusts) in his riches will napal (fall / be cast down), but the tzadayaq (righteous) shall parach (flourish) as the green ilah (leaf).
He who ikar (troubles) his own bayath (house) shall nachal (inherit) the rawach (spirit / wind). The awayal (foolish) shall be ibad (servant) to the chakam (wise) of lab (heart).
The paray (fruit) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is a itz (tree) of chay (life). He who is chakam (wise) laqach (take / seized) napash (living being/soul).
Behold, the tzadayaq (righteous) shall be repaid in the aratz (Earth/land); how much more the rashai (wicked) and the chataa (sinner)!
Whoever ahab (love) mawasar (correction) ahab (love) daith (knowledge), but he who shanaa (hate) thawakachah (reproof) is stupid.
A tawab (pleasant/functional) man shall pawaq (obtain) favor from Yahawah, but he will rashai (condemn) a ayash (husband/individual man) of wicked mazamah (devices).
A adam (man) shall not be kawan (established) by rashai (wickedness), but the sharash (root) of the tzadayaq (righteous) shall not be mawat (moved).
A chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ashah (wife/individual woman) is the itarah (crown) of her bail (husband), but a disgraceful wife is as raqab (rottenness) in his itzam (bones).
The machashabah (thoughts) of the tzadayaq (righteous) are mashapat (just), but the advice of the rashai (wicked) is deceitful.
The dabar (word / matter) of the rashai (wicked) are about lying in arab (wait) for dam (blood), but the pah (speech) of the yashar (upright) natzal (rescues) them.
The rashai (wicked) are overthrown, and are no more, but the bayath (house) of the tzadayaq (righteous) shall imad (stand).
A ayash (husband/individual man) shall be halal (praise) pah (according) to his shakal (wisdom), but he who has a warped lab (heart) shall be bawaz (despised).
Tawab (pleasant/functional) is he who is qalah (lightly) esteemed, and has a ibad (servant), than he who honors himself, and chasar (lacks) lacham (bread).
A tzadayaq (righteous) yadai (man) respects the napash (living being/soul) of his animal, but the tender racham (mercies) of the rashai (wicked) are akazaray (cruel).
He who ibad (servant) his adamah (land) shall shabai (have) plenty of lacham (bread), but he who radap (chases) fantasies is chasar (void) of lab (heart).
The rashai (wicked) chamad (desires) the plunder of rai (evil) men, but the sharash (root) of the tzadayaq (righteous) flourishes.
An rai (evil) man is mawaqash (trapped) by sinfulness of shapah (lips), but the tzadayaq (righteous) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out of tzarah (trouble).

A ayash (husband/individual man) shall be shabai (satisfied) with tawab (pleasant/functional) by the paray (fruit) of his pah (mouth). The gamawal (work) of a adam (man's) yad (hand) shall be shawab (turn back / repent) to him.
The darak (way) of a awayal (fool) is yashar (right) in his own iyan (eye), but he who is chakam (wise) shamai (hearken / hear) to itzah (counsel).
A awayal (fool) shows his annoyance the same yawam (day), but kasah (one) who overlooks an insult is irawam (prudent).
He who is truthful testifies honestly, but a shaqar (false) id (witness) lies.
There is one who bataa (speaks) rashly like the madaqarah (piercing) of a charab (sword), but the lashawan (tongue/language) of the chakam (wise) heals.
Amath (truth) shapah (lips) will be kawan (established) id (forever), but a shaqar (lying) lashawan (tongue/language) is only momentary.
Maramah (deceit) is in the lab (heart) of those who plot rai (evil), but shamachah (joy) comes to the promoters of shalawam (peace / safety).
No awan (mischief) shall anah (happen) to the tzadayaq (righteous), but the rashai (wicked) shall be malaa (filled) with rai (evil).
Shaqar (lying) shapah (lips) are an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, but those who ishah (make) the amawanah (truth) are his ratzawan (delight).
A irawam (prudent) adam (man) keeps his daith (knowledge), but the lab (heart) of kasayal (fools) qaraa (called) awalath (foolishness).
The yad (hand) of the charawatz (diligent) ones shall mashal (rule/have dominion), but laziness ends in slave labor.
Anxiety in a ayash (husband/individual man) lab (heart) weighs it down, but a kind dabar (word / matter) shamach (makes) it glad.
A tzadayaq (righteous) person is cautious in friendship, but the darak (way) of the rashai (wicked) leads them astray.
The ramayah (slothful) man doesn't charak (roast) his game, but the hawan (possessions) of charawatz (diligent) adam (men) are prized.
In the arach (way) of tzadaqah (righteousness) is chay (life); in its nathayab (path) there is no mawath (death).
A chakam (wise) ban (son) listens to his ab (father) mawasar (instruction), but a lawatz (scoffer) doesn't shamai (hearken / hear) to gairah (rebuke).
By the paray (fruit) of his lips, a ayash (husband/individual man) enjoys tawab (pleasant/functional) things; but the unfaithful crave chamas (violence).
He who guards his pah (mouth) guards his napash (living being/soul). One who pashaq (opens) wide his shapah (lips) comes to machathah (ruin).
The napash (living being/soul) of the itzal (sluggard) awah (desires), and napash (living being/soul) nothing, but the desire of the charawatz (diligent) shall be fully satisfied.
A tzadayaq (righteous) man shanaa (hate) lies, but a rashai (wicked) man chapar (brings) shame and disgrace.
Tzadaqah (righteousness) guards the darak (way) of tham (integrity), but rashaih (wickedness) salap (overthrows) the chataah (sin).
There are some who pretend to be ishar (rich), yet have nothing. There are some who pretend to be rawash (poor), yet rab (have) great hawan (wealth).
The kapar (ransom) of a ayash (husband/individual man) napash (living being/soul) is his riches, but the rawash (poor) shamai (hearken / hear) no threats.
The awar (light) of the tzadayaq (righteous) shines brightly, but the nayar (lamp) of the rashai (wicked) is snuffed out.
Zadawan (pride) only breeds quarrels, but with ones who yaitz (take) advice is chakamah (wisdom).
Hawan (wealth) gained dishonestly dwindles away, but he who qabatz (gathers) by yad (hand) rabah (makes) it grow.
Thawachalath (hope) mashak (deferred) makes the lab (heart) chalah (afflict), but when longing is fulfilled, it is a itz (tree) of chay (life).
Whoever bawaz (despises) instruction will pay for it, but he who respects a command will be shalam (rewarded).
The teaching of the chakam (wise) is a maqawar (spring) of chay (life), to sawar (turn) from the mawaqash (snares) of mawath (death).
Tawab (pleasant/functional) shakal (understanding) wins favor; but the darak (way) of the bagad (unfaithful) is ayathan (hard).
Every irawam (prudent) ishah (make) acts from daith (knowledge), but a kasayal (fool) exposes awalath (folly).
A rashai (wicked) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) napal (fall / be cast down) into rai (trouble), but a trustworthy envoy gains marapaa (healing).
Rayash (poverty) and qalawan (shame) come to him who parai (refuses) mawasar (discipline), but he who shamar (keep/guard) mawasar (correction) shall be honored.
Longing fulfilled is irab (evening) to the napash (living being/soul), but kasayal (fools) detest sawar (turning) from rai (evil).
One who halak (move) with chakam (wise) men grows chakam (wise), but a raih (companion) of kasayal (fools) suffers harm.
Misfortune radap (pursues) chataa (sinners), but tawab (pleasant/functional) shalam (rewards) the tzadayaq (righteous).
A tawab (pleasant/functional) man leaves an nachal (inheritance) to his ban (son) ban (son), but the wealth of the chataa (sinner) is stored for the tzadayaq (righteous).
An rab (abundance) of akal (food) is in rawash (poor) nayar (people's) fields, but injustice sweeps it away.
One who chashak (darkness) the shabat (rod) shanaa (hate) his ban (son), but one who ahab (love) him is careful to mawasar (discipline) him.
The tzadayaq (righteous) napash (living being/soul) akal (eat) to the shabai (satisfying) of his napash (living being/soul), but the batan (belly) of the rashai (wicked) goes hungry.
Chakamawath (every) wise ashah (wife/individual woman) banah (builds) her bayath (house), but the foolish haras (one) tears it down with her own yad (hand).
He who halak (move) in his yashar (uprightness) yaraa (fears) Yahawah, but he who is lawaz (perverse) in his darak (ways) bazah (despises) him.
The awayal (fool's) pah (talk) brings a chatar (rod) to his back, but the shapah (lips) of the chakam (wise) protect them.
Where no alap (oxen) are, the abawas (crib) is bar (clean), but much thabawaah (increase) is by the kach (strength / mighty / power) of the shawar (ox).
A truthful id (witness) will not kazab (lie), but a shaqar (false) id (witness) pours out kazab (lies).
A lawatz (scoffer) baqash (seeks) chakamah (wisdom), and doesn't find it, but daith (knowledge) comes easily to a bayan (between) person.
Stay away from a kasayal (foolish) ayash (husband/individual man), for you won't find daith (knowledge) on his shapah (lips).
The chakamah (wisdom) of the irawam (prudent) is to bayan (between) about his darak (way), but the awalath (folly) of kasayal (fools) is maramah (deceit).
Awayal (fools) lawatz (mock) at making atonement for asham (sins), but among the yashar (upright) there is good ratzawan (will).
The lab (heart) yadai (knows) its napash (living being/soul) marah (bitterness) and joy; he will not share these with a stranger.
The bayath (house) of the rashai (wicked) will be overthrown, but the ahal (tent) of the yashar (upright) will parach (flourish).
There is a darak (way) which seems yashar (right) to a ayash (husband/individual man), but in the acharayath (end) it leads to mawath (death).
