Even in shachawaq (laughter/joking matter) the lab (heart) may be kaab (sorrowful), and shamachah (mirth) may acharayath (end) in thawagah (heaviness).
The unfaithful will be repaid for his own darak (ways); likewise a tawab (pleasant/functional) ayash (husband/individual man) will be rewarded for his ways.
A pathay (simple) man aman (believe / have faith) everything, but the irawam (prudent) bayan (between) carefully considers his ashar (who/that).
A chakam (wise) man yaraa (fears), and shuns rai (evil), but the kasayal (fool) is hotheaded and reckless.
He who is quick to become angry will ishah (make) awalath (folly), and a crafty ayash (husband/individual man) is shanaa (hate).
The pathay (simple) nachal (inherit) awalath (folly), but the irawam (prudent) are kathar (crowned) with daith (knowledge).
The rai (evil) shachach (bow) down panayam (before) the tawab (pleasant/functional), and the rashai (wicked) at the shair (gates) of the tzadayaq (righteous).
The rawash (poor) person is shunned even by his own neighbor, but the ishayar (rich) person rab (has) many ahab (love).
He who bawaz (despises) his neighbor chataa (sins), but ashar (who/that) is he who chanan (has) pity on the inay (poor).
Don't they thaih (go) astray who plot rai (evil)? But chasad (grace) and amath (truth) belong to those who plan tawab (pleasant/functional).
In all hard itzab (work) there is mawathar (profit), but the dabar (word / matter) of the shapah (lips) leads only to machasawar (poverty).
The itarah (crown) of the chakam (wise) is their riches, but the awalath (folly) of kasayal (fools) crowns them with awalath (folly).
A truthful id (witness) natzal (saves) napash (living being/soul), but a maramah (false) witness is deceitful.
In the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is a secure fortress, and he will be a machasah (refuge) for his ban (son).
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is a maqawar (fountain) of chay (life), sawar (turning) people from the mawaqash (snares) of mawath (death).
In the rab (multitude) of im (people / nation) is the malak (king) glory, but in the lack of laam (people) is the machathah (destruction) of the razawan (prince).
He who is arak (slow) to ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) rab (has) great thabawan (understanding), but he who has a quick temper displays awalath (folly).
The chay (life) of the bashar (flesh) is a lab (heart) at marapaa (peace), but qanaah (envy) rots the itzam (bones).
He who oppresses the dal (poor) shows contempt for his Maker, but he who is kind to the abayawan (needy) honors him.
The rashai (wicked) is brought down in his rai (calamity), but in mawath (death), the tzadayaq (righteous) chasah (has) a refuge.
Chakamah (wisdom) nawach (rests) in the lab (heart) of one who has bayan (between), and is even yadai (made) known in the qarab (among / near) part of kasayal (fools).
Tzadaqah (righteousness) rawam (will lift up) a gaway (nation / people), but chataah (sin) is a disgrace to any laam (people).
The malak (king) favor is toward a ibad (servant) who deals shakal (wisely), but his ibarah (wrath) is toward one who bawash (causes) shame.
A gentle mainah (answer) shawab (turn back / repent) away chamah (wrath), but a harsh dabar (word / matter) ilah (go up / offer) up ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).
The lashawan (tongue/language) of the chakam (wise) commends daith (knowledge), but the pah (mouth) of kasayal (fools) gush out awalath (folly).
Yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) iyan (eye) are everywhere, keeping tzapah (watchman / keep watch) on the rai (evil) and the tawab (pleasant/functional).
A gentle lashawan (tongue/language) is a itz (tree) of chay (life), but deceit in it crushes the rawach (spirit / wind).
A awayal (fool) naatz (despises) his ab (father) mawasar (correction), but he who shamar (keep/guard) thawakachah (reproof) shows prudence.
In the bayath (house) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is much chasan (treasure), but the income of the rashai (wicked) brings ikar (trouble).
The shapah (lips) of the chakam (wise) zarah (spread) daith (knowledge); not so with the lab (heart) of kasayal (fools).
The zabach (sacrifice) made by the rashai (wicked) is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, but the thapalah (prayer) of the yashar (upright) is his ratzawan (delight).
The darak (way) of the rashai (wicked) is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, but he ahab (love) him who radap (follows) after tzadaqah (righteousness).
There is stern mawasar (discipline) for one who izab (forsakes) the arach (way): whoever shanaa (hate) thawakachah (reproof) shall mawath (death).
Shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife) and abadawan (abaddon) are before Yahawah— how much more then the labah (hearts) of the ban (son) of adam (men)!
A lawatz (scoffer) doesn't ahab (love) to be yakach (reproved); he will not yalak (go) to the chakam (wise).
A shamach (glad) lab (heart) yatab (makes) a cheerful panayam (face); but an aching lab (heart) nakaa (breaks) the rawach (spirit / wind).
The lab (heart) of one who has bayan (between) baqash (seeks) daith (knowledge), but the panayam (mouths) of kasayal (fools) raih (feed) on awalath (folly).
All the yawam (day) of the inay (afflicted) are wretched, but one who has a tawab (pleasant/functional) lab (heart) enjoys a thamayad (continual) mashathah (feast).
Tawab (pleasant/functional) is mait (little), with the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah, than rab (great) awatzar (treasure) with mahawamah (trouble).
Tawab (pleasant/functional) is a arachah (dinner) of yaraq (herbs), where ahabah (love) is, than a fattened calf with hatred.
A chamah (wrathful) ayash (husband/individual man) garah (stirs) up madawan (contention), but one who is arak (slow) to ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) appeases rayab (strife).
The darak (way) of the itzal (sluggard) is like a chadaq (thorn) patch, but the arach (path) of the yashar (upright) is a highway.
A chakam (wise) ban (son) makes a ab (father) shamach (glad), but a kasayal (foolish) adam (man) bazah (despises) his am (mother).
Awalath (folly) is shamachah (joy) to one who is chasar (void) of lab (heart), but a ayash (husband/individual man) of thabawan (understanding) keeps his yalak (way) yashar (straight).
Where there is no sawad (counsel), plans parar (fail); but in a rab (multitude) of yaitz (counselors) they are qawam (rise up).
Shamachah (joy) comes to a ayash (husband/individual man) with the reply of his pah (mouth). How tawab (pleasant/functional) is a dabar (word / matter) at the right ith (time)!
The arach (path) of chay (life) leads upward for the shakal (wise), to keep him from going matah (downward) to shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife).
Yahawah will uproot the bayath (house) of the gaah (proud), but he will keep the alamanah (widow's) gabawal (border/boundary) intact.
Yahawah detests the machashabah (thoughts) of the rai (wicked), but the thoughts of the tahawar (pure) are pleasing.
He who is batzai (greedy) for batzai (gain) ikar (troubles) his own bayath (house), but he who shanaa (hate) bribes will chayah (live).
The lab (heart) of the tzadayaq (righteous) weighs inah (answer / respond), but the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked) gushes out rai (evil).
Yahawah is rachawaq (far) from the rashai (wicked), but he shamai (hearken / hear) the thapalah (prayer) of the tzadayaq (righteous).
The maawar (Maawar/(Luminary)) of the iyan (eye) shamach (rejoices) the lab (heart). Tawab (pleasant/functional) shamawaih (news) gives health to the itzam (bones).
The azan (ear) that shamai (hearken / hear) to thawakachah (reproof) chay (life), and will be at home qarab (among / near) the chakam (wise).
He who parai (refuses) mawasar (correction) maas (despises) his own napash (living being/soul), but he who shamai (hearken / hear) to thawakachah (reproof) qanah (gets) lab (heart).
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah teaches chakamah (wisdom). Panayam (before) honor is inawah (humility).
The plans of the lab (heart) belong to adam (man), but the mainah (answer) of the lashawan (tongue/language) is from Yahawah.
All the darak (ways) of a ayash (husband/individual man) are zak (clean) in his own iyan (eye); but Yahawah thakan (weighs) the motives.
Galal (commit) your maishah (deeds) to Yahawah, and your plans shall succeed.
Yahawah has pail (made) everything for its own end— yes, even the rashai (wicked) for the yawam (day) of rashai (evil).
Everyone who is gabah (proud) in lab (heart) is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah: they shall certainly not be naqah (clean/innocent).
By chasad (grace) and amath (truth) iwan (guilt/iniquity) is atoned for. By the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah men sawar (depart) from rai (evil).
When a ayash (husband/individual man) darak (ways) ratzah (please) Yahawah, he makes even his ayab (enemy) to be at shalam (peace) with him.
Tawab (pleasant/functional) is a mait (little) with tzadaqah (righteousness), than rab (great) thabawaah (revenues) with injustice.
A adam (man's) lab (heart) plans his course, but Yahawah kawan (directs) his tzaid (steps).
Inspired qasam (judgments) are on the shapah (lips) of the malak (king). He shall not betray his pah (mouth).
Honest maazan (balances) and palas (scales) are yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)); all the aban (stone) in the kayas (bag) are his maishah (work).
It is an thawaibah (abomination) for malak (king) to ishah (make) wrong, for the kasaa (throne) is kawan (established) by tzadaqah (righteousness).
Tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) shapah (lips) are the ratzawan (delight) of malak (king). They value one who dabar (word / matter) the yashar (truth).
The malak (king) chamah (wrath) is a malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of mawath (death), but a chakam (wise) ayash (husband/individual man) will kapar (pacify) it.
In the awar (light) of the malak (king) panayam (face) is chay (life). His favor is like a ib (cloud) of the spring malaqawash (rain).
How much tawab (pleasant/functional) it is to qanah (get) chakamah (wisdom) than charawatz (gold)! Yes, to qanah (get) bayanah (understanding) is to be bachar (chosen) rather than kasap (silver).
The masalah (highway) of the yashar (upright) is to sawar (depart) from rai (evil). He who natzar (keeps) his darak (way) shamar (keep/guard) his napash (living being/soul).
Gaawan (pride) goes panayam (before) shabar (destruction), and a gabah (haughty) rawach (spirit / wind) panayam (before) a kashalawan (fall).
It is tawab (pleasant/functional) to be of a inay (lowly) rawach (spirit / wind) with the poor, than to chalaq (divide) the plunder with the gaah (proud).
He who heeds the dabar (word / matter) matzaa (finds) tawab (pleasant/functional). Whoever batach (trusts) in Yahawah is ashar (who/that).
The chakam (wise) in lab (heart) shall be qaraa (called) bayan (between). Pleasantness of the shapah (lips) promotes instruction.
Shakal (understanding) is a maqawar (fountain) of chay (life) to one who bail (has) it, but the punishment of awayal (fools) is their awalath (folly).
The lab (heart) of the chakam (wise) shakal (instructs) his pah (mouth), and yasap (adds) laqach (learning) to his shapah (lips).
Naim (pleasant) amar (spoke) are a tzawap (honeycomb), mathawaq (sweet) to the napash (living being/soul), and marapaa (health) to the itzam (bones).
There is a darak (way) which seems yashar (right) to a ayash (husband/individual man), but in the acharayath (end) it leads to mawath (death).
The appetite of the laboring napash (living being/soul) imal (labors) for him; for his pah (mouth) urges him on.
A worthless ayash (husband/individual man) devises rai (mischief). His shapah (speech) is like a scorching ash (fire).
A thahapakah (perverse) ayash (husband/individual man) stirs up madawan (strife). A naragan (whisperer) parad (separates) close alawap (friends).
A ayash (husband/individual man) of chamas (violence) pathah (entices) his neighbor, and yalak (leads) him in a darak (way) that is not tawab (pleasant/functional).
Itzah (one) who winks his iyan (eye) to plot perversities, qaratz (one) who compresses his shapah (lips), is bent on rai (evil).
Shayabah (old age / white hair (due to age)) hair is a itarah (crown) of glory. It is attained by a darak (life) of tzadaqah (righteousness).

One who is arak (slow) to ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) is tawab (pleasant/functional) than the gabawar (mighty); one who mashal (rule/have dominion) his rawach (spirit / wind), than he who lakad (takes) a iyar (city).
The gawaral (lot) is tawal (cast) into the chayaq (lap), but its every decision is from Yahawah.
Tawab (pleasant/functional) is a charab (dry) path (morsel) with shalawah (quietness), than a bayath (house) malaa (full) of feasting with rayab (strife).

A ibad (servant) who deals shakal (wisely) will mashal (rule/have dominion) over a ban (son) who bawash (causes) shame, and shall chalaq (have) a part in the nachalah (inheritance) thawak (midst) the ach (brother/kinsman).
The refining matzarap (pot) is for kasap (silver), and the kawar (furnace) for zahab (gold), but Yahawah tests the labah (hearts).
An evildoer qashab (heeds) awan (wicked) shapah (lips). A shaqar (liar) azan (gives) ear to a hawah (calamity/destruction) lashawan (tongue/language).
Whoever laig (mocks) the rawash (poor) reproaches his Maker. He who is shamach (glad) at ayad (calamity) shall not be naqah (clean/innocent).
Ban (son) ban (son) are the itarah (crown) of zaqan (old) men; the glory of ban (son) are their parents.
Arrogant shapah (speech) isn't fitting for a nabal (fool), much less do shaqar (lying) shapah (lips) fit a nadayab (prince).
A shachad (bribe) is a chan (precious) aban (stone) in the iyan (eye) of him who bail (gives) it; wherever he panah (turns), he shakal (prospers).
He who kasah (covers) an offense promotes ahabah (love); but he who shanah (repeats) a dabar (word / matter) parad (separates) best alawap (friends).
A gairah (rebuke) nachath (enters) deeper into bayan (between) who has understanding than a maah (hundred) lashes into a kasayal (fool).
An rai (evil) man baqash (seeks) only rebellion; therefore a akazaray (cruel) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) shall be shalach (send) against him.
Let a dab (bear) robbed of her cubs pagash (meet) a ayash (husband/individual man), al (rather) than a kasayal (fool) in his awalath (folly).
Whoever shawab (turn back / repent) rai (evil) for tawab (pleasant/functional), rai (evil) shall not depart from his bayath (house).
The raashayath (beginning) of madawan (strife) is like breaching a dam, therefore stop rayab (contention) panayam (before) quarreling breaks out.
He who justifies the rashai (wicked), and he who rashai (condemns) the tzadayaq (righteous), shanayam (two) of them alike are an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah.
Why is there money in the yad (hand) of a kasayal (fool) to qanah (buy) chakamah (wisdom), since he has no lab (heart)?
A rai (neigbor/another person) ahab (love) at all ith (times); and a ach (brother/kinsman) is yalad (birth / begot) for tzarah (adversity).
A adam (man) chasar (void) of lab (heart) thaqai (blow / sound alarm) kap (hands), and becomes collateral in the panayam (presence) of his neighbor.
He who ahab (love) disobedience ahab (love) matzah (strife). One who builds a gabah (high) pathach (gate) baqash (seeks) shabar (destruction).

One who has a iqash (perverse) lab (heart) doesn't matzaa (find) tawab (pleasant/functional), and hapak (one) who has a deceitful lashawan (tongue/language) napal (fall / be cast down) into rai (trouble).
He who becomes the yalad (birth / begot) of a kasayal (fool) grieves. The ab (father) of a nabal (fool) shamach (has) no joy.
A cheerful lab (heart) makes yatab (good) gahah (medicine), but a crushed rawach (spirit / wind) yabash (dry land) up the garam (bones).
A rashai (wicked) man laqach (take / seized) a shachad (bribe) in secret, to natah (pervert) the arach (ways) of mashapat (justice).
Chakamah (wisdom) is before the panayam (face) of one who has understanding, but the iyan (eye) of a kasayal (fool) wander to the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land).
A kasayal (foolish) ban (son) brings kais (grief) to his ab (father), and mamar (bitterness) to her who yalad (birth / begot) him.
Also to inash (punish) the tzadayaq (righteous) is not tawab (pleasant/functional), nor to flog officials for their integrity.
He who chashak (darkness) his amar (spoke) yadai (has) daith (knowledge). He who is even tempered is a ayash (husband/individual man) of thabawan (understanding).
Even a awayal (fool), when he charash (keeps) silent, is chashab (counted) chakam (wise). When he atam (shuts) his shapah (lips), he is bayan (between) to be discerning.
An unfriendly baqash (man) pursues selfishness, and defies all sound thawashayah (judgment).
A kasayal (fool) chapatz (has) no delight in thabawan (understanding), but only in galah (revealing) his own opinion.
When rashai (wickedness) bawaa (come), bawaz (contempt) also bawaa (come), and with charapah (shame) comes disgrace.

The dabar (word / matter) of a ayash (husband/individual man) pah (mouth) are like imaq (deep) mayam (Waters). The maqawar (fountain) of chakamah (wisdom) is like a nabai (flowing) nachal (stream / river).
To be partial to the panayam (faces) of the rashai (wicked) is not tawab (pleasant/functional), nor to deprive the innocent of mashapat (justice).
A kasayal (fool's) shapah (lips) bawaa (come) into rayab (strife), and his pah (mouth) qaraa (called) beatings.
A kasayal (fool's) pah (mouth) is his machathah (destruction), and his shapah (lips) are a mawaqash (snare) to his napash (living being/soul).
The dabar (word / matter) of a gossip are like dainty morsels: they yarad (go) down into a person's chadar (innermost) parts.
One who is rapah (slack) in his malaakah (work) is ach (brother/kinsman) to him who is a bail (master) of destruction.
The sham (name) of Yahawah is a iz (strength / might / refuge) magadal (tower): the tzadayaq (righteous) rawatz (run) to him, and are shagab (safe).
The ishayar (rich) man's hawan (wealth) is his iz (strength / might / refuge) qarayah (city), like an unscalable chawamah (wall) in his own imagination.
Panayam (before) shabar (destruction) the lab (heart) of ayash (husband/individual man) is gabah (proud), but panayam (before) honor is inawah (humility).
He who gives shawab (turn back / repent) before he shamai (hearken / hear), that is awalath (folly) and kalamah (shame) to him.
A ayash (husband/individual man) rawach (spirit / wind) will kawal (all/every/entire) him in machalah (sickness), but a crushed rawach (spirit / wind), who can nashaa (lift)?
The lab (heart) of the bayan (between) qanah (gets) daith (knowledge). The azan (ear) of the chakam (wise) baqash (seeks) daith (knowledge).
A adam (man's) mathan (gift) rachab (makes) room for him, and nachah (brings) him panayam (before) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) men.
He who pleads his rayab (cause) raashawan (first) seems right; until rai (neigbor/another person) bawaa (come) and questions him.
The gawaral (lot) settles disputes, and keeps itzawam (strong) parad (ones) apart.
A ach (brother/kinsman) pashai (offended) is more difficult than a fortified qarayah (city); and disputes are like the barayach (bars) of a aramawan (castle).
A ayash (husband/individual man) stomach is shabai (filled) with the paray (fruit) of his pah (mouth). With the harvest of his lips he is shabai (satisfied).
Mawath (death) and chay (life) are in the yad (hand) of the lashawan (tongue/language); those who ahab (love) it will akal (eat) its paray (fruit).
Whoever matzaa (finds) a ashah (wife/individual woman) matzaa (finds) a tawab (pleasant/functional) thing, and pawaq (obtains) favor of Yahawah.
The rawash (poor) plead for thachanawan (mercy), but the ishayar (rich) inah (answer / respond) harshly.
A ayash (husband/individual man) of many rai (neigbor/another person) may be ruined, but there is a ahab (love) who dabaq (sticks) closer than a ach (brother/kinsman).
Tawab (pleasant/functional) is the rawash (poor) who halak (move) in his tham (integrity) than he who is iqash (perverse) in his shapah (lips) and is a kasayal (fool).
It isn't tawab (pleasant/functional) to napash (living being/soul) zeal without daith (knowledge); nor being hasty with one's ragal (feet / foot) and chataa (missing) the way.
The awalath (foolishness) of adam (man) subverts his darak (way); his lab (heart) rages against Yahawah.
Hawan (wealth) yasap (adds) many rai (neigbor/another person), but the dal (poor) is parad (separated) from his rai (neigbor/another person).
A shaqar (false) id (witness) shall not be naqah (clean/innocent). He who pours out kazab (lies) shall not malat (go) free.
Many will entreat the favor of a nadayab (ruler), and everyone is a rai (neigbor/another person) to a ayash (husband/individual man) who gives mathan (gifts).
All the relatives of the rawash (poor) shun him: how much more do his marai (friends) avoid him! He radap (pursues) them with pleas, but they are gone.
He who qanah (gets) lab (heart) ahab (love) his own napash (living being/soul). He who shamar (keep/guard) thabawan (understanding) shall matzaa (find) tawab (pleasant/functional).
A shaqar (false) id (witness) shall not be naqah (clean/innocent). He who pawach (utters) kazab (lies) shall abad (destroy/perish).
Thainawag (delicate) living is not appropriate for a kasayal (fool), much less for a ibad (servant) to mashal (rule/have dominion) rule over shar (prince / ruler).
The shakal (discretion) of a adam (man) arak (makes) him slow to ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting). It is his glory to overlook an offense.
The malak (king) zaip (wrath) is like the naham (roaring) of a kapayar (lion), but his favor is like tal (dew) on the ishab (grass).
A kasayal (foolish) ban (son) is the hawah (calamity/destruction) of his ab (father). A ashah (wife/individual woman) quarrels are a tarad (continual) dripping.
Bayath (house) and riches are an nachalah (inheritance) from ab (father), but a shakal (prudent) ashah (wife/individual woman) is from Yahawah.
Itzalah (slothfulness) napal (fall / be cast down) into a tharadamah (deep) sleep. The ramayah (idle) napash (living being/soul) shall raib (suffer) hunger.
He who shamar (keep/guard) the matzawah (commandment) shamar (keep/guard) his napash (living being/soul), but he who is contemptuous in his darak (ways) shall mawath (death).
He who chanan (has) pity on the dal (poor) lawah (lends) to Yahawah; he will shalam (reward) him.
Discipline your ban (son), for there is thaqawah (hope); don't be a willing party to his mawath (death).
A hot - tempered garal (man) must pay the penalty, for if you natzal (rescue) him, you must yasap (do) it again.
Shamai (hearken / hear) to itzah (counsel) and qabal (receive) mawasar (instruction), that you may be chakam (wise) in your acharayath (latter) end.
There are many plans in a ayash (husband/individual man) lab (heart), but yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) itzah (counsel) will prevail.
That which makes a adam (man) to be thaawah (desired) is his chasad (grace). A rawash (poor) man is tawab (pleasant/functional) than a kazab (liar).
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah leads to chay (life), then contentment; he lawan (rests) and will not be touched by rai (trouble).
The itzal (sluggard) buries his yad (hand) in the tzalachath (dish); he will not so much as shawab (turn back / repent) it to his pah (mouth) again.
Flog a lawatz (scoffer), and the pathay (simple) will learn prudence; yakach (rebuke) one who has bayan (between), and he will gain daith (knowledge).
He who robs his ab (father) and barach (drives) away his am (mother), is a ban (son) who bawash (causes) shame and chapar (brings) reproach.
If you stop shamai (hearken / hear) to mawasar (instruction), my ban (son), you will stray from the amar (spoke) of daith (knowledge).
A corrupt id (witness) lawatz (mocks) mashapat (justice), and the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked) gulps down rashai (iniquity).
Penalties are kawan (prepared) for lawatz (scoffers), and beatings for the gaw (backs) of kasayal (fools).
Yayan (wine) is a lawatz (mocker), and beer is a brawler. Whoever is led shagah (astray) by them is not chakam (wise).
The ayamah (terror) of a malak (king) is like the naham (roaring) of a kapayar (lion). He who provokes him to ibar (pass over/through) forfeits his own napash (living being/soul).
It is an honor for a ayash (husband/individual man) to keep aloof from rayab (strife); but every awayal (fool) will be quarreling.
The itzal (sluggard) will not charash (plow) by reason of the charap (winter); therefore he shall shaal (beg) in qatzayar (harvest), and have nothing.
Itzah (counsel) in the lab (heart) of ayash (husband/individual man) is like imaq (deep) mayam (Waters); but a ayash (husband/individual man) of thabawan (understanding) will dalah (draw) it out.
Many adam (men) claim to be ayash (husband/individual man) of unfailing chasad (grace), but who can matzaa (find) a amawan (faithful) ayash (husband/individual man)?
A tzadayaq (righteous) halak (move) walks in tham (integrity). Ashar (who/that) are his ban (son) achar (other) him.
A malak (king) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the kasaa (throne) of dayan (judge) zarah (scatters) away all rai (evil) with his iyan (eye).
Who can amar (spoke), I have made my lab (heart) pure. I am zakah (clean) and without chataah (sin)?
Differing aban (stone) and differing ayapah (measures), shanayam (two) of them gam (indeed / moreover) are an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah.
Even a nair (child) makes himself nakar (known) by his mailal (doings), whether his pail (work) is zak (pure), and whether it is yashar (right).
The shamai (hearken / hear) azan (ear), and the seeing iyan (eye), Yahawah ishah (make) made even shanayam (two) of them.
Don't ahab (love) shanah (sleep), lest you yarash (come) to poverty. Paqach (open) your iyan (eye), and you shall be shabai (satisfied) with lacham (bread).
"It's no rai (good), it's no rai (good)," amar (spoke) the qanah (buyer); but when he is azal (gone) his way, then he halal (praise).
There is zahab (gold) and rab (abundance) of panayan (rubies); but the shapah (lips) of daith (knowledge) are a rare kalay (jewel).
Laqach (take / seized) the bagad (garment) of one who irab (evening) up collateral for a stranger; and hold him in chabal (pledge) for a wayward nakaray (woman).
Fraudulent lacham (food) is irab (evening) to a ayash (husband/individual man), but afterwards his pah (mouth) is malaa (filled) with chatzatz (gravel).
Plans are kawan (established) by thachabalah (advice); by wise guidance you wage malachamah (war)!
He who halak (move) about as a rakayal (tale-bearer) galah (reveals) sawad (secrets); therefore don't keep company with him who opens wide his shapah (lips).
Whoever qalal (curses) his ab (father) or his am (mother), his nayar (lamp) shall be daik (put) out in blackness of chashak (darkness).
An nachalah (inheritance) quickly gained at the raashawan (beginning), won't be barak (blessed) in the acharayath (end).
Don't amar (spoke), "I will shalam (pay) back rai (evil)." Qawah (gather/wait) for Yahawah, and he will yashai (salvation) you.
Yahawah detests differing aban (stone), and dishonest scales are not pleasing.
A gabar (man's) matzaid (steps) are from Yahawah; how then can adam (man) bayan (between) his darak (way)?
It is a mawaqash (snare) to a adam (man) to make a rash dedication, then later to consider his nadar (vow).
A chakam (wise) malak (king) zarah (winnows) out the rashai (wicked), and drives the threshing awapan (wheel) over them.
The nashamah (breathing thing) of adam (man) is yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) nayar (lamp), chapash (searching) all his chadar (innermost) chadar (parts).
Chasad (grace) and amath (truth) natzar (keep) the malak (king) safe. His kasaa (throne) is sustained by chasad (grace).
The glory of bachawar (young) men is their kach (strength / mighty / power). The splendor of zaqan (old) men is their shayabah (old age / white hair (due to age)) hair.
Patzai (wounding) blows cleanse away rai (evil), and beatings purge the chadar (innermost) chadar (parts).
The malak (king) lab (heart) is in yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) yad (hand) like the watercourses. He natah (turns) it wherever he chapatz (desires).
Every darak (way) of a ayash (husband/individual man) is yashar (right) in his own iyan (eye), but Yahawah thakan (weighs) the labah (hearts).
To ishah (make) tzadaqah (righteousness) and tzadaqah (righteousness) is more bachar (acceptable) to Yahawah than zabach (sacrifice).
A rawam (will lift up) iyan (eye), and a rachab (proud) lab (heart), the nayar (lamp) of the rashai (wicked), is chataah (sin).
The plans of the charawatz (diligent) surely lead to mawathar (profit); and everyone who is hasty surely rushes to machasawar (poverty).
Pail (getting) awatzar (treasures) by a shaqar (lying) lashawan (tongue/language) is a fleeting vapor for those who baqash (seek) mawath (death).
The violence of the rashai (wicked) will drive them away, because they maan (refuse) to ishah (make) what is mashapat (right).
The darak (way) of the guilty is devious, but the conduct of the innocent is yashar (upright).
It is tawab (pleasant/functional) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the panah (corner) of the housetop, than to share a bayath (house) with a madayan (contentious) ashah (wife/individual woman).
The napash (living being/soul) of the rashai (wicked) awah (desires) rai (evil); his neighbor finds no chanan (mercy) in his iyan (eye).
When the lawatz (mocker) is inash (punished), the pathay (simple) gains chakam (wisdom). When the chakam (wise) is shakal (instructed), he laqach (take / seized) daith (knowledge).
The tzadayaq (righteous) One shakal (considers) the bayath (house) of the rashai (wicked), and brings the rashai (wicked) to ruin.
Whoever atam (stops) his azan (ears) at the zaiq (cry) of the dal (poor), he will also qaraa (called) out, but shall not be inah (answer / respond).
A mathan (gift) in sathar (secret / hidden) kapah (pacifies) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting); and a shachad (bribe) in the cloak, iz (strong) chamah (wrath).
It is shamachah (joy) to the tzadayaq (righteous) to ishah (make) mashapat (justice); but it is a machathah (destruction) to the pail (workers) of awan (iniquity).
The adam (man) who thaih (wanders) out of the darak (way) of shakal (understanding) shall nawach (rest) in the qahal (assembly) of the rapaa (dead).
He who ahab (love) shamachah (pleasure) shall be a machasawar (poor) ayash (husband/individual man). He who ahab (love) yayan (wine) and shaman (oil) shall not be ishar (rich).
The rashai (wicked) is a kapar (ransom) for the tzadayaq (righteous); the bagad (treacherous) for the tzadayaq (righteous).
It is tawab (pleasant/functional) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) in a desert land, than with a madawan (contentious) and fretful ashah (wife/individual woman).
There is chamad (precious) awatzar (treasure) and shaman (oil) in the nawah (habitation) of the chakam (wise); but a kasayal (foolish) adam (man) balai (swallows) it up.
He who radap (follows) after tzadaqah (righteousness) and chasad (grace) matzaa (finds) chay (life), tzadaqah (righteousness), and honor.
A chakam (wise) man ilah (go up / offer) the iyar (city) of the gabawar (mighty), and yarad (brings) down the iz (strength / might / refuge) of its mabatach (confidence).
Whoever guards his pah (mouth) and his lashawan (tongue/language) shamar (keep/guard) his napash (living being/soul) from tzarah (troubles).
The zad (proud) and haughty man, "scoffer" is his sham (name); he ishah (make) in the arrogance of zadawan (pride).
The thaawah (desire) of the itzal (sluggard) mawath (death) him, for his yad (hand) maan (refuse) to ishah (make).
There are those who awah (covet) thaawah (greedily) all yawam (day) long; but the tzadayaq (righteous) nathan (give) and don't chashak (darkness).
The zabach (sacrifice) of the rashai (wicked) is an thawaibah (abomination): how much more, when he bawaa (come) it with a zamah (wicked) mind!
A kazab (false) id (witness) will abad (destroy/perish), and a ayash (husband/individual man) who shamai (hearken / hear) dabar (word / matter) to eternity.
A rashai (wicked) ayash (husband/individual man) izaz (hardens) his panayam (face); but as for the yashar (upright), he establishes his darak (ways).
There is no chakamah (wisdom) nor thabawan (understanding) nor itzah (counsel) against Yahawah.
The sawas (horse) is kawan (prepared) for the yawam (day) of malachamah (battle); but thashawaih (deliverance) is with Yahawah.
A good sham (name) is more desirable than rab (great) riches, and tawab (pleasant/functional) favor is better than kasap (silver) and zahab (gold).
The ishayar (rich) and the rawash (poor) have this in common: Yahawah is the maker of them all.
A irawam (prudent) man raah (see) danger, and sathar (hides) himself; but the pathay (simple) ibar (pass over/through) on, and suffer for it.
The result of inawah (humility) and the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is wealth, honor, and chay (life).
Tzan (thorns) and pach (snares) are in the darak (path) of the iqash (wicked): whoever guards his napash (living being/soul) stays from them.
Chanak (train) up a nair (child) in the darak (way) he should go, and when he is zaqan (old) he will not sawar (depart) from it.
The ishayar (rich) mashal (rule/have dominion) over the rawash (poor). The lawah (borrower) is ibad (servant) to the lender.
He who zarai (sows) iwal (wickedness) qatzar (reaps) trouble, and the shabat (rod) of his fury will be kalah (complete / finish).
He who has a generous iyan (eye) will be barak (blessed); for he shares his lacham (food) with the dal (poor).
Garash (drive) out the lawatz (mocker), and dayan (judge) will yatzaa (go out / come out) out; yes, quarrels and insults will stop.
He who ahab (love) purity of lab (heart) and speaks gracefully is the malak (king) rai (neigbor/another person).
The iyan (eye) of Yahawah watch over daith (knowledge); but he frustrates the dabar (word / matter) of the bagad (unfaithful).
The itzal (sluggard) amar (spoke), There is a aray (lion) outside! I will be ratzach (killed) in the rachab (streets)!
The pah (mouth) of an adulteress is a imaq (deep) shawachah (pit): he who is under yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) zaim (wrath) will napal (fall / be cast down) into it.
Awalath (folly) is qashar (bound) up in the lab (heart) of a nair (child): the shabat (rod) of mawasar (discipline) rachaq (drives) it far from him.
Whoever oppresses the dal (poor) for his own rabah (increase) and whoever nathan (give) to the ishayar (rich), both come to machasawar (poverty).
Natah (turn) your azan (ear), and listen to the dabar (word / matter) of the chakam (wise). Shayath (put / appoint / make) your lab (heart) to my teaching.
For it is a naiyam (pleasant) thing if you shamar (keep/guard) them batan (within) you, if yachad (all) of them are kawan (ready) on your shapah (lips).
That your mabatach (trust) may be in Yahawah, I yadai (teach) you today, even you.
Haven't I kathab (written) to you thirty excellent things of mawaitzah (counsel) and daith (knowledge),
To yadai (teach) you amath (truth), reliable amar (spoke), to give sound shawab (turn back / repent) to the ones who shalach (send) you?
Don't exploit the dal (poor), because he is dal (poor); and don't dakaa (crush) the inay (needy) in court;
For Yahawah will rayab (plead) their case, and plunder the napash (living being/soul) of those who plunder them.
Don't befriend a hot-tempered bail (man), and don't associate with bail (one) who harbors chamah (anger):
Lest you alap (learn) his arach (ways), and ensnare your napash (living being/soul).
Don't you be one of those who thaqai (blow / sound alarm) kap (hands), of those who are collateral for mashaah (debts).
If you don't have means to shalam (pay), why should he laqach (take / seized) away your mashakab (bed) from under you?
Don't move the iwalam (forever) boundary gabawal (border/boundary), which your ab (father) ishah (make) set up.
Do you chazah (see) a ayash (husband/individual man) skilled in his malaakah (work)? He will yatzab (serve) malak (king). He won't yatzab (serve) obscure men.
When you yashab (inhabit/dwell) to lacham (eat) with a mashal (rule/have dominion), bayan (between) bayan (between) what is panayam (before) you;
Shawam (place / establish / appoint) a shakayan (knife) to your lai (throat), if you are a bail (man) given to napash (living being/soul).
Don't be awah (desirous) of his mataim (dainties), since they are kazab (deceitful) lacham (food).
Don't yagai (weary) yourself to be ishar (rich). In your bayanah (wisdom), show restraint.
Why do you iwap (flying) your iyan (eye) on that which is not? For it ishah (make) sprouts kanap (wings) like an nashar (eagle) and iwap (flying) in the sky.
Don't lacham (eat) the lacham (food) of him who has a stingy iyan (eye), and don't crave his delicacies:
For as he shair (thinks) about the cost, so he is. "Akal (eat) and shathah (drinks)!" He amar (spoke) to you, but his lab (heart) is not with you.
The path (morsel) which you have akal (eat) you shall qawaa (vomit) up, and shachath (lose) your naiyam (good) dabar (word / matter).
Don't dabar (word / matter) in the azan (ears) of a kasayal (fool), for he will bawaz (despise) the shakal (wisdom) of your malah (words).
Don't move the iwalam (forever) boundary gabawal (border/boundary). Don't encroach on the shadah (fields) of the yathawam (fatherless):
For their Defender is chazaq (strong). He will rayab (plead) their case against you.
Bawaa (come) your lab (heart) to mawasar (instruction), and your azan (ears) to the amar (spoke) of daith (knowledge).
Don't manai (withhold) mawasar (correction) from a nair (child). If you nakah (punish) him with the shabat (rod), he will not mawath (death).
Nakah (punish) him with the shabat (rod), and natzal (save) his napash (living being/soul) from shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife).
My ban (son), if your lab (heart) is chakam (wise), then my lab (heart) will be shamach (glad), even anay (mine):
Yes, my kalayah (heart) will ilaz (rejoice), when your shapah (lips) dabar (word / matter) what is mayashar (right).
Don't let your lab (heart) qanaa (jealous) chataa (sinners); but rather yaraah (fear) Yahawah all the yawam (day) long.
Indeed surely there is a future thaqawah (hope), and your hope will not be karath (cut) off.
Shamai (hearken / hear), my ban (son), and be chakam (wise), and keep your lab (heart) on the right darak (path)!
Don't be among yayan (ones) drinking too much zalal (wine), or those who gorge themselves on meat:
For the sabaa (drunkard) and the zalal (glutton) shall become yarash (poor); and nawamah (drowsiness) labash (clothes) them in qarai (rags).
Shamai (hearken / hear) to your ab (father) who gave you yalad (birth / begot), and don't bawaz (despise) your am (mother) when she is zaqan (old).
Qanah (buy) the amath (truth), and don't makar (sell) it. Get chakamah (wisdom), mawasar (discipline), and bayanah (understanding).
The ab (father) of the tzadayaq (righteous) has great gayal (joy). Whoever yalad (birth / begot) a chakam (wise) child delights in him.
Let your ab (father) and your am (mother) be shamach (glad)! Let her who yalad (birth / begot) you gayal (rejoice)!
My ban (son), nathan (give) me your lab (heart); and let your iyan (eye) keep in my darak (ways).
For a prostitute is a imaq (deep) shawachah (pit); and a wayward wife is a tzar (oppressor / distressor) baar (well).
Yes, she lies in arab (wait) like a robber, and yasap (increases) the bagad (unfaithful) among adam (men).
Who has away (woe)? Who has abaway (sorrow)? Who has strife? Who has shayach (complaints)? Who has needless bruises? Who has bloodshot iyan (eye)?
Those who achar (other) long at the yayan (wine); those who bawaa (come) to chaqar (seek) out mixed mamasak (wine).
Don't raah (see) at the yayan (wine) when it is adam (red), when it sparkles in the kayas (cup), when it halak (move) down smoothly.
In the acharayath (end), it nashak (bites) like a snake, and poisons like a viper.
Your iyan (eye) will raah (see) zawar (strange) things, and your lab (heart) will imagine confusing things.
Yes, you will be as he who shakab (lies) down in the lab (heart) of the yam (sea/waters), or as he who shakab (lies) on raash (head) of the rigging:
They hit me, and I was not hurt! They halam (beat) me, and I don't yadai (feel) it! When will I qawatz (wake) up? I can do it again. I can find another.
Don't be qanaa (jealous) of rai (evil) ayash (husband/individual man); neither awah (desire) to be with them:
For their lab (heart) plot violence, and their shapah (lips) dabar (word / matter) about imal (mischief).
Through chakamah (wisdom) a bayath (house) is banah (built); by thabawan (understanding) it is kawan (established);
By daith (knowledge) the rooms are malaa (filled) with all rare and beautiful treasure.
A chakam (wise) gabar (man) has great kach (strength / mighty / power); and a knowledgeable ayash (husband/individual man) amatz (increases) kach (strength / mighty / power);
For by wise guidance you wage your malachamah (war); and thashawaih (deliverance) is in many advisors.
Chakamawath (wisdom) is rawam (will lift up) high for a awayal (fool): he doesn't pathach (open) his pah (mouth) in the shair (gate).
Chashab (one) who plots to do raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) will be qaraa (called) a schemer.
The schemes of awalath (folly) are chataah (sin). The lawatz (mocker) is detested by adam (men).
If you falter in the yawam (day) of tzarah (trouble), your kach (strength / mighty / power) is tzar (oppressor / distressor).
Natzal (rescue) those who are being led away to mawath (death)! Indeed, chashak (darkness) back those who are staggering to the harag (slaughter)!

If you amar (spoke), "Behold, we didn't yadai (know) this;" doesn't he who thakan (weighs) the labah (hearts) bayan (between) it? He who natzar (keeps) your napash (living being/soul), doesn't he yadai (know) it? Shall he not shawab (turn back / repent) to every adam (man) according to his pail (work)?
My ban (son), akal (eat) dabash (honey), for it is tawab (pleasant/functional); the droppings of the napath (honeycomb), which are mathawaq (sweet) to your chak (taste):

So you shall yadai (know) chakamah (wisdom) to be to your napash (living being/soul); if you matzaa (have) found it, then there yash (will) be a acharayath (reward), your thaqawah (hope) will not be karath (cut) off.
Don't arab (lay) in wait, rashai (wicked) man, against the nawah (habitation) of the tzadayaq (righteous). Don't shadad (destroy) his rabatz (resting) place:
For a tzadayaq (righteous) man napal (fall / be cast down) shabai (seven) times, and qawam (rise up) up again; but the rashai (wicked) are kashal (stumble / stagger) by rai (calamity).
Don't shamach (rejoice) when your ayab (enemy) napal (fall / be cast down). Don't let your lab (heart) be gayal (glad) when he is kashal (stumble / stagger);
Lest Yahawah raah (see) it, and it raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) him, and he shawab (turn back / repent) away his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) from him.
Don't charah (hot with anger) yourself because of evildoers; neither be qanaa (jealous) of the rashai (wicked):
For there will be no acharayath (reward) to the rai (evil) man; and the nayar (lamp) of the rashai (wicked) shall be snuffed out.
My ban (son), yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah and the malak (king). Don't join those who are rebellious:
For their ayad (calamity) will qawam (rise up) pathaawam (suddenly); the payad (destruction) from them both—who yadai (knows)?
These also are sayings of the chakam (wise). To show partiality in mashapat (judgment) is not tawab (pleasant/functional).
He who amar (spoke) to the rashai (wicked), "You are tzadayaq (righteous);" im (people / nation) shall naqab (curse) him, and im (people / nation) shall zaim (abhor) him—
But it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and a rich barakah (blessing) will bawaa (come) on them.
An honest dabar (word / matter) is like a nashaq (kiss) on the shapah (lips).
Kawan (prepare) your malaakah (work) outside, and get your shadah (fields) ithad (ready). Afterwards, banah (build) your bayath (house).
Don't be a id (witness) against your neighbor chanam (without) cause. Don't pathah (deceive) with your shapah (lips).
Don't amar (spoke), I will ishah (make) to him as he ishah (make) done to me; I will shawab (turn back / repent) to the ayash (husband/individual man) according to his pail (work).
I ibar (pass over/through) by the shadah (field) of the sluggard, by the karam (vineyard) of the adam (man) chasar (void) of lab (heart);
Behold, it was all ilah (go up / offer) over with qamashawan (thorns). Its surface was kasah (covered) with charawal (nettles), and its aban (stone) gadar (wall) was haras (broken) down.
Then I chazah (saw), and shayath (put / appoint / make) well. I raah (see), and laqach (take / seized) mawasar (instruction):
A mait (little) shanah (sleep), a mait (little) thanawamah (slumber), a mait (little) chabaq (folding) of the yad (hand) to sleep;
So your rayash (poverty) will bawaa (come) as a robber, and your machasawar (want) as an magan (shield) ayash (husband/individual man).
These also are mashal (proverbs) of Shalamah (Solomon), which the ayash (husband/individual man) of Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) ithaq (copied) out.
It is the kabawad (glory) of Alahayam to sathar (conceal) a thing, but the kabawad (glory) of malak (king) is to chaqar (search) out a dabar (word / matter).
As the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) for rawam (will lift up), and the aratz (Earth/land) for imaq (depth), so the lab (heart) of malak (king) are unsearchable.
Take hagah (away) the sayag (dross) from the kasap (silver), and material yatzaa (go out / come out) out for the refiner;
Take hagah (away) the rashai (wicked) from the malak (king) panayam (presence), and his kasaa (throne) will be kawan (established) in tzadaq (righteous / just / fair).
Don't exalt yourself in the panayam (presence) of the malak (king), or claim a maqawam (place) among gadawal (very great/important/mighty) men;

For it is tawab (pleasant/functional) that it be amar (spoke) to you, "ilah (go up / offer) up here," than that you should be shapal (put) lower in the panayam (presence) of the nadayab (prince), whom your iyan (eye) raah (see) seen.
Don't be hasty in yatzaa (go out / come out) charges to court. What will you ishah (make) in the acharayath (end) when your neighbor kalam (shames) you?
Rayab (debate) your case with your neighbor, and don't betray the confidence of achar (other);
Lest one who shamai (hearken / hear) it chasad (grace) you to shame, and your bad reputation never depart.
A dabar (word / matter) fitly dabar (word / matter) is like thapawach (apples) of zahab (gold) in settings of kasap (silver).
As an nazam (earring) of zahab (gold), and an chalay (ornament) of katham (fine) gold, so is a chakam (wise) yakach (reprover) to an shamai (hearken / hear) azan (ear).

As the tzanah (cold) of shalag (snow) in the yawam (day) of qatzayar (harvest), so is a aman (believe / have faith) tzayar (messenger) to those who shalach (send) him; for he refreshes the napash (living being/soul) of his adawan (master / lord).
As nashayaa (clouds) and rawach (spirit / wind) without gasham (rain), so is he who halal (praise) of mathath (gifts) deceptively.
By patience a qatzayan (ruler) is pathah (persuaded). A rak (soft) lashawan (tongue/language) shabar (breaks) the garam (bone).
Matzaa (have) you found dabash (honey)? Akal (eat) as much as is day (sufficient) for you, lest you eat too much, and qawaa (vomit) it.
Let your ragal (feet / foot) be seldom in your neighbor's bayath (house), lest he be shabai (weary) of you, and shanaa (hate) you.
A ayash (husband/individual man) who inah (answer / respond) shaqar (false) id (testimony) against his neighbor is like a club, a charab (sword), or a shanan (sharp) chatz (arrow).
Mabatach (confidence) in someone bagad (unfaithful) in yawam (day) of tzarah (trouble) is like a bad shan (tooth), or a lame ragal (feet / foot).
As one who idah (takes) away a bagad (garment) in qarah (cold) yawam (day), or chamatz (vinegar) on soda, so is one who shayar (sings) shayar (song) to a rai (heavy) lab (heart).
If your shanaa (hate) is raib (hungry), give him lacham (food) to akal (eat). If he is thirsty, give him mayam (Waters) to shaqah (drink):
For you will chathah (heap) gachal (coals) of fire on his raash (head), and Yahawah will shalam (reward) you.
The tzapawan (north) rawach (spirit / wind) chawal (brings) forth gasham (rain): so a sathar (secret / hidden) lashawan (tongue/language) brings an zaim (angry) panayam (face).
It is tawab (pleasant/functional) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the panah (corner) of the housetop, than to share a bayath (house) with a madawan (contentious) ashah (wife/individual woman).
Like qar (cold) mayam (Waters) to a iyap (thirsty) napash (living being/soul), so is tawab (pleasant/functional) shamawaih (news) from a marachaq (far) aratz (Earth/land).
Like a muddied maiyan (spring), and a polluted maqawar (well), so is a tzadayaq (righteous) mawat (man) who gives way panayam (before) the rashai (wicked).
It is not tawab (pleasant/functional) to akal (eat) much dabash (honey); nor is it honorable to seek kabawad (one's) own honor.
Like a iyar (city) that is paratz (broken) down and without chawamah (walls) is a ayash (husband/individual man) whose rawach (spirit / wind) is without restraint.
Like shalag (snow) in qayatz (summer), and as matar (rain) in qatzayar (harvest), so honor is not fitting for a kasayal (fool).
Like a fluttering tzapawar (sparrow), like a darting darawar (swallow), so the undeserved qalalah (curse) doesn't bawaa (come) to bawaa (come).
A shawat (whip) is for the sawas (horse), a mathag (bridle) for the donkey, and a shabat (rod) for the gaw (back) of kasayal (fools)!
Don't inah (answer / respond) a kasayal (fool) according to his awalath (folly), lest you also be shawah (like) him.
Inah (answer / respond) a kasayal (fool) according to his awalath (folly), lest he be chakam (wise) in his own iyan (eye).
One who shalach (send) a dabar (word / matter) by the yad (hand) of a kasayal (fool) is qatzah (end / extremity / border) off ragal (feet / foot) and shathah (drinks) chamas (violence).
Like the shawaq (legs) of the pasach (lame) that hang loose: so is a mashal (parable) in the pah (mouth) of kasayal (fools).
As one who binds a aban (stone) in a maragamah (sling), so is he who nathan (give) honor to a kasayal (fool).
Like a thornbush that ilah (go up / offer) into the yad (hand) of a drunkard, so is a mashal (parable) in the pah (mouth) of kasayal (fools).
As an archer who wounds all, so is he who shakar (hires) a kasayal (fool) or he who shakar (hires) those who ibar (pass over/through) by.
As a kalab (dog) that shawab (turn back / repent) to his qaa (vomit), so is a kasayal (fool) who shanah (repeats) his awalath (folly).
Do you raah (see) a ayash (husband/individual man) chakam (wise) in his own iyan (eye)? There is more thaqawah (hope) for a kasayal (fool) than for him.
The itzal (sluggard) amar (spoke), There is a shachal (lion) in the road! A fierce shachal (lion) roams the rachab (streets)!
As the dalath (door) sabab (turns) on its tzayar (hinges), so does the itzal (sluggard) on his matah (bed).
The itzal (sluggard) buries his yad (hand) in the tzalachath (dish). He is too lazy to shawab (turn back / repent) it back to his pah (mouth).
The itzal (sluggard) is wiser in his own iyan (eye) than shabai (seven) men who shawab (turn back / repent) with taim (discretion).
Like chazaq (one) who grabs a kalab (dog's) azan (ears) is ibar (pass over/through) who passes by and ibar (pass over/through) in a quarrel not his own.
Like a madman who yarah (shoots) torches, chatz (arrows), and mawath (death),
Is the ayash (husband/individual man) who ramah (deceives) his neighbor and amar (spoke), Am I not joking?
For lack of itz (wood) a ash (fire) kabah (goes) out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.
As pacham (coals) are to hot embers, and itz (wood) to ash (fire), so is a madawan (contentious) ayash (husband/individual man) to charar (kindling) rayab (strife).
The dabar (word / matter) of a naragan (whisperer) are as dainty morsels, they yarad (go) down into the innermost chadar (parts).
Like kasap (silver) sayag (dross) on an charash (earthen) vessel are the shapah (lips) of a fervent one with an rai (evil) lab (heart).
A malicious nakar (man) disguises himself with his shapah (lips), but he harbors maramah (evil) in his qarab (among / near).
When his speech is charming, don't aman (believe / have faith) him; for there are shabai (seven) thawaibah (abominations) in his lab (heart).
His malice may be kasah (concealed) by deception, but his rai (wickedness) will be exposed in the qahal (assembly).
Whoever karah (digs) a shachath (pit) shall napal (fall / be cast down) into it. Whoever galal (rolls) a aban (stone), it will shawab (turn back / repent) back on him.
A shaqar (lying) lashawan (tongue/language) shanaa (hate) those it hurts; and a chalaq (flattering) pah (mouth) ishah (make) madachah (ruin).
Don't halal (praise) about machar (tomorrow); for you don't yadai (know) what a machar (day) may yalad (birth / begot) forth.
Let another zawar (man) halal (praise) you, and not your own pah (mouth); a stranger, and not your own shapah (lips).
A aban (stone) is kabad (heavy), and chawal (sand) is a burden; but a awayal (fool's) kais (provocation) is kabad (heavier) than shanayam (two).
Chamah (wrath) is akazarayawath (cruel), and ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) is overwhelming; but who is able to imad (stand) panayam (before) qanaah (jealousy)?
Tawab (pleasant/functional) is galah (open) thawakachah (rebuke) than sathar (hidden) ahabah (love).
Aman (believe / have faith) are the patzai (wounds) of a ahab (love); although the kisses of an shanaa (hate) are profuse.
A shabai (full) napash (living being/soul) loathes a napath (honeycomb); but to a raib (hungry) napash (living being/soul), every mar (bitter) thing is mathawaq (sweet).
As a tzapawar (bird) that nadad (wanders) from her qan (nest), so is a ayash (husband/individual man) who nadad (wanders) from his maqawam (place).
Qatarath (perfume) and incense bring shamach (joy) to the lab (heart); so does earnest itzah (counsel) from a man's rai (neigbor/another person).

Don't izab (forsake) your rai (neigbor/another person) and your ab (father) rai (neigbor/another person). Don't bawaa (come) to your ach (brother/kinsman) bayath (house) in the yawam (day) of your disaster: tawab (pleasant/functional) is a neighbor who is qarawab (near) than a distant ach (brother/kinsman).
Be chakam (wise), my ban (son), and bring shamach (joy) to my lab (heart), then I can shawab (turn back / repent) my tormentor.
A irawam (prudent) man raah (see) danger and takes refuge; but the pathay (simple) ibar (pass over/through) on, and suffer for it.
Laqach (take / seized) his bagad (garment) when he irab (evening) up collateral for a stranger. Hold it for a wayward nakaray (woman)!
He who blesses his neighbor with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice) shakam (early) in the shakam (morning), it will be taken as a qalalah (curse) by him.
A tarad (continual) dalap (dropping) on a sagarayad (rainy) yawam (day) and a madawan (contentious) ashah (wife/individual woman) are alike:
Restraining her is like restraining the rawach (spirit / wind), or like grasping shaman (oil) in his right yamayan (right hand).
Barazal (iron) chadad (sharpens) barazal (iron); so a ayash (husband/individual man) chadad (sharpens) his rai (neigbor/another person) panayam (countenance).
Whoever tends the thaan (fig) tree shall akal (eat) its paray (fruit). He who shamar (keep/guard) after his adawan (master / lord) shall be honored.
As mayam (Waters) reflects a panayam (face), so a adam (man's) lab (heart) reflects the adam (man).
Shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife) and Abaddon are laa (NOT) shabai (satisfied); and a adam (man's) iyan (eye) are never shabai (satisfied).
The crucible is for kasap (silver), and the kawar (furnace) for zahab (gold); but ayash (husband/individual man) is refined by his mahalal (praise).
Though you grind a awayal (fool) in a makathash (mortar) with a ilay (went up) along with grain, yet his awalath (foolishness) will not be sawar (removed) from him.
Yadai (know) well the panayam (state) of your tzaan (flocks), and pay attention to your idar (herds):
For riches are not iwalam (forever), nor does even the nazar (crown / consecrate) endure to all dawar (generation / age / period).
The chatzayar (hay) is removed, and the new growth raah (see), the grasses of the har (mountain) are asap (gathered) in.
The kabash (lambs) are for your labawash (clothing), and the ithawad (goats) are the machayar (price) of a shadah (field).
There will be plenty of iz (goats)' chalab (milk) for your lacham (food), for your bayath (house) lacham (food), and for the nourishment of your nairah (servant) girls.
The rashai (wicked) nawas (flee) when no one radap (pursues); but the tzadayaq (righteous) are as batach (bold) as a kapayar (lion).
In pashai (rebellion), a aratz (Earth/land) rab (has) many shar (prince / ruler), but order is maintained by a adam (man) of bayan (between) and yadai (knowledge).
A rawash (needy) gabar (man) who oppresses the dal (poor) is like a driving matar (rain) which leaves no crops.
Those who izab (forsake) the thawarah (instruction) halal (praise) the rashai (wicked); but those who shamar (keep/guard) the thawarah (instruction) garah (contend) with them.
Rai (evil) ayash (husband/individual man) don't bayan (between) mashapat (justice); but those who baqash (seek) Yahawah bayan (between) it fully.
Tawab (pleasant/functional) is the rawash (poor) who halak (move) in his tham (integrity), than he who is iqash (perverse) in his darak (ways), and he is ishayar (rich).
Whoever natzar (keeps) the thawarah (instruction) is a bayan (between) ban (son); but he who is a raih (companion) of zalal (gluttons) kalam (shames) his ab (father).
He who rabah (increases) his hawan (wealth) by excessive interest qabatz (gathers) it for one who chanan (has) pity on the dal (poor).
He who sawar (turns) away his azan (ear) from shamai (hearken / hear) the thawarah (instruction), even his thapalah (prayer) is an thawaibah (abomination).

Whoever causes the yashar (upright) to shagah (go) astray in an rai (evil) darak (way), he will napal (fall / be cast down) into his own trap; but the blameless will nachal (inherit) tawab (pleasant/functional).
The ishayar (rich) ayash (husband/individual man) is chakam (wise) in his own iyan (eye); but the dal (poor) who has bayan (between) sees through him.
When the tzadayaq (righteous) ilatz (triumph), there is rab (great) glory; but when the rashai (wicked) qawam (rise up), adam (men) chapash (hide) themselves.
He who kasah (conceals) his pashai (sins) doesn't tzalach (prosper), but whoever confesses and renounces them finds racham (mercy).
Ashar (who/that) is the adam (man) who thamayad (always) pachad (fear / dread); but qashah (rough / hard) who hardens his lab (heart) napal (fall / be cast down) into rai (trouble).
As a naham (roaring) aray (lion) or a charging dab (bear), so is a rashai (wicked) mashal (rule/have dominion) over helpless im (people / nation).
A tyrannical nagayad (ruler) chasar (lacks) thabawan (judgment). One who shanaa (hate) ill-gotten gain will have arak (long) yawam (day).
A adam (man) who is tormented by napash (living being/soul) dam (blood) will be a fugitive until bawar (death); no thamak (one) will support him.
Whoever halak (move) blamelessly is kept yashai (salvation); but one with iqash (perverse) darak (ways) will napal (fall / be cast down) suddenly.
One who ibad (servant) his adamah (land) will shabai (have) an abundance of lacham (food); but one who radap (chases) fantasies will have his fill of rayash (poverty).
A amawanah (faithful) ayash (husband/individual man) is rich with barakah (blessings); but awatz (one) who is eager to be ishar (rich) will not go naqah (clean/innocent).
To show partiality is not tawab (pleasant/functional); yet a gabar (man) will do wrong for a path (piece) of lacham (bread).
A stingy iyan (eye) hurries after riches, and doesn't yadai (know) that chasar (poverty) waits for him.
One who yakach (rebukes) a adam (man) will afterward matzaa (find) more favor than one who chalaq (flatters) with the lashawan (tongue/language).
Whoever gazal (robs) his ab (father) or his am (mother), and amar (spoke), "It's not wrong." He is a partner with a destroyer.
Napash (living being/soul) who is greedy garah (stirs) up madawan (strife); but one who batach (trusts) in Yahawah will dashan (prosper).
One who batach (trusts) in himself is a kasayal (fool); but one who halak (move) in chakamah (wisdom) is kept safe.
One who nathan (give) to the rawash (poor) has no machasawar (lack); but ilam (one) who closes his iyan (eye) will rab (have) many maarah (curses).
When the rashai (wicked) qawam (rise up), adam (men) sathar (hide) themselves; but when they abad (destroy/perish), the tzadayaq (righteous) thrive.
He who is often thawakachah (rebuked) and stiffens his irap (neck) will be shabar (destroyed) pathai (suddenly), with no marapaa (remedy).
When the tzadayaq (righteous) thrive, the im (people / nation) shamach (rejoice); but when the rashai (wicked) mashal (rule/have dominion), the im (people / nation) anach (groan).
Ayash (husband/individual man) ahab (love) chakamah (wisdom) brings shamach (joy) to his ab (father); but a raih (companion) of prostitutes squanders his hawan (wealth).
The malak (king) by mashapat (justice) makes the aratz (Earth/land) stable, but he who takes bribes tears it down.
A gabar (man) who chalaq (flatters) his neighbor parash (spreads) a rashath (net) for his paim (feet).
An rai (evil) ayash (husband/individual man) is mawaqash (snared) by his pashai (sin), but the tzadayaq (righteous) can ranan (sing) and be shamach (glad).
The tzadayaq (righteous) care about dayan (judge) for the dal (poor). The rashai (wicked) aren't concerned about daith (knowledge).
Mockers stir up a qarayah (city), but chakam (wise) men shawab (turn back / repent) away ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).
If a chakam (wise) ayash (husband/individual man) goes to court with a awayal (foolish) ayash (husband/individual man), the fool ragaz (rages) or scoffs, and there is no nachath (peace).
The bloodthirsty shanaa (hate) a tham (man) of integrity; and they baqash (seek) the napash (living being/soul) of the yashar (upright).
A kasayal (fool) vents all of his rawach (spirit / wind), but a chakam (wise) shabach (man) brings himself under control.
If a mashal (rule/have dominion) listens to lies, all of his officials are rashai (wicked).
The rawash (poor) ayash (husband/individual man) and the oppressor have this in common: Yahawah gives iyan (eye) to the iyan (eye) of shanayam (two).
The malak (king) who fairly shapat (judges) the dal (poor), his kasaa (throne) shall be kawan (established) id (forever).
The shabat (rod) of thawakachah (correction) nathan (give) chakamah (wisdom), but a nair (child) shalach (send) to himself bawash (causes) shame to his am (mother).
When the rashai (wicked) rabah (increase), pashai (sin) rabah (increases); but the tzadayaq (righteous) will raah (see) their downfall.
Yasar (correct) your ban (son), and he will nawach (give) you peace; yes, he will nathan (give) maidan (delight) to your napash (living being/soul).
Where there is no revelation, the im (people / nation) cast off restraint; but one who shamar (keep/guard) the thawarah (instruction) is ashar (who/that).
A ibad (servant) can't be yasar (corrected) by dabar (word / matter). Though he bayan (between), yet he will not respond.
Do you chazah (see) a ayash (husband/individual man) who is hasty in his dabar (word / matter)? There is more thaqawah (hope) for a kasayal (fool) than for him.
He who pampers his ibad (servant) from nair (youth) will have him become a manawan (son) in the acharayath (end).
An angry ayash (husband/individual man) garah (stirs) up madawan (strife), and a chamah (wrathful) bail (man) rab (abounds) in pashai (sin).
A adam (man's) gaawah (pride) shapal (brings) him low, but shapal (one) of lowly rawach (spirit / wind) gains honor.
Whoever is an accomplice of a ganab (thief) is an shanaa (hate) of his own napash (living being/soul). He takes an alah (these), but dares not testify.
The charadah (fear) of adam (man) proves to be a mawaqash (snare), but whoever batach (puts) his trust in Yahawah is kept shagab (safe).
Many baqash (seek) the mashal (rule/have dominion) favor, but a ayash (husband/individual man) mashapat (justice) comes from Yahawah.
A dishonest ayash (husband/individual man) detests the tzadayaq (righteous), and the yashar (upright) in their darak (ways) detest the rashai (wicked).
The dabar (word / matter) of Agawar (Agur) the ban (son) of Yaqah (Jakeh), the oracle: the gabar (man) naam (declares (prophetically)) to Ayathayaal (Ithiel), to Ayathayaal (Ithiel) and Akal (Ucal):
Surely I am the most ignorant ayash (husband/individual man), and don't have a ayash (husband/individual man) bayanah (understanding).
I have not lamad (teach/instruct) chakamah (wisdom), neither do I yadai (have) the daith (knowledge) of the qadawash (holy) One.

Who has ilah (go up / offer) up into shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), and descended? Who has asap (gathered) the rawach (spirit / wind) in his chapan (fists)? Who has tzarar (bound) the mayam (Waters) in his shamalah (garment)? Who has qawam (rise up) all the apas (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land)? What is his sham (name), and what is his ban (son) sham (name), if you yadai (know)?
Every amarah (sayings) of Alawah is flawless. He is a magan (shield) to those who take chasah (refuge) in him.
Don't you yasap (add) to his dabar (word / matter), lest he yakach (reprove) you, and you be kazab (found) a liar.
Shanayam (two) things I have shaal (asked) of you; don't manai (deny) me before I mawath (death):
Rachaq (remove) far from me falsehood and lies. Nathan (give) me neither rayash (poverty) nor riches. Tarap (feed) me with the lacham (food) that is needful for me;
Lest I be shabai (full), kachash (deny) you, and amar (spoke), ‘Who is Yahawah?’ Or lest I be yarash (poor), and ganab (steal), and so dishonor the sham (name) of my Alahayam.
Don't lashan (slander) a ibad (servant) to his adawan (master / lord), lest he qalal (curse) you, and you be asham (held) guilty.
There is a dawar (generation / age / period) that qalal (curses) their ab (father), and doesn't barak (bless) their am (mother).
There is a dawar (generation / age / period) that is tahawar (pure) in their own iyan (eye), yet are not rachatz (washed) from their tzawaah (filthiness).
There is a dawar (generation / age / period), oh how rawam (will lift up) are their iyan (eye)! Their ipaip (eyelids) are nashaa (lift) up.

There is a dawar (generation / age / period) whose shan (teeth) are like charab (sword), and their mathalaih (jaws) like knives, to akal (eat) the inay (poor) from the aratz (Earth/land), and the abayawan (needy) from among adam (men).
The leach has shanayam (two) bath (daughter): ‘yahab (give), yahab (give).’ There are shalawash (three) things that are never shabai (satisfied); arabai (four) that don't say, ‘hawan (enough):’

Shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife), the itzar (barren) racham (womb); the aratz (Earth/land) that is not shabai (satisfied) with mayam (Waters); and the ash (fire) that doesn't amar (spoke), ‘hawan (enough).’

The iyan (eye) that laig (mocks) at his ab (father), and scorns obedience to his am (mother): the irab (evening) of the nachal (stream / river) shall naqar (pick) it out, the ban (son) nashar (eagles) shall akal (eat) it.
There are shalawash (three) things which are palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) amazing for me, arabai (four) which I don't yadai (understand):

The darak (way) of an nashar (eagle) in the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)); the darak (way) of a nachash (serpent) on a tzawar (rock); the darak (way) of a anayah (ship) in the lab (heart) of the yam (sea/waters); and the darak (way) of a gabar (man) with a maiden.
So is the darak (way) of an adulterous ashah (wife/individual woman): she akal (eat) and machah (wipes) her pah (mouth), and amar (spoke), ‘I have pail (done) nothing wrong.’
For shalawash (three) things the aratz (Earth/land) ragaz (tremble), and under arabai (four), it can't nashaa (lift) up:
For a ibad (servant) when he is malak (king); a nabal (fool) when he is shabai (filled) with lacham (food);
For an unloved woman when she is bail (married); and a handmaid who is heir to her gabarath (mistress).
There are arabai (four) things which are qatan (small/young/least) on the aratz (Earth/land), but they are exceedingly chakam (wise):
The namalah (ants) are not a iz (strong) im (people / nation), yet they kawan (provide) their lacham (food) in the qayatz (summer).
The Shapan (conies) are but a itzawam (feeble) im (people / nation), yet shawam (place / establish / appoint) they their bayath (house) in the salai (rocks).
The arabah (locusts) have no malak (king), yet they advance in ranks.
You can thapash (catch) a lizard with your yad (hand), yet it is in malak (king)' hayakal (palaces).
There are shalawash (three) things which are stately in their march, arabai (four) which are stately in yalak (going):
The layash (lion), which is mightiest among animals, and doesn't shawab (turn back / repent) away for any;
The mathan (greyhound), the male thayash (goat) also; and the malak (king) against whom there is no alaqawam (rising) up.
If you have nabal (done) foolishly in nashaa (lift) up yourself, or if you have zamam (thought) evil, put your yad (hand) over your pah (mouth).

For as the mayatz (churning) of chalab (milk) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth chamaah (butter), and the mayatz (wringing) of the ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth dam (blood); so the mayatz (forcing) of ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth rayab (strife).
The dabar (word / matter) of malak (king) Lamawaal (Lemuel); the oracle which his am (mother) yasar (taught) him.
Oh, my bar (son)! Oh, bar (son) of my batan (womb)! Oh, bar (son) of my nadar (vow)!
Don't nathan (give) your chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) to ashah (wife/individual woman), nor your darak (ways) to that which machah (destroys) malak (king).
It is not for malak (king), Lamawaal (Lemuel); it is not for malak (king) to shathah (drinks) yayan (wine); nor for razan (princes) to say, ‘Where is shakar (strong) drink?’
Lest they shathah (drinks), and shakach (forget) the chaqaq (law), and shanah (pervert) the dayan (judge) due to anyone who is ban (son).
Nathan (give) shakar (strong) drink to him who is ready to abad (destroy/perish); and yayan (wine) to the mar (bitter) in napash (living being/soul):
Let him shathah (drinks), and shakach (forget) his rayash (poverty), and zakar (remembrance/memory) his misery no more.
Pathach (open) your pah (mouth) for the mute, in the dayan (judge) of all who are left desolate.
Pathach (open) your pah (mouth), shapat (judge) righteously, and dayan (judge) justice to the inay (poor) and abayawan (needy).
Who can matzaa (find) a chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ashah (wife/individual woman)? For her makar (price) is rachawaq (far) above panayan (rubies).
The lab (heart) of her bail (husband) batach (trusts) in her. He shall have no chasar (lack) of gain.
She gamal (does) him tawab (pleasant/functional), and not rai (harm), all the yawam (day) of her chay (life).
She darash (seeks) tzamar (wool) and pashathah (flax), and ishah (make) eagerly with her kap (hands).
She is like the sachar (merchant) anayah (ships). She bawaa (come) her lacham (bread) from afar.
She qawam (rise up) also while it is yet layal (night), nathan (give) food to her bayath (house), and chaq (statute) for her nairah (servant) girls.
She zamam (considers) a shadah (field), and laqach (take / seized) it. With the paray (fruit) of her kap (hands), she natai (plants) a karam (vineyard).
She arms her waist with iz (strength / might / refuge), and makes her zarawai (arms) iz (strength / might / refuge).
She taim (perceives) that her sachar (merchandise) is profitable. Her nayar (lamp) doesn't kabah (go) out by layal (night).
She shalach (send) her yad (hand) to the palak (distaff), and her kap (hands) thamak (hold) the kayashawar (spindle).
She parash (opens) her arms to the inay (poor); yes, she extends her yad (hand) to the abayawan (needy).
She is not yaraa (fear / be afraid) of the shalag (snow) for her bayath (house); for all her bayath (house) are labash (clothed) with shanay (second).
She ishah (make) for herself carpets of marabad (tapestry). Her labawash (clothing) is shash (six) linen and aragaman (purple).
Her bail (husband) is yadai (respected) in the shair (gates), when he yashab (inhabit/dwell) among the zaqan (elders) of the aratz (Earth/land).
She ishah (make) sadayan (linen) garments and makar (sells) them, and nathan (give) sashes to the kanainay (Kanainay/(Canaanite)).
Iz (strength / might / refuge) and dignity are her labawash (clothing). She shachaq (laughs) at the yawam (day) to acharawan (come).
She pathach (opens) her pah (mouth) with chakamah (wisdom). Chasad (grace) instruction is on her lashawan (tongue/language).
She tzapah (watchman / keep watch) well to the halayakah (ways) of her bayath (house), and doesn't akal (eat) the lacham (bread) of itzalawath (idleness).
Her ban (son) qawam (rise up) up and ashar (who/that) her blessed. Her bail (husband) also halal (praise) her:
Many women ishah (make) noble things, but you ilah (go up / offer) them all.
Charm is shaqar (deceitful), and yapay (beauty) is habal (vain); but a ashah (wife/individual woman) who yaraa (fears) Yahawah, she shall be halal (praise).
Nathan (give) her of the paray (fruit) of her yad (hand)! Let her maishah (works) halal (praise) her in the shair (gates)!
The dabar (word / matter) of the qahalath (preacher), the ban (son) of Dawad (David), malak (king) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem):
"Habal (vanity) of habal (vanities)," amar (spoke) the qahalath (preacher); habal (vanity) of habal (vanities), all is habal (vanity).
What does adam (man) gain from all his imal (labor) in which he imal (labors) under the shamash (sun)?
One dawar (generation / age / period) halak (move), and another dawar (generation / age / period) bawaa (come); but the aratz (Earth/land) imad (remains) iwalam (forever).
The shamash (sun) also zarach (rises), and the shamash (sun) bawaa (come) down, and hurries to its maqawam (place) where it zarach (rises).

The rawach (spirit / wind) halak (move) toward the darawam (south), and sabab (turns) around to the tzapawan (north). It sabab (turns) around halak (move) as it goes, and the rawach (spirit / wind) shawab (turn back / repent) again to its courses.

All the nachal (stream / river) halak (move) into the yam (sea/waters), yet the yam (sea/waters) is not malaa (full). To the maqawam (place) where the nachal (stream / river) flow, there they flow again.
All things are yagai (full) of weariness beyond dabar (word / matter). The iyan (eye) is not shabai (satisfied) with seeing, nor the azan (ear) shabai (filled) with shamai (hearken / hear).
That which ishah (make) been is that which shall be; and that which has been done is that which shall be ishah (make): and there is no chadash (new) thing under the shamash (sun).
Is there a thing of which it may be amar (spoke), "raah (see), this is chadash (new)?" It has been long ago, in the ages which were panayam (before) us.
There is no memory of the raashawan (former); neither shall there be any memory of the acharawan (latter) that are to come, among those that shall acharawan (come) after.
I, the qahalath (preacher), was malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

I nathan (give) my lab (heart) to darash (seek) and to thawar (search) out by chakamah (wisdom) concerning all that is ishah (make) under the sky. It is a rai (heavy) burden that Alahayam nathan (give) given to the ban (son) of adam (men) to be inah (oppress / afflict) with.
I raah (see) seen all the maishah (works) that are ishah (make) under the shamash (sun); and behold, all is habal (vanity) and a chasing after rawach (spirit / wind).
That which is iwath (crooked) can't be made thaqan (straight); and that which is lacking can't be manah (counted).

I dabar (word / matter) to myself, Behold, I have obtained for myself gadal (great) chakamah (wisdom) above all who were panayam (before) me in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem). Yes, my lab (heart) rabah (has) had great raah (see) of chakamah (wisdom) and daith (knowledge).

I nathan (give) my lab (heart) to yadai (know) chakamah (wisdom), and to yadai (know) hawalalah (madness) and sakalawath (folly). I yadai (perceived) that this also was a chasing after rawach (spirit / wind).
For in much chakamah (wisdom) is much kais (grief); and he who yasap (increases) daith (knowledge) yasap (increases) makaab (sorrow).
I amar (spoke) in my lab (heart), "yalak (come) now, I will test you with shamachah (mirth): therefore raah (see) tawab (pleasant/functional);" and behold, this also was habal (vanity).
I amar (spoke) of shachawaq (laughter/joking matter), "It is foolishness;" and of shamachah (mirth), What ishah (make) it accomplish?

I thawar (searched) in my lab (heart) how to cheer my flesh with yayan (wine), my lab (heart) yet nahag (guiding) me with chakamah (wisdom), and how to achaz (lay) hold of sakalawath (folly), until I might raah (see) what it was tawab (pleasant/functional) for the ban (son) of adam (men) that they should ishah (make) under shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) masapar (all) the yawam (day) of their chay (life).
I gadal (made) myself great maishah (works). I banah (built) myself bayath (house). I natai (planted) myself karam (vineyards).
I ishah (make) myself ganah (gardens) and parks, and I natai (planted) itz (trees) in them of all kinds of paray (fruit).
I ishah (make) myself barakah (pools) of mayam (Waters), to shaqah (water) from it the yair (forest) where trees were reared.

I bought male ibad (servant) and female shapachah (servants), and had ban (son) born in my bayath (house). I also rabah (had) great maqanah (possessions) of tzaan (herds) and flocks, above all who were panayam (before) me in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem);

I also kanas (gathered) kasap (silver) and zahab (gold) for myself, and the treasure of malak (king) and of the madayanah (provinces). I ishah (make) myself male and female singers, and the thainawag (delights) of the ban (son) of men—musical shadah (instruments), and that of all sorts.
So I was gadal (great), and yasap (increased) more panayam (than) all who were before me in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem). My chakamah (wisdom) also imad (remained) with me.

Whatever my iyan (eye) shaal (desired), I didn't atzal (keep) from them. I didn't manai (withhold) my lab (heart) from any shamachah (joy), for my lab (heart) shamach (rejoiced) because of all my imal (labor), and this was my chalaq (portion) from all my imal (labor).

Then I panah (looked) at all the maishah (works) that my yad (hand) ishah (make) worked, and at the imal (labor) that I had imal (labored) to ishah (make); and behold, all was habal (vanity) and a chasing after rawach (spirit / wind), and there was no yatharawan (profit) under the shamash (sun).
