I panah (turned) myself to raah (see) chakamah (wisdom), hawalalah (madness), and sakalawath (folly): for what can the malak (king) successor ishah (make)? Just that which has been done long ago.
Then I raah (see) that chakamah (wisdom) excels sakalawath (folly), as far as awar (light) excels chashak (darkness).
The wise chakam (man's) iyan (eye) are in his raash (head), and the kasayal (fool) halak (move) in darkness—and yet I yadai (perceived) that achad (one) maqarah (event) qarah (happens) to them all.

Then I amar (spoke) in my lab (heart), "As it happens to the kasayal (fool), so will it qarah (happen) even to me; and why was I then more chakam (wise)?" Then I dabar (word / matter) in my lab (heart) that this also is habal (vanity).

For of the chakam (wise) im (man), even as of the kasayal (fool), there is no memory for iwalam (forever), since in the yawam (day) to bawaa (come) shakach (all) will have been long forgotten. Indeed, the chakam (wise) mawath (death) must die just like the kasayal (fool)!
So I shanaa (hate) chay (life), because the maishah (work) that is ishah (make) under the shamash (sun) was rai (grievous) to me; for all is habal (vanity) and a chasing after rawach (spirit / wind).
I shanaa (hate) all my imal (labor) in which I imal (labored) under the shamash (sun), because I must yanach (leave) it to the adam (man) who comes achar (other) me.

Who yadai (knows) whether he will be a chakam (wise) man or a sakal (fool)? Yet he will shalat (have) rule over all of my imal (labor) in which I have imal (labored), and in which I have shown myself chakam (wise) under the shamash (sun). This also is habal (vanity).
Therefore I began to cause my lab (heart) to yaash (despair) concerning all the imal (labor) in which I had imal (labored) under the shamash (sun).

For there is a adam (man) whose imal (labor) is with chakamah (wisdom), with daith (knowledge), and with skillfulness; yet he shall nathan (give) it for his chalaq (portion) to a adam (man) who has not labored for it. This also is habal (vanity) and a rab (great) rai (evil).
For what hawaa (which/who/that is) a adam (man) of all his imal (labor), and of the striving of his lab (heart), in which he imal (labors) under the shamash (sun)?
For all his yawam (day) are makaab (sorrows), and his inayan (travail) is kais (grief); yes, even in the layal (night) his lab (heart) takes no shakab (rest). This also is habal (vanity).

There is nothing tawab (pleasant/functional) for a adam (man) than that he should akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and make his napash (living being/soul) raah (see) tawab (pleasant/functional) in his imal (labor). Zah (this/that/these) also I raah (see), that it is from the yad (hand) of Alahayam.
For who can akal (eat), or who can have enjoyment, more than I?

For to the adam (man) who pleases him, Alahayam gives chakamah (wisdom), daith (knowledge), and shamachah (joy); but to the chataa (sinner) he nathan (give) inayan (travail), to asap (gather) and to kanas (heap) up, that he may nathan (give) to him who pleases Alahayam. This also is habal (vanity) and a chasing after rawach (spirit / wind).
For everything there is a zaman (season), and a zaman (time) for every chapatz (purpose) under shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)):
A ith (time) to be yalad (birth / begot), and a ith (time) to mawath (death); a ith (time) to natai (plant), and a ith (time) to iqar (pluck) up that which is natai (planted);
A ith (time) to harag (kill), and a ith (time) to rapaa (heal); a ith (time) to paratz (break) down, and a ith (time) to banah (build) up;
A ith (time) to bakah (weep), and a ith (time) to shachaq (laugh); a ith (time) to sapad (mourn), and a ith (time) to raqad (dance);

A ith (time) to shalak (cast) away aban (stone), and a ith (time) to kanas (gather) aban (stone) together; a ith (time) to chabaq (embrace), and a ith (time) to rachaq (refrain) from chabaq (embracing);
A ith (time) to baqash (seek), and a ith (time) to abad (destroy/perish); a ith (time) to shamar (keep/guard), and a ith (time) to shalak (cast) away;
A ith (time) to qarai (tear), and a ith (time) to thapar (sew); a ith (time) to chashah (keep) silence, and a ith (time) to dabar (word / matter);
A ith (time) to ahab (love), and a ith (time) to shanaa (hate); a ith (time) for malachamah (war), and a ith (time) for shalawam (peace / safety).
What yatharawan (profit) has he who ishah (make) in that in which he imal (labors)?
I raah (see) seen the burden which Alahayam nathan (give) given to the ban (son) of adam (men) to be inah (oppress / afflict) with.

He ishah (make) made everything yapah (beautiful) in its ith (time). He nathan (give) also set eternity in their lab (heart), yet so that adam (man) can't matzaa (find) out the maishah (work) that Alahayam has done from the raash (head) even to the sawap (end).
I yadai (know) that there is nothing tawab (pleasant/functional) for them than to shamach (rejoice), and to ishah (make) tawab (pleasant/functional) as long as they chay (life).
Also that every adam (man) should akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and raah (see) tawab (pleasant/functional) in all his imal (labor), is the mathath (gift) of Alahayam.

I yadai (know) that whatever Alahayam ishah (make), it shall be iwalam (forever). Ayan (nothing) can be yasap (added) to it, nor anything taken from it; and Alahayam ishah (make) done it, that men should yaraa (fear / be afraid) panayam (before) him.
That which is has been long ago, and that which is to be has been long ago: and Alahayam baqash (seeks) again that which is passed away.

Moreover I raah (see) under the shamash (sun), in the maqawam (place) of mashapat (justice), that rashai (wickedness) was there; and in the maqawam (place) of tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), that rashai (wickedness) was there.

I amar (spoke) in my lab (heart), Alahayam will shapat (judge) the tzadayaq (righteous) and the rashai (wicked); for there is a ith (time) there for every chapatz (purpose) and for every maishah (work).
I amar (spoke) in my lab (heart), As for the ban (son) of adam (men), Alahayam tests them, so that they may raah (see) that they themselves are like animals.

For that which happens to the ban (son) of adam (men) happens to animals. Even achad (one) thing happens to them. As the one mawath (death), so the other mawath (death). Yes, they have all achad (one) rawach (spirit / wind); and adam (man) has no advantage over the animals: for all is habal (vanity).
All halak (move) to achad (one) maqawam (place). All are from the ipar (dust), and all shawab (turn back / repent) to ipar (dust) again.

Who yadai (knows) the rawach (spirit / wind) of ban (son), whether it ilah (go up / offer) upward, and the rawach (spirit / wind) of the animal, whether it yarad (goes) matah (downward) to the aratz (Earth/land)?

Therefore I raah (see) that there is nothing tawab (pleasant/functional), than that a adam (man) should shamach (rejoice) in his maishah (works); for that is his chalaq (portion): for who can bawaa (come) him to raah (see) what will be achar (other) him?

Then I shawab (turn back / repent) and raah (see) all the ishawaq (oppressions) that are ishah (make) under the shamash (sun): and behold, the damaih (tears) of those who were ishaq (oppressed), and they had no comforter; and on the yad (hand) of their oppressors there was kach (strength / mighty / power); but they had no comforter.
Therefore I shabach (praised) the mawath (death) who have been long mawath (death) more than the chay (life) who are yet chay (life).
Yes, tawab (pleasant/functional) than them shanayam (two) is him who has not yet been, who raah (see) not seen the rai (evil) maishah (work) that is ishah (make) under the shamash (sun).
Then I raah (see) all the imal (labor) and achievement that is the qanaah (envy) of a ayash (husband/individual man) neighbor. This also is habal (vanity) and a striving after rawach (spirit / wind).
The kasayal (fool) chabaq (folds) his yad (hand) together and ruins himself.
Tawab (pleasant/functional) is a kap (handful), with nachath (quietness), than chapan (two) handfuls with imal (labor) and chasing after rawach (spirit / wind).
Then I shawab (turn back / repent) and raah (see) habal (vanity) under the shamash (sun).

There is achad (one) who is shanay (second), and he has neither ban (son) nor ach (brother/kinsman). There is no qatz (end) to all of his imal (labor), neither are his iyan (eye) shabai (satisfied) with wealth. "For whom then, do I imal (labor), and deprive my napash (living being/soul) of enjoyment?" This also is habal (vanity). Yes, it is a miserable inayan (business).
Shanayam (two) are tawab (pleasant/functional) than achad (one), because they yash (have) a tawab (pleasant/functional) shakar (reward) for their imal (labor).

For if they napal (fall / be cast down), the achad (one) will qawam (rise up) up his chabar (fellow); but ay (woe) to him who is achad (one) when he napal (fall / be cast down), and doesn't have shanay (second) to qawam (rise up) him up.
Again, if shanayam (two) shakab (lie) together, then they have warmth; but how can achad (one) keep yacham (warm) alone?
If a achad (one) thaqap (prevails) against one who is alone, shanayam (two) shall withstand him; and a threefold chawat (cord) is not maharah (quickly) nathaq (broken).
Tawab (pleasant/functional) is a masakan (poor) and chakam (wise) youth than an zaqan (old) and kasayal (foolish) malak (king) who doesn't yadai (know) how to receive admonition any more.
For out of asar (prison) he yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to be malak (king); yes, even in his malakawath (kingdom) he was yalad (birth / begot) rawash (poor).
I raah (see) all the chay (life) who halak (move) under the shamash (sun), that they were with the youth, the other, who succeeded him.

There was no qatz (end) of all the im (people / nation), even of all them over whom he was—yet those who acharawan (come) after shall not shamach (rejoice) in him. Surely this also is habal (vanity) and a chasing after rawach (spirit / wind).

Guard your steps when you yatzaa (go out / come out) to alahayam (Alahayam) house; for to draw near to listen is better than to give the sacrifice of fools, for they don't know that they dabar (word / matter) evil.
Don't be rash with your mouth, and don't let your heart be hasty to utter anything before Alahayam; for Alahayam is in heaven, and you on earth. Therefore let your dabar (word / matter) be few.
For as a dream comes with a multitude of cares, so a kasayal (fool's) speech with a multitude of words.
When you nadar (make vow) a nadar (make vow) to Alahayam, don't defer to shalam (pay) it; for he has no tawab (pleasant/functional) in fools. Shalam (pay) that which you nadar (make vow).
It is better that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not nathan (give).

Don't allow your mouth to lead you into sin. Don't protest before the messenger that this was a mistake. Why should Alahayam be angry at your voice, and destroy the dabar (word / matter) of your hands?
For in the multitude of dreams there are vanities, as well as in many words: but you must fear Alahayam.

If you see the oppression of the poor, and the violent taking away of justice and righteousness in a district, don't marvel at the matter: for one official is eyed by a higher one; and there are officials over them.
Moreover the profit of the earth is for all. The king profits from the field.
He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he who loves rabah (abundance), with rabah (increase): this also is vanity.
When goods rabah (increase), those who akal (eat) them are rabah (increased); and what advantage is there to its owner, am (mother) to feast on them with his eyes?
The sleep of a laboring rai (man) is sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the abundance of the ishar (wealth / riches) will not allow him to sleep.
There is a rai (grievous) rai (evil) which I abad (destroy/perish) seen under the sun: wealth kept by its owner to his rai (harm).
Those riches perish by misfortune, and if he has fathered a son, there is maawamah (nothing) in his yad (hand).
As he bawaa (come) forth from his mother's womb, naked shall he yalak (go) again as he bawaa (come), and shall bawaa (come) kal (every) for his labor, which he may yalak (carry) away in his hand.
This also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go. And what profit does he have who labors for the wind?
All his yawam (day) he also akal (eat) in darkness, he is frustrated, and has sickness and wrath.

Behold, that which I have seen to be good and proper is for one to akal (eat) and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his imal (labor), in which he imal (labors) under the sun, gam (indeed / moreover) the days of his life which Alahayam nathan (give) given him; for this is his chalaq (portion).

Every man also to whom Alahayam rabah (has) given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat of it, and to rabah (take) his portion, and to shamachah (rejoice) in his labor — this is the gift of Alahayam.
For he shall not often reflect on the yawam (day) of his chay (life); because Alahayam occupies him with the shamachah (joy) of his lab (heart).
There is an rai (evil) which I raah (see) seen under the shamash (sun), and it is heavy on adam (men):

A ayash (husband/individual man) to whom Alahayam nathan (give) riches, wealth, and honor, so that he chasar (lacks) nothing for his napash (living being/soul) of all that he awah (desires), yet Alahayam gives him no shalat (power) to akal (eat) of it, but an alien akal (eat) it. This is habal (vanity), and it is an rai (evil) chalay (disease).

If a ayash (husband/individual man) yalad (birth / begot) a maah (hundred) children, and chayah (lives) many shanah (years), so that the yawam (day) of his shanah (years) are many, but his napash (living being/soul) is not shabai (filled) with tawab (pleasant/functional), and moreover he has no qabawarah (burial); I amar (spoke), that a stillborn child is tawab (pleasant/functional) than he:
For it bawaa (come) in habal (vanity), and departs in chashak (darkness), and its sham (name) is kasah (covered) with chashak (darkness).
Moreover it raah (see) not seen the shamash (sun) nor yadai (known) it. Zah (this/that/these) has nachath (rest) rather zah (this/that/these) the other.
Yes, alaw (though) he chayah (live) a alap (thousand) shanah (years) paim (twice) told, and yet fails to raah (see) tawab (pleasant/functional), don't all halak (move) to achad (one) maqawam (place)?
All the imal (labor) of adam (man) is for his pah (mouth), and yet the napash (living being/soul) is not malaa (filled).
For what advantage has the chakam (wise) more than the kasayal (fool)? What has the inay (poor) yadai (man), that knows how to halak (move) before the chay (life)?
Tawab (pleasant/functional) is the maraah (sight) of the iyan (eye) than the halak (move) of the napash (living being/soul). This also is habal (vanity) and a chasing after rawach (spirit / wind).
Whatever has been, its qaraa (called) was given long ago; and it is yadai (known) what adam (man) is; neither yakal (can) he contend with him who is mightier than he.
For there are many dabar (word / matter) that rabah (create) habal (vanity). What does that yawathar (profit) adam (man)?

For who yadai (knows) what is tawab (pleasant/functional) for adam (man) in chay (life), masapar (all) the yawam (day) of his habal (vain) chay (life) which he ishah (make) like a tzal (shadow)? For who can nagad (tell) a adam (man) what will be achar (other) him under the shamash (sun)?
A good sham (name) is tawab (pleasant/functional) than tawab (pleasant/functional) perfume; and the yawam (day) of mawath (death) better than the yawam (day) of one's yalad (birth / begot).

It is tawab (pleasant/functional) to yalak (go) to the bayath (house) of abal (mourning) than to yalak (go) to the bayath (house) of mashathah (feasting): for that is the sawap (end) of all adam (men), and the chay (life) should nathan (give) this to lab (heart).
Kais (sorrow) is tawab (pleasant/functional) than shachawaq (laughter/joking matter); for by the rai (sadness) of the panayam (face) the lab (heart) is made yatab (good).
The lab (heart) of the chakam (wise) is in the bayath (house) of abal (mourning); but the lab (heart) of kasayal (fools) is in the bayath (house) of shamachah (mirth).

It is tawab (pleasant/functional) to shamai (hearken / hear) the gairah (rebuke) of the chakam (wise), than for a ayash (husband/individual man) to shamai (hearken / hear) the shayar (song) of kasayal (fools).
For as the qawal (sound / voice) of sayar (thorns) under a sayar (pot), so is the shachawaq (laughter/joking matter) of the kasayal (fool). This also is habal (vanity).
Surely ishaq (extortion) makes the wise chakam (man) foolish; and a bribe abad (destroy/perish) the lab (heart).

Tawab (pleasant/functional) is the acharayath (end) of a thing than its raashayath (beginning). The arak (patient) in rawach (spirit / wind) is tawab (pleasant/functional) than the gabah (proud) in rawach (spirit / wind).
Don't be hasty in your rawach (spirit / wind) to be kais (angry), for kais (anger) nawach (rests) in the chayaq (bosom) of kasayal (fools).
Don't amar (spoke), "Why were the raashawan (former) yawam (day) tawab (pleasant/functional) than these?" For you do not shaal (ask) chakamah (wisely) about this.
Chakamah (wisdom) is as tawab (pleasant/functional) as an nachalah (inheritance). Yes, it is more excellent for those who raah (see) the shamash (sun).

For chakamah (wisdom) is a defense, even as kasap (money) is a defense; but the yatharawan (excellency) of daith (knowledge) is that chakamah (wisdom) preserves the chayah (life) of him who bail (has) it.
Raah (see) the maishah (work) of Alahayam, for who yakal (can) make that thaqan (straight), which he has made iwath (crooked)?

In the yawam (day) of tawab (pleasant/functional) be tawab (pleasant/functional), and in the yawam (day) of rai (adversity) raah (see); yes, Alahayam ishah (make) made the imah (one) side by side with the other, to the dabarah (end) that adam (man) should not matzaa (find) out anything achar (other) him.

All this raah (see) I seen in my yawam (day) of habal (vanity): there is a tzadayaq (righteous) abad (destroy/perish) who perishes in his tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and there is a rashai (wicked) man who arak (lives) long in his evildoing.
Don't be overly tzadayaq (righteous), neither make yourself overly chakam (wise). Why should you shamam (destroy) yourself?
Don't be too rashai (wicked), neither be sakal (foolish). Why should you mawath (death) before your ith (time)?

It is tawab (pleasant/functional) that you should achaz (take) hold of zah (this/that/these). Yes, also from that don't yanach (withdraw) your yad (hand); for he who yaraa (fears) Alahayam will yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from them all.
Chakamah (wisdom) is a izaz (strength) to the chakam (wise) man more than ishar (ten) shalayat (rulers) who are in a iyar (city).
Surely there is not a tzadayaq (righteous) adam (man) on aratz (Earth/land), who ishah (make) tawab (pleasant/functional) and doesn't chataa (sin).
Also don't nathan (give) lab (heart) to all dabar (word / matter) that are dabar (word / matter), lest you shamai (hearken / hear) your ibad (servant) qalal (curse) you;
For often your own lab (heart) yadai (knows) that you yourself have likewise qalal (cursed) others.
All zah (this/that/these) have I nasah (proved) in chakamah (wisdom). I amar (spoke), "I will be chakam (wise);" but it was rachawaq (far) from me.
That which is, is rachawaq (far) off and exceedingly imaq (deep). Who can matzaa (find) it out?

I sabab (turned) around, and my lab (heart) sought to yadai (know) and to thawar (search) out, and to seek chakamah (wisdom) and the scheme of things, and to yadai (know) that rashai (wickedness) is stupidity, and that sakalawath (foolishness) is hawalalah (madness).

I matzaa (find) more mar (bitter) than mawath (death) the ashah (wife/individual woman) whose lab (heart) is matzawad (snares) and traps, whose yad (hand) are chains. Whoever pleases Alahayam shall malat (escape) from her; but the chataa (sinner) will be ensnared by her.
"Raah (see), I matzaa (have) found this," amar (spoke) the qahalath (preacher), achad (one) to another, to matzaa (find) out the scheme;

Which my napash (living being/soul) still baqash (seeks); but I matzaa (have) not found. Achad (one) adam (man) among a alap (thousand) matzaa (have) I found; but I matzaa (have) not found a ashah (wife/individual woman) among all those.
Raah (see), this only matzaa (have) I found: that Alahayam ishah (make) adam (man) yashar (upright); but they search for many schemes.

Who is like the chakam (wise) yadai (man)? And who knows the pashar (interpretation) of a thing? A adam (man's) chakamah (wisdom) makes his panayam (face) awar (light), and the hardness of his panayam (face) is shanaa (hate).
I say, "shamar (keep/guard) the malak (king) command!" Because of the shabawaih (oath) to Alahayam.
Don't be hasty to yalak (go) out of his panayam (presence). Don't persist in an rai (evil) thing, for he ishah (make) whatever pleases him,
For the malak (king) dabar (word / matter) is supreme. Who can amar (spoke) to him, What are you ishah (make)?
Whoever shamar (keep/guard) the matzawah (commandment) shall not yadai (come) to rai (harm), and his wise lab (heart) yadai (will) know the ith (time) and procedure.
For there is a ith (time) and procedure for every chapatz (purpose), although the rai (misery) of adam (man) is heavy on him.
For he doesn't yadai (know) that which will be; for who can nagad (tell) him how it will be?

There is no adam (man) who has shalayat (power) over the rawach (spirit / wind) to contain the rawach (spirit / wind); neither does he have shalatawan (power) over the yawam (day) of mawath (death). There is no mashalachath (discharge) in malachamah (war); neither shall rashai (wickedness) malat (deliver) bail (those) who practice it.

All this raah (see) I seen, and nathan (give) my lab (heart) to every maishah (work) that is ishah (make) under the shamash (sun). There is a ith (time) in which one adam (man) has shalat (power) over another to his rai (hurt).

So I raah (see) the rashai (wicked) qabar (bury). Bawaa (come) they came also from maqawam (place). They bawaa (come) and were shakach (forgotten) in the iyar (city) where they ishah (make) this. This also is habal (vanity).

Because pathagam (sentence) against an rai (evil) maishah (work) is not ishah (make) maharah (speedily), therefore the lab (heart) of the ban (son) of adam (men) is fully malaa (set) in them to ishah (make) rai (evil).

Though a chataa (sinner) ishah (make) crimes a maah (hundred) times, and arak (lives) long, yet surely I yadai (know) that it will be tawab (pleasant/functional) with those who yaraa (fear / be afraid) Alahayam, who are reverent panayam (before) him.
But it shall not be tawab (pleasant/functional) with the rashai (wicked), neither shall he arak (lengthen) yawam (day) like a tzal (shadow); panayam (because) he doesn't yaraa (fear) Alahayam.

There is a habal (vanity) which is ishah (make) on the aratz (Earth/land), that there are tzadayaq (righteous) men to whom it nagai (happens) according to the maishah (work) of the rashai (wicked). Again, there are rashai (wicked) men to whom it nagai (happens) according to the maishah (work) of the tzadayaq (righteous). I amar (spoke) that this also is habal (vanity).

Then I shabach (commended) shamachah (mirth), because a adam (man) has no tawab (pleasant/functional) thing under the shamash (sun), than to akal (eat), and to shathah (drinks), and to be shamach (joyful): for that will accompany him in his imal (labor) all the yawam (day) of his chay (life) which Alahayam nathan (give) given him under the shamash (sun).

When I nathan (give) my lab (heart) to yadai (know) chakamah (wisdom), and to raah (see) the inayan (business) that is ishah (make) on the aratz (Earth/land) (for also there is that neither yawam (day) nor layal (night) raah (see) shanah (sleep) with his iyan (eye)),

Then I raah (see) all the maishah (work) of Alahayam, that adam (man) can't matzaa (find) out the maishah (work) that is ishah (make) under the shamash (sun), ashar (who/that) however much a adam (man) imal (labors) to baqash (seek) it out, yet he won't matzaa (find) it. Yes even though a chakam (wise) man amar (spoke) he yadai (can) comprehend it, he won't be yakal (able) to matzaa (find) it.

For all this I nathan (give) to my lab (heart), even to explore all this: that the tzadayaq (righteous), and the chakam (wise), and their ibad (servant), are in the yad (hand) of Alahayam; whether it is ahabah (love) or hatred, adam (man) doesn't yadai (know) it; all is panayam (before) them.

All things come achad (one) to all. There is one maqarah (event) to the tzadayaq (righteous) and to the rashai (wicked); to the tawab (pleasant/functional), to the tahawar (clean), to the tamaa (unclean), to him who zabach (sacrifices), and to him who doesn't zabach (sacrifice). As is the tawab (pleasant/functional), so is the chataa (sinner); he who shabai (swear / take oath) an oath, as he who yaraa (fear / be afraid) an shabawaih (oath).

This is an rai (evil) in all that is ishah (make) under the shamash (sun), that there is achad (one) maqarah (event) to all: yes also, the lab (heart) of the ban (son) of adam (men) is malaa (full) of rai (evil), and hawalalah (madness) is in their labab (heart) while they chay (life), and achar (other) that they go to the mawath (death).
For to him who is bachar (joined) with all the chay (life) there is batachawan (hope); for a chay (life) kalab (dog) is tawab (pleasant/functional) than a mawath (death) aray (lion).

For the chay (life) yadai (know) that they will mawath (death), but the mawath (death) don't yadai (know) anything, neither do they have any more a shakar (reward); for their zakar (remembrance/memory) is shakach (forgotten).

Also their ahabah (love), their hatred, and their qanaah (envy) abad (destroy/perish) perished long ago; neither have they any more a chalaq (portion) iwalam (forever) in anything that is ishah (make) under the shamash (sun).

Go your yalak (way) — akal (eat) your lacham (bread) with shamachah (joy), and shathah (drinks) your yayan (wine) with a tawab (pleasant/functional) lab (heart); for Alahayam has kabar (already) ratzah (accepted) your maishah (works).
Let your bagad (garments) be ith (always) laban (white), and don't let your raash (head) chasar (lack) shaman (oil).

Chay (life) raah (see) with the ashah (wife/individual woman) whom you ahab (love) all the yawam (day) of your chay (life) of habal (vanity), which he nathan (give) given you under the shamash (sun), all your yawam (day) of habal (vanity): for that is your chalaq (portion) in chay (life), and in your imal (labor) in which you imal (labor) under the shamash (sun).

Whatever your yad (hand) matzaa (finds) to ishah (make), ishah (make) it with your kach (strength / mighty / power); for there is no maishah (work), nor chashabawan (device), nor daith (knowledge), nor chakamah (wisdom), in shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife), where you are halak (move).

I shawab (turn back / repent), and raah (see) under the shamash (sun), that the marawatz (race) is not to the qal (swift), nor the malachamah (battle) to the gabawar (strong), neither yet lacham (bread) to the chakam (wise), nor yet riches to men of bayan (between), nor yet favor to yadai (men) of skill; but ith (time) and pagai (chance) qarah (happen) to them all.

For adam (man) also doesn't yadai (know) his ith (time). As the dag (fish) that are achaz (taken) in an rai (evil) matzawad (net), and as the tzapawar (birds) that are achaz (caught) in the pach (snare), even so are the ban (son) of adam (men) yaqash (snared) in an rai (evil) ith (time), when it napal (fall / be cast down) pathaawam (suddenly) on them.
I raah (see) also seen chakamah (wisdom) under the shamash (sun) in zah (this/that/these) way, and it seemed gadawal (very great/important/mighty) to me.

There was a qatan (small/young/least) iyar (city), and mait (few) ayash (husband/individual man) within it; and a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) malak (king) bawaa (come) against it, sabab (besieged) it, and banah (built) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) matzawad (bulwarks) against it.

Now a masakan (poor) chakam (wise) ayash (husband/individual man) was matzaa (found) in it, and he by his chakam (wisdom) malat (delivered) the iyar (city); yet no adam (man) zakar (remembrance/memory) that same masakan (poor) adam (man).

Then I amar (spoke), "chakamah (wisdom) is tawab (pleasant/functional) than gabawarah (strength)." Nevertheless the masakan (poor) man's chakamah (wisdom) is bazah (despised), and his dabar (word / matter) are not shamai (hearken / hear).
The dabar (word / matter) of the chakam (wise) shamai (hearken / hear) in nachath (quiet) are better than the zaiq (cry) of him who mashal (rule/have dominion) among kasayal (fools).
Chakamah (wisdom) is tawab (pleasant/functional) than kalay (weapons) of qarab (war); but achad (one) chataa (sinner) abad (destroy/perish) much tawab (pleasant/functional).
Mawath (death) zabawab (flies) cause the shaman (oil) of the perfumer to nabai (send) forth an baash (evil) odor; so does a mait (little) sakalawath (folly) outweigh chakamah (wisdom) and honor.
A wise chakam (man's) lab (heart) is at his right yamayan (right hand), but a kasayal (fool's) lab (heart) at his shamaawal (left hand).
Yes also, when the sakal (fool) halak (move) by the darak (way), his lab (heart) chasar (fails) him, and he amar (spoke) to everyone that he is a sakal (fool).

If the rawach (spirit / wind) of the mashal (rule/have dominion) ilah (go up / offer) up against you, don't yanach (leave) your maqawam (place); for gentleness yanach (lays) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) offenses to chataa (rest).
There is an rai (evil) which I raah (see) seen under the shamash (sun), the sort of shagagah (error) which yatzaa (go out / come out) from the shalayat (ruler).
Sakal (folly) is nathan (give) in rab (great) marawam (dignity), and the ishayar (rich) yashab (inhabit/dwell) in a shapal (low) place.
I raah (see) seen ibad (servant) on sawas (horses), and shar (prince / ruler) halak (move) like ibad (servant) on the aratz (Earth/land).
He who chapar (digs) a gawamatz (pit) may napal (fall / be cast down) into it; and whoever paratz (breaks) through a gadar (wall) may be bitten by a snake.
Whoever carves out aban (stone) may be injured by them. Whoever splits itz (wood) may be sakan (endangered) thereby.
If the axe is qahah (blunt), and qalal (one) doesn't sharpen the panayam (edge), then he must use more chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor); but skill brings success.
If the snake nashak (bites) before it is lachash (charmed), then is there no yatharawan (profit) for the charmer's lashawan (tongue/language).
The dabar (word / matter) of a wise chakam (man's) pah (mouth) are chan (gracious); but a kasayal (fool) is balai (swallowed) by his own shapah (lips).
The thachalah (beginning) of the dabar (word / matter) of his pah (mouth) is sakalawath (foolishness); and the acharayath (end) of his pah (talk) is rai (mischievous) hawalalawath (madness).
A sakal (fool) also rabah (multiplies) dabar (word / matter). Adam (man) doesn't yadai (know) what will be; and that which will be achar (other) him, who can nagad (tell) him?
The imal (labor) of kasayal (fools) yagai (wearies) every one of them; for he doesn't yadai (know) how to yalak (go) to the iyar (city).
Ay (woe) to you, aratz (Earth/land), when your malak (king) is a nair (child), and your shar (prince / ruler) akal (eat) in the baqar (morning)!

Ashar (who/that) are you, aratz (Earth/land), when your malak (king) is the ban (son) of char (nobles), and your shar (prince / ruler) akal (eat) in due ith (season), for gabawarah (strength), and not for shathay (drunkenness)!
By itzalah (slothfulness) the roof sinks in; and through shapalawath (idleness) of the yad (hand) the bayath (house) leaks.
A feast is ishah (make) for shachawaq (laughter/joking matter), and yayan (wine) shamach (makes) the life glad; and kasap (money) is the inah (answer / respond) for all things.

Don't qalal (curse) the malak (king), no, not in your madai (thoughts); and don't qalal (curse) the ishayar (rich) in your bedroom: for a iwap (flying) of the sky may yalak (carry) your qawal (sound / voice), and that which bail (has) kanap (wings) may nagad (tell) the dabar (word / matter).
Shalach (send) your lacham (bread) on the mayam (Waters); for you shall matzaa (find) it after many yawam (day).
Nathan (give) a chalaq (portion) to shabai (seven), yes, even to shamanah (eight); for you don't yadai (know) what rai (evil) will be on the aratz (Earth/land).

If the ib (clouds) are malaa (full) of gasham (rain), they rawaq (empty) themselves on the aratz (Earth/land); and if a itz (tree) napal (fall / be cast down) toward the darawam (south), or toward the tzapawan (north), in the maqawam (place) where the itz (tree) napal (fall / be cast down), there shall it be.
He who shamar (keep/guard) the rawach (spirit / wind) won't zarai (sow); and he who raah (see) the ib (clouds) won't qatzar (reap).

As you don't yadai (know) what is the darak (way) of the rawach (spirit / wind), nor how the itzam (bones) grow in the batan (womb) of her who is with malaa (child); even so you don't yadai (know) the maishah (work) of Alahayam who ishah (make) all.

In the baqar (morning) zarai (sow) your zarai (seed), and in the irab (evening) don't yanach (withhold) your yad (hand); for you don't yadai (know) which will kashar (prosper), whether this or that, or whether they shanayam (two) will be equally tawab (pleasant/functional).
Truly the awar (light) is mathawaq (sweet), and a tawab (pleasant/functional) thing it is for the iyan (eye) to raah (see) the shamash (sun).

Yes, if a adam (man) chayah (lives) many shanah (years), let him shamach (rejoice) in them all; but let him zakar (remembrance/memory) the yawam (day) of chashak (darkness), for they shall be many. All that bawaa (come) is habal (vanity).

Shamach (rejoice), bachawar (young) man, in your yaladawath (youth), and let your lab (heart) shamach (cheer) you in the yawam (day) of your bacharawath (youth), and halak (move) in the darak (ways) of your lab (heart), and in the maraah (sight) of your maraah (eyes); but yadai (know) that for all these things Alahayam will bawaa (come) you into mashapat (judgment).
Therefore sawar (remove) kais (sorrow) from your lab (heart), and ibar (pass over/through) away rai (evil) from your bashar (flesh); for shacharawath (youth) and the dawn of life are habal (vanity).

Zakar (remembrance/memory) also your Creator in the yawam (day) of your bacharawath (youth), before the rai (evil) yawam (day) bawaa (come), and the shanah (years) nagai (draw) near, when you will amar (spoke), I have no chapatz (pleasure) in them;
Before the shamash (sun), the awar (light), the yarach (moon), and the kawakab (star) are chashak (darkness), and the ib (clouds) shawab (turn back / repent) achar (other) the gasham (rain);

In the yawam (day) when the keepers of the bayath (house) shall zawai (tremble), and the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ayash (husband/individual man) shall iwath (bow) themselves, and the tachan (grinders) batal (cease) because they are mait (few), and those who raah (see) out of the arabah (windows) are chashak (darkness),

And the dalath (doors) shall be sagar (shut) in the shawaq (street); when the qawal (sound / voice) of the tachanah (grinding) is shapal (low), and one shall qawam (rise up) up at the qawal (sound / voice) of a tzapawar (bird), and all the bath (daughter) of music shall be shachach (brought) low;

Yes, they shall be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of gabah (heights), and terrors will be in the darak (way); and the shaqad (almond) tree shall blossom, and the grasshopper shall be a sabal (burden), and abayawanah (desire) shall parar (fail); because adam (man) halak (move) to his iwalam (forever) bayath (house), and the sapad (mourners) sabab (go) about the shawaq (streets):

Laa (NOT) the kasap (silver) chabal (cord) is severed, or the zahab (gold) galah (spring / basin / bowl) is ratzatz (broken), or the kad (pitcher) is shabar (broken) at the mabawai (spring), or the galagal (wheel) ratzatz (broken) at the bawar (cistern),
And the ipar (dust) shawab (turn back / repent) to the aratz (Earth/land) as it was, and the rawach (spirit / wind) shawab (turn back / repent) to Alahayam who nathan (give) it.
"Habal (vanity) of habal (vanities)," amar (spoke) the qahalath (preacher). All is habal (vanity)!

Further, because the qahalath (preacher) was chakam (wise), he still lamad (teach/instruct) the im (people / nation) daith (knowledge). Yes, he pondered, chaqar (sought) out, and thaqan (set) in order many mashal (proverbs).
The qahalath (preacher) baqash (sought) to matzaa (find) out chapatz (acceptable) dabar (word / matter), and that which was kathab (written) blamelessly, dabar (word / matter) of amath (truth).

The dabar (word / matter) of the chakam (wise) are like darabawan (goads); and like mashamarah (nails) well natai (fastened) are words from the bail (masters) of asapah (assemblies), which are nathan (give) from achad (one) raih (shepherd).
Furthermore, my ban (son), be zahar (warn): of ishah (make) many sapar (book / scribed document) there is no qatz (end); and much lahag (study) is a yagaih (weariness) of the bashar (flesh).

This is the sawap (end) of the dabar (word / matter). All has been shamai (hearken / hear). Yaraa (fear / be afraid) Alahayam, and shamar (keep/guard) his matzawah (commandments); for this is the whole duty of adam (man).
For Alahayam will bawaa (come) every maishah (work) into mashapat (judgment), with every ilam (hidden) thing, whether it is tawab (pleasant/functional), or whether it is rai (evil).
The shayar (song) of shayar (song), which is Shalamah (Solomon's). Beloved
Let him nashaq (kiss) me with the kisses of his pah (mouth); for your dawad (love) is tawab (pleasant/functional) than yayan (wine).
Your shaman (oils) have a pleasing fragrance. Your sham (name) is shaman (oil) rawaq (poured) forth, therefore the ilamah (virgins) ahab (love) you.

Take me achar (other) with you. Let us hurry. The malak (king) bawaa (come) brought me into his rooms. Friends We will be gayal (glad) and shamach (rejoice) in you. We will zakar (remembrance/memory) your dawad (love) more than yayan (wine)! Beloved They are mayashar (right) to ahab (love) you.
I am dark, but lovely, you bath (daughter) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), like Qadar (Kedar's) ahal (tents), like Shalamah (Solomon's) yarayaih (curtains).

Don't raah (see) at me because I am dark, because the shamash (sun) has scorched me. My am (mother) ban (son) were charar (angry) with me. They shawam (place / establish / appoint) me natar (keeper) of the karam (vineyards). I haven't natar (kept) my own karam (vineyard).

Nagad (tell) me, you whom my napash (living being/soul) ahab (love), where you graze your flock, where you rabatz (rest) them at tzahar (noon); For why should I be as one who is veiled beside the idar (flocks) of your chabar (companions)? Lover
If you don't yadai (know), most yapah (beautiful) among ashah (wife/individual woman), follow the tracks of the tzaan (sheep). Graze your young goats beside the raih (shepherds)' mashakan (tents).
I have damah (compared) you, my raiyah (love), to a steed in Paraih (Pharaoh's) rakab (chariots).
Your lachay (cheeks) are naah (beautiful) with earrings, your tzawaar (neck) with strings of jewels.
We will ishah (make) you earrings of zahab (gold), with naqadah (studs) of kasap (silver). Beloved
While the malak (king) sat at his masab (table), my perfume spread its fragrance.
My dawad (beloved) is to me a sachet of mar (myrrh), that lawan (lies) between my shad (breasts).
My dawad (beloved) is to me a ashakawal (cluster) of henna blossoms from the karam (vineyards) of Iyanagaday (En) Gedi. Lover
Behold, you are yapah (beautiful), my raiyah (love). Behold, you are yapah (beautiful). Your iyan (eye) are yawanah (doves). Beloved
Behold, you are yapah (beautiful), my dawad (beloved), yes, naiyam (pleasant); and our irash (couch) is verdant. Lover
The qawarah (beams) of our bayath (house) are araz (cedars). Our rachayat (rafters) are barawath (firs).
I am a chabatzalath (rose) of Sharawan (Sharon), a shawashan (lily) of the imaq (valleys). Lover
As a shawashan (lily) among chawach (thorns), so is my raiyah (love) among the bath (daughter). Beloved

As the thapawach (apple) tree among the itz (trees) of the yair (wood), so is my dawad (beloved) among the ban (son). I yashab (inhabit/dwell) down under his tzal (shadow) with great chamad (delight), his paray (fruit) was mathawaq (sweet) to my chak (taste).
He bawaa (come) me to the banquet hall. His dagal (banner) over me is ahabah (love).
Strengthen me with raisins, refresh me with thapawach (apples); For I am faint with ahabah (love).
His left shamaawal (left hand) is under my raash (head). His right yamayan (right hand) chabaq (embraces) me.

I shabai (swear / take oath) you, bath (daughter) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), by the tzabay (roes), or by the ayalah (hinds) of the shadah (field), that you not iwar (rouse / awaken) up, nor awaken ahabah (love), until it so chapatz (desires).
The qawal (sound / voice) of my dawad (beloved)! Behold, he bawaa (come), dalag (leaping) on the har (mountain), qapatz (skipping) on the gabaih (hills).

My dawad (beloved) is damah (like) a tzabay (roe) or a ipar (young) ayal (hart). Behold, he imad (stands) achar (other) our kathal (wall)! He shagach (looks) in at the chalawan (windows). He glances through the charak (lattice).
My dawad (beloved) inah (answer / respond), and amar (spoke) to me, “qawam (rise up) up, my raiyah (love), my yapah (beautiful) one, and yalak (come) away.
For, behold, the sathaw (winter) is past. The gasham (rain) is over and halak (move).

The natzan (flowers) raah (see) on the aratz (Earth/land). The ith (time) of the qawal (sound / voice) has nagai (come), and the qawal (sound / voice) of the turtledove is shamai (hearken / hear) in our aratz (Earth/land).

The thaan (fig) tree ripens her pag (green) figs. The gapan (vines) are in blossom. They nathan (give) forth their fragrance. Qawam (rise up), my raiyah (love), my yapah (beautiful) one, and yalak (come) away.” Lover

My yawanah (dove) in the chagaw (clefts) of the salai (rock), In the sathar (secret / hidden) madaragah (places) of the mountainside, raah (see) me see your maraah (face). Shamai (hearken / hear) me hear your qawal (sound / voice); for your qawal (sound / voice) is irab (evening), and your maraah (face) is lovely.
Achaz (catch) for us the foxes, the qatan (small/young/least) foxes that chabal (spoil) the karam (vineyards); for our karam (vineyards) are in blossom. Beloved
My dawad (beloved) is mine, and I am his. He browses among the shawashan (lilies).

Until the yawam (day) is cool, and the tzalal (shadows) nawas (flee) away, sabab (turn), my dawad (beloved), and be damah (like) a tzabay (roe) or a ipar (young) ayal (hart) on the har (mountain) of bathar (bether).
By layal (night) on my mashakab (bed), I baqash (sought) him whom my napash (living being/soul) ahab (love). I baqash (sought) him, but I didn't matzaa (find) him.

I will qawam (rise up) up now, and sabab (go) about the iyar (city); in the shawaq (streets) and in the squares I will baqash (seek) him whom my napash (living being/soul) ahab (love). I baqash (sought) him, but I didn't matzaa (find) him.
The watchmen who sabab (go) about the iyar (city) matzaa (found) me; raah (see) you seen him whom my napash (living being/soul) ahab (love)?

I had scarcely ibar (pass over/through) from them, when I matzaa (found) him whom my napash (living being/soul) ahab (love). I achaz (held) him, and would not rapah (let) him go, until I bawaa (come) brought him into my am (mother) bayath (house), into the room of her who harah (conceived) me.

I shabai (swear / take oath) you, bath (daughter) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), by the tzabay (roes), or by the ayalah (hinds) of the shadah (field), that you not iwar (rouse / awaken) up, nor awaken ahabah (love), until it so chapatz (desires).

Who is this who ilah (go up / offer) up from the madabar (wilderness) like thayamarah (pillars) of ishan (smoke), perfumed with mar (myrrh) and labawanah (frankincense), with all spices of the rakal (merchant)?
Behold, it is Shalamah (Solomon's) carriage! Shashayam (sixty) gabawar (mighty) men are around it, of the gabawar (mighty) men of Yasharaal (Israel).

They all achaz (handle) the charab (sword), and are lamad (teach/instruct) in malachamah (war). Every ayash (husband/individual man) has his charab (sword) on his yarak (thigh), because of pachad (fear / dread) in the layal (night).
Malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon) ishah (make) himself a carriage of the itz (wood) of Labanawan (Lebanon).

He ishah (make) its imawad (pillar) of kasap (silver), its rapayadah (bottom) of zahab (gold), its seat of aragaman (purple), its thawak (midst) being ratzap (paved) with ahabah (love), from the bath (daughter) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

Yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, you bath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion), and raah (see) malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon), with the itarah (crown) with which his am (mother) has itar (crowned) him, in the yawam (day) of his weddings, in the yawam (day) of the shamachah (gladness) of his lab (heart). Lover

Behold, you are yapah (beautiful), my raiyah (love). Behold, you are yapah (beautiful). Your iyan (eye) are yawanah (doves) behind your tzamah (veil). Your shair (hair) is as a idar (flock) of iz (goats), that descend from har (mountain) Galaid (Gilead).

Your shan (teeth) are like a newly qatzab (shorn) idar (flock), which have ilah (go up / offer) up from the rachatzah (washing), where every one of them has thaam (twins). None is shakawal (bereaved) among them.
Your shapah (lips) are like shanay (second) chawat (thread). Your madabar (mouth) is lovely. Your raqah (temples) are like a palach (piece) of a ramawan (pomegranate) behind your tzamah (veil).
Your tzawaar (neck) is like Dawad (David's) magadal (tower) banah (built) for an armory, whereon a alap (thousand) magan (shield) thalah (hang), all the shalat (shields) of the gabawar (mighty) men.
Your shanayam (two) shad (breasts) are like shanayam (two) fawns that are thaawam (twins) of a roe, which raih (feed) among the shawashan (lilies).
Until the yawam (day) is cool, and the tzalal (shadows) nawas (flee) away, I will yalak (go) to the har (mountain) of mar (myrrh), to the gabaih (hill) of labawanah (frankincense).
You are all yapah (beautiful), my raiyah (love). There is no maawam (spot) in you.

Bawaa (come) with me from Labanawan (Lebanon), my kalah (complete / finish), with me from Labanawan (Lebanon). Shawar (look) from the raash (head) of Amanah (Amana), from the raash (head) of Shanayar (Senir) and Charamawan (Hermon), from the aray (lions)' maiwanah (dens), from the harar (mountains) of the namar (leopards).

You have ravished my labab (heart), my achawath (sister), my kalah (complete / finish). You have ravished my labab (heart) with achad (one) of your iyan (eye), with achad (one) inaq (chain) of your tzawaar (neck).

How yapah (beautiful) is your dawad (love), my achawath (sister), my kalah (complete / finish)! How much tawab (pleasant/functional) is your dawad (love) than yayan (wine)! The fragrance of your perfumes than all kinds of basham (spices)!

Your shapah (lips), my kalah (complete / finish), drip like the napath (honeycomb). Dabash (honey) and chalab (milk) are under your lashawan (tongue/language). The rayach (smell) of your shalamah (Shalamah/(Solomon) - Patriarch) is like the rayach (smell) of Labanawan (Lebanon).
A nail (locked) up gan (garden) is my achawath (sister), my kalah (complete / finish); a nail (locked) up gal (spring), a chatham (sealed) maiyan (fountain).
Your shoots are an paradas (orchard) of ramawan (pomegranates), with magad (precious) paray (fruits): henna with narad (spikenard) plants,

Narad (spikenard) and karakam (saffron), qanah (calamus) and qanamawan (cinnamon), with every kind of labawanah (incense) itz (tree); mar (myrrh) and ahalayam (aloes), with all the best basham (spices),
A maiyan (fountain) of gan (gardens), a baar (well) of chay (life) mayam (Waters), nazal (flowing) streams from Labanawan (Lebanon). Beloved

Iwar (rouse / awaken), north tzapawan (wind); and bawaa (come), you thayaman (south)! Pawach (blow) on my gan (garden), that its basham (spices) may nazal (flow) out. Let my dawad (beloved) bawaa (come) into his gan (garden), and taste his magad (precious) paray (fruits).

I bawaa (come) come into my gan (garden), my achawath (sister), my kalah (complete / finish). I have arah (gathered) my mar (myrrh) with my basham (spice); I have akal (eat) my yair (honeycomb) with my honey; I have shathah (drinks) my yayan (wine) with my chalab (milk). Friends akal (eat), rai (neigbor/another person)! Shathah (drinks), yes, shakar (drink) abundantly, dawad (beloved). Beloved

I was yashan (asleep), but my lab (heart) was iwar (rouse / awaken). It is the qawal (sound / voice) of my dawad (beloved) who dapaq (knocks): pathach (open) to me, my achawath (sister), my raiyah (love), my yawanah (dove), my tham (undefiled); for my raash (head) is malaa (filled) with tal (dew), and my hair with the dampness of the layal (night).
I have taken off my kathanath (robe). Indeed, must I labash (put) it on? I have rachatz (washed) my ragal (feet / foot). Indeed, must I soil them?
My dawad (beloved) thrust his yad (hand) in man (from) the latch opening. My maih (heart) pounded for him.
I qawam (rise up) up to pathach (open) for my dawad (beloved). My yad (hand) dripped with mar (myrrh), my atzabai (fingers) with liquid mar (myrrh), on the handles of the manaiwal (lock).

I pathach (opened) to my dawad (beloved); but my dawad (beloved) left; and ibar (pass over/through) gone away. My napash (living being/soul) yatzaa (go out / come out) out when he dabar (word / matter). I looked for him, but I didn't matzaa (find) him. I qaraa (called) him, but he didn't inah (answer / respond).
The watchmen who sabab (go) about the iyar (city) matzaa (found) me. They nakah (beat) me. They bruised me. The keepers of the chawamah (walls) took my cloak nashaa (lift) from me.
I shabai (swear / take oath) you, bath (daughter) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), If you matzaa (find) my dawad (beloved), that you nagad (tell) him that I am faint with ahabah (love). Friends

How is your dawad (beloved) better than another dawad (beloved), you fairest among ashah (wife/individual woman)? How is your dawad (beloved) better than another dawad (beloved), that you do so shabai (swear / take oath) us? Beloved
My dawad (beloved) is tzach (white) and adam (ruddy). The best among rababah (ten) thousand.
His raash (head) is like the purest paz (gold). His hair is thalathal (bushy), shachar (black) as a irab (evening).
His iyan (eye) are like yawanah (doves) beside the mayam (Waters) apayaq (brooks), rachatz (washed) with chalab (milk), mounted like jewels.
His lachay (cheeks) are like a irawagah (bed) of basham (spices) with towers of perfumes. His shapah (lips) are like shawashan (lilies), natap (dropping) liquid mar (myrrh).
His yad (hand) are like galayal (rings) of zahab (gold) malaa (set) with tharashayash (beryl). His body is like shan (ivory) ishath (work) ilap (overlaid) with sapayar (sapphires).

His shawaq (legs) are like imawad (pillar) of shash (six) yasad (set) on adan (sockets) of paz (fine) gold. His maraah (appearance) is like Labanawan (Lebanon), bachar (excellent) as the araz (cedars).
His chak (mouth) is sweetness; yes, he is altogether machamad (lovely). This is my dawad (beloved), and this is my rai (neigbor/another person), bath (daughter) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).
Where has your dawad (beloved) halak (move), you fairest among ashah (wife/individual woman)? Where has your dawad (beloved) panah (turned), that we may baqash (seek) him with you? Beloved
My dawad (beloved) has yarad (gone) down to his gan (garden), to the irawagah (beds) of basham (spices), to raih (feed) in the gan (gardens), and to laqat (gather) shawashan (lilies).
I am my dawad (beloved's), and my dawad (beloved) is mine. He browses among the shawashan (lilies),
You are yapah (beautiful), my raiyah (love), as Tharatzah (Tirzah), lovely as Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), awesome as an army with dagal (banners).
Sabab (turn) away your iyan (eye) from me, for they have rahab (overcome) me. Your shair (hair) is like a idar (flock) of iz (goats), that lie along the side of Galaid (Gilead).

Your shan (teeth) are like a idar (flock) of rachal (ewes), which have ilah (go up / offer) up from the rachatzah (washing); of which every one has thaam (twins); none is shakawal (bereaved) among them.
Your raqah (temples) are like a palach (piece) of a ramawan (pomegranate) behind your tzamah (veil).
There are shashayam (sixty) malakah (queens), shamanayam (eighty) payalagash (concubines), and ilamah (virgins) without masapar (number).

My yawanah (dove), my tham (perfect) achad (one), is unique. She is her am (mother) only achad (one). She is the favorite one of her who yalad (birth / begot) her. The bath (daughter) raah (see) her, and ashar (who/that) her blessed; the malakah (queens) and the payalagash (concubines), and they halal (praise) her.
Who is she who shaqap (looks) forth as the shachar (morning), yapah (beautiful) as the labanah (moon), bar (clear) as the chamah (sun), and awesome as an army with dagal (banners)?

I yarad (went) down into the agawaz (nut) tree grove, to raah (see) the green plants of the nachal (stream / river), to raah (see) whether the gapan (vine) nawatz (budded), and the ramawan (pomegranates) were in flower.
Without realizing it, my napash (living being/soul) shawam (place / establish / appoint) me with my royal napash (living being/soul) marakabah (chariots). Friends

Shawab (turn back / repent), shawab (turn back / repent), Shulammite! Shawab (turn back / repent), shawab (turn back / repent), that we may gaze at you. Lover Why do you desire to gaze at the Shulammite, as at the machalah (dance) of Mahanaim?
How beautiful are your feet in sandals, prince's daughter! Your rounded thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a skillful workman.
Your body is like a round goblet, no mixed wine is wanting. Your waist is like a heap of wheat, set about with lilies.
Your two breasts are like two fawns, that are twins of a roe.
Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are like the pools in Heshbon by the gate of Bathrabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.
Your head on you is like Carmel. The hair of your head like purple. The king is held captive in its tresses.
How beautiful and how pleasant you are, love, for delights!
This, your stature, is like a palm tree, your breasts like its fruit.
I said, "I will climb up into the thamar (palm) tree. I will take hold of its fruit." Let your shad (breasts) be like ashakawal (clusters) of the vine, the smell of your breath like apples, Beloved
Your mouth like the best wine, that ilah (go up / offer) down smoothly for my beloved, gliding through the lips of those who are asleep.
I am my dawad (beloved's). His desire is toward me.
Come, my dawad (beloved), let us go forth into the field. Let us lodge in the villages.
Let's go early up to the vineyards. Yalak (let's) see whether the vine has budded, its blossom is open, and the pomegranates are in flower. There I will give you my dawad (love).
The mandrakes nathan (give) forth fragrance. At our doors are all kinds of precious fruits, new and old, which I have stored up for you, my dawad (beloved).

Oh that you were like my ach (brother/kinsman), who yanaq (nursed) from the shad (breasts) of my am (mother)! If I matzaa (found) you outside, I would nashaq (kiss) you; yes, and no one would bawaz (despise) me.

I would nahag (lead) you, bawaa (come) you into my am (mother) bayath (house), who would lamad (teach/instruct) me. I would have you shaqah (drink) raqach (spiced) yayan (wine), of the isayas (juice) of my ramawan (pomegranate).
His left shamaawal (left hand) would be under my raash (head). His right yamayan (right hand) would chabaq (embrace) me.
I shabai (swear / take oath) you, bath (daughter) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), that you not iwar (rouse / awaken) up, nor awaken ahabah (love), until it so chapatz (desires). Friends

Who is this who ilah (go up / offer) up from the madabar (wilderness), rapaq (leaning) on her dawad (beloved)? Under the thapawach (apple) tree I aroused you. There your am (mother) conceived you. There she was in yalad (birth / begot) and bore you.

Shawam (place / establish / appoint) me as a chawatham (seal) on your lab (heart), as a chawatham (seal) on your zarawai (arm); for ahabah (love) is iz (strong) as mawath (death). Qanaah (jealousy) is as qashah (rough / hard) as shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife). Its flashes are flashes of ash (fire), a very flame of Yahawah.

Many mayam (Waters) can't kabah (quench) ahabah (love), neither can nahar (floods) shatap (drown) it. If a ayash (husband/individual man) nathan (give) give all the hawan (wealth) of his bayath (house) for ahabah (love), he would be bawaz (utterly) scorned. Friends
We have a qatan (small/young/least) achawath (sister). She has no shad (breasts). What shall we ishah (make) for our achawath (sister) in the yawam (day) when she is to be dabar (word / matter) for?
If she is a chawamah (wall), we will banah (build) on her a turret of kasap (silver). If she is a dalath (door), we will enclose her with lawach (boards) of araz (cedar). Beloved
I am a chawamah (wall), and my shad (breasts) like magadal (towers), then I was in his iyan (eye) like one who matzaa (found) shalawam (peace / safety).

Shalamah (Solomon) had a karam (vineyard) at Bailahamawan (Baal) Hamon. He leased out the karam (vineyard) to natar (keepers). Ayash (husband/individual man) was to bawaa (come) a alap (thousand) shekels of kasap (silver) for its paray (fruit).
My own karam (vineyard) is panayam (before) me. The alap (thousand) are for you, Shalamah (Solomon); two maah (hundred) for those who tend its paray (fruit). Lover
You who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the gan (gardens), with friends in attendance, let me qashab (hear) your qawal (sound / voice)! Beloved
Come barach (away), my dawad (beloved)! Be damah (like) a gazelle or a ipar (young) stag on the har (mountain) of basham (spices)!

The chazawan (vision) of Yashaiyah (Isaiah) the ban (son) of Amawatz (Amoz), which he chazah (saw) concerning Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), in the yawam (day) of Izayah (Uzziah), Yawatham (Jotham), Achaz (Ahaz), and Chazaqayah (Hezekiah), malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah).

Shamai (hearken / hear), shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), and listen, aratz (Earth/land); for Yahawah has dabar (word / matter): I have gadal (nourished) and rawam (will lift up) up ban (son), and they have pashai (rebelled) against me.
The shawar (ox) yadai (knows) his owner, and the donkey his bail (master's) abawas (crib); but Yasharaal (Israel) doesn't yadai (know), my im (people / nation) don't bayan (between).

Haway (Alas/Woe!) Sinful gaway (nation / people), a im (people / nation) loaded with iwan (guilt/iniquity), a zarai (seed) of evildoers, zarai (children) who deal corruptly! They have forsaken Yahawah. They have naatz (despised) the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel). They are zawar (estranged) and backward.
Why should you be nakah (beaten) more, that you sarah (revolt) more and more? The whole raash (head) is chalay (sick), and the whole labab (heart) daway (faint).

From the kap (sole) of the ragal (feet / foot) even to the raash (head) there is no matham (soundness) in it: patzai (wounds), welts, and open makah (sores). They haven't been zawar (closed), neither bandaged, neither soothed with shaman (oil).

Your aratz (Earth/land) is shamamah (desolate). Your iyar (cities) are sharap (burned) with ash (fire). Strangers akal (eat) your adamah (land) in your presence, and it is shamamah (desolate), as mahapakah (overthrown) by strangers.
The bath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion) is yathar (left) like a shelter in a karam (vineyard), like a hut in a field of melons, like a natzar (besieged) iyar (city).

Lawalaa (unless) Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) had yathar (left) to us a very mait (small) sharayad (remnant), we would hayah (came to pass) been as Sadam (Sodom); we would have been damah (like) Imarah (Gomorrah).

Shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, you qatzayan (rulers) of Sadam (Sodom)! Listen to the thawarah (instruction) of our Alahayam, you im (people / nation) of Imarah (Gomorrah)!

"Mah (what) are the rab (multitude) of your zabach (sacrifices) to me?," amar (spoke) Yahawah. I shabai (have) had enough of the burnt ilah (offerings) of ayal (rams), and the chalab (fat) of fed animals. I don't chapatz (delight) in the dam (blood) of par (bulls), or of kabash (lambs), or of male ithawad (goats).
When you bawaa (come) to raah (see) panayam (before) me, who has baqash (required) this at your yad (hand), to ramas (trample) my chatzar (courts)?

Bawaa (come) no more shawaa (vanity) manachah (offerings). Qatarath (incense) is an thawaibah (abomination) to me; new chadash (month), shabath (shabath/rest), and maqaraa (convocations): I can't bear with awan (evil) maqaraa (assemblies).
My napash (living being/soul) shanaa (hate) your New chadash (month) and your mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) feasts. They are a burden to me. I am laah (weary) of nashaa (lift) them.

When you parash (spread) forth your kap (hands), I will ilam (hide) my iyan (eye) from you. Yes, when you rabah (make) many thapalah (prayers), I will not shamai (hearken / hear). Your yad (hand) are malaa (full) of dam (blood).
Rachatz (wash) yourselves, make yourself zakah (clean). Sawar (put) away the rai (evil) of your mailal (doings) from before my iyan (eye). Chadal (cease) to do raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil).

Lamad (teach/instruct) to yatab (do) well. Darash (seek) mashapat (justice). Ashar (who/that) the chamawatz (oppressed). Shapat (judge) the yathawam (fatherless). Rayab (plead) for the alamanah (widow).

"Yalak (come) now, and let us yakach (reason) together," amar (spoke) Yahawah: Though your chataa (sins) be as shanay (second), they shall be as laban (white) as shalag (snow). Though they be adam (red) like thawalai (crimson), they shall be as tzamar (wool).
If you are abah (be willing / desire) and shamai (hearken / hear), you shall akal (eat) the tawab (pleasant/functional) of the aratz (Earth/land);
But if you maan (refuse) and marah (rebel), you shall be akal (eat) with the charab (sword); for the pah (mouth) of Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) it.
How the aman (believe / have faith) qarayah (city) has become a prostitute! She was full of mashapat (justice); tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) lawan (lodged) in her, but now ratzach (murderers).
Your kasap (silver) has become sayag (dross), your sabaa (wine) mahal (mixed) with mayam (Waters).

Your shar (prince / ruler) are sarar (rebellious), and chabar (companions) of thieves. Everyone ahab (love) shachad (bribes), and radap (follows) after shalaman (rewards). They don't shapat (judge) the yathawam (fatherless), neither does the rayab (cause) of the alamanah (widow) bawaa (come) to them.

Therefore the Adawan, Yahawah of tzabaa (troop), the abayar (mighty) One of Yasharaal (Israel), naam (declares (prophetically)): haway (Alas/Woe!), I will get relief from my tzar (oppressor / distressor), and naqam (avenge) myself of my ayab (enemy);
And I will shawab (turn back / repent) my yad (hand) on you, thoroughly tzarap (purge) away your sayag (dross), and will sawar (take) away all your badayal (divide).

I will shawab (turn back / repent) your shapat (judges) as at the raashawan (first), and your yaitz (counselors) as at the thachalah (beginning). Afterward you shall be qaraa (called) ‘The iyar (city) of tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), a aman (believe / have faith) town.’
Tzayawan (Zion) shall be padah (redeemed) with mashapat (justice), and her shawab (turn back / repent) with tzadaqah (righteousness).
But the shabar (destruction) of transgressors and chataa (sinners) shall be yachad (together), and those who izab (forsake) Yahawah shall be kalah (complete / finish).
For they shall be bawash (ashamed) of the ayal (oaks) which you have chamad (desired), and you shall be chapar (confounded) for the ganah (gardens) that you have bachar (chosen).
For you shall be as an alah (these) whose ilah (leaf) nabal (fades), and as a ganah (garden) that has no mayam (Waters).
The chasan (strong) will be like tinder, and his pail (work) like a nayatzawatz (spark). They will shanayam (two) bair (burn) yachad (together), and no one will kabah (quench) them.
This is dabar (word / matter) Yashaiyah (Isaiah) the ban (son) of Amawatz (Amoz) chazah (saw) concerning Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

It shall happen in the acharayath (latter) yawam (day), that the har (mountain) of yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) bayath (house) shall be kawan (established) on the raash (head) of the har (mountain), and shall be nashaa (lift) above the gabaih (hills); and all gaway (nation / people) shall nahar (flow) to it.

Many im (people / nation) shall halak (move) and amar (spoke), "yalak (come), let's ilah (go up / offer) up to the har (mountain) of Yahawah, to the bayath (house) of the Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob); and he will yarah (teach) us of his darak (ways), and we will yalak (walk) in his arach (paths)." For out of Tzayawan (Zion) the thawarah (instruction) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah from Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

He will shapat (judge) between the gaway (nation / people), and will decide concerning many gaway (nation / people); and they shall kathath (beat) their charab (sword) into ath (entirety), and their chanayath (spears) into mazamarah (pruning) hooks. Gaway (nation / people) shall not nashaa (lift) up charab (sword) against gaway (nation / people), neither shall they lamad (teach/instruct) malachamah (war) any more.
Bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob), yalak (come), and yalak (let) us walk in the awar (light) of Yahawah.

For you have forsaken your im (people / nation), the bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob), because they are malaa (filled) from the qadam (east), with those who practice divination like the Palashathay (Philistines), and they clasp hands with the yalad (birth / begot) of nakaray (foreigners).

Their aratz (Earth/land) is malaa (full) of kasap (silver) and zahab (gold), neither is there any qatzah (end / extremity / border) of their awatzar (treasures). Their aratz (Earth/land) also is malaa (full) of sawas (horses), neither is there any qatzah (end / extremity / border) of their marakabah (chariots).
Their aratz (Earth/land) also is malaa (full) of alayal (idols). They shachah (worship) the maishah (work) of their own yad (hand), that which their own atzabai (fingers) ishah (make) made.
Adam (man) is shachach (brought) low, and mankind is shapal (humbled); therefore don't nashaa (lift) them.
Bawaa (come) into the tzawar (rock), and taman (hide) in the ipar (dust), from panayam (before) the pachad (fear / dread) of Yahawah, and from the glory of his gaawan (majesty).

The gabahawath (lofty) iyan (eye) of adam (man) will be shapal (brought) low, the rawam (will lift up) of adam (men) will be shachach (bowed) down, and Yahawah alone will be shagab (exalted) in that yawam (day).
For there will be a yawam (day) of Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) for all that is gaah (proud) and haughty, and for all that is nashaa (lift) up; and it shall be shapal (brought) low:
For all the araz (cedars) of Labanawan (Lebanon), that are rawam (will lift up) and nashaa (lift) up, for all the alawan (oaks) of Bashan (Bashan),
For all the rawam (will lift up) har (mountain), for all the gabaih (hills) that are nashaa (lift) up,
For every gabah (lofty) magadal (tower), for every batzar (fortified) chawamah (wall),
For all the anayah (ships) of Tharashayash (Tarshish), and for all chamadah (pleasant) imagery.

The gabahawath (loftiness) of adam (man) shall be shachach (bowed) down, and the rawam (will lift up) of adam (men) shall be shapal (brought) low; and Yahawah alone shall be shagab (exalted) in that yawam (day).
The alayal (idols) shall kalayal (utterly) chalap (pass) away.

Men shall bawaa (come) into the mairah (caves) of the tzawar (rocks), and into the holes of the ipar (earth), from panayam (before) the pachad (fear / dread) of Yahawah, and from the glory of his gaawan (majesty), when he qawam (rise up) to shake the aratz (Earth/land) mightily.

In that yawam (day), adam (men) shall shalak (cast) away their alayal (idols) of kasap (silver), and their alayal (idols) of zahab (gold), which ishah (make) been made for themselves to shachah (worship), to the chapar (moles) and to the italap (bats);

To bawaa (come) into the caverns of the tzawar (rocks), and into the naqarah (clefts) of the ragged salai (rocks), from panayam (before) the pachad (fear / dread) of Yahawah, and from the glory of his gaawan (majesty), when he qawam (rise up) to shake the aratz (Earth/land) mightily.
Stop trusting in adam (man), whose nashamah (breathing thing) is in his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting); for of what chashab (account) is he?

For, behold, the Adawan, Yahawah of tzabaa (troop), sawar (takes) away from Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) and from Yahawadah (Judah) supply and support, the whole supply of lacham (bread), and the kal (every) supply of mayam (Waters);
The gabawar (mighty) man, the ayash (husband/individual man) of malachamah (war), the shapat (judge), the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), the diviner, the zaqan (elder),
The shar (prince / ruler) of chamashayam (fifty), the nashaa (lift) panayam (man), the yaitz (counselor), the skilled craftsman, and the clever enchanter.
I will nathan (give) nair (boys) to be their shar (prince / ruler), and nair (children) shall mashal (rule/have dominion) over them.

The im (people / nation) will be nagash (oppressed), everyone by ayash (husband/individual man), and everyone by his neighbor. The nair (child) will rahab (behave) himself proudly against the zaqan (old) man, and the qalah (base) against the honorable.

Indeed a ayash (husband/individual man) shall thapash (take) hold of his ach (brother/kinsman) in the bayath (house) of his ab (father), saying, You have shamalah (clothing), you be our qatzayan (ruler), and let this makashalah (ruin) be under your yad (hand).

In that yawam (day) he will cry out, amar (spoke), I will not be a chabash (healer); for in my bayath (house) is neither lacham (bread) nor shamalah (clothing). You shall not shawam (place / establish / appoint) me qatzayan (ruler) of the im (people / nation).

For Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) is kashal (stumble / stagger), and Yahawadah (Judah) is napal (fall / be cast down); because their lashawan (tongue/language) and their mailal (doings) are against Yahawah, to marah (provoke) the iyan (eye) of his kabawad (glory).

The look of their panayam (faces) inah (answer / respond) against them. They parade their chataah (sin) like Sadam (Sodom). They don't kachad (hide) it. Away (woe) to their napash (living being/soul)! For they have brought disaster upon themselves.
Amar (spoke) the tzadayaq (righteous) "tawab (pleasant/functional)!" For they shall akal (eat) the paray (fruit) of their deeds.
Away (woe) to the rashai (wicked)! Disaster is upon them; for the deeds of his yad (hand) will be paid back to him.

As for my im (people / nation), ilal (children) are their nagash (oppressors), and ashah (wife/individual woman) mashal (rule/have dominion) over them. My im (people / nation), those who ashar (who/that) you thaih (cause) you to err, and balai (destroy) the darak (way) of your arach (paths).
Yahawah natzab (stands) up to rayab (contend), and imad (stands) to dayan (judge) the im (people / nation).

Yahawah will bawaa (come) into mashapat (judgment) with the zaqan (elders) of his im (people / nation), and their leaders: "It is you who have bair (eaten) up the karam (vineyard). The gazalah (spoil) of the inay (poor) is in your bayath (house).
What do you mean that you dakaa (crush) my im (people / nation), and tachan (grind) the panayam (face) of the inay (poor)?" Naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (troop).

Moreover Yahawah amar (spoke), yain (because) the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion) are gabah (haughty), and yalak (walk) with natah (outstretched) garawan (necks) and flirting iyan (eye), halak (move) to trip as they yalak (go), jingling ornaments on their ragal (feet / foot);
Therefore the Adanay brings sores on the qadaqad (crown) of the head of the women of Tzayawan (Zion), and Yahawah will make their scalps bald.
In that yawam (day) the Adanay will sawar (take) away the thapaarah (beauty) of their anklets, the headbands, the crescent necklaces,
The earrings, the sharah (bracelets), the railah (veils),
The headdresses, the ankle chains, the sashes, the perfume bottles, the charms,
The signet tabaith (rings), the ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) tabaith (rings),
The fine robes, the capes, the cloaks, the purses,
The galayawan (hand) mirrors, the sadayan (fine) linen garments, the tiaras, and the shawls.

It shall happen that instead of basham (sweet) spices, there shall be maq (rottenness); instead of a belt, a rope; instead of maishah (well) set maqashah (hair), qarachah (baldness); instead of a robe, a wearing of sackcloth; and branding instead of yapay (beauty).
Your math (men) shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword), and your gabawarah (mighty) in the malachamah (war).
Her pathach (gates) shall anah (lament) and abal (mourn); and she shall be naqah (clean/innocent) and yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the aratz (Earth/land).

Shabai (seven) ashah (wife/individual woman) shall chazaq (take) hold of achad (one) ayash (husband/individual man) in that yawam (day), amar (spoke), We will akal (eat) our own lacham (bread), and labash (wear) our own shamalah (clothing): only let us be qaraa (called) by your sham (name). Asap (take) away our charapah (reproach).

In that yawam (day), yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) tzamach (branch) will be tzabay (beautiful) and kabawad (glorious), and the paray (fruit) of the aratz (Earth/land) will be the beauty and glory of the survivors of Yasharaal (Israel).

It will happen, that he who is shaar (left) in Tzayawan (Zion), and he who yathar (remains) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), shall be amar (spoke) qadawash (holy), even everyone who is kathab (written) among the chay (life) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem);

When the Adanay shall have rachatz (washed) away the tzawaah (filth) of the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion), and shall have dawach (purged) the dam (blood) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) from its qarab (among / near), by the rawach (spirit / wind) of mashapat (justice), and by the rawach (spirit / wind) of bair (burning).

Yahawah will baraa (created) over the whole makawan (habitation) of har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion), and over her maqaraa (assemblies), a inan (cloud) and ishan (smoke) by yawamam (by day), and the nagah (shining) of a lahabah (flaming) ash (fire) by layal (night); for over all the kabawad (glory) will be a canopy.
There will be a sakah (pavilion) for a tzal (shade) in the yawamam (by day) from the charab (heat), and for a machasah (refuge) and for a shelter from zaram (storm) and from matar (rain).
Let me shayar (sing) for my well yadayad (beloved) a shayar (song) of my dawad (beloved) about his karam (vineyard). My yadayad (beloved) had a karam (vineyard) on a very ban (son) qaran (horn).

He dug it up, gathered out its saqal (stones), natai (planted) it with the choicest vine, banah (built) a magadal (tower) in its thawak (midst), and also chatzab (cut) out a yaqab (winepress) therein. He qawah (gather/wait) for it to ishah (make) inab (grapes), but it ishah (make) baashayam (wild) grapes.
Now, yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) and ayash (husband/individual man) of Yahawadah (Judah), please shapat (judge) between me and my karam (vineyard).

What could ishah (make) been done more to my karam (vineyard), that I ishah (make) not done in it? Madawai (why), when I qawah (gather/wait) for it to ishah (make) inab (grapes), ishah (make) it yield baashayam (wild) grapes?

Now I yadai (will) tell you what I will ishah (make) to my karam (vineyard). I will sawar (take) away its mashawakah (hedge), and it will be bair (eaten) up. I will paratz (break) down its gadar (wall) of it, and it will be trampled down.

I will shayath (put / appoint / make) it a wasteland. It won't be zamar (pruned) nor hoed, but it will ilah (go up / offer) shamayar (briers) and shayath (thorns). I will also tzawah (command) the ib (clouds) that they matar (rain) no matar (rain) on it.

For the karam (vineyard) of Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) is the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), and the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yahawadah (Judah) his pleasant natai (plant): and he qawah (gather/wait) for mashapat (justice), but, behold, mashapach (oppression); for tzadaqah (righteousness), but, behold, a tzaiqah (cry) of distress.

Haway (Alas/Woe!) To those who nagai (join) bayath (house) to bayath (house), who lay shadah (field) to shadah (field), until there is no maqawam (place), and you are yashab (inhabit/dwell) to dwell alone in the qarab (among / near) of the aratz (Earth/land)!
In my azan (ears), Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) says: laa (NOT) many bayath (house) will be shamah (desolate), even gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and tawab (pleasant/functional), unoccupied.
For ishar (ten) tzamad (acres) of karam (vineyard) shall ishah (make) achad (one) bath (daughter), and a chamar (homer) of zarai (seed) shall ishah (make) an ayapah (ephah).

Haway (Alas/Woe!) To those who shakam (rise) up early in the baqar (morning), that they may radap (follow) shakar (strong) drink; who achar (other) late into the nashap (night), until yayan (wine) dalaq (inflames) them!

The kanawar (harp), lyre, tambourine, and flute, with yayan (wine), are at their mashathah (feasts); but they don't nabat (respect) the pail (work) of Yahawah, neither raah (see) they considered the operation of his yad (hand).

Therefore my im (people / nation) galah (go) into captivity for lack of daith (knowledge). Their honorable math (men) are raib (famished), and their hamawan (multitudes) are parched with tzamaa (thirst).

Therefore shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife) has enlarged its desire, and pair (opened) its pah (mouth) without chaq (statute); and their glory, their hamawan (multitude), their shaawan (pomp), and he who rejoices among them, descend into it.
So adam (man) is shachach (brought) low, mankind is shapal (humbled), and the iyan (eye) of the arrogant ones are shapal (humbled);
But Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) is gabah (exalted) in mashapat (justice), and Al the qadawash (holy) One is qadash (set apart/make holy) in tzadaqah (righteousness).
Then the kabash (lambs) will graze as in their pasture, and gawar (strangers) will akal (eat) the ruins of the rich.
