The ay (islands) raah (see) seen, and yaraa (fear / be afraid). The ends of the aratz (Earth/land) charad (tremble). They qarab (come close), and athah (come).
Everyone izar (helps) his neighbor. They amar (spoke) to their ach (brother/kinsman), Be chazaq (strong)!

So the charash (carpenter) chazaq (encourages) the tzarap (goldsmith). He who smoothes with the patayash (hammer) encourages him who strikes the paim (anvil), amar (spoke) of the dabaq (soldering), "It is tawab (pleasant/functional);" and he chazaq (fastens) it with masamar (nails), that it might not totter.
“But you, Yasharaal (Israel), my ibad (servant), Yaiqab (Jacob) whom I have bachar (chosen), the zarai (seed) of Abaraham (Abraham) my ahab (love),

You whom I have chazaq (taken) hold of from the ends of the aratz (Earth/land), and qaraa (called) from its corners, and amar (spoke) to you, ‘You are my ibad (servant), I have bachar (chosen) you and not maas (cast) you away;’

Don't you be yaraa (fear / be afraid), for I am with you. Don't be shaih (dismayed), for I am your Alahayam. I will amatz (strengthen) you. Yes, I will izar (help) you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right yamayan (right hand) of my tzadaq (righteous / just / fair).
Behold, all those who are charah (hot with anger) against you will be disappointed and kalam (confounded). Those who rayab (strive) with you will be like nothing, and shall abad (destroy/perish).
You will baqash (seek) them, and won't matzaa (find) them, even those who contend with you. Those who malachamah (war) against you will be as apas (nothing), as a non-existent thing.
For I, Yahawah your Alahayam, will chazaq (hold) your right yamayan (right hand), amar (spoke) to you, ‘Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). I will izar (help) you.’

Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), you thawalai (worm) Yaiqab (Jacob), and you math (men) of Yasharaal (Israel). I will izar (help) you,” naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, “and your gaal (redeemer) is the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).

Behold, I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) you into a chadash (new) charawatz (sharp) mawarag (threshing) instrument with payapayah (teeth). You will dawash (thresh) the har (mountain), and daqaq (beat) them small, and will shawam (place / establish / appoint) the gabaih (hills) like matz (chaff).

You will zarah (winnow) them, and the rawach (spirit / wind) will nashaa (lift) them away, and the sair (whirlwind) will pawatz (scatter) them. You will gayal (rejoice) in Yahawah. You will glory in the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).

The inay (poor) and abayawan (needy) baqash (seek) mayam (Waters), and there is none. Their lashawan (tongue/language) nashath (fails) for tzamaa (thirst). I, Yahawah, will inah (answer / respond) them. I, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), will not izab (forsake) them.

I will pathach (open) nahar (rivers) on the bare heights, and maiyan (springs) in the thawak (midst) of the baqaih (valleys). I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) the madabar (wilderness) a agam (pool) of mayam (Waters), and the tzayah (dry) aratz (Earth/land) mawatzaa (springs) of mayam (Waters).

I will nathan (give) araz (cedar), acacia, hadas (myrtle), and shaman (oil) trees in the madabar (wilderness). I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) fir itz (trees), thadahar (pine), and box trees yachad (together) in the irabah (desert);

That they may raah (see), yadai (know), shawam (place / establish / appoint), and shakal (understand) yachad (together), that the yad (hand) of Yahawah ishah (make) done this, and the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel) has baraa (created) it.
Qarab (come close) your rayab (cause),” amar (spoke) Yahawah. "Nagash (bring) forth your itzamah (strong) reasons," amar (spoke) the malak (king) of Yaiqab (Jacob).

Let them announce, and nagad (declare) to us what shall qarah (happen). Nagad (declare) the raashawan (former) things, what they are, that we may shawam (place / establish / appoint) them, and yadai (know) the acharayath (latter) end of them; or show us things to bawaa (come).

Nagad (declare) the things that are to athah (come) achawar (hereafter), that we may yadai (know) that you are Alahayam. Yes, do yatab (good), or do raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil), that we may be shaih (dismayed), and raah (see) it yachad (together).
Behold, you are of ayan (nothing), and your pail (work) is of nothing. He who bachar (chooses) you is an thawaibah (abomination).

I have iwar (rouse / awaken) up one from the tzapawan (north), and he has athah (come); from the mazarach (rising) of the shamash (sun), one who qaraa (called) on my sham (name); and he shall bawaa (come) on sagan (rulers) as on mortar, and as the yatzar (potter) ramas (treads) tayat (clay).

Who has nagad (declared) it from the raash (head), that we may yadai (know)? And panayam (before), that we may amar (spoke), ‘He is right?’ Nagad (surely), there is no one who declares. Shamai (hearken / hear), there is no one who shows. Shamai (hearken / hear), there is no one who hears your amar (spoke).
I am the raashawan (first) to say to Tzayawan (Zion), ‘hanah (Behold), look at them;’ and I will nathan (give) one who brings bashar (good) news to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).
When I raah (see), there is no ayash (husband/individual man); even among them there is no yaitz (counselor) who, when I shaal (ask) of them, can shawab (turn back / repent) a dabar (word / matter).
Behold, all of them, their maishah (works) are awan (vanity) and apas (nothing). Their molten nasak (images) are rawach (spirit / wind) and thahaw (formless).

Behold, my ibad (servant), whom I uphold; my bachayar (chosen), in whom my napash (living being/soul) ratzah (delights)— I nathan (give) put my rawach (spirit / wind) on him. He will yatzaa (go out / come out) mashapat (justice) to the gaway (nation / people).
He will not shout, nor nashaa (lift) his qawal (sound / voice), nor shamai (hearken / hear) it to be heard in the chawatz (street).
He won't shabar (break) a ratzatz (bruised) qanah (reed). He won't kabah (quench) a dimly burning wick. He will faithfully yatzaa (go out / come out) mashapat (justice).

He will not kahah (fail) nor be ratzatz (discouraged), until he has shawam (place / establish / appoint) mashapat (justice) in the aratz (Earth/land), and the ay (islands) will yachal (wait) for his thawarah (instruction).

Thus amar (spoke) Al Yahawah, he who baraa (created) the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) and natah (stretched) them out, he who raqai (spread) out the aratz (Earth/land) and that which comes out of it, he who nathan (give) nashamah (breathing thing) to its im (people / nation) and rawach (spirit / wind) to those who halak (move) in it.

I, Yahawah, have qaraa (called) you in tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and will chazaq (hold) your yad (hand), and will natzar (keep) you, and nathan (give) you a barayath (covenant) for the im (people / nation), as a awar (light) for the gaway (nation / people);
To paqach (open) the iwar (blind) iyan (eye), to bring the asayar (prisoners) out of the dungeon, and those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in chashak (darkness) out of the kalaa (prison).
I am Yahawah. That is my sham (name). I will not nathan (give) my kabawad (glory) to achar (other), nor my thahalah (praise) to engraved pasayal (images).
Behold, the raashawan (former) things bawaa (come) happened, and I nagad (declare) chadash (new) things. I shamai (hearken / hear) you about them before they come up.

Shayar (sing) to Yahawah a chadash (new) shayar (song), and his thahalah (praise) from the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land), you who yarad (go) down to the yam (sea/waters), and malaa (all) that is therein, the ay (islands) and their yashab (inhabit/dwell).

Let the madabar (wilderness) and its iyar (cities) nashaa (lift) their voices, with the chatzar (villages) that Qadar (Kedar) yashab (inhabit/dwell). Let the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Sela ranan (sing). Let them tzawach (shout) from the raash (head) of the har (mountain)!
Let them shawam (place / establish / appoint) kabawad (glory) to Yahawah, and nagad (declare) his thahalah (praise) in the ay (islands).

Yahawah will yatzaa (go out / come out) out like a gabawar (mighty) man. He will iwar (rouse / awaken) up qanaah (zeal) like a ayash (husband/individual man) of malachamah (war). He will raise a war rawai (cry). Yes, he will shout aloud. He will triumph over his ayab (enemy).

I have been chashah (silent) a iwalam (forever) time. I have been charash (quiet) and apaq (restrained) myself. Now I will paih (cry) out like a travailing yalad (birth / begot). I will yachad (both) gasp and shaap (pant).

I will charab (destroy) har (mountain) and gabaih (hills), and yabash (dry land) up all their ishab (herbs). I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) the nahar (rivers) ay (islands), and will yabash (dry land) up the agam (pools).

I will yalak (bring) the iwar (blind) by a darak (way) that they don't yadai (know). I will darak (lead) them in nathayab (paths) that they don't yadai (know). I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) machashak (darkness) awar (light) panayam (before) them, and maiqash (crooked) places mayashawar (straight). I will ishah (make) these things, and I will not izab (forsake) them.

Those who batach (trust) in engraved pasal (idol/graven image), who amar (spoke) molten pasal (idol/graven image), ‘You are our Alahayam’ will be sawag (turned) achawar (back). They will be utterly disappointed.
Shamai (hearken / hear), you charash (deaf), and nabat (look), you iwar (blind), that you may raah (see).

Who is iwar (blind), but my ibad (servant)? Or who is as charash (deaf) as my malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) whom I shalach (send)? Who is as iwar (blind) as he who is at shalam (peace), and as iwar (blind) as yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) ibad (servant)?
You raah (see) many things, but don't shamar (keep/guard). His azan (ears) are paqach (open), but he doesn't shamai (hearken / hear).
It chapatz (pleased) Yahawah, for his tzadaq (righteous / just / fair)' sake, to gadal (magnify) the thawarah (instruction), and make it honorable.

But this is a bazaz (robbed) and plundered im (people / nation). All of them are pachach (snared) in chawar (holes), and they are chabaa (hidden) in kalaa (prisons). They have become a baz (prey), and no one natzal (delivers); and a mashasah (spoil), and no one amar (spoke), ‘shawab (turn back / repent) them!’
Who is there among you who will azan (give) ear to this? Who will listen and shamai (hearken / hear) for the achawar (time) to come?

Who nathan (give) Yaiqab (Jacob) as plunder, and Yasharaal (Israel) to the bazaz (robbers)? Didn't Yahawah, he against whom we have chataa (sinned)? For they would not halak (move) in his darak (ways), and they disobeyed his thawarah (instruction).

Therefore he shapak (poured) the fierceness of his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) on him, and the izawaz (strength) of malachamah (battle); and it set him on lahat (fire) all around, but he didn't yadai (know); and it bair (burned) him, but he didn't shawam (place / establish / appoint) it to lab (heart).

But now thus amar (spoke) Yahawah who baraa (created) you, Yaiqab (Jacob), and he who yatzar (formed) you, Yasharaal (Israel): Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), for I have gaal (redeemed) you. I have qaraa (called) you by your sham (name). You are mine.

When you ibar (pass over/through) through the mayam (Waters), I will be with you; and ibar (pass over/through) the nahar (rivers), they will not shatap (overflow) you. When you yalak (walk) bamaw (through) the ash (fire), you will not be kawah (burned), and lahabah (flame) will not scorch you.

For I am Yahawah your Alahayam, the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel), your Savior. I nathan (give) given Matzarayam (Egypt) as your kapar (ransom), Kawash (Ethiopia) and Sabaa (Seba) in your place.

Since you have been yaqar (precious) and honored in my iyan (eye), and I have ahab (love) you; therefore I will nathan (give) adam (people) in your place, and laam (nations) instead of your napash (living being/soul).
Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid); for I am with you. I will bawaa (come) your zarai (seed) from the mazarach (east), and qabatz (gather) you from the mairab (west).

I will amar (spoke) the tzapawan (north), ‘nathan (give) them up!’ And tell the thayaman (south), ‘Don't hold them back! Bawaa (come) my ban (son) from rachawaq (far), and my bath (daughter) from the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land)—
Everyone who is qaraa (called) by my sham (name), and whom I have baraa (created) for my kabawad (glory), whom I have yatzar (formed), yes, whom I ishah (make) made.’
Yatzaa (go out / come out) out the iwar (blind) im (people / nation) who yash (have) iyan (eye), and the charash (deaf) who have azan (ears).

Let all the gaway (nation / people) be qabatz (gathered) yachad (together), and let the laam (peoples) be asap (assembled). Who among them can nagad (declare) this, and show us raashawan (former) things? Nathan (give) them bring their witnesses, that they may be justified; or shamai (hearken / hear) them hear, and amar (spoke), That is amath (truth).

"You are my witnesses," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, "With my ibad (servant) whom I have bachar (chosen); that you may yadai (know) and aman (believe / have faith) me, and bayan (between) that I am he. Panayam (before) me there was no Al yatzar (formed), neither will there be achar (other) me.
I myself am Yahawah; and balaiday (besides) me there is no savior.

I have nagad (declared), I have yashai (salvation), and I have shown; and there was no zawar (strange) Alahayam among you. Therefore you are my witnesses," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, and I am Al.
Yes, since the yawam (day) was I am he; and there is no one who can natzal (deliver) out of my yad (hand). I will pail (work), and who can shawab (turn back / repent) it?

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, your gaal (redeemer), the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel): For your sake, I have shalach (send) to Babal (Babylon), and I will bring all of them down as fugitives, even the Kashaday (Chaldeans), in the anayah (ships) of their ranah (rejoicing).
I am Yahawah, your qadawash (holy) One, the Creator of Yasharaal (Israel), your malak (king).
Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, who nathan (give) a darak (way) in the yam (sea/waters), and a nathayab (path) in the iz (mighty) mayam (Waters);

Who yatzaa (go out / come out) forth the rakab (chariot) and sawas (horse), the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) and the izawaz (mighty) man (they shakab (lie) down yachad (together), they shall not qawam (rise up); they are daik (extinct), they are kabah (quenched) like a wick):
Don't zakar (remembrance/memory) the raashawan (former) things, and don't bayan (between) the things of qadamawanay (old).

Behold, I will ishah (make) a chadash (new) thing. It tzamach (springs) forth now. Don't you yadai (know) it? I will even shawam (place / establish / appoint) a darak (way) in the madabar (wilderness), and nahar (rivers) in the yashayamawan (desert).

The animals of the shadah (field) shall honor me, the jackals and the ostriches; because I nathan (give) mayam (Waters) in the madabar (wilderness) and nahar (rivers) in the yashayamawan (desert), to shaqah (give) drink to my im (people / nation), my bachayar (chosen),
The im (people / nation) which I yatzar (formed) for myself, that they might set sapar (book) my thahalah (praise).
Yet you have not qaraa (called) on me, Yaiqab (Jacob); but you have been yagai (weary) of me, Yasharaal (Israel).

You bawaa (come) not brought me of your shah (sheep) for burnt ilah (offerings); neither kabad (have) you honored me with your zabach (sacrifices). I have not burdened you with manachah (offerings), nor yagai (wearied) you with labawanah (frankincense).

You have bought me no sweet qanah (cane) with kasap (money), nor have you rawah (filled) me with the chalab (fat) of your zabach (sacrifices); but you have burdened me with your chataah (sin). You have yagai (wearied) me with your iwan (guilt/iniquity).
I, even I, am he who machah (blots) out your pashai (transgressions) for my own sake; and I will not zakar (remembrance/memory) your chataah (sin).
Zakar (remembrance/memory) me in remembrance. Let us shapat (plead) yachad (together). Set sapar (book) your case, that you may be justified.
Your raashawan (first) ab (father) chataa (sinned), and your lawatz (teachers) have pashai (transgressed) against me.
Therefore I will chalal (profane) the shar (prince / ruler) of the qadash (set apart/make holy); and I will nathan (give) Yaiqab (Jacob) a charam (curse), and Yasharaal (Israel) an insult.
Yet shamai (hearken / hear) now, Yaiqab (Jacob) my ibad (servant), and Yasharaal (Israel), whom I have bachar (chosen).

This is what Yahawah who ishah (make) you, and yatzar (formed) you from the batan (womb), who will izar (help) you amar (spoke): Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), Yaiqab (Jacob) my ibad (servant); and you, Yasharawan (Jeshurun), whom I have bachar (chosen).

For I will yatzaq (pour) mayam (Waters) on him who is thirsty, and nazal (streams) on the dry yabashah (dry land). I will yatzaq (pour) my rawach (spirit / wind) on your zarai (seed), and my barakah (blessing) on your tzaatzaa (offspring):
And they will tzamach (spring) up bayan (between) the chatzayar (grass), as irab (evening) by the yabal (watercourses).

One will amar (spoke), ‘I am yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal));’ and another will be qaraa (called) by the sham (name) of Yaiqab (Jacob); and another will kathab (write) with his yad (hand) ‘to Yahawah,’ and honor the sham (name) of Yasharaal (Israel).

This is what Yahawah, the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), and his gaal (redeemer), Yahawah of tzabaa (troop), amar (spoke): I am the raashawan (first), and I am the acharawan (last); and balaiday (besides) me there is no Alahayam.

Who is like me? Who will qaraa (called), and will nagad (declare) it, and irak (set) it in order for me, since I established the iwalam (forever) im (people / nation)? Let them nagad (declare) the things that are bawaa (come), and that will happen.

Don't pachad (fear / dread), neither be rahah (afraid). Haven't I nagad (declared) it to you long ago, and shown it? You are my witnesses. Is there a Alawah balaiday (besides) me? Indeed, there is not. I don't yadai (know) any other tzawar (rock).

Everyone who yatzar (makes) an engraved pasal (idol/graven image) is thahaw (formless). The things that they delight in will not yail (profit). Their own witnesses don't raah (see), nor yadai (know), that they may be disappointed.
Who has yatzar (fashioned) a Al, or molds an pasal (idol/graven image) that is profitable for balathay (nothing)?

Behold, all his chabar (fellows) will be disappointed; and the workmen are mere adam (men). Let them all be qabatz (gathered) together. Let them imad (stand) up. They will pachad (fear / dread). They will be bawash (put) to shame yachad (together).

The blacksmith takes an axe, pail (works) in the pacham (coals), yatzar (fashions) it with maqabah (hammers), and pail (works) it with his strong zarawai (arm). He is raib (hungry), and his kach (strength / mighty / power) ayan (fails); he shathah (drinks) no mayam (Waters), and is yaip (faint).

The charash (carpenter) stretches out a qaw (line). He thaar (marks) it out with a pencil. He shapes it with maqatzaih (planes). He thaar (marks) it out with compasses, and shapes it like the thabanayath (figure) of a ayash (husband/individual man), with the thapaarah (beauty) of a adam (man), to reside in a bayath (house).

He karath (cut) down araz (cedars) for himself, and laqach (take / seized) the tharazah (cypress) and the alawan (oak), and amatz (strengthens) for himself one among the itz (trees) of the yair (forest). He natai (plants) a fir tree, and the gasham (rain) nourishes it.

Then it will be for a adam (man) to bair (burn); and he laqach (take / seized) some of it, and chamam (warms) himself. Yes, he bair (burns) it, and apah (bakes) lacham (bread). Yes, he pail (makes) a Al, and shachah (worships) it; he ishah (make) it an engraved pasal (idol/graven image), and sagad (falls) down to it.

He sharap (burns) chatzay (part) of it in the ash (fire). With chatzay (part) of it, he akal (eat) meat. He tzalay (roasts) a tzalah (roast), and is shabai (satisfied). Yes, he chamam (warms) himself, and amar (spoke), haach (aha)! I am chamam (warm). I raah (see) seen the awar (light).

The shaarayath (rest) of it he ishah (make) into a Al, even his engraved pasal (idol/graven image). He bows down to it and shachah (worships), and palal (prays) to it, and amar (spoke), natzal (deliver) me; for you are my Al!
They don't yadai (know), neither do they bayan (between): for he has shut their iyan (eye), that they can't raah (see); and their lab (heart), that they can't shakal (understand).

No lab (heart) thinks, neither is there daith (knowledge) nor thabawan (understanding) to amar (spoke), I have sharap (burned) chatzay (part) of it in the ash (fire). Yes, I have also apah (baked) lacham (bread) on its gachal (coals). I have tzalah (roasted) meat and akal (eat) it. Shall I ishah (make) the yathar (rest) of it into an thawaibah (abomination)? Shall I bow down to a itz (tree) trunk?

He raih (feeds) on ashes. A hathal (deceived) lab (heart) has natah (turned) him aside; and he can't natzal (deliver) his napash (living being/soul), nor amar (spoke), Isn't there a shaqar (lie) in my right yamayan (right hand)?

Zakar (remembrance/memory) these things, Yaiqab (Jacob) and Yasharaal (Israel); for you are my ibad (servant). I have yatzar (formed) you. You are my ibad (servant). Yasharaal (Israel), you will not be nashah (forgotten) by me.
I have machah (blotted) out, as a ib (thick) cloud, your pashai (transgressions), and, as a inan (cloud), your chataah (sin). Shawab (turn back / repent) to me, for I have gaal (redeemed) you.

Ranan (sing), you shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), for Yahawah ishah (make) done it! Rawai (shout), you lower thachathay (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land)! Patzach (break) out into ranah (singing), you har (mountain), O yair (forest), all of your itz (trees), for Yahawah has gaal (redeemed) Yaiqab (Jacob), and will paar (glorify) himself in Yasharaal (Israel).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, your gaal (redeemer), and he who yatzar (formed) you from the batan (womb): I am Yahawah, who ishah (make) all things; who natah (alone) stretches out the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)); who natah (spreads) out the aratz (Earth/land) by myself;

Who parar (frustrates) the awath (sign / mark / miracle) of the bad (liars), and makes diviners halal (praise); who shawab (turn back / repent) chakam (wise) men backward, and makes their daith (knowledge) foolish;

Who qawam (rise up) the dabar (word / matter) of his ibad (servant), and shalam (performs) the itzah (counsel) of his malaak (angel / messenger of Yah); who amar (spoke) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), ‘She will be yashab (inhabit/dwell);’ and of the iyar (cities) of Yahawadah (Judah), ‘They will be banah (built),’ and ‘I will qawam (rise up) up its charabah (waste) places;’
Who amar (spoke) to the tzawalah (deep), ‘Be charab (dry),’ and ‘I will yabash (dry land) up your nahar (rivers);’

Who amar (spoke) of Kawarash (Cyrus), ‘He is my shepherd, and shall shalam (perform) all my chapatz (pleasure),’ even amar (spoke) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), ‘She will be banah (built);’ and of the hayakal (temple), ‘Your yasad (foundation) will be laid.’

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah to his mashayach (anointed one), to Kawarash (Cyrus), whose right yamayan (right hand) I have chazaq (held), to radad (subdue) gaway (nation / people) panayam (before) him, and strip malak (king) of their armor; to pathach (open) the dalath (doors) panayam (before) him, and the dalath (gates) shall not be sagar (shut):

I will yalak (go) panayam (before) you, and yashar (make) the rough hadar (places) smooth. I will break the dalath (doors) of nachawashah (brass) in shabar (pieces), and gadai (cut) apart the barayach (bars) of barazal (iron).

I will nathan (give) you the awatzar (treasures) of chashak (darkness), and matamawan (hidden) riches of masathar (secret) places, that you may yadai (know) that it is I, Yahawah, who qaraa (called) you by your sham (name), even the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).

For Yaiqab (Jacob) my ibad (servant) sake, and Yasharaal (Israel) my bachayar (chosen), I have qaraa (called) you by your sham (name). I have kanah (surnamed) you, though you yadai (have) not known me.
I am Yahawah, and there is none else. Zawalah (besides) me, there is no Alahayam. I will strengthen you, though you yadai (have) not known me;
That they may yadai (know) from the mazarach (rising) of the shamash (sun), and from the mairab (west), that there is apas (none) balaiday (besides) me. I am Yahawah, and there is no one else.

I yatzar (form) the awar (light), and baraa (created) chashak (darkness). I ishah (make) shalawam (peace / safety), and baraa (created) rai (calamity). I am Yahawah, who ishah (make) all these things.

Raip (distil), you shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), from mail (top/above), and let the shachaq (skies) nazal (pour) down tzadaq (righteous / just / fair). Let the aratz (Earth/land) pathach (open), that it may parah (bring) forth yashai (salvation), and let it cause tzadaqah (righteousness) to tzamach (spring) up with it. I, Yahawah, have baraa (created) it.

Haway (Alas/Woe!) To him who rayab (strives) with his yatzar (maker)— a clay pot among the clay pots of the adamah (earth)! Shall the chamar (clay) ask him who yatzar (fashions) it, ‘What are you ishah (make)?’ Or your pail (work), ‘He has no yad (hand)?’
Haway (Alas/Woe!) To him who amar (spoke) to a ab (father), ‘What have you become the yalad (birth / begot) of?’ Or to a ashah (wife/individual woman), ‘To what have you given birth?’

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel), and his yatzar (maker): “You shaal (ask) me about the things that are to athah (come), concerning my ban (son), and you tzawah (command) me concerning the pail (work) of my yad (hand)!

I ishah (make) made the aratz (Earth/land), and baraa (created) adam (man) on it. I, even my yad (hand), have natah (stretched) out the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)); and I have tzawah (commanded) all their tzabaa (troop).

I have iwar (rouse / awaken) him up in tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and I will make yashar (straight) all his darak (ways). He shall banah (build) my iyar (city), and he shall let my exiles shalach (send) free, not for machayar (price) nor shachad (reward),” amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaa (troop).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: The yagayai (labor) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and the sachar (merchandise) of Kawash (Ethiopia), and the Sabaay (Sabeans), ayash (husband/individual man) of madah (stature), shall ibar (pass over/through) over to you, and they shall be yours. They will yalak (go) achar (other) you. They shall ibar (pass over/through) over in zayaqah (chains); and they will shachah (bow) down to you. They will palal (make) supplication to you: ‘Surely Alahayam is in you; and there is apas (none) else. There is no other Alahayam.
Most akan (certainly) you are a Al who sathar (hidden) yourself, Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), the Savior.’
They will be disappointed, yes, kalam (confounded), all of them. Those who are charash (makers) of tzayar (idols) will halak (move) into kalamah (confusion) yachad (together).
Yasharaal (Israel) will be yashai (salvation) by Yahawah with an iwalam (forever) thashawaih (deliverance). You will not be disappointed nor bawash (confounded) to ages id (everlasting).

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah who baraa (created) the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), the Alahayam who yatzar (formed) the aratz (Earth/land) and ishah (make) it, who kawan (established) it and didn't baraa (created) it a thahaw (formless), who yatzar (formed) it to be yashab (inhabit/dwell): I am Yahawah; and there is no other.

I have not dabar (word / matter) in sathar (secret / hidden), in a maqawam (place) of the aratz (Earth/land) of chashak (darkness). I didn't amar (spoke) to the zarai (seed) of Yaiqab (Jacob), ‘baqash (seek) me in thahaw (formless).’ I, Yahawah, dabar (word / matter) tzadaq (righteous / just / fair). I nagad (declare) things that are mayashar (right).

Qabatz (assemble) yourselves and bawaa (come). Nagash (draw) near yachad (together), you who have palayat (escaped) from the gaway (nation / people). Those have no yadai (knowledge) who nashaa (lift) the itz (wood) of their engraved pasal (idol/graven image), and palal (pray) to a Al that can't yashai (salvation).

Nagad (declare) and nagash (present) it. Yes, let them take yaitz (counsel) yachad (together). Who has shown this from qadam (ancient) time? Who has nagad (declared) it of old? Haven't I, Yahawah? There is no other Alahayam balaiday (besides) me, a tzadayaq (righteous) Al and a Savior; There is no ayan (one) zawalah (besides) me.
"Panah (look) to me, and be yashai (salvation), all the apas (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land); for I am Al, and there is no other.

I have shabai (swear / take oath) by myself, the dabar (word / matter) yatzaa (go out / come out) gone out of my pah (mouth) in tzadaqah (righteousness), and will not shawab (turn back / repent), that to me every barak (knee) shall karai (bow), every lashawan (tongue/language) shall take an shabai (swear / take oath).

They will amar (spoke) of me, ‘There is tzadaqah (righteousness) and iz (strength / might / refuge) only in Yahawah.’" Even to him shall men bawaa (come); and all those who were charah (hot with anger) against him shall be disappointed.
In Yahawah shall all the zarai (seed) of Yasharaal (Israel) be justified, and shall glory.

Bal (Bel) karai (bows) down, Nabaw (Nebo) qaras (stoops); their itzab (idols) are on the animals, and on the livestock: the things that you carried about are made a imas (load), a mashaa (burden) to the iyap (weary).
They qaras (stoop), they karai (bow) down yachad (together); they yakal (could) not malat (deliver) the mashaa (burden), but themselves have halak (move) into shabay (captivity).

Shamai (hearken / hear) to me, bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and all the shaarayath (remnant) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), that have been imas (borne) from their birth, that have been nashaa (lift) from the racham (womb);

And even to zaqanah (old) age I am he, and even to shayabah (old age / white hair (due to age)) hairs will I sabal (carry) you. I ishah (make) made, and I will nashaa (lift); yes, I will sabal (carry), and will malat (deliver).
To whom will you damah (liken) me, and shawah (make) me equal, and mashal (speak in proverb/parable) me, that we may be damah (like)?

Some pour out zahab (gold) from the kayas (bag), and shaqal (weigh) kasap (silver) in the qanah (balance). They shakar (hire) a tzarap (goldsmith), and he ishah (make) it a Al. They sagad (fall) down—yes, they shachah (worship).

They nashaa (lift) it on the kathap (shoulder), they sabal (carry) it, and yanach (set) it in its place, and it imad (stands), from its maqawam (place) it shall not move: yes, one may tzaiq (cry) to it, yet it can not inah (answer / respond), nor yashai (salvation) him out of his tzarah (trouble).
Zakar (remembrance/memory) this, and ayash (husband/individual man) yourselves men; shawab (turn back / repent) it again to lab (heart), you transgressors.
Zakar (remembrance/memory) the raashawan (former) things of iwalam (forever): for I am Al, and there is none else; I am Alahayam, and there is apas (none) kamaw (like) me;

Nagad (declaring) the acharayath (end) from the raashayath (beginning), and from qadam (ancient) times things that are not yet ishah (make); amar (spoke), My itzah (counsel) shall qawam (rise up), and I will ishah (make) all my chapatz (pleasure);

Qaraa (called) a iyat (ravenous) bird from the mazarach (east), the ayash (husband/individual man) of my itzah (counsel) from a marachaq (far) aratz (Earth/land); yes, I have dabar (word / matter), I will also bawaa (come) it to pass; I have yatzar (purposed), I will also ishah (make) it.
Shamai (hearken / hear) to me, you abayar (stout-hearted), who are rachawaq (far) from tzadaqah (righteousness):

I qarab (come close) near my tzadaqah (righteousness), it shall not be rachaq (far) off, and my thashawaih (deliverance) shall not wait; and I will nathan (give) thashawaih (deliverance) in Tzayawan (Zion) for Yasharaal (Israel) my glory.

Yarad (come) down, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the ipar (dust), bathawalah (virgin) bath (daughter) of Babal (Babylon); yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the aratz (Earth/land) without a kasaa (throne), bath (daughter) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans): for you shall no more be qaraa (called) rak (tender) and inag (delicate).

Laqach (take / seized) the millstones, and tachan (grind) qamach (meal); galah (remove) your tzamah (veil), strip off the train, galah (uncover) the shawaq (leg), ibar (pass over/through) through the nahar (rivers).
Your irawah (nakedness) shall be galah (uncovered), yes, your charapah (shame) shall be raah (see): I will laqach (take / seized) naqam (vengeance), and will spare no adam (man).
Our gaal (redeemer), Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) is his sham (name), the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).

Yashab (inhabit/dwell) in silence, and bawaa (come) into chashak (darkness), bath (daughter) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans); for you shall no more be qaraa (called) the gabarath (mistress) of mamalakah (kingdoms).

I was qatzap (angry) with my im (people / nation), I chalal (profaned) my nachalah (inheritance), and nathan (give) them into your yad (hand): you showed them no racham (mercy); on the zaqan (aged) you have very kabad (heavily) laid your il (over).

You amar (spoke), ‘I shall be a gabarath (mistress) iwalam (forever);’ so that you shawam (place / establish / appoint) not lay these things to your lab (heart), nor did you zakar (remembrance/memory) the acharayath (latter) end of it.

Now therefore shamai (hearken / hear) this, you who are idayan (given) to pleasures, who yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely, who amar (spoke) in your labab (heart), ‘I am, and there is apas (none) else besides me; I shall not yashab (inhabit/dwell) as a alamanah (widow), neither shall I yadai (know) the shakawal (loss) of children:’

But these shanayam (two) things shall bawaa (come) to you in a ragai (in an instance) in achad (one) yawam (day), the shakawal (loss) of children, and alaman (widowhood); in their tham (full) measure shall they bawaa (come) on you, in the rab (multitude) of your kashap (sorceries), and the maad (great) itzamah (abundance) of your chabar (enchantments).

For you have batach (trusted) in your rai (wickedness); you have amar (spoke), No one raah (see) me; your chakamah (wisdom) and your daith (knowledge), it has shawab (turn back / repent) you, and you have amar (spoke) in your lab (heart), I am, and there is apas (none) else besides me.

Therefore rai (evil) will bawaa (come) on you; you won't yadai (know) when it dawns: and hawah (calamity/destruction) will napal (fall / be cast down) on you; you will not be yakal (able) to kapar (put) it away: and shawaa (vanity) shall bawaa (come) on you pathaawam (suddenly), which you don't yadai (know).

Imad (stand) now with your chabar (enchantments), and with the rab (multitude) of your kashap (sorceries), in which you have labored from your naiwar (youth); if so be you shall be yakal (able) to yail (profit), if so be you may iratz (prevail).

You are laah (wearied) in the rab (multitude) of your itzah (counsels): let now the habar (astrologers), the chazah (stargazers), the chadash (month) yadai (prognosticators), imad (stand) up, and yashai (salvation) you from the things that shall bawaa (come) on you.

Behold, they shall be as qash (stubble); the ash (fire) shall sharap (burn) them; they shall not natzal (deliver) themselves from the yad (hand) of the lahabah (flame): it shall not be a gachal (coal) to chamam (warm) at, nor a awar (light) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) before.

Thus shall the things be to you in which you have labored: those who have sachar (trafficked) with you from your naiwar (youth) shall thaih (wander) everyone to his ibar (quarter); there shall be none to yashai (salvation) you.

Shamai (hearken / hear) this, bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob), you who are qaraa (called) by the sham (name) of Yasharaal (Israel), and yatzaa (go out / come out) come forth out of the mayam (Waters) of Yahawadah (Judah); who shabai (swear / take oath) by the sham (name) of Yahawah, and zakar (remembrance/memory) mention of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), but not in amath (truth), nor in tzadaqah (righteousness)
(For they qaraa (called) themselves of the qadash (set apart/make holy) iyar (city), and samak (stay) themselves on the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel); Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) is his sham (name)):

I have nagad (declared) the raashawan (former) things from of az (old); yes, they yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of my pah (mouth), and I showed them: pathaawam (suddenly) I ishah (make) them, and they happened.
Because I daith (knew) that you are qashah (rough / hard), and your irap (neck) is an barazal (iron) gayad (sinew), and your matzach (brow) nachawashah (brass);

Therefore I have nagad (declared) it to you from of az (old); before it bawaa (come) to pass I showed it to you; lest you should amar (spoke), ‘My itzab (idol) ishah (make) done them, and my engraved pasal (idol/graven image), and my molten nasak (image), has tzawah (commanded) them.’

You have shamai (hearken / hear) it; chazah (see) all this; and you, will you not nagad (declare) it? I have shown you new things from ithah (now / present moment) time, even natzar (hidden) things, which you yadai (have) not known.
They are baraa (created) now, and not from of panayam (old); and before this yawam (day) you didn't shamai (hearken / hear) them; lest you should amar (spoke), ‘Behold, I yadai (knew) them.’

Yes, you didn't shamai (hearken / hear); yes, you didn't yadai (know); yes, from of old your azan (ear) was not pathach (opened): for I yadai (knew) that you dealt very bagad (treacherously), and was qaraa (called) a transgressor from the batan (womb).
For my sham (name) sake will I arak (defer) my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and for my thahalah (praise) will I chatam (refrain) for you, that I not karath (cut) you off.
Behold, I have tzarap (refined) you, but not as kasap (silver); I have bachar (chosen) you in the kawar (furnace) of inay (affliction).
For my own sake, for my own sake, will I ishah (make) it; for how should my name be chalal (profaned)? I will not nathan (give) my kabawad (glory) to achar (other).
Shamai (hearken / hear) to me, O Yaiqab (Jacob), and Yasharaal (Israel) my qaraa (called): I am he; I am the raashawan (first), I also am the acharawan (last).

Yes, my yad (hand) has yasad (laid) the foundation of the aratz (Earth/land), and my right yamayan (right hand) has spread out the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)): when I qaraa (called) to them, they imad (stand) up yachad (together).

Qabatz (assemble) yourselves, all you, and shamai (hearken / hear); who among them has nagad (declared) these things? He whom Yahawah ahab (love) shall ishah (make) his chapatz (pleasure) on Babal (Babylon), and his zarawai (arm) shall be on the Kashaday (Chaldeans).
I, even I, have dabar (word / matter); yes, I have qaraa (called) him; I bawaa (come) brought him, and he shall make his darak (way) prosperous.

Qarab (come close) qarab (come close) to me and shamai (hearken / hear) this: "From the raash (head) I have not dabar (word / matter) in sathar (secret / hidden); from the ith (time) that it was, there am I." Now the Adanay Yahawah has shalach (send) me, with his rawach (spirit / wind).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, your gaal (redeemer), the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel): I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who teaches you to yail (profit), who darak (leads) you by the darak (way) that you should yalak (go).

Oh that you had listened to my matzawah (commandments)! Then your shalawam (peace / safety) would have been like a nahar (river), and your tzadaqah (righteousness) like the gal (waves) of the yam (sea/waters):
Your zarai (seed) also had been as the chawal (sand), and the tzaatzaa (offspring) of your body like its grains: his sham (name) would not be karath (cut) off nor destroyed from panayam (before) me.

Yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from Babal (Babylon), barach (flee) from the Kashaday (Chaldeans); with a qawal (sound / voice) of ranah (singing) nagad (declare), shamai (hearken / hear) this, yatzaa (go out / come out) it even to the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land): amar (spoke), Yahawah has gaal (redeemed) his ibad (servant) Yaiqab (Jacob).

They didn't tzamaa (thirst) when he yalak (led) them through the deserts; he caused the mayam (Waters) to nazal (flow) out of the tzawar (rock) for them; he split the tzawar (rock) also, and the mayam (Waters) zawab (flow) out.
"There is no shalawam (peace / safety)," amar (spoke) Yahawah, for the rashai (wicked).

Shamai (hearken / hear), ay (islands), to me; and listen, you laam (peoples), from rachawaq (far): Yahawah has qaraa (called) me from the batan (womb); from the maih (bowels) of my am (mother) has he zakar (remembrance/memory) mention of my sham (name):

And he has shawam (place / establish / appoint) my pah (mouth) like a chad (sharp) charab (sword); in the tzal (shadow) of his yad (hand), he has chabaa (hidden) me: and he has shawam (place / establish / appoint) me a barar (polished) chatz (shaft); in his ashapah (quiver) has he sathar (kept) me close:
And he amar (spoke) to me, You are my ibad (servant); Yasharaal (Israel), in whom I will be paar (glorified).

But I amar (spoke), I have labored in rayaq (vain), I kalah (complete / finish) spent my kach (strength / mighty / power) for thahaw (formless) and habal (vanity); yet akan (surely) the mashapat (justice) due to me is with Yahawah, and my pailah (reward) with my Alahayam.

Now amar (spoke) Yahawah who yatzar (formed) me from the batan (womb) to be his ibad (servant), to shawab (turn back / repent) Yaiqab (Jacob) again to him, and that Yasharaal (Israel) be asap (gathered) to him (for I am honorable in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, and my Alahayam has become my iz (strength / might / refuge));

Yes, he amar (spoke), It is too qalal (light) a thing that you should be my ibad (servant) to qawam (rise up) up the shabat (tribes) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and to shawab (turn back / repent) the natzayar (preserved) of Yasharaal (Israel): I will also nathan (give) you for a awar (light) to the gaway (nation / people), that you may be my yashawaih (salvation) to the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the gaal (redeemer) of Yasharaal (Israel), and his qadawash (holy) One, to him whom napash (living being/soul) bazah (despises), to him whom the gaway (nation / people) thaib (abhors), to a ibad (servant) of mashal (rule/have dominion): malak (king) shall raah (see) and qawam (rise up); shar (prince / ruler), and they shall shachah (worship); because of Yahawah who is aman (believe / have faith), even the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel), who has bachar (chosen) you.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, In an ratzawan (acceptable) ith (time) have I inah (answer / respond) you, and in a yawam (day) of yashawaih (salvation) have I izar (helped) you; and I will natzar (preserve) you, and nathan (give) you for a barayath (covenant) of the im (people / nation), to qawam (rise up) up the aratz (Earth/land), to nachal (make) them inherit the shamam (desolate) nachalah (heritage):

Amar (spoke) to those who are asar (bound), ‘yatzaa (go out / come out) out!’; to those who are in chashak (darkness), ‘Show yourselves!’ They shall raih (feed) in the darak (ways), and on all bare heights shall be their maraiyath (pasture).

They shall not raib (hunger) nor tzamaa (thirst); neither shall the sharab (heat) nor shamash (sun) nakah (strike) them: for he who has racham (mercy) on them will nahag (lead) them, even by mabawai (springs) of mayam (Waters) he will nahal (guide) them.
I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) all my har (mountain) a darak (way), and my masalah (highways) shall be rawam (will lift up).
Behold, these shall bawaa (come) from rachawaq (far); and behold, these from the tzapawan (north) and from the yam (sea/waters); and these from the aratz (Earth/land) of Sayanayam (Sinim).

Ranan (sing), shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)); and be gayal (joyful), aratz (Earth/land); and patzach (break) forth into ranah (singing), har (mountain): for Yahawah has nacham (turn away / repent) his im (people / nation), and will racham (have) compassion on his inay (afflicted).
But Tzayawan (Zion) amar (spoke), Yahawah has forsaken me, and the Adawan has shakach (forgotten) me.

“Can a ashah (wife/individual woman) shakach (forget) her nursing iwal (child), that she should not racham (have) compassion on the ban (son) of her batan (womb)? Yes, these may shakach (forget), yet I will not shakach (forget) you!
Behold, I have engraved you on the palms of my kap (hands); your chawamah (walls) are continually before me.
Your ban (son) mahar (make) haste; your destroyers and those who charab (made) you waste shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from you.

Nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye) all around, and raah (see): all these qabatz (gather) themselves together, and bawaa (come) to you. As I chay (life),” naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, you shall surely labash (clothe) yourself with them all as with an iday (ornament / adornment), and dress yourself with them, like a kalah (complete / finish).

For, as for your charabah (waste) and your shamam (desolate) places, and your aratz (Earth/land) that has been destroyed, surely now you shall be too small for the yashab (inhabit/dwell), and those who balai (swallowed) you up shall be rachaq (far) away.

The ban (son) of your bereavement shall yet amar (spoke) in your azan (ears), The maqawam (place) is too tzar (oppressor / distressor) for me; nagash (give) maqawam (place) to me that I may yashab (inhabit/dwell).

Then you will amar (spoke) in your labab (heart), ‘Who has conceived these for me, since I have been shakal (bereaved) of my children, and am galamawad (solitary), an galah (exile), and wandering sawar (back) and forth? Who has gadal (brought) up these? Behold, I was shaar (left) alone; these, ayapah (where) were they?’

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, Behold, I will nashaa (lift) up my yad (hand) to the gaway (nation / people), and rawam (will lift up) up my nas (banner) to the im (people / nation); and they shall bawaa (come) your ban (son) in their bosom, and your bath (daughter) shall be nashaa (lift) on their kathap (shoulders).

Malak (king) shall be your aman (believe / have faith) fathers, and their sharah (queens) your yanaq (nursing) mothers: they shall shachah (bow) down to you with their ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land), and lachak (lick) the ipar (dust) of your ragal (feet / foot); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah; and those who qawah (gather/wait) for me shall not be disappointed.
Shall the malaqawach (prey) be laqach (take / seized) from the gabawar (mighty), or the tzadayaq (righteous) shabay (captives) be malat (delivered)?

But thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, Even the shabay (captives) of the gabawar (mighty) shall be laqach (take / seized) away, and the malaqawach (prey) of the irayatz (terrible) shall be malat (delivered); for I will rayab (contend) with him who rayab (contends) with you, and I will yashai (salvation) your ban (son).

I will akal (eat) those who yanah (oppress) you with their own bashar (flesh); and they shall be shakar (drunken) with their own dam (blood), as with sweet isayas (wine): and all bashar (flesh) shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, am your Savior, and your gaal (redeemer), the abayar (mighty) One of Yaiqab (Jacob).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, Where is the sapar (book / scribed document) of your am (mother) karayathawath (divorce), with which I have shalach (send) her away? Or which of my nashah (creditors) is it to whom I have makar (sold) you? Behold, for your iwan (guilt/iniquity) were you makar (sold), and for your pashai (transgressions) was your am (mother) shalach (send) away.

Why, when I bawaa (come), was there no ayash (husband/individual man)? When I qaraa (called), was there none to inah (answer / respond)? Is my yad (hand) shortened at qatzar (all), that it can't padawath (redeem)? Or have I no kach (strength / mighty / power) to natzal (deliver)? Behold, at my gairah (rebuke) I charab (dry) up the yam (sea/waters), I shawam (place / establish / appoint) the nahar (rivers) a madabar (wilderness): their dagah (fish) baash (stink), because there is no mayam (Waters), and mawath (death) for tzamaa (thirst).
I labash (clothe) the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) with qadarawath (blackness), and I shawam (place / establish / appoint) sackcloth their kasawath (covering).

The Adanay Yahawah nathan (give) given me the lashawan (tongue/language) of those who are lamawad (taught), that I may yadai (know) how to sustain with dabar (word / matter) him who is yaip (weary): he wakens baqar (morning) by baqar (morning), he wakens my azan (ear) to shamai (hearken / hear) as those who are lamawad (taught).
The Adanay Yahawah pathach (has) opened my azan (ear), and I was not rebellious, neither sawag (turned) away backward.
I nathan (give) my gaw (back) to the strikers, and my lachay (cheeks) to those who marat (plucked) off the hair; I didn't sathar (hide) my panayam (face) from kalamah (shame) and raq (spitting).

For the Adanay Yahawah will izar (help) me; therefore I have not been kalam (confounded): therefore have I shawam (place / establish / appoint) my panayam (face) like a chalamayash (flint), and I yadai (know) that I shall not be disappointed.
He is qarawab (near) who justifies me; who will bring charges against me? Let us imad (stand) up yachad (together): who is my bail (adversary)? Let him nagash (come) near to me.
Behold, the Adanay Yahawah will izar (help) me; who is he who shall rashai (condemn) me? Behold, all they shall balah (wax) old as a bagad (garment), the ish (made) shall akal (eat) them up.

Who is among you who yaraa (fears) Yahawah, who shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of his ibad (servant)? He who halak (move) in chashakah (darkness), and has no nagah (light), let him batach (trust) in the sham (name) of Yahawah, and shain (rely) on his Alahayam.

Behold, all you who qadach (kindle) a ash (fire), who adorn yourselves with torches around yourselves; yalak (walk) in the awar (light) of your ash (fire), and among the brands that you have bair (kindled). You shall have this of my yad (hand); you shall shakab (lie) down in maitzabah (sorrow).

Shamai (hearken / hear) to me, you who radap (follow) after tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), you who baqash (seek) Yahawah: nabat (look) to the tzawar (rock) you were chatzab (cut) from, and to the hold of the bawar (pit) you were naqar (dug) from.

Nabat (look) to Abaraham (Abraham) your ab (father), and to Sharah (Sarah) who chawal (bore) you; for when he was but achad (one) I qaraa (called) him, and I barak (blessed) him, and rabah (made) him many.

For Yahawah has nacham (turn away / repent) Tzayawan (Zion); he has nacham (turn away / repent) all her charabah (waste) places, and has shawam (place / establish / appoint) her madabar (wilderness) like Idan (Eden), and her irabah (desert) like the gan (garden) of Yahawah; shashawan (joy) and shamachah (gladness) shall be matzaa (found) therein, thanksgiving, and the qawal (sound / voice) of zamarah (melody).

Qashab (attend) to me, my im (people / nation); and azan (give) ear to me, my laam (nation): for a thawarah (instruction) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from me, and I will establish my mashapat (justice) for a awar (light) of the im (people / nation).

My tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) is qarawab (near), my yashai (salvation) is yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and my zarawai (arms) shall shapat (judge) the im (people / nation); the ay (islands) shall qawah (gather/wait) for me, and on my zarawai (arm) shall they yachal (trust).

Nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye) to the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), and nabat (look) on the aratz (Earth/land) beneath; for the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) shall malach (vanish) away like ishan (smoke), and the aratz (Earth/land) shall balah (wax) old like a bagad (garment); and those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein shall mawath (death) in the same kan (for sure): but my yashawaih (salvation) shall be iwalam (forever), and my tzadaqah (righteousness) shall not be chathath (abolished).

Shamai (hearken / hear) to me, you who yadai (know) tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), the im (people / nation) in whose lab (heart) is my thawarah (instruction); don't yaraa (fear / be afraid) the charapah (reproach) of anawash (men), neither be chathath (dismayed) at their insults.

For the ish (made) shall akal (eat) them up like a bagad (garment), and the worm shall akal (eat) them like tzamar (wool); but my tzadaqah (righteousness) shall be iwalam (forever), and my yashawaih (salvation) to all dawar (generation / age / period).

Iwar (rouse / awaken), iwar (rouse / awaken), labash (put) on iz (strength / might / refuge), zarawai (arm) of Yahawah; iwar (rouse / awaken), as in the yawam (day) of iwalam (forever), the dawar (generation / age / period) of qadam (ancient) times. Isn't it you who chatzab (cut) Rahab (Rahab) in pieces, who pierced the thanayan (monster)?

Isn't it you who charab (dried) up the yam (sea/waters), the mayam (Waters) of the rab (great) thahawam (depths); who shawam (place / establish / appoint) the maimaq (depths) of the yam (sea/waters) a darak (way) for the gaal (redeemed) to ibar (pass over/through) over?

The padah (ransomed) of Yahawah shall shawab (turn back / repent), and bawaa (come) with ranah (singing) to Tzayawan (Zion); and iwalam (forever) shamachah (joy) shall be on their raash (head). They shall obtain shashawan (gladness) and shamachah (joy). Yagawan (sorrow) and anachah (sighing) shall nawas (flee) away.

I, even I, am he who nacham (turn away / repent) you: who are you, that you are yaraa (fear / be afraid) of anawash (man) who shall mawath (death), and of the ban (son) of adam (man) who shall be nathan (give) as chatzayar (grass);

And have shakach (forgotten) Yahawah your Maker, who natah (stretched) forth the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), and yasad (laid) the foundations of the aratz (Earth/land); and pachad (fear / dread) continually all the yawam (day) panayam (because) of the fury of the oppressor, when he kawan (makes) ready to shachath (destroy)? And where is the fury of the oppressor?
The tzaih (captive) exile shall mahar (speedily) be pathach (freed); and he shall not mawath (death) and go down into the shachath (pit), neither shall his lacham (bread) chasar (fail).
For I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who stirs up the yam (sea/waters), so that its gal (waves) hamah (they): Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) is his sham (name).

I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) my dabar (word / matter) in your pah (mouth), and have kasah (covered) you in the tzal (shadow) of my yad (hand), that I may natai (plant) the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), and yasad (lay) the foundations of the aratz (Earth/land), and amar (spoke) Tzayawan (Zion), ‘You are my im (people / nation).’

Iwar (rouse / awaken), iwar (rouse / awaken), qawam (rise up) up, Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), that have shathah (drinks) at the yad (hand) of Yahawah the kawas (cup) of his chamah (wrath); you have shathah (drinks) the bowl of the kawas (cup) of staggering, and drained it.

There is none to nahal (guide) her among all the ban (son) whom she has yalad (birth / begot) forth; neither is there any who chazaq (takes) her by the yad (hand) among all the ban (son) who she has gadal (brought) up.

These shanayam (two) things have qaraa (called) to you. Who will nawad (bemoan) you? Shad (desolation) and shabar (destruction), and the raib (famine) and the charab (sword); how shall I nacham (turn away / repent) you?

Your ban (son) have ilap (fainted), they shakab (lie) at the raash (head) of all the chawatz (streets), as an antelope in a makamar (net); they are malaa (full) of the chamah (wrath) of Yahawah, the gairah (rebuke) of your Alahayam.
Therefore shamai (hearken / hear) now this, you inay (afflicted), and shakar (drunken), but not with yayan (wine):

Thus amar (spoke) your Adawan Yahawah, and your Alahayam who rayab (pleads) the cause of his im (people / nation), Behold, I have laqach (take / seized) out of your yad (hand) the kawas (cup) of staggering, even the bowl of the kawas (cup) of my chamah (wrath); you shall no more shathah (drinks) it again:

And I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) it into the yad (hand) of those who yagah (afflict) you, who have amar (spoke) to your napash (living being/soul), ‘shachah (bow) down, that we may walk over you;’ and you have shawam (place / establish / appoint) your gaw (back) as the aratz (Earth/land), and as the chawatz (street), to those who walk over.

Iwar (rouse / awaken), iwar (rouse / awaken), labash (put) on your iz (strength / might / refuge), Tzayawan (Zion); labash (put) on your thapaarah (beautiful) bagad (garments), Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), the qadash (set apart/make holy) iyar (city): for yasap (henceforth) there shall no more bawaa (come) into you the iral (uncircumcised) and the tamaa (unclean).

Nair (shake) yourself from the ipar (dust)! Qawam (rise up), yashab (inhabit/dwell) up, Yarawashalam (Jerusalem)! Release yourself from the mawasar (bonds) of your tzawaar (neck), shabay (captive) bath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion)!
For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, You were makar (sold) for chanam (nothing); and you shall be gaal (redeemed) without kasap (money).

For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, My im (people / nation) yarad (went) down at the raashawan (first) into Matzarayam (Egypt) to live there: and the Ashawar (Assyrian) has ishaq (oppressed) them apas (without) cause.

"Now therefore, what do I do here," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, "seeing that my im (people / nation) are laqach (take / seized) away for chanam (nothing)? Those who mashal (rule/have dominion) over them mock," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, and my sham (name) continually all the yawam (day) is naatz (blasphemed).
Therefore my im (people / nation) shall yadai (know) my sham (name). Therefore they shall know in that yawam (day) that I am he who dabar (word / matter); behold, it is I.

How naah (beautiful) on the har (mountain) are the ragal (feet / foot) of him who brings bashar (good) news, who publishes shalawam (peace / safety), who brings bashar (good) news of tawab (pleasant/functional), who publishes yashawaih (salvation), who amar (spoke) to Tzayawan (Zion), Your Alahayam malak (king)!

The qawal (sound / voice) of your watchmen! They nashaa (lift) up the qawal (sound / voice), yachad (together) do they ranan (sing); for they shall raah (see) iyan (eye) to iyan (eye), when Yahawah shawab (turn back / repent) to Tzayawan (Zion).

Patzach (break) forth into joy, ranan (sing) yachad (together), you charabah (waste) places of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); for Yahawah has nacham (turn away / repent) his im (people / nation), he has gaal (redeemed) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

Yahawah has chashap (made) bare his qadash (set apart/make holy) zarawai (arm) in the iyan (eye) of all the gaway (nation / people); and all the apas (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land) raah (see) seen the yashawaih (salvation) of our Alahayam.

Sawar (depart), sawar (depart), yatzaa (go out / come out) out from there, nagai (touch) no tamaa (unclean) thing! Yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the thawak (midst) of her! Barar (cleanse) yourselves, you who nashaa (lift) the kalay (vessels) of Yahawah.

For you shall not yatzaa (go out / come out) out in chapazawan (haste), neither shall you halak (move) by manawasah (flight): for Yahawah will halak (move) panayam (before) you; and the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) will be your rear guard.
Behold, my ibad (servant) shall deal shakal (wisely), he shall be rawam (will lift up) and nashaa (lift) up, and shall be very gabah (high).

Like as many were shamam (astonished) at you (his maraah (appearance) was mashachath (marred) more than any ayash (husband/individual man), and his thaar (form) more than the ban (son) of adam (men)),

So shall he nazah (sprinkle) many gaway (nation / people); malak (king) shall qapatz (shut) their pah (mouths) at him: for that which had not been sapar (book) them shall they raah (see); and that which they had not shamai (hearken / hear) shall they bayan (between).
Who has aman (believe / have faith) our message? To whom has the zarawai (arm) of Yahawah been galah (revealed)?

For he ilah (go up / offer) up panayam (before) him as a yawanaq (tender) plant, and as a sharash (root) out of tzayah (dry) aratz (Earth/land). He has no thaar (good) looks or hadar (glory / majesty / splendor). When we raah (see) him, there is no beauty that we should chamad (desire) him.

He was bazah (despised), and chadal (rejected) by ayash (husband/individual man); a ayash (husband/individual man) of suffering, and acquainted with chalay (disease). He was bazah (despised) as one from whom men hide their panayam (face); and we didn't respect him.
Akan (surely) he has nashaa (lift) our chalay (sickness), and sabal (carried) our suffering; yet we chashab (considered) him nagai (plagued), nakah (struck) by Alahayam, and inah (oppress / afflict).

But he was pierced for our pashai (transgressions). He was dakaa (crushed) for our iwan (guilt/iniquity). The punishment that brought our shalawam (peace / safety) was on him; and by his chabawarah (wounds) we are rapaa (healed).
All we like tzaan (sheep) have thaih (gone) astray. Everyone has panah (turned) to his own darak (way); and Yahawah has pagai (laid) on him the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of us all.

He was nagash (oppressed), yet when he was inah (oppress / afflict) he didn't pathach (open) his pah (mouth). As a shah (lamb) that is yabal (led) to the tabach (slaughter), and as a rachal (sheep) that panayam (before) its gazaz (shearers) is mute, so he didn't pathach (open) his pah (mouth).

He was laqach (take / seized) away by itzar (oppression) and mashapat (judgment); and as for his dawar (generation / age / period), who considered that he was gazar (cut) off out of the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life) and nagai (stricken) for the disobedience of my im (people / nation)?

They nathan (give) his qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) with the rashai (wicked), and with a ishayar (rich) man in his mawath (death); although he ishah (make) done no chamas (violence), neither was any maramah (deceit) in his pah (mouth).

Yet it chapatz (pleased) Yahawah to dakaa (bruise) him. He has caused him to suffer. When you shawam (place / establish / appoint) his napash (living being/soul) an offering for asham (sin), he shall raah (see) his zarai (seed). He shall prolong his yawam (day), and the chapatz (pleasure) of Yahawah shall tzalach (prosper) in his yad (hand).

After the suffering of his napash (living being/soul), he will raah (see) the light and be shabai (satisfied). My tzadayaq (righteous) ibad (servant) will justify many by the daith (knowledge) of himself; and he will sabal (bear) their iwan (guilt/iniquity).

Therefore will I chalaq (divide) him a portion with the rab (great), and he shall chalaq (divide) the shalal (spoil) with the itzawam (strong); because he irah (poured) out his napash (living being/soul) to mawath (death), and was manah (numbered) with the transgressors; yet he nashaa (lift) the chataa (sin) of many, and pagai (made) intercession for the transgressors.

"Ranan (sing), iqar (barren), you who didn't yalad (birth / begot); patzach (break) forth into ranah (singing), and tzahal (cry) aloud, you who did not chawal (travail) with child: for more are the ban (son) of the shamam (desolate) than the ban (son) of the bail (married) wife," amar (spoke) Yahawah.

Enlarge the maqawam (place) of your ahal (tent), and natah (let) them stretch forth the yarayaih (curtains) of your mashakan (habitations); don't chashak (darkness): arak (lengthen) your mayathar (cords), and chazaq (strengthen) your yathad (stakes).

For you shall spread out on the right yamayan (right hand) and on the shamaawal (left hand); and your zarai (seed) shall yarash (possess) the gaway (nation / people), and shamam (make) the desolate iyar (cities) to be yashab (inhabit/dwell).

“Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid); for you shall not be bawash (ashamed): neither be kalam (confounded); for you shall not be disappointed: for you shall shakach (forget) the chapar (shame) of your ilawam (youth); and the charapah (reproach) of your alamanawath (widowhood) you shall zakar (remembrance/memory) no more.

For your Maker is your bail (husband); Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) is his sham (name): and the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel) is your gaal (redeemer); the Alahayam of the whole aratz (Earth/land) shall he be qaraa (called).

For Yahawah has qaraa (called) you as a ashah (wife/individual woman) forsaken and itzab (grieved) in rawach (spirit / wind), even a ashah (wife/individual woman) of naiwar (youth), when she is maas (cast) off,” amar (spoke) your Alahayam.
"For a qatan (small/young/least) ragai (in an instance) have I forsaken you; but with gadawal (very great/important/mighty) racham (mercies) will I qabatz (gather) you.

In overflowing qatzap (wrath) I sathar (hid) my panayam (face) from you for a ragai (in an instance); but with iwalam (forever) loving chasad (grace) will I have racham (mercy) on you," amar (spoke) Yahawah your gaal (redeemer).

"For this is like the mayam (Waters) of Nach (Noah) to me; for as I have shabai (swear / take oath) that the mayam (Waters) of Nach (Noah) shall no more ibar (pass over/through) over the aratz (Earth/land), so have I shabai (swear / take oath) that I will not be qatzap (angry) with you, nor gair (rebuke) you.

For the har (mountain) may depart, and the gabaih (hills) be mawat (removed); but my loving chasad (grace) shall not depart from you, neither shall my barayath (covenant) of shalawam (peace / safety) be mawat (removed)," amar (spoke) Yahawah who has racham (mercy) on you.

You inay (afflicted), tossed with storms, and not nacham (turn away / repent), behold, I will set your aban (stone) in beautiful colors, and rabatz (lay) your yasad (foundations) with sapayar (sapphires).
I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) your pinnacles of rubies, and your shair (gates) of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious aban (stone).
All your ban (son) shall be lamawad (taught) of Yahawah; and rab (great) shall be the shalawam (peace / safety) of your ban (son).

In tzadaqah (righteousness) you shall be kawan (established): you shall be rachaq (far) from ishaq (oppression), for you shall not be yaraa (fear / be afraid); and from machathah (terror), for it shall not qarab (come close) near you.
Behold, they may gawar (gather) together, but not by me: whoever shall gawar (gather) together against you shall napal (fall / be cast down) because of you.

"Behold, I have baraa (created) the charash (smith) who napach (blows) the ash (fire) of pacham (coals), and yatzaa (go out / come out) forth a kalay (weapon) for his maishah (work); and I have baraa (created) the shachath (waster) to chabal (destroy).

No kalay (weapon) that is yatzar (formed) against you will prevail; and you will rashai (condemn) every lashawan (tongue/language) that qawam (rise up) against you in mashapat (judgment). This is the nachalah (heritage) of the ibad (servant) of Yahawah, and their tzadaqah (righteousness) which is of me," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

Come, everyone who tzamaa (thirsts), to the mayam (Waters)! Yalak (come), he who has no kasap (money), shabar (buy), and akal (eat)! Yes, yalak (come), shabar (buy) yayan (wine) and chalab (milk) without kasap (money) and without machayar (price).

Why do you shaqal (spend) kasap (money) for that which is not lacham (bread)? And your yagayai (labor) for that which doesn't shabaih (seven)? Shamai (hearken / hear) shamai (hearken / hear) to me, and akal (eat) you that which is tawab (pleasant/functional), and let your napash (living being/soul) inag (delight) itself in dashan (fatness).

Natah (turn) your azan (ear), and yalak (come) to me; shamai (hearken / hear), and your napash (living being/soul) shall chayah (live): and I will karath (cut) an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant) with you, even the aman (believe / have faith) chasad (grace) of Dawad (David).
Behold, I nathan (give) given him for a id (witness) to the laam (peoples), a nagayad (leader) and commander to the laam (peoples).

Behold, you shall qaraa (called) a gaway (nation / people) that you don't yadai (know); and a gaway (nation / people) that didn't yadai (know) you shall rawatz (run) to you, because of Yahawah your Alahayam, and for the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel); for he has paar (glorified) you.
Darash (seek) Yahawah while he may be matzaa (found); qaraa (called) you on him while he is qarawab (near):

Let the rashai (wicked) izab (forsake) his darak (way), and the awan (unrighteous) ayash (husband/individual man) his machashabah (thoughts); and let him shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah, and he will have racham (mercy) on him; and to our Alahayam, for he will abundantly salach (forgive/pardon/make clean).
"For my machashabah (thoughts) are not your machashabah (thoughts), neither are your darak (ways) my darak (ways)," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

For as the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) are gabah (higher) than the aratz (Earth/land), so are my darak (ways) gabah (higher) than your darak (ways), and my machashabah (thoughts) than your machashabah (thoughts).

For as the gasham (rain) yarad (comes) down and the shalag (snow) from the sky, and doesn't shawab (turn back / repent) there, but rawah (waters) the aratz (Earth/land), and makes it yalad (birth / begot) forth and tzamach (bud), and nathan (give) zarai (seed) to the zarai (sower) and lacham (bread) to the eater;

So shall my dabar (word / matter) be that yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of my pah (mouth): it shall not shawab (turn back / repent) to me rayaqam (void), but it shall ishah (make) that which I please, and it shall tzalach (prosper) in the thing I shalach (send) it to do.

For you shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out with shamachah (joy), and be yabal (led) forth with shalawam (peace / safety): the har (mountain) and the gabaih (hills) shall patzach (break) forth panayam (before) you into ranah (singing); and all the itz (trees) of the shadah (fields) shall machaa (clap) their kap (hands).

Instead of the naitzawatz (thorn) shall ilah (go up / offer) up the barawash (fir) tree; and instead of the sarapad (brier) shall ilah (go up / offer) up the hadas (myrtle) tree: and it shall be to Yahawah for a sham (name), for an iwalam (forever) awath (sign / mark / miracle) that shall not be karath (cut) off.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, shamar (keep/guard) mashapat (justice), and ishah (make) tzadaqah (righteousness); for my yashawaih (salvation) is qarawab (near) to bawaa (come), and my tzadaqah (righteousness) to be galah (revealed).

Ashar (who/that) is the anawash (man) who ishah (make) this, and the ban (son) of adam (man) who chazaq (holds) it fast; who shamar (keep/guard) the shabath (shabath/rest) from chalal (profaning) it, and shamar (keep/guard) his yad (hand) from ishah (make) any rai (evil).

Neither let the foreigner, who has lawah (joined) himself to Yahawah, amar (spoke), amar (spoke), "Yahawah will surely badal (separated) me from his im (people / nation);" neither let the sarayas (eunuch) amar (spoke), Behold, I am a yabash (dry land) itz (tree).

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, To the sarayas (eunuchs) who shamar (keep/guard) my shabath (shabath/rest), and bachar (choose) the things that please me, and chazaq (hold) fast my barayath (covenant):

To them I will nathan (give) in my bayath (house) and within my chawamah (walls) a yad (hand) and a sham (name) tawab (pleasant/functional) than of ban (son) and of bath (daughter); I will nathan (give) them an iwalam (forever) sham (name), that shall not be karath (cut) off.

Also the foreigners who lawah (join) themselves to Yahawah, to sharath (minister) to him, and to ahab (love) the sham (name) of Yahawah, to be his ibad (servant), everyone who shamar (keep/guard) the shabath (shabath/rest) from chalal (profaning) it, and chazaq (holds) fast my barayath (covenant);

Even them will I bawaa (come) to my qadash (set apart/make holy) har (mountain), and shamach (make) them joyful in my bayath (house) of thapalah (prayer): their burnt ilah (offerings) and their zabach (sacrifices) shall be accepted on my mazabach (altar); for my bayath (house) shall be qaraa (called) a bayath (house) of thapalah (prayer) for all im (people / nation).

The Adanay Yahawah, who qabatz (gathers) the dachah (outcasts) of Yasharaal (Israel), naam (declares (prophetically)), Yet will I qabatz (gather) others to him, besides his own who are qabatz (gathered).
All you animals of the shadah (field), athah (come) to akal (eat), all you animals in the yair (forest).
His watchmen are iwar (blind), they are all without yadai (knowledge); they are all mute kalab (dogs), they can't nabach (bark); dreaming, lying down, ahab (love) to nawam (slumber).

Yes, the kalab (dogs) are iz (greedy), they yadai (can) never yadai (have) shabaih (seven); and these are raih (shepherds) who can't bayan (between): they have all panah (turned) to their own darak (way), ayash (husband/individual man) one to his batzai (gain), from every qatzah (end / extremity / border).

"Athah (come)," say they, I will laqach (take / seized) yayan (wine), and we will sabaa (fill) ourselves with shakar (strong) drink; and machar (tomorrow) shall be as this machar (day), maad (great) beyond measure.

The tzadayaq (righteous) perishes, and no ayash (husband/individual man) shawam (place / establish / appoint) it to lab (heart); and chasad (grace) ayash (husband/individual man) are asap (taken) away, none bayan (between) that the tzadayaq (righteous) is asap (taken) away from the rai (evil).
He bawaa (come) into shalawam (peace / safety); they nawach (rest) in their mashakab (beds), each one who halak (move) in his nakach (uprightness).
But qarab (come close) near here, you ban (son) of the sorceress, the zarai (seed) of the naap (adulterer) and the prostitute.

Against whom do you inag (sport) yourselves? Against whom do you rachab (make) a wide pah (mouth), and stick out your lashawan (tongue/language)? Aren't you yalad (birth / begot) of disobedience, a zarai (seed) of falsehood,
You who inflame yourselves among the oaks, under every rainan (green) itz (tree); who shachat (kill) the yalad (birth / begot) in the nachal (stream / river), under the clefts of the salai (rocks)?

Among the chalaq (smooth) stones of the nachal (stream / river) is your chalaq (portion); they, they are your gawaral (lot); you have even shapak (poured) a drink nasak (offering) to them. You have ilah (go up / offer) an manachah (offering). Shall I be appeased for these things?
On a nashaa (lift) and gabah (lofty) har (mountain) you have shawam (place / establish / appoint) your mashakab (bed); there also you ilah (go up / offer) up to zabach (offer) zabach (sacrifice).

Achar (other) the dalath (doors) and the mazawazah (posts) you have shawam (place / establish / appoint) up your zakarawan (memorial): for you have galah (uncovered) to someone besides me, and have ilah (go up / offer) up; you have enlarged your mashakab (bed), and karath (cut) you a covenant with them: you ahab (love) their mashakab (bed) yad (hand) you chazah (saw) it.

You shawar (went) to the malak (king) with shaman (oil), and rabah (increased) your raqach (perfumes), and shalach (send) your tzayar (ambassadors) rachawaq (far) off, and shapal (debased) yourself even to shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife).
You were yagai (wearied) with the length of your darak (way); yet you didn't amar (spoke), ‘It is in vain.’ You matzaa (found) a reviving of your yad (hand); therefore you weren't faint.

Of whom have you been daag (afraid) and in yaraa (fear / be afraid), that you kazab (lie), and have not zakar (remembrance/memory) me, nor shawam (place / establish / appoint) it to your lab (heart)? Haven't I held my chashah (peace) even of iwalam (forever) time, and you don't yaraa (fear / be afraid) me?
I will nagad (declare) your tzadaqah (righteousness); and as for your maishah (works), they shall not yail (profit) you.

When you zaiq (cry), let those who you have gathered natzal (deliver) you; but the rawach (spirit / wind) shall laqach (take / seized) them, a habal (breath) shall nashaa (lift) them all away: but he who laqach (take / seized) chasah (refuge) in me shall nachal (possess) the aratz (Earth/land), and shall yarash (inherit) my qadash (set apart/make holy) har (mountain).
He will amar (spoke), salal (cast) up, salal (cast) up, panah (prepare) the darak (way), rawam (will lift up) up the makashawal (stumbling-block) out of the darak (way) of my im (people / nation).

For thus amar (spoke) the rawam (will lift up) and nashaa (lift) One who shakan (inhabits) id (eternity), whose sham (name) is qadawash (holy): “I shakan (dwell) in the marawam (high) and qadawash (holy) place, with him also who is of a dakaa (contrite) and shapal (humble) rawach (spirit / wind), to chayah (revive) the rawach (spirit / wind) of the shapal (humble), and to chayah (revive) the lab (heart) of the dakaa (contrite).

For I will not rayab (contend) iwalam (forever), neither will I be natzach (always) qatzap (angry); for the rawach (spirit / wind) would itap (faint) panayam (before) me, and the nashamah (breathing thing) who I ishah (make) made.

For the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of his batzai (covetousness) was I qatzap (angry), and nakah (struck) him; I sathar (hid) myself and was qatzap (angry); and he yalak (went) on shawabab (backsliding) in the darak (way) of his lab (heart).
I raah (see) seen his darak (ways), and will rapaa (heal) him: I will nachah (lead) him also, and shalam (restore) nachawam (comforts) to him and to his mourners.

I baraa (created) the nawab (fruit) of the shapah (lips): shalawam (peace / safety), shalawam (peace / safety), to him who is rachawaq (far) off and to him who is qarawab (near),” amar (spoke) Yahawah; and I will rapaa (heal) them.
But the rashai (wicked) are like the garash (troubled) yam (sea/waters); for it can't shaqat (rest), and its mayam (Waters) garash (cast) up rapash (mire) and tayat (dirt).
"There is no shalawam (peace / safety)," amar (spoke) my Alahayam, for the rashai (wicked).
