Qaraa (called) garawan (aloud), don't chashak (darkness), rawam (will lift up) up your qawal (sound / voice) like a shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), and nagad (declare) to my im (people / nation) their disobedience, and to the bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob) their chataah (sin).

Yet they darash (seek) me yawam (day), and chapatz (delight) to daith (know) my darak (ways): as a gaway (nation / people) that ishah (make) tzadaqah (righteousness), and didn't izab (forsake) the mashapat (ordinance) of their Alahayam, they shaal (ask) of me righteous tzadaq (righteous / just / fair); they chapatz (delight) to qarabah (draw) near to Alahayam.

‘Why have we tzawam (fasted),’ say they, ‘and you don't raah (see)? Why have we inah (oppress / afflict) our napash (living being/soul), and you take no yadai (knowledge)?’ Behold, in the yawam (day) of your tzawam (fast) you matzaa (find) chapatz (pleasure), and nagash (exact) all your itzab (labors).

Behold, you tzawam (fast) for rayab (strife) and rayab (contention), and to nakah (strike) with the agarap (fist) of rashai (wickedness): you don't tzawam (fast) this yawam (day) so as to make your qawal (sound / voice) to be shamai (hearken / hear) on marawam (high).

Is such the tzawam (fast) that I have bachar (chosen)? The yawam (day) for a adam (man) to inah (oppress / afflict) his napash (living being/soul)? Is it to kapap (bow) down his raash (head) as a agamawan (rush), and to yatzai (spread) sackcloth and ashes under him? Will you qaraa (called) zah (this/that/these) a tzawam (fast), and an ratzawan (acceptable) yawam (day) to Yahawah?

Isn't this the tzawam (fast) that I have bachar (chosen): to release the bonds of rashai (wickedness), to nathar (undo) the bands of the mawatah (yoke), and to let the ratzatz (oppressed) shalach (send) chapashay (free), and that you nathaq (break) every mawatah (yoke)?

Isn't it to distribute your lacham (bread) to the raib (hungry), and that you bawaa (come) the inay (poor) who are marawad (cast) out to your bayath (house)? When you raah (see) the irawam (naked), that you kasah (cover) him; and that you not ilam (hide) yourself from your own bashar (flesh)?

Then your awar (light) shall baqai (break) forth as the shachar (morning), and your healing shall tzamach (spring) forth maharah (speedily); and your tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) shall halak (move) panayam (before) you; the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah shall be your rear guard.

Then you shall qaraa (called), and Yahawah will inah (answer / respond); you shall shawai (cry), and he will amar (spoke), ‘Here I am.’ If you sawar (take) away from the thawak (midst) of you the mawatah (yoke), the shalach (send) forth of the atzabai (finger), and dabar (word / matter) wickedly;

And if you pawaq (draw) out your napash (living being/soul) to the raib (hungry), and shabai (satisfy) the inah (oppress / afflict) napash (living being/soul): then your awar (light) shall zarach (rise) in apalah (darkness), and your chashak (darkness) be as the noonday;

And Yahawah will nachah (guide) you continually, and shabai (satisfy) your napash (living being/soul) in dry places, and chalatz (make) strong your itzam (bones); and you shall be like a rawah (watered) gan (garden), and like a mawatzaa (spring) of mayam (Waters), whose mayam (Waters) don't kazab (fail).

Those who shall be of you shall banah (build) the iwalam (forever) charabah (waste) places; you shall qawam (rise up) up the mawasadah (foundations) of many dawar (generation / age / period); and you shall be qaraa (called) The gadar (repairer) of the paratz (breach), The restorer of nathayab (paths) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) in.

“If you shawab (turn back / repent) away your ragal (feet / foot) from the shabath (shabath/rest), from ishah (make) your chapatz (pleasure) on my qadash (set apart/make holy) yawam (day); and qaraa (called) the shabath (shabath/rest) a inag (delight), and the qadawash (holy) of Yahawah honorable; and shall honor it, not ishah (make) your own darak (ways), nor matzaa (finding) your own chapatz (pleasure), nor dabar (word / matter) your own dabar (word / matter):

Then you shall inag (delight) yourself in Yahawah; and I will rakab (make) you to ride on the bamah (high) places of the aratz (Earth/land); and I will akal (eat) you with the nachalah (heritage) of Yaiqab (Jacob) your ab (father):” for the pah (mouth) of Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) it.
Han (behold), yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) yad (hand) is not shortened, that it can't yashai (salvation); neither his azan (ear) kabad (heavy), that it can't shamai (hearken / hear):

But your iwan (guilt/iniquity) have badal (separated) bayan (between) you and your Alahayam, and your chataah (sin) have sathar (hidden) his panayam (face) from you, so that he will not shamai (hearken / hear).

For your kap (hands) are gaal (defiled) with dam (blood), and your atzabai (fingers) with iwan (guilt/iniquity); your shapah (lips) have dabar (word / matter) shaqar (lies), your lashawan (tongue/language) hagah (mutters) iwal (wickedness).

None sues in tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and none shapat (pleads) in amawanah (truth): they batach (trust) in thahaw (formless), and dabar (word / matter) shawaa (vanity); they harah (conceive) imal (mischief), and yalad (birth / begot) forth awan (iniquity).

They baqai (hatch) tzapai (adders)' bayatzah (eggs), and weave the ikabayash (spider's) qawar (web): he who akal (eat) of their bayatzah (eggs) mawath (death); and that which is zawarah (crushed) baqai (breaks) out into a apaih (viper).

Their qawar (webs) shall not become bagad (garments), neither shall they kasah (cover) themselves with their maishah (works): their maishah (works) are maishah (works) of awan (iniquity), and the pail (act) of chamas (violence) is in their kap (hands).

Their ragal (feet / foot) rawatz (run) to rai (evil), and they mahar (make) haste to shapak (shed) naqay (innocent) dam (blood): their machashabah (thoughts) are machashabah (thoughts) of awan (iniquity); shad (desolation) and shabar (destruction) are in their masalah (paths).

The darak (way) of shalawam (peace / safety) they don't yadai (know); and there is no mashapat (justice) in their maigal (goings): they have iqash (made) them crooked nathayab (paths); whoever darak (goes) therein does not yadai (know) shalawam (peace / safety).

Therefore is mashapat (justice) rachaq (far) from us, neither does tzadaqah (righteousness) nashag (overtake) us: we qawah (gather/wait) for awar (light), but, behold, chashak (darkness); for nagahah (brightness), but we halak (move) in obscurity.

We gashash (grope) for the qayar (wall) like the iwar (blind); yes, we gashash (grope) as those who have no iyan (eye): we kashal (stumble / stagger) at noonday as in the nashap (twilight); among those who are lusty we are as mawath (death) men.

We hamah (they) all like dab (bears), and moan bitterly like yawanah (doves): we qawah (gather/wait) for mashapat (justice), but there is none; for yashawaih (salvation), but it is rachaq (far) off from us.

For our pashai (transgressions) are rabah (multiplied) before you, and our chataah (sin) inah (answer / respond) against us; for our pashai (transgressions) are with us, and as for our iwan (guilt/iniquity), we yadai (know) them:

Pashai (transgressing) and kachash (denying) Yahawah, and nasag (turning) away from following our Alahayam, dabar (word / matter) ishaq (oppression) and sarah (revolt), harah (conceiving) and hagah (uttering) from the lab (heart) dabar (word / matter) of falsehood.

Mashapat (justice) is nasag (turned) away backward, and tzadaqah (righteousness) imad (stands) rachawaq (afar) off; for amath (truth) is kashal (stumble / stagger) in the rachab (street), and nakachah (uprightness) can't bawaa (come).
Yes, amath (truth) is idar (lacking); and he who sawar (departs) from rai (evil) shalal (makes) himself a prey. Yahawah raah (see) it, and it displeased him that there was no mashapat (justice).

He raah (see) that there was no ayash (husband/individual man), and shamam (wondered) that there was no pagai (intercessor): therefore his own zarawai (arm) brought yashai (salvation) to him; and his tzadaqah (righteousness), it upheld him.

He labash (put) on tzadaqah (righteousness) as a sharayawan (breastplate), and a kawabai (helmet) of yashawaih (salvation) on his raash (head); and he labash (put) on bagad (garments) of naqam (vengeance) for thalabashath (clothing), and was itah (clad) with qanaah (zeal) as a maiyal (mantle).

Il (over) to their gamawalah (deeds), accordingly he will shalam (repay), chamah (wrath) to his tzar (oppressor / distressor), gamawal (recompense) to his ayab (enemy); to the ay (islands) he will shalam (repay) gamawal (recompense).

So shall they yaraa (fear / be afraid) the sham (name) of Yahawah from the mairab (west), and his kabawad (glory) from the mazarach (rising) of the shamash (sun); for he will bawaa (come) as a rushing stream, which the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah drives.
"A gaal (redeemer) will bawaa (come) to Tzayawan (Zion), and to those who shawab (turn back / repent) from disobedience in Yaiqab (Jacob)," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

"As for me, this is my barayath (covenant) with them," amar (spoke) Yahawah. "My rawach (spirit / wind) who is on you, and my dabar (word / matter) which I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) in your pah (mouth), shall not depart out of your pah (mouth), nor out of the pah (mouth) of your zarai (seed), nor out of the pah (mouth) of your zarai (seed's) zarai (seed)," amar (spoke) Yahawah, from henceforth and iwalam (forever).
Qawam (rise up), awar (light); for your awar (light) bawaa (come) come, and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah is zarach (risen) on you.

For, behold, chashak (darkness) shall kasah (cover) the aratz (Earth/land), and irapal (gross) darkness the laam (peoples); but Yahawah will arise on you, and his kabawad (glory) shall be raah (see) on you.
Gaway (nation / people) shall halak (move) to your awar (light), and malak (king) to the nagah (brightness) of your zarach (rising).

Nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye) all around, and raah (see): they all qabatz (gather) themselves together, they bawaa (come) to you; your ban (son) shall bawaa (come) from rachawaq (far), and your bath (daughter) shall be carried in the arms.

Then you shall raah (see) and be radiant, and your labab (heart) shall thrill and be enlarged; because the hamawan (abundance) of the yam (sea/waters) shall be hapak (turned) to you, the wealth of the gaway (nation / people) shall bawaa (come) to you.

The shapaih (multitude) of gamal (camels) shall kasah (cover) you, the bakar (dromedaries) of Madayan (Midian) and Iyapah (Ephah); all they from Shabaa (Sheba) shall bawaa (come); they shall nashaa (lift) zahab (gold) and labawanah (frankincense), and shall proclaim the thahalah (praises) of Yahawah.

All the tzaan (flocks) of Qadar (Kedar) shall be qabatz (gathered) together to you, the ayal (rams) of Nabayawath (Nebaioth) shall sharath (minister) to you; they shall ilah (go up / offer) up with acceptance on my mazabach (altar); and I will paar (glorify) the bayath (house) of my glory.
Who are these who iwap (flying) as a ib (cloud), and as the yawanah (doves) to their arabah (windows)?

Surely the ay (islands) shall qawah (gather/wait) for me, and the anayah (ships) of Tharashayash (Tarshish) raashawan (first), to bawaa (come) your ban (son) from rachawaq (far), their kasap (silver) and their zahab (gold) with them, for the sham (name) of Yahawah your Alahayam, and for the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel), because he has paar (glorified) you.

Foreigners shall banah (build) up your chawamah (walls), and their malak (king) shall sharath (minister) to you: for in my qatzap (wrath) I nakah (struck) you, but in my favor have I had racham (mercy) on you.

Your shair (gates) also shall be pathach (open) continually; they shall not be sagar (shut) yawamam (by day) nor layal (night); that men may bawaa (come) to you the wealth of the gaway (nation / people), and their malak (king) nahag (led) captive.
For that gaway (nation / people) and mamalakah (kingdom) that will not ibad (servant) you shall abad (destroy/perish); yes, those gaway (nation / people) shall be utterly charab (wasted).

The kabawad (glory) of Labanawan (Lebanon) shall bawaa (come) to you, the barawash (fir) tree, the thadahar (pine), and the box tree yachad (together), to paar (beautify) the maqawam (place) of my maqadash (sanctuary); and I will make the maqawam (place) of my ragal (feet / foot) kabad (glorious).

The ban (son) of those who inah (oppress / afflict) you shall halak (move) shachach (bending) to you; and all those who naatz (despised) you shall shachah (bow) themselves down at the kap (soles) of your ragal (feet / foot); and they shall qaraa (called) you The iyar (city) of Yahawah, The Tzayawan (Zion) of the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).

Thachath (under) you have been forsaken and shanaa (hate), so that no ibar (pass over/through) passed through you, I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) you an iwalam (forever) gaawan (excellency), a mashawash (joy) of many dawar (generation / age / period).

You shall also drink the chalab (milk) of the gaway (nation / people), and shall yanaq (nurse) from malak (king) shad (breasts); and you shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, am your Savior, and your gaal (redeemer), the abayar (mighty) One of Yaiqab (Jacob).

For nachashath (brass) I will bawaa (come) zahab (gold), and for barazal (iron) I will bawaa (come) kasap (silver), and for itz (wood) nachashath (brass), and for aban (stone) barazal (iron). I will also shawam (place / establish / appoint) your paqadah (officers) shalawam (peace / safety), and tzadaqah (righteousness) your nagash (ruler).

Chamas (violence) shall no more be shamai (hearken / hear) in your aratz (Earth/land), shad (desolation) nor shabar (destruction) within your gabawal (border/boundary); but you shall qaraa (called) your chawamah (walls) yashawaih (salvation), and your shair (gates) thahalah (praise).

The shamash (sun) shall be no more your awar (light) by yawamam (by day); neither for nagah (brightness) shall the yarach (moon) give awar (light) to you: but Yahawah will be to you an iwalam (forever) awar (light), and your Alahayam your glory.

Your shamash (sun) shall no more bawaa (come) down, neither shall your yarach (moon) asap (withdraw) itself; for Yahawah will be your iwalam (forever) awar (light), and the yawam (day) of your abal (mourning) shall be shalam (ended).

Your im (people / nation) also shall be all tzadayaq (righteous); they shall yarash (inherit) the aratz (Earth/land) iwalam (forever), the natzar (branch) of my matai (planting), the maishah (work) of my yad (hand), that I may be paar (glorified).
The qatan (small/young/least) one shall become a alap (thousand), and the tzaiyar (small) one a itzawam (strong) gaway (nation / people); I, Yahawah, will chawash (hasten) it in its ith (time).

The rawach (spirit / wind) of the Adanay Yahawah is on me; because Yahawah has mashach (anointed) me to preach bashar (good) news to the inaw (humble). He has shalach (send) me to chabash (bind) up the shabar (brokenhearted), to qaraa (called) darawar (liberty) to the shabah (captives), and release to those who are asar (bound);
To qaraa (called) the shanah (year) of yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) favor, and the yawam (day) of naqam (vengeance) of our Alahayam; to nacham (turn away / repent) all who abal (mourn);

To shawam (place / establish / appoint) to those who abal (mourn) in Tzayawan (Zion), to nathan (give) to them a garland for ashes, the shaman (oil) of shashawan (joy) for abal (mourning), the maitah (garment) of thahalah (praise) for the rawach (spirit / wind) of kahah (heaviness); that they may be qaraa (called) ayal (trees) of tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), the matai (planting) of Yahawah, that he may be paar (glorified).

They shall banah (build) the iwalam (forever) charabah (wastes), they shall qawam (rise up) up the raashawan (former) desolations, and they shall chadash (repair) the charab (waste) iyar (cities), the desolations of many dawar (generation / age / period).
Strangers shall imad (stand) and raih (feed) your tzaan (flocks), and foreigners shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers.

But you shall be qaraa (called) the kahan (priest) of Yahawah; men will amar (spoke) you the sharath (ministers) of our Alahayam: you will akal (eat) the wealth of the gaway (nation / people), and you will yamar (boast) in their kabawad (glory).

Instead of your bashath (shame) you shall have mashanah (double); and instead of dishonor they shall ranan (rejoice) in their chalaq (portion): therefore in their aratz (Earth/land) they shall yarash (possess) mashanah (double); iwalam (forever) shamachah (joy) shall be to them.

For I, Yahawah, ahab (love) mashapat (justice), I shanaa (hate) gazal (robbery) with ilah (iniquity); and I will nathan (give) them their recompense in amath (truth), and I will karath (cut) an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant) with them.

Their zarai (seed) shall be yadai (known) among the gaway (nation / people), and their tzaatzaa (offspring) thawak (midst) the im (people / nation); all who raah (see) them shall nakar (acknowledge) them, that they are the zarai (seed) which Yahawah has barak (blessed).

I will shawash (greatly) shawash (rejoice) in Yahawah, my napash (living being/soul) shall be gayal (joyful) in my Alahayam; for he has labash (clothed) me with the bagad (garments) of yashai (salvation), he has yait (covered) me with the maiyal (robe) of tzadaqah (righteousness), as a chathan (bridegroom) kahan (priest) himself with a garland, and as a kalah (complete / finish) idah (adorns) herself with her kalay (jewels).

For as the aratz (Earth/land) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth its tzamach (bud), and as the ganah (garden) causes the things that are zarawai (sown) in it to tzamach (spring) forth; so the Adanay Yahawah will cause tzadaqah (righteousness) and thahalah (praise) to tzamach (spring) forth before all the gaway (nation / people).

For Tzayawan (Zion's) sake will I not hold my chashah (peace), and for Yarawashalam (Jerusalem's) sake I will not shaqat (rest), until her tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth as nagah (brightness), and her yashawaih (salvation) as a lapayad (lamp) that bair (burns).

The gaway (nation / people) shall raah (see) your tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and all malak (king) your kabawad (glory), and you shall be qaraa (called) by a chadash (new) naqab (name), which the pah (mouth) of Yahawah shall sham (name).
You shall also be a itarah (crown) of thapaarah (beauty) in the yad (hand) of Yahawah, and a malawakah (royal) tzanayap (diadem) in the kap (hand) of your Alahayam.

You shall no more be amar (spoke) Forsaken; neither shall your aratz (Earth/land) any more be amar (spoke) shamamah (desolate): but you shall be qaraa (called) Chapatzayabah (Hephzibah), and your aratz (Earth/land) Beulah; for Yahawah chapatz (delights) in you, and your aratz (Earth/land) shall be bail (married).

For as a bachawar (young) man bail (marries) a bathawalah (virgin), so your ban (son) shall bail (marry) you; and as the chathan (bridegroom) mashawash (rejoices) over the kalah (complete / finish), so your Alahayam will shawash (rejoice) over you.

I paqad (visit) set watchmen on your chawamah (walls), Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); they shall thamayad (never) hold their chashah (peace) yawam (day) nor layal (night): you who zakar (remembrance/memory) on Yahawah, take no damay (rest),
And nathan (give) him no damay (rest), until he establishes, and until he shawam (place / establish / appoint) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) a thahalah (praise) in the aratz (Earth/land).

Yahawah has shabai (swear / take oath) by his right yamayan (right hand), and by the zarawai (arm) of his iz (strength / might / refuge), am (mother) I will no more nathan (give) your grain to be maakal (food) for your ayab (enemy); and foreigners shall not shathah (drinks) your new thayarawash (wine), for which you have labored:

But those who have garnered it shall akal (eat) it, and halal (praise) Yahawah; and those who have qabatz (gathered) it shall shathah (drinks) it in the chatzar (courts) of my qadash (set apart/make holy).

Ibar (pass over/through) through, ibar (pass over/through) through the shair (gates)! Panah (prepare) the darak (way) of the im (people / nation)! Salal (cast) up, salal (cast) up the masalah (highway)! Saqal (gather) out the aban (stone)! Rawam (will lift up) up a nas (banner) for the im (people / nation).

Behold, Yahawah has shamai (hearken / hear) to the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land), amar (spoke) to the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion), ‘Behold, your yashai (salvation) bawaa (come). Behold, his shakar (reward) is with him, and his recompense panayam (before) him.’
They shall qaraa (called) them The qadash (set apart/make holy) im (people / nation), The gaal (redeemed) of Yahawah: and you shall be qaraa (called) darash (sought) out, A iyar (city) not forsaken.

Who is this who bawaa (come) from Adam (Edom), with chamatz (dyed) bagad (garments) from Batzarah (Bozrah)? This who is hadar (glorious) in his labawash (clothing), marching in the greatness of his kach (strength / mighty / power)? It is I who dabar (word / matter) in tzadaqah (righteousness), rab (mighty) to yashai (salvation).
Why are you adam (red) in your labawash (clothing), and your bagad (garments) like him who darak (treads) in the gath (wine) vat?

I have darak (trodden) the pawarah (winepress) alone; and of the im (people / nation) there was no man with me: yes, I darak (trod) them in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and ramas (trampled) them in my chamah (wrath); and their lifeblood is nazah (sprinkled) on my bagad (garments), and I have gaal (stained) all my clothing.
For the yawam (day) of naqam (vengeance) was in my lab (heart), and the shanah (year) of my gaal (redeemed) bawaa (come) come.

I nabat (looked), and there was none to izar (help); and I shamam (wondered) that there was none to samak (uphold): therefore my own zarawai (arm) brought yashai (salvation) to me; and my chamah (wrath), it upheld me.

I bawas (trod) down the im (people / nation) in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and shakar (made) them drunk in my chamah (wrath), and I poured out their lifeblood on the aratz (Earth/land).

I will zakar (remembrance/memory) mention of the chasad (grace) kindnesses of Yahawah and the thahalah (praises) of Yahawah, according to all that Yahawah has gamal (bestowed) on us, and the rab (great) goodness toward the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), which he has gamal (bestowed) on them according to his racham (mercies), and according to the rab (multitude) of his chasad (grace) kindnesses.
For he amar (spoke), "Surely, they are my im (people / nation), ban (son) who will not shaqar (deal) falsely:" so he was their Savior.

In all their tzarah (affliction) he was tzar (oppressor / distressor), and the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of his panayam (presence) yashai (salvation) them: in his ahabah (love) and in his chamalah (pity) he gaal (redeemed) them; and he natal (bore) them, and nashaa (lift) them all the yawam (day) of iwalam (forever).

But they marah (rebelled), and itzab (grieved) his qadash (set apart/make holy) rawach (spirit / wind): therefore he was hapak (turned) to be their ayab (enemy), and he himself lacham (fought) against them.

Then he zakar (remembrance/memory) the yawam (day) of iwalam (forever), Mashah (Moses) and his im (people / nation), saying, Where is he who ilah (go up / offer) them up out of the yam (sea/waters) with the raih (shepherds) of his tzaan (flock)? Where is he who shawam (place / establish / appoint) his qadash (set apart/make holy) rawach (spirit / wind) in their qarab (among / near)?

Who caused his thapaarah (glorious) zarawai (arm) to yalak (go) at the right yamayan (right hand) of Mashah (Moses)? Who baqai (divided) the mayam (Waters) panayam (before) them, to ishah (make) himself an iwalam (forever) sham (name)?
Who yalak (led) them through the thahawam (depths), as a sawas (horse) in the madabar (wilderness), so that they didn't kashal (stumble / stagger)?

As the livestock that yarad (go) down into the baqaih (valley), the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah caused them to nawach (rest); so you nahag (led) your im (people / nation), to ishah (make) yourself a thapaarah (glorious) sham (name).

Raah (see) down from shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), and raah (see) from the zabawal (habitation) of your qadash (set apart/make holy) and of your glory: where are your qanaah (zeal) and your gabawarah (mighty) acts? The yearning of your maih (heart) and your compassion is apaq (restrained) toward me.

For you are our ab (father), though Abaraham (Abraham) doesn't know us, and Yasharaal (Israel) does not nakar (acknowledge) us: you, Yahawah, are our ab (father); our gaal (redeemer) from iwalam (forever) is your sham (name).

O Yahawah, why do you thaih (make) us to err from your darak (ways), and qashach (harden) our lab (heart) from your yaraah (fear)? Shawab (turn back / repent) for your ibad (servant)' sake, the shabat (tribes) of your nachalah (inheritance).
Your qadash (set apart/make holy) im (people / nation) yarash (possessed) it but a matzair (little) while: our tzar (oppressor / distressor) have bawas (trodden) down your maqadash (sanctuary).
We have become as they over whom you iwalam (forever) mashal (rule/have dominion) rule, as those who were not qaraa (called) by your sham (name).
Oh that you would tear the heavens, that you would yadai (come) down, that the mountains might quake at your panayam (presence),
As when har (mountain) kindles the brushwood, and the har (mountain) causes the waters to boil; to make your name known to your adversaries, that the nations may tremble at your panayam (presence)!
When you ishah (make) awesome things which we didn't iyan (eye) for, you came down, the mountains quaked at your iyan (eye).
For from of iwalam (forever) men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither has the eye seen a Alahayam besides you, who ishah (make) for him who waits for him.

You meet him who rejoices and works tzadaqah (righteousness), those who remember you in your hayah (came to pass). Behold, you were angry, and we iwan (guilt/iniquity). We have been in iwan (guilt/iniquity) for a long time; and shall we be saved?
For we have all become as one who is unclean, and all our righteousness is as a polluted garment: and we all fade as a leaf; and our iwan (guilt/iniquity), like the wind, chazaq (take) us away.
There is none who calls on your ab (father), who stirs up himself to take hold of you; for you have hidden your face from us, and have consumed us by yad (hand) of our iniquities.
But now, Yahawah, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you our potter; and we all are the work of your hand.
Don't be furious, Yahawah, neither remember iniquity forever: see, look, we beg you, we are all your people.
Your qadash (set apart/make holy) cities are become a wilderness, Zion has become a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.
Our holy and our beautiful house, where our fathers praised you, is burned with fire; and all our pleasant places are laid waste.
Will you refrain yourself for these things, Yahawah? Will you hold your chashah (peace), and inah (oppress / afflict) us very severely?

I am darash (inquired) of by those who didn't shaal (ask); I am matzaa (found) by those who didn't baqash (seek) me: I amar (spoke), See me, see me, to a gaway (nation / people) that was not qaraa (called) by my sham (name).

I have parash (spread) out my yad (hand) all the yawam (day) to a sarar (rebellious) im (people / nation), who halak (move) in a darak (way) that is not tawab (pleasant/functional), achar (other) their own machashabah (thoughts);
A im (people / nation) who kais (provoke) me to my panayam (face) continually, zabach (sacrificing) in ganah (gardens), and qatar (burning) incense on labanah (bricks);

Who yashab (inhabit/dwell) among the qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher), and lawan (lodge) in the secret places; who akal (eat) pig's bashar (flesh), and paraq (broth) of pagawal (abominable) things is in their kalay (vessels);

Who amar (spoke), qarab (come close) by yourself, don't nagash (come) near to me, for I am holier than you. These are a ishan (smoke) in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), a ash (fire) that yaqad (burns) all the yawam (day).
"Behold, it is kathab (written) panayam (before) me: I will not chashah (keep) silence, but will shalam (recompense), yes, I will shalam (recompense) into their chayaq (bosom),

Your own iwan (guilt/iniquity), and the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of your ab (father) yachad (together)," amar (spoke) Yahawah, who have qatar (burned) incense on the har (mountain), and charap (blasphemed) me on the gabaih (hills); therefore will I raashawan (first) madad (measure) their pailah (work) into their chayaq (bosom).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, As the new thayarawash (wine) is matzaa (found) in the ashakawal (cluster), and one amar (spoke), ‘Don't shachath (destroy) it, for a barakah (blessing) is in it:’ so will I ishah (make) for my ibad (servant)' sake, that I may not shachath (destroy) them all.

I will yatzaa (go out / come out) forth a zarai (seed) out of Yaiqab (Jacob), and out of Yahawadah (Judah) an inheritor of my har (mountain); and my bachayar (chosen) shall yarash (inherit) it, and my ibad (servant) shall shakan (dwell) there.

Sharawan (Sharon) shall be a nawah (habitation) of tzaan (flocks), and the imaq (valley) of Ikawar (Achor) a place for baqar (morning) to rabatz (lie) down in, for my im (people / nation) who have darash (sought) me.

But you who izab (forsake) Yahawah, who shakach (forget) my qadash (set apart/make holy) har (mountain), who irak (prepare) a shalachan (table) for Fortune, and who malaa (fill) up mixed mamasak (wine) Manay (to) Destiny;

I will destine you to the charab (sword), and you shall all karai (bow) down to the tabach (slaughter); because when I qaraa (called), you didn't inah (answer / respond); when I dabar (word / matter), you didn't shamai (hearken / hear); but you ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in my iyan (eye), and bachar (chose) that in which I didn't chapatz (delight).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, Behold, my ibad (servant) shall akal (eat), but you shall be raib (hungry); behold, my ibad (servant) shall shathah (drinks), but you shall be tzamaa (thirsty); behold, my ibad (servant) shall shamach (rejoice), but you shall be disappointed;

Behold, my ibad (servant) shall ranan (sing) for tawab (pleasant/functional) of lab (heart), but you shall tzaiq (cry) for kaab (sorrow) of lab (heart), and shall wail for anguish of rawach (spirit / wind).

You shall yanach (leave) your sham (name) for a shabawaih (curse) to my bachayar (chosen); and the Adanay Yahawah will mawath (death) you; and he will qaraa (called) his ibad (servant) by achar (other) sham (name):

So that he who blesses himself in the aratz (Earth/land) shall barak (bless) himself in the Alahayam of aman (believe / have faith); and he who shabai (swear / take oath) in the aratz (Earth/land) shall shabai (swear / take oath) by the Alahayam of aman (believe / have faith); because the raashawan (former) tzarah (troubles) are shakach (forgotten), and because they are sathar (hidden) from my iyan (eye).

For, behold, I baraa (created) chadash (new) shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) and a chadash (new) aratz (Earth/land); and the raashawan (former) things shall not be zakar (remembrance/memory), nor ilah (go up / offer) into lab (heart).

But be you shawash (glad) and gayal (rejoice) id (forever) in that which I baraa (created); for, behold, I baraa (created) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) a gayalah (rejoicing), and her im (people / nation) a mashawash (joy).

I will gayal (rejoice) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and shawash (joy) in my im (people / nation); and there shall be shamai (hearken / hear) in her no more the qawal (sound / voice) of bakay (weeping) and the qawal (sound / voice) of zaiq (crying).

“There shall be no more there an iwal (infant) of yawam (day), nor an old zaqan (man) who malaa (has) not filled his yawam (day); for the nair (child) shall mawath (death) one maah (hundred) shanah (years) ban (son), and the chataa (sinner) being one maah (hundred) shanah (years) ban (son) shall be qalal (accursed).
They shall banah (build) bayath (house), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) them; and they shall natai (plant) karam (vineyards), and akal (eat) their paray (fruit).

They shall not banah (build), and achar (other) yashab (inhabit/dwell); they shall not natai (plant), and achar (other) akal (eat): for as the yawam (day) of a itz (tree) shall be the yawam (day) of my im (people / nation), and my bachayar (chosen) shall balah (long) enjoy the maishah (work) of their yad (hand).
They shall not yagai (labor) in rayaq (vain), nor yalad (birth / begot) forth for calamity; for they are the zarai (seed) of the barak (blessed) of Yahawah, and their tzaatzaa (offspring) with them.
It shall happen that, before they qaraa (called), I will inah (answer / respond); and while they are yet dabar (word / matter), I will shamai (hearken / hear).

The zaab (wolf) and the talah (lamb) shall raih (feed) achad (one), and the aray (lion) shall akal (eat) thaban (straw) like the baqar (morning); and ipar (dust) shall be the nachash (serpent's) lacham (food). They shall not raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) nor shachath (destroy) in all my qadash (set apart/make holy) har (mountain),” amar (spoke) Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) is my kasaa (throne), and the aratz (Earth/land) is my footstool: what kind of bayath (house) will you banah (build) to me? And what maqawam (place) shall be my manawachah (rest)?

For all these things has my yad (hand) ishah (make), and so all these things came to be," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah: but to this man will I nabat (look), even to him who is inay (poor) and of a nakah (contrite) rawach (spirit / wind), and who trembles at my dabar (word / matter).

He who shachat (kills) an shawar (ox) is as he who nakah (kills) a ayash (husband/individual man); he who zabach (sacrifices) a shah (lamb), as he who irap (breaks) a kalab (dog's) irap (neck); he who ilah (go up / offer) an manachah (offering), as he who offers pig's dam (blood); he who zakar (remembrance/memory) labawanah (frankincense), as he who blesses an awan (idol). Yes, they have bachar (chosen) their own darak (ways), and their napash (living being/soul) chapatz (delights) in their shaqawatz (abominations):

I also will bachar (choose) their thailawal (delusions), and will bawaa (come) their magawarah (fears) on them; because when I qaraa (called), no one dabar (word / matter); when I dabar (word / matter), they didn't shamai (hearken / hear); but they ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in my iyan (eye), and bachar (chose) that in which I didn't chapatz (delight).

Shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, you who tremble at his dabar (word / matter): Your ach (brother/kinsman) who shanaa (hate) you, who nadah (cast) you out for my sham (name) sake, have amar (spoke), ‘Let Yahawah be kabad (glorified), that we may raah (see) your shamachah (joy);’ but it is those who shall be disappointed.

A qawal (sound / voice) of shaawan (tumult) from the iyar (city), a qawal (sound / voice) from the hayakal (temple), a qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah that shalam (renders) gamawal (recompense) to his ayab (enemy).
"Before she chawal (travailed), she yalad (birth / begot) forth; before her chabal (pain) bawaa (come), she malat (delivered) a zakar (remembrance/memory).

Who has shamai (hearken / hear) such a thing? Who raah (see) seen such things? Shall a aratz (Earth/land) be born in achad (one) yawam (day)? Shall a gaway (nation / people) be chawal (brought) forth at paim (once)? For as soon as Tzayawan (Zion) chawal (travailed), she yalad (birth / begot) forth her ban (son).

Shall I shabar (bring) to the birth, and not cause to yalad (birth / begot) forth?" Amar (spoke) Yahawah: "shall I who cause to yalad (birth / begot) forth itzar (shut) the womb?" Amar (spoke) your Alahayam.
Shamach (rejoice) with Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and be gayal (glad) for her, all you who ahab (love) her: shawash (rejoice) for mashawash (joy) with her, all you who abal (mourn) over her;

That you may yanaq (nurse) and be shabai (satisfied) at the thanachawam (comforting) shad (breasts); that you may drink deeply, and be inag (delighted) with the zayaz (abundance) of her kabawad (glory).

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, Behold, I will natah (extend) shalawam (peace / safety) to her like a nahar (river), and the kabawad (glory) of the gaway (nation / people) like an shatap (overflowing) nachal (stream / river): and you will yanaq (nurse). You will be nashaa (lift) on her tzad (side), and will be shaii (dandled) on her barak (knees).
As ayash (husband/individual man) whom his am (mother) nacham (turn away / repent), so will I nacham (turn away / repent) you; and you will be nacham (turn away / repent) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

You will raah (see) it, and your lab (heart) shall shawash (rejoice), and your itzam (bones) shall parach (flourish) like the tender dashaa (grass): and the yad (hand) of Yahawah shall be yadai (known) toward his ibad (servant); and he will have zaim (indignation) against his ayab (enemy).

For, behold, Yahawah will bawaa (come) with ash (fire), and his marakabah (chariots) shall be like the sawapah (whirlwind); to shawab (turn back / repent) his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) with fierceness, and his gairah (rebuke) with lahab (flames) of ash (fire).
For by ash (fire) will Yahawah execute shapat (judgment), and by his charab (sword), on all bashar (flesh); and the chalal (slain) of Yahawah shall be many.

"Those who qadash (set apart/make holy) themselves and tahar (purify) themselves to go to the ganah (gardens), achar (other) achad (one) in the thawak (midst), akal (eat) pig's bashar (flesh), and the shaqatz (abomination), and the ikabar (mouse), they shall come to an sawap (end) yachad (together)," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

For I know their maishah (works) and their machashabah (thoughts): the time bawaa (come), that I will qabatz (gather) all gaway (nation / people) and lashawan (tongue/language); and they shall bawaa (come), and shall raah (see) my kabawad (glory).

“I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) a awath (sign / mark / miracle) among them, and I will shalach (send) such as palayat (escape) of them to the gaway (nation / people), to Tharashayash (Tarshish), Pawal (Pul), and Lawad (Lud), who mashak (draw) the qashath (bow), to Thawabal (Tubal) and Yawan (Javan), to the ay (islands) rachawaq (afar) off, who have not shamai (hearken / hear) my shamai (fame), neither raah (see) seen my kabawad (glory); and they shall nagad (declare) my kabawad (glory) among the gaway (nation / people).

They shall bawaa (come) all your ach (brother/kinsman) out of all the gaway (nation / people) for an manachah (offering) to Yahawah, on sawas (horses), and in rakab (chariots), and in tzab (litters), and on parad (mules), and on dromedaries, to my qadash (set apart/make holy) har (mountain) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), amar (spoke) Yahawah, as the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) bawaa (come) their manachah (offering) in a tahawar (clean) kalay (vessel) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
Of them also will I laqach (take / seized) for kahan (priest) and for Lawayay (Levites),” amar (spoke) Yahawah.

"For as the chadash (new) shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) and the chadash (new) aratz (Earth/land), which I will ishah (make), shall imad (remain) panayam (before) me," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, "so your zarai (seed) and your sham (name) shall imad (remain).

It shall happen, that from one new chadash (month) to another, and from one shabath (shabath/rest) to another, shall all bashar (flesh) bawaa (come) to shachah (worship) panayam (before) me," amar (spoke) Yahawah.

They shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and raah (see) on the pagar (dead) bodies of the ayash (husband/individual man) who have pashai (transgressed) against me: for their thawalai (worm) shall not mawath (death), neither shall their ash (fire) be kabah (quenched); and they will be loathsome to all bashar (flesh).
The dabar (word / matter) of Yaramayah (Jeremiah) the ban (son) Chalaqayah (of) Hilkiah, of the kahan (priest) who were in Inathawath (Anathoth) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Banayamayan (Benjamin):

To whom the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came in the yawam (day) of Yaashayah (Josiah) the ban (son) of Amawan (Amon), malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), in the thirteenth shanah (year) of his malak (king).

It came also in the yawam (day) of Yahawayaqayam (Jehoiakim) the ban (son) of Yaashayah (Josiah), malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), to the thamam (end) of the ishathay (eleven) shanah (year) of Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah), the ban (son) of Yaashayah (Josiah), malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), to the galah (carrying) away of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) galah (captive) in the chamayashay (fifth) chadash (month).
Now the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Taram (before) I yatzar (formed) you in the batan (belly), I yadai (knew) you. Before you yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the racham (womb), I qadash (set apart/make holy) you. I nathan (give) appointed you a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) to the gaway (nation / people).
Then I amar (spoke), ahah (ah), Adanay Yahawah! Behold, I don't know how to dabar (word / matter); for I am a nair (child).

But Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, "Don't amar (spoke), ‘I am a nair (child);’ for to whoever I shall shalach (send) you, you shall yalak (go), and whatever I shall tzawah (command) you, you shall dabar (word / matter).
Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) panayam (because) of them; for I am with you to natzal (deliver) you," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.
Then Yahawah shalach (send) forth his yad (hand), and nagai (touched) my pah (mouth); and Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, Behold, I nathan (give) put my dabar (word / matter) in your pah (mouth).

Raah (see), I have this yawam (day) paqad (visit) you over the gaway (nation / people) and over the mamalakah (kingdoms), to nathash (pluck) up and to nathatz (break) down and to abad (destroy/perish) and to haras (overthrow), to banah (build) and to natai (plant).
Moreover the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke), "Yaramayah (Jeremiah), what do you raah (see)?" I amar (spoke), I raah (see) a branch of an shaqad (almond) tree.
Then Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, You raah (see) seen yatab (well); for I shaqad (watch) over my dabar (word / matter) to ishah (make) it.

The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me the shanay (second) time, amar (spoke), "What do you raah (see)?" I amar (spoke), I raah (see) a boiling sayar (caldron); and it is tipping away from the tzapawan (north).
Then Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, "Out of the tzapawan (north) rai (evil) will pathach (break) out on all the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the aratz (Earth/land).

For, behold, I will qaraa (called) all the mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) of the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the tzapawan (north)," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah; and they shall bawaa (come), and they shall ayash (husband/individual man) nathan (give) his kasaa (throne) at the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gates) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and against all its chawamah (walls) all around, and against all the iyar (cities) of Yahawadah (Judah).

I will dabar (word / matter) my mashapat (judgments) il (over) them touching all their rai (wickedness), in that they have forsaken me, and have qatar (burned) incense to other Alahayam, and shachah (worshiped) the maishah (works) of their own yad (hand).

“You therefore put your belt on your waist, qawam (rise up), and dabar (word / matter) to them all that I tzawah (command) you. Don't be chathath (dismayed) at them, lest I chathath (dismay) you panayam (before) them.

For, behold, I nathan (give) made you this yawam (day) a fortified iyar (city), and an barazal (iron) imawad (pillar), and bronze chawamah (walls), against the whole aratz (Earth/land), against the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), against its shar (prince / ruler), against its kahan (priest), and against the im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land).
They will lacham (fight) against you; but they will not yakal (prevail) against you; for I am with you,” naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, to natzal (deliver) you.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Halak (move), and qaraa (called) in the azan (ears) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), amar (spoke), ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "I zakar (remembrance/memory) for you the chasad (grace) of your naiwar (youth), the ahabah (love) of your weddings; how you yalak (went) achar (other) me in the madabar (wilderness), in a aratz (Earth/land) that was not zarai (sown).

Yasharaal (Israel) was qadash (set apart/make holy) to Yahawah, the raashayath (beginning) fruits of his thabawaah (increase). Akal (eat) who devour him shall be asham (held) guilty. Rai (evil) shall bawaa (come) on them,"’ naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.
Shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, O bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and all the mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel)!

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, What iwal (unrighteousness) have your ab (father) matzaa (found) in me, that they have rachaq (gone) far from me, and have yalak (walked) achar (other) habal (vanity), and are habal (become) vain?

Neither did they amar (spoke), ‘Where is Yahawah who ilah (go up / offer) us up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), who yalak (led) us through the madabar (wilderness), through a aratz (Earth/land) of irabah (deserts) and of shawachah (pits), through a aratz (Earth/land) of tzayah (drought) and of the shadow of tzalamawath (death), through a aratz (Earth/land) that ayash (husband/individual man) ibar (pass over/through) through, and where no ayash (husband/individual man) lived?’

I bawaa (come) you into a karamal (plentiful) aratz (Earth/land), to akal (eat) its paray (fruit) and its goodness; but when you bawaa (come), you tamaa (defiled) my aratz (Earth/land), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) my nachalah (heritage) an thawaibah (abomination).

The kahan (priest) didn't amar (spoke), ‘Where is Yahawah?’ And those who thapash (handle) the thawarah (instruction) didn't yadai (know) me. The raih (rulers) also pashai (transgressed) against me, and the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) nabaa (prophesied) by Bail (Baal), and halak (move) achar (other) things that yail (do) not profit.
"Therefore I will yet rayab (contend) with you," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, and I will rayab (contend) with your ban (son) ban (son).

For ibar (pass over/through) over to the ay (islands) of Kathay (Kittim), and raah (see); and shalach (send) to Qadar (Kedar), and bayan (between) maad (diligently); and raah (see) if there has been such a thing.
Has a gaway (nation / people) mawar (changed) its Alahayam, which really are no Alahayam? But my im (people / nation) have mawar (changed) their kabawad (glory) for that which yail (does) not profit.
"Be shamam (astonished), you shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), at this, and be horribly shair (dread / storm / horror). Be very charab (desolate)," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

For my im (people / nation) ishah (make) committed shanayam (two) rai (evils): they have forsaken me, the maqawar (spring) of chay (life) mayam (Waters), and chatzab (cut) them out baar (cisterns), shabar (broken) baar (cisterns), that kawal (all/every/entire) hold no mayam (Waters).
Is Yasharaal (Israel) a ibad (servant)? Is he a native-born slave? Madawai (why) has he become a baz (prey)?

The young kapayar (lions) have shaag (roared) at him, and yelled. They have shayath (put / appoint / make) his aratz (Earth/land) shamah (waste). His iyar (cities) are yatzath (burned) up, without yashab (inhabit/dwell).
The ban (son) Nap (also) of Memphis and Thachapanachas (Tahpanhes) have raih (broken) the qadaqad (crown) of your head.
Haven't you ishah (make) this to yourself, in that you have forsaken Yahawah your Alahayam, when he yalak (led) you by the darak (way)?

Now what have you to do in the darak (way) to Matzarayam (Egypt), to shathah (drinks) the mayam (Waters) of the Shayachawar (Shihor)? Or what have you to do in the darak (way) to Ashawar (Assyria), to shathah (drinks) the mayam (Waters) of the nahar (river)?

"Your own rai (wickedness) shall yasar (correct) you, and your mashawabah (backsliding) shall yakach (reprove) you. Yadai (know) therefore and raah (see) that it is an rai (evil) thing and a mar (bitter), that you have forsaken Yahawah your Alahayam, and that my pachadah (fear) is not in you," naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (troop).

“For of iwalam (forever) time I have shabar (broken) your il (over), and nathaq (burst) your mawasar (bonds); and you amar (spoke), ‘I will not ibad (servant);’ for on every gabah (high) gabaih (hill) and under every rainan (green) itz (tree) you bowed yourself, zanah (playing) the prostitute.
Yet I had natai (planted) you a sharaq (noble) vine, wholly a amath (truth) zarai (seed). How then have you hapak (turned) into the sawar (degenerate) branches of a foreign gapan (vine) to me?
For though you kabas (wash) yourself with lye, and use much soap, yet your iwan (guilt/iniquity) is katham (marked) panayam (before) me,” naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

How can you amar (spoke), ‘I am not tamaa (defiled). I have not halak (move) achar (other) the Bail (Baals)’? Raah (see) your darak (way) in the gayaa (valley). Yadai (know) what you ishah (make) done. You are a qal (swift) bakarah (dromedary) sharak (traversing) her darak (ways);

A paraa (wild) donkey used to the madabar (wilderness), that shaap (snuffs) up the rawach (spirit / wind) in her awah (desire). When she is in heat, who can shawab (turn back / repent) her away? All those who baqash (seek) her will not yaip (weary) themselves. In her chadash (month), they will matzaa (find) her.

Manai (withhold) your ragal (feet / foot) from yachap (being) unshod, and your throat from tzamaah (thirst). But you amar (spoke), ‘It is in vain. No, for I have ahab (love) strangers, and I will yalak (go) achar (other) them.’

As the ganab (thief) is bashath (ashamed) when he is matzaa (found), so is the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) bashath (ashamed); they, their malak (king), their shar (prince / ruler), and their kahan (priest), and their nabayaa (prophet/prophecy);

Who amar (spoke) itz (wood), ‘You are my ab (father);’ and a aban (stone), ‘You have yalad (birth / begot) me out:’ for they have panah (turned) their irap (neck) to me, and not their panayam (face); but in the ith (time) of their rai (trouble) they will amar (spoke), ‘qawam (rise up), and yashai (salvation) us.’

But where are your Alahayam that you ishah (make) made for yourselves? Let them qawam (rise up), if they can yashai (salvation) you in the ith (time) of your rai (trouble): for according to the masapar (number) of your iyar (cities) are your Alahayam, Yahawadah (Judah).
"Why will you rayab (contend) with me? You all have pashai (transgressed) against me," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

I have nakah (struck) your ban (son) in shawaa (vanity). They laqach (take / seized) no mawasar (correction). Your own charab (sword) has akal (eat) your nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), like a shachath (destroying) aray (lion).

Dawar (generation / age / period), raah (see) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah. Have I been a madabar (wilderness) to Yasharaal (Israel)? Or a aratz (Earth/land) of thick maapalayah (darkness)? Why do my im (people / nation) amar (spoke), ‘We rawad (have) broken loose. We will bawaa (come) to you no more?’

Can a bathawalah (virgin) shakach (forget) her iday (ornament / adornment), or a kalah (complete / finish) her qashar (attire)? Yet my im (people / nation) have shakach (forgotten) me for yawam (day) without masapar (number).
How yatab (well) you prepare your darak (way) to baqash (seek) ahabah (love)! Therefore you have lamad (teach/instruct) even the rai (wicked) women your darak (ways).

Also the dam (blood) of the napash (living being/soul) of the naqay (innocent) abayawan (poor) is matzaa (found) in your kanap (skirts). You did not matzaa (find) them machatharath (breaking) in; but it is because of all these things.

Yet you amar (spoke), ‘I am naqah (clean/innocent). Surely his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) has shawab (turn back / repent) away from me.’ Behold, I will shapat (judge) you, because you amar (spoke), ‘I have not chataa (sinned).’
Why do you azal (go) about so much to shanah (change) your darak (way)? You will be bawash (ashamed) of Matzarayam (Egypt) also, as you were bawash (ashamed) of Ashawar (Assyria).

From there also you shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, with your yad (hand) on your raash (head); for Yahawah has maas (rejected) those in whom you mabatach (trust), and you shall not tzalach (prosper) with them.

"They amar (spoke), ‘If a ayash (husband/individual man) shalach (send) away his ashah (wife/individual woman), and she halak (move) from him, and become achar (other) ayash (husband/individual man), will he shawab (turn back / repent) to her again?’ Wouldn't that aratz (Earth/land) be chanap (greatly) chanap (polluted)? But you have zanah (played) the prostitute with many rai (neigbor/another person); yet shawab (turn back / repent) again to me," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

Nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye) to the bare heights, and raah (see)! Ayapah (where) have you not been shagal (lain) with? You have yashab (inhabit/dwell) for them by the darak (ways), as an Irabay (Arabian) in the madabar (wilderness). You have chanap (polluted) the aratz (Earth/land) with your prostitution and with your rai (wickedness).
Therefore the rabayab (showers) have been withheld, and there has been no malaqawash (latter) rain; yet you have a prostitute's matzach (forehead), you maan (refused) to be kalam (ashamed).
Will you not from this time qaraa (called) to me, ‘My ab (father), you are the alawap (guide) of my naiwar (youth)?’
‘Will he retain his anger forever? Will he shamar (keep/guard) it to the natzach (end)?’ Behold, you have dabar (word / matter) and ishah (make) done rai (evil) things, and yakal (have) had your way.

Moreover, Yahawah amar (spoke) to me in the yawam (day) of Yaashayah (Josiah) the malak (king), “raah (see) you seen that which mashawabah (backsliding) Yasharaal (Israel) ishah (make) done? She has halak (move) up on every gabah (high) har (mountain) and under every rainan (green) itz (tree), and there has zanah (played) the prostitute.

I amar (spoke) achar (other) she ishah (make) done all these things, ‘She will shawab (turn back / repent) to me;’ but she didn't shawab (turn back / repent); and her bagawad (treacherous) achawath (sister) Yahawadah (Judah) raah (see) it.

I raah (see), when, for this very awadawath (cause) that mashawabah (backsliding) Yasharaal (Israel) had naap (committed) adultery, I had shalach (send) her away and nathan (give) her a sapar (book / scribed document) of karayathawath (divorce), yet bagad (treacherous) Yahawadah (Judah), her achawath (sister), didn't yaraa (fear / be afraid); but she also yalak (went) and zanah (played) the prostitute.
It happened through the qawal (sound / voice) of her prostitution, that the aratz (Earth/land) was chanap (polluted), and she naap (committed) adultery with aban (stone) and with itz (stocks).

Yet for all this her bagawad (treacherous) achawath (sister), Yahawadah (Judah), has not shawab (turn back / repent) to me with her whole lab (heart), but only in pretense,” naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.
Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, mashawabah (backsliding) Yasharaal (Israel) napash (living being/soul) shown herself more tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) than bagad (treacherous) Yahawadah (Judah).

Halak (move), and qaraa (called) these dabar (word / matter) toward the tzapawan (north), and amar (spoke), ‘shawab (turn back / repent), you mashawabah (backsliding) Yasharaal (Israel),’ naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah; ‘I will not look in panayam (anger) on you; for I am chasayad (merciful),’ naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah. ‘I will not natar (keep) anger forever.

Only yadai (acknowledge) your iwan (guilt/iniquity), that you have pashai (transgressed) against Yahawah your Alahayam, and have pazar (scattered) your darak (ways) to the strangers under every rainan (green) itz (tree), and you have not shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice),’ naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

"Shawab (turn back / repent), shawabab (backsliding) ban (son)," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah; "for I am a bail (husband) to you. I will laqach (take / seized) you achad (one) of a iyar (city), and shanayam (two) of a mashapachah (tribe/clan/family), and I will bawaa (come) you to Tzayawan (Zion).
I will nathan (give) you raih (shepherds) according to my lab (heart), who shall raih (feed) you with daih (knowledge) and shakal (understanding).

It shall come to pass, when you are rabah (multiplied) and parah (increased) in the aratz (Earth/land), in those yawam (day)," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, they shall amar (spoke) no more, ‘The arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah!’ Neither shall it ilah (go up / offer) to lab (heart); neither shall they zakar (remembrance/memory) it; neither shall they paqad (visit) it; neither shall it be ishah (make) any more.

At that ith (time) they shall qaraa (called) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) ‘The kasaa (throne) of Yahawah;’ and all the gaway (nation / people) shall be qawah (gather/wait) to it, to the sham (name) of Yahawah, to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem). Neither shall they yalak (walk) any more achar (other) the stubbornness of their rai (evil) lab (heart).

In those yawam (day) the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) shall yalak (walk) with the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), and they shall bawaa (come) yachad (together) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of the tzapawan (north) to the aratz (Earth/land) that I gave for an nachal (inheritance) to your ab (father).

But I amar (spoke), ‘How I would shayath (put / appoint / make) you among the ban (son), and nathan (give) you a chamadah (pleasant) aratz (Earth/land), a tzabay (goodly) nachalah (heritage) of the tzabaa (troop) of the gaway (nation / people)!’ And I amar (spoke), ‘You shall qaraa (called) me "My ab (father)," and shall not shawab (turn back / repent) away from achar (other) me.’

"Akan (surely) as a ashah (wife/individual woman) bagad (treacherously) departs from her rai (neigbor/another person), so you have dealt bagad (treacherously) with me, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel)," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

A qawal (sound / voice) is shamai (hearken / hear) on the bare heights, the bakay (weeping) and the petitions of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel); because they have iwah (perverted) their darak (way), they have shakach (forgotten) Yahawah their Alahayam.
Shawab (turn back / repent), you shawabab (backsliding) ban (son), I will rapaa (heal) your mashawabah (backsliding). Behold, we have athah (come) to you; for you are Yahawah our Alahayam.
Akan (truly) in shaqar (vain) is help from the gabaih (hills), the hamawan (tumult) on the har (mountain). Akan (truly) the thashawaih (deliverance) of Yasharaal (Israel) is in Yahawah our Alahayam.
But the shameful thing has akal (eat) the yagayai (labor) of our ab (father) from our naiwar (youth), their tzaan (flocks) and their baqar (morning), their ban (son) and their bath (daughter).

Let us shakab (lie) down in our bashath (shame), and let our kalamah (confusion) kasah (cover) us; for we have chataa (sinned) against Yahawah our Alahayam, we and our ab (father), from our naiwar (youth) even to this yawam (day). We have not shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah our Alahayam.

"If you will shawab (turn back / repent), Yasharaal (Israel)," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, if you will shawab (turn back / repent) to me, and if you will sawar (put) away your shaqawatz (abominations) out of my panayam (sight); then you shall not be nawad (removed);

And you shall shabai (swear / take oath), ‘As Yahawah chay (life),’ in amath (truth), in mashapat (justice), and in tzadaqah (righteousness). The gaway (nation / people) shall barak (bless) themselves in him, and in him shall they glory.

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah to the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yahawadah (Judah) and to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), nayar (break) up your fallow nayar (ground), and don't zarai (sow) among qawatz (thorns).

Mawal (circumcise) yourselves to Yahawah, and sawar (take) away the iralah (foreskins) of your labab (heart), you ayash (husband/individual man) of Yahawadah (Judah) and yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); lest my chamah (wrath) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth like ash (fire), and bair (burn) so that none can kabah (quench) it, panayam (because) of the rai (evil) of your mailal (doings).

Nagad (declare) in Yahawadah (Judah), and shamai (hearken / hear) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); and amar (spoke), ‘thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)) in the aratz (Earth/land)!’ Qaraa (called) aloud and amar (spoke), ‘asap (assemble) yourselves! Bawaa (come) us go into the fortified iyar (cities)!’

Nashaa (lift) up a nas (standard) toward Tzayawan (Zion). Iwaz (flee) for safety! Don't wait; for I will bawaa (come) rai (evil) from the tzapawan (north), and a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shabar (destruction).

A aray (lion) is ilah (go up / offer) up from his sabak (thicket), and a destroyer of gaway (nation / people); he is on his nasai (way), he is yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from his maqawam (place), to shawam (place / establish / appoint) your aratz (Earth/land) shamah (desolate), that your iyar (cities) be natzah (laid) waste, without yashab (inhabit/dwell).
For this clothe yourself with sackcloth, sapad (lament) and wail; for the charawan (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah hasn't shawab (turn back / repent) back from us.

"It shall happen at that yawam (day)," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, that the lab (heart) of the malak (king) shall abad (destroy/perish), and the lab (heart) of the shar (prince / ruler); and the kahan (priest) shall be shamam (astonished), and the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) shall thamah (wonder).

Then I amar (spoke), ahah (ah), Adanay Yahawah! Akan (surely) you have nashaa (lift) nashaa (lift) this im (people / nation) and Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), amar (spoke), ‘You shall have shalawam (peace / safety);’ whereas the charab (sword) reaches to the napash (living being/soul).

At that ith (time) shall it be amar (spoke) to this im (people / nation) and to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), A hot rawach (spirit / wind) from the bare heights in the madabar (wilderness) darak (toward) the bath (daughter) of my im (people / nation), not to zarah (winnow), nor to barar (cleanse);
A malaa (full) rawach (spirit / wind) from these shall bawaa (come) for me. Now I will also dabar (word / matter) mashapat (judgments) against them.

Behold, he shall ilah (go up / offer) up as inan (cloud), and his marakabah (chariots) shall be as the sawapah (whirlwind): his sawas (horses) are qalal (swifter) than nashar (eagles). Away (woe) to us! For we are ruined.

Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), kabas (wash) your lab (heart) from rai (wickedness), that you may be yashai (salvation). How long shall your awan (evil) machashabah (thoughts) lawan (lodge) qarab (among / near) you?
For a qawal (sound / voice) nagad (declares) Dan (from) Dan, and publishes awan (evil) Aparayam (from) the hills of Aparayam (Ephraim):

"Tell the gaway (nation / people); behold, shamai (hearken / hear) against Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), ‘natzar (watchers) bawaa (come) from a marachaq (far) aratz (Earth/land), and raise their qawal (sound / voice) against the iyar (cities) of Yahawadah (Judah).
As keepers of a shadah (field), they are against her all around, because she has been rebellious against me,’" naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.
Your darak (way) and your mailal (doings) ishah (make) brought these things to you. This is your rai (wickedness); for it is mar (bitter), for it reaches to your lab (heart).

My anguish, my anguish! I am chawal (pained) at my very lab (heart); my lab (heart) is hamah (they) in me; I can't hold my charash (peace); because you have shamai (hearken / hear), O my napash (living being/soul), the qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), the tharawaih (alarm) of malachamah (war).

Shabar (destruction) on shabar (destruction) is qaraa (called); for the whole aratz (Earth/land) is laid shadad (waste): pathaawam (suddenly) are my ahal (tents) shadad (destroyed), and my yarayaih (curtains) in a ragai (in an instance).
How long shall I raah (see) the nas (standard), and shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument))?

For my im (people / nation) are awayal (foolish), they don't yadai (know) me. They are sakal (foolish) ban (son), and they have no bayan (between). They are skillful in doing raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil), but to do yatab (good) they have no yadai (knowledge).
I raah (see) the aratz (Earth/land), and, behold, it was thahaw (formless) and bahaw (void); and the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), and they had no awar (light).
I raah (see) the har (mountain), and behold, they raish (trembled), and all the gabaih (hills) qalal (moved) back and forth.
I raah (see), and behold, there was no adam (man), and all the iwap (flying) of the sky had nadad (fled).

I raah (see), and behold, the karamal (fruitful) field was a madabar (wilderness), and all its iyar (cities) were nathatz (broken) down at the panayam (presence) of Yahawah, before his charawan (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).
For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, The whole aratz (Earth/land) shall be a shamamah (desolation); yet will I not ishah (make) a kalah (complete / finish) end.

For this the aratz (Earth/land) will abal (mourn), and the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) mail (top/above) be qadar (black); because I have dabar (word / matter) it, I have zamam (purposed) it, and I have not nacham (turn away / repent), neither will I shawab (turn back / repent) back from it.

Every iyar (city) barach (flees) for the qawal (sound / voice) of the horsemen and qashath (archers); they bawaa (come) into the ib (thickets), and ilah (go up / offer) up on the kap (rocks): every iyar (city) is forsaken, and not a ayash (husband/individual man) yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein.

You, when you are made desolate, what will you ishah (make)? Though you labash (clothe) yourself with shanay (second), though you idah (deck) you with iday (ornament / adornment) of zahab (gold), though you enlarge your iyan (eye) with pawak (paint), in shawaa (vanity) do you make yourself yapah (beautiful); your igab (lovers) maas (despise) you, they baqash (seek) your napash (living being/soul).

For I have shamai (hearken / hear) a qawal (sound / voice) as of a chalah (afflict) in travail, the tzarah (anguish) as of her who brings forth her bakar (first) child, the qawal (sound / voice) of the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion), who gasps for breath, who parash (spreads) her kap (hands), saying, away (woe) is me now! For my napash (living being/soul) faints before the harag (murderers).

Shawat (run) back and forth through the chawatz (streets) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and raah (see) now, and yadai (know), and baqash (seek) in the rachab (broad) places of it, if you can matzaa (find) a ayash (husband/individual man), if there are any who ishah (make) justly, who baqash (seeks) amawanah (truth); and I will salach (forgive/pardon/make clean) her.
Though they amar (spoke), ‘As Yahawah chay (life);’ surely they shabai (swear / take oath) falsely.

O Yahawah, don't your iyan (eye) look on amawanah (truth)? You have nakah (stricken) them, but they were not chawal (grieved). You kalah (complete / finish) consumed them, but they have maan (refused) to laqach (take / seized) mawasar (correction). They have made their panayam (faces) harder than a salai (rock). They have maan (refused) to shawab (turn back / repent).
Then I amar (spoke), "Surely these are dal (poor). They are yaal (foolish); for they don't yadai (know) the darak (way) of Yahawah, nor the mashapat (law) of their Alahayam.

I will yalak (go) to the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) men, and will dabar (word / matter) to them; for they yadai (know) the darak (way) of Yahawah, and the mashapat (law) of their Alahayam." But these with yachad (one) accord have shabar (broken) the il (over), and nathaq (burst) the mawasar (bonds).

Therefore a aray (lion) out of the yair (forest) shall nakah (kill) them, a zaab (wolf) of the irabah (evenings) shall shadad (destroy) them, a namar (leopard) shall shaqad (watch) against their iyar (cities); everyone who yatzaa (go out / come out) out there shall be tarap (torn) in pieces; because their pashai (transgressions) are many, and their mashawabah (backsliding) is itzam (increased).

"Ay (how) can I salach (forgive/pardon/make clean) you? Your ban (son) have forsaken me, and shabai (swear / take oath) by what are no Alahayam. When I had shabai (swear / take oath) them to the full, they naap (committed) adultery, and gadad (assembled) themselves in troops at the prostitutes' bayath (house).
They were as zawan (fed) sawas (horses) roaming at large: everyone tzahal (neighed) after his neighbor's ashah (wife/individual woman).
Shouldn't I paqad (visit) them for these things?" Naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah; and shouldn't my napash (living being/soul) be naqam (avenged) on such a gaway (nation / people) as this?

"Ilah (go up / offer) up on her sharah (walls), and shachath (destroy); but don't ishah (make) a kalah (complete / finish) end. Sawar (take) away her branches; for they are not yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)).
For the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) and the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) have dealt very bagad (treacherously) against me," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.
They have kachash (denied) Yahawah, and amar (spoke), It is not he; neither shall rai (evil) bawaa (come) on us; neither shall we raah (see) charab (sword) nor raib (famine).
The nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) shall become rawach (spirit / wind), and the word is not in them. Thus shall it be ishah (make) to them.

Therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (troop), "Because you dabar (word / matter) this dabar (word / matter), behold, I will nathan (give) my dabar (word / matter) in your pah (mouth) ash (fire), and this im (people / nation) itz (wood), and it shall akal (eat) them.

Behold, I will bawaa (come) a gaway (nation / people) on you from marachaq (far), bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel)," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah. It is a ayathan (mighty) gaway (nation / people). It is an iwalam (forever) gaway (nation / people), a gaway (nation / people) whose lashawan (tongue/language) you don't yadai (know), neither shamai (hearken / hear) what they dabar (word / matter).
Their ashapah (quiver) is an pathach (open) tomb, they are all gabawar (mighty) men.

They shall akal (eat) up your qatzayar (harvest), and your lacham (bread), which your ban (son) and your bath (daughter) should akal (eat). They shall akal (eat) up your tzaan (flocks) and your baqar (morning). They shall akal (eat) up your gapan (vines) and your thaan (fig) trees. They shall beat down your fortified iyar (cities), in which you batach (trust), with the charab (sword).
"But even in those yawam (day)," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, I will not ishah (make) a kalah (complete / finish) end with you.

It will happen, when you amar (spoke), ‘Why has Yahawah our Alahayam ishah (make) all these things to us?’ Then you shall amar (spoke) to them, ‘Just like you have forsaken me, and ibad (servant) foreign Alahayam in your aratz (Earth/land), so you shall ibad (servant) strangers in a aratz (Earth/land) that is not yours.’
Nagad (declare) this in the bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and shamai (hearken / hear) it in Yahawadah (Judah), amar (spoke),
‘Shamai (hearken / hear) now this, sakal (foolish) im (people / nation), and without lab (heart); who have iyan (eye), and don't raah (see); who have azan (ears), and don't shamai (hearken / hear):

Don't you yaraa (fear / be afraid) me?’ Naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah ‘Won't you chawal (tremble) at my panayam (presence), who have shawam (place / establish / appoint) the chawal (sand) for the gabawal (border/boundary) of the yam (sea/waters), by a iwalam (forever) chaq (statute), that it can't ibar (pass over/through) it? And though its gal (waves) gaish (toss) themselves, yet they can't yakal (prevail); though they hamah (they), yet they can't ibar (pass over/through) over it.’
But this im (people / nation) has a sarar (revolting) and a rebellious lab (heart); they have sawar (revolted) and yalak (gone).

Neither do they amar (spoke) in their labab (heart), ‘Let us now yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah our Alahayam, who nathan (give) gasham (rain), both the yawarah (former) and the malaqawash (latter), in its ith (season); who shamar (keep/guard) to us the chaqah (appointed) shabawai (weeks) of the qatzayar (harvest).’
Your iwan (guilt/iniquity) have natah (turned) away these things, and your chataah (sin) have withheld tawab (pleasant/functional) from you.

For among my im (people / nation) are matzaa (found) rashai (wicked) men. They watch, as yaqawash (fowlers) lie in shawar (wait). They natzab (set) a mashachayath (trap). They lakad (catch) im (people / nation).
As a kalawab (cage) is malaa (full) of iwap (flying), so are their bayath (house) malaa (full) of maramah (deceit). Therefore they have become gadal (great), and grew ishar (rich).

They have grown shaman (fat). They ishath (shine); yes, they excell in dabar (word / matter) of rai (wickedness). They don't plead the dayan (judge), the cause of the yathawam (fatherless), that they may tzalach (prosper); and they don't shapat (judge) the mashapat (right) of the abayawan (needy).
"Shall I not paqad (visit) for these things?" Naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah. Shall not my napash (living being/soul) be naqam (avenged) on such a gaway (nation / people) as this?
An astonishing and shairawarah (horrible) thing hayah (came to pass) happened in the aratz (Earth/land).

The nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) nabaa (prophesy) falsely, and the kahan (priest) radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) by their yad (hand) authority; and my im (people / nation) ahab (love) to ishah (make) it so. What will you do in the acharayath (end) of it?

Iwaz (flee) for safety, you ban (son) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), out of the qarab (among / near) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)) in Thaqawai (Tekoa), and nashaa (lift) up a signal on Bayathahakaram (Beth) Haccherem; for rai (evil) shaqap (looks) forth from the tzapawan (north), and a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shabar (destruction).
The naawah (comely) and inag (delicate) one, the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion), will I cut off.
Raih (shepherds) with their idar (flocks) shall bawaa (come) to her; they shall thaqai (blow / sound alarm) their ahal (tents) against her all around; they shall raih (feed) everyone in his place.

Qadash (set apart/make holy) malachamah (war) against her; qawam (rise up), and let us ilah (go up / offer) up at tzahar (noon). Away (woe) to us! For the yawam (day) declines, for the tzalal (shadows) of the irab (evening) are natah (stretched) out.
Qawam (rise up), and let us ilah (go up / offer) up by layal (night), and let us shachath (destroy) her aramawan (palaces).

For Yahawah of tzabaa (troop) amar (spoke), karath (cut) down itzah (trees), and shapak (cast) up a mound against Yarawashalam (Jerusalem): this is the iyar (city) to be paqad (visit); she is wholly ishaq (oppression) in the qarab (among / near) of her.

As a bawar (well) qawar (casts) forth its mayam (Waters), so she qawar (casts) forth her rai (wickedness): chamas (violence) and shad (destruction) is shamai (hearken / hear) in her; panayam (before) me continually is chalay (sickness) and makah (wounds).

Be yasar (instructed), Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), lest my napash (living being/soul) be yaqai (alienated) from you; lest I shawam (place / establish / appoint) you a shamamah (desolation), a aratz (Earth/land) not yashab (inhabit/dwell).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaa (troop), They shall ilal (thoroughly) ilal (glean) the shaarayath (remnant) of Yasharaal (Israel) like a gapan (vine). Shawab (turn back / repent) again your yad (hand) as a grape batzar (gatherer) into the salasalah (baskets).

To whom shall I dabar (word / matter) and testify, that they may shamai (hearken / hear)? Behold, their azan (ear) is iral (uncircumcised), and they can't listen. Behold, the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah has become a charapah (reproach) to them. They chapatz (have) no delight in it.

Therefore I am malaa (full) of the chamah (wrath) of Yahawah. I am laah (weary) with kawal (all/every/entire) in. Shapak (pour) it out on the iwalal (children) in the chawatz (street), and on the sawad (assembly) of bachawar (young) men yachad (together); for even the ayash (husband/individual man) with the ashah (wife/individual woman) shall be lakad (taken), the zaqan (aged) with him who is malaa (full) of yawam (day).

Their bayath (house) shall be sabab (turned) to others, their shadah (fields) and their wives yachad (together); for I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the aratz (Earth/land), naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

“For from their qatan (small/young/least) even to their greatest, everyone is batzai (given) to batzai (covetousness); and from the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) even to the kahan (priest), everyone ishah (make) falsely.

They have rapaa (healed) also the shabar (hurt) of my im (people / nation) superficially, amar (spoke), ‘shalawam (peace / safety), shalawam (peace / safety)!’ When there is no shalawam (peace / safety).

Were they yabash (dry land) when they ishah (make) committed thawaibah (abomination)? No, they were not at all bawash (ashamed), gam (indeed / moreover) yadai (could) they kalam (blush). Therefore they shall napal (fall / be cast down) among those who napal (fall / be cast down); at the ith (time) that I paqad (visit) them, they shall be kashal (stumble / stagger) down,” amar (spoke) Yahawah.
