It happened in the thashayaiy (ninth) shanah (year) of his malak (king), in the ishayaray (tenth) chadash (month), in the ishawar (tenth) day of the chadash (month), that Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) bawaa (come), he and all his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), against Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and chanah (encamped) against it; and they banah (built) dayaq (forts) against it sabayab (surrounding) about.
So the iyar (city) was matzawar (besieged) to the ishathay (eleven) shanah (year) of malak (king) Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah).

In the rabayaiy (fourth) chadash (month), in the thashai (nine) day of the chadash (month), the raib (famine) was severe in the iyar (city), so that there was no lacham (bread) for the im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land).

Then a baqai (breach) was made in the iyar (city), and all the ayash (husband/individual man) of malachamah (war) barach (fled), and yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the iyar (city) by layal (night) by the darak (way) of the shair (gate) between the two chawamah (walls), which was by the malak (king) gan (garden); (now the Kashaday (Chaldeans) were against the iyar (city) all around;) and they yalak (went) toward the irabah (arabah).

But the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans) radap (pursued) achar (other) the malak (king), and overtook Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah) in the irabah (plains) of Yarayachaw (Jericho); and all his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) was pawatz (scattered) from him.

Then they thapash (took) the malak (king), and ilah (go up / offer) him up to the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) to Rabalah (Riblah) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Chamath (Hamath); and he dabar (word / matter) mashapat (judgment) on him.

The malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) shachat (killed) the ban (son) of Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah) before his iyan (eye): he shachat (killed) also all the shar (prince / ruler) of Yahawadah (Judah) in Rabalah (Riblah).

He iwar (put) out the iyan (eye) of Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah); and the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) asar (bound) him in nachashath (fetters), and bawaa (come) him to Babal (Babylon), and nathan (give) him in bayath (house) until the yawam (day) of his mawath (death).

Now in the chamayashay (fifth) chadash (month), in the ishawar (tenth) day of the chadash (month), which was the nineteenth shanah (year) of malak (king) Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar), malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), bawaa (come) Nabawazaraadan (Nebuzaradan) the rab (captain) of the tabach (guard), who stood before the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), into Yarawashalam (Jerusalem):

And he sharap (burned) the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the malak (king) bayath (house); and all the bayath (house) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), even every gadawal (very great/important/mighty) bayath (house), sharap (burned) he with ash (fire).

All the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), who were with the rab (captain) of the tabach (guard), nathatz (broke) down all the chawamah (walls) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) all around.

Then Nabawazaraadan (Nebuzaradan) the rab (captain) of the tabach (guard) galah (carried) away captive of the poorest of the im (people / nation), and the yathar (residue) of the im (people / nation) who were shaar (left) in the iyar (city), and those who napal (fall / be cast down) away, who napal (fall / be cast down) to the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), and the yathar (residue) of the amawan (multitude).
But Nabawazaraadan (Nebuzaradan) the rab (captain) of the tabach (guard) shaar (left) of the poorest of the aratz (Earth/land) to be vineyard keepers and farmers.

The Kashaday (Chaldeans) shabar (broke) the imawad (pillar) of nachashath (brass) that were in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the makawanah (bases) and the bronze yam (sea/waters) that were in the bayath (house) of Yahawah in pieces, and nashaa (lift) all the of their nachashath (brass) to Babal (Babylon).

They also laqach (take / seized) away the sayar (pots), the yai (shovels), the mazamarah (snuffers), the basins, the kap (spoons), and all the kalay (vessels) of nachashath (brass) with which they sharath (ministered).

The rab (captain) of the tabach (guard) laqach (take / seized) laqach (take / seized) the cups, the machathah (fire) pans, the basins, the sayar (pots), the lampstands, the kap (spoons), and the manaqayath (bowls); that which was of zahab (gold), in zahab (gold), and that which was of kasap (silver), in kasap (silver).

They took the shanayam (two) imawad (pillar), the achad (one) yam (sea/waters), and the shanayam (two) bronze baqar (morning) that were under the makawanah (bases), which malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon) ishah (make) made for the bayath (house) of Yahawah. The nachashath (brass) of all these kalay (vessels) was without mashaqal (weight).

As for the imawad (pillar), the qawamah (height) of the achad (one) imawad (pillar) was eighteen amah (cubits); and a chawat (line) of shanayam (two) amah (cubits) encircled it; and its ibay (thickness) was arabai (four) atzabai (fingers). It was nabab (hollow).

A capital of nachashath (brass) was on it; and the qawamah (height) of the achad (one) capital was chamash (five) amah (cubits), with shabakah (network) and ramawan (pomegranates) on the capital all around, all of nachashath (brass): and the shanay (second) imawad (pillar) also had like these, and ramawan (pomegranates).
There were thashaiyam (ninety) - shash (six) ramawan (pomegranates) on the rawach (spirit / wind); all the ramawan (pomegranates) were one maah (hundred) on the shabakah (network) all around.

The rab (captain) of the tabach (guard) laqach (take / seized) Sharayah (Seraiah) the raash (head) kahan (priest), and Tzapanayah (Zephaniah) the mashanah (second) kahan (priest), and the shalawash (three) keepers of the sap (threshold):

And out of the iyar (city) he laqach (take / seized) an sarayas (officer) who paqayad (was) set over the achad (one) of malachamah (war); and shabai (seven) achad (one) of those who raah (see) the malak (king) panayam (face), who were matzaa (found) in the iyar (city); and the sapar (book) of the shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop), who tzabaa (troop) the im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land); and shashayam (sixty) ayash (husband/individual man) of the im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land), who were matzaa (found) in the thawak (midst) of the iyar (city).
Nabawazaraadan (Nebuzaradan) the rab (captain) of the tabach (guard) laqach (take / seized) them, and yalak (brought) them to the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) to Rabalah (Riblah).

The malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) nakah (struck) them, and put them to mawath (death) at Rabalah (Riblah) in the adamah (land) of Chamath (Hamath). So Yahawadah (Judah) was galah (carried) away captive out of his aratz (Earth/land).

This is the im (people / nation) whom Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) galah (carried) away captive: in the shabai (seven) shanah (year) shalawash (three) alap (thousand) isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three) Yahawaday (Jews);

In the eighteenth shanah (year) of Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) he carried away captive from Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) napash (living being/soul);

In the shalawash (three) and isharayam (twenty) shanah (year) of Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) Nabawazaraadan (Nebuzaradan) the rab (captain) of the tabach (guard) galah (carried) away captive of the Yahawaday (Jews) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - chamash (five) napash (living being/soul): all the napash (living being/soul) were arabai (four) alap (thousand) and shash (six) maah (hundred).

It happened in the shabai (seven) and shalawashayam (thirty) shanah (year) of the galawath (captivity) of Yahawayakayan (Jehoiachin) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), in the shanayam (two) chadash (month), in the chamash (five) and isharayam (twenty) day of the chadash (month), that awayalamaradak (evilmerodach) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), in the first shanah (year) of his malakawath (reign), nashaa (lift) up the raash (head) of Yahawayakayan (Jehoiachin) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and yatzaa (go out / come out) him forth out of bayath (house);
And he dabar (word / matter) tawab (pleasant/functional) to him, and nathan (give) his kasaa (throne) mail (top/above) the kasaa (throne) of the malak (king) who were with him in Babal (Babylon),
And shanah (changed) his kalaa (prison) bagad (garments). Jehoiachin akal (eat) lacham (bread) panayam (before) him continually all the yawam (day) of his chay (life):

And for his arachah (allowance), there was a thamayad (continual) arachah (allowance) nathan (give) him by the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), every yawam (day) a dabar (word / matter) until the yawam (day) of his mawath (death), all the yawam (day) of his chay (life).

How the iyar (city) yashab (inhabit/dwell) badad (solitary), that was rab (full) of im (people / nation)! She has become as a alamanah (widow), who was rab (great) among the gaway (nation / people)! She who was a sharah (princess) among the madayanah (provinces) has become mas (tributary)!

She bakah (weeps) bitterly in the layal (night), and her damaih (tears) are on her lachay (cheeks); among all her lovers she has none to nacham (turn away / repent) her: All her rai (neigbor/another person) have dealt bagad (treacherously) with her; they are become her ayab (enemy).

Yahawadah (Judah) is galah (gone) into captivity because of inay (affliction), and because of rab (great) servitude; she yashab (inhabit/dwell) among the gaway (nation / people), she matzaa (finds) no manawach (rest): all her persecutors overtook her within the matzar (straits).

The darak (ways) of Tzayawan (Zion) do abal (mourn), because none bawaa (come) to the solemn mawaid (Feast/Holy Day); all her shair (gates) are shamam (desolate), her kahan (priest) do anach (sigh): her bathawalah (virgins) are yagah (afflicted), and she herself is in bitterness.

Her tzar (oppressor / distressor) are become the raash (head), her ayab (enemy) shalah (prosper); for Yahawah has yagah (afflicted) her for the rab (multitude) of her pashai (transgressions): her young iwalal (children) are halak (move) into shabay (captivity) panayam (before) the tzar (oppressor / distressor).

From the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion) all her hadar (glory / majesty / splendor) is departed: her shar (prince / ruler) are become like ayal (harts) that matzaa (find) no maraih (pasture), they are yalak (gone) without kach (strength / mighty / power) panayam (before) the radap (pursuer).

Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) zakar (remembrance/memory) in the yawam (day) of her inay (affliction) and of her marawad (miseries) all her machamad (pleasant) things that were from the yawam (day) of qadam (old): when her im (people / nation) napal (fall / be cast down) into the yad (hand) of the tzar (oppressor / distressor), and no one izar (helped) her, The tzar (oppressor / distressor) raah (see) her, they shachaq (mocked) at her desolations.

Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) has chataa (grievously) chataa (sinned); therefore she has become as an kabad (unclean) thing; all who honored her zawal (despise) her, because they raah (see) seen her irawah (nakedness): yes, she anach (sighs), and shawab (turn back / repent) backward.

Her tamaah (filthiness) was in her shawal (skirts); she didn't zakar (remembrance/memory) her acharayath (latter) end; therefore is she yarad (come) down wonderfully; she has no comforter: raah (see), Yahawah, my inay (affliction); for the ayab (enemy) has gadal (magnified) himself.

The tzar (oppressor / distressor) has parash (spread) out his yad (hand) on all her machamad (pleasant) things: for she raah (see) seen that the gaway (nation / people) are bawaa (come) into her maqadash (sanctuary), concerning whom you tzawah (commanded) that they should not bawaa (come) into your qahal (assembly).

All her im (people / nation) anach (sigh), they baqash (seek) lacham (bread); they nathan (give) given their machamad (pleasant) things for akal (food) to shawab (turn back / repent) the napash (living being/soul): raah (see), Yahawah, and raah (see); for I am become abject.

Is it nothing to you, ibar (pass over/through) you who pass by? Nabat (look), and raah (see) if there is any makaab (sorrow) like my makaab (sorrow), which is brought on me, With which Yahawah has yagah (afflicted) me in the yawam (day) of his charawan (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).

From on marawam (high) has he shalach (send) ash (fire) into my itzam (bones), and it radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) against them; He has parash (spread) a rashath (net) for my ragal (feet / foot), he has shawab (turn back / repent) me achawar (back): He nathan (give) made me shamam (desolate) and dawah (faint) all the yawam (day).

The il (over) of my pashai (transgressions) is shaqad (bound) by his yad (hand); They are knit together, they have ilah (go up / offer) up on my tzawaar (neck); he has made my kach (strength / mighty / power) to kashal (stumble / stagger): The Adanay nathan (give) delivered me into their yad (hand), against whom I am not yakal (able) to qawam (rise up).

The Adanay has set at nothing all my abayar (mighty) men in the qarab (among / near) of me; He has qaraa (called) a solemn mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) against me to shabar (crush) my bachawar (young) men: The Adanay has darak (trodden) as in a gath (winepress) the bathawalah (virgin) bath (daughter) of Yahawadah (Judah).

For these things I bakah (weep); my iyan (eye), my iyan (eye) yarad (runs) down with mayam (Waters); Because the comforter who should shawab (turn back / repent) my napash (living being/soul) is rachaq (far) from me: My ban (son) are shamam (desolate), because the ayab (enemy) has gabar (prevailed).

Tzayawan (Zion) parash (spreads) forth her yad (hand); there is none to nacham (turn away / repent) her; Yahawah has tzawah (commanded) concerning Yaiqab (Jacob), that those who are around him should be his tzar (oppressor / distressor): Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) is among them as an nadah (unclean) thing.

Yahawah is tzadayaq (righteous); for I have marah (rebelled) against his commandment: Please shamai (hearken / hear) all you im (people / nation), and raah (see) my makaab (sorrow): My bathawalah (virgins) and my bachawar (young) men are halak (move) into shabay (captivity).

I qaraa (called) for my lovers, but they ramah (deceived) me: My kahan (priest) and my zaqan (elders) gawai (gave) up the spirit in the iyar (city), While they baqash (sought) them akal (food) to shawab (turn back / repent) their napash (living being/soul).

Raah (see), Yahawah; for I am in tzarar (distress); my maih (heart) is chamar (troubled); My lab (heart) is hapak (turned) qarab (among / near) me; for I have marah (grievously) marah (rebelled): chawatz (abroad) the charab (sword) shakal (bereaves), at bayath (house) there is as mawath (death).

They have shamai (hearken / hear) that I anach (sigh); there is none to nacham (turn away / repent) me; All my ayab (enemy) have shamai (hearken / hear) of my rai (trouble); they are shawash (glad) that you ishah (make) done it: You will bawaa (come) the yawam (day) that you have qaraa (called), and they shall be kamaw (like) me.

Let all their rai (wickedness) bawaa (come) panayam (before) you; ilal (do) to them, as you have ilal (done) to me for all my pashai (transgressions): For my anachah (sighs) are many, and my lab (heart) is daway (faint).

How has the Adanay iwab (covered) the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion) with a iwab (cloud) in his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting)! He has shalak (cast) down from shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) to the aratz (Earth/land) the thapaarah (beauty) of Yasharaal (Israel), And hasn't zakar (remembrance/memory) his hadam (footstool) in the yawam (day) of his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).

The Adanay has balai (swallowed) up all the naah (habitations) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and chamal (has) not pitied: He has haras (thrown) down in his ibarah (wrath) the strongholds of the bath (daughter) of Yahawadah (Judah); He has nagai (brought) them down to the aratz (Earth/land); he has chalal (profaned) the mamalakah (kingdom) and its shar (prince / ruler).

He has gadai (cut) off in charay (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) all the qaran (horn) of Yasharaal (Israel); He has shawab (turn back / repent) achawar (back) his right yamayan (right hand) from panayam (before) the ayab (enemy): He has bair (burned) up Yaiqab (Jacob) like a lahabah (flaming) ash (fire), which akal (eat) all around.

He has bent his qashath (bow) like an ayab (enemy), he has natzab (stood) with his right yamayan (right hand) as an tzar (oppressor / distressor), Has harag (killed) all that were machamad (pleasant) to the iyan (eye): In the ahal (tent) of the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion) he has shapak (poured) out his chamah (wrath) like ash (fire).

The Adanay has become as an ayab (enemy), he has balai (swallowed) up Yasharaal (Israel); He has balai (swallowed) up all her aramawan (palaces), he has shachath (destroyed) his strongholds; He rabah (has) multiplied in the bath (daughter) of Yahawadah (Judah) thaanayah (mourning) and anayah (lamentation).

He has chamas (violently) taken away his shak (tabernacle), as if it were of a gan (garden); he has shachath (destroyed) his place of mawaid (Feast/Holy Day): Yahawah has caused solemn mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) and shabath (shabath/rest) to be shakach (forgotten) in Tzayawan (Zion), Has naatz (despised) in the zaim (indignation) of his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) the malak (king) and the kahan (priest).

The Adanay has zanach (cast) off his mazabach (altar), he has naar (abhorred) his maqadash (sanctuary); He has sagar (given) up into the yad (hand) of the ayab (enemy) the chawamah (walls) of her aramawan (palaces): They nathan (give) made a qawal (sound / voice) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, as in the yawam (day) of a solemn mawaid (Feast/Holy Day).

Yahawah has chashab (purposed) to shachath (destroy) the chawamah (wall) of the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion); He has natah (stretched) out the qaw (line), he has not shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand) from balai (destroying); He has made the chayal (rampart) and chawamah (wall) to abal (lament); they amal (languish) yachad (together).

Her shair (gates) are tabai (sunk) into the aratz (Earth/land); he abad (destroy/perish) destroyed and shabar (broken) her barayach (bars): Her malak (king) and her shar (prince / ruler) are among the gaway (nation / people) where the thawarah (instruction) is not; Yes, her nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) matzaa (find) no chazawan (vision) from Yahawah.

The zaqan (elders) of the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion) yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the aratz (Earth/land), they damam (keep) silence; They have ilah (go up / offer) up ipar (dust) on their raash (head); they have clothed themselves with sackcloth: The bathawalah (virgins) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) yarad (hang) down their raash (head) to the aratz (Earth/land).

My iyan (eye) kalah (complete / finish) fail with damaih (tears), my maih (heart) is chamar (troubled); My kabad (liver) is shapak (poured) on the aratz (Earth/land), because of the shabar (destruction) of the bath (daughter) of my im (people / nation), Because the young iwalal (children) and the infants itap (swoon) in the rachab (streets) of the qarayah (city).

They amar (spoke) their am (mother), Where is grain and yayan (wine)? When they itap (swoon) as the chalal (wounded) in the rachab (streets) of the iyar (city), When their napash (living being/soul) is shapak (poured) out into their am (mother)' chayaq (bosom).

What shall I iwad (admonish/bear witness against) to you? Mah (what) shall I damah (liken) to you, bath (daughter) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem)? What shall I shawah (compare) to you, that I may nacham (turn away / repent) you, bathawalah (virgin) bath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion)? For your shabar (breach) is gadawal (very great/important/mighty) like the yam (sea/waters): who can rapaa (heal) you?

Your nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) have chazah (seen) for you shawaa (vanity) and thapal (foolish) visions; They have not galah (uncovered) your iwan (guilt/iniquity), to shawab (turn back / repent) back your shabawath (captivity), but have chazah (seen) for you shawaa (vanity) oracles and madawach (causes) of banishment.

Ibar (pass over/through) that pass by sapaq (clap) their kap (hands) at you. They sharaq (hiss) and nawai (wag) their raash (head) at the bath (daughter) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), saying, Is this the iyar (city) that men amar (spoke) The kalayal (perfection) of yapay (beauty), The mashawash (joy) of the whole aratz (Earth/land)?

All your ayab (enemy) have patzah (opened) their pah (mouth) wide against you; They sharaq (hiss) and charaq (gnash) the shan (teeth); they amar (spoke), We have balai (swallowed) her up; ak (certainly) this is the yawam (day) that we qawah (gather/wait) for; we matzaa (have) found, we raah (see) seen it.

Yahawah ishah (make) done that which he zamam (purposed); he has batzai (fulfilled) his amarah (sayings) that he tzawah (commanded) in the yawam (day) of qadam (old); He has haras (thrown) down, and chamal (has) not pitied: He has caused the ayab (enemy) to shamach (rejoice) over you; he has rawam (will lift up) the qaran (horn) of your tzar (oppressor / distressor).

Their lab (heart) tzaiq (cried) to the Adanay: chawamah (wall) of the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion), let damaih (tears) yarad (run) down like a nachal (stream / river) yawamam (by day) and layal (night); nathan (give) yourself no respite; don't let the bath (daughter) of your iyan (eye) damam (cease).

Qawam (rise up), ranan (cry) out in the layal (night), at the raash (head) of the watches; shapak (pour) out your lab (heart) like mayam (Waters) nakach (before) the panayam (face) of the Adanay: nashaa (lift) up your kap (hands) toward him for the napash (living being/soul) of your young iwalal (children), that itap (faint) for raib (hunger) at the raash (head) of every chawatz (street).

Raah (see), Yahawah, and raah (see) to whom you have ilal (done) thus! Shall the ashah (wife/individual woman) akal (eat) their paray (fruit), the iwalal (children) that are dandled in the hands? Shall the kahan (priest) and the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) be harag (killed) in the maqadash (sanctuary) of the Adanay?

The youth and the zaqan (old) man shakab (lie) on the aratz (Earth/land) in the chawatz (streets); My bathawalah (virgins) and my bachawar (young) men are napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword): You have tabach (killed) them in the yawam (day) of your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting); you have tabach (slaughtered), and not chamal (pitied).

You have qaraa (called), as in the yawam (day) of a mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) assembly, my magawar (terrors) on sabayab (surrounding) side; There was none that palayat (escaped) or sharayad (remained) in the yawam (day) of yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting): Those that I have dandled and rabah (brought) up has my ayab (enemy) kalah (complete / finish).
I am the gabar (man) that raah (see) seen inay (affliction) by the shabat (rod) of his ibarah (wrath).
He has nahag (led) me and yalak (caused) me to walk in chashak (darkness), and not in awar (light).
Surely against me he shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand) again and again all the yawam (day).
My bashar (flesh) and my iwar (skin) has he balah (made) old; he has shabar (broken) my itzam (bones).
He has banah (built) against me, and surrounded me with raash (head) and thalaah (travail).
He has yashab (inhabit/dwell) me to dwell in machashak (dark) places, as those that have been iwalam (forever) mawath (death).
He has walled me about, that I can't yatzaa (go out / come out) forth; he has made my nachashath (chain) kabad (heavy).
Yes, when I zaiq (cry), and zaiq (call) for help, he satham (shuts) out my thapalah (prayer).
He has walled up my darak (ways) with cut gazayath (stone); he has made my nathayab (paths) iwah (crooked).
He is to me as a dab (bear) lying in arab (wait), as a aray (lion) in masathar (secret) places.
He has sawar (turned) aside my darak (ways), and pashach (pulled) me in pieces; he has shawam (place / establish / appoint) me shamam (desolate).
He has bent his qashath (bow), and natzab (set) me as a mataraa (mark) for the chatz (arrow).
He has caused the shafts of his ashapah (quiver) to bawaa (come) into my kalayah (kidneys).
I am become a shachawaq (laughter/joking matter) to all my im (people / nation), and their nagayanah (song) all the yawam (day).
He shabai (has) filled me with marar (bitterness), he has sated me with lainah (wormwood).
He has also garas (broken) my shan (teeth) with chatzatz (gravel) stones; he has kapash (covered) me with ashes.
You have zanach (removed) my napash (living being/soul) zanach (far) off from shalawam (peace / safety); I nashah (forgot) tawab (pleasant/functional).
I amar (spoke), My natzach (strength) is abad (destroy/perish), and my expectation from Yahawah.
Zakar (remembrance/memory) my inay (affliction) and my marawad (misery), the lainah (wormwood) and the raash (head).
My napash (living being/soul) still remembers them, and is shawach (bowed) down within me.
This I shawab (turn back / repent) to my lab (heart); therefore yachal (have) I hope.
It is because of yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) chasad (grace) kindnesses that we are not thamam (consumed), because his racham (compassion) doesn't kalah (complete / finish).
They are chadash (new) every baqar (morning); rab (great) is your amawanah (faithfulness).
Yahawah is my chalaq (portion), amar (spoke) my napash (living being/soul); therefore will I yachal (hope) in him.
Yahawah is tawab (pleasant/functional) to those who qawah (gather/wait) for him, to the napash (living being/soul) that darash (seeks) him.
It is tawab (pleasant/functional) that a man yachayal (should) hope and dawamam (quietly) wait for the thashawaih (deliverance) of Yahawah.
It is tawab (pleasant/functional) for a gabar (man) that he nashaa (lift) the il (over) in his naiwar (youth).
Let him yashab (inhabit/dwell) badad (alone) and damam (keep) silence, because he has laid it on him.
Let him put his pah (mouth) in the ipar (dust), if so be there yash (may) be thaqawah (hope).
Nathan (give) him give his lachay (cheek) to him who nakah (strikes) him; let him be shabai (filled) full with charapah (reproach).
For the Adanay will not zanach (cast) off iwalam (forever).
For though he yagah (cause) grief, yet he will racham (have) compassion according to the rab (multitude) of his chasad (grace) kindnesses.
For he does not inah (oppress / afflict) lab (heart), nor yagah (grieve) the ban (son) of ayash (husband/individual man).
To dakaa (crush) under ragal (feet / foot) all the asayar (prisoners) of the aratz (Earth/land),
To natah (turn) aside the mashapat (right) of a gabar (man) before the panayam (face) of the Most ilayawan (high),
To iwath (subvert) a adam (man) in his rayab (cause), the Adanay doesn't raah (see).
Who is he who amar (spoke), and it comes to pass, when the Adanay doesn't tzawah (command) it?
Doesn't rai (evil) and tawab (pleasant/functional) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the pah (mouth) of the Most ilayawan (high)?
Why does a chay (life) adam (man) anan (complain), a gabar (man) for the punishment of his chataa (sins)?
Let us chapash (search) and chaqar (try) our darak (ways), and shawab (turn back / repent) again to Yahawah.
Let us nashaa (lift) up our labab (heart) with our kap (hands) to Al in the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)).
We have pashai (transgressed) and have marah (rebelled); you have not salach (forgive/pardon/make clean).
You have sakak (covered) with ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) and radap (pursued) us; you have harag (killed), you chamal (have) not pitied.
You have sakak (covered) yourself with a inan (cloud), so that no thapalah (prayer) can ibar (pass over/through) through.
You have shawam (place / establish / appoint) us an sachay (off-scouring) and maawas (refuse) in the qarab (among / near) of the im (people / nation).
All our ayab (enemy) have patzah (opened) their pah (mouth) wide against us.
Pachad (fear / dread) and the pachath (pit) have come on us, devastation and shabar (destruction).
My iyan (eye) yarad (runs) down with palag (streams) of mayam (Waters), for the shabar (destruction) of the bath (daughter) of my im (people / nation).
My iyan (eye) nagar (pours) down, and doesn't damah (cease), without any hapagah (intermission),
Until Yahawah shaqap (look) down, and raah (see) from shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)).
My iyan (eye) ilal (affects) my napash (living being/soul), because of all the bath (daughter) of my iyar (city).
They have tzawad (chased) me relentlessly like a tzapawar (bird), those who are my ayab (enemy) chanam (without) cause.
They have tzamath (cut) off my chay (life) in the bawar (dungeon), and have yadah (cast) a aban (stone) on me.
Mayam (Waters) tzawap (flowed) over my raash (head); I amar (spoke), I am gazar (cut) off.
I qaraa (called) on your sham (name), Yahawah, out of the lowest bawar (dungeon).
You shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice); don't ilam (hide) your azan (ear) at my rawachah (breathing), at my cry.
You qarab (come close) near in the yawam (day) that I qaraa (called) on you; you amar (spoke), Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid).
Adanay, you have rayab (pleaded) the rayab (causes) of my napash (living being/soul); you have gaal (redeemed) my chay (life).
Yahawah, you raah (see) seen my iwathah (wrong). Shapat (judge) my cause.
You raah (see) seen all their naqamah (vengeance) and all their machashabah (devices) against me.
You have shamai (hearken / hear) their charapah (reproach), Yahawah, and all their machashabah (devices) against me,
The shapah (lips) of those that qawam (rise up) up against me, and their hagayawan (device) against me all the yawam (day).
You nabat (see) their sitting down, and their qayamah (rising) up; I am their song.
You will shawab (turn back / repent) to them a gamawal (recompense), Yahawah, according to the maishah (work) of their yad (hand).
You will nathan (give) them hardness of lab (heart), your thaalah (curse) to them.
You will radap (pursue) them in ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and shamad (destroy) them from under the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) of Yahawah.

How the zahab (gold) has imam (become) dim! The most katham (pure) gold has shanaa (hate)! The aban (stone) of the qadash (set apart/make holy) are shapak (poured) out at the raash (head) of every chawatz (street).

The yaqar (precious) ban (son) of Tzayawan (Zion), comparable to paz (fine) gold, How are they chashab (esteemed) as charash (earthen) nabal (pitchers), the maishah (work) of the yad (hand) of the yatzar (potter)!

Even the jackals chalatz (draw) out the shad (breast), they yanaq (nurse) their gawar (young) ones: The bath (daughter) of my im (people / nation) has become akazar (cruel), like the ostriches in the madabar (wilderness).

The lashawan (tongue/language) of the yanaq (nursing) child clings to the roof of his chak (mouth) for tzamaa (thirst): The young iwalal (children) shaal (ask) lacham (bread), and no man parash (breaks) it to them.
Those who akal (eat) maidan (delicately) are shamam (desolate) in the chawatz (streets): Those who were aman (believe / have faith) up in thawalai (scarlet) chabaq (embrace) dunghills.

For the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the bath (daughter) of my im (people / nation) is greater than the chataah (sin) of Sadam (Sodom), That was overthrown as in a ragai (in an instance), and no yad (hand) were laid on her.

Her nobles were zakak (purer) than shalag (snow), they were tzachach (whiter) than chalab (milk); They were more ruddy in itzam (body) than panayan (rubies), their gazarah (polishing) was as of sapayar (sapphire).

Their appearance is blacker than a shachawar (coal); they are not nakar (known) in the chawatz (streets): Their iwar (skin) clings to their itzam (bones); it is yabash (dry land), it has become like a itz (stick).

Those who are chalal (killed) with the charab (sword) are tawab (pleasant/functional) than those who are chalal (killed) with raib (hunger); For these zawab (flow) away, daqar (stricken) through, for want of the thanawabah (fruits) of the shadah (field).

The yad (hand) of the rachamanay (pitiful) ashah (wife/individual woman) have bashal (boiled) their own yalad (birth / begot); They were their food in the shabar (destruction) of the bath (daughter) of my im (people / nation).

Yahawah kalah (complete / finish) accomplished his chamah (wrath), he has shapak (poured) out his charawan (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting); He has yatzath (kindled) a ash (fire) in Tzayawan (Zion), which has akal (eat) its yasawad (foundations).

The malak (king) of the aratz (Earth/land) didn't aman (believe / have faith), neither all the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the thabal (world), That the tzar (oppressor / distressor) and the ayab (enemy) would bawaa (come) into the shair (gates) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

It is because of the chataah (sin) of her nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of her kahan (priest), That have shapak (shed) the dam (blood) of the tzadayaq (righteous) in the qarab (among / near) of her.
They nawai (wander) as iwar (blind) men in the chawatz (streets), they are gaal (polluted) with dam (blood), So that men can't nagai (touch) their labawash (garments).

Sawar (depart)! They qaraa (called) to them, tamaa (unclean)! Sawar (depart), sawar (depart), don't nagai (touch)! When they nawatz (fled) away and nawai (wandered), men amar (spoke) among the gaway (nation / people), They shall not live here any more.

The panayam (anger) of Yahawah chalaq (has) scattered them; he will no more nabat (regard) them: They didn't nabat (respect) the panayam (persons) of the kahan (priest), they didn't favor the zaqan (elders).

Our iyan (eye) still kalah (complete / finish), looking in habal (vain) for our izarah (help): In our tzapayah (watching) we have tzapah (watchman / keep watch) for a gaway (nation / people) that could not yashai (salvation).

They tzawad (hunt) our tzaid (steps), so that we can't yalak (go) in our rachab (streets): Our qatz (end) is qarab (come close), our yawam (day) are malaa (fulfilled); for our qatz (end) bawaa (come) come.
Our radap (pursuers) were swifter than the nashar (eagles) of the sky: They dalaq (chased) us on the har (mountain), they arab (laid) wait for us in the madabar (wilderness).

The rawach (spirit / wind) of our ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), the mashayach (anointed one) of Yahawah, was lakad (taken) in their shachayath (pits); Of whom we amar (spoke), Under his tzal (shadow) we shall chayah (live) among the gaway (nation / people).

Shawash (rejoice) and be shamach (glad), bath (daughter) of Adam (Edom), that yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Iwatz (Uz): The kawas (cup) shall ibar (pass over/through) through to you also; you shall be shakar (drunken), and shall irah (make) yourself naked.

The punishment of your iwan (guilt/iniquity) is thamam (accomplished), bath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion); he will no more galah (carry) you away into captivity: He will paqad (visit) your iwan (guilt/iniquity), bath (daughter) of Adam (Edom); he will galah (uncover) your chataah (sin).
Zakar (remembrance/memory), Yahawah, what raah (see) come on us: Look, and raah (see) our charapah (reproach).
Our nachalah (inheritance) is hapak (turned) to strangers, Our bayath (house) to nakaray (aliens).
We are yathawam (orphans) and ayan (fatherless); Our am (mother) are as alamanah (widows).
We have shathah (drinks) our mayam (Waters) for kasap (money); Our itz (wood) is sold to us.
Our radap (pursuers) are on our tzawaar (necks): We are yagai (weary), and have no nawach (rest).
We nathan (give) given the yad (hand) to the Matzarayam (Egyptians), To the Ashawar (Assyrians), to be shabai (satisfied) with lacham (bread).
Our ab (father) chataa (sinned), and are no more; We have sabal (borne) their iwan (guilt/iniquity).
Ibad (servant) mashal (rule/have dominion) over us: There is none to paraq (deliver) us out of their yad (hand).
We bawaa (come) our lacham (bread) at the peril of our lives, panayam (because) of the charab (sword) of the madabar (wilderness).
Our iwar (skin) is kamar (black) like an thanawar (oven), panayam (because) of the burning heat of raib (famine).
They inah (oppress / afflict) the ashah (wife/individual woman) in Tzayawan (Zion), The bathawalah (virgins) in the iyar (cities) of Yahawadah (Judah).
Shar (prince / ruler) were hanged up by their yad (hand): The panayam (faces) of zaqan (elders) were not honored.
The bachawar (young) men bare the mill; The nair (children) kashal (stumble / stagger) under the itz (wood).
The zaqan (elders) have shabath (shabath/rest) from the shair (gate), The bachawar (young) men from their music.
The mashawash (joy) of our lab (heart) is shabath (shabath/rest); Our machawal (dance) is hapak (turned) into abal (mourning).
The itarah (crown) is napal (fall / be cast down) from our raash (head): away (woe) to us! For we have chataa (sinned).
For this our lab (heart) is dawah (faint); For these things our iyan (eye) are chashak (darkness);
For the har (mountain) of Tzayawan (Zion), which is shamam (desolate): The foxes halak (move) on it.
You, Yahawah, yashab (inhabit/dwell) iwalam (forever); Your kasaa (throne) is from dawar (generation / age / period) to dawar (generation / age / period).
Why do you shakach (forget) us natzach (forever), And izab (forsake) us so arak (length) yawam (day)?
Shawab (turn back / repent) us to yourself, Yahawah, and we shall be shawab (turn back / repent). Chadash (renew) our yawam (day) as of qadam (old).
But you have maas (utterly) maas (rejected) us; You are very qatzap (angry) against us.

Now it happened in the shalawashayam (thirty) shanah (year), in the rabayaiy (fourth) month, in the chamash (fifth) of the chadash (month), as I was thawak (midst) the gawalah (captives) by the nahar (river) Kabar (Chebar), that the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) were pathach (opened), and I raah (see) maraah (visions) of Alahayam.
In the chamash (fifth) of the chadash (month), which was the chamayashay (fifth) shanah (year) of malak (king) Yawayakayan (Jehoiachin's) galawath (captivity),

The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came expressly to Yachazaqaal (Ezekiel) the kahan (priest), the ban (son) of Bawazay (Buzi), in the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans) by the nahar (river) Kabar (Chebar); and the yad (hand) of Yahawah was there on him.

I raah (see), and behold, a stormy rawach (spirit / wind) bawaa (come) out of the tzapawan (north), a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) inan (cloud), with flashing lightning, and a nagah (brightness) around it, and out of its thawak (midst) as it were glowing metal, out of the thawak (midst) of the ash (fire).
Out of its thawak (midst) came the damawath (likeness) of arabai (four) chay (life) creatures. This was their maraah (appearance): they had the damawath (likeness) of a adam (man).
Everyone had arabai (four) panayam (faces), and achad (one) one of them had arabai (four) kanap (wings).

Their ragal (feet / foot) were yashar (straight) ragal (feet / foot); and the kap (sole) of their ragal (feet / foot) was like the kap (sole) of a igal (calf's) ragal (feet / foot); and they natzatz (sparkled) like qalal (burnished) nachashath (brass).
They had the yad (hand) of a adam (man) under their kanap (wings) on their arabai (four) rabai (fourth); and the arabai (four) of them had their panayam (faces) and their kanap (wings) thus:

Their kanap (wings) were chabar (joined) ashah (wife/individual woman) to achawath (another); they didn't sabab (turn) when they yalak (went); ayash (husband/individual man) one yalak (went) ibar (straight) forward.

As for the damawath (likeness) of their panayam (faces), they had the panayam (face) of a adam (man); and the arabai (four) of them had the panayam (face) of a aray (lion) on the yamayan (right hand) side; and the arabai (four) of them had the panayam (face) of an shawar (ox) on the shamaawal (left hand) side; the arabai (four) of them also had the panayam (face) of an nashar (eagle).

Such were their panayam (faces). Their kanap (wings) were spread out mail (top/above). Shanayam (two) wings of ayash (husband/individual man) ayash (husband/individual man) touched ayash (husband/individual man), and shanayam (two) kasah (covered) their gawayah (corpse).
Ayash (husband/individual man) one yalak (went) ibar (straight) forward: where the rawach (spirit / wind) was to yalak (go), they yalak (went); they didn't sabab (turn) when they yalak (went).

As for the damawath (likeness) of the chay (life) creatures, their maraah (appearance) was like bair (burning) gachal (coals) of ash (fire), like the maraah (appearance) of torches: the fire halak (move) up and down among the chay (life) creatures; and the ash (fire) was nagah (bright), and out of the ash (fire) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth baraq (lightning).
The chay (life) creatures ratzaa (ran) and shawab (turn back / repent) as the maraah (appearance) of a bazaq (flash) of lightning.
Now as I raah (see) the chay (life) creatures, behold, achad (one) awapan (wheel) on the aratz (Earth/land) beside the chay (life) creatures, for each of the arabai (four) panayam (faces) of it.

The maraah (appearance) of the awapan (wheels) and their maishah (work) was like a tharashayash (beryl): and the arabai (four) of them had achad (one) damawath (likeness); and their maraah (appearance) and their maishah (work) was as it were a awapan (wheel) thawak (midst) a awapan (wheel).
When they yalak (went), they yalak (went) in their arabai (four) directions: they didn't sabab (turn) when they yalak (went).
As for their rims, they were gabah (high) and yaraah (dreadful); and the arabai (four) of them had their rims malaa (full) of iyan (eye) all around.

When the chay (life) creatures yalak (went), the awapan (wheels) yalak (went) beside them; and when the chay (life) creatures were nashaa (lift) up from the aratz (Earth/land), the awapan (wheels) were nashaa (lift) up.

Wherever the rawach (spirit / wind) was to yalak (go), they yalak (went); there was the rawach (spirit / wind) to yalak (go): and the awapan (wheels) were nashaa (lift) up imah (beside) them; for the rawach (spirit / wind) of the chay (life) creature was in the awapan (wheels).

When those yalak (went), these yalak (went); and when those imad (stood), these imad (stood); and when those were nashaa (lift) up from the aratz (Earth/land), the awapan (wheels) were nashaa (lift) up imah (beside) them: for the rawach (spirit / wind) of the chay (life) creature was in the awapan (wheels).

Over the raash (head) of the chay (life) creature there was the damawath (likeness) of an expanse, like the awesome qarach (crystal) to look on, natah (stretched) forth over their raash (head) mail (top/above).

Under the expanse were their kanap (wings) yashar (straight), the ashah (wife/individual woman) toward the other: ayash (husband/individual man) one had shanayam (two) which kasah (covered) on hanah (Behold) side, and ayash (husband/individual man) one had shanayam (two) which kasah (covered) on that hanah (Behold), their gawayah (corpse).

When they yalak (went), I shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of their kanap (wings) like the qawal (sound / voice) of rab (great) mayam (Waters), like the qawal (sound / voice) of the Shaday, a qawal (sound / voice) of hamalah (tumult) like the qawal (sound / voice) of an machanah (army): when they imad (stood), they rapah (let) down their kanap (wings).
There was a qawal (sound / voice) above the expanse that was over their raash (head): when they imad (stood), they rapah (let) down their kanap (wings).

Mail (top/above) the expanse that was over their raash (head) was the damawath (likeness) of a kasaa (throne), as the maraah (appearance) of a sapayar (sapphire) aban (stone); and on the damawath (likeness) of the kasaa (throne) was a damawath (likeness) as the maraah (appearance) of a adam (man) on it mail (top/above).

I raah (see) as it were glowing metal, as the maraah (appearance) of ash (fire) bayath (house) it all around, from the maraah (appearance) of his waist and upward; and from the maraah (appearance) of his waist and matah (downward) I raah (see) as it were the maraah (appearance) of ash (fire), and there was nagah (brightness) around him.

As the maraah (appearance) of the rainbow that is in the inan (cloud) in the yawam (day) of gasham (rain), so was the maraah (appearance) of the nagah (brightness) all around. This was the maraah (appearance) of the damawath (likeness) of the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah. When I raah (see) it, I napal (fall / be cast down) on my panayam (face), and I shamai (hearken / hear) a qawal (sound / voice) of one that dabar (word / matter).
He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), imad (stand) on your ragal (feet / foot), and I will dabar (word / matter) with you.
The rawach (spirit / wind) bawaa (come) into me when he dabar (word / matter) to me, and imad (set) me on my ragal (feet / foot); and I shamai (hearken / hear) him who dabar (word / matter) to me.

He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), I shalach (send) you to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), to a gaway (nation / people) of marad (rebels) who have marad (rebelled) against me. They and their ab (father) have pashai (transgressed) against me even to this very yawam (day).
The ban (son) are qashah (rough / hard) and chazaq (stiff-hearted): I am shalach (send) you to them; and you shall amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah.

They, whether they will shamai (hearken / hear), or whether they will chadal (forbear), (for they are a rebellious bayath (house)), yet shall yadai (know) that there has been a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) thawak (midst) them.

You, ban (son) of adam (man), don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of them, neither be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of their dabar (word / matter), though sarab (briers) and salawan (thorns) are with you, and you do yashab (inhabit/dwell) among iqarab (scorpions): don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of their dabar (word / matter), nor be chathath (dismayed) at their panayam (looks), though they are a rebellious bayath (house).
You shall dabar (word / matter) my dabar (word / matter) to them, whether they will shamai (hearken / hear), or whether they will chadal (forbear); for they are most rebellious.

But you, ban (son) of adam (man), shamai (hearken / hear) what I dabar (word / matter) you; don't be rebellious like that rebellious bayath (house): patzah (open) your pah (mouth), and akal (eat) that which I nathan (give) you.
When I raah (see), behold, a yad (hand) was shalach (send) forth to me; and, behold, a scroll of a sapar (book / scribed document) was therein;

He parash (spread) it panayam (before) me: and it was kathab (written) within and achawar (without); and there were kathab (written) therein qayanah (lamentations), and hagah (mourning), and hay (exist).
He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), akal (eat) that which you matzaa (find). Akal (eat) this scroll, and yalak (go), dabar (word / matter) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).
So I pathach (opened) my pah (mouth), and he caused me to akal (eat) the scroll.

He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), cause your batan (belly) to akal (eat), and malaa (fill) your maih (bowels) with this scroll that I nathan (give) you. Then I akal (eat) it; and it was as mathawaq (sweet) as dabash (honey) in my pah (mouth).
He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), yalak (go) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), and dabar (word / matter) my dabar (word / matter) to them.
For you are not shalach (send) to a im (people / nation) of a imaq (strange) shapah (speech) and of a kabad (hard) lashawan (tongue/language), but to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel);

Not to many im (people / nation) of a imaq (strange) shapah (speech) and of a kabad (hard) lashawan (tongue/language), whose dabar (word / matter) you can not shamai (hearken / hear). Surely, if I shalach (send) you to them, they would shamai (hearken / hear) to you.

But the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) abah (be willing / desire) not shamai (hearken / hear) to you; for they abah (be willing / desire) not shamai (hearken / hear) to me: for all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) are obstinate and qashah (rough / hard).
Behold, I nathan (give) made your panayam (face) hard imah (against) their panayam (faces), and your matzach (forehead) hard imah (against) their matzach (foreheads).

As an shamayar (adamant) chazaq (harder) than tzar (flint) nathan (give) I made your matzach (forehead): don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of them, neither be chathath (dismayed) at their panayam (looks), though they are a rebellious bayath (house).

Moreover he amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), all my dabar (word / matter) that I shall dabar (word / matter) to you laqach (take / seized) in your labab (heart), and shamai (hearken / hear) with your azan (ears).

Yalak (go) to them of the gawalah (captivity), to the ban (son) of your im (people / nation), and dabar (word / matter) to them, and amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah; whether they will shamai (hearken / hear), or whether they will chadal (forbear).

Then the rawach (spirit / wind) nashaa (lift) me up, and I shamai (hearken / hear) achar (other) me the qawal (sound / voice) of a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) raish (rushing), saying, barak (blessed) be the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah from his maqawam (place).

I heard the qawal (sound / voice) of the kanap (wings) of the chay (life) creatures as they nashaq (touched) ashah (wife/individual woman) achawath (another), and the qawal (sound / voice) of the awapan (wheels) imah (beside) them, even the qawal (sound / voice) of a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) raish (rushing).

So the rawach (spirit / wind) nashaa (lift) me up, and laqach (take / seized) me away; and I yalak (went) in bitterness, in the chamah (heat) of my rawach (spirit / wind); and the yad (hand) of Yahawah was chazaq (strong) on me.

Then I bawaa (come) to them of the gawalah (captivity) at Thalaabayab (Tel) Aviv, that lived by the nahar (river) Kabar (Chebar), and to where they lived; and I yashab (inhabit/dwell) there overwhelmed thawak (midst) them shabai (seven) yawam (day).
It happened at the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of shabai (seven) yawam (day), that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), I nathan (give) made you a tzapah (watchman / keep watch) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel): therefore shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) from my pah (mouth), and give them zahar (warn) from me.

When I amar (spoke) the rashai (wicked), You shall mawath (death) mawath (death); and you give him no zahar (warn), nor dabar (word / matter) to zahar (warn) the rashai (wicked) from his rashai (wicked) darak (way), to chayah (save) his life; the same rashai (wicked) mawath (death) shall die in his iwan (guilt/iniquity); but his dam (blood) will I baqash (require) at your yad (hand).

Yet if you zahar (warn) the rashai (wicked), and he doesn't shawab (turn back / repent) from his rashai (wickedness), nor from his rashai (wicked) darak (way), he shall mawath (death) in his iwan (guilt/iniquity); but you have natzal (delivered) your napash (living being/soul).

Again, when a tzadayaq (righteous) man does shawab (turn back / repent) from his tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and ishah (make) iwal (iniquity), and I nathan (give) a makashawal (stumbling) block panayam (before) him, he shall mawath (death): because you have not given him zahar (warn), he shall mawath (death) in his chataah (sin), and his tzadaqah (righteousness) deeds which he ishah (make) done shall not be zakar (remembrance/memory); but his dam (blood) will I baqash (require) at your yad (hand).

Nevertheless if you zahar (warn) the tzadayaq (righteous) man, that the tzadayaq (righteous) not chataa (sin), and he does not chataa (sin), he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live), because he took zahar (warn); and you have natzal (delivered) your napash (living being/soul).
The yad (hand) of Yahawah was there on me; and he amar (spoke) to me, qawam (rise up), yatzaa (go out / come out) forth into the baqaih (plain), and I will there dabar (word / matter) with you.

Then I qawam (rise up), and yatzaa (go out / come out) forth into the baqaih (plain): and behold, the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah imad (stood) there, as the kabawad (glory) which I raah (see) by the nahar (river) Kabar (Chebar); and I napal (fall / be cast down) on my panayam (face).

Then the rawach (spirit / wind) bawaa (come) into me, and imad (set) me on my ragal (feet / foot); and he dabar (word / matter) with me, and amar (spoke) to me, bawaa (come), sagar (shut) yourself inside your bayath (house).
But you, ban (son) of adam (man), behold, they shall nathan (give) ibath (bands) on you, and shall asar (bind) you with them, and you shall not yatzaa (go out / come out) out thawak (midst) them:
And I will make your lashawan (tongue/language) dabaq (stick) to the roof of your chak (mouth), that you shall be mute, and shall not be to them a reprover; for they are a rebellious bayath (house).

But when I dabar (word / matter) with you, I will pathach (open) your pah (mouth), and you shall amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: He who shamai (hearken / hear), shamai (hearken / hear) him hear; and he who chadal (forbears), chadal (let) him forbear: for they are a rebellious bayath (house).
You also, ban (son) of adam (man), laqach (take / seized) a labanah (tile), and nathan (give) it panayam (before) yourself, and portray on it a iyar (city), even Yarawashalam (Jerusalem):

And nathan (give) matzawar (siege) against it, and banah (build) dayaq (forts) against it, and shapak (cast) up a mound against it; nathan (give) machanah (camps) also against it, and plant battering kar (rams) against it all around.

Laqach (take / seized) for yourself an barazal (iron) machabath (pan), and nathan (give) it for a qayar (wall) of barazal (iron) between you and the iyar (city): and kawan (set) your panayam (face) toward it, and it shall be matzawar (besieged), and you shall tzawar (lay) siege against it. This shall be a awath (sign / mark / miracle) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Moreover shakab (lie) on your shamaalay (left) tzad (side), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) on it; according to the masapar (number) of the yawam (day) that you shall shakab (lie) on it, you shall nashaa (lift) their iwan (guilt/iniquity).

For I nathan (give) appointed the shanah (years) of their iwan (guilt/iniquity) to be to you a masapar (number) of yawam (day), even shalawash (three) maah (hundred) thashaiyam (ninety) yawam (day): so you shall nashaa (lift) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Again, when you kalah (complete / finish) accomplished these, you shall shakab (lie) on your yamayanay (right) tzad (side), and shall nashaa (lift) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah): arabaiyam (forty) yawam (day), each yawam (day) for a shanah (year), nathan (give) I appointed it to you.
You shall kawan (set) your panayam (face) toward the matzawar (siege) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), with your zarawai (arm) chashap (uncovered); and you shall nabaa (prophesy) against it.

Behold, I nathan (give) ibath (bands) on you, and you shall not hapak (turn) you from one tzad (side) to the other, until you kalah (complete / finish) accomplished the yawam (day) of your matzawar (siege).

Laqach (take / seized) for yourself also chatah (wheat), and shairah (barley), and pawal (beans), and lentils, and dachan (millet), and spelt, and nathan (give) them in achad (one) kalay (vessel), and ishah (make) lacham (bread) of it; according to the masapar (number) of the yawam (day) that you shall shakab (lie) on your tzad (side), even shalawash (three) maah (hundred) thashaiyam (ninety) yawam (day), you shall akal (eat) of it.
Your maakal (food) which you shall akal (eat) shall be by mashaqawal (weight), isharayam (twenty) shaqal (shekels) a yawam (day): from ith (time) to ith (time) you shall akal (eat) it.
You shall shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters) by mashawarah (measure), the shashay (sixth) part of a hayan (hin): from ith (time) to ith (time) you shall shathah (drinks).
You shall akal (eat) it as shairah (barley) igah (cakes), and you shall iwag (bake) it in their iyan (eye) with galal (dung) that comes out of adam (man).
Yahawah amar (spoke), Even thus shall the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) akal (eat) their lacham (bread) tamaa (unclean), among the gaway (nation / people) where I will nadach (drive) them.

Then I amar (spoke), ahah (ah) Adanay Yahawah! Behold, my napash (living being/soul) has not been tamaa (polluted); for from my naiwar (youth) up even until now have I not akal (eat) of that which dies of nabalah (itself), or is tarapah (torn) of animals; neither bawaa (come) there pagawal (abominable) bashar (flesh) into my pah (mouth).
Then he amar (spoke) to me, raah (see), I nathan (give) given you baqar (morning) tzapawai (dung) for adam (man's) galal (dung), and you shall ishah (make) your lacham (bread) thereon.

Moreover he amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), behold, I will shabar (break) the matah (staff / rod / tribe) of lacham (bread) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem): and they shall akal (eat) lacham (bread) by mashaqal (weight), and with fearfulness; and they shall shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters) by mashawarah (measure), and in shamamawan (dismay):
That they may chasar (want) lacham (bread) and mayam (Waters), and be dismayed ayash (husband/individual man) with ach (brother/kinsman), and maqaq (pine) away in their iwan (guilt/iniquity).

You, ban (son) of adam (man), laqach (take / seized) a chad (sharp) charab (sword); You shall laqach (take / seized) it as a galab (barber's) thair (razor) to you, and shall ibar (pass over/through) it to pass on your raash (head) and on your zaqan (beard): then laqach (take / seized) maazan (balances) to weigh, and chalaq (divide) the hair.

A shalayashay (third) part you shall bair (burn) in the awar (light) in the thawak (midst) of the iyar (city), when the yawam (day) of the matzawar (siege) are malaa (fulfilled); and you shall laqach (take / seized) a shalayashay (third) part, and nakah (strike) with the charab (sword) around it; and a shalayashay (third) part you shall zarah (scatter) to the rawach (spirit / wind), and I will rawaq (draw) out a charab (sword) achar (other) them.
You shall laqach (take / seized) of it a mait (few) in masapar (number), and tzawar (bind) them in your kanap (skirts).

Of these again you shall take, and shalak (cast) them into the thawak (midst) of the ash (fire), and sharap (burn) them in the ash (fire); from it shall a ash (fire) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth into all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: This is Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) her in the thawak (midst) of the gaway (nation / people), and aratz (Earth/land) are around her.

She has marah (rebelled) against my mashapat (ordinances) in doing rashaih (wickedness) more than the gaway (nation / people), and against my chaqah (statutes) more than the aratz (Earth/land) that are around her; for they have maas (rejected) my mashapat (ordinances), and as for my chaqah (statutes), they have not halak (move) in them.

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you are turbulent more than the gaway (nation / people) that are around you, and have not halak (move) in my chaqah (statutes), neither ishah (make) kept my mashapat (ordinances), neither ishah (make) done after the mashapat (ordinances) of the gaway (nation / people) that are around you;

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I, even I, am against you; and I will ishah (make) mashapat (judgments) in the thawak (midst) of you in the iyan (eye) of the gaway (nation / people).
I will ishah (make) in you that which I ishah (make) not done, and whereunto I will not ishah (make) any more the like, yain (because) of all your thawaibah (abominations).

Therefore the ab (father) shall akal (eat) the ban (son) in the thawak (midst) of you, and the ban (son) shall akal (eat) their ab (father); and I will ishah (make) shapat (judgments) on you; and the whole shaarayath (remnant) of you will I zarah (scatter) to all the rawach (spirit / wind).

Therefore, as I chay (life), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, surely, because you have tamaa (defiled) my maqadash (sanctuary) with all your shaqawatz (detestable) things, and with all your thawaibah (abominations), therefore will I also garai (diminish) you; neither shall my iyan (eye) chawas (spare), and I also will chamal (have) no pity.

A shalayashay (third) part of you shall mawath (death) with the dabar (word / matter), and with raib (famine) shall they be kalah (complete / finish) in the thawak (midst) of you; and a shalayashay (third) part shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword) around you; and a shalayashay (third) part I will zarah (scatter) to all the rawach (spirit / wind), and will rawaq (draw) out a charab (sword) achar (other) them.

Thus shall my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) be kalah (complete / finish), and I will cause my chamah (wrath) toward them to nawach (rest), and I shall be nacham (turn away / repent); and they shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) in my qanaah (zeal), when I kalah (complete / finish) accomplished my chamah (wrath) on them.
Moreover I will nathan (give) you a desolation and a charapah (reproach) among the gaway (nation / people) that are around you, in the iyan (eye) of ibar (pass over/through) that pass by.

So it shall be a charapah (reproach) and a gadawapah (taunt), an mawasar (instruction) and an mashamah (astonishment), to the gaway (nation / people) that are around you, when I shall ishah (make) shapat (judgments) on you in ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) and in chamah (wrath), and in chamah (wrathful) thawakachah (rebukes); (I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it;)

When I shall shalach (send) on them the rai (evil) chatz (arrows) of raib (famine), that are for mashachayath (destruction), which I will shalach (send) to shachath (destroy) you: and I will yasap (increase) the raib (famine) on you, and will shabar (break) your matah (staff / rod / tribe) of lacham (bread);

And I will shalach (send) on you raib (famine) and rai (evil) animals, and they shall shakal (bereave) you; and dabar (word / matter) and dam (blood) shall ibar (pass over/through) through you; and I will bawaa (come) the charab (sword) on you: I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) toward the har (mountain) of Yasharaal (Israel), and nabaa (prophesy) to them,

And amar (spoke), You har (mountain) of Yasharaal (Israel), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of the Adanay Yahawah: Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah to the har (mountain) and to the gabaih (hills), to the watercourses and to the gayaa (valleys): Behold, I, even I, will bawaa (come) a charab (sword) on you, and I will abad (destroy/perish) your bamah (high) places.

Your mazabach (altars) shall become shamam (desolate), and your incense mazabach (altars) shall be shabar (broken); and I will napal (fall / be cast down) down your chalal (slain) men panayam (before) your galawal (idols).

I will nathan (give) the pagar (dead) bodies of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) panayam (before) their galawal (idols); and I will zarah (scatter) your itzam (bones) around your mazabach (altars).

In all your mawashab (dwelling) places the iyar (cities) shall be charab (laid) waste, and the bamah (high) places shall be yasham (desolate); that your mazabach (altars) may be charab (laid) waste and asham (made) desolate, and your galawal (idols) may be shabar (broken) and shabath (shabath/rest), and your incense chaman (altars) may be gadai (cut) down, and your maishah (works) may be machah (abolished).
The chalal (slain) shall napal (fall / be cast down) in the thawak (midst) of you, and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Yet will I yathar (leave) a remnant, in that you shall have some that palayat (escape) the charab (sword) among the gaway (nation / people), when you shall be zarah (scattered) through the aratz (Earth/land).

Those of you that palayat (escape) shall zakar (remembrance/memory) me among the gaway (nation / people) where they shall be shabah (carried) captive, how that I have been shabar (broken) with their lewd lab (heart), which has sawar (departed) from me, and with their iyan (eye), which zanah (play) the prostitute achar (other) their galawal (idols): and they shall qawat (loathe) panayam (themselves) in their own sight for the rai (evils) which they ishah (make) committed in all their thawaibah (abominations).
They shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah: I have not dabar (word / matter) in chanam (vain) that I would ishah (make) this rai (evil) to them.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: nakah (strike) with your kap (hand), and raqai (stamp) with your ragal (feet / foot), and amar (spoke), ach (brother/kinsman)! Because of all the rai (evil) thawaibah (abominations) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel); for they shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword), by the raib (famine), and by the dabar (word / matter).

He who is rachawaq (far) off shall mawath (death) of the dabar (word / matter); and he who is qarawab (near) shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword); and he who shaar (remains) and is natzar (besieged) shall mawath (death) by the raib (famine): thus will I kalah (complete / finish) my chamah (wrath) on them.

You shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when their chalal (slain) men shall be thawak (midst) their galawal (idols) around their mazabach (altars), on every rawam (will lift up) gabaih (hill), on all the raash (head) of the har (mountain), and under every rainan (green) itz (tree), and under every ibath (thick) alah (these), the maqawam (place) where they nathan (give) pleasant aroma to all their galawal (idols).

I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on them, and nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) shamamah (desolate) and waste, from the madabar (wilderness) Dabalah (toward) Diblah, throughout all their habitations: and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Moreover the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

You, ban (son) of adam (man), thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah to the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), An qatz (end): the qatz (end) bawaa (come) come on the arabai (four) kanap (corners) of the aratz (Earth/land).

Now is the qatz (end) on you, and I will shalach (send) my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) on you, and will shapat (judge) you according to your darak (ways); and I will nathan (give) on you all your thawaibah (abominations).

My iyan (eye) shall not chawas (spare) you, neither will I chamal (have) pity; but I will nathan (give) your darak (ways) on you, and your thawaibah (abominations) shall be in the thawak (midst) of you: and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: An rai (evil), an only rai (evil); behold, it bawaa (come).
An qatz (end) bawaa (come) come, the qatz (end) bawaa (come) come; it qawatz (awakes) bawaa (come) you; behold, it comes.

Your doom bawaa (come) come to you, yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the aratz (Earth/land): the ith (time) bawaa (come) come, the yawam (day) is qarawab (near), a day of mahawamah (tumult), and not of joyful shouting, on the har (mountain).

Now will I qarawab (shortly) shapak (pour) out my chamah (wrath) on you, and kalah (complete / finish) my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) against you, and will shapat (judge) you according to your darak (ways); and I will nathan (give) on you all your thawaibah (abominations).

My iyan (eye) shall not chawas (spare), neither will I chamal (have) pity: I will nathan (give) on you according to your darak (ways); and your thawaibah (abominations) shall be in the thawak (midst) of you; and you shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, do nakah (strike).
Behold, the yawam (day), behold, it bawaa (come): your doom is yatzaa (go out / come out) forth; the matah (staff / rod / tribe) has tzawatz (blossomed), zadawan (pride) has parach (budded).

Chamas (violence) has qawam (rise up) up into a matah (staff / rod / tribe) of rashai (wickedness). None of them shall remain, nor of their hamawan (multitude), nor of their wealth. There shall be nothing of value among them.

The ith (time) bawaa (come) come, the yawam (day) nagai (draws) near: don't let the qanah (buyer) shamach (rejoice), nor the seller abal (mourn); for charawan (wrath) is on all its hamawan (multitude).

For the seller shall not shawab (turn back / repent) to that which is mamakar (sold), although they be yet chay (life): for the chazawan (vision) is touching the whole hamawan (multitude) of it, none shall shawab (turn back / repent); neither shall any chazaq (strengthen) himself in the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of his chay (life).

They have thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the thaqawai (trumpet), and have kawan (made) all ready; but none halak (move) to the malachamah (battle); for my charawan (wrath) is on all its hamawan (multitude).

The charab (sword) is outside, and the dabar (word / matter) and the raib (famine) bayath (house): he who is in the shadah (field) shall mawath (death) with the charab (sword): and he who is in the iyar (city), raib (famine) and dabar (word / matter) shall akal (eat) him.

But those of those who palat (escape) shall palayat (escape), and shall be on the har (mountain) like yawanah (doves) of the gayaa (valleys), all of them moaning, ayash (husband/individual man) one in his iwan (guilt/iniquity).
All yad (hand) shall be rapah (feeble), and all barak (knees) shall be yalak (weak) as mayam (Waters).

They shall also clothe themselves with sackcloth, and palatzawath (horror) shall kasah (cover) them; and bawashah (shame) shall be on all panayam (faces), and qarachah (baldness) on all their raash (head).

They shall shalak (cast) their kasap (silver) in the chawatz (streets), and their zahab (gold) shall be as an nadah (unclean) thing; their kasap (silver) and their zahab (gold) shall not be yakal (able) to natzal (deliver) them in the yawam (day) of the ibarah (wrath) of Yahawah: they shall not shabai (satisfy) their napash (living being/soul), neither malaa (fill) their maih (bowels); because it has been the makashawal (stumbling) block of their iwan (guilt/iniquity).

As for the beauty of his iday (ornament / adornment), he shawam (place / establish / appoint) it in gaawan (majesty); but they ishah (make) the tzalam (likeness) of their thawaibah (abominations) and their shaqawatz (detestable) things therein: therefore nathan (give) I made it to them as an nadah (unclean) thing.
I will nathan (give) it into the yad (hand) of the strangers for a baz (prey), and to the rashai (wicked) of the aratz (Earth/land) for a shalal (spoil); and they shall chalal (profane) it.
My panayam (face) will I sabab (turn) also from them, and they shall chalal (profane) my tzapan (secret) place; and parayatz (robbers) shall bawaa (come) into it, and chalal (profane) it.
Ishah (make) the rathawaq (chain); for the aratz (Earth/land) is malaa (full) of bloody mashapat (crimes), and the iyar (city) is malaa (full) of chamas (violence).

Therefore I will bawaa (come) the rai (worst) of the gaway (nation / people), and they shall yarash (possess) their bayath (house): I will also make the gaawan (pride) of the iz (strong) to shabath (shabath/rest); and their qadash (set apart/make holy) places shall be chalal (profaned).
Qapadah (destruction) bawaa (come); and they shall baqash (seek) shalawam (peace / safety), and there shall be none.

Hawah (calamity/destruction) shall bawaa (come) on hawah (calamity/destruction), and shamawaih (rumor) shall be on shamawaih (rumor); and they shall baqash (seek) a chazawan (vision) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy); but the thawarah (instruction) shall abad (destroy/perish) from the kahan (priest), and itzah (counsel) from the zaqan (elders).

The malak (king) shall abal (mourn), and the nashayaa (prince) shall be labash (clothed) with shamamah (desolation), and the yad (hand) of the im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land) shall be bahal (troubled): I will ishah (make) to them after their darak (way), and according to their own mashapat (judgments) will I shapat (judge) them; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

It happened in the shashay (sixth) shanah (year), in the shashay (sixth) month, in the chamash (fifth) day of the chadash (month), as I yashab (inhabit/dwell) in my bayath (house), and the zaqan (elders) of Yahawadah (Judah) yashab (inhabit/dwell) panayam (before) me, that the yad (hand) of the Adanay Yahawah napal (fall / be cast down) there on me.

Then I raah (see), and behold, a damawath (likeness) as the maraah (appearance) of ash (fire); from the maraah (appearance) of his waist and matah (downward), ash (fire); and from his waist and upward, as the maraah (appearance) of zahar (brightness), as it were glowing metal.

He shalach (send) forth the thabanayath (form) of a yad (hand), and laqach (take / seized) me by a tzayatzath (lock) of my raash (head); and the rawach (spirit / wind) nashaa (lift) me up between aratz (Earth/land) and the sky, and bawaa (come) me in the maraah (visions) of Alahayam to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), to the pathach (door) of the shair (gate) of the inner court that panah (looks) toward the tzapawan (north); where there was the mawashab (seat) of the samal (image) of qanaah (jealousy), which qanah (provokes) to jealousy.
Behold, the kabawad (glory) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) was there, according to the maraah (appearance) that I raah (see) in the baqaih (plain).

Then he amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye) now the darak (way) toward the tzapawan (north). So I nashaa (lift) up my iyan (eye) the darak (way) toward the tzapawan (north), and see, northward of the shair (gate) of the mazabach (altar) this samal (image) of qanaah (jealousy) in the baah (entry).

He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), do you raah (see) what they ishah (make)? Even the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thawaibah (abominations) that the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) ishah (make) commit here, that I should rachaq (go) far off from my maqadash (sanctuary)? But you shall again raah (see) yet other gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thawaibah (abominations).
He bawaa (come) me to the pathach (door) of the chatzar (court); and when I raah (see), behold, a chawar (hole) in the qayar (wall).
Then he amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), chathar (dig) now in the qayar (wall): and when I had chathar (dug) in the qayar (wall), behold, a pathach (door).
He amar (spoke) to me, bawaa (come) in, and raah (see) the rai (wicked) thawaibah (abominations) that they ishah (make) here.

So I bawaa (come) in and raah (see); and see, every thabanayath (form) of ramash (creeping) things, and shaqatz (abominable) animals, and all the galawal (idols) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), chaqah (portrayed) around on the qayar (wall).

There imad (stood) panayam (before) them shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (husband/individual man) of the zaqan (elders) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel); and in their thawak (midst) imad (stood) Yaazanayah (Jaazaniah) the ban (son) Shapan (of) Shaphan, every ayash (husband/individual man) with his maqatarath (censer) in his yad (hand); and the odor of the inan (cloud) of qatarath (incense) ilah (go up / offer) up.

Then he amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), raah (see) you seen what the zaqan (elders) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) ishah (make) in the chashak (darkness), every ayash (husband/individual man) in his rooms of mashakayath (idol/carved image)? For they amar (spoke), Yahawah doesn't raah (see) us; Yahawah has forsaken the aratz (Earth/land).
He amar (spoke) also to me, You shall again raah (see) yet other gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thawaibah (abominations) which they ishah (make).

Then he bawaa (come) me to the pathach (door) of the shair (gate) of yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) bayath (house) which was toward the tzapawan (north); and see, there yashab (inhabit/dwell) the ashah (wife/individual woman) bakah (weeping) for Thamawaz (Tammuz).
Then he amar (spoke) to me, raah (see) you seen this, ban (son) of adam (man)? You shall again raah (see) yet greater thawaibah (abominations) than these.

He bawaa (come) me into the inner chatzar (court) of yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) bayath (house); and see, at the pathach (door) of the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, between the awalam (porch) and the mazabach (altar), were about isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) ayash (husband/individual man), with their achawar (backs) toward the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, and their panayam (faces) toward the qadam (east); and they were shachah (worshipping) the shamash (sun) toward the qadam (east).

Then he amar (spoke) to me, raah (see) you seen this, ban (son) of adam (man)? Is it a qalal (light) thing to the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) that they ishah (make) the thawaibah (abominations) which they ishah (make) here? For they malaa (have) filled the aratz (Earth/land) with chamas (violence), and have shawab (turn back / repent) again to provoke me to kais (anger): and behold, they shalach (send) the zamawarah (branch) to their ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).

Therefore will I also ishah (make) in chamah (wrath); my iyan (eye) shall not chawas (spare), neither will I chamal (have) pity; and though they qaraa (called) in my azan (ears) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice), yet will I not shamai (hearken / hear) them.

Then he qaraa (called) in my azan (ears) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice), amar (spoke), Cause those who are in paqadah (charge) of the iyar (city) to qarab (come close) near, every ayash (husband/individual man) with his mashachath (destroying) kalay (weapon) in his yad (hand).
