Behold, shash (six) ayash (husband/individual man) bawaa (come) from the darak (way) of the ilayawan (upper) shair (gate), which panah (lies) toward the tzapawan (north), every ayash (husband/individual man) with his mapatz (slaughter) kalay (weapon) in his yad (hand); and achad (one) ayash (husband/individual man) in their thawak (midst) labash (clothed) in bad (linen), with a sapar (book) qasath (inkhorn) by his mathan (side). They bawaa (come) in, and imad (stood) beside the bronze mazabach (altar).

The kabawad (glory) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) was ilah (go up / offer) up from the karawab (cherub), whereupon it was, to the mapathan (threshold) of the bayath (house): and he qaraa (called) to the ayash (husband/individual man) labash (clothed) in bad (linen), who had the sapar (book) qasath (inkhorn) by his mathan (side).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, ibar (pass over/through) through the thawak (midst) of the iyar (city), thawak (midst) the midst of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and thawah (set) a thaw (mark) on the matzach (foreheads) of the ibar (pass over/through) that anach (sigh) and that anaq (cry) over all the thawaibah (abominations) that are ishah (make) in its thawak (midst).

To the others he amar (spoke) in my azan (hearing), ibar (pass over/through) through the iyar (city) achar (other) him, and nakah (strike): don't let your iyan (eye) chawas (spare), neither chamal (have) pity;

Harag (kill) mashachayath (utterly) the zaqan (old) man, the bachawar (young) man and the bathawalah (virgin), and little tap (children) and ashah (wife/individual woman); but don't nagash (come) near any ayash (husband/individual man) on whom is the thaw (mark): and chalal (begin) at my maqadash (sanctuary). Then they chalal (began) at the zaqan (old) zaqan (men) that were panayam (before) the bayath (house).

He amar (spoke) to them, tamaa (defile) the bayath (house), and malaa (fill) the chatzar (courts) with the chalal (slain). Yatzaa (go out / come out) forth! They yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and nakah (struck) in the iyar (city).

It happened, while they were nakah (smiting), and I was shaar (left), that I napal (fall / be cast down) on my panayam (face), and zaiq (cried), and amar (spoke), ahah (ah) Adanay Yahawah! Will you shachath (destroy) all the shaarayath (residue) of Yasharaal (Israel) in your shapak (pouring) out of your chamah (wrath) on Yarawashalam (Jerusalem)?

Then he amar (spoke) to me, The iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah) is maad (exceedingly) gadawal (very great/important/mighty), and the aratz (Earth/land) is malaa (full) of dam (blood), and the iyar (city) malaa (full) of perversion: for they amar (spoke), Yahawah has forsaken the aratz (Earth/land), and Yahawah doesn't raah (see).
As for me also, my iyan (eye) shall not chawas (spare), neither will I chamal (have) pity, but I will nathan (give) their darak (way) on their raash (head).

Behold, the ayash (husband/individual man) labawash (clothed) in bad (linen), who had the qasath (inkhorn) by his mathan (side), reported the dabar (word / matter), amar (spoke), I ishah (make) done as you have tzawah (commanded) me.

Then I raah (see), and see, in the expanse that was over the raash (head) of the karawab (cherubim) there raah (see) above them as it were a sapayar (sapphire) aban (stone), as the maraah (appearance) of the damawath (likeness) of a kasaa (throne).

He amar (spoke) to the ayash (husband/individual man) labash (clothed) in bad (linen), and amar (spoke), bawaa (come) in bayan (between) the whirling galagal (wheels), even under the karawab (cherub), and malaa (fill) both your chapan (hands) with gachal (coals) of ash (fire) from bayan (between) the karawab (cherubim), and zaraq (scatter) them over the iyar (city). He bawaa (come) in as I watched.

Now the karawab (cherubim) imad (stood) on the yamayan (right hand) side of the bayath (house), when the ayash (husband/individual man) bawaa (come) in; and the inan (cloud) malaa (filled) the inner chatzar (court).

The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah rawam (will lift up) up from the karawab (cherub), and stood over the mapathan (threshold) of the bayath (house); and the bayath (house) was malaa (filled) with the inan (cloud), and the chatzar (court) was malaa (full) of the nagah (brightness) of yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) kabawad (glory).

The qawal (sound / voice) of the kanap (wings) of the karawab (cherubim) was shamai (hearken / hear) even to the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court), as the qawal (sound / voice) of Al Shaday when he dabar (word / matter).

It came to pass, when he tzawah (commanded) the ayash (husband/individual man) labash (clothed) in bad (linen), amar (spoke), laqach (take / seized) ash (fire) from between the whirling galagal (wheels), from between the karawab (cherubim), that he bawaa (come) in, and imad (stood) beside a awapan (wheel).

The karawab (cherub) shalach (send) forth his yad (hand) from between the karawab (cherubim) to the ash (fire) that was between the karawab (cherubim), and nashaa (lift) of it, and nathan (give) it into the chapan (hands) of him who was labash (clothed) in bad (linen), who laqach (take / seized) it and yatzaa (go out / come out) out.
There raah (see) in the karawab (cherubim) the thabanayath (form) of a adam (man's) yad (hand) under their kanap (wings).

I raah (see), and behold, arabai (four) awapan (wheels) beside the karawab (cherubim), achad (one) awapan (wheel) beside achad (one) karawab (cherub), and another awapan (wheel) beside another karawab (cherub); and the maraah (appearance) of the awapan (wheels) was like a tharashayash (beryl) aban (stone).
As for their maraah (appearance), the arabai (four) of them had achad (one) damawath (likeness), like a awapan (wheel) thawak (midst) a awapan (wheel).

When they yalak (went), they yalak (went) in their arabai (four) directions: they didn't sabab (turn) as they yalak (went), but to the maqawam (place) where the raash (head) panah (looked) they yalak (followed) it; they didn't sabab (turn) as they yalak (went).

Their whole bashar (flesh), and their gab (backs), and their yad (hand), and their kanap (wings), and the awapan (wheels), were malaa (full) of iyan (eye) all around, even the awapan (wheels) that the arabai (four) of them had.
As for the awapan (wheels), they were qaraa (called) in my azan (hearing), the whirling galagal (wheels).

Achad (one) one had arabai (four) panayam (faces): the achad (one) panayam (face) was the panayam (face) of the karawab (cherub), and the shanay (second) panayam (face) was the panayam (face) of a adam (man), and the shalayashay (third) panayam (face) the face of a aray (lion), and the rabayaiy (fourth) the panayam (face) of an nashar (eagle).
The karawab (cherubim) ramam (mounted) up: this is the chay (life) creature that I raah (see) by the nahar (river) Kabar (Chebar).

When the karawab (cherubim) yalak (went), the awapan (wheels) yalak (went) beside them; and when the karawab (cherubim) nashaa (lift) up their kanap (wings) to rawam (will lift up) up from the aratz (Earth/land), the awapan (wheels) also didn't sabab (turn) from beside them.
When they imad (stood), these imad (stood); and when they rawam (will lift up) up, these ramam (mounted) up with them: for the rawach (spirit / wind) of the chay (life) creature was in them.
The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from over the mapathan (threshold) of the bayath (house), and imad (stood) over the karawab (cherubim).

The karawab (cherubim) nashaa (lift) up their kanap (wings), and ramam (mounted) up from the aratz (Earth/land) in my iyan (eye) when they yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and the awapan (wheels) imah (beside) them: and they imad (stood) at the pathach (door) of the qadamawanay (east) shair (gate) of yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) bayath (house); and the kabawad (glory) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) was over them mail (top/above).
This is the chay (life) creature that I raah (see) under the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) by the nahar (river) Kabar (Chebar); and I yadai (knew) that they were karawab (cherubim).
Achad (one) one had arabai (four) panayam (faces), and achad (one) one arabai (four) kanap (wings); and the damawath (likeness) of the yad (hand) of a adam (man) was under their kanap (wings).

As for the damawath (likeness) of their panayam (faces), they were the panayam (faces) which I raah (see) by the nahar (river) Kabar (Chebar), their maraah (appearances) and themselves; they yalak (went) ayash (husband/individual man) one ibar (straight) forward.

Moreover the rawach (spirit / wind) nashaa (lift) me up, and bawaa (come) me to the qadamawanay (east) shair (gate) of yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) bayath (house), which panah (looks) eastward: and see, at the pathach (door) of the shair (gate) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) ayash (husband/individual man); and I raah (see) in their thawak (midst) Yaazanayah (Jaazaniah) the ban (son) of Izawar (Azzur), and Palatayah (Pelatiah) the ban (son) of Banayah (Benaiah), shar (prince / ruler) of the im (people / nation).
He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), these are the ban (son) who chashab (devise) awan (iniquity), and who yaitz (give) rai (wicked) itzah (counsel) in this iyar (city);
Who amar (spoke), The time is not qarawab (near) to banah (build) bayath (house): this is the sayar (caldron), and we are the meat.
Therefore nabaa (prophesy) against them, nabaa (prophesy), ban (son) of adam (man).

The rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah napal (fall / be cast down) on me, and he amar (spoke) to me, amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: Thus you have amar (spoke), bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel); for I yadai (know) the things that mailah (ascent/climbing up) into your rawach (spirit / wind).
You rabah (have) multiplied your chalal (slain) in this iyar (city), and you malaa (have) filled its chawatz (streets) with the chalal (slain).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Your chalal (slain) whom you have shawam (place / establish / appoint) in its thawak (midst), they are the meat, and this is the sayar (caldron); but you shall be yatzaa (go out / come out) out of its thawak (midst).
You have yaraa (fear / be afraid) the charab (sword); and I will bawaa (come) the charab (sword) on you, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
I will yatzaa (go out / come out) you forth out of its thawak (midst), and nathan (give) you into the yad (hand) of strangers, and will ishah (make) shapat (judgments) among you.
You shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword); I will shapat (judge) you in the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yasharaal (Israel); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
This shall not be your sayar (caldron), neither shall you be the meat in its thawak (midst); I will shapat (judge) you in the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yasharaal (Israel);

And you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah: for you have not halak (move) in my chaq (statute), neither ishah (make) you executed my mashapat (ordinances), but ishah (make) done after the mashapat (ordinances) of the gaway (nation / people) that are around you.

It happened, when I nabaa (prophesied), that Palatayah (Pelatiah) the ban (son) of Banayah (Benaiah) mawath (death). Then napal (fall / be cast down) I down on my panayam (face), and zaiq (cried) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice), and amar (spoke), ahah (ah) Adanay Yahawah! Will you ishah (make) a kalah (complete / finish) end of the shaarayath (remnant) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), your ach (brother/kinsman), even your ach (brother/kinsman), the ban (son) of your relatives, and all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), all of them, to whom the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) have amar (spoke), rachaq (go) far away from Yahawah. This aratz (Earth/land) nathan (give) been given to us for a mawarashah (possession).

Therefore amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Whereas I have rachaq (removed) them far off among the gaway (nation / people), and whereas I have pawatz (scattered) them among the aratz (Earth/land), yet will I be to them a maqadash (sanctuary) for a mait (little) while in the aratz (Earth/land) where they bawaa (come) come.

Therefore amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will qabatz (gather) you from the im (people / nation), and asap (assemble) you out of the aratz (Earth/land) where you have been pawatz (scattered), and I will nathan (give) you the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel).
They shall bawaa (come) there, and they shall sawar (take) away all the shaqawatz (detestable) things of it and all its thawaibah (abominations) from there.

I will nathan (give) them achad (one) lab (heart), and I will nathan (give) a chadash (new) rawach (spirit / wind) qarab (among / near) you; and I will sawar (take) the aban (stone) lab (heart) out of their bashar (flesh), and will nathan (give) them a lab (heart) of bashar (flesh);
That they may yalak (walk) in my chaqah (statutes), and shamar (keep/guard) my mashapat (ordinances), and ishah (make) them: and they shall be my im (people / nation), and I will be their Alahayam.

But as for them whose lab (heart) halak (move) after the lab (heart) of their shaqawatz (detestable) things and their thawaibah (abominations), I will nathan (give) their darak (way) on their own raash (head), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

Then the karawab (cherubim) nashaa (lift) up their kanap (wings), and the awapan (wheels) were imah (beside) them; and the kabawad (glory) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) was over them mail (top/above).
The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah ilah (go up / offer) up from the thawak (midst) of the iyar (city), and imad (stood) on the har (mountain) which is on the qadam (east) side of the iyar (city).

The rawach (spirit / wind) nashaa (lift) me up, and bawaa (come) me in the maraah (vision) by the rawach (spirit / wind) of Alahayam into Kashaday (Chaldea), to them of the gawalah (captivity). So the maraah (vision) that I raah (see) seen ilah (go up / offer) up from me.
Then I dabar (word / matter) to them of the gawalah (captivity) all the things that Yahawah raah (see) shown me.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah also came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), you yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the thawak (midst) of the rebellious bayath (house), who have iyan (eye) to raah (see), and don't raah (see), who have azan (ears) to shamai (hearken / hear), and don't shamai (hearken / hear); for they are a rebellious bayath (house).

Therefore, you ban (son) of adam (man), ishah (make) your kalay (stuff) for moving, and move by yawamam (by day) in their iyan (eye); and you shall move from your maqawam (place) to achar (other) maqawam (place) in their iyan (eye): it may be they will raah (see), though they are a rebellious bayath (house).

You shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth your kalay (stuff) by yawamam (by day) in their iyan (eye), as kalay (stuff) for moving; and you shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth yourself at even in their iyan (eye), as when men mawatzaa (go) forth into exile.
Chathar (dig) through the qayar (wall) in their iyan (eye), and yatzaa (go out / come out) your stuff out that way.

In their iyan (eye) you shall nashaa (lift) it on your kathap (shoulder), and yatzaa (go out / come out) it forth in the ilatah (dark); you shall kasah (cover) your panayam (face), so that you don't raah (see) the aratz (Earth/land): for I nathan (give) set you for a mawapath (sign) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

I ishah (make) so as I was tzawah (commanded): I yatzaa (go out / come out) forth my kalay (stuff) by yawamam (by day), as kalay (stuff) for gawalah (removing), and in the even I chathar (dug) through the qayar (wall) with my yad (hand); I yatzaa (go out / come out) it forth in the ilatah (dark), and nashaa (lift) it on my kathap (shoulder) in their iyan (eye).
In the baqar (morning) came the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), has not the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), the rebellious bayath (house), amar (spoke) to you, What are you ishah (make)?

Amar (spoke) to them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: This mashaa (burden) concerns the nashayaa (prince) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) thawak (midst) whom they are.
Amar (spoke), I am your mawapath (sign): like as I ishah (make) done, so shall it be ishah (make) to them; they shall yalak (go) into exile, into shabay (captivity).

The nashayaa (prince) who is thawak (midst) them shall nashaa (lift) on his kathap (shoulder) in the ilatah (dark), and shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth: they shall chathar (dig) through the qayar (wall) to yatzaa (go out / come out) out thereby: he shall kasah (cover) his panayam (face), yain (because) he shall not raah (see) the aratz (Earth/land) with his iyan (eye).

My rashath (net) also will I parash (spread) on him, and he shall be thapash (taken) in my matzawad (snare); and I will bawaa (come) him to Babal (Babylon) to the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans); yet shall he not raah (see) it, though he shall mawath (death) there.
I will zarah (scatter) toward every rawach (spirit / wind) all who are around him to izar (help) him, and all his agap (bands); and I will rawaq (draw) out the charab (sword) achar (other) them.
They shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shall zarah (disperse) them among the gaway (nation / people), and pawatz (scatter) them through the aratz (Earth/land).

But I will yathar (leave) a masapar (few) ayash (husband/individual man) of them from the charab (sword), from the raib (famine), and from the dabar (word / matter); that they may sapar (book) all their thawaibah (abominations) among the gaway (nation / people) where they bawaa (come); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Moreover the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), akal (eat) your lacham (bread) with raish (quaking), and shathah (drinks) your mayam (Waters) with ragazah (trembling) and with fearfulness;

And amar (spoke) the im (people / nation) of the adamah (land), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah concerning the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and the aratz (Earth/land) of Yasharaal (Israel): They shall akal (eat) their lacham (bread) with fearfulness, and shathah (drinks) their mayam (Waters) in shamamawan (dismay), that her aratz (Earth/land) may be yasham (desolate), and malaa (all) that is therein, because of the chamas (violence) of all those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein.
The iyar (cities) that are yashab (inhabit/dwell) shall be charab (laid) waste, and the aratz (Earth/land) shall be a shamamah (desolation); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), what is this mashal (proverb) that you have in the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), The yawam (day) are prolonged, and every chazawan (vision) abad (destroy/perish)?

Amar (spoke) them therefore, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will make this mashal (proverb) to shabath (shabath/rest), and they shall no more use it as a mashal (speak in proverb/parable) in Yasharaal (Israel); but dabar (word / matter) them, The yawam (day) are at qarab (come close), and the fulfillment of every chazawan (vision).
For there shall be no more any shawaa (vanity) chazawan (vision) nor chalaq (flattering) maqasam (divination) thawak (midst) the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

For I am Yahawah; I will dabar (word / matter), and the dabar (word / matter) that I shall dabar (word / matter) shall be ishah (make); it shall be no more mashak (deferred): for in your yawam (day), rebellious bayath (house), will I dabar (word / matter) the dabar (word / matter), and will ishah (make) it, dabar (word / matter) the Adanay Yahawah.
Again the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), behold, they of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke), The chazawan (vision) that he chazah (sees) is for many yawam (day) to come, and he prophesies of ith (times) that are rachawaq (far) off.

Therefore amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: None of my dabar (word / matter) shall be mashak (deferred) any more, but the dabar (word / matter) which I shall dabar (word / matter) shall be ishah (make), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy) against the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Yasharaal (Israel) who nabaa (prophesy), and amar (spoke) to those who nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) out of their own lab (heart), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah:
Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, haway (Alas/Woe!) To the foolish nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), who halak (move) their own rawach (spirit / wind), and raah (see) seen nothing!
Yasharaal (Israel), your nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) have been like foxes in the charabah (waste) places.

You have not ilah (go up / offer) up into the paratz (gaps), neither built up the gadar (wall) for the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), to imad (stand) in the malachamah (battle) in the yawam (day) of Yahawah.

They have chazah (seen) falsehood and kazab (lying) qasam (divination), who naam (declares (prophetically)), Yahawah amar (spoke); but Yahawah has not shalach (send) them: and they yachal (have) made men to hope that the dabar (word / matter) would be qawam (rise up).

Haven't you chazah (seen) a shawaa (vanity) machazah (vision), and haven't you dabar (word / matter) a shawaa (vanity) maqasam (divination), in that you amar (spoke), Yahawah naam (declares (prophetically)); but I have not amar (spoke)?

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you have dabar (word / matter) falsehood, and chazah (seen) kazab (lies), therefore, behold, I am against you, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

My yad (hand) shall be against the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) who chazah (see) shawaa (vanity) visions, and who qasam (divine) kazab (lies): they shall not be in the council of my im (people / nation), neither shall they be kathab (written) in the kathab (writing) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), neither shall they bawaa (come) into the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel); and you shall yadai (know) that I am the Adanay Yahawah.

Because, even because they have taih (seduced) my im (people / nation), amar (spoke), shalawam (peace / safety); and there is no shalawam (peace / safety); and when one banah (builds) up a chayatz (wall), hanah (Behold), they plaster it with whitewash:

Amar (spoke) those who plaster it with whitewash, that it shall napal (fall / be cast down): there shall be an shatap (overflowing) gasham (shower); and you, alagabayash (great) hailstones, shall napal (fall / be cast down); and a sair (stormy) rawach (spirit / wind) shall baqai (tear) it.
Behold, when the qayar (wall) napal (fall / be cast down) fallen, shall it not be amar (spoke) to you, Where is the plaster with which you have plastered it?

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will even baqai (tear) it with a sair (stormy) rawach (spirit / wind) in my chamah (wrath); and there shall be an shatap (overflowing) gasham (shower) in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and alagabayash (great) hailstones in chamah (wrath) to kalah (complete / finish) it.

So will I haras (break) down the qayar (wall) that you have plastered with whitewash, and nagai (bring) it down to the aratz (Earth/land), so that its yasawad (foundation) shall be galah (uncovered); and it shall napal (fall / be cast down), and you shall be kalah (complete / finish) in its thawak (midst): and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Thus will I kalah (complete / finish) my chamah (wrath) on the qayar (wall), and on those who have plastered it with whitewash; and I will amar (spoke) you, The qayar (wall) is no more, neither those who plastered it;

To wit, the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Yasharaal (Israel) who nabaa (prophesy) concerning Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and who chazah (see) chazawan (vision) of shalawam (peace / safety) for her, and there is no shalawam (peace / safety), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

You, ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) against the bath (daughter) of your im (people / nation), who nabaa (prophesy) out of their own lab (heart); and nabaa (prophesy) against them,

And amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: haway (Alas/Woe!) To the women who thapar (sew) kasath (pillows) on all elbows, and ishah (make) masapachah (kerchiefs) for the raash (head) of persons of every qawamah (stature) to tzawad (hunt) napash (living being/soul)! Will you tzawad (hunt) the napash (living being/soul) of my im (people / nation), and chayah (save) napash (living being/soul) chayah (alive) for yourselves?

You have chalal (profaned) me among my im (people / nation) for shail (handfuls) of shairah (barley) and for path (pieces) of lacham (bread), to mawath (death) the napash (living being/soul) who should not mawath (death), and to chayah (save) the napash (living being/soul) chayah (alive) who should not chayah (live), by your kazab (lying) to my im (people / nation) who shamai (hearken / hear) to kazab (lies).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against your kasath (pillows), with which you there tzawad (hunt) the napash (living being/soul) to parach (make) them fly, and I will qarai (tear) them from your zarawai (arms); and I will let the napash (living being/soul) shalach (send), even the napash (living being/soul) whom you tzawad (hunt) to parach (make) them fly.

Your masapachah (kerchiefs) also will I qarai (tear), and natzal (deliver) my im (people / nation) out of your yad (hand), and they shall be no more in your yad (hand) to be matzawad (hunted); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Because with shaqar (lies) you have kaah (grieved) the lab (heart) of the tzadayaq (righteous), whom I have not kaah (made) sad; and chazaq (strengthened) the yad (hand) of the rai (wicked), that he should not shawab (turn back / repent) from his rashai (wicked) darak (way), and be chayah (saved) alive:

Therefore you shall no more chazah (see) shawaa (vanity) visions, nor practice qasam (divination). I will natzal (deliver) my im (people / nation) out of your yad (hand); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Then bawaa (come) ayash (husband/individual man) of the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) to me, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) panayam (before) me.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), these ban (son) have ilah (go up / offer) their galawal (idols) into their lab (heart), and nathan (give) the makashawal (stumbling) block of their iwan (guilt/iniquity) nakach (before) their panayam (face): should I be darash (inquired) of at darash (all) by them?

Therefore dabar (word / matter) to them, and amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Every ayash (husband/individual man) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) who ilah (go up / offer) his galawal (idols) into his lab (heart), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the makashawal (stumbling) block of his iwan (guilt/iniquity) nakach (before) his panayam (face), and bawaa (come) to the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy); I Yahawah will inah (answer / respond) him therein according to the rab (multitude) of his galawal (idols);
That I may thapash (take) the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) in their own lab (heart), because they are all zawar (estranged) from me through their galawal (idols).

Therefore amar (spoke) the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: shawab (turn back / repent), and shawab (turn back / repent) yourselves from your galawal (idols); and shawab (turn back / repent) away your panayam (faces) from all your thawaibah (abominations).

For everyone of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), or of the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who live in Yasharaal (Israel), who nazar (crown / consecrate) himself from me, and ilah (go up / offer) his galawal (idols) into his lab (heart), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the makashawal (stumbling) block of his iwan (guilt/iniquity) nakach (before) his panayam (face), and bawaa (come) to the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) to darash (inquire) for himself of me; I Yahawah will inah (answer / respond) him by myself:

And I will nathan (give) my panayam (face) against that ayash (husband/individual man), and will shamam (make) him an astonishment, for a awath (sign / mark / miracle) and a mashal (proverb), and I will karath (cut) him off from the thawak (midst) of my im (people / nation); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

If the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) is pathah (deceived) and dabar (word / matter) a dabar (word / matter), I, Yahawah, have pathah (deceived) that nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on him, and will shamad (destroy) him from the thawak (midst) of my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel).
They shall nashaa (lift) their iwan (guilt/iniquity): the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) shall be even as the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of him who darash (seeks) him;

That the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) may thaih (go) no more astray from me, neither tamaa (defile) themselves any more with all their pashai (transgressions); but that they may be my im (people / nation), and I may be their Alahayam, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), when a aratz (Earth/land) chataa (sins) against me by committing a mail (top/above), and I natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on it, and shabar (break) the matah (staff / rod / tribe) of its lacham (bread), and shalach (send) raib (famine) on it, and karath (cut) off from it adam (man) and animal;

Though these shalawash (three) ayash (husband/individual man), Nach (Noah), Danayaal (Daniel), and Ayawab (Job), were in it, they should natzal (deliver) but their own napash (living being/soul) by their tzadaqah (righteousness), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

If I cause rai (evil) animals to ibar (pass over/through) through the aratz (Earth/land), and they ravage it, and it be made shamamah (desolate), so that no ibar (pass over/through) may pass through panayam (because) of the animals;

Though these shalawash (three) ayash (husband/individual man) were in it, as I chay (life), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, they should natzal (deliver) neither ban (son) nor bath (daughter); they only should be natzal (delivered), but the aratz (Earth/land) should be shamamah (desolate).

Or if I bawaa (come) a charab (sword) on that aratz (Earth/land), and amar (spoke), charab (sword), ibar (pass over/through) through the aratz (Earth/land); so that I karath (cut) off from it adam (man) and animal;

Though these shalawash (three) ayash (husband/individual man) were in it, as I chay (life), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, they should natzal (deliver) neither ban (son) nor bath (daughter), but they only should be natzal (delivered) themselves.
Or if I shalach (send) a dabar (word / matter) into that aratz (Earth/land), and shapak (pour) out my chamah (wrath) on it in dam (blood), to karath (cut) off from it adam (man) and animal;

Though Nach (Noah), Danayaal (Daniel), and Ayawab (Job), were in it, as I chay (life), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, they should natzal (deliver) neither ban (son) am (mother) bath (daughter); they should but natzal (deliver) their own napash (living being/soul) by their tzadaqah (righteousness).

For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: How much more when I shalach (send) my arabai (four) severe shapat (judgments) on Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), the charab (sword), and the raib (famine), and the rai (evil) animals, and the dabar (word / matter), to karath (cut) off from it adam (man) and animal!

Yet, behold, therein shall be yathar (left) a palayatah (remnant) that shall be yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, both ban (son) and bath (daughter): behold, they shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to you, and you shall raah (see) their darak (way) and their ilayalah (doings); and you shall be nacham (turn away / repent) concerning the rai (evil) that I bawaa (come) brought on Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), even concerning all that I bawaa (come) brought on it.

They shall nacham (turn away / repent) you, when you raah (see) their darak (way) and their ilayalah (doings); and you shall yadai (know) that I ishah (make) not done chanam (without) cause all that I ishah (make) done in it, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), what is the gapan (vine) itz (tree) more than any itz (tree), the vine-branch which is among the itz (trees) of the yair (forest)?
Shall itz (wood) be laqach (take / seized) of it to ishah (make) any malaakah (work)? Or will men laqach (take / seized) a yathad (pin) of it to thalah (hang) any kalay (vessel) thereon?

Behold, it is nathan (give) into the ash (fire) for fuel; the ash (fire) has akal (eat) shanayam (two) its ends, and its thawak (midst) is charar (burned): is it tzalach (profitable) for any malaakah (work)?

Behold, when it was thamayam (complete / whole), it was ishah (make) for no malaakah (work): how much less, when the ash (fire) has akal (eat) it, and it is charar (burned), shall it yet be ishah (make) for any malaakah (work)!

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: As the gapan (vine) itz (tree) among the itz (trees) of the yair (forest), which I nathan (give) given to the ash (fire) for fuel, so will I nathan (give) the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

I will nathan (give) my panayam (face) against them; they shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from the ash (fire), but the ash (fire) shall akal (eat) them; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shawam (place / establish / appoint) my panayam (face) against them.
I will nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) shamamah (desolate), because they have mail (top/above) a mail (top/above), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
Again the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), cause Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) to yadai (know) her thawaibah (abominations);

And amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem): Your makawarah (birth) and your birth is of the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kanainay (Canaanite); the Amaray (Amorite) was your ab (father), and your am (mother) was a Chathay (Hittite).

As for your birth, in the yawam (day) you were yalad (birth / begot) your shar (prince / ruler) was not karath (cut), neither were you rachatz (washed) in mayam (Waters) to cleanse you; you weren't malach (salted) at malach (all), nor chathal (swaddled) at chathal (all).

No iyan (eye) chawas (pitied) you, to ishah (make) any of these things to you, to chamal (have) compassion on you; but you were shalak (cast) out in the panayam (open) shadah (field), for that your napash (living being/soul) was abhorred, in the yawam (day) that you were yalad (birth / begot).

When I ibar (pass over/through) by you, and raah (see) you wallowing in your dam (blood), I amar (spoke) to you, Though you are in your dam (blood), chayah (live); yes, I amar (spoke) to you, Though you are in your dam (blood), chayah (live).

I nathan (give) you to rababah (multiply) as that which tzamach (grows) in the shadah (field), and you rabah (increased) and gadal (grew) great, and you bawaa (come) to iday (ornament / adornment) iday (ornament / adornment); your shad (breasts) were kawan (fashioned), and your shair (hair) was tzamach (grown); yet you were iyaram (naked) and bore.

Now when I ibar (pass over/through) by you, and raah (see) at you, behold, your ith (time) was the ith (time) of dawad (love); and I parash (spread) my kanap (skirt) over you, and kasah (covered) your irawah (nakedness): yes, I shabai (swear / take oath) to you, and bawaa (come) into a barayath (covenant) with you, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, and you became mine.
Then rachatz (washed) I you with mayam (Waters); yes, I thoroughly shatap (washed) away your dam (blood) from you, and I sawak (anointed) you with shaman (oil).
I labash (clothed) you also with embroidered raqamah (work), and shod you with sealskin, and I dressed you about with shash (six) linen, and kasah (covered) you with mashay (silk).
I idah (decked) you with iday (ornament / adornment), and I nathan (give) tzamayad (bracelets) on your yad (hand), and a rabayad (chain) on your garawan (neck).
I nathan (give) a ring on your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and igayal (earrings) in your azan (ears), and a thapaarah (beautiful) itarah (crown) on your raash (head).

Thus you were idah (decked) with zahab (gold) and kasap (silver); and your clothing was of shash (six) linen, and mashay (silk), and embroidered raqamah (work); you akal (eat) fine salath (flour), and dabash (honey), and shaman (oil); and you were maad (exceedingly) yapah (beautiful), and you tzalach (prospered) to malawakah (royal) estate.

Your sham (name) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth among the gaway (nation / people) for your yapay (beauty); for it was kalayal (perfect), through my hadar (glory / majesty / splendor) which I had shawam (place / establish / appoint) on you, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

But you batach (trusted) in your yapay (beauty), and zanah (played) the prostitute because of your sham (name), and shapak (poured) out your prostitution on everyone who ibar (pass over/through) by; his it was.

You laqach (take / seized) of your bagad (garments), and made for yourselves bamah (high) places ishah (make) with various colors, and zanah (played) the prostitute on them: the like things shall not bawaa (come), neither shall it be so.

You also laqach (take / seized) your thapaarah (beautiful) kalay (jewels) of my zahab (gold) and of my kasap (silver), which I nathan (give) given you, and ishah (make) for yourself tzalam (likeness) of zakar (remembrance/memory), and zanah (played) the prostitute with them;
And you laqach (take / seized) your embroidered bagad (garments), and kasah (covered) them, and nathan (give) my shaman (oil) and my qatarath (incense) panayam (before) them.

My lacham (bread) also which I nathan (give) you, fine salath (flour), and shaman (oil), and dabash (honey), with which I akal (eat) you, you even nathan (give) it panayam (before) them for a pleasant aroma; and thus it was, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

Moreover you have laqach (take / seized) your ban (son) and your bath (daughter), whom you have yalad (birth / begot) to me, and you have zabach (sacrificed) these to them to be akal (eat). Was your prostitution a mait (small) matter,
That you have shachat (slain) my ban (son), and nathan (give) them up, in ibar (pass over/through) them to pass through the fire to them?

In all your thawaibah (abominations) and your prostitution you have not zakar (remembrance/memory) the yawam (day) of your naiwar (youth), when you were iyaram (naked) and bore, and were wallowing in your dam (blood).
It has happened achar (other) all your rai (wickedness), (away (woe), away (woe) to you! Naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah),
That you have banah (built) for yourselves a vaulted gab (place), and ishah (make) made yourselves a lofty ramah (place) in every rachab (street).

You have banah (built) your lofty ramah (place) at the raash (head) of every darak (way), and have made your yapay (beauty) a thaib (abomination), and have pashaq (opened) your ragal (feet / foot) to everyone who ibar (pass over/through) by, and rabah (multiplied) your prostitution.
You have also zanah (committed) sexual immorality with the ban (son), your neighbors, gadal (great) of bashar (flesh); and rabah (have) multiplied your prostitution, to provoke me to kais (anger).

See therefore, I have natah (stretched) out my yad (hand) over you, and have garai (diminished) your ordinary food, and nathan (give) you to the napash (living being/soul) of those who shanaa (hate) you, the bath (daughter) of the Palashathay (Philistines), who are kalam (ashamed) of your zamah (lewd) darak (way).
You have zanah (played) the prostitute also with the ban (son), balathay (because) you were insatiable; yes, you have zanah (played) the prostitute with them, and yet you weren't shabaih (seven).
You rabah (have) moreover multiplied your prostitution to the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (merchants), to Kashaday (Chaldea); and yet you weren't shabai (satisfied) with zaath (this).
How amal (weak) is your labah (heart), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, since you ishah (make) all these things, the maishah (work) of a impudent prostitute;

In that you banah (build) your vaulted gab (place) at the raash (head) of every darak (way), and ishah (make) your lofty ramah (place) in every rachab (street), and have not been as a prostitute, in that you qalas (scorn) pay.
A ashah (wife/individual woman) who naap (commits) adultery! Who laqach (take / seized) strangers instead of her ayash (husband/individual man)!

They nathan (give) nadah (gifts) to all prostitutes; but you nathan (give) your nadan (gifts) to all your lovers, and bribe them, that they may bawaa (come) to you on sabayab (surrounding) side for your prostitution.

You are different from other ashah (wife/individual woman) in your prostitution, in that no one achar (other) you to zanah (play) the prostitute; and whereas you nathan (give) athanan (hire), and no athanan (hire) is nathan (give) to you, therefore you are different.
Therefore, prostitute, shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah:

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, Because your nachashath (filthiness) was shapak (poured) out, and your irawah (nakedness) galah (uncovered) through your prostitution with your lovers; and because of all the galawal (idols) of your thawaibah (abominations), and for the dam (blood) of your ban (son), that you nathan (give) to them;

Therefore see, I will qabatz (gather) all your lovers, with whom you have irab (evening) pleasure, and all those who you have ahab (love), with all those who you have shanaa (hate); I will even qabatz (gather) them against you on sabayab (surrounding) side, and will galah (uncover) your irawah (nakedness) to them, that they may raah (see) all your irawah (nakedness).

I will shapat (judge) you, as naap (women) who break wedlock and shapak (shed) dam (blood) are mashapat (judged); and I will nathan (give) on you the dam (blood) of chamah (wrath) and qanaah (jealousy).

I will also nathan (give) you into their yad (hand), and they shall haras (throw) down your vaulted gab (place), and nathatz (break) down your lofty ramah (places); and they shall pashat (strip) you of your clothes, and laqach (take / seized) your thapaarah (beautiful) kalay (jewels); and they shall yanach (leave) you iyaram (naked) and bore.
They shall also ilah (go up / offer) up a qahal (company) against you, and they shall ragam (stone) you with aban (stone), and bathaq (thrust) you through with their charab (sword).

They shall sharap (burn) your bayath (house) with ash (fire), and ishah (make) shapat (judgments) on you in the iyan (eye) of many ashah (wife/individual woman); and I will shabath (shabath/rest) you to cease from zanah (playing) the prostitute, and you shall also nathan (give) no athanan (hire) any more.
So will I cause my chamah (wrath) toward you to nawach (rest), and my qanaah (jealousy) shall sawar (depart) from you, and I will be shaqat (quiet), and will be no more kais (angry).

Because you have not zakar (remembrance/memory) the yawam (day) of your naiwar (youth), but have ragaz (raged) against me in all these things; therefore, haa (behold), I also will nathan (give) your darak (way) on your raash (head), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah: and you shall not ishah (make) this lewdness with all your thawaibah (abominations).
Behold, everyone who uses mashal (speak in proverb/parable) shall use this mashal (speak in proverb/parable) amar (spoke) you, saying, As is the am (mother), so is her bath (daughter).

You are the bath (daughter) of your am (mother), who loathes her ayash (husband/individual man) and her ban (son); and you are the achawath (sister) of your achawath (sisters), who loathed their ayash (husband/individual man) and their ban (son): your am (mother) was a Chathay (Hittite), and your ab (father) a Amaray (Amorite).

Your gadawal (very great/important/mighty) achawath (sister) is Shamarawan (Samaria), who yashab (inhabit/dwell) at your left shamaawal (left hand), she and her bath (daughter); and your younger achawath (sister), who yashab (inhabit/dwell) at your right yamayan (right hand), is Sadam (Sodom) and her bath (daughter).

Yet have you not halak (move) in their darak (ways), nor ishah (make) after their thawaibah (abominations); but, as if that were a very mait (little) thing, you were more shachath (corrupt) than they in all your darak (ways).

As I chay (life), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, Sadam (Sodom) your achawath (sister) ishah (make) not done, she nor her bath (daughter), as you ishah (make) done, you and your bath (daughter).

Behold, this was the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of your achawath (sister) Sadam (Sodom): gaawan (pride), fullness of lacham (bread), and prosperous ease was in her and in her bath (daughter); neither did she chazaq (strengthen) the yad (hand) of the inay (poor) and abayawan (needy).
They were gabah (haughty), and ishah (make) thawaibah (abomination) panayam (before) me: therefore I sawar (took) them away as I raah (see) good.

Neither has Shamarawan (Samaria) chataa (committed) chatzay (half) of your chataah (sin); but you rabah (have) multiplied your thawaibah (abominations) more than they, and have justified your achawath (sisters) by all your thawaibah (abominations) which you ishah (make) done.

You also, nashaa (lift) you your own kalamah (shame), in that you have given palal (judgment) for your achawath (sisters); through your chataah (sin) that you have thaib (committed) more abominable than they, they are more tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) that you: yes, be also bawash (confounded), and nashaa (lift) your kalamah (shame), in that you have justified your achawath (sisters).

I will shawab (turn back / repent) again their shabawath (captivity), the shabawath (captivity) of Sadam (Sodom) and her bath (daughter), and the shabawath (captivity) of Shamarawan (Samaria) and her bath (daughter), and the shabawath (captivity) of your shabawath (captives) in their thawak (midst);
That you may nashaa (lift) your own kalamah (shame), and may be kalam (ashamed) because of all that you ishah (make) done, in that you are a nacham (turn away / repent) to them.

Your achawath (sisters), Sadam (Sodom) and her bath (daughter), shall shawab (turn back / repent) to their qadamah (former) estate; and Shamarawan (Samaria) and her bath (daughter) shall shawab (turn back / repent) to their qadamah (former) estate; and you and your bath (daughter) shall shawab (turn back / repent) to your qadamah (former) estate.
For your achawath (sister) Sadam (Sodom) was not shamawaih (mentioned) by your pah (mouth) in the yawam (day) of your gaawan (pride),

Before your rai (wickedness) was galah (uncovered), as at the ith (time) of the charapah (reproach) of the bath (daughter) of Aram (Syria), and of all who are around her, the bath (daughter) of the Palashathay (Philistines), who do despite to you all around.
You have nashaa (lift) your lewdness and your thawaibah (abominations), naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.
For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will also ishah (make) with you as you ishah (make) done, who have bazah (despised) the alah (these) in parar (breaking) the barayath (covenant).
Nevertheless I will zakar (remembrance/memory) my barayath (covenant) with you in the yawam (day) of your naiwar (youth), and I will qawam (rise up) to you a iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant).

Then you shall zakar (remembrance/memory) your darak (ways), and be kalam (ashamed), when you shall laqach (take / seized) your achawath (sisters), your gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qatan (small/young/least) and your younger; and I will nathan (give) them to you for bath (daughter), but not by your barayath (covenant).
I will qawam (rise up) my barayath (covenant) with you; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah;

That you may zakar (remembrance/memory), and be bawash (confounded), and never pathachawan (open) your pah (mouth) any more, panayam (because) of your kalamah (shame), when I have kapar (forgiven) you all that you ishah (make) done, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), chawad (put) forth a chayadah (riddle), and mashal (speak in proverb/parable) a mashal (parable) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel);

And amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: A gadawal (very great/important/mighty) nashar (eagle) with gadawal (very great/important/mighty) kanap (wings) and long feathers, malaa (full) of nawatzah (feathers), which had various colors, bawaa (come) to Labanawan (Lebanon), and laqach (take / seized) the tzamarath (top) of the araz (cedar):

He qatap (cropped) off the topmost of the yanayaqah (young) twigs of it, and bawaa (come) it to a aratz (Earth/land) Kanain (of) traffic; he shawam (place / establish / appoint) it in a iyar (city) of rakal (merchants).

He laqach (take / seized) also of the zarai (seed) of the aratz (Earth/land), and planted it in a zarai (fruitful) shadah (soil); he laqach (take / seized) it beside many mayam (Waters); he shawam (place / establish / appoint) it as a tzapatzapah (willow) tree.

It tzamach (grew), and became a sarach (spreading) gapan (vine) of shapal (low) qawamah (stature), whose branches panah (turned) toward him, and its sharash (roots) were under him: so it became a gapan (vine), and ishah (make) forth branches, and shalach (send) forth paarah (sprigs).

There was also another gadawal (very great/important/mighty) nashar (eagle) with gadawal (very great/important/mighty) kanap (wings) and many nawatzah (feathers): and behold, this gapan (vine) bent its sharash (roots) toward him, and shalach (send) forth its branches toward him, from the irawagah (beds) of its plantation, that he might shaqah (water) it.

It was shathal (planted) in a tawab (pleasant/functional) shadah (soil) by many mayam (Waters), that it might ishah (make) forth branches, and that it might nashaa (lift) paray (fruit), that it might be a adarath (goodly) gapan (vine).

Amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Shall it tzalach (prosper)? Shall he not nathaq (pull) up its sharash (roots), and qasas (cut) off its paray (fruit), that it may yabash (dry land); that all its fresh tzamach (springing) leaves may yabash (dry land)? And not by a strong zarawai (arm) or many im (people / nation) can it be nashaa (lift) from its sharash (roots).

Yes, behold, being shathal (planted), shall it tzalach (prosper)? Shall it not yabash (dry land) yabash (dry land), when the qadayam (east) rawach (spirit / wind) touches it? It shall yabash (dry land) in the irawagah (beds) where it tzamach (grew).
Moreover the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Amar (spoke) now to the rebellious bayath (house), Don't you yadai (know) what these things mean? Amar (spoke) them, Behold, the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) bawaa (come) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and laqach (take / seized) its malak (king), and its shar (prince / ruler), and bawaa (come) them to him to Babal (Babylon):

And he laqach (take / seized) of the zarai (seed) malawakah (royal), and karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with him; he also bawaa (come) him under an alah (these), and bawaa (come) away the ayal (mighty) of the aratz (Earth/land);
That the mamalakah (kingdom) might be shapal (base), that it might not nashaa (lift) itself up, but that by shamar (keep/guard) his barayath (covenant) it might imad (stand).

But he marad (rebelled) against him in shalach (send) his malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) into Matzarayam (Egypt), that they might nathan (give) him sawas (horses) and many im (people / nation). Shall he tzalach (prosper)? Shall he malat (escape) who ishah (make) such things? Shall he parar (break) the barayath (covenant), and yet malat (escape)?

As I chay (life), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, surely in the maqawam (place) where the malak (king) dwells who made him malak (king), whose alah (these) he bazah (despised), and whose barayath (covenant) he parar (broke), even with him in the thawak (midst) of Babal (Babylon) he shall mawath (death).

Neither shall Paraih (Pharaoh) with his gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) and rab (great) qahal (company) help him in the malachamah (war), when they shapak (cast) up mounds and banah (build) dayaq (forts), to karath (cut) off many napash (living being/soul).

For he has bazah (despised) the alah (these) by parar (breaking) the barayath (covenant); and behold, he nathan (give) given his yad (hand), and yet ishah (make) done all these things; he shall not malat (escape).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: As I chay (life), surely my alah (these) that he has bazah (despised), and my barayath (covenant) that he has pawar (broken), I will even nathan (give) it on his own raash (head).

I will parash (spread) my rashath (net) on him, and he shall be thapash (taken) in my matzawad (snare), and I will bawaa (come) him to Babal (Babylon), and will enter into shapat (judgment) with him there for his mail (top/above) that he has mail (top/above) against me.

All his mabarach (fugitives) in all his agap (bands) shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword), and those who shaar (remain) shall be parash (scattered) toward every rawach (spirit / wind): and you shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will also laqach (take / seized) of the rawam (will lift up) tzamarath (top) of the araz (cedar), and will nathan (give) it; I will qatap (crop) off from the topmost of its yawanaqath (young) twigs a rak (tender) one, and I will shathal (plant) it on a gabah (high) and lofty har (mountain):

In the har (mountain) of the marawam (height) of Yasharaal (Israel) will I shathal (plant) it; and it shall nashaa (lift) forth inap (boughs), and ishah (make) paray (fruit), and be a adayar (goodly) araz (cedar): and under it shall shakan (dwell) all tzapawar (birds) of every kanap (wing); in the tzal (shade) of its branches shall they shakan (dwell).

All the itz (trees) of the shadah (field) shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have shapal (brought) down the gabah (high) itz (tree), have gabah (exalted) the shapal (low) itz (tree), have yabash (dry land) up the lach (green) itz (tree), and have made the yabash (dry land) itz (tree) to parach (flourish); I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) and ishah (make) done it.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me again, amar (spoke),

What do you mean, that you use this mashal (proverb) concerning the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), The ab (father) have akal (eat) basar (sour) grapes, and the ban (son) shan (teeth) are qahah (set) on edge?
As I chay (life), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, you shall not have occasion any more to use this mashal (proverb) in Yasharaal (Israel).

Behold, all napash (living being/soul) are mine; as the napash (living being/soul) of the ab (father), so also the napash (living being/soul) of the ban (son) is mine: the napash (living being/soul) who chataa (sins), he shall mawath (death).
But if a ayash (husband/individual man) is tzadayaq (righteous), and ishah (make) that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (righteousness),

And has not akal (eat) on the har (mountain), neither has nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye) to the galawal (idols) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), neither has tamaa (defiled) his neighbor's ashah (wife/individual woman), neither has qarab (come close) near to a ashah (wife/individual woman) in her impurity,

And has not wronged any, but has shawab (turn back / repent) to the chawab (debtor) his chabal (pledge), has gazal (taken) nothing by robbery, nathan (give) given his lacham (bread) to the raib (hungry), and has kasah (covered) the iyaram (naked) with a bagad (garment);

He who nathan (give) not given forth on interest, neither has laqach (take / seized) any tharabayath (increase), who has shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand) from iwal (iniquity), ishah (make) executed amath (truth) mashapat (justice) between ayash (husband/individual man) and ayash (husband/individual man),

Has halak (move) in my chaqah (statutes), and has shamar (keep/guard) my mashapat (ordinances), to ishah (make) truly; he is tzadayaq (righteous), he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
If he yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son) who is a parayatz (robber), a shedder of dam (blood), and who ishah (make) any achad (one) of these things,
And who ishah (make) not any of those duties, but even has akal (eat) on the har (mountain), and tamaa (defiled) his neighbor's ashah (wife/individual woman),

Has wronged the inay (poor) and abayawan (needy), has gazal (taken) by robbery, has not shawab (turn back / repent) the chabal (pledge), and has nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye) to the galawal (idols), ishah (make) committed thawaibah (abomination),

Nathan (give) given forth on interest, and has laqach (take / seized) tharabayath (increase); shall he then chayay (life)? He shall not chayah (live): he ishah (make) done all these thawaibah (abominations); he shall mawath (death) mawath (death); his dam (blood) shall be on him.
Now, behold, if he yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son), who raah (see) all his ab (father) chataah (sin), which he ishah (make) done, and raah (see), and ishah (make) not such like;

Who has not akal (eat) on the har (mountain), neither has nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye) to the galawal (idols) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), has not tamaa (defiled) his neighbor's ashah (wife/individual woman),

Neither has wronged any, has not taken anything to chabal (pledge), neither has gazal (taken) by robbery, but nathan (give) given his lacham (bread) to the raib (hungry), and has kasah (covered) the iyaram (naked) with a bagad (garment);

Who has shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand) from the inay (poor), who has not laqach (take / seized) interest nor tharabayath (increase), ishah (make) executed my mashapat (ordinances), has halak (move) in my chaqah (statutes); he shall not mawath (death) for the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of his ab (father), he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live).

As for his ab (father), because he ishaq (cruelly) ishaq (oppressed), gazal (robbed) his ach (brother/kinsman), and ishah (make) that which is not tawab (pleasant/functional) thawak (midst) his im (people / nation), behold, he shall mawath (death) in his iwan (guilt/iniquity).

Yet you amar (spoke), Why doesn't the ban (son) nashaa (lift) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the ab (father)? When the ban (son) ishah (make) done that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (righteousness), and has shamar (keep/guard) all my chaqah (statutes), and ishah (make) done them, he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live).

The napash (living being/soul) who chataa (sins), he shall mawath (death): the ban (son) shall not nashaa (lift) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the ab (father), neither shall the ab (father) nashaa (lift) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the ban (son); the tzadaqah (righteousness) of the tzadayaq (righteous) shall be on him, and the rashaih (wickedness) of the rashai (wicked) shall be on him.

But if the rashai (wicked) shawab (turn back / repent) from all his chataah (sin) that he ishah (make) committed, and shamar (keep/guard) all my chaqah (statutes), and ishah (make) that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (righteousness), he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live), he shall not mawath (death).
None of his pashai (transgressions) that he ishah (make) committed shall be zakar (remembrance/memory) against him: in his tzadaqah (righteousness) that he ishah (make) done he shall chayah (live).

Chapatz (have) I any chapatz (pleasure) in the mawath (death) of the rashai (wicked)? Naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah; and not rather that he should shawab (turn back / repent) from his darak (way), and chayah (live)?

But when the tzadayaq (righteous) shawab (turn back / repent) away from his tzadaqah (righteousness), and ishah (make) iwal (iniquity), and ishah (make) according to all the thawaibah (abominations) that the rashai (wicked) ishah (make) does, shall he chayay (life)? None of his tzadaqah (righteousness) deeds that he ishah (make) done shall be zakar (remembrance/memory): in his mail (top/above) that he has mail (top/above), and in his chataah (sin) that he has chataa (sinned), in them shall he mawath (death).

Yet you amar (spoke), The darak (way) of the Adanay is not thakan (equal). Shamai (hearken / hear) now, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel): Is my darak (way) not thakan (equal)? Aren't your darak (ways) thakan (unequal)?

When the tzadayaq (righteous) man shawab (turn back / repent) away from his tzadaqah (righteousness), and ishah (make) iwal (iniquity), and mawath (death) therein; in his iwal (iniquity) that he ishah (make) done shall he mawath (death).

Again, when the rashai (wicked) man shawab (turn back / repent) away from his rashaih (wickedness) that he ishah (make) committed, and ishah (make) that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (righteousness), he shall chayah (save) his napash (living being/soul) chayah (alive).
Because he raah (see), and shawab (turn back / repent) away from all his pashai (transgressions) that he ishah (make) committed, he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live), he shall not mawath (death).

Yet the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke), "The darak (way) of the Adanay is not fair." Bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), aren't my darak (ways) fair? Aren't your darak (ways) unfair?

Therefore I will shapat (judge) you, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), everyone according to his darak (ways), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah. Shawab (turn back / repent), and shawab (turn back / repent) yourselves from all your pashai (transgressions); so iwan (guilt/iniquity) shall not be your makashawal (ruin).

Shalak (cast) away from you all your pashai (transgressions), in which you have pashai (transgressed); and ishah (make) yourself a chadash (new) lab (heart) and a chadash (new) rawach (spirit / wind): for why will you mawath (death), bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel)?

For I chapatz (have) no pleasure in the mawath (death) of him who mawath (death), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah: therefore shawab (turn back / repent) yourselves, and chayah (live).
Moreover, nashaa (lift) up a qayanah (lamentation) for the nashayaa (princes) of Yasharaal (Israel),
And amar (spoke), What was your am (mother)? A labayaa (lioness): she couched among aray (lions), in the thawak (midst) of the young kapayar (lions) she rabah (nourished) her cubs.
She ilah (go up / offer) up achad (one) of her cubs: he became a young kapayar (lion), and he lamad (teach/instruct) to tarap (catch) the tarap (prey); he akal (eat) adam (men).

The gaway (nation / people) also shamai (hearken / hear) of him; he was thapash (taken) in their shachath (pit); and they bawaa (come) him with chach (hooks) to the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

Now when she raah (see) that she yachal (had) waited, and her thaqawah (hope) was abad (destroy/perish), then she laqach (take / seized) another of her cubs, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) him a young kapayar (lion).
He halak (move) up and down thawak (midst) the aray (lions); he became a young kapayar (lion), and he lamad (teach/instruct) to tarap (catch) the tarap (prey); he akal (eat) adam (men).

He yadai (knew) their palaces, and charab (laid) waste their iyar (cities); and the aratz (Earth/land) was yasham (desolate), and its fullness, because of the qawal (sound / voice) of his shaagah (roaring).

Then the gaway (nation / people) nathan (give) against him on sabayab (surrounding) side from the madayanah (provinces); and they parash (spread) their rashath (net) over him; he was thapash (taken) in their shachath (pit).

They nathan (give) him in a cage with chach (hooks), and bawaa (come) him to the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon); they bawaa (come) him into strongholds, that his qawal (sound / voice) should no more be shamai (hearken / hear) on the har (mountain) of Yasharaal (Israel).
Your am (mother) was like a gapan (vine), in your dam (blood), shathal (planted) by the mayam (Waters): it was parah (fruitful) and inap (full) of branches by reason of many mayam (Waters).

It had iz (strength / might / refuge) matah (staff / rod / tribe) for the scepters of those who mashal (rule/have dominion) rule, and their qawamah (stature) was gabah (exalted) among the ibath (thick) boughs, and they were raah (see) in their gabah (height) with the rab (multitude) of their branches.

But it was nathash (plucked) up in fury, it was shalak (cast) down to the aratz (Earth/land), and the qadayam (east) rawach (spirit / wind) yabash (dry land) up its paray (fruit): its iz (strength / might / refuge) matah (staff / rod / tribe) were paraq (broken) off and yabash (dry land); the ash (fire) akal (eat) them.
Now it is shathal (planted) in the madabar (wilderness), in a tzayah (dry) and tzamaa (thirsty) aratz (Earth/land).

Ash (fire) is yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the matah (staff / rod / tribe) of its branches, it has akal (eat) its paray (fruit), so that there is in it no iz (strength / might / refuge) matah (staff / rod / tribe) to be a scepter to mashal (rule/have dominion). This is a qayanah (lamentation), and shall be for a qayanah (lamentation).

It happened in the shabayaiy (seventh) shanah (year), in the chamayashay (fifth) month, the ishawar (tenth) day of the chadash (month), that ayash (husband/individual man) of the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) bawaa (come) to darash (inquire) of Yahawah, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) panayam (before) me.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), dabar (word / matter) to the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Is it to darash (inquire) of me that you bawaa (come) come? As I chay (life), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, I will not be darash (inquired) of by you.
Will you shapat (judge) them, ban (son) of adam (man), will you shapat (judge) them? Yadai (cause) them to know the thawaibah (abominations) of their ab (father);

And amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: In the yawam (day) when I bachar (chose) Yasharaal (Israel), and yad (hand) to the zarai (seed) of the bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and yadai (made) myself known to them in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), when I yad (hand) to them, amar (spoke), I am Yahawah your Alahayam;

In that yawam (day) I yad (hand) to them, to yatzaa (go out / come out) them forth out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) into a aratz (Earth/land) that I had thawar (searched) out for them, zawab (flow) with chalab (milk) and dabash (honey), which is the glory of all aratz (Earth/land).

I amar (spoke) to them, shalak (cast) away every ayash (husband/individual man) the shaqawatz (abominations) of his iyan (eye), and don't tamaa (defile) yourselves with the galawal (idols) of Matzarayam (Egypt); I am Yahawah your Alahayam.

But they marah (rebelled) against me, and would not shamai (hearken / hear) to me; they ayash (husband/individual man) didn't shalak (throw) away the shaqawatz (abominations) of their iyan (eye), neither did they izab (forsake) the galawal (idols) of Matzarayam (Egypt). Then I amar (spoke) I would shapak (pour) out my chamah (wrath) on them, to kalah (complete / finish) my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) against them in the thawak (midst) of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

But I ishah (make) for my sham (name) sake, that it should not be chalal (profaned) in the iyan (eye) of the gaway (nation / people), thawak (midst) which they were, in whose iyan (eye) I yadai (made) myself known to them, in yatzaa (go out / come out) them forth out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
So I yatzaa (go out / come out) them to go forth out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and bawaa (come) them into the madabar (wilderness).
I nathan (give) them my chaqah (statutes), and showed them my mashapat (ordinances), which if a adam (man) ishah (make), he shall chayay (life) in them.

Moreover also I nathan (give) them my shabath (shabath/rest), to be a awath (sign / mark / miracle) between me and them, that they might yadai (know) that I am Yahawah who qadash (set apart/make holy) them.

But the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) marah (rebelled) against me in the madabar (wilderness): they didn't halak (move) in my chaqah (statutes), and they maas (rejected) my mashapat (ordinances), which if a adam (man) ishah (make), he shall chayay (life) in them; and my shabath (shabath/rest) they maad (greatly) chalal (profaned). Then I amar (spoke) I would shapak (pour) out my chamah (wrath) on them in the madabar (wilderness), to kalah (complete / finish) them.
But I ishah (make) for my sham (name) sake, that it should not be chalal (profaned) in the iyan (eye) of the gaway (nation / people), in whose iyan (eye) I yatzaa (go out / come out) them out.

Moreover also I yad (hand) to them in the madabar (wilderness), that I would not bawaa (come) them into the aratz (Earth/land) which I nathan (give) given them, zawab (flow) with chalab (milk) and dabash (honey), which is the glory of all aratz (Earth/land);

Because they maas (rejected) my mashapat (ordinances), and didn't halak (move) in my chaqah (statutes), and chalal (profaned) my shabath (shabath/rest): for their lab (heart) halak (move) achar (other) their galawal (idols).
Nevertheless my iyan (eye) chawas (spared) them, and I didn't shachath (destroy) them, neither ishah (make) I make a kalah (complete / finish) end of them in the madabar (wilderness).

I amar (spoke) to their ban (son) in the madabar (wilderness), Don't yalak (walk) in the chaq (statute) of your ab (father), neither shamar (keep/guard) their mashapat (ordinances), nor tamaa (defile) yourselves with their galawal (idols).
I am Yahawah your Alahayam: yalak (walk) in my chaqah (statutes), and shamar (keep/guard) my mashapat (ordinances), and ishah (make) them;
And make my shabath (shabath/rest) qadash (set apart/make holy); and they shall be a awath (sign / mark / miracle) between me and you, that you may yadai (know) that I am Yahawah your Alahayam.

But the ban (son) marah (rebelled) against me; they didn't halak (move) in my chaqah (statutes), neither shamar (keep/guard) my mashapat (ordinances) to ishah (make) them, which if a adam (man) ishah (make), he shall chayay (life) in them; they chalal (profaned) my shabath (shabath/rest). Then I amar (spoke) I would shapak (pour) out my chamah (wrath) on them, to kalah (complete / finish) my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) against them in the madabar (wilderness).

Nevertheless I shawab (turn back / repent) my yad (hand), and ishah (make) for my sham (name) sake, that it should not be chalal (profaned) in the iyan (eye) of the gaway (nation / people), in whose iyan (eye) I yatzaa (go out / come out) them forth.
Moreover I yad (hand) to them in the madabar (wilderness), that I would pawatz (scatter) them among the gaway (nation / people), and zarah (disperse) them through the aratz (Earth/land);

Because they ishah (make) not executed my mashapat (ordinances), but had maas (rejected) my chaqah (statutes), and had chalal (profaned) my shabath (shabath/rest), and their iyan (eye) were achar (other) their ab (father)' galawal (idols).
Moreover also I nathan (give) them chaq (statute) that were not tawab (pleasant/functional), and mashapat (ordinances) in which they should not chayah (live);

And I tamaa (polluted) them in their own mathanah (gifts), in that they ibar (pass over/through) to pass through the fire all that patar (opens) the racham (womb), that I might shamam (make) them desolate, to the end that they might yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Therefore, ban (son) of adam (man), dabar (word / matter) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: In this moreover have your ab (father) gadap (blasphemed) me, in that they have mail (top/above) a mail (top/above) against me.

For when I bawaa (come) brought them into the aratz (Earth/land), which I yad (hand) to nathan (give) to them, then they raah (see) every rawam (will lift up) gabaih (hill), and every ibath (thick) itz (tree), and they zabach (offered) there their zabach (sacrifices), and there they presented the kais (provocation) of their zabach (offering); there also they shawam (place / establish / appoint) their pleasant aroma, and they nasak (poured) out there their drink nasak (offerings).
Then I amar (spoke) to them, What does the bamah (high) place where you bawaa (come) mean? So its sham (name) is qaraa (called) Bamah (Bamah) to this yawam (day).

Therefore amar (spoke) the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Do you tamaa (pollute) yourselves in the darak (way) of your ab (father)? And do you zanah (play) the prostitute achar (other) their shaqawatz (abominations)?

And when you offer your mathanah (gifts), when you make your ban (son) to ibar (pass over/through) through the ash (fire), do you tamaa (pollute) yourselves with all your galawal (idols) to this yawam (day)? And shall I be darash (inquired) of by you, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel)? As I chay (life), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, I will not be darash (inquired) of by you;

And that which ilah (go up / offer) into your rawach (spirit / wind) shall not be at all, in that you amar (spoke), We will be as the gaway (nation / people), as the mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) of the aratz (Earth/land), to sharath (serve) itz (wood) and aban (stone).

As I chay (life), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, surely with a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and with an natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm), and with chamah (wrath) poured out, will I be malak (king) over you:

And I will yatzaa (go out / come out) you out from the im (people / nation), and will qabatz (gather) you out of the aratz (Earth/land) in which you are pawatz (scattered), with a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and with an natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm), and with chamah (wrath) shapak (poured) out;
And I will bawaa (come) you into the madabar (wilderness) of the im (people / nation), and there will I enter into shapat (judgment) with you panayam (face) to panayam (face).

Like as I entered into shapat (judgment) with your ab (father) in the madabar (wilderness) of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), so will I enter into shapat (judgment) with you, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
I will ibar (pass over/through) you to pass under the shabat (rod), and I will bawaa (come) you into the masarath (bond) of the barayath (covenant);

And I will barar (purge) out from among you the marad (rebels), and those who disobey against me; I will yatzaa (go out / come out) them forth out of the aratz (Earth/land) magawar (where) they live, but they shall not bawaa (come) into the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel): and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

As for you, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: yalak (go), ibad (servant) everyone his galawal (idols), and achar (other) also, if you will not shamai (hearken / hear) to me; but my qadash (set apart/make holy) sham (name) you shall no more chalal (profane) with your mathanah (gifts), and with your galawal (idols).

For in my qadash (set apart/make holy) har (mountain), in the har (mountain) of the marawam (height) of Yasharaal (Israel), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, there shall all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), all of them, ibad (servant) me in the aratz (Earth/land): there will I ratzah (accept) them, and there will I darash (require) your tharawamah (offerings), and the raashayath (beginning) fruits of your mashaath (offerings), with all your qadash (set apart/make holy) things.

As a pleasant aroma will I ratzah (accept) you, when I yatzaa (go out / come out) you out from the im (people / nation), and qabatz (gather) you out of the aratz (Earth/land) in which you have been pawatz (scattered); and I will be qadash (set apart/make holy) in you in the sight of the gaway (nation / people).

You shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shall bawaa (come) you into the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), into the aratz (Earth/land) which I yad (hand) to nathan (give) to your ab (father).

There you shall zakar (remembrance/memory) your darak (ways), and all your ilayalah (doings), in which you have tamaa (polluted) yourselves; and you shall qawat (loathe) yourselves in your own panayam (sight) for all your rai (evils) that you ishah (make) committed.

You shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I ishah (make) dealt with you for my sham (name) sake, not according to your rai (evil) darak (ways), nor according to your shachath (corrupt) ilayalah (doings), you bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) darak (toward) the thayaman (south), and natap (drop) your word toward the darawam (south), and nabaa (prophesy) against the yair (forest) of the shadah (field) in the nagab (south);
