And amar (spoke) the yair (forest) of the nagab (south), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah: Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, Behold, I will yatzath (kindle) a ash (fire) in you, and it shall akal (eat) every lach (green) itz (tree) in you, and every yabash (dry land) itz (tree): the lahabah (flaming) shalahabath (flame) shall not be kabah (quenched), and all panayam (faces) from the nagab (south) to the tzapawan (north) shall be burnt thereby.
All bashar (flesh) shall raah (see) that I, Yahawah, have bair (kindled) it; it shall not be kabah (quenched).
Then I amar (spoke), ahah (ah) Adanay Yahawah! They amar (spoke) of me, Isn't he a speaker of mashal (parables)?
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) toward Jerusalem, and natap (drop) your word toward the sanctuaries, and nabaa (prophesy) against the shadah (land) of Israel;

And amar (spoke) the land of Yahawah (Israel), Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: Behold, I am against you, and will draw forth my sword out of its sheath, and will cut off from you the righteous and the wicked.
Kay (surely) then that I will cut off from you the righteous and the wicked, therefore shall my sword kabah (go) forth out of its sheath against all bashar (flesh) from the south to the north:
And all flesh shall know that I, Yahawah, have drawn forth my sword out of its sheath; it shall not return any more.
Sigh therefore, you son of man; with the hayah (came to pass) of your thighs and with bitterness you will sigh before their eyes.

It shall be, when they shawam (place / establish / appoint) you, Why do you sigh? That you shall say, Because of the news, for it ban (son); and every heart shall melt, and all hands shall be feeble, and every spirit shall faint, and all knees shall be weak as water: behold, it ban (son), and it shall be shawam (place / establish / appoint), says the Adanay Yahawah.
The word of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Son of man, prophesy, and say, Thus says Yahawah: Say, A charab (sword), a charab (sword), it is sharpened, and also furbished;
It is sharpened that it may make a slaughter; it is furbished that it may be as lightning: shall we then yadai (make) mirth? The rod of my son, it condemns every tree.
It is given to be furbished, that it may be handled: the sword, it is sharpened, yes, it is furbished, to give it into the hand of the killer.

Cry and wail, son of man; for it is on my naam (declares (prophetically)), it is on all the princes of Yahawah (Israel): they are delivered over to the sword with my naam (declares (prophetically)); bawaa (come) therefore on your thigh.
For there is a trial; and what if even the rod that condemns shall be no more? Dabar (word / matter) the Adanay Yahawah.

You therefore, ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy), and strike your hands together; and let the charab (sword) be doubled the third time, the charab (sword) of the deadly wounded: it is the charab (sword) of the great one who is deadly wounded, which enters into their rooms.

I hayah (came to pass) set the threatening sword against all their gates, that their shabat (heart) may maas (melt), and their stumblings be multiplied: ah! It is shawash (made) as baraq (lightning), it is pointed for tabach (slaughter).
Gather yourselves together, go to the right, set yourselves in array, go to the left, wherever your face is nathan (give).
I will also sapaq (strike) my hands together, and I will cause my wrath to rest: I, Yahawah, have spoken it.
The word of Yahawah came to me again, saying,

Also, you ban (son) of adam (man), appoint two ways, that the charab (sword) of the king of Babylon may ban (son); they al (both) shall ban (son) forth out of one land: and mark out a place, mark it out at the head of the way to the city.
You shall nathan (give) a way for the charab (sword) to nathan (give) to Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and to Judah in Jerusalem the fortified.

For the king of Babylon panayam (stood) at the parting of the achad (one), at the head of the two achad (one), to use divination: he shook the arrows back and forth, he consulted the teraphim, he shawam (place / establish / appoint) in the liver.

In his right kap (hand) was the divination for Jerusalem, to nawach (set) battering rams, to open the mouth in the nakah (slaughter), to lift up the voice with shouting, to nawach (set) battering rams against the gates, to nakah (cast) up mounds, to build forts.
It shall be to them as a false divination in their sight, who have sworn oaths to them; but he brings dabar (word / matter) to memory, that they may be taken.

Therefore thus says the Adanay Yahawah: Because you have made your iniquity to be remembered, in that your transgressions are uncovered, so that in all your shawam (place / establish / appoint) your sins yatzaa (go out / come out); because you have ban (son) to memory, you shall be shawam (place / establish / appoint) with the yad (hand).
You, deadly wounded wicked one, the prince of Israel, whose day bawaa (come) come, in the time of the iniquity of the end,
Thus says the Adanay Yahawah: Remove the turban, and raah (see) off the crown; this shall be no more the same; exalt that which is low, and abase that which is raash (head).

I will shawam (place / establish / appoint), shawam (place / establish / appoint), shawam (place / establish / appoint) it: this also shall be no more, until he hayah (came to pass) whose yamayan (right hand) it is; and I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) it him.

You, son of man, prophesy, and say, Thus says the Adanay Yahawah concerning the children of Ammon, and concerning their reproach; and say, A sword, a sword is drawn, for the slaughter it is furbished, to cause it to devour, that it may be as lightning;

While they raah (see) for you false visions, while they divine lies to you, to lay you on the necks of the wicked who are deadly wounded, whose yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) raah (see) come in the time of the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the end.
Cause it to return into its sheath. In the place where you were created, in the land of your birth, will I judge you.
I will pour out my indignation on you; I will blow on you with the fire of my wrath; and I will deliver you into the hand of brutish men, skillful to destroy.
You shall be for fuel to the fire; your blood shall be in the midst of the land; you shall be remembered no more: for I, Yahawah, have spoken it.
Moreover the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
You, ban (son) of adam (man), will you shapat (judge), will you shapat (judge) the bloody iyar (city)? Then yadai (cause) her to know all her thawaibah (abominations).

You shall amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: A iyar (city) that shapak (sheds) dam (blood) in the thawak (midst) of her, that her ith (time) may bawaa (come), and that ishah (make) galawal (idols) against herself to tamaa (defile) her!

You have become asham (guilty) in your dam (blood) that you have shapak (shed), and are tamaa (defiled) in your galawal (idols) which you ishah (make) made; and you have caused your yawam (day) to qarab (come close) near, and bawaa (come) come even to your shanah (years): therefore nathan (give) I made you a charapah (reproach) to the gaway (nation / people), and a qalasah (mocking) to all the aratz (Earth/land).
Those who are qarawab (near), and those who are rachawaq (far) from you, shall qalas (mock) you, you tamaa (infamous) one and rab (full) of mahawamah (tumult).
Behold, the nashayaa (princes) of Yasharaal (Israel), everyone according to his zarawai (power), have been in you to shapak (shed) dam (blood).

In you have they set qalal (light) by ab (father) and am (mother); in the thawak (midst) of you ishah (make) they dealt by ishaq (oppression) with the foreigner; in you have they wronged the yathawam (fatherless) and the alamanah (widow).
You have bazah (despised) my qadash (set apart/make holy) things, and have chalal (profaned) my shabath (shabath/rest).

Slanderous ayash (husband/individual man) have been in you to shapak (shed) dam (blood); and in you they have akal (eat) on the har (mountain): in the thawak (midst) of you they ishah (make) committed lewdness.
In you have they galah (uncovered) their ab (father)' irawah (nakedness); in you have they inah (oppress / afflict) her who was nadah (unclean) in her impurity.

Ayash (husband/individual man) ishah (make) committed thawaibah (abomination) with his neighbor's ashah (wife/individual woman); and ayash (husband/individual man) has lewdly tamaa (defiled) his kalah (complete / finish); and ayash (husband/individual man) in you has inah (oppress / afflict) his achawath (sister), his ab (father) bath (daughter).

In you have they laqach (take / seized) shachad (bribes) to shapak (shed) dam (blood); you have laqach (take / seized) interest and tharabayath (increase), and you have greedily batzai (gained) of your neighbors by ishaq (oppression), and have shakach (forgotten) me, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
Behold, therefore, I have nakah (struck) my kap (hand) at your dishonest batzai (gain) which you ishah (make) made, and at your dam (blood) which has been in the thawak (midst) of you.

Can your lab (heart) imad (endure), or can your yad (hand) be chazaq (strong), in the yawam (day) that I shall ishah (make) with you? I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it, and will ishah (make) it.
I will pawatz (scatter) you among the gaway (nation / people), and zarah (disperse) you through the aratz (Earth/land); and I will thamam (consume) your tamaah (filthiness) out of you.
You shall be chalal (profaned) in yourself, in the iyan (eye) of the gaway (nation / people); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) has become sayag (dross) to me: all of them are nachashath (brass) and badayal (divide) and barazal (iron) and iwaparath (lead), in the thawak (midst) of the kawar (furnace); they are the sayag (dross) of kasap (silver).
Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you have all become sayag (dross), therefore, behold, I will qabatz (gather) you into the thawak (midst) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

As they qabatzah (gather) kasap (silver) and nachashath (brass) and barazal (iron) and iwaparath (lead) and badayal (divide) into the thawak (midst) of the kawar (furnace), to napach (blow) the ash (fire) on it, to nathak (melt) it; so will I qabatz (gather) you in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) and in my chamah (wrath), and I will yanach (lay) you there, and nathak (melt) you.
Yes, I will kanas (gather) you, and napach (blow) on you with the ash (fire) of my ibarah (wrath), and you shall be nathak (melted) in its thawak (midst).

As kasap (silver) is hathawak (melted) in the thawak (midst) of the kawar (furnace), so you will be nathak (melted) in its thawak (midst); and you yadai (will) know that I, Yahawah, have shapak (poured) out my chamah (wrath) on you.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), amar (spoke) her, You are a aratz (Earth/land) that is not tahar (cleansed), nor gasham (rained) on in the yawam (day) of zaim (indignation).

There is a qashar (conspiracy) of her nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) in its thawak (midst), like a shaag (roaring) aray (lion) ravening the tarap (prey): they have akal (eat) napash (living being/soul); they laqach (take / seized) chasan (treasure) and yaqar (precious) things; they have made her alamanah (widows) many in its thawak (midst).

Her kahan (priest) have chamas (done) violence to my thawarah (instruction), and have chalal (profaned) my qadash (set apart/make holy) things: they have badal (separated) no distinction between the qadash (set apart/make holy) and the chal (common), neither yadai (have) they caused men to discern between the tamaa (unclean) and the tahawar (clean), and have ilam (hidden) their iyan (eye) from my shabath (shabath/rest), and I am chalal (profaned) thawak (midst) them.

Her shar (prince / ruler) in its qarab (among / near) are like wolves ravening the tarap (prey), to shapak (shed) dam (blood), and to abad (destroy/perish) napash (living being/soul), that they may batzai (get) dishonest batzai (gain).

Her nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) have plastered for them with whitewash, seeing shawaa (vanity) visions, and qasam (divining) kazab (lies) to them, amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, when Yahawah has not dabar (word / matter).

The im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land) have used ishaq (oppression), and gazal (exercised) gazal (robbery); yes, they have troubled the inay (poor) and abayawan (needy), and have ishaq (oppressed) the foreigner wrongfully.

I baqash (sought) for a ayash (husband/individual man) among them, who should build up the gadar (wall), and imad (stand) in the paratz (gap) panayam (before) me for the aratz (Earth/land), that I should not shachath (destroy) it; but I matzaa (found) none.

Therefore have I shapak (poured) out my zaim (indignation) on them; I kalah (complete / finish) consumed them with the ash (fire) of my ibarah (wrath): their own darak (way) nathan (give) I brought on their raash (head), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came again to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), there were shanayam (two) ashah (wife/individual woman), the bath (daughter) of achad (one) am (mother):

And they zanah (played) the prostitute in Matzarayam (Egypt); they zanah (played) the prostitute in their naiwar (youth); there were their shad (breasts) maik (pressed), and there was handled the bosom of their bathawalayam (virginity).

Their sham (name) were Ahalah (Oholah) the gadawal (very great/important/mighty), and Ahalayabah (Oholibah) her achawath (sister): and they became mine, and they yalad (birth / begot) ban (son) and bath (daughter). As for their sham (name), Shamarawan (Samaria) is Ahalah (Oholah), and Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) Ahalayabah (Oholibah).
Ahalah (Oholah) zanah (played) the prostitute when she thachath (under) mine; and she igab (doted) on her lovers, on the Ashawar (Assyrians) her neighbors,
Who were labash (clothed) with thakalath (blue), pachah (governors) and sagan (rulers), all of them chamad (desirable) bachawar (young) men, horsemen rakab (riding) on sawas (horses).

She nathan (give) her prostitution on them, the mabachar (choicest) ban (son) of Ashawar (Assyria) all of them; and on whoever she igab (doted), with all their galawal (idols) she tamaa (defiled) herself.

Neither has she izab (left) her prostitution since the days of Matzarayam (Egypt); for in her naiwar (youth) they shakab (lay) with her, and they handled the bosom of her bathawalayam (virginity); and they shapak (poured) out their prostitution on her.
Therefore I nathan (give) her into the yad (hand) of her lovers, into the yad (hand) of the ban (son), on whom she igab (doted).

These galah (uncovered) her irawah (nakedness); they laqach (take / seized) her ban (son) and her bath (daughter); and her they harag (killed) with the charab (sword): and she became a byword among ashah (wife/individual woman); for they ishah (make) shapawat (judgments) on her.

Her achawath (sister) Ahalayabah (Oholibah) raah (see) this, yet was she more shachath (corrupt) in her doting than she, and in her prostitution which were more than the prostitution of her achawath (sister).

She igab (doted) on the ban (son), pachah (governors) and sagan (rulers), her neighbors, labash (clothed) most makalawal (gorgeously), horsemen rakab (riding) on sawas (horses), all of them chamad (desirable) bachawar (young) men.
I raah (see) that she was tamaa (defiled); they shanayam (two) took achad (one) darak (way).

She yasap (increased) her prostitution; for she raah (see) ayash (husband/individual man) chaqah (portrayed) on the qayar (wall), the tzalam (likeness) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans) portrayed with vermilion,

Dressed with azawar (girdles) on their waists, with flowing turbans on their raash (head), all of them shalayash (princes) to look on, after the damawath (likeness) of the ban (son) in Kashaday (Chaldea), the aratz (Earth/land) of their birth.
As soon as she maraah (saw) them she igab (doted) on them, and shalach (send) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to them into Kashaday (Chaldea).

The ban (son) bawaa (come) to her into the mashakab (bed) of dawad (love), and they tamaa (defiled) her with their prostitution, and she was tamaa (polluted) with them, and her napash (living being/soul) was yaqai (alienated) from them.

So she galah (uncovered) her prostitution, and galah (uncovered) her irawah (nakedness): then my napash (living being/soul) was yaqai (alienated) from her, like as my napash (living being/soul) was naqai (alienated) from her achawath (sister).

Yet she rabah (multiplied) her prostitution, zakar (remembrance/memory) the yawam (day) of her naiwar (youth), in which she had zanah (played) the prostitute in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
She igab (doted) on their payalagash (paramours), whose bashar (flesh) is as the bashar (flesh) of donkeys, and whose zaramah (issue) is like the zaramah (issue) of sawas (horses).
Thus you called to memory the lewdness of your naiwar (youth), in the handling of your bosom by the Matzarayam (Egyptians) for the shad (breasts) of your naiwar (youth).

Ahalayabah (Therefore), Oholibah, thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will iwar (rouse / awaken) up your lovers against you, from whom your napash (living being/soul) is naqai (alienated), and I will bawaa (come) them against you on sabayab (surrounding) side:

The ban (son) and all the Kashaday (Chaldeans), Paqawad (Pekod) and Shawai (Shoa) and Qawai (Koa), and all the ban (son) with them; chamad (desirable) bachawar (young) men, pachah (governors) and sagan (rulers) all of them, sagan (princes) and men of renown, all of them rakab (riding) on sawas (horses).

They shall bawaa (come) against you with weapons, rakab (chariots), and wagons, and with a qahal (company) of im (people / nation); they shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) themselves against you with tzanah (buckler) and magan (shield) and qawabai (helmet) all around; and I will nathan (give) the mashapat (judgment) to them, and they shall shapat (judge) you according to their mashapat (judgments).

I will nathan (give) my qanaah (jealousy) against you, and they shall ishah (make) with you in fury; they shall sawar (take) away your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) and your azan (ears); and your acharayath (residue) shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword): they shall laqach (take / seized) your ban (son) and your bath (daughter); and your acharayath (residue) shall be akal (eat) by the ash (fire).
They shall also pashat (strip) you of your clothes, and laqach (take / seized) away your thapaarah (beautiful) kalay (jewels).

Thus will I make your lewdness to shabath (shabath/rest) from you, and your prostitution brought from the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt); so that you shall not nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye) to them, nor zakar (remembrance/memory) Matzarayam (Egypt) any more.

For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will nathan (give) you into the yad (hand) of them whom you shanaa (hate), into the yad (hand) of them from whom your napash (living being/soul) is naqai (alienated);

And they shall ishah (make) with you in hatred, and shall laqach (take / seized) away all your yagayai (labor), and shall izab (leave) you iyaram (naked) and irayah (bare); and the irawah (nakedness) of your prostitution shall be galah (uncovered), both your lewdness and your prostitution.
These things shall be ishah (make) to you, because you have zanah (played) the prostitute achar (other) the gaway (nation / people), and because you are tamaa (polluted) with their galawal (idols).
You have halak (move) in the darak (way) of your achawath (sister); therefore will I nathan (give) her kawas (cup) into your yad (hand).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: You will shathah (drinks) of your achawath (sister's) kawas (cup), which is imaq (deep) and rachab (large); you will be ridiculed and held in laig (derision); it kawal (all/every/entire) much.

You shall be malaa (filled) with shakarawan (drunkenness) and yagawan (sorrow), with the kawas (cup) of shamah (astonishment) and shamamah (desolation), with the kawas (cup) of your achawath (sister) Shamarawan (Samaria).

You shall even shathah (drinks) it and drain it out, and you shall garam (gnaw) the broken pieces of it, and shall tear your shad (breasts); for I have dabar (word / matter) it, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you have forgotten me, and shalak (cast) me achar (other) your gaw (back), therefore you also nashaa (lift) your lewdness and your prostitution.
Yahawah amar (spoke) moreover to me: ban (son) of adam (man), will you shapat (judge) Ahalah (Oholah) and Ahalayabah (Oholibah)? Then nagad (declare) to them their thawaibah (abominations).

For they have naap (committed) adultery, and dam (blood) is in their yad (hand); and with their galawal (idols) have they naap (committed) adultery; and they have also caused their ban (son), whom they yalad (birth / begot) to me, to ibar (pass over/through) through the fire to them to be akalah (devoured).
Moreover this they ishah (make) done to me: they have tamaa (defiled) my maqadash (sanctuary) in the same yawam (day), and have chalal (profaned) my shabath (shabath/rest).

For when they had shachat (slain) their ban (son) to their galawal (idols), then they bawaa (come) the same yawam (day) into my maqadash (sanctuary) to chalal (profane) it; and behold, thus ishah (make) they done in the thawak (midst) of my bayath (house).

Ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) you have shalach (send) for ayash (husband/individual man) who bawaa (come) from marachaq (far), to whom a malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) was shalach (send), and behold, they bawaa (come); for whom you did rachatz (wash) yourself, kachal (paint) your iyan (eye), and decorate yourself with iday (ornament / adornment),

And yashab (inhabit/dwell) on a kabawadah (stately) matah (bed), with a shalachan (table) irak (prepared) panayam (before) it, whereupon you shawam (place / establish / appoint) my qatarath (incense) and my shaman (oil).

The qawal (sound / voice) of a hamawan (multitude) being at shalaw (ease) was with her: and with ayash (husband/individual man) of the rab (common) sort were bawaa (come) Sabaa (drunkards) from the madabar (wilderness); and they nathan (give) tzamayad (bracelets) on their yad (hand) twain, and thapaarah (beautiful) itarah (crowns) on their raash (head).
Then I amar (spoke) of her who was balah (old) in naap (adulteries), Now will they zanah (play) the prostitute with her, and she with them.
They bawaa (come) in to her, as they bawaa (come) in to a prostitute: so bawaa (come) they in Ahalah (to) Oholah and Ahalayabah (to) Oholibah, the zamah (lewd) ashah (wife/individual woman).

Tzadayaq (righteous) ayash (husband/individual man), they shall shapat (judge) them with the mashapat (judgment) of adulteresses, and with the mashapat (judgment) of women who shapak (shed) dam (blood); because they are adulteresses, and dam (blood) is in their yad (hand).
For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will ilah (go up / offer) up a qahal (company) against them, and will nathan (give) them to be tossed back and forth and robbed.

The qahal (company) shall ragam (stone) them with aban (stone), and baraa (created) them with their charab (sword); they shall harag (kill) their ban (son) and their bath (daughter), and sharap (burn) up their bayath (house) with ash (fire).
Thus will I cause lewdness to shabath (shabath/rest) out of the aratz (Earth/land), that all ashah (wife/individual woman) may be yasar (taught) not to ishah (make) after your lewdness.
They shall nathan (give) your lewdness on you, and you shall nashaa (lift) the chataa (sins) of your galawal (idols); and you shall yadai (know) that I am the Adanay Yahawah.

Again, in the thashayaiy (ninth) shanah (year), in the ishayaray (tenth) chadash (month), in the ishawar (tenth) day of the chadash (month), the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), kathab (write) the sham (name) of the yawam (day), even of this same yawam (day): the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) drew close to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) this same yawam (day).

Mashal (speak in proverb/parable) a mashal (parable) to the rebellious bayath (house), and amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, shapath (set) on the sayar (caldron), shapath (set) it on, and also yatzaq (pour) mayam (Waters) into it:

Asap (gather) its nathach (pieces) into it, even every tawab (pleasant/functional) nathach (piece), the yarak (thigh), and the kathap (shoulder); malaa (fill) it with the mabachar (choice) itzam (bones).

Laqach (take / seized) the mabachar (choice) of the tzaan (flock), and also a pile of wood for the itzam (bones) under the caldron; make it rathach (boil) rathach (well); yes, let its itzam (bones) be bashal (boiled) in its thawak (midst).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: away (woe) to the bloody iyar (city), to the sayar (caldron) whose rust is therein, and whose rust is not yatzaa (go out / come out) out of it! Yatzaa (go out / come out) out of it nathach (piece) after nathach (piece); No gawaral (lot) is napal (fall / be cast down) on it.

For her dam (blood) is in the thawak (midst) of her; she shawam (place / establish / appoint) it on the bare salai (rock); she didn't shapak (pour) it on the aratz (Earth/land), to kasah (cover) it with ipar (dust).
That it may cause chamah (wrath) to ilah (go up / offer) up to naqam (take) naqam (vengeance), I nathan (give) set her dam (blood) on the bare salai (rock), that it should not be kasah (covered).
Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: away (woe) to the bloody iyar (city)! I also will make the madawarah (pile) gadal (great).
Rabah (heap) on the itz (wood), make the ash (fire) hot, boil maraqachah (well) the bashar (flesh), and raqach (make) thick the broth, and let the itzam (bones) be charar (burned).

Then imad (set) it rayaq (empty) on its gachal (coals), that it may be yacham (hot), and its nachashath (brass) may charar (burn), and that its tamaah (filthiness) may be molten in it, that its rust may be thamam (consumed).
She has laah (wearied) herself with toil; yet her rab (great) rust doesn't yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of her; her rust doesn't go forth by ash (fire).

In your tamaah (filthiness) is lewdness: because I have tahar (cleansed) you and you weren't tahar (cleansed), you shall not be tahar (cleansed) from your tamaah (filthiness) any more, until I have caused my chamah (wrath) toward you to nawach (rest).

I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it: it shall happen, and I will ishah (make) it: I will not parai (go) back, neither will I chawas (spare), neither will I nacham (turn away / repent); according to your darak (ways), and according to your ilayalah (doings), shall they shapat (judge) you, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
Also the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), behold, I will laqach (take / seized) away from you the machamad (desire) of your iyan (eye) with a magapah (stroke): yet you shall neither sapad (mourn) nor bakah (weep), neither shall your damaih (tears) bawaa (come) down.

Sigh, but not aloud, ishah (make) no abal (mourning) for the mawath (death); chabash (bind) your headdress on you, and put your nail (shoes) on your ragal (feet / foot), and don't itah (cover) your shapam (lips), and don't akal (eat) mawath (death) lacham (bread).

So I dabar (word / matter) to the im (people / nation) in the baqar (morning); and at even my ashah (wife/individual woman) mawath (death); and I ishah (make) in the baqar (morning) as I was tzawah (commanded).
The im (people / nation) amar (spoke) to me, Won't you nagad (tell) us what these things are to us, that you ishah (make) so?
Then I amar (spoke) to them, The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Amar (spoke) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will chalal (profane) my maqadash (sanctuary), the gaawan (pride) of your iz (strength / might / refuge), the machamad (desire) of your iyan (eye), and that which your napash (living being/soul) pities; and your ban (son) and your bath (daughter) whom you have izab (left) behind shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword).
You shall ishah (make) as I ishah (make) done: you shall not itah (cover) your shapam (lips), nor akal (eat) the lacham (bread) of ishah (make).

Your paar (tires) shall be on your raash (head), and your nail (shoes) on your ragal (feet / foot): you shall not sapad (mourn) nor bakah (weep); but you shall maqaq (pine) away in your iwan (guilt/iniquity), and moan ayash (husband/individual man) toward ach (brother/kinsman).

Thus Yachazaqaal (Ezekiel) shall be a mawapath (sign) to you; according to all that he ishah (make) done, you will ishah (make). When this bawaa (come), then you yadai (will) know that I am the Adanay Yahawah.

You, ban (son) of adam (man), shall it not be in the yawam (day) when I laqach (take / seized) from them their maiwaz (stronghold / fortress / protection), the mashawash (joy) of their glory, the machamad (desire) of their iyan (eye), and that whereupon they mashaa (set) their napash (living being/soul), their ban (son) and their bath (daughter),
That in that yawam (day) he who palayat (escapes) shall bawaa (come) to you, to hashamaiwath (cause) you to hear it with your azan (ears)?

In that yawam (day) your pah (mouth) will be pathach (opened) to him who has palayat (escaped), and you shall dabar (word / matter), and be no more mute: so you will be a mawapath (sign) to them; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) toward the ban (son) of Ammon, and nabaa (prophesy) against them:

And amar (spoke) the ban (son) of Ammon, shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of the Adanay Yahawah: Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, Because you amar (spoke), haach (aha), against my maqadash (sanctuary), when it was chalal (profaned); and against the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), when it was shamam (made) desolate; and against the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah), when they halak (move) into gawalah (captivity):

Therefore, behold, I will nathan (give) you to the ban (son) of the qadam (east) for a mawarashah (possession), and they shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) their encampments in you, and nathan (give) their mashakan (dwellings) in you; they shall akal (eat) your paray (fruit), and they shall shathah (drinks) your chalab (milk).
I will nathan (give) Rabah (Rabbah) a nawah (habitation) for gamal (camels), and the ban (son) of Ammon a resting marabatz (place) for tzaan (flocks): and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you have machaa (clapped) your yad (hand), and raqai (stamped) with the ragal (feet / foot), and shamach (rejoiced) with all the shaat (despite) of your napash (living being/soul) against the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel);

Therefore, behold, I have natah (stretched) out my yad (hand) on you, and will nathan (give) you for a bag (spoil) to the gaway (nation / people); and I will karath (cut) you off from the im (people / nation), and I will cause you to abad (destroy/perish) out of the aratz (Earth/land): I will shamad (destroy) you; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: yain (because) Mawaab (Moab) and Shaiyar (Seir) amar (spoke), Behold, the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) is like all the gaway (nation / people);

Therefore, behold, I will pathach (open) the kathap (side) of Mawaab (Moab) from the iyar (cities), from his iyar (cities) which are on his qatzah (end / extremity / border), the glory of the aratz (Earth/land), Bayathahayashayamawath (Beth) Jeshimoth, Bailamaiwan (Baal) Meon, and Qarayathayam (Kiriathaim),

To the ban (son) of the qadam (east), to go against the ban (son) of Ammon; and I will nathan (give) them for a mawarashah (possession), that the ban (son) of Ammon may not be zakar (remembrance/memory) among the gaway (nation / people).
And I will ishah (make) shapat (judgments) on Mawaab (Moab); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because Adam (Edom) ishah (make) dealt against the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) by naqam (taking) naqam (vengeance), and has asham (greatly) asham (offended), and naqam (revenged) himself on them;

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on Adam (Edom), and will karath (cut) off adam (man) and animal from it; and I will nathan (give) it charabah (desolate) from Thayaman (Teman); even to Dadan (Dedan) shall they napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword).

I will nathan (give) my naqamah (vengeance) on Adam (Edom) by the yad (hand) of my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel); and they shall ishah (make) in Adam (Edom) according to my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) and according to my chamah (wrath); and they shall yadai (know) my naqamah (vengeance), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because the Palashathay (Philistines) ishah (make) dealt by naqamah (revenge), and have naqam (taken) naqam (vengeance) with shaat (despite) of napash (living being/soul) to mashachayath (destroy) with iwalam (forever) enmity;

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, Behold, I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on the Palashathay (Philistines), and I will karath (cut) off the Karathay (Cherethites), and abad (destroy/perish) the shaarayath (remnant) of the yam (sea/waters) chawap (coast).

I will ishah (make) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) naqamah (vengeance) on them with chamah (wrathful) thawakachah (rebukes); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shall nathan (give) my naqamah (vengeance) on them.
It happened in the ishathay (eleven) shanah (year), in the achad (one) day of the chadash (month), that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), because Tzar (Tyre) has amar (spoke) against Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), haach (aha), she is shabar (broken): the dalath (gate) of the im (people / nation); she is sabab (turned) to me; I shall be malaa (replenished), now that she is charab (laid) waste:

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, Behold, I am against you, Tzar (Tyre), and will cause many gaway (nation / people) to ilah (go up / offer) up against you, as the yam (sea/waters) causes its gal (waves) to ilah (go up / offer) up.

They shall shachath (destroy) the chawamah (walls) of Tzar (Tyre), and haras (break) down her magadal (towers): I will also sachah (scrape) her ipar (dust) from her, and nathan (give) her a bare salai (rock).

She shall be a place for the mashatawach (spreading) of charam (nets) in the thawak (midst) of the yam (sea/waters); for I have dabar (word / matter) it, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah; and she shall become a baz (spoil) to the gaway (nation / people).
Her bath (daughter) who are in the shadah (field) shall be harag (slain) with the charab (sword): and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will bawaa (come) on Tzar (Tyre) Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), malak (king) of malak (king), from the tzapawan (north), with sawas (horses), and with rakab (chariots), and with horsemen, and a qahal (company), and many im (people / nation).

He shall harag (kill) your bath (daughter) in the shadah (field) with the charab (sword); and he shall nathan (give) dayaq (forts) against you, and shapak (cast) up a mound qawam (rise up) you, and raise up the tzanah (buckler) against you.
He shall nathan (give) his battering machay (engines) against your chawamah (walls), and with his charab (sword) he shall nathatz (break) down your magadal (towers).

By reason of the shapaih (abundance) of his sawas (horses) their abaq (dust) shall kasah (cover) you: your chawamah (walls) shall raish (shake) at the qawal (sound / voice) of the horsemen, and of the wagons, and of the rakab (chariots), when he shall bawaa (come) into your shair (gates), as mabawaa (men) enter into a iyar (city) in which is baqai (made) a breach.

With the parasah (hoofs) of his sawas (horses) shall he ramas (tread) down all your chawatz (streets); he shall harag (kill) your im (people / nation) with the charab (sword); and the matzabah (pillars) of your iz (strength / might / refuge) shall yarad (go) down to the aratz (Earth/land).

They shall shalal (make) a spoil of your riches, and make a bazaz (prey) of your rakalah (merchandise); and they shall haras (break) down your chawamah (walls), and nathatz (destroy) your chamadah (pleasant) bayath (house); and they shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) your aban (stone) and your itz (timber) and your ipar (dust) in the thawak (midst) of the mayam (Waters).
I will cause the hamawan (noise) of your shayar (song) to shabath (shabath/rest); and the qawal (sound / voice) of your kanawar (harps) shall be no more shamai (hearken / hear).

I will nathan (give) you a bare salai (rock); you shall be a place for the mashatawach (spreading) of charam (nets); you shall be banah (built) no more: for I Yahawah have dabar (word / matter) it, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adawan Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah to Tzar (Tyre): shall not the ay (islands) raish (shake) at the qawal (sound / voice) of your mapalath (fall), when the chalal (wounded) anaq (groan), when the harag (slaughter) is harag (made) in the thawak (midst) of you?

Then all the nashayaa (princes) of the yam (sea/waters) shall yarad (come) down from their kasaa (thrones), and sawar (lay) aside their maiyal (robes), and pashat (strip) off their embroidered bagad (garments): they shall labash (clothe) themselves with charadah (trembling); they shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the aratz (Earth/land), and shall charad (tremble) every ragai (in an instance), and be shamam (astonished) at you.

They shall nashaa (lift) up a qayanah (lamentation) over you, and amar (spoke) you, How you are abad (destroy/perish), who were yashab (inhabit/dwell) by seafaring yam (sea/waters), the halal (praise) iyar (city), who was chazaq (strong) in the yam (sea/waters), she and her yashab (inhabit/dwell), who nathan (give) their chathayath (terror) to be on all who lived there!
Now shall the ay (islands) charad (tremble) in the yawam (day) of your mapalath (fall); yes, the ay (islands) that are in the yam (sea/waters) shall be bahal (dismayed) at your departure.

For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: When I shall nathan (give) you a charab (desolate) iyar (city), like the iyar (cities) that are not yashab (inhabit/dwell); when I shall ilah (go up / offer) up the thahawam (depths) on you, and the rab (great) mayam (Waters) shall kasah (cover) you;

Then will I yarad (bring) you down with those who descend into the bawar (pit), to the im (people / nation) of iwalam (forever) time, and will make you to dwell in the lower thachathay (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land), in the places that are charabah (desolate) of iwalam (forever), with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit), that you be not yashab (inhabit/dwell); and I will nathan (give) glory in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life):

I will nathan (give) you a balahah (terror), and you shall no more have any being; though you are baqash (sought) for, yet you will iwalam (forever) be matzaa (found) again, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came again to me, amar (spoke),
You, ban (son) of adam (man), nashaa (lift) up a qayanah (lamentation) over Tzar (Tyre);

And amar (spoke) Tzar (Tyre), you who yashab (inhabit/dwell) at the mabawaah (entry) of the yam (sea/waters), who are the rakal (merchant) of the im (people / nation) to many ay (islands), thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: You, Tzar (Tyre), have amar (spoke), I am kalayal (perfect) in yapay (beauty).
Your gabawal (border/boundary) are in the lab (heart) of the yam (sea/waters); your banah (builders) have kalal (perfected) your yapay (beauty).
They have banah (made) all your planks of barawash (fir) trees from Shanayar (Senir); they have laqach (take / seized) a araz (cedar) from Labanawan (Lebanon) to ishah (make) a tharan (mast) for you.

Of the alawan (oaks) of Bashan (Bashan) ishah (make) they made your mashawat (oars); they ishah (make) made your benches of shan (ivory) inlaid Ashar (in) boxwood, from the ay (islands) of Kathay (Kittim).

Of shash (six) linen with embroidered raqamah (work) from Matzarayam (Egypt) was your nas (sail), that it might be to you for a banner; thakalath (blue) and aragaman (purple) from the ay (islands) of Alayashah (Elishah) was your awning.
The yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Tzayadawan (Sidon) and Arawad (Arvad) were your shawat (rowers): your chakam (wise) men, Tzar (Tyre), were in you, they were your chabal (pilots).

The zaqan (old) men of Gabal (Gebal) and the chakam (wise) men of it were in you your repairers of anayah (ship) seams: all the ships of the yam (sea/waters) with their malach (mariners) were in you to deal in your mairab (merchandise).

Paras (Persia) and Lawad (Lud) and Pawat (Put) were in your chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), your chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) of malachamah (war): they hanged the magan (shield) and kawabai (helmet) in you; they nathan (give) forth your hadar (glory / majesty / splendor).

The ban (son) of Arawad (Arvad) with your chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) were on your chawamah (walls) all around, and Gamad (valorous) men were in your magadal (towers); they hanged their shalat (shields) on your chawamah (walls) all around; they have kalal (perfected) your yapay (beauty).

Tharashayash (Tarshish) was your sachar (merchant) by reason of the rab (multitude) of all kinds of riches; with kasap (silver), barazal (iron), badayal (divide), and iwaparath (lead), they nathan (give) for your izabawan (wares).

Yawan (Javan), Thawabal (Tubal), and Mashak (Meshech), they were your traffickers; they nathan (give) the napash (living being/soul) of adam (men) and kalay (vessels) of nachashath (brass) for your mairab (merchandise).
They of the bayath (house) of Thawagaramah (Togarmah) nathan (give) for your wares with sawas (horses) and war horses and parad (mules).

The ban (son) of Dadan (Dedan) were your traffickers; many ay (islands) were the market of your yad (hand): they shawab (turn back / repent) you in exchange qaran (horn) of shan (ivory) and haban (ebony).

Aram (Syria) was your sachar (merchant) by reason of the rab (multitude) of your handiworks: they nathan (give) for your izabawan (wares) with napak (emeralds), aragaman (purple), and embroidered raqamah (work), and bawatz (fine) linen, and raamah (coral), and rubies.

Yahawadah (Judah), and the aratz (Earth/land) of Yasharaal (Israel), they were your traffickers: they nathan (give) for your mairab (merchandise) chatah (wheat) of Manayath (Minnith), and confections, and dabash (honey), and shaman (oil), and tzaray (balm).

Damashaq (Damascus) was your sachar (merchant) for the rab (multitude) of your handiworks, by reason of the rab (multitude) of all kinds of riches, with the yayan (wine) Chalabawan (of) Helbon, and tzachar (bright / glisten) tzamar (wool).
Wadan (Vedan) and Yawan (Javan) traded with yarn for your izabawan (wares): ishawath (bright) barazal (iron), qadah (cassia), and qanah (calamus), were among your mairab (merchandise).
Dadan (Dedan) was your trafficker in chapash (precious) bagad (cloths) for riding.

Irab (Arabia), and all the nashayaa (princes) of Qadar (Kedar), they were the sachar (merchants) of your yad (hand); in kar (lambs), and ayal (rams), and ithawad (goats), in these were they your sachar (merchants).

The traffickers of Shabaa (Sheba) and Raimah (Raamah), they were your traffickers; they nathan (give) for your izabawan (wares) with the raash (head) of all basham (spices), and with all yaqar (precious) aban (stone), and zahab (gold).
Charan (Haran) and Kanah (Canneh) and Idan (Eden), the traffickers of Shabaa (Sheba), Ashawar (Asshur) and Kalamad (Chilmad), were your traffickers.

These were your traffickers in choice wares, in wrappings of thakalath (blue) and embroidered raqamah (work), and in ganaz (chests) of barawam (rich) clothing, chabash (bound) with chabal (cords) and araz (made) of cedar, among your marakalath (merchandise).

The anayah (ships) of Tharashayash (Tarshish) were your caravans for your mairab (merchandise): and you were malaa (replenished), and made very kabad (glorious) in the lab (heart) of the yam (sea/waters).
Your shawat (rowers) bawaa (come) brought you into rab (great) mayam (Waters): the qadayam (east) rawach (spirit / wind) has shabar (broken) you in the lab (heart) of the yam (sea/waters).

Your riches, and your izabawan (wares), your mairab (merchandise), your malach (mariners), and your chabal (pilots), your repairers of ship seams, and the dealers in your mairab (merchandise), and all your chazaq (men) of malachamah (war), who are in you, with all your qahal (company) which is in the thawak (midst) of you, shall napal (fall / be cast down) into the lab (heart) of the yam (sea/waters) in the yawam (day) of your mapalath (ruin).
At the qawal (sound / voice) of the zaiq (cry) of your chabal (pilots) the magarash (suburbs) shall raish (shake).

All who thapash (handled) the mashawat (oar), the malach (mariners), and all the chabal (pilots) of the yam (sea/waters), shall yarad (come) down from their anayah (ships); they shall imad (stand) on the aratz (Earth/land),

And shall cause their qawal (sound / voice) to be shamai (hearken / hear) over you, and shall zaiq (cry) bitterly, and shall ilah (go up / offer) up ipar (dust) on their raash (head), they shall wallow themselves in the ashes:

And they shall make themselves qarach (bald) for you, and clothe them with sackcloth, and they shall bakah (weep) for you in bitterness of napash (living being/soul) with mar (bitter) masapad (mourning).

In their nay (wailing) they shall nashaa (lift) up a qayanah (lamentation) for you, and qawan (lament) over you, saying, Who is there like Tzar (Tyre), like her who is brought to silence in the thawak (midst) of the yam (sea/waters)?

When your izabawan (wares) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the yam (sea/waters), you shabai (filled) many im (people / nation); you enriched the malak (king) of the aratz (Earth/land) with the rab (multitude) of your riches and of your mairab (merchandise).

In the ith (time) that you were shabar (broken) by the yam (sea/waters) in the maimaq (depths) of the mayam (Waters), your mairab (merchandise) and all your qahal (company) napal (fall / be cast down) in your thawak (midst).

All the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the ay (islands) are shamam (astonished) at you, and their malak (king) are shair (horribly) shair (dread / storm / horror); they are raim (troubled) in their panayam (face).
The sachar (merchants) among the im (people / nation) sharaq (hiss) at you; you are become a balahah (terror), and you shall nevermore have any being.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came again to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), amar (spoke) the nagayad (prince) of Tzar (Tyre), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because your lab (heart) is gabah (lifted) up, and you have amar (spoke), I am a Al, I yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the mawashab (seat) of Alahayam, in the lab (heart) of the yam (sea/waters); yet you are adam (man), and not Al, though you nathan (give) your lab (heart) as the lab (heart) of Alahayam—
Behold, you are wiser than Danayaal (Daniel); there is no satham (secret) that is satham (hidden) from you;
By your chakamah (wisdom) and by your thabawan (understanding) you ishah (make) gotten yourself riches, and ishah (make) gotten zahab (gold) and kasap (silver) into your awatzar (treasures);
By your rab (great) chakamah (wisdom) and by your rakalah (traffic) you rabah (have) increased your riches, and your labab (heart) is gabah (lifted) up because of your riches—
Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you nathan (give) set your lab (heart) as the labab (heart) of Alahayam,

Therefore, behold, I will bawaa (come) strangers on you, the irayatz (terrible) of the gaway (nation / people); and they shall rawaq (draw) their charab (sword) against the yapay (beauty) of your chakamah (wisdom), and they shall chalal (defile) your yapaih (brightness).
They shall yarad (bring) you down to the shachath (pit); and you shall mawath (death) the mamawath (death) of those who are chalal (slain), in the lab (heart) of the yam (sea/waters).
Will you yet amar (spoke) panayam (before) him who harag (kills) you, I am Alahayam? But you are adam (man), and not Al, in the yad (hand) of him who chalal (wounds) you.
You shall mawath (death) the mawath (death) of the iral (uncircumcised) by the yad (hand) of strangers: for I have dabar (word / matter) it, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
Moreover the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), nashaa (lift) up a qayanah (lamentation) over the malak (king) of Tzar (Tyre), and amar (spoke) him, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: You chatham (seal) up the thakanayath (sum), malaa (full) of chakamah (wisdom), and kalayal (perfect) in yapay (beauty).

You were in Idan (Eden), the gan (garden) of Alahayam; every yaqar (precious) aban (stone) adorned you: ruby, patadah (topaz), emerald, chrysolite, shaham (Onyx), yashapah (jasper), sapayar (sapphire), turquoise, and beryl. Zahab (gold) malaakah (work) of tambourines and of naqab (pipes) was in you. In the yawam (day) that you were baraa (created) they were kawan (prepared).

You were the mamashach (anointed) karawab (cherub) who sakak (covers): and I nathan (give) you, so that you were on the qadash (set apart/make holy) har (mountain) of Alahayam; you have halak (move) up and down in the thawak (midst) of the aban (stone) of ash (fire).
You were thamayam (complete / whole) in your darak (ways) from the yawam (day) that you were baraa (created), until iwal (unrighteousness) was matzaa (found) in you.

By the rab (abundance) of your rakalah (traffic) they malaa (filled) the thawak (midst) of you with chamas (violence), and you have chataa (sinned): therefore I have cast you as chalal (profane) out of the har (mountain) of Alahayam; and I abad (destroy/perish) destroyed you, sakak (covering) karawab (cherub), from the thawak (midst) of the aban (stone) of ash (fire).

Your lab (heart) was gabah (lifted) up because of your yapay (beauty); you have shachath (corrupted) your chakamah (wisdom) by reason of your yapaih (brightness): I have shalak (cast) you to the aratz (Earth/land); I nathan (give) laid you panayam (before) malak (king), that they may raah (see) you.

By the rab (multitude) of your iwan (guilt/iniquity), in the iwal (unrighteousness) of your rakalah (traffic), you have chalal (profaned) your maqadash (sanctuaries); therefore yatzaa (go out / come out) I brought forth a ash (fire) from the thawak (midst) of you; it has akal (eat) you, and I nathan (give) turned you to ashes on the aratz (Earth/land) in the iyan (eye) of all those who raah (see) you.
All those who yadai (know) you among the im (people / nation) shall be shamam (astonished) at you: you have become a balahah (terror), and you shall nevermore have any being.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) toward Tzayadawan (Sidon), and nabaa (prophesy) against it,

And amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against you, Tzayadawan (Sidon); and I will be kabad (glorified) in the thawak (midst) of you; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shall ishah (make) executed shapat (judgments) in her, and shall be qadash (set apart/make holy) in her.

For I will shalach (send) dabar (word / matter) into her, and dam (blood) into her chawatz (streets); and the chalal (wounded) shall napal (fall / be cast down) in the thawak (midst) of her, with the charab (sword) on her on sabayab (surrounding) side; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

There shall be no more a pricking salawan (brier) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), nor a hurting qawatz (thorn) of any that are around them, that scorned them; and they shall yadai (know) that I am the Adanay Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: When I shall have qabatz (gathered) the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) from the im (people / nation) among whom they are pawatz (scattered), and shall be qadash (set apart/make holy) in them in the iyan (eye) of the gaway (nation / people), then shall they yashab (inhabit/dwell) in their own adamah (land) which I nathan (give) to my ibad (servant) Yaiqab (Jacob).

They shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely therein; yes, they shall banah (build) bayath (house), and natai (plant) karam (vineyards), and shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely, when I ishah (make) executed shapat (judgments) on all those who do them despite all around them; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah their Alahayam.
In the ishayaray (tenth) shanah (year), in the ishayaray (tenth) month, on the shanayam (two) day of the chadash (month), the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) against Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and nabaa (prophesy) against him and against all Matzarayam (Egypt).

Dabar (word / matter) and amar (spoke), ‘Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against you, Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thanayan (monster) that rabatz (lies) in the thawak (midst) of his yaar (rivers), that has amar (spoke), ‘My yaar (river) is my own, and I ishah (make) made it for myself.’

I will nathan (give) chach (hooks) in your lachay (jaws), and I will make the dagah (fish) of your yaar (rivers) dabaq (stick) to your qashaqashath (scales); and I will ilah (go up / offer) you up out of the thawak (midst) of your yaar (rivers), with all the dagah (fish) of your yaar (rivers) which dabaq (stick) to your qashaqashath (scales).

I'll natash (cast) you forth into the madabar (wilderness), you and all the dagah (fish) of your yaar (rivers). You'll napal (fall / be cast down) on the panayam (open) shadah (field). You won't be asap (brought) together, nor qabatz (gathered). I nathan (give) given you for akalah (food) to the animals of the aratz (Earth/land) and to the iwap (flying) of the sky.
All the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Matzarayam (Egypt) yadai (will) know that I am Yahawah, because they have been a mashainah (staff) of qanah (reed) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

When they thapash (took) hold of you by your kap (hand), you ratzatz (broke), and baqai (tore) all their kathap (shoulders); and when they shain (leaned) on you, you shabar (broke), and paralyzed all of their thighs.
Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will bawaa (come) a charab (sword) on you, and will karath (cut) off adam (man) and animal from you.

The aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) shall be a shamamah (desolation) and a charabah (waste); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah. Because he has amar (spoke), ‘The yaar (river) is mine, and I ishah (make) made it;’

Therefore, behold, I am against you, and against your yaar (rivers), and I will nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) an utter charabah (waste) and shamamah (desolation), from the Magadawal (tower) Sawanah (of) Seveneh even to the gabawal (border/boundary) of Kawash (Ethiopia).

No ragal (feet / foot) of adam (man) shall ibar (pass over/through) through it, nor ragal (feet / foot) of animal shall ibar (pass over/through) through it, neither shall it be yashab (inhabit/dwell) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years).

I will nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) a shamamah (desolation) in the thawak (midst) of the aratz (Earth/land) that are shamam (desolate); and her iyar (cities) thawak (midst) the iyar (cities) that are charab (laid) waste shall be a shamamah (desolation) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years); and I will pawatz (scatter) the Matzarayam (Egyptians) among the gaway (nation / people), and will zarah (disperse) them through the aratz (Earth/land).

For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: “At the qatz (end) of arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years) will I qabatz (gather) the Matzarayam (Egyptians) from the im (people / nation) where they were pawatz (scattered);

And I will shawab (turn back / repent) back the shabawath (captivity) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and will cause them to shawab (turn back / repent) into the aratz (Earth/land) of Patharawas (Pathros), into the aratz (Earth/land) of their makawarah (birth); and they shall be there a shapal (base) mamalakah (kingdom).

It shall be the shapal (base) of the mamalakah (kingdoms); neither shall it any more nashaa (lift) itself up above the gaway (nation / people): and I will mait (diminish) them, that they shall no more radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) over the gaway (nation / people).

It shall be no more the mabatach (confidence) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), zakar (remembrance/memory) iwan (guilt/iniquity) to memory, when they panah (turn) to look achar (other) them: and they shall yadai (know) that I am the Adanay Yahawah.”'

It came to pass in the shabai (seven) and isharayam (twenty) shanah (year), in the raashawan (first) month, in the achad (one) day of the chadash (month), the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) ibad (servant) his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) to ibad (servant) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) ibadah (service) against Tzar (Tyre): every raash (head) was qarach (made) bald, and every kathap (shoulder) was worn; yet had he no shakar (wages), nor his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), from Tzar (Tyre), for the ibadah (service) that he had ibad (servant) against it.

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) to Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon); and he shall nashaa (lift) off her hamawan (multitude), and nashaa (lift) her shalal (spoil), and take her baz (prey); and it shall be the shakar (wages) for his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor).

I nathan (give) given him the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) as his recompense for which he ibad (servant), because they ishah (make) for me, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

In that yawam (day) will I tzamach (cause) a qaran (horn) to tzamach (bud) forth to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), and I will nathan (give) you the pathachawan (opening) of the pah (mouth) in their thawak (midst); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came again to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy), and amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Wail, Alas for the yawam (day)!
For the yawam (day) is qarawab (near), even the yawam (day) of Yahawah is qarawab (near); it shall be a yawam (day) of inan (cloud), a ith (time) of the gaway (nation / people).

A charab (sword) shall bawaa (come) on Matzarayam (Egypt), and anguish shall be in Kawash (Ethiopia), when the chalal (slain) shall napal (fall / be cast down) in Matzarayam (Egypt); and they shall laqach (take / seized) away her hamawan (multitude), and her yasawad (foundations) shall be haras (broken) down.

Kawash (Ethiopia), and Pawat (Put), and Lawad (Lud), and all the mixed ban (son), and Cub, and the ban (son) of the aratz (Earth/land) that is allied with them, shall napal (fall / be cast down) with them by the charab (sword).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: They also who samak (uphold) Matzarayam (Egypt) shall napal (fall / be cast down); and the gaawan (pride) of her iz (strength / might / refuge) shall yarad (come) down: from the Magadawal (tower) Sawanah (of) Seveneh shall they napal (fall / be cast down) in it by the charab (sword), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

They shall be shamam (desolate) in the thawak (midst) of the aratz (Earth/land) that are shamam (desolate); and her iyar (cities) shall be in the thawak (midst) of the iyar (cities) that are charab (wasted).
They shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I nathan (give) set a ash (fire) in Matzarayam (Egypt), and all her helpers are shabar (destroyed).

In that yawam (day) shall malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from panayam (before) me in tzay (ships) to make the batach (careless) Kawash (Ethiopians) charad (afraid); and there shall be anguish on them, as in the yawam (day) of Matzarayam (Egypt); for, behold, it bawaa (come).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will also make the hamawan (multitude) of Matzarayam (Egypt) to shabath (shabath/rest), by the yad (hand) of Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon).

He and his im (people / nation) with him, the irayatz (terrible) of the gaway (nation / people), shall be bawaa (come) in to shachath (destroy) the aratz (Earth/land); and they shall rawaq (draw) their charab (sword) against Matzarayam (Egypt), and malaa (fill) the aratz (Earth/land) with the chalal (slain).

I will nathan (give) the yaar (rivers) charabah (dry), and will makar (sell) the aratz (Earth/land) into the yad (hand) of rai (evil) men; and I will make the aratz (Earth/land) shamam (desolate), and malaa (all) that is therein, by the yad (hand) of strangers: I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will also abad (destroy/perish) the galawal (idols), and I will cause the alayal (images) to shabath (shabath/rest) Nap (from) Memphis; and there shall be no more a nashayaa (prince) from the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt): and I will nathan (give) a yaraah (fear) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
I will make Patharawas (Pathros) shamam (desolate), and will nathan (give) a ash (fire) in Tzain (Zoan), and will ishah (make) shapat (judgments) Naa (on) No.
I will shapak (pour) my chamah (wrath) on sayan (sin), the stronghold of Matzarayam (Egypt); and I will karath (cut) off the hamawan (multitude) Naa (of) No.

I will nathan (give) a ash (fire) in Matzarayam (Egypt): sayan (sin) shall be in chawal (great) anguish, and No shall be baqai (broken) Nap (up); and Memphis shall have tzar (oppressor / distressor) in the yawamam (by day).
The bachawar (young) men of Awan (Aven) and of Payabasath (Pibeseth) shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword); and these cities shall yalak (go) into shabay (captivity).

At Thachapanachas (Tehaphnehes) also the yawam (day) shall withdraw itself, when I shall shabar (break) there the mawatah (yokes) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and the gaawan (pride) of her iz (strength / might / refuge) shall shabath (shabath/rest) in her: as for her, a inan (cloud) shall kasah (cover) her, and her bath (daughter) shall yalak (go) into shabay (captivity).
Thus will I ishah (make) shapat (judgments) on Matzarayam (Egypt); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
It happened in the eleventh shanah (year), in the raashawan (first) month, in the shabai (seven) day of the chadash (month), that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), I have shabar (broken) the zarawai (arm) of Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt); and behold, it has not been chabash (bound) up, to apply rapaah (healing) medicines, to shawam (place / establish / appoint) a bandage to chabash (bind) it, that it be chazaq (strong) to thapash (hold) the charab (sword).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and will shabar (break) his zarawai (arms), the chazaq (strong) arm, and that which was shabar (broken); and I will cause the charab (sword) to napal (fall / be cast down) out of his yad (hand).
I will pawatz (scatter) the Matzarayam (Egyptians) among the gaway (nation / people), and will zarah (disperse) them through the aratz (Earth/land).

I will chazaq (strengthen) the zarawai (arms) of the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), and nathan (give) my charab (sword) in his yad (hand): but I will shabar (break) the zarawai (arms) of Paraih (Pharaoh), and he shall naaq (groan) panayam (before) him with the naaqah (groanings) of a deadly chalal (wounded) man.

I will chazaq (hold) up the zarawai (arms) of the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon); and the zarawai (arms) of Paraih (Pharaoh) shall napal (fall / be cast down) down; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shall nathan (give) my charab (sword) into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), and he shall natah (stretch) it out on the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
I will pawatz (scatter) the Matzarayam (Egyptians) among the gaway (nation / people), and zarah (disperse) them through the aratz (Earth/land); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
It happened in the eleventh shanah (year), in the shalayashay (third) month, in the achad (one) day of the chadash (month), that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), amar (spoke) Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and to his hamawan (multitude): Whom are you damah (like) in your gadal (greatness)?

Behold, the Ashawar (Assyrian) was a araz (cedar) in Labanawan (Lebanon) with yapah (beautiful) branches, and with a forest-like Charash (shade), and of gabah (high) qawamah (stature); and its tzamarath (top) was among the ibath (thick) boughs.

The mayam (Waters) gadal (nourished) it, the thahawam (depths) rawam (will lift up) it to grow: its nahar (rivers) halak (move) all around its plantation; and it shalach (send) out its channels to all the itz (trees) of the shadah (field).

Therefore its qawamah (stature) was gabah (exalted) above all the itz (trees) of the shadah (field); and its saraipah (boughs) were rabah (multiplied), and its branches arak (became) long by reason of many mayam (Waters), when it shalach (send) them forth.

All the iwap (flying) of the sky qanan (made) their nests in its saipah (boughs); and under its branches all the animals of the shadah (field) yalad (birth / begot) forth their young; and all rab (great) gaway (nation / people) lived under its tzal (shadow).
Thus was it yapah (beautiful) in its gadal (greatness), in the arak (length) of its branches; for its sharash (root) was by many mayam (Waters).

The araz (cedars) in the gan (garden) of Alahayam could not imam (hide) it; the barawash (fir) trees were not damah (like) its saipah (boughs), and the plane iramawan (trees) were not as its branches; nor was any itz (tree) in the gan (garden) of Alahayam damah (like) it in its yapay (beauty).
I ishah (make) it yapah (beautiful) by the rab (multitude) of its branches, so that all the itz (trees) of Idan (Eden), that were in the gan (garden) of Alahayam, qanaa (jealous) it.

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you are gabah (exalted) in qawamah (stature), and he nathan (give) set his tzamarath (top) among the ibath (thick) boughs, and his labab (heart) is rawam (will lift up) up in his gabah (height);

I will even nathan (give) him into the yad (hand) of the mighty one of the gaway (nation / people); he shall ishah (make) ishah (make) with him; I have garash (driven) him out for his rashai (wickedness).

Strangers, the irayatz (terrible) of the gaway (nation / people), have karath (cut) him off, and have natash (left) him: on the har (mountain) and in all the gayaa (valleys) his branches are napal (fall / be cast down), and his paarah (boughs) are shabar (broken) by all the watercourses of the aratz (Earth/land); and all the im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land) are yarad (gone) down from his tzal (shadow), and have natash (left) him.
On his mapalath (ruin) all the iwap (flying) of the sky shall shakan (dwell), and all the animals of the shadah (field) shall be on his branches;

To the end that none of all the itz (trees) by the mayam (Waters) gabah (exalt) themselves in their qawamah (stature), neither nathan (give) their tzamarath (top) among the ibath (thick) boughs, nor that their ayal (mighty) ones imad (stand) up on their gabah (height), even all who shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters): for they are all nathan (give) to mawath (death), to the lower thachathay (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land), in the thawak (midst) of the ban (son) of adam (men), with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: In the yawam (day) when he yarad (went) down to shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife) I caused a abal (mourning): I kasah (covered) the thahawam (depths) for him, and I manai (restrained) its nahar (rivers); and the rab (great) mayam (Waters) were kalaa (stayed); and I caused Labanawan (Lebanon) to qadar (mourn) for him, and all the itz (trees) of the shadah (field) ilapah (fainted) for him.

I made the gaway (nation / people) to raish (shake) at the qawal (sound / voice) of his mapalath (fall), when I yarad (cast) him down to shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife) with those who descend into the bawar (pit); and all the itz (trees) of Idan (Eden), the mabachar (choice) and tawab (pleasant/functional) of Labanawan (Lebanon), all that shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters), were nacham (turn away / repent) in the lower thachathay (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land).

They also yarad (went) down into shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife) with him to those who are chalal (slain) by the charab (sword); yes, those who were his zarawai (arm), that lived under his tzal (shadow) in the thawak (midst) of the gaway (nation / people).

To whom are you thus damah (like) in kabawad (glory) and in gadal (greatness) among the itz (trees) of Idan (Eden)? Yet you will be yarad (brought) down with the itz (trees) of Idan (Eden) to the lower thachathay (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land): you shall shakab (lie) in the thawak (midst) of the iral (uncircumcised), with those who are chalal (slain) by the charab (sword). This is Paraih (Pharaoh) and all his hamawan (multitude), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
It happened in the shanayam (two) shanah (year), in the twelfth chadash (month), in the achad (one) day of the chadash (month), that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), nashaa (lift) up a qayanah (lamentation) over Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and amar (spoke) him, You were damah (likened) to a young kapayar (lion) of the gaway (nation / people): yet you are as a monster in the yam (sea/waters); and you gayach (broke) out with your nahar (rivers), and dalach (troubled) the mayam (Waters) with your ragal (feet / foot), and rapash (fouled) their nahar (rivers).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will parash (spread) out my rashath (net) on you with a qahal (company) of many im (people / nation); and they shall ilah (go up / offer) you up in my charam (net).

I will natash (leave) you on the aratz (Earth/land), I will tawal (cast) you forth on the panayam (open) shadah (field), and will cause all the iwap (flying) of the sky to settle on you, and I will shabai (satisfy) the animals of the whole aratz (Earth/land) with you.
I will nathan (give) your bashar (flesh) on the har (mountain), and malaa (fill) the gayaa (valleys) with your ramawath (height).
I will also shaqah (water) with your dam (blood) the aratz (Earth/land) in which you swim, even to the har (mountain); and the watercourses shall be malaa (full) of you.

When I shall extinguish you, I will kasah (cover) the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), and make its kawakab (star) qadar (dark); I will kasah (cover) the shamash (sun) with a inan (cloud), and the yarach (moon) shall not awar (light) its awar (light).

All the maawar (Maawar/(Luminary)) awar (light) of the sky will I make qadar (dark) over you, and nathan (give) chashak (darkness) on your aratz (Earth/land), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

I will also trouble the lab (heart) of many im (people / nation), when I shall bawaa (come) your shabar (destruction) among the gaway (nation / people), into the aratz (Earth/land) which you yadai (have) not known.

Yes, I will make many im (people / nation) shamam (amazed) at you, and their malak (king) shall be shair (horribly) shair (dread / storm / horror) for you, when I shall iwap (flying) my charab (sword) panayam (before) them; and they shall charad (tremble) at every ragai (in an instance), every ayash (husband/individual man) for his own napash (living being/soul), in the yawam (day) of your mapalath (fall).
For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: The charab (sword) of the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) shall bawaa (come) on you.

By the charab (sword) of the gabawar (mighty) will I cause your hamawan (multitude) to napal (fall / be cast down); the irayatz (terrible) of the gaway (nation / people) are they all: and they shall bring to nothing the gaawan (pride) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and all its hamawan (multitude) shall be destroyed.

I will abad (destroy/perish) also all its animals from beside many mayam (Waters); neither shall the ragal (feet / foot) of adam (man) dalach (trouble) them any more, nor the parasah (hoofs) of animals dalach (trouble) them.
Then will I make their mayam (Waters) clear, and cause their nahar (rivers) to yalak (run) like shaman (oil), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

When I shall nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) shamamah (desolate) and waste, a aratz (Earth/land) shamam (destitute) of that of which it malaa (was) full, when I shall nakah (strike) all those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein, then shall they yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

This is the qayanah (lamentation) with which they shall qawan (lament); the bath (daughter) of the gaway (nation / people) shall qawan (lament) therewith; over Matzarayam (Egypt), and over all her hamawan (multitude), shall they qawan (lament) therewith, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
It happened also in the shanayam (two) shanah (year), in the fifteenth day of the chadash (month), that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), nahah (wail) for the hamawan (multitude) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and yarad (cast) them down, even her, and the bath (daughter) of the adayar (famous) gaway (nation / people), to the lower thachathay (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land), with those who yarad (go) down into the bawar (pit).
Whom do you naim (pass) in beauty? Yarad (go) down, and be shakab (laid) with the iral (uncircumcised).

They shall napal (fall / be cast down) in the thawak (midst) of those who are chalal (slain) by the charab (sword): she is nathan (give) to the charab (sword); mashak (draw) her away and all her hamawan (multitudes).

The al (strong) among the gabawar (mighty) shall dabar (word / matter) to him out of the thawak (midst) of shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife) with those who izar (help) him: they are yarad (gone) down, they shakab (lie) still, even the iral (uncircumcised), chalal (slain) by the charab (sword).
Ashawar (Asshur) is there and all her qahal (company); her qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) are all around her; all of them chalal (slain), napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword);

Whose qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) are nathan (give) in the uttermost parts of the bawar (pit), and her qahal (company) is around her qabawarah (grave); all of them chalal (slain), napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword), who nathan (give) chathayath (terror) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life).

There is Iyalam (Elam) and all her hamawan (multitude) around her qabawarah (grave); all of them chalal (slain), napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword), who are yarad (gone) down iral (uncircumcised) into the lower thachathay (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land), who nathan (give) their chathayath (terror) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life), and have nashaa (lift) their kalamah (shame) with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit).

They nathan (give) set her a mashakab (bed) in the thawak (midst) of the chalal (slain) with all her hamawan (multitude); her qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) are around her; all of them iral (uncircumcised), chalal (slain) by the charab (sword); for their chathayath (terror) was nathan (give) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life), and they have nashaa (lift) their kalamah (shame) with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit): he is nathan (give) in the thawak (midst) of those who are chalal (slain).

There is Mashak (Meshech), Thawabal (Tubal), and all their hamawan (multitude); their qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) are around them; all of them iral (uncircumcised), chalal (slain) by the charab (sword); for they nathan (give) their chathayath (terror) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life).

They shall not shakab (lie) with the gabawar (mighty) who are napal (fall / be cast down) of the iral (uncircumcised), who are yarad (gone) down to shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife) with their kalay (weapons) of malachamah (war), and nathan (give) laid their charab (sword) under their raash (head), and their iwan (guilt/iniquity) are on their itzam (bones); for they were the chathayath (terror) of the gabawar (mighty) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life).
But you shall be shabar (broken) in the thawak (midst) of the iral (uncircumcised), and shall shakab (lie) with those who are chalal (slain) by the charab (sword).

There is Adam (Edom), her malak (king) and all her nashayaa (princes), who in their gabawarah (might) are nathan (give) with those who are chalal (slain) by the charab (sword): they shall shakab (lie) with the iral (uncircumcised), and with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit).
