There are the nasayak (princes) of the tzapawan (north), all of them, and all the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), who are yarad (gone) down with the chalal (slain); in the chathayath (terror) which they caused by their gabawarah (might) they are bawash (put) to shame; and they shakab (lie) iral (uncircumcised) with those who are chalal (slain) by the charab (sword), and nashaa (lift) their kalamah (shame) with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit).

Paraih (Pharaoh) shall raah (see) them, and shall be nacham (turn away / repent) over all his hamawan (multitude), even Paraih (Pharaoh) and all his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), chalal (slain) by the charab (sword), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

For I nathan (give) put his chathayath (terror) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life); and he shall be shakab (laid) in the thawak (midst) of the iral (uncircumcised), with those who are chalal (slain) by the charab (sword), even Paraih (Pharaoh) and all his hamawan (multitude), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), dabar (word / matter) to the ban (son) of your im (people / nation), and amar (spoke) them, When I bawaa (come) the charab (sword) on a aratz (Earth/land), and the im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land) laqach (take / seized) a ayash (husband/individual man) from among them, and nathan (give) him for their tzapah (watchman / keep watch);

If, when he raah (see) the charab (sword) bawaa (come) on the aratz (Earth/land), he thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), and zahar (warn) the im (people / nation);

Then whoever shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), and doesn't take zahar (warn), if the charab (sword) bawaa (come), and laqach (take / seized) him away, his dam (blood) shall be on his own raash (head).

He shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), and didn't take zahar (warn); his dam (blood) shall be on him; whereas if he had taken zahar (warn), he would have malat (delivered) his napash (living being/soul).

But if the tzapah (watchman / keep watch) raah (see) the charab (sword) bawaa (come), and doesn't thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)), and the im (people / nation) aren't zahar (warn), and the charab (sword) bawaa (come), and laqach (take / seized) any napash (living being/soul) from among them; he is laqach (take / seized) away in his iwan (guilt/iniquity), but his dam (blood) will I darash (require) at the tzapah (watchman / keep watch) yad (hand).

So you, ban (son) of adam (man), I nathan (give) set you a tzapah (watchman / keep watch) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel); therefore shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) at my pah (mouth), and give them zahar (warn) from me.

When I amar (spoke) the rashai (wicked), O rashai (wicked) mawath (death), you shall surely mawath (death), and you don't dabar (word / matter) to zahar (warn) the rashai (wicked) from his darak (way); that rashai (wicked) mawath (death) shall die in his iwan (guilt/iniquity), but his dam (blood) will I baqash (require) at your yad (hand).

Nevertheless, if you zahar (warn) the rashai (wicked) of his darak (way) to shawab (turn back / repent) from it, and he doesn't shawab (turn back / repent) from his darak (way); he shall mawath (death) in his iwan (guilt/iniquity), but you have natzal (delivered) your napash (living being/soul).

You, ban (son) of adam (man), amar (spoke) the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel): Thus you amar (spoke), amar (spoke), Our pashai (transgressions) and our chataah (sin) are on us, and we maqaq (pine) away in them; how then can we chayah (live)?

Amar (spoke) them, As I chay (life), amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, I chapatz (have) no pleasure in the mawath (death) of the rashai (wicked); but that the rashai (wicked) shawab (turn back / repent) from his darak (way) and chayah (live): shawab (turn back / repent), shawab (turn back / repent) from your rai (evil) darak (ways); for why will you mawath (death), bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel)?

You, ban (son) of adam (man), amar (spoke) the ban (son) of your im (people / nation), The tzadaqah (righteousness) of the tzadayaq (righteous) shall not natzal (deliver) him in the yawam (day) of his disobedience; and as for the rashaih (wickedness) of the rashai (wicked), he shall not kashal (stumble / stagger) thereby in the yawam (day) that he shawab (turn back / repent) from his rashai (wickedness); neither shall he who is tzadayaq (righteous) be yakal (able) to chayah (live) thereby in the yawam (day) that he chataa (sins).

When I amar (spoke) the tzadayaq (righteous), that he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live); if he batach (trust) to his tzadaqah (righteousness), and ishah (make) iwal (iniquity), none of his tzadaqah (righteousness) deeds shall be zakar (remembrance/memory); but in his iwal (iniquity) that he ishah (make) committed, therein shall he mawath (death).

Again, when I amar (spoke) to the rashai (wicked), You shall mawath (death) mawath (death); if he shawab (turn back / repent) from his chataah (sin), and ishah (make) that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (righteousness);

If the rashai (wicked) shawab (turn back / repent) the chabal (pledge), shalam (give) again that which he had taken by robbery, halak (move) in the chaqah (statutes) of chay (life), ishah (make) no iwal (iniquity); he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live), he shall not mawath (death).

None of his chataah (sin) that he has chataa (committed) shall be zakar (remembrance/memory) against him: he ishah (make) done that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (righteousness); he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live).
Yet the ban (son) of your im (people / nation) amar (spoke), The darak (way) of the Adanay is not thakan (equal): but as for them, their darak (way) is not thakan (equal).
When the tzadayaq (righteous) shawab (turn back / repent) from his tzadaqah (righteousness), and ishah (make) iwal (iniquity), he shall even mawath (death) therein.
When the rashai (wicked) shawab (turn back / repent) from his rashaih (wickedness), and ishah (make) that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (righteousness), he shall chayah (live) thereby.

Yet you amar (spoke), The darak (way) of the Adanay is not thakan (equal). Bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), I will shapat (judge) ayash (husband/individual man) one of you after his darak (ways).

It happened in the shanayam (two) shanah (year) of our galawath (captivity), in the ishayaray (tenth) month, in the chamash (fifth) day of the chadash (month), that one who had palayat (escaped) out of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) bawaa (come) to me, amar (spoke), The iyar (city) has been nakah (struck).

Now the yad (hand) of Yahawah had been on me in the irab (evening), panayam (before) he who was palayat (escaped) bawaa (come); and he pathach (had) opened my pah (mouth), until he bawaa (come) to me in the baqar (morning); and my pah (mouth) was pathach (opened), and I was no more mute.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), they who yashab (inhabit/dwell) those charabah (waste) places in the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (spoke), amar (spoke), Abaraham (Abraham) was achad (one), and he yarash (inherited) the aratz (Earth/land): but we are many; the aratz (Earth/land) is nathan (give) us for mawarashah (inheritance).

Therefore amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: You akal (eat) with the dam (blood), and nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye) to your galawal (idols), and shapak (shed) dam (blood): and shall you yarash (possess) the aratz (Earth/land)?

You imad (stand) on your charab (sword), you ishah (make) thawaibah (abomination), and ayash (husband/individual man) one of you tamaa (defiles) his neighbor's ashah (wife/individual woman): and shall you yarash (possess) the aratz (Earth/land)?

You shall amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: As I chay (life), surely those who are in the charabah (waste) places shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword); and him who is in the panayam (open) shadah (field) will I nathan (give) to the animals to be akal (eat); and those who are in the strongholds and in the mairah (caves) shall mawath (death) of the dabar (word / matter).

I will nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) a shamamah (desolation) and an astonishment; and the gaawan (pride) of her iz (strength / might / refuge) shall shabath (shabath/rest); and the har (mountain) of Yasharaal (Israel) shall be shamam (desolate), so that none shall ibar (pass over/through) through.

Then shall they yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I nathan (give) made the aratz (Earth/land) a shamamah (desolation) and an astonishment, because of all their thawaibah (abominations) which they ishah (make) committed.

As for you, ban (son) of adam (man), the ban (son) of your im (people / nation) dabar (word / matter) of you by the qayar (walls) and in the pathach (doors) of the bayath (house), and dabar (word / matter) chad (one) to another, everyone to his ach (brother/kinsman), amar (spoke), Please bawaa (come) and shamai (hearken / hear) what is the dabar (word / matter) that yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from Yahawah.

They bawaa (come) to you as the im (people / nation) mabawaa (come), and they yashab (inhabit/dwell) panayam (before) you as my im (people / nation), and they shamai (hearken / hear) your dabar (word / matter), but don't ishah (make) them; for with their pah (mouth) they show much igab (love), but their lab (heart) halak (move) achar (other) their batzai (gain).

Behold, you are to them as a very igab (lovely) shayar (song) of one who has a yapah (pleasant) qawal (sound / voice), and can tawab (pleasant/functional) well on an nagan (instrument); for they shamai (hearken / hear) your dabar (word / matter), but they don't ishah (make) them.
When this bawaa (come) to pass, (behold, it bawaa (come)), then shall they yadai (know) that a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) has been thawak (midst) them.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy) against the raih (shepherds) of Yasharaal (Israel), nabaa (prophesy), and amar (spoke) them, even to the raih (shepherds), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: haway (Alas/Woe!) To the raih (shepherds) of Yasharaal (Israel) who raih (feed) themselves! Shouldn't the raih (shepherds) raih (feed) the tzaan (sheep)?
You akal (eat) the chalab (fat), and you labash (clothe) yourself with the tzamar (wool), you zabach (kill) the fatlings; but you don't barayaa (feed) the tzaan (sheep).

You haven't chazaq (strengthened) the chalah (afflict), neither have you rapaa (healed) that which was chalah (afflict), neither have you chabash (bound) up that which was shabar (broken), neither have you shawab (turn back / repent) back that which was nadach (driven) away, neither have you baqash (sought) that which was abad (destroy/perish); but with chazaqah (force) and with rigor you radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) ruled over them.
They were pawatz (scattered), because there was no raih (shepherd); and they became akalah (food) to all the animals of the shadah (field), and were pawatz (scattered).

My tzaan (sheep) shagah (wandered) through all the har (mountain), and on every rawam (will lift up) gabaih (hill): yes, my tzaan (sheep) were pawatz (scattered) on all the surface of the aratz (Earth/land); and there was none who darash (searched) or baqash (sought).
Therefore, you raih (shepherds), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah:

As I chay (life), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, surely because my tzaan (sheep) became a baz (prey), and my tzaan (sheep) became akalah (food) to all the animals of the shadah (field), because there was no raih (shepherd), neither did my raih (shepherds) darash (search) for my tzaan (sheep), but the raih (shepherds) raih (fed) themselves, and didn't raih (feed) my tzaan (sheep);
Therefore, you raih (shepherds), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah:

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against the raih (shepherds); and I will darash (require) my tzaan (sheep) at their yad (hand), and shabath (shabath/rest) them to cease from raih (feeding) the tzaan (sheep); neither shall the raih (shepherds) raih (feed) themselves any more; and I will natzal (deliver) my tzaan (sheep) from their pah (mouth), that they may not be akalah (food) for them.
For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I myself, even I, will darash (search) for my tzaan (sheep), and will baqar (morning) them out.

As a raih (shepherd) baqarah (seeks) out his idar (flock) in the yawam (day) that he is thawak (midst) his tzaan (sheep) that are parash (scattered) abroad, so will I baqar (morning) out my tzaan (sheep); and I will natzal (deliver) them out of all maqawam (place) where they have been pawatz (scattered) in the inan (cloud) and irapal (dark) yawam (day).

I will yatzaa (go out / come out) them out from the im (people / nation), and qabatz (gather) them from the aratz (Earth/land), and will bawaa (come) them into their own adamah (land); and I will raih (feed) them on the har (mountain) of Yasharaal (Israel), by the watercourses, and in all the mawashab (inhabited) places of the aratz (Earth/land).

I will raih (feed) them with tawab (pleasant/functional) maraih (pasture); and on the har (mountain) of the marawam (height) of Yasharaal (Israel) shall their nawah (habitation) be: there shall they rabatz (lie) down in a tawab (pleasant/functional) nawah (habitation); and on shaman (fat) maraih (pasture) shall they raih (feed) on the har (mountain) of Yasharaal (Israel).
I myself will be the raih (shepherd) of my tzaan (sheep), and I will rabatz (cause) them to lie down, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

I will baqash (seek) that which was abad (destroy/perish), and will shawab (turn back / repent) back that which was nadach (driven) away, and will chabash (bind) up that which was shabar (broken), and will chazaq (strengthen) that which was chalah (afflict): but the shaman (fat) and the chazaq (strong) I will shamad (destroy); I will raih (feed) them in mashapat (justice).
As for you, O my tzaan (flock), thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I shapat (judge) between shah (sheep) and shah (sheep), the ayal (rams) and the male ithawad (goats).

Does it seem a mait (small) thing to you to have raih (fed) on the tawab (pleasant/functional) maraih (pasture), but you must ramas (tread) down with your ragal (feet / foot) the yathar (residue) of your maraih (pasture)? And to have shathah (drinks) of the clear mayam (Waters), but you must rapash (foul) the yathar (residue) with your ragal (feet / foot)?

As for my tzaan (sheep), they raih (eat) that which you have maramas (trodden) with your ragal (feet / foot), and they shathah (drinks) that which you marapash (have) fouled with your ragal (feet / foot).
Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah to them: Behold, I, even I, will shapat (judge) between the baray (fat) shah (sheep) and the razah (lean) shah (sheep).
Because you hadap (thrust) with tzad (side) and with kathap (shoulder), and nagach (push) all the chalah (afflict) with your qaran (horn), until you have pawatz (scattered) them chawatz (abroad);
Therefore will I yashai (salvation) my tzaan (flock), and they shall no more be a baz (prey); and I will shapat (judge) between shah (sheep) and shah (sheep).
I will qawam (rise up) up achad (one) raih (shepherd) over them, and he shall raih (feed) them, even my ibad (servant) Dawad (David); he shall raih (feed) them, and he shall be their raih (shepherd).
I, Yahawah, will be their Alahayam, and my ibad (servant) Dawad (David) nashayaa (prince) thawak (midst) them; I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it.

I will karath (cut) with them a barayath (covenant) of shalawam (peace / safety), and will cause rai (evil) animals to shabath (shabath/rest) out of the aratz (Earth/land); and they shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely in the madabar (wilderness), and sleep in the yair (woods).

I will nathan (give) them and the sabayab (surrounding) around my gabaih (hill) a barakah (blessing); and I will cause the gasham (shower) to yarad (come) down in its ith (season); there shall be gasham (showers) of barakah (blessing).

The itz (tree) of the shadah (field) shall nathan (give) its paray (fruit), and the aratz (Earth/land) shall nathan (give) its yabawal (increase), and they shall be batach (secure) in their adamah (land); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I have shabar (broken) the bars of their il (over), and have natzal (delivered) them out of the yad (hand) of those who ibad (servant) slaves of them.

They shall no more be a baz (prey) to the gaway (nation / people), neither shall the animals of the aratz (Earth/land) akal (eat) them; but they shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely, and none shall make them charad (afraid).

I will qawam (rise up) up to them a plantation for sham (name), and they shall be no more asap (consumed) with raib (famine) in the aratz (Earth/land), neither nashaa (lift) the kalamah (shame) of the gaway (nation / people) any more.

They shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, their Alahayam am with them, and that they, the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), are my im (people / nation), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
You my tzaan (sheep), the tzaan (sheep) of my maraiyath (pasture), are adam (men), and I am your Alahayam, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
Moreover the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) against har (mountain) Shaiyar (Seir), and nabaa (prophesy) against it,

And amar (spoke) it, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against you, har (mountain) Shaiyar (Seir), and I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) against you, and I will nathan (give) you a shamamah (desolation) and an astonishment.
I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) your iyar (cities) charabah (waste), and you shall be shamamah (desolate); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Because you have had a iwalam (forever) enmity, and have given over the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) to the yad (hand) of the charab (sword) in the ith (time) of their ayad (calamity), in the ith (time) of the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the qatz (end);

Therefore, as I chay (life), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, I will ishah (make) you for dam (blood), and dam (blood) shall radap (pursue) you: am (mother) you have not shanaa (hate) dam (blood), therefore dam (blood) shall radap (pursue) you.

Thus will I nathan (give) har (mountain) Shaiyar (Seir) an astonishment and a shamamah (desolation); and I will karath (cut) off from it him who passes through and him who shawab (turn back / repent).

I will malaa (fill) its har (mountain) with its chalal (slain): in your gabaih (hills) and in your gayaa (valleys) and in all your watercourses shall they napal (fall / be cast down) who are chalal (slain) with the charab (sword).
I will nathan (give) you a iwalam (forever) shamamah (desolation), and your iyar (cities) shall not be inhabited; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Because you have amar (spoke), These shanayam (two) gaway (nation / people) and these shanayam (two) aratz (Earth/land) shall be mine, and we will yarash (possess) it; whereas Yahawah was there:

Therefore, as I chay (life), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, I will ishah (make) according to your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and according to your qanaah (envy) which you ishah (make) shown out of your hatred against them; and I yadai (will) make myself known among them, when I shall shapat (judge) you.

You shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have shamai (hearken / hear) all your insults which you have amar (spoke) against the har (mountain) of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), They are shamam (laid) desolate, they nathan (give) been given us to akalah (devour).
You have gadal (magnified) yourselves against me with your pah (mouth), and have ithar (multiplied) your dabar (word / matter) against me: I have shamai (hearken / hear) it.
Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: When the whole aratz (Earth/land) shamach (rejoices), I will ishah (make) you shamamah (desolate).

As you shamachah (rejoiced) over the nachalah (inheritance) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), because it was shamam (desolate), so will I ishah (make) to you: you shall be shamamah (desolate), har (mountain) Shaiyar (Seir), and all Adam (Edom), even all of it; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

You, ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy) to the har (mountain) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (spoke), You har (mountain) of Yasharaal (Israel), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah.
Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because the ayab (enemy) has amar (spoke) against you, haach (aha)! And, The iwalam (forever) bamah (high) places are ours in mawarashah (possession);

Therefore nabaa (prophesy), and amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because, even because they have shamam (made) you desolate, and shaap (swallowed) you up on sabayab (surrounding) side, that you might be a mawarashah (possession) to the shaarayath (residue) of the gaway (nation / people), and you are ilah (go up / offer) up in the shapah (lips) of lashawan (tongue/language), and the dabah (evil) report of the im (people / nation);

Therefore, you har (mountain) of Yasharaal (Israel), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of the Adanay Yahawah: Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah to the har (mountain) and to the gabaih (hills), to the watercourses and to the gayaa (valleys), to the charabah (desolate) charabah (wastes) and to the iyar (cities) that are forsaken, which are become a baz (prey) and laig (derision) to the shaarayath (residue) of the gaway (nation / people) that are all around;

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Surely in the ash (fire) of my qanaah (jealousy) have I dabar (word / matter) against the shaarayath (residue) of the gaway (nation / people), and against all Adam (Edom), that nathan (give) appointed my aratz (Earth/land) to themselves for a mawarashah (possession) with the shamachah (joy) of all their labab (heart), with shaat (despite) of labab (soul), to magarash (cast) it out for a baz (prey).

Therefore nabaa (prophesy) concerning the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (spoke) the har (mountain) and to the gabaih (hills), to the watercourses and to the gayaa (valleys), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I have dabar (word / matter) in my qanaah (jealousy) and in my chamah (wrath), because you have nashaa (lift) the kalamah (shame) of the gaway (nation / people):
Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I have yad (hand), saying, Surely the gaway (nation / people) that are around you, they shall nashaa (lift) their kalamah (shame).

But you, har (mountain) of Yasharaal (Israel), you shall nathan (give) forth your branches, and nashaa (lift) your paray (fruit) to my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel); for they are at qarab (come close) to bawaa (come).
For, behold, I am for you, and I will panah (turn) into you, and you shall be ibad (servant) and zarai (sown);

And I will rabah (multiply) adam (men) on you, all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), even all of it; and the iyar (cities) shall be yashab (inhabit/dwell), and the charabah (waste) places shall be banah (built);

And I will rabah (multiply) on you adam (man) and animal; and they shall rabah (increase) and be parah (fruitful); and I will yashab (inhabit/dwell) you to be inhabited after your qadamah (former) estate, and will tawab (pleasant/functional) better to you than at your raashah (beginnings): and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Yes, I will cause adam (men) to yalak (walk) on you, even my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel); and they shall yarash (possess) you, and you shall be their nachalah (inheritance), and you shall no more henceforth shakal (bereave) them of children.
Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because they amar (spoke) to you, You are a devourer of adam (men), and have been a bereaver of your gaway (nation / people);
Therefore you shall akal (eat) adam (men) no more, neither kashal (stumble / stagger) your gaway (nation / people) any more, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah;

Neither will I shamai (hearken / hear) you hear any more the kalamah (shame) of the gaway (nation / people), neither shall you nashaa (lift) the charapah (reproach) of the im (people / nation) any more, neither shall you cause your gaway (nation / people) to kashal (stumble / stagger) any more, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
Moreover the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), when the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) lived in their own adamah (land), they tamaa (defiled) it by their darak (way) and by their ilayalah (doings): their darak (way) panayam (before) me was as the tamaah (uncleanness) of a nadah (woman) in her impurity.

Therefore I shapak (poured) out my chamah (wrath) on them for the dam (blood) which they had shapak (poured) out on the aratz (Earth/land), and because they had tamaa (defiled) it with their galawal (idols);

And I pawatz (scattered) them among the gaway (nation / people), and they were zarah (dispersed) through the aratz (Earth/land): according to their darak (way) and according to their ilayalah (doings) I shapat (judged) them.

When they bawaa (come) to the gaway (nation / people), where they bawaa (come), they chalal (profaned) my qadash (set apart/make holy) sham (name); in that men amar (spoke) of them, These are the im (people / nation) of Yahawah, and are yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of his aratz (Earth/land).

But I chamal (had) respect for my qadash (set apart/make holy) sham (name), which the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) had chalal (profaned) among the gaway (nation / people), where they bawaa (come).

Therefore amar (spoke) the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I don't ishah (make) this for your sake, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), but for my qadash (set apart/make holy) sham (name), which you have chalal (profaned) among the gaway (nation / people), where you bawaa (come).

I will qadash (set apart/make holy) my gadawal (very great/important/mighty) sham (name), which has been chalal (profaned) among the gaway (nation / people), which you have chalal (profaned) in their thawak (midst); and the gaway (nation / people) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adawan Yahawah, when I shall be qadash (set apart/make holy) in you before their iyan (eye).
For I will laqach (take / seized) you from man (from) the gaway (nation / people), and qabatz (gather) you out of all the aratz (Earth/land), and will bawaa (come) you into your own adamah (land).
I will zaraq (sprinkle) tahawar (clean) mayam (Waters) on you, and you shall be tahar (clean): from all your tamaah (filthiness), and from all your galawal (idols), will I tahar (cleanse) you.

I will also nathan (give) you a chadash (new) lab (heart), and I will nathan (give) a chadash (new) rawach (spirit / wind) qarab (among / near) you; and I will sawar (take) away the aban (stone) lab (heart) out of your bashar (flesh), and I will nathan (give) you a lab (heart) of bashar (flesh).

I will nathan (give) my rawach (spirit / wind) qarab (among / near) you, and cause you to yalak (walk) in my chaq (statute), and you shall shamar (keep/guard) my mashapat (ordinances), and ishah (make) them.
You shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the aratz (Earth/land) that I nathan (give) to your ab (father); and you shall be my im (people / nation), and I will be your Alahayam.
I will yashai (salvation) you from all your tamaah (uncleanness): and I will qaraa (called) for the grain, and will rabah (multiply) it, and nathan (give) no raib (famine) on you.

I will rabah (multiply) the paray (fruit) of the itz (tree), and the thanawabah (increase) of the shadah (field), that you may laqach (take / seized) no more the charapah (reproach) of raib (famine) among the gaway (nation / people).

Then you shall zakar (remembrance/memory) your rai (evil) darak (ways), and your mailal (doings) that were not tawab (pleasant/functional); and you shall qawat (loathe) yourselves in your own panayam (sight) for your iwan (guilt/iniquity) and for your thawaibah (abominations).

Nor for your sake ishah (make) I this, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, be it yadai (known) to you: be bawash (ashamed) and kalam (confounded) for your darak (ways), bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: In the yawam (day) that I tahar (cleanse) you from all your iwan (guilt/iniquity), I will cause the iyar (cities) to be yashab (inhabit/dwell), and the charabah (waste) places shall be banah (built).
The aratz (Earth/land) that was shamam (desolate) shall be ibad (servant), whereas it was a shamamah (desolation) in the iyan (eye) of ibar (pass over/through) who passed by.

They shall amar (spoke), halazaw (this) aratz (Earth/land) that was shamam (desolate) has become like the gan (garden) of Idan (Eden); and the charab (waste) and shamam (desolate) and haras (ruined) iyar (cities) are batzar (fortified) and yashab (inhabit/dwell).

Then the gaway (nation / people) that are shaar (left) around you shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have banah (built) the haras (ruined) places, and natai (planted) that which was shamam (desolate): I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it, and I will ishah (make) it.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: For this, moreover, will I be darash (inquired) of by the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), to ishah (make) it for them: I will rabah (increase) them with adam (men) like a tzaan (flock).

As the tzaan (flock) for qadash (set apart/make holy), as the tzaan (flock) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) in her mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) feasts, so shall the charab (waste) iyar (cities) be malaa (filled) with tzaan (flocks) of adam (men); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

The yad (hand) of Yahawah was on me, and he yatzaa (go out / come out) me out in the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah, and nawach (set) me down in the thawak (midst) of the baqaih (valley); and it malaa (was) full of itzam (bones).
He ibar (pass over/through) me to pass by them all around: and behold, there were very many in the panayam (open) baqaih (valley); and behold, they were very yabash (dry land).
He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), can these itzam (bones) chayah (live)? I amar (spoke), Adanay Yahawah, you yadai (know).
Again he amar (spoke) to me, nabaa (prophesy) over these itzam (bones), and amar (spoke) them, you yabash (dry land) itzam (bones), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah.
Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah to these itzam (bones): Behold, I will cause rawach (spirit / wind) to bawaa (come) into you, and you shall chayah (live).

I will nathan (give) gayad (sinews) on you, and will ilah (go up / offer) up bashar (flesh) on you, and qaram (cover) you with iwar (skin), and nathan (give) rawach (spirit / wind) in you, and you shall chayah (live); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

So I nabaa (prophesied) as I was tzawah (commanded): and as I nabaa (prophesied), there was a qawal (sound / voice), and behold, an raish (earthquake); and the itzam (bones) qarab (come close) together, itzam (bone) to its itzam (bone).

I raah (see), and, behold, there were gayad (sinews) on them, and bashar (flesh) ilah (go up / offer) up, and iwar (skin) qaram (covered) them mail (top/above); but there was no rawach (spirit / wind) in them.

Then he amar (spoke) to me, nabaa (prophesy) to the rawach (spirit / wind), nabaa (prophesy), ban (son) of adam (man), and amar (spoke) the rawach (spirit / wind), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: bawaa (come) from the arabai (four) rawach (spirit / wind), rawach (spirit / wind), and breathe on these harag (slain), that they may chayah (live).

So I nabaa (prophesied) as he tzawah (commanded) me, and the rawach (spirit / wind) bawaa (come) into them, and they chayah (lived), and imad (stood) up on their ragal (feet / foot), an maad (exceedingly) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor).

Then he amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), these itzam (bones) are the whole bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel): behold, they amar (spoke), Our itzam (bones) are yabash (dry land) up, and our thaqawah (hope) is abad (destroy/perish); we are clean gazar (cut) off.

Therefore nabaa (prophesy), and amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will pathach (open) your qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher), and ilah (go up / offer) you to come up out of your qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher), my people; and I will bawaa (come) you into the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel).

You shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I pathach (have) opened your qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher), and ilah (go up / offer) you to come up out of your qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher), my im (people / nation).

I will nathan (give) my rawach (spirit / wind) in you, and you shall chayah (live), and I will yanach (place) you in your own adamah (land): and you shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it and ishah (make) it, naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came again to me, amar (spoke),

You, ban (son) of adam (man), laqach (take / seized) achad (one) itz (stick), and kathab (write) on it, For Yahawadah (Judah), and for the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) his chabar (companions): then laqach (take / seized) another itz (stick), and kathab (write) on it, For Yawasap (Joseph), the itz (stick) of Aparayam (Ephraim), and for all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) his chabar (companions):
And qarab (come close) them for you achad (one) to another into achad (one) itz (stick), that they may become achad (one) in your yad (hand).
When the ban (son) of your im (people / nation) shall amar (spoke) to you, amar (spoke), Will you not show us what you mean by these?

Dabar (word / matter) them, Thus dabar (word / matter) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will laqach (take / seized) the itz (stick) of Yawasap (Joseph), which is in the yad (hand) of Aparayam (Ephraim), and the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) his chabar (companions); and I will nathan (give) them with it, even with the itz (stick) of Yahawadah (Judah), and ishah (make) them achad (one) itz (stick), and they shall be achad (one) in my yad (hand).
The itz (sticks) whereon you kathab (write) shall be in your yad (hand) before their iyan (eye).

Dabar (word / matter) to them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will laqach (take / seized) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) from bayan (between) the gaway (nation / people), where they are halak (move), and will qabatz (gather) them on sabayab (surrounding) side, and bawaa (come) them into their own adamah (land):

And I will ishah (make) them achad (one) gaway (nation / people) in the aratz (Earth/land), on the har (mountain) of Yasharaal (Israel); and achad (one) malak (king) shall be malak (king) to them iwad (more/again); and they shall be no more shanayam (two) gaway (nation / people), neither shall they be chatzah (divided) into shanayam (two) mamalakah (kingdoms) any more at all;

Neither shall they tamaa (defile) themselves any more with their galawal (idols), nor with their shaqawatz (detestable) things, nor with any of their pashai (transgressions); but I will yashai (salvation) them out of all their mawashab (dwelling) places, in which they have chataa (sinned), and will tahar (cleanse) them: so shall they be my im (people / nation), and I will be their Alahayam.

My ibad (servant) Dawad (David) shall be malak (king) over them; and they all shall have achad (one) raih (shepherd): they shall also yalak (walk) in my mashapat (ordinances), and shamar (keep/guard) my chaqah (statutes), and ishah (make) them.

They shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the aratz (Earth/land) that I nathan (give) given to Yaiqab (Jacob) my ibad (servant), in which your ab (father) lived; and they shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein, they, and their ban (son), and their ban (son) ban (son), iwalam (forever): and Dawad (David) my ibad (servant) shall be their nashayaa (prince) for iwalam (forever).

Moreover I will karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) of shalawam (peace / safety) with them; it shall be an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant) with them; and I will nathan (give) them, and rabah (multiply) them, and will nathan (give) my maqadash (sanctuary) in their thawak (midst) forevermore.
My mashakan (tent) also shall be with them; and I will be their Alahayam, and they shall be my im (people / nation).
The gaway (nation / people) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah who qadash (set apart/make holy) Yasharaal (Israel), when my maqadash (sanctuary) shall be in their thawak (midst) forevermore.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) toward Gawag (Gog), of the aratz (Earth/land) of Magawag (Magog), the nashayaa (prince) of Rosh, Mashak (Meshech), and Thawabal (Tubal), and nabaa (prophesy) against him,
And amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against you, Gawag (Gog), raash (head) of Rosh, Mashak (Meshech), and Thawabal (Tubal):

And I will shawab (turn back / repent) you around, and nathan (give) chach (hooks) into your lachay (jaws), and I will yatzaa (go out / come out) you forth, with all your chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), sawas (horses) and horsemen, all of them labash (clothed) in full armor, a rab (great) qahal (company) with tzanah (buckler) and magan (shield), all of them thapash (handling) charab (sword);
Paras (Persia), Kawash (Cush), and Pawat (Put) with them, all of them with magan (shield) and kawabai (helmet);
Gamar (Gomer), and all his hordes; the bayath (house) of Thawagaramah (Togarmah) in the uttermost yarakah (parts) of the tzapawan (north), and all his hordes; even many im (people / nation) with you.
Be kawan (prepared), yes, kawan (prepare) yourself, you, and all your qahal (companies) who are qahal (assembled) to you, and be a mashamar (guard) to them.

After many yawam (day) you shall be paqad (visit): in the acharayath (latter) shanah (years) you shall bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land) that is shawab (turn back / repent) back from the charab (sword), that is qabatz (gathered) out of many im (people / nation), on the har (mountain) of Yasharaal (Israel), which have been a thamayad (continual) charabah (waste); but it is yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the im (people / nation), and they shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely, all of them.

You shall ilah (go up / offer), you shall bawaa (come) like a shawaa (vanity), you shall be like a inan (cloud) to kasah (cover) the aratz (Earth/land), you, and all your hordes, and many im (people / nation) with you.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: It shall happen in that yawam (day), that things shall ilah (go up / offer) into your labab (mind), and you shall chashab (devise) an rai (evil) machashabah (device):

And you shall amar (spoke), I will ilah (go up / offer) up to the aratz (Earth/land) of parazah (unwalled) villages; I will bawaa (come) to those who are at shaqat (rest), who yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely, all of them yashab (inhabit/dwell) without chawamah (walls), and having neither barayach (bars) nor dalath (gates);

To take the shalal (spoil) and to bazaz (take) the baz (prey); to shawab (turn back / repent) your yad (hand) against the charabah (waste) places that are now yashab (inhabit/dwell), and against the im (people / nation) who are asap (gathered) out of the gaway (nation / people), who ishah (make) gotten livestock and qanayan (goods), who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the tabawar (middle) of the aratz (Earth/land).

Shabaa (Sheba), and Dadan (Dedan), and the sachar (merchants) of Tharashayash (Tarshish), with all the young kapayar (lions) of it, shall amar (spoke) you, bawaa (come) you come to take the shalal (spoil)? Have you qahal (assembled) your qahal (company) to bazaz (take) the baz (prey)? To nashaa (lift) away kasap (silver) and zahab (gold), to laqach (take / seized) away livestock and qanayan (goods), to take gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shalal (spoil)?

Therefore, ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy), and amar (spoke) Gawag (Gog), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: In that yawam (day) when my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel) yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely, shall you not yadai (know) it?

You shall bawaa (come) from your maqawam (place) out of the uttermost yarakah (parts) of the tzapawan (north), you, and many im (people / nation) with you, all of them rakab (riding) on sawas (horses), a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qahal (company) and a rab (mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor);

And you shall ilah (go up / offer) up against my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel), as a inan (cloud) to kasah (cover) the aratz (Earth/land): it shall happen in the acharayath (latter) yawam (day), that I will bawaa (come) you against my aratz (Earth/land), that the gaway (nation / people) may yadai (know) me, when I shall be qadash (set apart/make holy) in you, Gawag (Gog), before their iyan (eye).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Are you he of whom I dabar (word / matter) in qadamawanay (old) yawam (day) by my ibad (servant) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Yasharaal (Israel), who nabaa (prophesied) in those yawam (day) for many shanah (years) that I would bawaa (come) you against them?

It shall happen in that yawam (day), when Gawag (Gog) shall bawaa (come) against the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, that my chamah (wrath) shall ilah (go up / offer) up into my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).

For in my qanaah (jealousy) and in the ash (fire) of my ibarah (wrath) have I dabar (word / matter), Surely in that yawam (day) there shall be a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) raish (shaking) in the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel);

So that the dag (fish) of the yam (sea/waters), and the iwap (flying) of the sky, and the animals of the shadah (field), and all ramash (creeping) things who ramash (creep) on the adamah (earth), and all the adam (men) who are on the surface of the adamah (earth), shall raish (shake) at my panayam (presence), and the har (mountain) shall be haras (thrown) down, and the madaragah (steep) places shall napal (fall / be cast down), and every chawamah (wall) shall napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land).

I will qaraa (called) for a charab (sword) against him to all my har (mountain), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah: every ayash (husband/individual man) charab (sword) shall be against his ach (brother/kinsman).

With dabar (word / matter) and with dam (blood) will I enter into shapat (judgment) with him; and I will matar (rain) on him, and on his hordes, and on the many im (people / nation) who are with him, an shatap (overflowing) gasham (shower), and alagabayash (great) hailstones, ash (fire), and sulfur.

I will gadal (magnify) myself, and qadash (set apart/make holy) myself, and I yadai (will) make myself known in the iyan (eye) of many gaway (nation / people); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

You, ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy) against Gawag (Gog), and amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against you, Gawag (Gog), raash (head) of Rosh, Mashak (Meshech), and Thawabal (Tubal):

And I will shawab (turn back / repent) you around, and will lead you on, and will ilah (go up / offer) you to come up from the uttermost yarakah (parts) of the tzapawan (north); and I will bawaa (come) you on the har (mountain) of Yasharaal (Israel);

And I will nakah (strike) your qashath (bow) out of your shamaawal (left hand) yad (hand), and will cause your chatz (arrows) to napal (fall / be cast down) out of your yamayan (right hand) yad (hand).

You shall napal (fall / be cast down) on the har (mountain) of Yasharaal (Israel), you, and all your hordes, and the im (people / nation) who are with you: I will nathan (give) you to the iyat (ravenous) tzapawar (birds) of every kanap (sort), and to the animals of the shadah (field) to be akalah (devoured).
You shall napal (fall / be cast down) on the panayam (open) shadah (field); for I have dabar (word / matter) it, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on Magawag (Magog), and on those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely in the ay (islands); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

My qadash (set apart/make holy) sham (name) yadai (will) I make known in the thawak (midst) of my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel); neither will I allow my qadash (set apart/make holy) sham (name) to be chalal (profaned) any more: and the gaway (nation / people) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, the qadawash (holy) One in Yasharaal (Israel).
Behold, it bawaa (come), and it shall be hayah (came to pass), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah; this is the yawam (day) about which I have dabar (word / matter).

Those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the iyar (cities) of Yasharaal (Israel) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and shall make ash (fire) of the nashaq (weapons) and nashaq (burn) them, both the magan (shield) and the tzanah (bucklers), the qashath (bows) and the chatz (arrows), and the war clubs, and the ramach (spears), and they shall make ash (fire) of them shabai (seven) shanah (years);

So that they shall nashaa (lift) no itz (wood) out of the shadah (field), neither chatab (cut) down any out of the yair (forests); for they shall make ash (fire) of the nashaq (weapons); and they shall plunder those who plundered them, and bazaz (rob) those who bazaz (robbed) them, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

It shall happen in that yawam (day), that I will nathan (give) to Gawag (Gog) a maqawam (place) for burial in Yasharaal (Israel), the gayaa (valley) of those who ibar (pass over/through) through on the qadamah (east) of the yam (sea/waters); and it shall chasam (stop) those who ibar (pass over/through) through: and there shall they qabar (bury) Gawag (Gog) and all his hamawan (multitude); and they shall qaraa (called) it The gayaa (valley) Hamawanagawag (of) Hamon Gog.
Shabai (seven) chadash (month) shall the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) be qabar (bury) them, that they may tahar (cleanse) the aratz (Earth/land).

Yes, all the im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land) shall qabar (bury) them; and it shall be to them a sham (name) in the yawam (day) that I shall be kabad (glorified), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

They shall set apart ayash (husband/individual man) of thamayad (continual) employment, who shall ibar (pass over/through) through the aratz (Earth/land), and, with those who ibar (pass over/through) through, those who qabar (bury) those who yathar (remain) on the surface of the aratz (Earth/land), to tahar (cleanse) it: qatzah (end / extremity / border) the end of shabai (seven) chadash (month) shall they chaqar (search).

Those who ibar (pass over/through) through the aratz (Earth/land) shall ibar (pass over/through) through; and when any raah (see) a adam (man's) itzam (bone), then shall he banah (set) up a tzayawan (visible marker/identifier/landmark) by it, until the undertakers have qabar (bury) it in the gayaa (valley) Hamawanagawag (of) Hamon Gog.
Hamawanah (Hamonah) shall also be the sham (name) of a iyar (city). Thus shall they tahar (cleanse) the aratz (Earth/land).

You, ban (son) of adam (man), thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: amar (spoke) to the tzapawar (birds) of every kanap (sort), and to every animal of the shadah (field), qabatz (assemble) yourselves, and bawaa (come); asap (gather) yourselves on sabayab (surrounding) side to my zabach (sacrifice) that I do zabach (sacrifice) for you, even a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) zabach (sacrifice) on the har (mountain) of Yasharaal (Israel), that you may akal (eat) bashar (flesh) and shathah (drinks) dam (blood).

You shall akal (eat) the bashar (flesh) of the gabawar (mighty), and shathah (drinks) the dam (blood) of the nashayaa (princes) of the aratz (Earth/land), of ayal (rams), of kar (lambs), and of ithawad (goats), of par (bulls), all of them fatlings of Bashan (Bashan).
You shall akal (eat) chalab (fat) until you be shabaih (seven), and shathah (drinks) dam (blood) until you are shakarawan (drunk), of my zabach (sacrifice) which I have zabach (sacrificed) for you.

You shall be shabai (filled) at my shalachan (table) with sawas (horses) and rakab (chariots), with gabawar (mighty) men, and with all ayash (husband/individual man) of malachamah (war), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

I will nathan (give) my kabawad (glory) among the gaway (nation / people); and all the gaway (nation / people) shall raah (see) my mashapat (judgment) that I ishah (make) executed, and my yad (hand) that I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) on them.
So the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah their Alahayam, from that yawam (day) and halaah (forward).

The gaway (nation / people) shall yadai (know) that the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) galah (went) into captivity for their iwan (guilt/iniquity); because they mail (top/above) against me, and I sathar (hid) my panayam (face) from them: so I nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of their tzar (oppressor / distressor), and they napal (fall / be cast down) all of them by the charab (sword).
According to their tamaah (uncleanness) and according to their pashai (transgressions) ishah (make) I to them; and I sathar (hid) my panayam (face) from them.

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Now will I shawab (turn back / repent) back the shabawath (captivity) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and have racham (mercy) on the whole bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel); and I will be qanaa (jealous) for my qadash (set apart/make holy) sham (name).

They shall nashaa (lift) their kalamah (shame), and all their trespasses by which they have mail (top/above) against me, when they shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely in their adamah (land), and none shall make them charad (afraid);

When I have shawab (turn back / repent) them back from the im (people / nation), and qabatz (gathered) them out of their ayab (enemy)' aratz (Earth/land), and am qadash (set apart/make holy) in them in the iyan (eye) of many gaway (nation / people).

They shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah their Alahayam, in that I caused them to galah (go) into captivity among the gaway (nation / people), and have kanas (gathered) them to their own adamah (land); and I will yathar (leave) none of them any more there;

Neither will I sathar (hide) my panayam (face) any more from them; for I have shapak (poured) out my rawach (spirit / wind) on the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

In the chamash (five) and isharayam (twenty) shanah (year) of our galawath (captivity), in the raash (head) of the shanah (year), in the ishawar (tenth) day of the chadash (month), in the fourteenth shanah (year) achar (other) that the iyar (city) was nakah (struck), in the same yawam (day), the yad (hand) of Yahawah was on me, and he bawaa (come) me there.

In the maraah (visions) of Alahayam bawaa (come) he me into the aratz (Earth/land) of Yasharaal (Israel), and nawach (set) me down on a very gabah (high) har (mountain), whereon was as it were the mabanah (frame) of a iyar (city) on the nagab (south).

He bawaa (come) me there; and, behold, there was a ayash (husband/individual man), whose maraah (appearance) was like the maraah (appearance) of nachashath (brass), with a pathayal (line) of pashathah (flax) in his yad (hand), and a madah (measuring) qanah (reed); and he imad (stood) in the shair (gate).

The ayash (husband/individual man) dabar (word / matter) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), raah (see) with your iyan (eye), and shamai (hearken / hear) with your azan (ears), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) your lab (heart) on all that I shall show you; for, to the intent that I may show them to you, you are bawaa (come) here: nagad (declare) all that you raah (see) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Behold, a chawamah (wall) on the outside of the bayath (house) all around, and in the ayash (husband/individual man) yad (hand) a madah (measuring) qanah (reed) shash (six) amah (cubits) long, of a amah (cubit) and a tapach (handbreadth) each: so he madad (measured) the thickness of the banayan (building), achad (one) qanah (reed); and the qawamah (height), achad (one) qanah (reed).

Then bawaa (come) he to the shair (gate) which panayam (looks) darak (toward) the qadayam (east), and ilah (go up / offer) up its mailah (ascent/climbing up): and he madad (measured) the sap (threshold) of the shair (gate), achad (one) qanah (reed) rachab (broad); and the other sap (threshold), achad (one) qanah (reed) rachab (broad).

Every lodge was achad (one) qanah (reed) arak (length), and achad (one) qanah (reed) rachab (broad); and the space between the lodges was chamash (five) amah (cubits); and the sap (threshold) of the shair (gate) by the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate) toward the house was one qanah (reed).
He madad (measured) also the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate) toward the house, one qanah (reed).

Then madad (measured) he the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate), shamanah (eight) amah (cubits); and its ayal (posts), shanayam (two) amah (cubits); and the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate) was toward the bayath (house).

The lodges of the shair (gate) darak (eastward) were shalawash (three) on pah (this) side, and shalawash (three) on that pah (side); they shalawash (three) were of achad (one) madah (measure): and the ayal (posts) had achad (one) madah (measure) on this side and on that side.
He madad (measured) the rachab (breadth) of the pathach (opening) of the shair (gate), ishar (ten) amah (cubits); and the arak (length) of the shair (gate), thirteen amah (cubits);

And a gabawal (border/boundary) panayam (before) the lodges, achad (one) amah (cubit) on this side, and a gabawal (border/boundary), one amah (cubit) on that side; and the lodges, shash (six) amah (cubits) on this side, and shash (six) amah (cubits) on that side.

He madad (measured) the shair (gate) from the gag (roof) of the thaa (one) lodge to the gag (roof) of the other, a rachab (breadth) of isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amah (cubits); pathach (door) against pathach (door).
He ishah (make) also ayal (posts), shashayam (sixty) amah (cubits); and the chatzar (court) reached to the ayal (posts), around the shair (gate).
From the panayam (forefront) of the shair (gate) at the yaathawan (entrance) to the panayam (forefront) of the inner awalam (porch) of the shair (gate) were chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits).

There were closed chalawan (windows) to the lodges, and to their ayal (posts) panayamah (within) the shair (gate) all around, and likewise to the arches; and chalawan (windows) were around inward; and on each ayal (post) were thamar (palm) trees.

Then bawaa (come) he me into the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court); and behold, there were rooms and a ratzapah (pavement), ishah (make) for the chatzar (court) all around: shalawashayam (thirty) rooms were on the ratzapah (pavement).
The ratzapah (pavement) was by the kathap (side) of the shair (gates), answerable to the arak (length) of the shair (gates), even the thachathawan (lower) ratzapah (pavement).

Then he madad (measured) the rachab (breadth) from the panayam (forefront) of the thachathawan (lower) shair (gate) to the panayam (forefront) of the inner chatzar (court) outside, one maah (hundred) amah (cubits), both on the qadayam (east) and on the tzapawan (north).
The shair (gate) of the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court) whose prospect is darak (toward) the tzapawan (north), he madad (measured) its arak (length) and its rachab (breadth).

The lodges of it were shalawash (three) on this side and shalawash (three) on that side; and its ayal (posts) and its arches were after the madah (measure) of the raashawan (first) shair (gate): its arak (length) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits), and the rachab (breadth) twenty - five amah (cubits).

The chalawan (windows) of it, and its arches, and the thamar (palm) trees of it, were after the madah (measure) of the shair (gate) whose prospect is darak (toward) the qadayam (east); and they ilah (go up / offer) up to it by shabai (seven) mailah (ascent/climbing up); and its arches were panayam (before) them.

There was a shair (gate) to the inner chatzar (court) over against the other shair (gate), both on the tzapawan (north) and on the qadayam (east); and he madad (measured) from shair (gate) to shair (gate) one maah (hundred) amah (cubits).

He yalak (led) me darak (toward) the darawam (south); and behold, a shair (gate) darak (toward) the darawam (south): and he madad (measured) its ayal (posts) and its arches according to these madah (measures).

There were chalawan (windows) in it and in its arches all around, like those chalawan (windows): the arak (length) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits), and the rachab (breadth) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amah (cubits).

There were shabai (seven) mailah (ascent/climbing up) to ilah (go) up to it, and its arches were panayam (before) them; and it had thamar (palm) trees, achad (one) on this side, and another on that side, on its ayal (posts).

There was a shair (gate) to the inner chatzar (court) darak (toward) the darawam (south): and he madad (measured) from shair (gate) to shair (gate) darak (toward) the darawam (south) a maah (hundred) amah (cubits).
Then he bawaa (come) me to the inner chatzar (court) by the darawam (south) shair (gate): and he madad (measured) the darawam (south) shair (gate) according to these madah (measures);

And its lodges, and its ayal (posts), and its arches, according to these madah (measures): and there were chalawan (windows) in it and in its arches all around; it was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits) arak (length), and isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amah (cubits) rachab (broad).
There were arches all around, isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amah (cubits) arak (length), and chamash (five) amah (cubits) rachab (broad).
The arches of it were toward the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court); and thamar (palm) trees were on its ayal (posts): and the mailah (ascent) to it had shamanah (eight) mailah (ascent/climbing up).
He bawaa (come) me into the inner chatzar (court) darak (toward) the qadayam (east): and he madad (measured) the shair (gate) according to these madah (measures);

And its lodges, and its ayal (posts), and its arches, according to these madah (measures): and there were chalawan (windows) therein and in its arches all around; it was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits) arak (length), and isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amah (cubits) rachab (broad).

The arches of it were toward the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court); and thamar (palm) trees were on its ayal (posts), on this side, and on that side: and the mailah (ascent) to it had shamanah (eight) mailah (ascent/climbing up).
He bawaa (come) me to the tzapawan (north) shair (gate): and he madad (measured) it according to these madah (measures);

Its lodges, its ayal (posts), and its arches: and there were chalawan (windows) therein all around; the arak (length) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits), and the rachab (breadth) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amah (cubits).

The ayal (posts) of it were toward the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court); and thamar (palm) trees were on its ayal (posts), on this side, and on that side: and the mailah (ascent) to it had shamanah (eight) mailah (ascent/climbing up).
A room with its pathach (door) was by the ayal (posts) at the shair (gates); there they dawach (washed) the burnt ilah (offering).

In the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate) were shanayam (two) shalachan (tables) on this side, and two shalachan (tables) on that side, to shachat (kill) thereon the burnt ilah (offering) and the chataah (sin) offering and the asham (trespass) offering.

On the one kathap (side) outside, as one ilah (go up / offer) up to the entry of the shair (gate) toward the tzapawan (north), were shanayam (two) shalachan (tables); and on the other kathap (side), which belonged to the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate), were shanayam (two) shalachan (tables).

Arabai (four) shalachan (tables) were on this side, and arabai (four) shalachan (tables) on that kathap (side), by the side of the shair (gate); shamanah (eight) shalachan (tables), whereupon they shachat (killed) the sacrifices.

There were arabai (four) shalachan (tables) for the burnt ilah (offering), of cut aban (stone), a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half) arak (length), and a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half) rachab (broad), and achad (one) amah (cubit) gabah (high); whereupon they yanach (laid) the kalay (instruments) with which they shachat (killed) the burnt ilah (offering) and the zabach (sacrifice).
The shapath (hooks), a tapach (handbreadth) long, were kawan (fastened) bayath (house) all around: and on the shalachan (tables) was the bashar (flesh) of the qaraban (offering).

Outside of the inner shair (gate) were rooms for the singers in the inner chatzar (court), which was at the kathap (side) of the tzapawan (north) shair (gate); and their prospect was darak (toward) the darawam (south); achad (one) at the kathap (side) of the qadayam (east) shair (gate) having the prospect darak (toward) the tzapawan (north).
He dabar (word / matter) to me, zah (this/that/these) room, whose prospect is darak (toward) the darawam (south), is for the kahan (priest), the keepers of the duty of the bayath (house);

And the room whose prospect is darak (toward) the tzapawan (north) is for the kahan (priest), the keepers of the duty of the mazabach (altar): these are the ban (son) of Tzadawaq (Zadok), who from among the ban (son) of Laway (Levi) qarab (come) near to Yahawah to sharath (minister) to him.

He madad (measured) the chatzar (court), one maah (hundred) amah (cubits) arak (length), and a maah (hundred) amah (cubits) rachab (broad), rabai (fourth); and the mazabach (altar) panayam (was) before the bayath (house).

Then he bawaa (come) me to the awalam (porch) of the bayath (house), and madad (measured) each ayal (post) of the awalam (porch), chamash (five) amah (cubits) on this side, and chamash (five) amah (cubits) on that side: and the rachab (breadth) of the shair (gate) was shalawash (three) amah (cubits) on this side, and shalawash (three) amah (cubits) on that side.

The arak (length) of the awalam (porch) was isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits), and the rachab (breadth) ishathay (eleven) amah (cubits); even by the mailah (ascent/climbing up) by which they ilah (go up / offer) up to it: and there were imawad (pillar) by the ayal (posts), achad (one) on this side, and another on that side.

He bawaa (come) me to the hayakal (temple), and madad (measured) the ayal (posts), shash (six) amah (cubits) rachab (broad) on the one pah (side), and shash (six) amah (cubits) rachab (broad) on the other pah (side), which was the rachab (breadth) of the ahal (tent).

The rachab (breadth) of the pathach (entrance) was ishar (ten) amah (cubits); and the kathap (sides) of the pathach (entrance) were chamash (five) amah (cubits) on the one side, and chamash (five) amah (cubits) on the other side: and he madad (measured) its arak (length), arabaiyam (forty) amah (cubits), and the rachab (breadth), isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits).

Then bawaa (come) he inward, and madad (measured) each ayal (post) of the pathach (entrance), shanayam (two) amah (cubits); and the pathach (entrance), shash (six) amah (cubits); and the rachab (breadth) of the pathach (entrance), shabai (seven) amah (cubits).

He madad (measured) its arak (length), isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits), and the rachab (breadth), isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits), panayam (before) the hayakal (temple): and he amar (spoke) to me, This is the most qadash (set apart/make holy) place.

Then he madad (measured) the qayar (wall) of the bayath (house), shash (six) amah (cubits); and the rachab (breadth) of every tzalai (side) room, arabai (four) amah (cubits), all around the bayath (house) on sabayab (surrounding) side.

The tzalai (side) rooms were in shalawash (three) stories, tzalai (one) over another, and shalawashayam (thirty) in paim (order); and they bawaa (come) into the qayar (wall) which belonged to the bayath (house) for the tzalai (side) rooms all around, that they might achaz (have) hold therein, and not achaz (have) hold in the qayar (wall) of the bayath (house).

The tzalai (side) rooms were broader as they encompassed the mail (top/above) higher and higher; for the encompassing of the bayath (house) went higher and higher around the bayath (house): therefore the rachab (breadth) of the bayath (house) continued upward; and so one ilah (go up / offer) up from the thachathawan (lowest) room to the highest by the thayakawan (middle) room.

I raah (see) also that the bayath (house) had a raised base all around: the mayasadah (foundations) of the tzalai (side) rooms were a malaa (full) qanah (reed) of shash (six) atzayal (great) amah (cubits).

The rachab (thickness) of the qayar (wall), which was for the tzalai (side) rooms, on the outside, was chamash (five) amah (cubits): and that which was yanach (left) was the bayath (house) of the tzalai (side) rooms that belonged to the bayath (house).
Between the rooms was a rachab (breadth) of isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) around the bayath (house) on sabayab (surrounding) side.

The pathach (doors) of the tzalai (side) rooms were toward the yanach (place) that was left, achad (one) pathach (door) darak (toward) the tzapawan (north), and another pathach (door) toward the darawam (south): and the rachab (breadth) of the maqawam (place) that was yanach (left) was chamash (five) amah (cubits) all around.

The banayan (building) that panayam (was) before the gazarah (separate) place at the paah (side) darak (toward) the yam (sea/waters) was shabaiyam (seventy) amah (cubits) rachab (broad); and the qayar (wall) of the banayan (building) was chamash (five) amah (cubits) thick all around, and its arak (length) thashaiyam (ninety) amah (cubits).

So he madad (measured) the bayath (house), one maah (hundred) amah (cubits) arak (length); and the gazarah (separate) place, and the banayah (building), with its qayar (walls), one maah (hundred) amah (cubits) arak (length);
Also the rachab (breadth) of the panayam (face) of the bayath (house), and of the gazarah (separate) place toward the qadayam (east), one maah (hundred) amah (cubits).

He madad (measured) the arak (length) of the banayan (building) panayam (before) the gazarah (separate) place which was at its achar (other), and its athawaq (galleries) on the one side and on the other side, one maah (hundred) amah (cubits); and the inner hayakal (temple), and the porches of the chatzar (court);

The sap (thresholds), and the closed chalawan (windows), and the athawaq (galleries) around on their shalawash (three) stories, over nagad (against) the sap (threshold), with itz (wood) ceilings all around, and from the aratz (Earth/land) up to the chalawan (windows), (now the chalawan (windows) were kasah (covered)),
To the space above the pathach (door), even to the inner bayath (house), and outside, and by all the qayar (wall) all around inside and outside, by madah (measure).

It was ishah (make) with karawab (cherubim) and thamar (palm) trees; and a thamar (palm) tree was between karawab (cherub) and karawab (cherub), and every karawab (cherub) had shanayam (two) panayam (faces);

So that there was the panayam (face) of a adam (man) toward the thamar (palm) tree on the one side, and the panayam (face) of a young kapayar (lion) toward the thamar (palm) tree on the other side. Thus was it ishah (make) through all the bayath (house) all around:
From the aratz (Earth/land) to above the pathach (door) were karawab (cherubim) and thamar (palm) trees ishah (make): thus was the qayar (wall) of the hayakal (temple).

As for the hayakal (temple), the mazawazah (door) posts were rabai (fourth); and as for the panayam (face) of the qadash (set apart/make holy), the maraah (appearance) of it was as the maraah (appearance) of the temple.

The mazabach (altar) was of itz (wood), shalawash (three) amah (cubits) gabah (high), and its arak (length) shanayam (two) amah (cubits); and its maqatzawai (corners), and its arak (length), and its qayar (walls), were of itz (wood): and he dabar (word / matter) to me, This is the shalachan (table) that is panayam (before) Yahawah.
The hayakal (temple) and the qadash (set apart/make holy) had shanayam (two) dalath (doors).
The dalath (doors) had shanayam (two) leaves apiece, shanayam (two) mawasabah (turning) leaves: shanayam (two) leaves for the achad (one) dalath (door), and shanayam (two) leaves for the other.

There were ishah (make) on them, on the dalath (doors) of the hayakal (temple), karawab (cherubim) and thamar (palm) trees, like as were ishah (make) on the qayar (walls); and there was a threshold of itz (wood) on the panayam (face) of the awalam (porch) outside.

There were closed chalawan (windows) and thamar (palm) trees on the one kathap (side) and on the other side, on the sides of the awalam (porch): thus were the tzalai (side) rooms of the bayath (house), and the thresholds.

Then he yatzaa (go out / come out) me forth into the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court), the darak (way) toward the tzapawan (north): and he bawaa (come) me into the room that was over against the gazarah (separate) place, and which was over against the banayan (building) toward the tzapawan (north).
Panayam (before) the arak (length) of one maah (hundred) amah (cubits) was the tzapawan (north) pathach (door), and the rachab (breadth) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits).

Over against the isharayam (twenty) cubits which belonged to the inner chatzar (court), and over against the ratzapah (pavement) which belonged to the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court), was athawaq (gallery) panayam (against) athawaq (gallery) in the shalayashay (third) story.

Panayam (before) the rooms was a mahalak (walk) of ishar (ten) amah (cubits)' rachab (breadth) inward, a darak (way) of achad (one) amah (cubit); and their pathach (doors) were toward the tzapawan (north).
Now the ilayawan (upper) rooms were shorter; for the athawaq (galleries) took away from these, more than from the thachathawan (lower) and the thayakawan (middle), in the banayan (building).

For they were in shalash (three) stories, and they didn't have imawad (pillar) as the imawad (pillar) of the chatzar (courts): therefore the uppermost was atzal (straitened) more than the thachathawan (lowest) and the thayakawan (middle) from the aratz (Earth/land).
The gadar (wall) that was outside by the side of the rooms, toward the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court) panayam (before) the rooms, its arak (length) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits).

For the arak (length) of the rooms that were in the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits): and behold, panayam (before) the hayakal (temple) were one maah (hundred) amah (cubits).
From under these rooms was the mabawaa (entry) on the qadayam (east) side, as one bawaa (come) into them from the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court).

In the rachab (thickness) of the gadar (wall) of the chatzar (court) darak (toward) the qadayam (east), panayam (before) the gazarah (separate) place, and panayam (before) the banayan (building), there were rooms.

The darak (way) panayam (before) them was like the maraah (appearance) of the lashakah (way) of the rooms which were darak (toward) the tzapawan (north); according to their arak (length) so was their breadth: and all their exits were both according to their mashapat (fashions), and according to their pathach (doors).

According to the pathach (doors) of the rooms that were darak (toward) the darawam (south) was a pathach (door) at the raash (head) of the darak (way), even the darak (way) hagayan (directly) panayam (before) the gadarah (wall) darak (toward) the qadayam (east), as one bawaa (come) into them.

Then he amar (spoke) to me, The tzapawan (north) rooms and the darawam (south) rooms, which are panayam (before) the gazarah (separate) place, they are the qadash (set apart/make holy) rooms, where the kahan (priest) who are qarawab (near) to Yahawah shall akal (eat) the most qadash (set apart/make holy) things: there shall they yanach (lay) the most qadash (set apart/make holy) things, and the meal manachah (offering), and the chataah (sin) offering, and the asham (trespass) offering; for the maqawam (place) is qadawash (holy).

When the kahan (priest) bawaa (come) in, then shall they not bawaa (come) out of the qadash (set apart/make holy) place into the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court), but there they shall yanach (lay) their bagad (garments) in which they sharath (minister); for they are qadash (set apart/make holy): and they shall labash (put) on other bagad (garments), and shall qarab (come close) to that which pertains to the im (people / nation).

Now when he kalah (complete / finish) made an end of madah (measuring) the inner bayath (house), he yatzaa (go out / come out) me forth by the darak (way) of the shair (gate) whose prospect is darak (toward) the qadayam (east), and madad (measured) it all around.

He madad (measured) on the qadayam (east) rawach (spirit / wind) with the madah (measuring) qanah (reed) chamash (five) amah (hundred) qanah (reeds), with the madah (measuring) qanah (reed) all around.
He madad (measured) on the tzapawan (north) rawach (spirit / wind) chamash (five) maah (hundred) qanah (reeds) with the madah (measuring) qanah (reed) all around.
He madad (measured) on the darawam (south) rawach (spirit / wind) chamash (five) maah (hundred) qanah (reeds) with the madah (measuring) qanah (reed).
He sabab (turned) about to the yam (sea/waters) rawach (spirit / wind), and madad (measured) chamash (five) maah (hundred) qanah (reeds) with the madah (measuring) qanah (reed).

He madad (measured) it on the arabai (four) rawach (spirit / wind): it had a chawamah (wall) around it, the arak (length) chamash (five) maah (hundred), and the rachab (breadth) chamash (five) maah (hundred), to badal (separated) a separation between that which was qadash (set apart/make holy) and that which was chal (common).
Afterward he yalak (brought) me to the shair (gate), even the shair (gate) that panah (looks) darak (toward) the qadayam (east).

Behold, the kabawad (glory) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) bawaa (come) from the darak (way) of the qadayam (east): and his qawal (sound / voice) was like the qawal (sound / voice) of many mayam (Waters); and the aratz (Earth/land) shined with his kabawad (glory).

It was according to the maraah (appearance) of the maraah (vision) which I raah (see), even according to the maraah (vision) that I raah (see) when I bawaa (come) to shachath (destroy) the iyar (city); and the maraah (visions) were like the maraah (vision) that I raah (see) by the nahar (river) Kabar (Chebar); and I napal (fall / be cast down) on my panayam (face).
The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) by the darak (way) of the shair (gate) whose prospect is darak (toward) the qadayam (east).
The rawach (spirit / wind) nashaa (lift) me up, and bawaa (come) me into the inner chatzar (court); and behold, the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah malaa (filled) the bayath (house).
I shamai (hearken / hear) one dabar (word / matter) to me out of the bayath (house); and a ayash (husband/individual man) imad (stood) by me.

He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), this is the maqawam (place) of my kasaa (throne), and the maqawam (place) of the kap (soles) of my ragal (feet / foot), where I will shakan (dwell) in the thawak (midst) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) iwalam (forever). The bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) shall no more tamaa (defile) my qadash (set apart/make holy) sham (name), neither they, nor their malak (king), by their prostitution, and by the pagar (dead) bodies of their malak (king) in their bamah (high) places;

In their nathan (give) of their sap (threshold) by my sap (threshold), and their doorpost beside my doorpost, and there was but the qayar (wall) between me and them; and they have tamaa (defiled) my qadash (set apart/make holy) sham (name) by their thawaibah (abominations) which they ishah (make) committed: therefore I nathan (give) consumed them in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).
Now let them rachaq (put) away their prostitution, and the pagar (dead) bodies of their malak (king), rachaq (far) from me; and I will shakan (dwell) in their thawak (midst) iwalam (forever).

You, ban (son) of adam (man), show the bayath (house) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), that they may be kalam (ashamed) of their iwan (guilt/iniquity); and let them madad (measure) the thakanayath (pattern).

If they be kalam (ashamed) of all that they ishah (make) done, yadai (make) known to them the tzawarah (form) of the bayath (house), and its thakawanah (fashion), and its exits, and its entrances, and all its tzawarah (forms), and all its chaqah (ordinances), and all its tzawarah (forms), and all its thawarah (instruction); and kathab (write) it in their iyan (eye); that they may shamar (keep/guard) the whole tzawarah (form) of it, and all its chaqah (ordinances), and ishah (make) them.

This is the thawarah (instruction) of the bayath (house): on the raash (head) of the har (mountain) the whole gabawal (border/boundary) around it shall be most qadash (set apart/make holy). Behold, this is the thawarah (instruction) of the bayath (house).

These are the madah (measures) of the mazabach (altar) by amah (cubits) (the amah (cubit) is a amah (cubit) and a tapach (handbreadth)): the chayaq (bottom) shall be a amah (cubit), and the tapach (breadth) a amah (cubit), and its gabawal (border/boundary) around its shapah (edge) a zarath (span); and this shall be the base of the mazabach (altar).
