From the chayaq (bottom) on the aratz (Earth/land) to the thachathawan (lower) ledge shall be shanayam (two) amah (cubits), and the rachab (breadth) achad (one) amah (cubit); and from the qatan (small/young/least) ledge to the greater ledge shall be arabai (four) amah (cubits), and the rachab (breadth) a amah (cubit).
The upper araayal (Araayal/(lion of Al)) shall be arabai (four) amah (cubits); and from the araayal (Araayal/(lion of Al)) hearth and upward there shall be arabai (four) qaran (horn).
The araayal (Araayal/(lion of Al)) hearth shall be shanayam (two) cubits arak (length) by shanayam (two) rachab (broad), rabai (fourth) in the arabai (four) rabai (fourth) of it.

The ledge shall be fourteen cubits arak (length) by fourteen rachab (broad) in the arabai (four) rabai (fourth) of it; and the gabawal (border/boundary) sabayab (surrounding) it shall be chatzay (half) a amah (cubit); and its chayaq (bottom) shall be a amah (cubit) around; and its mailah (ascent/climbing up) shall panah (look) toward the qadayam (east).

He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: These are the chaqah (ordinances) of the mazabach (altar) in the yawam (day) when they shall ishah (make) it, to ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilah (offerings) thereon, and to zaraq (sprinkle) dam (blood) thereon.

You shall nathan (give) to the kahan (priest) the Lawayay (Levites) who are of the zarai (seed) of Tzadawaq (Zadok), who are qarawab (near) to me, to sharath (minister) to me, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, a ban (son) par (bull) for a chataah (sin) offering.

You shall laqach (take / seized) of its dam (blood), and nathan (give) it on the arabai (four) qaran (horn) of it, and on the arabai (four) panah (corners) of the ledge, and on the gabawal (border/boundary) all around: thus you shall chataa (cleanse) it and make kapar (atonement) for it.
You shall also laqach (take / seized) the par (bull) of the chataah (sin) offering, and it shall be burnt in the mapaqad (appointed) place of the bayath (house), outside of the maqadash (sanctuary).

On the shanay (second) yawam (day) you shall qarab (come close) a male iz (goat) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish for a chataah (sin) offering; and they shall chataa (cleanse) the mazabach (altar), as they chataa (cleansed) it with the par (bull).

When you have finished chataa (cleansing) it, you shall qarab (come close) a ban (son) par (bull) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish, and a ayal (ram) out of the tzaan (flock) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish.

You shall qarab (come close) them near to Yahawah, and the kahan (priest) shall shalak (cast) malach (salt) on them, and they shall ilah (go up / offer) them up for a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah.

Shabai (seven) yawam (day) you shall ishah (make) every yawam (day) a shaiyar (goat) for a chataah (sin) offering: they shall also ishah (make) a ban (son) par (bull), and a ayal (ram) out of the tzaan (flock), thamayam (complete / whole) blemish.
Shabai (seven) yawam (day) shall they make kapar (atonement) for the mazabach (altar) and purify it; so shall they malaa (consecrate) it.

When they kalah (complete / finish) accomplished the yawam (day), it shall be that on the shamayanay (eighth) yawam (day), and halaah (forward), the kahan (priest) shall ishah (make) your burnt ilah (offerings) on the mazabach (altar), and your shalam (peace) offerings; and I will ratzah (accept) you, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

Then he shawab (turn back / repent) me back by the darak (way) of the chayatzawan (outer) shair (gate) of the maqadash (sanctuary), which panah (looks) toward the qadayam (east); and it was sagar (shut).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, This shair (gate) shall be sagar (shut); it shall not be pathach (opened), neither shall any ayash (husband/individual man) bawaa (come) in by it; for Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), bawaa (come) entered in by it; therefore it shall be sagar (shut).

As for the nashayaa (prince), he shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein as nashayaa (prince) to akal (eat) lacham (bread) panayam (before) Yahawah; he shall bawaa (come) by the darak (way) of the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate), and shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out by the darak (way) of the same.

Then he bawaa (come) me by the darak (way) of the tzapawan (north) shair (gate) panayam (before) the bayath (house); and I raah (see), and behold, the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah malaa (filled) the bayath (house) of Yahawah: and I napal (fall / be cast down) on my panayam (face).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) lab (heart), and raah (see) with your iyan (eye), and shamai (hearken / hear) with your azan (ears) all that I dabar (word / matter) you concerning all the chaqah (ordinances) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and all its thawarah (instruction); and shawam (place / establish / appoint) lab (heart) the mabawaa (entrance) of the bayath (house), with every exit of the maqadash (sanctuary).

You shall amar (spoke) the rebellious, even to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: you bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), let it rab (suffice) you of all your thawaibah (abominations),

In that you bawaa (come) brought in foreigners, iral (uncircumcised) in lab (heart) and iral (uncircumcised) in bashar (flesh), to be in my maqadash (sanctuary), to chalal (profane) it, even my bayath (house), when you qarab (come close) my lacham (bread), the chalab (fat) and the dam (blood), and they have parar (broken) my barayath (covenant), to add to all your thawaibah (abominations).
You have not performed the duty of my qadash (set apart/make holy) things; but you have shawam (place / establish / appoint) performers of my duty in my maqadash (sanctuary) for yourselves.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, No foreigner, iral (uncircumcised) in lab (heart) and iral (uncircumcised) in bashar (flesh), shall bawaa (come) into my maqadash (sanctuary), of any foreigners who are thawak (midst) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel).

But the Lawayay (Levites) who rachaq (went) far from me, when Yasharaal (Israel) thaih (went) astray, who thaih (went) astray from me achar (other) their galawal (idols), they shall nashaa (lift) their iwan (guilt/iniquity).

Yet they shall be sharath (ministers) in my maqadash (sanctuary), having paqadah (oversight) at the shair (gates) of the bayath (house), and sharath (ministering) in the bayath (house): they shall shachat (kill) the burnt ilah (offering) and the zabach (sacrifice) for the im (people / nation), and they shall imad (stand) panayam (before) them to sharath (minister) to them.

Because they sharath (ministered) to them panayam (before) their galawal (idols), and became a makashawal (stumbling) block of iwan (guilt/iniquity) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel); therefore have I nashaa (lift) up my yad (hand) against them, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, and they shall nashaa (lift) their iwan (guilt/iniquity).

They shall not nagash (come) near to me, to execute the office of kahan (priest) to me, nor to nagash (come) near to any of my qadash (set apart/make holy) things, to the things that are most qadash (set apart/make holy); but they shall nashaa (lift) their kalamah (shame), and their thawaibah (abominations) which they ishah (make) committed.
Yet will I nathan (give) them performers of the duty of the bayath (house), for all its ibadah (service), and for all that shall be ishah (make) therein.

But the kahan (priest) the Lawayay (Levites), the ban (son) of Tzadawaq (Zadok), who performed the duty of my maqadash (sanctuary) when the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) thaih (went) astray from me, they shall qarab (come close) near to me to sharath (minister) to me; and they shall imad (stand) panayam (before) me to qarab (come close) to me the chalab (fat) and the dam (blood), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah:
They shall bawaa (come) into my maqadash (sanctuary), and they shall qarab (come close) near to my shalachan (table), to sharath (minister) to me, and they shall shamar (keep/guard) my instruction.

It shall be that, when they bawaa (come) in at the shair (gates) of the inner chatzar (court), they shall be labash (clothed) with pashathah (linen) bagad (garments); and no tzamar (wool) shall ilah (go up / offer) on them, while they sharath (minister) in the shair (gates) of the inner chatzar (court), and bayath (house).

They shall have pashathah (linen) paar (tires) on their raash (head), and shall have pashathah (linen) breeches on their waists; they shall not clothe themselves with anything that causes yazai (sweat).

When they yatzaa (go out / come out) forth into the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court), even into the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court) to the im (people / nation), they shall pashat (put) off their bagad (garments) in which they sharath (minister), and yanach (lay) them in the qadash (set apart/make holy) rooms; and they shall labash (put) on other bagad (garments), that they not qadash (set apart/make holy) the im (people / nation) with their bagad (garments).
Neither shall they galach (shave) their raash (head), nor allow their parai (freegrowing locks) to shalach (send) long; they shall only cut off the hair of their raash (head).
Neither shall any of the kahan (priest) shathah (drinks) yayan (wine), when they bawaa (come) into the inner chatzar (court).

Neither shall they laqach (take / seized) for their wives a alamanah (widow), nor her who is garash (put) away; but they shall laqach (take / seized) bathawalah (virgins) of the zarai (seed) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), or a alamanah (widow) who is the widow of a kahan (priest).

They shall yarah (teach) my im (people / nation) the difference between the qadash (set apart/make holy) and the chal (common), and yadai (cause) them to discern between the tamaa (unclean) and the tahawar (clean).

In a rayab (controversy) they shall imad (stand) to shapat (judge); according to my shapat (ordinances) shall they shapat (judge) it: and they shall shamar (keep/guard) my thawarah (instruction) and my chaqah (statutes) in all my mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) feasts; and they shall make my shabath (shabath/rest) qadash (set apart/make holy).

They shall bawaa (come) in to no mawath (death) adam (person) to tamaa (defile) themselves; but for ab (father), or for am (mother), or for ban (son), or for bath (daughter), for ach (brother/kinsman), or for achawath (sister) who has had no ayash (husband/individual man), they may tamaa (defile) themselves.
Achar (other) he is taharah (cleansed), they shall sapar (book) to him shabai (seven) yawam (day).

In the yawam (day) that he bawaa (come) into the qadash (set apart/make holy), into the inner chatzar (court), to sharath (minister) in the qadash (set apart/make holy), he shall qarab (come close) his chataah (sin) offering, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
They shall have an nachalah (inheritance): I am their nachalah (inheritance); and you shall nathan (give) them no achazah (possession) in Yasharaal (Israel); I am their achazah (possession).
They shall akal (eat) the meal manachah (offering), and the chataah (sin) offering, and the asham (trespass) offering; and every charam (devoted) thing in Yasharaal (Israel) shall be theirs.

The raashayath (beginning) of all the bakawar (first) fruits of every thing, and every tharawamah (offering) of everything, of all your tharawamah (offerings), shall be for the kahan (priest): you shall also nathan (give) to the kahan (priest) the raashayath (beginning) of your irayasah (dough), to cause a barakah (blessing) to nawach (rest) on your bayath (house).
The kahan (priest) shall not akal (eat) of anything that dies of nabalah (itself), or is tarapah (torn), whether it be iwap (flying) or animal.

Moreover, when you shall napal (fall / be cast down) by lot the aratz (Earth/land) for nachalah (inheritance), you shall rawam (will lift up) an tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah, a qadash (set apart/make holy) portion of the aratz (Earth/land); the arak (length) shall be the arak (length) of isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) reeds, and the rachab (breadth) shall be ishar (ten) alap (thousand): it shall be qadash (set apart/make holy) in all its gabawal (border/boundary) all around.

Of this there shall be for the qadash (set apart/make holy) place chamash (five) maah (hundred) in length by chamash (five) maah (hundred) in breadth, rabai (fourth) all around; and chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits) for its magarash (suburbs) all around.

Of this madah (measure) you shall madad (measure) a arak (length) of isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand), and a rachab (breadth) of ishar (ten) alap (thousand): and in it shall be the maqadash (sanctuary), which is most qadash (set apart/make holy).

It is a qadash (set apart/make holy) portion of the aratz (Earth/land); it shall be for the kahan (priest), the sharath (ministers) of the maqadash (sanctuary), who qarab (come) near to sharath (minister) to Yahawah; and it shall be a maqawam (place) for their bayath (house), and a maqadash (holy) place for the maqadash (sanctuary).

Isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) in arak (length), and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) in rachab (breadth), shall be to the Lawayay (Levites), the sharath (ministers) of the bayath (house), for a achazah (possession) to themselves, for isharayam (twenty) rooms.

You shall nathan (give) the achazah (possession) of the iyar (city) chamash (five) alap (thousand) rachab (broad), and isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) arak (length), side by side with the tharawamah (offering) of the qadash (set apart/make holy) portion: it shall be for the whole bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Whatever is for the nashayaa (prince) shall be on the one side and on the other side of the qadash (set apart/make holy) tharawamah (offering) and of the achazah (possession) of the iyar (city), in panayam (front) of the qadash (set apart/make holy) tharawamah (offering) and in panayam (front) of the achazah (possession) of the iyar (city), on the yam (sea/waters) paah (side) westward, and on the qadam (east) paah (side) eastward; and in arak (length) answerable to achad (one) of the chalaq (portions), from the yam (sea/waters) gabawal (border/boundary) to the qadayam (east) gabawal (border/boundary).

In the aratz (Earth/land) it shall be to him for a achazah (possession) in Yasharaal (Israel): and my nashayaa (princes) shall no more yanah (oppress) my im (people / nation); but they shall nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) according to their shabat (tribes).

Thus naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah: Let it rab (suffice) you, nashayaa (princes) of Yasharaal (Israel): sawar (remove) chamas (violence) and shad (spoil), and ishah (make) mashapat (justice) and tzadaqah (righteousness); dispossessing my im (people / nation), amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah.
You shall have tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) maazan (balances), and a tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) ayapah (ephah), and a tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) bath (daughter).

The ayapah (ephah) and the bath (daughter) shall be of achad (one) thakan (measure), that the bath (daughter) may nashaa (lift) the maishar (tenth) part of a chamar (homer), and the ayapah (ephah) the ishayaray (tenth) part of a chamar (homer): its mathakanath (measure) shall be after the chamar (homer).

The shaqal (shekel) shall be isharayam (twenty) garah (gerahs). Isharayam (twenty) shaqal (shekels) plus isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) shaqal (shekels) plus chamash (fifteen) shaqal (shekels) shall be your mina.

This is the tharawamah (offering) that you shall rawam (will lift up): the shashay (sixth) part of an ayapah (ephah) from a chamar (homer) of chatah (wheat); and you shall give the shashah (sixth) part of an ayapah (ephah) from a chamar (homer) of shairah (barley);

And the chaq (statute) portion of shaman (oil), of the bath (daughter) of shaman (oil), the maishar (tenth) part of a bath (daughter) out of the kar (cor), which is ishar (ten) bath (daughter), even a chamar (homer); (for ishar (ten) bath (daughter) are a chamar (homer);)

And achad (one) shah (lamb) of the tzaan (flock), out of two maah (hundred), from the well-watered mashaqah (pastures) Yasharaal (of) Israel—for a meal manachah (offering), and for a burnt ilah (offering), and for shalam (peace) offerings, to make kapar (atonement) for them, naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
All the im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land) shall give to this tharawamah (offering) for the nashayaa (prince) in Yasharaal (Israel).

It shall be the nashayaa (prince's) part to give the burnt ilah (offerings), and the meal manachah (offerings), and the drink nasak (offerings), in the chag (feast/festival), and on the new chadash (month), and on the shabath (shabath/rest), in all the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) feasts of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel): he shall ishah (make) the sin manachah (offering), and the meal ilah (offering), and the burnt ilah (offering), and the shalam (peace) offerings, to make kapar (atonement) for the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: In the raashawan (first) month, in the achad (one) day of the chadash (month), you shall laqach (take / seized) a ban (son) par (bull) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish; and you shall chataa (cleanse) the maqadash (sanctuary).

The kahan (priest) shall laqach (take / seized) of the dam (blood) of the chataah (sin) offering, and nathan (give) it on the mazawazah (door) posts of the bayath (house), and on the arabai (four) panah (corners) of the ledge of the mazabach (altar), and on the mazawazah (posts) of the shair (gate) of the inner chatzar (court).

So you shall ishah (make) on the shabai (seven) day of the chadash (month) for everyone who shagah (errs), and for him who is pathay (simple): so you shall make kapar (atonement) for the bayath (house).

In the raashawan (first) month, in the fourteenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month), you shall have the pasach (passover), a chag (feast/festival) of shabawai (seven) yawam (day); unleavened matzah (bread) shall be akal (eat).
On that yawam (day) shall the nashayaa (prince) ishah (make) for himself and for all the im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land) a par (bull) for a chataah (sin) offering.

The shabai (seven) yawam (day) of the chag (feast/festival) he shall ishah (make) a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah, shabai (seven) par (bulls) and shabai (seven) ayal (rams) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish yawam (day) the shabai (seven) yawam (day); and a male shaiyar (goat) yawam (day) for a chataah (sin) offering.
He shall ishah (make) a meal manachah (offering), an ayapah (ephah) for a par (bull), and an ayapah (ephah) for a ayal (ram), and a hayan (hin) of shaman (oil) to an ayapah (ephah).

In the shabai (seven) month, in the fifteenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month), in the chag (feast/festival), shall he ishah (make) the like the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day); according to the chataah (sin) offering, according to the burnt ilah (offering), and according to the meal manachah (offering), and according to the shaman (oil).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: The shair (gate) of the inner chatzar (court) that panah (looks) toward the qadayam (east) shall be sagar (shut) the shash (six) maishah (working) yawam (day); but on the shabath (shabath/rest) day it shall be pathach (opened), and on the yawam (day) of the new chadash (month) it shall be pathach (opened).

The nashayaa (prince) shall bawaa (come) by the darak (way) of the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate) outside, and shall imad (stand) by the mazawazah (post) of the shair (gate); and the kahan (priest) shall ishah (make) his burnt ilah (offering) and his shalam (peace) offerings, and he shall shachah (worship) at the mapathan (threshold) of the shair (gate): then he shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth; but the shair (gate) shall not be sagar (shut) until the irab (evening).

The im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land) shall shachah (worship) at the pathach (door) of that shair (gate) panayam (before) Yahawah on the shabath (shabath/rest) and on the new chadash (month).

The burnt ilah (offering) that the nashayaa (prince) shall qarab (come close) to Yahawah shall be on the shabath (shabath/rest) yawam (day) shash (six) kabash (lambs) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish and a ayal (ram) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish;

And the meal manachah (offering) shall be an ayapah (ephah) for the ayal (ram), and the meal manachah (offering) for the kabash (lambs) as he is yad (hand) to give, and a hayan (hin) of shaman (oil) to an ayapah (ephah).

On the yawam (day) of the new chadash (month) it shall be a ban (son) par (bull) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish, and shash (six) kabash (lambs), and a ayal (ram); they shall be thamayam (complete / whole) blemish:

And he shall ishah (make) a meal manachah (offering), an ayapah (ephah) for the par (bull), and an ayapah (ephah) for the ayal (ram), and for the kabash (lambs) according as he is nashag (able), and a hayan (hin) of shaman (oil) to an ayapah (ephah).
When the nashayaa (prince) shall bawaa (come), he shall bawaa (come) in by the darak (way) of the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate), and he shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth by its darak (way).

But when the im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land) shall bawaa (come) panayam (before) Yahawah in the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) feasts, he who bawaa (come) by the darak (way) of the tzapawan (north) shair (gate) to shachah (worship) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth by the darak (way) of the nagab (south) shair (gate); and he who bawaa (come) by the darak (way) of the nagab (south) shair (gate) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth by the darak (way) of the tzapawan (north) shair (gate): he shall not shawab (turn back / repent) by the darak (way) of the shair (gate) by which he bawaa (come) in, but shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth straight nakach (before) him.
The nashayaa (prince), when they bawaa (come) in, shall bawaa (come) in with of them; and when they yatzaa (go out / come out) out, he shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out.

In the chag (feast/festival) and in the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) the meal manachah (offering) shall be an ayapah (ephah) for a par (bull), and an ayapah (ephah) for a ayal (ram), and for the kabash (lambs) as he is yad (hand) to give, and a hayan (hin) of shaman (oil) to an ayapah (ephah).

When the nashayaa (prince) shall ishah (make) a nadabah (voluntary / freewill offering) ilah (offering), a burnt ilah (offering) or shalam (peace) offerings as a freewill nadabah (voluntary / freewill offering) to Yahawah, one shall pathach (open) for him the shair (gate) that panah (looks) toward the qadayam (east); and he shall ishah (make) his burnt ilah (offering) and his shalam (peace) offerings, as he does on the shabath (shabath/rest) yawam (day): then he shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth; and achar (other) his yatzaa (go out / come out) forth one shall sagar (shut) the shair (gate).

You shall ishah (make) a kabash (lamb) a shanah (year) old thamayam (complete / whole) blemish for a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah yawam (day): baqar (morning) by baqar (morning) you shall ishah (make) it.

You shall ishah (make) a meal manachah (offering) with it baqar (morning) by baqar (morning), the shashay (sixth) part of an ayapah (ephah), and the shalayashay (third) part of a hayan (hin) of shaman (oil), to moisten the fine salath (flour); a meal manachah (offering) to Yahawah continually by a iwalam (forever) chaqah (ordinance).
Thus shall they ishah (make) the kabash (lamb), and the meal manachah (offering), and the shaman (oil), baqar (morning) by morning, for a thamayad (continual) burnt ilah (offering).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: If the nashayaa (prince) nathan (give) a mathanah (gift) to any of his ban (son), it is his nachalah (inheritance), it shall belong to his ban (son); it is their achazah (possession) by nachalah (inheritance).

But if he nathan (give) of his nachalah (inheritance) a mathanah (gift) to achad (one) of his ibad (servant), it shall be his to the shanah (year) of darawar (liberty); then it shall shawab (turn back / repent) to the nashayaa (prince); but as for his nachalah (inheritance), it shall be for his ban (son).

Moreover the nashayaa (prince) shall not laqach (take / seized) of the im (people / nation) nachalah (inheritance), to thrust them out of their achazah (possession); he shall give nachal (inheritance) to his ban (son) out of his own achazah (possession), that my im (people / nation) not be pawatz (scattered) every ayash (husband/individual man) from his achazah (possession).

Then he bawaa (come) me through the mabawaa (entry), which was at the kathap (side) of the shair (gate), into the qadash (set apart/make holy) rooms for the kahan (priest), which panah (looked) toward the tzapawan (north): and behold, there was a maqawam (place) on the hinder yarakah (part) westward.

He amar (spoke) to me, This is the maqawam (place) where the kahan (priest) shall bashal (boil) the asham (trespass) offering and the chataah (sin) offering, and where they shall apah (bake) the meal manachah (offering); that they not yatzaa (go out / come out) them forth into the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court), to qadash (set apart/make holy) the im (people / nation).

Then he yatzaa (go out / come out) me forth into the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court), and ibar (pass over/through) me to pass by the arabai (four) maqatzawai (corners) of the chatzar (court); and behold, in every maqatzawai (corner) of the chatzar (court) there was a chatzar (court).

In the arabai (four) maqatzawai (corners) of the chatzar (court) there were chatzar (courts) enclosed, arabaiyam (forty) cubits arak (length) and shalawashayam (thirty) rachab (broad): these arabai (four) in the qatzai (corners) were of achad (one) madah (measure).
There was a wall around in them, around the arabai (four), and mabashalah (boiling) places were ishah (make) under the walls all around.
Then he amar (spoke) to me, These are the bashal (boiling) bayath (house), where the sharath (ministers) of the bayath (house) shall bashal (boil) the zabach (sacrifice) of the im (people / nation).

He shawab (turn back / repent) me back to the pathach (door) of the bayath (house); and behold, mayam (Waters) yatzaa (go out / come out) out from under the mapathan (threshold) of the bayath (house) eastward; (for the panayam (forefront) of the bayath (house) was toward the qadayam (east);) and the mayam (Waters) yarad (came) down from under, from the yamanay (right) kathap (side) of the bayath (house), on the nagab (south) of the mazabach (altar).

Then he yatzaa (go out / come out) me out by the darak (way) of the shair (gate) northward, and led me round by the darak (way) outside to the outer shair (gate), by the darak (way) of the shair (gate) that panah (looks) toward the qadayam (east); and behold, there pakah (ran) out mayam (Waters) on the yamanay (right) kathap (side).

When the ayash (husband/individual man) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth eastward with the qaw (line) in his yad (hand), he madad (measured) one alap (thousand) amah (cubits), and he ibar (pass over/through) me to pass through the mayam (Waters), mayam (Waters) that were to the apas (ankles).

Again he madad (measured) one alap (thousand), and ibar (pass over/through) me to pass through the mayam (Waters), mayam (Waters) that were to the barak (knees). Again he madad (measured) one alap (thousand), and ibar (pass over/through) me to pass through the mayam (Waters), mathan (waters) that were to the waist.

Afterward he madad (measured) one alap (thousand); and it was a nachal (stream / river) that I yakal (could) not ibar (pass over/through) through; for the mayam (Waters) were gaah (risen), mayam (Waters) to shachaw (swim) in, a nachal (stream / river) that could not be ibar (pass over/through) through.
He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), raah (see) you seen this? Then he yalak (brought) me, and caused me to shawab (turn back / repent) to the shapah (bank) of the nachal (stream / river).
Now when I had shawab (turn back / repent), behold, on the shapah (bank) of the nachal (stream / river) were very many itz (trees) on the one side and on the other.

Then he amar (spoke) to me, These mayam (Waters) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth toward the eastern region, and shall bawaa (come) down into the irabah (arabah); and they shall go toward the yam (sea/waters); into the yam (sea/waters) shall the waters yatzaa (go out / come out) which were made to issue forth; and the mayam (Waters) shall be rapaa (healed).

It shall happen, that every living napash (living being/soul) which swarms, in every place where the nachal (stream / river) bawaa (come), shall chayah (live); and there shall be a very rab (great) multitude of dagah (fish); for these mayam (Waters) bawaa (come) come there, and the waters of the sea shall be rapaa (healed), and everything shall chayay (life) wherever the nachal (stream / river) bawaa (come).

It shall happen, that fishermen shall imad (stand) by it: from Iyanagaday (En) Gedi even to Iyanaigalayam (En) Eglaim shall be a place for the mashatawach (spreading) of charam (nets); their dagah (fish) shall be after their mayan (species), as the dagah (fish) of the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) yam (sea/waters), maad (exceeding) many.
But the miry places of it, and its marshes, shall not be rapaa (healed); they shall be nathan (give) up to malach (salt).

By the nachal (stream / river) on its shapah (bank), on this side and on that side, shall ilah (go up / offer) every itz (tree) for maakal (food), whose ilah (leaf) shall not nabal (wither), neither shall its paray (fruit) thamam (fail): it shall bakar (bring) forth new fruit every chadash (month), because its mayam (Waters) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the maqadash (sanctuary); and its paray (fruit) shall be for maakal (food), and its ilah (leaf) for healing.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: gah (this) shall be the gabawal (border/boundary), by which you shall divide the aratz (Earth/land) for nachal (inheritance) according to the shanayam (two) shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel): Yawasap (Joseph) shall have two chabal (portions).

You shall nachal (inherit) it, ayash (husband/individual man) as well as ach (brother/kinsman); for I yad (hand) to nathan (give) it to your ab (father): and this aratz (Earth/land) shall napal (fall / be cast down) to you for nachalah (inheritance).

This shall be the gabawal (border/boundary) of the aratz (Earth/land): On the tzapawan (north) paah (side), from the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) yam (sea/waters), by the darak (way) of Chathalan (Hethlon), to the entrance of Tzadad (Zedad);

Chamath (Hamath), Barawathah (Berothah), Sabarayam (Sibraim), which is between the gabawal (border/boundary) of Damashaq (Damascus) and the gabawal (border/boundary) of Chamath (Hamath); Hazer Chatzarahathayakawan (Hatticon), which is by the gabawal (border/boundary) of Chawaran (Hauran).

The gabawal (border/boundary) from the yam (sea/waters), shall be Chatzaraiyanawan (Hazar) Enon at the gabawal (border/boundary) of Damashaq (Damascus); and on the tzapawan (north) northward is the gabawal (border/boundary) of Chamath (Hamath). This is the tzapawan (north) paah (side).

The qadayam (east) paah (side), bayan (between) Chawaran (Hauran) and Damashaq (Damascus) and Galaid (Gilead), and the aratz (Earth/land) of Yasharaal (Israel), shall be the Yaradan (Jordan); from the north gabawal (border/boundary) to the qadamawanay (east) yam (sea/waters) you shall madad (measure). This is the qadayam (east) paah (side).

The nagab (south) paah (side) southward shall be from Thamar (Tamar) as far as the mayam (Waters) of Meriboth Qadash (Kadesh), to the nachal (stream / river) of Egypt, to the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) yam (sea/waters). This is the thayaman (south) paah (side) southward.

The yam (sea/waters) paah (side) shall be the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) yam (sea/waters), from the south gabawal (border/boundary) as far as over nakach (against) the entrance of Chamath (Hamath). This is the yam (sea/waters) paah (side).
So you shall chalaq (divide) this aratz (Earth/land) to you according to the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel).

It shall happen, that you shall napal (fall / be cast down) it by lot for an nachalah (inheritance) to you and to the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who live thawak (midst) you, who shall yalad (birth / begot) ban (son) thawak (midst) you; and they shall be to you as the native - azarach (born) among the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel); they shall napal (fall / be cast down) nachalah (inheritance) with you thawak (midst) the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel).

It shall happen, that in what shabat (tribe) the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) lives, there you shall nathan (give) him his nachalah (inheritance), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

Now these are the sham (name) of the shabat (tribes): From the tzapawan (north) qatzah (end / extremity / border), yad (hand) the darak (way) of Chathalan (Hethlon) to the entrance of Chamath (Hamath), Chatzaraiyanan (Hazar) Enan at the gabawal (border/boundary) of Damashaq (Damascus), northward yad (hand) Chamath (Hamath), (and they shall have their paah (sides) qadayam (east) and yam (sea/waters)), Dan (Dan), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) Dan (of) Dan, from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Ashar (Asher), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Ashar (Asher), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) even to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Napathalay (Naphtali), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Napathalay (Naphtali), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Manashah (Manasseh), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Manashah (Manasseh), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Aparayam (Ephraim), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Aparayam (Ephraim), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) even to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Raawaban (Reuben), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Raawaban (Reuben), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Yahawadah (Judah), achad (one) portion.

By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yahawadah (Judah), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), shall be the tharawamah (offering) which you shall rawam (will lift up), twenty - five alap (thousand) reeds in rachab (breadth), and in arak (length) as achad (one) of the chalaq (portions), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side): and the maqadash (sanctuary) shall be in its thawak (midst).

The tharawamah (offering) that you shall rawam (will lift up) to Yahawah shall be isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) reeds in arak (length), and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) in rachab (breadth).

For these, even for the kahan (priest), shall be the qadash (set apart/make holy) tharawamah (offering): toward the tzapawan (north) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) in length, and toward the yam (sea/waters) ishar (ten) alap (thousand) in rachab (breadth), and toward the qadayam (east) ishar (ten) alap (thousand) in rachab (breadth), and toward the nagab (south) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) in arak (length): and the maqadash (sanctuary) of Yahawah shall be in its thawak (midst).

It shall be for the kahan (priest) who are qadash (set apart/make holy) of the ban (son) of Tzadawaq (Zadok), who have shamar (keep/guard) my instruction, who didn't thaih (go) astray when the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) thaih (went) astray, as the Lawayay (Levites) thaih (went) astray.

It shall be to them an tharawamayah (offering) from the tharawamah (offering) of the aratz (Earth/land), a thing most qadash (set apart/make holy), by the gabawal (border/boundary) of the Lawayay (Levites).

Answerable to the gabawal (border/boundary) of the kahan (priest), the Lawayay (Levites) shall have isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) in arak (length), and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) in rachab (breadth): all the arak (length) shall be isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand), and the rachab (breadth) ishar (ten) alap (thousand).

They shall makar (sell) none of it, nor mawar (exchange) it, nor shall the raashayath (beginning) fruits of the aratz (Earth/land) be ibar (pass over/through); for it is qadash (set apart/make holy) to Yahawah.

The chamash (five) alap (thousand) that are yathar (left) in the rachab (breadth), in panayam (front) of the isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand), shall be for chal (common) use, for the iyar (city), for mawashab (dwelling) and for magarash (suburbs); and the iyar (city) shall be in its thawak (midst).

These shall be its madah (measures): the tzapawan (north) paah (side) arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred), and the nagab (south) paah (side) arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred), and on the qadayam (east) paah (side) arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred), and the yam (sea/waters) paah (side) arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred).

The iyar (city) shall have magarash (suburbs): toward the tzapawan (north) two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty), and toward the nagab (south) two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty), and toward the qadayam (east) two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty), and toward the yam (sea/waters) two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty).

The remainder in the arak (length), answerable to the qadash (set apart/make holy) tharawamah (offering), shall be ishar (ten) alap (thousand) eastward, and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) westward; and it shall be answerable to the qadash (set apart/make holy) tharawamah (offering); and its thabawaah (increase) shall be for lacham (food) to those who ibad (servant) in the iyar (city).
Those who ibad (servant) in the iyar (city), out of all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), shall cultivate it.

All the tharawamah (offering) shall be isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) by isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand): you shall rawam (will lift up) the qadash (set apart/make holy) tharawamah (offering) rabayaiy (foursquare), with the achazah (possession) of the iyar (city).

The yathar (residue) shall be for the nashayaa (prince), on the one side and on the other of the qadash (set apart/make holy) tharawamah (offering) and of the achazah (possession) of the iyar (city); in panayam (front) of the isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) of the tharawamah (offering) toward the qadayam (east) gabawal (border/boundary), and westward in panayam (front) of the isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) toward the yam (sea/waters) gabawal (border/boundary), answerable to the chalaq (portions), it shall be for the nashayaa (prince): and the qadash (set apart/make holy) tharawamah (offering) and the maqadash (sanctuary) of the bayath (house) shall be in its thawak (midst).

Moreover from the achazah (possession) of the Lawayay (Levites), and from the achazah (possession) of the iyar (city), being in the thawak (midst) of that which is the nashayaa (prince's), between the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yahawadah (Judah) and the gabawal (border/boundary) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), it shall be for the nashayaa (prince).
As for the yathar (rest) of the shabat (tribes): from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Banayamayan (Benjamin), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Shamaiwan (Simeon), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Shamaiwan (Simeon), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Yashashakar (Issachar), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yashashakar (Issachar), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Zabawalawan (Zebulun), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Zabawalawan (Zebulun), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Gad (Gad), achad (one) portion.

By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Gad (Gad), at the nagab (south) paah (side) southward, the gabawal (border/boundary) shall be even from Thamar (Tamar) to the mayam (Waters) of Meribath Qadash (Kadesh), to the nachal (stream / river) of Egypt, to the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) yam (sea/waters).

This is the aratz (Earth/land) which you shall napal (fall / be cast down) by lot to the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) for nachalah (inheritance), and these are their several machalaqath (portions), naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.
These are the exits of the iyar (city): On the tzapawan (north) paah (side) arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred) reeds by madah (measure);

And the shair (gates) of the iyar (city) shall be after the sham (name) of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), shalawash (three) shair (gates) northward: the shair (gate) of Raawaban (Reuben), achad (one); the shair (gate) of Yahawadah (Judah), achad (one); the shair (gate) of Laway (Levi), achad (one).

At the qadayam (east) paah (side) arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred) reeds, and shalawash (three) shair (gates): even the shair (gate) of Yawasap (Joseph), achad (one); the shair (gate) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), achad (one); the shair (gate) Dan (of) Dan, achad (one).

At the nagab (south) paah (side) arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred) reeds by madah (measure), and shalawash (three) shair (gates): the shair (gate) of Shamaiwan (Simeon), achad (one); the shair (gate) of Yashashakar (Issachar), achad (one); the shair (gate) of Zabawalawan (Zebulun), achad (one).

At the yam (sea/waters) paah (side) arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred) reeds, with their shalawash (three) shair (gates): the shair (gate) of Gad (Gad), achad (one); the shair (gate) of Ashar (Asher), achad (one); the shair (gate) of Napathalay (Naphtali), achad (one).
It shall be eighteen alap (thousand) reeds around: and the sham (name) of the iyar (city) from that yawam (day) shall be, Yahawah is there.

In the shalawash (three) shanah (year) of the malakawath (reign) of Yahawayaqayam (Jehoiakim) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) bawaa (come) Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and tzawar (besieged) it.

The Adanay nathan (give) Yahawayaqayam (Jehoiakim) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) into his yad (hand), with qatzath (part) of the kalay (vessels) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam; and he bawaa (come) them into the aratz (Earth/land) of Shanair (Shinar) to the bayath (house) of his Alahayam: and he bawaa (come) the kalay (vessels) into the awatzar (treasure) bayath (house) of his Alahayam.

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Ashapanaz (Ashpenaz) the rab (master) of his sarayas (eunuchs), that he should bawaa (come) in certain of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), even of the zarai (seed) malawakah (royal) and of the paratham (nobles);

Youths in whom was no maawam (blemish), but tawab (pleasant/functional) - favored, and shakal (skillful) in all chakamah (wisdom), and endowed with daith (knowledge), and bayan (between) madai (science), and such as had kach (strength / mighty / power) to imad (stand) in the malak (king) hayakal (palace); and that he should lamad (teach/instruct) them the sapar (book / scribed document) and the lashawan (tongue/language) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans).

The malak (king) manah (appointed) for them a yawam (day) dabar (word / matter) of the malak (king) dainties, and of the yayan (wine) which he mashathah (drank), and that they should be gadal (nourished) shalawash (three) shanah (years); that at its qatzath (end) they should imad (stand) panayam (before) the malak (king).
Now among these were, of the ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah), Danayaal (Daniel), Chananayah (Hananiah), Mayashaal (Mishael), and Izarayah (Azariah).

The shar (prince / ruler) of the sarayas (eunuchs) shawam (place / establish / appoint) sham (name) to them: to Danayaal (Daniel) he shawam (place / establish / appoint) the name of Balatashaatzar (Belteshazzar); and to Chananayah (Hananiah), of Shadarak (Shadrach); and to Mayashaal (Mishael), Mayashak (of) Meshach; and to Izarayah (Azariah), of Ibadanagaw (Abednego).

But Danayaal (Daniel) shawam (place / establish / appoint) in his lab (heart) that he would not gaal (defile) himself with the malak (king) dainties, nor with the yayan (wine) which he mashathah (drank): therefore he baqash (requested) of the shar (prince / ruler) of the sarayas (eunuchs) that he might not gaal (defile) himself.
Now Alahayam nathan (give) Danayaal (Daniel) to find chasad (grace) and racham (compassion) in the panayam (sight) of the shar (prince / ruler) of the sarayas (eunuchs).

The shar (prince / ruler) of the sarayas (eunuchs) amar (spoke) to Danayaal (Daniel), I yaraa (fear) my Adawan the malak (king), who has manah (appointed) your maakal (food) and your mashathah (drink): for why should he raah (see) your panayam (faces) worse raah (see) than the youths who are of your own age? So would you chawab (endanger) my raash (head) with the malak (king).

Then Danayaal (Daniel) amar (spoke) to the steward whom the shar (prince / ruler) of the sarayas (eunuchs) had manah (appointed) over Danayaal (Daniel), Chananayah (Hananiah), Mayashaal (Mishael), and Izarayah (Azariah):
Test your ibad (servant), I beg you, ishar (ten) yawam (day); and nathan (give) them give us vegetables to akal (eat), and mayam (Waters) to shathah (drinks).

Then let our maraah (faces) be raah (see) on panayam (before) you, and the maraah (face) of the youths who akal (eat) of the malak (king) dainties; and as you raah (see), ishah (make) with your ibad (servant).
So he shamai (hearken / hear) to them in this dabar (word / matter), and nasah (proved) them ishar (ten) yawam (day).
At the qatzath (end) of ishar (ten) yawam (day) their maraah (faces) raah (see) fairer, and they were fatter in bashar (flesh), than all the youths who akal (eat) of the malak (king) dainties.
So the steward nashaa (lift) away their dainties, and the yayan (wine) that they should mashathah (drink), and nathan (give) them zarai (pulse).

Now as for these arabai (four) youths, Alahayam nathan (give) them madai (knowledge) and shakal (skill) in all sapar (book / scribed document) and chakamah (wisdom): and Danayaal (Daniel) had bayan (between) in all chazawan (vision) and chalawam (dreams).

At the qatzath (end) of the yawam (day) which the malak (king) had amar (spoke) for bawaa (come) them in, the shar (prince / ruler) of the sarayas (eunuchs) bawaa (come) them in panayam (before) Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar).

The malak (king) dabar (word / matter) with them; and among them all was matzaa (found) none like Danayaal (Daniel), Chananayah (Hananiah), Mayashaal (Mishael), and Izarayah (Azariah): therefore imad (stood) they panayam (before) the malak (king).

In every dabar (word / matter) of chakamah (wisdom) and bayanah (understanding), concerning which the malak (king) inquired of them, he matzaa (found) them ishar (ten) times better than all the charatam (magicians) and enchanters who were in all his malakawath (realm).
Danayaal (Daniel) continued even to the achad (one) shanah (year) of malak (king) Kawarash (Cyrus).

In the shanayam (two) shanah (year) of the malakawath (reign) of Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar), Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) chalam (dream) chalawam (dreams); and his rawach (spirit / wind) was paim (troubled), and his shanah (sleep) went from him.

Then the malak (king) commanded to qaraa (called) the charatam (magicians), and the enchanters, and the kashap (sorcerers), and the Kashaday (Chaldeans), to nagad (tell) the malak (king) his chalawam (dreams). So they bawaa (come) in and imad (stood) panayam (before) the malak (king).
The malak (king) amar (spoke) to them, I have chalam (dream) a chalawam (dream), and my rawach (spirit / wind) is paim (troubled) to yadai (know) the chalawam (dream).

Then dabar (word / matter) the Kashaday (Chaldeans) to the malak (king) in the Aramayath (Syrian) language, O malak (king), chayaa (live) ilam (forever): amar (spoke) your ibad (servant) the dream, and we will show the pashar (interpretation).

The malak (king) inah (oppress / afflict) the Kashaday (Chaldeans), The thing is azad (gone) from me: if you don't yadai (make) known to me the dream and its pashar (interpretation), you shall be ibad (servant) in hadam (pieces), and your bayath (house) shall be shawam (place / establish / appoint) a nawalaw (dunghill).

But if you show the dream and its pashar (interpretation), you shall qabal (receive) of me mathanaa (gifts) and nabazabah (rewards) and shagayaa (great) honor: therefore show me the dream and its pashar (interpretation).
They inah (oppress / afflict) the thanayanawath (second) time and amar (spoke), Let the malak (king) amar (spoke) his ibad (servant) the dream, and we will show the pashar (interpretation).
The malak (king) inah (oppress / afflict), I yadai (know) of a yatzayab (certainty) that you would zaban (gain) idan (Idan/Eden), qabal (because) you chazaa (see) the thing is azad (gone) from me.

But if you don't yadai (make) known to me the dream, there is but hawaa (which/who/that is) dath (law) for you; for you have zaman (prepared) kadab (lying) and shachath (corrupt) malah (words) to amar (spoke) qadam (before) me, id (until) the idan (Idan/Eden) be shanaa (hate): day (therefore) amar (spoke) me the dream, and I shall yadai (know) that you can show me its pashar (interpretation).

The Kashaday (Chaldeans) inah (oppress / afflict) qadam (before) the malak (king), and amar (spoke), There is not a anash (man) on the yabashath (earth) who yakal (can) show the malak (king) malah (matter), qabal (because) no malak (king), Adawan, or shalayat (ruler), has shaal (asked) such a thing of any charatam (magician), or enchanter, or Kashaday (Chaldean).

It is a yaqayar (rare) thing that the malak (king) shaal (requires), and there is no other who can show it qadam (before) the malak (king), lahan (except) the Alahayam, whose madawar (dwelling) is not with bashar (flesh).
For dan (this) kal (every) the malak (king) was banas (angry) and very qatzap (furious), and commanded to abad (destroy/perish) kal (every) the chakayam (wise) men of Babal (Babylon).
So the dath (decree) napaq (went) forth, and the chakayam (wise) men were to be qatal (slain); and they baia (sought) Danayaal (Daniel) and his chabar (companions) to be qatal (slain).

Then Danayaal (Daniel) thawab (returned) answer with itaa (counsel) and prudence to Arayawak (Arioch) the rab (captain) of the malak (king) tabach (guard), who was napaq (gone) forth to kill the chakayam (wise) men of Babal (Babylon);

He inah (oppress / afflict) Arayawak (Arioch) the malak (king) shalayat (captain), mah (why) is the dath (decree) so chatzap (urgent) from the malak (king)? Then Arayawak (Arioch) made the thing yadai (known) to Danayaal (Daniel).
Danayaal (Daniel) ilal (went) in, and baia (desired) of the malak (king) that he would appoint him a zaman (time), and he would show the malak (king) the pashar (interpretation).
Then Danayaal (Daniel) azal (went) to his bayath (house), and made the thing yadai (known) to Chananayah (Hananiah), Mayashaal (Mishael), and Izarayah (Azariah), his chabar (companions):

That they would baia (desire) racham (mercies) of the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven) il (over) dan (this) raz (secret); that Danayaal (Daniel) and his chabar (companions) should not abad (destroy/perish) with the shaar (rest) of the chakayam (wise) men of Babal (Babylon).
Then was the raz (secret) galah (revealed) to Danayaal (Daniel) in a chazaw (vision) of the layalayaa (night). Then Danayaal (Daniel) barak (blessed) the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven).
Danayaal (Daniel) inah (oppress / afflict), barak (blessed) be the sham (name) of Alahayam id (forever) and ilam (ever); for chakamah (wisdom) and gabawarah (might) are his.

He shanaa (hate) the idan (Idan/Eden) and the zaman (seasons); he idaa (removes) malak (king), and qawam (rise up) up malak (king); he yahab (gives) chakamah (wisdom) to the chakayam (wise), and manadai (knowledge) to those who have bayanah (understanding);
He galah (reveals) the imayaq (deep) and sathar (secret) things; he yadai (knows) mah (what) is in the chashawak (darkness), and the nahayar (light) sharaa (dwells) with him.

I yadaa (thank) you, and shabach (praise) you, you Alahayam of my ab (father), who have yahab (given) me chakamah (wisdom) and gabawarah (might), and have kain (now) yadai (made) known to me what we baia (desired) of you; for you have yadai (made) known to us the malak (king) malah (matter).

Qabal (therefore) Danayaal (Daniel) ilal (went) in to Arayawak (Arioch), whom the malak (king) had appointed to abad (destroy/perish) the chakayam (wise) men of Babal (Babylon); he azal (went) and amar (spoke) kan (for sure) to him: Don't abad (destroy/perish) the chakayam (wise) men of Babal (Babylon); ilal (bring) me in qadam (before) the malak (king), and I will show to the malak (king) the pashar (interpretation).

Then Arayawak (Arioch) ilal (brought) in Danayaal (Daniel) qadam (before) the malak (king) in bahal (haste), and amar (spoke) kan (for sure) to him, I have shakach (found) a gabar (man) of the ban (son) of the captivity of Yahawad (Judah), who will yadai (make) known to the malak (king) the pashar (interpretation).

The malak (king) inah (oppress / afflict) Danayaal (Daniel), whose sham (name) was Balatashaatzar (Belteshazzar), Are you kahal (able) to yadai (make) known to me the dream which I chazaa (have) seen, and its pashar (interpretation)?

Danayaal (Daniel) inah (oppress / afflict) qadam (before) the malak (king), and amar (spoke), The raz (secret) which the malak (king) has shaal (demanded) yakal (can) neither chakayam (wise) men, enchanters, charatam (magicians), nor gazar (soothsayers), show to the malak (king);

But there is a Alahayam in shamayan (heaven) who galah (reveals) raz (secrets), and he has yadai (made) known to the malak (king) Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) mah (what) shall be in the acharayath (latter) yawam (day). Your dream, and the chazaw (visions) of your raash (head) on your mashakab (bed), are these:

As for you, O malak (king), your raiyawan (thoughts) salaq (came) into your il (over) on your mashakab (bed), mah (what) should happen achar (other); and he who galah (reveals) raz (secrets) has yadai (made) known to you mah (what) shall happen.

But as for me, dan (this) raz (secret) is not galah (revealed) to me for any chakamah (wisdom) that I ayathay (have) more man (from) any chay (life), but to the intent that the pashar (interpretation) may be yadai (made) known to the malak (king), and that you may yadai (know) the raiyawan (thoughts) of your labab (heart).

You, O malak (king), hawaa (which/who/that is), and alaw (behold), a great tzalam (likeness). Dakan (this) tzalam (likeness), which was rab (mighty), and whose zayaw (brightness) was yathayar (excellent), qawam (rise up) qabal (before) you; and its aspect was awesome.

As for this tzalam (likeness), its raash (head) was of tab (fine) dahab (gold), its chaday (breast) and its darai (arms) of kasap (silver), its maih (belly) and its yarakaa (thighs) of nachash (brass),
Its shaq (legs) of parazal (iron), its ragal (feet) man (from) of parazal (iron), and man (from) of chasap (clay).

You chazaa (saw) id (until) a aban (stone) was gazar (cut) out laa (NOT) yad (hand), which struck the tzalam (likeness) on its ragal (feet) that were of parazal (iron) and chasap (clay), and daqaq (broke) them in daqaq (pieces).

Then was the parazal (iron), the chasap (clay), the nachash (brass), the kasap (silver), and the dahab (gold), daqaq (broken) in pieces chad (together), and hawaa (which/who/that is) like the iwar (chaff) of the qayat (summer) threshing floors; and the rawach (spirit / wind) nashaa (lift) them nashaa (lift), so that no athar (place) was shakach (found) for them: and the aban (stone) that struck the tzalam (likeness) hawaa (which/who/that is) a rab (great) tawar (mountain), and malaa (filled) the kal (every) arai (earth).
Dan (this) is the dream; and we will amar (spoke) its pashar (interpretation) qadam (before) the malak (king).
You, O malak (king), are malak (king) of malak (king), to whom the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven) has yahab (given) the malakaw (kingdom), the chasan (power), and the thaqap (strength), and the glory;

And wherever the ban (son) of anash (men) dawar (dwell), the animals of the bar (field) and the birds of the sky has he yahab (given) into your yad (hand), and shalat (has) made you to rule over them kal (every): you are the raash (head) of dahab (gold).

Athar (after) you shall arise acharay (another) malakaw (kingdom) inferior to you; and acharay (another) thalayathay (third) malakaw (kingdom) of nachash (brass), which shall shalat (bear) rule over kal (every) the arai (earth).

The rabayaiy (fourth) malakaw (kingdom) shall be thaqayap (strong) as parazal (iron), because parazal (iron) daqaq (breaks) in pieces and chashal (subdues) kal (every) things; and as parazal (iron) that crushes kal (every) these, shall it daqaq (break) in pieces and raii (crush).

Whereas you chazaa (saw) the ragal (feet) and atzabai (toes), man (from) of pachar (potters)' chasap (clay), and man (from) of parazal (iron), it shall be a palag (divided) malakaw (kingdom); but there shall be in it of the natzabah (strength) of the parazal (iron), because you chazaa (saw) the parazal (iron) irab (evening) with tayan (miry) chasap (clay).
As the atzabai (toes) of the ragal (feet) were man (from) of parazal (iron), and man (from) of chasap (clay), so the malakaw (kingdom) shall be partly thaqayap (strong), and partly thabar (broken).

Whereas you chazaa (saw) the parazal (iron) irab (evening) with tayan (miry) chasap (clay), they shall hawaa (which/who/that is) themselves with the zarai (seed) of anash (men); but they shall not cling to dan (one) dan (another), even as parazal (iron) does not irab (evening) with chasap (clay).

In the yawam (day) of those malak (king) shall the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven) qawam (rise up) up a malakaw (kingdom) which shall ilam (never) be chabal (destroyed), nor shall its sovereignty be shabaq (left) to acharan (another) im (people); but it shall daqaq (break) in pieces and sawap (consume) kal (every) these malakaw (kingdoms), and it shall qawam (rise up) ilam (forever).

Because you chazaa (saw) that a aban (stone) was gazar (cut) out of the tawar (mountain) laa (NOT) yad (hand), and that it daqaq (broke) in pieces the parazal (iron), the nachash (brass), the chasap (clay), the kasap (silver), and the dahab (gold); the rab (great) Alahayam has yadai (made) known to the malak (king) mah (what) shall happen achar (other): and the dream is yatzayab (certain), and its pashar (interpretation) aman (believe / have faith).

Then the malak (king) Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) napal (fall / be cast down) on his anap (face), and sagad (worshiped) Danayaal (Daniel), and commanded that they should nasak (offer) an manachah (offering) and nayachawach (sweet) odors to him.

The malak (king) inah (oppress / afflict) to Danayaal (Daniel), and amar (spoke), Of a qashawat (truth) your Alahayam is the Alahayam of Alahayam, and the Adawan of malak (king), and a revealer of raz (secrets), since you have been yakal (able) to galah (reveal) dan (this) raz (secret).

Then the malak (king) rabah (made) Danayaal (Daniel) rabarab (great), and yahab (gave) him many rabarab (great) mathanaa (gifts), and made him to shalat (rule) over the kal (every) madayanah (province) of Babal (Babylon), and to be rab (chief) sagan (governor) over kal (every) the chakayam (wise) men of Babal (Babylon).

Danayaal (Daniel) baia (requested) of the malak (king), and he appointed Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego), over the ibayadah (affairs) of the madayanah (province) of Babal (Babylon): but Danayaal (Daniel) was in the tharai (gate) of the malak (king).

Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king) ibad (servant) an tzalam (likeness) of dahab (gold), whose rawam (will lift up) was shathayan (sixty) amah (cubits), and its pathay (breadth) shath (six) amah (cubits): he qawam (rise up) it up in the baqaia (plain) of Dawaraa (Dura), in the madayanah (province) of Babal (Babylon).

Then Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king) shalach (sent) to kanash (gather) together the satraps, the deputies, and the pachah (governors), the adaragazar (judges), the gadabar (treasurers), the counselors, the thapathay (sheriffs), and kal (every) the shalatawan (rulers) of the madayanah (provinces), to athah (come) to the chanakaa (dedication) of the tzalam (likeness) which Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king) had qawam (rise up) up.

Then the satraps, the deputies, and the pachah (governors), the adaragazar (judges), the gadabar (treasurers), the counselors, the thapathay (sheriffs), and kal (every) the shalatawan (rulers) of the madayanah (provinces), were kanash (gathered) together to the chanakaa (dedication) of the tzalam (likeness) that Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king) had qawam (rise up) up; and they qawam (rise up) qabal (before) the tzalam (likeness) that Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) had qawam (rise up) up.
Then the karawaz (herald) qaraa (called) chayal (aloud), To you it is commanded, im (peoples), amah (nations), and lashan (languages),

That whenever you shamai (hear) the qal (sound) of the qaran (horn), masharawaqay (flute), zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and kal (every) zan (kinds) of music, you napal (fall / be cast down) down and sagad (worship) the dahab (golden) tzalam (likeness) that Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king) has qawam (rise up) up;
And whoever doesn't napal (fall / be cast down) down and sagad (worship) shall the same shaih (hour) be ramah (cast) into the gaw (midst) of a yaqad (burning) nawar (fiery) athawan (furnace).

Qabal (therefore) at that zaman (time), when kal (every) the im (peoples) shamai (heard) the qal (sound) of the qaran (horn), masharawaqay (flute), zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and kal (every) zan (kinds) of music, kal (every) the im (peoples), the amah (nations), and the lashan (languages), napal (fall / be cast down) down and sagad (worshiped) the dahab (golden) tzalam (likeness) that Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king) had qawam (rise up) up.
Qabal (therefore) at that zaman (time) gabar (certain) Kashaday (Chaldeans) qarab (came) near, and brought accusation against the Yahawadaay (Jews).
They inah (oppress / afflict) Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king), O malak (king), chayaa (live) for ilam (ever).

You, O malak (king), have shawam (place / establish / appoint) a taim (decree), that kal (every) anash (man) that shall shamai (hear) the qal (sound) of the qaran (horn), masharawaqay (flute), zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and kal (every) zan (kinds) of music, shall napal (fall / be cast down) down and sagad (worship) the dahab (golden) tzalam (likeness);
And whoever doesn't napal (fall / be cast down) down and sagad (worship) shall be ramah (cast) into the gaw (midst) of a yaqad (burning) nawar (fiery) athawan (furnace).

There are gabar (certain) Yahawadaay (Jews) whom you have appointed over the ibayadah (affairs) of the madayanah (province) of Babal (Babylon): Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego); these gabar (men), O malak (king), have not respected you. They don't palach (serve) your Alahayam, nor sagad (worship) the dahab (golden) tzalam (likeness) which you have qawam (rise up) up.

Then Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) in his ragaz (rage) and chamaa (fury) commanded to athah (bring) Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego). Then they athah (brought) these gabar (men) qadam (before) the malak (king).

Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) inah (oppress / afflict) them, Is it on purpose, Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego), that you don't palach (serve) my Alahayam, nor sagad (worship) the dahab (golden) tzalam (likeness) which I have qawam (rise up) up?

Kain (now) if you are ithayad (ready) whenever you shamai (hear) the qal (sound) of the qaran (horn), masharawaqay (flute), zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and kal (every) zan (kinds) of music to napal (fall / be cast down) down and sagad (worship) the tzalam (likeness) which I have ibad (servant), well: but if you don't sagad (worship), you shall be ramah (cast) the same shaih (hour) into the gaw (midst) of a yaqad (burning) nawar (fiery) athawan (furnace); and who is that Alahayam that shall shazab (deliver) you out of my yad (hand)?

Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego) inah (oppress / afflict) the malak (king), Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar), we have no chashach (need) to thawab (answer) you in dan (this) pathagam (matter).

If it be so, our Alahayam whom we palach (serve) is yakal (able) to shazab (deliver) us from the yaqad (burning) nawar (fiery) athawan (furnace); and he will shazab (deliver) us out of your yad (hand), O malak (king).

But if not, be it yadai (known) to you, O malak (king), that we ayathay (will) not palach (serve) your Alahayam, nor sagad (worship) the dahab (golden) tzalam (likeness) which you have qawam (rise up) up.

Then was Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malaa (full) of chamaa (fury), and the tzalam (likeness) of his appearance was shanaa (hate) il (over) Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego): therefore he inah (oppress / afflict), and commanded that they should azaa (heat) the athawan (furnace) shabaih (seven) times more day (than) it was usually azaa (heated).

He commanded certain gabar (mighty) gabar (men) who were in his chayal (army) to kapath (bind) Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego), and to ramah (cast) them into the yaqad (burning) nawar (fiery) athawan (furnace).

Then these gabar (men) were kapath (bound) in their pants, their tunics, and their mantles, and their other labawash (garments), and were ramah (cast) into the gaw (midst) of the yaqad (burning) nawar (fiery) athawan (furnace).

Therefore man (from) the malak (king) commandment was chatzap (urgent), and the athawan (furnace) yathayar (exceeding) azaa (hot), the shabayab (flame) of the nawar (fire) killed alak (those) gabar (men) who nasaq (took) up Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego).

These thalath (three) gabar (men), Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego), napal (fall / be cast down) down kapath (bound) into the gaw (midst) of the yaqad (burning) nawar (fiery) athawan (furnace).

Then Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king) was astonished, and qawam (rise up) up in bahal (haste): he inah (oppress / afflict) and amar (spoke) to his counselors, Didn't we ramah (cast) thalath (three) gabar (men) kapath (bound) into the gaw (midst) of the nawar (fire)? They inah (oppress / afflict) the malak (king), yatzayab (true), O malak (king).

He inah (oppress / afflict), Look, I chazaa (see) arabai (four) gabar (men) sharaa (loose), halak (move) in the gaw (midst) of the nawar (fire), and they are unharmed; and the aspect of the rabayaiy (fourth) is like a bar (son) of the Alahayam.

Then Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) qarab (came) near to the tharai (mouth) of the yaqad (burning) nawar (fiery) athawan (furnace): he inah (oppress / afflict) and amar (spoke), Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego), you ibad (servant) of the Most ilay (went up) Alahayam, napaq (come) forth, and athah (come) here. Then Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego) napaq (came) forth out of the gaw (midst) of the nawar (fire).

The satraps, the deputies, and the pachah (governors), and the malak (king) counselors, being kanash (gathered) together, chazaa (saw) these gabar (men), that the nawar (fire) had no shalat (power) on their gasham (bodies), nor was the shair (hair) of their raash (head) charak (singed), laa (NOT) were their pants shanaa (hate), nor had the rayach (smell) of nawar (fire) idaa (passed) on them.

Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) inah (oppress / afflict) and amar (spoke), barak (blessed) be the Alahayam of Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego), who has shalach (sent) his malaak (angel / messenger of Yah), and shazab (delivered) his ibad (servant) who rachatz (trusted) in him, and have shanaa (hate) the malak (king) malah (word), and have yahab (yielded) their gasham (bodies), that they might not palach (serve) nor sagad (worship) any Alahayam, lahan (except) their own Alahayam.

Therefore I shawam (place / establish / appoint) a taim (decree), that kal (every) im (people), amah (nation), and lashan (language), which amar (spoke) anything evil il (over) the Alahayam of Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego), shall be ibad (servant) in hadam (pieces), and their bayath (house) shall be shawah (made) a nawalaw (dunghill); qabal (because) there is no other Alahayam who is able to natzal (deliver) dan (after) this sort.
Then the malak (king) tzalach (promoted) Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego) in the madayanah (province) of Babal (Babylon).
Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the king, to all the peoples, nations, and languages, who dwell in all the earth: Peace be multiplied to you.
It has seemed good to me to show the signs and wonders that the Ilayawan Alahayam has worked toward me.
How great are his signs! And how mighty are his wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his dominion is from generation to generation.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at rest in my house, and flourishing in my palace.
I saw a dream which made me afraid; and the thoughts on my bed and the visions of my head troubled me.
Therefore yadai (made) I a decree to bring in kal (every) the wise men of Babylon before me, that they might yadai (make) known to me the pashar (interpretation) of the dream.
Then hawaa (which/who/that is) in the magicians, the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers; and I told the dream before them; but they did not make known to me its interpretation.
But at the last Daniel came in before me, whose name was Belteshazzar, according to the name of my Alahayam, and in whom is the spirit of the holy Alahayam: and I told the dream before him, saying,

Belteshazzar, master of the magicians, because I know that the spirit of the holy Alahayam is in you, and no secret troubles you, tell me the visions of my dream that I talal (have) seen, and its interpretation.
Thus were the chazaw (visions) of my raash (head) on my mashakab (bed): I hawaa (which/who/that is), and alaw (behold), a tree in the midst of the earth; and its height was great.
The ayalan (tree) grew, and was strong, and its height reached to the sky, and its sight to the end of all the earth.

The shabaq (leaves) of it were beautiful, and its fruit much, and in it was food for all: the animals of the bar (field) had shadow under it, and the birds of the sky lived in its branches, and all flesh was fed from it.
I saw in the visions of my head on my bed, and behold, a watcher and a holy one came down from the sky.
He cried aloud, and said thus, Cut down the tree, and cut off its branches, shake off its leaves, and scatter its fruit: let the animals get away from under it, and the fowls from its branches.

Nevertheless leave the stump of its roots in the earth, even with a band of iron and brass, in the tender grass of the field; and let it be wet with the dew of the sky: and let his portion be with the animals in the grass of the earth:
Let his heart be changed from man's, and let an animal's heart be given to him; and let seven adayan (times) pass over him.

The sentence is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the holy ones; to the intent that the living may know that the Ilayawan rules in the kingdom of rabah (men), and gives it to whomever he will, and sets up over it the lowest of rabah (men).

This dream I, king Nebuchadnezzar, shakan (have) seen; and you, Belteshazzar, declare the interpretation, because kal (every) the wise men of my kingdom are not able to make known to me the interpretation; but you are able; for the spirit of the holy Alahayam is in you.

Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was stricken mute for a while, and his thoughts troubled him. The malak (king) answered, Belteshazzar, don't let the dream, or the interpretation, trouble you. Belteshazzar answered, My Adawan, the dream be to those who hate you, and its interpretation to your adversaries.
The ayalan (tree) that you chazaa (saw), which grew, and was strong, whose height reached to the sky, and its sight to all the arai (earth);
Whose leaves were beautiful, and its fruit much, and in it was food for all; under which the animals of the field lived, and on whose branches the birds of the sky had their habitation:
It is you, O king, that are grown and hawaa (which/who/that is) strong; for your greatness is grown, and reaches to the sky, and your dominion to the end of the earth.

Whereas the king saw a watcher and a holy one coming down from the sky, and amar (spoke), Cut down the ayalan (tree), and destroy it; nevertheless shabaq (leave) the iqar (stump) of its sharash (roots) in the earth, even with a band of iron and brass, in the tender grass of the field, and let it be wet with the dew of the sky: and let his portion be with the animals of the field, day (until) seven times pass over him;
This is the interpretation, O malak (king), and it is the decree of the Ilayawan, which has hawaa (which/who/that is) on my Adawan the malak (king):

That you shall be driven from men, and your dwelling shall be with the animals of the field, and you shall be made to eat grass as oxen, and shall be wet with the dew of the sky, and seven times shall pass over you; until you know that the Ilayawan rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he will.
Whereas they commanded to leave the stump of the roots of the tree; your malakaw (kingdom) shall be sure to you, after that you shall have known that the heavens do rule.

Day (therefore), O malak (king), let my counsel be acceptable to you, and break off your sins by righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor; if there may be a lengthening of your tranquility.
All this came on the malak (king) Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar).
At the end of twelve months he was walking in the royal palace of Babylon.
The king spoke and said, Is not this rabah (great) Babylon, which I have built for the royal dwelling place, by the might of my power and for the glory of my majesty?
While the word was in the king's mouth, there fell a voice from the sky, saying, O king Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar), to you it is spoken: The malakaw (kingdom) has departed from you:

And you shall be driven from men; and your dawar (dwelling) shall be with the animals of the field; you shall be ibad (servant) to eat grass as oxen; and seven times shall pass over you; day (until) you know that the Ilayawan rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he tzabaa (troop).

The same hour was the thing fulfilled on Nebuchadnezzar: and he was driven from men, and ate grass as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the sky, until his hair was grown like eagles' feathers, and his nails like birds' claws.

At the end of the days I, Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar), lifted up my eyes to shamayan (heaven), and my understanding returned to me, and I blessed the Ilayawan, and I shabach (praised) and honored him who lives forever; for his dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom from generation to generation.

Kal (every) the inhabitants of the arai (earth) are chashab (reputed) as laa (NOT); and he ibad (servant) according to his tzabaa (troop) in the chayal (army) of shamayan (heaven), and among the inhabitants of the arai (earth); and none ayathay (can) machaa (stay) his yad (hand), or ask him, mah (what) are you ibad (servant)?

At the same zaman (time) my manadai (understanding) thawab (returned) to me; and for the glory of my malakaw (kingdom), my hadar (majesty) and zayaw (brightness) thawab (returned) to me; and my counselors and my rabaraban (lords) baia (sought) to me; and I was thaqan (established) in my malakaw (kingdom), and yathayar (excellent) rabaw (greatness) was yasap (added) to me.

Kain (now) I, Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar), shabach (praise) and rawam (will lift up) and honor the malak (king) of shamayan (heaven); for kal (every) his maibad (works) are qashawat (truth), and his arach (ways) dayan (judge); and those who halak (move) in gawah (pride) he is yakal (able) to shapal (abase).

Balashaatzar (Belshazzar) the malak (king) ibad (servant) a rab (great) lacham (feast) to a alap (thousand) of his rabaraban (lords), and shathah (drinks) chamar (wine) qabal (before) the alap (thousand).

Balashaatzar (Belshazzar), while he tasted the chamar (wine), commanded to athah (bring) the dahab (golden) and kasap (silver) maan (vessels) which Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) his ab (father) had napaq (taken) out of the hayakal (temple) which was in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); that the malak (king) and his rabaraban (lords), his wives and his lachanah (concubines), might shathah (drinks) from them.

Then they athah (brought) the dahab (golden) maan (vessels) that were napaq (taken) out of the hayakal (temple) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam which was at Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); and the malak (king) and his rabaraban (lords), his wives and his lachanah (concubines), shathah (drinks) from them.
They shathah (drinks) chamar (wine), and shabach (praised) the Alahayam of dahab (gold), and of kasap (silver), of nachash (brass), of parazal (iron), of ai (wood), and of aban (stone).

In the same shaih (hour) napaq (came) forth the atzabai (fingers) of a anash (man's) yad (hand), and kathab (wrote) over qabal (against) the lampstand on the gayar (plaster) of the kathal (wall) of the malak (king) hayakal (palace): and the malak (king) chazaa (saw) the part of the yad (hand) that kathab (wrote).

Then the malak (king) zayaw (face) was shanaa (hate) in him, and his raiyawan (thoughts) bahal (troubled) him; and the qatar (joints) of his thighs were loosened, and his arakabah (knees) struck daa (one) against daa (another).
