The malak (king) qaraa (called) chayal (aloud) to ilal (bring) in the enchanters, the Kashaday (Chaldeans), and the gazar (soothsayers). The malak (king) inah (oppress / afflict) and amar (spoke) to the chakayam (wise) men of Babal (Babylon), Whoever shall qaraa (called) dan (this) kathab (writing), and show me its pashar (interpretation), shall be labash (clothed) with aragawan (purple), and have a hamanayak (chain) of dahab (gold) il (over) his tzawaar (neck), and shall be the thalayathay (third) shalat (ruler) in the malakaw (kingdom).

Then ilal (came) in kal (every) the malak (king) chakayam (wise) men; but they kahal (could) not qaraa (called) the kathab (writing), nor yadai (make) known to the malak (king) the pashar (interpretation).
Then was malak (king) Balashaatzar (Belshazzar) shagayaa (greatly) bahal (troubled), and his zayaw (face) was shanaa (hate) in him, and his rabaraban (lords) were perplexed.

Now the malakaa (queen) by qabal (reason) of the malah (words) of the malak (king) and his rabaraban (lords) ilal (came) into the mashathah (banquet) bayath (house): the malakaa (queen) inah (oppress / afflict) and amar (spoke), O malak (king), chayaa (live) ilam (forever); don't let your raiyawan (thoughts) bahal (trouble) you, nor let your zayaw (face) be shanaa (hate).

There is a gabar (man) in your malakaw (kingdom), in whom is the rawach (spirit / wind) of the qadayash (holy) Alahayam; and in the yawam (day) of your ab (father) nahayar (light) and shakalathanaw (understanding) and chakamah (wisdom), like the chakamah (wisdom) of the Alahayam, were shakach (found) in him; and the malak (king) Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) your ab (father), the malak (king), I say, your ab (father), qawam (rise up) him rab (master) of the charatam (magicians), enchanters, Kashaday (Chaldeans), and gazar (soothsayers);

Qabal (because) an yathayar (excellent) rawach (spirit / wind), and manadai (knowledge), and shakalathanaw (understanding), pashar (interpreting) of dreams, and achawah (showing) of dark achayadah (sentences), and sharaa (dissolving) of qatar (doubts), were shakach (found) in the same Danayaal (Daniel), whom the malak (king) shawam (place / establish / appoint) Balatashaatzar (Belteshazzar). Kain (now) let Danayaal (Daniel) be qaraa (called), and he will show the pashar (interpretation).

Then was Danayaal (Daniel) ilal (brought) in qadam (before) the malak (king). The malak (king) inah (oppress / afflict) and amar (spoke) to Danayaal (Daniel), Are you that Danayaal (Daniel), who are of the ban (son) of the galawath (captivity) of Yahawad (Judah), whom the malak (king) my ab (father) athah (brought) out of Yahawad (Judah)?

I have shamai (heard) of you, that the rawach (spirit / wind) of the Alahayam is in you, and that nahayar (light) and shakalathanaw (understanding) and yathayar (excellent) chakamah (wisdom) are shakach (found) in you.

Kain (now) the chakayam (wise) men, the enchanters, have been ilal (brought) in qadam (before) me, that they should qaraa (called) dan (this) kathab (writing), and yadai (make) known to me its pashar (interpretation); but they kahal (could) not show the pashar (interpretation) of the thing.

But I have shamai (heard) of you, that you yakal (can) give pashar (interpretations), and sharaa (dissolve) qatar (doubts); kain (now) if you yakal (can) qaraa (called) the kathab (writing), and yadai (make) known to me its pashar (interpretation), you shall be labash (clothed) with aragawan (purple), and have a hamanayak (chain) of dahab (gold) il (over) your tzawaar (neck), and shall be the thalath (third) shalat (ruler) in the malakaw (kingdom).

Then Danayaal (Daniel) inah (oppress / afflict) qadam (before) the malak (king), Let your mathanaa (gifts) be to yourself, and yahab (give) your nabazabah (rewards) to acharan (another); baram (nevertheless) I will qaraa (called) the kathab (writing) to the malak (king), and yadai (make) known to him the pashar (interpretation).
You, malak (king), the Most ilay (went up) Alahayam yahab (gave) Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) your ab (father) the malakaw (kingdom), and rabaw (greatness), and glory, and hadar (majesty):

And man (from) of the rabaw (greatness) that he yahab (gave) him, kal (every) the im (peoples), amah (nations), and lashan (languages) hawaa (which/who/that is) and dachal (feared) man (from) him: whom he hawaa (which/who/that is) he killed, and whom he hawaa (which/who/that is) he hawaa (which/who/that is) alive; and whom he hawaa (which/who/that is) he raised up, and whom he hawaa (which/who/that is) he hawaa (which/who/that is) down.

But when his labab (heart) was rawam (will lift up) up, and his rawach (spirit / wind) was thaqap (hardened) so that he dealt proudly, he was nachath (deposed) from his malakaw (kingly) karasaa (throne), and they idaa (took) his glory from him:

And he was tarad (driven) from the ban (son) of anash (men), and his labab (heart) was shawah (made) im (like) the animals', and his madawar (dwelling) was with the irad (wild) donkeys; he was taim (fed) with grass like oxen, and his gasham (body) was tzabai (wet) with the tal (dew) of the sky; id (until) he yadai (knew) that the Most ilay (went up) Alahayam shalayat (rules) in the malakaw (kingdom) of anash (men), and that he qawam (rise up) up over it whomever he tzabaa (troop).
You, his bar (son), Balashaatzar (Belshazzar), have not shapal (humbled) your labab (heart), qabal (though) you yadai (knew) kal (every) dan (this),

But have rawam (will lift up) up yourself il (over) the Adawan of shamayan (heaven); and they have athah (brought) the maan (vessels) of his bayath (house) qadam (before) you, and you and your rabaraban (lords), your wives and your lachanah (concubines), have shathah (drinks) chamar (wine) from them; and you have shabach (praised) the Alahayam of kasap (silver) and dahab (gold), of nachash (brass), parazal (iron), ai (wood), and aban (stone), which don't chazaa (see), nor shamai (hear), nor yadai (know); and the Alahayam in whose yad (hand) your nashamaa (breath) is, and whose are kal (every) your arach (ways), you have not hadar (glorified).
Then was the part of the yad (hand) shalach (sent) from qadam (before) him, and dan (this) kathab (writing) was inscribed.
Dan (this) is the kathab (writing) that was inscribed: manaa (mene), manaa (mene), thaqal (tekel), paras (upharsin).
Dan (this) is the pashar (interpretation) of the thing: manaa (mene); Alahayam has manaa (numbered) your malakaw (kingdom), and brought it to an end;
Thaqal (tekel); you are thaqal (weighed) in the maazan (balances), and are shakach (found) chasayar (wanting).
PERES; your malakaw (kingdom) is paras (divided), and yahab (given) to the Maday (Medes) and Paras (Persians).

Then commanded Balashaatzar (Belshazzar), and they labash (clothed) Danayaal (Daniel) with aragawan (purple), and put a hamanayak (chain) of dahab (gold) il (over) his tzawaar (neck), and karaz (made) proclamation il (over) him, that he should be the thalath (third) shalayat (ruler) in the malakaw (kingdom).
In that layalayaa (night) Balashaatzar (Belshazzar) the Kashaday (Chaldean) malak (king) was qatal (slain).
Darayawash (Darius) the Mede qabal (received) the malakaw (kingdom), being about shathayan (sixty) - tharayan (two) shanah (years) bar (old).
It pleased Darayawash (Darius) to set over the malakaw (kingdom) one hundred twenty satraps, who should be throughout the whole malakaw (kingdom);
And over them three presidents, of whom Daniel was one; that these satraps might hawaa (which/who/that is) account to them, and that the king should hawaa (which/who/that is) no damage.

Then this Danayaal (Daniel) was distinguished above the sarak (presidents) and the satraps, because an excellent spirit was in him; and the malak (king) thought to hawaa (which/who/that is) him over the whole realm.

Then the sarak (presidents) and the satraps hawaa (which/who/that is) to find occasion against Danayaal (Daniel) as touching the malakaw (kingdom); but they could find no occasion nor fault, qabal (because) he was faithful, neither was there any error or fault found in him.
Then these men said, We shall not shakach (find) any ilah (occasion) il (over) qabal (this) Danayaal (Daniel), except we shakach (find) it against him concerning the law of his Alahayam.
Then these presidents and satraps assembled together to the king, and amar (spoke) dan (thus) to him, King Darius, live forever.

All the sarak (presidents) of the kingdom, the deputies and the satraps, the counselors and the governors, have consulted together to establish a malak (king) statute, and to make a strong decree, that whoever shall ask a petition of any Alahayam or man for thirty days, except of you, O malak (king), he shall be cast into the den of lions.
Day (now), O malak (king), qawam (rise up) the asar (decree), and sign the writing, that it not be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which doesn't alter.
Day (therefore) malak (king) Darius rasham (signed) the kathab (writing) and the asar (decree).

When Daniel knew that the kathab (writing) was rasham (signed), he went into his house (now his windows were open in his room toward Jerusalem) and he kneeled on his knees three dan (times) a day, and prayed, and gave thanks qabal (before) his Alahayam, as he did before.
Then these men assembled together, and found Danayaal (Daniel) yadai (making) petition and supplication qadam (before) his Alahayam.

Then they came near, and spoke qadam (before) the king concerning the king's decree: Haven't you signed an decree, that every gabar (man) who shall baia (make) petition to any Alahayam or gabar (man) within thirty days, except to you, O king, shall be cast into the den of lions? The king answered, The thing is true, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which doesn't alter.

Then inah (oppress / afflict) they and amar (spoke) qadam (before) the malak (king), That Paras (Daniel), who is of the children of the captivity of Judah, doesn't respect you, O malak (king), nor the asar (decree) that you have rasham (signed), but baia (makes) his petition three adayan (times) a yawam (day).

Then the malak (king), when he heard these words, was very displeased, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) his heart on Danayaal (Daniel) to deliver him; and he labored day (until) the going down of the sun to rescue him.

Then these men assembled together to the malak (king), and said to the malak (king), Know, O malak (king), that it is a law of the Medes and Persians, that no decree nor statute which the malak (king) establishes may be changed.

Then the malak (king) commanded, and they brought Paras (Daniel), and cast him into the den of lions. Now the malak (king) amar (spoke) and amar (spoke) to Paras (Daniel), Your Alahayam whom you serve continually, he will deliver you.

A stone was athah (brought), and laid on the mouth of the gab (den); and the malak (king) sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that nothing might be changed concerning Danayaal (Daniel).
Then the malak (king) went to his palace, and passed the night fasting; laa (NOT) were instruments of music athah (brought) before him: and his sleep fled from him.
Then the malak (king) arose very early in the morning, and azal (went) in haste to the den of lions.

When he came near to the gab (den) to Daniel, he cried with a lamentable voice; the malak (king) spoke and said to Daniel, Daniel, servant of the living Alahayam, is your Alahayam, whom you serve continually, able to deliver you from the arayah (lions)?
Then Danayaal (Daniel) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), O malak (king), live forever.
My Alahayam has sent his angel, and has shut the lions' mouths, and they have not hurt me; because as before him innocence was found in me; and also before you, O malak (king), have I done no hurt.

Then was the malak (king) exceeding glad, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no kind of harm was shakach (found) on him, because he had trusted in his Alahayam.

The malak (king) commanded, and they brought those men who had accused Danayaal (Daniel), and they cast them into the gab (den) of lions, them, their children, and their wives; and the lions mauled them, and broke kal (every) their bones in pieces, before they came to the bottom of the gab (den).
Then malak (king) Darius wrote to kal (every) the peoples, nations, and languages, who dwell in kal (every) the earth: Peace be multiplied to you.

I make a decree, that in all the dominion of my kingdom men tremble and fear before the Alahayam of Daniel; for he is the living Alahayam, and steadfast forever, His kingdom that which shall not be destroyed; and his dominion shall be even to the end.
He delivers and rescues, and he works signs and wonders in heaven and in earth, who has delivered Danayaal (Daniel) from the power of the lions.
So this Danayaal (Daniel) prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.

In the chad (first) shanah (year) of Balashaatzar (Belshazzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) Danayaal (Daniel) chazaa (had) a dream and chazaw (visions) of his raash (head) on his mashakab (bed): then he kathab (wrote) the dream and amar (spoke) the raash (head) of the malah (matters).

Danayaal (Daniel) inah (oppress / afflict) and amar (spoke), I chazaa (saw) in my chazaw (vision) by layalayaa (night), and, araw (behold), the arabai (four) rawach (spirit / wind) of the sky broke forth on the rab (great) yam (sea).
Arabai (four) rabarab (great) animals salaq (came) up from the yam (sea), shanaa (hate) daa (one) from daa (another).

The qadamay (first) was like a arayah (lion), and had nashar (eagle's) gap (wings): I hawaa (which/who/that is) id (until) its gap (wings) were marat (plucked), and it was lifted up from the arai (earth), and qawam (rise up) to stand on two ragal (feet) as a anash (man); and a anash (man's) labab (heart) was yahab (given) to it.

Araw (behold), acharay (another) animal, a thanayan (second), damah (like) a dab (bear); and it was qawam (rise up) up on chad (one) shatar (side), and thalath (three) ilai (ribs) were in its pam (mouth) bayan (between) its shan (teeth): and they amar (spoke) kan (for sure) to it, Arise, akal (devour) much bashar (flesh).

Athar (after) dan (this) I hawaa (which/who/that is), and araw (behold), acharay (another), like a namar (leopard), which had on its gab (back) arabai (four) gap (wings) of a bird; the animal had also arabai (four) raash (head); and shalatan (dominion) was yahab (given) to it.

Athar (after) dan (this) I hawaa (which/who/that is) in the layalayaa (night) chazaw (visions), and, araw (behold), a rabayaiy (fourth) animal, awesome and powerful, and thaqayap (strong) yathayar (exceedingly); and it had rabarab (great) parazal (iron) shan (teeth); it akal (devoured) and daqaq (broke) in pieces, and rapas (stamped) the shaar (residue) with its ragal (feet): and it was shanaa (hate) from kal (every) the animals that were qadam (before) it; and it had ishar (ten) qaran (horns).

I hawaa (which/who/that is) the qaran (horns), and alaw (behold), there salaq (came) up bayan (between) them acharay (another) qaran (horn), a zaiyar (little) one, qadam (before) which thalath (three) of the qadamay (first) qaran (horns) were iqar (plucked) up by the roots: and alaw (behold), in daa (this) qaran (horn) were iyan (eye) like the iyan (eye) of a anash (man), and a pam (mouth) malal (speaking) rabarab (great) things.

I hawaa (which/who/that is) id (until) karasaa (thrones) were placed, and one who was ithayaq (ancient) of yawam (day) yathab (sat): his clothing was chawar (white) as thalag (snow), and the shair (hair) of his raash (head) like naqaa (pure) imar (wool); his karasaa (throne) was nawar (fiery) shabayab (flames), and its galagal (wheels) dalaq (burning) nawar (fire).

A nawar (fiery) nahar (stream) nagad (issued) and napaq (came) forth from qadam (before) him: alap (thousands) of alap (thousands) shamash (around/in attendance) to him, and rabaw (ten) thousand times rabaw (ten) thousand qawam (rise up) qadam (before) him: the dayan (judge) was yathab (set), and the sapar (book) were pathach (opened).

I hawaa (which/who/that is) at that adayan (time) man (from) of the qal (voice) of the rabarab (great) malah (words) which the qaran (horn) malal (spoke); I hawaa (which/who/that is) even id (until) the animal was qatal (slain), and its gasham (body) abad (destroy/perish), and it was yahab (given) to be burned with ash (fire).
As for the shaar (rest) of the animals, their shalatan (dominion) was idaa (taken) away: yet their lives were yahab (prolonged) for a zaman (season) and a idan (Idan/Eden).

I hawaa (which/who/that is) in the layalayaa (night) chazaw (visions), and araw (behold), there athah (came) with the inan (cloud) of the sky one like a bar (son) of anash (man), and he mataa (came) even to the ithayaq (ancient) of yawam (day), and they brought him qarab (near) qadam (before) him.

There was yahab (given) him shalatan (dominion), and glory, and a malakaw (kingdom), that kal (every) the im (peoples), amah (nations), and lashan (languages) should palach (serve) him: his shalatan (dominion) is an ilam (everlasting) shalatan (dominion), which shall not idaa (pass) away, and his malakaw (kingdom) that which shall not be chabal (destroyed).
As for me, Danayaal (Daniel), my rawach (spirit / wind) was karaa (grieved) in the gaw (midst) of my nadanah (body), and the chazaw (visions) of my raash (head) bahal (troubled) me.

I qarab (came) near to chad (one) of those who qawam (rise up) by, and baia (asked) him the yatzayab (truth) concerning kal (every) dan (this). So he amar (spoke) me, and yadai (made) me know the pashar (interpretation) of the things.
These rabarab (great) animals, which are arabai (four), are arabai (four) malak (king), who shall arise out of the arai (earth).
But the qadayash (saints) of the Most ilayawan (high) shall qabal (receive) the malakaw (kingdom), and chasan (possess) the malakaw (kingdom) ilam (forever), even ilam (forever) and ilam (ever).

Then I desired to know the yatzab (truth) il (over) the rabayaiy (fourth) animal, which was shanaa (hate) from kal (every) of them, yathayar (exceedingly) dachal (terrible), whose shan (teeth) were of parazal (iron), and its tapar (nails) of nachash (brass); which akal (devoured), daqaq (broke) in pieces, and rapas (stamped) the shaar (residue) with its ragal (feet);

And concerning the ishar (ten) qaran (horns) that were on its raash (head), and the other horn which salaq (came) up, and man (from) which thalath (three) napal (fall / be cast down), even that qaran (horn) that had iyan (eye), and a pam (mouth) that malal (spoke) rabarab (great) things, whose chazaw (look) was more rab (stout) man (from) its fellows.
I hawaa (which/who/that is), and the same qaran (horn) ibad (servant) qarab (war) with the qadayash (saints), and yakal (prevailed) against them;

Id (until) the ithayaq (ancient) of yawam (day) athah (came), and dayan (judge) was yahab (given) to the qadayash (saints) of the Most ilayawan (high), and the zaman (time) mataa (came) that the qadayash (saints) chasan (possessed) the malakaw (kingdom).

Kan (for sure) he amar (spoke), The rabayaiy (fourth) animal shall be a rabayaiy (fourth) malakaw (kingdom) on arai (earth), which shall be shanaa (hate) from kal (every) the malakaw (kingdoms), and shall akal (devour) the kal (every) arai (earth), and shall dawash (tread) it down, and daqaq (break) it in pieces.

As for the ishar (ten) qaran (horns), out of this malakaw (kingdom) shall ishar (ten) malak (king) arise: and acharan (another) shall arise achar (other) them; and he shall be shanaa (hate) from the former, and he shall shapal (put) down thalath (three) malak (king).

He shall malal (speak) malah (words) tzad (against) the Most ilay (went up), and shall balaa (wear) out the qadayash (saints) of the Most ilayawan (high); and he shall sabar (think) to shanaa (hate) the zaman (times) and the dath (law); and they shall be yahab (given) into his yad (hand) id (until) a idan (Idan/Eden) and idan (Idan/Eden) and half a idan (Idan/Eden).
But the dayan (judge) shall be yathab (set), and they shall idaa (take) away his shalatan (dominion), to shamad (consume) and to abad (destroy/perish) it to the sawap (end).

The malakaw (kingdom) and the shalatan (dominion), and the rabaw (greatness) of the malakaw (kingdoms) under the kal (every) sky, shall be yahab (given) to the im (people) of the qadayash (saints) of the Most ilayawan (high): his malakaw (kingdom) is an ilam (everlasting) malakaw (kingdom), and kal (every) shalatan (dominions) shall palach (serve) and shamai (obey) him.

Here is the sawap (end) of the malah (matter). As for me, Danayaal (Daniel), my thoughts much bahal (troubled) me, and my zayaw (face) was shanaa (hate) in me: but I natar (kept) the malah (matter) in my lab (heart).

In the shalawash (three) shanah (year) of the malakawath (reign) of malak (king) Balashaatzar (Belshazzar) a chazawan (vision) raah (see) to me, even to me, Danayaal (Daniel), achar (other) that which raah (see) to me at the thachalah (first).

I raah (see) in the chazawan (vision); now it was so, that when I raah (see), I was in the citadel Shawashan (of) Susa, which is in the madayanah (province) of Iyalam (Elam); and I raah (see) in the chazawan (vision), and I was by the awabal (river) Awalay (Ulai).

Then I nashaa (lift) up my iyan (eye), and raah (see), and behold, there imad (stood) panayam (before) the awabal (river) a ayal (ram) which had two qaran (horn): and the two qaran (horn) were gabah (high); but achad (one) was gabah (higher) than the other, and the gabah (higher) ilah (go up / offer) up acharawan (last).

I raah (see) the ayal (ram) nagach (pushing) westward, and northward, and southward; and no animals could imad (stand) panayam (before) him, neither was there any who could natzal (deliver) out of his yad (hand); but he ishah (make) according to his ratzawan (will), and gadal (magnified) himself.

As I was bayan (between), behold, a male tzapayar (goat) bawaa (come) from the mairab (west) over the surface of the whole aratz (Earth/land), and didn't nagai (touch) the aratz (Earth/land): and the tzapayar (goat) had a chazawath (notable) qaran (horn) between his iyan (eye).

He bawaa (come) to the ayal (ram) that bail (had) the two qaran (horn), which I raah (see) imad (standing) panayam (before) the awabal (river), and rawatz (ran) on him in the fury of his kach (strength / mighty / power).

I raah (see) him nagai (come) close to the ayal (ram), and he was marar (moved) with anger against him, and nakah (struck) the ayal (ram), and shabar (broke) his shanayam (two) qaran (horn); and there was no kach (strength / mighty / power) in the ayal (ram) to imad (stand) panayam (before) him; but he shalak (cast) him down to the aratz (Earth/land), and ramas (trampled) on him; and there was none who could natzal (deliver) the ayal (ram) out of his yad (hand).

The male iz (goat) gadal (magnified) himself maad (exceedingly): and when he was itzam (strong), the gadal (great) qaran (horn) was shabar (broken); and instead of it there ilah (go up / offer) up arabai (four) notable horns toward the arabai (four) rawach (spirit / wind) of the sky.

Out of achad (one) of them yatzaa (go out / come out) forth a matzaiyarah (little) qaran (horn), which grew yathar (exceeding) gadal (great), toward the nagab (south), and toward the mazarach (east), and toward the tzabay (glorious) land.

It gadal (grew) great, even to the tzabaa (troop) of the sky; and some of the tzabaa (troop) and of the kawakab (star) it napal (fall / be cast down) down to the aratz (Earth/land), and ramas (trampled) on them.

Yes, it gadal (magnified) itself, even to the shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop); and it rawam (will lift up) away from him the thamayad (continual) burnt offering, and the makawan (place) of his maqadash (sanctuary) was shalak (cast) down.

The tzabaa (troop) was nathan (give) over to it together with the thamayad (continual) burnt pashai (offering) through disobedience; and it shalak (cast) down amath (truth) to the aratz (Earth/land), and it ishah (make) its pleasure and tzalach (prospered).

Then I shamai (hearken / hear) a qadawash (holy) one dabar (word / matter); and another holy one amar (spoke) to that palamawanay (certain) one who dabar (word / matter), How long shall be the chazawan (vision) concerning the thamayad (continual) burnt pashai (offering), and the disobedience that shamam (makes) desolate, to nathan (give) both the qadash (set apart/make holy) and the tzabaa (troop) to be trodden under maramas (foot)?
He amar (spoke) to me, To two alap (thousand) and shalawash (three) maah (hundred) irab (evening) and mornings; then shall the qadash (set apart/make holy) be tzadaq (righteous / just / fair).

It happened, when I, even I Danayaal (Daniel), raah (see) seen the chazawan (vision), that I baqash (sought) to understand it; and behold, there imad (stood) before me as the maraah (appearance) of a gabar (man).

I shamai (hearken / hear) a adam (man's) qawal (sound / voice) between the banks of the Awalay (Ulai), which qaraa (called), and amar (spoke), Gabarayaal (Gabriel), make halaz (this) bayan (between) to understand the maraah (vision).

So he bawaa (come) atzal (near) where I imad (stood); and when he bawaa (come), I was frightened, and napal (fall / be cast down) on my panayam (face): but he amar (spoke) to me, bayan (between), ban (son) of adam (man); for the chazawan (vision) belongs to the ith (time) of the qatz (end).
Now as he was dabar (word / matter) with me, I fell into a radam (deep) sleep with my panayam (face) toward the aratz (Earth/land); but he nagai (touched) me, and imad (set) me upright.
He amar (spoke), Behold, I yadai (will) make you know what shall be in the acharayath (latter) time of the zaim (indignation); for it belongs to the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) time of the qatz (end).
The ayal (ram) which you raah (see), that bail (had) the two qaran (horn), they are the malak (king) of Maday (Media) and Paras (Persia).

The shaiyar (rough) male tzapayar (goat) is the malak (king) Yawan (of) Greece: and the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qaran (horn) that is between his iyan (eye) is the raashawan (first) malak (king).

As for that which was shabar (broken), in the place where arabai (four) imad (stood) up, arabai (four) malakawath (kingdoms) shall imad (stand) up out of the gaway (nation / people), but not with his kach (strength / mighty / power).

In the acharayath (latter) time of their malakawath (kingdom), when the transgressors thamam (have) come to the full, a malak (king) of iz (fierce) panayam (face), and bayan (between) chayadah (dark) sentences, shall imad (stand) up.

His kach (strength / mighty / power) shall be itzam (mighty), but not by his own kach (strength / mighty / power); and he shall shachath (destroy) wonderfully, and shall tzalach (prosper) and ishah (make) his pleasure; and he shall shachath (destroy) the itzawam (mighty) ones and the qadawash (holy) im (people / nation).

Through his shakal (policy) he shall cause maramah (craft) to tzalach (prosper) in his yad (hand); and he shall gadal (magnify) himself in his labab (heart), and in their security shall he shachath (destroy) many: he shall also imad (stand) up against the shar (prince / ruler) of shar (prince / ruler); but he shall be shabar (broken) apas (without) yad (hand).
The maraah (vision) of the irab (evening) and baqar (morning) which has been amar (spoke) is amath (truth): but seal up the chazawan (vision); for it belongs to many yawam (day) to come.

I, Danayaal (Daniel), hayah (came to pass), and was chalah (afflict) certain yawam (day); then I qawam (rise up) up, and ishah (make) the malak (king) malaakah (business): and I shamam (wondered) at the maraah (vision), but none bayan (between) it.

In the achad (one) shanah (year) of Darayawash (Darius) the ban (son) of Achashawarawash (Ahasuerus), of the zarai (seed) of the Maday (Medes), who was made malak (king) over the malakawath (realm) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans),

In the achad (one) shanah (year) of his malak (king) I, Danayaal (Daniel), bayan (between) by the sapar (book / scribed document) the masapar (number) of the shanah (years) about which the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Yaramayah (Jeremiah) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), for the malaa (accomplishing) of the desolations of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), even shabaiyam (seventy) shanah (years).
I nathan (give) my panayam (face) to the Adanay Alahayam, to baqash (seek) by thapalah (prayer) and petitions, with tzawam (fasting) and sackcloth and ashes.

I palal (prayed) to Yahawah my Alahayam, and made yadah (confession), and amar (spoke), Oh, Adanay, the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and yaraa (fear / be afraid) Al, who shamar (keep/guard) barayath (covenant) and loving chasad (grace) with those who ahab (love) him and shamar (keep/guard) his matzawah (commandments),

We have chataa (sinned), and have dealt iwah (perversely), and have rashai (done) wickedly, and have marad (rebelled), even sawar (turning) aside from your matzawah (precepts) and from your mashapat (ordinances);

Neither have we shamai (hearken / hear) to your ibad (servant) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), who dabar (word / matter) in your sham (name) to our malak (king), our shar (prince / ruler), and our ab (father), and to all the im (people / nation) of the aratz (Earth/land).

Adanay, tzadaqah (righteousness) belongs to you, but to us bashath (confusion) of panayam (face), as at this yawam (day); to the ayash (husband/individual man) of Yahawadah (Judah), and to the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and to all Yasharaal (Israel), who are qarawab (near), and who are rachawaq (far) off, through all the aratz (Earth/land) where you have nadach (driven) them, because of their mail (top/above) that they have mail (top/above) against you.
Adanay, to us belongs bashath (confusion) of panayam (face), to our malak (king), to our shar (prince / ruler), and to our ab (father), because we have chataa (sinned) against you.
To the Adanay our Alahayam belong racham (mercies) and salayachah (forgiveness); for we have marad (rebelled) against him;

Neither have we shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah our Alahayam, to yalak (walk) in his thawarah (instruction), which he nathan (give) panayam (before) us by his ibad (servant) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy).

Yes, all Yasharaal (Israel) ibar (pass over/through) transgressed your thawarah (instruction), sawar (turning) aside, that they should not shamai (hearken / hear) your qawal (sound / voice): therefore the alah (these) and the shabawaih (oath) kathab (written) in the thawarah (instruction) of Mashah (Moses) the ibad (servant) of Alahayam has been nathak (poured) out on us; for we have chataa (sinned) against him.

He has qawam (rise up) his dabar (word / matter), which he dabar (word / matter) against us, and against our shapat (judges) who shapat (judged) us, by bawaa (come) on us a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) rai (evil); for under the whole sky, such ishah (make) not been done as ishah (make) been done to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

As it is kathab (written) in the thawarah (instruction) of Mashah (Moses), all this rai (evil) bawaa (come) come on us: yet have we not entreated the favor of Yahawah our Alahayam, that we should shawab (turn back / repent) from our iwan (guilt/iniquity), and shakal (have) discernment in your amath (truth).

Therefore has Yahawah shaqad (watched) over the rai (evil), and bawaa (come) it on us; for Yahawah our Alahayam is tzadayaq (righteous) in all his maishah (works) which he ishah (make), and we have not shamai (hearken / hear) his qawal (sound / voice).

Now, Adanay our Alahayam, who yatzaa (go out / come out) brought your im (people / nation) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) with a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and ishah (make) gotten yourself sham (name), as at this yawam (day); we have chataa (sinned), we have rashai (done) wickedly.

Adanay, according to all your tzadaqah (righteousness), let your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) and please let your chamah (wrath) be shawab (turn back / repent) away from your iyar (city) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), your qadash (set apart/make holy) har (mountain); because for our chataa (sins), and for the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of our ab (father), Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) and your im (people / nation) have become a charapah (reproach) to all who are around us.

Now therefore, our Alahayam, shamai (hearken / hear) to the thapalah (prayer) of your ibad (servant), and to his petitions, and cause your panayam (face) to awar (light) on your maqadash (sanctuary) that is shamam (desolate), for the adanay (master) sake.

My Alahayam, natah (turn) your azan (ear), and shamai (hearken / hear); paqach (open) your iyan (eye), and raah (see) our desolations, and the iyar (city) which is qaraa (called) by your sham (name): for we do not napal (fall / be cast down) our petitions panayam (before) you for our tzadaqah (righteousness), but for your rab (great) racham (mercies)' sake.

Adanay, shamai (hearken / hear); Adanay, salach (forgive/pardon/make clean); Adanay, listen and ishah (make); don't achar (other), for your own sake, my Alahayam, because your iyar (city) and your im (people / nation) are qaraa (called) by your sham (name).

While I was dabar (word / matter), and palal (praying), and yadah (confessing) my chataah (sin) and the chataah (sin) of my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel), and napal (fall / be cast down) my thachanah (supplication) panayam (before) Yahawah my Alahayam for the qadash (set apart/make holy) har (mountain) of my Alahayam;

Yes, while I was dabar (word / matter) in thapalah (prayer), the ayash (husband/individual man) Gabarayaal (Gabriel), whom I raah (see) seen in the chazawan (vision) at the thachalah (beginning), being yaip (caused) to fly yaip (swiftly), nagai (touched) me about the ith (time) of the irab (evening) manachah (offering).
He bayan (between) me, and dabar (word / matter) with me, and amar (spoke), Danayaal (Daniel), I am now yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to give you shakal (wisdom) and bayanah (understanding).

At the thachalah (beginning) of your petitions the commandment yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and I bawaa (come) come to nagad (tell) you; for you are greatly beloved: therefore bayan (between) the dabar (word / matter), and bayan (between) the maraah (vision).

Shabaiyam (seventy) shabawai (weeks) are decreed on your im (people / nation) and on your qadash (set apart/make holy) iyar (city), to kalaa (finish) disobedience, and to chatham (make) an end of chataah (sin), and to kapar (make) reconciliation for iwan (guilt/iniquity), and to bawaa (come) in iwalam (forever) tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and to chatham (seal) up chazawan (vision) and nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and to mashach (anoint) the most qadash (set apart/make holy).

Yadai (know) therefore and discern, that from the mawatzaa (going) forth of the commandment to shawab (turn back / repent) and to banah (build) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) to the mashayach (anointed one) One, the nagayad (prince), shall be shabai (seven) shabawai (weeks), and shashayam (sixty) - shanayam (two) shabawai (weeks): it shall be banah (built) again, with rachab (street) and moat, even in troubled ith (times).

Achar (other) the shashayam (sixty) - shanayam (two) shabawai (weeks) the mashayach (anointed one) One shall be karath (cut) off, and shall have nothing: and the im (people / nation) of the nagayad (prince) who shall bawaa (come) shall shachath (destroy) the iyar (city) and the qadash (set apart/make holy); and its qatz (end) shall be with a shatap (flood), and even to the qatz (end) shall be malachamah (war); desolations are charatz (determined).

He shall make a firm barayath (covenant) with many for achad (one) shabawai (week): and in the chatzay (midst) of the shabawai (week) he shall cause the zabach (sacrifice) and the manachah (offering) to shabath (shabath/rest); and on the kanap (wing) of shaqawatz (abominations) shall come one who shamam (makes) desolate; and even to the kalah (complete / finish) end, and that charatz (determined), shall wrath be nathak (poured) out on the shamam (desolate).

In the shalawash (three) shanah (year) of Kawarash (Cyrus) malak (king) of Paras (Persia) a thing was galah (revealed) to Danayaal (Daniel), whose sham (name) was qaraa (called) Balatashaatzar (Belteshazzar); and the thing was amath (truth), even a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) tzabaa (troop): and he bayan (between) the thing, and had bayanah (understanding) of the maraah (vision).
In those yawam (day) I, Danayaal (Daniel), was abal (mourning) shalawash (three) yawam (day) shabawai (weeks).

I akal (eat) no chamad (pleasant) lacham (bread), neither bawaa (come) bashar (flesh) nor yayan (wine) into my pah (mouth), neither did I sawak (anoint) myself at sawak (all), until shalawash (three) yawam (day) shabawai (weeks) were malaa (fulfilled).

In the arabai (four) and isharayam (twenty) yawam (day) of the raashawan (first) chadash (month), as I was by the yad (hand) of the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) nahar (river), which is Chadaqal (Hiddekel),
I nashaa (lift) up my iyan (eye), and raah (see), and behold, a ayash (husband/individual man) labash (clothed) in bad (linen), whose thighs were adorned with katham (pure) gold of Awapaz (Uphaz):

His gawayah (corpse) also was like the tharashayash (beryl), and his panayam (face) as the maraah (appearance) of baraq (lightning), and his iyan (eye) as ash (fire) torches, and his zarawai (arms) and his maragalah (feet) like qalal (burnished) nachashath (brass), and the qawal (sound / voice) of his dabar (word / matter) like the qawal (sound / voice) of a hamawan (multitude).

I, Danayaal (Daniel), alone raah (see) the maraah (vision); for the ayash (husband/individual man) who were with me didn't raah (see) the maraah (vision); but a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) charadah (quaking) napal (fall / be cast down) on them, and they barach (fled) to chabaa (hide) themselves.

So I was shaar (left) alone, and raah (see) this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) maraah (vision), and there shaar (remained) no kach (strength / mighty / power) in me; for my hawad (comeliness) was hapak (turned) in me into mashachayath (corruption), and I itzar (retained) no kach (strength / mighty / power).

Yet shamai (hearken / hear) I the qawal (sound / voice) of his dabar (word / matter); and when I shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of his dabar (word / matter), then was I fallen into a radam (deep) sleep on my panayam (face), with my panayam (face) toward the aratz (Earth/land).
Behold, a yad (hand) nagai (touched) me, which nawai (set) me on my barak (knees) and on the kap (palms) of my yad (hand).

He amar (spoke) to me, Danayaal (Daniel), you ayash (husband/individual man) greatly beloved, bayan (between) the dabar (word / matter) that I dabar (word / matter) to you, and imad (stand) upright; for am I now shalach (send) to you. When he had dabar (word / matter) this dabar (word / matter) to me, I imad (stood) raid (trembling).

Then he amar (spoke) to me, Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), Danayaal (Daniel); for from the raashawan (first) yawam (day) that you nathan (give) your lab (heart) to bayan (between), and to inah (oppress / afflict) yourself panayam (before) your Alahayam, your dabar (word / matter) were shamai (hearken / hear): and I bawaa (come) come for your dabar (word / matter)' sake.

But the shar (prince / ruler) of the malakawath (kingdom) of Paras (Persia) withstood me isharayam (twenty) - achad (one) yawam (day); but, behold, Mayakaal (Michael), achad (one) of the chief shar (prince / ruler), bawaa (come) to izar (help) me: and I yathar (remained) there with the malak (king) of Paras (Persia).

Now I bawaa (come) come to bayan (between) you understand what shall qarah (happen) to your im (people / nation) in the acharayath (latter) yawam (day); for the chazawan (vision) is yet for many yawam (day):
And when he had dabar (word / matter) to me according to these dabar (word / matter), I nathan (give) my panayam (face) toward the aratz (Earth/land), and was mute.

Behold, one in the damawath (likeness) of the ban (son) of adam (men) nagai (touched) my shapah (lips): then I pathach (opened) my pah (mouth), and dabar (word / matter) and amar (spoke) to him who imad (stood) before me, my Adawan, by reason of the maraah (vision) my tzayar (sorrows) are hapak (turned) on me, and I itzar (retain) no kach (strength / mighty / power).

For hayak (how) yakal (can) the ibad (servant) of this my Adawan dabar (word / matter) with this my Adawan? For as for me, immediately there imad (remained) no kach (strength / mighty / power) in me, neither was there nashamah (breathing thing) shaar (left) in me.
Then there nagai (touched) me again one like the maraah (appearance) of a adam (man), and he chazaq (strengthened) me.

He amar (spoke), "Greatly beloved ayash (husband/individual man), don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid): shalawam (peace / safety) be to you, be chazaq (strong), yes, be chazaq (strong)." When he dabar (word / matter) to me, I was chazaq (strengthened), and amar (spoke), Let my Adawan dabar (word / matter); for you have chazaq (strengthened) me.

Then he amar (spoke), Do you yadai (know) why I bawaa (come) come to you? Now I will shawab (turn back / repent) to lacham (fight) with the shar (prince / ruler) of Paras (Persia). When I yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, behold, the shar (prince / ruler) Yawan (of) Greece shall bawaa (come).

But I will nagad (tell) you that which is inscribed in the kathab (writing) of amath (truth): and there is none who chazaq (holds) with me against these, but Mayakaal (Michael) your shar (prince / ruler).
As for me, in the achad (one) shanah (year) of Darayawash (Darius) the maday (mede), I imad (stood) up to chazaq (confirm) and maiwaz (stronghold / fortress / protection) him.

Now will I show you the amath (truth). Behold, there shall imad (stand) up yet shalawash (three) malak (king) in Paras (Persia); and the rabayaiy (fourth) shall be ishar (wealth / riches) richer than they all: and when he has grown chazaqah (strong) through his riches, he shall iwar (rouse / awaken) up all against the malakawath (realm) Yawan (of) Greece.
A gabawar (mighty) malak (king) shall imad (stand) up, who shall mashal (rule/have dominion) with rab (great) mamashal (authority), and ishah (make) according to his ratzawan (will).

When he shall imad (stand) up, his malakawath (kingdom) shall be shabar (broken), and shall be chatzah (divided) toward the arabai (four) rawach (spirit / wind) of the sky, but not to his acharayath (posterity), nor according to his mashal (dominion) with which he mashal (rule/have dominion); for his malakawath (kingdom) shall be nathash (plucked) up, even for others besides these.

The malak (king) of the nagab (south) shall be chazaq (strong), and one of his shar (prince / ruler); and he shall be chazaq (strong) above him, and mashal (rule/have dominion) dominion; his mamashalah (dominion) shall be a rab (great) mamashal (authority).

At the qatz (end) of shanah (years) they shall chabar (join) themselves together; and the bath (daughter) of the malak (king) of the nagab (south) shall bawaa (come) to the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north) to ishah (make) an mayashar (agreement): but she shall not itzar (retain) the kach (strength / mighty / power) of her zarawai (arm); neither shall he imad (stand), nor his zarawai (arm); but she shall be nathan (give) up, and those who bawaa (come) her, and he who became the yalad (birth / begot) of her, and he who chazaq (strengthened) her in those ith (times).

But out of a shoot from her sharash (roots) shall one imad (stand) up in his kan (for sure), who shall bawaa (come) to the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), and shall bawaa (come) into the maiwaz (stronghold / fortress / protection) of the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north), and shall ishah (make) against them, and shall chazaq (prevail).

Also their Alahayam, with their molten nasayak (images), and with their chamadah (goodly) kalay (vessels) of kasap (silver) and of zahab (gold), shall he bawaa (come) shabay (captive) into Matzarayam (Egypt); and he shall refrain some shanah (years) from the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north).
He shall bawaa (come) into the malakawath (realm) of the malak (king) of the nagab (south), but he shall shawab (turn back / repent) into his own adamah (land).

His ban (son) shall war, and shall asap (assemble) a hamawan (multitude) of rab (great) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), which shall bawaa (come) on, and shatap (overflow), and ibar (pass over/through) through; and they shall shawab (turn back / repent) and war, even to his maiwaz (stronghold / fortress / protection).

The malak (king) of the nagab (south) shall be marar (moved) with anger, and shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth and lacham (fight) with him, even with the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north); and he shall imad (set) forth a rab (great) hamawan (multitude), and the hamawan (multitude) shall be nathan (give) into his yad (hand).

The hamawan (multitude) shall be rawam (will lift up) up, and his labab (heart) shall be rawam (will lift up); and he shall napal (fall / be cast down) down rabaw (tens) of thousands, but he shall not izaz (prevail).

The malak (king) of the tzapawan (north) shall shawab (turn back / repent), and shall imad (set) forth a hamawan (multitude) greater than the raashawan (former); and he shall bawaa (come) on at the qatz (end) of the ith (times), even of shanah (years), with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) and with much rakawash (wealth / property / goods / possessions).

In those ith (times) there shall many imad (stand) up against the malak (king) of the nagab (south): also the ban (son) of the violent among your im (people / nation) shall nashaa (lift) themselves up to imad (establish) the chazawan (vision); but they shall kashal (stumble / stagger).

So the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north) shall bawaa (come), and shapak (cast) up a mound, and lakad (take) a well-fortified iyar (city): and the forces of the nagab (south) shall not imad (stand), neither his mabachar (chosen) im (people / nation), neither shall there be any kach (strength / mighty / power) to imad (stand).

But he who bawaa (come) against him shall ishah (make) according to his ratzawan (own) will, and none shall imad (stand) panayam (before) him; and he shall imad (stand) in the tzabay (glorious) aratz (Earth/land), and in his yad (hand) shall be destruction.

He shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) his panayam (face) to bawaa (come) with the thaqap (strength) of his whole malakawath (kingdom), and with him equitable conditions; and he shall ishah (make) them: and he shall nathan (give) him the bath (daughter) of ashah (wife/individual woman), to shachath (corrupt) her; but she shall not imad (stand), neither be for him.

After this shall he shawab (turn back / repent) his panayam (face) to the ay (islands), and shall lakad (take) many: but a qatzayan (prince) shall cause the charapah (reproach) offered by him to shabath (shabath/rest); yes, moreover, he shall cause his charapah (reproach) to shawab (turn back / repent) on him.

Then he shall shawab (turn back / repent) his panayam (face) toward the fortresses of his own aratz (Earth/land); but he shall kashal (stumble / stagger) and napal (fall / be cast down), and shall not be matzaa (found).

Then shall imad (stand) up in his kan (for sure) ibar (pass over/through) who shall cause a nagash (tax) collector to pass through the malakawath (kingdom) to maintain its glory; but within achad (one) yawam (day) he shall be shabar (destroyed), neither in ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), nor in malachamah (battle).

In his kan (for sure) shall imad (stand) up a bazah (contemptible) person, to whom they nathan (give) not given the honor of the malakawath (kingdom): but he shall bawaa (come) in time of security, and shall obtain the malakawath (kingdom) by chalaqalaqah (flatteries).
The overwhelming forces shall be shatap (overwhelmed) from panayam (before) him, and shall be shabar (broken); yes, also the nagayad (prince) of the barayath (covenant).
After the treaty made with him he shall ishah (make) deceitfully; for he shall ilah (go up / offer) up, and shall become itzam (strong), with a mait (small) gaway (nation / people).

In time of security shall he bawaa (come) even on the fattest mashaman (places) of the madayanah (province); and he shall ishah (make) that which his ab (father) ishah (make) not done, nor his ab (father)' ab (father); he shall bazar (scatter) among them bazah (prey), and shalal (spoil), and rakawash (wealth / property / goods / possessions): yes, he shall chashab (devise) his machashabah (devices) against the strongholds, even for a ith (time).

He shall iwar (rouse / awaken) up his kach (strength / mighty / power) and his labab (courage) against the malak (king) of the nagab (south) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor); and the malak (king) of the nagab (south) shall war in malachamah (battle) with an maad (exceeding) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and itzawam (mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor); but he shall not imad (stand); for they shall chashab (devise) machashabah (devices) against him.

Yes, they who akal (eat) of his dainties shall shabar (destroy) him, and his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) shall shatap (overflow); and many shall napal (fall / be cast down) down chalal (slain).

As for shanayam (two) these malak (king), their labab (hearts) shall be to marai (do) mischief, and they shall dabar (word / matter) kazab (lies) at achad (one) shalachan (table): but it shall not tzalach (prosper); for yet the qatz (end) shall be at the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) appointed.

Then shall he shawab (turn back / repent) into his aratz (Earth/land) with gadawal (very great/important/mighty) rakawash (wealth / property / goods / possessions); and his labab (heart) shall be against the qadash (set apart/make holy) barayath (covenant); and he shall ishah (make) his pleasure, and shawab (turn back / repent) to his own aratz (Earth/land).

At the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) appointed he shall shawab (turn back / repent), and bawaa (come) into the nagab (south); but it shall not be in the acharawan (latter) raashawan (time) as it was in the former.

For tzay (ships) of Kathay (Kittim) shall bawaa (come) against him; therefore he shall be kaah (grieved), and shall shawab (turn back / repent), and have zaim (indignation) against the qadash (set apart/make holy) barayath (covenant), and shall ishah (make) his pleasure: he shall even shawab (turn back / repent), and bayan (between) regard to those who izab (forsake) the qadash (set apart/make holy) barayath (covenant).

Forces shall imad (stand) on his part, and they shall chalal (profane) the maqadash (sanctuary), even the maiwaz (stronghold / fortress / protection), and shall sawar (take) away the thamayad (continual) burnt nathan (give), and they shall set up the shaqawatz (abomination) that shamam (makes) desolate.

Such as rashai (do) wickedly against the barayath (covenant) shall he pervert by chalaqah (flatteries); but the im (people / nation) who yadai (know) their Alahayam shall be chazaq (strong), and ishah (make) exploits.

Those who are shakal (wise) among the im (people / nation) shall bayan (between) many; yet they shall kashal (stumble / stagger) by the charab (sword) and by lahabah (flame), by shabay (captivity) and by bazah (spoil), many yawam (day).
Now when they shall kashal (stumble / stagger), they shall be izar (helped) with a mait (little) izar (help); but many shall lawah (join) themselves to them with chalaqalaqah (flatteries).

Some of those who are shakal (wise) shall kashal (stumble / stagger), to tzarap (refine) them, and to barar (purify), and to laban (make) them white, even to the ith (time) of the qatz (end); because it is yet for the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) appointed.

The malak (king) shall ishah (make) according to his ratzawan (will); and he shall rawam (will lift up) himself, and gadal (magnify) himself above every Al, and shall dabar (word / matter) palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) things against the Al of Al; and he shall tzalach (prosper) until the zaim (indignation) be kalah (complete / finish); for that which is charatz (determined) shall be ishah (make).

Neither shall he bayan (between) the Alahayam of his ab (father), nor the chamadah (desire) of ashah (wife/individual woman), nor bayan (between) any Alawah; for he shall gadal (magnify) himself above all.

But in his kan (for sure) shall he honor the Alawah of fortresses; and a Alawah whom his ab (father) didn't yadai (know) shall he honor with zahab (gold), and kasap (silver), and with yaqar (precious) aban (stone), and chamad (pleasant) things.

He shall ishah (make) with the strongest fortresses by the help of a foreign Alawah: whoever nakar (acknowledges) him he will rabah (increase) with kabawad (glory); and he shall mashal (rule/have dominion) them to rule over many, and shall chalaq (divide) the adamah (land) for a machayar (price).

At the ith (time) of the qatz (end) shall the malak (king) of the nagab (south) contend with him; and the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north) shall shair (dread / storm / horror) against him like a whirlwind, with rakab (chariots), and with horsemen, and with many anayah (ships); and he shall bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land), and shall shatap (overflow) and ibar (pass over/through) through.

He shall bawaa (come) also into the tzabay (glorious) aratz (Earth/land), and many countries shall be kashal (stumble / stagger); but these shall be malat (delivered) out of his yad (hand): Adam (Edom), and Mawaab (Moab), and the raashayath (beginning) of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon).
He shall shalach (send) forth his yad (hand) also on the aratz (Earth/land); and the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) shall not palayatah (escape).

But he shall have mashal (rule/have dominion) over the makaman (treasures) of zahab (gold) and of kasap (silver), and over all the chamad (precious) things of Matzarayam (Egypt); and the lawabay (libyans) and the Kawashay (Ethiopians) shall be at his matzaid (steps).

But shamawaih (news) out of the mazarach (east) and out of the tzapawan (north) shall bahal (trouble) him; and he shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth with gadawal (very great/important/mighty) fury to shamad (destroy) and charam (utterly) to sweep away many.

He shall natai (plant) the ahal (tents) of his apadan (palace) between the yam (sea/waters) and the tzabay (glorious) qadash (set apart/make holy) har (mountain); yet he shall bawaa (come) to his qatz (end), and none shall izar (help) him.

At that ith (time) shall Mayakaal (Michael) imad (stand) up, the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shar (prince / ruler) who imad (stands) for the ban (son) of your im (people / nation); and there shall be a ith (time) of tzarah (trouble), such as never was since there was a gaway (nation / people) even to that same ith (time): and at that ith (time) your im (people / nation) shall be malat (delivered), everyone who shall be matzaa (found) kathab (written) in the sapar (book / scribed document).
Many of those who sleep in the ipar (dust) of the adamah (earth) shall qawatz (awake), some to iwalam (forever) chay (life), and some to charapah (shame) and iwalam (forever) daraawan (contempt).

Those who are shakal (wise) shall zahar (warn) as the zahar (brightness) of the expanse; and those who rab (turn) many to tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) as the kawakab (star) id (forever) and iwalam (forever).

But you, Danayaal (Daniel), satham (shut) up the dabar (word / matter), and chatham (seal) the sapar (book / scribed document), even to the ith (time) of the qatz (end): many shall shawat (run) back and forth, and daith (knowledge) shall be rabah (increased).

Then I, Danayaal (Daniel), raah (see), and behold, shanayam (two) others imad (stood), achad (one) on the yaar (river) shapah (bank) on hanah (here) side, and the other on the yaar (river) shapah (bank) on that side.

One amar (spoke) to the ayash (husband/individual man) labash (clothed) in bad (linen), who was mail (top/above) the mayam (Waters) of the yaar (river), How long shall it be to the qatz (end) of these palaa (wonders)?

I shamai (hearken / hear) the ayash (husband/individual man) labash (clothed) in bad (linen), who was mail (top/above) the mayam (Waters) of the yaar (river), when he rawam (will lift up) up his right yamayan (right hand) and his left shamaawal (left hand) to shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), and shabai (swear / take oath) by him who chay (life) iwalam (forever) that it shall be for a mawaid (Feast/Holy Day), mawaid (Feast/Holy Day), and a chatzay (half); and when they kalah (complete / finish) made an end of napatz (breaking) in pieces the yad (hand) of the qadash (set apart/make holy) im (people / nation), all these things shall be kalah (complete / finish).
I shamai (hearken / hear), but I didn't bayan (between): then I amar (spoke), my Adawan, what shall be the issue of these things?
He amar (spoke), Go your yalak (way), Danayaal (Daniel); for the dabar (word / matter) are satham (shut) up and chatham (sealed) until the ith (time) of the qatz (end).

Many shall barar (purify) themselves, and laban (make) themselves white, and be tzarap (refined); but the rashai (wicked) shall rashai (do) wickedly; and none of the rashai (wicked) shall bayan (between); but those who are shakal (wise) shall bayan (between).

From the ith (time) that the thamayad (continual) burnt offering shall be sawar (taken) away, and the shaqawatz (abomination) that shamam (makes) desolate nathan (give) up, there shall be one alap (thousand) two maah (hundred) thashaiyam (ninety) yawam (day).
Ashar (who/that) is he who chakah (waits), and nagai (comes) to the one alap (thousand) shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - chamash (five) yawam (day).
But go you your yalak (way) until the qatz (end); for you shall nawach (rest), and shall imad (stand) in your gawaral (lot), at the qatz (end) of the yawam (day).

The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah that came to Hawashai (Hosea) the ban (son) of Baaray (Beeri), in the yawam (day) of Izayah (Uzziah), Yawatham (Jotham), Achaz (Ahaz), and Chazaqayah (Hezekiah), malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and in the yawam (day) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Yawaash (Joash), malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).

When Yahawah amar (spoke) at thachalah (first) by Hawashai (Hosea), Yahawah amar (spoke) to Hawashai (Hosea), yalak (go), laqach (take / seized) for yourself a ashah (wife/individual woman) of prostitution and yalad (birth / begot) of unfaithfulness; for the aratz (Earth/land) zanah (commits) great adultery, forsaking Yahawah.
So he yalak (went) and laqach (take / seized) Gamar (Gomer) the bath (daughter) of Dabalayam (Diblaim); and she harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) him a ban (son).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, qaraa (called) his sham (name) Yazaraial (Jezreel); for yet a mait (little) while, and I will paqad (visit) the dam (blood) of Yazaraial (Jezreel) on the bayath (house) of Yahawaa (Jehu), and will cause the mamalakawath (kingdom) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) to shabath (shabath/rest).
It will happen in that yawam (day) that I will shabar (break) the qashath (bow) of Yasharaal (Israel) in the imaq (valley) of Yazaraial (Jezreel).

She harah (conceived) again, and yalad (birth / begot) a bath (daughter). Then he amar (spoke) to him, qaraa (called) her sham (name) laarachamah (lo-ruhamah); for I will no longer have racham (mercy) on the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), that I should in any way nashaa (lift) them.

But I will have racham (mercy) on the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah), and will yashai (salvation) them by Yahawah their Alahayam, and will not yashai (salvation) them by qashath (bow), charab (sword), malachamah (battle), sawas (horses), or horsemen.
Now when she had weaned laarachamah (lo-ruhamah), she harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son).
He amar (spoke), qaraa (called) his sham (name) laaimay (lo-ammi); for you are not my im (people / nation), and I will not be yours.

Yet the masapar (number) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) will be as the chawal (sand) of the yam (sea/waters), which can't be madad (measured) nor sapar (book); and it will come to pass that, in the maqawam (place) where it was amar (spoke) to them, ‘You are not my im (people / nation),’ they will be amar (spoke) ‘ban (son) of the chay (life) Al.’

The ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah) and the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) will be qabatz (gathered) yachad (together), and they will shawam (place / establish / appoint) themselves achad (one) raash (head), and will ilah (go up / offer) up from the aratz (Earth/land); for gadawal (very great/important/mighty) will be the yawam (day) of Yazaraial (Jezreel).
“Amar (spoke) to your brothers, ‘My im (people / nation)!’ And to your sisters, ‘My loved one!’

Contend with your mother! Contend, for she is not my wife, neither am I her husband; and let her shawam (place / establish / appoint) away her prostitution from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts;
Lest I strip her naked, and make her bare as in the day that she was born, and make her like a wilderness, and set her like a dry land, and kill her with thirst.
Indeed, on her children I will have no mercy; for they are children of unfaithfulness;

For their mother has played the prostitute. She who conceived them has done shamefully; for she said, ‘I will go after my lovers, who shawam (place / establish / appoint) me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink.’
Therefore, behold, I will hedge up your zanawan (way) with thorns, and I will build a wall against her, that she can't racham (find) her zanawan (way).

She will yalak (follow) after her lovers, but she won't overtake them; and she will seek them, but won't find them. Then she will amar (spoke), ‘I will yalak (go) and return to my first husband; for then was it better with me than kay (surely).’
For she did not know that I gave her the grain, the new wine, and the oil, and multiplied to her silver and gold, which they used for Baal.

Therefore I will nashag (take) shawab (turn back / repent) my grain in its raashawan (time), and my new wine in its season, and will pluck away my wool and my flax which should have covered her nakedness.
Now I will uncover her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and no one will nathan (give) her out of my hand.
I will also cause all her celebrations to shawab (turn back / repent): her mawaid (Feast/Holy Day), her new moons, her Sabbaths, and all her solemn mawaid (Feast/Holy Day).
I will lay waste her vines and her fig trees, about which she has said, ‘These are my wages that my lovers have given me; and I will make them a forest,’ and the animals of the field shall eat them.
I will visit on her the days of the Baals, to which she burned incense, when she decked herself with her earrings and her jewels, and went after her lovers, and forgot me,” says Yahawah.
"Therefore, behold, I will allure her, and shamam (bring) her into the wilderness, and amar (spoke) tenderly to her.

I will paqad (visit) her vineyards from there, and the valley of Achor for a door of hope; and she will respond there, as in the yawam (day) of her youth, and as in the yawam (day) when she yalak (came) up out of the land of Egypt.
It will be in that day," dabar (word / matter) Yahawah, “that you will call me ‘my husband,’ and no longer call me ‘my master.’
For I will nathan (give) away the names of the Baals out of her mouth, and they will no longer be ilah (go up / offer) by name.

In that yawam (day) I will make a covenant for them with the animals of the field, and with the birds of the sky, and with the creeping things of the ground. I will hayah (came to pass) the bow, the sword, and the battle out of the land, and will make them lie down safely.
I will betroth you to me forever. Yes, I will betroth you to me in righteousness, in justice, in loving kindness, and in compassion.
I will even betroth you to me in faithfulness; and you shall know Yahawah.
It will happen in that day, I will respond,” says Yahawah, I will respond to the heavens, and they will respond to the earth;
And the earth will respond to the grain, and the new wine, and the oil; and they will respond to Jezreel.

I will sow her to me in the aratz (Earth/land); and I will have naam (declares (prophetically)) on her who had not obtained naam (declares (prophetically)); and I will tell those who were not my naam (declares (prophetically)), ‘You are my naam (declares (prophetically));’ and they will inah (answer / respond), ‘My Alahayam!’

Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, yalak (go) again, ahab (love) a ashah (wife/individual woman) ahab (love) by rai (neigbor/another person), and an naap (adulteress), even as Yahawah ahabah (loves) the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), though they panah (turn) to other Alahayam, and ahab (love) cakes of raisins.
So I bought her for myself for fifteen pieces of kasap (silver) and a chamar (homer) and a lathak (half) of shairah (barley).

I amar (spoke) to her, You shall stay with me many yawam (day). You shall not zanah (play) the prostitute, and you shall not be with any other ayash (husband/individual man). I will also be so toward you.

For the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) shall live many yawam (day) without malak (king), and without shar (prince / ruler), and without zabach (sacrifice), and without sacred matzabah (stone), and without apawad (ephod) or tharapayam (idols).

Afterward the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) shall shawab (turn back / repent), and baqash (seek) Yahawah their Alahayam, and Dawad (David) their malak (king), and shall come with trembling to Yahawah and to his tawab (pleasant/functional) in the acharayath (last) yawam (day).

Shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, you ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel); for Yahawah has a charge against the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the aratz (Earth/land): Indeed there is no amath (truth), nor goodness, nor daith (knowledge) of Alahayam in the aratz (Earth/land).
There is alah (these), kachash (lying), ratzach (murder), ganab (stealing), and naap (committing) adultery; they paratz (break) boundaries, and bloodshed causes bloodshed.

Therefore the aratz (Earth/land) will abal (mourn), and everyone who yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein will waste away. All chay (life) things in her, even the animals of the shadah (field) and the iwap (flying) of the sky; yes, the dag (fish) of the yam (sea/waters) also asap (die).
Yet let no ayash (husband/individual man) bring a charge, neither let any yakach (man) accuse; For your im (people / nation) are like those who bring charges against a kahan (priest).

You will kashal (stumble / stagger) in the yawam (day), and the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) will also kashal (stumble / stagger) with you in the layal (night); and I will damah (destroy) your am (mother).

My im (people / nation) are damah (destroyed) for lack of daith (knowledge). Because you have maas (rejected) daith (knowledge), I will also maas (reject) you, that you may be no kahan (priest) to me. Because you have shakach (forgotten) your alahayam (Alahayam) thawarah (instruction), I will also shakach (forget) your ban (son).
As they were multiplied, so they chataa (sinned) against me. I will mawar (change) their kabawad (glory) into qalawan (shame).
They akal (eat) on the chataah (sin) of my im (people / nation), and nashaa (lift) their napash (living being/soul) on their iwan (guilt/iniquity).
It will be, like im (people / nation), like kahan (priest); and I will paqad (visit) them for their darak (ways), and will repay them for their deeds.
They will akal (eat), and not shabai (have) enough. They will zanah (play) the prostitute, and will not paratz (increase); because they have abandoned giving to Yahawah.
Prostitution, yayan (wine), and new thayarawash (wine) laqach (take / seized) away lab (heart).

My im (people / nation) shaal (consult) with their wooden idol, and answer to a stick of wood. Indeed the rawach (spirit / wind) of prostitution has led them thaih (astray), and they have been unfaithful to their Alahayam.

They zabach (sacrifice) on the raash (head) of the har (mountain), and qatar (burn) incense on the gabaih (hills), under alawan (oaks) and labanah (poplars) and terebinths, because its tzal (shade) is tawab (pleasant/functional). Therefore your bath (daughter) zanah (play) the prostitute, and your kalah (complete / finish) naap (commit) adultery.

I will not paqad (visit) your bath (daughter) when they zanah (play) the prostitute, nor your kalah (complete / finish) when they naap (commit) adultery; because the men consort with prostitutes, and they zabach (sacrifice) with the shrine prostitutes; so the im (people / nation) without bayan (between) will come to ruin.

Though you, Yasharaal (Israel), zanah (play) the prostitute, yet don't let Yahawadah (Judah) asham (offend); and don't bawaa (come) to Galagal (Gilgal), neither ilah (go up / offer) up to Bayathaawan (Beth) Aven, nor shabai (swear / take oath), ‘As Yahawah chay (life).’
For Yasharaal (Israel) has behaved extremely stubbornly, like a sarar (stubborn) parah (heifer). Then how will Yahawah raih (feed) them like a kabash (lamb) in a meadow.
Aparayam (Ephraim) is chabar (joined) to itzab (idols). Leave him yanach (alone)!
Their sabaa (drink) has become sawar (sour). They zanah (play) the prostitute zanah (continually). Her magan (shield) dearly ahab (love) their shameful qalawan (way).
The rawach (spirit / wind) has wrapped her up in its kanap (wings); and they shall be disappointed because of their zabach (sacrifices).

Shamai (hearken / hear) to this, you kahan (priest)! Listen, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), and azan (give) ear, bayath (house) of the malak (king)! For the mashapat (judgment) is against you; for you have been a pach (snare) Matzapah (at) Mizpah, and a rashath (net) parash (spread) on Thabawar (Tabor).
The rebels are imaq (deep) in shachat (slaughter); but I mawasar (discipline) all of them.
I yadai (know) Aparayam (Ephraim), and Yasharaal (Israel) is not kachad (hidden) from me; for now, Aparayam (Ephraim), you have zanah (played) the prostitute. Yasharaal (Israel) is tamaa (defiled).
Their deeds won't allow them to shawab (turn back / repent) to their Alahayam; for the rawach (spirit / wind) of prostitution is qarab (among / near) them, and they don't yadai (know) Yahawah.

The gaawan (pride) of Yasharaal (Israel) inah (answer / respond) to his panayam (face). Therefore Yasharaal (Israel) and Aparayam (Ephraim) will kashal (stumble / stagger) in their iwan (guilt/iniquity). Yahawadah (Judah) also will kashal (stumble / stagger) with them.
They will yalak (go) with their tzaan (flocks) and with their baqar (morning) to baqash (seek) Yahawah; but they won't matzaa (find) him. He has chalatz (withdrawn) himself from them.
They are bagad (unfaithful) to Yahawah; for they have yalad (birth / begot) illegitimate ban (son). Now the new chadash (month) will akal (eat) them with their fields.

Thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)) in Gabaih (Gibeah), and the chatzatzarah (trumpet) in Ramah (Ramah)! Rawai (sound) a battle cry at Bayathaawan (Beth) Aven, achar (other) you, Banayamayan (Benjamin)!

Aparayam (Ephraim) will become a shamah (desolation) in the yawam (day) of thawakachah (rebuke). Among the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), I yadai (have) made known that which will aman (believe / have faith) be.
The shar (prince / ruler) of Yahawadah (Judah) are like those who nasag (remove) a gabawal (border/boundary). I will shapak (pour) out my ibarah (wrath) on them like mayam (Waters).
Aparayam (Ephraim) is ishaq (oppressed), he is ratzatz (crushed) in mashapat (judgment); Because he is intent in his pursuit of idols.
Therefore I am to Aparayam (Ephraim) like a ish (made), and to the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) like raqab (rottenness).

When Aparayam (Ephraim) raah (see) his chalay (sickness), and Yahawadah (Judah) his mazawar (wound), Then Aparayam (Ephraim) yalak (went) to Ashawar (Assyria), and shalach (send) to malak (king) Yarab (Jareb): but he is not yakal (able) to rapaa (heal) you, neither will he gahah (cure) you of your mazawar (wound).

For I will be to Aparayam (Ephraim) like a shachal (lion), and like a young kapayar (lion) to the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah). I myself will tarap (tear) in pieces and yalak (go) away. I will nashaa (lift) off, and there will be no one to natzal (deliver).

I will yalak (go) and shawab (turn back / repent) to my maqawam (place), until they acknowledge their offense, and baqash (seek) my panayam (face). In their tzar (oppressor / distressor) they will shachar (seek) me earnestly.
Yalak (come), and let us shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah; for he has tarap (torn) us to pieces, and he will rapaa (heal) us; he has injured us, and he will chabash (bind) up our wounds.
After yawam (day) days he will chayah (revive) us. On the shalayashay (third) yawam (day) he will qawam (rise up) us up, and we will chayah (live) panayam (before) him.

Yadai (let) us acknowledge Yahawah. Let us press on to yadai (know) Yahawah. As surely as the sun rises, Yahawah will appear. He will bawaa (come) to us like the rain, like the spring rain that waters the aratz (Earth/land).

Aparayam (Ephraim), what shall I ishah (make) to you? Yahawadah (Judah), what shall I ishah (make) to you? For your chasad (grace) is like a baqar (morning) inan (cloud), and like the tal (dew) that disappears shakam (early).

Therefore I have chatzab (cut) them to pieces with the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy); I harag (killed) them with the amar (spoke) of my pah (mouth). Your mashapat (judgments) are like a flash of awar (light).
For I chapatz (desire) chasad (grace), and not zabach (sacrifice); and the daith (knowledge) of Alahayam more than burnt ilah (offerings).
But they, like Adam, ibar (pass over/through) broken the barayath (covenant). They were bagad (unfaithful) to me, there.
Galaid (Gilead) is a qarayah (city) of those who pail (work) awan (iniquity); it is stained with dam (blood).

As gangs of robbers chakah (wait) to ambush a ayash (husband/individual man), so the chabar (company) of kahan (priest) ratzach (murder) in the darak (way) toward Shechem, ishah (make) shameful zamah (crimes).
In the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) I raah (see) seen a shairawarah (horrible) thing. There is prostitution in Aparayam (Ephraim). Yasharaal (Israel) is tamaa (defiled).
Also, Yahawadah (Judah), there is a qatzayar (harvest) shayath (put / appoint / make) for you, when I shawab (turn back / repent) the fortunes of my im (people / nation).

When I would rapaa (heal) Yasharaal (Israel), then the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of Aparayam (Ephraim) is galah (uncovered), also the rai (wickedness) of Shamarawan (Samaria); for they pail (commit) falsehood, and the ganab (thief) bawaa (come) in, and the gang of robbers ravages outside.
They don't amar (spoke) in their labab (hearts) that I zakar (remembrance/memory) all their rai (wickedness). Now their own deeds have engulfed them. They are before my panayam (face).
They make the malak (king) shamach (glad) with their rai (wickedness), and the shar (prince / ruler) with their kachash (lies).

They are all naap (adulterers). They are bair (burning) like an thanawar (oven) that the baker stops iwar (rouse / awaken), from the lawash (kneading) of the batzaq (dough), until it is chamatz (leavened).
On the yawam (day) of our malak (king), the shar (prince / ruler) chalah (afflict) themselves sick with the chamah (heat) of yayan (wine). He joined his yad (hand) with mockers.

For they have prepared their lab (heart) like an thanawar (oven), while they lie in arab (wait). Their baker sleeps all the layal (night). In the baqar (morning) it bair (burns) as a lahabah (flaming) ash (fire).
They are all chamam (hot) as an thanawar (oven), and akal (eat) their shapat (judges). All their malak (king) napal (fall / be cast down) fallen. There is no one among them who qaraa (called) to me.
Aparayam (Ephraim), he mixes himself among the im (people / nation). Aparayam (Ephraim) is a pancake not hapak (turned) over.

Strangers have akal (eat) his kach (strength / mighty / power), and he doesn't realize it. Indeed, shayabah (old age / white hair (due to age)) hairs are here and there on him, and he doesn't realize it.
The gaawan (pride) of Yasharaal (Israel) inah (answer / respond) to his panayam (face); yet they haven't shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah their Alahayam, nor baqash (sought) him, for all this.
Aparayam (Ephraim) is like an easily pathah (deceived) yawanah (dove), without lab (heart). They qaraa (called) to Matzarayam (Egypt). They halak (move) to Ashawar (Assyria).

When they yalak (go), I will parash (spread) my rashath (net) on them. I will yarad (bring) them down like the iwap (flying) of the sky. I will yasar (chastise) them, as their idah (congregation) has shamai (heard).

Away (woe) to them! For they have nadad (wandered) from me. Shad (destruction) to them! For they have trespassed against me. Though I would padah (redeem) them, yet they have dabar (word / matter) kazab (lies) against me.

They haven't zaiq (cried) to me with their lab (heart), but they yalal (howl) on their mashakab (beds). They gawar (assemble) themselves for grain and new thayarawash (wine). They sawar (turn) away from me.
Though I have yasar (taught) and chazaq (strengthened) their zarawai (arms), yet they plot rai (evil) against me.

They shawab (turn back / repent), but not to the Most il (over). They are like a faulty qashath (bow). Their shar (prince / ruler) will napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword) for the zaim (rage) of their lashawan (tongue/language). Zaw (this) will be their laig (derision) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

Put the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)) to your lips! Something like an nashar (eagle) is over yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) bayath (house), because they ibar (pass over/through) broken my barayath (covenant), and pashai (rebelled) against my thawarah (instruction).
They zaiq (cry) to me, ‘My Alahayam, we Israel yadai (acknowledge) you!’
Yasharaal (Israel) has zanach (cast) off that which is tawab (pleasant/functional). The ayab (enemy) will radap (pursue) him.

They have set up malak (king), but not by me. They have made sharar (princes), and I didn't approve. Of their kasap (silver) and their zahab (gold) they ishah (make) made themselves itzab (idols), that they may be karath (cut) off.
