Let Shamarawan (Samaria) throw out his igal (calf) idol! My ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) charah (hot with anger) against them! How long will it be until they are capable of purity?
For this is even from Yasharaal (Israel)! The charash (workman) ishah (make) it, and it is no Alahayam; indeed, the igal (calf) of Shamarawan (Samaria) shall be shabab (broken) in pieces.

For they zarai (sow) the rawach (spirit / wind), and they will qatzar (reap) the sawapah (whirlwind). He has no standing grain. The stalk will ishah (make) no qamach (head). If it ishah (make) yield, strangers will balai (swallow) it up.
Yasharaal (Israel) is balai (swallowed) up. Now they are among the gaway (nation / people) like a worthless thing.
For they have ilah (go up / offer) up to Ashawar (Assyria), like a paraa (wild) donkey wandering badad (alone). Aparayam (Ephraim) has thanah (hired) ahab (love) for himself.

But although they sold themselves among the gaway (nation / people), I will now qabatz (gather) them; and they begin to waste mashaa (away) because of the oppression of the malak (king) of mighty ones.
Because Aparayam (Ephraim) rabah (has) multiplied mazabach (altars) for chataa (sinning), they became for him mazabach (altars) for chataa (sinning).
I kathab (wrote) for him the many things of my thawarah (instruction); but they were chashab (regarded) as a zawar (strange) thing.

As for the zabach (sacrifices) of my habahab (offerings), they zabach (sacrifice) bashar (flesh) and akal (eat) it; But Yahawah doesn't ratzah (accept) them. Now he will zakar (remembrance/memory) their iwan (guilt/iniquity), and paqad (visit) their chataah (sin). They will shawab (turn back / repent) to Matzarayam (Egypt).

For Yasharaal (Israel) has shakach (forgotten) his Maker and banah (built) hayakal (palaces); and Yahawadah (Judah) rabah (has) multiplied batzar (fortified) iyar (cities); but I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on his iyar (cities), and it will akal (eat) its fortresses.

Don't shamach (rejoice), Yasharaal (Israel), to jubilation like the im (people / nation); for you were unfaithful to your Alahayam. You ahab (love) the wages of a prostitute at every grain garan (threshing) floor.
The garan (threshing) floor and the yaqab (winepress) won't raih (feed) them, and the new thayarawash (wine) will kachash (fail) her.

They won't yashab (inhabit/dwell) in yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) aratz (Earth/land); but Aparayam (Ephraim) will shawab (turn back / repent) to Matzarayam (Egypt), and they will akal (eat) tamaa (unclean) food in Ashawar (Assyria).

They won't nasak (pour) out yayan (wine) offerings to Yahawah, neither will they be pleasing to him. Their zabach (sacrifices) will be to them like the lacham (bread) of awan (mourners); akal (eat) who eat of it will be tamaa (polluted); for their lacham (bread) napash (living being/soul) be for their appetite. It will not bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
What will you ishah (make) in the yawam (day) of mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) assembly, and in the yawam (day) of the chag (feast/festival) of Yahawah?

For, behold, they have halak (move) away from shad (destruction). Matzarayam (Egypt) will qabatz (gather) them up. Map (Memphis) will qabar (bury) them. Qamawash (nettles) will yarash (possess) their machamad (pleasant) things of kasap (silver). Chawach (thorns) will be in their ahal (tents).

The yawam (day) of paqadah (visitation) bawaa (come) come. The yawam (day) of reckoning bawaa (come) come. Yasharaal (Israel) yadai (will) consider the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) to be a awayal (fool), and the ayash (husband/individual man) who is inspired to be insane, because of the rab (abundance) of your iwan (guilt/iniquity), and because your hostility is rab (great).
A nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) watches over Aparayam (Ephraim) with my Alahayam. A yaqawash (fowler's) pach (snare) is on all of his darak (paths), and hostility in the bayath (house) of his Alahayam.

They imaq (have) deeply shachath (corrupted) themselves, as in the yawam (day) of Gabaih (Gibeah). He will zakar (remembrance/memory) their iwan (guilt/iniquity). He will paqad (visit) them for their chataah (sin).

I matzaa (found) Yasharaal (Israel) like inab (grapes) in the madabar (wilderness). I raah (see) your ab (father) as the bakawarah (first) ripe in the thaan (fig) tree at its raashayath (beginning) season; but they bawaa (come) to Bailapaiwar (Baal) Peor, and nazar (crown / consecrate) themselves to the shameful thing, and became abominable ahab (love) that which they loved.
As for Aparayam (Ephraim), their kabawad (glory) will iwap (flying) away like a iwap (flying). There will be no yalad (birth / begot), none with child, and no harawan (conception).
Though they gadal (bring) up their ban (son), yet I will shakal (bereave) them, so that not a adam (man) shall be left. Indeed, away (woe) also to them when I sawar (depart) from them!

I raah (see) seen Aparayam (Ephraim), like Tzar (Tyre), shathal (planted) in a nawah (habitation) place; but Aparayam (Ephraim) will yatzaa (go out / come out) out his ban (son) to the harag (murderer).
Nathan (give) them—Yahweh what will you nathan (give)? Nathan (give) them a shakal (miscarrying) racham (womb) and tzamaq (dry) shad (breasts).

All their rai (wickedness) is in Galagal (Gilgal); for there I shanaa (hate) them. Because of the rai (wickedness) of their deeds I will garash (drive) them out of my bayath (house)! I will ahabah (love) them no more. All their shar (prince / ruler) are rebels.

Aparayam (Ephraim) is nakah (struck). Their sharash (root) has yabash (dry land) up. They will ishah (make) no paray (fruit). Even though they yalad (birth / begot) forth, yet I will mawath (death) the machamad (beloved) ones of their batan (womb).
My Alahayam will maas (cast) them away, because they did not shamai (hearken / hear) to him; and they will be wanderers among the gaway (nation / people).

Yasharaal (Israel) is a luxuriant gapan (vine) that puts shawah (forth) his paray (fruit). According to the rab (abundance) of his paray (fruit) he rabah (has) multiplied his mazabach (altars). As their aratz (Earth/land) has prospered, they have adorned their sacred matzabah (stones).
Their lab (heart) is chalaq (divided). Now they will be asham (found) guilty. He will demolish their mazabach (altars). He will shadad (destroy) their sacred matzabah (stones).
Surely now they will amar (spoke), We have no malak (king); for we don't yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah; and the malak (king), what can he ishah (make) for us?

They make dabar (word / matter), alah (these) shawaa (vanity) in karath (cut) barayath (covenant). Therefore mashapat (judgment) parach (springs) up like poisonous weeds in the thalam (furrows) of the shadah (field).

The shakan (inhabitants) of Shamarawan (Samaria) will be in terror for the calves of Bayathaawan (Beth) Aven; for its im (people / nation) will abal (mourn) over it, Along with its kamar (priests) who gayal (rejoiced) over it, for its kabawad (glory), because it has departed from it.

It also will be yabal (carried) to Ashawar (Assyria) for a manachah (present) to a great malak (king). Aparayam (Ephraim) will laqach (take / seized) bashanah (shame), and Yasharaal (Israel) will be bawash (ashamed) of his own itzah (counsel).
Shamarawan (Samaria) and her malak (king) float away, like a twig on the mayam (Waters).

The bamah (high) places also of Aven, the chataah (sin) of Yasharaal (Israel), will be destroyed. The qawatz (thorn) and the daradar (thistle) will ilah (go up / offer) up on their mazabach (altars). They will amar (spoke) the har (mountain), "kasah (cover) us!" And the gabaih (hills), napal (fall / be cast down) on us!

Yasharaal (Israel), you have chataa (sinned) from the yawam (day) of Gabaih (Gibeah). There they imad (remained). The malachamah (battle) against the ban (son) of ilawah (iniquity) doesn't nashag (overtake) them in Gabaih (Gibeah).
When it is my awah (desire), I will yasar (chastise) them; and the im (people / nation) will be asap (gathered) against them, when they are asar (bound) to their shanayam (two) iyan (eye).

Aparayam (Ephraim) is a trained igalah (heifer) that ahab (love) to dawash (thresh); so I will ibar (pass over/through) a yoke on her beautiful tzawaar (neck). I will rakab (set) a rider on Aparayam (Ephraim). Yahawadah (Judah) will charash (plow). Yaiqab (Jacob) will shadad (break) his clods.

Zarai (sow) to yourselves in tzadaqah (righteousness), qatzar (reap) according to chasad (grace). Nayar (break) up your fallow nayar (ground); for it is ith (time) to darash (seek) Yahawah, until he bawaa (come) and rains tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) on you.

You have charash (plowed) rashai (wickedness). You have qatzar (reaped) iwal (iniquity). You have akal (eat) the paray (fruit) of kachash (lies), for you batach (trusted) in your darak (way), in the rab (multitude) of your gabawar (mighty) men.

Therefore a battle roar will qawam (rise up) among your im (people / nation), and all your fortresses will be shadad (destroyed), as Shalaman (Shalman) destroyed Bayathaarabaal (Beth) Arbel in the yawam (day) of malachamah (battle). The am (mother) was ratash (dashed) in pieces with her ban (son).
So Bayathaal (Bethel) will ishah (make) to you panayam (because) of your rai (great) rai (wickedness). At daybreak the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) will be damah (destroyed).
When Yasharaal (Israel) was a nair (child), then I ahab (love) him, and qaraa (called) my ban (son) out of Matzarayam (Egypt).
They qaraa (called) to them, so they halak (move) from them. They zabach (sacrificed) to the Bail (Baals), and qatar (burned) incense to engraved pasayal (images).
Yet I tharagal (taught) Aparayam (Ephraim) to walk. I laqach (take / seized) them by his zarawai (arms); but they didn't yadai (know) that I rapaa (healed) them.

I mashak (drew) them with chabal (cords) of a adam (man), with ties of ahabah (love); and I was to them like those who rawam (will lift up) up the il (over) on their necks; and I bent down to him and I akal (eat) him.

They won't shawab (turn back / repent) into the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt); but the Ashawar (Assyrian) will be their malak (king), because they maan (refused) to shawab (turn back / repent).
The charab (sword) will chawal (fall) on their iyar (cities), and will kalah (complete / finish) the bad (bars) of their gates, and will put an end to their plans.
My im (people / nation) are determined to mashawabah (turn) from me. Though they qaraa (called) to the Most il (over), he certainly won't rawam (will lift up) them.

“How can I nathan (give) you up, Aparayam (Ephraim)? How can I magan (hand) you over, Yasharaal (Israel)? How can I nathan (give) you like Adamah (Admah)? How can I nathan (give) you like Tzabaayam (Zeboiim)? My lab (heart) is hapak (turned) within me, my compassion is aroused.

I will not ishah (make) the charawan (fierceness) of my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting). I will not shawab (turn back / repent) to shachath (destroy) Aparayam (Ephraim): for I am Al, and not ayash (husband/individual man); the qadawash (holy) One in the qarab (among / near) of you; and I will not bawaa (come) in iyar (wrath).
They will yalak (walk) achar (other) Yahawah, who will shaag (roar) like a aray (lion); for he will shaag (roar), and the ban (son) will come charad (trembling) from the yam (sea/waters).

They will come charad (trembling) like a tzapawar (bird) out of Matzarayam (Egypt), and like a yawanah (dove) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Ashawar (Assyria); and I will yashab (inhabit/dwell) them in their bayath (house),” naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

Aparayam (Ephraim) surrounds me with falsehood, and the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) with maramah (deceit). Yahawadah (Judah) still strays from Al, and is unfaithful to the qadawash (holy) One.
Aparayam (Ephraim) feeds on wind, and chases the east wind. He continually multiplies kachash (lies) and desolation. They sabab (make) a covenant with Assyria, and oil is sabab (carried) into Egypt.
Yahawah also has a controversy with Judah, and will punish Jacob according to his ways; according to his deeds he will repay him.
In the womb he took his brother by the heel; and in his manhood he contended with Alahayam.
Indeed, he struggled with the alahayam (Alahayam), and prevailed; he wept, and made supplication to him. He found him at Bethel, and there he spoke with us,
Even Yahawah, the Alahayam of Armies; Yahawah is his dabar (word / matter) of renown!
Therefore turn to your Alahayam. Keep kindness and justice, and wait continually for your Alahayam.
A merchant has dishonest scales in his hand. He chasad (grace) to defraud.
Ephraim said, Surely I have become rich, I have found myself wealth. In all my wealth they won't find in me any iniquity that is sin.
But I am Yahawah your Alahayam from the land of Egypt. I will yet again ishar (make) you dwell in tents, as in the days of the solemn feast.
I have also spoken to the ahal (prophets), and I have multiplied visions; and by the ministry of the ahal (prophets) I have used parables.
If Gilead is wicked, surely they are worthless. In Gilgal they sacrifice bulls. Indeed, their altars are like rabah (heaps) in the furrows of the field.
Jacob fled into the shadah (country) of Aram, and Israel served to get a wife, and for a wife he tended flocks and herds.
By a prophet Yahawah ibad (servant) Yasharaal (Israel) up out of Egypt, and by a prophet he was shamar (keep/guard).
Ephraim has bitterly provoked anger. Therefore his blood will be left on him, and his Adawan will repay his contempt.
When Aparayam (Ephraim) dabar (word / matter), there was rathath (trembling). He nashaa (lift) himself in Yasharaal (Israel), but when he became asham (guilty) in Bail (Baal), he mawath (death).

Now they chataa (sin) more and more, and ishah (make) made themselves masakah (molten) images of their kasap (silver), even itzab (idols) according to their own thabawan (understanding), all of them the maishah (work) of the craftsmen. They amar (spoke) of them, ‘They offer human zabach (sacrifice) and nashaq (kiss) the calves.’

Therefore they will be like the baqar (morning) mist, and like the tal (dew) that passes halak (move) shakam (early), like the matz (chaff) that is sair (driven) with the whirlwind out of the garan (threshing) floor, and like the ishan (smoke) out of the arabah (chimney).
Yet I am Yahawah your Alahayam from the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt); and you shall yadai (acknowledge) no Alahayam but me, and balathay (besides) me there is no savior.
I yadai (knew) you in the madabar (wilderness), in the aratz (Earth/land) of thalaawabah (great) drought.
According to their maraiyath (pasture), so were they shabai (filled); they were shabai (filled), and their lab (heart) was rawam (will lift up). Therefore they have shakach (forgotten) me.
Therefore I am like a shachal (lion) to them. Like a namar (leopard), I will lurk by the darak (path).

I will pagash (meet) them like a dab (bear) that is shakawal (bereaved) of her cubs, and will qarai (tear) the covering of their lab (heart). There I will akal (eat) them like a labayaa (lioness). The shadah (wild) animal will baqai (tear) them.
You are shachath (destroyed), Yasharaal (Israel), because you are against me, against your izar (help).

Apaw (where) is your malak (king) now, that he may yashai (salvation) you in all your iyar (cities)? And your shapat (judges), of whom you amar (spoke), ‘nathan (give) me a malak (king) and shar (prince / ruler)?’
I nathan (give) given you a malak (king) in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and have laqach (take / seized) him away in my ibarah (wrath).
The iwan (guilt/iniquity) of Aparayam (Ephraim) is stored up. His chataah (sin) is stored up.
The chabal (sorrows) of a travailing yalad (birth / begot) will bawaa (come) on him. He is an unwise ban (son); for when it is ith (time), he doesn't come to the opening of the womb.

I will padah (ransom) them from the yad (hand) of shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife). I will gaal (redeem) them from mawath (death)! Mawath (death), where are your dabar (word / matter)? Shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife), where is your qatab (destruction)? Compassion ahay (will) be sathar (hidden) from my iyan (eye).

Though he is paraa (fruitful) among his ach (brother/kinsman), an east qadayam (wind) will bawaa (come), the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah ilah (go up / offer) up from the madabar (wilderness); and his maqawar (spring) will bawash (become) dry, and his maiyan (fountain) will be charab (dried) up. He will plunder the storehouse of awatzar (treasure).

Shamarawan (Samaria) will bear her asham (guilt); for she has marah (rebelled) against her Alahayam. They will napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword). Their iwalal (infants) will be ratash (dashed) in pieces, and their pregnant women will be baqai (ripped) open.
Israel, return to Yahawah your Alahayam; for you have napal (fall / be cast down) because of your sin.

Shawab (turn back / repent) words with you, and shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah. Tell him, Forgive all our iwan (guilt/iniquity), and accept that which is good: so we offer our lips like bulls.
Assyria can't save us. We won't ride on horses; neither will we amar (spoke) any more to the dabar (word / matter) of our hands, ‘Our Alahayam!’ For in you the fatherless finds mercy.
I will heal their waywardness. I will racham (love) them freely; for my anger is turned away from him.
I will be like the dew to Israel. He will blossom like the lily, and send down his roots like Lebanon.
His branches will parach (spread), and his beauty will be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like Labanawan (Lebanon).
Men will live in his shade. They will revive like the grain, and blossom like the vine. Their fragrance will be like the wine of Labanawan (Lebanon).
Ephraim, what have I to do any more with idols? I shawab (turn back / repent), and will take care of him. I am like a green fir tree; from me your fruit is found.
Who is wise, that he may understand these things? Who is prudent, that he may know them? For the ways of Yahawah are right, and the righteous walk in them; But the rebellious stumble in them.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah that came to Yawaal (Joel), the ban (son) of Pathawaal (Pethuel).

Shamai (hearken / hear) this, you zaqan (elders), And listen, all you yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the aratz (Earth/land). Has this ever happened in your yawam (day), or in the yawam (day) of your ab (father)?
Sapar (book) your ban (son) about it, and have your ban (son) tell their ban (son), and their ban (son), achar (other) dawar (generation / age / period).

What the swarming locust has yathar (left), the great arabah (locust) has akal (eat). What the great arabah (locust) has yathar (left), the grasshopper has akal (eat). What the grasshopper has yathar (left), the chasayal (caterpillar) has akal (eat).
Qawatz (wake) up, you drunkards, and bakah (weep)! Wail, all you drinkers of yayan (wine), because of the sweet isayas (wine); for it is karath (cut) off from your pah (mouth).

For a gaway (nation / people) has ilah (go up / offer) up on my aratz (Earth/land), itzawam (strong), and without masapar (number). His shan (teeth) are the shan (teeth) of a aray (lion), and he has the fangs of a labayaa (lioness).

He has shawam (place / establish / appoint) my gapan (vine) shamah (waste), and stripped my thaan (fig) tree. He has stripped its bark, and shalak (thrown) it away. Its branches are laban (made) white.
Mourn like a bathawalah (virgin) dressed in sackcloth for the bail (husband) of her naiwar (youth)!

The meal manachah (offering) and the drink nasak (offering) are karath (cut) off from yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) bayath (house). The kahan (priest), yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) sharath (ministers), abal (mourn).

The shadah (field) is laid shadad (waste). The adamah (land) abal (mourns), for the grain is shadad (destroyed), The new thayarawash (wine) has yabash (dry land) up, and the yatzahar (fresh oil) languishes.
Be bawash (confounded), you farmers! Wail, you vineyard keepers; for the chatah (wheat) and for the shairah (barley); for the qatzayar (harvest) of the shadah (field) abad (destroy/perish) perished.

The gapan (vine) has yabash (dry land) up, and the thaan (fig) tree withered; the ramawan (pomegranate) tree, the palm tree also, and the thapawach (apple) tree, even all of the itz (trees) of the shadah (field) are yabash (dry land); for shashawan (joy) has yabash (dry land) away from the ban (son) of adam (men).

Chagar (put) on sackcloth and sapad (mourn), you kahan (priest)! Wail, you sharath (ministers) of the mazabach (altar). Bawaa (come), lie all lawan (night) in sackcloth, you sharath (ministers) of my Alahayam, for the meal manachah (offering) and the drink nasak (offering) are withheld from your alahayam (Alahayam) bayath (house).

Qadash (set apart/make holy) a tzawam (fast). Qaraa (called) a solemn itzarah (assembly). Asap (gather) the zaqan (elders), and all the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the aratz (Earth/land), to the bayath (house) of Yahawah, your Alahayam, and zaiq (cry) to Yahawah.
Ahah (alas) for the yawam (day)! For the yawam (day) of Yahawah is at qarawab (hand), and it will bawaa (come) as shad (destruction) from the Shaday.
Isn't the akal (food) karath (cut) off before our iyan (eye); shamachah (joy) and gayal (gladness) from the bayath (house) of our Alahayam?
The paradah (seeds) rot under their magarapah (clods). The granaries are shamam (laid) desolate. The barns are haras (broken) down, for the grain has yabash (dry land).
How the animals anach (groan)! The idar (herds) of livestock are perplexed, because they have no maraih (pasture). Yes, the idar (flocks) of tzaan (sheep) are asham (made) desolate.

Yahawah, I qaraa (called) to you, For the ash (fire) has akal (eat) the naah (pastures) of the madabar (wilderness), and the lahabah (flame) has lahat (burned) all the itz (trees) of the shadah (field).

Yes, the animals of the shadah (field) irag (pant) to you, for the mayam (Waters) apayaq (brooks) have yabash (dry land) up, And the ash (fire) has akal (eat) the naah (pastures) of the madabar (wilderness).

Thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)) in Tzayawan (Zion), and rawai (sound) an alarm in my qadash (set apart/make holy) har (mountain)! Let all the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the aratz (Earth/land) ragaz (tremble), for the yawam (day) of Yahawah bawaa (come), for it is close at qarawab (hand):

A yawam (day) of chashak (darkness) and apalah (gloominess), a yawam (day) of inan (cloud) and irapal (thick) darkness. As the dawn parash (spreading) on the har (mountain), a rab (great) and itzawam (strong) im (people / nation); there has iwalam (forever) been the like, neither will there be any more achar (other) them, even to the shanah (years) of many dawar (generation / age / period).

A ash (fire) akal (eat) panayam (before) them, and achar (other) them, a lahabah (flame) lahat (burns). The aratz (Earth/land) is as the gan (garden) of Idan (Eden) panayam (before) them, and achar (other) them, a shamamah (desolate) madabar (wilderness). Yes, and no one has palayatah (escaped) them.
Their maraah (appearance) is as the maraah (appearance) of sawas (horses), and as horsemen, so do they rawatz (run).

Like the qawal (sound / voice) of marakabah (chariots) on the raash (head) of the har (mountain) do they raqad (leap), like the qawal (sound / voice) of a lahab (flame) of ash (fire) that akal (eat) the qash (stubble), as a itzawam (strong) im (people / nation) set in malachamah (battle) irak (array).
At their panayam (presence) the im (people / nation) are in anguish. All panayam (faces) have grown pale.

They rawatz (run) like gabawar (mighty) men. They ilah (go up / offer) the chawamah (wall) like malachamah (warriors). They ayash (husband/individual man) yalak (march) in his line, and they don't swerve off course.
Neither does ayash (husband/individual man) jostle ach (brother/kinsman); they yalak (march) everyone in his masalah (path), and they burst through the defenses, and don't break ranks.
They rush on the iyar (city). They rawatz (run) on the chawamah (wall). They ilah (go up / offer) up into the bayath (house). They bawaa (come) in at the chalawan (windows) like thieves.

The aratz (Earth/land) ragaz (quakes) panayam (before) them. The shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) raish (tremble). The shamash (sun) and the yarach (moon) are qadar (darkened), and the kawakab (star) asap (withdraw) their nagah (shining).

Yahawah thunders his qawal (sound / voice) panayam (before) his chayal (army); for his forces are very rab (great); for he is itzawam (strong) who obeys his command; for the yawam (day) of Yahawah is gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and very awesome, and who kawal (all/every/entire) endure it?

"Yet even now," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, shawab (turn back / repent) to me with all your labab (heart), and with tzawam (fasting), and with bakay (weeping), and with masapad (mourning).

Qarai (tear) your labab (heart), and not your bagad (garments), and shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah, your Alahayam; for he is chanawan (gracious) and rachawam (merciful), arak (slow) to ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and abundant in loving chasad (grace), and relents from sending rai (calamity).

Who yadai (knows)? He may shawab (turn back / repent) and relent, and shaar (leave) a barakah (blessing) achar (other) him, even a meal manachah (offering) and a drink nasak (offering) to Yahawah, your Alahayam.
Thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)) in Tzayawan (Zion)! Qadash (set apart/make holy) a tzawam (fast). Qaraa (called) a solemn itzarah (assembly).

Asap (gather) the im (people / nation). Qadash (set apart/make holy) the qahal (assembly). Qabatz (assemble) the zaqan (elders). Asap (gather) the iwalal (children), and those who yanaq (nurse) from shad (breasts). Let the chathan (bridegroom) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from his room, and the kalah (complete / finish) out of her room.

Let the kahan (priest), the sharath (ministers) of Yahawah, bakah (weep) between the awalam (porch) and the mazabach (altar), and let them amar (spoke), chawas (spare) your im (people / nation), Yahawah, and don't nathan (give) your nachalah (heritage) to charapah (reproach), that the gaway (nation / people) should mashal (rule/have dominion) over them. Why should they amar (spoke) among the im (people / nation), ‘Where is their Alahayam?’
Then Yahawah was qanaa (jealous) for his aratz (Earth/land), And chamal (had) pity on his im (people / nation).

Yahawah inah (answer / respond) his im (people / nation), "Behold, I will shalach (send) you grain, new thayarawash (wine), and yatzahar (fresh oil), and you will be shabai (satisfied) with them; and I will no more nathan (give) you a charapah (reproach) among the gaway (nation / people).

But I will remove the tzapawanay (northern) army rachaq (far) away from you, and will nadach (drive) it into a tzayah (barren) and shamamah (desolate) aratz (Earth/land), its panayam (front) into the eastern yam (sea/waters), and its back into the western yam (sea/waters); and its stench will ilah (go up / offer) up, and its bad smell will ilah (go up / offer)." Ishah (make) he has done gadal (great) things.
Adamah (land), don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). Be gayal (glad) and shamach (rejoice), for Yahawah ishah (make) done gadal (great) things.

Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), you animals of the shadah (field); for the naah (pastures) of the madabar (wilderness) dashaa (spring) up, for the itz (tree) nashaa (lift) its paray (fruit). The thaan (fig) tree and the gapan (vine) nathan (give) their chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor).

Be gayal (glad) then, you ban (son) of Tzayawan (Zion), and shamach (rejoice) in Yahawah, your Alahayam; for he nathan (give) you the former mawarah (rain) in just measure, and he causes the gasham (rain) to yarad (come) down for you, the former mawarah (rain) and the malaqawash (latter) rain, as raashawan (before).
The garan (threshing) floors will be malaa (full) of bar (wheat), and the vats will shawaq (overflow) with new thayarawash (wine) and yatzahar (fresh oil).

I will shalam (restore) to you the shanah (years) that the swarming arabah (locust) has akal (eat), the great locust, the grasshopper, and the caterpillar, my gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), which I shalach (send) among you.

You will have akal (eat) to akal (eat), and be shabai (satisfied), and will halal (praise) the sham (name) of Yahawah, your Alahayam, who ishah (make) dealt wondrously with you; and my im (people / nation) will iwalam (forever) again be disappointed.

You yadai (will) know that I am in the qarab (among / near) of Yasharaal (Israel), and that I am Yahawah, your Alahayam, and there is no one else; and my im (people / nation) will iwalam (forever) again be disappointed.

It will happen afterward, that I will shapak (pour) out my rawach (spirit / wind) on all bashar (flesh); and your ban (son) and your bath (daughter) will nabaa (prophesy). Your zaqan (old) men will dream chalawam (dreams). Your bachawar (young) men will raah (see) chazayawan (visions).
And also on the ibad (servant) and on the handmaids in those yawam (day), I will shapak (pour) out my rawach (spirit / wind).
I will show mawapath (wonders) in the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) and in the aratz (Earth/land): dam (blood), ash (fire), and thayamarah (pillars) of ishan (smoke).

The shamash (sun) will be hapak (turned) into chashak (darkness), and the yarach (moon) into dam (blood), panayam (before) the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and yaraa (fear / be afraid) yawam (day) of Yahawah bawaa (come).

It will happen that whoever will qaraa (called) on the sham (name) of Yahawah shall be malat (saved); for in har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion) and in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) there will be those who palayatah (escape), as Yahawah has amar (spoke), and among the sharayad (remnant), those whom Yahawah qaraa (called).
For, behold, in those hayah (came to pass), and in that il (over), when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,

I will gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat; and I will execute judgment on them there for my people, and for my heritage, Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations. They il (over) divided my land,
And have nathan (give) lots for my people, and nathan (give) given a boy for a prostitute, and sold a girl for wine, that they may drink.
Yes, and what are you to me, Tyre, and Sidon, and all the regions of Philistia? Will you repay me? And if you repay me, I will swiftly and speedily return your repayment on your own head.
Because you have taken my silver and my gold, and hayah (came to pass) carried my finest treasures into your temples,

And have makar (sold) the ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah) and the ban (son) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) to the sons of the Yawanay (Greeks), that you may rachaq (remove) them far from their gabawal (border/boundary).
Behold, I will iwar (rouse / awaken) them up out of the maqawam (place) where you have makar (sold) them, and will shawab (turn back / repent) your repayment on your own raash (head);

And I will makar (sell) your ban (son) and your bath (daughter) into the yad (hand) of the ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah), and they will makar (sell) them to the men of Sheba, to a faraway gaway (nation / people), for Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) it.

Qaraa (called) this among the gaway (nation / people): "qadash (set apart/make holy) for malachamah (war)! Iwar (rouse / awaken) up the gabawar (mighty) men. Let all the malachamah (warriors) nagash (draw) near. Let them ilah (go up / offer) up.
Kathath (beat) your ath (entirety) into charab (sword), and your mazamarah (pruning) hooks into ramach (spears). Let the chalash (weak) amar (spoke), ‘I am gabawar (strong).’
Hurry and bawaa (come), all you surrounding gaway (nation / people), and gather yourselves qabatz (together)." Cause your gabawar (mighty) ones to nachath (come) down there, Yahawah.

Let the gaway (nation / people) arouse themselves, and ilah (go up / offer) up to the imaq (valley) of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat); for there will I yashab (inhabit/dwell) to shapat (judge) all the surrounding gaway (nation / people).

Shalach (send) in the magal (sickle); for the qatzayar (harvest) is ripe. Bawaa (come), tread, for the gath (winepress) is malaa (full), the vats shawaq (overflow), for their rai (wickedness) is rab (great).
Hamawan (multitudes), hamawan (multitudes) in the imaq (valley) of charawatz (decision)! For the yawam (day) of Yahawah is qarawab (near), in the imaq (valley) of charawatz (decision).
The shamash (sun) and the yarach (moon) are qadar (darkened), and the kawakab (star) asap (withdraw) their nagah (shining).

Yahawah will shaag (roar) from Tzayawan (Zion), and qawal (sound / voice) from Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); and the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)) and the aratz (Earth/land) will raish (shake); but Yahawah will be a machasah (refuge) to his im (people / nation), and a stronghold to the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel).

So you yadai (will) know that I am Yahawah, your Alahayam, shakan (dwelling) in Tzayawan (Zion), my qadash (set apart/make holy) har (mountain). Then Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) will be qadash (set apart/make holy), and no strangers will ibar (pass over/through) through her any more.

It will happen in that yawam (day), that the har (mountain) will natap (drop) down sweet isayas (wine), the gabaih (hills) will yalak (flow) with chalab (milk), all the apayaq (brooks) of Yahawadah (Judah) will yalak (flow) with mayam (Waters), and a maiyan (fountain) will yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and will shaqah (water) the nachal (stream / river) of Shatayam (Shittim).

Matzarayam (Egypt) will be a shamamah (desolation), and Adam (Edom) will be a shamamah (desolate) madabar (wilderness), for the chamas (violence) done to the ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah), because they have shapak (shed) naqay (innocent) dam (blood) in their aratz (Earth/land).
But Yahawadah (Judah) will be yashab (inhabit/dwell) iwalam (forever), and Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) from dawar (generation / age / period) to dawar (generation / age / period).
I will naqah (clean/innocent) their dam (blood), that I have not naqah (clean/innocent): for Yahawah shakan (dwells) in Tzayawan (Zion).

The dabar (word / matter) of Imawas (Amos), who was among the herdsmen of Thaqawai (Tekoa), which he chazah (saw) concerning Yasharaal (Israel) in the yawam (day) of Izayah (Uzziah) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and in the yawam (day) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Yawaash (Joash) malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), two shanah (years) panayam (before) the raish (earthquake).

He amar (spoke): Yahawah will shaag (roar) from Tzayawan (Zion), and nathan (give) his qawal (sound / voice) from Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); and the naah (pastures) of the raih (shepherds) will abal (mourn), and the raash (head) of Karamal (Carmel) will yabash (dry land).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: “For shalawash (three) pashai (transgressions) of Damashaq (Damascus), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they have dawash (threshed) Galaid (Gilead) with charawatz (threshing) instruments of barazal (iron);
But I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) into the bayath (house) of Chazaal (Hazael), and it will akal (eat) the aramawan (palaces) Banahadad (of) Ben Hadad.

I will shabar (break) the barayach (bar) of Damashaq (Damascus), and karath (cut) off the yashab (inhabit/dwell) from the baqaih (valley) of Awan (Aven), and him who thamak (holds) the scepter from the bayath (house) of Eden; and the im (people / nation) of Aram (Syria) shall galah (go) into captivity to Qayar (Kir),” amar (spoke) Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: “For shalawash (three) pashai (transgressions) of Izah (Gaza), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they galah (carried) away captive the shalam (full / whole / complete) community, to sagar (deliver) them up to Adam (Edom);
But I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on the chawamah (wall) of Izah (Gaza), and it will akal (eat) its aramawan (palaces).

I will karath (cut) off the yashab (inhabit/dwell) Ashadawad (from) Ashdod, and him who thamak (holds) the scepter from Ashaqalawan (Ashkelon); and I will shawab (turn back / repent) my yad (hand) against Iqarawan (Ekron); and the shaarayath (remnant) of the Palashathay (Philistines) will abad (destroy/perish),” amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: For shalawash (three) pashai (transgressions) of Tzar (Tyre), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they sagar (delivered) up the shalam (full / whole / complete) community to Adam (Edom), and didn't zakar (remembrance/memory) the ach (brother/kinsman) barayath (covenant);
But I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on the chawamah (wall) of Tzar (Tyre), and it will akal (eat) its aramawan (palaces).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: For shalawash (three) pashai (transgressions) of Adam (Edom), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because he radap (pursued) his ach (brother/kinsman) with the charab (sword), and shachath (cast) off all racham (pity), and his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) raged continually, and he shamar (keep/guard) his ibarah (wrath) natzach (forever);
But I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on Thayaman (Teman), and it will akal (eat) the aramawan (palaces) of Batzarah (Bozrah).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: “For shalawash (three) pashai (transgressions) of the ban (son) of Imawan (Ammon), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they have baqai (ripped) open the pregnant women of Galaid (Gilead), that they may enlarge their gabawal (border/boundary).

But I will yatzath (kindle) a ash (fire) in the chawamah (wall) of Rabah (Rabbah), and it will akal (eat) its aramawan (palaces), with tharawaih (shouting) in the yawam (day) of malachamah (battle), with a sair (storm) in the yawam (day) of the sawapah (whirlwind);
And their malak (king) will halak (move) into gawalah (captivity), he and his shar (prince / ruler) yachad (together),” amar (spoke) Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: “For shalawash (three) pashai (transgressions) of Mawaab (Moab), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because he sharap (burned) the itzam (bones) of the malak (king) of Adam (Edom) into shayad (lime);

But I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on Mawaab (Moab), and it will akal (eat) the aramawan (palaces) of Qarayawath (Kerioth); and Mawaab (Moab) will mawath (death) with shaawan (tumult), with tharawaih (shouting), and with the qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument));
And I will karath (cut) off the shapat (judge) from their qarab (among / near), and will harag (kill) all its shar (prince / ruler) with him,” amar (spoke) Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: For shalawash (three) pashai (transgressions) of Yahawadah (Judah), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they have maas (rejected) yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)) thawarah (instruction), and have not shamar (keep/guard) his chaq (statute), and their kazab (lies) have led them thaih (astray), achar (other) which their ab (father) halak (move);
But I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on Yahawadah (Judah), and it will akal (eat) the aramawan (palaces) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: “For shalawash (three) pashai (transgressions) of Yasharaal (Israel), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they have makar (sold) the tzadayaq (righteous) for kasap (silver), and the abayawan (needy) for a pair of nail (shoes);

They trample on the ipar (dust) of the aratz (Earth/land) on the raash (head) of the dal (poor), and deny darak (justice) to the oppressed; and a ayash (husband/individual man) and his ab (father) use the same nairah (maiden), to chalal (profane) my qadash (set apart/make holy) sham (name);

And they natah (lay) themselves down beside every mazabach (altar) on clothes taken in chabal (pledge); and in the bayath (house) of their Alahayam they shathah (drinks) the yayan (wine) of those who have been fined.

Yet I destroyed the Amaray (Amorite) panayam (before) them, whose gabah (height) was like the gabah (height) of the araz (cedars), and he was chasan (strong) as the alawan (oaks); yet I destroyed his paray (fruit) from mail (top/above), and his sharash (roots) from beneath.

Also I ilah (go up / offer) you up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and yalak (led) you arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years) in the madabar (wilderness), to yarash (possess) the aratz (Earth/land) of the Amaray (Amorite).

I qawam (rise up) up some of your ban (son) for nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and some of your bachawar (young) men for Nazirites. Isn't this true, you ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel)?” Naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.
“But you gave the Nazirites yayan (wine) to shaqah (drink), and tzawah (commanded) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), amar (spoke), ‘Don't nabaa (prophesy)!’
Behold, I will iwaq (crush) you in your place, as a igalah (cart) crushes that is full of grain.

Manawas (flight) will abad (destroy/perish) from the qal (swift); and the chazaq (strong) won't amatz (strengthen) his kach (strength / mighty / power); neither shall the gabawar (mighty) malat (deliver) himself;

Neither shall he imad (stand) who thapash (handles) the qashath (bow); and he who is qal (swift) of ragal (feet / foot) won't malat (escape); neither shall he who rakab (rides) the sawas (horse) malat (deliver) himself;
And he who is amayatz (courageous) among the gabawar (mighty) will nawas (flee) away irawam (naked) on that yawam (day),” naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

Shamai (hearken / hear) this dabar (word / matter) that Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) against you, ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), against the whole mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) which I ilah (go up / offer) up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), amar (spoke):
You only yadai (have) I chosen of all the mashapachah (tribe/clan/family) of the adamah (earth). Therefore I will paqad (visit) you for all of your iwan (guilt/iniquity).
Do shanayam (two) yalak (walk) yachad (together), unless they have yaid (agreed)?
Will a aray (lion) shaag (roar) in the thicket, when he has no tarap (prey)? Does a young kapayar (lion) nathan (give) out of his maiwanah (den), if he has lakad (caught) balathay (nothing)?

Can a tzapawar (bird) napal (fall / be cast down) in a mawaqash (trap) on the aratz (Earth/land), where no pach (snare) is set for him? Does a pach (snare) ilah (go up / offer) up from the adamah (ground), when there is nothing to lakad (catch)?

Does the shawapar (Shawapar(Shofar) - Ram's horn (instrument)) alarm sound in a iyar (city), without the im (people / nation) being charad (afraid)? Does rai (evil) happen to a iyar (city), and Yahawah hasn't ishah (make) it?
Surely the Adanay Yahawah will ishah (make) nothing, unless he galah (reveals) his sawad (secret) to his ibad (servant) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy).
The aray (lion) has shaag (roared). Who will not yaraa (fear / be afraid)? The Adanay Yahawah has dabar (word / matter). Who can but nabaa (prophesy)?

Shamai (hearken / hear) in the aramawan (palaces) Ashadawad (at) Ashdod, and in the aramawan (palaces) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and amar (spoke), asap (assemble) yourselves on the har (mountain) of Shamarawan (Samaria), and raah (see) what unrest is in her, and what ishawaq (oppression) is thawak (midst) them.
"Indeed they don't yadai (know) to ishah (make) nakachah (right)," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, Who hoard plunder and loot in their aramawan (palaces).
Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: An tzar (oppressor / distressor) will overrun the aratz (Earth/land); and he will pull down your strongholds, and your fortresses will be plundered.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: As the raih (shepherd) natzal (rescues) out of the pah (mouth) of the aray (lion) shanayam (two) karai (legs), or a badal (separated) of an azan (ear), so shall the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel) be natzal (rescued) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in Shamarawan (Samaria) on the paah (corner) of a couch, and Damashaq (on) the silken cushions of a matah (bed).
"Shamai (hearken / hear), and iwad (admonish/bear witness against) against the bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob)," naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (troop).

"For in the yawam (day) that I paqad (visit) the pashai (transgressions) of Yasharaal (Israel) on him, I will also paqad (visit) the mazabach (altars) of Bayathaal (Bethel); and the qaran (horn) of the mazabach (altar) will be gadai (cut) off, and napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land).

I will nakah (strike) the charap (winter) bayath (house) with the qayatz (summer) bayath (house); and the bayath (house) of shan (ivory) will abad (destroy/perish), and the rab (great) bayath (house) will sawap (have) an end," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

Shamai (hearken / hear) to this dabar (word / matter), you parah (cows) of Bashan (Bashan), who are on the har (mountain) of Shamarawan (Samaria), who ishaq (oppress) the dal (poor), who ratzatz (crush) the abayawan (needy), who amar (spoke) their adawan (master / lord), bawaa (come) us shathah (drinks)!

The Adanay Yahawah has shabai (swear / take oath) by his qadash (set apart/make holy) that behold, "The yawam (day) shall bawaa (come) on you that they will nashaa (lift) you away with tzanah (hooks), and the acharayath (last) of you with fish tzanah (hooks).

You will yatzaa (go out / come out) out at the breaks in the wall, everyone straight before her; and you will shalak (cast) Haramawan (yourselves) into Harmon," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

"Bawaa (come) to Bayathaal (Bethel), and pashai (sin); to Galagal (Gilgal), and pashai (sin) more. Bawaa (come) your zabach (sacrifices) every baqar (morning), your maishar (tithes) every shalawash (three) yawam (day),

Qatar (offer) a qatar (sacrifice) of thanksgiving of that which is chamatz (leavened), and qaraa (called) free will nadabah (voluntary / freewill offering) and brag about them: for kan (for sure) pleases you, you ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel)," naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah.

"I also nathan (give) given you naqayawan (cleanness) of shan (teeth) in all your iyar (cities), and lack of lacham (bread) in every town; yet you haven't shawab (turn back / repent) to me," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

"I also have withheld the gasham (rain) from you, when there were yet shalawash (three) chadash (month) to the qatzayar (harvest); and I caused it to matar (rain) on achad (one) iyar (city), and caused it not to matar (rain) on another iyar (city). Achad (one) chalaqah (place) was matar (rained) on, and the chalaqah (piece) where it didn't matar (rain) yabash (dry land).

So shanayam (two) or shalawash (three) iyar (cities) nawai (staggered) to achad (one) iyar (city) to shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters), and were not shabai (satisfied): yet you haven't shawab (turn back / repent) to me," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

"I nakah (struck) you with blight and mildew many times in your ganah (gardens) and your karam (vineyards); and your thaan (fig) trees and your zayath (olive) trees have the swarming locust akal (eat): yet you haven't shawab (turn back / repent) to me," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

"I shalach (send) dabar (word / matter) among you like I did Matzarayam (Egypt). I have harag (slain) your bachawar (young) men with the charab (sword), and have carried shabay (away) your sawas (horses); and I filled your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) with the stench of your machanah (camp), yet you haven't shawab (turn back / repent) to me," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

"I have overthrown some of you, as when Alahayam mahapakah (overthrew) Sadam (Sodom) and Imarah (Gomorrah), and you were like a burning stick natzal (plucked) out of the sharapah (fire); yet you haven't shawab (turn back / repent) to me," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

Therefore thus will I ishah (make) to you, Yasharaal (Israel); iqab (award / effect after the cause) I will ishah (make) this to you, kawan (prepare) to qaraah (meet) your Alahayam, Yasharaal (Israel).

For, behold, he who yatzar (forms) the har (mountain), and baraa (created) the rawach (spirit / wind), and nagad (declares) to adam (man) what is his shach (thought); who ishah (make) the shachar (morning) iyapah (darkness), and darak (treads) on the bamah (high) places of the aratz (Earth/land): Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (troop), is his sham (name).
Shamai (hearken / hear) to this dabar (word / matter) which I nashaa (lift) up for a qayanah (lamentation) over you, O bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

The bathawalah (virgin) of Yasharaal (Israel) napal (fall / be cast down) fallen; She shall qawam (rise up) no more. She is natash (cast) down on her adamah (land); there is no one to qawam (rise up) her up.

For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: The iyar (city) that yatzaa (go out / come out) forth a alap (thousand) shall have a maah (hundred) shaar (left), and that which yatzaa (go out / come out) forth one maah (hundred) shall have ishar (ten) shaar (left) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).
For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel): darash (seek) me, and you will chayah (live);

But don't darash (seek) Bayathaal (Bethel), nor bawaa (come) into Galagal (Gilgal), and don't ibar (pass over/through) Baarashabai (to) Beersheba: for Galagal (Gilgal) shall galah (surely) galah (go) into captivity, and Bayathaal (Bethel) shall come to nothing.

Darash (seek) Yahawah, and you will chayah (live); lest he tzalach (break) out like ash (fire) in the bayath (house) of Yawasap (Joseph), and it akal (eat), and there be no one to kabah (quench) it in Bayathaal (Bethel).
You who hapak (turn) mashapat (justice) to lainah (wormwood), and yanach (cast) down tzadaqah (righteousness) to the aratz (Earth/land):

Seek him who ishah (make) the kayamah (pleiades) and kasayal (orion), and hapak (turns) the shadow of tzalamawath (death) into the baqar (morning), and makes the yawam (day) chashak (darkness) with layal (night); who qaraa (called) for the mayam (Waters) of the yam (sea/waters), and shapak (pours) them out on the surface of the aratz (Earth/land), Yahawah is his sham (name),
Who brings sudden shad (destruction) on the iz (strong), so that shad (destruction) bawaa (come) on the mabatzar (fortress).
They shanaa (hate) him who yakach (reproves) in the shair (gate), and they thaib (abhor) him who dabar (word / matter) blamelessly.

Yain (forasmuch) therefore as you trample on the dal (poor), and laqach (take / seized) taxes from him of bar (wheat): You have banah (built) bayath (house) of cut gazayath (stone), but you will not yashab (inhabit/dwell) in them. You have natai (planted) chamad (pleasant) karam (vineyards), but you shall not shathah (drinks) their yayan (wine).

For I yadai (know) how many your offenses, and how itzawam (great) are your chataah (sin)— you who tzarar (afflict) the tzadayaq (righteous), who laqach (take / seized) a kapar (bribe), and who natah (turn) aside the abayawan (needy) in the courts.
Therefore a shakal (prudent) person damam (keeps) silent in such a ith (time), for it is an rai (evil) ith (time).
Darash (seek) tawab (pleasant/functional), and not rai (evil), that you may chayah (live); and so Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (troop), will be with you, as you amar (spoke).

Shanaa (hate) rai (evil), ahab (love) tawab (pleasant/functional), and yatzag (establish) mashapat (justice) in the courts. It may be that Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (troop), will be gracious to the shaarayath (remnant) of Yawasap (Joseph).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (troop), the Adanay: "masapad (wailing) will be in all the rachab (broad) ways; and they will amar (spoke) in all the chawatz (streets), ‘haw (alas)! Haw (alas)!’ And they will qaraa (called) the farmer to abal (mourning), and those who are skillful in nahay (lamentation) to masapad (wailing).
In all karam (vineyards) there will be masapad (wailing); for I will ibar (pass over/through) qarab (among / near) the midst of you," amar (spoke) Yahawah.
Haway (Alas/Woe!) To you who awah (desire) the yawam (day) of Yahawah! Mah (why) do you long for the yawam (day) of Yahawah? It is chashak (darkness), and not awar (light).

As if a ayash (husband/individual man) nawas (fled) from a aray (lion), and a dab (bear) pagai (met) him; Or he bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) and samak (leaned) his yad (hand) on the qayar (wall), and a snake bit him.
Won't the yawam (day) of Yahawah be chashak (darkness), and not awar (light)? Even very apal (dark), and no nagah (brightness) in it?
I shanaa (hate), I maas (despise) your chag (feast/festival), and I can't stand your solemn itzarah (assemblies).

Yes, though you ilah (go up / offer) me your burnt ilah (offerings) and meal manachah (offerings), I will not ratzah (accept) them; neither will I nabat (regard) the shalam (peace) offerings of your marayaa (fat) animals.
Sawar (take) away from me the hamawan (noise) of your shayar (song)! I will not shamai (hearken / hear) to the music of your harps.
But let mashapat (justice) galal (roll) on like mayam (Waters), and tzadaqah (righteousness) like a ayathan (mighty) nachal (stream / river).
"Did you nagash (bring) to me zabach (sacrifices) and manachah (offerings) in the madabar (wilderness) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years), bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
You also nashaa (lift) the sakawath (tent) of your king and the Kayawan (shrine) of your tzalam (likeness), the kawakab (star) of your Alahayam, which you ishah (make) for yourselves.
Therefore will I cause you to galah (go) into captivity halaah (beyond) Damashaq (Damascus)," amar (spoke) Yahawah, whose sham (name) is the Alahayam of tzabaa (troop).

Haway (Alas/Woe!) To those who are at shaanan (ease) in Tzayawan (Zion), and to those who are batach (secure) on the har (mountain) of Shamarawan (Samaria), the notable men of the raashayath (beginning) of the gaway (nation / people), to whom the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) bawaa (come)!

Ibar (pass over/through) to Kalanah (Calneh), and raah (see); and from there yalak (go) to Hamath the rab (great); then yarad (go) down to gath (gath) of the Palashathay (Philistines). Are they tawab (pleasant/functional) than these mamalakah (kingdoms)? Or is their gabawal (border/boundary) greater than your gabawal (border/boundary)?
Those who nadah (put) far away the rai (evil) yawam (day), and cause the shabath (shabath/rest) of chamas (violence) to nagash (come) near;

Who shakab (lie) on matah (beds) of shan (ivory), and sarach (stretch) themselves on their couches, and akal (eat) the kar (lambs) out of the tzaan (flock), and the calves out of the thawak (midst) of the marabaq (stall);
Who strum on the strings of a harp; who chashab (invent) for themselves kalay (instruments) of music, like Dawad (David);
Who shathah (drinks) yayan (wine) in mazaraq (bowls), and mashach (anoint) themselves with the best shaman (oils); but they are not chalah (afflict) for the shabar (affliction) of Yawasap (Joseph).
Therefore they will now galah (go) captive with the raash (head) who galah (go) captive; and the feasting and lounging will end.

"The Adanay Yahawah has shabai (swear / take oath) by himself," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (troop): I thaab (abhor) the gaawan (pride) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and detest his fortresses. Therefore I will sagar (deliver) up the iyar (city) with malaa (all) that is in it.
It will happen, if there yathar (remain) ishar (ten) ayash (husband/individual man) in achad (one) bayath (house), that they shall mawath (death).

When a dawad (man's) relative nashaa (lift) him, even he who sarap (burns) him, to yatzaa (go out / come out) bodies out of the bayath (house), and asks him who is in the innermost yarakah (parts) of the bayath (house), ‘Is there yet any with you?’ And he amar (spoke), ‘No;’ then he will amar (spoke), ‘Hush! Indeed we must not zakar (remembrance/memory) the sham (name) of Yahawah.’
“For, behold, Yahawah tzawah (commands), and the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) bayath (house) will be smashed to pieces, and the qatan (small/young/least) bayath (house) into bits.

Do sawas (horses) rawatz (run) on the rocky crags? Does one charash (plow) there with oxen? But you have hapak (turned) mashapat (justice) into raash (head), and the paray (fruit) of tzadaqah (righteousness) into bitterness;
You who shamach (rejoice) in a thing of nothing, who amar (spoke), ‘Haven't we laqach (take / seized) for ourselves qaran (horn) by our own chazaq (strength)?’

For, behold, I will qawam (rise up) up against you a gaway (nation / people), bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel),” naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (troop); and they will lachatz (afflict) you from the entrance of Chamath (Hamath) to the nachal (stream / river) of the irabah (arabah).

Thus the Adanay Yahawah showed me: and behold, he yatzar (formed) locusts in the thachalah (beginning) of the ilah (go up / offer) up of the laqash (latter) growth; and behold, it was the laqash (latter) growth achar (other) the malak (king) harvest.

It happened that, when they kalah (complete / finish) an end of akal (eat) the ishab (grass) of the aratz (Earth/land), then I amar (spoke), Adanay Yahawah, salach (forgive/pardon/make clean), I beg you! How could Yaiqab (Jacob) qawam (rise up)? For he is qatan (small/young/least).
Yahawah relented concerning this. "It shall not be," amar (spoke) Yahawah.

Thus the Adanay Yahawah showed me and behold, the Adanay Yahawah qaraa (called) for rayab (judgment) by ash (fire); and it dried up the rab (great) thahawam (depths), and would have akal (eat) the chalaq (land).
Then I amar (spoke), Adanay Yahawah, stop, I beg you! How could Yaiqab (Jacob) qawam (rise up)? For he is qatan (small/young/least).
Yahawah relented concerning this. "This also shall not be," amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah.
Thus he showed me and behold, the Adanay natzab (stood) beside a chawamah (wall) made by a anak (plumb) line, with a anak (plumb) line in his yad (hand).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, "Imawas (Amos), what do you raah (see)?" I amar (spoke), "A anak (plumb) line." Then the Adanay amar (spoke), Behold, I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) a anak (plumb) line in the qarab (among / near) of my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel). I will not again ibar (pass over/through) by them any more.

The bamah (high) places of Yashachaq (Isaac) will be shamam (desolate), the maqadash (sanctuaries) of Yasharaal (Israel) will be charab (laid) waste; and I will qawam (rise up) against the bayath (house) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) with the charab (sword).

Then Amatzayah (Amaziah) the kahan (priest) of Bayathaal (Bethel) shalach (send) to Yarabaim (Jeroboam) malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (spoke), Imawas (Amos) has qashar (conspired) against you in the qarab (among / near) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel). The aratz (Earth/land) is not yakal (able) to kawal (all/every/entire) all his dabar (word / matter).
For Imawas (Amos) amar (spoke), ‘Yarabaim (Jeroboam) will mawath (death) by the charab (sword), and Yasharaal (Israel) shall galah (surely) be galah (led) away captive out of his adamah (land).’

Amatzayah (Amaziah) also amar (spoke) to Imawas (Amos), You chazah (seer), yalak (go), barach (flee) away into the aratz (Earth/land) of Yahawadah (Judah), and there akal (eat) lacham (bread), and nabaa (prophesy) there:
But don't nabaa (prophesy) again any more at Bayathaal (Bethel); for it is the malak (king) maqadash (sanctuary), and it is a mamalakah (royal) bayath (house)!

Then Imawas (Amos) inah (answer / respond) Amatzayah (Amaziah), I was no nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), neither was I a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) ban (son); but I was a herdsman, and a farmer of shaqamah (sycamore) figs;
And Yahawah laqach (take / seized) me from achar (other) the tzaan (flock), and Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, ‘yalak (go), nabaa (prophesy) to my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel).’

Now therefore shamai (hearken / hear) to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah: ‘You amar (spoke), Don't nabaa (prophesy) against Yasharaal (Israel), and don't preach against the bayath (house) of Yashachaq (Isaac).’

Therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: ‘Your ashah (wife/individual woman) shall be a prostitute in the iyar (city), and your ban (son) and your bath (daughter) shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword), and your adamah (land) shall be chalaq (divided) by chabal (line); and you yourself shall mawath (death) in a adamah (land) that is tamaa (unclean), and Yasharaal (Israel) shall galah (surely) be galah (led) away captive out of his adamah (land).’
Thus the Adanay Yahawah showed me: behold, a kalawab (basket) of qayatz (summer) fruit.

He amar (spoke), "Imawas (Amos), what do you raah (see)?" I amar (spoke), "A kalawab (basket) of qayatz (summer) fruit." Then Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, "The qatz (end) bawaa (come) come on my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel). I will not again ibar (pass over/through) by them any more.

The shayar (song) of the hayakal (temple) will be wailings in that yawam (day)," naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah. The pagar (dead) bodies will be many. In every maqawam (place) they will shalak (throw) them out with hasah (silence).
Shamai (hearken / hear) this, you who shaap (desire) to swallow up the abayawan (needy), and shabath (shabath/rest) the abayawan (poor) of the aratz (Earth/land) to shabath (shabath/rest),

Amar (spoke), ‘When will the new chadash (month) be ibar (pass over/through), that we may shabar (sell) grain? And the shabath (shabath/rest), that we may market bar (wheat), making the ayapah (ephah) qatan (small/young/least), and the shaqal (shekel) large, and iwath (dealing) falsely with maazan (balances) of maramah (deceit);
That we may qanah (buy) the dal (poor) for kasap (silver), and the abayawan (needy) for a pair of nail (shoes), and shabar (sell) the sweepings with the bar (wheat)?’
Yahawah has shabai (swear / take oath) by the gaawan (pride) of Yaiqab (Jacob), "Surely I will never shakach (forget) any of their maishah (works).

Won't the aratz (Earth/land) ragaz (tremble) for this, and everyone abal (mourn) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in it? Yes, it will ilah (go up / offer) up wholly like the yaar (river); and it will be stirred up and sink again, like the yaar (river) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

It will happen in that yawam (day)," naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, "that I will cause the shamash (sun) to bawaa (come) down at tzahar (noon), and I will chashak (darkness) the aratz (Earth/land) in the awar (light) yawam (day).

I will hapak (turn) your chag (feast/festival) into abal (mourning), and all your shayar (song) into qayanah (lamentation); and I will ilah (go up / offer) you wear sackcloth on all your bodies, and qarachah (baldness) on every raash (head). I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) it like the abal (mourning) for an only son, and its acharayath (end) like a mar (bitter) yawam (day).

Behold, the yawam (day) bawaa (come)," naam (declares (prophetically)) the Adanay Yahawah, that I will shalach (send) a raib (famine) in the aratz (Earth/land), not a raib (famine) of lacham (bread), nor a tzamaa (thirst) for mayam (Waters), but of shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah.

They will nawai (wander) from yam (sea/waters) to yam (sea/waters), and from the tzapawan (north) even to the mazarach (east); they will shawat (run) back and forth to baqash (seek) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, and will not matzaa (find) it.
In that yawam (day) the yapah (beautiful) bathawalah (virgins) and the bachawar (young) men will ilap (faint) for tzamaa (thirst).

Those who shabai (swear / take oath) by the ashamah (sin) of Shamarawan (Samaria), and amar (spoke), ‘As your Alahayam, Dan (Dan), chay (life);’ and, ‘As the darak (way) Baarashabai (of) Beersheba chay (life);’ they will napal (fall / be cast down), and never qawam (rise up) up again.

I raah (see) the Adanay natzab (standing) beside the mazabach (altar), and he amar (spoke), “nakah (strike) the tops of the pillars, that the sap (thresholds) may raish (shake); and break them in pieces on the raash (head) of all of them; and I will harag (kill) the acharayath (last) of them with the charab (sword): there shall not one of them nawas (flee) nawas (away), and there shall not one of them palayat (escape).

Though they chathar (dig) into shaawal (Shaawal/afterlife), there my yad (hand) will laqach (take / seized) them; and though they ilah (go up / offer) up to shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), there I will yarad (bring) them down.

Though they chabaa (hide) themselves in the raash (head) of Karamal (Carmel), I will chapash (search) and laqach (take / seized) them out there; and though they be sathar (hidden) from my iyan (eye) in the qaraqai (bottom) of the yam (sea/waters), there I will tzawah (command) the nachash (serpent), and it will nashak (bite) them.

Though they yalak (go) into shabay (captivity) panayam (before) their ayab (enemy), there I will tzawah (command) the charab (sword), and it will harag (kill) them. I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) my iyan (eye) on them for rai (evil), and not for tawab (pleasant/functional).

For the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (troop), is he who touches the aratz (Earth/land) and it mawag (melts), and all who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in it will abal (mourn); and it will ilah (go up / offer) up wholly like the yaar (river), and will shaqai (sink) again, like the yaar (river) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

It is he who banah (builds) his rooms in the shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), and has founded his vault on the aratz (Earth/land); he who qaraa (called) for the mayam (Waters) of the yam (sea/waters), and shapak (pours) them out on the surface of the aratz (Earth/land); Yahawah is his sham (name).

Are you not like the ban (son) of the Kawashay (Ethiopians) to me, ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel)?” Naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah. "Haven't I ilah (go up / offer) up Yasharaal (Israel) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and the Palashathay (Philistines) from Kapathar (Caphtor), and the Aram (Syrians) from Qayar (Kir)?

Behold, the iyan (eye) of the Adanay Yahawah are on the sinful mamalakah (kingdom), and I will shamad (destroy) it from off the surface of the adamah (earth); except that I will not shamad (utterly) shamad (destroy) the bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob)," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

“For, behold, I will tzawah (command), and I will nawai (sift) the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) among all the gaway (nation / people), as grain is nawai (sifted) in a kabarah (sieve), yet not the tzarawar (least) kernel will napal (fall / be cast down) on the aratz (Earth/land).
All the chataa (sinners) of my im (people / nation) will mawath (death) by the charab (sword), who amar (spoke), ‘rai (evil) won't nagash (overtake) nor qadam (meet) us.’

In that yawam (day) I will qawam (rise up) up the sakah (tent) of Dawad (David) who is napal (fall / be cast down), and gadar (close) up its breaches, and I will qawam (rise up) up its harayasah (ruins), and I will banah (build) it as in the yawam (day) of iwalam (forever);

That they may yarash (possess) the shaarayath (remnant) of Adam (Edom), and all the gaway (nation / people) who are qaraa (called) by my sham (name),” naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah who ishah (make) this.

"Behold, the yawam (day) bawaa (come)," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, “that the plowman shall nagash (overtake) the qatzar (reaper), and the one darak (treading) inab (grapes) him who mashak (sows) zarai (seed); and sweet isayas (wine) will drip from the gabaih (mountains), and flow from the gabaih (hills).

I will bring my im (people / nation) Yasharaal (Israel) shawab (turn back / repent) from shabawath (captivity), and they will rebuild the ruined iyar (cities), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) them; and they will natai (plant) karam (vineyards), and shathah (drinks) yayan (wine) from them. They shall also ishah (make) ganah (gardens), and akal (eat) their paray (fruit).
I will natai (plant) them on their adamah (land), and they will no more be nathash (plucked) up out of their adamah (land) which I nathan (give) given them,” amar (spoke) Yahawah your Alahayam.

The chazawan (vision) of Ibadayah (Obadiah). This is what the Adanay Yahawah amar (spoke) about Adam (Edom). We have shamai (hearken / hear) shamawaih (news) from Yahawah, and an tzayar (ambassador) is shalach (send) among the gaway (nation / people), saying, “qawam (rise up), and let's qawam (rise up) up against her in malachamah (battle).
Behold, I nathan (give) made you qatan (small/young/least) among the gaway (nation / people). You are maad (greatly) bazah (despised).

The zadawan (pride) of your lab (heart) has nashaa (lift) you, you who shakan (dwell) in the chagaw (clefts) of the salai (rock), whose shakan (habitation) is marawam (high), who amar (spoke) in his lab (heart), ‘Who will yarad (bring) me down to the aratz (Earth/land)?’

Though you gabah (mount) on high as the nashar (eagle), and though your qan (nest) is shawam (place / establish / appoint) among the kawakab (star), I will yarad (bring) you down from there,” naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah.

If thieves bawaa (come) to you, if shadad (robbers) by layal (night)— oh, what disaster awaits you— wouldn't they only ganab (steal) until they had day (enough)? If grape pickers bawaa (come) to you, wouldn't they shaar (leave) some gleaning ilalah (grapes)?
How Ishaw (Esau) will be ransacked! How his matzapan (hidden) treasures are sought out!

All the ayash (husband/individual man) of your alliance have shalach (send) you on your way, even to the gabawal (border/boundary). The ayash (husband/individual man) who were at shalawam (peace / safety) with you have nashaa (lift) you, and yakal (prevailed) against you. Friends who eat your lacham (bread) shawam (place / establish / appoint) a snare under you. There is no thabawan (understanding) in him.

"Won't I in that yawam (day)," naam (declares (prophetically)) Yahawah, “abad (destroy/perish) the chakam (wise) men out of Adam (Edom), and thabawan (understanding) out of the har (mountain) of Ishaw (Esau)?
Your gabawar (mighty) men, Thayaman (Teman), will be chathath (dismayed), to the end that everyone may be karath (cut) off from the har (mountain) of Ishaw (Esau) by qatal (slaughter).
For the chamas (violence) done to your ach (brother/kinsman) Yaiqab (Jacob), bawashah (shame) will kasah (cover) you, and you will be karath (cut) off iwalam (forever).

In the yawam (day) that you imad (stood) on the other side, in the yawam (day) that strangers shabah (carried) away his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), and nakaray (foreigners) bawaa (come) into his shair (gates), and yadad (cast) gawaral (lots) for Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), even you were like achad (one) of them.

But don't raah (see) down on your ach (brother/kinsman) in the yawam (day) of his disaster, and don't shamach (rejoice) over the ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah) in the yawam (day) of their abad (destroy/perish). Don't pah (speak) gadal (proudly) in the yawam (day) of tzarah (distress).

Don't bawaa (come) into the shair (gate) of my im (people / nation) in the yawam (day) of their ayad (calamity). Don't raah (see) down on their rai (affliction) in the yawam (day) of their ayad (calamity), neither seize their wealth on the yawam (day) of their ayad (calamity).
Don't imad (stand) in the crossroads to karath (cut) off those of his who palayat (escape). Don't sagar (deliver) up those of his who sharayad (remain) in the yawam (day) of tzarah (distress).

For the yawam (day) of Yahawah is qarawab (near) all the gaway (nation / people)! As you ishah (make) done, it will be ishah (make) to you. Your deeds will shawab (turn back / repent) upon your own raash (head).

For as you have shathah (drinks) on my qadash (set apart/make holy) har (mountain), so will all the gaway (nation / people) shathah (drinks) continually. Yes, they will shathah (drinks), lawai (swallow) down, and will be as laa (NOT) they had not been.

But in har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion), there will be those who palayatah (escape), and it will be qadash (set apart/make holy). The bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob) will yarash (possess) their mawarash (possessions).

The bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob) will be a ash (fire), the bayath (house) of Yawasap (Joseph) a lahabah (flame), and the bayath (house) of Ishaw (Esau) for qash (stubble). They will dalaq (burn) among them, and akal (eat) them. There will not be any sharayad (remaining) to the bayath (house) of Ishaw (Esau).” Indeed, Yahawah has dabar (word / matter).

Those of the nagab (south) will yarash (possess) the har (mountain) of Ishaw (Esau), and those of the lowland, the Palashathay (Philistines). They will yarash (possess) the shadah (field) of Aparayam (Ephraim), and the shadah (field) of Shamarawan (Samaria). Banayamayan (Benjamin) will possess Galaid (Gilead).

The galawath (captives) of this chayal (army) of the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel), who are among the Kanainay (Canaanites), will possess even to Tzarapath (Zarephath); and the galawath (captives) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), who are in Saparad (Sepharad), will yarash (possess) the iyar (cities) of the Negev.

Saviors will ilah (go up / offer) up on har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion) to shapat (judge) the har (mountain) of Ishaw (Esau), and the malawakah (kingdom) will be yahawah (Yahawah (Alahay of Yasharaal)).
Now the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Yawanah (Jonah) the ban (son) of Amathay (Amittai), amar (spoke),

Qawam (rise up), yalak (go) to Nayanawah (Nineveh), that gadawal (very great/important/mighty) iyar (city), and qaraa (called) against it, for their rai (wickedness) has ilah (go up / offer) up panayam (before) me.

But Yawanah (Jonah) qawam (rise up) up to barach (flee) to Tharashayash (Tarshish) from the panayam (presence) of Yahawah. He yarad (went) down to Yapaw (Joppa), and matzaa (found) a anayah (ship) bawaa (come) to Tharashayash (Tarshish); so he nathan (give) its fare, and yarad (went) down into it, to bawaa (come) with them to Tharashayash (Tarshish) from the panayam (presence) of Yahawah.

But Yahawah tawal (sent) out a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) rawach (spirit / wind) on the yam (sea/waters), and there was a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) sair (storm) on the yam (sea/waters), so that the anayah (ship) was likely to shabar (break) up.

Then the malach (mariners) were yaraa (fear / be afraid), and every ayash (husband/individual man) zaiq (cried) to his Alahayam. They threw the cargo that was in the anayah (ship) into the yam (sea/waters) to lighten the ship. But Yawanah (Jonah) had yarad (gone) down into the innermost yarakah (parts) of the sapayanah (ship), and he was shakab (laying) down, and was radam (fast) asleep.

So the rab (shipmaster) qarab (come close) to him, and amar (spoke) to him, What do you mean, sleeper? Qawam (rise up), qaraa (called) on your Alahayam! Maybe your Alahayam will notice us, so that we won't abad (destroy/perish).

They all amar (spoke) to ayash (husband/individual man) other, "yalak (come), napal (fall / be cast down) us cast gawaral (lots), that we may yadai (know) who is responsible for this rai (evil) that is on us." So they napal (fall / be cast down) gawaral (lots), and the gawaral (lot) napal (fall / be cast down) on Yawanah (Jonah).

Then they asked him, nagad (tell) us, please, for whose cause this rai (evil) is on us. What is your malaakah (occupation)? Ayan (where) do you bawaa (come) from? What is your aratz (Earth/land)? Of what im (people / nation) are you?
He amar (spoke) to them, I am a ibaray (hebrew), and I yaraa (fear) Yahawah, the Alahayam of shamayam (Shamayam/(Heavens)), who ishah (make) made the yam (sea/waters) and the dry yabashah (dry land).

Then were the ayash (husband/individual man) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) yaraa (fear / be afraid), and amar (spoke) to him, "What is this that you ishah (make) done?" For the ayash (husband/individual man) yadai (knew) that he was fleeing from the panayam (presence) of Yahawah, because he had nagad (told) them.
Then they amar (spoke) to him, "What shall we ishah (make) to you, that the yam (sea/waters) may be shathaq (calm) to us?" For the yam (sea/waters) halak (move) more and more stormy.

He amar (spoke) to them, nashaa (lift) me up, and throw me into the yam (sea/waters). Then the yam (sea/waters) will be shathaq (calm) for you; for I yadai (know) that because of me this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) sair (storm) is on you.

Nevertheless the ayash (husband/individual man) chathar (rowed) hard to shawab (turn back / repent) them back to the yabashah (dry land); but they yakal (could) not, for the yam (sea/waters) halak (move) more and more stormy against them.

Therefore they qaraa (called) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), We beg you, Yahawah, we beg you, don't let us die for this ayash (husband/individual man) napash (living being/soul), and don't nathan (give) on us naqay (innocent) dam (blood); for you, Yahawah, ishah (make) done as it chapatz (pleased) you.
So they nashaa (lift) up Yawanah (Jonah), and threw him into the yam (sea/waters); and the yam (sea/waters) imad (ceased) its zaip (raging).
Then the ayash (husband/individual man) yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah gadawal (very great/important/mighty); and they zabach (offered) a zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah, and made nadar (vow).

Yahawah manah (prepared) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) dag (fish) to balai (swallow) up Yawanah (Jonah), and he was in the maih (belly) of the dag (fish) shalawash (three) yawam (day) and shalawash (three) layal (nights).
Then Yawanah (Jonah) prayed to Yahawah, his Alahayam, out of the dag (fish's) maih (belly).
He said, I called because of my affliction to Yahawah. He answered me. Out of the maih (belly) of Sheol I cried. You heard my voice.
For you threw me into the depths, in the heart of the seas. The flood was all around me. All your waves and your billows passed over me.
I said, ‘I have been banished from your sight; yet I will look again toward your holy temple.’
The waters surrounded me, even to the soul. The deep was around me. The weeds were wrapped around my head.
